# Glossary

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/glossary.htm

## Glossary

The following table lists definitions of terms used in the documentation:

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Pipeline Pilot Server | Server used by Discovery Studio that uses data pipelining to perform complex calculations. See About Pipeline Pilot . |
| ADME | Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion. You can use the Calculate Molecular Properties tools to calculate these properties. |
| AminoAcid | An AminoAcid object in the Molecule Window represents a single amino acid residue. |
| AminoAcidChain | An AminoAcidChain object in the Molecule Window represents a collection of amino acid residues. Residues are listed from amino to carboxyl terminus. Consecutive residues are connected by peptide bonds unless there are gaps. |
| Animation | A series of molecular conformations, typically the results of a molecular dynamics analysis, representing the state of a structure through time. Animations can be played to visualize the behavior of a system. You can create and play animations from the Structure \| Animation menu. |
| Application Programming Interface (API) | A set of routines, methods, and tools for building software applications. Critical components of a good API are a rich programmatic interface provided with complete documentation. A good API makes it easier to develop a program by providing all the building blocks for a programmer to assemble. |
| Application Workspace | The central area of the visualizer client where the editor and viewer windows are located. |
| Attribute | An attribute of an object in Discovery Studio is a specific data variable that can be modified either by the user or the application. You can view and in some cases edit attributes by using the Attributes dialog . |
| BLAST | Basic Local Alignment Search Tool. For more information, see BLAST Search . |
| Bioinformatic Sequence Markup Language (BSML) | An extensible language specification and container for bioinformatic data. For more information, see Bioinformatic Sequence Markup Language (BSML) . |
| Cambridge Crystallographic Data Center (CCDC) | CCDC is a non-profit, charitable Institution whose objectives are the general advancement and promotion of the science of chemistry and crystallography for the public benefit. Discovery Studio uses CCDC GOLD for some ligand docking protocols. For more information see Dock Ligands (GOLD) and Score Ligand Poses . |
| Catalyst | A scientific server application that provides functionality for analyzing pharmacophore data. For more information, see Catalyst . |
| Cell | A cell object in the Molecule Window represents the 3D repeat unit of a periodic, infinite structure. The geometry of the cell, a parallelepiped, is characterized by the three cell lengths (a, b, c) and the three cell angles (alpha, beta, gamma). Symmetry constraints beyond the translational periodicity may also be present and are identified by one of the 230 possible crystallographic symmetry space groups. In the Hierarchy View, cells are found as top-level objects that contain one or more molecules. |
| Cerius 2 | Cerius 2 is a user-friendly graphical molecular modelling program that incorporates a wide variety of popular molecular modelling codes in materials sciences, life sciences and drug design. |
| CentOS | CentOS is a Linux distribution that provides a free, enterprise-class, community-supported computing platform functionally compatible with Red Hat Enterprise Linux. |
| Chain | A chain object in the Molecule Window represents a collection of residues that cannot be classified as either amino acids or nucleotides. For example, in structures from the PDB repository, water molecules are collected in a single chain labeled "Water". |
| Chain Break | A chain break is a location in a protein sequence that indicates a physical break between two polymer chains in that structure. Chain breaks are stored as features in the sequence data model, and are visually represented by vertical lines in the Sequence Window. For more information, see Working with sequence data . |
| CHARMm | A scientific server application that provides functionality for performing molecular mechanics based analysis of molecular structure data. For more information, see CHARMm . |
| CHARMm forcefields | CHARMm, CHARMm Polar H, charmm19, charmm22, charmm27, and charmm36 forcefields are supported. For more information, see Work with forcefields and Supported forcefields . |
| Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD) | A dictionary containing the definition (in mmCIF format) of all small molecules found in the PDB, including macromolecular building blocks (amino acids, nucleotides), ions, ligands, cofactors, inhibitors and solvent molecules. Residues in files read from the PDB in pdb or mmCIF format have a 3 or 5 character CCD ID, referred to in Discovery Studio as the PDB Name. |
| Clipping Plane | Clipping planes are used to prevent the Graphics view from rendering portions of a structure at extreme distances from the viewer. A clipping plane is usually perpendicular to the observer and occupies the entire viewing port. Adjusting the position of clipping planes improves your ability to focus on a particular aspect of a 3D structure. You can control clipping planes with the Clipping Planes dialog . |
| CNX | Crystallography and NMR eXplorer (CNX) is a software program suite for three-dimensional structure determination and analysis of macromolecules using experimental crystallographic diffraction or nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) data. For more information, see MODELER . |
| Component | In Pipeline Pilot Server , data processing functionality is packaged in building blocks called components, which are assembled into protocols to pipe and process data. They act like a "black box" where internal workings carry out the specific function of the component on items in a data stream. As data flows through a pipeline, each component processes the data and then passes it on to a subsequent component or outputs it to a file. Data enters a component through its input port and exits via the output ports. Depending on the type of component, it may or may not use all of the available input and output ports. For more information, see Using Pipeline Pilot . |
| Conformation | A conformation represents alternate 3D coordinates, occupancies, and isotropic displacements for a collection of atoms. Conformations are typically created for molecules that have a large number of alternate locations for a large subset of the atoms. This representation does not treat the conformations as separate atoms, but as separate data for the same atoms. When a conformation is made the active conformation, its 3D coordinates, occupancies, and isotropic displacements are substituted for those of the atoms. Only one conformation can be considered the active conformation at a given time. Geometry monitors reflect the properties of this active conformation. Conformations can be created using the Generate Conformations protocol. |
| Conformer | Conformers are typically created for molecules that have a small number of alternate locations for a small subset of the atoms. Conformers are represented by conformer atoms and conformer bonds, which can be manipulated similarly to, and independently of, other atoms and bonds. There are no constraints on the number of conformers, although there are usually between 2 and 4 for the residues where conformers are defined. In the Data Table View, conformers can be found under the Conformer tab, conformer atoms are listed under the ConformerAtom tab, and conformer bonds are found under the ConformerBond tab. Conformers belonging to the same model are grouped under a conformer model, which is listed under the ConformerModel tab. For more information, see Generating Conformers for Molecules . |
| Contact Plot | A two-dimensional matrix plot that represents all pairwise distances between the residues of a protein structure. Contact plots are a useful for visualizing the similarity patterns within a structure. For more information, see Contact Plot . |
| Consistent Force Field (cff) | Class II all-atom forcefield for proteins, nucleic acids, and general organic molecules. For for information, see Work with forcefields and Supported forcefields . |
| Context Menu | A menu that offers a list of commands appropriate for the context of the command and the object selected. Context menus are invoked by right-clicking in the user interface. |
| CUDA | CUDA is a parallel computing platform and application programming interface (API) model created by NVIDIA. It supports GPU computing on NVIDIA graphics cards. |
| Data Model | A data model is an abstract model that describes how data is represented and accessed. In the context of Discovery Studio , data models are the programmatic constructs that contain information about the properties and state of different data. Examples of data models are the molecular data model (MDM), the sequence data model (SDM) and the force field data model (FFDM). You can access data models directly through the DiscoveryScript API. |
| Data Pipelining | The rapid, independent processing of data through a branching network of computational steps. It is a powerful tool for connecting different data sources, databases, and applications. |
| Data Table View | An interactive spreadsheet view of data in the Molecule Window. Selections in this view are also made in the Graphics and Hierarchy views. Press CTRL+T to toggle the view. For more information, see Data Table View . |
| PBEQ | A scientific server application that provides functionality for performing electrostatics analysis. |
| Dendrogram | A tree diagram used to illustrate hierarchical clustering of genes or samples. |
| Density Map | Electron density map, but also used to refer to any set of 1D data values defined on a finite, regular 3D grid whose boundaries form a parallelepiped. The density map can be visualized as one or more 3D contours representing surfaces of constant data values, or the data values themselves can be visualized. 3D contours created from a density map are also referred to as density maps; the underlying volumetric data are shared. You can generate an electron density map using the Generate Electron Density Maps protocol. |
| DMol 3 | A scientific server application that provides functionality for performing density functional theory (DFT) quantum mechanics. You can use the Calculate Energy (DFT) protocol to calculate the energy or optimize the geometry of a set of small molecules using density functional quantum mechanics method in DMol 3 . |
| Dock | Refers to different locations in the Discovery Studio Visualizer where Explorer Windows can be displayed. There are three dock locations: Left, Bottom, and Right. You can use shortcut keys to quickly toggle the visibility of Explorer windows located in the different docks. For more information, see Customizing the client . |
| Dreiding Minimization | The application of the Dreiding forcefield with a steepest descent minimizer to optimize all, or a selected portion, of a structure. You can perform Dreiding minimization using the Minimize Ligands tools . |
| Entity | In the RCSB database, the term refers to a unique molecule, which may be a polymer chain, water molecule, or moiety such as a ligand or ion. In Discovery Studio , the Entity property is read for protein and nucleic acid chains from mmCIF format files. It is important to remember that these entities represent ideal molecular structures or sequences rather than the resolved experimental structures. A multimeric structure can contain multiple instances of the same entity. For further information, see PDB/mmCIF Data Category entity . |
| Extensible Markup Language (XML) | General standard for creating more specific schema that describe the structure of data. For more information, see Extensible Markup Language (XML) . |
| Files Explorer | A dockable view that allows you to view and manage files that are accessible on your local machine. For more information, see Files Explorer . |
| Forcefield | The functional form and parameter sets used to describe the potential energy of a system of particles. For more information, see Change Forcefield tools . For more information about choosing a forcefield, see Supported forcefields . |
| Genetic Optimization for Ligand Docking (GOLD) | A scientific server application for calculating the docking modes of small molecules in protein binding sites. It is developed and distributed by the Cambridge Crystallographic Data Centre ( CCDC ). For more information see Dock Ligands (GOLD) and Score Ligand Poses . |
| GDPR | General Data Protection Regulation , referred to as GDPR. |
| GPU | GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) runs heavily parallelized calculations on graphics cards.Originally developed for manipulating computer graphics and image processing, it is used extensively for scientific computing. Some server programs, such as CHARMm in Discovery Studio , can be run on GPU. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_processing_unit . |
| Graphics Hardware Accelerator | Coprocessors that assist in drawing graphics on computers. Accelerators are generally more efficient than CPU for rendering graphics because they are closer to the graphics memory. The client has a hardware acceleration preference that you can set manually from the Graphics subpage - Preferences dialog . The client automatically checks your graphics configuration and opens the Hardware Acceleration dialog if you have a supported configuration but have the preference disabled, or if you have the preference enabled, but you do not have a supported graphics configuration. |
| Graphics View | This view provides an interactive visual representation of the data in the Molecule Window. Selections in this view are also made in the Data Table and Hierarchy views. Press CTRL+G to toggle this view. For more information, see Graphics View . |
| Group | You can select a number of objects in the Molecule Window and create a group by right-clicking and choosing Group... . You can choose the group from the Hierarchy View at any time to reselect that group of objects. |
| Hierarchy View | Provides an interactive tree view of the data in the Molecule Window. Selections in this view are also made in the Data Table and Graphics Table views. You can toggle it by pressing CTRL+H. Fore more information, see Hierarchy View . |
| Homology | Similarity between molecular sequences or structures that is due to their shared ancestry. You can create homology models using the Create Homology Models tools . |
| HyperText Markup Language (HTML) | Predominant markup language for web pages. For more information, see Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) . |
| Integrated Development Environment (IDE) | Set of integrated tools for developing software. Discovery Studio scripts can be developed and run in a Perl interactive development environment. For more information, see Running scripts . |
| Isosurface | An isosurface is a 3D contour map displayed as a surface that represents points of constant value of a single-valued function f defined within a volume of 3D space: f(x, y, z) = c where x, y, z are the Cartesian coordinates of a point in 3D space and c is the contour value or isovalue. In the Visualizer data model, a density map or an isosurface object represents the contour. |
| Insight II | Insight II is a comprehensive graphic molecular modeling program. |
| Jobs Explorer | A dockable view in the Discovery Studio Visualizer that provides information about jobs launched by Discovery Studio . You can use the Jobs Explorer to monitor or cancel jobs that are running, and access the results of completed jobs. For more information, see Jobs Explorer . |
| Ludi | A scientific server application for performing de novo molecular design. You can access this functionality from the Fragment Based Design tools . |
| Material properties | Characteristic properties of OpenGL objects that define the ambient, diffuse, emission colors, shininess, and specular of emitted light. |
| Menu bar | Located at the top of the interface, the menus provide access to groups of tools that range from basic copy-paste and file opening functionality to tools that affect the display of data or run calculations. For more information, see Working with menu tools . |
| Merck Molecular Force Field (MMFF) | A family of force fields developed by Merck Research Laboratories, based on the MM3 forcefield. For for information, see Work with forcefields and Supported forcefields . |
| MODELER | A scientific server package for performing protein modeling tasks. MODELER is used for many homology modeling tasks in Discovery Studio . For more information, see MODELER . |
| Molecular Dynamics (MD) | A simulation in which a set of atoms interacts for a period of time under the laws of classical mechanics. This can yield a model of a structure's motion or explore conformations. You can set up and run molecular dynamics simulations using the Run Simulations tools . |
| Molecular Data Model (MDM) | Data model used by Discovery Studio to define molecular objects. Properties include atoms, bonds, chains, etc. |
| Molecular Mechanics (MM) | The use of Newtonian mechanics to model molecular systems. Atoms are represented as balls and bonds as springs. The potential energy of the system can be calculated and minimized using an appropriate forcefield. For for information, see Work with forcefields . |
| Molecule Window | Provides a view of molecular data in graphics, data table, and hierarchy views. For more information, see Working with the Molecule Window . |
| Molecular Surface | A surface that represents the three-dimensional shape of a molecule. In the Molecule Window, molecular surfaces can also be constructed for parts of molecules or for molecular assemblies. For more information, see Working with surfaces . |
| Monitor | A monitor is an object created in the Visualizer that allows you to track a particular measurement in a system as other parts of that system vary. For example, a distance monitor reports the physical distance between two objects and updates its value as those objects are moved relative to each other. You can set monitors from the Structure \| Monitor menu. |
| National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) | Part of the United States National Library of Medicine (NLM), a branch of the NIH, maintains genome sequencing data in GenBank. GenBank can be searched using the BLAST and Entrez programs. Discovery Studio provides access to these programs via the BLAST Search and NCBI Entrez Sequence Search protocols. |
| NucleicAcidChain | A NucleicAcidChain object in the Molecule Window represents a collection of nucleotide residues that belong to a single strand of a nucleic acid. Residues are listed from 3' to 5' terminus. Consecutive residues are connected by phosphodiester bonds unless there are gaps. |
| Nucleotide | A Nucleotide class in the Molecule Window represents a single nucleotide residue. |
| NucleotideSequence | A NucleotideSequence class in the Molecule Window represents the nucleotide sequence of all nucleic acid chains belonging to a single molecule. In the Hierarchy View, the NucleotideSequence appears directly under the Molecule. |
| OpenCL | OpenCL (Open Computing Language) is a framework for writing programs that execute across heterogeneous platforms consisting of central processing units (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), digital signal processors (DSPs), field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), and other processors and hardware accelerators. Discovery Studio uses OpenCL for certain server GPU calculations, such as CHARMm OpenMM GPU. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenCL . |
| OpenGL | An API for creating 2D and 3D graphics. Discovery Studio uses OpenGL to create its 3D molecular graphics and 3D plots. Some graphics card configurations may not support all of the OpenGL features used. You can use the Check Graphics Card window to test your configuration and disable unsupported features. |
| OpenMM | OpenMM is a high performance toolkit for molecular simulation. See http://openmm.org/ . |
| Open Reading Frame (ORF) | A length of DNA or RNA sequence, defined by a start and stop codon, that can be translated into a peptide sequence. You can set preferences for ORF search options from the Auto Features subpage - Preferences dialog . |
| Parallelepiped | A geometric solid with three pairs of intersecting parallel faces. |
| Parameter Help Explorer | A dockable view in the Discovery Studio Visualizer that provides help information on protocols or protocol parameters selected in the Protocols and Parameter Explorer windows. For more information, see Parameter Help Explorer . |
| Perl | Perl is a rich scripting language, used extensively in Discovery Studio . |
| Pharmacophore | The ensemble of steric and electronic features that is necessary to ensure the optimal supramolecular interactions with a specific biological target structure, and to trigger (or to block) its biological response. Typical pharmacophore features indicate regions in a molecule that are hydrophobic, aromatic, can participate in hydrogen bonding or are positively or negatively ionizable. For more information, see Work with pharmacophores . |
| Piecewise Linear Potential (PLP) | Fast, simple, docking function that has been shown to correlate well with protein-ligand binding affinities. For more information, see Piecewise Linear Potential (PLP) . |
| Pipeline Pilot Designer for Applications | Discovery Studio comes with a version of Pipeline Pilot Client called > Pipeline Pilot Designer for Applications . This is a client for the Pipeline Pilot Server . You can use it to assemble the Discovery Studio components into protocols that read, process, and report data. For more information, see Using Pipeline Pilot . |
| Profiles-3D | A scientific server application that provides functionality for analyzing the validity of protein structures. You can access this functionality using the Verify Protein (Profiles-3D) protocol. |
| Potential of Mean Force (PMF) | Scoring function developed based on statistical analysis of the 3D structures of protein-ligand complexes. For more information, see Potential of Mean Force (PMF) . |
| Principal Component Analysis (PCA) | Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is an orthogonal linear transformation technique that transforms the data into a new coordinate system such that the variance of the data is maximized on the first coordinate (called the first principal component), the rest of the variance maximized on the second coordinate, and so on. For more information, see Principal Component Analysis . |
| Process | A single instance of a computer program that is being executed. |
| Probability Density Function (PDF) | Density of a continuous random variable is a function that describes the relative likelihood for the random variable to occur at a given point. For more information and links to topics that describe specific types of PDFs available in Discovery Studio , see Probability density functions . |
| Protein Data Bank (PDB) | The RCSB Protein Data Bank, which is the worldwide repository for macromolecular structural information. The abbreviation PDB can also refer to the .pdb file format, which was primarily designed for storage of biopolymer structures such as proteins or nucleic acids for which bonding and bond orders are known and can be accurately assigned. For more information, see Opening a Protein Data Bank (PDB) file . |
| Protein Sequence | A Protein Sequence in the Molecule Window represents the amino acid sequence of all amino acid chains belonging to a single molecule. In the Hierarchy View, the Protein Sequence appears directly under the Molecule. |
| Protocol | In Pipeline Pilot, various components that read, filter, manipulate, and output data are piped together to perform data processing. Discovery Studio comes with a collection of protocols that can be run from tool panels. For more information, see Working with protocols . Note that you also have the option to run protocols from a web page or the Pipeline Pilot Client . You can also customize or create new protocols using the Pipeline Pilot Client . For more information, see About Pipeline Pilot . |
| Protocols Explorer | A dockable view that allows you to view and launch protocols stored in the Pipeline Pilot Server to which the client is connected. For more information, see Protocols Explorer . |
| Proxy Server | A server that provide a gateway between a local area network and the Internet. The local network is protected by firewall software installed on the proxy server. You can set proxy server preferences from the Internet Proxy subpage - Preferences dialog . |
| Python | Python is a scripting language used internally by the MODELER program. |
| Quantitative Structure Activity Relationship (QSAR) | Process by which chemical structure is quantitatively correlated with a well defined process, such as biological activity or chemical reactivity. You can use the Create QSAR Model tools to prepare for and build various QSAR models. |
| Quantitative Structure Toxicity Relationship (QStr) | Process by which chemical structure is quantitatively correlated with toxicity. The Toxicity Prediction (TOPKAT) protocol employs robust and cross-validated QStr models for assessing various measures of toxicity. |
| Quantum Mechanics (QM) | Quantum mechanics describes the evolution of physical systems via a mathematical structure called the wave function. Quantum mechanics brings a higher level of theory over traditional molecular mechanics methods, allowing additional phenomena such as identifying where chemical reactions occur and accurate descriptors related to charge and energy to be modeled. |
| Ramachandran Plot | A graphical representation of the local backbone conformation of each residue in a protein structure. For more information, see Ramachandran Plot . |
| RCSB | The Research Collaboratory for Structural Bioinformatics. See https://www.rcsb.org |
| RDOCK | A scientific server application that provides functionality for scoring protein-protein interactions. It complements the ZDOCK application. You can access this functionality using the Refine Docked Proteins (RDOCK) protocol. |
| Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) | Plot used to indicate how often a model correctly identifies true positives and true negatives.The Calculate ROC Curve and Create Bayesian Model protocols allow you to create ROC plots. |
| Receptor Surface | You can generate receptor surfaces to visualize the interaction or receptors and ligands using the View Interactions tools. |
| Recursive Partitioning (RP) | Data classification method used to uncover the relationship between a dependent property (Y variable) to a set of independent properties (X variables). For more information, see Recursive Partitioning . |
| Residue | A Residue object in the Molecule Window represents a single residue that has not been classified as an amino acid or nucleotide (e.g., cofactors, ligands, and water molecules). In the Data Table View, amino acid and nucleotide residues are listed in the AminoAcid and Nucleotide tabs (not the Residue tab). |
| Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD) | Statistical measure of the difference between two sets of values. |
| Script Command | A command that can be invoked from the Discovery Studio client that runs a Perl script. Commands can be invoked though menus , toolbars , and tool panels . |
| Script Language | A programming language that enables you to control another computer program. Important examples of scripting languages include Perl and Python. |
| Sequence Data Model (SDM) | Data model used by Discovery Studio to define sequence objects. |
| Server | Often used to refer to a remote hardware resource that runs one or more scientific server processes. However, it is also commonly used to refer to a computational process or an executable that is used to perform some task (e.g., analysis computation). In Discovery Studio , the term server often refers to the Pipeline Pilot Server . |
| Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (SMILES) | Specification in form of a line notation for describing the structure of chemical molecules using short ASCII strings. |
| SMILES Arbitrary Target Specification (SMARTS) | Language for specifying substructural patterns in molecules. Discovery Studio allows you to Create Features from SMARTS and Filter by SMARTS . You can also remove substructures by using the Filter Smarts parameter when running the Prepare Ligands protocol. |
| Soft Molecular Surface | A molecular surface that is the isosurface of an approximate electron density. For more information, see Working with surfaces . |
| Solvent Excluded Volume | The solvent-excluded volume of a molecule is the set of all points not accessible to a solvent molecule due to overlap with the molecule. To obtain the solvent surface, the solvent molecule is approximated as a spherical probe, and the molecule's atoms are approximated as atom-centered spheres as well. All points that cannot be reached by the probe unless the probe sphere overlaps with at least one atomic sphere make up the solvent-excluded volume. |
| Solvent Molecular Surface | A molecular surface that encloses the solvent excluded volume. For more information, see Working with surfaces . |
| Storyboard | Navigate, manage, and animate multiple views of the same structure. You can access the storyboard options from the View \| Storyboard menu. Storyboards are saved in .dsv files. For details, see Create and view storyboards . |
| Structural Classification of Proteins (SCOP) | Database of protein structural domains classified based on similarities of their amino acid sequences and three-dimensional structures. BLAST search results include the SCOP codes. You can perform BLAST searches using the Search Sequences by Similarity tools . |
| Structure Based Design (SBD) | Type of drug design that relies on knowledge of the structure of a candidate to determine target binding affinity and selectivity. This is opposed to ligand based design where known target binding molecules are used to generate a pharmacophore model that defines the minimum structural characteristics that a candidate must posess in order to bind to the target. |
| Target | A protein or other macromolecular system to be modulated by a small molecule drug or other therapeutic. |
| Tool | A tool is any element of the graphical user interface that provides access to a command. Tools can be menu items, tool bar buttons or tool panel buttons. |
| Toolbar | Groups of buttons available above the workspace. You can toggle the display from the View \| Toolbars menu. For more information, see Working with toolbars . |
| Tool Panel | A set of related tools, grouped together and displayed within the Tools Explorer. For more information, see Working with tool panels . |
| Tool Set | A set of related tool panels, grouped together and displayed within the Tools Explorer. You can switch between different sets using the Tool Set toolbar. For more information, see Working with tool panels . |
| Tools Explorer | A dockable view in the Discovery Studio Visualizer that provides access to different tool panels. For more information, see Tools Explorer . |
| TOPKAT | A scientific server application that provides functionality for predicting toxicity of ligands. You can access this functionality using the Toxicity Prediction (TOPKAT) protocol. |
| Uniform Resource Location (URL) | An internet address that specifies where the identified resource is available and the protocol for retrieving it (e.g., http, ftp). You can open files on any network-accessible resource such as a file server on your local area network or a web server on the internet using the Open URL/Insert From URL dialogs . |
| VAMP | A scientific server application that provides functionality for performing semi-empirical molecular orbital analysis. |
| Van Der Waals Molecular (VDW) Surface | A molecular surface obtained by the superposition of atom-centered spheres, where the spheres' radii are given by the atomic van der Waals radii. You can create this surface using the Create Surface dialog . |
| X-Ray Reflection Data | The X-ray diffraction pattern of crystal sample that is used to generate an electron density map. For more information, see Working with X-ray data . |
| ZDOCK | A scientific server application that provides functionality for predicting and analyzing protein-protein interactions. It complements the RDOCK application. You can access this functionality using the Dock and Analyze Protein Complexes tools . |

## Localization

To ensure consistent handling of numbers:

* For Windows, the region must be configured to English (United States), English (Europe), or English (World).

* For Linux, the locale must be en_US.UTF-8 .

# BIOVIA products

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/product_line.htm

## BIOVIA products

Discovery Studio is part of a range of BIOVIA products that can be used together by researchers working
in the Life Sciences. The range includes clients that provide access to functionality on Pipeline Pilot Server as well as free clients that allow collaborators to view output files from Discovery Studio without having to purchase the software. For an overview of how these products are tied together, see Discovery Studio overview .

### Product descriptions

The following sections describe the different 
products and their potential application:

* Discovery Studio Client

* Discovery Studio Visualizer

* Pipeline Pilot Client and Pipeline Pilot Designer for Applications

* Web Port

* Pipeline Pilot Server

The Discovery Studio Client is the primary desktop interface used to perform visualization, editing, 
and analysis tasks. The client provides access to Pipeline Pilot and is capable of launching any protocol
that has been appropriately modified.

The Discovery Studio Visualizer is a free product that allows users to view and edit data files
created with the Discovery Studio Client and other applications. The client provides the ability to view and edit molecular
structures, sequences, sequence alignments, and Perl scripts. In addition the client provides 
access to a subset of the Discovery Studio Perl API.

Pipeline Pilot Client is a desktop application that provides access to Pipeline Pilot server. The client is the only application that provides the ability to create new components and
protocols. The client also provides the ability to run protocols. Pipeline Pilot Designer for Applications is provided with Discovery Studio ; it is similar to the full Pipeline Pilot Client , but with use restricted to the Discovery Studio entitlements. For details, see About Pipeline Pilot .

Web Port is a package that allows users to access protocols through a web browser
interface. Any protocol, including the Discovery Studio protocols, can be adapted to run through Web Port with minimal modification.

Pipeline Pilot Server is a database and job execution environment for components and protocols. 
The server runs on Windows and Linux and is designed to scale in a range of deployment scenarios.

### Feature comparison

| Molecular Structure Editor | + | + | - | - | - |
| Molecular Sequence Viewer | + | + | - | - | - |
| Molecular Sequence Editor | + | + | - | - | - |
| X-Ray Reflection Data Editor/Viewer | + | - | - | - | - |
| Forcefield Data Editor/Viewer | + | - | - | - | - |
| Charting | + | - | - | - | + |
| Perl Script IDE Editor/Launcher | + | + | + | - | - |
| Protocol/Component Editor | - | - | + | - | - |

# What's New in Discovery Studio 2026

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes.htm

## What's New in Discovery Studio 2026

This topic details the new features, enhancements, and important fixes available for Discovery Studio 2026 .

For more detailed information and system requirements, see the Discovery Studio Product Release Document and Discovery Studio Documentation files on the Dassault Systèmes Download Platform .

### 2026 GA

#### General

* Discovery Studio requires an installation of Pipeline Pilot 2026. See the Discovery Studio Installation Guide for details.

* Discovery Studio Python components are updated to maintain compatibility with the Pipeline Pilot server.

* Perl is updated to version 5.40.2. For information, see https://www.perl.org/ .

#### Client

* A new script for exporting trajectory conformations as images, Save Trajectory as Images, is available from the Scripts > Export menu.

* A new script for exporting macromolecules as mmCIF files, Save as mmCIF, is available from the Scripts > Export menu.

#### Macromolecules

* The protocols that use Modeler are enhanced to allow structures which cannot be accommodated within the RCSB pdb file format to be used, including those with chain names more than one character long.

* MODELER is updated to version 10.7.

* The example protocols Update BLAST Databases and Update Antibody Databases are enhanced to process mmCIF files.

* The PDB, PDB_nr95, and Swiss-Prot BLAST databases are updated using data available as of April, 2025.

* The antibody database is updated with data from 8083 antibody structures from the RCSB database as of April 2025.

* The RCSB Structure Search protocol can now filter hits by organism and sequence similarity.

#### Simulation

* A new protocol, Set up Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE) , prepares inputs for the Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE) protocol using new atom mapping schemes and by designing a ligand perturbation network. Free energy calculations are improved by increased chemical space coverage, handling of stereoisomers and symmetries, and perturbation network.

* A new protocol, Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE), runs relative binding free energy (RBFE) calculations using the OpenFE framework, which leverages the OpenFF forcefield and OpenMM. The OpenFE framework supports better forcefield coverage of small molecules, which increases the accuracy of RBFE calculations.

* A new protocol, Standard Dynamics Cascade (OpenMM), runs a standard dynamics cascade with GPU acceleration using OpenMM. The complete molecular dynamics simulation workflow is accelerated, with significantly faster preparation and execution of production-ready simulations.

* A new protocol, Export Conformations as Trajectory , exports conformations from a molecule window to a trajectory file in DCD format.

* A new protocol, Detect and Analyze Pockets , assesses changes in pocket characteristics by analyzing and identifying transient and static pockets within the protein structure across an input trajectory.

* The Measure Trajectory Features protocol was updated to add a new feature "Pocket Detection" that allows for detection and measurement of pocket volumes on the basis of occurrence and spatial analysis.

* A new protocol, Analyze Trajectory Features, analyzes allosteric motions from trajectories using features of interest.

# Discovery Studio 2016

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes16.htm

## Discovery Studio 2016

This topic details the new features, enhancements, and important bug fixes available for Discovery Studio 2016.

### General

* You can now add folders of protocols to the Discovery Studio Protocol Explorer . 
For example, you can add the BIOVIA Discovery Studio Examples folder to the Protocol Explorer for easy access.

* The Information section of the protocol reports was expanded to include more server details.

* Added new options to the protocol context menu to close tabs.

### Macromolecules

* The SEQRES information in PDB files is now parsed when the file is read, and is stored on the relevant Chain objects. This allows for the analysis of missing residues to be performed correctly if some of the chains have been deleted from the structure prior to the use of the Clean Protein or Protein Report tools.

* A failure could occur in the Prepare Protein protocol or when using the Clean Protein tool if there were extraneous bonds in the C-terminal residue of a protein chain. This issue has been fixed. The bonding algorithm was improved to avoid the formation of incorrect bonds in the C-terminus if a structure with incorrectly placed atoms is read.

* The PDB resolution data required by the Find PDB Resolution component may require updating in order to correctly determine the resolution for a PDB file deposited after the creation of the Pipeline Pilot installation. This can be accomplished by downloading the file ftp://ftp.wwpdb.org/pub/pdb/derived_data/index/resolu.idx and placing it in the public/DS/BLASTDB folder of the Pipeline Pilot installation. This copy will then be used instead of the standard installed copy located in apps/scitegic/dscore/server/share/PDBUtils.

* Fixed an issue to correctly sort the negative Developability Index values in the Calculate Developability Indices protocol report.

* The coloring of an Aggregation Propensity Surface generated by the Calculate Aggregation Scores protocol will no longer be altered after another type of surface is displayed. In addition, if the coloring of an Aggregation Propensity Surface is changed, it can now be restored by use of the Reset Display tool on the Predict Protein Aggregation tools panel.

* Improved the opening response time for the Annotate Antibody Sequence protocol.

* Fixed a Calculate Mutation Energy (Stability) protocol failure when requesting a large number of mutations due to the creation of too many temporary folders.

* Corrected the energies reported by the Side-Chain Refinement protocol.

### Pharmacophores

* Fixed a file association issue when opening files from the report page of the Create 3D QSAR Model protocol.

* Improved formatting of large numbers in the Hypotheses Results table of the 3D QSAR Pharmacophore Generation protocol report.

* The Steric Refinement with Excluded Volumes protocol can now handle identical ligand names.

### Simulation

* Two new protocols, Steered Molecular Dynamics and Calculate Free Energy from Steering Forces , 
allow simulation of
protein or protein-ligand complexes while applying steering forces to the system. You can use these protocols to estimate the ligand binding
free energy and to study the atomic level detail of the ligand unbinding process, protein unfolding, or conformational changes.

* Added phosphoserine, phosphotyrosine, and phosphothreonine patches into the charmm36 forcefield to allow proper typing of those residues using the 
Assign Forcefield Types (Prototype) protocol.

* Fixed an issue in the Assign Forcefield Types (Prototype) protocol so that the atoms are reordered to be consistent with the CHARMm atom order to allow consistent input to subsequent CHARMm simulation tasks.

* Increased the warning level (WARLEV) in CHARMm when running the Calculate Energy protocol in debug mode to print out missing force field parameters.

* The templates for phosphoserine and phosphotyrosine residues used by Build and Edit protein tools and the CHARMm or CHARMm Polar H forcefields are made consistent so that the peptides built can be properly typed by those forcefields. This has entailed changing the templates within Discovery Studio to the mono-anionic form.

* Fixed an issue in Dynamics protocols so that they can be run without specifying a value for the random number seed parameter.

* Fixed several hanging issues when running CHARMm in parallel using MPI on Windows, including the case when not enough licenses are available.

* Changed the Total Energy from the Calculate Energy (QM-MM) protocol to Hartree units.

### Small Molecules

* Removed the optimized CDOCKER scores from the Score Ligand Poses protocol.

* Added a ligand pose alignment step to the Generate Conformations protocol when using Systematic Search, Random Search, or Boltzmann Jump to ensure diverse conformations.

* Fixed an issue with the Analyze Ligand Poses protocol affecting ligands with rotated atom properties.

* The CHARMm based ligand-conformation minimization speed was improved by over an order of magnitude. Protocols such as Generate Conformations and Calculate Binding Energies will benefit from this enhancement.

* Submitted the Toxicity Models to the European Commission Joint Research Center (JRC).

### Pipeline Pilot and Third Party Enhancements

* Discovery Studio 2016 is compatible with Pipeline Pilot 2016.

* ANTIBODY database is updated to include the latest antibody template structures from the PDB.

* MODELER is updated to the latest academic version 9v15.

* CHARMm is updated to the latest academic release 40b1.

* The RCSB ligand database was updated for the RCSB Structure Search protocol (October 2015, 20861 entries).

* DMOL3 is updated to version 2016

The Predict Stabilizing Mutations protocol was deprecated. Most of the protocol functionality is available in the Calculate Mutation Energy (Stability) protocol. 
The deprecated protocol will be removed in the next Discovery Studio release.

# Discovery Studio 2017 R2

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes17r2.htm

## Discovery Studio 2017 R2

This topic details the new features, enhancements, and important bug fixes available for Discovery Studio 2017 R2.

* The system requirements changed in Discovery Studio 2017 R2.

### Client

* Improved the Chirality perception for bridged rings.

* You can now save molecules in the COLLAborative Design Activity (DAE) file format.

* The Non-bond Interactions display options settings persist now.

### Protein Modeling

* The Model Full Length Antibody protocol has been enhanced: You can graft a Fab structure onto the full-length template prior to performing the homology modeling, in order to start from a more appropriate model structure. You can model bispecific full-length antibodies, in which the two heavy and light chains are not identical to each other.

* You can graft a Fab structure onto the full-length template prior to performing the homology modeling, in order to start from a more appropriate model structure.

* You can model bispecific full-length antibodies, in which the two heavy and light chains are not identical to each other.

* The Antibody Modeling Cascade protocol has been enhanced: You can graft a modeled Fab structure onto a full-length antibody template structure to quickly produce an approximate full-length antibody structure for the target sequence. The Report produced by the Antibody Modeling Cascade now includes a View Results option that opens all of the final models in one window. The first structure will be visible and the remainder hidden. If the option to graft a modeled Fab structure onto a full-length template has been used, the report will include columns for the Fab and the grafted structures, and the View Results button will open the grafted structures.

* You can graft a modeled Fab structure onto a full-length antibody template structure to quickly produce an approximate full-length antibody structure for the target sequence.

* The Report produced by the Antibody Modeling Cascade now includes a View Results option that opens all of the final models in one window. The first structure will be visible and the remainder hidden. If the option to graft a modeled Fab structure onto a full-length template has been used, the report will include columns for the Fab and the grafted structures, and the View Results button will open the grafted structures.

* The Scripts menu now includes a Sequences submenu which includes example scripts. One allows selection of a whole sequence if any residues are selected and the remainder are for coloring CDR regions of antibody sequences according to different numbering schemes.

* The Loop Refinement protocol has an improved looper algorithm with better accuracy of the predicted loop conformation and added option to run the calculation in coarse grain parallelization.

### Forcefields

* The patch mechanisms provided in the CHARMm forcefield RTF file are now used directly when using the Assign Forcefield protocol to type molecules using the charmm36 forcefield. Also, user provided templates and patches are also applied in the same manner. This change ensures that the forcefield parameters are more accurately applied during simulation, including improper torsions, cmap terms for amino acids, etc.

* The charmm36 forcefield is updated to the latest academic release (February 2016).

### Receptor-Ligand Interactions

* Added new parameter, Calculate Solvent Accessibility , to the Analyze Ligand Poses protocol to calculate the SASA, and the change during ligand binding.

* The default settings of the Dock Ligands (GOLD) protocol was updated to better match the CCDC GOLD default settings.

* New properties were added to the Minimize Ligands protocol indicate the initial and final RMS gradient for each ligand minimized.

* A new option was added to the Prepare Ligands protocol to preserve the initial ligand position during conformation generation, if possible.

* A new protocol, Generate Analog Conformations , allows you to obtain 3D geometries of ligands in a congeneric analog series of compounds, given the 3D geometry of one or more lead compounds in a series and the corresponding target protein structure. See Generate Analog Conformations .

* For lead optimization, several prototype protocols have been developed for calculating relative free energy of ligand binding: Set Up Relative FEP Calculations : Sets up NAMD input for free energy perturbation using dual topology. Free Energy Perturbation (NAMD) : Estimates the relative free energy of ligand binding using NAMD's free energy perturbation (FEP). Analyze FEP Results: Calculates the relative free energy of ligand binding from NAMD relative free energy perturbation (FEP) results.

* Set Up Relative FEP Calculations : Sets up NAMD input for free energy perturbation using dual topology.

* Free Energy Perturbation (NAMD) : Estimates the relative free energy of ligand binding using NAMD's free energy perturbation (FEP).

* Analyze FEP Results: Calculates the relative free energy of ligand binding from NAMD relative free energy perturbation (FEP) results.

* Compatibility with Pipeline Pilot 2017 R2

# What's New in Discovery Studio 2020

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes2020.htm

## What's New in Discovery Studio 2020

This topic details the new features, enhancements, and important fixes available for Discovery Studio 2020.

### Client

* 2D binding site diagram : The 2D binding sites diagram can now also be used with nucleic acid-ligand complexes.

* Non-bond interactions : The non-bond interactions tools now use a more sophisticated method to determine hydrophobic regions on ligands.

* Licenses : A new documentation section explaining the licensing model was added to the help.

* Change Server Jobs explorer : You can now reconnect to jobs which were interrupted due to network errors.

### Pharmacophores

* 3D QSAR Pharmacophore Generation : The ligand mappings for the validation set are now retained.

* Interaction Pharmacophore Generation : Added a new protocol to generate pharmacophores from ligand-receptor non-bond interactions.

* Ensemble Pharmacophore Generation : Added a new protocol to generate ensemble pharmacophores from a set of active ligands.

* Ligand Profiler : Enhanced the results tables to be sortable.

* Ligand Profiler and Ligand Pharmacophore Mapping now produce identical FitValues.

* PharmaDB: Updated PharmaDB to the latest version based on scPDB release 2017. It now contains over 16,000 entries.

### Protein Modeling

* Solvate with Explicit Membrane : Added a new protocol that adds an explicit bilayer of lipids, water and optionally counterions to a transmembrane protein.

* Calculate Protein Formulation Properties : 
Added a new protocol to calculate the protein Developability Index (DI), antibody viscosity, and protein solubility.

* Prepare Proteins : Enhanced to take multiple protein molecules as input and be processed in parallel.

* Predict Humanizing Mutations : Added new parameters to specify V and J genes for the H and L chains.

* BLAST Search and PSI-BLAST Search protocols now support both NCBI nr and nr_v5 databases. It also supports UniRef90 database from UniProt. 
Therefore, the nr and UniRef90 BLAST databases are no longer distributed with this release, although the previous versions are still available from the Dassault Systèmes Download Platform.

### Receptor-Ligand Interactions

* Dock Ligands (GOLD) : The GOLD docking protocol now supports covalent ligand docking.

### Simulation

* A set of new protocols to set up, run, and analyze Multi-Site Lambda Dynamics (MSLD) simulations:

* Enumerate Ligands for MSLD : Generates a combinatorial library of ligands to be screened by MSLD.

* Set Up MSLD Calculations : Generates simulation systems to enable running MSLD simulations.

* MSLD Bias Optimization: Iteratively optimizes biasing functions for MSLD simulation systems.

* MSLD Production: Runs MSLD production simulations to sample different combinatorial ligands.

* Collate MSLD Simulation Results : Estimates the relative binding free energies by analyzing results from MSLD simulations.

* Assign Forcefield : 
Added new templates and parameters from CGenFF 4.1.

* CHARMm Structure (PSF) files : Bond and forcefield information is now read from a PSF file and a paired CRD or PDB file to construct a fully typed molecule.

### Database Updates

* Antibody database : Updated based on the PDB data in July 2019.

* Local databases : Updated PDB and PDB_nr95 based on the PDB data in July 2019. Updated Swiss-Prot using the uniprot_sprot.fasta file download from UniProt in August 2019.

* RCSB Structure Search : Protocol database was updated based on the PDB data in August 2019.

### Third Party Enhancements

* Compatibility with Pipeline Pilot 2026

* MODELER 9.22

* CHARMm 43b2

* GOLD 2019

## What's New in Discovery Studio 2021

This topic details the new features, enhancements, and important fixes available for Discovery Studio 2021.

For more detailed information and system requirements, see the Discovery Studio Product Release Document and Discovery Studio Documentation.zip files on the Dassault Systèmes Download Platform.

### Client

* 4K support: The Discovery Studio Client for Windows now supports high resolution monitors.

### Pharmacophores

* Pharmacophore features : Non-bond pharmacophore features are now supported in the ligand-based pharmacophore protocols. They are available as an option in the Features parameter of these protocols and the Edit and Cluster Features tools panel.

* Ligand Profiler :

* The full PharmaDB database no longer requires separate installation and is available by default.

* The PharmaDB database was regenerated using the new non-bond pharmacophore features.

### Protein Modeling

* Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) : You can now accelerate the protocol by running on GPU (Linux and Windows).

* RCSB Structure Search : RCSB announced that legacy search APIs will be discontinued from November 2020. The protocol has been updated to use the new APIs.

* Calculate Protein Formulation Properties : The protocol now calculates molecular surfaces colored by the surface charge map and aggregation scores for display in the results.

* Blast Search (NCBI Server) : The protocol has been updated to include new Composition Based Statistics options and a Time Out parameter. Polling of the server and error handling have been improved.

### Receptor-Ligand Interactions

* Hybridization : The Pipeline Pilot perception for Nitrogen hybridization was updated.

* Dock Ligands (GOLD) : The protocol is now compatible with GOLD 2020 .

### Simulation

* Solvate with Explicit Membrane : You can now accelerate the protocol by running on GPU (Linux and Windows).

* Dynamics (NAMD) : You can now accelerate the protocol by running on GPU (Linux and Windows).

It also allows supports protein-ligand complex and free ligand systems in the same protocol. You can accelerate the protocol by running on GPU (Linux).

* A new protocol, CHARMm Relative FEP Calculations , allows you to run FEP calculations on GPU (Linux) and collate results from multiple systems. It also allows running of both protein-ligand complex and free ligand systems in the same protocol.

* Type Ligands with MATCH (Prototype) : The protocol implements a new hierarchical atom typer that assigns atom types more accurately. A new example protocol, Retrieve Antibody Templates from Database , reads the template structures from the database.

## What's New in Discovery Studio 2022

### General

The Pipeline Pilot security settings have been updated. For more information, see the Pipeline Pilot Installation and Configuration Guide.

* Enhanced the RCSB Structure Search protocol. RCSB has recently added substructure search for ligand query. The protocol is extended to include all available match types from the RCSB server.

### Simulation

* Enhanced the Assign Forcefield protocol to work with RNA and DNA templates from custom RTF files.

## What's New in Discovery Studio 2023

### General

* Discovery Studio now requires an installation of Pipeline Pilot 2023 SP1.

* CHARMm is upgraded to version 47b1.

### Client

* The trajectory animations in the Discovery Studio Client are enhanced with the inclusion of frame numbers. Also, you can change the current frame by moving a slider.

### Pharmacophores

* Two new protocols, PharmaDB Filter and PharmaDB Profiler are available from the Pharmacophore Search, Screen, and Profile tool panel.

* The Ligand Profiler protocol now adds shape similarity properties (4FeatShape#ShapeSimilarity and 4FeatShape#PercentFilled) to the output ligands.

* The PharmaDB is updated based on the scPDB release 2022 ( http://bioinfo-pharma.u-strasbg.fr/scPDB ), and now contains over 37,000 entries.

### Macromolecules

* The Predict Humanizing Mutations protocol includes a new published machine learning (ML) method that can distinguish between human and murine sequences.

* The performance of the Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) protocol is improved by 10-20%, depending on the settings.

* Several protein modeling protocols, Prepare Proteins , Calculate Protein Ionization and Residue pK , Calculate Mutation Energy (Binding) , Calculate Mutation Energy (Stability) , and Calculate Protein Formulation Properties , now support the charmm36 forcefield.

* The Antibody Database is updated with 6711 antibody structures from the PDB database release of July 2022.

* The residue database for the RCSB Structure Search protocol is updated based on the PDB release from May 2023, which contains 40,322 residue entries.

* The PDB, PDB_nr95, and Swiss-Prot BLAST databases are updated using data available as of May, 2023.

### Receptor-Ligand Interactions

* Dock Ligands (GOLD) supports CCDC GOLD 2023.

### Simulation

* A new protocol, GaMD Equilibration , allows you to configure a Gaussian accelerated Molecular Dynamics simulation and automatically parametrize boost potentials.

* A new protocol, GaMD Production , allows you to run and restart Gaussian accelerated Molecular Dynamics simulations.

* A new protocol, Estimate Free Energy Landscape , estimates a free energy landscape from a data set or a set of simulations, allowing for statistical reweighting of GaMD simulations.

* A new protocol, Measure Trajectory Features , measures time-series features (such as SASA, RMSD, Dihedrals) from molecular dynamics trajectories for further analysis.

* A new protocol, Cluster Conformations , discretizes conformational states from simulation trajectories.

* The MSLD Bias Optimization and Production protocol is updated to use the BLaDE software, which results in a significant speed increase.

* The Assign Forcefield and Type Ligands with MATCH (Prototype) protocols expand chemical space coverage with an option for assigning charges through an ML model trained on ESP-fit QM data, and torsion parameters that are generated by fitting to QM data.

### Small Molecules

* The Filter by SMARTS protocol has a new option to filter ligands by PAINS (Pan Assay Interference Compounds) substructures.

# What's New in Discovery Studio 2025

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes2025.htm

## What's New in Discovery Studio 2025

### 2025 SP1

* Discovery Studio requires an installation of Pipeline Pilot 2025 SP1. See the Discovery Studio Installation Guide for details.

* For Linux installations, NAMD is updated to NAMD 3.0.1.

* MODELER is updated to version 10.6.

### 2025 GA

#### General

* Discovery Studio MOL2 format files can now store multi-character chain names.

* Detailed information for updating licenses is now available in the Discovery Studio help under Managing Discovery Studio > Licensing > Licenses . For more information, see Licenses .

#### Macromolecules

* A new protocol, Predict Antibody Paratopes , predicts the antigen binding site residues in antibody CDR loops.

* The Prepare Germline Sources protocol now uses the ClustalW2 engine to align sequences.

* The RCSB Structure Search protocol now reads mmCIF format files by default, which allows all hits to be read.

* Chemical component definition (CCD) records are now read from mmCIF structure files, enabling ligand bond orders and formal charges to be assigned correctly.

* Secondary structure definitions can now be read from mmCIF files into the PDB Secondary property, and are displayed in the same way as those read from PDB files.

* Information about residues in the sequence of a macromolecule that is missing from its structure is now read from mmCIF files. This allows the missing residues to be shown in the Protein Report and modeled using Build and Edit Proteins tools.

* The Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) protocol no longer has a chain name length restriction for the input proteins.

* The PDB Ligand Bond Orders script is upgraded to use Chemical Component Dictionary files to assign bond orders and formal charges to all ligands and other small molecules read from RCSB PDB files.

* The PDB property name limit is increased from three to five characters.

* MODELER is updated to version 10.5.

#### Pharmacophore

* PharmaDB is updated based on scPDB release 2024 (http://bioinfo-pharma.u-strasbg.fr/scPDB), and now contains over 41,000 entries.

* The PharmaDB Profiler protocol now stores the function information in a CSV file, and includes the total entries that map for the function as an additional property.

* The Interaction Pharmacophore Generation protocol now supports producing a diverse set of pharmacophores or top scoring pharmacophores. Previously, the protocol only calculated the top scoring pharmacophores. The latest PharmaDB database was built using the new diverse option.

#### Simulation

* The Solvate with Explicit Membrane protocol is updated to include improved constraints during equilibration, which results in better equilibrated and solvated systems.

* Extended CHARMm's ability to handle extra large molecular systems (up to 1 million atoms) by initializing with additional memory.

* NAMD is updated to version 3.0 on Linux.

#### Small Molecules

* Dock Ligands (GOLD) protocol now supports CCDC GOLD version 2024.1. The torsions sampled by GOLD during docking are improved. A new Flexibility parameter, Torsion Angle Distribution, is available in the Dock Ligands (GOLD) protocol.

# Discovery Studio 2.1

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes21.htm

## Discovery Studio 2.1

### Contents

* Overview

* New features and products since version 2.0

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio protocols

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio servers

* Enhancements to the Discovery Studio Visualizer

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio scripting

* Enhancements to customized features

* Critical bug fixes

* Platform support

* Licensing changes

Discovery Studio 2.1 includes a set of new functionality and enhancements to 
existing features that further strengthen its capabilities as a comprehensive 
modeling and simulation platform for the life sciences. Powerful new analysis tools in the 
area of Quantum Mechanics-Molecular Mechanics (QM-MM) offer new capabilities 
for analyzing protein-ligand systems. Enhancements to the ligand profiling 
protocol enable you to work with commercial curated databases of structure 
based pharmacophores. Also, CHARMm has been updated to version 34b1.

This release delivers many customer-reported enhancements in the Visualizer that 
greatly improve its overall usability. In particular, many performance 
improvements have been made to the Graphics View that improve its ability to 
work with macromolecular data. A large number of enhancements have been made to 
tools for viewing and analyzing pharmacophore and sequence data. The Perl 
scripting interface has also been significantly improved.

In addition to program upgrades, this release also includes significant 
additions to the product documentation. To 
complement this, several new example scripts and protocols have been provided 
to demonstrate new capabilities.

QM-MM . In this release two new protocols have been 
added that enable you to perform QM-MM analysis: Calculate Energy (QM-MM) and 
Minimization (QM-MM). Both of these protocols are located in the Simulation 
folder.

These protocols have been designed to work with protein ligand systems. Quantum 
mechanical treatment of the ligand region allows a higher level of theory. 
This enables you to model additional phenomena to traditional forcefield 
techniques, for example, where polarization 
effects play an important role. The remaining bulk of the structure is 
described using a forcefield.

HypoDB Database Support . In DS 2.0, the Ligand 
Profiler protocol was added. This enables you to map a set of ligands against a 
set of pharmacophores using a series of Catalyst compare/fit operations. 
Additional protocols were added to create and maintain profile databases. In DS 
2.1, full support has been added for the curated pharmacophore database, 
HypoDB, from Inte:Ligand. This database provides access to thousands of 
pharmacophore models that can be used in activity profiling.

#### ADMET

* A new protocol, Filter by SMARTS, has been added. This protocol allows you to 
filter a set of small molecules and select only those molecules that meet the 
rules specified by the set of selected SMARTS rules. SMARTS is a widely used 
language that allows you to specify substructures using rules that are 
straightforward extensions of the SMILES language.

#### Electrostatics

* The Calculate Protein Ionization and Residue pK protocol has been enhanced to 
add reference titration curves for each titratable residue in a protein.

#### Library Design and Analysis

* Find Similar Molecules by Numeric Properties now filters out ligands with missing 
properties.

* An example protocol (accessed using Pipeline Pilot) has been added that allows 
you to specify a Custom Score protocol and a Custom Score Property when using both the Optimize Subset Library with Pareto Method and Optimize 
Combinatorial Library with Pareto Method protocols.

#### Pharmacophores

* A protocol for converting SMARTS rules to Discovery Studio pharmacophores has 
been added.

* Inter-feature distances and RMS values used to calculate the distance matrix 
are returned from the Cluster Pharmacophore protocol.

* An enhancement has been made to the CAESAR mode of the Diverse Conformation Generation protocol 
to allow you to constrain specific bonds and atoms when it creates 
conformations.

* You can now append to databases created with
earlier versions of Catalyst using catDB.

* The Ligand Profiler protocol has been enhanced to visualize the pharmacophores 
aligned to the ligands.

* The Build 3D Database protocol has been enhanced to provide a browsable 
location option for the Database Files directory.

* The Screen Library protocol has been enhanced to output non-fitting 
ligands.

* Parameters have been added to several protocols that increase the number of 
mappings to consider by default.

* The Build 3D Database protocol has been modified to report failed 
compounds.

#### Protein Modeling

* ZRank is now provided as a scoring option for the Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) protocol.

* The Align and Superimpose Proteins protocol has been enhanced to allow secondary 
structure information to be used in the alignment.

* Modifications have been made to the Align Structures and Align Structures 
(MODELER) protocols to superimpose the structures by alignment.

* A utility protocol has been provided in the Examples folder (accessed using Pipeline Pilot) that enables InsightII users to import 
ZDOCK data.

#### QSAR

* The Delete User Models protocol has been added that allows you to delete user-generated QSAR models.

* In the Calculate Molecular Properties protocol, the properties have been 
reorganized into 1D, 2D, and 3D categories.

* The Calculate Molecular Properties protocol now allows DMol 3 geometry optimization.

#### Receptor-Ligand Interactions

* Several enhancements have been made in the Flexible Docking
protocol, improving its speed and reducing its resource (memory and
disk space) requirements. Also, redundant poses are now
filtered out by default.

* The Dock Ligands (LibDock) protocol has
improved hotspot matching. The protocol also provides information about which
hotspots were used for docking.

* The performance and accuracy has been improved for the Dock Ligands (Pharmacophore
Restraints with CHARMm) protocol.

#### Simulations

* You can now view the charging algorithm
used for each molecule in the Data Table
View of the Molecule Window.

* An option has been added to specify whether van der
Waals or user specified radii should be used for GBMV, GBSW, and PBSA
implicit solvent models.

* All protocols have been enhanced to use newly optimized
Generalized Born parameters by default.

* The minimization and molecular dynamics protocols have all been updated
to expose a GBMV option.

* The GBSW implicit solvent method has been enhanced to use molecular
surface definition for the dielectric boundary.

* The Calculate Interaction Energies protocol has been enhanced to
report residue level interaction energies.

* All protocols have been enhanced to indicate which forcefield was used.

* The Equilibration protocol has been renamed Dynamics (Equilibration).

* The salt concentration can now be specified for the GBSW implicit solvent model.

CHARMm. The CHARMm server has been upgraded to the latest available version, CHARMm 
34b1. This version includes a number of important enhancements. For a complete list, visit https://www.charmm.org/ .

ZDOCK. The ZDOCK server for protein-protein interaction analysis has been upgraded to 
version 2.3. For backwards compatibility, version 2.1 is also included.

Catalyst. The Catalyst servers have been enhanced to support creation and 
modification of large (>2 GB) database files. Databases in the old 
format can be appended to and merged. Shape indexing is done on 
disk rather than in memory and now uses very little memory.

A range of improvements have been made to the visualizer:

* The application startup time has been significantly improved.

* An interface for editing forcefield parameter files has been added.

* The Tools Explorer includes a scroll bar to improve navigation and general
usability. The tool panel title bars have also been redesigned to include
buttons instead of dropdown lists.

* Significant improvements to the rendering performance of the Graphics View have been 
made.

* A shortcut has been provided that enables you to create a Group from the
current selection using the context menu.

* A preference has been provided that enables you to set the Valence parameters 
and van der Waals parameters for the Dreiding Minimizer.

* The ability to merge amino acid chains with the same ID has been incorporated
into the .pdb file importer.

* Hydrogen bond angle data is now displayed in the Data Table View of the 3D 
Window.

* The ability to specify the angle criteria for Hydrogen Bond monitors has been
added.

* The validity of queries being added to the feature dictionary is now checked.

* The performance of the CSV file importer has been improved.

* The binding site editor and related features have been improved to ease the 
handling of multiple visible binding sites.

* Improved support for handling structures with more than one site sphere has 
been provided.

* Enhancements have been made that improve the ability to label Heat Maps.

* The dialogs for setting up 2D and 3D charts have been improved.

* The ability to export data from a plot to a CSV file has
been added.

* The ability to add error bars to a 2D plot has been provided.

* To improve visualization, the Heat Map can now highlight minimum and maximum values.

* The procedure for creating mappings from pharmacophore features has been 
simplified.

* Functionality for merging pharmacophores has been added.

* Query bonds and query atom labels can be removed from the display
in a single click.

* The Hierarchy View has been enhanced to allow the identification of
pharmacophore feature vectors by name.

* The Protein Health report has been enhanced to include Chi angles.

* The Clean button in Protein Reports
and Utilities now lists alternate
conformers that have been removed from the
protein.

* All charges in Mol V3000 files are now read by Discovery Studio .

* The alignment consensus is no longer shown by
default in the Sequence Window.

* Sequences are now updated and remain linked when residues are deleted from
protein structures in the Molecule Window.

* Customized coloring schemes for sequence alignments can now be saved in .bsml files.

* The solvent accessibility calculation has been enhanced to take ligands into 
account when present.

Many enhancements have been made to the DiscoveryScript Perl API:

* Common high-level operations in the user
interface have been exposed in a new
category called
Commands.

* You can now define the folder used when running protocols via DiscoveryScript.

* The molecular overlay functionality can now be accessed.

* A proteinColorByMolecule data type has been added to Mdm::ProteinColorScheme to
enable coloring by molecule.

* The performance for running a script for the first time in the client has been improved.

* A function that gets a list of all property names for an object has been added.

* Additional scripts have been included on the Scripts menu.

* An Arguments tab has been added to the Script Window to allow the input of
command-line parameters to scripts.

* A function has been added for predicting DSC secondary structure.

* Access to the Electrostatics tools has been added.

* The ability to add, remove, and edit constraints has been provided.

* A function that returns the current window extents has been provided.

* The feature visualization has been improved for quick analysis of the associated chemistry.

* Standard pharmacophore feature elements have been renamed in the Hierarchy view to aid understanding.

* "Pharmacophore A" OR "Pharmacophore B" type queries can be created with a single click.

* Automation has been added for customized query creation to improve usability (e.g., aromatic bonds are automatically perceived and set.)

* The ability to use "Customized Features" in the Feature Mapping protocol has been added.

* Error handling has been improved (e.g., check features before adding to the dictionary and disallow additions of bad queries.)

* The Create Features from SMARTS protocol has been added.

A number of important defects have been addressed in this release. Critical 
fixes include the following:

* MSV files created from InsightII PSV files containing polydot surfaces can now be opened successfully.

* If there is a problem opening a .mol2 file, you can now continue to import other .mol2 files without error.

* The percent identity and similarity for selected sequences is now correctly updated in the Sequence Window.

* The percent identity and similarity is now displayed when pasting sequences into the Sequence Window.

* The background color is now displayed correctly in the Sequence Window.

* Sequences can now be copied from a text document and pasted into the Sequence Window.

* Sequences can by pasted into an alignment consensus sequence of the Sequence Window without corruption.

* Chain breaks are now displayed when sequences are pasted into the Sequence Window.

* Results from the Align and Superimpose Proteins protocol are now linked to existing
structures.

* All chain breaks in proteins are now preserved after they are used in MODELER-based
protocols.

#### Platforms added

Discovery Studio client and server support has been added for the following 
configuration:

* Red Hat Enterprise Linux 4.1, Updates 3-6 for x86-64 (64-bit)

#### Platforms removed

Discovery Studio 2.1 supports all operating systems supported in version 2.0. 
However, please note that in the next release of Discovery Studio , platform 
support will be discontinued for:

* Red Hat Enterprise Linux 3.0

* Windows 2000

#### Pipeline Pilot compatibility

Discovery Studio 2.1 is compatible with the following versions of Pipeline 
Pilot:

* Pipeline Pilot 6.1.6

* SciTegic Enterprise Server 7.0.1

By default, DS 2.1 is installed with Pipeline Pilot 6.1.6.

This version of Discovery Studio comes with the latest version of BIOVIA License Pack, version 7.5.1. If an existing version of License Pack is 
detected during installation, it will be updated to this 
version.
