# Discovery Studio 2.5

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes25.htm

## Discovery Studio 2.5

This topic details the newest functionality, enhancements, and critical bug fixes available for version 2.5.

### Contents

* Overview

* New features for version 2.5

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio protocols

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio component collections

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio standalone applications

* Enhancements to the Discovery Studio Client

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio scripting

* Database Updates

* Critical bug fixes

* Platform support

* Licensing changes

Discovery Studio 2.5 provides major new features and enhancements in all areas
of the product. 

Key new capabilities included in this version include:

* support for
fragment based design

* building and refining molecular structures from X-ray data

* modeling transmembrane proteins

* conformational analysis of small molecules

* parallelized pharmacophore
database building and searching

* receptor-ligand visualization

Emphasis has been placed on improving the support for large molecular 
data sets in the Discovery Studio Client.
Capabilities for handling small molecule libraries 
previously included in the Table Browser window are now supported in the Molecule Window. 
The Table Browser and 3D windows have been retired from the product and all molecular visualization
is now performed in the Molecule Window. In addition to simplifying the overall interface, 
significant new functionality has been provided for analyzing and filtering small 
molecule data sets.

For more information about the changes made prior to 2.5.5, 
see Discovery Studio version 2.1 Release Notes .

Molecule Window: This window consolidates and replaces the functionality previously provided in the 3D 
and Table Browser windows. It offers better support for working with large data sets. The 
primary improvement is the integration of browsing support of large data sets, enabling you to view 
molecular properties without loading 3D structures into memory until requested. In addition, key molecular 
properties are calculated in the background as you load a file. For details, see Molecule Window .

The functionality in the Molecule Window is complemented by a new file format, .dsv , that provides
better performance when loading large data sets.
A broad set of filtering, sorting, and editing features have also been added to the Molecule Window,
providing a greatly improved environment for working with large data sets.

Native 64 bit Linux server support: Discovery Studio has been upgraded to work with the 64 bit 
version of the Pipeline Pilot 7.5 server. This simplifies the installation process, as you no longer need to 
maintain both 32 and 64 bit versions, and helps you to improve performance of processor heavy calculations by 
allowing you to run them on 64 bit servers.

Fragment Based Design: New functionality is provided 
for performing fragment based design. A new protocol, Dock Fragments (MCSS) allows you to place fragments in an active receptor site. This protocol uses the Multiple Copy 
Simultaneous Search (MCSS) algorithm, which generates a collection of oriented 
chemical functional groups that interact with the binding-site region of a 
molecule. Calculate Ligand Efficiency has been added to complement this.

X-ray: A new collection of protocols has been added to 
provide functionality for building and refining molecular 
structure models from X-ray crystallographic data. All of these protocols are 
located in the X-ray folder and use the CNX server for 
underlying computations.

The following new protocols are included:

* Generate Electron Density Maps

* Pick Water

* Place Ligands

* Refinement Cascade

* Validate Model Molecule

To support Refinement Cascade, enhancements have been made to the forcefield
tools.

Transmembrane Protein Analysis: A new set of 
tools, Analyze and Edit Transmembrane Proteins ,
is provided for modeling transmembrane proteins. These include a simple tool for performing transmembrane helix identification
from protein sequences using a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) approach.

Tools have also been added for creating and positioning membranes on protein structures
as well as monitoring the protein position relative to a membrane. Several of the protein modeling 
and simulation protocols have been modified to support implicit
membrane solvation models.

Parallel Pharmacophore Database Building and Searching: The 
pharmacophore database building and searching protocols now enable you to take advantage of 
multi-core and multi-processor computers for improved performance for database computations.

2D Window: A new window provides a 2D
representation of molecules. This window interacts with the Molecule Window, allowing
you to make selections in a three-dimensional structure from a 2D representation.

Draw Ligand Interaction Diagram: A new command 
generates a two-dimensional representation of three-dimensional ligand-receptor
binding site interactions. This enables you to view a ligand's 2D structure 
and its interactions with surrounding binding site residues. Selections are synchronized 
with the 3D-Window, enabling you to explore 2D and 3D structures simultaneously.

Conformational Analysis Tools and Protocols: Significant 
improvements have been made to the product's small molecule conformational analysis 
capabilities. Several tools have been added to the new Search Small Molecule Conformations tool
panel that enable rapid conformational searching and analysis. In addition, new protocols 
have been added that provide access to advanced conformational searching methods and analysis 
capabilities useful for high throughput analysis.

General Purpose Protocols: A new protocol folder has been
included that provides access to a set of general purpose protocols. The protocols included in 
this folder perform various general tasks including ligand preparation, protein preparation, and
molecular property calculation.

Quick Launch Protocols: Many of the protocols in Discovery Studio are short running tasks that require minimal set up. For convenience, a number of these protocols can be run with 
a single button click from a tool panel when the appropriate data is loaded.

Discovery Guides: A new tool panel layout called 
Discovery Guides
has been added. This serves as a central location to which you can import or create 
specialized tool panels that guide you through multi-step tasks. Discovery Studio Client 
includes several Discovery Guides, including one for performing protein
homology modeling and another to create and map pharmacophore features. Some examples of other
customizations that can be created and added to the application are also included in the Customization subfolder in the Samples folder.

Welcome Page: A welcome page is now displayed when you start the application. This 
page contains links that open sample files, guide you through basic tasks, and provide access to 
important information sources. You can customize this page or disable it if desired.

See Critical bug fixes for information about additional changes.

#### ADMET

* New data has been added to extend the existing TOPKAT toxicity data models. This results 
in more robust models than in earlier versions of Discovery Studio .

* The Toxicity Prediction (TOPKAT) protocol has been rewritten to make use of extensible 
models in Pipeline Pilot. This allows you to extend 
the models with your own data to improve their applicability to specific data sets. The old 
version has been retained for backwards compatibility, and the new protocol is named Toxicity Prediction (Extensible)

* Several improvements have been made. Reports now contain information about moiety effect (regions of the molecule 
that contribute positively or negatively to the toxicity prediction). Also, the most similar ligands
from the model are optionally exported for each predicted ligand.

#### Conformations

* A new protocol folder, Small Molecules tools , has been added. This folder contains 
protocols for performing conformational searching and analysis of small molecules. The Diverse 
Conformation Generation protocol that was provided in previous versions of Discovery Studio is now located here: A new protocol, Generate Conformations , has been
added. This allows you specify a subset of rotatable bonds for torsion searches. It also provides options
for minimizing generated conformations, either in gas phase or in solution using various solvation models
and force fields. A new protocol, Analyze Conformations ,
has been added. This protocol assesses conformational diversity
and coverage of a set of small molecule conformations.

* A new protocol, Generate Conformations , has been
added. This allows you specify a subset of rotatable bonds for torsion searches. It also provides options
for minimizing generated conformations, either in gas phase or in solution using various solvation models
and force fields.

* A new protocol, Analyze Conformations ,
has been added. This protocol assesses conformational diversity
and coverage of a set of small molecule conformations.

#### Electrostatics

* The Calculate 
Protein Ionization protocol has been modified to allow calculation
of the protein ionization and pH dependent properties of a molecule in the presence of a membrane.
Changes have also been made to preserve properties from the input molecule.

#### General Purpose

* A new protocol folder has been included that provides access to a set of general purpose 
protocols. These protocols provide access to tasks that may be useful in a variety of different 
scenarios. Three protocols have been moved from other folders: Prepare Ligands Filter by SMARTS Calculate Molecular Properties The following new or updated protocols are available in General Purpose: Align to Selected Substructure enables you to align one or more molecular structures to a reference structure
based on a selected substructure in the reference. Calculate Ligand Efficiency normalizes a selected set of numeric molecular properties by a measure
of the molecule size. Prepare Ligands is extended to enumerate ionization states using a set of pre-defined ionization rules. These rules were adapted from the
rules encoded in the LigandGen program. It has also been extended to score and filter tautomers to reduce
the number generated. In addition the protocol now provides support for parallel execution. Prepare Protein fixes common problems in input protein structures that
are to be further processed in other protocols. The following tasks are performed: Atom names are standardized, missing atoms in residues are inserted, and alternate conformations are removed. Missing Loop Regions are inserted based on SEQRES data. Short and Medium Size Loop Regions are optimized with the Looper Algorithm. Remaining Loop Regions are minimized. pK and Protonation states are computed and hydrogen positions are optimized.

* Prepare Ligands

* Filter by SMARTS

* Calculate Molecular Properties

* Align to Selected Substructure enables you to align one or more molecular structures to a reference structure
based on a selected substructure in the reference.

* Calculate Ligand Efficiency normalizes a selected set of numeric molecular properties by a measure
of the molecule size.

* Prepare Ligands is extended to enumerate ionization states using a set of pre-defined ionization rules. These rules were adapted from the
rules encoded in the LigandGen program. It has also been extended to score and filter tautomers to reduce
the number generated. In addition the protocol now provides support for parallel execution.

* Prepare Protein fixes common problems in input protein structures that
are to be further processed in other protocols. The following tasks are performed: Atom names are standardized, missing atoms in residues are inserted, and alternate conformations are removed. Missing Loop Regions are inserted based on SEQRES data. Short and Medium Size Loop Regions are optimized with the Looper Algorithm. Remaining Loop Regions are minimized. pK and Protonation states are computed and hydrogen positions are optimized.

* Atom names are standardized, missing atoms in residues are inserted, and alternate conformations are removed.

* Missing Loop Regions are inserted based on SEQRES data.

* Short and Medium Size Loop Regions are optimized with the Looper Algorithm.

* Remaining Loop Regions are minimized.

* pK and Protonation states are computed and hydrogen positions are optimized.

* A new protocol, Filter by Property: , has been added. This allows you to 
filter ligands by a wide range of properties such as Top (#), Begins with, etc. This is a useful tool 
for extracting summary information from very large result sets (e.g., high throughput 
screen).

* A new protocol, RCSB Structure Search has 
been added. This protocol allows you to search for protein structures in the Research Collaboratory for Structural Bioinformatics 
Protein Data Bank (RCSB PDB). It provides access to the advanced search capabilities from 
the RCSB and adds the ability to align structures based on ligand substructures.

* The Prepare Protein protocol has
been enhanced to add missing N- and C-terminal residues.

#### Library Analysis/Design

* The Enumerate 
Library from Ligands protocol is enhanced to take sketched molecules as input.

* The Enumerate Library from Ligands protocol has been modified to no longer fail if ligands have bad valences.

#### Pharmacophore

* The Build 3D Database and Search 3D Database protocols have been rewritten to support parallel execution. Both protocols now scale linearly if you 
run them on multiple processors.

* Several enhancements have been made to pharmacophore feature capabilities. For example, it is now possible
for a single atom to map more than one pharmacophore feature or to designate a pharmacophore feature that cannot be present in a particular location (NOT feature).

* The database building protocol has been enhanced to report details about the database in the report, such as 
the number of molecules built and the average conformers.

* When accessing a database from a protocol parameter, extra information is displayed to indicate the number of
molecules in the database.

* The Screen Library protocol is enhanced to reduce the time and memory required when using a large number of input 
features.

* To improve efficiency, index files are now built in parallel by the Build 3D Database protocol
when databases are built in parallel.

* Several new customer-requested pharmacophore features have been added to the standard dictionary. These 
include a zinc binder, a positive ionizable that can map pyridyl, a hydrogen bond donor that can map 
aromatic C-H, and several others.

* The Screen Library protocol has been enhanced to allow specification of advanced pharmacophore feature group logic, which 
allows for more flexible searching. It is now possible to search for ligands that have a minimum or maximum number of 
features from user-defined groups. For example, queries can be created that map either a hydrogen bond 
acceptor or a hydrogen bond donor at a specific point.

#### Protein Modeling

* A
new protocol, Align 
Sequence to Templates , has been added. This protocol simplifies the process of creating a protein
homology model from a sequence by combining three key steps: creation of a sequence profile (BLAST Search); alignment 
of template structures, and alignment of the model sequence with templates.

* The following updates have been made to the Build Homology Models protocol: You can select a template and fix part of the model structure according to that template. You can specify nucleic acid residues to be copied from a template to the model structure. It keeps the ligand structure rigid when copying from a template to model, including ligands that span several residues. It creates groups for the model structure for easy analysis and model refinement.

* You can select a template and fix part of the model structure according to that template.

* You can specify nucleic acid residues to be copied from a template to the model structure.

* It keeps the ligand structure rigid when copying from a template to model, including ligands that span several residues.

* It creates groups for the model structure for easy analysis and model refinement.

* The MODELER salign algorithm is now used in the Alignment Structures (MODELER) protocol. 
This algorithm is superior to the malign3d algorithm that it replaces. It aligns protein structure 
based on both sequence and structure similarity.

* The Build Mutants protocol has been modified to use a new faster and more accurate method based on 
the recent publication by Andrej Sali's group.

* The performance of the solvation term computation made by the Loop Refinement (MODELER) protocol has been significantly improved.

* The Align Sequence with Structure protocol (align2d) has been deprecated. For now, the old version is available in the Examples
folder of the Discovery Studio protocols. It will be removed in the next major release.

* The Multiple Sequence Alignment
protocol now allows the use of transmembrane helices
as alignment anchors.

* Modifications have been made to the Model 
Antibody Loops protocol to fix the framework of the 
antibody structure at its input coordinates and only optimize the loop region. In addition, you can now alter the loop definition and create groups for each loop on the input 
structure and the model created.

* Modifications have been made to the Verify Protein (Profiles-3D) to score membrane proteins appropriately.

* A new protocol, Add 
Membrane and Orient Molecule , has been added that automatically adds a membrane to a protein and 
positions the protein in the membrane using a CHARMm energy based method. This is a more rigorous (and 
slower) method than the Add Membrane tool that is included in the new Transmembrane tool panel.

* The X-BUILD Search Rotamer search command and associated dialog is now available in a new Search Side-Chain Rotamers tool panel. 
The new tool panel allows you to select side-chain rotamers without opening a dialog box, which makes it
easier to interact with the protein while stepping through the rotamers.
In addition, access to several monitors (hydrogen-bond, bump, and Dreiding energy) is provided to facilitate manual selection of side-chain rotamers.

* The Loop Refinement and Loop Refinement (MODELER) protocols now use the conformation data model and clusters the loop conformation based on backbone RMSD for easier analysis of the results.

* The BLAST Search (DS server) and PSI-BLAST Search protocols now return hits from a specific organism.

* The Align and Superimpose Proteins protocol 
now allows superimposition of a protein based on a set of selected residues (e.g., ligand binding site residues), and can take a large set of protein structures 
as input. Because this change requires a change to the protocol interface, .pr_xml files
generated in Discovery Studio 2.1 and earlier are not compatible with the new protocol.

* The Align and 
Superimpose Protein protocol has been modified to return results using the Ca Wire display style 
used instead of the Ca stick style.

#### QSAR

* A new protocol, Create Recursive 
Partitioning , has been added. Related enhancements have been made to the Dendrogram Window to improve decision tree viewing.

* Several of the QSAR model generation methods have been enhanced. For example, many of the learners
have optimum prediction space and feature tracking capabilities. A warning is generated if 
a prediction is performed on a molecule outside the optimum prediction space or contains
a molecular feature not seen in the training set.

* The Create Genetic Function 
Approximation Model protocol has been upgraded to use the GFA component that was included with Pipeline Pilot 7.5. Because this updated component exposes many different parameters, .pr_xml files
generated in Discovery Studio 2.1 and earlier are not compatible with the new protocol.

* A new protocol, Create 3D QSAR model , has been added. This protocol creates 
regression models built from whole molecular steric and electrostatic fields, which are useful for predicting 
activity and visualizing favorable and unfavorable interactions.

* The usability of the QSAR protocols has been improved by allowing a separate test set to be used for 
validating the models.

#### Receptor-Ligand Interactions

* The Calculate 
Binding Energies protocol can now compute the conformational entropy of
the ligand. This adds a term to account for the loss in conformational entropy from the 
starting set of conformations to a single docked conformation.

* The Dock Ligands 
(CDOCKER) protocol now exposes the gradient tolerance as a parameter. An optional 
clustering step increases pose diversity.

* The Dock Ligands 
(LibDock) protocol exposes two new parameters: Rigid Optimization
controls whether rigid docking is allowed, and Keep Hydrogens controls whether to remove the 
hydrogens during the hotspot alignment phase (this option is only available if post optimization 
is disabled). A parameter to perform an in-situ ligand minimization has also been added.

* The Calculate Binding 
Energies protocol can now perform an in-situ ligand 
minimization.

* The Dock Ligands (GOLD) protocol has been modified to support version 2026 of GOLD. The following new features can now be accessed
through the Discovery Studio Client: New scoring functions: Astex Statistical Potential (ASP), Piecewise Linear Potential (CHEMPLP), ChemScore Receptor
Density Scaling (ChemScore RDS) A new GOLD scoring component that includes the complete list of GOLD scoring functions including target
specific versions: kinases and cytochromes (this functionality is accessible through the Score Ligand Poses protocol) Ring template matching (uses a library of CSD ring conformations to explore flexible ring conformations) Flexible amino acid side chains Scaffold constraints Expanded Genetic Algorithm (GA) settings

* New scoring functions: Astex Statistical Potential (ASP), Piecewise Linear Potential (CHEMPLP), ChemScore Receptor
Density Scaling (ChemScore RDS)

* A new GOLD scoring component that includes the complete list of GOLD scoring functions including target
specific versions: kinases and cytochromes (this functionality is accessible through the Score Ligand Poses protocol)

* Ring template matching (uses a library of CSD ring conformations to explore flexible ring conformations)

* Flexible amino acid side chains

* Scaffold constraints

* Expanded Genetic Algorithm (GA) settings

#### Simulation

* Enhancements have been made to improve the performance of high-throughput docking 
protocols using CHARMm.

* Several protocols in the Simulation folder have been upgraded to 
deal with protein:membrane systems more effectively.

#### General

The high-level layout of the Discovery Studio component collections has been updated
to provide consistency with the revised high-level structure of the component collections in
Pipeline Pilot 7.5. A detailed description of the components is available in the DS Component
Collection User Guide, accessible from the Pipeline Pilot Help Center . The following is an overview of the changes:

* The ADMET, Library Design, Pharmacophore, Receptor-Ligand Interactions, and
Simulations collections have been moved to the Chemistry folder.

* The Electrostatics, Protein-Modeling, and X-Ray collections have been moved to the
Biology folder.

* The components formerly included in the QSAR folder have been either included directly in 
the corresponding protocols or moved to the Chemistry | Molecular Properties and Chemistry | Utilities 
folders.

* The Readers/Writers folders have been moved to Chemistry | Data Access and Manipulation | Readers/Writers | Discovery Studio .

* Many improvements and enhancements have been made to help text for the components 
and protocols.

Command-line executables (Catalyst, CHARMm, CNX, and Modeler) can now be deployed from the Discovery Studio installer. When prompted for a type during installation, choose the Custom installation option and choose any of the available standalone applications you want to install.

The MODELER server for protein homology analysis has been upgraded to version 9v7. This version 
includes a number of bug fixes and enhancements including:

* A native 64 bit version of the package.

* The new version complies with the latest PDB format for DNA/RNA, ligands, and ions 
(now reads and writes metal ions correctly).

* The speed of GB/SA calculations has been significantly increased.

* To provide Windows support, the io_data.atom_files_directory is now a Python list of directories, rather than a 
colon-separated string.

* When reading or writing compressed files, the uncompressed versions are now 
written into writable local storage (${MODELLER_TMPDIR} if set, otherwise the system temporary 
directory if possible, or the current working directory). Previously, these files were 
written into the same directory as the compressed versions, which is problematic when that directory 
is read-only or is on network storage.

Discovery Studio version 2.5.5 now supports version 9v7 of MODELER which addresses a few critical issues and supports 64-bit processing.

The CNX server for performing analysis of X-ray crystallographic 
data is included with this release of Discovery Studio . CNX integrates X-ray diffraction and NMR spectroscopic 
data with molecular mechanics, dynamics, and energy minimization to aid in the solution of 3D molecular 
structures.

CHARMm Upgrade: CHARMm has been upgraded to version 35b1, and includes a native 64 bit 
version of the package.

New features and enhancements have been added to the following areas:

#### General Usability Enhancements

* The explorer dockable windows now feature an autohide mode. In this mode
explorer windows are automatically collapsed when not in use to provide more workspace for visualization. 
See Customizing the client for more information.

* You can now undock tabbed windows and manage them separately outside of the main application window. This feature is particularly useful when working with multiple monitors.
See Working with windows for more information.

* A folder named Discovery Studio Client is now created in your home directory when you start the application
for the first time. This is the default location for all protocol results and newly created files.

* The Samples folder now 
includes new files that illustrate a broader range of capabilities of the client.

* A search utility, the Feature 
Search box , allows you to quickly find any command, protocol, or preference in the application.

* Adding script commands no longer requires a restart of the application for the commands to become
available.

* You can now export multiple script commands into a single file. These files
can be imported into the application by other users to rapidly deploy new functionality. This function is 
accessible through the Script Commands subpage of the Preferences dialog.

* The Text Window has been upgraded on Linux to provide better rendering of .html . 

The new window also provides improved compatibility with the Pipeline Pilot Reporting collection.

* A new command, Arrange, is available from the Windows menu . This 
command maximizes windows to fit into the application work space but are stacked to aid navigation.

* A new command, Choose..., is available from the Windows menu . This 
command switches the workspace view to show images of all open windows to help you find the window you are looking for.

* New buttons in the Tools explorer to allow you to expand and compress all tool
panels in a single operation.

* New tool panels can be created and edited directly from the Tools Explorer . The 
functionality can be accessed by right-clicking the explorer. This functionality was previously located in the Preferences dialog.

* A folder called Customization has been added to the 
Samples folder. This folder contains example file that contain examples of customizations that can 
be imported into the application to extend its functionality.

* Several tool panels have been renamed to provide more descriptive titles. The specific changes are: 3D Pointer and Labels has been renamed Navigate and Label 3D Structure Binding Site has been renamed Define and Edit Binding Site Binding Site Analysis has been renamed Analyze Binding Site Electrostatics has been renamed Assign Electrostatic Parameters Evolutionary Trace has been renamed Analyzed Protein Conservation Pattern Forcefield has been renamed Simulate Structures Phylogenetics has been renamed Analyze Sequences Protein Health has been renamed Validate Protein Structure X-BUILD has been renamed Build and Refine X-ray Structure X-LIGAND has been renamed Place and Refine X-ray Ligand Structure X-ray has been renamed Edit X-ray Structure

* 3D Pointer and Labels has been renamed Navigate and Label 3D Structure

* Binding Site has been renamed Define and Edit Binding Site

* Binding Site Analysis has been renamed Analyze Binding Site

* Electrostatics has been renamed Assign Electrostatic Parameters

* Evolutionary Trace has been renamed Analyzed Protein Conservation Pattern

* Forcefield has been renamed Simulate Structures

* Phylogenetics has been renamed Analyze Sequences

* Protein Health has been renamed Validate Protein Structure

* X-BUILD has been renamed Build and Refine X-ray Structure

* X-LIGAND has been renamed Place and Refine X-ray Ligand Structure

* X-ray has been renamed Edit X-ray Structure

* Functionality from the Modify Conformation dialog has been merged with the new Search and Analyze 
Conformations tool panel. The Coordinate Kick command has been deprecated.

* Functionality from the Evolutionary Trace tool panel has been merged with functionality in the 
Analyze Complexes tool panel.

* You can exit full-screen mode by pressing the ESC or F11 key.

* When you position your cursor over a window tab, the location of the data file is indicated by a tool tip in the status bar.

* A new command, Check for Updates, is available from the Help menu . This 
will check on the BIOVIA web site for product updates and open a web page with details if a newer version of the 
product is available.

* Tooltips have been enhanced to provide more information about specific features. The tooltips
include links to the relevant help topics and in some cases provide links to related information. Information
about features is no longer displayed in the Status bar.

* Context menu items have been added to the Molecule Window to provide access to the Apply Forcefield and
Show Sequence actions.

* The behavior of the Tool Panels Explorer has been modified so that double clicking on the header of
a panel opens it and closes all other panels. This makes it easier to manage and access tool panels.

#### Molecule Window

* The Molecule Window replaces the 3D and Table Browser windows. This 
window provides better support for loading and manipulating large molecular data sets.

* The .msv file format is replaced with the .dsv format. This new format is specifically designed
to provide better support for large data sets of small molecules. You can still 
import .msv files created with older versions of the application, but older versions of Discovery
Studio will not be able to read the new format. 
Files saved in the DSV format are able to store window layout and other application state information that was previously only available as general preferences (such as window background,
lighting), which affected all open files. The selection and visibility state of individual molecules in files are also be stored.

* Navigation Keys are now provided in the 
Molecules tab of the Data Table View . 
These keys allow you to quickly scroll through a set of molecules without having to manually set and reset 
the visibility of molecules. Keys are also provided to navigate to the first and last molecules
of a data set.

* The two dimensional chemistry of small molecules can now be viewed in the Data Table View .

* Multiple properties can now be calculated for small molecules when they are loaded into the
Molecule Window. The calculation is performed in the background, which allows you to continue
to work while the computation is performed. This option is available in the Molecule Window preferences .

* Sequences and secondary structures are extracted as properties from .pdb and .mol2 files, enabling you align structural data sets by 
sequence and secondary structure without loading the 3D structures into memory.

* Advanced filtering functionality is available in the Data Table View . This 
functionality can be accessed through the context menu and enables you to select molecules based on all available 
properties. For details, see Filter dialog .

* You can tag molecules of interest for rapid selection at a later point.

* You can lock the visibility of individual molecules. This feature can be used in conjunction with 
new navigation keys in the Molecules tab of the Data Table to compare reference structures against
a larger set of structures.

* Molecule files can now be appended by dragging 
the file from the Files Explorer to an open Molecule Window. Matching columns are automatically matched
while unique columns are appended.

* Molecule files can now be merged by row. Files can be processed 
in a protocol and then calculated properties subsequently merged into the original file.

* Molecular data sets can now be merged. The Insert from File command
identifies common molecules in two data files and appends the matching data in new columns.

* The Transmembrane Protein Tool Panel has functionality that allows you to add implicit membranes to a protein structure.

* Additional options are available in the Atom 
Display Style dialog to color carbon atoms of a molecule using a custom color, or automatically assign color to different 
molecules.

* A new toolbar, Atom Colors , has been added. 
This provides access to several convenient methods for coloring 3D structures. Available methods include: Color by Element Color Carbons only Differently Color Molecules Differently Color Chains Differently

* Color by Element

* Color Carbons only Differently

* Color Molecules Differently

* Color Chains Differently

* A new monitor type, Menu | Structure | Monitor | Dreiding Energy , has been added to show the energy of a selected set of atoms based on Dreiding 
forcefield.

* A new monitor type, Menu | Structure | Monitor | Pi Interactions, 
has been added to show Pi-Pi, Cation-Pi, and Sigma-Pi interactions.

* A new command, Menu | Chemistry | Bond | Localize Bonds , has been added for localizing bonds and charges. This command now provides a solution to problems 
previously reported with exporting molecules in .mol and .sd formats.

* A new command, Menu | Chemistry | Bond | Perceive Aromaticity , has been added for calculating aromatic bonds.

* The Menu | Chemistry | Hydrogens | Remove Hydrogens command now works on all 
atoms, regardless of their visibility.

* A number of display style settings (e.g., Background Color, Quality, Lighting, Materials) previously
only available as global application preferences, can now be set on a per-window basis via the Display Style dialog (right-click the window and choose Display Style...). The default application settings can still be set through the Molecule Window | Graphics subpage of the 
Preferences dialog.

* The Select dialog no longer disables the rest of the interface while it is open, which 
makes selecting the intersection of two sets of objects in the Molecule Window easier. In addition, there is a new option to create a
group from the selected atoms directly from the dialog.

* The Create Surface command now allows Coloring by Grid. It is also 
possible to specify transparency levels for the reverse surface.

* A new option Context is selected atoms only has been added to the Solvent Accessibility dialog.
This enables the calculation of the solvent accessibility of a specific set of selected residues in the 
context of the rest of the molecule.

* The HBonds monitor has been modified to report on hydrogen bonds between two regions
of a protein only when other proteins are present.

* The default color scheme for protein secondary structures has been changed from Amino Acid to 
Secondary Structure.

* A new item Pi Interaction has been added to the Structure | Monitors submenu. This 
shows pi interactions between proteins and ligand.

* The ability to group pharmacophore features during analysis in order to be able to 
select one or two features to map from each group/sub-set of features from a query has been added.

#### Sequence Window

* A new command, Sequence | Secondary Structure | Edit ,
has been added to allow editing of the secondary structure data for the selected residues of a sequence. 
The secondary structure assignments of individual residues or selections can now be edited directly 
in the Sequence Window using the Edit Secondary Structure dialog.

* The secondary structure prediction algorithm has been enhanced to create secondary structure
motifs as sequence features. Sequence features can be viewed in the Sequence 
Annotation Window .

* The Sequence Window Display Style dialog has been enhanced 
to enable toggling of the visibility status of different types of secondary structure predictions such as DSC or 
Kabsch-Sander.

* Sequences can now be hidden in the Sequence Window , 
allowing you to work with subsets of sequences without discarding the rest of the window contents.

* The Sequence Window Display Style dialog now 
provides a better preview of the appearance of color formatted residues.

* The ability to report sequence similarity on a set of selected residues is now provided. This functionality can be accessed through
the Sequence | Similarity subpage of the Preferences dialog.

* A new deletion mode replaces residues with gaps when they are deleted from a linked sequence.

* A new toolbar, Sequence , has been added to the Sequence 
Window. This provides convenient access to a number of commands that allow you to quickly change the layout 
of the window. Available methods include: Wrapped View Ruler Secondary Structure Cartoon Alignment Consensus Remove Gaps Remove Aligned Gaps Remove Alignment Coloring Color Alignment by Similarity Color Alignment by Hydrophobicity

* Wrapped View

* Ruler

* Secondary Structure Cartoon

* Alignment Consensus

* Remove Gaps

* Remove Aligned Gaps

* Remove Alignment Coloring

* Color Alignment by Similarity

* Color Alignment by Hydrophobicity

* A new command has been added to extract a sequence alignment based on a protein structure superimposition.

* An enhancement has been made that allows the selection of a set of residues by 
clicking on the secondary structure cartoon.

* A new action Select Fixed Residue 
Blocks has been added to the Sequence Window. This is useful when removing fixed residues 
from an alignment.

* A preference has been added that specifies whether secondary structure cartoons should be shown when
a sequence is opened.

* The ability to recognize the .aa file extension as a sequence file format has been added.

#### Charts

* The behavior of interactions between charts and data in the Molecule Window has been 
redesigned to take advantage of new features. Charts now display the data that is viewable in the Molecules
tab, allowing you to filter out data that is not of interest. Selection is still fully supported between
charts and molecular data, allowing you to identify points of interest in charts and quickly access the
corresponding data in the Molecule Window.

* You can now make multiple selections in the Choose Plot Axes dialogs by SHIFT-clicking the corresponding checkboxes.

#### Analyze and Edit Transmembrane Proteins Tools

* A new tool panel, Analyze and Edit Transmembrane Proteins , has 
been added. This contains tools for predicting transmembrane protein helices and defining membranes. A new command, Predict Transmembrane Helices, is included. This tool uses an HMM based
method to predict helical secondary structure motifs from protein sequences. A new command group, Membranes, provides tools for creating and editing implicit membrane objects. These
membranes are recognized by various molecular mechanics based methods. A new command group, Edit Protein, provides tools for selecting and editing protein transmembrane regions.

* A new command, Predict Transmembrane Helices, is included. This tool uses an HMM based
method to predict helical secondary structure motifs from protein sequences.

* A new command group, Membranes, provides tools for creating and editing implicit membrane objects. These
membranes are recognized by various molecular mechanics based methods.

* A new command group, Edit Protein, provides tools for selecting and editing protein transmembrane regions.

#### Analyze Sequences Tools

* The Phylogenetics tools have been moved to a new tool 
panel, Analyze Sequences .

* Three new tools have been added that provide searching and alignment functionality: BLAST Search (DS Server) provides a shortcut
to the corresponding protocol. BLAST Search provides a shortcut
to the corresponding protocol. Basic Sequence Alignment (NCBI Server) performs
rapid alignments of sequences using the ClustalW program.

* BLAST Search (DS Server) provides a shortcut
to the corresponding protocol.

* BLAST Search provides a shortcut
to the corresponding protocol.

* Basic Sequence Alignment (NCBI Server) performs
rapid alignments of sequences using the ClustalW program.

#### Analyze Binding Site Tools

* A new action, Decorate Sequence , has been added to the Analyzing Binding Site tool panel. 
This annotates residues in a linked sequence to indicate interaction sites in a receptor. This can be used when the sequence has been opened after interaction
sites have been created in a Molecule Window.

#### Analyze Protein Conservation Pattern

* The Evolutionary Trace tools have been moved to a new tool panel called Analyze Protein 
Conservation Pattern .

#### Build and Edit Nucleic Acid Tools

* The ability to convert between DNA and RNA has been added to the Build and Edit Nucleic Acids tool panel.

#### Build and Edit Protein Tools

* A new action Insert Loop has been added to the Build and Edit Protein tool panel. 
This closes a gap in a protein structure by inserting a set of residues. It uses the random tweak method 
by Shenkin to quickly find a loop conformation that has no bumps or minimum bumps between the 
inserted loop and the rest of the protein.

* The ability to mutate all selected residues to a specific residue type in a single step has been added.

#### Define Binding Site Tools

* You can now expand or contract the Binding Sphere with the Contract/Expand Sites command.

#### Protein Reports and Utilities Tools

* Nucleic acid information is now included in the report generated by the Protein Report tool.

* The Protein Report tool now creates groups of 
residues where missing segments are found based on comparison of 
ATOM and SEQRES record in .pdb files. The missing segments are stored as residue properties that are more conveniently used by the Insert commands.

#### Dock Ligands Discovery Guide

* A new Discovery Guide, Dock Ligands,
has been added. This simplifies the task of preparing, executing, and analyzing a protein receptor-ligand
docking study.

#### Search Small Molecule Conformation Tools

* A new tool panel, Search Small Molecule Conformations , has been added to consolidate the 
conformational search and analysis tools.

* A new set of commands have been provided for performing conformational searches. These methods are intended to
complement the conformational search methods exposed in the Conformations protocols folder, which are intended 
for high-throughput analysis of small molecule data sets. Conformation Method: Three methods are available: random, systematic, and Boltzmann jump. Energy Threshold: Sets the maximum energy threshold for a search.

* Conformation Method: Three methods are available: random, systematic, and Boltzmann jump.

* Energy Threshold: Sets the maximum energy threshold for a search.

#### Simulate Structure Tools

* You can now directly choose the partial charge algorithm from the 
Simulate Structures tool panel.

* A command has now been added to the Simulate Structure tool panel that enables you to clear the current 
forcefield.

* Forcefield parameters can now be edited directly after typing.

* You can now add customized residues, new atom types, and new parameters directly into the 
forcefield and re-use them for typing.

* The XPROliG forcefield has been modified to handle alternate conformers correctly.

* The XPROliG forcefield has been modified to prevent it from adding hydrogens to water, DNA, and RNA 
molecules.

* You can now create distance restraints between pseudo-atoms (or centroids).

* Functionality from the Constraints tool panel has been merged with the new Simulate Structures tool 
panel.

* Two new tools have been added that enable you to launch CHARMm energy and minimization calculations
directly for structures loaded in the Molecule Window.

#### Sketch and Align Molecules Discovery Guide

* A new Discovery Guide, Sketch and Align Molecules ,
has been added. This simplifies the task of creating and aligning small molecule structures.

#### Superimpose Proteins Tools

* A new tool panel, Superimpose Proteins ,
has been added. This simplifies the task of superimposing proteins and manually aligning protein 
structures. The Superimpose by Alignment and Superimpose by Residue commands have been superseded by functionality on the new tool panel and as a result have been removed.

#### Visualize Receptor-Ligand Interactions Tools

* A new tool panel, Visualize Receptor-Ligand Interactions, has been added. This 
provides functionality for defining receptor-ligand interaction monitors.

#### Protocol Launcher

* You can now save modified default parameters for protocols. This 
allows you to save your preferences locally without modifying the protocol. This 
functionality is accessed by right-clicking the Parameters Explorer window. You can also reset the original default preferences if desired.

* Launch time for protocols has been significantly reduced.

* The time to download large numbers of result files has been reduced substantially.

* Protocols that require minimal setup such as Feature Mapping, Generate Conformations, Calculate Properties, BLAST 
and Minimization now offer a new mechanism for launching protocols synchronously without saving files.

* Some quick running protocols can now be run with a single click from tool panels. You can see an example of this in the Validate Protein Structure tool panel.

* You can now open a protocol in the Pipeline Pilot Client directly from the Protocols
Explorer. Note that the Pipeline Pilot Client is only available on Windows and 
this feature is limited that platform.

* Any protocol on a Pipeline Pilot server can be exposed in the Discovery Studio Client without having to copy or move protocols in the Pipeline Pilot Client . For details, see Customizing protocols .

#### Help

* The integrated help viewer has been significantly improved. Key 
enhancements included improved html rendering quality and faster searching.

* Extensive reorganization and improved linking makes help topics easier to find.

* Literature citations now link directly to the corresponding item in the references. Links have also 
been provided where available to use a reference's Digital Object Identifier (DOI) to link to the
corresponding information on the internet. Note that this capability requires an active internet 
connection. For more information about DOIs see: http://www.doi.org/index.html .

* A comprehensive set of tutorials are now included with the help that can also be accessed online.

* New API elements have been added to support the Transmembrane Analysis tools.

* The Sequence Data Model API has been extended to improve the ability to create and manipulate 
features. New capabilities include the ability to: access a feature location from a feature manipulate the level of a feature manipulate the text label of a feature

* access a feature location from a feature

* manipulate the level of a feature

* manipulate the text label of a feature

* Scripting API elements have been added for the resonant structure localization and
aromatization commands added to the Chemistry | Bond menu.

The following databases have been updated:

* BLAST databases

* MODELER profile databases

* Antibody Loop database

* A memory leak in the Perl API that caused problems when attempting to open large numbers of files with single 
script has been fixed.

* A memory issue when running Dock Ligands (LigandFit) and Score Ligand Poses protocols that resulted in
losing some results is resolved.

* Terminal oxygen atoms are correctly placed after inserting missing residues into protein chains.

* The Feature Mapping protocol now maps of certain customized features correctly.

* The C-alpha chirality issue when running Loop Refinement protocol using the CHARMm forcefield is resolved.

* An issue resulting in the incorrect bonding of structures produced by the Loop Refinement protocol for
multi-chain proteins with disulfide bridges is resolved.

* The Screen Library protocol now groups the results appropriately and returns multiple .sd files
instead of a single file.

* Creation of large pharmacophore databases has been improved on Windows. A problem 
whereby some hits were not returned in the results has been addressed. This correction may require 
re-indexing of Catalyst databases (the search protocol will indicate if this is necessary).

* An error that could occur when running a bootstrap analysis of nucleotide sequence data is fixed.

* A problem whereby sequences corresponding to nodes in bootstrap trees were not all selected is resolved.

##### Known Issues

* GOLD pr_xml parameter files created in previous version of Discovery Studio may not work correctly in 
version 2.5.5.

* The typing of some systems, notably terminal residues of proteins, has now been improved for all molecules. Some
structures typed before DS 2.5.5 should be re-typed to get these improvements.
Protocols that re-type (e.g., Calculate Binding Energy)
will give different results. Note that this only affects a small portion of proteins as most of the terminal residues were typed
correctly before.

#### Platforms added

This release adds platform support for:

* Microsoft Windows XP Professional, SP3

* Microsoft Windows Vista, Business and Enterprise Editions, SP1

* Red Hat Enterprise 4.1 Update 7

* Red Hat Enterprise 5.0 Update 2 (5.2)

* Windows 2008 Server running in 64-bit mode for Pipeline Pilot and the Discovery Studio servers and components.

#### Platforms removed

In this release of Discovery Studio , support has been discontinued for the following platforms:

* Red Hat Enterprise Linux 3.0

* Red Hat Enterprise Linux 4.1 Update 3

* SUSE Linux Enterprise 10 Retail. Only SP1 and higher are supported.

* Windows 2000

#### Pipeline Pilot compatibility

Discovery Studio 2.5 is compatible with the following versions of Pipeline Pilot:

* Pipeline Pilot 7.5

By default, DS 2.5 is installed with Pipeline Pilot 7.5.4 which includes Collection Update 4 (CU4).

This version of Discovery Studio comes with the latest version of BIOVIA License Pack, version 7.6.1. If an existing version of License Pack is 
detected during installation, it will be updated.

# Discovery Studio 2.5.1

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes251.htm

## Discovery Studio 2.5.1

The following enhancements and critical bug fixes are provided in version 2.5.1:

* .bsml files with missing residue attribute data can now be loaded. Missing residue attributes are replaced by default values.

* Various enhancements have been made to the Undo feature.

* Improved Data Table View performance when handling large data sets.

* Edit | Invert Selection no longer ignores objects that are under hidden molecules.

* .dsv files now preserve zoom level, translation, and rotation view.

* Improved the stability of .dsv files.

* Full screen view now works correctly on Linux.

* You can now copy and paste molecules from other applications that support MDL Mol/SD clipboard format (e.g., MDL Draw and Accord Draw).

* Stability improvements have been made for updating preferences.

* When inserting or dragging and dropping multiple files, all the files are now correctly processed, and Undo can be performed.

* The Hardware Stereo now works correctly for the following configuration: Linux RedHat 4 Update 4 with an ATI FireGL V7600 card and driver version 8.583.

* Improvements have been made for typing modified nucleic acid templates.

* The output from a Calculate Binding Energy protocol run with the receptor flexibility option now opens correctly.

* Inserting a nonstandard AA via scripting now works.

* Using scripting to add user defined secondary structure to a sequence is now possible.

* Import/Export of scripts between Windows/Linux platforms is now possible.

* Opening a .mol2 file containing multiple molecules through scripting now works correctly. This also corrects a related issue in the DS Molecule Reader.

* Fixed a rare case where molecular properties were occasionally not stored in .dsv files.

* Fixed a rare issue that occurred when exporting .sd files from a window containing invisible molecules loaded from a .dsv file.

# Discovery Studio 2.5.5

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes255.htm

## Discovery Studio 2.5.5

This topic details the newest functionality, enhancements, and critical bug fixes available for version 2.5.5.

### Contents

* General Enhancements

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio protocols

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio component collections

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio standalone applications

* Enhancements to the Discovery Studio Client

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio scripting

* Critical bug fixes

Native 64 bit Linux server support: Discovery Studio has been upgraded to work with the 64 bit
version of the Pipeline Pilot 7.5 server. This simplifies the installation process, as you no longer need to
maintain both 32 and 64 bit versions, and helps you to improve performance of processor heavy calculations by
allowing you to run them on 64 bit servers.

#### ADMET

* The Toxicity Prediction (TOPKAT) protocol was simplified by removing most of the choices in the Submodels parameter. The appropriate submodel will be used automatically.

* Several improvements have
been made to the Toxicity Prediction (Extensible) protocol. Reports now contain information about moiety effect (regions of the molecule
that contribute positively or negatively to the toxicity prediction). Also, the most similar ligands
from the model are optionally exported for each predicted ligand.

#### General Purpose

* A new protocol, Filter by Property , has been added. This allows you to
filter ligands by a wide range of properties such as Top (#), Begins with, etc. This is a useful tool
for extracting summary information from very large result sets (e.g., high throughput
screen).

* A new protocol, RCSB Structure Search has
been added. This protocol allows you to search for protein structures in the Research Collaboratory for Structural Bioinformatics
Protein Data Bank (RCSB PDB). It provides access to the advanced search capabilities from
the RCSB and adds the ability to align structures based on ligand substructures.

#### Library Analysis/Design

* The Enumerate Library from Ligands protocol has been modified to no longer fail if ligands have bad valences.

#### Pharmacophore

* To improve efficiency, index files are now built in parallel by the Build 3D Database protocol
when databases are built in parallel.

* Several new customer-requested pharmacophore features have been added to the standard dictionary. These
include a zinc binder, a positive ionizable that can map pyridyl, a hydrogen bond donor that can map
aromatic C-H, and several others.

* The Screen Library protocol has been enhanced to allow specification of advanced pharmacophore feature group logic, which
allows for more flexible searching. It is now possible to search for ligands that have a minimum or maximum number of
features from user-defined groups. For example, queries can be created that map either a hydrogen bond
acceptor or a hydrogen bond donor at a specific point.

#### Protein Modeling

* The Align and
Superimpose Protein protocol has been modified to return results using the Ca Wire display style
instead of the Ca stick style.

#### QSAR

* A new protocol, Create 3D QSAR Model , has been added. This protocol creates
regression models built from whole molecular steric and electrostatic fields, which are useful for predicting
activity and visualizing favorable and unfavorable interactions.

* The usability of the QSAR protocols has been improved by allowing a separate test set to be used for
validating the models.

#### Receptor-Ligand Interactions

* The Dock Ligands (GOLD) protocol has been modified to support version 2026 of GOLD. The following new features can now be accessed
through the Discovery Studio Client: New scoring functions: Astex Statistical Potential (ASP), Piecewise Linear Potential (CHEMPLP), ChemScore Receptor
Density Scaling (ChemScore RDS) A new GOLD scoring component that includes the complete list of GOLD scoring functions including target
specific versions: kinases and cytochromes (this functionality is accessible through the Score Ligand Poses protocol) Ring template matching (uses a library of CSD ring conformations to explore flexible ring conformations) Flexible amino acid side chains Scaffold constraints Expanded Genetic Algorithm (GA) settings

* New scoring functions: Astex Statistical Potential (ASP), Piecewise Linear Potential (CHEMPLP), ChemScore Receptor
Density Scaling (ChemScore RDS)

* A new GOLD scoring component that includes the complete list of GOLD scoring functions including target
specific versions: kinases and cytochromes (this functionality is accessible through the Score Ligand Poses protocol)

* Ring template matching (uses a library of CSD ring conformations to explore flexible ring conformations)

* Flexible amino acid side chains

* Scaffold constraints

* Expanded Genetic Algorithm (GA) settings

#### Simulation

* You can now create and visualize HOMO and LUMO orbitals using the QMMM protocols: Calculate Energy (QM-MM) and Minimization (QM-MM) .

#### Electrostatics

* A new example protocol, Residue Electrostatic Energy, has been added under Discovery Studio | Examples | Electrostatics.
The protocol calculates the contribution of individual amino acid to the electrostatic and van der Waals interaction energy 
in a protein structure and those energy terms can be used to identify the hotspots for protein 
thermostability, pH dependent stability, and protein-protein binding affinity.

#### General

* Many improvements and enhancements have been made to help text for the components
and protocols.

* MODELER Upgrade: MODELER is upgraded to version 9v7, and includes native 64 bit
version of the package. In addition, the new version complies with the latest PDB format for DNA/RNA, ligands, and ions
(now reads and writes metal ions correctly).

* CHARMm Upgrade: CHARMm has been upgraded to version 35b1, and includes a native 64 bit
version of the package.

New features and enhancements have been added to the following areas:

#### General Usability Enhancements

* Tooltips have been enhanced to provide more information about specific features. The tooltips
include links to the relevant help topics and in some cases provide links to related information. Information
about features is no longer displayed in the Status bar.

* Context menu items have been added to the Molecule Window to provide access to the Apply Forcefield and
Show Sequence actions.

* The behavior of the Tool Panels Explorer has been modified so that double clicking on the header of
a panel opens it and closes all other panels. This makes it easier to manage and access tool panels.

#### Molecule Window

* A new option Context is selected atoms only has been added to the Solvent Accessibility dialog.
This enables the calculation of the solvent accessibility of a specific set of selected residues in the
context of the rest of the molecule.

* The HBond monitor has been modified to report on hydrogen bonds between two regions
of a protein only when other proteins are present.

* The default color scheme for protein secondary structures has been changed from Amino Acid to
Secondary Structure.

* A new item Pi Interaction has been added to the Structure | Monitors submenu. This
shows pi interactions between proteins and ligand.

* The ability to group pharmacophore features during analysis in order to be able to
select one or two features to map from each group/sub-set of features from a query has been added.

#### Sequence Window

* An enhancement has been made that allows the selection of a set of residues by
clicking on the secondary structure cartoon.

* A new action Select Fixed Residue Blocks has been added to the Sequence Window. This is useful when removing fixed residues
from an alignment.

* A preference has been added that specifies whether secondary structure cartoons should be shown when
a sequence is opened.

* The ability to recognize the .aa file extension as a sequence file format has been added.

#### Analyze Binding Site Tools

* A new action, Decorate Sequence , has been added to the Analyze Complexes tool panel.
This annotates residues in a linked sequence to indicate interaction sites in a receptor. This can be used when the sequence has been opened after interaction
sites have been created in a Molecule Window.

#### Analyze Protein Conservation Pattern Tools

* The Evolutionary Trace tools have been moved to a new tool panel called Analyze Protein
Conservation Pattern .

#### Build and Edit Nucleic Acid Tools

* The ability to convert between DNA and RNA has been added to the Build and Edit Nucleic Acids tool panel.

#### Build and Edit Protein Tools

* A new action Insert Loop has been added to the Build and Edit Protein tool panel.
This closes a gap in a protein structure by inserting a set of residues. It uses the random tweak method
to quickly find a loop conformation that has no bumps or minimum bumps between the
inserted loop and the rest of the protein.

* The ability to mutate all selected residues to a specific residue type in a single step has been added.

#### Dock Ligands Discovery Guide

* A new Discovery Guide, Dock Ligands,
has been added. This simplifies the task of preparing, executing, and analyzing a protein receptor-ligand
docking study.

#### Sketch and Align Molecules Discovery Guide

* A new Discovery Guide, Sketch and Align Molecules ,
has been added. This simplifies the task of creating and aligning small molecule structures.

#### Superimpose Proteins Tools

* A new tool panel, Superimpose Proteins ,
has been added. This simplifies the task of superimposing proteins and manually aligning protein
structures. The Superimpose by Alignment and Superimpose by Residue commands have been superseded by functionality on the new tool panel and as a result have been removed.

* Script methods have been added to provide access to the Hitrate, Histogram, Ramachandran,
Contact, and 2D ligand plots.

* Script methods have been added to provide access to the Cluster Structure and Recursive
Partitioning dendrogram views.

* The ability to create Pi-interaction monitors has been added to the scripting interface.

* A method to create rotatable bond monitors from selected bonds has been added.

* Support has been added for saving graphical images from the Molecule Window using scripting.

* The memory usage and performance of the Molecule Window for visualizing large sets of macromolecules
are greatly improved.

* The size of .dsv files has been significantly reduced.

* The speed with which molecules can be browsed in the Molecule Window has been increased.

* The time to compute surfaces for proteins when multiple molecules are present in a window has been greatly
reduced.

* Numerous improvements have been made to the handling of trajectories including increasing the size
of files that can be loaded.

* The responsiveness to selection of objects in the Molecule Window has been improved.

* Several issues in the Edit | Select dialog have been addressed.

* A problem that occurred when assigning partial charges using MMFF94 to SO2 containing
molecules has been resolved.

* The speed with which sequences are generated from a set of macromolecular structures
has been significantly improved.

* A problem whereby colors were lost when opening certain legacy .psv files
has been corrected.

* The Prepare Ligands protocol has been enhanced to add hydrogens to positively charged
atoms in the ionization step.

* A restriction that limited the length of protein sequences that could be aligned with
the Basic Sequence Alignment tool has been removed.

* Compounds with names containing underscore characters are now processed correctly by the 3D QSAR
Pharmacophore generation protocol.

##### Known Issues

* GOLD pr_xml parameter files created in previous version of Discovery Studio may not work correctly in
version 2.5.5.

* The typing of some systems, notably terminal residues of proteins, has now been improved for all molecules. Some
structures typed before DS 2.5.5 should be re-typed to get these improvements. Protocols that re-type (e.g., Calculate Binding Energy)
will give different results. Note that this only affects a small portion of proteins as most of the terminal residues were typed
correctly before.

#### Further information

Previous releases of Discovery Studio
