# Discovery Studio 3.0

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes300.htm

## Discovery Studio 3.0

This topic details the newest functionality, enhancements, and critical bug fixes available for
version 3.0.

### Contents

* Overview

* New features for version 3.0

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio protocols

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio component collections

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio standalone applications

* Enhancements to the Discovery Studio Client

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio scripting

* Database Updates

* Platform support

* Licensing changes

* Installer changes

Discovery Studio 3.0 provides major new features and enhancements in all areas
of the product.
Key new capabilities provided in this version include:

* Redesigned and simplified user interface

* Significant improvements to the quality and performance of 3D structure visualization

* Many performance improvements in both the client and protocols

* Enhanced sequence editing capabilities including a protein chain viewing mode

* Improved integration with Pipeline Pilot and support for Pipeline Pilot 8.0

* Many new tool panels providing new functionality and improved access to existing functionality

* Antibody and protein design tools

* Support for GOLD 5.0, CHARMm 35b3, and Modeler 9v8

* Automated tools for fast generation of pharmacophores from known structures

* Access to the Tools Explorer, which provides advanced functionality such
as forcefield typing, pharmacophore editing, and side-chain rotamer searching

* Functionality for building small molecules, and protein and nucleic acid structures

* The ability to create 2D interaction plots of receptor-ligand interactions

* The ability to create charts from numerical and structural data

Customized pharmacophore features and user Forcefield libraries are not migrated automatically. For instructions on how to migrate these files, see the installation guide .

A major goal of this release has been to improve accessibility to functionality through the Discovery Studio Client interface. Features that were previously only available in the protocols
explorer can now be launched directly through the tools explorer and used to analyze data interactively.
Functionality has also been arranged into a smaller set of functional categories and organized to
better match the workflows in which they are most commonly used. To complement these changes in the
design of the graphical user interface, significant performance improvements have also been made
in a number of areas.

This release greatly extends the functionality available in the Discovery Studio . In
addition, the user interface has been significantly redesigned to provide easy access to analysis
functionality. To complement these changes in the design of the graphical user interface, significant
performance improvements have also been made in a number of areas.

For more information about the changes made prior to 3.0,
see Previous releases of Discovery Studio .

Redesigned User Interface: The Discovery Studio Client user interface has been redesigned to improve
usability. Most functionality is now accessible through an expanded set of
tool panels, which are organized into tool sets
that make it easier to locate related features.

Improved 3D Structure Visualization: The Molecule Window has been enhanced to significantly improve the quality and performance
of 3D structures displayed in the Graphics View. New features include ambient and
direct shadowing effects, customized backgrounds, and depth of field viewing. The
application has also been upgraded to take advantage of graphics hardware features
when available.

Storyboards: You can now create storyboards of structures in the
Graphics view of the Molecule Window that are saved in the .dsv file and can be easily
be shared with other users.

Antibody Design: These new features support antibody design and include protocols
for predicting the antibody structures, the mutation effect on folding stability and binding affinity, 
and improved antibody sequence editing with the sequence analysis tools.

Automated Pharmacophore Generation: New tools
have been added to facilitate automated generation of pharmacophore features for
bioactive conformations and for receptor-ligand complexes.

Native Windows 64-bit server: Native versions
of the Discovery Studio components and protocols have been provided for the
Windows 2008 64 bit server platform.

Improved Pipeline Pilot integration: Enhancements
have been made to the Discovery Studio component collections that simplify
integration of protocols into the DS client.

A number of general improvements have been made to the protocols including:

* Protocols are
now more easily accessed from tool panels. The most
commonly accessed protocols have been added to each
tool and the protocols explorer is now hidden by
default. You can add any protocols to your custom
tool panels.

* There are new Getting Started example
protocols available from the DS Dev Client or Pipeline Pilot Client to demonstrate how you can build your own
protocols for Discovery Studio .

* The protocol folders have been reorganized to match the organization of tool panels in the Discovery Studio Client. The following folders are now included in the Discovery Studio protocols
folder: Macromolecules Pharmacophores Receptor-Ligand Interactions Simulation Small Molecules X-ray

* Macromolecules

* Pharmacophores

* Receptor-Ligand Interactions

* Simulation

* Small Molecules

* X-ray

* The major categories listed above contain an additional set of folders that group the
protocols into functionally-related tasks. These folders also correspond to the new tool panels
included in the DS Client.

* Protocol reports have been redesigned to make it easier to view the output from protocols in DS.

* General performance has been improved by eliminating the need to generate temporary protocols when jobs are launched in the Discovery Studio client.

* The performance of the DS Molecule Reader was significantly improved.

* Many protocols have been modified to reduce the number of parameters exposed at the top
level in the protocols explorer. Where appropriate, only the most important parameters are retained
at the top level. The remaining parameters are now located under the advanced group.

The following sections detail protocols that have been added or significantly modified in this
release.

* The Align
Structures protocol has been enhanced
to retain the pairwise alignment wherever possible so that the multiple structure alignment does not reduce to
the common core residues when structures are aligned progressively according to the guiding tree.

* The Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) protocol has been modified to improve the details included in the interactive
progress reports.

* A new protocol, NCBI Entrez Sequence Search , provides the ability
to search the NCBI protein and nucleotide databases by keyword and download the sequences directly
to the Discovery Studio client. This protocol can be launched from the Query Online Databases tools .

* The Build
Homology Models protocol now supports parallel processing. The protocol has also been enhanced to
allow copying of part of the input model structure while modeling other parts.

* The model representation from different protein modeling protocols has been standardized
so that the output models are stored as molecules in a single output file. The following
protocols have been updated: Build Homology Models Model Antibody Loops Loop Refinement Loop Refinement (MODELER) Build Mutants Refine Docked Proteins (RDOCK)

* Build Homology Models

* Model Antibody Loops

* Loop Refinement

* Loop Refinement (MODELER)

* Build Mutants

* Refine Docked Proteins (RDOCK)

* A new protocol, Model Antibody Framework , builds
a homology model for an antibody framework structure by superimposing templates for the light and heavy
chains onto a template structure that determines the relative spatial orientation of the two chains. This protocol can be launched from the Model Antibody tools .

* The Align Sequence Profiles protocol was renamed to Align Sequence Profiles (MODELER) .

* A new protocol, Model Full Length Antibody , builds
a full length homology model for Immunoglobulin G based on templates for IgG1 and IgG2. This protocol can be launched from the Model Antibody tools .

* The Model Antibody Loops protocol now
includes a Loops to Model parameter to choose which loop type to model.
It also has more loop definition types, including Kabat, Chothia, Honegger, and IMGT.
Additionally, the protocol can now filter results by organism.

* A new example protocol, Update Antibody Databases, updates the antibody database from previous releases. It takes existing full and non-redundant antibody
variable domain sequences as input and searches the latest PDB BLAST database using NCBI BLAST server
to identify the new antibody sequences. It can also take user local PDB files and automatically identify
the antibody variable domain and CDR loop regions and adds those into the existing database.

* A new protocol, Calculate
Mutation Energy (Binding) , calculates the effect of single-point mutation on the binding affinity
of protein complexes. It supports coarse grain parallel processing.
This protocol can be launched from the Design Protein tools

* A new protocol, Calculate
Mutation Energy (Stability) , calculates the effect of single-point mutation on protein stability. It supports
coarse grain parallel processing and can be launched from the Design
Protein tools .

* A new protocol,
Predict Stabilizing Mutations,
predicts the most stabilizing two sites or three sites mutations in a protein structure among the list of mutations specified.
This protocol can be launched from the Design Protein tools .

* The Align Multiple Sequences protocol has been split into two new protocols. The Align Sequences protocol performs an alignment of a set of unaligned
sequences.
The previous version of the protocol was deprecated to Align Multiple Sequences (Deprecated).
The Align Sequence
Profiles (Align123) protocol performs an alignment of two sequence profiles or a set of sequences to a
sequence profile.

* The Align Sequences protocol has 
a new option to align protein sequences by chains.

* Output from BLAST searches has been enhanced to include organism information for hits.

* A new protocol, Annotate Antibody
Sequence ,
identifies and annotates domains and hypervariable loop regions in the amino acid
sequence of an antibody. This protocol can be launched from the Model
Antibody tools .

* Two new example protocols, Download BLAST DB Files and Update BLAST Databases, have been added. The protocols
create DS BLAST databases with the latest publicly available sequences and structures.

* A new protocol, Auto Pharmacophore
Generation , enumerates a set
of candidate pharmacophore models from a set of automatically predicted features, and then uses a
Genetic Function Approximation model to choose the most selective model. This protocol can be launched from
the Create Pharmacophore Automatically tools .

* A new protocol, Receptor-Ligand
Pharmacophore Generation , generates pharmacophore models based on receptor-ligand structures. This protocol can be launched from the Create Pharmacophore Automatically tools .

* A new protocol, Browse 3D Database ,
browses a ligand database.
This protocol can be launched from the Search, Screen and Profile tools .

* More detailed progress reporting has been added to the Pharmacophore searching protocols.

* The Dock Ligands
(GOLD) protocol has been updated to support the latest version of CCDC GOLD 5.0 .
The protocol provides access to new features in GOLD including the ability to dock to protein ensembles and improved handling of water molecules in the docking.

* The visibility of GOLD toggled water atoms is correctly set when reviewing docking results in the Molecule Window.

* The Ligand Minimization protocol was renamed to In Situ Ligand Minimization .
This protocol can be launched
from the Minimize Ligands tools .

* The Analyze Ligand Poses protocol was modified; the ROC curve and RMSD calculations were moved into separate protocols for easier access.

* The molecular dynamics protocols have been modified to provide more detailed progress
updates. Percentage completion values are now reported, and progress can be seen in the Molecule Window during production dynamics.

* Restart files are now written periodically during molecular dynamics runs, allowing a manual restart process for failed jobs.

* Support for CHARMm format constraints has been added, if you prefer to use them over graphically defined restraints.

* The minimization protocol now supports minimizing only selected atoms of a molecule if a
selection is made before launching the protocol.

* A new "BestFit" option for harmonic restraints has been added (accessible via the data table). This allows you to run partial or complete rigid body simulations.

* It is no longer necessary to type a molecule before
running a simulation. The molecule will be typed with
the current forcefield when simulations jobs are launched.

* It is no longer necessary to remove alternate
conformations before running a simulation. Alternate
conformations are removed when jobs are launched.

* New example protocols have been added which run NAMD simulations. This requires a separate installation of NAMD. If you are planning to use this protocol, download the NAMD package from the following website: http://www.ks.uiuc.edu . Unzip the contents of the file, and set the Advanced | NAMD Directory parameter to point to the location of the package.

If you are planning to use this protocol, download the NAMD package from the following website: http://www.ks.uiuc.edu . Unzip the contents of the file, and set the Advanced | NAMD Directory parameter to point to the location of the package.

* Many improvements to the handling of very large trajectories have been added.

* A new protocol, Calculate Molecular Properties , was created and the previous version was deprecated. The new version has been simplified and the advanced functionality was moved into separate protocols (that is, Correlation and Statistics and Basic Arithmetic ). QM atomic
charges (ESP, Coulson, Mulliken, Hirshfeld and Fukui) can now be calculated using VAMP and DMol 3 . 
This protocol can be launched from the Calculate Molecular Properties tools .

* A new protocol, Correlation and
Statistics , provides the ability to perform correlation analysis and compute basic statistics for
properties. This protocol can be launched from the Calculate
Molecular Properties tools .

* A new protocol, Basic Arithmetic , enables the derivation
of new properties from existing properties using basic mathematical operations. This protocol can be launched
from the Calculate Molecular Properties tools .

* A new protocol, Calculate ROC Curve , was added to easily assess high throughput screening performance.
This protocol can be launched from the Calculate
Molecular Properties tools .

* Performance improvements have been made to the Generate Conformations protocol. In particular, the RMSD filtering step has been accelerated.

* The following protocols were deprecated:
Create Back Propagation Neural Network Model to Create Back Propagation Neural Network Model (Deprecated).

* A new protocol, Generate Novel Ligands , uses the
BREED method [Pierce et al., 2004] to generate new ligands from a set of overlaid ligands. This protocol can be launched from the Design and Analyze Libraries tools .

* A new protocol, Calculate RMSD , allows for quick root-mean-square deviations calculations. This protocol can be launched
from the Calculate Molecular Properties tools .

* The Prepare Ligands , protocol was updated and
the Lipinski filter was moved into a new protocol Filter by Lipinski and Veber Rules .
This protocol can be launched from the Prepare or Filter Ligands tools .

* A new protocol, Filter by Lipinski and Veber Rules , selects drug-like ligands according to rules formulated by Lipinski (Rule of Five) and Veber.
This protocol can be launched from the Prepare or Filter Ligands tools .

* Performance improvements have been made to improve the process of parameter set up in the Screen Library protocol.

* The Generate RECAP Fragments has been updated and
moved to Library Design folder.

* The Create Partial Least Squares Model protocol has been updated and cross-validation was added. The number of components can be set automatically 
based on the cross-validation results to build the model with optimal predictability.

* The Create 3D QSAR Model protocol now includes cross-validation.
The protocol has also been enhanced to improve performance.

* The Create Bayesian Model protocol now includes
cross-validation.

* A new protocol, Prepare Ligands for QSAR ,
prepares a set of ligands for a QSAR analysis by performing the various steps such as add hydrogens and Kekulize.
This protocol can be launched from the Create QSAR Model tools .

* A new protocol, Generate Training and Test Data ,
provides methods for splitting a data set into a training set and a test set. The training set can be used to build a QSAR model and the test set can be used to assess the performance of the model.
This protocol can be launched from the Create QSAR Model tools .

* A new protocol, Prepare Dependent Property ,
was added to scale the data and/or convert a continuous property to a discrete property as required by some QSAR models.
This protocol can be launched from the Create QSAR Model tools .

#### General

Many components have been redesigned to improve performance. In some cases enhanced components
are as much as an order of magnitude faster.

For more details, see the Discovery Studio Collection Release Notes in the Pipeline Pilot Help Center. To access the help center, see Accessing Pipeline Pilot help .

* CHARMm c35b3 Upgrade : CHARMm has been upgraded to version c35b3.

* MODELER 9v8 Upgrade : MODELER has been upgraded to version 9v8.

#### General Usability Enhancements

* The Tools Explorer has several enhancements:

The Tools Explorer has been included in the Discovery Studio Client. The
tool panels exposed in the Explorer provide access to a set of specialized features such as small- and macro-molecular
builders, forcefield typing tools, and pharmacophore editors. The design of the Tools Explorer has been modified to arrange tool panels into
sets. Different sets can be accessed through a new toolbar. A scripting interface to this capability
is also provided. A single mouse click on a tool panel title bar opens it. Other open tool panels are automatically closed to provide
an optimal view. Multiple tool panels can be opened by right-clicking the tool panel and selecting Expand. The appearance of tool panels has been enhanced to improve readability. Group headers are now shown
with a solid, colored background. Additional text is displayed in tool panels on a lighter colored background. Tool panels in the different tool sets are arranged by functionality instead of alphabetically. The ability to
include separators between different tool groups has also been added to help differentiate different sets. Most protocols can now be accessed through buttons in the tool panels. Set up of jobs
has been simplified, and on completion the results of analyses are automatically displayed in the client. Tool panels can contain links to related tools. When clicked, the links invoke the corresponding tool.
Links are a useful way of providing quick access to functionality that is not critical to a workflow, but which
is occasionally needed.

* The design of the Tools Explorer has been modified to arrange tool panels into
sets. Different sets can be accessed through a new toolbar. A scripting interface to this capability
is also provided.

* A single mouse click on a tool panel title bar opens it. Other open tool panels are automatically closed to provide
an optimal view. Multiple tool panels can be opened by right-clicking the tool panel and selecting Expand.

* The appearance of tool panels has been enhanced to improve readability. Group headers are now shown
with a solid, colored background. Additional text is displayed in tool panels on a lighter colored background.

* Tool panels in the different tool sets are arranged by functionality instead of alphabetically. The ability to
include separators between different tool groups has also been added to help differentiate different sets.

* Most protocols can now be accessed through buttons in the tool panels. Set up of jobs
has been simplified, and on completion the results of analyses are automatically displayed in the client.

* Tool panels can contain links to related tools. When clicked, the links invoke the corresponding tool.
Links are a useful way of providing quick access to functionality that is not critical to a workflow, but which
is occasionally needed.

* A new menu, Tools , has been added to provide quick
access to individual tool panels.

* The ability to apply different window layouts to the application workspace has been added. Different
layouts can be selected using the Window | Arrange windows submenu.

* Window tabs have been redesigned to replace the label with an icon to identify the window.
The close button on the window tab is now always visible regardless of whether it is in focus.

* A resource monitor has been added to the status bar to report the current load of the Pipeline Pilot server. The status bar has also been enhanced to include
the version of the Discovery Studio server.

* The Open URL dialog has been enhanced
to make it easier to switch between searching different data
sources. New data sources can be added using the URL Location subpage of the Files Explorer Preferences dialog.

* The Import tab of the Molecule Window | Display Styles
subpage - Preferences dialog has been enhanced to allow the specification of custom ligand protein display
styles.

#### Molecule Window

* The graphics code in the Molecule Window has been rewritten to take better advantage of dedicated
graphics hardware. Significant improvements in performance and quality are now obtained when using the
application with supported graphics cards. In particular, the application is significantly more responsive when
displaying structures in ball and stick and CPK display styles, but improvements have been made to all display styles.

* Ambient lighting, direct lighting, and depth blur can be applied to structures in the Graphics view. To set these values, use
the Lighting tab of the
Display Style dialog or Lighting subpage - Preferences dialog .

* Atom Outline effects can be applied to structures in the Graphics view. Atom Outlines can be used in conjunction with certain
display styles to generate a cartoon-like representation of a structure. To set the value, use the Lighting tab of the Display Style dialog or Lighting subpage - Preferences dialog .

* The performance of creating surfaces has been improved. In particular the speed with which
open surfaces can be created for large structures is significantly faster.

* Custom images can be set as the background for structures in the Graphics view.
To set the value, use the Graphics tab of the
Display Style dialog or Graphics subpage - Preferences
dialog . Example background images are included in the Samples folder.

* The responsiveness of the Molecule Window has been improved when rotating one
molecule relative to another.

* The ability to create storyboards of the Graphics view in the Molecule Window has been added. You
can create storyboards by pressing INSERT to capture particular scenes when visualizing structures
in the Graphics View. You can quickly view the scenes in a storyboard by choosing View | Storyboard | Storyboard
to open a dialog with clickable thumbnails. The scenes are saved with the file and can be shared with
colleagues. For details,
see Create and view storyboards .

* The DSV file format has been updated. DS 3.0 can read all earlier versions of the file, but files created
in DS 3.0 cannot be opened in earlier versions of Discovery Studio (MSV files can be used to share
molecules with these versions). The new DSV format
adds the ability to load and save much longer molecular dynamics trajectories and significantly larger molecules.

* Structure-sequence linking is supported for nucleic acids.

* Dimming of pharmacophore features has been enhanced for customized features.

* Separate default display styles for proteins, nucleic acids, and ligands
are now supported. To set the import preferences, use the Molecule Window |
Display Styles page of the Display Style dialog.

* File opening performance has been improved.

* Undo performance has been improved.

* A progress bar now tracks trajectory loading and the Molecule Window is updated in real time.

* An enhancement has been made to the Display Style toolbar button that provides quick access to a
set of customizable display styles. Clicking on the drop-down button in the new control reveals
a set of preview images that enable simple selection of the available styles. The different
display styles can be defined in the Display Styles page Molecule Window preferences.

* A status message is displayed when downloading PDB structures to indicate progress, and a progress bar is shown when opening the file for large structures.

* Dragging PDB and other molecule files into the Molecule Window results in structures being displayed
by default. A preference has been included in the Molecule Window |
Import page of the Preferences dialog to set the maximum number of structures that display
when multiple structures are opened. This prevents the inadvertent opening of large numbers of structures that might take considerable time
to display.

* The Spin functionality for animating
structures in the Molecule Window has been extended to add Rock and Wiggle functions. The Spin function
has also been enhanced so that the spin direction and speed can be determined by dragging and releasing
the mouse in the desired trajectory.

#### 2D Window

* You can adjust atom and residue coordinates by selecting and dragging the corresponding
objects.

* The graphics performance of the 2D ligand interaction plot has been improved.

* The colors have been softened to improve readability of the labels.

#### Sequence Window

* You can now control the secondary structure visibility for individual sequences.

* Insertions, deletions, and mutations made to sequences with linked structures automatically update
the structure. To facilitate this, only one-to-one linking is supported.

* Renumbering of residues is now permitted for sequences that do not have a link to a structure.

* Residues now have residue IDs and insertion codes that can be persisted to .bsml files.

* The ability to persist the identity of nonstandard amino acid and nucleotide residues to bsml files has been added. The rules used to enable structure-sequence linking
include checks for nonstandard residues.

* Sequences can be searched by name and regular expression.

* Sequence annotation and alignment information can be preserved in DSV files.

* A chain view has been added to the Sequence Window. This viewing option breaks protein chains (or domains) into
multiple views in the window. Individual chains can be moved from one view to another to facilitate alignment and
analysis of homologous chains between sequences.

* The Select... dialog has been updated to allow selection of residues in the Sequence Window by Feature type and
by Organism.

* New Sequence | Alignment menu commands are available to calculate and report the pairwise sequence identity and similarity matrix for a sequence alignment. For details, see Sequence | Alignment .

#### Tool Panels

A major change in the Discovery Studio client is the consolidation of all analysis functionality into tool panels.
Functionality available only through the Protocols Explorer in previous versions has been updated so that
it can be accessed more conveniently through the tool panels alongside other related features. As part of the
consolidation, a number of tool panels have been added and many others enhanced. The following sections detail
the major changes in the different high level functional categories:

* A new tool panel, Align Sequences and Structures , provides access to the functionality previously
contained in the Align Multiple Sequences protocol on the Analyze Sequences menu. The two new tools,
Align Sequences and Align Sequence Profiles, allow you to interactively align sets of sequences and
profiles in the client.
Access is also provided to the Align Structures tool. This command performs a structural alignment on
two or more protein structures and outputs a sequence alignment.

* On Build and Edit Nucleic Acid tool panel,
additional tools have been provided for modifying the sugars on individual nucleotide and to
to define nonstandard nucleic acids.

* New Perl APIs to the Build Nucleic Acid tools have been provided.

* Several tools for refining structures have been moved to the Minimize and
Refine Protein tool panel.

* On Build and Edit Proteins tool panel, 
a new tool, Create Structure from Sequence, enables the creation of a basic structure from a
sequence in a Sequence Window.

* The Create Homology Models guide has been renamed and
redesigned to improve accessibility.

* A new tool panel, Design Protein , allows you to predict model structures for a
mutated protein from the original structure,
or to calculate the energy effect of mutation for protein stability and protein binding affinity. It
also calculates the pH dependent energy to predict the optimal solution pH for a protein.

* A new tool panel, Dock and Analyze Protein Complexes , replaces the Analyze
Docked Protein tool panel. New tools have been provided
that make it easier to browse a set of docked protein poses.
The visibility of the full structure of a docked pose can be locked while browsing to other poses.

* A new tool panel, Minimize and Refine Protein , allows you to optimize part or all of a protein structure using CHARMm.

* A new tool panel, Model Antibody , contains tools for
annotating antibody sequences and for creating homology models for antibodies and refining CDR loops.

* A new tool panel, Prepare Protein , allows you
to perform various tasks typically required before analyzing a
protein structure. The panel includes tools for manually manipulating protein structures,
protonating proteins, as well as a tool for automatically preparing a protein. A new tool is added to
easily graft a loop from a template structure to a model interactively.

* A new tool panel, Query Online Databases , allows you to search and retrieve
structures and sequences from online databases such as RCSB and NCBI.

* A new tool panel, Search Sequences by Similarity , allows you to search either local or online sequence databases using BLAST
methods. For local searches, the PDB_nr95 and the PDB_Antibody sequence databases are available
by default.

* A new tool panel, Fragment Based Design , contains tools
for analyzing receptor binding sites using various fragment based
methods.

* A new tool panel, Analyze Complexes replaces the previous
Analyze Binding Site tools. It allows easy browsing of the ligands and definition of the receptor.
The tools can be applied to an experimental protein ligand complex or a docked ligand to a receptor. Additionally, a new entry in the Hierarchy, Ligands Groups, is created when importing PDB files.

* A new tool panel, Analyze Docking Results, contains a set of tools that are useful for visualizing and analyzing the results of protein-ligand docking
studies.

* The tools in the Analyze Poses group (Analyze Ligand Poses and Calculate Binding Energies) have been moved
to the Analyze Docking Results and Dock Ligands tool panels.

* The Define and Edit Binding Site tool panel has been redesigned to
improve usability.

* A new tool panel, Build Ligand and Pharmacophore Database, allows you to build ligand and pharmacophore databases.

* A new tool panel, Compare Pharmacophores , contains tools for comparing two pharmacophores
or for clustering a set of pharmacophores.

* A new tool panel, Create Pharmacophore Automatically , contains tools for automatically
building pharmacophore
models from a ligand, receptor, or receptor-ligand complex.

* A new tool panel, Create Pharmacophore Manually , contains tools for manually
creating a pharmacophore
model from a template molecule.

* A new tool panel, Search, Screen and Profile , allows you to map ligands to pharmacophores using various methods, search a ligand database with a pharmacophore, and browse a ligand database.

* The Create Features from SMARTS tool has been added to the Customize
Pharmacophore Features tool panel.

* A new tool panel, Run Simulations , allows you to run molecular simulations on structures loaded in the
Molecule Window.

* A new tool panel, Setup Constraints , allows you to put constraints on atoms in structures before
running CHARMm simulations.

* A new tool panel, Change Forcefield , contains tools for preparing structures
for a simulation and running molecular simulations. In previous versions, this functionality was accessed through the Simulate
Structures tool panel.

* Tools previously provided in the Assign Electrostatic Parameters have been moved to a new tool panel,
Calculate Electrostatics.

* The tools in the Apply Templates group have been reorganized to improve usability. The different templates
are now organized into a drop-down list. Once a template has been selected, it can be applied using the Apply
Parameters tool.

* A tool to calculate Solvation Energy has been added.

* The speed of forcefield typing has been improved significantly.

* A new tool panel, Calculate Molecular Properties , contains tools that can be used calculate and analyze
molecular properties of small molecules.

* A new tool panel, Create QSAR Model , provides a workflow for preparing the training
set and the test set, preparing
the dependent property, and building various QSAR models. The resulting QSAR models can be shared among colleagues.

* A new tool panel, Design and Analyze Libraries , contains tools for performing
various tasks required to analyze or design a library, such as
clustering molecules, computing diversity metrics, or generating ligands from enumeration.

* A new tool panel, Minimize Ligands , provides quick access
to different methods for minimizing ligand molecules.

* A new tool panel, Prepare or Filter Ligands , contains tools for preparing ligands
for other techniques (for example, docking).

* A new tool panel, Select Subset Libraries , allows you to create subsets of large libraries using various methods.

#### Protocol Launcher

* A test button has been added to the Change Server dialog that enables a server to be validated before connecting.

* We recommend that you use the Tools Explorer to launch protocols instead of the
Protocols Explorer. The Protocols Explorer is no longer displayed
by default when the application is started. However, the Protocols Explorer can still
be opened from the View | Explorers menu, and protocols can still be opened and run.

* A new scripting module, NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript, has been added. This provides the ability to build and edit nucleic
acids using scripting.

* The MessageBox function now allows you to
specify whether the dialog should include a "Do not display this message again".
If the user checks this option, the dialog is listed in the General | Disabled page of the Preferences dialog.

The following databases have been updated:

* BLAST databases

* MODELER profile databases

* Antibody Loop database

#### Platforms added

This release adds platform support for:

* Microsoft Windows 7.0

* Red Hat Enterprise 5.0 Update 3 (5.3)

* Windows 2008 Server running in 64-bit mode for Pipeline Pilot and the Discovery Studio servers and components.

#### Platforms removed

In this release of Discovery Studio , support has been discontinued for the following platforms:

* Red Hat Enterprise Linux 3.0

* Red Hat Enterprise Linux 4.1 Update 3

* SUSE Linux Enterprise 10 Retail. Only SP1 and higher are supported.

* Windows 2000

#### Pipeline Pilot compatibility

Discovery Studio 3.0 is compatible with the following versions of Pipeline Pilot:

* Pipeline Pilot 8.0

By default, DS 3.0 is installed with Pipeline Pilot 8.0.500, which includes Collection Update
2 (CU2).

This version of Discovery Studio comes with the latest version of BIOVIA License Pack version 7.6.5. If an existing version of License Pack is
detected during installation, it will be updated.

The installers for DS have been simplified. You can now install
both the DS client and server simply by running the Pipeline Pilot
installer with a valid license. We are also providing a smaller
client-only installer for faster download and deployment. Also, you
can download and install the client from a link on the Pipeline
Pilot server web page.
Note that the Pipeline Pilot installer for Linux is now a command-line
tool and does not require a graphical display.

# Discovery Studio 3.1

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes310.htm

## Discovery Studio 3.1

This topic details the newest functionality, enhancements, and critical bug fixes available for
version 3.1.

### Contents

* Overview

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio protocols

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio component collections

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio standalone applications

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio Client

* Enhancements to the DS ActiveX Control

* Enhancements to scripting

* Database Updates

* Critical bug fixes

* Platform support

* Installer changes

* Known issues

Discovery Studio 3.1 is primarily intended to provide compatibility with version 8.5 of
Pipeline Pilot. It also provides new features and enhancements in many areas including:

* A new version of the DS ActiveX control

* New storyboard features including the ability to export movies

* A set of tools for predicting and modeling protein aggregation propensity
to assist in protein formulation. Note that Aggregation propensity functionality is currently licensed separately and it is not part of maintenance updates.

* A new protocol, HT-XPIPE, for performing high throughput placement and refinement of
protein ligand complexes from X-ray reflection data

* Enhancements to several of the Pharmacophore and Macromolecule protocols

For more information about the changes made prior to 3.1,
see Previous releases of Discovery Studio .

### Enhancements to the Discovery Studio protocols

Stability and performance of protocols running on clusters of grids has been enhanced in Pipeline Pilot 8.5. In addition, a number of specific changes have been made to the Discovery Studio protocols and components:

#### Macromolecules

* A new protocol, Calculate Protein Aggregation Scores ,
has been added. This protocol calculates the aggregation propensity of protein residues and predicts surface patches
that are prone to aggregate. Note that Aggregation propensity functionality is currently licensed separately and it is not part of maintenance updates.

* Build
Homology Models has been enhanced so that residue IDs used to define
disulfide bridges and cis-prolines are consistent with custom residue numbers in the
Sequence Window.

* Model Full Length Antibody has been updated to include the 1hzh structure as an available template.

* Annotate Antibody
Sequence in the Annotate Antibody Sequence protocol has been modified to correctly match the CDR2 definition with the IMGT definition.

* The mutation energy protocols have been updated to correct a problem whereby elements could be
lost for non-standard residues. Input residue numbers, insertion codes, and chain ids on the input molecule
are now correctly saved in all situations.

#### Pharmacophores

* The pharmacophore generation protocols have been
enhanced to automatically validate the pharmacophores using a test set. Results are graphically
represented in the final report. In addition, several protocols have been enhanced to use large databases
as input without using excessive disk space.

* Auto Pharmacophore
Generation has been modified to allow multiple solutions to be reported in the results.

* Screen Library has been enhanced to explore a larger set of potential solutions before returning results.

* Common Feature Pharmacophore Generation has been modified to correctly handle unknown stereocenters for
structures regardless if they are visible in the Molecule Window when the protocol is
launched.

#### Simulations

* A problem has been resolved in the Electrostatic Potential calculations that could cause proteins
with insertion codes to be treated incorrectly.

#### Small Molecules

* Create 3D QSAR Model now limits the number of descriptors selected after de-correlation
to 1,000. This significantly reduces run times in some situations.

#### X-ray

* A new protocol, HT-XPIPE , has been added. This protocol automatically
places and refines protein-ligand complexes in high throughput mode. For each system, a reflection file, a
model structure, and a set of ligands is used as input.

#### General

In general, a number of components have been updated to improve performance.

* A new component, Calculate Aggregation Propensity, is added which calculates the aggregation propensity of protein residues. Note that Aggregation propensity functionality is currently licensed separately and it is not part of maintenance updates.

* The DS Sequence Viewer component has been improved to correctly retain information about sequence
feature formatting. This component is used in the Annotate Antibody Sequence protocol.

* Most components in the Discovery Studio component collections have now been unlocked, making
it possible to open and inspect their contents in the Pipeline Pilot client.

* Components that support parallel execution have been modified to take advantage of the new
Local Temp Directory global variable introduced with Pipeline Pilot 8.5. When configured appropriately,
this variable specifies a location in local storage (as opposed to an NFS mount) to which temporary
files are written. Reducing the amount of activity on shared NFS mounts can provide significant
performance improvements when analyzing large data sets.

* A new protocol, Parallel Testing, has been added to the Utilities folder in the Examples
protocols. This protocol is designed to assist in validating that a server is correctly
configured for running parallelized jobs.

* The ZRank executable is modified so that it can take protein docking poses generated by 3rd party programs as input. This change does not directly affect any components that use ZRank executable in this release. However, the change allows you to create a new component to integrate ZRank with 3rd party docking programs.

### Enhancements to standalone applications

* Updated CHARMm version: CHARMm has been upgraded to version 35b5. It has
also been ported to run natively on all 64 bit platforms supported by Discovery Studio .

#### Molecule Window

* A set of new options has been added when saving from Discovery Studio Client. Structures can now be
embedded within a DS ActiveX Control in a PowerPoint presentation or
html file (.ppt, .xml, .html, .htm).

* A number of new features and enhancements have been added to the storyboards . The following
options are now available from the storyboard dialog: The storyboards can be played like a movie, with options for setting transition
and pause time. You can export storyboard movies as WebM files for
use in presentations and web pages. For details about working with these types of files, see Export and use storyboard movies .

* The storyboards can be played like a movie, with options for setting transition
and pause time.

* You can export storyboard movies as WebM files for
use in presentations and web pages. For details about working with these types of files, see Export and use storyboard movies .

* The amount of memory used when displaying large proteins in ribbon display style mode
has been reduced.

* The amount of memory used when displaying binding site points has been reduced.

* The ability to export conformations to a DCD file has been provided.
This enables the analysis of such sets of conformations with analysis protocols such as Trajectory Principal Component Analysis .

* The default type for surfaces in the Create
Surface dialog has been changed from Closed to Open.

* A new property, Motion, has been added to the Angle Monitor . This makes it
possible to control which end of the angle moves and which stays fixed when the angle is changed.

* Theta and Lambda angles are now reported for Pi Interaction Monitors in the Data Table.

* A new property, Sticky, has been added to 2D text annotations.
This makes their coordinates a property of the screen, rather than
the model, so they are not affected by zoom or translate operations.

#### 2D Window

* The default layout and display style of ligand interaction diagrams has been improved.

#### Sequence Window

* A new command, Residue Composition , has been added to the Sequence Window. This reports the residue
composition at a particular site in a protein or nucleotide alignment.

* Printing from the Sequence Window has been improved and automatically wraps sequences to ensure
all residues in an alignment are captured.

* A new option, Block residue deletion from keyboard , has been added to the Sequence
Window preferences . This is turned off by default, but can be enabled
to avoid accidental deletion of residues during editing of alignments.

#### Tool Panels

In general, modifications to tool panels have been restricted in this release. The main changes
are in the Macromolecules tool set.

* A new set of tools has been added to the Design Protein tool panel. These tools enable you to easily set up and review the results of protein aggregation propensity
analyses. Note that Aggregation propensity functionality is currently licensed separately and it is not part of maintenance updates.

#### Protocol Launcher

* You can now switch between the protocol dialog, which is launched from a tool
panel, and the protocol Parameter Explorer. This allows you to make changes in the Molecule Window
before running the protocol in the foreground or background as desired.

The ActiveX control has been significantly enhanced in version 3.1. The following content provides an overview
of the new features but for details of all enhancements, see the release notes in the DS ActiveX Control help.

* You can now create an ActiveX enabled web page or Powerpoint
presentation directly from Discovery Studio using File | Save . The
data is embedded, so you do not need to keep separate files along
with your presentation.

* The API has been updated and includes new methods and properties that include access
to storyboard functionality and a property for saving a dsv file with the object.

* Storyboards are now supported. Storyboards can now be played like a movie, with settings
for pause and transition. You also have the option to export the movie as a WebM file.

* Spin is now supported.

* You can now synchronize multiple views within a slide or web page.

* New monitors (e.g., Pi monitors) introduced in Discovery Studio Client since the last version
of the control are now included.

* Simplified display style settings have been added.

To make use of the new functionality and
API of the new activeX control, you should re-create your presentations and applications. Existing
users of ActiveX 2.0.2 can install 3.1 side by side to continue using the
old control.

### Enhancements to Discovery Studio scripting

* A new function, UpdateSequence, has been added to the SdmDiscoveryScript package. The method
allows you to update information in one sequence (e.g., features, annotations) with information
from another.

* The command AnnotateWindow now uses the new Sticky property to
improve handling of labels when changing the zoom level.

The following databases have been updated:

* BLAST databases

* MODELER profile databases

* Antibody Loop database

* Distance values for Distance Monitors and other labels in the Molecule Window now
print correctly.

* Non-standard charges are now applied correctly to modified nucleotide
residues.

* Analyze Trajectory can now be run without specifying a particular property. This
is useful if you want to use it to reduce the number of frames in a trajectory file
(using the parameters in the Trajectory File group).

* The Open URL dialog no longer automatically removes the .gz extension from a URL string.

* CSV files containing SMILES strings now open correctly, a new
preference for handling embedded line break sequences (\n) has been added.

* Columns in the Data Table View can be hidden correctly in output
generated by Build
Homology Models .

* Hyperlinks in the Align
Structures report now link to the correct result files.

* A problem in the Build
Homology Models protocol that caused it to fail in some situations when
being run in parallel mode has been corrected.

* Surfaces stored in DSV files open faster.

* Images are saved correctly from the Molecule Window when depth cue is turned on.

* Generate Electron
Density Map handles protein structures with alternate conformations correctly.

* Models returned by Build
Homology Models are now sorted according to their PDF values.

This release adds platform support for:

* SUSE Linux Enterprise 11 Retail running in 64-bit mode.

#### Pipeline Pilot compatibility

Discovery Studio 3.1 is compatible with the following versions of Pipeline Pilot:

* Pipeline Pilot 8.5

By default, DS 3.1 is installed with Pipeline Pilot 8.5.0.

The DS ActiveX control is provided in a separate installer.

* Some instability has been observed when running Discovery Studio Client on Linux platforms
with version 8.83.5.3 of the ATI graphics driver installed. Replacing the driver with the
previous version of the driver resolves this problem.

* Security-Enhanced Linux (SELinux) must be disabled before installation of the Pipeline
Pilot server.

# Discovery Studio 3.5.1

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes351.htm

## Discovery Studio 3.5.1

This topic details the newest functionalities, enhancements, and important bug fixes available for Discovery Studio 3.5.0 and 3.5.1.

### Contents

* Changes for Discovery Studio Client 3.5.1

* Overview of Discovery Studio Client 3.5

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio Client

* Updates to third-party software

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio component collections

* Database Updates

* Critical bug fixes

* Known issues

#### Enhancements

* Pipeline Pilot 9.0 is now supported. Note that the server was previously known as the Pipeline Pilot server.

* The Grow Scaffold protocol esterification reaction file was corrected to create esters instead of ethers.

* The Catalyst Configuration File parameter of the Common Feature Pharmacophore Generation 
protocol is now correctly used when aligning the ligands to the generated pharmacophores.

* The Common Feature Pharmacophore Generation protocol has a new parameter, Input Ligands Preprocessing, which removes ligand fragments and clear ligand chirality.

#### Grid setup

* For grid and cluster operation there is a new administration portal setting, Internal Server Name, which is the name of the server as seen from inside the cluster. This name can be specified as an IP address as well. You can use this setting to take advantage of high speed back end networks for communication between nodes in a cluster.

* When setting up the server for load balanced or grid operations the registry setting for StatusUpdateInterval is now set automatically. For load balanced operation the default is 200ms, for grid operation the default is 1 sec. If you want to manually adjust these settings, edit the Registry.2.xml file.

#### Bug Fixes

* Resolved an issue that caused the client to take a long time to open when loading Jobs.xml files for a protocols that generate a large number of files.

* Fixed an issue where minimizing ligands with large number of poses containing rotatable atom properties 
could create failures on Windows.

* Fixed an issue where protein typing with nonstandard receptor residues would fail when minimizing ligand poses containing rotatable atom properties could.

* Fixed a defect in the Hierarchy View where the incorrect object hierarchy would be displayed when running the conformations to molecules script from the Structure Editing submenu of the Scripts menu.

* Fixed an issue where the molecule window import preferences resulted in replacing the partial charges stored in mol2 files with Gasteiger partial charges.

* Added theory documentation for the ADMET Developmental Toxicity Potential model.

* Fixed an issue with the Basic Arithmetic that caused the protocol to fail when using functionality that requires two properties.

* You now have the option to exclude curly brackets (i.e., "{" and "}") from Job folder names.

* Resolved an issue that occurred when using ambient shadow and translating clipping planes.

* Resolved an issue with the Dock Ligands (CDOCKER) and the In Situ Ligand Minimization protocols that caused the selected ligand partial charging algorithm to be applied to all ligands in the input receptor when specifying a ligand partial charging method other than Momany-Rone (i.e., CFF, MMFF).

* Resolved an issue that caused the application to crash when loading CIF files with unspecified angles.

* Resolved an issue that caused the application to freeze when deselecting everything in a model that contains an animation.

* Resolved an issue with the DS Molecule Reader protocol that caused the insertion code on the residue to be lost when passing through the Keep Properties component.

* Resolved an issue in the Prepare Protein protocol so that the bond order in ligands will be preserved when the protocol runs with the Build Loops option set to True.

* Fixed an issue in the Replace Fragment protocol where the shape matching algorithm did not return the best matching fragment conformation for one attachment library types.

#### Known Issue

If the Prepare Protein protocol is run on a protein that has non standard-residues not recognized by MODELER (e.g., MSE) with the Build Loops option set to True, the ligand bond order, as well as the chemistry of the nonstandard residues may not be preserved in the final output structure.

* New ligand profiling database, PharmaDB , for drug repurposing or to study selectivity and side effects.

* New in-situ fragment based lead optimization and core-hopping tools.

* New Study SAR Activity cliff analysis tools using matched molecular pairs.

* New Developability Index tool for ranking protein-protein aggregation propensity.

* New pH-dependent option for scanning mutagenesis tools for both protein-protein binding and protein stability .

* New surfaces tool for studying receptor-ligand interactions.

* Updated Annotate Antibody Sequence tool with new numbering schemes and improved alignments.

* Updated Model Antibody tools for homology modeling with more automated methods of identifying key regions.

* Latest updates to CHARMm 36b2 and Modeler 9v10.

* Updates to the interface to improve usability.

* New interactive Bar Chart tool and improved charts.

* Added limited support for embedded Intel graphics cards.

#### General

* A new, simpler look and feel to the application, with a customizable
color scheme, fewer default toolbars, and new context menu toolbars for fast
access to the commands you use the most.

* The welcome experience has been improved to reduce the number and complexity of dialogs that appear when the application is opened for the first time.

* Added graphical controls to quickly show and hide the graphics, hierarchy, and data table views of the molecule window.

* The Feature Search Box now appears in a more standard location and now provides results in a tabular format instead of displaying the hierarchy.

* You can now rename objects in the Hierarchy View.

* The performance and reliability of copy/paste for larger structures has been improved. As a result, you are no longer be able to perform a complete copy/paste from version 3.5 to versions earlier than 3.0. Instead, export as an MSV file and import into the older application.

* Surfaces are now drawn with higher resolution (smoothness) when using a graphics configuration with sufficient performance.

* Depth cue has been improved to support more display styles and now fades completely at the rear clipping plane. Anti-alias now renders with smoother lines. Anti-aliasing is now disabled if hardware acceleration is not enabled.

* A legend is now available for the 2D Window generated by the Show 2D Diagram tool (in Analyze Complexes tools) that describes the color coding of the different types of residues interacting with the ligand.

* You can now choose from several styles for the interface in the General page - Preferences dialog .

* In the Jobs Explorer , completed jobs now feature a tree view with links to the protocol report and output files.

* To open the directory where the files reside in the Files Explorer, use the right click, Locate command (double clicking on the Job row will no longer function in this manner).

* The report title of the Window displaying the report been changed from Report to the name of the protocol (i.e., Ligand Preparation). This will make it easier to navigate through multiple reports.

#### Charts

* You now have the option to plot only selected rows for 3D, point, line, and bar charts.

* Interactive bar charts are now available.

* Bar Charts, Line Plots, and Point Plots now allow you to differentiate values by coloring by a data series.

#### Sequence Window

* The context menu options are now distinct based on context within the window (the options now differ when the mouse is over the ruler, sequence name, or residue views). Added new context menu options to control ruler display, and BLAST Search and Align Sequences options.

* The ruler display now remains at the top of the Sequence Window view, which ensures that the ruler is always visible when scrolling. Additionally, the ruler now uses less space.

* Added new display style options to show residue IDs in the Sequence Window ruler. These options set the residue IDs on the ruler to be either residue IDs of the first sequence or consensus residue IDs from an alignment.

* Added capabilities to add insertion codes to residue number for a selected range of residues and shift residue numbers up and down by a specified value. Improved the user interface to make the commands clear and consistent. Added scripting API to renumber a range of residues by giving the specific residue identifier for each residue.

* Added capability to report the residue type frequencies for each of the selected alignment positions in a table.

* Added capability to show the chain ID in the Sequence Window chain view.

* Added a new menu option, Sequence | Alignment | Align Residue Identifiers that aligns sequences in the Sequence Window by the residue identifiers (including insertion codes).

* Added a sequence alignment color scheme to color residues that match residues in the first sequence.

* Added a sequence window color scheme to color residues by column frequency.

* Chain breaks are now easier to see in the Sequence Window. Additionally, the chain break tooltip now includes a chain icon.

* Double-clicking on a hit in the Blast Window (Table View) now opens a Sequence Annotation window.

* The Sequence Window Display Style dialog and preference pages have been simplified. The dialog now contains a General tab, a single consolidated Color Scheme tab, and a Consensus tab. The display style preferences can be set and reset directly from the dialog.

* You can now insert sequences by choosing File | Insert From... | URL from the menu bar .

* You can sort sequences by sequence name.

* You can insert sequences by copying a molecule from a Molecule Window and pasting in the Sequence Window.

* Customized display style settings are persisted in BSML files when saved.

* Added buttons to context menu to decorate residues. You can color residues and text background and format residues with overline, underline, and carets.

* Added buttons to the context menu to perform common tasks.

#### Macromolecules

Aggregation propensity functionality is currently licensed separately and it is not part of maintenance updates.

* Some tool panels have been renamed: Analyze and Edit Transmembrane Proteins is now Analyze Transmembrane Proteins . Place and Refine X-ray Ligand is now Place X-ray Ligand Structures .

* Analyze and Edit Transmembrane Proteins is now Analyze Transmembrane Proteins .

* Place and Refine X-ray Ligand is now Place X-ray Ligand Structures .

* Added a new option to the menu bar, Scripting | Structure Editing | Copy Sequence Alignment Indices , that copies the residue position index in a sequence alignment to the linked protein molecule as amino acid property or to the linked nucleic acid molecule as residue property. This index can be useful in creating a line plot of residue properties for multiple proteins or multiple nucleic acids with aligned X-axis values.

* Added a new option, L/D Conversion , to the Build and Edit Protein tools that interconverts L and D amino acids.

* The Renumber Sequences tool in the Prepare Protein tools is enhanced so that the residue IDs of the selected sequences can be set according to
one of the new ruler labels, which are defined using display styles.

* The Superimpose Proteins tool panel has been reorganized for usability and improved workflow.

* Removed the Advanced parameter Delete Protein-Metal Bonds from the Prepare Protein protocol. The protein-metal bonds are always deleted.

* The parameter, Selected Residues, has been removed from the Verify Protein (Profiles-3D) protocol to simplify the interface.

* A new parameter, Input Protein Structures, has been added, which allows selection of protein structures from a molecule window or by browsing files. This new parameter is available in several existing protocols (e.g., Align Structures, the new Calculate Developability Indices protocol, etc.)

* The BLAST Search (DS Server) protocol has been renamed BLAST Search.

* The database used by the Blast Search protocol, PDB_Antibody, has been updated with 1294 non-redundant antibody PDB sequences.

* Added a new protocol, Analyze Protein Interface to the Dock and Analyze Protein Complexes tool panel. This protocol determines the interface between the ligand and the remaining complex, and then calculates the hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, and Pi bonds at the interface.

* The Calculate Mutation Energy (Binding) protocol now allows you to calculate pH-dependent mutation energy.

* Calculate Mutation Energy (Binding) and Calculate Mutation Energy (Stability) now automatically create a mutation energy bar chart.

* The Calculate Aggregation Scores protocol has been enhanced to calculate an average score for input proteins that have multiple conformations.

* Added a new protocol Calculate Developability Indices , to the Design Protein tool panel. This method can be used to rank the developability of a set of homologous proteins based on their likelihood to aggregate. The developability index is an important indicator whether a protein will be stable in concentrated solution and will be a good candidate for downstream development.

* The aggregation score calculated by the Calculate Aggregation Scores protocol is now calculated as the sum of the atomic scores to make it consistent with the score required for the Calculate Developability Indices protocol. Previously, the molecular aggregation score was calculated as the sum of the residue scores, which in turn are calculated as the average atomic scores.

* When viewing aggregation sites, the coloring of the atoms and surface is now based on per atom scores rather than the residue scores.

* The Annotate Antibody Sequence protocol has been enhanced: Added capability to number the residues according to one of the four numbering schemes: IMGT, Chothia, Kabat, and Honegger. Enhanced the user interface to accept multiple sequences as input and optionally align the input sequences according to the selected numbering scheme. As a result, the alignment of the variable domains, especially the CDR regions is improved. It is possible to annotate either germline sequences or mature sequences and align them accordingly. Changed the display style of the annotated sequences so that the CDR regions of the light chain and heavy chain are colored differently and domains are annotated by carets of different colors. Corrected inconsistencies in the CDR domain boundaries compared to the literature. For the Chothia heavy chain variable domain, the CDR 3 region was shortened by one residue at both N- and C-terminal of the loop. For the Chothia heavy chain variable domain, the numbering for CDR 3 region was changed to include insertion codes 100Y and 100Z to improve the alignment when aligning by residue id. The default for the Annotation Scheme is changed to IMGT. The advanced parameter, CDR Annotation Method , has been removed. The HMM method is now used exclusively.

* Added capability to number the residues according to one of the four numbering schemes: IMGT, Chothia, Kabat, and Honegger.

* Enhanced the user interface to accept multiple sequences as input and optionally align the input sequences according to the selected numbering scheme. As a result, the alignment of the variable domains, especially the CDR regions is improved. It is possible to annotate either germline sequences or mature sequences and align them accordingly.

* Changed the display style of the annotated sequences so that the CDR regions of the light chain and heavy chain are colored differently and domains are annotated by carets of different colors.

* Corrected inconsistencies in the CDR domain boundaries compared to the literature. For the Chothia heavy chain variable domain, the CDR 3 region was shortened by one residue at both N- and C-terminal of the loop. For the Chothia heavy chain variable domain, the numbering for CDR 3 region was changed to include insertion codes 100Y and 100Z to improve the alignment when aligning by residue id.

* The default for the Annotation Scheme is changed to IMGT.

* The advanced parameter, CDR Annotation Method , has been removed. The HMM method is now used exclusively.

* Added a new protocol, Identify Framework Templates to the Model Antibody tools . This protocol generates an alignment of the VH, CH1, VL, and CL domains of the input sequence and the corresponding domains in databases of pre-aligned antibody variable (VH, VL) and constant (CH1, CL) domains.

* The Model Antibody Loops protocol has been enhanced: Added capability to filter templates by canonical structure type. If filtering is enabled and a CDR loop region in the input structure is of a recognized canonical loop type, the protocol only considers templates of the same canonical loop type when ranking templates. Otherwise, all loops are considered. Enhanced the report to include information about canonical structure types of the CDR loop regions in the input structure. The antibody databases used by this protocol have been updated and the content and format have been modified to accommodate the enhancements to the protocols. The database consists of 2265 non-redundant antibody domains, including 1676 variable domains and 589 constant domains (light chain and CH1). Antibody databases from previous version are not compatible with Discovery Studio 3.5.

* A new protocol, Calculate Energy (DFT) , has been added to the Run Simulations tools . It calculates the energy or optimizes the geometry of a set of small molecules using the density functional quantum mechanics method in DMol3.

* The report now includes a link, Detailed Analysis Report, that opens a graphical cost analysis and a graphical summary of the other key parameters from the log file.

* Added a parameter, Inactive Spread , to automatically identify inactive molecules. Molecules with activity values greater than this value from the most active molecule are considered inactive.

* The Pharmacophore Comparison protocol has been enhanced with tethers. It is possible to specific force pharmacophore features from each pharmacophore to match during the mapping using these tethers.

* The Screen Library protocol has a new parameter, Advanced | Map Each Conformation Separately , that allows you to map each conformation of a ligand separately. This can be useful when processing docked poses or in a similar situation where all conformations need to be considered separately.

* A new parameter, PharmaDB , has been added to the Ligand Profiler protocol to access the pharmacophore database. The PharmaDB is the largest ever reported collection of structure-based pharmacophores (139,482 entries) derived from 7,687 protein-ligand x-ray structures. The database was built in collaboration with Didier Rognan of the University of Strasbourg. See http://bioinfo-pharma.u-strasbg.fr/scPDB . An example subset is provided with the default installation. The full PharmaDB must be installed separately.
