* CAESAR has been enhanced to allow contiguous atom regions to remain rigid. The remaining section of the molecule, including rings, is sampled to create the conformations.

* The Calculate RMSD protocol has been enhanced: The RMSD calculation is now up to five times faster. The algorithm has been improved to find more groups with hydrogen resonance (e.g., carboxylic acids, phosphates, sulfates, etc.) to ensure that the lowest RMSD value is calculated. A new parameter, Calculate Pairwise Atom Distance, has been added, which allows you to add a new property containing the pairwise atom distances used in the RMSD calculation.

* The RMSD calculation is now up to five times faster.

* The algorithm has been improved to find more groups with hydrogen resonance (e.g., carboxylic acids, phosphates, sulfates, etc.) to ensure that the lowest RMSD value is calculated.

* A new parameter, Calculate Pairwise Atom Distance, has been added, which allows you to add a new property containing the pairwise atom distances used in the RMSD calculation.

* There is a new Small Molecules tool panel, Study SAR , that provides access to two new protocols: Find Activity Cliffs using MMPs and Analyze Activity Effects using MMPs . These protocols perform Matched Molecular Pairs (MMPs) transformations to find ligand activity cliffs and to explore changes and identify trends of fragment substitutions on ligand activity.

* A new protocol, Split Ligands into Multiple Files , allows you to create multiple smaller files from a large input SD file. Note that this protocol is only available from the Protocols Explorer .

* The Prepare Dependent Property protocol has a new option for the Scaling Type parameter to convert IC50 to pIC50 values.

#### Scripting

* The SdmDiscoveryScript's UpdateSequence method will now update the residue identifiers (including insertion codes) in addition to other sequence properties and attributes. Additionally, this method now pushes the residue identifiers to linked molecules when the script is run inside Discovery Studio .

* CHARMm is upgraded to version 36b2.

* Modeler is updated to 9v10.

* Discovery Studio 3.5 supports Pipeline Pilot 8.5 CU3.

#### New components and protocols

* Mutation Energy (Binding): A new component and protocol calculates the free energy of mutation for protein-protein binding.

* Mutation Energy (Stability): A new component and protocol calculates the effect of single-point mutations on protein stability.

* Calculate Developability Index: A new component and protocol calculates the developability index of a protein structure.

* Identify Antibody Templates: A new component and protocol identifies template proteins for modeling the antibody Fv or Fab framework regions based on the overall framework sequence similarity between the query and the templates.

* Analyze Protein Interface: Determines the interface between the ligand and the remaining complex, and then calculates the hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, and Pi bonds at the interface.

* Grow Scaffold: This new protocol grows a ligand scaffold in a receptor binding site

* Replace Fragment: This new protocol replaces parts of a ligand to generate novel structures.

* Generate Fragment Libraries: This new example protocol creates fragment libraries for the Replace Fragment protocol.

* Analyze Activity Effects using MMPs: This new protocol performs Matched Molecular Pairs (MMPs) transformations to explore changes in ligand activities.

* Find Activity Cliffs using MMPs: This new protocol performs Matched Molecular Pairs (MMPs) transformations to find ligand activity cliffs.

* Split Ligands into Multiple Files: This new protocol creates several smaller files from an input SD file.

* Create Free-Wilson Least Squares Model: This new example protocol builds a Free-Wilson least squares (linear regression) model to analyze the structure-activity relationship in a series of substituted compounds.

* Transpose Array Properties: This new example protocol transposes ligand array properties into individual properties.

#### Enhancements to existing components

* DS Alignment Reader: A new option, Keep Features , allows for reading of sequence features and annotations from bsml alignment files.

* RMSD Calculator: A new option, Calculate Pairwise Atom Distance , allows you to add a new property containing the pairwise atom distance used in the RMSD calculation.

* Pose Analysis: A new option, Hydrogen Bonds Distance Criterion , allows you to adjust the hydrogen bond distance.

#### Deprecated components

* Identify Antibody Loops: The new component uses Hidden Markov Models to find antibody loops. It is faster and more consistent with the methodology used in the other components in the Antibody Area than the previous version that is based on a BLAST search. That version of the component has been deprecated.

* Find Antibody Domains (Deprecated): The new component was created to work with a sequence data record used by the latest version of the Annotate Antibody Sequence protocol, which can now handle multiple sequences.

* Superimpose Proteins by Alignment: The new component with the same name always passes the superimposed protein molecules through the output port, and no longer passes the alignment object. The new component is applied to several existing protocols (e.g., Align Structures, Align and Superimpose Proteins, etc.)

* The PharmaDB is the largest ever reported collection of structure-based pharmacophores (139,482 entries) derived from 7,687 protein-ligand x-ray structures. The database was built in collaboration with Didier Rognan of the University of Strasbourg. See http://bioinfo-pharma.u-strasbg.fr/scPDB . An example subset is provided with the default installation. The full PharmaDB must be installed separately.

* A new ligand diverse, drug-like Catalyst database has been added and is available in several Pharmacophore protocols via the Input Database parameter. This database was used to build the GFA model that ranked the pharmacophores to use for the PharmaDB database. In addition, it is the database that is used in the Receptor-Ligand Pharmacophore Generation protocol when using the Database option of the Advanced | Selectivity Scoring parameter. The database consists of 3000 drug-like compounds randomly selected from the BioinfoDB database (http://bioinfo-pharma.u-strasbg.fr/bioinfo) and 2390 selected from the CAP database. The following drug-like criteria are used: Molecular weight is 150-550 0-15 rotatable bonds 0-10 HBAs 0-5 HBDs There are fewer than three charged atoms Polar surface area less than 150 Å²

The database consists of 3000 drug-like compounds randomly selected from the BioinfoDB database (http://bioinfo-pharma.u-strasbg.fr/bioinfo) and 2390 selected from the CAP database. The following drug-like criteria are used:

* Molecular weight is 150-550

* 0-15 rotatable bonds

* 0-10 HBAs

* 0-5 HBDs

* There are fewer than three charged atoms

* Polar surface area less than 150 Å²

* A new ligand Catalyst database (scPDB) has been added and is available in several Pharmacophore protocols. The database contains 5465 ligands, which are all of the unique ligands found in the scPDB database. See http://bioinfo-pharma.u-strasbg.fr/scPDB .

* The BLAST databases have been updated to include new additions to the public sequence databases. The number of sequences in the databases are as follows: PDB_nr95: 30,193 sequences PDB: 135,056 sequences Swiss-Prot: 534,695 sequences UniRef90: 10,181,634 sequences nrdb: 17,378,729 sequences

* PDB_nr95: 30,193 sequences

* PDB: 135,056 sequences

* Swiss-Prot: 534,695 sequences

* UniRef90: 10,181,634 sequences

* nrdb: 17,378,729 sequences

* Certain nonstandard PDB files can now be opened. (DSC-14759)

* Fixed a stability issue when viewing the attributes of invisible molecules. (DSC-13025)

* Resolved memory issues that occurred when applying a transformation matrix to a large number of chains. (DSC-7999)

* Fixed an issue where some ligands were interpreted as amino acids when importing PDB files from the RCSB database. (DSC-14625)

* Fixed a stability issue while renaming a sequence when there multiple molecule windows open. (DSC-13853)

* Fixed several issue in chain view related to deleting, shifting chains, and undo. (DSC-13773)

* Fixed an issue with opening a file from a URL when using a proxy server setting. (DSC-13349)

* Reduced memory usage when loading more than six structures on a 32 bit machine. (DSC-11954)

* The Update TOPKAT Model protocol has been enhanced to handle models with undefined global variables. (DSC-14333)

* Fixed an issue with the Enumerate from Ligands protocol that caused output to appear flat when the core contained more than one chiral center. (DSC-12471)

* Fixed an issue where the Protein Aggregation protocol would unexpectedly fail for certain proteins. (DSC-12515)

* Fixed an issue that caused incorrect residue numbering for models generated by the Model Antibody Framework protocol. (DSC-15845)

* Input ligands that contain poses that differ only in chirality (i.e., enantiomers) are now handled correctly. In the previous release, only one of the enatiomers was used for flexible docking. (DSC-15227)

* Improved the stability of the Build Fragment Library Component when the library destination was a mounted network location. (DSC-15059)

* The Define Site from Receptor Cavities tool now generates sites regardless if the crystal cell is removed. (DSC-14620)

* Fixed default behavior of the Site Detection component to output DSV files. (DSC-12290)

* Job completion dialogs for multiple jobs no longer appear outside the screen. (DSC-12283)

* Improved error reporting when attempting to run a minimization with a protein membrane and a set of fixed atoms using the GBIM solvent model. (DSC-12880)

* Fixed an issue that prevented minimization of small molecules with restraints. (DSC-12709)

* Fixed an issue in the X-ray Refinement protocol where the CNX log file was not returned after an error. (DSC-13158)

* Note for Internet Explorer 9 users: IE9 is not currently supported and there are known issues. Customers have reported that using IE9 in compatibility mode mitigates most of those issues.

* There is a known issue with the Input Reflection Data parameter that is used in the X-ray protocols. This issue prevents running from an existing protocol.pr_xml file directly if the Input Reflection Data is specified from a Reflection Data Window. The workaround is to click on the Input Reflection Data parameter and select the correct reflection data again.

* Changes have been made to a number of parameters and protocols in this release. Some old protocol settings files (pr_xml) may not be fully compatible with the new version. Typically you only need to reset the Input Protein Structures parameter.

* Side-by-side installation is not supported on Windows for Pipeline Pilot users who own the Java Server Collection. If you have installed a side by side installation of the Java Server Collection, see Troubleshooting - Installation .

# Discovery Studio 4.0

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes400.htm

## Discovery Studio 4.0

This topic details the new features, enhancements, and important bug fixes available for Discovery Studio 4.0.

### Contents

* Overview of Discovery Studio Client 4.0

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio Client

* Updates to third-party software

* Enhancements to Discovery Studio component collections

* Database Updates

* Fixed issues

* Known issues

* Powerful New Interactions Tool: Rapidly detect a host of new key non-bonded interactions and analyze important favorable and unfavorable interactions in a simple one-click interface and tool
panel that is easy to use for new and expert users alike.

* Faster Production Dynamics: A new protocol that runs the high-performance simulation program NAMD is now part of the Discovery Studio installation, adding faster, more scalable, production dynamics with zero configuration. See Dynamics (NAMD) .

* Valuable New Protein Design Tools: Predict and create disulfide bridges : Identify compatible residue pairs that are suitable for creating new stabilizing bridges. Calculate mutation energy : New features for improving protein stability and calculating mutation energy for multiple simultaneous mutations. See Protein Design Tools .

* Predict and create disulfide bridges : Identify compatible residue pairs that are suitable for creating new stabilizing bridges.

* Added a set of tools to the Design Protein tools panel to predict sites that can form disulfide bridges by mutating pairs of residues to cysteine.

# Discovery Studio 4.1

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes410.htm

## Discovery Studio 4.1

This topic details the new features, enhancements, and important bug fixes available for Discovery Studio 4.1.

### General

* Discovery Studio 4.1 supports Pipeline Pilot 9.2.

* License Pack has been upgraded to 7.6.10.

* A browser-based help system has been added, providing faster searching and better indexing along with the ability to bookmark and print more easily.

* The elapsed time for jobs is now consistently reported as the time it takes for the protocol to run on the server, and excludes time to launch, idle time, or time to collect the results.

### Client

* There is now a 64-bit version of the Windows client.

* A new red/cyan (anaglyph) stereo option has been added and the stereo preferences have been re-worked.

* Custom clipping planes can now be enabled or disabled. Their position and whether they are enabled are now saved in each storyboard scene.

* The torsion rotation tool has been enhanced for easier selection and rotation of bonds, particularly in Fischer projection orientation.

* You can now save an image (PNG) with a transparent background.

### Macromolecules

* Predict Sequence Properties: This new protocol calculates biophysical properties, such as isoelectric points, molecular charge, molar extinction coefficient, etc., for protein sequences and identifies sequence motifs (e.g., for possible post-translational modification sites). See Predict Sequence Properties .

* BLAST Search and PSI-BLAST Search: These protocols have been upgraded to use the blast+ program.

* Identify Framework Templates: The Identify Framework Templates protocol has a new advanced parameter, Template Ranking, that specifies whether template hits are ranked by sequence similarity or by sequence identity.

* Calculate Aggregation Scores: The protein chains in the line plot of the per residue aggregation score are now colored differently for easy visualization.

### Simulation

* The simulation protocols have enhanced memory usage. They can now handle systems with hundreds of thousands of atoms with moderate memory use.

* The CHARMm Simulation protocols now use the latest published values for Nina radii.

* Standard Dynamics Cascade , Dynamics (Production) , and Dynamics (Equilibration) : The incompatible VVER option in the Dynamics Integrator parameter is no longer available when the equilibration or production stage is set to run with constant pressure.

* Process Trajectory Files: Simplified the Process Trajectory Files protocol interface. Also, trajectory files from incomplete/stopped dynamics simulations are now processed correctly. The Process Trajectory Files protocol has been redesigned to improve performance. In addition, it is more robust in handling mixed-endianness and incomplete trajectories. You can now process the dcd files from interrupted dynamics runs.

* Simplified the Process Trajectory Files protocol interface. Also, trajectory files from incomplete/stopped dynamics simulations are now processed correctly.

* The Process Trajectory Files protocol has been redesigned to improve performance. In addition, it is more robust in handling mixed-endianness and incomplete trajectories.

* You can now process the dcd files from interrupted dynamics runs.

* Dynamics (NAMD): Constraints created by the Setup Constraints tool panel can now be used in the Dynamics (NAMD) protocol the same as the other simulation protocols.

* Analyze Trajectory: The report now has a heat map for non-bonded interactions that were selected for analysis. Also, to reduce memory usage when opening the molecule, non-bonded interaction results are no longer reported in the Data Table and are saved in separate csv files.

* Standard Dynamics Cascade: Changed the default minimization method in the second minimization stage from Conjugate Gradient to Adopted Basis NR to improve the stability of the run.

### Receptor-Ligand Interactions

* Dock Ligands (GOLD): The Docking Templates parameter has been updated. The parameter contains a list of all docking templates in the GOLD/templates directory. You can add/remove templates from this directory, or modify existing templates as desired. Note that the template settings will override your protocol settings.

* Analyze Ligand Poses: The statistical report page now includes information on simultaneous residue interactions.

* Replace Fragment: An energy filter was added to improve the quality and geometry of the linked fragments. The Generate Fragment Conformations parameter now allows you to include fragments with two and three attachment points.

* An energy filter was added to improve the quality and geometry of the linked fragments.

* The Generate Fragment Conformations parameter now allows you to include fragments with two and three attachment points.

* Score Ligand Poses: The Score Ligand Poses protocol now has the option to calculate CDOCKER energy scores.

* Dock Ligands (Pharmacophore Restraints and CHARMm): Added clustering to ensure the docked poses are more diverse.

### Small Molecules

* Filter By SMARTs: Improved the reporting of the Filter By SMARTs protocol. The report now includes compounds that failed and shows the highlighted substructure of the failed filters and additional details.

* Filter by Lipinski and Veber Rules: The FailReason property created by the Filter by Lipinski and Veber Rules protocol was improved to better indicate the failure.

* Find Activity Cliffs using MMPs: This protocol has a new parameter, Partner Activity Cutoff. At least one of the molecular pairs must have an activity value equal to or below this threshhold.

### Component Collection

* Antibody Domains: The Antibody Domains component now allows you to annotate the canonical loop type.

# Discovery Studio 4.5

Source type: HTML

Source section: dsvisualizer

Source file: dsvisualizer/releasenotes450.htm

## Discovery Studio 4.5

This topic details the new features, enhancements, and important bug fixes available for Discovery Studio 4.5.

* The system requirements changed in Discovery Studio 4.5.

### General

* Discovery Studio 4.5 includes the first prototype release of its next generation Web Viewer. It is based on WebGL technology available in modern web browsers, which requires no plugins to download or security warnings to click through, with rendering performance comparable to the Discovery Studio client. A number of Pipeline Pilot example protocols are included with this release, showcasing the new Web Viewer capabilities, including 3D/2D interactivity with the updated 2D Ligand Interaction Diagram component.

* The 2D Ligand Interaction Diagram now includes support for Discovery Studio’s extended library of non-bond interaction types. The performance, reliability, and layout have been improved and a number of new display options, including an improved legend, have been added. You can now export the diagram in SVG format and new automated methods are available via scripting so that you can run create a diagram using a Pipeline Pilot component.

### Macromolecules

* A new protocol, Antibody Modeling Cascade, enables you to easily and automatically generate 3D model structures for one or more antibody Fab or Fv regions, starting from a set of antibody light and heavy chain sequences.

* The Predict Protein Ionization and Residue pK protocol includes new capabilities: generate a fully protonated structure with mean atomic charges (qi(pH)) at given pH, calculate the dipole moment as a function of pH, and calculate the electrostatic contribution of transfer energy, ΔΔGSolv, between solvated and solid states. Those properties have been shown to correlate with protein solubility and viscosity.

* The Annotate Antibody Sequence protocol now includes the ability to add the Chothia Canonical Loop Type and the ability to identify Antibody Germline Sequences.

### Simulation

* A new protocol, Assign ForceField Types (Prototype), provides a new way to assign atom types for charmm36, charmm27, and charmm22 forcefields, based on substructure matches instead of the traditional template name matching approach. It includes the ability to import and assign custom atom types and parameters. The new method improves typing for many chemical functional groups supported by the charmm36 forcefield, including carbohydrates, lipids, and ligands, etc.(e.g., retinol.) It also correctly types modified amino acid residues such as glycosylated Asn.

### Pipeline Pilot and Third Party Enhancements

* Discovery Studio 4.5 is compatible with Pipeline Pilot 9.5.

* BLAST databases are updated for PDB_nr95, PDB, UniRef90, Swiss-Prot, and NR.

* ANTIBODY is updated to include the latest antibody template structures from the PDB.

* MODELER is updated to the latest academic version 9v14.

* CHARMm is updated to the latest academic release 39b1.

## Previous releases

For details about the current version, see What's New in Discovery Studio 2026 .

| Release | Highlights |
| --- | --- |
| 2025 | Discovery Studio MOL2 format files can now store multi-character chain names. A new protocol, Predict Antibody Paratopes , predicts the antigen binding site residues in antibody CDR loops. The Prepare Germline Sources protocol now uses the ClustalW2 engine to align sequences. The RCSB Structure Search protocol now reads mmCIF format files by default, which allows all hits to be read. PharmaDB is updated based on scPDB release 2024 (http://bioinfo-pharma.u-strasbg.fr/scPDB), and now contains over 41,000 entries. The Solvate with Explicit Membrane protocol is updated to include improved constraints during equilibration, which results in better equilibrated and solvated systems. Dock Ligands (GOLD) protocol now supports CCDC GOLD version 2024.1. |
| 2024 | The Discovery Studio client EBI AlphaFold DB default site definitions in the Open URL dialog now retrieves version v4 rather than v1. You can now color the backbone of nucleic acid chains by residue in the Discovery Studio client Graphics View. The PharmaDB Profiler protocol now reports mapping details for every unique function. Also, it is now possible to filter using pdb_id or scpdb_id using the PharmaDB Filter protocol. Perl is updated to version 5.36.3. For information, see https://www.perl.org/ . |
| 2023 | The trajectory animations in the Discovery Studio Client are enhanced with the inclusion of frame numbers. Also, you can change the current frame by moving a slider. Two new protocols, PharmaDB Filter and PharmaDB Profiler are available from the Pharmacophore Search, Screen, and Profile tool panel. The Predict Humanizing Mutations protocol includes a new published machine learning (ML) method that can distinguish between human and murine sequences. A new protocol, GaMD Equilibration , allows you to configure a Gaussian accelerated Molecular Dynamics simulation and automatically parametrize boost potentials. A new protocol, GaMD Production , allows you to run and restart Gaussian accelerated Molecular Dynamics simulations. A new protocol, Estimate Free Energy Landscape , estimates a free energy landscape from a data set or a set of simulations, allowing for statistical reweighting of GaMD simulations. A new protocol, Measure Trajectory Features , measures time-series features (such as SASA, RMSD, Dihedrals) from molecular dynamics trajectories for further analysis. A new protocol, Cluster Conformations , discretizes conformational states from simulation trajectories. |
| 2022 | Protocols no longer require an active server when creating reports with sortable tables. Added a new visualization script, Color by AlphaFold Model Confidence, to color protein loaded from AlphaFold Protein Structure Database based on the per-residue confidence score. For more information, see Scripts \| Visualization . Enhanced the Interaction Pharmacophore Generation protocol. Added a new protocol, Predict Excipient Interactions , that predicts the preferential interaction of common excipients with antibody surface residues for antibody formulation. # About Pipeline Pilot

Source type: HTML

Source section: pipelinepilot

Source file: pipelinepilot/pipelinepilot.htm

## About Pipeline Pilot

Discovery Studio has been designed to not only provide complex computational
tasks in an easy-to-use environment, but also to make it easy to create new
tasks. The foundation for providing this functionality is Pipeline Pilot . This
powerful software platform is available as a stand alone product that can be used 
not only for creating and deploying tasks, but also for deploying scientific methods
to multiple users.

It is not essential to understand the details of Pipeline Pilot to be
able to use Discovery Studio effectively. However, having a basic understanding
of what Pipeline Pilot is, and how it is used to combine different scientific
capabilities will greatly increase your ability to customize and create scientific
tasks with the Discovery Studio environment.

### Pipeline Pilot Server

Discovery Studio is powered by Pipeline Pilot Server , a high-throughput data analysis
and data mining system for drug discovery informatics. Pipeline Pilot is built to perform 
complex series of operations on extremely large data sets in real time. The result is 
unprecedented flexibility in processing the growing volume of data being generated in 
modern automated laboratories. Pipeline Pilot can further enhance performance by taking 
advantage of parallel processing techniques and grid computing. See Installing Discovery Studio for further information.

### Pipeline Pilot Client and Pipeline Pilot Designer for Applications

Pipeline Pilot Client is a desktop application that provides access to Pipeline Pilot Server . The client is the only application that provides the ability to create new components and protocols. The client also provides the ability to run protocols. Pipeline Pilot Designer for Applications is provided with Discovery Studio ; it is similar to the full Pipeline Pilot Client , but with use restricted to the Discovery Studio entitlements.

See Customizing protocols to learn how to modify protocols using either version of the client.

### Discovery Studio and Pipeline Pilot integration

Discovery Studio and Pipeline Pilot use HTTP, the technology that powers the web, to transfer information between the client and the server. Pipeline Pilot takes requests submitted by the client and passes them to the server codes installed on the server machine, which then run
calculations. Pipeline Pilot also reports job status and results to Discovery Studio .

With Discovery Studio , you can launch calculations from your PC client to run on dedicated Windows or Linux servers. Jobs
can be run in disconnected mode so that they do not tie up the resources of your PC. You can log off your PC and the job will continue to run on the
server. When you log back on to your PC, you can view the status or the results of the calculation. These calculations can also be run locally on
the same PC running Windows or Linux.

You can set up Pipeline Pilot and Discovery Studio on a single machine or multiple Windows or Linux machines 
depending on your needs. See Installing Discovery Studio for details about configuring the software.

Licenses are made available when the software is purchased. If you need further assistance relating to licenses you should initially contact your account manager.

#### Further information

Accessing Pipeline Pilot help

# Catalyst

Source type: HTML

Source section: scientificapplications

Source file: scientificapplications/catalyst.htm

## Catalyst

Catalyst algorithms are used to support most of the pharmacophore
related tasks in Discovery Studio . These tasks include automatic 
creation of pharmacophores, creation of ligand conformations, 
creation of compact, indexed ligand databases that can be searched by 
pharmacophores, and many others. This functionality is available from Discovery Studio through protocols and components that run Catalyst executables.

In addition to accessing this functionality from Discovery Studio , you can run Catalyst executables from the command line. For more information on running the application from the command line, see Running Catalyst .

If you are installing a new version of Pipeline Pilot , you will need to copy Catalyst databases you have created in previous versions to a new location. For details, see Copying Catalyst Databases from a Previous Installation .

#### Further Information

Running Catalyst Using Catalyst

# catConf

Source type: HTML

Source section: scientificapplications

Source file: scientificapplications/catalyst_catconf.htm

## catConf

catConf is the Catalyst conformer generation tool. It takes input
files of compounds and outputs conformational models
(sets of conformers) for each input compound. One of the particular
strengths of catConf is its ability to efficiently give broad coverage of
conformational space [Smellie et al., 
1995b] , thus avoiding repetitious groups of conformers all representing 
local minima.

catConf supports fast- and
best-quality conformational analysis. Both methods generate conformers that provide broad coverage
of the accessible conformational space. Fast generation takes less time,
and best quality provides more complete coverage of conformational space.
The options are -fast and -best (default).

#### Further reading

* [Smellie et al., 1995a]

* [Smellie et al., 1995b]

* [Smellie et al., 1995c]

#### Further information

Using catConf Command Line catConf Options Generating Conformers for Molecules Catalyst Standalone Applications

# Generating Conformers for Molecules

Source type: HTML

Source section: scientificapplications

Source file: scientificapplications/catalyst_catconf_generating_conformers.htm

## Generating Conformers for Molecules

### Generating conformers for a single molecule

Usage:

```text
catConf <name> <SOURCE> <DIR> <OPTIONS> <num>
```

where:

* <name> is the name of file without the file type extension.

* <SOURCE> is the file type (-cpd, -mol, -smi, -mmod, -mol2).

* <DIR> is the directory where the input file is located.

* <OPTIONS> are any non-default options. See catConf Options for more details.

* <num> is the desired number of conformers.

#### Example

To create a maximum of 250 conformers using fast, for the input molecule ala-gly.cpd in the "inputs" directory, use the command in the directory above the directory "inputs":

```text
> catConf ala-gly -cpd inputs -fast 250
```

A file called ala-gly.cpd will be created in the working directory that contains the conformer model. Note that when the input and output file types are the same, the directory where catConf is executed must be different than the input directory.

### Generating conformers for molecules in a spreadsheet file

```text
catConf -spst <file.spst> <SOURCE> <OPTIONS> <num>
```

* <file.spst> is the file name for the spreadsheet file.

* <SOURCE>, <OPTIONS>, and <num> are as described Generating conformers for a single molecule

To generate conformer models for all molecules in the aceapp.spst spreadsheet, use the command:

```text
> catConf -spst aceapp.spst -cpd inputs 250
```

This assumes that input files for each molecule listed in the aceapp.spst spreadsheet is located in the directory "inputs" as a .cpd file.

### Generating conformers for molecules in a .sd file

```text
catConf -sd <file.sd> <OPTIONS> <num>
```

* <file.sd> is the name of the .sd file that contains one or more molecules. It can also contain one conformer or multiple conformers for each molecule.

### Generating conformers for molecules in a smiles file

```text
catConf -smiles <file.smi> <OPTIONS> <num>
```

* <file.smi> is the name of a SMILES file that contains one or more molecules.

### Generating conformers for molecules in a list file

```text
catConf -list <file> <SOURCE> <OPTIONS> <num>
```

* <file> is a text file containing the names (without the file type extension) of the input molecule files.

To generate conformers for input molecules (ala-gly.cpd, ala-his.cpd, ala-leu.cpd, ala-pro.cpd, and ala-val.cpd) located in the directory "inputs", use the command in the directory above the directory "inputs":

```text
> catConf -list input_names -cpd inputs 250
```

where input_names is a text file containing:

```text
ala-gly
ala-his
ala-leu
ala-pro
ala-val
```

and the directory "inputs" contains the following input files:

```text
ala-gly.cpd
ala-his.cpd
ala-leu.cpd
ala-pro.cpd
ala-val.cpd
```

New output files (ala-gly.cpd, ala-his.cpd, ala-leu.cpd, ala-pro.cpd, ala-val.cpd) that contain the conformer models will be created in the working directory. As previously mentioned, if the input and output types (e.g., cpd) are the same, then the working directory and the input directory must be different.

# catConf Options

Source type: HTML

Source section: scientificapplications

Source file: scientificapplications/catalyst_catconf_options.htm

## catConf Options

<OPTIONS> may be one or more of the following:

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| -fast | Use this option to use the fast conformer generation algorithm to compute the conformers. If the conformer generation type (-fast or -best) is not specified on the command line, the best conformer generation routine will be used by default. | off |
| -best | Use this option to use the best conformer generation algorithm to compute the conformers. If the conformer generation type (-fast or -best) is not specified on the command line, the best conformer generation routine will be used by default. | on |
| -as2D | Use this option if you want to export the molecules in a 2D representation only. This option can only be used when exporting .sd files. Only one conformer will be exported. Example: > catConf -list input_names -cpd inputs -as2D -out-type sd -outsd out.sd The <num> (number of conformers) parameter is not needed. The options -outtype and -outsd are described below. The -as2D option can also be used with the other input options of catConf (e.g., -spst, -sd, -smiles, etc.) | off |
| -rel | Using the -rel option treats any absolute stereocenter in the starting molecule as a relative stereocenter instead of an absolute one. If the starting molecule is A(R)-B(R)-C(S), then conformers of the stereochemical form A(R*)-B(R*)-C(S*) and A(S*)-B(S*)-C(R*) will be generated by catConf. These chiral centers will be labeled as relative in the output .cpd file. | off |
| -abs | Using the -abs option treats any relative stereocenter in the starting molecule as an absolute stereocenter instead of a relative one. If the starting molecule is A(R*)-B(R*)-C(S*), then only conformers of the stereochemical form A(R)-B(R)-C(S) are generated by catConf, and these chiral centers are labeled as absolute in the output .cpd file. | off |
| -keep | When using this option, any old unregistered conformers (if any) are considered by the conformer generation analysis and may be retained. All registered conformers will be retained. -keep is the default option if -keep or -scratch is not specified. | on |
| -scratch | When using this option, any old unregistered conformers are deleted before analysis. | off |
| -addH | Use this option to add hydrogens to an input set of molecules. The coordinates of the heavy atoms will be preserved. Example: > catConf -sd input.sd -addH -outsd out.sd The <num> (number of conformers) parameter is not needed. | off |
| -energy <e> kcal | Use this option to set the energy threshold to <e> kcal/mol. | 20 kcal/mol |
| -energy <e> kj | Use this option to set the energy threshold to <e> kjoules/mol. | 20 kcal |
| -outcpd <out.cpd> | Use this option to change the name of the cpd file written. By default, when the output type is cpd, a file named <name>.cpd will be created. Where <name> is the name of the input file (without the file type extension). When using the -outcpd <out.cpd> option, the cpd file name will be <out.cpd> instead. This option is only valid if a single-molecule is used as input. For example, the command: > catConf ala-gly -cpd inputs -outcpd ala-gly-confs.cpd 250 will import the file inputs/ala-gly.cpd, compute up to a maximum of 250 conformers using the best conformer generation routine, and then export the model to the file (e.g., -gly-confs.cpd) in the directory where catConf was run. | off (exports as <name>.cpd) |
| -outmol2 <out.mol2> | Similar to -outcpd, use this option to change the name of the .mol2 file written. This option will write to <out.mol2> instead of <name>.mol2. The assumptions are that the output type is .mol2 and a single molecule is used as input. | off (exports as <name>.mol2) |
| -outmmod <out.mmod> | This option will write to <out.mmod> instead of <name>.mmod. The assumptions are that the output file type is mmod and a single molecule is used as the input. | off (exports as <name>.mmod) |
| -outsd <out.sd> | This option will write to <out.sd> instead of <name>.sd. If specified, all the conformers of all the compounds will be written to <out.sd>. The output type must be .sd . Note that this option can support multiple molecules. For example, the command: > catConf -list file_names -cpd inputs -outtype sd -fast 250 will write a separate .sd file called <name>.sd for every input file listed in "file_names". But the command: > catConf -list file_names -cpd inputs -outtype sd -outsd outputs.sd -fast 250 will write all the conformers of all the molecules to a single file named outputs.sd. | off (exports as <name>.sd) |
| -outtype <type> | Use this option to indicate the format of file the output conformers should be written in. <type> can be cpd , mol2 , mmod , or sd . If this is not specified .the conformer models will be exported as cpd by default. | cpd |
| -log <file> | This option will create a log <file> that will report important information necessary to repeat the calculation. The log file will contain the version of the catConf executable used, the command line used, and any non-default parameters that were used. It will also report the total elapsed time in seconds. | off |
| -noUseFragments | This parameter will turn off the re-use of ring conformations. When this parameter is used, a new ring conformation is created whenever needed without regard to previous ring conformations. By default, catConf will keep ring conformations in memory during conformer generation and will reuse these rings for subsequent calculations. | off |
| -readFragments | If this option is used, catConf will read a fragment database file (fragments.data) at startup if available. By default, catConf will not read a fragments.data file. | off |
| -writeFragments | This option will print the estimated maximum number of conformers that would be created by FAST. | off |
| -estimateMaxConf | Print the estimated maximum number of conformers by FAST. | off |
| -writeFragments | Write a fragment database file at program completion. | off |

Use this option if you want to export the molecules in a 2D representation only. This option can only be used when exporting .sd files. Only one conformer will be exported. Example:

```text
> catConf -list input_names -cpd inputs -as2D -out-type sd -outsd out.sd
```

The <num> (number of conformers) parameter is not needed. The options -outtype and -outsd are described below. The -as2D option can also be used with the other input options of catConf (e.g., -spst, -sd, -smiles, etc.)

Use this option to add hydrogens to an input set of molecules. The coordinates of the heavy atoms will be preserved. Example:

```text
> catConf -sd input.sd -addH -outsd out.sd
```

The <num> (number of conformers) parameter is not needed.

Use this option to change the name of the cpd file written. By default, when the output type is cpd, a file named <name>.cpd will be created. Where <name> is the name of the input file (without the file type extension). When using the -outcpd <out.cpd> option, the cpd file name will be <out.cpd> instead. This option is only valid if a single-molecule is used as input. For example, the command:

```text
> catConf ala-gly -cpd inputs -outcpd ala-gly-confs.cpd 250
```

will import the file inputs/ala-gly.cpd, compute up to a maximum of 250 conformers using the best conformer generation routine, and then export the model to the file (e.g., -gly-confs.cpd) in the directory where catConf was run.

This option will write to <out.sd> instead of <name>.sd. If specified, all the conformers of all the compounds will be written to <out.sd>. The output type must be .sd . Note that this option can support multiple molecules. For example, the command:

```text
> catConf -list file_names -cpd inputs -outtype sd -fast 250
```

```text
> catConf -list file_names -cpd inputs -outtype sd -outsd outputs.sd -fast 250
```

will write all the conformers of all the molecules to a single file named outputs.sd.

# catDB

Source type: HTML

Source section: scientificapplications

Source file: scientificapplications/catalyst_catdb.htm

## catDB

The catDB program allows you to create, modify, move, delete, and get summary information about a Catalyst database. The first argument specifies the command to be executed.

Catalyst databases can be ordinary or composite. An ordinary Catalyst database is divided into three separate components: 2D/3D structural data, 2D indexes, and 3D indexes. A composite database consists of a set of ordinary databases. In this topic, unless otherwise specified, the term 'database' refers to an ordinary database.

Ordinary and composite databases are identified by a configuration ( .bdb ) file that records the location of each database component on the network and additional information. The catDB CONFIG and catDB MULTI_CONFIG commands are used to create ordinary and composite database configuration files respectively. Similarly, the RECONFIG and MULTI_RECONFIG commands are used to reconfigure ordinary and composite databases, including moving one or more components to new locations when appropriate.

A major function provided by catDB is the building of databases from various descriptions of molecular topology and, optionally, geometry. The CPD, TPL, MOL, SMILES, SD, RGFile, CREATE, and SPST_CREATE commands all build databases. They share many options and general functionality, differing only in the format in which the molecular descriptions are provided.

If two or more compounds with the same name are encountered during a build command, the second and succeeding compounds are skipped and an error message is displayed or sent to an error file.

Unless the APPEND option is specified, all build commands will issue an error and terminate if the specified database already exists. A maximum number of conformers can be specified with the MaxConfs option. The ExistingConfs options control the use of any 3D conformers in the input data. All options are described in detail in catDB Options .

# catDB Options

Source type: HTML

Source section: scientificapplications

Source file: scientificapplications/catalyst_catdb_options.htm

## catDB Options

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| StartAfter-<cmpd> | Starts at a specified compound in an input file. <cmpd> can either be a double quoted compound name (e.g., StartAfter-"XX579935") or a singly quoted compound number preceded by a '$' (e.g., StartAfter-'$1000'). This option is valid with the CPD, MOL, SD, SD_UPDATE, SMILES, and TPL commands. | off |
| StopAfter-<cmpd> | Stops at a specified compound in an input file. <cmpd> can either be a double quoted compound name (e.g., StopAfter-"XX579935") or a singly quoted compound number preceded by a '$' (e.g., StopAfter-'$1000'). This option is valid with the CPD, MOL, SD, SD_UPDATE, SMILES, and TPL commands. Default is to stop after the last compound in the input file. | off |
| errFile-<errfile name> | A one-line error message is output to the specified file for any compound that is invalid, has problems with conformer generation, or has a duplicate name. | <databasename>.err |
| errData-<errdata name> | All unprocessed data is output to the specified file in the same format as the input. This permits the user to collect all unprocessed data, and to iteratively solve the problems that prevent loading into the database. This option is only valid with the CPD, MOL, SD, SMILES, and TPL commands. Default: by default unprocessed data is output to a file name with the following pattern: <db>_err<num>.<type>. Example: ACD_ err0.sd. | <databaseName>_errN.sd |
| MaxConfs-<N> | For each compound in the database, try to generate up to N conformers. This option is interpreted in conjunction with the ExistingConfs option. When ExistingConfs=Use more conformations will be added to molecules that have less than N conformations. When ExistingConfs=Discard all pre-existing conformations are removed and up to N conformations are created for each ligand. When MaxConfs=0 and ExistingConfs=Use, conformational analysis is done _only_ for input compounds with _no_ existing conformational models. | 100 |
| ExistingConfs-Discard | All 3D conformers that come with the input file are discarded when generating the database (i.e., only the connectivity information is retained and used for conformational analysis). | |
| ExistingConfs-Use | Any conformers in the input file are entered in the database. If there were fewer than MaxConfs conformers, conformational analysis is performed to generate additional conformers up to the maximum. If there were the specified maximum number of conformers or more already in the input file, all existing conformers are kept and conformational analysis is not performed. When MaxConfs is specified as zero (0), conformational analysis is only performed for any compounds that have no existing conformational model. | on |
| BEST | Uses "Best" conformational analysis when generating conformers. | off |
| FAST | Uses "Fast" conformational analysis when generating conformers. | on |
| No2DIndex | Prevents the generation of 2D indexing information. | compute indices |
| No3DIndex | Prevents the generation of 3D indexing information. Since the database dictionary is only needed for 3D index generation, a dictionary is not required when this option is set. | compute indices |
| APPEND | If APPEND is specified, the output DB must already exist and the output generated by the operation will be added to the database. If StartCref is specified, its value is used unless there is a potential conflict with crefs (internal, unique numbers) already in the database, which flags an error. Otherwise, StartCref is set to a cref that is larger than all crefs in the database. | off |
| outputDB-<db.bdb> | Specifies the output database configuration file. Default is the name of the .esp file, with the .esp extension replaced by .esp . This option is only valid with the CREATE command. | off |
| AllowNFS | Allows writing to files across NFS mounted disk partitions even though the such files cannot be write-locked. This is a very unsafe practice that can result in data corruption if the files are accessed by another process. | |
| StartCref-<number> | Each compound in a database has an internal, unique number called a "cref". By default, when building a database, catDB starts the numbering from 1. However, if the you anticipate that the database will be merged with another database in the future, each database must have unique crefs. | 1 |
| NoUseFragments | By default, ring fragments of molecules are cached in memory during conformational analysis. This option prevents this caching and so will save runtime memory usage but will degrade performance. Specifying NoUseFragments implies NoReadFragments and NoWriteFragments. | use fragment database |
| NoReadFragments | Do not read in ring fragments of molecules that are stored in the file "fragments.data" in /shares/Catalyst/conf/ or the local startup directory. This option will save runtime memory usage, but will degrade performance if ring systems in "fragments.data" are encountered during the current catDB run. | reads fragment database |
| NoWriteFragments | Do not output the ring fragments of molecules stored in memory into the file "fragments.data" (located in the local directory) upon normal catDB termination. This option will cause future catDB runs that encounter the same ring fragments to regenerate them and decrease the run performance. | write fragment database |
| ReadAllConfs | This option is valid with the SD command. When this option is used, catDB will attempt to read multiple conformers rather than considering each entry as a separate molecule. | off |
| log-<logfile> | Write log messages to <logfile> | none |
| 2DCompounds-<n> | Set the number of random compounds to check for 2D validation. | off |
| 3DCompounds-<n> | Set the number of random compounds to check for 3D validation. | off |

# Using catDB

Source type: HTML

Source section: scientificapplications

Source file: scientificapplications/catalyst_catdb_usage.htm

## Using catDB

The following tasks are available from the catDB command line:

* Get catDB help

* Specify or change configuration information of a database

* Specify or change configuration information of a composite database

* Create or append to a database from .cpd , .tpl , or .mol files

* Create or append to a database with compounds referenced in an ESP file

* Create or append to a database from .sd input

* Create or append to a database from SMILES input

* Create or append to a database the compounds listed in an SPST file

* Merge multiple parts of a database which were built separately

* Recalculate 2D and 3D indexes for the database

* Validate structures in a database, deleting invalid compounds

* Repair a range of crefs (compound reference numbers)

* Delete compounds listed in input file

* Delete a database

* Summarize database information

To get catDB help

```text
catDB HELP
```

A help screen is displayed when catDB is given insufficient or inaccurate
arguments, or when executed with the HELP option.

To specify or change configuration information of a database

```text
catDB CONFIG <db.bdb>
catDB RECONFIG <db.bdb>
```

When configuring, you can specify the database name, database ID, the host, path,
server, etc. for each relevant component of the database, or confirm
the default values.

When reconfiguring, you can add or delete database components (conformer database,
2D indexes, 3D indexes) or change each component. If
you change the location of the structural, 2d index or 3d index components
of the database, catDB will attempt to move the files accordingly.

To specify or change configuration information of a composite database

```text
catDB MULTI_CONFIG <db.bdb>
catDB MULTI_RECONFIG <db.bdb>
```

When configuring a composite database, you can specify the location of the various ordinary databases that comprise the database.

When reconfiguring, you can add, delete, or modify existing components.

To create or append to a database from .cpd , .tpl , or .mol files

```text
catDB <filetype> <masterfile> <db.bdb> [
<options>
]
```

<filetype> is either cpd , tpl , or mol . The file
<masterfile> contains the name of a separate file for each compound to
be added to the database, one name per line. The file names should be
relative to the current directory and should include the appropriate suffix
(tpl, mol, or cpd). Each compound file consists of a single topology
and zero or more conformers. The resulting structure database is output to <db.bdb>.

To create or append to a database with compounds referenced in a .esp file

```text
catDB CREATE <file.esp> [
<options>
]
```

The file <file.esp> is a spreadsheet
containing references to compounds in existing databases. A new 
2D/3D database is created for the output DB.

The default name for the database is taken from the .esp file's name. For
example, using myname.esp will operate on database myname.bdb. A
different database name may be specified using the "OUTPUT" option
(see below). If the .bdb file does not already exist, catDB will interactively
prompt you for the configuration information (similar to the
CONFIG command). You can choose to use all default values or
review and change each value if desired.

If any option is specified, including the DEFAULT option, all other
input options will assume their default values. Otherwise, if no options
are given, catDB will interactively prompt you to select the options you
want.

If any compound in the .esp file comes from a StockroomDB, the topology
and conformers for the compound must be present as a .cpd file of
file name <compoundname>.cpd in the same directory where catDB is
run.

To create or append to a database from .sd input

```text
catDB SD <SDfile> <db.bdb> [
<options>
]
```

Create or append to a database from .sd input. The file <SDfile> consists
of concatenated .mol files. catDB
SD uses the distributed database building mechanism described at the
end of this topic. By default, a new compound is built from each
entry in the .sd file. It is possible to consider multiple conformers using
the ReadAllConfs option (see below).

To create or append to a database from SMILES input

```text
catDB SMILES <smilesfile> <db.bdb> [
<options>
]
```

The file <smilesfile>
consists of multiple lines of SMILES input, each specifying the
topology of one compound. Otherwise, it is similar to catDB CPD. catDB
SMILES uses the distributed database building mechanism described
at the end of this document.

To create or append to a database the compounds listed in an SPST file

```text
catDB SPST_CREATE <file.spst> <db.bdb> <directory> <format> [
<options>
]
```

The <file.spst> contains the name of the compound. For each 
compound named in the spreadsheet, it is assumed that a
<compound_name>.<format> file exists in the directory <directory>.
The <format> is one of SMILES, CPD, TPL, MOL. For example, if the
format is TPL, the directory is /home/database, and the SPST file contains
compounds c1 and c2, then /home/database/c1.tpl and /home/database/
c2.tpl are the corresponding topology or conformer files.

To merge multiple parts of a database which were built separately

```text
catDB MERGE <outputdb> DBlist-<db1>,<db2>,... [errFile-<errfile>]
```

Merges two or more existing databases created with the catDB program
and outputs the resulting database to "outDB". If there are only two
databases in the merge list, and one of the databases being merged is the
same as outDB, this database will be overwritten with the combined
information.

No two compounds in a database can have identical names. If the same
compound name exists in both input databases, only the first compound
of that name is output to the outDB. The other compound with a duplicate
name will be excluded from outDB. All duplicate compound names
will be reported.

The MERGE command is NOT intended for general merging of two
unrelated databases, but rather is a method for creating a big database
by building of pieces of a database in parallel and then merging them. This is performed automatically when using the Parallel option in the Build 3D Database protocol used in Discovery Studio .

The MERGE command requires that the input databases have
disjoint internal compound reference numbers, or "crefs".

To recalculate 2D and 3D indexes for the database

```text
catDB RECALC <db.bdb>
```

To validate structures in a database, deleting invalid compounds

```text
catDB VALIDATE <inputdb.bdb> [Parts-all|0d,2d,3d] [
<options>
]
```

This command validates the integrity of the specified parts of the database, where the
default is 'Parts-all', which is equivalent to 'Parts-0d,2d,3d'. 
If '0d' is specified, catDB will validate the 2D/3D structural 
integrity of all compounds in the database; the name of any invalid compound
will be displayed and that compound will be deleted from the database.
A valid compound is one that has valid 2D/3D structures. 
If
'2d' is specified, the 2d indexes' integrity will be verified. If '3d' is specified, the 3d indexes' integrity will be verified.

To repair a range of crefs (compound reference numbers)

```text
catDB REPAIR_DB <db.bdb>
```

This command causes crefs to be renumbered starting at StartCref. It is required that
no 2D indices or 3D indices exists in the DB.

To delete compounds listed in input file

```text
catDB DELETE <file.esp>
```

The first command deletes compounds specified in the .esp file from the database in which they reside.
You cannot delete all the compounds in the database using
this method. Use "catDB DELETE_DB" instead.

To delete a database

```text
catDB DELETE_DB <db.bdb>
```

DELETE_DB deletes pre-existing database from disk. All data in the database is lost forever.

To summarize database information

```text
catDB INFO <inputdb.bdb> [Detail]
```

If [Detail] information is required, catDB will compute the number of
compounds, fragments, and average number of conformers per fragment.
The average molecular weight for compounds in the database is
reported, as is the name of the last compound.

catDB Options catDB Command Line Catalyst Standalone Applications

# catHypo

Source type: HTML

Source section: scientificapplications

Source file: scientificapplications/catalyst_cathypo.htm

## catHypo

catHypo is a program for automatically generating pharmacophore models.
There are two main algorithms used in catHypo, HypoGen [Li et al., 2000] and
HipHop [Barnum et al., 1996] . HypoGen attempts to derive SAR pharmacophore models from a set of molecules for which activity values on a given biological target have been measured. HipHop is intended to derive common feature pharmacophore models using information from a set of active compounds. In addition, both algorithms have been modified to incorporate excluded volumes into the pharmacophores. HypoGenRefine will attempt to add excluded volumes during the optimization phase of HypoGen in order to improve the overall correlation with activity and estimated activity.

HipHopRefine is an algorithm that adds excluded volumes to any feature-based pharmacophore with location constraints. Typically this algorithm is used as a post-processor to the HipHop algorithm. HipHopRefine adds excluded volumes in regions that are occupied by inactive molecules only.

#### Further reading

* [Guner et al., 2001]

* [Guner et al., 2004]

#### Further information

HypoGen HIPHOP HIPHOPREFINE catHypo Options Standalone Applications

# Adding Excluded Volumes to a Hypothesis

Source type: HTML

Source section: scientificapplications

Source file: scientificapplications/catalyst_cathypo_add_volumes.htm

## Adding Excluded Volumes to a Hypothesis

The following are required to add excluded volumes to existing 
pharmacophores:

* A .spst spreadsheet file with the appropriate values set for the principle column

* .cpd files for all the molecules in the spreadsheet file

* An input .ds_chm file

To add excluded volumes to an existing pharmacophore

```text
catHypo input.spst . cpd output_hypo output_log -excludedvolumes 100 -in input.ds_chm
```

input.spst is a spreadsheet of active and inactive compounds with the Principal values set. input.ds_chm is any feature-based pharmacophore. catHypo will use the same algorithm used to add excluded volumes to the HipHop pharmacophores in HipHopRefine.

#### Further information

Using catHypo Command Line catHypo Options catHypo Command Line Catalyst Standalone Applications

# HIPHOP

Source type: HTML

Source section: scientificapplications

Source file: scientificapplications/catalyst_cathypo_hiphop.htm

## HIPHOP

HipHop derives common feature pharmacophore models using information from a set of active compounds.

#### Usage

```text
catHypo in.spst . cpd hypo_name log_name -dict dict.ds_chm -sel feat.lst -common
```

where in.spst is a tab delimited spreadsheet file that contains the compound
name, Principal value, and MaxOmitFeat value as shown here:

```text
INTEGER INTEGER TEXT
Principal MaxOmitFeat Name
1 2 A74704-9hvp
1 2 JG365-7hvp
1 2 SKF108738-hef
1 2 SKBVa-aaq
2 2 SB203386-sbg
1 2 U75875-hiv
```

In the Principal column, a value of 2 ensures that all of the chemical features
in the compound will be considered in building pharmacophore space.
A value of 1 ensures that features will be considered when generating
pharmacophores and that at least one mapping for each generated pharmacophore
will be found unless the Misses or CompleteMisses options are used. A
value of 0 means the compound will be ignored completely.

The MaxOmitFeat value specifies how many pharmacophore features
must map to the chemical features in each compound. A value of 0
forces mapping of all features, 1 means that all but one feature
must map, and 2 allows pharmacophores to which no compound features
map.

The -common flag instructs catHypo to use the HipHop algorithm.

#### Further information

Using catHypo Command Line catHypo Options catHypo Command Line Catalyst Standalone Applications

==============================================================================================================
DOCUMENT 706
==============================================================================================================

# HIPHOPREFINE

Source type: HTML

Source section: scientificapplications

Source file: scientificapplications/catalyst_cathypo_hiphoprefine.htm

## HIPHOPREFINE

Use the -excludedvolumes option to add excluded volumes to HipHop
pharmacophores.

#### Usage

```text
catHypo in.spst . cpd hypo_name log_name -dict dict.ds_chm -sel feat.lst -common -excludedvolumes 100
```

The first option (in.spst) is a spreadsheet file that contains the compound names, the
Principal values, and the MaxOmitFeat values. The HipHopRefine
algorithm requires inactive molecules to place the excluded volumes.
These should be given a Principal value of 0. Use the same logic above
to assign the Principal values to the active molecules.

The MaxOmitFeat value serves two purposes when adding
excluded volumes to HipHop models. First, during the HipHop phase,
it specifies which active molecules are allowed to miss features. A
value of 1 means that this molecule is allowed to miss one feature. Second,
during the Excluded Volume addition, the values are used to find
candidate Excluded Volume locations. A value of 1 means that all mappings
where either all n or a subset of n-1 features map will be considered.
For more complicated data sets, it may be better to set
MaxOmitFeat to 0 for the inactive molecules to avoid placing too many
excluded volumes.

#### Further information

Using catHypo Command Line catHypo Options catHypo Command Line Catalyst Standalone Applications

# HypoGen

Source type: HTML

Source section: scientificapplications

Source file: scientificapplications/catalyst_cathypo_hypogen.htm

## HypoGen

HypoGen attempts to derive SAR pharmacophore models from a set of molecules
for which activity values on a given biological target have been
measured.

#### Usage

```text
catHypo in.spst . cpd hypo_name log_name -dict dict.ds_chm -sel feat.lst
```

The first option (in.spst) indicates a tab-delimited spreadsheet file that contains the compound
Names, Activity values, and Uncertainty as shown here:

| TEXT | FLOAT | FLOAT |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | Activ | Uncert |
| nleu-ala-pro | 700 | 3 |
| val-trp | 1700 | 3 |
| leu-ala-pro | 2300 | 3 |
| ile-tyr | 3700 | 3 |
| phe-ala-pro | 4200 | 3 |
| arg-ala-pro | 16000 | 3 |
| phe-pro-pro | 78000 | 3 |
| ile-pro | 150000 | 3 |
| ala-pro | 270000 | 3 |
| ala-val | 300000 | 3 |
| glu-ala-pro | 360000 | 3 |
| val-pro | 420000 | 3 |
| gly-phe | 450000 | 3 |
| ala-leu | 1.6e+06 | 3 |
| ala-gly | 2.5e+06 | 3 |
| gly-glu | 5.4e+06 | 3 |
| gly-lys | 5.4e+06 | 3 |
| pro-pro | 7.5e+06 | 3 |
| ala-his | 9e+06 | 3 |
| gly-asp | 9.2e+06 | 3 |

Next is the directory that contains the conformer models. A
"." indicates that the .cpd files are contained in the current directory.

The next option is the file type that contains the conformer
models. Valid values for this field are: tpl, cpd, mmod, or mol2.

The next option (hypo_name) is the pharmacophore name. This is the
base name that will be used for the pharmacophore files.

The option (log_name) is the log file name. This is the base
name that will be used for the log files generated.

The -dict option is used to specify the file that contains the feature definitions
to be used. dict.ds_chm contains the query definitions of the features.
For example, if you want HypoGen to construct pharmacophores that
contain Hydrophobic and Hydrogen Bond Acceptor groups, dict.ds_chm
must contain the following:

```text
!BioCAD CHM format, all rights reserved Monday 22 August 2005 11:30:01
!VERSION 1.1
QUERY HYDROPHOBIC
{
AND HYDROPHOBIC ( ) 
{
ATTRIBUTES :
COORD2D ( 0 0 ) ;
COORD3D ( 0 0 0 ) ;
PROP ( SOURCE "BIOCAD_FUNCTION" ) ;
ROOT ;
OBJECTS :
POINT Hydrophobic
COORD2D ( 0 0 )
COORD3D ( 0 0 0 )
HYDROPHOBE 
PROP ( INDEX_CODE "11" ) ;
}
}
!BioCAD CHM format, all rights reserved Monday 22 August 2005 11:30:01
!VERSION 1.1
QUERY HB_ACCEPTOR
{
AND atomWithLP ( ) 
{
ATTRIBUTES :
COORD2D ( 0 0 ) ;
COORD3D ( 0 0 0 ) ;
TOPOLOGY :
ATOM #NOS#3
ELEMENTS ( N O S )
CHARGE ( -7 -6 -5 -4 -3 -2 -1 0 )
VALENCE ( 2 3 )
LPCOUNT ( 1 2 3 )
COORDINATION ( 1 2 )
COORD2D ( 0 0 )
COORD3D ( 0 0 0 ) ;
OBJECTS :
POINT AcceptorPt1
COORD2D ( 0 300 )
COORD3D ( 0 300 0 ) ;
VECTOR Acceptor1 HEAD ( AcceptorPt1 ) TAIL ( #NOS#3 ) HBACCEPTOR ;
}
AND goodN ( ) 
{
ATTRIBUTES :
COORD2D ( 0 0 ) ;
COORD3D ( 0 0 0 ) ;
TOPOLOGY :
ATOM #N#3
ELEMENTS ( N )
LPCOUNT ( 1 )
COORDINATION ( 3 )
COORD2D ( 0 0 )
COORD3D ( 0 0 0 ) ;
ATOM #NonC#3
ELEMENTS ( ANY_NONCARBON )
COORD2D ( 150 0 )
COORD3D ( 150 0 0 ) ;
BOND N-NonC ( #N#3 #NonC#3 ) SINGLE DOUBLE TRIPLE AROMATIC ;
OBJECTS :
POINT AcceptorPt1-1
COORD2D ( 0 300 )
COORD3D ( 0 300 0 ) ;
VECTOR Acceptor1-1 HEAD ( AcceptorPt1-1 ) TAIL ( #N#3 ) HBACCEPTOR ;
}
OR HBA ( atomWithLP goodN ) 
{
ATTRIBUTES :
COORD2D ( 0 0 ) ;
COORD3D ( 0 0 0 ) ;
PROP ( SOURCE "BIOCAD_FUNCTION" ) ;
ROOT ;
OBJECTS :
ATOM heavyAtom 
COORD2D ( 0 0 )
COORD3D ( 0 0 0 )
MAP ( atomWithLP/#NOS#3 goodN/#N#3 ) 
PROP ( INDEX_CODE "14" ) ;
POINT AcceptorPt 
COORD2D ( 0 300 )
COORD3D ( 0 300 0 )
MAP ( atomWithLP/AcceptorPt1 goodN/AcceptorPt1-1 ) 
PROP ( INDEX_CODE "15" ) ;
VECTOR Acceptor HEAD ( AcceptorPt ) TAIL ( heavyAtom ) 
MAP ( atomWithLP/Acceptor1 goodN/Acceptor1-1 ) ;
}
}
```

The feature definitions can be found in the /shares/Catalyst/conf/Dictionary.ds_chm file. If -dict is not specified, catHypo will use /shares/Catalyst/conf/Dictionary.ds_chm. If customized features are not used, then the -dict option is not necessary.

The -sel option lists the features that will be used. The file feat.lst contains the features that will be used and their minimum and maximum values, as shown here:

```text
HYDROPHOBIC 0 5
HB_ACCEPTOR 0 5
```

#### HypogenRefine

Use the -excludedvolumes option to include the option of adding excluded volumes to the pharmacophores during the optimization phase.

Typical usage:

```text
catHypo in.spst . cpd hypo_name log_name -dict dict.ds_chm -sel feat.lst -excludedvolumes 3
```

In addition to the compound name, activity, and uncertainty values, you can optionally add a Principal column in HypoGenRefine. A value of 0 for this parameter causes HypoGenRefine to ignore this compound when adding excluded volumes. A value of 1 causes HypoGenRefine to treat this compound as an inactive molecule when placing the excluded volume. A value of 2 causes HypoGenRefine to treat this compound as an active when placing the excluded volumes.

The option -excludedvolumes 3 causes HypoGenRefine to potentially add up to 3 excluded volumes to the pharmacophores. Note that it is possible that the final pharmacophores will not have excluded volumes if adding them does not improve the models.

#### Further information

Using catHypo Command Line catHypo Options catHypo Command Line Catalyst Standalone Applications
