# Add function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/add_function.htm

## Add function

### Description

Add adds the coordinates and radii of all suitable atoms in the supplied array to a shape feature.

### Applies to

The Add function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::ShapeFeature

### Using the Add function

#### Instance

$object->Add( <arrayofobjects> );

$object->Add( { ArrayOfObjects => <arrayofobjects> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <arrayofobjects> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::ShapeFeature |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create napthalene
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c12ccccc1cccc2');

# Create version with added Cl atom
$document->InsertFromSmiles('[Cl]c2ccc1ccccc1c2');

# Create shape query based on the two molecules
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();
my $shapeOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryShape');
my $shapefeatureObject =
$shapeOperator->CreateShapeFeature( $document->Molecules->[0]->Atoms );
$shapefeatureObject->Add( $document->Molecules->[1]->Atoms );

# Print properties
my $propertyNames = $shapefeatureObject->PropertyNames();
foreach my $propertyName (@$propertyNames)
{
my $value = $shapefeatureObject->GetProperty($propertyName);
print "$propertyName - $value \n";
}
```

# AddAndOrientMembrane function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/addandorientmembrane_function.htm

## AddAndOrientMembrane function

### Description

AddAndOrientMembrane creates a new Mdm::Membrane object
for the specified protein molecule. The created membrane will be oriented
with its normal along the Z-axis. The relative orientation of the
protein to the membrane is determined by optimization a simplified solvation
energy.
The following parameters are available:

* Protein specifies the membrane protein.

* MembraneThickness specifies the thickness of the membrane in angstroms.

### Applies to

The AddAndOrientMembrane function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the AddAndOrientMembrane function

#### Instance

my $membraneObject = $object->AddAndOrientMembrane( <protein>, [membranethickness] );

my $membraneObject = $object->AddAndOrientMembrane( { Protein => <protein>, MembraneThickness => [membranethickness] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $membraneObject | | | Mdm::Membrane |
| <protein> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| [membranethickness] | Optional | 30.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate creation, placement and orientation of a membrane.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

# Remove all chains except the first.
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

my $membrane = $document->AddAndOrientMembrane($molecule);
$membrane->Select();

my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms();
my $membraneOrientation =
$molecule->CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor( $membrane, $atoms,
Mdm::objectCentered, Mdm::referenceAxisZ );

print "Original membrane position:\n";
my $shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
my $tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
my $rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);

print "Modified membrane position:\n";
$document->SetMembraneOrientation( $atoms, $membrane, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 );
$shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
$tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
$rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);

print "Modified membrane position:\n";
$document->SetMembraneOrientation( $atoms, $membrane, 10.0, 30.0, 90.0 );
$shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
$tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
$rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);

my $transmembraneResidues =
$document->TransmembraneResidues( $molecule, $membrane );
$document->SplitTransmembraneSegments( $molecule, $membrane,
$transmembraneResidues );

foreach my $residue (@$transmembraneResidues)
{
$residue->Select();
}
```

# AddBondType function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/addbondtype_function.htm

## AddBondType function

### Description

AddBondType adds a bond type to a query bond.

### Applies to

The AddBondType function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryBond

### Using the AddBondType function

#### Instance

$object->AddBondType( <bondtype> );

$object->AddBondType( { BondType => <bondtype> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <bondtype> | Required | | enum Mdm::QueryBondType |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryBond |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');

$document->CreateAndTopology();

# The query bonds are automatically created using
# the CreateAndTopology function. However, to show
# how to create them using CreateBondQuery, we will delete
# them and then add them again.

my $querybonds = $document->QueryBonds;
foreach my $querybond (@$querybonds)
{
$querybond->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

my $bonds = $document->Bonds;
foreach my $bond (@$bonds)
{
my $querybond =
$document->QueryOperators()->Item(0)->CreateQueryBond($bond);
$querybond->AddBondType('queryAnyBond');
}

# removes the first query bond's bond type
$document->QueryBonds->Item(0)->RemoveBondType('queryAnyBond');
```

# AddChiralHydrogenAtoms function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/addchiralhydrogenatoms_function.htm

## AddChiralHydrogenAtoms function

### Description

AddChiralHydrogenAtoms adds chiral hydrogen atoms ( Mdm::Atom ) to the selected atoms.

### Applies to

The AddChiralHydrogenAtoms function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the AddChiralHydrogenAtoms function

#### Instance

$object->AddChiralHydrogenAtoms( [hydrogenset] );

$object->AddChiralHydrogenAtoms( { HydrogenSet => [hydrogenset] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [hydrogenset] | Optional | allHydrogenAtoms | enum Mdm::HydrogenSet |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate functions to manipulate hydrogen atoms.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# change display style
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStick );
printf "Total Atoms: %d\n" , $document->Atoms->Count;
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;

# Add all missing hydrogen atoms.
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms( Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms, True );
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Remove any non-polar hydrogen atoms.
$document->RemoveHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::nonEssentialHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Hide the remaining polar hydrogen atoms.
$document->HideHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::essentialHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;

sleep(1);

# Show the all existing hydrogen atoms.
$document->ShowHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Remove hydrogen atoms connected to specified atom.

$document->Atoms->Item(0)->RemoveHydrogens();
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Add chiral hydrogen atoms.
$document->RemoveHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;

$document->AddChiralHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
```

# AddConformations function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/addconformations_function.htm

## AddConformations function

### Description

AddConformations creates conformations using molecules from a specified molecular file. Supported file formats are .dsv , .mol2 , PDB, and .sd files. Note that the current document can only have a single molecule that is the same as those in the molecular file.

### Applies to

The AddConformations function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the AddConformations function

#### Instance

$object->AddConformations( <filename> );

$object->AddConformations( { FileName => <filename> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <filename> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Adds conformations from molecules in a molecular file (*.dsv, *.msv,
# *.pdb, *.mol2, *.sd) into a molecule and animate the conformations.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage()
{
print "This example script is intended to run with two input files.\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1 Prepare a molecule.mol2 file which contains a "
. "single molecule.\n";
print " 2 Prepare a conformations.sd file which contains multiple "
. "conformations of the same molecule.\n";
print " 3 Run this script with the two files at the same folder.\n";
exit;
}

# Check files exist.
Usage() unless ( -e 'molecule.mol2' && -e 'conformations.sd' );

my $document = DiscoveryScript::Open('molecule.mol2');

# Inserts conformations stored in a .sd file.
$document->AddConformations('conformations.sd');

# Animates the conformations.
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
$document->AnimateConformations;

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->Save("molecule_conformations.dsv", 'dsv');
$document->Close();
```

# AddCTerminalCappingGroup function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/addcterminalcappinggroup_function.htm

## AddCTerminalCappingGroup function

### Description

AddCTerminalCappingGroup adds a specified capping group to the C-terminal of amino acid chains.
The following arguments are available:

* Group specifies the capping group. Valid groups include NH2, NME, OH and CH3.

* SeparateResidues specifies whether to create the cap as a separate non-amino acid residue or incorporate it in the terminal amino acid.

### Applies to

The AddCTerminalCappingGroup function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the AddCTerminalCappingGroup function

# AddFrame function

Source type: HTML

## AddFrame function

### Description

AddFrame adds a new frame to the end of an MDM animation. An animation frame can
be any MDM object. When active, the frame is displayed; otherwise, it is hidden.

### Applies to

The AddFrame function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Animation

### Using the AddFrame function

#### Instance

$object->AddFrame( <frame> );

$object->AddFrame( { Frame => <frame> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <frame> | Required | | Mdm::Object |
| $object | | | Mdm::Animation |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage()
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing conformations.\n";
print " 3 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Opens a molecule with conformations from the active Molecule Window.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage() unless ($document);
Usage() unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );
Usage() unless ( $document->Conformations->Count > 0 );

print "Create an animation using conformation objects.\n";
my $animation = $document->CreateAnimation( $document->Conformations );
my $frameCount = $animation->FrameCount;
print "Number of animation frames: $frameCount frames.\n";

print "Saving the first frame to file.\n";
$animation->ActivateFirstFrame();
$document->Save( "FirstFrame.mol2", "mol2" );

# Illustrate how to activate the next and previous frames.
$animation->ActivateNextFrame();
$animation->ActivatePreviousFrame();

print "Saving the last frame to file.\n";
$animation->ActivateLastFrame();
$document->Save( "LastFrame.mol2", "mol2" );

print "Removing the first frame.\n";
my $firstFrame = $document->Conformations->Item(0);
$animation->RemoveFrame($firstFrame);

print "Adding the first frame back.\n";
$animation->AddFrame($firstFrame);
my $isTracked = $animation->IsFrameSelectionTracked();
if ($isTracked)
{
print "Frame selection is tracked.\n";
}
else
{
print "Frame selection is not tracked.\n";
}

print "Removing and de-activating all animation frames.\n";
$animation->RemoveAllFrames();
$animation->ResetFrame();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate functions to manipulate hydrogen atoms.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# change display style
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStick );
printf "Total Atoms: %d\n" , $document->Atoms->Count;
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;

# Add all missing hydrogen atoms.
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms( Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms, True );
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Remove any non-polar hydrogen atoms.
$document->RemoveHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::nonEssentialHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Hide the remaining polar hydrogen atoms.
$document->HideHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::essentialHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;

sleep(1);

# Show the all existing hydrogen atoms.
$document->ShowHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Remove hydrogen atoms connected to specified atom.

$document->Atoms->Item(0)->RemoveHydrogens();
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Add chiral hydrogen atoms.
$document->RemoveHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;

$document->AddChiralHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
```

Source type: HTML

## AddItem function

### Description

AddItem adds an item to a collection.

### Applies to

The AddItem function can be used with the following objects:

DiscoveryScript::ColorArray , DiscoveryScript::DocumentArray , DiscoveryScript::IntegerArray , DiscoveryScript::ObjectMap , DiscoveryScript::RealArray , DiscoveryScript::StringArray , Mdm::Array , Mdm::OfflineableArray , Mdm::PointArray , Mdm::Set , Protocol::ParameterMap , Sdm::Array , Sdm::AttributeMap , Sdm::ResidueArray , Sdm::SequenceArray

### Using the AddItem function

#### Instance

$object->AddItem( <item> );

$object->AddItem( <item>, [addtofront] );

$object->AddItem( <key>, <item> );

$object->AddItem( <keyname>, <value> );

$object->AddItem( { Item => <item> } );

$object->AddItem( { Item => <item>, AddToFront => [addtofront] } );

$object->AddItem( { Key => <key>, Item => <item> } );

$object->AddItem( { KeyName => <keyname>, Value => <value> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <item> | Required | | DiscoveryScript::Object Mdm::Object |
| <key> | Required | | String |
| <keyname> | Required | | String |
| <value> | Required | | String |
| [addtofront] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript , MdmDiscoveryScript , SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to manipulate items in an Mdm::Array.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

my $atoms = $document->Atoms;

# Collect all cysteine atoms.
my $cysteineAtomArray = Mdm::Array::Create();
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
$cysteineAtomArray->AddItem($atom)
if ( $atom->GetProperty("Parent") =~ /CYS/i );
}

# Find the common ancestor of all atoms in the array in cysteineAtomArray.
my $parent = $cysteineAtomArray->FindCommonAncestor();
print "The common parent object of all CYS atoms: "
. $parent->ClassName . " "
. $parent->Name . "\n";

die "No cysteine atoms found! Exiting.\n" if $cysteineAtomArray->IsEmpty;

my $cysteineAtomCount = $cysteineAtomArray->Count;
print "Number of atoms in cysteine residues: " . $cysteineAtomCount . "\n";

# Delete all atoms except C-alpha and C-beta.
# Note: When deleting items from an array, the array is traversed in
# reverse order. This avoids having to account for changes in the item
# indices as the array is modified.
for ( my $i = $cysteineAtomCount - 1 ; $i >= 0 ; --$i )
{
my $atom = $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i);
if ( $atom->Name !~ /(cb|ca)\b/i )
{
$cysteineAtomArray->DeleteItem($i);
}
}
print "Number of C-alpha and C-beta atoms in cysteine residues: "
. $cysteineAtomArray->Count . "\n";

# Create a copy of the original array in reverse order.
$cysteineAtomCount = $cysteineAtomArray->Count;
my $reverseCysteineArray = Mdm::Array::Create();

# Use the AddItem function to insert the first atom.
# Note: the InsertItem function cannot be used on an empty array.
$reverseCysteineArray->AddItem( $cysteineAtomArray->Item(0) );
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $cysteineAtomCount ; ++$i )
{
$reverseCysteineArray->InsertItem( 0, $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i) );
}

# Swap the first two elements or the original array.
my $tempItem = $cysteineAtomArray->Item(0);
$cysteineAtomArray->ReplaceItem( 0, $cysteineAtomArray->Item(1) );
$cysteineAtomArray->ReplaceItem( 1, $tempItem );

# Print out the IDs of the atoms in the two arrays side by side.
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $cysteineAtomCount ; ++$i )
{
my $atom1Id = $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i)->Id;
my $atom2Id = $reverseCysteineArray->Item($i)->Id;
print "item $i\t $atom1Id\t $atom2Id\n";
}

# Remove all remaining items in the original array.
$cysteineAtomArray->ClearItems();
print "The array now has " . $cysteineAtomArray->Count . " elements\n";
```

# AddProteinSecondaryStructure function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/addproteinsecondarystructure_function.htm

## AddProteinSecondaryStructure function

### Description

AddProteinSecondaryStructure adds or replaces a secondary structure to
an Sdm::AminoAcidSequence . The following arguments are available:

* Predictor specifies the enum Sdm::AminoAcidSecondaryStructurePredictor .

* SecondaryStructre specifies the secondary structure as a string.
The string length must have the same length as the sequence. Each character in the
string specifies the secondary structure of the corresponding residue using the
characters H, S, and C to denote helical, sheet, or coil conformations. All other
characters are interpreted as a coil.

* Propensity specifies the propensity as a string of digits. This is an optional
argument and can be an empty string.
The string length must have the same length as the sequence. See ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity for addition help on propensities.

The following two arguments only apply to user-defined enum Sdm::AminoAcidSecondaryStructurePredictor types:

* UserDefinedPredictorHasProbabilityData specifies if the secondary structure
is defined from probability data similar to the DSC predictor (when set True).

* UserDefinedDescriptor specifies the type of secondary structure. Allowed
values include standard descriptor type (Sdm::secondaryStructureType) identifying
helical, sheet, and coil regions, or a transmembrane descriptor type
(Sdm::transmembraneSecondaryStructureType).

### Applies to

The AddProteinSecondaryStructure function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence

### Using the AddProteinSecondaryStructure function

#### Instance

my $secondarystructureObject = $object->AddProteinSecondaryStructure( <predictor>, [secondarystructre], [propensity], [userdefinedpredictorhasprobabilitydata], [userdefineddescriptor] );

my $secondarystructureObject = $object->AddProteinSecondaryStructure( { Predictor => <predictor>, SecondaryStructre => [secondarystructre], Propensity => [propensity], UserDefinedPredictorHasProbabilityData => [userdefinedpredictorhasprobabilitydata], UserDefinedDescriptor => [userdefineddescriptor] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $secondarystructureObject | | | Sdm::SecondaryStructure |
| <predictor> | Required | | enum Sdm::AminoAcidSecondaryStructurePredictor |
| [propensity] | Optional | "" | String |
| [secondarystructre] | Optional | "" | String |
| [userdefineddescriptor] | Optional | Sdm::secondaryStructureType | enum Sdm::SecondaryStructureDescriptorType |
| [userdefinedpredictorhasprobabilitydata] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Sdm::AminoAcidSequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl
# Illustrate how to add a secondary structure.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0);

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$sdmDocument->DeleteAlignmentSequences();
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule($molecule);

my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown = True;
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

my $sequence = $alignment->Sequence(0);
my $secondaryStructure = $sequence->AddProteinSecondaryStructure(
{
Predictor => Sdm::userDefinedSecondaryStructureType1,
SecondaryStructre => 'HHHHHHHHHHSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC',
UserDefinedPredictorHasProbabilityData => False,
UserDefinedDescriptor => Sdm::secondaryStructureType
}
);
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$sdmDocument->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $sdmDocument->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Publication class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'Y13252-truncated',
'TCTAGAGTAACATTTAGAATTAAGGTGGGAAATTATCTTAAAATCT' );

my $title =
'Nonfixed duplication containing the Adh gene and a truncated form '
. 'of the Adhr gene in the Drosophila funebris species group: different '
. 'modes of evolution of Adh relative to Adhr in Drosophila';

# Create publication object with sample data.
my $publication01 = Sdm::Publication::Create( 'Amador, A., Juan, E.',
$title, 'Molec. Biol. Evol.' );

# Create publication and add content separately.
my $publication02 = Sdm::Publication::Create();
$publication02->Authors = 'Amador, A., Juan, E.';
$publication02->Title = $title;
$publication02->Journal = 'Molec. Biol. Evol.';
$publication02->Reference = '16(11): 1439--1456 (1999)';
$publication02->PubMedId = '10555275';
$publication02->Comment = 'y13252';

#$publication02->Consortium = '';
#$publication02->DigitalObjectId = '';
#$publication02->MedlineId = '';
#$publication02->PubMedId = '';

# Associate publications with a sequence object.
# NOTE: To see the publications in Discovery Studio, double-click on the
# sequence in the sequence window to open a sequence annotation window.
# Publications are listed in the data table's Literature Citation tab.
$sequence->AddPublication($publication01);
$sequence->AddPublication($publication02);

my $publicationCount = $sequence->PublicationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $publicationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $publication = $sequence->Publication($index);
printf "%d: %s, %s. %s %s.\n",
$index + 1,
$publication->Authors,
$publication->Title,
$publication->Journal,
$publication->Reference;
}

$sequence->DeletePublication(0);
```

AddQualifier adds a descriptor to an Sdm::Feature object.
Each qualifier of a feature must have a unique key.

### Applies to

The AddQualifier function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Feature

### Using the AddQualifier function

#### Instance

$object->AddQualifier( <key>, <value> );

$object->AddQualifier( { Key => <key>, Value => <value> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <key> | Required | | String |
| <value> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Sdm::Feature |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate use of Sdm::Qualifier objects.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';
my $filePath = $samplesFolder . 'D.funebris ADH Gene.bsml';

my $document = DiscoveryScript::Open($filePath);
my $feature = $document->Features->Item(0);

# Add qualifier to feature
$feature->AddQualifier( 'Test', "Value of Test" );

# Get qualifiers using filter
my $qualifiers = $feature->Qualifiers;
my $count = $qualifiers->Count();
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $count ; ++$i )
{

# List qualifier Key-Value data
my $qualifier = $qualifiers->Item($i);
print 'Qualifier Key: '
. $qualifier->Key . "\t"
. ' Value: '
. $qualifier->Value . "\n";
}

print "All qualifiers can be printed using the Comments property.\n";
print "Comments: " . $feature->Comment;

# Remove qualifier from feature
$feature->DeleteQualifier('TestKey');
```

# AddRotatableBondMonitors function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/addrotatablebondmonitors_function.htm

## AddRotatableBondMonitors function

### Description

AddRotatableBondMonitors adds rotatable bond monitors to the molecules with selected rotatable bonds or to all molecules
if no bonds are selected. Rotatable bond monitors identify rotatable bonds.

### Applies to

The AddRotatableBondMonitors function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the AddRotatableBondMonitors function

#### Instance

$object->AddRotatableBondMonitors();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
# This script illustrates how to perform a molecular overlay.
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use SbdDiscoveryScript;

# Create a new MDM document.
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $name1 = 'Molecule1';
my $name2 = 'Molecule2';

my %MolecSMARTS = (
$name1 => 'O=C([O-])C1=CC(=CC=C1)C([O-])=O',
$name2 => 'C/C1=C/C=C(C=C1)C([O-])=O'
);

# Insert two molecules 'Molecule1' and 'Molecule2' from SMILES strings.
$document->InsertFromSmiles( $MolecSMARTS{$name1} );
my $molecule1 = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
$molecule1->Name($name1);

$document->InsertFromSmiles( $MolecSMARTS{$name2} );
my $molecule2 = $document->Molecules->Item(1);
$molecule2->Name($name2);

# name of the overlay similarity property
my $overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay Similarity/' . $molecule1->Name;

# Add rotatable bond monitors to both molecules.
# These are used with flexible field alignment.
$document->AddRotatableBondMonitors;

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection(10.0, 5.0, 0.0);
$document->DeselectAll;

# Calculate the similarity before the rigid field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using rigid field alignment, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated similarity is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Rigid field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the similarity before the rigid field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using rigid field alignment.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False
}
);

printf( "Rigid field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection(5.0, 10.0, 0.0);
$document->DeselectAll;

# Calculate the similarity before flexible field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using flexible field alignment, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated similarity is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Flexible field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the similarity before flexible field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay molecules using flexible field alignment.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True
}
);

$overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay Similarity/' . $molecule1->Name;
printf( "Flexible field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

#
# Overlay molecules using tethers (tuple monitors).
#

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection( 10, 10, 5 );
$document->DeselectAll;

my $molecule1Atoms = $molecule1->Atoms;
my $molecule2Atoms = $molecule2->Atoms;

# atom mapping indices
my %atomIndices = (
0 => 8,
2 => 9,
6 => 1
);

print(" Overlay with atom tethers\n");
foreach my $id1 (sort {$a <=> $b} keys %atomIndices) {
my $id2 = $atomIndices{$id1};
my $tupleArray = Mdm::Array::Create();
$tupleArray->AddItem( $molecule1Atoms->Item($id1) );
$tupleArray->AddItem( $molecule2Atoms->Item($id2) );
$document->CreateTupleMonitor($tupleArray);
printf( " Map %s atom: %d to: %s atom: %d\n",
$molecule1->Name, $id1 + 1, $molecule2->Name, $id2 + 1 );
}

# name of the property
$overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay RMS/' . $molecule1->Name;

# Calculate the RMSD value before the alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using tethers, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated RMSD is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the RMSD value before the alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using tethers.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Remove the tethers
my $monitors = $document->TupleMonitors;
foreach my $monitor (@$monitors)
{
$monitor->Select;
}
$document->DeleteObjects;

$document->FitView;
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# AddSegment function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/addsegment_function.htm

## AddSegment function

### Description

AddSegment adds a sequence position or range of positions to
a specified Sdm::Location .

### Applies to

The AddSegment function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Location

### Using the AddSegment function

#### Instance

$object->AddSegment( <segment> );

$object->AddSegment( { Segment => <segment> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <segment> | Required | | Sdm::Segment |
| $object | | | Sdm::Location |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Segment class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence =
$document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASCDFACSGHACSJCKLA' );

# Create a location consisting of all cysteine residues.
print "Creating location for all cysteine residues\n";
my $location = Sdm::Location::Create(Sdm::locationTypeJoin);

my $sequenceString = $sequence->SequenceString;
my $residueCount = length($sequenceString);
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
if ( substr( $sequenceString, $i, 1 ) eq 'C' )
{
my $segment = Sdm::Segment::Create( $i, $i );
$location->AddSegment($segment);
}
}

my $segmentCount = $location->SegmentCount;
print "Location has $segmentCount segments\n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $segmentCount ; ++$index )
{
my $segment = $location->Segment($index);
printf( "Segment %d ...\n", $index + 1);
print "\tStart position:\t" . $segment->StartPosition . "\n";
print "\tEnd position:\t" . $segment->EndPosition . "\n";
print "\tSegement type:\t" . $segment->Type . "\n";
print "\tIs complement?:\t" . $segment->IsComplement . "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Create a feature to and add it to the sequence.
my $feature =
Sdm::Feature::CreateCustomFeature( 'Cysteine residues', $location );
$feature->AddQualifier("KeyName", 'Example feature qualifier');
$sequence->AddFeature($feature);

print 'The feature key name is ' . $feature->Key . "\n";
```

# AlignByResidueId function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/alignbyresidueid_function.htm

## AlignByResidueId function

### Description

AlignByResidueId modifies the gap positions of the specified Sdm::Sequence objects to align residues with
matching identifiers from left to right. Fixed blocks and
chain domain boundaries are maintained. By default, all visible
sequences are aligned. The parameter AlignSelectedOnly specifies
if only selected sequences should be aligned (False by default).

### Applies to

The AlignByResidueId function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the AlignByResidueId function

#### Instance

$object->AlignByResidueId( [alignselectedonly] );

$object->AlignByResidueId( { AlignSelectedOnly => [alignselectedonly] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [alignselectedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to align residue identifiers. 
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdm = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1TGN');
$mdm->InsertFromUrl(PdbUrlPrefix . '1TGT.pdb');

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures($mdm);

$document->Alignment->AlignByResidueId();

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);
```

# AlignmentIndex property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/alignmentindex_property.htm

## AlignmentIndex property

### Description

AlignmentIndex specifies the alignment column index for a given
sequence residue index.

* SequenceIndex is the 0-based sequence index for the residue.

* ResidueIndex is the 0-based residue index.

### Applies to

The AlignmentIndex property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the AlignmentIndex property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->AlignmentIndex( <sequenceindex>, <residueindex> );

my $integerValue = $object->AlignmentIndex( { SequenceIndex => <sequenceindex>, ResidueIndex => <residueindex> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| <residueindex> | Required | | Integer |
| <sequenceindex> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to convert residue indices between the
# sequence and alignment perspectives.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $sequence0 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'MIASDFADSG' );
my $sequence1 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S2', 'MAACDFIDSA' );

# Figure out the length of the alignment
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $alignmentStrings = $alignment->AlignmentStrings();
my $alignmentLength = $alignment->AlignmentLength;

# Insert a gap
$alignment->InsertGap( 1, 2 );

# Print out first 5 aligned residues
print "First 5 aligned residues in the 2 sequences:\n";
my $residueCount = $sequence0->ResidueCount;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 5 ; ++$i )
{
my $residue0 = $sequence0->Residue($i);

# Get the alignment-based index of the residue (i.e., convert the residue
# position from the sequence to the position in the alignment).
my $alignmentIndex = $alignment->AlignmentIndex( 0, $i );

# Get the sequence-based index of the residue in second sequence
# (i.e., convert the residue position from the alignment to the
# residue position in the sequence).
my $sequenceIndex = $alignment->ResidueIndex( 1, $alignmentIndex );

# Get type of residues in both sequences.
my $type0 = $residue0->Symbol;
my $type1 = "-";
if ( $sequenceIndex >= 0 )
{
my $residue1 = $sequence1->Residue($sequenceIndex);
$type1 = $residue1->Symbol;
}

print $i . "\t" . $type0 . "\t" . $type1 . "\n";
}
```

# AlignmentLayout property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/alignmentlayout_property.htm

## AlignmentLayout property

### Description

AlignmentLayout indicates the display layout of the Sequence Window.

### Applies to

The AlignmentLayout property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the AlignmentLayout property

#### Get

my $alignmentlayouttypeEnum = $object->AlignmentLayout;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $alignmentlayouttypeEnum | | | enum Sdm::AlignmentLayoutType |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate use of alignment layout (client only).
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use strict;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

sub SetLayout($$$)
{
# This function will invoke the specified layout.
# Graphically, the UI will update after each action.

my ($document, $layout, $action) = @_;
my $originalLayout = $document->Alignment->AlignmentLayout;

print 'Change to ' . $layout . " layout ...\n";
$document->InvokeAction($action);

my $newLayout = $document->Alignment->AlignmentLayout;
die 'Failure: Layout not set to ' . $layout . " layout.\n"
unless ( $newLayout eq $layout );

sleep(2);
}

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences;
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(0, 'S1', 
'AAAAABBBBBCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(1, 'S2', 
'AAAAABBBBBCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(2, 'S3', 
'AAAAABBBBBCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(3, 'S4', 
'AAAAABBBBBCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC');

$alignment->Sequence(0)->MarkStartOfChain(5);
$alignment->Sequence(1)->MarkStartOfChain(5);
$document->UpdateViews();

SetLayout($document, "chainViewLayout", 'ActionChainViewLayout');
SetLayout($document, "extendedLayout", 'ActionExtendedViewLayout');
SetLayout($document, "wrappedLayout", 'ActionWrappedViewLayout');
```

# AlignmentLength property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/alignmentlength_property.htm

## AlignmentLength property

### Description

AlignmentLength specifies the total number of residues and gaps in an Sdm::Alignment .
The length includes terminal gaps such that each sequence in an alignment returns the same count.

### Applies to

The AlignmentLength property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the AlignmentLength property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->AlignmentLength;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several alignment function.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();

$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $sequence0 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'MIASDFADSG' );
my $sequence1 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S2', 'MAASDFIDSA' );
my $sequence2 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S3', 'IIISDFADSA' );

if ( !$document->HasAlignment )
{
die "No alignment found!\n";
}

my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
$alignment->BackgroundColorScheme = Sdm::colorByChargeSimilarity;

# Insert two gaps into first sequence at 0-based position 2.
$alignment->InsertGap( { Index => 0, StartPosition => 2, Count => 2 } );

# Insert addition gaps in second and third sequences.
$alignment->InsertGap( 1, 1, 1 );
$alignment->InsertGap( 1, 2, 1 );
$alignment->InsertGap( 2, 2, 1 );
$alignment->InsertGap( 2, 3, 1 );

my $alignmentStrings = $alignment->AlignmentStrings();
my $alignmentLength = $alignment->AlignmentLength;

print "The first sequence in the alignment has gaps at positions:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $alignmentLength ; ++$i )
{
if ( $alignment->IsGap( 0, $i ) )
{
print "$i ";
}
}
print "\n";
```

# AlignmentStrings property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/alignmentstrings_property.htm

## AlignmentStrings property

### Description

AlignmentStrings specifies the alignment object as an array of strings.
The array consists of one string for each sequence in the alignment excluding
the consensus sequence. Sequence that are not visible are also included.
Each sequence string includes gaps as shown in the sequence window. Sequences
excluding gaps can be found using SequenceString .

The AlignmentStrings property can be used with the following objects:

```text
{

print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

my $offlineablearrayObject = $object->AllConformations;

| $offlineablearrayObject | | | Mdm::OfflineableArray |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use the offline commands for offline conformations.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';

my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . 'Bacteriorhodopsin Trajectory.dsv';
my $document =
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $inputFile, LoadAllObjects => False } );
my $onlineConformations = $document->Conformations;
my $offlineConformations = $document->AllConformations;
print "There are "
. $offlineConformations->Count
. " conformations in the file.\n";
print "There are "
. $onlineConformations->Count
. " conformations loaded in memory.\n";
print "Visualize the first 10 conformations...\n";

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 10 ; $i++ )
{
my $conf = $offlineConformations->Item($i);
$conf->SetVisible();
}
$onlineConformations = $document->Conformations;
print "There are "
. $onlineConformations->Count
. " conformations loaded in memory now.\n";
print "Offline all the online conformations to release memory.\n";
my $count = $onlineConformations->Count;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $count ; $i++ )
{
my $conf = $offlineConformations->Item($i);
$conf->Offline();
}
print "Closing the document.\n";
$document->Close();
```

# AllNonbondCriterionTypes function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/allnonbondcriteriontypes_function.htm

## AllNonbondCriterionTypes function

### Description

AllNonbondCriterionTypes specifies an array containing all
possible criterion parameter of enum Mdm::NonbondCriterionType .

### Applies to

The AllNonbondCriterionTypes function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::NonbondMonitor

### Using the AllNonbondCriterionTypes function

#### Static

my $stringarrayObject = Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor::AllNonbondCriterionTypes();

my $stringarrayObject = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllNonbondCriterionTypes();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::StringArray |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the basic non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "Create a non-bond monitor for a subset of atoms.\n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus();
$ligand->Select();
my $ligandAtoms = $document->SelectedObjects()->Atoms;
$document->FitView();
$document->DeselectAll();

my $monitor = $document->CreateNonbondMonitor($ligandAtoms);
$monitor->Name = "myname";
$document->UpdateViews();

my $monitors = $document->NonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d NonbondMonitor(s).\n", $monitors->Count;
print "\n";

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "The properties NonbondCriterion and DefaultNonbondCriterion \n";
print "access the parameters used to identify non-bonds (see the \n";
print "documentation for full description of criteria).\n\n";

print "A list of criteria a their values follows:\n";
my $allCriteria = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllNonbondCriterionTypes();
foreach my $criterionType (@$allCriteria)
{
printf "Mdm::%s:\t %6.2f (default: %6.2f) \n",
$criterionType,
$monitor->NonbondCriterion($criterionType),
$monitor->DefaultNonbondCriterion($criterionType);
}
print "\n";

# -- Changing an interaction criterion ------------------------------

print 'Using the default criteria, the number of non-bond '
. 'interactions is ' . $monitor->Nonbonds->Count . ".\n\n";

my $maxHBond = 1.0 + $monitor->NonbondCriterion(
Mdm::hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum);
print 'After increasing the classical hydrogen bond distance to '
. $maxHBond . " A, ";

$monitor->NonbondCriterion(
Mdm::hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum) = $maxHBond;
$document->UpdateObjects;
print 'the number of non-bond interactions increases to '
. $monitor->Nonbonds->Count . ".\n\n";

print "Changes made to the non-bond criteria can be reset " .
"to the original defaults using ResetNonbondCriteria.\n";
$monitor->ResetNonbondCriteria();
```

The AllPerceivedAromaticRingBonds property can be used with the following objects:

### Using the AllPerceivedAromaticRingBonds property

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->AllPerceivedAromaticRingBonds;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::RingPerception |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the perceive rings class.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $smilesString =
'O=C(C/C1=C/C=C[S]1)N(Cc2ccccc2OC)[C@@]([H])(c3cc(OC)c(cc3)OC)C(=O)N[C@]4([H])CCCCC4';

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles($smilesString);

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
foreach my $molecule (@$molecules)
{
my $ringPerception = $molecule->PerceiveRings(
{
FindSmallestSetOfRings => True,
PerceiveAromaticity => True,
FindLonePairDonors => True
}
);

my $ringCount = $ringPerception->RingCount;
my $aromaticRingCount = $ringPerception->AromaticRingCount;

print "Ring analysis of molecule: $smilesString\n";
print "Molecule has: " . $ringCount . " rings\n";
print "Molecule has: " . $aromaticRingCount . " aromatic rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all atoms in rings.
my $ringAtoms = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedRingAtoms;
print "Molecule has: " . $ringAtoms->Count . " atoms in rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all bonds in rings.
my $ringBonds = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedRingBonds;
print "Molecule has: " . $ringBonds->Count . " bonds in rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all aromatic bonds in rings.
my $aromaticRingBonds = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedAromaticRingBonds;
print "Molecule has: "
. $aromaticRingBonds->Count
. " aromatic bonds in rings.\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all lone pair donor atoms in aromatic rings.
my $lonePairDonors = $ringPerception->PerceivedLonePairDonors;
print "Molecule has: "
. $lonePairDonors->Count
. " lone pair donor atoms in rings.\n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $ringCount ; ++$index )
{

# Get an Mdm::Array of atoms in the specified ring.
my $atoms = $ringPerception->PerceivedRingAtoms($index);

# Get an Mdm::Array of bonds in the specified ring.
my $bonds = $ringPerception->PerceivedRingBonds($index);

my $ringnum = $index + 1;
print "Ring ( $ringnum ) contains "
. $atoms->Count
. " atoms and "
. $bonds->Count
. " bonds.\n";
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# AllUnfavorableNonbondTypes function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/allunfavorablenonbondtypes_function.htm

## AllUnfavorableNonbondTypes function

### Description

AllUnfavorableNonbondTypes specifies an array containing all
possible values of an enum Mdm::NonbondType corresponding to unfavorable interaction types.

### Applies to

The AllUnfavorableNonbondTypes function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::NonbondMonitor

### Using the AllUnfavorableNonbondTypes function

#### Static

my $stringarrayObject = Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor::AllUnfavorableNonbondTypes();

my $stringarrayObject = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllUnfavorableNonbondTypes();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::StringArray |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several ways to create arrays of NonbondType
# enumerators.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

print "The static function AllNonbondTypes returns an array of \n";
print "all non-bond interaction types and can be used to iterate \n";
print "over the non-bond interaction types.\n";
my $allNonbondTypes = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllNonbondTypes();
foreach my $type (@$allNonbondTypes) {
printf "- %s \n", $type;
}
print "\n";

print "The static function AllFavorableNonbondTypes returns \n";
print "only the favorable non-bond interaction types.\n";
my $nonbondTypes = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllFavorableNonbondTypes();
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
printf "- %s \n", $type;
}
print "\n";

print "The static function AllUnfavorableNonbondTypes returns \n";
print "only the unfavorable non-bond interaction types.\n";
my $nonbondTypes = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllUnfavorableNonbondTypes();
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
printf "- %s \n", $type;
}
print "\n";

print "Non-bond type arrays can also be defined by category:\n";
my $nonbondTypes = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::NonbondTypesByCategory(
Mdm::allHydrogenBondTypes);
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
printf "- %s \n", $type;
}
print "\n";

print "In addition, custom arrays can defined.\n";
my $nonbondTypes = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$nonbondTypes->AddItem(Mdm::saltBridgeType);
$nonbondTypes->AddItem(Mdm::unfavorableVdwBumpType);
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
printf "- %s \n", $type;
}
print "\n";
```

# Alpha property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/alpha_property.htm

## Alpha property

### Description

Alpha is the blending value of a color. If the alpha value of the color is zero, the color is fully transparent.
If the alpha value is 255, the color is fully opaque. Values between one and 254 give a transparency scaled by the alpha value.

### Applies to

The Alpha property can be used with the following objects:

DiscoveryScript::Color , Mdm::Color

### Using the Alpha property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->Alpha;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | DiscoveryScript::Color Mdm::Color |

#### Set

$object->Alpha = <alpha>;

$object->Alpha( <alpha> );

$object->Alpha( { Alpha => <alpha> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <alpha> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | DiscoveryScript::Color Mdm::Color |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use the Mdm::Color object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1CRN.pdb" );
die "Failed to open MDM document." unless $document;

my $chain = $document->AminoAcidChains->Item(0);
die "Molecule contains no chains." unless $chain;

# This example assumes the protein display is on.
# Ensure this is the case here.
$document->SelectByProperty('Atom Name="*"');
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleAtomStick);
$document->DeselectAll();
$chain->DisplayStyle = Mdm::styleProteinRibbonTube;

print "Select cysteine residues and color them orange...\n\n";
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="CYS.*" ; Atom Name="*"');
my $cysteines = $document->SelectedObjects();
die "No cysteine residues." unless ($cysteines && $cysteines->Count > 0);
my $color = Mdm::Color::Create();
$color->Red = 255;
$color->Green = 200;
$color->Blue = 0;
$document->SetColor($color);
$document->DeselectAll();

print "Coloring the ribbon pseudo-transparent...\n\n";
my $chain = $document->Chains()->Item(0);
my $color = Mdm::Color::Create();
$color->Red = 0;
$color->Green = 255;
$color->Blue = 0;
$color->Alpha = 128;
$chain->Color($color);

print "Coloring the background dark blue...\n\n";
my $bkColor = Mdm::Color::Create();
$bkColor->Red = 0;
$bkColor->Green = 0;
$bkColor->Blue = 100;
$document->BackgroundColor = $bkColor;
```

# AmbientShadow property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/ambientshadow_property.htm

## AmbientShadow property

### Description

AmbientShadow sets the level of ambient shadow. The accepted values are from 0.0 (no ambient shadow) to 1.0 (maximum ambient shadow). Setting this property is an asynchronous operation. The actual shadow may appear some time after
this property changes.

The AmbientShadow property can be used with the following objects:

# AmideCarbon property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/amidecarbon_property.htm

## AmideCarbon property

### Description

AmideCarbon looks for the carbon atom labeled "C" in an amino acid.

### Applies to

The AmideCarbon property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid

### Using the AmideCarbon property

#### Get

my $atomObject = $object->AmideCarbon;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $atomObject | | | Mdm::Atom |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9INS.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleAtomLine } );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $sequence = $molecule->AminoAcidSequence;
print "AminoAcidSequence: $sequence\n";

my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
my $aminoAcid1 = $aminoAcids->Item(0);
my $aminoAcid2 = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
my $aminoAcid3 = $aminoAcids->Item(2);

my $distance = $document->CreateDistanceMonitor( $aminoAcid1->CAlpha, $aminoAcid2->CAlpha );

printf "Distance between CAlpha atoms of $aminoAcid1->{Name} and $aminoAcid2->{Name}: %8.3f\n", $distance->Distance;

my $angle = $document->CreateAngleMonitor( $aminoAcid1->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid1->AmideNitrogen, $aminoAcid1->CAlpha );

printf "Angle between amide carbon, nitrogen, and CAlpha atoms of $aminoAcid1->{Name}: %8.3f\n", $angle->Angle;

my $phiTorsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$aminoAcid1->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid2->AmideNitrogen,
$aminoAcid2->CAlpha, $aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon
);

my $psiTorsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$aminoAcid2->AmideNitrogen, $aminoAcid2->CAlpha,
$aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid3->AmideNitrogen
);

print "Amino acid $aminoAcid2->{Name}: ";
printf "phi = %8.3f, psi = %8.3f\n", $phiTorsion->Angle, $psiTorsion->Angle;
```

```text
$aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid3->AmideNitrogen
);

print "Amino acid $aminoAcid2->{Name}: ";
printf "phi = %8.3f, psi = %8.3f\n", $phiTorsion->Angle, $psiTorsion->Angle;
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This example shows how to alter the characteristics of protein termini.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Subroutine to print atoms in N terminal residue.
sub PrintNTerminus($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $chains = $document->AminoAcidChains;
my $nTerminus = $chains->Item(0)->NTerminus();
my $atoms = $nTerminus->Atoms;
my $atomCount = $atoms->Count;
printf "Number of atoms in N terminal residue %s : %d\n",
$nTerminus->Name(), $atomCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atomCount ; ++$index )
{
my $atom = $atoms->Item($index);
printf
" Name : %s Formal charge %d/%d\n",
$atom->Name(),
$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,
$atom->FormalCharge->Denominator;
}
}

# Subroutine to print atoms in C terminal residue.
sub PrintCTerminus($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $chains = $document->AminoAcidChains;
my $nTerminus = $chains->Item(0)->CTerminus();
my $atoms = $nTerminus->Atoms;
my $atomCount = $atoms->Count;
printf "Number of atoms in C terminal residue %s : %d\n",
$nTerminus->Name(), $atomCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atomCount ; ++$index )
{
my $atom = $atoms->Item($index);
printf
" Name : %s Formal charge %d/%d\n",
$atom->Name(),
$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,
$atom->FormalCharge->Denominator;
}
}

# Subroutine to print atoms in N and C terminal residues.
sub PrintTermini($$)
{
my ( $document, $title ) = @_;
printf "\n%s :\n", $title;
PrintNTerminus($document);
PrintCTerminus($document);
}

# Load molecule from PDB.
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Mutate the termini to alanine. With the side chain removed,
# the atom listing will be clearer.
my $chain = $document->AminoAcidChains->Item(0);
my $nTerminus = $chain->NTerminus();
my $cTerminus = $chain->CTerminus();

$document->MutateAminoAcid( $nTerminus, Mdm::ala );
$document->MutateAminoAcid( $cTerminus, Mdm::ala );
$document->DeselectAll();

# Uncomment this line to add hydrogen atoms.
# AddHydrogens($document);

# List atoms in current configuration.
PrintTermini( $document, "At start" );

# Remove terminal residue characteristics and list atoms.
$chain->RemoveNTerminusCap();
$chain->RemoveCTerminusCap();
PrintTermini( $document, "After removing caps" );

# Make termini normal (i.e. charged) and list atoms.
$nTerminus->MakeNTerminus(True);
$cTerminus->MakeCTerminus(True);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making charged termini" );

# Make termini uncharged and list atoms.
$nTerminus->MakeNTerminus(False);
$cTerminus->MakeCTerminus(False);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making neutral termini" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 1.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(1.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(1.0);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 1.0" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 7.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(7.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(7.0);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 7.0" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 13.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(13.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(130);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 13.0" );

$document->UpdateViews();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl
# Illustrate how to remove aligned gaps.

use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument('SDM');
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

# Create an example alignment view.
$alignment->InsetAlignmentString( 0, 0, 'GASD-EFG-HI--DFGHIKIHG' );
$alignment->Sequence(0)->Name = 'S1';
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString( 1, 'S2', "AASD--FG-HI--PY" );

my $count = $document->AminoAcidSequences()->Count;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $count ; ++$i ) {
print $i+1 .") " . $document->AminoAcidSequences->Item($i)->Name . "\n";
}

# Pause to see gaps removed by following function DeleteAlignedGaps.
sleep(3);

$document->Alignment->DeleteAlignedGaps();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

### Description

When finding pi-sigma interactions, the C-H-centroid angle must not deviate more than the Angle Deviation (default 20°) from linearity.

The AngleDeviation property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor

### Using the AngleDeviation property

#### Set

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script shows how to create pi interaction monitors.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1kim.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Creates pi interaction monitors
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

#if no array of atoms is passed in then the monitor is created
#for the whole molecule (or other object).
my $pipiMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor();
my $piCationMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiCationMonitor();
my $piSigmaMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiSigmaMonitor();

$pipiMonitor->Name = "Pi-Pi";
$piCationMonitor->Name = "Pi-Cation";
$piSigmaMonitor->Name = "Pi-Sigma";

my $piPiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piPiInteractionCount = $piPiInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piPiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

# Change criteria settings to non-default values.
$piCationMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piCationMonitor->MinimumAngle = 60.0;
my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule\n";

$piSigmaMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->MinimumAngle = 30.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->AngleDeviation = 15.0;
my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

$pipiMonitor->MaximumCenterDistance = 7.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumClosestAtomDistance = 4.0;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumLambda = 20.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumTheta = 45.;
my $pipiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount = $pipiInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $pipiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piInteractions = $molecule->PiInteractionMonitors();
my $piCount = $piInteractions->Count();
print "\nThere are " . $piCount . " pi interaction monitors: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $piCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $piInteractions->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Interactions") );
}

#If we want to limit the scope of the monitoring, we can pass in
#an array of atoms. This is similar to creating a monitor from the UI
# when atoms are selected. Pi interactions will then be calculated within
#these, and between these and the parent object
my $residue = FilterByString( $document, "THM1" )->Item(0);
my $atom_array = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $atoms = $residue->Atoms();
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atoms->Count() ; ++$index )
{
$atom_array->AddItem( $atoms->Item($index) );
}
my $pipiMonitor2 = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor($atom_array);
my $pipiInteractions2 = $pipiMonitor2->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount2 = $pipiInteractions2->Count();
print "Number of pi-pi interactions between "
. $residue->Name()
. " and the rest of the molecule: "
. $pipiInteractionCount2 . "\n";

my $picatmonitors = $document->PiCationMonitors;
print "Number of pi-cation monitors: ". $picatmonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pipimonitors = $document->PiPiMonitors;
print "Number of pi-pi monitors: ". $pipimonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pisigmonitors = $document->PiSigmaMonitors;
print "Number of pi-sigma monitors: ". $pisigmonitors->Count . "\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w

use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

# Create an angle constraint.

$document->Atoms->Item(0)->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -4.27, 3.44, 0 );
$atom_array->AddItem( $document->Atoms->Item(0) );
$document->Atoms->Item(1)->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -4.34, 4.94, 0 );

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("N");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -4.11, -.745, 0 );
$atom_array->AddItem($atomObject);
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("S");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.242, -0.664, 0 );
$atom_array->AddItem($atomObject);

$document->CreateAndTopology();
$document->QueryOperators()->Item(0)
->CreateAngleFeature( $atom_array, 80, 100 );

my $propertyNames = $document->AngleFeatures()->Item(0)->PropertyNames;
foreach my $propertyName (@$propertyNames)
{
my $value =
$document->AngleFeatures()->Item(0)->GetProperty($propertyName);
print "$propertyName - $value\n";
}
```

# AngleGamma property

Source type: HTML

## AngleGamma property

### Description

AngleGamma indicates the angle in degrees formed by the basis vector a and b of an Mdm::Cell .

### Applies to

The AngleGamma property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Cell

### Using the AngleGamma property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->AngleGamma;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Cell |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate use of Mdm::Cell class.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('9INS');

my $cell = $document->Cells->Item(0);

print "Crystal cell parameters:\n";
my $format = "\t%s = %8.3f\n\t%s = %8.3f\n\t%s = %8.3f\n";
printf $format, 'a', $cell->LengthA, 'b', $cell->LengthB, 'c', $cell->LengthC;
printf $format,
'alpha', $cell->AngleAlpha,
'beta', $cell->AngleBeta,
'gamma', $cell->AngleGamma;

my $cartesian = $cell->CartesianToFractionMatrix;
printf "\t Cartesian to fractional transformation matrix:\n";
for ( my $row = 0 ; $row < 3 ; ++$row )
{
printf "\t%8.3f\t%8.3f\t%8.3f\n",
$cartesian->GetEntry( $row, 0 ),
$cartesian->GetEntry( $row, 1 ),
$cartesian->GetEntry( $row, 2 );
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the MarkBondAngleViolations function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '9INS.pdb' );

# Mark bond angle violations.
my $tolerance = 3.0;
my $blue = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 200, 200, 255 );
$document->MarkBondAngleViolations( $tolerance, $blue );

# Get the bond angle violation monitors, a type of AngleMonitor.
my $monitors = $document->AngleMonitors;
my $monitors = $document->FilterByProperty('BondAngleViolationMonitor name="*"');

my $allmonitors = $document->Monitors;
print "Total number of monitors: ". $allmonitors->Count ."\n";

# Report the number of violations.
my $violationCount = $monitors->Count();
print "Structure has " . $violationCount . " bond angle violations.\n\n";

# print a table of violations
printf("Index\t Violation name\t Angle\t Expected\t Minimum\t Maximum \n");
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $violationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);
printf(
"%d \t %s \t %f \t %f \t %f \t %f\n",
$index, $monitor->Name(),
$monitor->Angle(), $monitor->GetProperty("Expected"),
$monitor->GetProperty("Minimum"), $monitor->GetProperty("Maximum")
);

$monitors->Item($index)->SetVisible;
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# AnimateConformations function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/animateconformations_function.htm

## AnimateConformations function

### Description

AnimateConformations creates a Molecular Data Model animation for molecules with conformations.
When run, each animation frame displays a different conformation.

### Applies to

The AnimateConformations function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the AnimateConformations function

#### Command

$object->AnimateConformations();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script adds conformations from a CHARMm trajectory file (*.dcd)
# into a molecule and animate the conformations.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage()
{
print "This example script is intended to run with two input files.\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1 Prepare a 1crn.pdb file which contains the coordinates "
. "of 1crn.\n";
print " 2 Prepare a 1crn.dcd file which can be generated from "
. "running a CHARMm dynamics simulation.\n";
print " 3 Run this script with the two files at the same folder.\n";
exit;
}

Usage() unless ( -e '1crn.pdb' && -e '1crn.dcd' );

my $document = DiscoveryScript::Open('1crn.pdb');
$document->GenerateDcdConformations( '1crn.dcd', True );

$document->AnimateConformations;

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->Save( "1crn_animation.dsv", "dsv" );
$document->Close();
```

# AnnotationXYZ property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/annotationxyz_property.htm

## AnnotationXYZ property

### Description

AnnotationXYZ indicates the coordinate of the annotation of a normal monitor object.

### Applies to

The AnnotationXYZ property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::NormalFeature , Mdm::NormalMonitor

### Using the AnnotationXYZ property

#### Get

my $pointObject = $object->AnnotationXYZ;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $pointObject | | | Mdm::Point |
| $object | | | Mdm::NormalFeature Mdm::NormalMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Show how to create an Mdm::NormalMonitor.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9INS.pdb" );

my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
my $aminoAcid2 = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
my $aminoAcid3 = $aminoAcids->Item(2);

my $collection = Mdm::Array::Create();
$collection->AddItem( $aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon );
$collection->AddItem( $aminoAcid2->AmideOxygen );
$collection->AddItem( $aminoAcid2->CAlpha );
$collection->AddItem( $aminoAcid3->AmideNitrogen );

my $planeMonitor = $document->CreatePlaneMonitor($collection);
my $normalMonitor =
$document->CreateNormalMonitor( $planeMonitor, $aminoAcid2->CAlpha );

my $xyz = $normalMonitor->AnnotationXYZ;
print "Annotation coordinate: $xyz->{X} \t $xyz->{Y} \t $xyz->{Z} \n";

my $normal = $normalMonitor->Normal;
print "Normal: $normal->{X} \t $normal->{Y} \t $normal->{Z} \n";

print "Normal length: $normalMonitor->{NormalLength}\n";

$document->UpdateViews;
```
