## AppendSequence function

### Description

AppendSequence appends an Sdm::Sequence to an Sdm::Alignment .

### Applies to

The AppendSequence function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the AppendSequence function

#### Instance

$object->AppendSequence( <sequence> );

$object->AppendSequence( { Sequence => <sequence> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <sequence> | Required | | Sdm::Sequence |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to copy sequences between documents
# either by insert at a specified index or appending.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $annotationDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId({Id => 'y13252', Database => "nuccore"});
my $sequence = $annotationDocument->Sequence(0);

# Append annotation window sequence to a new document.
my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateNucleotideDocument();
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();
$document->Alignment->AppendSequence($sequence);

# Insert sequence to a new document.
my $document2 = Sdm::Document::CreateNucleotideDocument();
$document2->DeleteAlignmentSequences();
$document2->Alignment->InsertSequence( 0, $sequence );
$document2->Alignment->InsertSequence( 1, $sequence );

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

# ApplyConformationDisplayToReference function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/applyconformationdisplaytoreference_function.htm

## ApplyConformationDisplayToReference function

### Description

ApplyConformationDisplayToReference applies the display settings of a conformation
to its reference.

### Applies to

The ApplyConformationDisplayToReference function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Conformation , Mdm::OfflineableConformation

### Using the ApplyConformationDisplayToReference function

#### Instance

$object->ApplyConformationDisplayToReference();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Conformation Mdm::OfflineableConformation |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use Mdm::Conformation objects.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage()
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing conformations.\n";
print " 3 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
Usage() unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage() unless ($document);

my $conformations = $document->Conformations;
Usage() unless ( $conformations->Count > 0 );

print "Getting the first conformation...\n";
my $conformation = $conformations->Item(0);

my $xyz = $conformation->ConformationXYZ(0);
print "Coordinate of first atom in this conformation: "
. $xyz->X . ","
. $xyz->Y . ","
. $xyz->Z . "\n";

$xyz->X += 0.1;
$xyz->Y += 0.1;
$xyz->Z += 0.1;
print "Changing the first atom's coordinate to: "
. $xyz->X . ","
. $xyz->Y . ","
. $xyz->Z . "\n";
$conformation->ConformationXYZ( 0, $xyz );

print "Applying the new conformation to the reference...\n";
$conformation->ApplyConformationToReference();

my $atom = $document->Atoms->Item(0);
$atom->XYZ->X -= 0.1;
print "Applying the reference to the conformation...\n";
$conformation->ApplyReferenceToConformation();

my $referenceXYZ = $conformation->ReferenceXYZ($atom);
print "Coordinate of first atom in the reference: "
. $referenceXYZ->X . ","
. $referenceXYZ->Y . ","
. $referenceXYZ->Z . "\n";

print "Applying the display data from reference to conformation...\n";
$conformation->ApplyReferenceDisplayToConformation();
print "Applying the display data from conformation to reference...\n";
$conformation->ApplyConformationDisplayToReference();
```

# ApplyForceField function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/applyforcefield_function.htm

## ApplyForceField function

### Description

ApplyForceField applies a specific forcefield to a document.

### Applies to

The ApplyForceField function can be used with the following objects:

Ffdm::Document

### Using the ApplyForceField function

#### Instance

my $forcefieldstatusEnum = $object->ApplyForceField( <mdmdocument>, [updatehydrogenatoms], [estimateparameters], [updatepartialcharges], [partialchargemethod], [localizebonds] );

my $forcefieldstatusEnum = $object->ApplyForceField( { MdmDocument => <mdmdocument>, UpdateHydrogenAtoms => [updatehydrogenatoms], EstimateParameters => [estimateparameters], UpdatePartialCharges => [updatepartialcharges], PartialChargeMethod => [partialchargemethod], LocalizeBonds => [localizebonds] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $forcefieldstatusEnum | | | enum Ffdm::ForceFieldStatus |
| <mdmdocument> | Required | | Mdm::Document |
| [estimateparameters] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [localizebonds] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [partialchargemethod] | Optional | useMomanyRonePartialCharges | enum Ffdm::PartialChargeMethod |
| [updatehydrogenatoms] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [updatepartialcharges] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Ffdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ForceFieldDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
# Demonstrate creating a force field document
# and applying a forcefield to a molecule.
use strict;
use ForceFieldDiscoveryScript;
use File::Path;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

my $tempDir = DiscoveryScript::GetTemporaryFolder()."/typingEx";

mkdir $tempDir if(not -e $tempDir);

print "Creating CHARMm force field document.\n";
my $forcefield = Ffdm::Document::Create(Ffdm::charmmForceField);

print "Applying CHARMm force field to 1crn.\n";
my $status = $forcefield->ApplyForceField( $document, True, True, True,
Ffdm::useMomanyRonePartialCharges );

if ( $status == Ffdm::applyForceFieldCompleted )
{
print "Molecule successfully typed.\n";
$forcefield->Save($tempDir.'/1crn.ffml');
}
else
{
die "Failed to type molecule.\n";
}

my @properties = ("Forcefield","PartialChargeMethod","UseResidueTemplateCharge","ForcefieldBase" );
my $molecules = $document->Molecules()->Item(0);
foreach my $pname (@properties)
{
my $prop = $molecules->GetProperty($pname);
print "$pname: $prop\n";
}

print "\tName\tType\tCharge\n";
my $atoms = $molecules->Atoms;
my $count = 0;
foreach $a (@$atoms)
{
my $fftype = $a->GetProperty('ForcefieldType');
my $ffcharge = $a->GetProperty('Partial Charge');
printf("%5d)\t%-4s\t%-4s\t%.3f\n", ++$count, $a->Name , $fftype, $ffcharge);
}

# remove file
unlink ($tempDir.'/1crn.ffml');
rmtree $tempDir;
```

# ApplyMatrix function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/applymatrix_function.htm

## ApplyMatrix function

### Description

ApplyMatrix applies the model-view transformation to the
coordinates of all objects and resets the model-view matrix.

### Applies to

The ApplyMatrix function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ApplyMatrix function

#### Command

$object->ApplyMatrix();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to apply the model-view transformation to all
# objects using the ApplyMatrix function.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Change the view angle and view position of the document.
my $firstXYZ = $document->Molecules->Item(0)->Atoms->Item(0)->XYZ;
printf "Atom 1 before translation XYZ: %.5f %.5f %.5f\n", $firstXYZ->X,$firstXYZ->Z,$firstXYZ->Y;
$document->RotateView( 20.0, 30.0, 40.0 );
$document->Translate( 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 );

# Saving without applying matrix save the original coordinates.
# $document->Save( '1crnOriginalXyz.pdb', 'pdb' );

$document->ApplyMatrix();
$firstXYZ = $document->Molecules->Item(0)->Atoms->Item(0)->XYZ;
printf "Atom 1 after translation XYZ: %.5f %.5f %.5f\n", $firstXYZ->X,$firstXYZ->Z,$firstXYZ->Y;

# After applying the view matrix, the saved coordinates reflect the view.
# $document->Save( '1crnViewedXyz.pdb', 'pdb' );
```

# ApplyRotamer function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/applyrotamer_function.htm

## ApplyRotamer function

### Description

Applies a rotamer to an amino acid. The function has two required arguments
specifying the rotamer number, which must lie between 1 and RotamerCount, and
the amino acid object that is to have its chi angles adjusted. There is
also an optional argument specifying the rotamer library to be used, which
defaults to Mdm::ponderAndRichardsRotamerLibrary, the other valid options
being Mdm::sutcliffeRotamerLibrary, Mdm::oldfieldRotamerLibrary and
Mdm::richardsonAndRichardsonRotamerLibrary.

After execution of this function, the amino acid will be in the conformation
defined by the specified rotamer.

### Applies to

The ApplyRotamer function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ApplyRotamer function

#### Instance

my $booleanValue = $object->ApplyRotamer( <rotamernumber>, <residue>, [rotamerlibrary] );

my $booleanValue = $object->ApplyRotamer( { RotamerNumber => <rotamernumber>, Residue => <residue>, RotamerLibrary => [rotamerlibrary] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| <residue> | Required | | Mdm::AminoAcid |
| <rotamernumber> | Required | | Integer |
| [rotamerlibrary] | Optional | ponderAndRichardsRotamerLibrary | enum Mdm::RotamerLibrary |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

#Script which demonstrates how to step through rotamers for an amino acid
#including some methods of assessment.
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# create an array of all aminoacids in the system
my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;

#get one to search - (this is TYR29)
my $aminoAcid = $aminoAcids->Item(28);

# retrieve the residue name
my $aminoAcidName = $aminoAcid->Name;

#and the atoms - we really only want the sidechain. There may be a better way to do this!
my $aaAtoms = $aminoAcid->Atoms;
my $sideChainAtoms = Mdm::Array::Create();
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $aaAtoms->Count ; ++$i )
{
my $atomName = $aaAtoms->Item($i)->Name;
if ( ( $atomName ne 'N' )
&& ( $atomName ne 'CA' )
&& ( $atomName ne 'C' )
&& ( $atomName ne 'O' )
&& ( $atomName ne 'HN' )
&& ( $atomName ne 'HA' ) )
{
$sideChainAtoms->AddItem( $aaAtoms->Item($i) );
}
}

#Get the original coordinates so we can restore them at the end if we want to
my $originalCoordinates = Mdm::PointArray::Create();
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $sideChainAtoms->Count ; ++$i )
{
$originalCoordinates->AddItem( $sideChainAtoms->[$i]->XYZ );
}

#Make some monitors so we can assess the rotamers
my $bumpMonitor = $document->CreateBumpMonitor( $sideChainAtoms, False );
print
"Number of bumps to original side-chain position: $bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} \n";
my $hbondMonitor = $document->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( $sideChainAtoms,
Mdm::allAtomHydrogenBonds, Mdm::allMolecularHydrogenBonds );
print
"Number of hydrogen bonds between side-chain and the rest of protein $hbondMonitor->{HydrogenBondCount}\n";
print "\nPerforming rotamer search for $aminoAcidName \n";

my $numRotamers =
$document->RotamerCount( $aminoAcid, Mdm::oldfieldRotamerLibrary );
print "Number of rotamers is $numRotamers\n";

if ( $numRotamers > 0 )
{
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i <= $numRotamers ; ++$i )
{
my $probability = $document->RotamerProbability( $i, $aminoAcid,
Mdm::oldfieldRotamerLibrary );
print "Applying rotamer $i, probability $probability\n";
$document->ApplyRotamer( $i, $aminoAcid,
Mdm::oldfieldRotamerLibrary );

#Check the number of bumps and hbonds. One might want to keep track of fewest bumps/most hbonds
#to decide which monitor to
print
"Number of bumps $bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} ;number of hydrogen bonds $hbondMonitor->{HydrogenBondCount}\n";

#for demo purposes so we can see each rotamer
sleep(2);
}
}

#restore original
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $sideChainAtoms->Count ; ++$i )
{
$sideChainAtoms->[$i]->XYZ = $originalCoordinates->[$i];
}
```

# ApplyTransformationMatrices function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/applytransformationmatrices_function.htm

## ApplyTransformationMatrices function

### Description

ApplyTransformationMatrices applies a collection of matrices specifying geometric transformations
(e.g., rotations and translations) to a molecule.

### Applies to

The ApplyTransformationMatrices function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ApplyTransformationMatrices function

#### Instance

$object->ApplyTransformationMatrices( <molecule>, <arrayofmatrixnames>, [applytoselectedonly] );

$object->ApplyTransformationMatrices( { Molecule => <molecule>, ArrayOfMatrixNames => <arrayofmatrixnames>, ApplyToSelectedOnly => [applytoselectedonly] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <arrayofmatrixnames> | Required | | DiscoveryScript::StringArray |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| [applytoselectedonly] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Example for the ApplyTransformationMatrices function.
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Get the active Molecule Window
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1LP3.pdb" );
die "The document could not be opened" unless $document;

# Return an error message and exit if there is not an active Molecule Window
die "No Molecule Window!" unless $document;

# Get the molecules from the document
my $molecules = $document->Molecules();
die "No collection of molecule objects" unless $molecules;
die "No molecules" unless $molecules->Count > 0;

my $molecule = $molecules->[0];

my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
die "No collection of chain objects" unless $chains;

my $countChains = $chains->Count;
print "Number of chains in initial structure: " . $countChains . "\n";

my $names = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
# possibly up to 60 in this case.
for (my $i=2; $i<=6; $i++)
{
$names->AddItem("BIOMT_$i");
}

$document->ApplyTransformationMatrices($molecule, $names);

$chains = $molecule->Chains;
die "No collection of chain objects" unless $chains;

$countChains = $chains->Count;
print "Number of chains in final structure: " . $countChains . "\n";

$document->Close();
$document = undef;
```

# ApplyTransformationMatrix function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/applytransformationmatrix_function.htm

## ApplyTransformationMatrix function

### Description

ApplyTransformationMatrix applies a matrix specifying a geometric transformation
such as rotation or translation to a molecule.

### Applies to

The ApplyTransformationMatrix function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ApplyTransformationMatrix function

#### Instance

$object->ApplyTransformationMatrix( <molecule>, [matrixname], [applytoselectedonly], [createcopy] );

$object->ApplyTransformationMatrix( { Molecule => <molecule>, MatrixName => [matrixname], ApplyToSelectedOnly => [applytoselectedonly], CreateCopy => [createcopy] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| [applytoselectedonly] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [createcopy] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [matrixname] | Optional | "NCS" | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrates the transformation matrix properties and functions.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1rvf');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $ncsMatrixName = 'BIOMT_4';

my $translateX = 0.0;
my $translateY = 0.0;
my $translateZ = 0.0;

my $ncsMatrix = Mdm::Matrix4x4::Create(
-0.309017, 0.500000, 0.809017, 0.0,
-0.500000, -0.809017, 0.309017, 0.0,
0.809017, -0.309017, 0.500000, 0.0,
$translateX, $translateY, $translateZ, 1.0
);

# Add a transformation matrix to a molecule and
# verify the matrix exists a property of the molecule.
$molecule->NcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName) = $ncsMatrix;
print "Found matrix $ncsMatrixName.\n"
if ( $molecule->HasNcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName) );

# Apply the transformation matrix to molecule's coordinates.
$document->ApplyTransformationMatrix( $molecule, $ncsMatrixName );

# Remove the matrix from molecule.
$molecule->RemoveNcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName);
print "Removed matrix $ncsMatrixName.\n"
if ( not $molecule->HasNcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName) );
```

# ApproximateVolume property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/approximatevolume_property.htm

## ApproximateVolume property

### Description

ApproximateVolume indicates an approximate volume of a molecule. It is calculated as the total van der Waals volume of all the atoms subtracted by the overlap volume of bonded atoms, and scaled to 95%. The resulting volume is estimated to be 4% of the true volume using a small test set.

### Applies to

The ApproximateVolume property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the ApproximateVolume property

| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

MdmDiscoveryScript

```text
$molecule->IsChargeCalculated = True;

print "The following is a list of molecule properties:\n";
print 'Name: ' . $molecule->Name . "\n";
print 'Approximate volume: ' . $molecule->ApproximateVolume . "\n";
print 'Atom count: ' . $molecule->AtomCount . "\n";

my $centerOfMass = $molecule->CenterOfMass;

print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
```

my $realValue = $object->Area;

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |

| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Surface |

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to create a transparent surface.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '101m.pdb' );

# Select heme atoms.
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="HEM.*"; Atom label="*"');

# Create an array of all heme atoms.
my $hemeAtoms = $document->Filter( { Selected => 1 } )->Atoms;

# Create transparent surface around the heme group.
my $transparentSurface =
$document->CreateTransparentSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential,
1.3, 0.6 );

$transparentSurface->IsBackSideColorEnabled(True);
$transparentSurface->IsBackSideTransparencyEnabled(True);

# Also create wiremesh surface around the heme group.
my $wiremeshSurface =
$document->CreateWiremeshSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential, 2.0 );

print "Surface area: "
. $transparentSurface->Area . "\n"
. "Surface Volume: "
. $transparentSurface->Volume . "\n";
print "Surface probe radius: "
. $transparentSurface->ProbeRadius . "\n"
. "Transparency Level: "
. $transparentSurface->TransparencyLevel . "\n";

# Select all atoms within 6A of the heme and the surface.
$document->SelectByRadius( 6.0, 'Atom' );
$transparentSurface->Select();

# Show only the heme and neighboring atoms (other than water).
$document->FitView();
$document->InvertSelection();
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue name="HOH.*"; Atom label="*"');
$document->Hide();
$document->DeselectAll();

# Display the wiremesh surface with delay.
sleep(2);
$wiremeshSurface->SetVisible();
```

# AromaticRingCount property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/aromaticringcount_property.htm

## AromaticRingCount property

### Description

AromaticRingCount specifies the number of aromatic rings by an Mdm::RingPerception .

### Applies to

The AromaticRingCount property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::RingPerception

### Using the AromaticRingCount property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->AromaticRingCount;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::RingPerception |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the perceive rings class.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $smilesString =
'O=C(C/C1=C/C=C[S]1)N(Cc2ccccc2OC)[C@@]([H])(c3cc(OC)c(cc3)OC)C(=O)N[C@]4([H])CCCCC4';

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles($smilesString);

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
foreach my $molecule (@$molecules)
{
my $ringPerception = $molecule->PerceiveRings(
{
FindSmallestSetOfRings => True,
PerceiveAromaticity => True,
FindLonePairDonors => True
}
);

my $ringCount = $ringPerception->RingCount;
my $aromaticRingCount = $ringPerception->AromaticRingCount;

print "Ring analysis of molecule: $smilesString\n";
print "Molecule has: " . $ringCount . " rings\n";
print "Molecule has: " . $aromaticRingCount . " aromatic rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all atoms in rings.
my $ringAtoms = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedRingAtoms;
print "Molecule has: " . $ringAtoms->Count . " atoms in rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all bonds in rings.
my $ringBonds = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedRingBonds;
print "Molecule has: " . $ringBonds->Count . " bonds in rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all aromatic bonds in rings.
my $aromaticRingBonds = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedAromaticRingBonds;
print "Molecule has: "
. $aromaticRingBonds->Count
. " aromatic bonds in rings.\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all lone pair donor atoms in aromatic rings.
my $lonePairDonors = $ringPerception->PerceivedLonePairDonors;
print "Molecule has: "
. $lonePairDonors->Count
. " lone pair donor atoms in rings.\n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $ringCount ; ++$index )
{

# Get an Mdm::Array of atoms in the specified ring.
my $atoms = $ringPerception->PerceivedRingAtoms($index);

# Get an Mdm::Array of bonds in the specified ring.
my $bonds = $ringPerception->PerceivedRingBonds($index);

my $ringnum = $index + 1;
print "Ring ( $ringnum ) contains "
. $atoms->Count
. " atoms and "
. $bonds->Count
. " bonds.\n";
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# Array property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/array_property.htm

## Array property

### Description

Array specifies an Mdm::Array of child objects in an Mdm::Group object.

### Applies to

The Array property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Group

### Using the Array property

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->Array;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::Group |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

# Use DSCommands to get all ligands.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);

# Create a ligand group.
my $group = $document->CreateGroup( "Ligands", $ligands );

# Get the group name.
print "Group name: " . $group->Name . "\n";

# Get the array of objects in the group, in no particular order.
my $ligand_array = $group->Array;

print "Group members:\n";
foreach my $ligand (sort {$a->Name cmp $b->Name} @$ligand_array)
{
printf "%s\n", $ligand->Name;
}

# Get the array of objects in the group in the order in which they
# would appear when performing a depth first traversal of the
# object hierarchy starting from the root object
$ligand_array = $group->ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder();

print "Group members:\n";
foreach my $ligand (@$ligand_array)
{
printf "%s\n", $ligand->Name;
}

# Remove group.

my $left = Mdm::Group::RemoveGroup($group);
printf "Items left in group after removal: %d\n", $left;
```

# ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/arrayindepthfirsthierarchyorder_property.htm

## ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder property

### Description

ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder specifies an Mdm::Array of child objects in an Mdm::Group object, with the objects returned in a reproducible order.

### Applies to

The ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Group

### Using the ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder property

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::Group |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrates how to find all residues belonging to the 
# same ligand as a given residue.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use MdmCommands;
use strict;

# Load an example structure.
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('2AEP');
die "Failed to create a valid MDM document!" unless $document;

# Pick a specific target ligand residue in the structure.
my $ligandResidue = SelectByString($document,"NAG1");
my $queryResidue = $ligandResidue->Residues->Item(0);
my $queryResidueId = $queryResidue->UniqueId;

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

# This creates/updates the ligand groups. Each ligand 
# consists of a set of covalently bonded residues.
my $nLigands = $molecule->PerceiveLigandGroups( 
{ MaximumNumberOfHeavyAtoms => 100, RequireCarbonContent => True } );

# Get the ligand group assembly.
my $ligandGroups = $molecule->Filter( 
{ Type=>"Assembly", Property => "Name", Name => "Ligand Groups" } );
if ($ligandGroups->Count == 1) {

# Iterate over all ligands groups.
my $ligands = $ligandGroups->Item(0)->Groups; 
foreach my $ligand (@$ligands) { 

# Get the group content in a defined order.
# Use Array() if the order in which group members are returned
# is not important.
my $ligandResidueList = $ligand->ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder();
my $found = 0;
# Check if this is the group that contains the target residue.
foreach my $ligandResidue (@$ligandResidueList ) {

if ( $ligandResidue->IsA('Mdm::Residue') ) {
if ($ligandResidue->UniqueId == $queryResidueId) {

$found = 1;
last;
}
}
}

# Print out information about the ligand if we found it.
if ($found) {

print "Found residue " . $queryResidue->Name . 
" in " . $ligand->Name . ".\n";

print "This Ligand Consists of residue(s):\n";
foreach my $ligandResidue (@$ligandResidueList ) {
print " - " .$ligandResidue->Name . "\n";
}

$ligand->Select();
last;
}
}
}

print "Done\n";
```

# Atom1 property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/atom1_property.htm

## Atom1 property

### Description

Atom1 specifies the first of two atoms connected by a bond or being monitored.

### Applies to

The Atom1 property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Bond , Mdm::Bump , Mdm::CAlphaPair , Mdm::ConformerBond , Mdm::HydrogenBond , Mdm::Neighbor

### Using the Atom1 property

#### Get

my $atomObject = $object->Atom1;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $atomObject | | | Mdm::Atom |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how use the hydrogen bond monitor and to change the distance cutoff.

use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Creates a hbond monitor between ligand atoms and receptor
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $LigName = $ligands->Item(0)->Name;
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $monitor = $document->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( $ligandAtoms,
Mdm::allAtomHydrogenBonds, Mdm::allMolecularHydrogenBonds );

# Shows the label for each of the hbonds
$monitor->IsLabelShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll(); 

printf "Default distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->DefaultDistanceCriterion;
printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor.\n\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $newHBDist = 3.0;
$monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared( $newHBDist* $newHBDist );

# update view to ensure the correct HB count
$document->UpdateViews();
printf "Set the distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared;

printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor:\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $hbonds = $document->HydrogenBonds;
my $count = $hbonds->Count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $hbond = $hbonds->Item($index);
my $dist = $hbond->Distance;
my $atom1 = $hbond->Atom1;
my $atom2 = $hbond->Atom2;
my $res = $atom1->Parent;

if ( $res->Name eq $LigName ) {
$atom2->Parent->Select; 
}
else{
$atom1->Parent->Select; 
}
printf "%d) Distance: %.3f A H-bond between Atom %s:%s:%s and Atom %s:%s:%s\n",
$index+1, $dist,
$atom1->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom1->Parent->Name, $atom1->Name,
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name ;
} 

$document->FitView(); 
my $display_style = { DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' };
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle($display_style);
$document->DeselectAll();
```

```text
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $LigName = $ligands->Item(0)->Name;
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $monitor = $document->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( $ligandAtoms,
Mdm::allAtomHydrogenBonds, Mdm::allMolecularHydrogenBonds );

# Shows the label for each of the hbonds
$monitor->IsLabelShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll(); 

printf "Default distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->DefaultDistanceCriterion;
printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor.\n\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $newHBDist = 3.0;
$monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared( $newHBDist* $newHBDist );

# update view to ensure the correct HB count
$document->UpdateViews();
printf "Set the distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared;

printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor:\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $hbonds = $document->HydrogenBonds;
my $count = $hbonds->Count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $hbond = $hbonds->Item($index);
my $dist = $hbond->Distance;
my $atom1 = $hbond->Atom1;
my $atom2 = $hbond->Atom2;
my $res = $atom1->Parent;

if ( $res->Name eq $LigName ) {
$atom2->Parent->Select; 
}
else{
$atom1->Parent->Select; 
}
printf "%d) Distance: %.3f A H-bond between Atom %s:%s:%s and Atom %s:%s:%s\n",
$index+1, $dist,
$atom1->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom1->Parent->Name, $atom1->Name,
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name ;
} 

$document->FitView(); 
my $display_style = { DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' };
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle($display_style);
$document->DeselectAll();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to convert an amino acid property
# (Hydrophobicity) to an atom property and color the atoms by the
# new Hydrophobicity property.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

my $atoms = $document->Atoms;

# For each atom, create a Hydrophobicity property with
# the value of its parent residue's Hydrophobicity.
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
my $residue = $atom->Parent;
my $hydrophobicity = $residue->Hydrophobicity;
$atom->SetProperty( 'Hydrophobicity', $hydrophobicity );
}

# Color the atoms by the new atomic Hydrophobicity property.
$document->SetAtomPropertyColorScheme(
{
PropertyName => 'Hydrophobicity',
SpectrumType => Mdm::spectrumRedWhiteBlue,
NumberOfBands => 32,
RangeMinimum => -10,
RangeMaximum => 10,
Clip => 0
}
);

printf "Molecule Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$document->ModelName,$atoms->Count();
```

# AttachedAtom property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/attachedatom_property.htm

## AttachedAtom property

### Description

AttachedAtom indicates one of the atoms ( Mdm::Atom ) bonded
to this atom. Use BondCount to find the number of attached atoms.

### Applies to

The AttachedAtom property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Atom , Mdm::ConformerAtom

### Using the AttachedAtom property

#### Get

my $atomObject = $object->AttachedAtom( <index> );

my $atomObject = $object->AttachedAtom( { Index => <index> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $atomObject | | | Mdm::Atom |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Atom Mdm::ConformerAtom |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

# AttributeMap property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/attributemap_property.htm

## AttributeMap property

### Description

AttributeMap specifies key value data of an Sdm::ObjectWithAttributes .

### Applies to

The AttributeMap property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment , Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::Feature , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::ObjectWithAttributes , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the AttributeMap property

#### Get

my $attributemapObject = $object->AttributeMap;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $attributemapObject | | | Sdm::AttributeMap |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the Sdm::AttributeMap.
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $mdm = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('4phv');
my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures($mdm);
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

# Copy current document state to object attributes. Generally the 
# attribute data is not updated after loading a BSML file. To get 
# the current state as attributes call this function. 
$document->ClearBsmlAttributes();
$document->BuildBsmlAttributes();

# List the Alignment object attributes.
print "Alignment attributes...\n";
my $attributes = $alignment->AttributeMap;
my $key = $attributes->FirstKey;
while (!$key->IsEndKey)
{
print $key->Name . ":\t" . $attributes->Item($key) . "\n";
$key = $attributes->NextKey($key);
}
print "end\n\n";

# List the Sequence object attributes.
my $sequences = $document->Sequences;
my $i = 0;
foreach my $sequence (@$sequences)
{
print "Sequence $i attributes...\n";
my $attributes = $sequence->AttributeMap;
my $key = $attributes->FirstKey;
while (!$key->IsEndKey)
{
print $key->Name . ":\t" . $attributes->Item($key) . "\n";
$key = $attributes->NextKey($key);
}
print "end\n\n";

my $k = $attributes->FindItem('ResidueID');
print 'Find Name: ' . $k->Name . "\tValue: "
. $attributes->Item($k) . "\n\n";

# List the Feature object attributes.
my $features = $sequence->Features;
my $f = 0;
foreach my $feature (@$features)
{
print "Feature $f attributes...\n";
my $fattributes = $feature->AttributeMap;
my $fkey = $fattributes->FirstKey;
print $feature->Key . "\n";
while (!$fkey->IsEndKey)
{
print $fkey->Name . ":\t" . $fattributes->Item($fkey) . "\n";
$fkey = $fattributes->NextKey($fkey);
}

print "end\n\n";
++$f;
} 

++$i; 
}

# Update the current document to match attribute data.
$document->UpdateFromBsmlAttributes();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

| <authors> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Sdm::Publication |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Publication class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'Y13252-truncated',
'TCTAGAGTAACATTTAGAATTAAGGTGGGAAATTATCTTAAAATCT' );

my $title =
'Nonfixed duplication containing the Adh gene and a truncated form '
. 'of the Adhr gene in the Drosophila funebris species group: different '
. 'modes of evolution of Adh relative to Adhr in Drosophila';

# Create publication object with sample data.
my $publication01 = Sdm::Publication::Create( 'Amador, A., Juan, E.',
$title, 'Molec. Biol. Evol.' );

# Create publication and add content separately.
my $publication02 = Sdm::Publication::Create();
$publication02->Authors = 'Amador, A., Juan, E.';
$publication02->Title = $title;
$publication02->Journal = 'Molec. Biol. Evol.';
$publication02->Reference = '16(11): 1439--1456 (1999)';
$publication02->PubMedId = '10555275';
$publication02->Comment = 'y13252';

#$publication02->Consortium = '';
#$publication02->DigitalObjectId = '';
#$publication02->MedlineId = '';
#$publication02->PubMedId = '';

# Associate publications with a sequence object.
# NOTE: To see the publications in Discovery Studio, double-click on the
# sequence in the sequence window to open a sequence annotation window.
# Publications are listed in the data table's Literature Citation tab.
$sequence->AddPublication($publication01);
$sequence->AddPublication($publication02);

my $publicationCount = $sequence->PublicationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $publicationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $publication = $sequence->Publication($index);
printf "%d: %s, %s. %s %s.\n",
$index + 1,
$publication->Authors,
$publication->Title,
$publication->Journal,
$publication->Reference;
}

$sequence->DeletePublication(0);
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w

. $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount . "\n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $operator = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperator($index);
print "Symmetry operator $index\n";
print "\tName: " . $operator->Name . "\n";

my $rotation = $operator->Rotation;
my $format = "\t %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n";
print "\tRotation Matrix:\n";
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 0, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 1, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 2 );

my $translation = $operator->Translation;
print "\tTranslation:\n";
printf "$format", $translation->X, $translation->Y, $translation->Z;
}
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use the Mdm::Color object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1CRN.pdb" );
die "Failed to open MDM document." unless $document;

my $chain = $document->AminoAcidChains->Item(0);
die "Molecule contains no chains." unless $chain;

# This example assumes the protein display is on.
# Ensure this is the case here.
$document->SelectByProperty('Atom Name="*"');
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleAtomStick);
$document->DeselectAll();
$chain->DisplayStyle = Mdm::styleProteinRibbonTube;

print "Select cysteine residues and color them orange...\n\n";
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="CYS.*" ; Atom Name="*"');
my $cysteines = $document->SelectedObjects();
die "No cysteine residues." unless ($cysteines && $cysteines->Count > 0);
my $color = Mdm::Color::Create();
$color->Red = 255;
$color->Green = 200;
$color->Blue = 0;
$document->SetColor($color);
$document->DeselectAll();

print "Coloring the ribbon pseudo-transparent...\n\n";
my $chain = $document->Chains()->Item(0);
my $color = Mdm::Color::Create();
$color->Red = 0;
$color->Green = 255;
$color->Blue = 0;
$color->Alpha = 128;
$chain->Color($color);

print "Coloring the background dark blue...\n\n";
my $bkColor = Mdm::Color::Create();
$bkColor->Red = 0;
$bkColor->Green = 0;
$bkColor->Blue = 100;
$document->BackgroundColor = $bkColor;
```

# BackgroundColorScheme property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

## BackgroundColorScheme property

### Description

BackgroundColorScheme specifies how to color the residue background in the Sequence Window.

### Applies to

The BackgroundColorScheme property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the BackgroundColorScheme property

#### Get

my $colorschemeEnum = $object->BackgroundColorScheme;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $colorschemeEnum | | | enum Sdm::ColorScheme |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Set

$object->BackgroundColorScheme = [scheme];

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [scheme] | Optional | Sdm::colorBySequenceSimilarity | enum Sdm::ColorScheme |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to custom color the alignment window.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $sequence0 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'ASDFASD' );
my $sequence1 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S2', 'ASDFASD' );

# Enable custom coloring of residues (instead of auto coloring).
# NOTE: The existing colors are not changed until individual
# residues are colored
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
$alignment->BackgroundColorScheme = Sdm::colorByCustomColor;
$alignment->ForegroundColorScheme = Sdm::colorByCustomColor;

my $black = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 0, 0, 0 );
my $white = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 255, 255, 255 );

# Reset the colors to black text on a white background.
my $sequenceCount = $alignment->SequenceCount;
my $residueFgColorType = Sdm::colorText;
my $residueBgColorType = Sdm::colorBackground;
for (
my $sequenceIndex = 0 ;
$sequenceIndex < $sequenceCount ;
++$sequenceIndex
)
{
my $sequence = $alignment->Sequence($sequenceIndex);
my $residueCount = $sequence->ResidueCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $residueCount ; ++$index )
{
$sequence->Residue($index)->Color( $residueFgColorType, $black );
$sequence->Residue($index)->Color( $residueBgColorType, $white );
}
}

# Apply custom colors to residues foreground.
my $count = $sequence0->ResidueCount;
my $color = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 255, 0, 0 );
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
$sequence0->Residue($index)->Color( Sdm::colorText, $color );
}

$alignment->Sequence(2)->IsVisible = True;
$document->UpdateViews();

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

# BeginBatch function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/beginbatch_function.htm

## BeginBatch function

### Description

BeginBatch begins a batch molecule or conformation property update
on a document. It is complemented by EndBatch which ends a batch
molecule or conformation property update on a document.
Any molecule or conformation property modifications made between
a pair of BeginBatch and EndBatch statements will result in a bulk
update of these properties, which can result in a significant
improvement in performance.

### Applies to

The BeginBatch function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the BeginBatch function

#### Instance

$object->BeginBatch();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w

use strict;

use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use Time::HiRes qw(time);
use POSIX qw(strftime);

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
my $molecule = $molecules->Item(0);

for (my $i = 0; $i < 1000; ++$i) {
my $name = "Property #" . ($i + 1);
$molecule->SetProperty($name, "DATA");
}

my $t = time;
$document->WaitForUpdater();
$t = time - $t;
print "Time spent waiting = " . sprintf("%.3f seconds\n", $t) ;

$document->BeginBatch();
for (my $i = 0; $i < 1000; ++$i) {
my $name = "Property #" . ($i + 1);
$molecule->SetProperty($name, "MORE DATA");
}
$document->EndBatch();

$t = time;
$document->WaitForUpdater();
$t = time - $t;
print "Time spent waiting = " . sprintf("%.3f seconds\n", $t) ;

$t = time;
$document->Save("Output.dsv", "dsv");
$t = time - $t;
print "Time spent saving = " . sprintf("%.3f seconds\n", $t) ;

$document->Close();
```

### Using the BindingSitePoints filter

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->BindingSitePoints;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the use of BindingSite objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

Delete( $document, GetLigands($document) );
Delete( $document, GetWaters($document) );

my $protein = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

# Find all binding site from receptor cavities.
my $bindingSites = $document->CreateBindingSitesFromCavities($protein);
print "Number of binding sites found: " . $bindingSites->Count . "\n";

# Loop through all binding sites and determine volume, point count
# and min/max dimension.
my $bsCount = 0;

foreach my $s (@$bindingSites)
{
my $volume = $s->GetProperty("Volume");
my $bcount = $s->BindingSitePoints->Count;
my $bindingSitePoints = $s->BindingSitePoints;
print " Site: " . ++$bsCount . "\n";
print "\tVolume: $volume\n";
print "\tPoint count: $bcount\n";

# Loop over the binding site points to find
# the minimum and maximum values.
my $max = Mdm::Point::Create( -1.e6, -1.e6, -1.e6 );
my $min = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.e6, 1.e6, 1.e6 );
foreach my $xyz (@$bindingSitePoints)
{
$max->X = $xyz->XYZ->X if ( $max->X < $xyz->XYZ->X );
$max->Y = $xyz->XYZ->Y if ( $max->Y < $xyz->XYZ->Y );
$max->Z = $xyz->XYZ->Z if ( $max->Z < $xyz->XYZ->Z );
$min->X = $xyz->XYZ->X if ( $min->X > $xyz->XYZ->X );
$min->Y = $xyz->XYZ->Y if ( $min->Y > $xyz->XYZ->Y );
$min->Z = $xyz->XYZ->Z if ( $min->Z > $xyz->XYZ->Z );
}
print "\tSite Minimum: x: "
. $min->X . " y: "
. $min->Y . " z: "
. $min->Z . "\n";
print "\tSite Maximum: x: "
. $max->X . " y: "
. $max->Y . " z: "
. $max->Z . "\n";
}
```

Source type: HTML

## Blue property

### Description

Blue defines the intensity of blue in the color. Valid values are between 0 and 255.

### Applies to

The Blue property can be used with the following objects:

DiscoveryScript::Color , Mdm::Color

### Using the Blue property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->Blue;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | DiscoveryScript::Color Mdm::Color |

#### Set

$object->Blue = <b>;

$object->Blue( <b> );

$object->Blue( { B => <b> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <b> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | DiscoveryScript::Color Mdm::Color |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use the Mdm::Color object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1CRN.pdb" );
die "Failed to open MDM document." unless $document;

my $chain = $document->AminoAcidChains->Item(0);
die "Molecule contains no chains." unless $chain;

# This example assumes the protein display is on.
# Ensure this is the case here.
$document->SelectByProperty('Atom Name="*"');
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleAtomStick);
$document->DeselectAll();
$chain->DisplayStyle = Mdm::styleProteinRibbonTube;

print "Select cysteine residues and color them orange...\n\n";
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="CYS.*" ; Atom Name="*"');
my $cysteines = $document->SelectedObjects();
die "No cysteine residues." unless ($cysteines && $cysteines->Count > 0);
my $color = Mdm::Color::Create();
$color->Red = 255;
$color->Green = 200;
$color->Blue = 0;
$document->SetColor($color);
$document->DeselectAll();

print "Coloring the ribbon pseudo-transparent...\n\n";
my $chain = $document->Chains()->Item(0);
my $color = Mdm::Color::Create();
$color->Red = 0;
$color->Green = 255;
$color->Blue = 0;
$color->Alpha = 128;
$chain->Color($color);

print "Coloring the background dark blue...\n\n";
my $bkColor = Mdm::Color::Create();
$bkColor->Red = 0;
$bkColor->Green = 0;
$bkColor->Blue = 100;
$document->BackgroundColor = $bkColor;
```

```text
use strict;

my $residueAtomName = 'THR2:CA';

{
($residueAtomName) = @ARGV;
}

print 'Formal Charge: '
. $atom->FormalCharge->Numerator . "/"
. $atom->FormalCharge->Denominator . "\n";

print 'VDW Radius: ' . $atom->VdwRadius . "\n";
print 'Covalent Radius: ' . $atom->CovalentRadius . "\n";
print 'Chirality: ' . $atom->Chirality . "\n";
print 'Bond count: ' . $atom->BondCount . "\n";
print 'Bonding radius: ' . $atom->BondingRadius . "\n";
print 'Hybridization: ' . $atom->Hybridization . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen Count: ' . $atom->HydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'ImplicitHydrogen Count: ' . $atom->ImplicitHydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Acceptor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondAcceptor . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Donor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondDonor . "\n";
print 'Isotropic Displacement: ' . $atom->IsotropicDisplacement . "\n";
print 'Is Terminal Hydrogen: ' . $atom->IsTerminalHydrogen . "\n";

printf "\n%s:\n", 'Display Properties';

print 'Stick Radius: ' . $atom->StickRadius . "\n";
```

# BondOrder property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/bondorder_property.htm

## BondOrder property

### Description

BondOrder is the order of a bond.
For example, a double bond has bond order 2.

### Applies to

The BondOrder property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Bond , Mdm::ConformerBond

### Using the BondOrder property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->BondOrder;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Bond Mdm::ConformerBond |

#### Set

$object->BondOrder = <bondorder>;

$object->BondOrder( <bondorder> );

$object->BondOrder( { BondOrder => <bondorder> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <bondorder> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Bond Mdm::ConformerBond |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

#### Get

##### Parameters

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to perceive aromatic bonds.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Subroutine to print bond orders and formal charges.
sub ListBondOrderAndCharge($$)
{
my ( $document, $bonds ) = @_;

my $index = 0;
foreach my $b (@$bonds)
{
my $charge1 =
$b->Atom1->FormalCharge->Numerator /
$b->Atom1->FormalCharge->Denominator;
my $charge2 =
$b->Atom2->FormalCharge->Numerator /
$b->Atom2->FormalCharge->Denominator;
print ++$index
. ') Bond: '
. $b->Atom1->Name . "("
. $charge2 . ") to:"
. $b->Atom2->Name . " ("
. $charge2 . ")"
. " order: "
. $b->BondOrder . "\n";
}
print "\n";
sleep(3);
$document->UpdateViews();
}

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1C(=O)[O-]');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $bonds = $molecule->Bonds;
my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms;
print "Initial formal charges and bonds orders:\n";
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );

print "Modified formal charges and bonds orders...\n";
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( $atom->Element eq 'O' )
{
$atom->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 2 );
my $carbon = $atom->AttachedAtom(0);
my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $carbon, $atom );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::partialDoubleBond;
}
}
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );

print "Localizing bond orders and formal charges...\n\n";
$molecule->LocalizeBonds();
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );

print "De-localizing bond orders and formal charges...\n\n";
$molecule->PerceiveAromaticBonds();
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

# Boolean datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/boolean_datatype.htm

## Boolean datatype

### Description

The Boolean is a native datatype that can either be True or
False. Non-zero values are considered True values and zero values are
considered False. The constants True and False can be used in scripts.

Note. Because all non-zero values are considered True, you should not
compare a Boolean value returned from a function or property directly
with True. Instead, consider comparing implicitly, such as in the coding
example below. Use the True and False constants when passing in Boolean
values to functions or properties.

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/bottomcenter_property.htm

## BottomCenter property

### Description

BottomCenter specifies a cylinder object's bottom center point.

### Applies to

The BottomCenter property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Cylinder

### Using the BottomCenter property

Please see the description of the Mdm::Point for more information about modifying returned Mdm::Point instances.

#### Get

my $pointObject = $object->BottomCenter;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $pointObject | | | Mdm::Point |
| $object | | | Mdm::Cylinder |

#### Set

$object->BottomCenter = <xyz>;

$object->BottomCenter( <xyz> );

$object->BottomCenter( { XYZ => <xyz> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <xyz> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| $object | | | Mdm::Cylinder |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Creates an empty molecule
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();

# Create oxygen atoms
my $O1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);
my $O2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

# Assign coordinates to atoms
my $xyz1 = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O1->XYZ = $xyz1;

my $xyz2 = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O2->XYZ = $xyz2;

# Create Spheres centered on atom position
my $sphere1 = $O1->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz1, Radius => 0.4 } );
my $sphere2 = $O2->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz2, Radius => 0.4 } );

# Create Cylinder
my $cylinder =
$O1->CreateCylinder( { Begin => $xyz1, End => $xyz2, Radius => 0.2 } );
my $bottom = $cylinder->{BottomCenter};
printf "Cylinder bottom center: %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n Radius: %8.3f\n",
$bottom->X, $bottom->Y, $bottom->Z, $cylinder->Radius;

# Make cylinder transparent
$cylinder->IsTransparent(True);

# Create a slicing plane perpendicular to the cylinder axis
my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
my $slicingplaneObject = $document->CreateSlicingPlane(
{
Index => 1,
ArrayOfObjects => $atoms,
Origin => Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 ),
Normal => Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 )
}
);

# Get all 3D Objects
my $objects3d = $document->Geometric3ds;

# Print their name and class name
foreach my $object (@$objects3d)
{
print $object->ClassName . "\t" . $object->Name . "\n";
}

# Get all slicing planes
my $slicplanes = $document->SlicingPlanes;
print "Number of slicing planes" . $slicplanes->Count. "\n";
```

# BreakSequenceStructureLink function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/breaksequencestructurelink_function.htm

## BreakSequenceStructureLink function

### Description

BreakSequenceStructureLink breaks the connection between a Sdm::Sequence and a Mdm::Molecule .

### Applies to

The BreakSequenceStructureLink function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the BreakSequenceStructureLink function

#### Instance

$object->BreakSequenceStructureLink( <sequence> );

$object->BreakSequenceStructureLink( { Sequence => <sequence> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <sequence> | Required | | Sdm::Sequence |
| $object | | | Sdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate linking a sequence to a structure.
# NOTE: Sequences and structures can only be linked in the DS client.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId('1CRN_A');
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0);

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0);

# Link the 1crn sequence and molecule.
$sdmDocument->LinkSequenceStructure( $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0),
$mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0) );
print "The sequence and molecule are now linked.\n";

# Selecting (and deselecting) the molecule also selects the sequence
# after updating the view. Here the update views call is required
# not only to display the sequence selection, but to synchronize the
# data models.
$molecule->Select();
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();
print 'After selecting the molecule and updating the SDM document view, '
. "the sequence is also selected.\n"
if ( $sequence->IsSelected() );

# Selecting (and deselecting) from the sequence does not
# require an update views call to synchronize the data models.
# The call is requires to display the updated sequence
# selection.
$sequence->Deselect( 0, 10 );
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();

# Break the sequence and molecule link.
$sdmDocument->BreakSequenceStructureLink( $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0) );
print "The sequence-molecule link is now broken.\n";

$sequence->Select( 0, 5 );
print "The first 5 residues in sequence are selected.\n"
if ( $sdmDocument->Alignment->IsSelected( 0, 0, 5 ) );

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();
print "The first 5 residues in sequence are selected.\n"
if ( $sdmDocument->Alignment->IsSelected( 0, 0, 5 ) );
```

# BuildBsmlAttributes function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/buildbsmlattributes_function.htm

## BuildBsmlAttributes function

### Description

BuildBsmlAttributes converts Sequence Data Model (SDM) object
data to attributes (in an Sdm::AttributeMap ) in a manner
analogous to saving a BSML file.
Attributes are primarily used to persist non-standard data to BSML files.
Attributes are generally not updated until the SDM
is persisted to a BSML file and are used to define SDM objects on loading
a BSML file. This method updates the attributes to the current
object state. The UpdateFromBsmlAttributes can be used to
force an object's attributes to reset the objects's properties.

### Applies to

The BuildBsmlAttributes function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the BuildBsmlAttributes function

#### Instance

$object->BuildBsmlAttributes();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Sdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the Sdm::AttributeMap.
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $mdm = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('4phv');
my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures($mdm);
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

# Copy current document state to object attributes. Generally the 
# attribute data is not updated after loading a BSML file. To get 
# the current state as attributes call this function. 
$document->ClearBsmlAttributes();
$document->BuildBsmlAttributes();

# List the Alignment object attributes.
print "Alignment attributes...\n";
my $attributes = $alignment->AttributeMap;
my $key = $attributes->FirstKey;
while (!$key->IsEndKey)
{
print $key->Name . ":\t" . $attributes->Item($key) . "\n";
$key = $attributes->NextKey($key);
}
print "end\n\n";

# List the Sequence object attributes.
my $sequences = $document->Sequences;
my $i = 0;
foreach my $sequence (@$sequences)
{
print "Sequence $i attributes...\n";
my $attributes = $sequence->AttributeMap;
my $key = $attributes->FirstKey;
while (!$key->IsEndKey)
{
print $key->Name . ":\t" . $attributes->Item($key) . "\n";
$key = $attributes->NextKey($key);
}
print "end\n\n";

my $k = $attributes->FindItem('ResidueID');
print 'Find Name: ' . $k->Name . "\tValue: "
. $attributes->Item($k) . "\n\n";

# List the Feature object attributes.
my $features = $sequence->Features;
my $f = 0;
foreach my $feature (@$features)
{
print "Feature $f attributes...\n";
my $fattributes = $feature->AttributeMap;
my $fkey = $fattributes->FirstKey;
print $feature->Key . "\n";
while (!$fkey->IsEndKey)
{
print $fkey->Name . ":\t" . $fattributes->Item($fkey) . "\n";
$fkey = $fattributes->NextKey($fkey);
}

print "end\n\n";
++$f;
} 

++$i; 
}

# Update the current document to match attribute data.
$document->UpdateFromBsmlAttributes();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# BumpCount property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/bumpcount_property.htm

## BumpCount property

### Description

BumpCount indicates the number of close contacts from the bump monitor.

### Applies to

The BumpCount property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::BumpMonitor

### Using the BumpCount property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->BumpCount;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::BumpMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Search for and print bumps between ligand and receptor.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Add hydrogen atoms to all heavy atoms.
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms( Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms, True );

# Creates a bump monitor between ligand and receptor atoms.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $bumpMonitor = $document->CreateBumpMonitor( $ligandAtoms, False );

$bumpMonitor->IsLabelShown = True;
$bumpMonitor->IsIntermolecularOnlyShown = False;

print "Default percent VDW Radius: $bumpMonitor->{DefaultPercentVdwRadius}\n";
print "$bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} bumps between ligand and receptor.\n";

$bumpMonitor->PercentVdwRadius = 90;

print "$bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} bumps between ligand and receptor "
. "when VDW radius set to 90%.\n";

my $bumps = $bumpMonitor->Bumps;
my $count = $bumps->Count;

# Create a bump hash.
my %bumpHash;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $bump = $bumps->Item($index);
$bumpHash{$index}{'bump'} = $bump;
$bumpHash{$index}{'Id1'} = $bump->Atom1->Id;
$bumpHash{$index}{'Id2'} = $bump->Atom2->Id;
}

# Print information for each bump, sorted by Atom1->Id followed by Atom2->Id.
my $counter = 0;
for my $b (
sort { 
my $x = $bumpHash{$a}{'Id1'};
my $y = $bumpHash{$b}{'Id1'};
($x != $y) ? ($x <=> $y) : ($bumpHash{$a}{'Id2'} <=> $bumpHash{$b}{'Id2'})
}
keys %bumpHash
)
{
my $bump = $bumpHash{$b}{'bump'};
my $atom1 = $bump->Atom1;
my $atom2 = $bump->Atom2;
printf
"%3d) Bump: %.3f A between Atom id %d %s:%s:%s and Atom id %d %s:%s:%s\n",
++$counter, $bump->Distance(),
$bumpHash{$b}{'Id1'},
$atom1->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom1->Parent->Name, $atom1->Name,
$bumpHash{$b}{'Id2'},
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name;
}
```

# C1Prime property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/c1prime_property.htm

## C1Prime property

### Description

C1Prime looks for the nucleotide sugar carbon atom labeled C1', C1*, or C1P.
It is connected by an N-glycosidic bond to the nucleotide base.

### Applies to

The C1Prime property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::Nucleotide

### Using the C1Prime property

#### Get

my $atomObject = $object->C1Prime;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $atomObject | | | Mdm::Atom |
| $object | | | Mdm::NucleicAcid Mdm::Nucleotide |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the use of Mdm::Nucleotide objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "3CRO.pdb" );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

print "Nucleic acid sequence: $molecule->{NucleicAcidSequence}\n";

my $nucleotides = $document->Nucleotides;
my $nucleotide1 = $nucleotides->Item(0);
my $nucleotide2 = $nucleotides->Item(1);
my $nucleotide3 = $nucleotides->Item(2);
my $nucleotide4 = $nucleotides->Item(3);

my $distance =
$document->CreateDistanceMonitor( $nucleotide1->C1Prime,
$nucleotide1->C2Prime );
printf
"Distance between C1' and C2' atoms of $nucleotide1->{Name}: %8.3f angstroms\n",
$distance->Distance;

my $angle =
$document->CreateAngleMonitor( $nucleotide2->C2, $nucleotide2->C3Prime,
$nucleotide2->C4 );

my $torsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide3->C4Prime, $nucleotide3->C5,
$nucleotide3->C5Prime, $nucleotide3->C6
);

my $torsion2 =
$document->CreateTorsionMonitor( $nucleotide3->N1, $nucleotide3->N3,
$nucleotide3->N7, $nucleotide3->N9 );

my $torsion3 = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide4->O1P, $nucleotide4->O2P,
$nucleotide4->O3Prime, $nucleotide4->O4Prime
);

print $nucleotide1->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsDeoxyribose );
print "a deoxyribose.\n";

print $nucleotide2->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsRibose );
print "a ribose.\n";

print $nucleotide3->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPurine );
print "have a purine ring system.\n";

print $nucleotide4->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPyrimidine );
print "have a pyrimidine ring system.\n";
```

Properties Scripting

```text
my $nucleotide3 = $nucleotides->Item(2);
my $nucleotide4 = $nucleotides->Item(3);

my $distance =
$document->CreateDistanceMonitor( $nucleotide1->C1Prime,
$nucleotide1->C2Prime );
printf
"Distance between C1' and C2' atoms of $nucleotide1->{Name}: %8.3f angstroms\n",
$distance->Distance;

my $angle =
$document->CreateAngleMonitor( $nucleotide2->C2, $nucleotide2->C3Prime,
$nucleotide2->C4 );

my $torsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide3->C4Prime, $nucleotide3->C5,
$nucleotide3->C5Prime, $nucleotide3->C6
);

my $torsion2 =
$document->CreateTorsionMonitor( $nucleotide3->N1, $nucleotide3->N3,
$nucleotide3->N7, $nucleotide3->N9 );

my $torsion3 = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide4->O1P, $nucleotide4->O2P,
$nucleotide4->O3Prime, $nucleotide4->O4Prime
);

print $nucleotide1->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsDeoxyribose );
print "a deoxyribose.\n";

print $nucleotide2->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsRibose );
print "a ribose.\n";

print $nucleotide3->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPurine );
print "have a purine ring system.\n";

print $nucleotide4->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPyrimidine );
print "have a pyrimidine ring system.\n";
```

# CalculateAllAtomRmsd function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculateallatomrmsd_function.htm

## CalculateAllAtomRmsd function

### Description

CalculateAllAtomRmsd calculates the all atom RMSD between two
molecules or conformations, including hydrogen atoms.

The following criteria are required:

* The number of atoms must match.

* Each element must match.

* The connectivity must match.

* The molecules must be small molecules that can be
represented by a .sd file.

### Applies to

The CalculateAllAtomRmsd function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateAllAtomRmsd function

#### Instance

my $realValue = $object->CalculateAllAtomRmsd( <molecule1>, <molecule2> );

my $realValue = $object->CalculateAllAtomRmsd( { Molecule1 => <molecule1>, Molecule2 => <molecule2> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| <molecule1> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <molecule2> | Required | | Mdm::Object |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SbdDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use the CalculateAllAtomRmsd function.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use SbdDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window and sketch a small molecule "
. "with hydrogen atoms.\n";
print " 3 Select all atoms, use CTRL+C to make a copy on the "
. "clipboard.\n";
print " 4 Use Structure/Clean Geometry on the original molecule.\n";
print " 5 Use CTRL+V to paste the copy of the un-cleaned molecule "
. "into the Molecule Window.\n";
print " 6 Rename the second molecule.\n";
print " 7 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

# The script assume the last active document contains molecules.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage("This example requires an open Molecule Window containing 2 molecules")
unless ($document);

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
Usage("This example requires an open Molecule Window containing 2 molecules")
unless ( $molecules->Count == 2 );

my $mol1 = $molecules->Item(0);
my $mol2 = $molecules->Item(1);

my $rmsdAll = $document->CalculateAllAtomRmsd( $mol1, $mol2 );

print "All atom RMSD between molecules "
. $mol1->Name . " and "
. $mol2->Name . " = "
. $rmsdAll . ".\n";

my $rmsdHeavy = $document->CalculateHeavyAtomRmsd( $mol1, $mol2 );
print "Heavy atom RMSD between molecules "
. $mol1->Name . " and "
. $mol2->Name . " = "
. $rmsdHeavy . ".\n";
```
