# CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculateallproteinalignmentrmsd_function.htm

## CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd function

### Description

CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd calculates the RMSD values between heavy atoms of aligned amino acids of two protein structures. By default the ResidueReport option is True and the function returns an array of real numbers which contain the per-residue RMSD values and includes the overall RMSD value in the last element; if ResidueReport is false the array only contains the overall value.

In the cases where the aligned residues are of a different type, this function uses/matches heavy atoms with the same atom name. Other atoms are ignored.

### Applies to

The CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd( <reference>, <referencesequence>, <molecule>, <moleculesequence>, [selectedonly], [residuereport] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd( { Reference => <reference>, ReferenceSequence => <referencesequence>, Molecule => <molecule>, MoleculeSequence => <moleculesequence>, SelectedOnly => [selectedonly], ResidueReport => [residuereport] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <moleculesequence> | Required | | String |
| <reference> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <referencesequence> | Required | | String |
| [residuereport] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [selectedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use alignment superimposition functions and
# RMSD calculation functions for amino acids or non-standard residues.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1gaf.pdb' );

my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1gaf = $document->Molecules->[1];

# H chain V domains only
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
$molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
$molecule1gaf->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
}

my $Sequence1aj7 = $molecule1aj7->AminoAcidSequence;
my $Sequence1gaf = $molecule1gaf->AminoAcidSequence;
my $sequences = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1aj7);
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1gaf);

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms. The function returns an array
# of RMSD values between the reference and all molecules, starting with itself.
my $rmsds =
$document->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment( $document->Molecules, $sequences,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms, True );

print "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $document->Molecules->Count() ; ++$i )
{
print "\t"
. $document->Molecules->[$i]->Name . " to "
. $molecule1aj7->Name . ": ";
printf "%.3f\n", $rmsds->[$i];
}
print "\n";

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD
# Note that these functions return an array of real numbers. These are the
# per residue RMSD values plus, in the last element, the overall RMSD.
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it (the value will be zero). This can happen for
# unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation only for
# selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the required atoms for
# the requested type of calculation.
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item( $apRmsd->Count() - 1 );
print "\n";

# This demonstrates that the array is for all residues plus overall
# value, not just selected, and that as the first chain(L) is
# unselected (its values are 0).
printf "Number of values returned is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain.
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H chain.
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

# Get antigen NPE from 1aj7.
my $antigen1 = $document->Molecules->[0]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Get antigen NPE from 1gaf.
my $antigen2 = $document->Molecules->[1]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Copy antigen residues to a new document.
my $tmpDocument = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $tmpMolecule1 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen1Copy = $antigen1->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen1Copy, $tmpMolecule1 );
my $tmpMolecule2 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen2Copy = $antigen2->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen2Copy, $tmpMolecule2 );

$tmpDocument->FitView();

# Calculate NPE RMSD.
my $rmsd =
$tmpDocument->CalculateOtherResidueRmsd( $tmpMolecule1, $tmpMolecule2 );
printf "NPE RMSD: %.3f\n", $rmsd->[1];
```

# CalculateAllProteinRmsd function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculateallproteinrmsd_function.htm

## CalculateAllProteinRmsd function

### Description

CalculateAllProteinRmsd calculates the heavy atom RMSD values between amino acids of two proteins that have the same sequence. By default the ResidueReport
option is True and the function returns an array of real numbers which contain
the per-residue RMSD values and includes the overall RMSD value in the last
element; if ResidueReport is false the array only contains the overall value.

### Applies to

The CalculateAllProteinRmsd function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateAllProteinRmsd function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateAllProteinRmsd( <reference>, <molecule>, [selectedonly], [residuereport] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateAllProteinRmsd( { Reference => <reference>, Molecule => <molecule>, SelectedOnly => [selectedonly], ResidueReport => [residuereport] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <reference> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| [residuereport] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [selectedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use superimposition functions
# and RMSD calculation functions for amino acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load 2rcs (an unligated antibody) from PDB.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '2rcs.pdb' );

# Load 1aj7 (a ligated antibody having the same sequence as 2crs) from PDB.
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

my $molecule2rcs = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[1];

my $hv2rcs = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 2rcs H chain V domain
my $hv1aj7 = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 1aj7 H chain V domain

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $molecule2rcs->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv2rcs->AddItem($aminoAcid);

$aminoAcid = $molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv1aj7->AddItem($aminoAcid);
}

# Show the transformation matrix which would superimpose the Vh
# domains by C-alpha atoms. This does not alter the coordinates
# of either structure.
my $matrix = $document->GetSuperimposeProteinMatrix( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
print "Transformation matrix:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 4 ; ++$i )
{
print "\t";
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < 4 ; ++$j )
{
printf "%.3f ", $matrix->GetEntry( $i, $j );
}
print "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms
my $rmsd = $document->SuperimposeProtein( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
printf "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms: %.3f\n\n", $rmsd;

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD. Note that by default the functions return an
# array of per-residue RMSD values, finishing with the overall RMSD
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it in which case the value will be zero. This can happen
# for unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation
# only for selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the
# required atoms for the requested type of calculation. 
# If you do not want per-residue RMSDs, set the 4th parameter ResidueReport
# False. In this case the array will only contain the overall RMSD.
# In this example, the all protein rmsd has no residue values calculated
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True, False );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item(0);
print "\n";

#Show that the all protein array contains just the overall RMSD.
printf "Number of values returned for all protein is %d\n", $apRmsd->Count();

# Demonstrating that the array is for all residues plus overall value not
# just selected and that as the first chain(L) is unselected its values
# are 0.
printf "Number of values returned for sidechains is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0), $scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

#Create a C-Alpha monitor
my $caMonitor = $document->CreateCAlphaMonitor();

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs before superimposing.\n";
if ($cAlphaPairs->Count > 0) {
printf "The first C-alpha to C-alpha pair distance is %.3f Angstroms.\n",
$cAlphaPairs->Item(0)->Distance;
}

#Lets do it for all matching atoms just to show the argument
my $rmsdByCA =
$document->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( $document->Molecules(), $caMonitor,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingAllAtoms );

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs after superimposing.\n";

#The values returned are like for Superimpose By Alignment - the first value
# is ref-ref (ie 0) then ref-mover for each superimposed molecule.
my $numVal = $rmsdByCA->Count();
printf( "Number of values returned for SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs %d\n",
$numVal );
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $numVal ; ++$i )
{
printf( "RMSD %d is %f\n", $i, $rmsdByCA->[$i] );
}

# use the filter function to retrieve the CAlpha atoms
my $cAlphaMonitors = $document->CAlphaMonitors;
foreach my $m (@$cAlphaMonitors)
{
print $m->ClassName ." filter entries: " . $m->CAlphaPairs->Count. "\n";
}

print "Finished Superimpose Script Example\n";
```

# CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculatecalphaalignmentrmsd_function.htm

## CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd function

### Description

CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd calculates the RMSD values between C-alpha atoms of aligned amino acids of two protein structures. By default the ResidueReport
option is True and the function returns an array of real numbers which contain
the per-residue RMSD values and includes the overall RMSD value in the last
element; if ResidueReport is false the array only contains the overall value.

### Applies to

The CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd( <reference>, <referencesequence>, <molecule>, <moleculesequence>, [selectedonly], [residuereport] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd( { Reference => <reference>, ReferenceSequence => <referencesequence>, Molecule => <molecule>, MoleculeSequence => <moleculesequence>, SelectedOnly => [selectedonly], ResidueReport => [residuereport] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <moleculesequence> | Required | | String |
| <reference> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <referencesequence> | Required | | String |
| [residuereport] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [selectedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use alignment superimposition functions and
# RMSD calculation functions for amino acids or non-standard residues.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1gaf.pdb' );

my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1gaf = $document->Molecules->[1];

# H chain V domains only
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
$molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
$molecule1gaf->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
}

my $Sequence1aj7 = $molecule1aj7->AminoAcidSequence;
my $Sequence1gaf = $molecule1gaf->AminoAcidSequence;
my $sequences = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1aj7);
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1gaf);

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms. The function returns an array
# of RMSD values between the reference and all molecules, starting with itself.
my $rmsds =
$document->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment( $document->Molecules, $sequences,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms, True );

print "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $document->Molecules->Count() ; ++$i )
{
print "\t"
. $document->Molecules->[$i]->Name . " to "
. $molecule1aj7->Name . ": ";
printf "%.3f\n", $rmsds->[$i];
}
print "\n";

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD
# Note that these functions return an array of real numbers. These are the
# per residue RMSD values plus, in the last element, the overall RMSD.
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it (the value will be zero). This can happen for
# unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation only for
# selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the required atoms for
# the requested type of calculation.
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item( $apRmsd->Count() - 1 );
print "\n";

# This demonstrates that the array is for all residues plus overall
# value, not just selected, and that as the first chain(L) is
# unselected (its values are 0).
printf "Number of values returned is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain.
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H chain.
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

# Get antigen NPE from 1aj7.
my $antigen1 = $document->Molecules->[0]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Get antigen NPE from 1gaf.
my $antigen2 = $document->Molecules->[1]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Copy antigen residues to a new document.
my $tmpDocument = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $tmpMolecule1 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen1Copy = $antigen1->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen1Copy, $tmpMolecule1 );
my $tmpMolecule2 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen2Copy = $antigen2->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen2Copy, $tmpMolecule2 );

$tmpDocument->FitView();

# Calculate NPE RMSD.
my $rmsd =
$tmpDocument->CalculateOtherResidueRmsd( $tmpMolecule1, $tmpMolecule2 );
printf "NPE RMSD: %.3f\n", $rmsd->[1];

# CalculateCharges function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculatecharges_function.htm

## CalculateCharges function

### Description

CalculateCharges calculates the partial charges for all atoms
in each selected molecule or each molecule with selected atoms. Charges may
need to be calculated when a change is made to the chemical structure of a molecule
that effects the partial atomic charges.

### Applies to

The CalculateCharges function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateCharges function

#### Command

$object->CalculateCharges();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

# CalculateDefaultResidueNeighborhoodFeatures function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculatedefaultresidueneighborhoodfeatures_function.htm

## CalculateDefaultResidueNeighborhoodFeatures function

### Description

This requires precomputed SAA (solvent accessible area), protrusion indices, depth indices and electrostatic potential properties. It is the equivalent of the CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures method with:

* Radii: 0,3,5,7,10,12,15,20,25

* PropertyNames: CX,DPX,SAA,Charge,EPOT

* Operations: "average,minimum,maximum","average,minimum,maximum","total,hydrophobic,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,aromatic,backbone,sidechain","total,exposed","total"

### Applies to

The CalculateDefaultResidueNeighborhoodFeatures function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateDefaultResidueNeighborhoodFeatures function

#### Command

$object->CalculateDefaultResidueNeighborhoodFeatures( [exposedonly] );

$object->CalculateDefaultResidueNeighborhoodFeatures( { ExposedOnly => [exposedonly] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [exposedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
##########
#
# Assign various properties to amino acids and their atoms 
# These may then be used to calculate 'residue feature' values over spatial neighborhoods.
# 

use MdmDiscoveryScript; # For working with Molecule Window
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

# Set this False to calculate custom residue neighborhood feature set
my $default = "True";
#property for surface display and site creation can be set on the command line.
#note that it is case sensitive
my $propertyName = "0A_CX_average";

if(@ARGV != 0){
($propertyName) = @ARGV;
}

# to run on a molecule in the active window, use this instead of OpenURL
# my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl(PdbUrlPrefix. '1aqk.pdb');

# Return an error message and exit if there is not an active Molecule Window
die "No Molecule Window!" unless $document;
$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);
print "Calculating atom properties\n";
# Many of the residue features depend on solvent surface accessibility and require that the atoms 
# have a precomputed SAA property, which is typically calculated using CHARMm.
# However, for demonstration purposes we can use the DS method and rename the property.

#check if the first atom already has SAA property, if not then do calculation.
my $atoms = $document->Atoms();
my $atom = $atoms->Item(0);
if(! $atom->HasProperty("SAA")) {
print "No precomputed SAA properties, calculating Solvent Accessible Surface\n";
$document->SolventAccessibleSurface();
$document->RenameUserProperty("Atom Solvent Accessibility","SAA",$atom->ClassName());
$document->RenameUserProperty("Percent Sidechain Solvent Accessibility","Fractional Sidechain SAA",$atom->Parent()->ClassName()); 
$document->RenameUserProperty("Percent Solvent Accessibility","Fractional Residue SAA",$atom->Parent()->ClassName());
#convert the percent accessibilities to fractional values for consistency with the method below 
foreach my $atom(@$atoms){
if($atom->HasProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA")){
my $sa = $atom->GetProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA")/100.0;
$atom->SetProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA",$sa);
}
if($atom->HasProperty("Fractional Residue SAA")){
my $sa = $atom->GetProperty("Fractional Residue SAA")/100.0;
$atom->SetProperty("Fractional Residue SAA",$sa);
}
}
}else{
#This calculates the Sidechain and Residue fractional exposures, using the precomputed SAA atom properties.
#the extended tripeptide exposures have been calculated for various CHARMm forcefields, with the appropriate 
#set used according to the forcefield setting on the structure.
$document->CalculateFractionalResidueExposures(True,True);
}
#Set the Black and Mould hydrophobicities for each amino acid residue. The argument specifies whether to 'normalize' the values
#to set the hydrophobicity of glycine to zero.

$document->SetBlackAndMouldHydrophobicities(False);

#Calculate the 'protrusion indices'. This sets a property CX on each atom. If the 'approximate' method
# is used (first argument True) then there are no prerequisites - the calculation will be performed as
# in the original paper by Pintar et al, using only non-hydrogen atoms and a single atom volume of 20.1.
#Otherwise, all atoms are used; if they have a property VDWRadius set (eg corresponding to the CHARMm forcefield values)
#these will be used, otherwise the standard DS element VDW radii are used. The second argument is the sphere radius used
#for the calculation.

$document->CalculateProtrusionIndices(False,10.0);

#Calculate the 'depth indices'. This sets a property DPX on each atom. It requires precomputed atom SAA properties.
#Exposed atoms will always have a DPX of zero. In addition, atoms will have a property DPX_RAD assigned. This is the VDW radius of
#the nearest surface atom, which is required for the simple electrostatic potential calculation. If a property VDWRadius set
# (eg corresponding to the CHARMm forcefield values)
#these will be used, otherwise the standard DS element VDW radii are used.

$document->CalculateDepthIndices();

#Performs a simple electrostatic potential calculation and sets atom properties EPOT. It requires the DPX and DPX_RAD properties to get the distance of the
#atom from the surface, so will run the Depth Indices calculation if they aren't already set. It therefore also requires SAA atom properties.
#Ideally the atomic charges should be set using the desired CHARMm forcefield.

$document->CalculateElectrostaticPotentials();

#The following lines demonstrate how to calculate 'residue neighborhood features'.
#These are the result of taking an existing property value for each atom within a given radius of any atom
#in the residue for which the property is being calculated, and then performing operations such as total or average.
# Note that a radius of 0 will give the result of the operation on just the residue itself.
#The new residue property names will be formed from radius_property_operation eg
# 5A_SAA_hydrophilic
#
#The choice of operations is:
# average: average of the property over all the atoms in the neighborhood
# minimum: minimum value for the property in the neighborhood
# maximum: maximum value for the property in the neighborhood
# total: sum of the property over all atoms in the neighborhood
# hydrophobic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Ala,Ile,Leu,Met,Phe,Trp,Tyr or Val
# hydrophilic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Arg,His,Lys,Asp,Glu,Ser,Thr,Asn or Gln (His is any protonation state of histidine)
# positive: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Arg,Hsp or Lys (Hsp is positively charged Histidine)
# negative: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Asp or Glu
# aromatic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues His, Phe, Trp and Tyr
# backbone: sum over all backbone atoms C CA N O and attached hydrogens
# sidechain: sum over all non-backbone atoms
# exposed: sum over all surface exposed atoms. (obviously SAA is a prerequisite)
#
# The ExposedOnly argument allows the feature calculation to be restricted to residues which have some
# surface exposure ie atoms with SAA >0
# 
#The first form calculates these residue features for a default set of properties, operations and radii. These are:
# radii 0,3,5,7,10,12,15,20,25
# properties operations
# CX average,minimum,maximum 
# DPX average,minimum,maximum
# SAA total,hydrophobic,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,backbone,sidechain 
# Charge total,exposed
# EPOT total
#
#The second allows for any numeric user defined properties with any combination of operators, and any integer radii.

print "Calculating Residue Neighborhood Features, default $default\n";

if($default eq "True"){
$document->CalculateDefaultResidueNeighborhoodFeatures(False);
}else{
my $radii= DiscoveryScript::IntegerArray::Create();
$radii->AddItem(0);
$radii->AddItem(3);
$radii->AddItem(5);
$radii->AddItem(7);
my $featureNames = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
my $subTypes = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$featureNames->AddItem("CX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("DPX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("Charges");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,exposed");
$featureNames->AddItem("SAA");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,aromatic,backbone,sidechain");
$document->CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures($radii,$featureNames,$subTypes,False);
}
print "Finished calculating features\n";
#now demonstrate the generic patch group creation API
#get the maximum value for this property

my $residues = $document->Residues();
my $atoms = $document->Atoms();
my $max = -999999;
my $min = 999999;
my $minPatchCutoff = 0.0;
my $minPeakCutoff = 0.1;
foreach my $res (@$residues){
if($res->HasProperty($propertyName)){
my $val = $res->GetProperty($propertyName);
if($val > $max){$max = $val;}
if($val < $min){$min = $val;}
}
}
#the range setting may not be ideal for all properties. 
if($max != -999999){
$minPeakCutoff = $max/5;
$minPatchCutoff = $max/10;
$max = $max/2;
$min = -1.0*$max;

#create a surface colored by this property
my $surface = $document->CreateSolidSurface($atoms,Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent);
$surface->Name = "$propertyName Surface";

my $surfacePropertyColorScheme = Mdm::spectrumBlueWhiteRed;
$surface->Select();
$document->SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme( $propertyName,
$surfacePropertyColorScheme, 32, $min,$max, False, "" );
$surface->IsTransparent(True);
$surface->IsLegendShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll();
$document->FindSurfacePropertySites($propertyName,5.0,$max,$minPatchCutoff);
}else{
print "Property for surface patches $propertyName not present\n";
}
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
$document->UpdateViews();

print "Finished script example\n";
```

# CalculateDistance function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculatedistance_function.htm

## CalculateDistance function

### Description

CalculateDistance calculates the distance between two points in two or three dimensions.

### Applies to

The CalculateDistance function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Point2d , Mdm::Point

### Using the CalculateDistance function

#### Instance

my $realValue = $object->CalculateDistance( <point> );

my $realValue = $object->CalculateDistance( <xyz> );

my $realValue = $object->CalculateDistance( { Point => <point> } );

my $realValue = $object->CalculateDistance( { XYZ => <xyz> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| <point> | Required | | Mdm::Point2d |
| <xyz> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| $object | | | Mdm::Point2d Mdm::Point |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use the Mdm::Point objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Working with 2D points.
my $xy1 = Mdm::Point2d::Create( -1.0, -1.0 );
my $xy2 = Mdm::Point2d::Create( 1.0, 1.0 );

print "Point1 is: (" . $xy1->X . "," . $xy1->Y . ")\n";
print "Point2 is: (" . $xy2->X . "," . $xy2->Y . ")\n";
print "Sum of squares of Point1 is: " . $xy1->SumSquares . "\n";

my $distance = $xy1->CalculateDistance($xy2);
print "The distance between these points is: $distance\n";

print "The dot product between points is: "
. $xy1->CalculateDotProduct($xy2) . "\n";

$xy1->SetXY( 2.0, 2.0 );
print "Changing Point1 to: (" . $xy1->X . "," . $xy1->Y . ")\n\n";

# Working with 3D points.
my $xyz = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 );
print "Creating 3D point with value: ("
. $xyz->X . ","
. $xyz->Y . ","
. $xyz->Z . ")\n";

$xyz->SetXYZ( 0.0, 1.0, 2.0 );
print "Changing 3D point to: ("
. $xyz->X . ","
. $xyz->Y . ","
. $xyz->Z . ")\n";
```

# CalculateDockedRmsd function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculatedockedrmsd_function.htm

## CalculateDockedRmsd function

### Description

CalculateDockedRmsd calculates the RMSD of atoms in the ligand binding interface of docked protein poses with respect to a reference pose.

The CalculateDockedRMSD function will generate the full structure of the docked complex as well as a group containing the binding site atoms
in the Hierarchy View if the script is run inside Discovery Studio.

The script below demonstrates how to use the function and how to access the resulting RMSD values. The values in the result array
are in the same order as the poses in the <poses> array passed in the second parameter.

The function is typically applied to the output of the Protein Docking protocols.
To run the example below, such a document should be loaded. Alternatively, the
example script for the Mdm::ProteinPose can be executed to generate
a small set of example data.

### Applies to

The CalculateDockedRmsd function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateDockedRmsd function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateDockedRmsd( <reference>, <arrayofposes>, [interfacecutoff] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateDockedRmsd( { Reference => <reference>, ArrayOfPoses => <arrayofposes>, InterfaceCutoff => [interfacecutoff] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <arrayofposes> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| <reference> | Required | | Mdm::Geometric3d |
| [interfacecutoff] | Optional | 5.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing docked protein poses\n";
print " 3 Enter a cluster ID in the Arguments tab\n";
print " 4 Run this script within Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

# The script assume the last active document contains ProteinPoses
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ($document);

# get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter
my $poses = $document->ProteinPoses;
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ( $poses->Count > 0 );

# store the first pose in a variable
my $pose1 = $poses->Item(0);

# Calculate the ligand binding interface RMSD using the interface residues of the
# first pose as reference
my $rmsds = $document->CalculateDockedRmsd( $pose1, $document->ProteinPoses );

print "RMSD of poses with respect to " . $pose1->Name . "\n";
my $count = $rmsds->Count();
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < $count ; ++$j )
{
my $rms = $rmsds->Item($j);
$rms =~ s/\s+//g;
my $name = $poses->Item($j)->Name;
print "$name\t$rms\n";
}

## CalculateDockedRmsdFromReferencePose function

### Description

CalculateDockedRmsdFromReferencePose calculates the RMSD of atoms in the ligand binding interface of docked protein poses with respect to a reference pose. It generates the full structure of the docked complex and a group containing the binding site atoms
in the Hierarchy View if the script is run from Discovery Studio.

The script below demonstrates how to use the function and access the resulting RMSD values. The values in the result array
are in the same order as the poses in the <poses> array passed in the second parameter.

The function is typically applied to the output of the Protein Docking protocols, which should be loaded before running this example. Alternatively, the
example script for the Mdm::ProteinPose can be executed to generate
a small set of example data.

### Applies to

The CalculateDockedRmsdFromReferencePose function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateDockedRmsdFromReferencePose function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateDockedRmsdFromReferencePose( <reference>, <arrayofposes>, [interfacecutoff] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateDockedRmsdFromReferencePose( { Reference => <reference>, ArrayOfPoses => <arrayofposes>, InterfaceCutoff => [interfacecutoff] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <arrayofposes> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| <reference> | Required | | Mdm::Geometric3d |
| [interfacecutoff] | Optional | 5.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing docked protein poses\n";
print " 3 Enter a cluster ID in the Arguments tab\n";
print " 4 Run this script within Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

# The script assume the last active document contains ProteinPoses
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ($document);

# get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter
my $poses = $document->ProteinPoses;
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ( $poses->Count > 0 );

# store the first pose in a variable
my $pose1 = $poses->Item(0);

# Calculate the ligand binding interface RMSD using the interface residues of the
# first pose as reference
my $rmsds =
$document->CalculateDockedRmsdFromReferencePose( $pose1,
$document->ProteinPoses );

# Output RMSD values
print "RMSD of poses with respect to " . $pose1->Name . "\n";
my $count = $rmsds->Count();
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < $count ; ++$j )
{
my $rms = $rmsds->Item($j);
$rms =~ s/\s+//g;
my $name = $poses->Item($j)->Name;

}

It generates a group containing the binding site atoms in the Hierarchy View if the script is run from Discovery Studio.

The script below demonstrates how to use the function and how to access the resulting RMSD values. The values in the result array are in the same order as the poses in the <poses> array passed in the second parameter.

The function is typically applied to the output of the Protein Docking protocols, which should be loaded before running this example. Additionally, the reference XRay structure
must be inserted into the same Molecule Window.

### Applies to

The CalculateDockedRmsdFromXRayStructure function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateDockedRmsdFromXRayStructure function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateDockedRmsdFromXRayStructure( <arrayofreceptorchains>, <arrayofposes>, [interfacecutoff] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateDockedRmsdFromXRayStructure( { ArrayOfReceptorChains => <arrayofreceptorchains>, ArrayOfPoses => <arrayofposes>, InterfaceCutoff => [interfacecutoff] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <arrayofposes> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| <arrayofreceptorchains> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| [interfacecutoff] | Optional | 5.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing docked protein poses\n";
print
" 3 Insert the reference XRay structure into the Molecule Window\n";
print " 4 Run this script within Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

# The script assume the last active document contains ProteinPoses
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ($document);

# get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter
my $poses = $document->ProteinPoses;
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ( $poses->Count > 0 );

# get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter
my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing a reference XRay Structure"
) unless ( $molecules->Count == 3 );

# get the XRay Structure which is assumed to be the third molecule in the hierarchy
my $XRayStructure = $document->Molecules->Item(2);

# Put all amino acid chains of the ligand part of the XRays structure into array
# Here we assume the ligand is the second amino acid chain
my $ligandChains = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $ligandChain = $XRayStructure->AminoAcidChains->Item(1);
$ligandChains->AddItem($ligandChain);

# Calculate the ligand binding interface RMSD using the interface residues of the
# XRay structure
my $rmsds =
$document->CalculateDockedRmsdFromXRayStructure( $ligandChains,
$document->ProteinPoses );

# Output RMSD values
print "RMSD of poses with respect to " . $XRayStructure->Name . "\n";
my $count = $rmsds->Count();
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < $count ; ++$j )
{
my $rms = $rmsds->Item($j);
$rms =~ s/\s+//g;
my $name = $poses->Item($j)->Name;
print "$name\t$rms\n";

}

Mdm::Point2d , Mdm::Point

### Using the CalculateDotProduct function

#### Instance

my $realValue = $object->CalculateDotProduct( <point> );

my $realValue = $object->CalculateDotProduct( <xyz> );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |

| $realValue | | | Real |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use the Mdm::Point objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Working with 2D points.
my $xy1 = Mdm::Point2d::Create( -1.0, -1.0 );
my $xy2 = Mdm::Point2d::Create( 1.0, 1.0 );

print "Point1 is: (" . $xy1->X . "," . $xy1->Y . ")\n";
print "Point2 is: (" . $xy2->X . "," . $xy2->Y . ")\n";
print "Sum of squares of Point1 is: " . $xy1->SumSquares . "\n";

my $distance = $xy1->CalculateDistance($xy2);
print "The distance between these points is: $distance\n";

print "The dot product between points is: "
. $xy1->CalculateDotProduct($xy2) . "\n";

$xy1->SetXY( 2.0, 2.0 );
print "Changing Point1 to: (" . $xy1->X . "," . $xy1->Y . ")\n\n";

# Working with 3D points.
my $xyz = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 );
print "Creating 3D point with value: ("
. $xyz->X . ","
. $xyz->Y . ","
. $xyz->Z . ")\n";

$xyz->SetXYZ( 0.0, 1.0, 2.0 );
print "Changing 3D point to: ("
. $xyz->X . ","
. $xyz->Y . ","
. $xyz->Z . ")\n";

# CalculateElectrostaticPotentials function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculateelectrostaticpotentials_function.htm

## CalculateElectrostaticPotentials function

### Description

Sets a property EPOT for each atom. This is a simple charge metric modified by distance to the surface. It is dependent on the Depth Indices calculation, and requires that atomic charges have been set appropriately.

### Applies to

The CalculateElectrostaticPotentials function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateElectrostaticPotentials function

#### Command

$object->CalculateElectrostaticPotentials();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
##########
#
# Assign various properties to amino acids and their atoms 
# These may then be used to calculate 'residue feature' values over spatial neighborhoods.
# 

use MdmDiscoveryScript; # For working with Molecule Window
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

# Set this False to calculate custom residue neighborhood feature set
my $default = "True";
#property for surface display and site creation can be set on the command line.
#note that it is case sensitive
my $propertyName = "0A_CX_average";

if(@ARGV != 0){
($propertyName) = @ARGV;
}

# to run on a molecule in the active window, use this instead of OpenURL
# my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl(PdbUrlPrefix. '1aqk.pdb');

# Return an error message and exit if there is not an active Molecule Window
die "No Molecule Window!" unless $document;
$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);
print "Calculating atom properties\n";
# Many of the residue features depend on solvent surface accessibility and require that the atoms 
# have a precomputed SAA property, which is typically calculated using CHARMm.
# However, for demonstration purposes we can use the DS method and rename the property.

#check if the first atom already has SAA property, if not then do calculation.
my $atoms = $document->Atoms();
my $atom = $atoms->Item(0);
if(! $atom->HasProperty("SAA")) {
print "No precomputed SAA properties, calculating Solvent Accessible Surface\n";
$document->SolventAccessibleSurface();
$document->RenameUserProperty("Atom Solvent Accessibility","SAA",$atom->ClassName());
$document->RenameUserProperty("Percent Sidechain Solvent Accessibility","Fractional Sidechain SAA",$atom->Parent()->ClassName()); 
$document->RenameUserProperty("Percent Solvent Accessibility","Fractional Residue SAA",$atom->Parent()->ClassName());
#convert the percent accessibilities to fractional values for consistency with the method below 
foreach my $atom(@$atoms){
if($atom->HasProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA")){
my $sa = $atom->GetProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA")/100.0;
$atom->SetProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA",$sa);
}
if($atom->HasProperty("Fractional Residue SAA")){
my $sa = $atom->GetProperty("Fractional Residue SAA")/100.0;
$atom->SetProperty("Fractional Residue SAA",$sa);
}
}
}else{
#This calculates the Sidechain and Residue fractional exposures, using the precomputed SAA atom properties.
#the extended tripeptide exposures have been calculated for various CHARMm forcefields, with the appropriate 
#set used according to the forcefield setting on the structure.
$document->CalculateFractionalResidueExposures(True,True);
}
#Set the Black and Mould hydrophobicities for each amino acid residue. The argument specifies whether to 'normalize' the values
#to set the hydrophobicity of glycine to zero.

$document->SetBlackAndMouldHydrophobicities(False);

#Calculate the 'protrusion indices'. This sets a property CX on each atom. If the 'approximate' method
# is used (first argument True) then there are no prerequisites - the calculation will be performed as
# in the original paper by Pintar et al, using only non-hydrogen atoms and a single atom volume of 20.1.
#Otherwise, all atoms are used; if they have a property VDWRadius set (eg corresponding to the CHARMm forcefield values)
#these will be used, otherwise the standard DS element VDW radii are used. The second argument is the sphere radius used
#for the calculation.

$document->CalculateProtrusionIndices(False,10.0);

#Calculate the 'depth indices'. This sets a property DPX on each atom. It requires precomputed atom SAA properties.
#Exposed atoms will always have a DPX of zero. In addition, atoms will have a property DPX_RAD assigned. This is the VDW radius of
#the nearest surface atom, which is required for the simple electrostatic potential calculation. If a property VDWRadius set
# (eg corresponding to the CHARMm forcefield values)
#these will be used, otherwise the standard DS element VDW radii are used.

$document->CalculateDepthIndices();

#Performs a simple electrostatic potential calculation and sets atom properties EPOT. It requires the DPX and DPX_RAD properties to get the distance of the
#atom from the surface, so will run the Depth Indices calculation if they aren't already set. It therefore also requires SAA atom properties.
#Ideally the atomic charges should be set using the desired CHARMm forcefield.

$document->CalculateElectrostaticPotentials();

#The following lines demonstrate how to calculate 'residue neighborhood features'.
#These are the result of taking an existing property value for each atom within a given radius of any atom
#in the residue for which the property is being calculated, and then performing operations such as total or average.
# Note that a radius of 0 will give the result of the operation on just the residue itself.
#The new residue property names will be formed from radius_property_operation eg
# 5A_SAA_hydrophilic
#
#The choice of operations is:
# average: average of the property over all the atoms in the neighborhood
# minimum: minimum value for the property in the neighborhood
# maximum: maximum value for the property in the neighborhood
# total: sum of the property over all atoms in the neighborhood
# hydrophobic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Ala,Ile,Leu,Met,Phe,Trp,Tyr or Val
# hydrophilic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Arg,His,Lys,Asp,Glu,Ser,Thr,Asn or Gln (His is any protonation state of histidine)
# positive: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Arg,Hsp or Lys (Hsp is positively charged Histidine)
# negative: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Asp or Glu
# aromatic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues His, Phe, Trp and Tyr
# backbone: sum over all backbone atoms C CA N O and attached hydrogens
# sidechain: sum over all non-backbone atoms
# exposed: sum over all surface exposed atoms. (obviously SAA is a prerequisite)
#
# The ExposedOnly argument allows the feature calculation to be restricted to residues which have some
# surface exposure ie atoms with SAA >0
# 
#The first form calculates these residue features for a default set of properties, operations and radii. These are:
# radii 0,3,5,7,10,12,15,20,25
# properties operations
# CX average,minimum,maximum 
# DPX average,minimum,maximum
# SAA total,hydrophobic,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,backbone,sidechain 
# Charge total,exposed
# EPOT total
#
#The second allows for any numeric user defined properties with any combination of operators, and any integer radii.

print "Calculating Residue Neighborhood Features, default $default\n";

if($default eq "True"){
$document->CalculateDefaultResidueNeighborhoodFeatures(False);
}else{
my $radii= DiscoveryScript::IntegerArray::Create();
$radii->AddItem(0);
$radii->AddItem(3);
$radii->AddItem(5);
$radii->AddItem(7);
my $featureNames = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
my $subTypes = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$featureNames->AddItem("CX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("DPX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("Charges");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,exposed");
$featureNames->AddItem("SAA");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,aromatic,backbone,sidechain");
$document->CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures($radii,$featureNames,$subTypes,False);
}
print "Finished calculating features\n";
#now demonstrate the generic patch group creation API
#get the maximum value for this property

my $residues = $document->Residues();
my $atoms = $document->Atoms();
my $max = -999999;
my $min = 999999;
my $minPatchCutoff = 0.0;
my $minPeakCutoff = 0.1;
foreach my $res (@$residues){
if($res->HasProperty($propertyName)){
my $val = $res->GetProperty($propertyName);
if($val > $max){$max = $val;}
if($val < $min){$min = $val;}
}
}
#the range setting may not be ideal for all properties. 
if($max != -999999){
$minPeakCutoff = $max/5;
$minPatchCutoff = $max/10;
$max = $max/2;
$min = -1.0*$max;

#create a surface colored by this property
my $surface = $document->CreateSolidSurface($atoms,Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent);
$surface->Name = "$propertyName Surface";

my $surfacePropertyColorScheme = Mdm::spectrumBlueWhiteRed;
$surface->Select();
$document->SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme( $propertyName,
$surfacePropertyColorScheme, 32, $min,$max, False, "" );
$surface->IsTransparent(True);
$surface->IsLegendShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll();
$document->FindSurfacePropertySites($propertyName,5.0,$max,$minPatchCutoff);
}else{
print "Property for surface patches $propertyName not present\n";
}
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
$document->UpdateViews();

print "Finished script example\n";
```

# 
#The first form calculates these residue features for a default set of properties, operations and radii. These are:
# radii 0,3,5,7,10,12,15,20,25
# properties operations
# CX average,minimum,maximum 
# DPX average,minimum,maximum
# SAA total,hydrophobic,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,backbone,sidechain 
# Charge total,exposed
# EPOT total
#
#The second allows for any numeric user defined properties with any combination of operators, and any integer radii.

print "Calculating Residue Neighborhood Features, default $default\n";

if($default eq "True"){
$document->CalculateDefaultResidueNeighborhoodFeatures(False);
}else{
my $radii= DiscoveryScript::IntegerArray::Create();
$radii->AddItem(0);
$radii->AddItem(3);
$radii->AddItem(5);
$radii->AddItem(7);
my $featureNames = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
my $subTypes = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$featureNames->AddItem("CX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("DPX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("Charges");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,exposed");
$featureNames->AddItem("SAA");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,aromatic,backbone,sidechain");
$document->CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures($radii,$featureNames,$subTypes,False);
}
print "Finished calculating features\n";
#now demonstrate the generic patch group creation API
#get the maximum value for this property

my $residues = $document->Residues();
my $atoms = $document->Atoms();
my $max = -999999;
my $min = 999999;
my $minPatchCutoff = 0.0;
my $minPeakCutoff = 0.1;
foreach my $res (@$residues){
if($res->HasProperty($propertyName)){
my $val = $res->GetProperty($propertyName);
if($val > $max){$max = $val;}
if($val < $min){$min = $val;}
}
}
#the range setting may not be ideal for all properties. 
if($max != -999999){
$minPeakCutoff = $max/5;
$minPatchCutoff = $max/10;
$max = $max/2;
$min = -1.0*$max;

#create a surface colored by this property
my $surface = $document->CreateSolidSurface($atoms,Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent);
$surface->Name = "$propertyName Surface";

my $surfacePropertyColorScheme = Mdm::spectrumBlueWhiteRed;
$surface->Select();
$document->SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme( $propertyName,
$surfacePropertyColorScheme, 32, $min,$max, False, "" );
$surface->IsTransparent(True);
$surface->IsLegendShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll();
$document->FindSurfacePropertySites($propertyName,5.0,$max,$minPatchCutoff);
}else{
print "Property for surface patches $propertyName not present\n";
}
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
$document->UpdateViews();

print "Finished script example\n";
```

# CalculateHeavyAtomRmsd function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculateheavyatomrmsd_function.htm

## CalculateHeavyAtomRmsd function

### Description

CalculateHeavyAtomRmsd calculates the RMSD between two
molecules or conformations, excluding hydrogen atoms.

The following criteria are required for the calculation to be performed:

* The number of non-hydrogen atoms must match.

* Each element must match.

* The connectivity must match.

* The molecules must be small molecules--defined as molecules that can
be
represented by a .sd file.

### Applies to

The CalculateHeavyAtomRmsd function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateHeavyAtomRmsd function

#### Instance

my $realValue = $object->CalculateHeavyAtomRmsd( <molecule1>, <molecule2> );

my $realValue = $object->CalculateHeavyAtomRmsd( { Molecule1 => <molecule1>, Molecule2 => <molecule2> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| <molecule1> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <molecule2> | Required | | Mdm::Object |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SbdDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use the CalculateAllAtomRmsd function.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use SbdDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window and sketch a small molecule "
. "with hydrogen atoms.\n";
print " 3 Select all atoms, use CTRL+C to make a copy on the "
. "clipboard.\n";
print " 4 Use Structure/Clean Geometry on the original molecule.\n";
print " 5 Use CTRL+V to paste the copy of the un-cleaned molecule "
. "into the Molecule Window.\n";
print " 6 Rename the second molecule.\n";
print " 7 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

# The script assume the last active document contains molecules.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage("This example requires an open Molecule Window containing 2 molecules")
unless ($document);

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
Usage("This example requires an open Molecule Window containing 2 molecules")
unless ( $molecules->Count == 2 );

my $mol1 = $molecules->Item(0);
my $mol2 = $molecules->Item(1);

my $rmsdAll = $document->CalculateAllAtomRmsd( $mol1, $mol2 );

print "All atom RMSD between molecules "
. $mol1->Name . " and "
. $mol2->Name . " = "
. $rmsdAll . ".\n";

my $rmsdHeavy = $document->CalculateHeavyAtomRmsd( $mol1, $mol2 );
print "Heavy atom RMSD between molecules "
. $mol1->Name . " and "
. $mol2->Name . " = "
. $rmsdHeavy . ".\n";
```

# CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculatemainchainalignmentrmsd_function.htm

## CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd function

### Description

CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd calculates the RMSD values between main chain atoms of aligned amino acids of two protein structures. By default the ResidueReport
option is True and the function returns an array of real numbers which contain
the per-residue RMSD values and includes the overall RMSD value in the last
element; if ResidueReport is false the array only contains the overall value.

### Applies to

The CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd( <reference>, <referencesequence>, <molecule>, <moleculesequence>, [selectedonly], [residuereport] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd( { Reference => <reference>, ReferenceSequence => <referencesequence>, Molecule => <molecule>, MoleculeSequence => <moleculesequence>, SelectedOnly => [selectedonly], ResidueReport => [residuereport] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <moleculesequence> | Required | | String |
| <reference> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <referencesequence> | Required | | String |
| [residuereport] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [selectedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use alignment superimposition functions and
# RMSD calculation functions for amino acids or non-standard residues.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1gaf.pdb' );

my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1gaf = $document->Molecules->[1];

# H chain V domains only
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
$molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
$molecule1gaf->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
}

my $Sequence1aj7 = $molecule1aj7->AminoAcidSequence;
my $Sequence1gaf = $molecule1gaf->AminoAcidSequence;
my $sequences = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1aj7);
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1gaf);

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms. The function returns an array
# of RMSD values between the reference and all molecules, starting with itself.
my $rmsds =
$document->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment( $document->Molecules, $sequences,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms, True );

print "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $document->Molecules->Count() ; ++$i )
{
print "\t"
. $document->Molecules->[$i]->Name . " to "
. $molecule1aj7->Name . ": ";
printf "%.3f\n", $rmsds->[$i];
}
print "\n";

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD
# Note that these functions return an array of real numbers. These are the
# per residue RMSD values plus, in the last element, the overall RMSD.
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it (the value will be zero). This can happen for
# unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation only for
# selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the required atoms for
# the requested type of calculation.
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item( $apRmsd->Count() - 1 );
print "\n";

# This demonstrates that the array is for all residues plus overall
# value, not just selected, and that as the first chain(L) is
# unselected (its values are 0).
printf "Number of values returned is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain.
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H chain.
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

# Get antigen NPE from 1aj7.
my $antigen1 = $document->Molecules->[0]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Get antigen NPE from 1gaf.
my $antigen2 = $document->Molecules->[1]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Copy antigen residues to a new document.
my $tmpDocument = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $tmpMolecule1 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen1Copy = $antigen1->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen1Copy, $tmpMolecule1 );
my $tmpMolecule2 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen2Copy = $antigen2->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen2Copy, $tmpMolecule2 );

$tmpDocument->FitView();

# Calculate NPE RMSD.
my $rmsd =
$tmpDocument->CalculateOtherResidueRmsd( $tmpMolecule1, $tmpMolecule2 );
printf "NPE RMSD: %.3f\n", $rmsd->[1];
```

# CalculateMainChainRmsd function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculatemainchainrmsd_function.htm

## CalculateMainChainRmsd function

### Description

CalculateMainChainRmsd calculates the RMSD values between main chain atoms of amino acids of two protein structures. By default the ResidueReport
option is True and the function returns an array of real numbers which contain
the per-residue RMSD values and includes the overall RMSD value in the last
element; if ResidueReport is false the array only contains the overall value.

The two proteins have to have the same sequence.

### Applies to

The CalculateMainChainRmsd function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateMainChainRmsd function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateMainChainRmsd( <reference>, <molecule>, [selectedonly], [residuereport] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateMainChainRmsd( { Reference => <reference>, Molecule => <molecule>, SelectedOnly => [selectedonly], ResidueReport => [residuereport] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <reference> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| [residuereport] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [selectedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use superimposition functions
# and RMSD calculation functions for amino acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load 2rcs (an unligated antibody) from PDB.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '2rcs.pdb' );

# Load 1aj7 (a ligated antibody having the same sequence as 2crs) from PDB.
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

my $molecule2rcs = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[1];

my $hv2rcs = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 2rcs H chain V domain
my $hv1aj7 = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 1aj7 H chain V domain

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $molecule2rcs->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv2rcs->AddItem($aminoAcid);

$aminoAcid = $molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv1aj7->AddItem($aminoAcid);
}

# Show the transformation matrix which would superimpose the Vh
# domains by C-alpha atoms. This does not alter the coordinates
# of either structure.
my $matrix = $document->GetSuperimposeProteinMatrix( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
print "Transformation matrix:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 4 ; ++$i )
{
print "\t";
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < 4 ; ++$j )
{
printf "%.3f ", $matrix->GetEntry( $i, $j );
}
print "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms
my $rmsd = $document->SuperimposeProtein( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
printf "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms: %.3f\n\n", $rmsd;

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD. Note that by default the functions return an
# array of per-residue RMSD values, finishing with the overall RMSD
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it in which case the value will be zero. This can happen
# for unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation
# only for selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the
# required atoms for the requested type of calculation. 
# If you do not want per-residue RMSDs, set the 4th parameter ResidueReport
# False. In this case the array will only contain the overall RMSD.
# In this example, the all protein rmsd has no residue values calculated
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True, False );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item(0);
print "\n";

#Show that the all protein array contains just the overall RMSD.
printf "Number of values returned for all protein is %d\n", $apRmsd->Count();

# Demonstrating that the array is for all residues plus overall value not
# just selected and that as the first chain(L) is unselected its values
# are 0.
printf "Number of values returned for sidechains is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0), $scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

#Create a C-Alpha monitor
my $caMonitor = $document->CreateCAlphaMonitor();

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs before superimposing.\n";
if ($cAlphaPairs->Count > 0) {
printf "The first C-alpha to C-alpha pair distance is %.3f Angstroms.\n",
$cAlphaPairs->Item(0)->Distance;
}

#Lets do it for all matching atoms just to show the argument
my $rmsdByCA =
$document->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( $document->Molecules(), $caMonitor,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingAllAtoms );

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs after superimposing.\n";

#The values returned are like for Superimpose By Alignment - the first value
# is ref-ref (ie 0) then ref-mover for each superimposed molecule.
my $numVal = $rmsdByCA->Count();
printf( "Number of values returned for SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs %d\n",
$numVal );
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $numVal ; ++$i )
{
printf( "RMSD %d is %f\n", $i, $rmsdByCA->[$i] );
}

# use the filter function to retrieve the CAlpha atoms
my $cAlphaMonitors = $document->CAlphaMonitors;
foreach my $m (@$cAlphaMonitors)
{
print $m->ClassName ." filter entries: " . $m->CAlphaPairs->Count. "\n";
}

print "Finished Superimpose Script Example\n";
```

## CalculateNucleicAcidBackboneRmsd function

### Description

CalculateNucleicAcidBackboneRmsd calculates the RMSD values between corresponding backbone of two nucleic acid structures. By default the ResidueReport
option is True and the function returns an array of real numbers which contain
the per-residue RMSD values and includes the overall RMSD value in the last
element; if ResidueReport is false the array only contains the overall value.

The two nucleic acid structures have to have the same sequence.

### Applies to

The CalculateNucleicAcidBackboneRmsd function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateNucleicAcidBackboneRmsd function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateNucleicAcidBackboneRmsd( <reference>, <molecule>, [selectedonly], [residuereport] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateNucleicAcidBackboneRmsd( { Reference => <reference>, Molecule => <molecule>, SelectedOnly => [selectedonly], ResidueReport => [residuereport] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <reference> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| [residuereport] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [selectedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use RMSD calculation functions for
# nucleic acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1omh.pdb' );

# Load 1zm5
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1zm5.pdb' );

my $molecule1 = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule2 = $document->Molecules->[1];

# Calculate RMSD
my $rmsd1 = $document->CalculateNucleicAcidBaseRmsd( $molecule1, $molecule2 );
my $rmsd2 =
$document->CalculateNucleicAcidBackboneRmsd( $molecule1, $molecule2 );
my $rmsd3 = $document->CalculateNucleicAcidRmsd( $molecule1, $molecule2 );

print "RMSD:\n";
printf "\tBase atoms: %.3f\n", $rmsd1->Item( $rmsd1->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tBackbone atoms: %.3f\n", $rmsd2->Item( $rmsd2->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms: %.3f\n", $rmsd3->Item( $rmsd3->Count() - 1 );
```
