## CalculateNucleicAcidRmsd function

### Description

CalculateNucleicAcidRmsd calculates the RMSD values between corresponding nucleic acid residues of two structures. By default the ResidueReport
option is True and the function returns an array of real numbers which contain
the per-residue RMSD values and includes the overall RMSD value in the last
element; if ResidueReport is false the array only contains the overall value.

The two nucleic acid structures have to have the same sequence.

### Applies to

The CalculateNucleicAcidRmsd function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateNucleicAcidRmsd function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateNucleicAcidRmsd( <reference>, <molecule>, [selectedonly], [residuereport] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateNucleicAcidRmsd( { Reference => <reference>, Molecule => <molecule>, SelectedOnly => [selectedonly], ResidueReport => [residuereport] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <reference> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| [residuereport] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [selectedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use RMSD calculation functions for
# nucleic acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1omh.pdb' );

# Load 1zm5
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1zm5.pdb' );

my $molecule1 = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule2 = $document->Molecules->[1];

# Calculate RMSD
my $rmsd1 = $document->CalculateNucleicAcidBaseRmsd( $molecule1, $molecule2 );
my $rmsd2 =
$document->CalculateNucleicAcidBackboneRmsd( $molecule1, $molecule2 );
my $rmsd3 = $document->CalculateNucleicAcidRmsd( $molecule1, $molecule2 );

print "RMSD:\n";
printf "\tBase atoms: %.3f\n", $rmsd1->Item( $rmsd1->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tBackbone atoms: %.3f\n", $rmsd2->Item( $rmsd2->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms: %.3f\n", $rmsd3->Item( $rmsd3->Count() - 1 );
```

# CalculateOtherResidueRmsd function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculateotherresiduermsd_function.htm

## CalculateOtherResidueRmsd function

### Description

Calculates the RMSD values between residues that are neither amino acids nor
nucleic acids. By default the ResidueReport
option is True and the function returns an array of real numbers which contain
the per-residue RMSD values and includes the overall RMSD value in the last
element; if ResidueReport is false the array only contains the overall value.

### Applies to

The CalculateOtherResidueRmsd function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateOtherResidueRmsd function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateOtherResidueRmsd( <reference>, <molecule>, [selectedonly], [residuereport] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateOtherResidueRmsd( { Reference => <reference>, Molecule => <molecule>, SelectedOnly => [selectedonly], ResidueReport => [residuereport] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <reference> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| [residuereport] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [selectedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use alignment superimposition functions and
# RMSD calculation functions for amino acids or non-standard residues.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1gaf.pdb' );

my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1gaf = $document->Molecules->[1];

# H chain V domains only
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
$molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
$molecule1gaf->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
}

my $Sequence1aj7 = $molecule1aj7->AminoAcidSequence;
my $Sequence1gaf = $molecule1gaf->AminoAcidSequence;
my $sequences = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1aj7);
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1gaf);

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms. The function returns an array
# of RMSD values between the reference and all molecules, starting with itself.
my $rmsds =
$document->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment( $document->Molecules, $sequences,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms, True );

print "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $document->Molecules->Count() ; ++$i )
{
print "\t"
. $document->Molecules->[$i]->Name . " to "
. $molecule1aj7->Name . ": ";
printf "%.3f\n", $rmsds->[$i];
}
print "\n";

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD
# Note that these functions return an array of real numbers. These are the
# per residue RMSD values plus, in the last element, the overall RMSD.
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it (the value will be zero). This can happen for
# unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation only for
# selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the required atoms for
# the requested type of calculation.
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item( $apRmsd->Count() - 1 );
print "\n";

# This demonstrates that the array is for all residues plus overall
# value, not just selected, and that as the first chain(L) is
# unselected (its values are 0).
printf "Number of values returned is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain.
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H chain.
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

# Get antigen NPE from 1aj7.
my $antigen1 = $document->Molecules->[0]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Get antigen NPE from 1gaf.
my $antigen2 = $document->Molecules->[1]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Copy antigen residues to a new document.
my $tmpDocument = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $tmpMolecule1 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen1Copy = $antigen1->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen1Copy, $tmpMolecule1 );
my $tmpMolecule2 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen2Copy = $antigen2->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen2Copy, $tmpMolecule2 );

$tmpDocument->FitView();

# Calculate NPE RMSD.
my $rmsd =
$tmpDocument->CalculateOtherResidueRmsd( $tmpMolecule1, $tmpMolecule2 );
printf "NPE RMSD: %.3f\n", $rmsd->[1];
```

# CalculateProtrusionIndices function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculateprotrusionindices_function.htm

## CalculateProtrusionIndices function

### Description

Sets a property named CX for each atom. The protrusion index is a measure of the protrusion of an atom from the surface of the protein. There are two parameters available:

* Approximate: specifies whether to use the more approximate method from the literature, which uses a single sphere volume for all heavy atoms, or use the VDW radii for each atom to determine its volume.

* SphereRadius: specifies the sphere radius for the calculation, default 10 angstroms

### Applies to

The CalculateProtrusionIndices function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateProtrusionIndices function

#### Command

$object->CalculateProtrusionIndices( [approximate], [sphereradius] );

$object->CalculateProtrusionIndices( { Approximate => [approximate], SphereRadius => [sphereradius] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [approximate] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [sphereradius] | Optional | 10.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
##########
#
# Assign various properties to amino acids and their atoms 
# These may then be used to calculate 'residue feature' values over spatial neighborhoods.
# 

use MdmDiscoveryScript; # For working with Molecule Window
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

# Set this False to calculate custom residue neighborhood feature set
my $default = "True";
#property for surface display and site creation can be set on the command line.
#note that it is case sensitive
my $propertyName = "0A_CX_average";

if(@ARGV != 0){
($propertyName) = @ARGV;
}

# to run on a molecule in the active window, use this instead of OpenURL
# my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl(PdbUrlPrefix. '1aqk.pdb');

# Return an error message and exit if there is not an active Molecule Window
die "No Molecule Window!" unless $document;
$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);
print "Calculating atom properties\n";
# Many of the residue features depend on solvent surface accessibility and require that the atoms 
# have a precomputed SAA property, which is typically calculated using CHARMm.
# However, for demonstration purposes we can use the DS method and rename the property.

#check if the first atom already has SAA property, if not then do calculation.
my $atoms = $document->Atoms();
my $atom = $atoms->Item(0);
if(! $atom->HasProperty("SAA")) {
print "No precomputed SAA properties, calculating Solvent Accessible Surface\n";
$document->SolventAccessibleSurface();
$document->RenameUserProperty("Atom Solvent Accessibility","SAA",$atom->ClassName());
$document->RenameUserProperty("Percent Sidechain Solvent Accessibility","Fractional Sidechain SAA",$atom->Parent()->ClassName()); 
$document->RenameUserProperty("Percent Solvent Accessibility","Fractional Residue SAA",$atom->Parent()->ClassName());
#convert the percent accessibilities to fractional values for consistency with the method below 
foreach my $atom(@$atoms){
if($atom->HasProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA")){
my $sa = $atom->GetProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA")/100.0;
$atom->SetProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA",$sa);
}
if($atom->HasProperty("Fractional Residue SAA")){
my $sa = $atom->GetProperty("Fractional Residue SAA")/100.0;
$atom->SetProperty("Fractional Residue SAA",$sa);
}
}
}else{
#This calculates the Sidechain and Residue fractional exposures, using the precomputed SAA atom properties.
#the extended tripeptide exposures have been calculated for various CHARMm forcefields, with the appropriate 
#set used according to the forcefield setting on the structure.
$document->CalculateFractionalResidueExposures(True,True);
}
#Set the Black and Mould hydrophobicities for each amino acid residue. The argument specifies whether to 'normalize' the values
#to set the hydrophobicity of glycine to zero.

$document->SetBlackAndMouldHydrophobicities(False);

#Calculate the 'protrusion indices'. This sets a property CX on each atom. If the 'approximate' method
# is used (first argument True) then there are no prerequisites - the calculation will be performed as
# in the original paper by Pintar et al, using only non-hydrogen atoms and a single atom volume of 20.1.
#Otherwise, all atoms are used; if they have a property VDWRadius set (eg corresponding to the CHARMm forcefield values)
#these will be used, otherwise the standard DS element VDW radii are used. The second argument is the sphere radius used
#for the calculation.

$document->CalculateProtrusionIndices(False,10.0);

#Calculate the 'depth indices'. This sets a property DPX on each atom. It requires precomputed atom SAA properties.
#Exposed atoms will always have a DPX of zero. In addition, atoms will have a property DPX_RAD assigned. This is the VDW radius of
#the nearest surface atom, which is required for the simple electrostatic potential calculation. If a property VDWRadius set
# (eg corresponding to the CHARMm forcefield values)
#these will be used, otherwise the standard DS element VDW radii are used.

$document->CalculateDepthIndices();

#Performs a simple electrostatic potential calculation and sets atom properties EPOT. It requires the DPX and DPX_RAD properties to get the distance of the
#atom from the surface, so will run the Depth Indices calculation if they aren't already set. It therefore also requires SAA atom properties.
#Ideally the atomic charges should be set using the desired CHARMm forcefield.

$document->CalculateElectrostaticPotentials();

#The following lines demonstrate how to calculate 'residue neighborhood features'.
#These are the result of taking an existing property value for each atom within a given radius of any atom
#in the residue for which the property is being calculated, and then performing operations such as total or average.
# Note that a radius of 0 will give the result of the operation on just the residue itself.
#The new residue property names will be formed from radius_property_operation eg
# 5A_SAA_hydrophilic
#
#The choice of operations is:
# average: average of the property over all the atoms in the neighborhood
# minimum: minimum value for the property in the neighborhood
# maximum: maximum value for the property in the neighborhood
# total: sum of the property over all atoms in the neighborhood
# hydrophobic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Ala,Ile,Leu,Met,Phe,Trp,Tyr or Val
# hydrophilic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Arg,His,Lys,Asp,Glu,Ser,Thr,Asn or Gln (His is any protonation state of histidine)
# positive: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Arg,Hsp or Lys (Hsp is positively charged Histidine)
# negative: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Asp or Glu
# aromatic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues His, Phe, Trp and Tyr
# backbone: sum over all backbone atoms C CA N O and attached hydrogens
# sidechain: sum over all non-backbone atoms
# exposed: sum over all surface exposed atoms. (obviously SAA is a prerequisite)
#
# The ExposedOnly argument allows the feature calculation to be restricted to residues which have some
# surface exposure ie atoms with SAA >0
# 
#The first form calculates these residue features for a default set of properties, operations and radii. These are:
# radii 0,3,5,7,10,12,15,20,25
# properties operations
# CX average,minimum,maximum 
# DPX average,minimum,maximum
# SAA total,hydrophobic,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,backbone,sidechain 
# Charge total,exposed
# EPOT total
#
#The second allows for any numeric user defined properties with any combination of operators, and any integer radii.

print "Calculating Residue Neighborhood Features, default $default\n";

if($default eq "True"){
$document->CalculateDefaultResidueNeighborhoodFeatures(False);
}else{
my $radii= DiscoveryScript::IntegerArray::Create();
$radii->AddItem(0);
$radii->AddItem(3);
$radii->AddItem(5);
$radii->AddItem(7);
my $featureNames = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
my $subTypes = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$featureNames->AddItem("CX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("DPX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("Charges");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,exposed");
$featureNames->AddItem("SAA");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,aromatic,backbone,sidechain");
$document->CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures($radii,$featureNames,$subTypes,False);
}
print "Finished calculating features\n";
#now demonstrate the generic patch group creation API
#get the maximum value for this property

my $residues = $document->Residues();
my $atoms = $document->Atoms();
my $max = -999999;
my $min = 999999;
my $minPatchCutoff = 0.0;
my $minPeakCutoff = 0.1;
foreach my $res (@$residues){
if($res->HasProperty($propertyName)){
my $val = $res->GetProperty($propertyName);
if($val > $max){$max = $val;}
if($val < $min){$min = $val;}
}
}
#the range setting may not be ideal for all properties. 
if($max != -999999){
$minPeakCutoff = $max/5;
$minPatchCutoff = $max/10;
$max = $max/2;
$min = -1.0*$max;

#create a surface colored by this property
my $surface = $document->CreateSolidSurface($atoms,Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent);
$surface->Name = "$propertyName Surface";

my $surfacePropertyColorScheme = Mdm::spectrumBlueWhiteRed;
$surface->Select();
$document->SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme( $propertyName,
$surfacePropertyColorScheme, 32, $min,$max, False, "" );
$surface->IsTransparent(True);
$surface->IsLegendShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll();
$document->FindSurfacePropertySites($propertyName,5.0,$max,$minPatchCutoff);
}else{
print "Property for surface patches $propertyName not present\n";
}
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
$document->UpdateViews();

print "Finished script example\n";
```

# CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculateresidueneighborhoodfeatures_function.htm

## CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures function

### Description

For each residue, finds all atoms within given radii of it and then for specified properties applies a choice of operations to yield the neighborhood features properties. The new residue property names will be formed from radius_property_operation e.g. 5A_SAA_hydrophilic. The parameters are:

* Radii: an integer array containing the radii to be used.

* PropertyNames: A string array containing the names of the atom properties.

* Operations: A string array containing for each of the PropertyNames a comma-delimited string specifying the required operations. The available operations are average,minimum,maximum,total,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,aromatic,backbone,sidechain,exposed.

* ExposedOnly: Specifies whether to limit the calculation to residues with solvent surface exposure.

### Applies to

The CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures function

#### Instance

$object->CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures( <radii>, <propertynames>, <operations>, [exposedonly] );

$object->CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures( { Radii => <radii>, PropertyNames => <propertynames>, Operations => <operations>, ExposedOnly => [exposedonly] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <operations> | Required | | DiscoveryScript::StringArray |
| <propertynames> | Required | | DiscoveryScript::StringArray |
| <radii> | Required | | DiscoveryScript::IntegerArray |
| [exposedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

```text
$radii->AddItem(0);
$radii->AddItem(3);
$radii->AddItem(5);
$radii->AddItem(7);
my $featureNames = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
my $subTypes = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$featureNames->AddItem("CX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("DPX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("Charges");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,exposed");
$featureNames->AddItem("SAA");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,aromatic,backbone,sidechain");
$document->CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures($radii,$featureNames,$subTypes,False);
}
print "Finished calculating features\n";
#now demonstrate the generic patch group creation API
#get the maximum value for this property

my $residues = $document->Residues();
my $atoms = $document->Atoms();
my $max = -999999;
my $min = 999999;
my $minPatchCutoff = 0.0;
my $minPeakCutoff = 0.1;
foreach my $res (@$residues){
if($res->HasProperty($propertyName)){
my $val = $res->GetProperty($propertyName);
if($val > $max){$max = $val;}
if($val < $min){$min = $val;}
}
}
#the range setting may not be ideal for all properties. 
if($max != -999999){
$minPeakCutoff = $max/5;
$minPatchCutoff = $max/10;
$max = $max/2;
$min = -1.0*$max;

#create a surface colored by this property
my $surface = $document->CreateSolidSurface($atoms,Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent);
$surface->Name = "$propertyName Surface";

my $surfacePropertyColorScheme = Mdm::spectrumBlueWhiteRed;
$surface->Select();
$document->SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme( $propertyName,
$surfacePropertyColorScheme, 32, $min,$max, False, "" );
$surface->IsTransparent(True);
$surface->IsLegendShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll();
$document->FindSurfacePropertySites($propertyName,5.0,$max,$minPatchCutoff);
}else{
print "Property for surface patches $propertyName not present\n";
}
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
$document->UpdateViews();

print "Finished script example\n";
```

# CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculatesidechainalignmentrmsd_function.htm

## CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd function

### Description

CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd calculates the RMSD values between side-chain atoms of aligned amino acids of two protein structures. By default the ResidueReport
option is True and the function returns an array of real numbers which contain
the per-residue RMSD values and includes the overall RMSD value in the last
element; if ResidueReport is false the array only contains the overall value.

In the cases where the aligned residues are of different type, this function uses/matches side-chain atoms with the same atom name. Other atoms are ignored.

### Applies to

The CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd( <reference>, <referencesequence>, <molecule>, <moleculesequence>, [selectedonly], [residuereport] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd( { Reference => <reference>, ReferenceSequence => <referencesequence>, Molecule => <molecule>, MoleculeSequence => <moleculesequence>, SelectedOnly => [selectedonly], ResidueReport => [residuereport] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <moleculesequence> | Required | | String |
| <reference> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <referencesequence> | Required | | String |
| [residuereport] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [selectedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use alignment superimposition functions and
# RMSD calculation functions for amino acids or non-standard residues.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1gaf.pdb' );

my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1gaf = $document->Molecules->[1];

# H chain V domains only
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
$molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
$molecule1gaf->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
}

my $Sequence1aj7 = $molecule1aj7->AminoAcidSequence;
my $Sequence1gaf = $molecule1gaf->AminoAcidSequence;
my $sequences = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1aj7);
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1gaf);

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms. The function returns an array
# of RMSD values between the reference and all molecules, starting with itself.
my $rmsds =
$document->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment( $document->Molecules, $sequences,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms, True );

print "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $document->Molecules->Count() ; ++$i )
{
print "\t"
. $document->Molecules->[$i]->Name . " to "
. $molecule1aj7->Name . ": ";
printf "%.3f\n", $rmsds->[$i];
}
print "\n";

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD
# Note that these functions return an array of real numbers. These are the
# per residue RMSD values plus, in the last element, the overall RMSD.
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it (the value will be zero). This can happen for
# unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation only for
# selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the required atoms for
# the requested type of calculation.
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item( $apRmsd->Count() - 1 );
print "\n";

# This demonstrates that the array is for all residues plus overall
# value, not just selected, and that as the first chain(L) is
# unselected (its values are 0).
printf "Number of values returned is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain.
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H chain.
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

# Get antigen NPE from 1aj7.
my $antigen1 = $document->Molecules->[0]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Get antigen NPE from 1gaf.
my $antigen2 = $document->Molecules->[1]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Copy antigen residues to a new document.
my $tmpDocument = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $tmpMolecule1 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen1Copy = $antigen1->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen1Copy, $tmpMolecule1 );
my $tmpMolecule2 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen2Copy = $antigen2->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen2Copy, $tmpMolecule2 );

$tmpDocument->FitView();

# Calculate NPE RMSD.
my $rmsd =
$tmpDocument->CalculateOtherResidueRmsd( $tmpMolecule1, $tmpMolecule2 );
printf "NPE RMSD: %.3f\n", $rmsd->[1];
```

# CalculateSideChainRmsd function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/calculatesidechainrmsd_function.htm

## CalculateSideChainRmsd function

### Description

CalculateSideChainRmsd calculates the RMSD values between side-chain atoms on residues of two protein structures. By default the ResidueReport
option is True and the function returns an array of real numbers which contain
the per-residue RMSD values and includes the overall RMSD value in the last
element; if ResidueReport is false the array only contains the overall value.

The two proteins have to have the same sequence.

### Applies to

The CalculateSideChainRmsd function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CalculateSideChainRmsd function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateSideChainRmsd( <reference>, <molecule>, [selectedonly], [residuereport] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->CalculateSideChainRmsd( { Reference => <reference>, Molecule => <molecule>, SelectedOnly => [selectedonly], ResidueReport => [residuereport] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <reference> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| [residuereport] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [selectedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use superimposition functions
# and RMSD calculation functions for amino acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load 2rcs (an unligated antibody) from PDB.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '2rcs.pdb' );

# Load 1aj7 (a ligated antibody having the same sequence as 2crs) from PDB.
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

my $molecule2rcs = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[1];

my $hv2rcs = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 2rcs H chain V domain
my $hv1aj7 = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 1aj7 H chain V domain

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $molecule2rcs->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv2rcs->AddItem($aminoAcid);

$aminoAcid = $molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv1aj7->AddItem($aminoAcid);
}

# Show the transformation matrix which would superimpose the Vh
# domains by C-alpha atoms. This does not alter the coordinates
# of either structure.
my $matrix = $document->GetSuperimposeProteinMatrix( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
print "Transformation matrix:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 4 ; ++$i )
{
print "\t";
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < 4 ; ++$j )
{
printf "%.3f ", $matrix->GetEntry( $i, $j );
}
print "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms
my $rmsd = $document->SuperimposeProtein( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
printf "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms: %.3f\n\n", $rmsd;

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD. Note that by default the functions return an
# array of per-residue RMSD values, finishing with the overall RMSD
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it in which case the value will be zero. This can happen
# for unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation
# only for selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the
# required atoms for the requested type of calculation. 
# If you do not want per-residue RMSDs, set the 4th parameter ResidueReport
# False. In this case the array will only contain the overall RMSD.
# In this example, the all protein rmsd has no residue values calculated
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True, False );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item(0);
print "\n";

#Show that the all protein array contains just the overall RMSD.
printf "Number of values returned for all protein is %d\n", $apRmsd->Count();

# Demonstrating that the array is for all residues plus overall value not
# just selected and that as the first chain(L) is unselected its values
# are 0.
printf "Number of values returned for sidechains is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0), $scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

#Create a C-Alpha monitor
my $caMonitor = $document->CreateCAlphaMonitor();

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs before superimposing.\n";
if ($cAlphaPairs->Count > 0) {
printf "The first C-alpha to C-alpha pair distance is %.3f Angstroms.\n",
$cAlphaPairs->Item(0)->Distance;
}

#Lets do it for all matching atoms just to show the argument
my $rmsdByCA =
$document->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( $document->Molecules(), $caMonitor,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingAllAtoms );

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs after superimposing.\n";

#The values returned are like for Superimpose By Alignment - the first value
# is ref-ref (ie 0) then ref-mover for each superimposed molecule.
my $numVal = $rmsdByCA->Count();
printf( "Number of values returned for SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs %d\n",
$numVal );
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $numVal ; ++$i )
{
printf( "RMSD %d is %f\n", $i, $rmsdByCA->[$i] );
}

# use the filter function to retrieve the CAlpha atoms
my $cAlphaMonitors = $document->CAlphaMonitors;
foreach my $m (@$cAlphaMonitors)
{
print $m->ClassName ." filter entries: " . $m->CAlphaPairs->Count. "\n";
}

print "Finished Superimpose Script Example\n";
```

# CAlpha property

Source type: HTML

## CAlpha property

### Description

CAlpha looks for the carbon atom labeled "CA" in an amino acid.

### Applies to

The CAlpha property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid

### Using the CAlpha property

#### Get

my $atomObject = $object->CAlpha;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $atomObject | | | Mdm::Atom |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9INS.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleAtomLine } );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $sequence = $molecule->AminoAcidSequence;
print "AminoAcidSequence: $sequence\n";

my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
my $aminoAcid1 = $aminoAcids->Item(0);
my $aminoAcid2 = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
my $aminoAcid3 = $aminoAcids->Item(2);

my $distance = $document->CreateDistanceMonitor( $aminoAcid1->CAlpha, $aminoAcid2->CAlpha );

printf "Distance between CAlpha atoms of $aminoAcid1->{Name} and $aminoAcid2->{Name}: %8.3f\n", $distance->Distance;

my $angle = $document->CreateAngleMonitor( $aminoAcid1->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid1->AmideNitrogen, $aminoAcid1->CAlpha );

printf "Angle between amide carbon, nitrogen, and CAlpha atoms of $aminoAcid1->{Name}: %8.3f\n", $angle->Angle;

my $phiTorsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$aminoAcid1->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid2->AmideNitrogen,
$aminoAcid2->CAlpha, $aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon
);

my $psiTorsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$aminoAcid2->AmideNitrogen, $aminoAcid2->CAlpha,
$aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid3->AmideNitrogen
);

print "Amino acid $aminoAcid2->{Name}: ";
printf "phi = %8.3f, psi = %8.3f\n", $phiTorsion->Angle, $psiTorsion->Angle;
```

```text
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item(0);
print "\n";

#Show that the all protein array contains just the overall RMSD.
printf "Number of values returned for all protein is %d\n", $apRmsd->Count();

# Demonstrating that the array is for all residues plus overall value not
# just selected and that as the first chain(L) is unselected its values
# are 0.
printf "Number of values returned for sidechains is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0), $scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

#Create a C-Alpha monitor
my $caMonitor = $document->CreateCAlphaMonitor();

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs before superimposing.\n";
if ($cAlphaPairs->Count > 0) {
printf "The first C-alpha to C-alpha pair distance is %.3f Angstroms.\n",
$cAlphaPairs->Item(0)->Distance;
}

#Lets do it for all matching atoms just to show the argument
my $rmsdByCA =
$document->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( $document->Molecules(), $caMonitor,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingAllAtoms );

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs after superimposing.\n";

#The values returned are like for Superimpose By Alignment - the first value
# is ref-ref (ie 0) then ref-mover for each superimposed molecule.
my $numVal = $rmsdByCA->Count();
printf( "Number of values returned for SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs %d\n",
$numVal );
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $numVal ; ++$i )
{
printf( "RMSD %d is %f\n", $i, $rmsdByCA->[$i] );
}

# use the filter function to retrieve the CAlpha atoms
my $cAlphaMonitors = $document->CAlphaMonitors;
foreach my $m (@$cAlphaMonitors)
{
print $m->ClassName ." filter entries: " . $m->CAlphaPairs->Count. "\n";
}

print "Finished Superimpose Script Example\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use superimposition functions
# and RMSD calculation functions for amino acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load 2rcs (an unligated antibody) from PDB.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '2rcs.pdb' );

# Load 1aj7 (a ligated antibody having the same sequence as 2crs) from PDB.
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

my $molecule2rcs = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[1];

my $hv2rcs = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 2rcs H chain V domain
my $hv1aj7 = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 1aj7 H chain V domain

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $molecule2rcs->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv2rcs->AddItem($aminoAcid);

$aminoAcid = $molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv1aj7->AddItem($aminoAcid);
}

# Show the transformation matrix which would superimpose the Vh
# domains by C-alpha atoms. This does not alter the coordinates
# of either structure.
my $matrix = $document->GetSuperimposeProteinMatrix( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
print "Transformation matrix:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 4 ; ++$i )
{
print "\t";
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < 4 ; ++$j )
{
printf "%.3f ", $matrix->GetEntry( $i, $j );
}
print "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms
my $rmsd = $document->SuperimposeProtein( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
printf "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms: %.3f\n\n", $rmsd;

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD. Note that by default the functions return an
# array of per-residue RMSD values, finishing with the overall RMSD
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it in which case the value will be zero. This can happen
# for unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation
# only for selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the
# required atoms for the requested type of calculation. 
# If you do not want per-residue RMSDs, set the 4th parameter ResidueReport
# False. In this case the array will only contain the overall RMSD.
# In this example, the all protein rmsd has no residue values calculated
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True, False );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item(0);
print "\n";

#Show that the all protein array contains just the overall RMSD.
printf "Number of values returned for all protein is %d\n", $apRmsd->Count();

# Demonstrating that the array is for all residues plus overall value not
# just selected and that as the first chain(L) is unselected its values
# are 0.
printf "Number of values returned for sidechains is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0), $scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

#Create a C-Alpha monitor
my $caMonitor = $document->CreateCAlphaMonitor();

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs before superimposing.\n";
if ($cAlphaPairs->Count > 0) {
printf "The first C-alpha to C-alpha pair distance is %.3f Angstroms.\n",
$cAlphaPairs->Item(0)->Distance;
}

#Lets do it for all matching atoms just to show the argument
my $rmsdByCA =
$document->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( $document->Molecules(), $caMonitor,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingAllAtoms );

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs after superimposing.\n";

#The values returned are like for Superimpose By Alignment - the first value
# is ref-ref (ie 0) then ref-mover for each superimposed molecule.
my $numVal = $rmsdByCA->Count();
printf( "Number of values returned for SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs %d\n",
```

# CapNucleotide function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/capnucleotide_function.htm

## CapNucleotide function

### Description

CapNucleotide changes the phosphate group at 5' to a hydroxyl group
and adds a hydrogen to the O3' atom at the 3' end.
Capping also changes the residue inside a chain when there is a break
(i.e., two consecutive residues are not bonded to each other in the chain).

### Applies to

The CapNucleotide function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::Nucleotide

### Using the CapNucleotide function

#### Instance

$object->CapNucleotide();

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w

use strict;

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

);

print "Amino acid $aminoAcid2->{Name}: ";
printf "phi = %8.3f, psi = %8.3f\n", $phiTorsion->Angle, $psiTorsion->Angle;
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate use of Mdm::Cell class.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('9INS');

my $cell = $document->Cells->Item(0);

print "Crystal cell parameters:\n";
my $format = "\t%s = %8.3f\n\t%s = %8.3f\n\t%s = %8.3f\n";
printf $format, 'a', $cell->LengthA, 'b', $cell->LengthB, 'c', $cell->LengthC;
printf $format,
'alpha', $cell->AngleAlpha,
'beta', $cell->AngleBeta,
'gamma', $cell->AngleGamma;

my $cartesian = $cell->CartesianToFractionMatrix;
printf "\t Cartesian to fractional transformation matrix:\n";
for ( my $row = 0 ; $row < 3 ; ++$row )
{
printf "\t%8.3f\t%8.3f\t%8.3f\n",
$cartesian->GetEntry( $row, 0 ),
$cartesian->GetEntry( $row, 1 ),
$cartesian->GetEntry( $row, 2 );
}
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the basic non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3fzm');
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;
$document->Zoom(15);
$document->IsHierarchyViewShown = True;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Create a non-bond monitor for a subset of atoms.\n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $monitor = $document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();

# -- Analyze the identified interactions. ---------------------------
my $nonbonds = $monitor->Nonbonds;
my $count = $nonbonds->Count;
printf "Found %d non-bond interactions (total):\n", $count;

print $monitor->FavorableNonbonds->Count 
. " of these are favorable interactions (such as H-bonds).\n";
print $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds->Count
. " of these are unfavorable interactions (such as bumps).\n\n";

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Analyze first non-bond interaction:\n";
my $nonbond = $nonbonds->Item(0);

my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$nonbond->Distance;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
my $unfavorableNonbonds = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds;
if ($unfavorableNonbonds->Count > 0) 
{
print "Analyze first unfavorable non-bond interaction:\n";
my $unfavorableNonbond = $unfavorableNonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $unfavorableNonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $unfavorableNonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$unfavorableNonbond->Distance;
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "All non-bonds of a particular type can be retrieved ";
print "using the NonbondsOfType filter.\n";
my $hBonds = $monitor->NonbondsOfType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType);
printf "Found %d hydrogen bonds using NonbondOfType filter.\n\n", $hBonds->Count;

print "Alternatively the IsMatchingNonbondType property can be used to \n";
print "identify interactions of a specific types. The following atom pairs \n";
print "indicate classical hydrogen bonding: \n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
if ($nonbond->IsMatchingNonbondType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType))
{
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);

print '* ' . $atom1->FullName . " (";
print 'donor ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrogenDonor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHalogen);
print 'positive ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPositive);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ') and ';

print $atom2->FullName . " (";
print 'acceptor ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrogenAcceptor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHalogen);
print 'negative ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsNegative);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ")\n";
}
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "\nThe NonbondTypes property can be used to identify all \n";
print "interaction types of a non-bond.\n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
printf "- %s (%s) and %s (%s):",
$nonbond->FromSite->Name,
$nonbond->FromSite->ChemistryName,
$nonbond->ToSite->Name,
$nonbond->ToSite->ChemistryName;

#these are the type enums 
print " Types: ";
my $nonbondTypes = $nonbond->NonbondTypes;
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
print "$type ";
}

#these are the category enums 
print " Categories: ";
my $nonbondCategories = $nonbond->NonbondCategories;
foreach my $category (@$nonbondCategories) {
print "$category ";
}

#these APIs give the name(s) of the type/categories as a string 
#(the same as appears in the Nonbond tab of the DS MDT)
print " : Type Names: ";
my $typeNames = $nonbond->TypeNames;
print "$typeNames";

print " : Category Names: ";
my $categories = $nonbond->CategoryNames;
print "$categories";

print "\n";
}
print "\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
#This is used for the script apis
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $temp = 0;
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('4ins');

#By default, the script returns string containing a csv file of properties for the predicted disulfides.
#Only new disulfides are found, for any chain combination, minimum sequence separation 5,
#maximum energy 10.0
# i.e. default args are novelDisulfidesOnly, anyChainDisulfides, 5, 10.0, true will use this one to show how to get the residues/bonds

my $csvFile=$document->PredictDisulfides();

#save the csv file
my $name=$document->ModelName();
my $fileName=$name . "Predicted_New_Disulfides.csv";
open FILE, '>' . $fileName;
print FILE $csvFile;
close FILE;

my $molecules=$document->Molecules();

#note that if validation of existing disulfides is performed (by using Mdm::existingDisulfidesOnly#or Mdm::novelAndExistingDisulfides then a second molecule containing the modelled disulfide
#bridges and with additional properties on the bond and molecule 

my $numMols=$molecules->Count; 
if($numMols == 1){

$document->DeselectAll();
my $molecule=$molecules->Item(0);
my $residuePairsAssembly = $molecule->Filter(
{ Type=>"Assembly", Property => "Name", Name => "Predicted Disulfide Bridge Residues" } );
if($residuePairsAssembly->Count() == 1){
print "Potential residue pairs for mutation to cysteine to form disulfide bridge in ".$molecule->Name . ": \n";
my $residuePairs=$residuePairsAssembly->Item(0)->Groups();
foreach my $residuePair (@$residuePairs) {
my $residuePairList=$residuePair->ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder();
#should be 2 residues in here
if($residuePairList->Count == 2){
my $residue1 = $residuePairList->Item(0);
my $residue2 = $residuePairList->Item(1);
print "Group " . $residuePair->Name . " contains residues: ". $residue1->Name . " and " . $residue2->Name . "\n";
}
}
}

#this should now also contain predicted site objects from which we can extract more properties
print "Sites for mutation to cysteine\n";
my $sites = $document->DisulfideBridgeSites;
my $numSites = $sites->Count();
print $numSites . " sites\n";
for(my $index = 0; $index < $numSites; ++$index){
my $site=$sites->Item($index);
my $label = $site->Name;
my $score = $site->GetProperty("Score");
my $energy = $site->GetProperty("Energy");
my $badContacts = $site->GetProperty("Bad Contacts");
my $depth = $site->GetProperty("Residue Depth");
my $mobility = $site->GetProperty("Thermal Mobility");
my $sep = $site->GetProperty("Sequence Separation");
my $volchange = $site->GetProperty("Volume Change");
my $env = $site->GetProperty("Environment");
my $SA = $site->GetProperty("Solvent Accessibility");
my $chi3 = $site->GetProperty("Chi3");
print " site " . $label . " score " . $score . " energy " . $energy . " Bad contacts " . $badContacts ." residue depth " . $depth . " mobility " . $mobility . " sep " . $sep . " volchange " . $volchange . " env " . $env . " SA " . $SA . " chi3 " . $chi3 . "\n";

my $SG1Coord = $site->SG1Coord;
my $SG2Coord = $site->SG2Coord;
print " SG coordinates (" . $SG1Coord->X . ", " . $SG1Coord->Y . ", " . $SG1Coord->Z . ") and " .
"(" . $SG2Coord->X . ", " . $SG2Coord->Y . ", " . $SG2Coord->Z . ")\n";
my $residues = $site->ResiduesToMutate;
if($residues->Count == 2){
print "residue 1 " . $residues->Item(0)->Name . " residue 2 " . $residues->Item(1)->Name . "\n";
}else{
print " error - site should contain two residues\n";
}

#create S-S bridge from a site - the command works on any selected DisulfideBridgeSite
if($score > 80.0){
print "Score " . $score . " - Creating S-S bridge\n"; 
$site->Select();
$document->CreateDisulfideBridges();
$site->Deselect();
}

}

}
```

# CellChoice property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/cellchoice_property.htm

## CellChoice property

### Description

Mdm::CellChoice identifies the symmetry axes. For some space groups, alternate
settings are possible, and the CellChoice property, in conjunction with the
Mdm::AxisOriginType property, allows this to be specified for a cell. For
instance, the non-standard space group P21/N is space group 14 (P21/C) with cell choice 2.

### Applies to

The CellChoice property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::SpaceGroup

### Using the CellChoice property

#### Get

my $cellchoiceEnum = $object->CellChoice;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $cellchoiceEnum | | | enum Mdm::CellChoice |
| $object | | | Mdm::SpaceGroup |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use Mdm::SpaceGroup objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Get space group from document.
my $cell = $document->Cells->Item(0);
my $spacegroup = $cell->SpaceGroup;

print "The following is a list of space group properties:\n";
print "Number:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->Number . "\n";
print "Short Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->Symbol . "\n";
print "SchoenfliesSymbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->SchoenfliesSymbol . "\n";
print "Full Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->FullSymbol . "\n";
print "Lattice type:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->LatticeType . "\n";
print "Cell choice:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->CellChoice . "\n";
print "AxisOriginType:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->AxisOriginType . "\n";
print "Number of sym. operator:\t\t"
. $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount . "\n";

my $count = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $operator = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperator($index);
print "Symmetry operator $index\n";
print "\tName: " . $operator->Name . "\n";

my $rotation = $operator->Rotation;
my $format = "\t %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n";
print "\tRotation Matrix:\n";
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 0, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 1, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 2 );

my $translation = $operator->Translation;
print "\tTranslation:\n";
printf "$format", $translation->X, $translation->Y, $translation->Z;
}
```

# Center function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/center_function.htm

## Center function

### Description

Center moves the view point to the center of the selected objects
or to the center of all objects if none are selected.

### Applies to

The Center function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the Center function

#### Command

$object->Center();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to center the view on a selection.
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });
# Center the view on selected residue.
my $atoms = SelectByString( $document, "A:1:*" );

my $index =0;
foreach my $atom (@$atoms) {
printf "%3d) Atom: %s\n", ++$index, $atom->Name;
}

$document->Center();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use the CentroidMonitors filter.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
$document->CreateCentroidMonitor($atoms);

my $centroidMonitors = $document->CentroidMonitors;
die "No centroid monitors found.\n" if ( not $centroidMonitors->Count > 0 );

my $centroidMonitor = $centroidMonitors->Item(0);

print "Properties of centroid monitor object:\n";
my $propertyNames = $centroidMonitor->PropertyNames();
foreach my $propertyName (@$propertyNames)
{
my $propertyValue = $centroidMonitor->GetProperty($propertyName);
print "\t $propertyName: $propertyValue\n";
}
print "\n";

# If object is a center of geometry monitor convert to
# center of mass monitor.
if ( !$centroidMonitor->IsCenterOfMassMonitor() )
{
my $xyz = $centroidMonitor->Center();
print 'The center of geometry of 1crn is: ';
printf "(%5.3f %5.3f %5.3f)\n", $xyz->X, $xyz->Y, $xyz->Z;

# Change monitor to a center-of-mass monitor.
$centroidMonitor->IsCenterOfMassMonitor = "True";
}

my $center = $centroidMonitor->Center();
print "The center of mass of 1crn is: ";
printf "(%5.3f %5.3f %5.3f)\n", $center->X, $center->Y, $center->Z;
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create some features on the query
# Create a ring aromatic
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Name("benzene");
my $ringAromaticOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$ringAromaticOperator->Name('RA1');
my $ringAromaticFeatureObject =
$ringAromaticOperator->CreateRingAromaticFeature(
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Atoms );
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Select(); # delete later

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature(
$ringAromaticFeatureObject->CentroidFeature(), 1.6 );
my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature(
$ringAromaticFeatureObject->NormalFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create a donor feature
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -2, -4, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# Give the hydrogen bond donor a higher weight (2.0) than the default (1.0)
$donorOperator->Weight(2.0);

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create an acceptor feature at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );

printf "%s Head: x: %.4f y: %.4f z: %.4f\n",
$locationFeatureHead->ClassName, 
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->X, 
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->Y,
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->Z;

my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

printf "%s Tail: x: %.4f y: %.4f z: %.4f\n",
$locationFeatureHead->ClassName,
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->X, 
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->Y,
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->Z;

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use the CentroidMonitors filter.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
$document->CreateCentroidMonitor($atoms);

my $centroidMonitors = $document->CentroidMonitors;
die "No centroid monitors found.\n" if ( not $centroidMonitors->Count > 0 );

my $centroidMonitor = $centroidMonitors->Item(0);

print "Properties of centroid monitor object:\n";
my $propertyNames = $centroidMonitor->PropertyNames();
foreach my $propertyName (@$propertyNames)
{
my $propertyValue = $centroidMonitor->GetProperty($propertyName);
print "\t $propertyName: $propertyValue\n";
}
print "\n";

# If object is a center of geometry monitor convert to
# center of mass monitor.
if ( !$centroidMonitor->IsCenterOfMassMonitor() )
{
my $xyz = $centroidMonitor->Center();
print 'The center of geometry of 1crn is: ';
printf "(%5.3f %5.3f %5.3f)\n", $xyz->X, $xyz->Y, $xyz->Z;

# Change monitor to a center-of-mass monitor.
$centroidMonitor->IsCenterOfMassMonitor = "True";
}

my $center = $centroidMonitor->Center();
print "The center of mass of 1crn is: ";
printf "(%5.3f %5.3f %5.3f)\n", $center->X, $center->Y, $center->Z;
```

# ChangeFormalCharge function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/changeformalcharge_function.htm

## ChangeFormalCharge function

### Description

ChangeFormalCharge changes the formal charge of the selected atoms. When the
Set parameter is True, the formal charge is set to the specified value. Otherwise, the formal
charge is incremented by the specified value.

### Applies to

The ChangeFormalCharge function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ChangeFormalCharge function

#### Command

$object->ChangeFormalCharge( <numerator>, <denominator>, [set] );

$object->ChangeFormalCharge( { Numerator => <numerator>, Denominator => <denominator>, Set => [set] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <denominator> | Required | | Integer |
| <numerator> | Required | | Integer |
| [set] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

# ChangeObjectParent function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/changeobjectparent_function.htm

## ChangeObjectParent function

### Description

ChangeObjectParent changes the child object's parent.

IMPORTANT! The SetParent should be used for most reparenting needs.
The ChangeObjectParent function is intended for advanced users.

ChangeObjectParent allows for the parent object to be in the
same document as the child or in a different document. Use 0 to remove an object from the document.

### Applies to

The ChangeObjectParent function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ChangeObjectParent function

#### Instance

$object->ChangeObjectParent( <child>, <parent> );

$object->ChangeObjectParent( { Child => <child>, Parent => <parent> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <child> | Required | | Mdm::Object |
| <parent> | Required | | Mdm::Object |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script will illustrate the use of RootObject and ChangeObjectParent.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
die "An open Molecule Window is required to " 
. "run this example script." unless $document;

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
printf "Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$molecule->Name,$molecule->Atoms->Count();

# Create a copy of the molecule.
my $moleculeCopy = $molecule->Copy();

# Reparent the copy to a new document's root object.
my $newDocument = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $newDocumentRoot = $newDocument->RootObject;
$newDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $moleculeCopy, $newDocumentRoot );

$newDocument->FitView();

printf "Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$newDocument->Molecules->Item(0)->Name,
$newDocument->Atoms->Count();
```

# ChargeCenter property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/chargecenter_property.htm

## ChargeCenter property

### Description

ChargeCenter indicates the coordinates of the center of
charge used in the calculation of the dipole moment by a dipole moment monitor.

The charge center is calculated as:

Σ(i) |q i |R i / Σ(i) |q i |

where q i is the partial charge of the i-th atom,
R i are the coordinates of the i-th atom, and the summation
Σ(i) runs over all atoms in the molecule.
For a molecule where all partial charges are zero, the center of mass
is used as the charge center.

### Applies to

The ChargeCenter property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::DipoleMomentMonitor

### Using the ChargeCenter property

#### Get

my $pointObject = $object->ChargeCenter;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $pointObject | | | Mdm::Point |
| $object | | | Mdm::DipoleMomentMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

my $monitor = $molecule->CreateDipoleMomentMonitor();

my $center = $monitor->ChargeCenter();
my $vector = $monitor->Vector();
printf "Dipole moment center: %4.2f, %4.2f, %4.2f\n",
$center->X, $center->Y, $center->Z;
print "Dipole magnitude: " . $monitor->Magnitude . "\n";
printf "Dipole vector: (%4.2f, %4.2f, %4.2f)\n",
$vector->X, $vector->Y, $vector->Z;
```

```text
use strict;
```

# ChartDiscoveryScript package

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/chartdiscoveryscript_package.htm

## ChartDiscoveryScript package

### Description

ChartDiscoveryScript provides data structures, functions, and properties
to access and manipulate Discovery Studio plots and maps. This package
is only accessible from the Discovery Studio client.

### Using the ChartDiscoveryScript package

Access to the ChartDiscoveryScript API is through the Perl use directive:

```text
use strict;
use ChartDiscoveryScript;
```

The strict directive is optional, but strongly recommended as it restricts
the use of unsafe constructs. All available classes will be imported from the ChartDiscoveryScript module.

#### Classes

Chart::Document

#### Properties

PlotAxisLabel PlotTitle

#### Functions

AddTrendLine Create3dPointPlot CreateBarPlot CreateClusterStructureDendrogram CreateContactMap CreateHeatMap CreateHistogram CreateHitRate CreateLinePlot CreatePointPlot CreateRamachandranMap CreateRecursivePartitioningDendrogram UpdateViews

#### Uses

DiscoveryStudioScript

#### Module

ChartDiscoveryScript.pm

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to create a point plot (client only).
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ChartDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

my $pointPlot = Chart::Document::CreatePointPlot(
{
MdmDocument => $mdmDocument,
DataTableTabName => 'Atom',
XAxisProperty => 'Partial Charge',
YAxisProperties => 'Isotropic Displacement,Occupancy'
}
);

print "Model Type: Chart2dModelType\n"
if ( $pointPlot->ModelType eq Chart2dModelType );

$pointPlot->AddTrendLine('Isotropic Displacement');
$pointPlot->UpdateViews();
```
