# ChemistryName property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/chemistryname_property.htm

## ChemistryName property

### Description

ChemistryName provides a chemical description of the
type of interaction involved in an Mdm::Nonbond .

### Applies to

The ChemistryName property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::NonbondSite , Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond

### Using the ChemistryName property

#### Get

my $stringValue = $object->ChemistryName;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::NonbondSite Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the basic non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3fzm');
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;
$document->Zoom(15);
$document->IsHierarchyViewShown = True;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Create a non-bond monitor for a subset of atoms.\n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $monitor = $document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();

# -- Analyze the identified interactions. ---------------------------
my $nonbonds = $monitor->Nonbonds;
my $count = $nonbonds->Count;
printf "Found %d non-bond interactions (total):\n", $count;

print $monitor->FavorableNonbonds->Count 
. " of these are favorable interactions (such as H-bonds).\n";
print $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds->Count
. " of these are unfavorable interactions (such as bumps).\n\n";

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Analyze first non-bond interaction:\n";
my $nonbond = $nonbonds->Item(0);

my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$nonbond->Distance;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
my $unfavorableNonbonds = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds;
if ($unfavorableNonbonds->Count > 0) 
{
print "Analyze first unfavorable non-bond interaction:\n";
my $unfavorableNonbond = $unfavorableNonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $unfavorableNonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $unfavorableNonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$unfavorableNonbond->Distance;
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "All non-bonds of a particular type can be retrieved ";
print "using the NonbondsOfType filter.\n";
my $hBonds = $monitor->NonbondsOfType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType);
printf "Found %d hydrogen bonds using NonbondOfType filter.\n\n", $hBonds->Count;

print "Alternatively the IsMatchingNonbondType property can be used to \n";
print "identify interactions of a specific types. The following atom pairs \n";
print "indicate classical hydrogen bonding: \n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
if ($nonbond->IsMatchingNonbondType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType))
{
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);

print '* ' . $atom1->FullName . " (";
print 'donor ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrogenDonor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHalogen);
print 'positive ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPositive);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ') and ';

print $atom2->FullName . " (";
print 'acceptor ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrogenAcceptor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHalogen);
print 'negative ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsNegative);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ")\n";
}
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "\nThe NonbondTypes property can be used to identify all \n";
print "interaction types of a non-bond.\n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
printf "- %s (%s) and %s (%s):",
$nonbond->FromSite->Name,
$nonbond->FromSite->ChemistryName,
$nonbond->ToSite->Name,
$nonbond->ToSite->ChemistryName;

#these are the type enums 
print " Types: ";
my $nonbondTypes = $nonbond->NonbondTypes;
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
print "$type ";
}

#these are the category enums 
print " Categories: ";
my $nonbondCategories = $nonbond->NonbondCategories;
foreach my $category (@$nonbondCategories) {
print "$category ";
}

#these APIs give the name(s) of the type/categories as a string 
#(the same as appears in the Nonbond tab of the DS MDT)
print " : Type Names: ";
my $typeNames = $nonbond->TypeNames;
print "$typeNames";

print " : Category Names: ";
my $categories = $nonbond->CategoryNames;
print "$categories";

print "\n";
}
print "\n";
```

## ChiralAtomCount property

### Description

ChiralAtomCount indicates the number of chiral atoms
in a chiral monitor object.

### Applies to

The ChiralAtomCount property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::ChiralityMonitor

### Using the ChiralAtomCount property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->ChiralAtomCount;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::ChiralityMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use chirality monitors.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9INS.pdb" );
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms();

my $monitor = $document->CreateChiralityMonitor();
my $chirals = $monitor->Chirals;
my $count = $monitor->ChiralAtomCount;

printf "Molecule has %4d chiral atoms:\n", $count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $chiral = $chirals->Item($index);
my $atom = $chiral->Atom;
my $residue = $atom->Parent;
my $chain = $residue->Parent;

my $label = $chain->Name . ':' . $residue->Name . ':' . $atom->Name;
printf "\t%s\n", $label;
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of various atom properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

# Define atom properties to list.
# This may be specified on the command line.
my $residueAtomName = 'THR2:CA';
if ( @ARGV != 0 )
{
($residueAtomName) = @ARGV;
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Get the specified atom.
my $atoms = FilterByString( $document, $residueAtomName );
die "Atom $residueAtomName not found. Aborting!\n\n"
if ( $atoms->Count == 0 );

my $atom = $atoms->[0];

# Print various atom properties. In the DiscoveryStudio client, the
# output will appear in the output pane of the scripting window.
print "List of properties for atom $residueAtomName:\n\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
print 'Element: ' . $atom->Element . "\n";
print 'Element Name: ' . $atom->ElementName . "\n";
print 'Element Symbol: ' . $atom->ElementSymbol . "\n";
print 'Mass: ' . $atom->Mass . "\n";
print 'Atomic number: ' . $atom->AtomicNumber . "\n";
print 'Charge: ' . $atom->Charge . "\n";
print 'Formal Charge: '
. $atom->FormalCharge->Numerator . "/"
. $atom->FormalCharge->Denominator . "\n";

print 'VDW Radius: ' . $atom->VdwRadius . "\n";
print 'Covalent Radius: ' . $atom->CovalentRadius . "\n";
print 'Chirality: ' . $atom->Chirality . "\n";
print 'Bond count: ' . $atom->BondCount . "\n";
print 'Bonding radius: ' . $atom->BondingRadius . "\n";
print 'Hybridization: ' . $atom->Hybridization . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen Count: ' . $atom->HydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'ImplicitHydrogen Count: ' . $atom->ImplicitHydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Acceptor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondAcceptor . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Donor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondDonor . "\n";
print 'Isotropic Displacement: ' . $atom->IsotropicDisplacement . "\n";
print 'Is Terminal Hydrogen: ' . $atom->IsTerminalHydrogen . "\n";
print 'Is Valence Satisfied: ' . $atom->IsValenceSatisfied . "\n";
print 'Lone Pair Count: ' . $atom->LonePairCount . "\n";
print 'Valence Count: ' . $atom->ValenceCount . "\n";
print 'Occupancy: ' . $atom->Occupancy . "\n";

printf "\n%s:\n", 'Display Properties';
print 'DisplayStyle: ' . $atom->DisplayStyle . "\n";
print 'Ball Size: ' . $atom->BallSize . "\n";
print 'Ball Size Default: ' . $atom->BallSizeDefault . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale: ' . $atom->CPKScale . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale Default: ' . $atom->CPKScaleDefault . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius: ' . $atom->StickRadius . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius Default: ' . $atom->StickRadiusDefault . "\n";

### Using the ChiralityMonitors filter

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->ChiralityMonitors;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use chirality monitors.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9INS.pdb" );
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms();

my $monitor = $document->CreateChiralityMonitor();
my $chirals = $monitor->Chirals;
my $count = $monitor->ChiralAtomCount;

printf "Molecule has %4d chiral atoms:\n", $count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $chiral = $chirals->Item($index);
my $atom = $chiral->Atom;
my $residue = $atom->Parent;
my $chain = $residue->Parent;

my $label = $chain->Name . ':' . $residue->Name . ':' . $atom->Name;
printf "\t%s\n", $label;
}
```

## Classes

### Description

describing its state and behaviors. The Classes provided in Discovery Studio
Scripting provide an interface to the underlying Discovery Studio data models
and methods. The following table provides a brief description of all available

# Classes Hierarchy

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/classes_hierarchy.htm

## Classes Hierarchy

### Description

The Classes within scripting can both derive to, and be derived from other classes.
This gives rise to a class hierarchy. Families of classes can
share Properties , Functions and Filters . For example, the Mdm::Object class has the IsSelected property which indicates if
an object is selected. This means that all derived classes such as Mdm::Geometric3d and Mdm::AcceptorFeature also
have the same property, which can then be used to determine if these objects
are themselves selected.

Within the documentation all Properties , Functions and Filters available to a class are listed. Some of these are provided directly to a class
while others are provided by way of the class, or classes, they are derived from.

For Functions that take objects as arguments, they can also
be used with any object derived from the one listed. For example, the CreateDistanceMonitor function takes two Mdm::Geometric3d objects as arguments. This means that you can
also use this function with any class that is derived from
the Mdm::Geometric3d class, such
as Mdm::Atom , Mdm::Sphere and Mdm::BindingSitePoint .

The hierarchy below shows the class hierarchy for all the available classes,
all of which are derived from the DiscoveryScript::Object class.
This can used to quickly identify how classes are related and
which ones can be substituted when using Functions .

# ClassName property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/classname_property.htm

## ClassName property

### Description

ClassName indicates the class name of a Discovery Script object.
All objects of a given class will have the same class name.
For example, the class name of an Mdm::Molecule is "Mdm::Molecule".

# Clean function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/clean_function.htm

## Clean function

### Description

Clean uses a fast, Dreiding like forcefield to improve the geometry of the selected atoms.
When no atoms are selected, all atoms are cleaned. This can be used to
generate reasonable 3D coordinates from 2D, random or nonsensical
geometries. The number of iterations can be specified as an parameter. The
Clean Energy will be added as an property of the molecules.

IMPORTANT! The ChargingMethod argument is a prototype. The API may be changed or removed
in the future and its use is not currently supported.

### Applies to

The Clean function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the Clean function

#### Command

$object->Clean( [iterations], [includeintermolecularforces], [cleanonlyselectedatoms], [perceiveandupdatearomaticity], [updatehydrogens], [chargingmethod], [ignoreautocalculatechargesflag], [chargethreshold], [reportenergyterms], [energyprefix], [includereceptoratoms] );

$object->Clean( { Iterations => [iterations], IncludeIntermolecularForces => [includeintermolecularforces], CleanOnlySelectedAtoms => [cleanonlyselectedatoms], PerceiveAndUpdateAromaticity => [perceiveandupdatearomaticity], UpdateHydrogens => [updatehydrogens], ChargingMethod => [chargingmethod], IgnoreAutoCalculateChargesFlag => [ignoreautocalculatechargesflag], ChargeThreshold => [chargethreshold], ReportEnergyTerms => [reportenergyterms], EnergyPrefix => [energyprefix], IncludeReceptorAtoms => [includereceptoratoms] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [chargethreshold] | Optional | 0.000001 | Real |
| [chargingmethod] | Optional | calculateGasteigerCharges | enum Mdm::ChargingMethod |
| [cleanonlyselectedatoms] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [energyprefix] | Optional | "" | String |
| [ignoreautocalculatechargesflag] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [includeintermolecularforces] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [includereceptoratoms] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [iterations] | Optional | 1000 | Integer |
| [perceiveandupdatearomaticity] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [reportenergyterms] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [updatehydrogens] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to access MDM objects and create a minimize molecule.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Create a document containing a molecule.
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom1 = $molecule->CreateAtom('C');
my $atom2 = $molecule->CreateAtom('C');
my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $atom1, $atom2, Mdm::doubleBond );

# Add hydrogen atoms.
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms();

# Calculate partial charges for the minimization step.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Perform a geometry minimization using the clean forcefield.
$document->Clean();

$molecule->Name = 'Ethene';
print "Created molecule " . $molecule->Name . ".\n";
```

# CleanProtein function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/cleanprotein_function.htm

## CleanProtein function

### Description

CleanProteins cleans protein molecules in a document by correcting problems commonly encountered in protein structures. The following parameters determine which problems are to be corrected:

* HydrogenRepresentation is an enum Mdm::HydrogenRepresentation that specifies whether the structure should have all, polar, or no hydrogens, and
will be used by any of the options that can create or delete hydrogen atoms.

* pH specifies the desired pH of ionizable side-chains and termini. It is
used if AdjustHydrogens or ModifyTermini is true.

* AdjustHydrogens modifies the entire structure to
have all, polar, or no hydrogens according to the setting of the
HydrogenRepresentation parameter.

* DeleteDisorder clears crystallographic alternate conformations
are and resets all occupancies to 1.0.

* StandardizeNames standardizes common nomenclature variations in terminal
groups, amide hydrogens and Isoleucine.

* CompleteResidues adds missing atoms to amino acid backbones or
sidechains.

* ModifyTermini adjusts termini.

* RemoveTermini removes or adds terminal characteristics
if the ModifyTermini parameter is true.

* FixBonds corrects connectivity and bond orders.

* TerminalOxygenNames is a enum Mdm::AminoAcidCTerminalOxygenNames that specifies the
nomenclature to be applied to oxygen atoms on the C terminus.

* UsePredictedpK specifies whether to use predicted or standard pK values to
set the protonation state of ionizable side-chains and termini. It is used if
AdjustHydrogens or ModifyTermini is true.

* MergeCappingGroups specifies whether to merge capping groups defined as separate non-amino acid residues into the first/last amino acid in the chain.

### Applies to

The CleanProtein function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CleanProtein function

#### Instance

my $stringValue = $object->CleanProtein( [hydrogenrepresentation], [ph], [adjusthydrogens], [deletedisorder], [standardizenames], [completeresidues], [modifytermini], [removetermini], [fixbonds], [terminaloxygennames], [usepredictedpk], [mergecappinggroups] );

my $stringValue = $object->CleanProtein( { HydrogenRepresentation => [hydrogenrepresentation], pH => [ph], AdjustHydrogens => [adjusthydrogens], DeleteDisorder => [deletedisorder], StandardizeNames => [standardizenames], CompleteResidues => [completeresidues], ModifyTermini => [modifytermini], RemoveTermini => [removetermini], FixBonds => [fixbonds], TerminalOxygenNames => [terminaloxygennames], UsePredictedpK => [usepredictedpk], MergeCappingGroups => [mergecappinggroups] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| [adjusthydrogens] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [completeresidues] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [deletedisorder] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [fixbonds] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [hydrogenrepresentation] | Optional | noHydrogenRepresentation | enum Mdm::HydrogenRepresentation |
| [mergecappinggroups] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [modifytermini] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [ph] | Optional | 7.0 | Real |
| [removetermini] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [standardizenames] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [terminaloxygennames] | Optional | oxygenNamesOAndOXT | enum Mdm::AminoAcidCTerminalOxygenNames |
| [usepredictedpk] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1u7e');

# this would use CleanProtein with default parameters
# my $cleanResults = $document->CleanProtein();

# However, to demonstrate the datatype for controlling terminal
# oxygen names, lets set a couple of arguments - this will give CHARMm-type
# nomenclature on the C terminal oxygens instead of O/OXT
my $cleanResults = $document->CleanProtein(
{
ModifyTermini => True,
TerminalOxygenNames => Mdm::oxygenNamesOCT1AndOCT2
}
);

# if you want to save the results to a file, $clean_results
# are in html format
open( OUTREPORT, '>cleanreport.html' )
or die "Cannot open cleanreport.html: $!";

print OUTREPORT $cleanResults;
```

# ClearBsmlAttributes function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/clearbsmlattributes_function.htm

## ClearBsmlAttributes function

### Description

ClearBsmlAttributes removes attributes generated by
the BuildBsmlAttributes function.

### Applies to

The ClearBsmlAttributes function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the ClearBsmlAttributes function

#### Instance

$object->ClearBsmlAttributes();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Sdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the Sdm::AttributeMap.
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $mdm = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('4phv');
my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures($mdm);
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

# Copy current document state to object attributes. Generally the 
# attribute data is not updated after loading a BSML file. To get 
# the current state as attributes call this function. 
$document->ClearBsmlAttributes();
$document->BuildBsmlAttributes();

# List the Alignment object attributes.
print "Alignment attributes...\n";
my $attributes = $alignment->AttributeMap;
my $key = $attributes->FirstKey;
while (!$key->IsEndKey)
{
print $key->Name . ":\t" . $attributes->Item($key) . "\n";
$key = $attributes->NextKey($key);
}
print "end\n\n";

# List the Sequence object attributes.
my $sequences = $document->Sequences;
my $i = 0;
foreach my $sequence (@$sequences)
{
print "Sequence $i attributes...\n";
my $attributes = $sequence->AttributeMap;
my $key = $attributes->FirstKey;
while (!$key->IsEndKey)
{
print $key->Name . ":\t" . $attributes->Item($key) . "\n";
$key = $attributes->NextKey($key);
}
print "end\n\n";

my $k = $attributes->FindItem('ResidueID');
print 'Find Name: ' . $k->Name . "\tValue: "
. $attributes->Item($k) . "\n\n";

# List the Feature object attributes.
my $features = $sequence->Features;
my $f = 0;
foreach my $feature (@$features)
{
print "Feature $f attributes...\n";
my $fattributes = $feature->AttributeMap;
my $fkey = $fattributes->FirstKey;
print $feature->Key . "\n";
while (!$fkey->IsEndKey)
{
print $fkey->Name . ":\t" . $fattributes->Item($fkey) . "\n";
$fkey = $fattributes->NextKey($fkey);
}

print "end\n\n";
++$f;
} 

++$i; 
}

# Update the current document to match attribute data.
$document->UpdateFromBsmlAttributes();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# ClearItems function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/clearitems_function.htm

## ClearItems function

### Description

ClearItems removes all entries from a collection.

### Applies to

The ClearItems function can be used with the following objects:

DiscoveryScript::ColorArray , DiscoveryScript::DocumentArray , DiscoveryScript::IntegerArray , DiscoveryScript::ObjectMap , DiscoveryScript::RealArray , DiscoveryScript::StringArray , Mdm::Array , Mdm::OfflineableArray , Mdm::PointArray , Mdm::Set , Protocol::ParameterMap , Sdm::Array , Sdm::ResidueArray , Sdm::SequenceArray

### Using the ClearItems function

#### Instance

$object->ClearItems();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to manipulate items in an Mdm::Array.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

my $atoms = $document->Atoms;

# Collect all cysteine atoms.
my $cysteineAtomArray = Mdm::Array::Create();
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
$cysteineAtomArray->AddItem($atom)
if ( $atom->GetProperty("Parent") =~ /CYS/i );
}

# Find the common ancestor of all atoms in the array in cysteineAtomArray.
my $parent = $cysteineAtomArray->FindCommonAncestor();
print "The common parent object of all CYS atoms: "
. $parent->ClassName . " "
. $parent->Name . "\n";

die "No cysteine atoms found! Exiting.\n" if $cysteineAtomArray->IsEmpty;

my $cysteineAtomCount = $cysteineAtomArray->Count;
print "Number of atoms in cysteine residues: " . $cysteineAtomCount . "\n";

# Delete all atoms except C-alpha and C-beta.
# Note: When deleting items from an array, the array is traversed in
# reverse order. This avoids having to account for changes in the item
# indices as the array is modified.
for ( my $i = $cysteineAtomCount - 1 ; $i >= 0 ; --$i )
{
my $atom = $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i);
if ( $atom->Name !~ /(cb|ca)\b/i )
{
$cysteineAtomArray->DeleteItem($i);
}
}
print "Number of C-alpha and C-beta atoms in cysteine residues: "
. $cysteineAtomArray->Count . "\n";

# Create a copy of the original array in reverse order.
$cysteineAtomCount = $cysteineAtomArray->Count;
my $reverseCysteineArray = Mdm::Array::Create();

# Use the AddItem function to insert the first atom.
# Note: the InsertItem function cannot be used on an empty array.
$reverseCysteineArray->AddItem( $cysteineAtomArray->Item(0) );
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $cysteineAtomCount ; ++$i )
{
$reverseCysteineArray->InsertItem( 0, $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i) );
}

# Swap the first two elements or the original array.
my $tempItem = $cysteineAtomArray->Item(0);
$cysteineAtomArray->ReplaceItem( 0, $cysteineAtomArray->Item(1) );
$cysteineAtomArray->ReplaceItem( 1, $tempItem );

# Print out the IDs of the atoms in the two arrays side by side.
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $cysteineAtomCount ; ++$i )
{
my $atom1Id = $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i)->Id;
my $atom2Id = $reverseCysteineArray->Item($i)->Id;
print "item $i\t $atom1Id\t $atom2Id\n";
}

# Remove all remaining items in the original array.
$cysteineAtomArray->ClearItems();
print "The array now has " . $cysteineAtomArray->Count . " elements\n";
```

## Close function

### Description

Close closes the document.

### Applies to

The Close function can be used with the following objects:

Chart::Document , DiscoveryScript::Document , Ffdm::Document , Mdm::Document , Protocol::Document , Sdm::Document

### Using the Close function

#### Instance

$object->Close();

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Create an MDM document containing small molecules.
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles(
'OC(=O)C1=CC=C(C=C1)CN/C2=C/C=C(C=C2)C=CC(=O)C[Cl]');
$document->InsertFromSmiles('[CH3][CH2][OH]');
$document->InsertFromSmiles('C1=CC=CC=C1');
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');
$document->InsertFromSmiles('C1=NC=CC=C1');
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c12ccccc1cccc2');

printf "Document contains Molecules: %d Total Atoms: %d\n", $document->Molecules->Count,$document->Atoms->Count;

my $outputFolder = DiscoveryScript::GetTemporaryFolder();
my $filename = $outputFolder.'/ExampleOpen.sd';
my $format = 'mol';
$document->Save( $filename, $format );
$document->Close();
sleep(1);

# Open MDM document in Molecule Window
my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::Open(
{
Path => $filename,
ModelType => MdmModelType
}
);

printf "Document contains Molecules: %d Total Atoms: %d\n", $mdmDocument->Molecules->Count,$mdmDocument->Atoms->Count;
sleep(1);
$mdmDocument->Close();

# remove file
unlink ($filename);
```

# Cluster property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/cluster_property.htm

## Cluster property

### Description

Cluster specifies Mdm::ProteinPose belongs to

### Applies to

The Cluster property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::ProteinPose

### Using the Cluster property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->Cluster;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::ProteinPose |

#### Set

$object->Cluster = <cluster>;

$object->Cluster( <cluster> );

$object->Cluster( { Cluster => <cluster> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <cluster> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::ProteinPose |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use ProteinPose properties.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing docked protein poses.\n";
print " 3 Enter a cluster ID in the Arguments tab.\n";
print " 4 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

my ($clusterID) = @ARGV;

if ( $clusterID !~ /^\d+$/ )
{
$clusterID = 1;
}

# The script assume the last active document contains ProteinPoses.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage( 'This example requires an open Molecule Window containing '
. 'docked protein poses.' )
unless ($document);

# Get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter.
my $poseGroups = $document->DockedProteinPoseAssemblies;
Usage( 'This example requires an open Molecule Window containing '
. 'docked protein poses.' )
unless ( $poseGroups->Count > 0 );

my $poses = $document->ProteinPoses;

my $topClusterPose;

# Show all poses in cluster $clusterID, color green.
foreach my $pose (@$poses)
{
if ( $pose->Cluster == $clusterID )
{
$pose->SetVisible();

# Represent best ranked pose in the cluster as sphere and color light green.
if ( $pose->IsTopClusterPose )
{
$pose->DisplayStyle(Mdm::styleProteinPoseSphere);
$pose->Color( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 0 ) );
$topClusterPose = $pose;
}

# Represent other cluster members as jacks and color dark green.
else
{
$pose->DisplayStyle(Mdm::styleProteinPoseJack);
$pose->Color( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 122, 0 ) );
}
}
else
{

# Hide all poses not in the cluster.
$pose->SetInvisible();
}
}
```

die "Failed to open MDM document." unless $document;

my $chain = $document->AminoAcidChains->Item(0);
die "Molecule contains no chains." unless $chain;

# This example assumes the protein display is on.
# Ensure this is the case here.
$document->SelectByProperty('Atom Name="*"');
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleAtomStick);
$document->DeselectAll();
$chain->DisplayStyle = Mdm::styleProteinRibbonTube;

print "Select cysteine residues and color them orange...\n\n";
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="CYS.*" ; Atom Name="*"');
my $cysteines = $document->SelectedObjects();
die "No cysteine residues." unless ($cysteines && $cysteines->Count > 0);
my $color = Mdm::Color::Create();
$color->Red = 255;
$color->Green = 200;
$color->Blue = 0;
$document->SetColor($color);
$document->DeselectAll();

print "Coloring the ribbon pseudo-transparent...\n\n";
my $chain = $document->Chains()->Item(0);
my $color = Mdm::Color::Create();
$color->Red = 0;
$color->Green = 255;
$color->Blue = 0;
$color->Alpha = 128;
$chain->Color($color);

print "Coloring the background dark blue...\n\n";
my $bkColor = Mdm::Color::Create();
$bkColor->Red = 0;
$bkColor->Green = 0;
$bkColor->Blue = 100;
$document->BackgroundColor = $bkColor;
```

Commands are created to simplify common tasks or to mimic the functionality
found in the user interface. The Commands are defined in Perl modules (.pm
files) located in the lib folder of the installation.

# Comment (deprecated) property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/comment__deprecated__property.htm

## Comment (deprecated) property

### Description

Comment summarizes additional notes for objects such as
a literature citation from
an Sdm::Publication .

### Applies to

The Comment (deprecated) property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Feature

### Using the Comment (deprecated) property

#### Set

This property is deprecated. It has been replaced by in Sdm::Feature

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Publication class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'Y13252-truncated',
'TCTAGAGTAACATTTAGAATTAAGGTGGGAAATTATCTTAAAATCT' );

my $title =
'Nonfixed duplication containing the Adh gene and a truncated form '
. 'of the Adhr gene in the Drosophila funebris species group: different '
. 'modes of evolution of Adh relative to Adhr in Drosophila';

# Create publication object with sample data.
my $publication01 = Sdm::Publication::Create( 'Amador, A., Juan, E.',
$title, 'Molec. Biol. Evol.' );

# Create publication and add content separately.
my $publication02 = Sdm::Publication::Create();
$publication02->Authors = 'Amador, A., Juan, E.';
$publication02->Title = $title;
$publication02->Journal = 'Molec. Biol. Evol.';
$publication02->Reference = '16(11): 1439--1456 (1999)';
$publication02->PubMedId = '10555275';
$publication02->Comment = 'y13252';

#$publication02->Consortium = '';
#$publication02->DigitalObjectId = '';
#$publication02->MedlineId = '';
#$publication02->PubMedId = '';

# Associate publications with a sequence object.
# NOTE: To see the publications in Discovery Studio, double-click on the
# sequence in the sequence window to open a sequence annotation window.
# Publications are listed in the data table's Literature Citation tab.
$sequence->AddPublication($publication01);
$sequence->AddPublication($publication02);

my $publicationCount = $sequence->PublicationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $publicationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $publication = $sequence->Publication($index);
printf "%d: %s, %s. %s %s.\n",
$index + 1,
$publication->Authors,
$publication->Title,
$publication->Journal,
$publication->Reference;
}

$sequence->DeletePublication(0);
```

# Complement function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/complement_function.htm

## Complement function

### Description

Complement performs a complement on the range (StartPosition, StartPosition + Count) of a sequence.
There are several parameters:

* StartPosition is the index of the first residue to perform a complement.

* Count is the number of residues to complement.

### Applies to

The Complement function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the Complement function

#### Instance

$object->Complement( <startposition>, [count] );

$object->Complement( { StartPosition => <startposition>, Count => [count] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <startposition> | Required | | Integer |
| [count] | Optional | 1 | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence Sdm::Sequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate sequence complement and reverse functions.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateNucleotideDocument();
my $sequence =
$document->CreateSequence( 'Seq', 'CGACCTCGCGGGTTTTCGCTATTTATGAAA' );
my $residueCount = $sequence->ResidueCount;

print 'Sequence is ' . $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";

$sequence->Complement( 0, $residueCount );
print 'Complement of sequence is ' . $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";

$sequence->Reverse( 0, $residueCount );
print 'Reverse of sequence is ' . $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";

$sequence->ReverseComplement( 0, $residueCount );
print 'Reverse complement of sequence is ' . $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
```

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This scripts illustrates how to access several properties of
# the Mdm::Molecule object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

$molecule->IsChargeCalculated = True;

print "The following is a list of molecule properties:\n";
print 'Name: ' . $molecule->Name . "\n";
print 'Approximate volume: ' . $molecule->ApproximateVolume . "\n";
print 'Atom count: ' . $molecule->AtomCount . "\n";

my $centerOfMass = $molecule->CenterOfMass;
printf "Center of mass: %8.3f\t%8.3f\t%8.3f\n",
$centerOfMass->X,
$centerOfMass->Y,
$centerOfMass->Z;

print 'Chiral center count: ' . $molecule->ChiralCenterCount . "\n";
print 'Composition: ' . $molecule->Composition . "\n";
print 'Density: ' . $molecule->Density . "\n";
print 'Exact molecular weight: ' . $molecule->ExactMolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen bond acceptor count: '
. $molecule->HydrogenBondAcceptorCount . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen bond donor count: '
. $molecule->HydrogenBondDonorCount . "\n";
print 'Lipinski violation count: ' . $molecule->LipinskiViolationCount . "\n";
print 'Molecular formula: ' . $molecule->MolecularFormula . "\n";
print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Radius of gyration: ' . $molecule->RadiusOfGyration . "\n";
print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Rotatable bond count: ' . $molecule->RotatableBondCount . "\n";
print 'Surface area: ' . $molecule->SurfaceArea . "\n";

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use Mdm::Conformation objects.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage()
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing conformations.\n";
print " 3 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
Usage() unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage() unless ($document);

my $conformations = $document->Conformations;
Usage() unless ( $conformations->Count > 0 );

print "Getting the first conformation...\n";
my $conformation = $conformations->Item(0);

my $xyz = $conformation->ConformationXYZ(0);
print "Coordinate of first atom in this conformation: "
. $xyz->X . ","
. $xyz->Y . ","
. $xyz->Z . "\n";

$xyz->X += 0.1;
$xyz->Y += 0.1;
$xyz->Z += 0.1;
print "Changing the first atom's coordinate to: "
. $xyz->X . ","
. $xyz->Y . ","
. $xyz->Z . "\n";
$conformation->ConformationXYZ( 0, $xyz );

print "Applying the new conformation to the reference...\n";
$conformation->ApplyConformationToReference();

my $atom = $document->Atoms->Item(0);
$atom->XYZ->X -= 0.1;
print "Applying the reference to the conformation...\n";
$conformation->ApplyReferenceToConformation();

my $referenceXYZ = $conformation->ReferenceXYZ($atom);
print "Coordinate of first atom in the reference: "
. $referenceXYZ->X . ","
. $referenceXYZ->Y . ","
. $referenceXYZ->Z . "\n";

print "Applying the display data from reference to conformation...\n";
$conformation->ApplyReferenceDisplayToConformation();
print "Applying the display data from conformation to reference...\n";
$conformation->ApplyConformationDisplayToReference();
```

#!/usr/bin/perl -w

use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('9INS');

sleep(1);

my $conformerModel = $document->ConformerModels->Item(0);
printf "Residue %s has alternate conformations.\n",
$conformerModel->Parent->Name;

my $conformer = $conformerModel->Conformers->Item(0);
$conformer->Select();
printf "Residue %s has an alternate conformations named %s.\n",
$conformer->Parent->Parent->Name, $conformer->Name;

my $conformerAtoms = $conformerModel->ConformerAtoms;
my $conformerBonds = $conformerModel->ConformerBonds;
printf "This alternate conformation has %d conformer atoms and %d conformer bonds.\n",
$conformerAtoms->Count,
$conformerBonds->Count;

foreach my $conformerAtom (@$conformerAtoms)
{
my $xyz = $conformerAtom->XYZ;
printf "Alternate atom %s is at (%f, %f, %f).\n", 
$conformerAtom->Name, $xyz->X, $xyz->Y, $xyz->Z;
}

#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates the use ConformerModel.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('9INS');
die "No Molecule Window!" unless $document;

# Ensure atoms are displayed to see alternate conformations.
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleAtomLine);
sleep(1);

my $conformerModels = $document->ConformerModels;
printf "This complex contains %d residues with alternate conformations.\n",
$conformerModels->Count;

# Select all alternate conformation models for deletion.
$document->DeselectAll();
foreach my $model (@$conformerModels)
{
$model->Select();
}
sleep(1);
$document->DeleteObjects();

printf "After deletion, the complex contains %d alternate conformations.\n",
$document->ConformerModels->Count;
```

{

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Publication class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'Y13252-truncated',
'TCTAGAGTAACATTTAGAATTAAGGTGGGAAATTATCTTAAAATCT' );

my $title =
'Nonfixed duplication containing the Adh gene and a truncated form '
. 'of the Adhr gene in the Drosophila funebris species group: different '
. 'modes of evolution of Adh relative to Adhr in Drosophila';

# Create publication object with sample data.
my $publication01 = Sdm::Publication::Create( 'Amador, A., Juan, E.',
$title, 'Molec. Biol. Evol.' );

# Create publication and add content separately.
my $publication02 = Sdm::Publication::Create();
$publication02->Authors = 'Amador, A., Juan, E.';
$publication02->Title = $title;
$publication02->Journal = 'Molec. Biol. Evol.';
$publication02->Reference = '16(11): 1439--1456 (1999)';
$publication02->PubMedId = '10555275';
$publication02->Comment = 'y13252';

#$publication02->Consortium = '';
#$publication02->DigitalObjectId = '';
#$publication02->MedlineId = '';
#$publication02->PubMedId = '';

# Associate publications with a sequence object.
# NOTE: To see the publications in Discovery Studio, double-click on the
# sequence in the sequence window to open a sequence annotation window.
# Publications are listed in the data table's Literature Citation tab.
$sequence->AddPublication($publication01);
$sequence->AddPublication($publication02);

my $publicationCount = $sequence->PublicationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $publicationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $publication = $sequence->Publication($index);
printf "%d: %s, %s. %s %s.\n",
$index + 1,
$publication->Authors,
$publication->Title,
$publication->Journal,
$publication->Reference;
}

$sequence->DeletePublication(0);
```

Mdm::RingAromaticFeature , Mdm::RotatableBondMonitor , Mdm::ScreenLabel , Mdm::Set , Mdm::ShapeFeature , Mdm::SideChainConformationViolationMonitor , Mdm::SlicingPlane , Mdm::Sphere , Mdm::Surface , | $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Example filter_constraints
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Fix backbone atoms in sheet or helix
my $helicalBackboneAtoms = $document->FilterByProperty(
'Residue Secondary="Helix",Secondary="Sheet"; Atom label="CA",label="C",label="O",label="N"'
);
$document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($helicalBackboneAtoms);

# Add harmonic constraint on all backbone atoms in coils
my $coiledBackboneAtoms = $document->FilterByProperty(
'Residue Secondary="Coil";Atom label="CA",label="C",label="O",label="N"');
$document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint(
{ ArrayOfAtoms => $coiledBackboneAtoms, ForceConstant => 1.2 } );

# Add cross-strand distance restraint
{
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "THR2:CA" );
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "ILE34:CA" );
$document->CreateDistanceRestraint(
{
ArrayOfAtoms1 => $atom1,
ArrayOfAtoms2 => $atom2,
RMin => 2,
RMax => 5
}
);
}

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
{
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
$document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);
}

# Get arrays with for each type of constraint using the corresponding filters
# Note that the constraint filter includes constraints and restraints
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
my $fixedAtomConstraints = $document->FixedAtomConstraints;

# Note that the restraint filter includes dihedral, distance and harmonic restraints
my $restraints = $document->Restraints;
my $dihedralRestraints = $document->DihedralRestraints;
my $distanceRestraints = $document->DistanceRestraints;
my $harmonicRestraints = $document->HarmonicAtomRestraints;

# Print out total number of constraints, along with a list of their names
print "There are " . $constraints->Count . " constraints (\t";
foreach my $constraint (@$constraints)
{
my $name = $constraint->GetProperty("Name");
print "$name\t";
}

# Print out the number of each type of constraints
print ")\nout of which ";
print $restraints->Count . " are Restraints :\n";
print " " . $dihedralRestraints->Count . " DihedralRestraint(s)\n";
print " " . $distanceRestraints->Count . " DistanceRestraint(s)\n";
print " " . $harmonicRestraints->Count . " HarmonicAtomRestraint(s)\n";
print "and \n";
print " " . $fixedAtomConstraints->Count . "FixedAtomConstraint(s)\n";
```

## ContextAtomArray property

ContextAtomArray specifies the context atoms used to define the display extents in Mdm::Isosurface .

### Applies to

The ContextAtomArray property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Isosurface

### Using the ContextAtomArray property

#### Set

$object->ContextAtomArray = <arrayofcontextatoms>;

$object->ContextAtomArray( <arrayofcontextatoms> );

$object->ContextAtomArray( { ArrayOfContextAtoms => <arrayofcontextatoms> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <arrayofcontextatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::Isosurface |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
print "It operates on a document with grid data\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1. Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2. Open a structure with grid data\n";
print
" (for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
print " 3. Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}
else
{

}

# Connect to an Sdm::Document from the last active sequence window
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

# Get array with all isosurfaces using Isosurfaces filter
my $isosurfaces = $document->Isosurfaces;

if ( $isosurfaces->Count == 0 )
{
print "To run this script, please open a structure with grid data.\n";
print "(for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
exit;
}

$document->ShowAll();
my $chain1 = $document->Chains->[0];

# Get the first isosurface
my $isosurface = $isosurfaces->[0];

# Create a isosurfaces at 0.5 and 0.4 isovalue
my $newContour = $isosurface->CreateIsosurface(0.5);
my $newContour2 = $isosurface->CreateIsosurface(0.4);

# Set the context array for the first surface
$chain1->Select();
$newContour->DisplayStyle(Mdm::isosurfaceStyleSolid);
$newContour->ContextAtomArray( $chain1->Atoms );
$document->UpdateViews();

sleep(1);

# Set Display extend for second isosurface
$document->DeselectAll();

# Pick 2 arbitrary atoms and get their coordinates
my $atom1 = $document->Atoms->[4324];
my $atom2 = $document->Atoms->[5100];
$atom1->Select();
$atom2->Select();
my $xyz1 = $atom1->XYZ;
my $xyz2 = $atom2->XYZ;
print $xyz1->X . "\t" . $xyz1->Y . "\t" . $xyz1->Z . "\n";
print $xyz2->X . "\t" . $xyz2->Y . "\t" . $xyz2->Z . "\n";

# Set style to isosurfaceStyleQuadMesh
$newContour2->DisplayStyle(Mdm::isosurfaceStyleQuadMesh);
$newContour2->SetDisplayExtent( $xyz1, $xyz2 );
$document->UpdateViews();

sleep(1);

# Display full extend of second isosurface
$newContour2->DisplayAll();
```

# Contract function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/contract_function.htm

## Contract function

### Description

Contract deletes the atom ( Mdm::Atom ) adjacent to
the selected bond ( Mdm::Bond ), thereby contracting
a ring or chain by one atom.

### Applies to

The Contract function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the Contract function

#### Command

$object->Contract( [sprouthydrogens] );

$object->Contract( { SproutHydrogens => [sprouthydrogens] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [sprouthydrogens] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to contract a ring.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

print "Create a benzene molecule...\n\n";
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles('C1=CC=CC=C1');
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms();

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
$molecule->Name = 'Benzene';
$document->Bonds->Item(1)->Select();
sleep(3);

print 'Contract the selected bond. This effectively removes the '
. "select bond and merges the bonded atoms.\n";
$document->Contract();
$document->DeselectAll();
```

## ContractBindingSite function

### Description

ContractBindingSite contracts the size of a binding site.

### Applies to

The ContractBindingSite function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ContractBindingSite function

#### Command

$object->ContractBindingSite( <bindingsite>, [numberofcycles] );

$object->ContractBindingSite( { BindingSite => <bindingsite>, NumberOfCycles => [numberofcycles] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <bindingsite> | Required | | Mdm::BindingSite |
| [numberofcycles] | Optional | 1 | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

SbdDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate binding site contraction.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '4PHV.pdb' );

# Remove ligands and water from complex (using DSCommands).
Delete( $document, GetLigands($document) );
Delete( $document, GetWaters($document) );

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

# Change display to protein ribbon tubes.
TurnOffProteinAtoms($document);
ApplyProteinDisplayStyle( $document, Mdm::styleProteinRibbonTube );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Find binding sites.
$document->CreateBindingSitesFromCavities($molecule);
my $bindingSites = $document->BindingSites;
my $site = $bindingSites->Item(0);
my $volume = $site->GetProperty("Volume");

print "Volume before contraction: $volume\n";

# Contract a binding site by 2 cycles. After contraction,
# the binding sites will have changed.
$document->ContractBindingSite( $site, 2 );
$bindingSites = $document->BindingSites;
$site = $bindingSites->Item(0);
$volume = $site->GetProperty("Volume");

print "Volume after contraction: $volume\n";
```

# ContractShell function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/contractshell_function.htm

## ContractShell function

### Description

ContractShell progressively hides supporting non-bond interactions
between the ligand and receptor of a Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor object. Each call to the ExpandShell function
includes additional receptor interactions with receptor residues
already identified as either interacting with the ligand or
supporting interactions with the ligand.
The function ContractShell progressively hides these
shells of interactions.

### Applies to

The ContractShell function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor

### Using the ContractShell function

#### Instance

my $booleanValue = $object->ContractShell();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the create a ligand non-bond monitor, 
# browse ligands and show supporting non-bond interactions. 

use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('2FL6');
die "Failed to create a valid MDM document!" unless $document;

my $receptor = $document->ReceptorInFocus;
die "The open document does not have a defined receptor!" unless $receptor;

$document->FocusOnFirstLigand;
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
die "The open document does not have a defined ligand!" unless $ligand;

my $ligandNonbondMonitor =
$document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();
$document->UpdateViews();

my $nonbondMonitors = $document->NonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d NonbondMonitors.\n", $nonbondMonitors->Count;
my $ligandNonbondMonitors = $document->LigandNonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d LigandNonbondMonitors.\n", $ligandNonbondMonitors->Count;

# Step through the ligands
while ($document->FocusOnNextLigand())
{
sleep(2);
}

# Step through the ligands backwards
$document->FocusOnLastLigand();
while ($document->FocusOnPreviousLigand())
{
sleep(2);
}

# Expand shell to progressively view supporting interactions.
$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

# Contract shell to hide supporting interactions.
$ligandNonbondMonitor->ContractShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

print "Done\n";
```

# ConvertDnaToRna function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/convertdnatorna_function.htm

## ConvertDnaToRna function

### Description

ConvertDnaToRna modifies the Mdm::NucleicAcidChain object
by converting the thymine nucleotides to uracil and all deoxyribose units
to ribose.

### Applies to

The ConvertDnaToRna function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ConvertDnaToRna function

#### Instance

$object->ConvertDnaToRna( <chain> );

$object->ConvertDnaToRna( { Chain => <chain> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <chain> | Required | | Mdm::NucleicAcidChain |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to convert nucleic acids.
use strict;
use NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

print "Creating an RNA duplex molecule\n";
my $nucleicAcid =
$document->CreateNucleicAcid( "CGUAA", Mdm::rnaDuplex, Mdm::aHelix );

my $nucleotide = $nucleicAcid->Chains->Item(0)->NucleicAcids->Item(0);
print ' Nucleotide is deoxyribonucleotide: '
. $nucleotide->IsDeoxyribose . "\n";
print ' Nucleotide is ribonucleotide: ' . $nucleotide->IsRibose . "\n";
$document->Save( 'rna1.pdb', 'pdb' );
sleep(1);

print "Converting RNA to DNA\n";
my $senseStrand = $nucleicAcid->Chains->Item(0);
my $antisenseStrand = $nucleicAcid->Chains->Item(1);

my $n3p = $antisenseStrand->NucleotideAt3PrimeTerminus;
my $n5p = $antisenseStrand->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus;

$document->DeselectAll();
$document->ConvertRnaToDna($senseStrand);
$document->ConvertRnaToDna($antisenseStrand);
$document->Save( 'dna.pdb', 'pdb' );
print ' Nucleotide is deoxyribonucleotide: '
. $nucleotide->IsDeoxyribose . "\n";
print ' Nucleotide is ribonucleotide: ' . $nucleotide->IsRibose . "\n";
sleep(1);

print "Converting DNA back to RNA\n";
$document->ConvertDnaToRna($senseStrand);
$document->ConvertDnaToRna($antisenseStrand);
$document->Save( 'rna2.pdb', 'pdb' );
print ' Nucleotide is deoxyribonucleotide: '
. $nucleotide->IsDeoxyribose . "\n";
print ' Nucleotide is ribonucleotide: ' . $nucleotide->IsRibose . "\n";
```

# ConvertRnaToDna function

Source type: HTML

## ConvertRnaToDna function

### Description

ConvertDnaToRna modifies the Mdm::NucleicAcidChain object
by converting the uracil nucleotides to thymine and all ribose sugar
units to deoxyribose.

### Applies to

The ConvertRnaToDna function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ConvertRnaToDna function

#### Instance

$object->ConvertRnaToDna( <chain> );

$object->ConvertRnaToDna( { Chain => <chain> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <chain> | Required | | Mdm::NucleicAcidChain |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to convert nucleic acids.
use strict;
use NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

print "Creating an RNA duplex molecule\n";
my $nucleicAcid =
$document->CreateNucleicAcid( "CGUAA", Mdm::rnaDuplex, Mdm::aHelix );

my $nucleotide = $nucleicAcid->Chains->Item(0)->NucleicAcids->Item(0);
print ' Nucleotide is deoxyribonucleotide: '
. $nucleotide->IsDeoxyribose . "\n";
print ' Nucleotide is ribonucleotide: ' . $nucleotide->IsRibose . "\n";
$document->Save( 'rna1.pdb', 'pdb' );
sleep(1);

print "Converting RNA to DNA\n";
my $senseStrand = $nucleicAcid->Chains->Item(0);
my $antisenseStrand = $nucleicAcid->Chains->Item(1);

my $n3p = $antisenseStrand->NucleotideAt3PrimeTerminus;
my $n5p = $antisenseStrand->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus;

$document->DeselectAll();
$document->ConvertRnaToDna($senseStrand);
$document->ConvertRnaToDna($antisenseStrand);
$document->Save( 'dna.pdb', 'pdb' );
print ' Nucleotide is deoxyribonucleotide: '
. $nucleotide->IsDeoxyribose . "\n";
print ' Nucleotide is ribonucleotide: ' . $nucleotide->IsRibose . "\n";
sleep(1);

print "Converting DNA back to RNA\n";
$document->ConvertDnaToRna($senseStrand);
$document->ConvertDnaToRna($antisenseStrand);
$document->Save( 'rna2.pdb', 'pdb' );
print ' Nucleotide is deoxyribonucleotide: '
. $nucleotide->IsDeoxyribose . "\n";
print ' Nucleotide is ribonucleotide: ' . $nucleotide->IsRibose . "\n";
```

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| <sequence> | Required | | String |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the conversion between 1 and 3 letter coded sequence strings.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Create arbitrary amino acid sequence string.
my $sequenceString = 'MIASDFADSG';
printf "%s:\n%s\n\n", 'Initial sequence string', $sequenceString;

# Convert to 3 letter residue codes.
my $sequenceString3Letter =
Mdm::AminoAcidChain::ConvertToThreeLetterSequence($sequenceString);
printf "%s:\n%s\n\n", 'Sequence string after converting to 3 letter codes',
$sequenceString3Letter;

# Revert to 1 letter code.

Mdm::AminoAcidChain::ConvertToOneLetterSequence($sequenceString3Letter);

$sequenceString1Letter;

, Mdm::Constraint , Mdm::Cylinder , Mdm::DihedralFeature , Mdm::DihedralRestraint , Mdm::DipoleMomentMonitor , Mdm::DistanceFeature , Mdm::DistanceMonitor , Mdm::DistanceRestraint , Mdm::DisulfideBridgeSite , Mdm::DockedProteinPoseAssembly , Mdm::DonorFeature , Mdm::ExclusionFeature , Mdm::FixedAtomConstraint , Mdm::Geometric3d , Mdm::Group , Mdm::HarmonicAtomRestraint , Mdm::OfflineableConformation , Mdm::PiBond , Mdm::PiCationMonitor , Mdm::PiInteractionMonitor , Mdm::PiPiMonitor , Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor , Mdm::PlanarPeptideViolationMonitor , Mdm::PlaneFeature , Mdm::PlaneMonitor , Mdm::PointFeature , Mdm::PointOffsetFeature , Mdm::Polydot , Mdm::PropertyLabel , Mdm::ProteinChiralityViolationMonitor , Mdm::ProteinNomenclatureViolationMonitor , Mdm::ProteinPose , Mdm::Query , Mdm::QueryAtom , Mdm::QueryBond , Mdm::QueryFeatureMap , Mdm::QueryOperator , Mdm::Residue , Mdm::Restraint , Mdm::RingAromaticFeature , Mdm::RotatableBondMonitor , Mdm::ScreenLabel , Mdm::ShapeFeature , Mdm::SideChainConformationViolationMonitor , Mdm::SlicingPlane , Mdm::Sphere , Mdm::Surface , Mdm::TorsionMonitor , Mdm::TupleMonitor , Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond , Mdm::Valence , Mdm::ValenceMonitor , Mdm::VectorFeature

### Using the Copy function

#### Instance

my $objectObject = $object->Copy();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $objectObject | | | Mdm::Object |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use alignment superimposition functions and
# RMSD calculation functions for amino acids or non-standard residues.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1gaf.pdb' );

my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1gaf = $document->Molecules->[1];

# H chain V domains only
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
$molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
$molecule1gaf->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
}

my $Sequence1aj7 = $molecule1aj7->AminoAcidSequence;
my $Sequence1gaf = $molecule1gaf->AminoAcidSequence;
my $sequences = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1aj7);
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1gaf);

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms. The function returns an array
# of RMSD values between the reference and all molecules, starting with itself.
my $rmsds =
$document->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment( $document->Molecules, $sequences,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms, True );

print "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $document->Molecules->Count() ; ++$i )
{
print "\t"
. $document->Molecules->[$i]->Name . " to "
. $molecule1aj7->Name . ": ";
printf "%.3f\n", $rmsds->[$i];
}
print "\n";

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD
# Note that these functions return an array of real numbers. These are the
# per residue RMSD values plus, in the last element, the overall RMSD.
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it (the value will be zero). This can happen for
# unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation only for
# selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the required atoms for
# the requested type of calculation.
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item( $apRmsd->Count() - 1 );
print "\n";

# This demonstrates that the array is for all residues plus overall
# value, not just selected, and that as the first chain(L) is
# unselected (its values are 0).
printf "Number of values returned is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain.
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H chain.
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

# Get antigen NPE from 1aj7.
my $antigen1 = $document->Molecules->[0]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Get antigen NPE from 1gaf.
my $antigen2 = $document->Molecules->[1]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Copy antigen residues to a new document.
my $tmpDocument = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $tmpMolecule1 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen1Copy = $antigen1->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen1Copy, $tmpMolecule1 );
my $tmpMolecule2 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen2Copy = $antigen2->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen2Copy, $tmpMolecule2 );

$tmpDocument->FitView();

# Calculate NPE RMSD.
my $rmsd =
$tmpDocument->CalculateOtherResidueRmsd( $tmpMolecule1, $tmpMolecule2 );
printf "NPE RMSD: %.3f\n", $rmsd->[1];
```

# CopyAndAmend function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/copyandamend_function.htm

## CopyAndAmend function

### Description

CopyAndAmend creates a new copy of an object and all of its
descendent objects.
If the object being copied is a residue, the residue will be placed
in a chain that will be placed in a molecule.
If the object being copied is a chain, the chain will be placed
in a molecule.
In all cases, the object returned is the copy of
the object being copied.
The new copy initially has no parent object and you must specify
one using SetParent or ChangeObjectParent .

Mdm::ConformerModel , Mdm::Constraint , Mdm::Cylinder , Mdm::DihedralFeature , Mdm::DihedralRestraint , Mdm::DipoleMomentMonitor , Mdm::DistanceFeature , Mdm::DistanceMonitor , Mdm::DistanceRestraint , Mdm::DisulfideBridgeSite , Mdm::DockedProteinPoseAssembly , Mdm::DonorFeature , Mdm::ExclusionFeature , Mdm::FixedAtomConstraint , Mdm::Geometric3d , Mdm::Group , Mdm::HarmonicAtomRestraint , Mdm::OfflineableConformation , Mdm::PiBond , Mdm::PiCationMonitor , Mdm::PiInteractionMonitor , Mdm::PiPiMonitor , Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor , Mdm::PlanarPeptideViolationMonitor , Mdm::PlaneFeature , Mdm::PlaneMonitor , Mdm::PointFeature , Mdm::PointOffsetFeature , Mdm::Polydot , Mdm::PropertyLabel , Mdm::ProteinChiralityViolationMonitor , Mdm::ProteinNomenclatureViolationMonitor , Mdm::ProteinPose , Mdm::Query , Mdm::QueryAtom , Mdm::QueryBond , Mdm::QueryFeatureMap , Mdm::QueryOperator , Mdm::Residue , Mdm::Restraint , Mdm::RingAromaticFeature , Mdm::RotatableBondMonitor , Mdm::ScreenLabel , Mdm::ShapeFeature , Mdm::SideChainConformationViolationMonitor , Mdm::SlicingPlane , Mdm::Sphere , Mdm::Surface , Mdm::TorsionMonitor , Mdm::TupleMonitor , Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond , Mdm::Valence , Mdm::ValenceMonitor , Mdm::VectorFeature

### Using the CopyAndAmend function

#### Instance

my $objectObject = $object->CopyAndAmend();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $objectObject | | | Mdm::Object |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of CopyAndAmend
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1CRN.pdb" );
die "Failed to open document" unless defined $document;

#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Using CopyAndAmend to create a copy of a residue in a new molecule
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
die "Failed to load document" unless defined $aminoAcids;

my $aminoAcid = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
my $name = $aminoAcid->Name;
print "Copying residue <".$name.">\n";

my $copy = $aminoAcid->CopyAndAmend;
die "Copy failed" unless defined $copy;
my $copyClassName = $copy->ClassName;
die "Copy failed - object is of type <".$copyClassName.">"
unless $copyClassName eq 'Mdm::Molecule';

$aminoAcids = $copy->AminoAcids;
die "Copy failed" unless $aminoAcids->Count == 1;
$aminoAcid = $aminoAcids->Item(0);
$name = $aminoAcid->Name;
print "Copied residue <".$name.">\n";

# The residue has been copied and a new molecule has been created.
# The new molecule still needs to be associated with a document.
# Before doing this, the document contains one molecule.
my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
print "#(molecules) = ", $molecules->Count, "\n";

my $root = $document->RootObject;
die "Document has no root object" unless defined $root;
$document->ChangeObjectParent($copy, $root);

# After adding the new molecule to the root object of the document,
# the document contains two molecules.
$molecules = $document->Molecules;
print "#(molecules) = ", $molecules->Count, "\n";

print "Done\n";
```

### Description

CopyLoopCoordinates takes the coordinates of a loop defined for a template

Mdm::Document

### Using the CopyLoopCoordinates function

#### Command

$object->CopyLoopCoordinates( <targetstart>, <templatestart>, <templateend>, [stemlength] );

$object->CopyLoopCoordinates( { TargetStart => <targetstart>, TemplateStart => <templatestart>, TemplateEnd => <templateend>, StemLength => [stemlength] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <targetstart> | Required | | Mdm::AminoAcid |
| <templateend> | Required | | Mdm::AminoAcid |
| <templatestart> | Required | | Mdm::AminoAcid |
| [stemlength] | Optional | 2 | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

# This example copies a loop from one protein to another.
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('2cha');
$document->InsertFromUrl(PdbUrlPrefix . '1est.pdb');

#$document->SetProteinDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleProteinNone } );
#$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( Mdm::styleAtomLine );

$document->UpdateViews();

#This is not really a robust method of obtaining the correct objects -
# really need to ensure correct molecule and chain
my $targetStart=FilterByString($document,"LYS202")->Item(0);
$targetStart->Select();
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( Mdm::styleAtomLine );
printf ("target start %s\n",$targetStart->Name);
my $templateStart=FilterByString($document,"LEU202")->Item(0);
$templateStart->Select();
printf("template start %s\n",$templateStart->Name);
my $templateEnd=FilterByString($document,"TYR207")->Item(0);
$templateEnd->Select();
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( Mdm::styleAtomLine );
printf("template end %s\n",$templateEnd->Name);

#copy loop coordinates, the stem length will default to 2 residues
$document->CopyLoopCoordinates($targetStart,$templateStart,$templateEnd);
```

# Create3dPointer function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/create3dpointer_function.htm

## Create3dPointer function

### Description

Create3dPointer makes a molecule's ( Mdm::Molecule ) 3D pointer visible.
If the molecule does not have a 3D pointer, one is created and placed
at the center of geometry of the molecule.

### Applies to

The Create3dPointer function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the Create3dPointer function

#### Command

$object->Create3dPointer();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of 3D pointer functions.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;
use MdmCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Create 3D pointer at the center.
$document->Create3dPointer();

my ( $maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ) = Get3DWindowExtents( $document );
printf "Window Max: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f Min: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n",$maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ;

# Translate document to illustrate pointer functions.
$document->Translate( 10, 10, 10 );
sleep(1);

my ( $maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ) = Get3DWindowExtents( $document );
printf "Window Max: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f Min: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n",$maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ;

# Center the view on the 3D point.
$document->Goto3dPointer();
sleep(1);

my ( $maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ) = Get3DWindowExtents( $document );
printf "Window Max: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f Min: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n",$maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ;

# Remove the pointer.
$document->Remove3dPointer();

# Place the pointer at ALA38.
$document->AminoAcids->[37]->Select();
$document->SetCurrent3dPointerResidue();
$document->Goto3dPointer();

my ( $maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ) = Get3DWindowExtents( $document );
printf "Window Max: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f Min: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n",$maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ;
sleep(1);

# Move to the next residue.
$document->GotoNext3dPointerResidue();

my ( $maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ) = Get3DWindowExtents( $document );
printf "Window Max: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f Min: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n",$maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ;
sleep(1);

# Move to the previous residue.
$document->GotoPrevious3dPointerResidue();
my ( $maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ) = Get3DWindowExtents( $document );
printf "Window Max: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f Min: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n",$maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ;

sleep(1);
```
