# Create3dPointPlot function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/create3dpointplot_function.htm

## Create3dPointPlot function

### Description

Create3dPointPlot creates a 3-dimensional point plot from the Data Table View.
The following arguments are available:

* MdmDocument specifies the Mdm::Document whose data will be plotted.

* DataTableTabName specifies the tab whose data will be plotted.

* XAxisProperty is the name of the column to use as the X-axis.

* YAxisProperties specifies a comma separated list of column names to use as the Y-axes.

* ZAxisProperty is the name of the column to use as the Z-axis.

* ColorProperty specifies the name of the column to color the points in the plot. If this is not specified, the ZAxisProperty will be used.

### Applies to

The Create3dPointPlot function can be used with the following objects:

Chart::Document

### Using the Create3dPointPlot function

#### Static

my $documentObject = Chart::Document::Create3dPointPlot( <mdmdocument>, <datatabletabname>, <xaxisproperty>, <yaxisproperties>, <zaxisproperty>, [colorproperty], [fromselection] );

my $documentObject = Chart::Document::Create3dPointPlot( { MdmDocument => <mdmdocument>, DataTableTabName => <datatabletabname>, XAxisProperty => <xaxisproperty>, YAxisProperties => <yaxisproperties>, ZAxisProperty => <zaxisproperty>, ColorProperty => [colorproperty], FromSelection => [fromselection] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | Chart::Document |
| <datatabletabname> | Required | | String |
| <mdmdocument> | Required | | Mdm::Document |
| <xaxisproperty> | Required | | String |
| <yaxisproperties> | Required | | String |
| <zaxisproperty> | Required | | String |
| [colorproperty] | Optional | "" | String |
| [fromselection] | Optional | False | Boolean |

#### Defined by

ChartDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to create a 3D point plot (client only).
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ChartDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

my $pointPlot = Chart::Document::Create3dPointPlot(
{
MdmDocument => $mdmDocument,
DataTableTabName => 'Atom',
XAxisProperty => 'Partial Charge',
YAxisProperties => 'Isotropic Displacement',
ZAxisProperty => 'Oxidation State'
}
);

print "Model Type: Chart3dModelType\n"
if ( $pointPlot->ModelType == Chart3dModelType );

$pointPlot->UpdateViews();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrates how to create protein and nucleotide sequence documents.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

# Create protein sequence documents.
my $sdmProteinDocument =
Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument(SdmAlignmentModelType);
printf "CreateProteinDocument creates document of type %s\n",
$sdmProteinDocument->Type;

# Create amino acid sequence objects.
my $sequence1 =
$sdmProteinDocument->CreateSequence( 'Sequence1', 'qreqytweqtetwq' );
my $sequence2 =
$sdmProteinDocument->CreateAASequence( 'Sequence2', 'ASDFDSFASFA' );

printf
"On an amino acid document, CreateSequence creates sequence of type %s\n",
$sequence1->Type;
printf "CreateAASequence also creates sequence of type %s\n",
$sequence2->Type;

# Create nucleotide sequence documents and viewed in the Annotation Window.
my $sdmNucleotideDocument =
Sdm::Document::CreateNucleotideDocument(SdmAnnotationModelType);
printf "CreateNucleotideDocument creates document of type %s\n",
$sdmNucleotideDocument->Type;

# Edit and create nucleotide sequence object.
my $dnaSequence1 = $sdmNucleotideDocument->Sequence(0);
$dnaSequence1->InsetSequenceString( 0, 'CAGTU' );
my $dnaSequence2 =
$sdmNucleotideDocument->CreateNASequence( 'Sequence2', 'CAGTU' );

printf
"On a nucleic acid document, CreateSequence creates sequence of type %s\n",
$dnaSequence1->Type;
printf "CreateNASequence also creates sequence of type %s\n",
$dnaSequence2->Type;
```

# CreateAcceptorFeature function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createacceptorfeature_function.htm

## CreateAcceptorFeature function

### Description

CreateAcceptorFeature creates an acceptor feature for the specified atom.

### Applies to

The CreateAcceptorFeature function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the CreateAcceptorFeature function

#### Instance

my $acceptorfeatureObject = $object->CreateAcceptorFeature( <atom> );

my $acceptorfeatureObject = $object->CreateAcceptorFeature( { Atom => <atom> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $acceptorfeatureObject | | | Mdm::AcceptorFeature |
| <atom> | Required | | Mdm::Atom |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty queries
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();
my $query2 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create some features on the queries
# Create a donor feature on query1 at 0,0,0
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# Create an acceptor feature on query2 at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $query2->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

# Merge two queries into one:
my $queries = $document->Queries;
$document->MergeQueries( @$queries[0], @$queries[1] );

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# CreateAminoAcidChain function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createaminoacidchain_function.htm

## CreateAminoAcidChain function

### Description

CreateAminoAcidChain creates a new amino acid chain.

### Applies to

The CreateAminoAcidChain function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the CreateAminoAcidChain function

#### Instance

my $aminoacidchainObject = $object->CreateAminoAcidChain();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $aminoacidchainObject | | | Mdm::AminoAcidChain |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate methods for building and editing proteins.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# This is how to create an amino acid chain containing an alanine residue:
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $chain = $molecule->CreateAminoAcidChain();
my $aminoAcid1 = $chain->CreateResidue(Mdm::alanine);

my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
my $count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The current number of amino acids is $count.\n";

# Define a string consisting of 1-letter amino acid residue codes.
my $wideSequence = "AlaPheGlyProHisIleLysAlaAlaAla";
my $sequence = Mdm::AminoAcidChain::ConvertToOneLetterSequence($wideSequence);

print
"Converted wide sequence: $wideSequence to narrow sequence: $sequence.\n";

# Demonstrate how to append a sequence of residues at the C-terminus.
# Let's make it helical rather than the default extended conformation.
$document->GrowAminoAcidChain(
{
InsertAt => $chain,
Sequence => $sequence,
ConformationType => Mdm::rightAlphaHelixConformation,
GrowAtNTerminal => False
}
);

$aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
$count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The number of amino acid residues after growing chain "
. "at the C-terminus is $count.\n";

# Demonstrate how to grow amino acid chain at the N terminal.
# This will prepend the residue His0.
$document->GrowAminoAcidChain(
{
InsertAt => $chain,
Sequence => "H",
GrowAtNTerminal => True
}
);

$aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
$count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The number of amino acid residues after growing chain "
. "at the N-terminus is $count.\n";

# Insertion a residue within the chain.
my $insertionpoint = $aminoAcids->Item( $count - 2 );
my $sequence = "GANDT";
$document->InsertAminoAcid( $insertionpoint, $sequence );

$aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
$count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The number of amino acid residues after insertion is $count.\n";

# Demonstrate how to mutate a residue.
my $residuetomutate = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
print 'Amino acid name before the mutation: '
. $residuetomutate->Name() . "\n";
$document->MutateAminoAcid( $residuetomutate, Mdm::tyr );
print 'Amino acid name after the mutation: '
. $residuetomutate->Name() . "\n";

# At this point we have various insertion codes - lets renumber
print "Residue names before renumbering: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
print " " . $aminoAcids->Item($index)->Name() . " ";
}
print "\n";

$document->RenumberSequence( $aminoAcids->Item(0), 1, $count, True );
print "Residue names after renumbering: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
print " " . $aminoAcids->Item($index)->Name() . " ";
}
print "\n";

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# CreateAndTopology function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createandtopology_function.htm

## CreateAndTopology function

### Description

CreateAndTopology creates a query for matching all substructures
derived from the list of currently selected molecules.

### Applies to

The CreateAndTopology function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateAndTopology function

#### Command

$object->CreateAndTopology( [queryfeatures] );

$object->CreateAndTopology( { QueryFeatures => [queryfeatures] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [queryfeatures] | Optional | noQueryFeatures | enum Mdm::AddTopologyQueryFeatures |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Create a distance constraint (7.5 to 9.5 angstroms) between O and [N,O,S]
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create Mdm::Array to store atoms to use for distance constraint.
my $atoms = Mdm::Array::Create();

# Create an oxygen atom at (-15.6, 2.2, 0.0).
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -15.6, 2.2, 0 );
$atoms->AddItem($atomObject);

# Create a Nitrogen atom at (-7.2, 2.3, 0.0).
my $molecule1 = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject1 = $molecule1->CreateAtom("N");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -7.2, 2.3, 0 );
$atoms->AddItem($atomObject1);

# Create an 'AND' query containing the selected molecules (all
# molecules are used if none selected). This will be used as the
# top level for the distance constraint.
$document->CreateAndTopology();

# Get the Root operator.
my $operators = $document->QueryOperators;
my $rootOperator;
foreach my $operator (@$operators)
{
if ( $operator->IsRoot )
{
$rootOperator = $operator;
}
}

# Create the distance constraint off the root operator.
my $distanceConstraint =
$rootOperator->CreateDistanceFeature( $atoms, 7.5, 9.5 );

# Get N QueryAtom and change it to N,O,S.
my $queryAtoms = $document->QueryAtoms;
foreach my $queryAtom (@$queryAtoms)
{
my $atomList = $queryAtom->GetProperty("List");
if ( $atomList eq 'N' )
{
$queryAtom->SetProperty( "List", "N O S" );
$queryAtom->Parent()->Select; # select it for the color command below
}
}

# Color the QueryAtom with multiple definitions another color
$document->SetColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 170, 85, 127 ) );
$document->DeselectAll();
```

# CreateAngleFeature function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createanglefeature_function.htm

## CreateAngleFeature function

### Description

CreateAngleFeature creates an angle feature with the limits for the atoms defined by
the objects argument. The objects argument must contain three atoms, two bonds connected to one
common atom, or one bond and one atom not connected to the bond.
The limits are expressed as angles in degrees.

### Applies to

The CreateAngleFeature function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the CreateAngleFeature function

#### Instance

my $anglefeatureObject = $object->CreateAngleFeature( <arrayofobjects>, [lowerlimit], [upperlimit] );

my $anglefeatureObject = $object->CreateAngleFeature( { ArrayOfObjects => <arrayofobjects>, LowerLimit => [lowerlimit], UpperLimit => [upperlimit] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $anglefeatureObject | | | Mdm::AngleFeature |
| <arrayofobjects> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| [lowerlimit] | Optional | 0.0 | Real |
| [upperlimit] | Optional | 180.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

# Create an angle constraint.

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $atom_array = Mdm::Array::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles('C=O');
$document->Atoms->Item(0)->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -4.27, 3.44, 0 );
$atom_array->AddItem( $document->Atoms->Item(0) );
$document->Atoms->Item(1)->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -4.34, 4.94, 0 );

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("N");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -4.11, -.745, 0 );
$atom_array->AddItem($atomObject);
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("S");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.242, -0.664, 0 );
$atom_array->AddItem($atomObject);

$document->CreateAndTopology();
$document->QueryOperators()->Item(0)
->CreateAngleFeature( $atom_array, 80, 100 );

my $propertyNames = $document->AngleFeatures()->Item(0)->PropertyNames;
foreach my $propertyName (@$propertyNames)
{
my $value =
$document->AngleFeatures()->Item(0)->GetProperty($propertyName);
print "$propertyName - $value\n";
}
```

### Description

CreateAngleMonitor creates a new angle monitor for the specified geometric objects.

drawn through items 2 and 3.

| <item2> | Required | | Mdm::Geometric3d |
| <item3> | Required | | Mdm::Geometric3d |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9INS.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleAtomLine } );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $sequence = $molecule->AminoAcidSequence;
print "AminoAcidSequence: $sequence\n";

my $aminoAcid3 = $aminoAcids->Item(2);

my $distance = $document->CreateDistanceMonitor( $aminoAcid1->CAlpha, $aminoAcid2->CAlpha );

printf "Distance between CAlpha atoms of $aminoAcid1->{Name} and $aminoAcid2->{Name}: %8.3f\n", $distance->Distance;

my $angle = $document->CreateAngleMonitor( $aminoAcid1->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid1->AmideNitrogen, $aminoAcid1->CAlpha );

printf "Angle between amide carbon, nitrogen, and CAlpha atoms of $aminoAcid1->{Name}: %8.3f\n", $angle->Angle;

my $phiTorsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$aminoAcid1->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid2->AmideNitrogen,
$aminoAcid2->CAlpha, $aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon
);

my $psiTorsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$aminoAcid2->AmideNitrogen, $aminoAcid2->CAlpha,
$aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid3->AmideNitrogen
```

# CreateAnimation function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createanimation_function.htm

## CreateAnimation function

### Description

CreateAnimation creates a new MDM animation for the specified collection of objects.
Each object in the collection is used as an animation frame.

### Applies to

The CreateAnimation function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateAnimation function

#### Instance

my $animationObject = $object->CreateAnimation( <arrayofframes> );

my $animationObject = $object->CreateAnimation( { ArrayOfFrames => <arrayofframes> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $animationObject | | | Mdm::Animation |
| <arrayofframes> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage()
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing conformations.\n";
print " 3 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Opens a molecule with conformations from the active Molecule Window.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage() unless ($document);
Usage() unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );
Usage() unless ( $document->Conformations->Count > 0 );

print "Create an animation using conformation objects.\n";
my $animation = $document->CreateAnimation( $document->Conformations );
my $frameCount = $animation->FrameCount;
print "Number of animation frames: $frameCount frames.\n";

print "Saving the first frame to file.\n";
$animation->ActivateFirstFrame();
$document->Save( "FirstFrame.mol2", "mol2" );

# Illustrate how to activate the next and previous frames.
$animation->ActivateNextFrame();
$animation->ActivatePreviousFrame();

print "Saving the last frame to file.\n";
$animation->ActivateLastFrame();
$document->Save( "LastFrame.mol2", "mol2" );

print "Removing the first frame.\n";
my $firstFrame = $document->Conformations->Item(0);
$animation->RemoveFrame($firstFrame);

print "Adding the first frame back.\n";
$animation->AddFrame($firstFrame);
my $isTracked = $animation->IsFrameSelectionTracked();
if ($isTracked)
{
print "Frame selection is tracked.\n";
}
else
{
print "Frame selection is not tracked.\n";
}

print "Removing and de-activating all animation frames.\n";
$animation->RemoveAllFrames();
$animation->ResetFrame();
```

# CreateAtom function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createatom_function.htm

## CreateAtom function

### Description

CreateAtom creates an atom of the specified chemical element.

### Applies to

The CreateAtom function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid , Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::Nucleotide , Mdm::Offlineable , Mdm::Residue

### Using the CreateAtom function

#### Instance

my $atomObject = $object->CreateAtom( <element> );

my $atomObject = $object->CreateAtom( { Element => <element> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $atomObject | | | Mdm::Atom |
| <element> | Required | | enum Mdm::ElementType |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

## CreateBindingSitesFromCavities function

### Description

CreateBindingSitesFromCavities creates binding sites from a specified receptor.
The newly created binding sites are returned in an Mdm::Array .
The receptor heavy atom radius, receptor Hydrogen radius, grid resolution, and site opening
arguments must be distances expressed in angstroms.

### Applies to

The CreateBindingSitesFromCavities function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateBindingSitesFromCavities function

#### Instance

my $arrayObject = $object->CreateBindingSitesFromCavities( <receptor>, [receptorheavyatomradius], [receptorhydrogenradius], [gridresolution], [siteopening], [minimumsitepointcount] );

my $arrayObject = $object->CreateBindingSitesFromCavities( { Receptor => <receptor>, ReceptorHeavyAtomRadius => [receptorheavyatomradius], ReceptorHydrogenRadius => [receptorhydrogenradius], GridResolution => [gridresolution], SiteOpening => [siteopening], MinimumSitePointCount => [minimumsitepointcount] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| <receptor> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| [gridresolution] | Optional | 0.5 | Real |
| [minimumsitepointcount] | Optional | 100 | Integer |
| [receptorheavyatomradius] | Optional | 2.5 | Real |
| [receptorhydrogenradius] | Optional | 2.0 | Real |
| [siteopening] | Optional | 5.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SbdDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the use of BindingSite objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

Delete( $document, GetLigands($document) );
Delete( $document, GetWaters($document) );

my $protein = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

# Find all binding site from receptor cavities.
my $bindingSites = $document->CreateBindingSitesFromCavities($protein);
print "Number of binding sites found: " . $bindingSites->Count . "\n";

# Loop through all binding sites and determine volume, point count
# and min/max dimension.
my $bsCount = 0;

foreach my $s (@$bindingSites)
{
my $volume = $s->GetProperty("Volume");
my $bcount = $s->BindingSitePoints->Count;
my $bindingSitePoints = $s->BindingSitePoints;
print " Site: " . ++$bsCount . "\n";
print "\tVolume: $volume\n";
print "\tPoint count: $bcount\n";

# Loop over the binding site points to find
# the minimum and maximum values.
my $max = Mdm::Point::Create( -1.e6, -1.e6, -1.e6 );
my $min = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.e6, 1.e6, 1.e6 );
foreach my $xyz (@$bindingSitePoints)
{
$max->X = $xyz->XYZ->X if ( $max->X < $xyz->XYZ->X );
$max->Y = $xyz->XYZ->Y if ( $max->Y < $xyz->XYZ->Y );
$max->Z = $xyz->XYZ->Z if ( $max->Z < $xyz->XYZ->Z );
$min->X = $xyz->XYZ->X if ( $min->X > $xyz->XYZ->X );
$min->Y = $xyz->XYZ->Y if ( $min->Y > $xyz->XYZ->Y );
$min->Z = $xyz->XYZ->Z if ( $min->Z > $xyz->XYZ->Z );
}
print "\tSite Minimum: x: "
. $min->X . " y: "
. $min->Y . " z: "
. $min->Z . "\n";
print "\tSite Maximum: x: "
. $max->X . " y: "
. $max->Y . " z: "
. $max->Z . "\n";
}
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to create binding sites from ligands.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

print 'Remove water molecules. '
. "Identify and move ligand molecule out of the binding pocket...\n\n";
Delete( $document, GetWaters($document) );
my $movedLigand = MoveIntoNewMolecule( $document, GetLigands($document) );
sleep(3);

print "Change the protein display to a solid ribbon tube...\n\n";
TurnOffProteinAtoms($document);
ApplyProteinDisplayStyle( $document, Mdm::styleProteinRibbonTube );
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms();
sleep(3);

print "Create binding sites from the ligand molecule...\n\n";
my $receptor = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $ReceptorHeavyAtomRadius = 2.5;
my $ReceptorHydrogenRadius = 2.0;
my $LigandHeavyAtomRadius = 2.5;
my $LigandHydrogenRadius = 2.0;
my $GridResolution = 0.4;
my $SiteOpening = 10.0;
my $MinimumSitePointCount = 100;
$document->CreateBindingSitesFromLigand(
$receptor, $movedLigand,
$ReceptorHeavyAtomRadius, $ReceptorHydrogenRadius,
$LigandHeavyAtomRadius, $LigandHydrogenRadius,
$GridResolution, $SiteOpening,
$MinimumSitePointCount
);
sleep(3);

my $site = $document->BindingSites->Item(0);
my $volume = $site->GetProperty('Volume');
print "Volume of principle binding site: $volume\n\n";

my $fileName = 'LigandFitSite.txt';
print "Saving LigandFit binding site data to file $fileName...\n\n";
my $ligandFitSiteFileText = $site->LigandFitBindingSiteFileText();
open FH, "> $fileName" or die "Cannot open $fileName: $!";
print FH $ligandFitSiteFileText;
close FH;
```

# CreateBond function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createbond_function.htm

## CreateBond function

### Description

CreateBond creates a bond between two atoms of the specified type.
If the bond type is left out, a single bond is constructed.

### Applies to

The CreateBond function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateBond function

#### Instance

my $bondObject = $object->CreateBond( <atom1>, <atom2>, [bondtype] );

my $bondObject = $object->CreateBond( { Atom1 => <atom1>, Atom2 => <atom2>, BondType => [bondtype] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $bondObject | | | Mdm::Bond |
| <atom1> | Required | | Mdm::Atom |
| <atom2> | Required | | Mdm::Atom |
| [bondtype] | Optional | single | enum Mdm::BondType |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

# CreateBumpMonitor function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createbumpmonitor_function.htm

## CreateBumpMonitor function

### Description

CreateBumpMonitor creates a monitor that tracks close contacts between
atoms. If InternalBumps is True, close contacts between
atoms within the specified collection are tracked. Otherwise, close
contacts with atoms outside the specified collection are also tracked.

### Applies to

The CreateBumpMonitor function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateBumpMonitor function

#### Instance

my $bumpmonitorObject = $object->CreateBumpMonitor( <arrayofmonitoredatoms>, [internalbumps] );

my $bumpmonitorObject = $object->CreateBumpMonitor( { ArrayOfMonitoredAtoms => <arrayofmonitoredatoms>, InternalBumps => [internalbumps] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $bumpmonitorObject | | | Mdm::BumpMonitor |
| <arrayofmonitoredatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| [internalbumps] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Search for and print bumps between ligand and receptor.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Add hydrogen atoms to all heavy atoms.
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms( Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms, True );

# Creates a bump monitor between ligand and receptor atoms.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $bumpMonitor = $document->CreateBumpMonitor( $ligandAtoms, False );

$bumpMonitor->IsLabelShown = True;
$bumpMonitor->IsIntermolecularOnlyShown = False;

print "Default percent VDW Radius: $bumpMonitor->{DefaultPercentVdwRadius}\n";
print "$bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} bumps between ligand and receptor.\n";

$bumpMonitor->PercentVdwRadius = 90;

print "$bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} bumps between ligand and receptor "
. "when VDW radius set to 90%.\n";

my $bumps = $bumpMonitor->Bumps;
my $count = $bumps->Count;

# Create a bump hash.
my %bumpHash;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $bump = $bumps->Item($index);
$bumpHash{$index}{'bump'} = $bump;
$bumpHash{$index}{'Id1'} = $bump->Atom1->Id;
$bumpHash{$index}{'Id2'} = $bump->Atom2->Id;
}

# Print information for each bump, sorted by Atom1->Id followed by Atom2->Id.
my $counter = 0;
for my $b (
sort { 
my $x = $bumpHash{$a}{'Id1'};
my $y = $bumpHash{$b}{'Id1'};
($x != $y) ? ($x <=> $y) : ($bumpHash{$a}{'Id2'} <=> $bumpHash{$b}{'Id2'})
}
keys %bumpHash
)
{
my $bump = $bumpHash{$b}{'bump'};
my $atom1 = $bump->Atom1;
my $atom2 = $bump->Atom2;
printf
"%3d) Bump: %.3f A between Atom id %d %s:%s:%s and Atom id %d %s:%s:%s\n",
++$counter, $bump->Distance(),
$bumpHash{$b}{'Id1'},
$atom1->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom1->Parent->Name, $atom1->Name,
$bumpHash{$b}{'Id2'},
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name;
}
```

# CreateCAlphaMonitor function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createcalphamonitor_function.htm

## CreateCAlphaMonitor function

### Description

Creates a C-Alpha monitor that identifies pairs of C-Alpha atoms in different protein
molecules that are within a specified cutoff distance (default
2.5 Å). This can be used to assess the fit between superimposed protein
molecules and find matching residue pairs for performing superimposition.

### Applies to

The CreateCAlphaMonitor function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateCAlphaMonitor function

#### Instance

my $calphamonitorObject = $object->CreateCAlphaMonitor();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $calphamonitorObject | | | Mdm::CAlphaMonitor |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use superimposition functions
# and RMSD calculation functions for amino acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load 2rcs (an unligated antibody) from PDB.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '2rcs.pdb' );

# Load 1aj7 (a ligated antibody having the same sequence as 2crs) from PDB.
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

my $molecule2rcs = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[1];

my $hv2rcs = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 2rcs H chain V domain
my $hv1aj7 = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 1aj7 H chain V domain

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $molecule2rcs->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv2rcs->AddItem($aminoAcid);

$aminoAcid = $molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv1aj7->AddItem($aminoAcid);
}

# Show the transformation matrix which would superimpose the Vh
# domains by C-alpha atoms. This does not alter the coordinates
# of either structure.
my $matrix = $document->GetSuperimposeProteinMatrix( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
print "Transformation matrix:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 4 ; ++$i )
{
print "\t";
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < 4 ; ++$j )
{
printf "%.3f ", $matrix->GetEntry( $i, $j );
}
print "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms
my $rmsd = $document->SuperimposeProtein( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
printf "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms: %.3f\n\n", $rmsd;

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD. Note that by default the functions return an
# array of per-residue RMSD values, finishing with the overall RMSD
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it in which case the value will be zero. This can happen
# for unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation
# only for selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the
# required atoms for the requested type of calculation. 
# If you do not want per-residue RMSDs, set the 4th parameter ResidueReport
# False. In this case the array will only contain the overall RMSD.
# In this example, the all protein rmsd has no residue values calculated
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True, False );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item(0);
print "\n";

#Show that the all protein array contains just the overall RMSD.
printf "Number of values returned for all protein is %d\n", $apRmsd->Count();

# Demonstrating that the array is for all residues plus overall value not
# just selected and that as the first chain(L) is unselected its values
# are 0.
printf "Number of values returned for sidechains is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0), $scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

#Create a C-Alpha monitor
my $caMonitor = $document->CreateCAlphaMonitor();

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs before superimposing.\n";
if ($cAlphaPairs->Count > 0) {
printf "The first C-alpha to C-alpha pair distance is %.3f Angstroms.\n",
$cAlphaPairs->Item(0)->Distance;
}

#Lets do it for all matching atoms just to show the argument
my $rmsdByCA =
$document->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( $document->Molecules(), $caMonitor,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingAllAtoms );

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs after superimposing.\n";

#The values returned are like for Superimpose By Alignment - the first value
# is ref-ref (ie 0) then ref-mover for each superimposed molecule.
my $numVal = $rmsdByCA->Count();
printf( "Number of values returned for SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs %d\n",
$numVal );
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $numVal ; ++$i )
{
printf( "RMSD %d is %f\n", $i, $rmsdByCA->[$i] );
}

# use the filter function to retrieve the CAlpha atoms
my $cAlphaMonitors = $document->CAlphaMonitors;
foreach my $m (@$cAlphaMonitors)
{
print $m->ClassName ." filter entries: " . $m->CAlphaPairs->Count. "\n";
}

print "Finished Superimpose Script Example\n";
```

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the CreateCentroidFeature function

#### Instance

my $centroidfeatureObject = $object->CreateCentroidFeature( <arrayofatoms> );

my $centroidfeatureObject = $object->CreateCentroidFeature( { ArrayOfAtoms => <arrayofatoms> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $centroidfeatureObject | | | Mdm::CentroidFeature |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');

$document->CreateAndTopology();

# The query bonds are automatically created using
# the CreateAndTopology function. However, to show
# how to create them using CreateBondQuery, we will delete
# them and then add them again.

my $querybonds = $document->QueryBonds;
foreach my $querybond (@$querybonds)
{
$querybond->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

my $bonds = $document->Bonds;
foreach my $bond (@$bonds)
{
my $querybond =
$document->QueryOperators()->Item(0)->CreateQueryBond($bond);
$querybond->AddBondType('queryAnyBond');
}

# removes the first query bond's bond type
$document->QueryBonds->Item(0)->RemoveBondType('queryAnyBond');
```

Source type: HTML

Source file: scripting/createcentroidmonitor_function.htm

## CreateCentroidMonitor function

### Description

CreateCentroidMonitor creates a centroid monitor at the geometric center of
the specified atoms. If the atoms move, the centroid monitor will also move to remain in the geometric center. You can change the centroid monitor from geometric to center of mass by changing the IsCenterOfMassMonitor to True.

### Applies to

The CreateCentroidMonitor function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateCentroidMonitor function

#### Instance

my $centroidmonitorObject = $object->CreateCentroidMonitor( <arrayofmonitoredatoms> );

my $centroidmonitorObject = $object->CreateCentroidMonitor( { ArrayOfMonitoredAtoms => <arrayofmonitoredatoms> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $centroidmonitorObject | | | Mdm::CentroidMonitor |
| <arrayofmonitoredatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Creates a centroid monitor

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create the molecules for the substructure query
$document->InsertFromSmiles('C1=NC=CC=C1');

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
```

# CreateChain function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createchain_function.htm

## CreateChain function

### Description

CreateChain creates an empty chemical chain. To construct amino acid
or nucleic acid chains, use CreateAminoAcidChain or CreateNucleicAcidChain , respectively.

### Applies to

The CreateChain function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the CreateChain function

#### Instance

my $chainObject = $object->CreateChain();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $chainObject | | | Mdm::Chain |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Create sample PDB-style ligand molecule.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Create empty document, molecule and chain.
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $chain = $molecule->CreateChain();
$chain->Name = "A";

# Create empty residue.
my $residue = $chain->CreateResidue(Mdm::unk);
$residue->Name = "LIG1";

# Create and name atom objects.
my $N = $residue->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
$N->Name = "N";
my $C1 = $residue->CreateAtom(Mdm::C);
$C1->Name = "C1";
my $C2 = $residue->CreateAtom(Mdm::C);
$C2->Name = "C2";
my $O = $residue->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);
$O->Name = "O";
my $C3 = $residue->CreateAtom(Mdm::C);
$C3->Name = "C3";

# Create bonds.
$document->CreateBond( $N, $C1 );
$document->CreateBond( $C1, $C2 );
$document->CreateBond( $C2, $O, Mdm::doubleBond );
$document->CreateBond( $C1, $C3 );

$document->Clean(100);

print 'Created molecule with molecular formula: '
. $molecule->MolecularFormula . "\n";

#$document->Save( "sample.sd", "mol" );
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use chirality monitors.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9INS.pdb" );
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms();

my $monitor = $document->CreateChiralityMonitor();

{

printf "\t%s\n", $label;
}
```

# CreateClusterStructureDendrogram function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createclusterstructuredendrogram_function.htm

## CreateClusterStructureDendrogram function

### Description

CreateClusterStructureDendrogram creates a cluster structure dendrogram
from the distance matrix defined in the Data Table View.
The following arguments are available:

* MdmDocument specifies the Mdm::Document whose data will be plotted.

* DataTableTabName specifies the tab that contains the distance matrix.

* KeyProperty is the name of the property that identifies each object in the distance matrix uniquely.

* KeyProperties is the list of property names identifying the row of distances for each object.

* ValueProperies is the list of values for each object as defined in KeyProperty.

The number of values in KeyProperties and ValueProperties should be equal to the dimension of the distance matrix contained in the Data Table View. One identifies the rows and the other identifies the columns.

### Applies to

The CreateClusterStructureDendrogram function can be used with the following objects:

Chart::Document

### Using the CreateClusterStructureDendrogram function

#### Static

my $documentObject = Chart::Document::CreateClusterStructureDendrogram( <mdmdocument>, <datatabletabname>, <keyproperty>, <keyproperties>, <valueproperties> );

my $documentObject = Chart::Document::CreateClusterStructureDendrogram( { MdmDocument => <mdmdocument>, DataTableTabName => <datatabletabname>, KeyProperty => <keyproperty>, KeyProperties => <keyproperties>, ValueProperties => <valueproperties> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | Chart::Document |
| <datatabletabname> | Required | | String |
| <keyproperties> | Required | | String |
| <keyproperty> | Required | | String |
| <mdmdocument> | Required | | Mdm::Document |
| <valueproperties> | Required | | String |

#### Defined by

ChartDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to create a cluster structure dendrogram (client only)
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ChartDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';
my $filePath = $samplesFolder . 'Tutorials/Conformations/dendrogram_1.sd';

my $document = DiscoveryScript::Open($filePath);
sleep 2; # Pause while molecules load.

my $dendrogram = Chart::Document::CreateClusterStructureDendrogram(
{
MdmDocument => $document,
DataTableTabName => 'Molecule',
KeyProperty => 'conformation',
KeyProperties => 'conformation 1,conformation 2,conformation 3',
ValueProperties => 'conformation 1,conformation 2,conformation 3'
}
);

print "Model Type: DendrogramModelType\n"
if ( $dendrogram->ModelType == DendrogramModelType );

$dendrogram->UpdateViews();
```

my $conformationObject = $object->CreateConformation();

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Create a few conformations by rotating the phi torsion
# angle of the first amino acid residue.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Get first three amino acids
my $aminoAcid1 = $aminoAcids->Item(0);
my $aminoAcid2 = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
my $aminoAcid3 = $aminoAcids->Item(2);

# Creates a monitor for the phi angle
my $phiTorsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$aminoAcid1->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid2->AmideNitrogen,
$aminoAcid2->CAlpha, $aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon
);

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index <= 6 ; ++$index )
{
my $torsionValue = $index * 60.0;

# rotates the first residue's phi angle
$phiTorsion->SetProperty( "Angle", "$torsionValue" );

# creates a new conformation
my $conformation = $molecule->CreateConformation();
$conformation->MakeActive();

# sets the current conformation to be invisible
# so the next newly created conformation will be "active" and updated with new coordinates
$conformation->SetInvisible(True);
}
my $activeConformation = $aminoAcid1->FindActiveConformation();

# creates an animation using the newly created conformations
my $animation = $document->CreateAnimation( $molecule->Conformations );
my $frameCount = $animation->FrameCount;
print "Number of animation frames: $frameCount frames\n";

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $frameCount ; $i++ )
{
printf " Frame: %d\n", $i + 1; 
$animation->ActivateNextFrame();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(1);
}
```

## CreateCustomFeature (deprecated) function

### Description

CreateCustomFeature creates a custom feature with the specified
key, at the specified location.

### Applies to

The CreateCustomFeature (deprecated) function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the CreateCustomFeature (deprecated) function

#### Instance

This function is deprecated. It has been replaced by in Sdm::Sequence .

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Location class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASDFGHJKL' );

# Create a join feature for residues DFGH.
my $segmentStart = 2;
my $segmentCount = 4;
my $location = Sdm::Location::Create( Sdm::locationTypeJoin, $segmentStart,
$segmentCount );

print "Location properties\n";

my $locationType = $location->Type;
print "Location type\t" . $locationType . "\n";

my $segmentCount = $location->SegmentCount;
print "Segment count\t$segmentCount \n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $segmentCount ; ++$index )
{
my $segment = $location->Segment($index);
print "Segment $index...\n";
print "\tStart position:\t" . $segment->StartPosition . "\n";
print "\tEnd position:\t" . $segment->EndPosition . "\n";
print "\tSegementType:\t" . $segment->Type . "\n";
print "\tIs complement?:\t" . $segment->IsComplement . "\n";
}

my $feature =
Sdm::Feature::CreateCustomFeature( 'Custom feature', $location );

# Add this feature to the sequence.
$sequence->AddFeature($feature);
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script will illustrate functions and properties of the
# Sdm::Feature class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASDFGHJKL' );

# Create a join feature for residues DFGH and add it the sequence.
my $segmentStart = 2;
my $segmentCount = 4;
my $feature = $sequence->CreateCustomSequenceFeature( 'Custom feature',
Sdm::locationTypeJoin, $segmentStart, $segmentCount );
$feature->AddQualifier("InfoKey", 'Example feature');

$sequence->AddFeature($feature);

my $count = $sequence->FeatureCount;
print "Sequence has $count features\n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $feature = $sequence->Feature($index);
my $location = $feature->Location;

print "\tKey\t" . $feature->Key . "\n";
print "\tShape\t" . $feature->Shape . "\n";

my $color = $feature->FillColor;
print "\tFill color\t("
. $color->Red . ' '
. $color->Green . ' '
. $color->Blue . ")\n";
$color = $feature->OutlineColor;
print "\tOutline color\t("
. $color->Red . ' '
. $color->Green . ' '
. $color->Blue . ")\n";
print "\t" . "Label\t" . $feature->LabelText . "\n";
$color = $feature->LabelColor;
print "\t"
. "Label color\t("
. $color->Red . ' '
. $color->Green . ' '
. $color->Blue . ")\n";
print "\t" . "Label type\t" . $feature->LabelFromType . "\n";
print "\t" . "Is label visible\t" . $feature->IsLabelVisible . "\n";
print "\t" . "Is label horizontal\t" . $feature->IsLabelHorizontal . "\n";
print "\t" . "Feature Location type\t" . $location->Type . "\n";
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Creates an empty molecule
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();

# Create oxygen atoms
my $O1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);
my $O2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

# Assign coordinates to atoms
my $xyz1 = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O1->XYZ = $xyz1;

my $xyz2 = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O2->XYZ = $xyz2;

# Create Spheres centered on atom position
my $sphere1 = $O1->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz1, Radius => 0.4 } );
my $sphere2 = $O2->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz2, Radius => 0.4 } );

# Create Cylinder
my $cylinder =
$O1->CreateCylinder( { Begin => $xyz1, End => $xyz2, Radius => 0.2 } );
my $bottom = $cylinder->{BottomCenter};
printf "Cylinder bottom center: %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n Radius: %8.3f\n",
$bottom->X, $bottom->Y, $bottom->Z, $cylinder->Radius;

# Make cylinder transparent
$cylinder->IsTransparent(True);

# Create a slicing plane perpendicular to the cylinder axis
my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
my $slicingplaneObject = $document->CreateSlicingPlane(
{
Index => 1,
ArrayOfObjects => $atoms,
Origin => Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 ),
Normal => Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 )
}
);

# Get all 3D Objects
my $objects3d = $document->Geometric3ds;

# Print their name and class name
foreach my $object (@$objects3d)
{
print $object->ClassName . "\t" . $object->Name . "\n";
}

# Get all slicing planes
my $slicplanes = $document->SlicingPlanes;
print "Number of slicing planes" . $slicplanes->Count. "\n";
```

# CreateDihedralFeature function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createdihedralfeature_function.htm

## CreateDihedralFeature function

### Description

CreateDihedralFeature creates a dihedral feature with the limits
for the atoms defined by the objects argument. The objects argument must
contain four atoms, two bonds not connected to a common atom, or one bond
and two atoms not connected to the bond. The limits are expressed as
angles in degrees.

### Applies to

The CreateDihedralFeature function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the CreateDihedralFeature function

#### Instance

my $dihedralfeatureObject = $object->CreateDihedralFeature( <arrayofobjects>, [lowerlimit], [upperlimit] );

my $dihedralfeatureObject = $object->CreateDihedralFeature( { ArrayOfObjects => <arrayofobjects>, LowerLimit => [lowerlimit], UpperLimit => [upperlimit] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $dihedralfeatureObject | | | Mdm::DihedralFeature |
| <arrayofobjects> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| [lowerlimit] | Optional | 0.0 | Real |
| [upperlimit] | Optional | 180.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

# Create a dihedral constraint.

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $atom_array = Mdm::Array::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles('CCCC');

$document->CreateAndTopology();
my $dihedralfeatureObject =
$document->QueryOperators()->Item(0)
->CreateDihedralFeature( $document->Atoms, -60, -10 );

# Print some information of the DihedralFeatures
my $dihedralfeatures = $document->DihedralFeatures();
foreach my $feature (@$dihedralfeatures)
{
my $propertyNames = $feature->PropertyNames();
foreach my $propertyName (@$propertyNames)
{
my $propertyValue = $feature->GetProperty($propertyName);
print "$propertyName - $propertyValue \n";
}
}
```

# CreateDihedralRestraint function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createdihedralrestraint_function.htm

## CreateDihedralRestraint function

### Description

CreateDihedralRestraint creates a harmonic restraint on the dihedral
angle formed by four atoms. The restraint holds the angle harmonically
during simulations. A restraint has an associated force constant
(kcal/mol/radian^2 for periodicity=0 or kcal/mol for all other values), reference angle
in degrees and periodicity. The option UseCurrentGeometrySettings
determines if the reference angle if initialized from the current geometry
or from the optional ReferenceAngle argument.

### Applies to

The CreateDihedralRestraint function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateDihedralRestraint function

#### Instance

my $dihedralrestraintObject = $object->CreateDihedralRestraint( <atom1>, <atom2>, <atom3>, <atom4>, [forceconstant], [referenceangle], [periodicity], [name], [color], [usecurrentgeometrysettings] );

my $dihedralrestraintObject = $object->CreateDihedralRestraint( { Atom1 => <atom1>, Atom2 => <atom2>, Atom3 => <atom3>, Atom4 => <atom4>, ForceConstant => [forceconstant], ReferenceAngle => [referenceangle], Periodicity => [periodicity], Name => [name], Color => [color], UseCurrentGeometrySettings => [usecurrentgeometrysettings] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $dihedralrestraintObject | | | Mdm::DihedralRestraint |
| <atom1> | Required | | Mdm::Atom |
| <atom2> | Required | | Mdm::Atom |
| <atom3> | Required | | Mdm::Atom |
| <atom4> | Required | | Mdm::Atom |
| [color] | Optional | DiscoveryScript::Color::Create(0, 0, 255) | DiscoveryScript::Color |
| [forceconstant] | Optional | 1.0 | Real |
| [name] | Optional | "" | String |
| [periodicity] | Optional | | Integer |
| [referenceangle] | Optional | 0.0 | Real |
| [usecurrentgeometrysettings] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Fix the backbone
my $backbone = FilterByString( $document, ':CA,C,N,O,HN,HA' );
$document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($backbone);

# Restrain beta carbon atoms
my $cbeta = FilterByString( $document, ':CB' );
$document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint( $cbeta, 10, Mdm::BestFit );

# Add cross-strand distance restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "THR2:CA" );
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "ILE34:CA" );
$document->CreateDistanceRestraint(
{
ArrayOfAtoms1 => $atom1,
ArrayOfAtoms2 => $atom2,
RMin => 2,
RMax => 5,
RMinForceConstant => 10,
RMaxForceConstant => 20,
ForceMaximum => 20
}
);

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
$document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);

# Print the total number of restraints (4)
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
print "There are ", $constraints->Count, " constraints\n";
```

# CreateDistanceFeature function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createdistancefeature_function.htm

## CreateDistanceFeature function

### Description

CreateDistanceFeature creates a distance constraint with the limits
for the atoms defined by the objects argument. The objects argument must
contain two atoms or one bond and no atoms. The limits are distances expressed
in angstroms.

### Applies to

The CreateDistanceFeature function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the CreateDistanceFeature function

#### Instance

my $distancefeatureObject = $object->CreateDistanceFeature( <arrayofobjects>, [lowerlimit], [upperlimit] );

my $distancefeatureObject = $object->CreateDistanceFeature( { ArrayOfObjects => <arrayofobjects>, LowerLimit => [lowerlimit], UpperLimit => [upperlimit] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $distancefeatureObject | | | Mdm::DistanceFeature |
| <arrayofobjects> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| [lowerlimit] | Optional | 0.0 | Real |
| [upperlimit] | Optional | 8.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Create a distance constraint (7.5 to 9.5 angstroms) between O and [N,O,S]
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create Mdm::Array to store atoms to use for distance constraint.
my $atoms = Mdm::Array::Create();

# Create an oxygen atom at (-15.6, 2.2, 0.0).
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -15.6, 2.2, 0 );
$atoms->AddItem($atomObject);

# Create a Nitrogen atom at (-7.2, 2.3, 0.0).
my $molecule1 = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject1 = $molecule1->CreateAtom("N");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -7.2, 2.3, 0 );
$atoms->AddItem($atomObject1);

# Create an 'AND' query containing the selected molecules (all
# molecules are used if none selected). This will be used as the
# top level for the distance constraint.
$document->CreateAndTopology();

# Get the Root operator.
my $operators = $document->QueryOperators;
my $rootOperator;
foreach my $operator (@$operators)
{
if ( $operator->IsRoot )
{
$rootOperator = $operator;
}
}

# Create the distance constraint off the root operator.
my $distanceConstraint =
$rootOperator->CreateDistanceFeature( $atoms, 7.5, 9.5 );

# Get N QueryAtom and change it to N,O,S.
my $queryAtoms = $document->QueryAtoms;
foreach my $queryAtom (@$queryAtoms)
{
my $atomList = $queryAtom->GetProperty("List");
if ( $atomList eq 'N' )
{
$queryAtom->SetProperty( "List", "N O S" );
$queryAtom->Parent()->Select; # select it for the color command below
}
}

# Color the QueryAtom with multiple definitions another color
$document->SetColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 170, 85, 127 ) );
$document->DeselectAll();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w

use strict;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9INS.pdb" );

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

);

$aminoAcid2->AmideNitrogen, $aminoAcid2->CAlpha,
$aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid3->AmideNitrogen
);

print "Amino acid $aminoAcid2->{Name}: ";
printf "phi = %8.3f, psi = %8.3f\n", $phiTorsion->Angle, $psiTorsion->Angle;
```

# CreateDistanceRestraint function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createdistancerestraint_function.htm

## CreateDistanceRestraint function

### Description

CreateDistanceRestraint creates an NOE (Nuclear Overhauser Effect) like
distance restraint between two atoms.
The restraint allows you to specify minimum and maximum distances
(angstroms), force constants for the lower and upper bounds
(kcal/mol/angstrom^2), and the maximum force at which a linear restraint is
applied (kcal/mol/angstrom). Note: The method currently allows creation of
distances between two arrays of atoms for future use. Today, only a single
atom in each array is supported.

### Applies to

The CreateDistanceRestraint function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateDistanceRestraint function

#### Instance

my $distancerestraintObject = $object->CreateDistanceRestraint( <arrayofatoms1>, <arrayofatoms2>, [rmin], [rmax], [rminforceconstant], [rmaxforceconstant], [forcemaximum], [name], [color] );

my $distancerestraintObject = $object->CreateDistanceRestraint( { ArrayOfAtoms1 => <arrayofatoms1>, ArrayOfAtoms2 => <arrayofatoms2>, RMin => [rmin], RMax => [rmax], RMinForceConstant => [rminforceconstant], RMaxForceConstant => [rmaxforceconstant], ForceMaximum => [forcemaximum], Name => [name], Color => [color] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $distancerestraintObject | | | Mdm::DistanceRestraint |
| <arrayofatoms1> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| <arrayofatoms2> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| [color] | Optional | DiscoveryScript::Color::Create(0, 255, 0) | DiscoveryScript::Color |
| [forcemaximum] | Optional | 2.0 | Real |
| [name] | Optional | "" | String |
| [rmax] | Optional | 0.0 | Real |
| [rmaxforceconstant] | Optional | 1.0 | Real |
| [rmin] | Optional | 0.0 | Real |
| [rminforceconstant] | Optional | 1.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Fix the backbone
my $backbone = FilterByString( $document, ':CA,C,N,O,HN,HA' );
$document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($backbone);

# Restrain beta carbon atoms
my $cbeta = FilterByString( $document, ':CB' );
$document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint( $cbeta, 10, Mdm::BestFit );

# Add cross-strand distance restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "THR2:CA" );
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "ILE34:CA" );
$document->CreateDistanceRestraint(
{
ArrayOfAtoms1 => $atom1,
ArrayOfAtoms2 => $atom2,
RMin => 2,
RMax => 5,
RMinForceConstant => 10,
RMaxForceConstant => 20,
ForceMaximum => 20
}
);

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
$document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);

# Print the total number of restraints (4)
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
print "There are ", $constraints->Count, " constraints\n";
```

# CreateDisulfideBridges function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createdisulfidebridges_function.htm

## CreateDisulfideBridges function

### Description

CreateDisulfideBridges creates a disulfide bridge for each selected Predicted Disulfide Bridge Site.

### Applies to

The CreateDisulfideBridges function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateDisulfideBridges function

#### Command

$object->CreateDisulfideBridges();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
#This is used for the script apis
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $temp = 0;
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('4ins');

#By default, the script returns string containing a csv file of properties for the predicted disulfides.
#Only new disulfides are found, for any chain combination, minimum sequence separation 5,
#maximum energy 10.0
# i.e. default args are novelDisulfidesOnly, anyChainDisulfides, 5, 10.0, true will use this one to show how to get the residues/bonds

my $csvFile=$document->PredictDisulfides();

#save the csv file
my $name=$document->ModelName();
my $fileName=$name . "Predicted_New_Disulfides.csv";
open FILE, '>' . $fileName;
print FILE $csvFile;
close FILE;

my $molecules=$document->Molecules();

#note that if validation of existing disulfides is performed (by using Mdm::existingDisulfidesOnly#or Mdm::novelAndExistingDisulfides then a second molecule containing the modelled disulfide
#bridges and with additional properties on the bond and molecule 

my $numMols=$molecules->Count; 
if($numMols == 1){

$document->DeselectAll();
my $molecule=$molecules->Item(0);
my $residuePairsAssembly = $molecule->Filter(
{ Type=>"Assembly", Property => "Name", Name => "Predicted Disulfide Bridge Residues" } );
if($residuePairsAssembly->Count() == 1){
print "Potential residue pairs for mutation to cysteine to form disulfide bridge in ".$molecule->Name . ": \n";
my $residuePairs=$residuePairsAssembly->Item(0)->Groups();
foreach my $residuePair (@$residuePairs) {
my $residuePairList=$residuePair->ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder();
#should be 2 residues in here
if($residuePairList->Count == 2){
my $residue1 = $residuePairList->Item(0);
my $residue2 = $residuePairList->Item(1);
print "Group " . $residuePair->Name . " contains residues: ". $residue1->Name . " and " . $residue2->Name . "\n";
}
}
}

#this should now also contain predicted site objects from which we can extract more properties
print "Sites for mutation to cysteine\n";
my $sites = $document->DisulfideBridgeSites;
my $numSites = $sites->Count();
print $numSites . " sites\n";
for(my $index = 0; $index < $numSites; ++$index){
my $site=$sites->Item($index);
my $label = $site->Name;
my $score = $site->GetProperty("Score");
my $energy = $site->GetProperty("Energy");
my $badContacts = $site->GetProperty("Bad Contacts");
my $depth = $site->GetProperty("Residue Depth");
my $mobility = $site->GetProperty("Thermal Mobility");
my $sep = $site->GetProperty("Sequence Separation");
my $volchange = $site->GetProperty("Volume Change");
my $env = $site->GetProperty("Environment");
my $SA = $site->GetProperty("Solvent Accessibility");
my $chi3 = $site->GetProperty("Chi3");
print " site " . $label . " score " . $score . " energy " . $energy . " Bad contacts " . $badContacts ." residue depth " . $depth . " mobility " . $mobility . " sep " . $sep . " volchange " . $volchange . " env " . $env . " SA " . $SA . " chi3 " . $chi3 . "\n";

my $SG1Coord = $site->SG1Coord;
my $SG2Coord = $site->SG2Coord;
print " SG coordinates (" . $SG1Coord->X . ", " . $SG1Coord->Y . ", " . $SG1Coord->Z . ") and " .
"(" . $SG2Coord->X . ", " . $SG2Coord->Y . ", " . $SG2Coord->Z . ")\n";
my $residues = $site->ResiduesToMutate;
if($residues->Count == 2){
print "residue 1 " . $residues->Item(0)->Name . " residue 2 " . $residues->Item(1)->Name . "\n";
}else{
print " error - site should contain two residues\n";
}

#create S-S bridge from a site - the command works on any selected DisulfideBridgeSite
if($score > 80.0){
print "Score " . $score . " - Creating S-S bridge\n"; 
$site->Select();
$document->CreateDisulfideBridges();
$site->Deselect();
}

}

}
```

my $proteinposeObject = $object->CreateDockedProteinPoseAssembly( <ligand>, <ligandcenter>, <receptor>, <receptorcenter>, <startingangles> );

my $proteinposeObject = $object->CreateDockedProteinPoseAssembly( { Ligand => <ligand>, LigandCenter => <ligandcenter>, Receptor => <receptor>, ReceptorCenter => <receptorcenter>, StartingAngles => <startingangles> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $proteinposeObject | | | Mdm::ProteinPose |
| <ligand> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <ligandcenter> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| <receptor> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <receptorcenter> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| <startingangles> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates the use for scripting functions for the protein-protein
# docking area.
# NOTE: Most of the functions connected to generating the DockedPoseAssembly and
# DockedProtein objects are designed to process output from the Dock Proteins (ZDOCK)
# protocols, which generates a set of numbers describing the relative orientations
# of the two proteins in a docked protein complex. Those numbers are necessary to
# generate the objects described in the this example but cannot be easily
# generated by hand. The numerical values hard-coded to avoid having
# to load a Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) output file . The values used are derived
# from the output of a Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) run on two small proteins: chain A of 2ptn and
# chain I of 2sta.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document =
DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "2ptn.pdb" ); # receptor
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "2sta.pdb" ); # ligand

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
my $receptor = $molecules->Item(0);
my $ligand = $molecules->Item(1);

# Only keep ligand chain that was used in ZDOCK run
my $ligandChains = $ligand->Chains;
foreach my $chain (@$ligandChains)
{
if ( $chain->Name ne "I" )
{
$chain->Select();
}
}

# Only keep receptor chain that was used in ZDOCK run
my $receptorChains = $receptor->Chains;
foreach my $chain (@$receptorChains)
{
if ( $chain->Name ne "A" )
{
$chain->Select();
}
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# Label receptor and ligand with identifying tags
# These tags are used by other commands
$receptor->SetProperty( "COMPLEX_TYPE", "RECEPTOR" );
$ligand->SetProperty( "COMPLEX_TYPE", "LIGAND" );

# Define general properties of the structures in the complex
# Note that these numbers are part of the output generated by the
# ZDock protein docking program.
# All numerical values were taken from ZDock run output for this system
my $N = 84;
my $spacing = 1.2;
my $receptorCenter = Mdm::Point::Create( 2.5130, 7.5200, 23.7720 );
my $ligandCenter = Mdm::Point::Create( 14.5890, 21.1360, 40.4300 );
my $startingAngles = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 );

# Create the DockedProteinPoseAssembly object which contains
# information about the proteins in the docked complex that
# common to all poses
my $poseAssembly =
$document->CreateDockedProteinPoseAssembly( $ligand, $ligandCenter,
$receptor, $receptorCenter, $startingAngles );

# The next three commands are redundant with the constructor above
# and are only included as example of how they are used.
# However, they can be used to set the DockedProteinPoseAssembly
# properties to different values if desired
$poseAssembly->LigandCenter($ligandCenter);
$poseAssembly->ReceptorCenter($receptorCenter);
$poseAssembly->StartingAngles($startingAngles);

# Set the ZDock grid size and grid spacing
# These values are internally used by the ZDock program
# they are stored mainly to be able to produce input files
# for the Process Poses and Refine Docked Protein protocols
$poseAssembly->SetPropertyAsInteger( "N", $N );
$poseAssembly->SetPropertyAsReal( "spacing", $spacing );
$poseAssembly->HideProperty("N");
$poseAssembly->HideProperty("spacing");

$poseAssembly->SetProperty( "Center", "Receptor" );
$poseAssembly->Name = "Docked Poses";

# Generate the numeric data for the first docked pose
# All numerical values taken from pose 1 of ZDock run output
my $position = Mdm::Point::Create( -5.1821, 20.9576, 21.2807 );
my $translation = Mdm::Point::Create( 6.0000, -16.8000, 2.4000 );
my $rotation = Mdm::Point::Create( 120.0000, 171.0266, 111.9815 );
my $cluster = 1;
my $topClusterPose = 1;
my ( $receptorCenterX, $receptorCenterY, $receptorCenterZ ) =
( 0.018, 14.954, 22.56 );
my ( $ligandCenterX, $ligandCenterY, $ligandCenterZ ) =
( 12.464, 24.22, 40.03 );

# Generate a new pose. The parameters of the constructor function are
# the position of the spherical pose representation
# the translation of the ligand from the starting to the docked position
# the rotation of the ligand from the starting to the docked position
# the cluster the pose belongs to
# whether or not the pose is the best ranked pose in the cluster 
my $newPose =
$poseAssembly->CreateProteinPose( $position, $translation, $rotation,
$cluster, $topClusterPose );

# The following sets of number represent the coordinates center of the binding interface
# on the receptor and the ligand. The values are store as properties which are
# used to toggle between receptor and ligand centric views in the DS client
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_x", "$receptorCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_y", "$receptorCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_z", "$receptorCenterZ" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_x", "$ligandCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_y", "$ligandCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_z", "$ligandCenterZ" );

# Set the name of the pose
$newPose->Name = "Pose1";

# Generate the numeric data for a second docked pose.
# All numerical values taken from pose 2 of ZDock run output
my $position = Mdm::Point::Create( 6.1596049, 17.94953, 5.095075 );
my $translation = Mdm::Point::Create( 4.8000, -14.4000, 4.8000 );
my $rotation = Mdm::Point::Create( 90.0000, 107.4457, 6.1356 );
my $cluster = 1;
my $topClusterPose = 0;
my ( $receptorCenterX, $receptorCenterY, $receptorCenterZ ) =
( 6.88, 14.615, 5.83 );
my ( $ligandCenterX, $ligandCenterY, $ligandCenterZ ) =
( 2.522, 27.292, 11.48 );
$newPose =
$poseAssembly->CreateProteinPose( $position, $translation, $rotation,
$cluster, $topClusterPose );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_x", "$receptorCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_y", "$receptorCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_z", "$receptorCenterZ" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_x", "$ligandCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_y", "$ligandCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_z", "$ligandCenterZ" );
$newPose->Name = "Pose2";
```
