# CreateDocumentFromStructures function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createdocumentfromstructures_function.htm

## CreateDocumentFromStructures function

### Description

Creates a sequence document. There is one required argument, the Mdm::Document containing the structures from which sequences are to
be extracted. There is an optional argument to specify the type of
sequence document to be created. By default, it will be a Protein Sequence
Data Model document containing all protein sequences found in the Mdm::Document . However, if the argument is set to "True", it will be
a Nucleic Acid
Sequence Data Model document containing all the nucleic acid sequences
extracted.

### Applies to

The CreateDocumentFromStructures function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the CreateDocumentFromStructures function

#### Static

my $documentObject = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures( <mdmdocument>, [dna] );

my $documentObject = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures( { MdmDocument => <mdmdocument>, Dna => [dna] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | Sdm::Document |
| <mdmdocument> | Required | | Mdm::Document |
| [dna] | Optional | False | Boolean |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print
" 2 Load a file containing multiple protein and/or dna molecules.\n";
print " 3 Try with some online and some offline\n";
print " 4 run this script\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

# The script assume the last active document contains molecules
# They can be online or offline
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing protein and/or dna molecules"
) unless ($document);

#By default, protein sequences are extracted
my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures($document);

#If you want to create nucleic acid sequences, set the second argument true:
my $sdmNADocument =
Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures( $document, True );

my $count = $sdmDocument->{SequenceCount};
print "First document contains $count protein sequences.\n";

my $NACount = $sdmNADocument->{SequenceCount};
print "Second document contains $NACount nucleic acid sequences.\n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->Sequence($index);
print "Sequence $index contains $sequence->{ResidueCount} residues.\n";
my $rawSequence = $sequence->SequenceString();
print "dump: $rawSequence\n";
}
```

Source type: HTML

## CreateDonorFeature function

### Description

CreateDonorFeature creates a donor feature for the specified atom.

### Applies to

The CreateDonorFeature function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the CreateDonorFeature function

#### Instance

my $donorfeatureObject = $object->CreateDonorFeature( <atom> );

my $donorfeatureObject = $object->CreateDonorFeature( { Atom => <atom> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $donorfeatureObject | | | Mdm::DonorFeature |
| <atom> | Required | | Mdm::Atom |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty queries
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();
my $query2 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create some features on the queries
# Create a donor feature on query1 at 0,0,0
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# Create an acceptor feature on query2 at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $query2->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

# Merge two queries into one:
my $queries = $document->Queries;
$document->MergeQueries( @$queries[0], @$queries[1] );

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# CreateExcludeTopology function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createexcludetopology_function.htm

## CreateExcludeTopology function

### Description

CreateExcludeTopology creates a query to either not match a single
2D substructure, or to match a first 2D substructure while not to match
additional 2D substructures which contain the first 2D substructure.

### Applies to

The CreateExcludeTopology function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateExcludeTopology function

#### Command

$object->CreateExcludeTopology();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

# Create C=O query, but exclude C(=O)O from the definition
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles('C=O');
$document->CreateAndTopology();

# Create C(=O)O
$document->InsertFromSmiles('C(=O)O');

# Make selections for Exclusion ( select 'And' operator of C=O and Acid molecule)
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Parent()->Select;
$document->Molecules()->Item(1)->Select;

# Exclude the acid from the C=O query
$document->CreateExcludeTopology();
$document->DeselectAll();

# Map the sp2 Oxygen atoms together
my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( ( $atom->Element() eq 'O' ) && ( $atom->Hybridization() eq 'sp2' ) )
{
$atom->Select();
}
}

$document->CreateMapping();
```

# CreateExclusionFeature function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createexclusionfeature_function.htm

## CreateExclusionFeature function

### Description

CreateExclusionFeature creates an exclusion feature with the specified radius for
the atom. The radius is expressed in angstroms.

### Applies to

The CreateExclusionFeature function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the CreateExclusionFeature function

#### Instance

my $exclusionfeatureObject = $object->CreateExclusionFeature( <atom>, [radius] );

my $exclusionfeatureObject = $object->CreateExclusionFeature( { Atom => <atom>, Radius => [radius] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $exclusionfeatureObject | | | Mdm::ExclusionFeature |
| <atom> | Required | | Mdm::Atom |
| [radius] | Optional | 1.2 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

# Create a query from a template molecules. Add HBAs to =O,
# HBD to N, and excluded volumes to all Halogens and
# projection points of HBAs and HBDs.

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles(
'OC(=O)C1=CC=C(C=C1)CN/C2=C/C=C(C=C2)C=CC(=O)C[Cl]');
AddHydrogens($document);

my $atoms = $document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $double_bond_oxygens = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $nitrogens = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $halogens = Mdm::Array::Create();

foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( ( $atom->Element eq 'O' ) && ( $atom->BondCount == 1 ) )
{
$double_bond_oxygens->AddItem($atom);
}
$nitrogens->AddItem($atom) if ( $atom->Element eq 'N' );
$halogens->AddItem($atom) if ( $atom->Element =~ /(Cl|F|Br|I)\b/i );
}

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Features and location constraints
my $featureCount = 0;
foreach my $atom (@$double_bond_oxygens)
{
++$featureCount;
my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
my $featureName = "HBA_" . $featureCount;
$acceptorOperator->Name($featureName);
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atom);

# create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );
}

foreach my $atom (@$nitrogens)
{
++$featureCount;
my $featureName = "HBD_" . $featureCount;
my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name($featureName);
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atom);

#create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );
}

# Add excluded volumes at the location of halogen atoms
foreach my $atom (@$halogens)
{
my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

# Add excluded volumes at the projection point of HBAs and HBDs
my $acceptorfeatures = $fitOperator->AcceptorFeatures;
foreach my $acceptor (@$acceptorfeatures)
{
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atom->XYZ = $acceptor->HeadXYZ();
$molecule->Select();

my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

my $donorfeatures = $fitOperator->DonorFeatures;
foreach my $donor (@$donorfeatures)
{
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atom->XYZ = $donor->HeadXYZ();
$molecule->Select();

my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

my $exclusionfeatures = $document->ExclusionFeatures();
my $exclusionfeatureCount = 0;
foreach my $exclusionfeature (@$exclusionfeatures)
{
++$exclusionfeatureCount;
my $name = "EV_" . $exclusionfeatureCount;
$exclusionfeature->Name($name);
}

# We will delete temporary atoms used to create EVs
# on projection points. Need to update objects before
# deleting so we preserve the X,Y,Z location.
$document->UpdateObjects();

# Delete temporary atoms
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# CreateFixedAtomConstraint function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createfixedatomconstraint_function.htm

## CreateFixedAtomConstraint function

### Description

CreateFixedAtomConstraint creates a constraint that will fix the location
of the set of atoms. During simulation, these atoms are not allowed to move.
See also CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint .

### Applies to

The CreateFixedAtomConstraint function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateFixedAtomConstraint function

#### Instance

my $fixedatomconstraintObject = $object->CreateFixedAtomConstraint( <arrayofatoms> );

my $fixedatomconstraintObject = $object->CreateFixedAtomConstraint( { ArrayOfAtoms => <arrayofatoms> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $fixedatomconstraintObject | | | Mdm::FixedAtomConstraint |
| <arrayofatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Fix the backbone
my $backbone = FilterByString( $document, ':CA,C,N,O,HN,HA' );
$document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($backbone);

# Restrain beta carbon atoms
my $cbeta = FilterByString( $document, ':CB' );
$document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint( $cbeta, 10, Mdm::BestFit );

# Add cross-strand distance restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "THR2:CA" );
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "ILE34:CA" );
$document->CreateDistanceRestraint(
{
ArrayOfAtoms1 => $atom1,
ArrayOfAtoms2 => $atom2,
RMin => 2,
RMax => 5,
RMinForceConstant => 10,
RMaxForceConstant => 20,
ForceMaximum => 20
}
);

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
$document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);

# Print the total number of restraints (4)
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
print "There are ", $constraints->Count, " constraints\n";
```

# CreateFromSequenceId function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createfromsequenceid_function.htm

## CreateFromSequenceId function

### Description

CreateFromSequenceId loads the sequence file for the specified identifier into a new Sdm::Document . By default the sequence is loaded from the ncbi protein database, but if the sequence is not protein then the appropriate database should be specified, e.g. nuccore for nucleic acid sequences.

### Applies to

The CreateFromSequenceId function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the CreateFromSequenceId function

#### Static

my $documentObject = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId( <id>, [nodisplay], [loadallobjects], [database] );

my $documentObject = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId( { Id => <id>, NoDisplay => [nodisplay], LoadAllObjects => [loadallobjects], Database => [database] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | Sdm::Document |
| <id> | Required | | String |
| [database] | Optional | "protein" | String |
| [loadallobjects] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [nodisplay] | Optional | False | Boolean |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to create a sequence from a locus id or
# gi number, for example y13252 or 1crn. Note that for nucleic acid sequences such as 
# y13252, the Database must be specified as "nuccore", rather than the default "protein".
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

# Open SDM document from a sequence identifier.
my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId('1CRN_A');

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

### Using the CreateGroup function

#### Instance

my $groupObject = $object->CreateGroup( <name>, <arrayofobjects> );

my $groupObject = $object->CreateGroup( { Name => <name>, ArrayOfObjects => <arrayofobjects> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $groupObject | | | Mdm::Group |
| <arrayofobjects> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| <name> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

# Use DSCommands to get all ligands.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);

# Create a ligand group.
my $group = $document->CreateGroup( "Ligands", $ligands );

# Get the group name.
print "Group name: " . $group->Name . "\n";

# Get the array of objects in the group, in no particular order.
my $ligand_array = $group->Array;

print "Group members:\n";
foreach my $ligand (sort {$a->Name cmp $b->Name} @$ligand_array)
{
printf "%s\n", $ligand->Name;
}

# Get the array of objects in the group in the order in which they
# would appear when performing a depth first traversal of the
# object hierarchy starting from the root object
$ligand_array = $group->ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder();

print "Group members:\n";
foreach my $ligand (@$ligand_array)
{
printf "%s\n", $ligand->Name;
}

# Remove group.

my $left = Mdm::Group::RemoveGroup($group);
printf "Items left in group after removal: %d\n", $left;
```

# CreateGroupUnderMoleculeIfPossible function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/creategroupundermoleculeifpossible_function.htm

## CreateGroupUnderMoleculeIfPossible function

### Description

CreateGroupUnderMoleculeIfPossible creates a new named group object
for the specified array of molecular data model objects.
If the array of molecular data model objects belongs to a single
molecule, the group is added to the molecule instead of to the
root object.

### Applies to

The CreateGroupUnderMoleculeIfPossible function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateGroupUnderMoleculeIfPossible function

#### Instance

my $groupObject = $object->CreateGroupUnderMoleculeIfPossible( <name>, <arrayofobjects> );

my $groupObject = $object->CreateGroupUnderMoleculeIfPossible( { Name => <name>, ArrayOfObjects => <arrayofobjects> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $groupObject | | | Mdm::Group |
| <arrayofobjects> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| <name> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create() or die "No document created";

my $root = $document->RootObject or die "No root object";

# Create molecule 1
my $molecule_1 = $document->CreateMolecule() or die "No molecule created";
$molecule_1->Name = "Molecule 1";

my $atom_1_1 = $molecule_1->CreateAtom(Mdm::C)
or die "No atom created";
$atom_1_1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 1.0, 0.0 );

my $atom_1_2 = $molecule_1->CreateAtom(Mdm::C)
or die "No atom created";
$atom_1_2->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 2.5, 0.0 );

my $bond_1_1_2 =
$document->CreateBond( $atom_1_1, $atom_1_2, Mdm::singleBond )
or die "No bond created";

# Create molecule 2
my $molecule_2 = $document->CreateMolecule() or die "No molecule created";
$molecule_2->Name = "Molecule 2";

my $atom_2_1 = $molecule_2->CreateAtom(Mdm::C)
or die "No atom created";
$atom_2_1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 );

my $atom_2_2 = $molecule_2->CreateAtom(Mdm::C)
or die "No atom created";
$atom_2_2->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 2.5, 0.0, 0.0 );

my $bond_2_1_2 =
$document->CreateBond( $atom_2_1, $atom_2_2, Mdm::singleBond )
or die "No bond created";

# Define group of atoms of molecule 1

my $members_1 = Mdm::Array::Create()
or die "No array created";
$members_1->AddItem($atom_1_1);
$members_1->AddItem($atom_1_2);

my $group_1 =
$document->CreateGroupUnderMoleculeIfPossible( "Group 1", $members_1 );

my $parent_1 = $group_1->Parent;
if ( $parent_1->UniqueId == $molecule_1->UniqueId )
{
printf("Group #1 is attached to molecule 1\n");
}

# Define group of atoms of molecule 2

my $members_2 = Mdm::Array::Create()
or die "No array created";
$members_2->AddItem($atom_2_1);
$members_2->AddItem($atom_2_2);

my $group_2 =
$document->CreateGroupUnderMoleculeIfPossible( "Group 2", $members_2 );

my $parent_2 = $group_2->Parent;
if ( $parent_2->UniqueId == $molecule_2->UniqueId )
{
printf("Group #2 is attached to molecule 2\n");
}

# Define group of atoms of molecules 1 and 2

my $members_3 = Mdm::Array::Create()
or die "No array created";
$members_3->AddItem($atom_1_1);
$members_3->AddItem($atom_1_2);
$members_3->AddItem($atom_2_1);
$members_3->AddItem($atom_2_2);

my $group_3 =
$document->CreateGroupUnderMoleculeIfPossible( "Group 3", $members_3 );

my $parent_3 = $group_3->Parent;
if ( $parent_3->UniqueId == $root->UniqueId )
{
printf("Group #3 is attached to the root object\n");
}
```

# CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createharmonicatomrestraint_function.htm

## CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint function

### Description

CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint creates an harmonic restraint on an atom. Similar
to CreateFixedAtomConstraint, but in this case the atom is allowed to move
somewhat during simulation. The force constant (kcal/mol/angstrom^2) and the
restraint type (Absolute or BestFit) can be supplied.

### Applies to

The CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint function

#### Instance

my $harmonicatomrestraintObject = $object->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint( <arrayofatoms>, [forceconstant], [harmonicrestrainttype] );

my $harmonicatomrestraintObject = $object->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint( { ArrayOfAtoms => <arrayofatoms>, ForceConstant => [forceconstant], HarmonicRestraintType => [harmonicrestrainttype] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $harmonicatomrestraintObject | | | Mdm::HarmonicAtomRestraint |
| <arrayofatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| [forceconstant] | Optional | 1.0 | Real |
| [harmonicrestrainttype] | Optional | Absolute | enum Mdm::HarmonicRestraintType |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Fix the backbone
my $backbone = FilterByString( $document, ':CA,C,N,O,HN,HA' );
$document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($backbone);

# Restrain beta carbon atoms
my $cbeta = FilterByString( $document, ':CB' );
$document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint( $cbeta, 10, Mdm::BestFit );

# Add cross-strand distance restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "THR2:CA" );
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "ILE34:CA" );
$document->CreateDistanceRestraint(
{
ArrayOfAtoms1 => $atom1,
ArrayOfAtoms2 => $atom2,
RMin => 2,
RMax => 5,
RMinForceConstant => 10,
RMaxForceConstant => 20,
ForceMaximum => 20
}
);

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
$document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);

# Print the total number of restraints (4)
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
print "There are ", $constraints->Count, " constraints\n";
```

# CreateHeatMap function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createheatmap_function.htm

## CreateHeatMap function

### Description

CreateHeatMap creates a heat map from the Data Table View.
The following arguments are available:

* MdmDocument specifies the Mdm::Document whose data will be plotted.

* DataTableTabName specifies the tab whose data will be plotted.

* XAxisProperties specifies a comma separated list of column names to plot against the X-axis.

* YAxisProperty is the name of the column to use as the Y-axis.

### Applies to

The CreateHeatMap function can be used with the following objects:

Chart::Document

### Using the CreateHeatMap function

#### Static

my $documentObject = Chart::Document::CreateHeatMap( <mdmdocument>, <datatabletabname>, <xaxisproperties>, <yaxisproperty> );

my $documentObject = Chart::Document::CreateHeatMap( { MdmDocument => <mdmdocument>, DataTableTabName => <datatabletabname>, XAxisProperties => <xaxisproperties>, YAxisProperty => <yaxisproperty> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | Chart::Document |
| <datatabletabname> | Required | | String |
| <mdmdocument> | Required | | Mdm::Document |
| <xaxisproperties> | Required | | String |
| <yaxisproperty> | Required | | String |

#### Defined by

ChartDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to create a heat map (client only).
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ChartDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

my $heatMap = Chart::Document::CreateHeatMap(
{
MdmDocument => $mdmDocument,
DataTableTabName => 'Atom',
XAxisProperties => 'Partial Charge',
YAxisProperty => 'Isotropic Displacement'
}
);

print "Model Type: Chart2dModelType\n"
if ( $heatMap->ModelType == Chart2dModelType );

$heatMap->UpdateViews();
```

### Using the CreateHotSpotsLabels command

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

#### Defined by

# CreateHydrogenBondMonitor function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createhydrogenbondmonitor_function.htm

## CreateHydrogenBondMonitor function

### Description

CreateHydrogenBondMonitor creates a monitor to track hydrogen bonds
for a collection of atoms. A hydrogen bond monitor displays
hydrogen bonds between donor and acceptor atom pairs. Two arguments modify
this monitor's behavior. SelectionScope specifies whether hydrogen bonds
internal, external, or both internal and external to the selection are tracked.
MolecularScope specifies whether intermolecular, intramolecular, or both
inter- and intramolecular hydrogen bonds are tracked. When called from a
Cell, Chain, Molecule, or Residue object, the monitored atom collection
consists of all the constituent atoms. When called from an Mdm::Document,
the monitored atom collection must be explicitly defined.

### Applies to

The CreateHydrogenBondMonitor function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid , Mdm::AminoAcidChain , Mdm::Cell , Mdm::Chain , Mdm::Document , Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::NucleicAcidChain , Mdm::Nucleotide , Mdm::Offlineable , Mdm::Residue

### Using the CreateHydrogenBondMonitor function

#### Instance

my $hydrogenbondmonitorObject = $object->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( <arrayofmonitoredatoms>, [selectionscope], [molecularscope] );

my $hydrogenbondmonitorObject = $object->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( [molecularscope] );

my $hydrogenbondmonitorObject = $object->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( { ArrayOfMonitoredAtoms => <arrayofmonitoredatoms>, SelectionScope => [selectionscope], MolecularScope => [molecularscope] } );

my $hydrogenbondmonitorObject = $object->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( { MolecularScope => [molecularscope] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $hydrogenbondmonitorObject | | | Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor |
| <arrayofmonitoredatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| [molecularscope] | Optional | allMolecularInteractions | enum Mdm::MolecularScope |
| [selectionscope] | Optional | allAtomHydrogenBonds | enum Mdm::SelectionScope |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how use the hydrogen bond monitor and to change the distance cutoff.

use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Creates a hbond monitor between ligand atoms and receptor
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $LigName = $ligands->Item(0)->Name;
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $monitor = $document->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( $ligandAtoms,
Mdm::allAtomHydrogenBonds, Mdm::allMolecularHydrogenBonds );

# Shows the label for each of the hbonds
$monitor->IsLabelShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll(); 

printf "Default distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->DefaultDistanceCriterion;
printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor.\n\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $newHBDist = 3.0;
$monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared( $newHBDist* $newHBDist );

# update view to ensure the correct HB count
$document->UpdateViews();
printf "Set the distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared;

printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor:\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $hbonds = $document->HydrogenBonds;
my $count = $hbonds->Count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $hbond = $hbonds->Item($index);
my $dist = $hbond->Distance;
my $atom1 = $hbond->Atom1;
my $atom2 = $hbond->Atom2;
my $res = $atom1->Parent;

if ( $res->Name eq $LigName ) {
$atom2->Parent->Select; 
}
else{
$atom1->Parent->Select; 
}
printf "%d) Distance: %.3f A H-bond between Atom %s:%s:%s and Atom %s:%s:%s\n",
$index+1, $dist,
$atom1->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom1->Parent->Name, $atom1->Name,
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name ;
} 

$document->FitView(); 
my $display_style = { DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' };
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle($display_style);
$document->DeselectAll();
```

### Applies to

Mdm::Isosurface

### Using the CreateIsosurface function

#### Instance

my $isosurfaceObject = $object->CreateIsosurface( <isovalue> );

my $isosurfaceObject = $object->CreateIsosurface( { Isovalue => <isovalue> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $isosurfaceObject | | | Mdm::Isosurface |
| <isovalue> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Isosurface |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
print "It operates on a document with grid data\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a structure with grid data\n";
print
" (for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
print " 3 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Connect to an Sdm::Document from the last active sequence window
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

# Get array with all isosurfaces using Isosurfaces filter
my $isosurfaces = $document->Isosurfaces;

if ( $isosurfaces->Count == 0 )
{
print "To run this script, please open a structure with grid data.\n";
print "(for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
exit;
}

# Get the first isosurface
my $isosurface = $isosurfaces->[0];

# Create a new isosurface at 0.5 isovalue
my $newContour = $isosurface->CreateIsosurface(0.5);
$newContour->ContextAtomArray( $document->Atoms );

if ( !$newContour->IsContextAtomArrayDefined() )
{
print "Please define a context atom array\n";
}
$newContour->IsNormalFlipped(False);
$newContour->IsBoundaryDrawn(True);
print "The line width is: $newContour->{LineWidth}\n";

# Print the isovalues
$isosurfaces = $document->Isosurfaces;
foreach my $surface (@$isosurfaces)
{
print $surface->Name . " has isovalue " . $surface->Isovalue . "\n";
}

# Array with available display styles
my @displayStyles = (
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleNone, Mdm::isosurfaceStyleQuadMesh,
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleSolid, Mdm::isosurfaceStyleTriMesh,
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleVolume
);

# Iterate over the available display styles
print "\nIterating over isosurface display styles:\n";
foreach my $displayStyle (@displayStyles)
{
sleep(1);
$newContour->DisplayStyle = $displayStyle;
print "$displayStyle\n";
$document->UpdateViews();
}

$newContour->RemoveContextAtomArray();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to tile the Molecule Window.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);

# Create SMILES for several small molecules.
my %molecules = (
'benzene' => 'C1=CC=CC=C1',
'aspirin' => 'C(=O)(O)c1ccccc1OC(=O)C',
'acetaminophen' => 'O=C(O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1',
'dioxin' => 'ClC1=CC2=C(C=C1Cl)OC3=C(C=C(C(=C3)Cl)Cl)O2'
);
while ( my ( $name, $smiles ) = each(%molecules) )
{
$document->InsertFromSmiles($smiles);

my $index = $document->Molecules->Count - 1;
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item($index);
$molecule->Name = $name;
my $labelObject = $molecule->CreateLabel($name);
}

$document->AddHydrogenAtoms();
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);

print "Displaying all molecules in the original layout...\n";
sleep(3);

print "Displaying all molecules after TileMolecules...\n";
$document->TileMolecules();
sleep(3);

print "Displaying all molecules after UntileMolecules...\n";
$document->UntileMolecules();
```

# CreateLigandNonbondMonitor function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createligandnonbondmonitor_function.htm

## CreateLigandNonbondMonitor function

### Description

CreateLigandNonbondMonitor creates an Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor object to track non-bond
interaction between the current LigandInFocus and ReceptorInFocus .
See Mdm::NonbondMonitor .

A non-bond monitor displays interactions between pairs of atoms
(e.g., steric bump, hydrogen bond) or groups (e.g., pi-orbital interaction).
See Mdm::NonbondMonitor and Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor .

This function has three (3) optional arguments:

* IsMonitoringIntraligandNonbonds is a Boolean datatype that specifies
whether interactions within the ligand are to be included.
This option is True by default to display supporting interactions.

* RequirePredefinedLigand is a Boolean datatype specifying whether
the LigandInFocus should be defined prior to calling
this function. This option is True by default.

* AddHydrogens is a Boolean datatype. If set to True, hydrogen
atoms will be added. This option is True by default.

### Applies to

The CreateLigandNonbondMonitor function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateLigandNonbondMonitor function

#### Instance

my $ligandnonbondmonitorObject = $object->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor( [ismonitoringintraligandnonbonds], [requirepredefinedligand], [addhydrogens] );

my $ligandnonbondmonitorObject = $object->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor( { IsMonitoringIntraligandNonbonds => [ismonitoringintraligandnonbonds], RequirePredefinedLigand => [requirepredefinedligand], AddHydrogens => [addhydrogens] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $ligandnonbondmonitorObject | | | Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor |
| [addhydrogens] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [ismonitoringintraligandnonbonds] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [requirepredefinedligand] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the create a ligand non-bond monitor, 
# browse ligands and show supporting non-bond interactions. 

use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('2FL6');
die "Failed to create a valid MDM document!" unless $document;

my $receptor = $document->ReceptorInFocus;
die "The open document does not have a defined receptor!" unless $receptor;

$document->FocusOnFirstLigand;
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
die "The open document does not have a defined ligand!" unless $ligand;

my $ligandNonbondMonitor =
$document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();
$document->UpdateViews();

my $nonbondMonitors = $document->NonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d NonbondMonitors.\n", $nonbondMonitors->Count;
my $ligandNonbondMonitors = $document->LigandNonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d LigandNonbondMonitors.\n", $ligandNonbondMonitors->Count;

# Step through the ligands
while ($document->FocusOnNextLigand())
{
sleep(2);
}

# Step through the ligands backwards
$document->FocusOnLastLigand();
while ($document->FocusOnPreviousLigand())
{
sleep(2);
}

# Expand shell to progressively view supporting interactions.
$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

# Contract shell to hide supporting interactions.
$ligandNonbondMonitor->ContractShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

print "Done\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the ligand non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );
die "Failed to create a valid MDM document!" unless $document;

print "To create a ligand interaction monitor, first ensure the ligand ";
print "is defined. \n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand;
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
die "Failed to identify a ligand! Try setting the ligand manually\n" .
"using the LigandInFocus property." unless $ligand;
printf "Ligand: %s\n\n", $ligand->Name;

my $monitor = $document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();
die "The ligand and or receptor is not undefined!" unless $monitor;
$document->UpdateViews();

my $monitors = $document->LigandNonbondMonitors();
printf "Document contains %d LigandNonbondMonitors.\n", $monitors->Count;

# Ligand non-bond monitors are also NonbondMonitor.
$monitors = $document->NonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d NonbondMonitors.\n", $monitors->Count;
print "\n";

# Analyze the identified interactions.
my $nonbonds = $monitor->Nonbonds;
my $count = $nonbonds->Count;
my $favorableNonbonds = $monitor->FavorableNonbonds;
my $favorableCount = $favorableNonbonds->Count;
my $unfavorableCount = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds->Count;
printf "Found %d non-bond interactions (total):\n", $count;
printf " %d of these are favorable interactions (such as H-bonds)\n",
$favorableCount;
printf " %d of these are unfavorable interactions (such as bumps).\n",
$unfavorableCount;
print "\n";

print "Analyze first non-bond interaction:\n";
my $nonbond = $nonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n",
$nonbond->Distance;
print "\n";

my $unfavorableNonbonds = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds;
if ($unfavorableNonbonds->Count > 0) 
{
print "Analyze first unfavorable non-bond interaction:\n";
my $unfavorableNonbond = $unfavorableNonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $unfavorableNonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $unfavorableNonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n",
$unfavorableNonbond->Distance;
print "\n";
}

print "All non-bonds of a particular type can be retrieved ";
print "using the NonbondsOfType filter.\n";
my $hBonds = $monitor->NonbondsOfType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType);
printf "Found %d hydrogen bonds using NonbondOfType filter.\n\n", $hBonds->Count;

print "Alternatively the IsMatchingNonbondType property can be used to \n";
print "identify interactions of a various type. The following atom pairs \n";
print "indicate classical hydrogen bonding: \n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
if ($nonbond->IsMatchingNonbondType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType))
{
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);

print '* ' . $atom1->FullName . " (";
print 'donor ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrogenDonor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHalogen);
print 'positive ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPositive);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ') and ';

print $atom2->FullName . " (";
print 'acceptor ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrogenAcceptor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHalogen);
print 'negative ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsNegative);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ")\n";
}
}
print "\n";

print "The NonbondTypes property can be used to identify all \n";
print "interaction types of a non-bond.\n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
printf "- %s (%s) and %s (%s):", 
$nonbond->FromSite->Name,
$nonbond->FromSite->ChemistryName,
$nonbond->ToSite->Name,
$nonbond->ToSite->ChemistryName;

my $nonbondTypes = $nonbond->NonbondTypes;
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
print " $type";
}

print "\n";
}
print "\n";

print "The properties NonbondCriterion and DefaultNonbondCriterion are \n";
print "access the parameters used to identify non-bonds (see the \n";
print "documentation for full description of criteria):\n";
my $allCriteria = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllNonbondCriterionTypes();
foreach my $criterionType (@$allCriteria)
{
printf "Mdm::%s:\t %6.2f (default: %6.2f) \n",
$criterionType,
$monitor->NonbondCriterion($criterionType),
$monitor->DefaultNonbondCriterion($criterionType);
}
print "\n";

# Changing an interaction criterion.
my $maxHBond = 1.0 + $monitor->NonbondCriterion(
Mdm::hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum);
printf "After increasing the classical hydrogen bond distance to %f A, \n",
$maxHBond;
$monitor->NonbondCriterion(
Mdm::hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum) = $maxHBond;
$document->UpdateObjects;
printf "the number of non-bond interactions increases to %d.\n",
$monitor->Nonbonds->Count;
print "\n";

print "Changes made to the non-bond criteria can be reset " .
"to the original defaults using ResetNonbondCriteria.\n";
$monitor->ResetNonbondCriteria();
print "\n";

print "The visibility of various non-bond types can be shown or hidden.\n";
print "This code demonstrates how to show only non-bond identifying \n";
print "classical hydrogen bond interactions with distance labels.\n";
$monitor->HideAllNonbonds();
$monitor->IsNonbondTypeShown(Mdm::conventionalHBondType) = True;
$monitor->IsLabelShown = True;
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

print "The default settings are to show all non-bond interactions \n";
print "(without distance labels). This is accomplished as follows.\n";
$monitor->ShowAllNonbonds({ ShowDistanceLabels=>False });
$document->UpdateViews();
print "\n";

print "The static AllNonbondTypes function can be loop through all";
print "the non-bond interaction types.\n";
my $allNonbondTypes = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllNonbondTypes();
foreach my $type (@$allNonbondTypes) {
printf "- %s \n", $type;
}
print "\n";

print "The static AllFavorableNonbondTypes function can be loop\n";
print "favorable non-bond interaction types.\n";
my $nonbondTypes = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllFavorableNonbondTypes();
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
printf "- %s \n", $type;
}
print "\n";

print "The static AllFavorableNonbondTypes function can be loop\n";
print "unfavorable non-bond interaction types.\n";
my $nonbondTypes = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllUnfavorableNonbondTypes();
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
printf "- %s \n", $type;
}
print "\n";
```

# CreateLocationFeature function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createlocationfeature_function.htm

## CreateLocationFeature function

### Description

CreateLocationFeature creates a location feature with the specified radius for
the specified atom or point feature. The radius argument is expressed in
angstroms.

### Applies to

The CreateLocationFeature function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the CreateLocationFeature function

#### Instance

my $locationfeatureObject = $object->CreateLocationFeature( <feature>, <radius> );

my $locationfeatureObject = $object->CreateLocationFeature( { Feature => <feature>, Radius => <radius> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $locationfeatureObject | | | Mdm::LocationFeature |
| <feature> | Required | | Mdm::Geometric3d |
| <radius> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create some features on the query
# Create a donor feature at 0,0,0
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create an acceptor feature at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

# create the location constraint. The $fitOperator and the parent operator of $acceptorOperator are the same in this case.
# Either can be used to create the location constraint.
my $locationfeatureHead =
$acceptorOperator->GetParentOperator()
->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Check to see if a proper query has been made and print out some information
if ( $fitOperator->HasChildOperators() )
{
print "Query successfully made, fit operator has child operators.\n";
my $headPoint = $newAcceptor->HeadXYZ;
my $tailPoint = $newAcceptor->TailXYZ;
printf "Head : %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n", $headPoint->X, $headPoint->Y,
$headPoint->Z;
printf "Tail : %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n", $tailPoint->X, $tailPoint->Y,
$tailPoint->Z;
print "Radius of location constraint on tail "
. $newAcceptor->TailFeature()->LocationSphereRadius . "\n";
}
$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# CreateMapping function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createmapping_function.htm

## CreateMapping function

### Description

CreateMapping creates a mapping between atoms, bonds, 3D point features, 3D vector features,
or 3D plane features which belong to different parts of a pharmacophore query.
The association is used to define the common substructure of matching and non-matching
substructures, and to identify 3D query features common to a list of substructures.

### Applies to

The CreateMapping function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateMapping function

#### Command

$object->CreateMapping();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');

$document->CreateAndTopology();

# The query bonds are automatically created using
# the CreateAndTopology function. However, to show
# how to create them using CreateBondQuery, we will delete
# them and then add them again.

my $querybonds = $document->QueryBonds;
foreach my $querybond (@$querybonds)
{
$querybond->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

my $bonds = $document->Bonds;
foreach my $bond (@$bonds)
{
my $querybond =
$document->QueryOperators()->Item(0)->CreateQueryBond($bond);
$querybond->AddBondType('queryAnyBond');
}

# removes the first query bond's bond type
$document->QueryBonds->Item(0)->RemoveBondType('queryAnyBond');
```

Source type: HTML

## CreateMembrane function

### Description

CreateMembrane creates a new Mdm::Membrane object.
There are several parameters:

* Center is the center position of the membrane.

* Normal is a vector point along the normal axis.

* Thickness is the depth of the membrane in angstroms.

* SurfaceLength is the displayed membrane length.

* SurfaceWidth is the displayed membrane width.

### Applies to

The CreateMembrane function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateMembrane function

#### Instance

my $membraneObject = $object->CreateMembrane( <center>, <normal>, <thickness>, [surfacelength], [surfacewidth] );

my $membraneObject = $object->CreateMembrane( { Center => <center>, Normal => <normal>, Thickness => <thickness>, SurfaceLength => [surfacelength], SurfaceWidth => [surfacewidth] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $membraneObject | | | Mdm::Membrane |
| <center> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| <normal> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| <thickness> | Required | | Real |
| [surfacelength] | Optional | 40.0 | Real |
| [surfacewidth] | Optional | 40.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrate how to create a membrane.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

# Remove all chains except the first.
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# "Guess" some value for the membrane position.
my $center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, -3.2 );
my $normal = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.521, 0.106, 0.847 );
my $membrane =
$document->CreateMembrane( $center, $normal, 60.0, 60.0, 30.0 );

# Pick a different color scheme from default.
$membrane->CytosolColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 255 ) ); # cyan
$membrane->ExtracellularColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 255, 255, 0 ) ); # yellow
$document->SetParent( $molecule, $membrane );
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

# Change some membrane properties.
$center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, 3.2 );
$normal = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.521, -0.106, -0.847 );

$membrane->Thickness = 35;
$membrane->Normal = $normal;
$membrane->Center = $center;
```

## CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor function

### Description

CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor creates a new Mdm::MembraneOrientationMonitor object that tracks the relative orientation of the specified Mdm::Membrane and the principal
axis of a specified set of atoms.
There are several parameters available:

* Membrane is the membrane to monitor.

* ArrayOfAtoms specifies the set of protein atoms used as reference for the membrane orientation.

* Location specifies where the membrane orientation monitor should be displayed.

* ReferenceAxis specifies which principal axis of the set of atoms is used to measure the membrane orientation.

### Applies to

The CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor function

#### Instance

my $membraneorientationmonitorObject = $object->CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor( <membrane>, <arrayofatoms>, <location>, <referenceaxis> );

##### Parameters

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $membraneorientationmonitorObject | | | Mdm::MembraneOrientationMonitor |
| <arrayofatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| <location> | Required | | enum Mdm::MembraneOrientationDisplayLocation |
| <membrane> | Required | | Mdm::Membrane |
| <referenceaxis> | Required | | enum Mdm::ReferenceAxis |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with membranes.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

# Remove all chains except the first.
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# "Guess" some value for the membrane position
my $center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, -3.2 );
my $normal = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.521, 0.106, 0.847 );

my $membrane =
$document->CreateMembrane( $center, $normal, 60.0, 60.0, 30.0 );

# Pick a different color scheme from default
$membrane->CytosolColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 255 ) );
$membrane->ExtracellularColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 255, 255, 0 ) );

$document->SetParent( $molecule, $membrane );

my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms();

my $membraneOrientation =
$molecule->CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor( $membrane, $atoms,
Mdm::objectCentered, Mdm::referenceAxisZ );
my $shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
my $tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
my $rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);

$document->UpdateViews();

sleep(4);

$center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, 3.2 );
$normal = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.521, -0.106, -0.847 );

$membrane->Thickness = 35;
$membrane->Normal = $normal;
$membrane->Center = $center;
$document->UpdateObjects();

$shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
$tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
$rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);
```

# CreateMolecule function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createmolecule_function.htm

## CreateMolecule function

### Description

CreateMolecule creates an empty molecule.

### Applies to

The CreateMolecule function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Cell , Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateMolecule function

#### Instance

my $moleculeObject = $object->CreateMolecule();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $moleculeObject | | | Mdm::Molecule |
| $object | | | Mdm::Cell Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

```text
# Create protein sequence documents.

Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument(SdmAlignmentModelType);

$sdmProteinDocument->Type;

# Create amino acid sequence objects.

$sdmProteinDocument->CreateSequence( 'Sequence1', 'qreqytweqtetwq' );
my $sequence2 =
$sdmProteinDocument->CreateAASequence( 'Sequence2', 'ASDFDSFASFA' );

$sequence1->Type;

$sequence2->Type;

Sdm::Document::CreateNucleotideDocument(SdmAnnotationModelType);

$sdmNucleotideDocument->Type;

# Edit and create nucleotide sequence object.

$dnaSequence1->InsetSequenceString( 0, 'CAGTU' );

$sdmNucleotideDocument->CreateNASequence( 'Sequence2', 'CAGTU' );
```

### Applies to

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateNeighborMonitor function

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script shows how to create a neighbor monitor.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Creates a neighbor monitor near ligand atoms.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;

my $neighborMonitor = $document->CreateNeighborMonitor( $ligandAtoms, 3 );
$neighborMonitor->IsLabelShown(True);
$neighborMonitor->IsIntermolecularOnlyShown(False);

my $neighbors = $neighborMonitor->Neighbors;
my $count = $neighbors->Count;

print "Found $count atoms within "
. $neighborMonitor->NeighborRadius
. " angstroms of ligand.\n";

my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $count )
{
my $bump = $neighbors->Item($index);
my $atom2 = $bump->Atom2;
printf "\t%4d %s:%s:%s \n", ++$index,
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name;
}
```

# CreateNonbondMonitor function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createnonbondmonitor_function.htm

## CreateNonbondMonitor function

### Description

CreateNonbondMonitor creates a monitor to track non-bond interactions
for a user-defined collection of atoms.
A non-bond monitor displays interactions between pairs of atoms
(e.g., hydrogen bond, bump) or groups of atoms (e.g., Pi-orbital interaction).
There are several parameters available:

* ArrayOfMonitoredAtoms specifies the set of atoms to monitor for interactions.

* MonitoredPairScope specifies MonitoredPairScope property.

* MolecularScope specifies MolecularScope property.

* MonitoredNonbondTypes is an array of enum Mdm::NonbondType that specifies which non-bond interaction types are monitored. All types are monitored if this is not defined.

* IsUnsatisfiedCalculated specifies unsatisfied classical hydrogen bonds and charge interaction are identified if possible. See the Non bond Interactions topic in help.

### Applies to

The CreateNonbondMonitor function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateNonbondMonitor function

#### Instance

my $nonbondmonitorObject = $object->CreateNonbondMonitor( <arrayofmonitoredatoms>, [monitoredpairscope], [molecularscope], [monitorednonbondtypes], [isunsatisfiedcalculated] );

my $nonbondmonitorObject = $object->CreateNonbondMonitor( { ArrayOfMonitoredAtoms => <arrayofmonitoredatoms>, MonitoredPairScope => [monitoredpairscope], MolecularScope => [molecularscope], MonitoredNonbondTypes => [monitorednonbondtypes], IsUnsatisfiedCalculated => [isunsatisfiedcalculated] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $nonbondmonitorObject | | | Mdm::NonbondMonitor |
| <arrayofmonitoredatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| [isunsatisfiedcalculated] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [molecularscope] | Optional | allMolecularInteractions | enum Mdm::MolecularScope |
| [monitorednonbondtypes] | Optional | | DiscoveryScript::StringArray |
| [monitoredpairscope] | Optional | allInteractions | enum Mdm::MonitoredPairScope |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to create non-bond monitors.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3fzm');
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;
$document->Zoom(20);
$document->IsHierarchyViewShown = True;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "Create a monitor for all non-bond interactions.\n";
my $allAtoms = $document->Atoms;
my $nonbondMonitor = 
$document->CreateNonbondMonitor($allAtoms);
$nonbondMonitor->Name = 'Monitor All Nonbonds';

$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(1);
$nonbondMonitor->IsVisible = False;
$document->UpdateViews();

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "Create a monitor for unfavorable interactions only.\n";
my $unfavorableTypes = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::NonbondTypesByCategory(
Mdm::allUnfavorableNonbondTypes);

my $unfavorableMonitor = $document->CreateNonbondMonitor({
ArrayOfMonitoredAtoms => $document->Atoms,
MonitoredNonbondTypes => $unfavorableTypes,
IsUnsatisfiedCalculated=> False});
$unfavorableMonitor->Name = 'Monitor Unfavorable';

$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(1);
$unfavorableMonitor->IsVisible = False;
$document->UpdateViews();

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "Create a custom monitor for specific interaction types only.\n";
my $nonbondTypes = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$nonbondTypes->AddItem(Mdm::saltBridgeType);
$nonbondTypes->AddItem(Mdm::unfavorableVdwBumpType);

my $customMonitor = $document->CreateNonbondMonitor({
ArrayOfMonitoredAtoms => $document->Atoms,
MonitoredNonbondTypes => $nonbondTypes,
IsUnsatisfiedCalculated=> False});
$customMonitor->Name = 'Monitor Custom';
$document->UpdateViews();
```

```text
#! /usr/bin/perl -w
#
# File: NonbondsForSuperimposedMolecules.pl
#
# Function: creates a monitor for each molecule, only monitoring within it.
# This is useful if you wish to examine interactions for a set
# of superimposed structures.
#_____________________________________________________________________________

use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $msg = "This script creates nonbond monitor for each visible molecule discretely.\n";

# Get the molecule window
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

if ( ! defined($document) ) { 
$document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );
}

# Ensure all view updates turned off so action appears atomic
$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);

my $molecules = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $allMolecules = $document->Molecules;
foreach my $molecule(@$allMolecules)
{
if($molecule->IsVisible()) {
$molecules->AddItem($molecule);
}
}

die "$msg\n No charged atoms found in molecule window.\n" unless $molecules->Count > 0;
foreach my $molecule (@$molecules)
{
my $atoms=$molecule->Atoms;
#this will monitor all interactions within each molecule. So we will get 
#any interactions between chains of a molecule, but not interactions between
#the different molecules.
my $NBMonitor=$document->CreateNonbondMonitor($atoms,Mdm::interactionsWithinMonitoredScope,Mdm::allMolecularInteractions);
$NBMonitor->Name = "Non-bond Monitor for ".$molecule->Name;
print "Created monitor ". $NBMonitor->Name . "\n";

# Analyze the identified interactions.
my $nonbonds = $NBMonitor->Nonbonds;
my $count = $nonbonds->Count;
my $favorableNonbonds = $NBMonitor->FavorableNonbonds;
my $favorableCount = $favorableNonbonds->Count;
my $unfavorableCount = $NBMonitor->UnfavorableNonbonds->Count;
printf "Found %d non-bond interactions (total):\n", $count;
printf " %d of these are favorable interactions (such as H-bonds)\n",$favorableCount;
printf " %d of these are unfavorable interactions (such as bumps).\n",$unfavorableCount; 
}

END {
# Turn view updates back on
$document and $document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
$document and $document->UpdateViews();
}
```

# CreateNucleicAcid function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createnucleicacid_function.htm

## CreateNucleicAcid function

### Description

CreateNucleicAcid creates a nucleic acid molecule having the specified
sequence of nucleotide residues identified by their 1-letter symbols.
While the sequence must consist of standard nucleotides, the MutateNucleotide can be used to mutate nucleotides to
supported nonstandard types ( enum Mdm::ResidueType ).
The following arguments are available:

* Sequence specifies the nucleic acid sequence using their 1-letter symbols.

* NucleicAcidType specifies the enum Mdm::NucleicAcidChainType to create.

* ConformationType specifies the enum Mdm::NucleicAcidConformationType .

The following table lists the standard nucleotides and their 1-letter symbol.

| Nucleotide | Symbol |
| --- | --- |
| Adenosine | A |
| Guanosine | G |
| Thymidine | T |
| Cytosine | C |
| Uridine | U |

### Applies to

The CreateNucleicAcid function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateNucleicAcid function

#### Instance

my $moleculeObject = $object->CreateNucleicAcid( <sequence>, [nucleicacidtype], [conformationtype] );

my $moleculeObject = $object->CreateNucleicAcid( { Sequence => <sequence>, NucleicAcidType => [nucleicacidtype], ConformationType => [conformationtype] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $moleculeObject | | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <sequence> | Required | | String |
| [conformationtype] | Optional | Mdm::aHelix | enum Mdm::NucleicAcidConformationType |
| [nucleicacidtype] | Optional | Mdm::dnaDuplex | enum Mdm::NucleicAcidChainType |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to build nucleic acids.
use strict;
use NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create and append to a DNA duplex molecule.
my $naType = Mdm::dnaDuplex;
my $nucleicAcidMolecule =
$document->CreateNucleicAcid( "CGT", $naType, Mdm::aHelix );
my $senseChain1 = $nucleicAcidMolecule->Chains->Item(0);
my $na3Prime = $senseChain1->NucleotideAt3PrimeTerminus;
$na3Prime = $document->GrowNucleicAcid( $na3Prime, "GGG", Mdm::aHelix );

printf "Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$document->ModelName,
$document->Atoms->Count();

# Create and prepend to a second DNA duplex molecule.
my $nucleicAcid2 =
$document->CreateNucleicAcid( "ACT", $naType, Mdm::aHelix );
my $senseChain2 = $nucleicAcid2->Chains->Item(0);
my $na5Prime = $senseChain2->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus;
$na5Prime = $document->GrowNucleicAcid( $na5Prime, "AAA", Mdm::aHelix );

my $secondMoleculeName = "Nucleic Acid 2";
$nucleicAcid2->Name = $secondMoleculeName;

# Ligate the two molecules using the sense strand.
$document->DeselectAll();
$na3Prime->Select;
$na5Prime->Select;
$document->LigateNucleotides( $na3Prime, $na5Prime );

# Mutate first sense nucleotide to thymidine.
$document->DeselectAll();
$senseChain1->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus->Select;
$document->MutateNucleotide( $senseChain1->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus,
Mdm::thymidine );

# Change the nucleic acid display style.
$senseChain1->DisplayStyle = Mdm::styleDnaArrowLadder;
$nucleicAcidMolecule->Chains->Item(1)->DisplayStyle =
Mdm::styleDnaArrowLadder;

printf "Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$document->ModelName,
$document->Atoms->Count();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w

my $sequence2 =

$sdmNucleotideDocument->CreateNASequence( 'Sequence2', 'CAGTU' );

$dnaSequence1->Type;
```

# CreatePiCationMonitor function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createpicationmonitor_function.htm

## CreatePiCationMonitor function

### Description

CreatePiCationMonitor creates a monitor for a collection of atoms to track interactions
between cations and rings consisting of conjugated pi bonds.

If an array of atoms is specified, then all interactions between these atoms
and the rest of the system are monitored. If no array is specified, then
interactions for all atoms are monitored.

### Applies to

The CreatePiCationMonitor function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid , Mdm::AminoAcidChain , Mdm::Chain , Mdm::Document , Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::NucleicAcidChain , Mdm::Nucleotide , Mdm::Offlineable , Mdm::Residue

### Using the CreatePiCationMonitor function

#### Instance

my $picationmonitorObject = $object->CreatePiCationMonitor( [arrayofobjects] );

my $picationmonitorObject = $object->CreatePiCationMonitor( { ArrayOfObjects => [arrayofobjects] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $picationmonitorObject | | | Mdm::PiCationMonitor |
| [arrayofobjects] | Optional | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script shows how to create pi interaction monitors.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1kim.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Creates pi interaction monitors
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

#if no array of atoms is passed in then the monitor is created
#for the whole molecule (or other object).
my $pipiMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor();
my $piCationMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiCationMonitor();
my $piSigmaMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiSigmaMonitor();

$pipiMonitor->Name = "Pi-Pi";
$piCationMonitor->Name = "Pi-Cation";
$piSigmaMonitor->Name = "Pi-Sigma";

my $piPiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piPiInteractionCount = $piPiInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piPiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

# Change criteria settings to non-default values.
$piCationMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piCationMonitor->MinimumAngle = 60.0;
my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule\n";

$piSigmaMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->MinimumAngle = 30.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->AngleDeviation = 15.0;
my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

$pipiMonitor->MaximumCenterDistance = 7.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumClosestAtomDistance = 4.0;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumLambda = 20.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumTheta = 45.;
my $pipiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount = $pipiInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $pipiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piInteractions = $molecule->PiInteractionMonitors();
my $piCount = $piInteractions->Count();
print "\nThere are " . $piCount . " pi interaction monitors: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $piCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $piInteractions->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Interactions") );
}

#If we want to limit the scope of the monitoring, we can pass in
#an array of atoms. This is similar to creating a monitor from the UI
# when atoms are selected. Pi interactions will then be calculated within
#these, and between these and the parent object
my $residue = FilterByString( $document, "THM1" )->Item(0);
my $atom_array = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $atoms = $residue->Atoms();
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atoms->Count() ; ++$index )
{
$atom_array->AddItem( $atoms->Item($index) );
}
my $pipiMonitor2 = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor($atom_array);
my $pipiInteractions2 = $pipiMonitor2->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount2 = $pipiInteractions2->Count();
print "Number of pi-pi interactions between "
. $residue->Name()
. " and the rest of the molecule: "
. $pipiInteractionCount2 . "\n";

my $picatmonitors = $document->PiCationMonitors;
print "Number of pi-cation monitors: ". $picatmonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pipimonitors = $document->PiPiMonitors;
print "Number of pi-pi monitors: ". $pipimonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pisigmonitors = $document->PiSigmaMonitors;
print "Number of pi-sigma monitors: ". $pisigmonitors->Count . "\n";
```

```text
my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

# Change criteria settings to non-default values.
$piCationMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piCationMonitor->MinimumAngle = 60.0;
my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule\n";

$piSigmaMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->MinimumAngle = 30.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->AngleDeviation = 15.0;
my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

$pipiMonitor->MaximumCenterDistance = 7.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumClosestAtomDistance = 4.0;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumLambda = 20.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumTheta = 45.;
my $pipiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount = $pipiInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $pipiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piInteractions = $molecule->PiInteractionMonitors();
my $piCount = $piInteractions->Count();
print "\nThere are " . $piCount . " pi interaction monitors: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $piCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $piInteractions->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Interactions") );
}

#If we want to limit the scope of the monitoring, we can pass in
#an array of atoms. This is similar to creating a monitor from the UI
# when atoms are selected. Pi interactions will then be calculated within
#these, and between these and the parent object
my $residue = FilterByString( $document, "THM1" )->Item(0);
my $atom_array = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $atoms = $residue->Atoms();
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atoms->Count() ; ++$index )
{
$atom_array->AddItem( $atoms->Item($index) );
}
my $pipiMonitor2 = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor($atom_array);
my $pipiInteractions2 = $pipiMonitor2->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount2 = $pipiInteractions2->Count();
print "Number of pi-pi interactions between "
. $residue->Name()
. " and the rest of the molecule: "
. $pipiInteractionCount2 . "\n";

my $picatmonitors = $document->PiCationMonitors;
print "Number of pi-cation monitors: ". $picatmonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pipimonitors = $document->PiPiMonitors;
print "Number of pi-pi monitors: ". $pipimonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pisigmonitors = $document->PiSigmaMonitors;
print "Number of pi-sigma monitors: ". $pisigmonitors->Count . "\n";
```
