# CreatePiSigmaMonitor function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createpisigmamonitor_function.htm

## CreatePiSigmaMonitor function

### Description

CreatePiSigmaMonitor creates a monitor for a collection of atoms to track
interactions between sigma bonds and rings consisting of conjugated pi bonds.

If an array of atoms is specified, then all interactions between these atoms
and the rest of the system are monitored. If no array is specified, then
interactions for all atoms are monitored.

### Applies to

The CreatePiSigmaMonitor function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid , Mdm::AminoAcidChain , Mdm::Chain , Mdm::Document , Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::NucleicAcidChain , Mdm::Nucleotide , Mdm::Offlineable , Mdm::Residue

### Using the CreatePiSigmaMonitor function

#### Instance

my $pisigmamonitorObject = $object->CreatePiSigmaMonitor( [arrayofobjects] );

my $pisigmamonitorObject = $object->CreatePiSigmaMonitor( { ArrayOfObjects => [arrayofobjects] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $pisigmamonitorObject | | | Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor |
| [arrayofobjects] | Optional | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

MdmDiscoveryScript

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreatePlaneMonitor function

#### Instance

my $planemonitorObject = $object->CreatePlaneMonitor( <arrayofobjects> );

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Show how to create an Mdm::NormalMonitor.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9INS.pdb" );

my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
my $aminoAcid2 = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
my $aminoAcid3 = $aminoAcids->Item(2);

my $collection = Mdm::Array::Create();
$collection->AddItem( $aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon );
$collection->AddItem( $aminoAcid2->AmideOxygen );
$collection->AddItem( $aminoAcid2->CAlpha );
$collection->AddItem( $aminoAcid3->AmideNitrogen );

my $planeMonitor = $document->CreatePlaneMonitor($collection);
my $normalMonitor =
$document->CreateNormalMonitor( $planeMonitor, $aminoAcid2->CAlpha );

my $xyz = $normalMonitor->AnnotationXYZ;
print "Annotation coordinate: $xyz->{X} \t $xyz->{Y} \t $xyz->{Z} \n";

my $normal = $normalMonitor->Normal;
print "Normal: $normal->{X} \t $normal->{Y} \t $normal->{Z} \n";

print "Normal length: $normalMonitor->{NormalLength}\n";

$document->UpdateViews;
```

### Description

argument must contain at least one atom.

The CreatePointFeature function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the CreatePointFeature function

#### Instance

my $pointfeatureObject = $object->CreatePointFeature( <arrayofatoms> );

my $pointfeatureObject = $object->CreatePointFeature( { ArrayOfAtoms => <arrayofatoms> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $pointfeatureObject | | | Mdm::PointFeature |
| <arrayofatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create a Hydrophobe
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -14, 6, 0 );

my $hydrophobeOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$hydrophobeOperator->Name('Hydrophobe');
my $hydrophobe = $hydrophobeOperator->CreatePointFeature( $document->Atoms );
$hydrophobe->Type() = 'hydrophobePointFeature';
$hydrophobe->CreateLabel('Hydrophobe');
my $hydrophobeColor = $hydrophobe->HydrophobeColor();
print "RGB of a Hydrophobic is: "
. $hydrophobeColor->Red . " "
. $hydrophobeColor->Green . " "
. $hydrophobeColor->Blue . "\n";

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();

# Create a Hydrophobe Aromatic
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -14, 4.5, 0 );

my $hydrophobeOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$hydrophobeOperator->Name('Hydrophobe Aromatic');
my $hydrophobe = $hydrophobeOperator->CreatePointFeature( $document->Atoms );
$hydrophobe->Type() = 'hydrophobeAromaticPointFeature';
$hydrophobe->CreateLabel('Hydrophobic Aromatic');
my $hydrophobeColor = $hydrophobe->HydrophobeAromaticColor();
print "RGB of a Hydrophobic Aromatic is: "
. $hydrophobeColor->Red . " "
. $hydrophobeColor->Green . " "
. $hydrophobeColor->Blue . "\n";

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();

# Create a Hydrophobe Aliphatic
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -14, 3, 0 );

my $hydrophobeOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$hydrophobeOperator->Name('Hydrophobe Aliphatic');
my $hydrophobe = $hydrophobeOperator->CreatePointFeature( $document->Atoms );
$hydrophobe->Type() = 'hydrophobeAliphaticPointFeature';
$hydrophobe->CreateLabel('Hydrophobic Aliphatic');
my $hydrophobeColor = $hydrophobe->HydrophobeAliphaticColor();
print "RGB of a Hydrophobic Aliphatic is: "
. $hydrophobeColor->Red . " "
. $hydrophobeColor->Green . " "
. $hydrophobeColor->Blue . "\n";

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# CreatePointPlot function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createpointplot_function.htm

## CreatePointPlot function

### Description

CreatePointPlot creates a point plot from the Data Table View.
The following arguments are available:

* MdmDocument specifies the Mdm::Document whose data will be plotted.

* DataTableTabName specifies the tab whose data will be plotted.

* XAxisProperty is the name of the column to use as the X-axis.

* YAxisProperties specifies a comma separated list of column names to plot against the Y-axis.

### Applies to

The CreatePointPlot function can be used with the following objects:

Chart::Document

### Using the CreatePointPlot function

#### Static

my $documentObject = Chart::Document::CreatePointPlot( <mdmdocument>, <datatabletabname>, <xaxisproperty>, <yaxisproperties>, [colorproperty], [fromselection] );

my $documentObject = Chart::Document::CreatePointPlot( { MdmDocument => <mdmdocument>, DataTableTabName => <datatabletabname>, XAxisProperty => <xaxisproperty>, YAxisProperties => <yaxisproperties>, ColorProperty => [colorproperty], FromSelection => [fromselection] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | Chart::Document |
| <datatabletabname> | Required | | String |
| <mdmdocument> | Required | | Mdm::Document |
| <xaxisproperty> | Required | | String |
| <yaxisproperties> | Required | | String |
| [colorproperty] | Optional | "" | String |
| [fromselection] | Optional | False | Boolean |

#### Defined by

ChartDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to create a point plot (client only).
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ChartDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

my $pointPlot = Chart::Document::CreatePointPlot(
{
MdmDocument => $mdmDocument,
DataTableTabName => 'Atom',
XAxisProperty => 'Partial Charge',
YAxisProperties => 'Isotropic Displacement,Occupancy'
}
);

print "Model Type: Chart2dModelType\n"
if ( $pointPlot->ModelType eq Chart2dModelType );

$pointPlot->AddTrendLine('Isotropic Displacement');
$pointPlot->UpdateViews();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to create a polydot object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $pointArray = Mdm::PointArray::Create();
my $colorArray = DiscoveryScript::ColorArray::Create();

# Generate 500 random points and colors.
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 500 ; ++$i )
{
my $randX = rand();
my $randY = rand();
my $randZ = rand();
my $randColor = Mdm::Color::Create(
int( $randX * 255 ),
int( $randY * 255 ),
int( $randZ * 255 )
);
my $newPt = Mdm::Point::Create( $randX, $randY, $randZ );
$pointArray->AddItem($newPt);
$colorArray->AddItem($randColor);
}

# Create a new polydot object from the point and color arrays.
$molecule->CreatePolydot(
{ ArrayOfDots => $pointArray, ArrayOfColors => $colorArray } );

# Find and name the polydot object.
my $polydotArray = $document->Polydots;
$polydotArray->Item(0)->Name('Point Cloud 1');
$document->FitView();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# CreateProteinDocument function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createproteindocument_function.htm

## CreateProteinDocument function

### Description

CreateProteinDocument creates a protein Sequence Data Model document.
The following arguments are supported:

* ModelType specifies the client views to open.

* NoDisplay specifies if the client view will not be displayed.

Valid ModelTypes include:

* SdmAlignmentModelType indicates the document will be viewed in the Sequence Window.

* SdmAnnotationModelType indicates the document will be viewed in the Sequence Annotation Window. A Sequence Window will also be opened.

### Applies to

The CreateProteinDocument function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the CreateProteinDocument function

#### Static

my $documentObject = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument( [modeltype], [nodisplay] );

my $documentObject = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument( { ModelType => [modeltype], NoDisplay => [nodisplay] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | Sdm::Document |
| [modeltype] | Optional | SequenceAlignmentModelType | String |
| [nodisplay] | Optional | False | Boolean |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrates how to create protein and nucleotide sequence documents.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

# Create protein sequence documents.
my $sdmProteinDocument =
Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument(SdmAlignmentModelType);
printf "CreateProteinDocument creates document of type %s\n",
$sdmProteinDocument->Type;

# Create amino acid sequence objects.
my $sequence1 =
$sdmProteinDocument->CreateSequence( 'Sequence1', 'qreqytweqtetwq' );
my $sequence2 =
$sdmProteinDocument->CreateAASequence( 'Sequence2', 'ASDFDSFASFA' );

printf
"On an amino acid document, CreateSequence creates sequence of type %s\n",
$sequence1->Type;
printf "CreateAASequence also creates sequence of type %s\n",
$sequence2->Type;

# Create nucleotide sequence documents and viewed in the Annotation Window.
my $sdmNucleotideDocument =
Sdm::Document::CreateNucleotideDocument(SdmAnnotationModelType);
printf "CreateNucleotideDocument creates document of type %s\n",
$sdmNucleotideDocument->Type;

# Edit and create nucleotide sequence object.
my $dnaSequence1 = $sdmNucleotideDocument->Sequence(0);
$dnaSequence1->InsetSequenceString( 0, 'CAGTU' );
my $dnaSequence2 =
$sdmNucleotideDocument->CreateNASequence( 'Sequence2', 'CAGTU' );

printf
"On a nucleic acid document, CreateSequence creates sequence of type %s\n",
$dnaSequence1->Type;
printf "CreateNASequence also creates sequence of type %s\n",
$dnaSequence2->Type;
```

# CreateProteinPose function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createproteinpose_function.htm

## CreateProteinPose function

### Description

CreateProteinPose creates a protein pose with the specified position,
translation, and rotation. The position and translation arguments are the
x, y, and z distances in angstroms and the rotation argument are the
Euler angles in degrees. (Note that the CreateProteinPose function is
designed to process data from the ZDock program and the numerical values
of the position, translation and rotation arguments are not easily generated
by other means).

### Applies to

The CreateProteinPose function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::DockedProteinPoseAssembly

### Using the CreateProteinPose function

#### Instance

my $proteinposeObject = $object->CreateProteinPose( <position>, <translation>, <rotation>, <cluster>, <clustercenter> );

my $proteinposeObject = $object->CreateProteinPose( { Position => <position>, Translation => <translation>, Rotation => <rotation>, Cluster => <cluster>, ClusterCenter => <clustercenter> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $proteinposeObject | | | Mdm::ProteinPose |
| <cluster> | Required | | Integer |
| <clustercenter> | Required | | Boolean |
| <position> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| <rotation> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| <translation> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| $object | | | Mdm::DockedProteinPoseAssembly |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates the use for scripting functions for the protein-protein
# docking area.
# NOTE: Most of the functions connected to generating the DockedPoseAssembly and
# DockedProtein objects are designed to process output from the Dock Proteins (ZDOCK)
# protocols, which generates a set of numbers describing the relative orientations
# of the two proteins in a docked protein complex. Those numbers are necessary to
# generate the objects described in the this example but cannot be easily
# generated by hand. The numerical values hard-coded to avoid having
# to load a Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) output file . The values used are derived
# from the output of a Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) run on two small proteins: chain A of 2ptn and
# chain I of 2sta.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document =
DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "2ptn.pdb" ); # receptor
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "2sta.pdb" ); # ligand

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
my $receptor = $molecules->Item(0);
my $ligand = $molecules->Item(1);

# Only keep ligand chain that was used in ZDOCK run
my $ligandChains = $ligand->Chains;
foreach my $chain (@$ligandChains)
{
if ( $chain->Name ne "I" )
{
$chain->Select();
}
}

# Only keep receptor chain that was used in ZDOCK run
my $receptorChains = $receptor->Chains;
foreach my $chain (@$receptorChains)
{
if ( $chain->Name ne "A" )
{
$chain->Select();
}
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# Label receptor and ligand with identifying tags
# These tags are used by other commands
$receptor->SetProperty( "COMPLEX_TYPE", "RECEPTOR" );
$ligand->SetProperty( "COMPLEX_TYPE", "LIGAND" );

# Define general properties of the structures in the complex
# Note that these numbers are part of the output generated by the
# ZDock protein docking program.
# All numerical values were taken from ZDock run output for this system
my $N = 84;
my $spacing = 1.2;
my $receptorCenter = Mdm::Point::Create( 2.5130, 7.5200, 23.7720 );
my $ligandCenter = Mdm::Point::Create( 14.5890, 21.1360, 40.4300 );
my $startingAngles = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 );

# Create the DockedProteinPoseAssembly object which contains
# information about the proteins in the docked complex that
# common to all poses
my $poseAssembly =
$document->CreateDockedProteinPoseAssembly( $ligand, $ligandCenter,
$receptor, $receptorCenter, $startingAngles );

# The next three commands are redundant with the constructor above
# and are only included as example of how they are used.
# However, they can be used to set the DockedProteinPoseAssembly
# properties to different values if desired
$poseAssembly->LigandCenter($ligandCenter);
$poseAssembly->ReceptorCenter($receptorCenter);
$poseAssembly->StartingAngles($startingAngles);

# Set the ZDock grid size and grid spacing
# These values are internally used by the ZDock program
# they are stored mainly to be able to produce input files
# for the Process Poses and Refine Docked Protein protocols
$poseAssembly->SetPropertyAsInteger( "N", $N );
$poseAssembly->SetPropertyAsReal( "spacing", $spacing );
$poseAssembly->HideProperty("N");
$poseAssembly->HideProperty("spacing");

$poseAssembly->SetProperty( "Center", "Receptor" );
$poseAssembly->Name = "Docked Poses";

# Generate the numeric data for the first docked pose
# All numerical values taken from pose 1 of ZDock run output
my $position = Mdm::Point::Create( -5.1821, 20.9576, 21.2807 );
my $translation = Mdm::Point::Create( 6.0000, -16.8000, 2.4000 );
my $rotation = Mdm::Point::Create( 120.0000, 171.0266, 111.9815 );
my $cluster = 1;
my $topClusterPose = 1;
my ( $receptorCenterX, $receptorCenterY, $receptorCenterZ ) =
( 0.018, 14.954, 22.56 );
my ( $ligandCenterX, $ligandCenterY, $ligandCenterZ ) =
( 12.464, 24.22, 40.03 );

# Generate a new pose. The parameters of the constructor function are
# the position of the spherical pose representation
# the translation of the ligand from the starting to the docked position
# the rotation of the ligand from the starting to the docked position
# the cluster the pose belongs to
# whether or not the pose is the best ranked pose in the cluster 
my $newPose =
$poseAssembly->CreateProteinPose( $position, $translation, $rotation,
$cluster, $topClusterPose );

# The following sets of number represent the coordinates center of the binding interface
# on the receptor and the ligand. The values are store as properties which are
# used to toggle between receptor and ligand centric views in the DS client
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_x", "$receptorCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_y", "$receptorCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_z", "$receptorCenterZ" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_x", "$ligandCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_y", "$ligandCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_z", "$ligandCenterZ" );

# Set the name of the pose
$newPose->Name = "Pose1";

# Generate the numeric data for a second docked pose.
# All numerical values taken from pose 2 of ZDock run output
my $position = Mdm::Point::Create( 6.1596049, 17.94953, 5.095075 );
my $translation = Mdm::Point::Create( 4.8000, -14.4000, 4.8000 );
my $rotation = Mdm::Point::Create( 90.0000, 107.4457, 6.1356 );
my $cluster = 1;
my $topClusterPose = 0;
my ( $receptorCenterX, $receptorCenterY, $receptorCenterZ ) =
( 6.88, 14.615, 5.83 );
my ( $ligandCenterX, $ligandCenterY, $ligandCenterZ ) =
( 2.522, 27.292, 11.48 );
$newPose =
$poseAssembly->CreateProteinPose( $position, $translation, $rotation,
$cluster, $topClusterPose );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_x", "$receptorCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_y", "$receptorCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_z", "$receptorCenterZ" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_x", "$ligandCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_y", "$ligandCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_z", "$ligandCenterZ" );
$newPose->Name = "Pose2";
```

# CreateProteinReport function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createproteinreport_function.htm

## CreateProteinReport function

### Description

CreateProteinReport generates a protein report of the Mdm::Document .

### Applies to

The CreateProteinReport function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateProteinReport function

#### Instance

my $stringValue = $object->CreateProteinReport();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to create a protein report.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Generate a protein report.
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $report = $document->CreateProteinReport();
my $name = $document->ModelName;

my $tempDir = DiscoveryScript::GetTemporaryFolder();

# Save report to file.

my $reportName = $name . ' Protein Report.html';
my $fileName = $tempDir.'/'.$reportName;

print "Writing report to file $reportName.\n";
open FILE, '>' . $fileName or die "can't write report!";
print FILE $report;

#we can also create report properties on the protein molecule
$document->CreateProteinReportProperties();

#This retrieves the cell information
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

my @PropertyNames = ( 'Atoms with fractional formal charges',
'Resolution',
'Report Crystallographic Information',
'Report Crystallographic Resolution',
'Report Experimental pH',
'Report Protein Molecular Weight',
'Report Protein Chains',
'Report Number of Amino Acids',
'Report Biomolecule Generation',
'Report PDB Headers');

foreach (@PropertyNames) {
printf"%s:\n%s\n\n", $_, $molecule->GetProperty($_);
}

print "\nHTML Report: %s\n", $report;

# remove the file after we done.
unlink ($fileName);
```

# CreateQuery function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createquery_function.htm

## CreateQuery function

### Description

CreateQuery creates an empty query.

### Applies to

The CreateQuery function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateQuery function

#### Instance

my $queryObject = $object->CreateQuery();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $queryObject | | | Mdm::Query |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty queries
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();
my $query2 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create some features on the queries
# Create a donor feature on query1 at 0,0,0
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# Create an acceptor feature on query2 at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $query2->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

# Merge two queries into one:
my $queries = $document->Queries;
$document->MergeQueries( @$queries[0], @$queries[1] );

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# CreateQueryAtom function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createqueryatom_function.htm

## CreateQueryAtom function

### Description

CreateQueryAtom creates a query atom for the specified atom. The molecule
containing the specified atom is moved into the query. It is rare to create
queries using the function. Typically you would use CreateOrTopology or
CreateAndTopology to create these types of queries. These functions
automatically create the query atoms and bonds.

### Applies to

The CreateQueryAtom function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the CreateQueryAtom function

#### Instance

my $queryatomObject = $object->CreateQueryAtom( <atom> );

my $queryatomObject = $object->CreateQueryAtom( { Atom => <atom> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $queryatomObject | | | Mdm::QueryAtom |
| <atom> | Required | | Mdm::Atom |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");

$document->CreateAndTopology();

# CreateAndTopology automatically creates the query atom which is
# typically how query atoms and bonds are created. Here
# we delete the query atom to show how to add it again
# using CreateQueryAtom.
$document->QueryAtoms->Item(0)->SetProperty( "List", "halogen" );
$document->QueryAtoms->Item(0)->Select();
$document->DeleteObjects();

# Add the query atom back using CreateQueryAtom - set the possible
# values to halogen.
$document->QueryOperators->Item(0)->CreateQueryAtom($atomObject);
$document->QueryAtoms->Item(0)->SetProperty( "List", "halogen" );
```

# CreateQueryBond function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createquerybond_function.htm

## CreateQueryBond function

### Description

CreateQueryBond creates a query bond for the specified bond. The molecule
containing the specified bond is moved into the query. It is rare to build
a query using this function. Instead it is typical to use the CreateOrTopology
or CreateAndTopology functions to create queries containing query atoms and
bonds. These functions automatically convert all atoms and bonds to query
atoms and bonds.

### Applies to

The CreateQueryBond function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the CreateQueryBond function

#### Instance

my $querybondObject = $object->CreateQueryBond( <bond> );

my $querybondObject = $object->CreateQueryBond( { Bond => <bond> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $querybondObject | | | Mdm::QueryBond |
| <bond> | Required | | Mdm::Bond |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');

$document->CreateAndTopology();

# The query bonds are automatically created using
# the CreateAndTopology function. However, to show
# how to create them using CreateBondQuery, we will delete
# them and then add them again.

my $querybonds = $document->QueryBonds;
foreach my $querybond (@$querybonds)
{
$querybond->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

my $bonds = $document->Bonds;
foreach my $bond (@$bonds)
{
my $querybond =
$document->QueryOperators()->Item(0)->CreateQueryBond($bond);
$querybond->AddBondType('queryAnyBond');
}

# removes the first query bond's bond type
$document->QueryBonds->Item(0)->RemoveBondType('queryAnyBond');
```

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

## CreateQueryFeatureMap function

### Description

CreateQueryFeatureMap creates a query feature map for the specified features. If the ExcludeMap parameter is True, then the feature is excluded from the definition.

### Applies to

The CreateQueryFeatureMap function can be used with the following objects:

#### Instance

# CreateQueryOperator function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createqueryoperator_function.htm

## CreateQueryOperator function

### Description

CreateQueryOperator creates a query operator. The type argument must be
Mdm::queryNoOperation, Mdm::queryAnd, Mdm::queryOr, Mdm::queryExclude,
Mdm::queryFit, Mdm::queryShape, or Mdm::queryInclude.

### Applies to

The CreateQueryOperator function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Query , Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the CreateQueryOperator function

#### Instance

my $queryoperatorObject = $object->CreateQueryOperator( <type> );

my $queryoperatorObject = $object->CreateQueryOperator( { Type => <type> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $queryoperatorObject | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |
| <type> | Required | | enum Mdm::QueryOperation |
| $object | | | Mdm::Query Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty queries
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();
my $query2 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create some features on the queries
# Create a donor feature on query1 at 0,0,0
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# Create an acceptor feature on query2 at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $query2->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

# Merge two queries into one:
my $queries = $document->Queries;
$document->MergeQueries( @$queries[0], @$queries[1] );

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# CreateReceptorSurface function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createreceptorsurface_function.htm

## CreateReceptorSurface function

### Description

CreateReceptorSurface creates a receptor surface around a ligand.

### Applies to

The CreateReceptorSurface function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateReceptorSurface function

#### Command

$object->CreateReceptorSurface();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Example for the CreateReceptorSurface function.
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1KIM.pdb" );
die "The document could not be opened" unless $document;

my $surfaces = $document->Surfaces;
die "No surface collection" unless $surfaces;

my $countSurfaces = $surfaces->Count;
die "Surfaces have already been created" unless ($countSurfaces == 0);

$document->CreateReceptorSurface();

$surfaces = $document->Surfaces;
die "No surface collection" unless $surfaces;

$countSurfaces = $surfaces->Count;
die "The receptor surface has not been created" unless ($countSurfaces == 1);

my $surface = $surfaces->Item(0);
die "No receptor surface" unless $surface;
my $surfaceName = $surface->Name;

print "The receptor surface <" . $surfaceName . "> has been created.\n";

$document->Close();
$document = undef;
```

# CreateRecursivePartitioningDendrogram function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createrecursivepartitioningdendrogram_function.htm

## CreateRecursivePartitioningDendrogram function

### Description

CreateRecursivePartitioningDendrogram creates a recursive partitioning dendrogram
from the node hierarchy contained in the Hierarchy View.
The following arguments are available:

* MdmDocument specifies the Mdm::Document whose data will be plotted.

* DataTableTabName specifies the tab whose data will be plotted.

* NodeProperty is the property defining the node hierarchy in the recursive partitioning tree. Each node property lists the node IDs that the molecule is assigned to starting from the root node. It is an array property.

* BranchProperty is the property containing the conditions for branching from the root node to the leaf node. It is an array property.

* ModelProperty is the classification property being modeled in the recursive partitioning tree model.

### Applies to

The CreateRecursivePartitioningDendrogram function can be used with the following objects:

Chart::Document

### Using the CreateRecursivePartitioningDendrogram function

#### Static

my $documentObject = Chart::Document::CreateRecursivePartitioningDendrogram( <mdmdocument>, <datatabletabname>, <nodeproperty>, <branchproperty>, <modelproperty> );

my $documentObject = Chart::Document::CreateRecursivePartitioningDendrogram( { MdmDocument => <mdmdocument>, DataTableTabName => <datatabletabname>, NodeProperty => <nodeproperty>, BranchProperty => <branchproperty>, ModelProperty => <modelproperty> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | Chart::Document |
| <branchproperty> | Required | | String |
| <datatabletabname> | Required | | String |
| <mdmdocument> | Required | | Mdm::Document |
| <modelproperty> | Required | | String |
| <nodeproperty> | Required | | String |

#### Defined by

ChartDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to create a recursive partitioning dendrogram (client only).
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ChartDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';
my $filePath = $samplesFolder . 'Tutorials/QSAR/pk-400_Tree1.sd';

my $document = DiscoveryScript::Open($filePath);

my $dendrogram = Chart::Document::CreateRecursivePartitioningDendrogram(
{
MdmDocument => $document,
DataTableTabName => 'Molecule',
NodeProperty => 'RPTempModel#NodeID',
BranchProperty => 'RPTempModel#Rules',
ModelProperty => 'Inhibition'
}
);

print "Model Type: DendrogramModelType\n"
if ( $dendrogram->ModelType == DendrogramModelType );

$dendrogram->UpdateViews();
```

# CreateResidue function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createresidue_function.htm

## CreateResidue function

### Description

CreateResidue creates an empty residue object of the specified
chemical residue type. An amino acid residue is
created for amino acid residue types, and a nucleotide
residue is created for nucleotide residue types. Otherwise,
a generic residue is created.

### Applies to

The CreateResidue function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcidChain , Mdm::Chain , Mdm::NucleicAcidChain

### Using the CreateResidue function

#### Instance

my $residueObject = $object->CreateResidue( <type> );

my $residueObject = $object->CreateResidue( { Type => <type> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $residueObject | | | Mdm::Residue |
| <type> | Required | | enum Mdm::ResidueType |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcidChain Mdm::Chain Mdm::NucleicAcidChain |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate methods for building and editing proteins.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# This is how to create an amino acid chain containing an alanine residue:
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $chain = $molecule->CreateAminoAcidChain();
my $aminoAcid1 = $chain->CreateResidue(Mdm::alanine);

my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
my $count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The current number of amino acids is $count.\n";

# Define a string consisting of 1-letter amino acid residue codes.
my $wideSequence = "AlaPheGlyProHisIleLysAlaAlaAla";
my $sequence = Mdm::AminoAcidChain::ConvertToOneLetterSequence($wideSequence);

print
"Converted wide sequence: $wideSequence to narrow sequence: $sequence.\n";

# Demonstrate how to append a sequence of residues at the C-terminus.
# Let's make it helical rather than the default extended conformation.
$document->GrowAminoAcidChain(
{
InsertAt => $chain,
Sequence => $sequence,
ConformationType => Mdm::rightAlphaHelixConformation,
GrowAtNTerminal => False
}
);

$aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
$count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The number of amino acid residues after growing chain "
. "at the C-terminus is $count.\n";

# Demonstrate how to grow amino acid chain at the N terminal.
# This will prepend the residue His0.
$document->GrowAminoAcidChain(
{
InsertAt => $chain,
Sequence => "H",
GrowAtNTerminal => True
}
);

$aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
$count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The number of amino acid residues after growing chain "
. "at the N-terminus is $count.\n";

# Insertion a residue within the chain.
my $insertionpoint = $aminoAcids->Item( $count - 2 );
my $sequence = "GANDT";
$document->InsertAminoAcid( $insertionpoint, $sequence );

$aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
$count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The number of amino acid residues after insertion is $count.\n";

# Demonstrate how to mutate a residue.
my $residuetomutate = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
print 'Amino acid name before the mutation: '
. $residuetomutate->Name() . "\n";
$document->MutateAminoAcid( $residuetomutate, Mdm::tyr );
print 'Amino acid name after the mutation: '
. $residuetomutate->Name() . "\n";

# At this point we have various insertion codes - lets renumber
print "Residue names before renumbering: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
print " " . $aminoAcids->Item($index)->Name() . " ";
}
print "\n";

$document->RenumberSequence( $aminoAcids->Item(0), 1, $count, True );
print "Residue names after renumbering: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
print " " . $aminoAcids->Item($index)->Name() . " ";
}
print "\n";

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# CreateRingAromaticFeature function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createringaromaticfeature_function.htm

## CreateRingAromaticFeature function

### Description

CreateRingAromaticFeature creates a ring aromatic feature for the specified atoms.
The atoms argument must contain at least two atoms, each of which must have at least
one aromatic bond.

### Applies to

The CreateRingAromaticFeature function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the CreateRingAromaticFeature function

#### Instance

my $ringaromaticfeatureObject = $object->CreateRingAromaticFeature( <arrayofatoms> );

my $ringaromaticfeatureObject = $object->CreateRingAromaticFeature( { ArrayOfAtoms => <arrayofatoms> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $ringaromaticfeatureObject | | | Mdm::RingAromaticFeature |
| <arrayofatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create some features on the query
# Create a ring aromatic
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Name("benzene");
my $ringAromaticOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$ringAromaticOperator->Name('RA1');
my $ringAromaticFeatureObject =
$ringAromaticOperator->CreateRingAromaticFeature(
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Atoms );
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Select(); # delete later

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature(
$ringAromaticFeatureObject->CentroidFeature(), 1.6 );
my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature(
$ringAromaticFeatureObject->NormalFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create a donor feature
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -2, -4, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# Give the hydrogen bond donor a higher weight (2.0) than the default (1.0)
$donorOperator->Weight(2.0);

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create an acceptor feature at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );

printf "%s Head: x: %.4f y: %.4f z: %.4f\n",
$locationFeatureHead->ClassName, 
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->X, 
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->Y,
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->Z;

my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

printf "%s Tail: x: %.4f y: %.4f z: %.4f\n",
$locationFeatureHead->ClassName,
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->X, 
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->Y,
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->Z;

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# CreateRotatableBondMonitor function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createrotatablebondmonitor_function.htm

## CreateRotatableBondMonitor function

### Description

CreateRotatableBondMonitor creates an Mdm::RotatableBondMonitor for
the indicated bond. This function is intended to be used instead of CreateRotatableBondMonitors when it is necessary to extend
the definition of rotatable bonds. Except for the exclusion of terminal bonds,
no restrictions are place on the definition of rotatable.

### Applies to

The CreateRotatableBondMonitor function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Bond , Mdm::ConformerBond

### Using the CreateRotatableBondMonitor function

#### Instance

my $rotatablebondmonitorObject = $object->CreateRotatableBondMonitor();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $rotatablebondmonitorObject | | | Mdm::RotatableBondMonitor |
| $object | | | Mdm::Bond Mdm::ConformerBond |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to create rotatable bond monitors for a molecule.
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Remove all atoms except the first ligand found.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
$ligands->Item(0)->Select();
$document->InvertSelection();
$document->DeleteObjects();
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

print
"Creating rotatable bond monitors for each non-terminal bond in the ligand.\n";
print "Note: a warning will be issued for any terminal bonds. \n\n";
my $bonds = $molecule->Bonds;
foreach my $b (@$bonds)
{
# terminal bond check no avoid aromatics
if ( $b->BondType eq "singleBond" and
( $b->Atom1->BondCount> 1 and $b->Atom2->BondCount > 1 ) ) { 
my $bCount = $b->CreateRotatableBondMonitor();
printf "Bond: %s to %s Angle: %.4f\n", 
$b->Atom1->Name, $b->Atom2->Name, $bCount->Angle,;
}
}
```

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the CreateRotatableBondMonitors function

#### Instance

my $integerValue = $object->CreateRotatableBondMonitors();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to create rotatable bond monitors for a molecule.
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Remove all atoms except the first ligand found.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
$ligands->Item(0)->Select();
$document->InvertSelection();
$document->DeleteObjects();
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

print "Creating rotatable bond monitors for ligand...\n";
my $rotatableBondMonitorCount = $molecule->CreateRotatableBondMonitors();
print "Found $rotatableBondMonitorCount rotatable bonds.\n";
my $arrayrotbonds = $document->RotatableBondMonitors; 
print "Number of rotatable bonds monitors: ". $arrayrotbonds->Count. "\n";

my $j = 0;
foreach my $monitor (@$arrayrotbonds) { 
my @IDs = ();
for (my $i = 0; $i < 4; ++$i) {
my $atom = $monitor->Object($i);
push (@IDs,$atom->Id. " " . $atom->Name );
}
my $IDscal = join(", ", @IDs);
printf "%3i) Id/Name: %s Torsion %.4f\n ", ++$j, $IDscal , $monitor->Angle;
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
```

```text
my $sequence2 =

$dnaSequence1->Type;

$dnaSequence2->Type;
```

# CreateSequenceFromFeature function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createsequencefromfeature_function.htm

## CreateSequenceFromFeature function

### Description

CreateSequenceFromFeature creates a new Sdm::Sequence object using
the residues associated with an Sdm::Feature .

### Applies to

The CreateSequenceFromFeature function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Feature

### Using the CreateSequenceFromFeature function

#### Instance

my $sequenceObject = $object->CreateSequenceFromFeature();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $sequenceObject | | | Sdm::Sequence |
| $object | | | Sdm::Feature |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script will illustrate the use of the function CreateSequenceFromRange.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence =
$document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'ASDFEXTRACTTHISGHJKLANDTHISHJKASDFGHJK' );

# Create a join feature.
my $segment1 = Sdm::Segment::Create( 4, 14 );
my $segment2 = Sdm::Segment::Create( 19, 25 );
my $location = Sdm::Location::Create(Sdm::locationTypeJoin);
$location->AddSegment($segment1);
$location->AddSegment($segment2);

my $feature = Sdm::Feature::CreateCustomFeature( 'This Feature', $location );
$sequence->AddFeature($feature);

# Create a new sequence using residues indices specified in a feature.
my $featureSequence = $feature->CreateSequenceFromFeature();

# Insert the newly created sequence into $document.
$document->Alignment->InsertSequence( 2, $featureSequence );

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

# CreateSequenceFromMolecule function

Source type: HTML

## CreateSequenceFromMolecule function

### Description

CreateSequenceFromMolecule creates a new Sdm::Sequence from
an Mdm::Molecule .

### Applies to

The CreateSequenceFromMolecule function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the CreateSequenceFromMolecule function

#### Instance

my $sequenceObject = $object->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( <molecule>, [addtoalignment] );

my $sequenceObject = $object->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( { Molecule => <molecule>, AddToAlignment => [addtoalignment] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $sequenceObject | | | Sdm::Sequence |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| [addtoalignment] | Optional | True | Boolean |

#### Defined by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to predict and retrieve secondary structure.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

my $sequence =
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( $mdmDocument->Molecules->[0] );
$alignment->PredictSecondaryStructureByDsc();

# Example accessing the secondary structure string from sequence property.
my $kabschAndSander =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructure(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType);
print "Kabsch and Sander secondary structure:\n";
print "Encoded: $kabschAndSander\n";

# Ensure alignment is displaying secondary structure.
if ( !( $alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown ) )
{
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown = True;
}

# Ensure KAS is displayed
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureVisible(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType) =
True;

# Example accessing the secondary structure data from object.
print "DSC secondary structure:\n";
my $ssObject =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructureObject(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);

print 'Predictor: ' . $ssObject->Predictor . "\n";
print 'Has probabilities: ' . $ssObject->IsPredicted . "\n";

my $dsc = $ssObject->SecondaryStructureString;
print "Encoded: $dsc\n";

my $propensity =
$sequence
->ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);
print "Propensity: $propensity\n";

my $helicalResidueCount = 0;
my $sheetResidueCount = 0;
my $coilResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $ssObject->ResidueCount;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $ssObject->SsType($i);
++$helicalResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$sheetResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::sheet || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
++$coilResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::coil || $type eq Sdm::extracellular );
}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print 'Analysis: The DSC secondary structure for this sequence has '
. $helicalResidueCount
. ' amino acid residues in helical formations, '
. $sheetResidueCount
. ' in sheet formations and '
. $coilResidueCount
. " in coil formations.\n";

my $secstrucfilter = $sdmDocument->SecondaryStructures;
print "Number of secondary Structures: ", $secstrucfilter->Count . "\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrates how to edit linked amino acid sequences
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Create a linked sequence
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$sdmDocument->DeleteAlignmentSequences();
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule($molecule);

my $residue = $molecule->AminoAcids->Item(1);
print 'Mutate 2nd residue from ' . $residue->Type . " to leu.\n";
$document->MutateAminoAcid( $residue, Mdm::leu );

print "Append amino acid sequence ASD.\n";
my $last = $sequence->ResidueCount - 1;
$residue = $molecule->AminoAcids->Item($last);
$document->InsertAminoAcid( $residue, "ASD" );

print "Delete third, fourth and fifth amino acids.\n";
$document->DeselectAll();
$molecule->Residues->Item(2)->Select;
$molecule->Residues->Item(3)->Select;
$molecule->Residues->Item(4)->Select;

$document->DeleteObjects();

# Ensure views are updated
$document->UpdateViews();
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use the Load/CreateSimFiles functions to create simulation files
# from a typed molecule.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ForceFieldDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';
my $outputFolder = DiscoveryScript::GetTemporaryFolder()."/typing";

my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . 'Bacteriorhodopsin Trajectory.dsv';
my $document = DiscoveryScript::Open($inputFile);
printf "Loading embedded forcefield from a typed molecule %s\n" , $document->ModelName;
my $forcefield = Ffdm::Document::Load($document);
if ($forcefield)
{
printf "Creating simulation files\n"; 
$forcefield->CreateSimulationFiles( $document, $outputFolder );
}
$document->Close();

# list all files in the output directory
opendir my $dh, $outputFolder or die "Could not open '$outputFolder' for reading '$!'\n";
my @files = grep {$_ ne '.' and $_ ne '..'} readdir $dh;
closedir $dh;

my $count = 0;
foreach my $file (sort @files) {
printf "%d) %s\n", ++$count, $file;
}
```

# CreateSlicingPlane function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createslicingplane_function.htm

## CreateSlicingPlane function

### Description

CreateSlicingPlane creates the specified slicing plane for the specified
objects. The index argument identifies the slicing plane to create and must
be between 1 and 6. The origin parameter specifies the 3D coordinates
of the origin of the slicing plane relative to the coordinate origin.
The normal parameter specifies the 3D coordinates of a 3D vector which is
perpendicular to the slicing plane. The 3D coordinates are expressed
in angstroms.

### Applies to

The CreateSlicingPlane function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateSlicingPlane function

#### Instance

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create oxygen atoms
my $O1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

my $xyz1 = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );

my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
my $slicingplaneObject = $document->CreateSlicingPlane(
{

ArrayOfObjects => $atoms,
Origin => Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 ),
Normal => Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 )
}
);

# Get all 3D Objects
my $objects3d = $document->Geometric3ds;

# Print their name and class name
foreach my $object (@$objects3d)
{
print $object->ClassName . "\t" . $object->Name . "\n";
}

# Get all slicing planes
my $slicplanes = $document->SlicingPlanes;
```

# CreateSolidSurface function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createsolidsurface_function.htm

## CreateSolidSurface function

### Description

CreateSolidSurface creates a solid (solvent, soft, or van der Waals) molecular surface for
an array of atoms or any object that contains atoms (e.g.,
residues, chains, molecules).
You must provide an Mdm::Array of such objects in the ArrayOfAtoms argument. The following arguments control the style:

* The display style argument specifies the type of surface: Soft (default) creates a surface that is similar to a solvent surface employing
a faster, more approximate algorithm. Solvent creates a solvent surface similar to a Connolly surface. van der Waals creates a VDW
surface, based on the van der Waals radius of each atom in the molecule.

* Soft (default) creates a surface that is similar to a solvent surface employing
a faster, more approximate algorithm.

* Solvent creates a solvent surface similar to a Connolly surface.

* van der Waals creates a VDW
surface, based on the van der Waals radius of each atom in the molecule.

* When True (default), the open surface argument includes breaks in the surface where it
contacts atoms that were not used to create the surface. When False, the surface
will completely enclose all of the atoms used to create it.

* The color scheme argument specifies the surface coloring: Electrostatic potential (default) uses colors mapped to the Gasteiger charges of the atoms that comprise the surface. Parent color colors the surface using the colors of the parent objects of the atoms that comprise the surface. Atom charge maps the partial charges of the atoms to the surface. Atom color colors the surface using the colors of the atoms that comprise the surface. Hydrogen bond donor/acceptor colors the surface by mapping fictional charges of +1 and -1 assigned to any hydrogen bond donor and acceptor atoms that comprise the surface. Hydrophobicity colors the surface by mapping the hydrophobicity of any amino acid parent objects of the atoms that comprise the surface. pKa colors the surface by mapping the pKa of any amino acid parent objects of the atoms that comprise the surface.

* Electrostatic potential (default) uses colors mapped to the Gasteiger charges of the atoms that comprise the surface.

* Parent color colors the surface using the colors of the parent objects of the atoms that comprise the surface.

* Atom charge maps the partial charges of the atoms to the surface.

* Atom color colors the surface using the colors of the atoms that comprise the surface.

* Hydrogen bond donor/acceptor colors the surface by mapping fictional charges of +1 and -1 assigned to any hydrogen bond donor and acceptor atoms that comprise the surface.

* Hydrophobicity colors the surface by mapping the hydrophobicity of any amino acid parent objects of the atoms that comprise the surface.

* pKa colors the surface by mapping the pKa of any amino acid parent objects of the atoms that comprise the surface.

* The probe radius argument specify the size of the radius of the sphere
that represents a solvent. The default probe radius is 1.4 angstroms.

### Applies to

The CreateSolidSurface function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateSolidSurface function

#### Instance

my $surfaceObject = $object->CreateSolidSurface( <arrayofatoms>, [displaystyle], [opensurface], [colorscheme], [proberadius] );

my $surfaceObject = $object->CreateSolidSurface( { ArrayOfAtoms => <arrayofatoms>, DisplayStyle => [displaystyle], OpenSurface => [opensurface], ColorScheme => [colorscheme], ProbeRadius => [proberadius] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $surfaceObject | | | Mdm::Surface |
| <arrayofatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| [colorscheme] | Optional | surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential | enum Mdm::SurfaceColorScheme |
| [displaystyle] | Optional | Mdm::surfaceStyleSoft | enum Mdm::SurfaceDisplayStyle |
| [opensurface] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [proberadius] | Optional | 1.4 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to colors selected surfaces.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Generate array with Color Scheme values.
my @surfaceColorSchemes = (
Mdm::surfaceColorByAtomCharge,
Mdm::surfaceColorByAtomColor,
Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential,
Mdm::surfaceColorByParentColor
);

print "Creating a solid surface (this may take a few seconds)...\n\n";
my $allAtoms = $document->Atoms;
my $surface =
$document->CreateSolidSurface( $allAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent, False,
Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential, 1.3 );
sleep(1);

foreach my $surfaceColorScheme (@surfaceColorSchemes)
{
print "Color surface by surface color scheme: $surfaceColorScheme...\n\n";
$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);
$surface->Select();

$document->SetSurfaceColorScheme($surfaceColorScheme);

$surface->Deselect();
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(1);
}
```

Align 2 molecules using tethers

```text
use strict;
use MdmCommands;

my $document = FileNew();

## create 2 molecules
$document->InsertFromSmiles( 'c1ccccc1' );
$document->InsertFromSmiles( 'c1ccccc1c1ccccc1' );

## select atoms from each molecule
$document->Molecules->Item(0)->Atoms->Item(0)->Select();
$document->Molecules->Item(1)->Atoms->Item(0)->Select();
## created tethers from selection
CreateTethers($document);

$document->DeselectAll();
$document->Molecules->Item(0)->Atoms->Item(3)->Select();
$document->Molecules->Item(1)->Atoms->Item(3)->Select();

CreateTethers($document); # created tethers from selection
## Align molecules to the tethers
```

# CreateTransparentSurface function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createtransparentsurface_function.htm

## CreateTransparentSurface function

### Description

CreateTransparentSurface creates a solid (solvent, soft, or van der Waals)
molecular surface for an array of atoms or any object that contains atoms (e.g.,
residues, chains, molecules). You must provide an Mdm::Array of such objects
in the ArrayOfAtoms argument. The following arguments control the style:

* The display style argument specifies the type of surface: Soft (default) creates a surface that is similar to a solvent surface employing
a faster, more approximate algorithm. Solvent creates a solvent surface similar to a Connolly surface. van der Waals creates a VDW
surface, based on the van der Waals radius of each atom in the molecule.

* Soft (default) creates a surface that is similar to a solvent surface employing
a faster, more approximate algorithm.

* Solvent creates a solvent surface similar to a Connolly surface.

* van der Waals creates a VDW
surface, based on the van der Waals radius of each atom in the molecule.

* When True (default), the open surface argument includes breaks in the surface where it
contacts atoms that were not used to create the surface. When False, the surface
will completely enclose all of the atoms used to create it.

* The color scheme argument specifies the surface coloring: Electrostatic potential (default) uses
colors mapped to the Gasteiger charges of the atoms that comprise the surface. Parent
colors the surface the same as its parent object. Atom charge maps the partial charges of the atoms to the surface. Atom color scheme colors
the surface using the colors of the atoms that comprise the surface.

* Electrostatic potential (default) uses
colors mapped to the Gasteiger charges of the atoms that comprise the surface.

* Parent
colors the surface the same as its parent object.

* Atom charge maps the partial charges of the atoms to the surface.

* Atom color scheme colors
the surface using the colors of the atoms that comprise the surface.

* The probe radius argument specify the size of the radius of the sphere
that represents a solvent. The default probe radius is 1.4 angstroms.

* The transparency argument sets the level of surface transparency. The value must be
between 0 and 1, where the smaller values result in less transparency. The default transparency is 0.5.

### Applies to

The CreateTransparentSurface function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateTransparentSurface function

#### Instance

my $surfaceObject = $object->CreateTransparentSurface( <arrayofatoms>, [displaystyle], [opensurface], [colorscheme], [proberadius], [transparency] );

my $surfaceObject = $object->CreateTransparentSurface( { ArrayOfAtoms => <arrayofatoms>, DisplayStyle => [displaystyle], OpenSurface => [opensurface], ColorScheme => [colorscheme], ProbeRadius => [proberadius], Transparency => [transparency] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $surfaceObject | | | Mdm::Surface |
| <arrayofatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| [colorscheme] | Optional | surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential | enum Mdm::SurfaceColorScheme |
| [displaystyle] | Optional | Mdm::surfaceStyleSoft | enum Mdm::SurfaceDisplayStyle |
| [opensurface] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [proberadius] | Optional | 1.4 | Real |
| [transparency] | Optional | 0.5 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to create a transparent surface.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '101m.pdb' );

# Select heme atoms.
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="HEM.*"; Atom label="*"');

# Create an array of all heme atoms.
my $hemeAtoms = $document->Filter( { Selected => 1 } )->Atoms;

# Create transparent surface around the heme group.
my $transparentSurface =
$document->CreateTransparentSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential,
1.3, 0.6 );

$transparentSurface->IsBackSideColorEnabled(True);
$transparentSurface->IsBackSideTransparencyEnabled(True);

# Also create wiremesh surface around the heme group.
my $wiremeshSurface =
$document->CreateWiremeshSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential, 2.0 );

print "Surface area: "
. $transparentSurface->Area . "\n"
. "Surface Volume: "
. $transparentSurface->Volume . "\n";
print "Surface probe radius: "
. $transparentSurface->ProbeRadius . "\n"
. "Transparency Level: "
. $transparentSurface->TransparencyLevel . "\n";

# Select all atoms within 6A of the heme and the surface.
$document->SelectByRadius( 6.0, 'Atom' );
$transparentSurface->Select();

# Show only the heme and neighboring atoms (other than water).
$document->FitView();
$document->InvertSelection();
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue name="HOH.*"; Atom label="*"');
$document->Hide();
$document->DeselectAll();

# Display the wiremesh surface with delay.
sleep(2);
$wiremeshSurface->SetVisible();
```

# CreateTupleMonitor function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createtuplemonitor_function.htm

## CreateTupleMonitor function

### Description

CreateTupleMonitor creates a tuple monitor for specified objects in
two or more molecules. Tuple monitors are used to create tethers for
superposition with Align or MolecularOverlay .
Valid object types include Mdm::Atom , Mdm::CentroidMonitor , and Mdm::PointFeature .

The object input array arguments must contain a valid object from
each tethered molecule. If multiple tether points are needed, each monitor must contain the following:

* a unique object from each molecule

* the same number of objects

* an object from the same set of molecules (specified in the same order)

### Applies to

The CreateTupleMonitor function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateTupleMonitor function

#### Instance

my $tuplemonitorObject = $object->CreateTupleMonitor( <arrayofmonitoredobjects> );

my $tuplemonitorObject = $object->CreateTupleMonitor( { ArrayOfMonitoredObjects => <arrayofmonitoredobjects> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $tuplemonitorObject | | | Mdm::TupleMonitor |
| <arrayofmonitoredobjects> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
# This script illustrates how to perform a molecular overlay.
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use SbdDiscoveryScript;

# Create a new MDM document.
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $name1 = 'Molecule1';
my $name2 = 'Molecule2';

my %MolecSMARTS = (
$name1 => 'O=C([O-])C1=CC(=CC=C1)C([O-])=O',
$name2 => 'C/C1=C/C=C(C=C1)C([O-])=O'
);

# Insert two molecules 'Molecule1' and 'Molecule2' from SMILES strings.
$document->InsertFromSmiles( $MolecSMARTS{$name1} );
my $molecule1 = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
$molecule1->Name($name1);

$document->InsertFromSmiles( $MolecSMARTS{$name2} );
my $molecule2 = $document->Molecules->Item(1);
$molecule2->Name($name2);

# name of the overlay similarity property
my $overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay Similarity/' . $molecule1->Name;

# Add rotatable bond monitors to both molecules.
# These are used with flexible field alignment.
$document->AddRotatableBondMonitors;

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection(10.0, 5.0, 0.0);
$document->DeselectAll;

# Calculate the similarity before the rigid field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using rigid field alignment, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated similarity is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Rigid field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the similarity before the rigid field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using rigid field alignment.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False
}
);

printf( "Rigid field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection(5.0, 10.0, 0.0);
$document->DeselectAll;

# Calculate the similarity before flexible field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using flexible field alignment, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated similarity is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Flexible field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the similarity before flexible field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay molecules using flexible field alignment.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True
}
);

$overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay Similarity/' . $molecule1->Name;
printf( "Flexible field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

#
# Overlay molecules using tethers (tuple monitors).
#

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection( 10, 10, 5 );
$document->DeselectAll;

my $molecule1Atoms = $molecule1->Atoms;
my $molecule2Atoms = $molecule2->Atoms;

# atom mapping indices
my %atomIndices = (
0 => 8,
2 => 9,
6 => 1
);

print(" Overlay with atom tethers\n");
foreach my $id1 (sort {$a <=> $b} keys %atomIndices) {
my $id2 = $atomIndices{$id1};
my $tupleArray = Mdm::Array::Create();
$tupleArray->AddItem( $molecule1Atoms->Item($id1) );
$tupleArray->AddItem( $molecule2Atoms->Item($id2) );
$document->CreateTupleMonitor($tupleArray);
printf( " Map %s atom: %d to: %s atom: %d\n",
$molecule1->Name, $id1 + 1, $molecule2->Name, $id2 + 1 );
}

# name of the property
$overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay RMS/' . $molecule1->Name;

# Calculate the RMSD value before the alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using tethers, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated RMSD is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the RMSD value before the alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using tethers.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Remove the tethers
my $monitors = $document->TupleMonitors;
foreach my $monitor (@$monitors)
{
$monitor->Select;
}
$document->DeleteObjects;

$document->FitView;
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# CreateValenceMonitor function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createvalencemonitor_function.htm

## CreateValenceMonitor function

### Description

CreateValenceMonitor creates a monitor identifying atoms
from the specified array having valences over or under the
expected value.

### Applies to

The CreateValenceMonitor function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document , Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the CreateValenceMonitor function

#### Instance

my $valencemonitorObject = $object->CreateValenceMonitor( <arrayofatoms> );

my $valencemonitorObject = $object->CreateValenceMonitor( <arrayofmonitoredatoms> );

my $valencemonitorObject = $object->CreateValenceMonitor( { ArrayOfAtoms => <arrayofatoms> } );

my $valencemonitorObject = $object->CreateValenceMonitor( { ArrayOfMonitoredAtoms => <arrayofmonitoredatoms> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $valencemonitorObject | | | Mdm::ValenceMonitor |
| <arrayofatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| <arrayofmonitoredatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of ValenceMonitor objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "3ptb.pdb" );

# Creates a hydrogen-bond monitor between ligand and receptor atoms.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $monitor = $document->CreateValenceMonitor($ligandAtoms);

$monitor->IsUnderValenceShown = True;

print "Found " . $monitor->OverValenceCount . " atoms over valence.\n";
print "Found " . $monitor->UnderValenceCount . " atoms under valence.\n";

my $valences = $monitor->Valences;

my $count = $valences->Count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $valence = $valences->Item($index);
printf "Expected valence (for %s): %d \t Current valence: %d\n",
$valence->Name, $valence->ExpectedValence, $valence->Valence;
}
```
