# CreateWiremeshSurface function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/createwiremeshsurface_function.htm

## CreateWiremeshSurface function

### Description

CreateWiremeshSurface creates a wire frame solid (solvent, soft, or van der Waals)
molecular surface for an array of atoms or any object that contains atoms (e.g.,
residues, chains, molecules).
You must provide an Mdm::Array of such objects in the ArrayOfAtoms argument.
The following arguments control the style:

* The display style argument specifies the type of surface: Soft (default) creates a surface that is similar to a solvent surface employing
a faster, more approximate algorithm. Solvent creates a solvent surface similar to a Connolly surface. van der Waals creates a VDW
surface, based on the van der Waals radius of each atom in the molecule.

* Soft (default) creates a surface that is similar to a solvent surface employing
a faster, more approximate algorithm.

* Solvent creates a solvent surface similar to a Connolly surface.

* van der Waals creates a VDW
surface, based on the van der Waals radius of each atom in the molecule.

* When True (default), the open surface argument includes breaks in the surface where it
contacts atoms that were not used to create the surface. When False, the surface
will completely enclose all of the atoms used to create it.

* The color scheme argument specifies the surface coloring: Electrostatic potential (default) uses
colors mapped to the Gasteiger charges of the atoms that comprise the surface. Parent
colors the surface the same as its parent object. Atom charge maps the partial charges of the atoms to the surface. Atom color scheme colors
the surface using the colors of the atoms that comprise the surface.

* Electrostatic potential (default) uses
colors mapped to the Gasteiger charges of the atoms that comprise the surface.

* Parent
colors the surface the same as its parent object.

* Atom charge maps the partial charges of the atoms to the surface.

* Atom color scheme colors
the surface using the colors of the atoms that comprise the surface.

* The probe radius argument specify the size of the radius of the sphere
that represents a solvent. The default probe radius is 1.4 angstroms.

### Applies to

The CreateWiremeshSurface function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the CreateWiremeshSurface function

#### Instance

my $surfaceObject = $object->CreateWiremeshSurface( <arrayofatoms>, [displaystyle], [opensurface], [colorscheme], [proberadius] );

my $surfaceObject = $object->CreateWiremeshSurface( { ArrayOfAtoms => <arrayofatoms>, DisplayStyle => [displaystyle], OpenSurface => [opensurface], ColorScheme => [colorscheme], ProbeRadius => [proberadius] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $surfaceObject | | | Mdm::Surface |
| <arrayofatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| [colorscheme] | Optional | surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential | enum Mdm::SurfaceColorScheme |
| [displaystyle] | Optional | Mdm::surfaceStyleSoft | enum Mdm::SurfaceDisplayStyle |
| [opensurface] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [proberadius] | Optional | 1.4 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to create a transparent surface.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '101m.pdb' );

# Select heme atoms.
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="HEM.*"; Atom label="*"');

# Create an array of all heme atoms.
my $hemeAtoms = $document->Filter( { Selected => 1 } )->Atoms;

# Create transparent surface around the heme group.
my $transparentSurface =
$document->CreateTransparentSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential,
1.3, 0.6 );

$transparentSurface->IsBackSideColorEnabled(True);
$transparentSurface->IsBackSideTransparencyEnabled(True);

# Also create wiremesh surface around the heme group.
my $wiremeshSurface =
$document->CreateWiremeshSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential, 2.0 );

print "Surface area: "
. $transparentSurface->Area . "\n"
. "Surface Volume: "
. $transparentSurface->Volume . "\n";
print "Surface probe radius: "
. $transparentSurface->ProbeRadius . "\n"
. "Transparency Level: "
. $transparentSurface->TransparencyLevel . "\n";

# Select all atoms within 6A of the heme and the surface.
$document->SelectByRadius( 6.0, 'Atom' );
$transparentSurface->Select();

# Show only the heme and neighboring atoms (other than water).
$document->FitView();
$document->InvertSelection();
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue name="HOH.*"; Atom label="*"');
$document->Hide();
$document->DeselectAll();

# Display the wiremesh surface with delay.
sleep(2);
$wiremeshSurface->SetVisible();
```

# CTerminus property

Source type: HTML

## CTerminus property

### Description

CTerminus specifies the c-terminus Mdm::AminoAcid in a Mdm::AminoAcidChain object.

### Applies to

The CTerminus property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcidChain

### Using the CTerminus property

#### Get

my $aminoacidObject = $object->CTerminus;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $aminoacidObject | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcidChain |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This example shows how to alter the characteristics of protein termini.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Subroutine to print atoms in N terminal residue.
sub PrintNTerminus($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $chains = $document->AminoAcidChains;
my $nTerminus = $chains->Item(0)->NTerminus();
my $atoms = $nTerminus->Atoms;
my $atomCount = $atoms->Count;
printf "Number of atoms in N terminal residue %s : %d\n",
$nTerminus->Name(), $atomCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atomCount ; ++$index )
{
my $atom = $atoms->Item($index);
printf
" Name : %s Formal charge %d/%d\n",
$atom->Name(),
$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,
$atom->FormalCharge->Denominator;
}
}

# Subroutine to print atoms in C terminal residue.
sub PrintCTerminus($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $chains = $document->AminoAcidChains;
my $nTerminus = $chains->Item(0)->CTerminus();
my $atoms = $nTerminus->Atoms;
my $atomCount = $atoms->Count;
printf "Number of atoms in C terminal residue %s : %d\n",
$nTerminus->Name(), $atomCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atomCount ; ++$index )
{
my $atom = $atoms->Item($index);
printf
" Name : %s Formal charge %d/%d\n",
$atom->Name(),
$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,
$atom->FormalCharge->Denominator;
}
}

# Subroutine to print atoms in N and C terminal residues.
sub PrintTermini($$)
{
my ( $document, $title ) = @_;
printf "\n%s :\n", $title;
PrintNTerminus($document);
PrintCTerminus($document);
}

# Load molecule from PDB.
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Mutate the termini to alanine. With the side chain removed,
# the atom listing will be clearer.
my $chain = $document->AminoAcidChains->Item(0);
my $nTerminus = $chain->NTerminus();
my $cTerminus = $chain->CTerminus();

$document->MutateAminoAcid( $nTerminus, Mdm::ala );
$document->MutateAminoAcid( $cTerminus, Mdm::ala );
$document->DeselectAll();

# Uncomment this line to add hydrogen atoms.
# AddHydrogens($document);

# List atoms in current configuration.
PrintTermini( $document, "At start" );

# Remove terminal residue characteristics and list atoms.
$chain->RemoveNTerminusCap();
$chain->RemoveCTerminusCap();
PrintTermini( $document, "After removing caps" );

# Make termini normal (i.e. charged) and list atoms.
$nTerminus->MakeNTerminus(True);
$cTerminus->MakeCTerminus(True);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making charged termini" );

# Make termini uncharged and list atoms.
$nTerminus->MakeNTerminus(False);
$cTerminus->MakeCTerminus(False);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making neutral termini" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 1.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(1.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(1.0);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 1.0" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 7.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(7.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(7.0);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 7.0" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 13.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(13.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(130);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 13.0" );

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# Cursor property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/cursor_property.htm

## Cursor property

### Description

Cursor specifies the Sdm::Cursor object in an Sdm::Alignment .

### Applies to

The Cursor property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the Cursor property

#### Get

my $cursorObject = $object->Cursor;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $cursorObject | | | Sdm::Cursor |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to manipulate the alignment cursor.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
print "Please try running again from within Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences;
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(0, 'S1', 'ALKDFLASDFLKASLFKASLFKD');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(1, 'S2', 'ALDFKLAFLASFLSAFADFALFAS');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(2, 'S3', '-');
$alignment->Sequence(0)->MarkStartOfChain(11);
$alignment->Sequence(1)->MarkStartOfChain(13);
$document->InvokeAction('ActionChainViewLayout');

# Move cursor to start of second domain.
my $cursor = $alignment->Cursor;
$cursor->CursorColumnIndex = $alignment->DomainStart(1);
$cursor->CursorSequenceIndex = 0;
$cursor->IsCursorBeforeBoundary = False;
$alignment->InsetSymbolsAtCursor('BEGIN-');

# Move cursor to end of first domain.
my $cursor = $alignment->Cursor;
$cursor->CursorColumnIndex = $alignment->DomainEnd(0);
$cursor->CursorSequenceIndex = 0;
$cursor->IsCursorBeforeBoundary = True;
$alignment->InsetSymbolsAtCursor('-END');
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to manipulate the alignment cursor.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
print "Please try running again from within Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences;
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(0, 'S1', 'ALKDFLASDFLKASLFKASLFKD');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(1, 'S2', 'ALDFKLAFLASFLSAFADFALFAS');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(2, 'S3', '-');
$alignment->Sequence(0)->MarkStartOfChain(11);
$alignment->Sequence(1)->MarkStartOfChain(13);
$document->InvokeAction('ActionChainViewLayout');

# Move cursor to start of second domain.
my $cursor = $alignment->Cursor;
$cursor->CursorColumnIndex = $alignment->DomainStart(1);
$cursor->CursorSequenceIndex = 0;
$cursor->IsCursorBeforeBoundary = False;
$alignment->InsetSymbolsAtCursor('BEGIN-');

# Move cursor to end of first domain.
my $cursor = $alignment->Cursor;
$cursor->CursorColumnIndex = $alignment->DomainEnd(0);
$cursor->CursorSequenceIndex = 0;
$cursor->IsCursorBeforeBoundary = True;
$alignment->InsetSymbolsAtCursor('-END');
```

# CytosolColor property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/cytosolcolor_property.htm

## CytosolColor property

### Description

CytosolColor specifies the color of the cytosolic plane of an Mdm::Membrane object.
The cytosolic plane is defined as the plane in the positive direction from the membrane Center (i.e., in direction of the membrane Normal ).

### Applies to

The CytosolColor property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Membrane

### Using the CytosolColor property

#### Get

my $colorObject = $object->CytosolColor;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $colorObject | | | DiscoveryScript::Color |
| $object | | | Mdm::Membrane |

#### Set

$object->CytosolColor = <color>;

$object->CytosolColor( <color> );

$object->CytosolColor( { Color => <color> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <color> | Required | | DiscoveryScript::Color |
| $object | | | Mdm::Membrane |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrate how to create a membrane.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

# Remove all chains except the first.
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# "Guess" some value for the membrane position.
my $center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, -3.2 );
my $normal = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.521, 0.106, 0.847 );
my $membrane =
$document->CreateMembrane( $center, $normal, 60.0, 60.0, 30.0 );

# Pick a different color scheme from default.
$membrane->CytosolColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 255 ) ); # cyan
$membrane->ExtracellularColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 255, 255, 0 ) ); # yellow
$document->SetParent( $molecule, $membrane );
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

# Change some membrane properties.
$center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, 3.2 );
$normal = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.521, -0.106, -0.847 );

$membrane->Thickness = 35;
$membrane->Normal = $normal;
$membrane->Center = $center;
```

# Datatypes

Source type: HTML

## Datatypes

### Description

Datatypes define the types of data (for example constants and variables) that can be
used by a script. Each type of data can hold a specific value from a set of values.
Discovery Studio scripting employs enumerations and native data type constants and variables.
Native data types convey typical programming information (for example integer numbers, floating
point numbers, or logical values). Enumerations are named values that provide for the
storage and manipulation of information that is specific to the Discovery Studio application
(for example ElementType or HybridizationType).

# DefaultDistanceCriterion property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/defaultdistancecriterion_property.htm

## DefaultDistanceCriterion property

### Description

DefaultDistanceCriterion indicates the default distance criterion
used for the hydrogen bond monitor.

### Applies to

The DefaultDistanceCriterion property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor

### Using the DefaultDistanceCriterion property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->DefaultDistanceCriterion;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how use the hydrogen bond monitor and to change the distance cutoff.

use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Creates a hbond monitor between ligand atoms and receptor
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $LigName = $ligands->Item(0)->Name;
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $monitor = $document->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( $ligandAtoms,
Mdm::allAtomHydrogenBonds, Mdm::allMolecularHydrogenBonds );

# Shows the label for each of the hbonds
$monitor->IsLabelShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll(); 

printf "Default distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->DefaultDistanceCriterion;
printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor.\n\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $newHBDist = 3.0;
$monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared( $newHBDist* $newHBDist );

# update view to ensure the correct HB count
$document->UpdateViews();
printf "Set the distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared;

printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor:\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $hbonds = $document->HydrogenBonds;
my $count = $hbonds->Count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $hbond = $hbonds->Item($index);
my $dist = $hbond->Distance;
my $atom1 = $hbond->Atom1;
my $atom2 = $hbond->Atom2;
my $res = $atom1->Parent;

if ( $res->Name eq $LigName ) {
$atom2->Parent->Select; 
}
else{
$atom1->Parent->Select; 
}
printf "%d) Distance: %.3f A H-bond between Atom %s:%s:%s and Atom %s:%s:%s\n",
$index+1, $dist,
$atom1->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom1->Parent->Name, $atom1->Name,
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name ;
} 

$document->FitView(); 
my $display_style = { DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' };
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle($display_style);
$document->DeselectAll();
```

# DefaultNonbondCriterion property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/defaultnonbondcriterion_property.htm

## DefaultNonbondCriterion property

### Description

DefaultNonbondCriterion specifies the default distance and
angle criteria used by the Mdm::NonbondMonitor .
See enum Mdm::NonbondCriterionType for a description
of the various criterion.

### Applies to

The DefaultNonbondCriterion property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::NonbondMonitor

### Using the DefaultNonbondCriterion property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->DefaultNonbondCriterion( <criterion> );

my $realValue = $object->DefaultNonbondCriterion( { Criterion => <criterion> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| <criterion> | Required | | enum Mdm::NonbondCriterionType |
| $object | | | Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor Mdm::NonbondMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the basic non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "Create a non-bond monitor for a subset of atoms.\n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus();
$ligand->Select();
my $ligandAtoms = $document->SelectedObjects()->Atoms;
$document->FitView();
$document->DeselectAll();

my $monitor = $document->CreateNonbondMonitor($ligandAtoms);
$monitor->Name = "myname";
$document->UpdateViews();

my $monitors = $document->NonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d NonbondMonitor(s).\n", $monitors->Count;
print "\n";

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "The properties NonbondCriterion and DefaultNonbondCriterion \n";
print "access the parameters used to identify non-bonds (see the \n";
print "documentation for full description of criteria).\n\n";

print "A list of criteria a their values follows:\n";
my $allCriteria = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllNonbondCriterionTypes();
foreach my $criterionType (@$allCriteria)
{
printf "Mdm::%s:\t %6.2f (default: %6.2f) \n",
$criterionType,
$monitor->NonbondCriterion($criterionType),
$monitor->DefaultNonbondCriterion($criterionType);
}
print "\n";

# -- Changing an interaction criterion ------------------------------

print 'Using the default criteria, the number of non-bond '
. 'interactions is ' . $monitor->Nonbonds->Count . ".\n\n";

my $maxHBond = 1.0 + $monitor->NonbondCriterion(
Mdm::hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum);
print 'After increasing the classical hydrogen bond distance to '
. $maxHBond . " A, ";

$monitor->NonbondCriterion(
Mdm::hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum) = $maxHBond;
$document->UpdateObjects;
print 'the number of non-bond interactions increases to '
. $monitor->Nonbonds->Count . ".\n\n";

print "Changes made to the non-bond criteria can be reset " .
"to the original defaults using ResetNonbondCriteria.\n";
$monitor->ResetNonbondCriteria();
```

## DefaultPercentVdwRadius property

### Description

DefaultPercentVdwRadius indicates the default van der Waals percentage

#### Get

##### Parameters

| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::BumpMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Search for and print bumps between ligand and receptor.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Add hydrogen atoms to all heavy atoms.
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms( Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms, True );

# Creates a bump monitor between ligand and receptor atoms.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $bumpMonitor = $document->CreateBumpMonitor( $ligandAtoms, False );

$bumpMonitor->IsLabelShown = True;
$bumpMonitor->IsIntermolecularOnlyShown = False;

print "Default percent VDW Radius: $bumpMonitor->{DefaultPercentVdwRadius}\n";
print "$bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} bumps between ligand and receptor.\n";

$bumpMonitor->PercentVdwRadius = 90;

print "$bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} bumps between ligand and receptor "
. "when VDW radius set to 90%.\n";

my $bumps = $bumpMonitor->Bumps;
my $count = $bumps->Count;

# Create a bump hash.
my %bumpHash;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $bump = $bumps->Item($index);
$bumpHash{$index}{'bump'} = $bump;
$bumpHash{$index}{'Id1'} = $bump->Atom1->Id;
$bumpHash{$index}{'Id2'} = $bump->Atom2->Id;
}

# Print information for each bump, sorted by Atom1->Id followed by Atom2->Id.
my $counter = 0;
for my $b (
sort { 
my $x = $bumpHash{$a}{'Id1'};
my $y = $bumpHash{$b}{'Id1'};
($x != $y) ? ($x <=> $y) : ($bumpHash{$a}{'Id2'} <=> $bumpHash{$b}{'Id2'})
}
keys %bumpHash
)
{
my $bump = $bumpHash{$b}{'bump'};
my $atom1 = $bump->Atom1;
my $atom2 = $bump->Atom2;
printf
"%3d) Bump: %.3f A between Atom id %d %s:%s:%s and Atom id %d %s:%s:%s\n",
++$counter, $bump->Distance(),
$bumpHash{$b}{'Id1'},
$atom1->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom1->Parent->Name, $atom1->Name,
$bumpHash{$b}{'Id2'},
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name;
}
```

# DefaultSession property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/defaultsession_property.htm

## DefaultSession property

### Description

DefaultSession specifies the current Pipeline Pilot server session within the
Discovery Studio interface. When run from the command line, an empty
session will be returned.

### Applies to

The DefaultSession property can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Document

### Using the DefaultSession property

#### Static Get

my $sessionObject = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $sessionObject | | | Protocol::Session |
| $object | | | Protocol::Document |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

# DeleteItem function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/deleteitem_function.htm

## DeleteItem function

### Description

DeleteItem removes an item from a collection.

### Applies to

The DeleteItem function can be used with the following objects:

DiscoveryScript::ColorArray , DiscoveryScript::DocumentArray , DiscoveryScript::IntegerArray , DiscoveryScript::ObjectMap , DiscoveryScript::RealArray , DiscoveryScript::StringArray , Mdm::Array , Mdm::OfflineableArray , Mdm::PointArray , Mdm::Set , Protocol::ParameterMap , Sdm::Array , Sdm::AttributeMap , Sdm::ResidueArray , Sdm::SequenceArray

### Using the DeleteItem function

#### Instance

$object->DeleteItem( <index> );

$object->DeleteItem( <item> );

$object->DeleteItem( <key> );

$object->DeleteItem( { Index => <index> } );

$object->DeleteItem( { Item => <item> } );

$object->DeleteItem( { Key => <key> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| <item> | Required | | Mdm::Object |
| <key> | Required | | String Sdm::AttributeMapKey |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript , MdmDiscoveryScript , SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to manipulate items in an Mdm::Array.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

my $atoms = $document->Atoms;

# Collect all cysteine atoms.
my $cysteineAtomArray = Mdm::Array::Create();
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
$cysteineAtomArray->AddItem($atom)
if ( $atom->GetProperty("Parent") =~ /CYS/i );
}

# Find the common ancestor of all atoms in the array in cysteineAtomArray.
my $parent = $cysteineAtomArray->FindCommonAncestor();
print "The common parent object of all CYS atoms: "
. $parent->ClassName . " "
. $parent->Name . "\n";

die "No cysteine atoms found! Exiting.\n" if $cysteineAtomArray->IsEmpty;

my $cysteineAtomCount = $cysteineAtomArray->Count;
print "Number of atoms in cysteine residues: " . $cysteineAtomCount . "\n";

# Delete all atoms except C-alpha and C-beta.
# Note: When deleting items from an array, the array is traversed in
# reverse order. This avoids having to account for changes in the item
# indices as the array is modified.
for ( my $i = $cysteineAtomCount - 1 ; $i >= 0 ; --$i )
{
my $atom = $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i);
if ( $atom->Name !~ /(cb|ca)\b/i )
{
$cysteineAtomArray->DeleteItem($i);
}
}
print "Number of C-alpha and C-beta atoms in cysteine residues: "
. $cysteineAtomArray->Count . "\n";

# Create a copy of the original array in reverse order.
$cysteineAtomCount = $cysteineAtomArray->Count;
my $reverseCysteineArray = Mdm::Array::Create();

# Use the AddItem function to insert the first atom.
# Note: the InsertItem function cannot be used on an empty array.
$reverseCysteineArray->AddItem( $cysteineAtomArray->Item(0) );
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $cysteineAtomCount ; ++$i )
{
$reverseCysteineArray->InsertItem( 0, $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i) );
}

# Swap the first two elements or the original array.
my $tempItem = $cysteineAtomArray->Item(0);
$cysteineAtomArray->ReplaceItem( 0, $cysteineAtomArray->Item(1) );
$cysteineAtomArray->ReplaceItem( 1, $tempItem );

# Print out the IDs of the atoms in the two arrays side by side.
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $cysteineAtomCount ; ++$i )
{
my $atom1Id = $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i)->Id;
my $atom2Id = $reverseCysteineArray->Item($i)->Id;
print "item $i\t $atom1Id\t $atom2Id\n";
}

# Remove all remaining items in the original array.
$cysteineAtomArray->ClearItems();
print "The array now has " . $cysteineAtomArray->Count . " elements\n";
```

#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Publication class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'Y13252-truncated',
'TCTAGAGTAACATTTAGAATTAAGGTGGGAAATTATCTTAAAATCT' );

my $title =
'Nonfixed duplication containing the Adh gene and a truncated form '
. 'of the Adhr gene in the Drosophila funebris species group: different '
. 'modes of evolution of Adh relative to Adhr in Drosophila';

# Create publication object with sample data.
my $publication01 = Sdm::Publication::Create( 'Amador, A., Juan, E.',
$title, 'Molec. Biol. Evol.' );

# Create publication and add content separately.
my $publication02 = Sdm::Publication::Create();
$publication02->Authors = 'Amador, A., Juan, E.';
$publication02->Title = $title;
$publication02->Journal = 'Molec. Biol. Evol.';
$publication02->Reference = '16(11): 1439--1456 (1999)';
$publication02->PubMedId = '10555275';
$publication02->Comment = 'y13252';

#$publication02->Consortium = '';
#$publication02->DigitalObjectId = '';
#$publication02->MedlineId = '';
#$publication02->PubMedId = '';

# Associate publications with a sequence object.
# NOTE: To see the publications in Discovery Studio, double-click on the
# sequence in the sequence window to open a sequence annotation window.
# Publications are listed in the data table's Literature Citation tab.
$sequence->AddPublication($publication01);
$sequence->AddPublication($publication02);

my $publicationCount = $sequence->PublicationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $publicationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $publication = $sequence->Publication($index);
printf "%d: %s, %s. %s %s.\n",
$index + 1,
$publication->Authors,
$publication->Title,
$publication->Journal,
$publication->Reference;
}

$sequence->DeletePublication(0);

# DeleteStartOfChainMark function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/deletestartofchainmark_function.htm

## DeleteStartOfChainMark function

### Description

DeleteStartOfChainMark deletes a chain break mark
at the specified 0-based residue index.

### Applies to

The DeleteStartOfChainMark function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the DeleteStartOfChainMark function

#### Instance

$object->DeleteStartOfChainMark( <index> );

$object->DeleteStartOfChainMark( { Index => <index> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence Sdm::Sequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrates how to manipulate chain breaks in sequences.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();

$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $sequence0 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'MIASDFADSG' );
my $sequence1 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S2', 'MAACDFIDSA' );

# Insert chain breaks by marking the start of new chains using
# 0-based residue indices.
$sequence0->MarkStartOfChain(4);
$sequence1->MarkStartOfChain(4);
$sequence1->MarkStartOfChain(6);

# Find the starting residue index for each new chain.
my $residueCount0 = $sequence0->ResidueCount;
print "In the first sequence, there is a start of chain at ";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount0 ; ++$i )
{
if ( $sequence0->Residue($i)->IsStartOfChain )
{
print "$i ";
}
}
print "\n";
$document->UpdateViews();

$sequence1->DeleteStartOfChainMark(4);
$document->UpdateViews();

# Find the starting residue index for each new chain in
# second sequence.
my $residueCount1 = $sequence1->ResidueCount;
print "In the second sequence, there is a start of chain at ";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount1 ; ++$i )
{
if ( $sequence1->Residue($i)->IsStartOfChain )
{
print "$i ";
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# DelinkMdmDocument function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/delinkmdmdocument_function.htm

## DelinkMdmDocument function

### Description

DelinkMdmDocument breaks the link between specified documents if one exists.

### Applies to

The DelinkMdmDocument function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the DelinkMdmDocument function

#### Instance

$object->DelinkMdmDocument();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Sdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to link/delink SDM and MDM documents.
# NOTE: Sequence-Structure linking is only supported on the client.
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Create 1crn sequence manually so prevent auto-linking of documents.
# To link, the residue order, object names and chain breaks must match.
my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0);
$sequence->InsetAbbreviations( 0,
'ThrThrCysCysProSerIleValAlaArgSerAsnPheAsnValCysArgLeuProGlyThrProGlu'
. 'AlaIleCysAlaThrTyrThrGlyCysIleIleIleProGlyAlaThrCysProGlyAspTyrAlaAsn'
);
$sequence->Name = '1crn';

# Link documents (this will break any existing linked documents)
# and any match sequence-molecules.
# Note the sequence name shows the molecule icon indicating it is linked.
$sdmDocument->LinkMdmDocument($mdmDocument);

print 'Is sequence linked: ' . $sequence->IsLinked . "\n";

# Break document link.
# Uncomment to break the SDM-MDM document link.
#$sdmDocument->DelinkMdmDocument();
```

# Denominator property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/denominator_property.htm

## Denominator property

### Description

Denominator specifies the denominator of a rational.

### Applies to

The Denominator property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Rational

### Using the Denominator property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->Denominator;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Rational |

#### Set

$object->Denominator = <denominator>;

$object->Denominator( <denominator> );

$object->Denominator( { Denominator => <denominator> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <denominator> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Rational |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

## Density property

### Description

Density indicates the density of a molecule. It is calculated as the molecular weight divided by the approximate volume.Its unit is g/mol/Å 3 .

#!/usr/bin/perl -w

use strict;

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

$molecule->IsChargeCalculated = True;

print "The following is a list of molecule properties:\n";

print 'Hydrogen bond acceptor count: '
. $molecule->HydrogenBondAcceptorCount . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen bond donor count: '
. $molecule->HydrogenBondDonorCount . "\n";
print 'Lipinski violation count: ' . $molecule->LipinskiViolationCount . "\n";
print 'Molecular formula: ' . $molecule->MolecularFormula . "\n";
print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Radius of gyration: ' . $molecule->RadiusOfGyration . "\n";
print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Rotatable bond count: ' . $molecule->RotatableBondCount . "\n";
print 'Surface area: ' . $molecule->SurfaceArea . "\n";

Mdm::ProteinPose , Mdm::Query , Mdm::QueryAtom , Mdm::QueryBond , Mdm::QueryFeatureMap , Mdm::QueryOperator , Mdm::Residue , Mdm::Restraint , Mdm::RingAromaticFeature , Mdm::RotatableBondMonitor , Mdm::ScreenLabel , Mdm::ShapeFeature , Mdm::SideChainConformationViolationMonitor , Mdm::SlicingPlane , Mdm::Sphere , Mdm::Surface , Mdm::TorsionMonitor , Mdm::TupleMonitor , Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond , ### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1avd');

# retrieve the third chain in 1avd. These are the ligands
my $ligandsChain = $document->Chains->[2];

# select this chain
$ligandsChain->Select();

# select all amino acids that are within 3 angstrom of the ligands
$document->SelectByRadius( 3.0, 'AminoAcid' );

printf("Selected objects: %d\n", $document->SelectedObjects->Count );

# de-select the ligands chain so that the remaining selection
# is just the amino acid residues in the vicinity of the ligands
$ligandsChain->Deselect();

## DeselectAll function

### Applies to

The DeselectAll function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document , Sdm::Alignment , Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the DeselectAll function

#### Instance

$object->DeselectAll();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document Sdm::Alignment Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence Sdm::Sequence |

#### Command

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document Sdm::Alignment Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence Sdm::Sequence |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript , SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to select or deselect all MDM objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

print "Selecting all objects...\n\n";
$document->SelectAll();

my $selection = $document->SelectedObjects();
printf "%s selection %d\n" , $document->ModelName, $selection->Count;
my $count = 0;
foreach my $atom (@$selection)
{
printf "%d %s\n",++$count, $atom->Name;
}

$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

print "De-selecting all objects...\n";

$document->DeselectAll();
$document->UpdateViews();

my $selection = $document->SelectedObjects();
printf "%s selection %d\n" , $document->ModelName, $selection->Count;
```

## DeselectByProperty function

### Description

Mdm::Document

### Using the DeselectByProperty function

#### Instance

$object->DeselectByProperty( <description> );

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use the Mdm::Color object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1CRN.pdb" );
die "Failed to open MDM document." unless $document;

my $chain = $document->AminoAcidChains->Item(0);
die "Molecule contains no chains." unless $chain;

# This example assumes the protein display is on.
# Ensure this is the case here.
$document->SelectByProperty('Atom Name="*"');
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleAtomStick);
$document->DeselectAll();
$chain->DisplayStyle = Mdm::styleProteinRibbonTube;

print "Select cysteine residues and color them orange...\n\n";
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="CYS.*" ; Atom Name="*"');
my $cysteines = $document->SelectedObjects();
die "No cysteine residues." unless ($cysteines && $cysteines->Count > 0);
my $color = Mdm::Color::Create();
$color->Red = 255;
$color->Green = 200;
$color->Blue = 0;
$document->SetColor($color);
$document->DeselectAll();

print "Coloring the ribbon pseudo-transparent...\n\n";
my $chain = $document->Chains()->Item(0);
my $color = Mdm::Color::Create();
$color->Red = 0;
$color->Green = 255;
$color->Blue = 0;
$color->Alpha = 128;
$chain->Color($color);

print "Coloring the background dark blue...\n\n";
my $bkColor = Mdm::Color::Create();
$bkColor->Red = 0;
$bkColor->Green = 0;
$bkColor->Blue = 100;
$document->BackgroundColor = $bkColor;
```

'TCTAGAGTAACATTTAGAATTAAGGTGGGAAATTATCTTAAAATCT' );

my $title =
'Nonfixed duplication containing the Adh gene and a truncated form '
. 'of the Adhr gene in the Drosophila funebris species group: different '
. 'modes of evolution of Adh relative to Adhr in Drosophila';

# Create publication object with sample data.
my $publication01 = Sdm::Publication::Create( 'Amador, A., Juan, E.',
$title, 'Molec. Biol. Evol.' );

# Create publication and add content separately.
my $publication02 = Sdm::Publication::Create();
$publication02->Authors = 'Amador, A., Juan, E.';
$publication02->Title = $title;
$publication02->Journal = 'Molec. Biol. Evol.';
$publication02->Reference = '16(11): 1439--1456 (1999)';
$publication02->PubMedId = '10555275';
$publication02->Comment = 'y13252';

#$publication02->Consortium = '';
#$publication02->DigitalObjectId = '';
#$publication02->MedlineId = '';
#$publication02->PubMedId = '';

# Associate publications with a sequence object.
# NOTE: To see the publications in Discovery Studio, double-click on the
# sequence in the sequence window to open a sequence annotation window.
# Publications are listed in the data table's Literature Citation tab.
$sequence->AddPublication($publication01);
$sequence->AddPublication($publication02);

my $publicationCount = $sequence->PublicationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $publicationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $publication = $sequence->Publication($index);
printf "%d: %s, %s. %s %s.\n",
$index + 1,
$publication->Authors,
$publication->Title,
$publication->Journal,
$publication->Reference;
}

$sequence->DeletePublication(0);
```

# DihedralAngle property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/dihedralangle_property.htm

## DihedralAngle property

### Description

DihedralAngle describes the current dihedral angle created by the atoms monitored by
the DihedralRestraint.

### Applies to

The DihedralAngle property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::DihedralRestraint

### Using the DihedralAngle property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->DihedralAngle;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::DihedralRestraint |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
my $restraint = $document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);

printf( "The current angle is: %.4f.\n ", $restraint->DihedralAngle );
print "The dihedral atom names are:\n";
my $atoms = $restraint->DihedralAtoms;

# loop over all dihedral atoms
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
my $atomName = $atom->Name;
print $atomName;
print "\n";
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Example filter_constraints
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Fix backbone atoms in sheet or helix
my $helicalBackboneAtoms = $document->FilterByProperty(
'Residue Secondary="Helix",Secondary="Sheet"; Atom label="CA",label="C",label="O",label="N"'
);
$document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($helicalBackboneAtoms);

# Add harmonic constraint on all backbone atoms in coils
my $coiledBackboneAtoms = $document->FilterByProperty(
'Residue Secondary="Coil";Atom label="CA",label="C",label="O",label="N"');
$document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint(
{ ArrayOfAtoms => $coiledBackboneAtoms, ForceConstant => 1.2 } );

# Add cross-strand distance restraint
{
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "THR2:CA" );
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "ILE34:CA" );
$document->CreateDistanceRestraint(
{
ArrayOfAtoms1 => $atom1,
ArrayOfAtoms2 => $atom2,
RMin => 2,
RMax => 5
}
);
}

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
{
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
$document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);
}

# Get arrays with for each type of constraint using the corresponding filters
# Note that the constraint filter includes constraints and restraints
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
my $fixedAtomConstraints = $document->FixedAtomConstraints;

# Note that the restraint filter includes dihedral, distance and harmonic restraints
my $restraints = $document->Restraints;
my $dihedralRestraints = $document->DihedralRestraints;
my $distanceRestraints = $document->DistanceRestraints;
my $harmonicRestraints = $document->HarmonicAtomRestraints;

# Print out total number of constraints, along with a list of their names
print "There are " . $constraints->Count . " constraints (\t";
foreach my $constraint (@$constraints)
{
my $name = $constraint->GetProperty("Name");
print "$name\t";
}

# Print out the number of each type of constraints
print ")\nout of which ";
print $restraints->Count . " are Restraints :\n";
print " " . $dihedralRestraints->Count . " DihedralRestraint(s)\n";
print " " . $distanceRestraints->Count . " DistanceRestraint(s)\n";
print " " . $harmonicRestraints->Count . " HarmonicAtomRestraint(s)\n";
print "and \n";
print " " . $fixedAtomConstraints->Count . "FixedAtomConstraint(s)\n";
```

# Disable function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/disable_function.htm

## Disable function

### Description

Disable disables an Mdm::Constraint . Disabled Mdm::Constraint objects cannot be selected when setting up a protocol. See also Enable.

### Applies to

The Disable function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Constraint , Mdm::DihedralRestraint , Mdm::DistanceRestraint , Mdm::FixedAtomConstraint , Mdm::HarmonicAtomRestraint , Mdm::Restraint

### Using the Disable function

#### Instance

$object->Disable();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Fix the backbone
my $backbone = FilterByString( $document, ':CA,C,N,O,HN,HA' );
my $fixed = $document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($backbone);

# Enable the constraint (this is not required, it is enabled by default)
$fixed->Enable();

# Fix the CB
my $backbone = FilterByString( $document, ':CB' );
my $restraint = $document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint($backbone);

# disable this constraint
$restraint->Disable();

# Loop over all constraints
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
foreach my $constraint (@$constraints)
{
print "Constraint: " . $constraint->Name . "\n";
if ( $constraint->IsEnabled )
{

# Highlight the enabled constraints in turn
$constraint->Color( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 0 ) );
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

# Reset color to default
$constraint->Color( $constraint->GetDefaultColor() );
}
}
```

# DiscoveryScript::Color class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/discoveryscript__color_class.htm

## DiscoveryScript::Color class

### Description

The DiscoveryScript::Color represents a set of red ( Red ),
green ( Green ), and blue ( Blue ) color
components and a blending value, alpha ( Alpha ).
The color components of red, green, and blue can be specified using Integer values between 0 and 255.

Alpha is the blending value. If the alpha component of the color is zero, the
color is considered fully transparent. If the alpha component is 255, the color is considered to be fully opaque. Values between one and 254 give an apparent transparency scaled by the alpha component.

Note that for values of alpha approaching zero, the graphics primitive is more
transparent. For increasing values of alpha, the graphics primitive is more opaque.
When a color is converted into a composite RGB value (e.g., a Windows COLORREF),
no blending is performed.

### Using the DiscoveryScript::Color object

The DiscoveryScript::Color object can be accessed via the DiscoveryScript package.

Alpha , Blue , ClassName , Green , Red

#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the MarkChiralityViolations function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Open a protein structure having D-amino acids so we see some violations.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1c4b.pdb' );

# This structure has multiple models - select just the first (we could also
# make a loop and check for violations in each model).
my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
$molecules->Item(0)->Select();

# Mark chirality violations.
my $pink = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 255, 200, 200 );
$document->MarkChiralityViolations($pink);

# Get the chirality violation monitors.
my $monitors =
$document->FilterByProperty('ProteinChiralityMonitor name="*"');

# Report the number of violations.
my $violationCount = $monitors->Count;
print "Structure has "
. $violationCount
. " CAlpha chirality violations.\n\n";

# Print a table of violations.
if ( $violationCount > 0 )
{
printf("Index\t Name\t\t Residue \n");
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $violationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);

printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Residues") );

$monitors->Item($index)->SetVisible;
}
}

$document->DeselectAll(); 
$document->UpdateViews();
```

#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to create a polydot object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $pointArray = Mdm::PointArray::Create();
my $colorArray = DiscoveryScript::ColorArray::Create();

# Generate 500 random points and colors.

{

);

$pointArray->AddItem($newPt);
$colorArray->AddItem($randColor);
}

$molecule->CreatePolydot(
{ ArrayOfDots => $pointArray, ArrayOfColors => $colorArray } );

# Find and name the polydot object.
my $polydotArray = $document->Polydots;
$polydotArray->Item(0)->Name('Point Cloud 1');
$document->FitView();
$document->UpdateViews();

## DiscoveryScript::ObjectMap class

### Description

The DiscoveryScript::ObjectMap represents a collection of DiscoveryScript::Objects.

### Using the DiscoveryScript::ObjectMap object

The DiscoveryScript::ObjectMap object can be accessed via the DiscoveryScript package.

#### Properties

ClassName , Count , FirstKey , IsEmpty , Item , ItemExists , NextKey

#### Functions

AddItem , ClearItems , DeleteItem , InsertItem , ReplaceItem

#### Used by

Filter

#### Derived from

DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to create a transparent surface.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '101m.pdb' );

# Select heme atoms.
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="HEM.*"; Atom label="*"');

# Create an array of all heme atoms.
my $hemeAtoms = $document->Filter( { Selected => 1 } )->Atoms;

# Create transparent surface around the heme group.
my $transparentSurface =
$document->CreateTransparentSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential,
1.3, 0.6 );

$transparentSurface->IsBackSideColorEnabled(True);
$transparentSurface->IsBackSideTransparencyEnabled(True);

# Also create wiremesh surface around the heme group.
my $wiremeshSurface =
$document->CreateWiremeshSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential, 2.0 );

print "Surface area: "
. $transparentSurface->Area . "\n"
. "Surface Volume: "
. $transparentSurface->Volume . "\n";
print "Surface probe radius: "
. $transparentSurface->ProbeRadius . "\n"
. "Transparency Level: "
. $transparentSurface->TransparencyLevel . "\n";

# Select all atoms within 6A of the heme and the surface.
$document->SelectByRadius( 6.0, 'Atom' );
$transparentSurface->Select();

# Show only the heme and neighboring atoms (other than water).
$document->FitView();
$document->InvertSelection();
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue name="HOH.*"; Atom label="*"');
$document->Hide();
$document->DeselectAll();

# Display the wiremesh surface with delay.
sleep(2);
$wiremeshSurface->SetVisible();
```

# DiscoveryScript::RealArray class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/discoveryscript__realarray_class.htm

## DiscoveryScript::RealArray class

### Description

The DiscoveryScript::RealArray represents an array of real numbers.

### Using the DiscoveryScript::RealArray object

The DiscoveryScript::RealArray object can be accessed via the DiscoveryScript package.

#### Properties

ClassName , Count , IsEmpty , Item

#### Functions

AddItem , ClearItems , DeleteItem , DiscoveryScript::RealArray::Create , InsertItem , ReplaceItem

#### Returned by

CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd , CalculateAllProteinRmsd , CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd , CalculateCAlphaRmsd , CalculateDockedRmsd , CalculateDockedRmsdFromReferencePose , CalculateDockedRmsdFromXRayStructure , CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd , CalculateMainChainRmsd , CalculateNucleicAcidBackboneRmsd , CalculateNucleicAcidBaseRmsd , CalculateNucleicAcidRmsd , CalculateOtherResidueRmsd , CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd , CalculateSideChainRmsd , DiscoveryScript::RealArray::Create , ObjectRadii , SequenceIdentityArray , SequenceSimilarityArray , SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs , SuperimposeProteinByAlignment

#### Derived from

DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use superimposition functions
# and RMSD calculation functions for amino acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load 2rcs (an unligated antibody) from PDB.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '2rcs.pdb' );

# Load 1aj7 (a ligated antibody having the same sequence as 2crs) from PDB.
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

my $molecule2rcs = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[1];

my $hv2rcs = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 2rcs H chain V domain
my $hv1aj7 = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 1aj7 H chain V domain

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $molecule2rcs->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv2rcs->AddItem($aminoAcid);

$aminoAcid = $molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv1aj7->AddItem($aminoAcid);
}

# Show the transformation matrix which would superimpose the Vh
# domains by C-alpha atoms. This does not alter the coordinates
# of either structure.
my $matrix = $document->GetSuperimposeProteinMatrix( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
print "Transformation matrix:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 4 ; ++$i )
{
print "\t";
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < 4 ; ++$j )
{
printf "%.3f ", $matrix->GetEntry( $i, $j );
}
print "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms
my $rmsd = $document->SuperimposeProtein( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
printf "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms: %.3f\n\n", $rmsd;

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD. Note that by default the functions return an
# array of per-residue RMSD values, finishing with the overall RMSD
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it in which case the value will be zero. This can happen
# for unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation
# only for selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the
# required atoms for the requested type of calculation. 
# If you do not want per-residue RMSDs, set the 4th parameter ResidueReport
# False. In this case the array will only contain the overall RMSD.
# In this example, the all protein rmsd has no residue values calculated
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True, False );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item(0);
print "\n";

#Show that the all protein array contains just the overall RMSD.
printf "Number of values returned for all protein is %d\n", $apRmsd->Count();

# Demonstrating that the array is for all residues plus overall value not
# just selected and that as the first chain(L) is unselected its values
# are 0.
printf "Number of values returned for sidechains is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0), $scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

#Create a C-Alpha monitor
my $caMonitor = $document->CreateCAlphaMonitor();

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs before superimposing.\n";
if ($cAlphaPairs->Count > 0) {
printf "The first C-alpha to C-alpha pair distance is %.3f Angstroms.\n",
$cAlphaPairs->Item(0)->Distance;
}

#Lets do it for all matching atoms just to show the argument
my $rmsdByCA =
$document->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( $document->Molecules(), $caMonitor,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingAllAtoms );

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs after superimposing.\n";

#The values returned are like for Superimpose By Alignment - the first value
# is ref-ref (ie 0) then ref-mover for each superimposed molecule.
my $numVal = $rmsdByCA->Count();
printf( "Number of values returned for SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs %d\n",
$numVal );
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $numVal ; ++$i )
{
printf( "RMSD %d is %f\n", $i, $rmsdByCA->[$i] );
}

# use the filter function to retrieve the CAlpha atoms
my $cAlphaMonitors = $document->CAlphaMonitors;
foreach my $m (@$cAlphaMonitors)
{
print $m->ClassName ." filter entries: " . $m->CAlphaPairs->Count. "\n";
}

print "Finished Superimpose Script Example\n";
```

### Applies to

The DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create function can be used with the following objects:

DiscoveryScript::StringArray

### Using the DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create function

#### Static

my $stringarrayObject = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::StringArray |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use alignment superimposition functions and
# RMSD calculation functions for amino acids or non-standard residues.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1gaf.pdb' );

my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1gaf = $document->Molecules->[1];

# H chain V domains only
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
$molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
$molecule1gaf->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
}

my $Sequence1aj7 = $molecule1aj7->AminoAcidSequence;
my $Sequence1gaf = $molecule1gaf->AminoAcidSequence;
my $sequences = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1aj7);
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1gaf);

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms. The function returns an array
# of RMSD values between the reference and all molecules, starting with itself.
my $rmsds =
$document->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment( $document->Molecules, $sequences,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms, True );

print "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $document->Molecules->Count() ; ++$i )
{
print "\t"
. $document->Molecules->[$i]->Name . " to "
. $molecule1aj7->Name . ": ";
printf "%.3f\n", $rmsds->[$i];
}
print "\n";

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD
# Note that these functions return an array of real numbers. These are the
# per residue RMSD values plus, in the last element, the overall RMSD.
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it (the value will be zero). This can happen for
# unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation only for
# selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the required atoms for
# the requested type of calculation.
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item( $apRmsd->Count() - 1 );
print "\n";

# This demonstrates that the array is for all residues plus overall
# value, not just selected, and that as the first chain(L) is
# unselected (its values are 0).
printf "Number of values returned is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain.
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H chain.
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

# Get antigen NPE from 1aj7.
my $antigen1 = $document->Molecules->[0]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Get antigen NPE from 1gaf.
my $antigen2 = $document->Molecules->[1]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Copy antigen residues to a new document.
my $tmpDocument = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $tmpMolecule1 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen1Copy = $antigen1->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen1Copy, $tmpMolecule1 );
my $tmpMolecule2 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen2Copy = $antigen2->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen2Copy, $tmpMolecule2 );

$tmpDocument->FitView();

# Calculate NPE RMSD.
my $rmsd =
$tmpDocument->CalculateOtherResidueRmsd( $tmpMolecule1, $tmpMolecule2 );
printf "NPE RMSD: %.3f\n", $rmsd->[1];
```

# DiscoveryScript package

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/discoveryscript_package.htm

## DiscoveryScript package

### Description

DiscoveryScript provides functions and data structures for accessing
Discovery Studio data using client or server-side scripts. This package
is extended by the DiscoveryStudioScript to include client-only
functions.

### Using the DiscoveryScript package

Access to the DiscoveryScript API is through the Perl use directive:

```text
use strict;
use DiscoveryScript;
```

The strict directive is optional, but strongly recommended as it restricts
the use of unsafe constructs. All available classes will be imported from the DiscoveryScript module.

#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use DiscoveryScript;

my $messageBoxResult = DiscoveryScript::MessageBox(
"An example message with Yes and No buttons to allow interactive user input.\nPlease click a button",
"More Detailed information about the message should appear here.\n",
DiscoveryScript::messageBoxFlagsYesNo,
DiscoveryScript::messageBoxIconInfo
);

if ( $messageBoxResult eq DiscoveryScript::messageBoxResultYes )
{
print "You clicked Yes.\n";
}
elsif ( $messageBoxResult eq DiscoveryScript::messageBoxResultNo )
{
print "You clicked No.\n";
}
elsif ( $messageBoxResult eq DiscoveryScript::messageBoxResultCancel )
{
print "You closed the window without answering the question.\n";
}

# DisplayAll function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/displayall_function.htm

## DisplayAll function

### Description

DisplayAll displays the full extents of an isosurface.

### Applies to

The DisplayAll function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Isosurface

### Using the DisplayAll function

#### Instance

$object->DisplayAll();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Isosurface |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
print "It operates on a document with grid data\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1. Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2. Open a structure with grid data\n";
print
" (for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
print " 3. Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}
else
{

}

# Connect to an Sdm::Document from the last active sequence window
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

# Get array with all isosurfaces using Isosurfaces filter
my $isosurfaces = $document->Isosurfaces;

if ( $isosurfaces->Count == 0 )
{
print "To run this script, please open a structure with grid data.\n";
print "(for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
exit;
}

$document->ShowAll();
my $chain1 = $document->Chains->[0];

# Get the first isosurface
my $isosurface = $isosurfaces->[0];

# Create a isosurfaces at 0.5 and 0.4 isovalue
my $newContour = $isosurface->CreateIsosurface(0.5);
my $newContour2 = $isosurface->CreateIsosurface(0.4);

# Set the context array for the first surface
$chain1->Select();
$newContour->DisplayStyle(Mdm::isosurfaceStyleSolid);
$newContour->ContextAtomArray( $chain1->Atoms );
$document->UpdateViews();

sleep(1);

# Set Display extend for second isosurface
$document->DeselectAll();

# Pick 2 arbitrary atoms and get their coordinates
my $atom1 = $document->Atoms->[4324];
my $atom2 = $document->Atoms->[5100];
$atom1->Select();
$atom2->Select();
my $xyz1 = $atom1->XYZ;
my $xyz2 = $atom2->XYZ;
print $xyz1->X . "\t" . $xyz1->Y . "\t" . $xyz1->Z . "\n";
print $xyz2->X . "\t" . $xyz2->Y . "\t" . $xyz2->Z . "\n";

# Set style to isosurfaceStyleQuadMesh
$newContour2->DisplayStyle(Mdm::isosurfaceStyleQuadMesh);
$newContour2->SetDisplayExtent( $xyz1, $xyz2 );
$document->UpdateViews();

sleep(1);

# Display full extend of second isosurface
$newContour2->DisplayAll();
```

## DisplayLocation property

### Description

DisplayLocation specifies where are Mdm::MembraneOrientationMonitor is displayed.
See enum Mdm::MembraneOrientationDisplayLocation for additional information.

### Applies to

The DisplayLocation property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::MembraneOrientationMonitor

### Using the DisplayLocation property

#### Get

my $membraneorientationdisplaylocationEnum = $object->DisplayLocation;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $membraneorientationdisplaylocationEnum | | | enum Mdm::MembraneOrientationDisplayLocation |
| $object | | | Mdm::MembraneOrientationMonitor |

#### Set

$object->DisplayLocation = <location>;

$object->DisplayLocation( <location> );

$object->DisplayLocation( { Location => <location> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <location> | Required | | enum Mdm::MembraneOrientationDisplayLocation |
| $object | | | Mdm::MembraneOrientationMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use properties of the MembraneOrientationMonitor
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load structure of BOVINE RHODOPSIN, 1f88 and keep only first chain
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# "Guess" some value for the membrane position
my $center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, -3.2 );
my $normal = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.521, 0.106, 0.847 );

my $membrane =
$document->CreateMembrane( $center, $normal, 60.0, 60.0, 30.0 );

$document->SetParent( $molecule, $membrane );

my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms();

# Illustrate on how to use MembraneOrientationMonitor preferences
my $membraneOrientation =
$molecule->CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor( $membrane, $atoms,
Mdm::objectCentered, Mdm::referenceAxisZ );

$document->UpdateViews();

my $monitors = $document->MembraneOrientationMonitors;
print "Number of membrane monitors: ". $monitors->Count. "\n";

my $membranes = $document->Membranes;
print "Number of membranes: ". $membranes->Count. "\n";

sleep(2);

$membraneOrientation->DisplayLocation = Mdm::membraneCentered;
$membraneOrientation->ProteinReferenceAxis = Mdm::referenceAxisX;
```

# DisplayMatrix property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/displaymatrix_property.htm

## DisplayMatrix property

### Description

DisplayMatrix specifies the view transformation (as an Mdm::Matrix4x4 )
of objects in the Mdm::Document .

### Applies to

The DisplayMatrix property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the DisplayMatrix property

#### Get

my $matrix4x4Object = $object->DisplayMatrix;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $matrix4x4Object | | | Mdm::Matrix4x4 |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Set

$object->DisplayMatrix = <matrix>;

$object->DisplayMatrix( <matrix> );

$object->DisplayMatrix( { Matrix => <matrix> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <matrix> | Required | | Mdm::Matrix4x4 |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

# This subroutine prints the contents of a 3x3 or 4x4 matrix.
sub PrintMatrix($)
{
my ($matrix) = @_;
my $size = 3;
$size = 4 if ( $matrix->ClassName eq 'Mdm::Matrix4x4' );

for ( my $row = 0 ; $row < $size ; ++$row )
{
for ( my $column = 0 ; $column < $size ; ++$column )
{
printf " %8.3f", $matrix->GetEntry( $row, $column );
}
print "\n";
}
print "\n";
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

my $displaymatrix = $document->DisplayMatrix;

print "Matrix:\n";

PrintMatrix($displaymatrix);
```

#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of various atom properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

# Define atom properties to list.
# This may be specified on the command line.
my $residueAtomName = 'THR2:CA';
if ( @ARGV != 0 )
{
($residueAtomName) = @ARGV;
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Get the specified atom.
my $atoms = FilterByString( $document, $residueAtomName );
