```text
if ( $atoms->Count == 0 );

my $atom = $atoms->[0];

# Print various atom properties. In the DiscoveryStudio client, the
# output will appear in the output pane of the scripting window.
print "List of properties for atom $residueAtomName:\n\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
print 'Element: ' . $atom->Element . "\n";
print 'Element Name: ' . $atom->ElementName . "\n";
print 'Element Symbol: ' . $atom->ElementSymbol . "\n";
print 'Mass: ' . $atom->Mass . "\n";
print 'Atomic number: ' . $atom->AtomicNumber . "\n";
print 'Charge: ' . $atom->Charge . "\n";
print 'Formal Charge: '
. $atom->FormalCharge->Numerator . "/"
. $atom->FormalCharge->Denominator . "\n";

print 'VDW Radius: ' . $atom->VdwRadius . "\n";
print 'Covalent Radius: ' . $atom->CovalentRadius . "\n";
print 'Chirality: ' . $atom->Chirality . "\n";
print 'Bond count: ' . $atom->BondCount . "\n";
print 'Bonding radius: ' . $atom->BondingRadius . "\n";
print 'Hybridization: ' . $atom->Hybridization . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen Count: ' . $atom->HydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'ImplicitHydrogen Count: ' . $atom->ImplicitHydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Acceptor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondAcceptor . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Donor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondDonor . "\n";
print 'Isotropic Displacement: ' . $atom->IsotropicDisplacement . "\n";
print 'Is Terminal Hydrogen: ' . $atom->IsTerminalHydrogen . "\n";
print 'Is Valence Satisfied: ' . $atom->IsValenceSatisfied . "\n";
print 'Lone Pair Count: ' . $atom->LonePairCount . "\n";
print 'Valence Count: ' . $atom->ValenceCount . "\n";
print 'Occupancy: ' . $atom->Occupancy . "\n";

printf "\n%s:\n", 'Display Properties';
print 'DisplayStyle: ' . $atom->DisplayStyle . "\n";
print 'Ball Size: ' . $atom->BallSize . "\n";
print 'Ball Size Default: ' . $atom->BallSizeDefault . "\n";

print 'CPK Scale Default: ' . $atom->CPKScaleDefault . "\n";

print 'Stick Radius Default: ' . $atom->StickRadiusDefault . "\n";
```

### Applies to

Mdm::BondLengthViolationMonitor , Mdm::Bump , Mdm::CAlphaPair , Mdm::CAlphaViolationMonitor , Mdm::DistanceFeature , Mdm::DistanceMonitor , Mdm::DistanceRestraint , Mdm::HydrogenBond , Mdm::Neighbor , Mdm::Nonbond , Mdm::PiBond

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <distance> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9INS.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleAtomLine } );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $sequence = $molecule->AminoAcidSequence;
print "AminoAcidSequence: $sequence\n";

my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
my $aminoAcid1 = $aminoAcids->Item(0);
my $aminoAcid2 = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
my $aminoAcid3 = $aminoAcids->Item(2);

my $distance = $document->CreateDistanceMonitor( $aminoAcid1->CAlpha, $aminoAcid2->CAlpha );

printf "Distance between CAlpha atoms of $aminoAcid1->{Name} and $aminoAcid2->{Name}: %8.3f\n", $distance->Distance;

my $angle = $document->CreateAngleMonitor( $aminoAcid1->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid1->AmideNitrogen, $aminoAcid1->CAlpha );

printf "Angle between amide carbon, nitrogen, and CAlpha atoms of $aminoAcid1->{Name}: %8.3f\n", $angle->Angle;

my $phiTorsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$aminoAcid1->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid2->AmideNitrogen,
$aminoAcid2->CAlpha, $aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon
);

my $psiTorsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$aminoAcid2->AmideNitrogen, $aminoAcid2->CAlpha,
$aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid3->AmideNitrogen
);

print "Amino acid $aminoAcid2->{Name}: ";
printf "phi = %8.3f, psi = %8.3f\n", $phiTorsion->Angle, $psiTorsion->Angle;
```

# DistanceCutoff property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/distancecutoff_property.htm

## DistanceCutoff property

### Description

When determining pi-sigma interactions,
the distances between carbon atoms bearing explicit or implicit hydrogen atoms and the centers of pi rings must be
within the Distance Cutoff (default 4 Å).
When determining pi-cation interactions, the distance between each cation and
the centroid of each pi ring is tested to find those within 1 Å more than the
Distance Cutoff (i.e., 7 Å by default). In such cases, the distance between
the cation and the mean plane of the ring is determined to find those within
the Distance Cutoff (default 6 Å).

### Applies to

The DistanceCutoff property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::PiCationMonitor , Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor

### Using the DistanceCutoff property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->DistanceCutoff;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::PiCationMonitor Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor |

#### Set

$object->DistanceCutoff = <distance>;

$object->DistanceCutoff( <distance> );

$object->DistanceCutoff( { Distance => <distance> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <distance> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::PiCationMonitor Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script shows how to create pi interaction monitors.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1kim.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Creates pi interaction monitors
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

#if no array of atoms is passed in then the monitor is created
#for the whole molecule (or other object).
my $pipiMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor();
my $piCationMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiCationMonitor();
my $piSigmaMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiSigmaMonitor();

$pipiMonitor->Name = "Pi-Pi";
$piCationMonitor->Name = "Pi-Cation";
$piSigmaMonitor->Name = "Pi-Sigma";

my $piPiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piPiInteractionCount = $piPiInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piPiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

# Change criteria settings to non-default values.
$piCationMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piCationMonitor->MinimumAngle = 60.0;
my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule\n";

$piSigmaMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->MinimumAngle = 30.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->AngleDeviation = 15.0;
my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

$pipiMonitor->MaximumCenterDistance = 7.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumClosestAtomDistance = 4.0;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumLambda = 20.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumTheta = 45.;
my $pipiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount = $pipiInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $pipiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piInteractions = $molecule->PiInteractionMonitors();
my $piCount = $piInteractions->Count();
print "\nThere are " . $piCount . " pi interaction monitors: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $piCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $piInteractions->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Interactions") );
}

#If we want to limit the scope of the monitoring, we can pass in
#an array of atoms. This is similar to creating a monitor from the UI
# when atoms are selected. Pi interactions will then be calculated within
#these, and between these and the parent object
my $residue = FilterByString( $document, "THM1" )->Item(0);
my $atom_array = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $atoms = $residue->Atoms();
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atoms->Count() ; ++$index )
{
$atom_array->AddItem( $atoms->Item($index) );
}
my $pipiMonitor2 = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor($atom_array);
my $pipiInteractions2 = $pipiMonitor2->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount2 = $pipiInteractions2->Count();
print "Number of pi-pi interactions between "
. $residue->Name()
. " and the rest of the molecule: "
. $pipiInteractionCount2 . "\n";

my $picatmonitors = $document->PiCationMonitors;
print "Number of pi-cation monitors: ". $picatmonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pipimonitors = $document->PiPiMonitors;
print "Number of pi-pi monitors: ". $pipimonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pisigmonitors = $document->PiSigmaMonitors;
print "Number of pi-sigma monitors: ". $pisigmonitors->Count . "\n";
```

### Using the DistanceRestraints filter

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->DistanceRestraints;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Example filter_constraints
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Fix backbone atoms in sheet or helix
my $helicalBackboneAtoms = $document->FilterByProperty(
'Residue Secondary="Helix",Secondary="Sheet"; Atom label="CA",label="C",label="O",label="N"'
);
$document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($helicalBackboneAtoms);

# Add harmonic constraint on all backbone atoms in coils
my $coiledBackboneAtoms = $document->FilterByProperty(
'Residue Secondary="Coil";Atom label="CA",label="C",label="O",label="N"');
$document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint(
{ ArrayOfAtoms => $coiledBackboneAtoms, ForceConstant => 1.2 } );

# Add cross-strand distance restraint
{
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "THR2:CA" );
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "ILE34:CA" );
$document->CreateDistanceRestraint(
{
ArrayOfAtoms1 => $atom1,
ArrayOfAtoms2 => $atom2,
RMin => 2,
RMax => 5
}
);
}

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
{
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
$document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);
}

# Get arrays with for each type of constraint using the corresponding filters
# Note that the constraint filter includes constraints and restraints
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
my $fixedAtomConstraints = $document->FixedAtomConstraints;

# Note that the restraint filter includes dihedral, distance and harmonic restraints
my $restraints = $document->Restraints;
my $dihedralRestraints = $document->DihedralRestraints;
my $distanceRestraints = $document->DistanceRestraints;
my $harmonicRestraints = $document->HarmonicAtomRestraints;

# Print out total number of constraints, along with a list of their names
print "There are " . $constraints->Count . " constraints (\t";
foreach my $constraint (@$constraints)
{
my $name = $constraint->GetProperty("Name");
print "$name\t";
}

# Print out the number of each type of constraints
print ")\nout of which ";
print $restraints->Count . " are Restraints :\n";
print " " . $dihedralRestraints->Count . " DihedralRestraint(s)\n";
print " " . $distanceRestraints->Count . " DistanceRestraint(s)\n";
print " " . $harmonicRestraints->Count . " HarmonicAtomRestraint(s)\n";
print "and \n";
print " " . $fixedAtomConstraints->Count . "FixedAtomConstraint(s)\n";
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
#This is used for the script apis
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $temp = 0;
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('4ins');

#By default, the script returns string containing a csv file of properties for the predicted disulfides.
#Only new disulfides are found, for any chain combination, minimum sequence separation 5,
#maximum energy 10.0
# i.e. default args are novelDisulfidesOnly, anyChainDisulfides, 5, 10.0, true will use this one to show how to get the residues/bonds

my $csvFile=$document->PredictDisulfides();

#save the csv file
my $name=$document->ModelName();
my $fileName=$name . "Predicted_New_Disulfides.csv";
open FILE, '>' . $fileName;
print FILE $csvFile;
close FILE;

my $molecules=$document->Molecules();

#note that if validation of existing disulfides is performed (by using Mdm::existingDisulfidesOnly#or Mdm::novelAndExistingDisulfides then a second molecule containing the modelled disulfide
#bridges and with additional properties on the bond and molecule 

my $numMols=$molecules->Count; 
if($numMols == 1){

$document->DeselectAll();
my $molecule=$molecules->Item(0);
my $residuePairsAssembly = $molecule->Filter(
{ Type=>"Assembly", Property => "Name", Name => "Predicted Disulfide Bridge Residues" } );
if($residuePairsAssembly->Count() == 1){
print "Potential residue pairs for mutation to cysteine to form disulfide bridge in ".$molecule->Name . ": \n";
my $residuePairs=$residuePairsAssembly->Item(0)->Groups();
foreach my $residuePair (@$residuePairs) {
my $residuePairList=$residuePair->ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder();
#should be 2 residues in here
if($residuePairList->Count == 2){
my $residue1 = $residuePairList->Item(0);
my $residue2 = $residuePairList->Item(1);
print "Group " . $residuePair->Name . " contains residues: ". $residue1->Name . " and " . $residue2->Name . "\n";
}
}
}

#this should now also contain predicted site objects from which we can extract more properties
print "Sites for mutation to cysteine\n";
my $sites = $document->DisulfideBridgeSites;
my $numSites = $sites->Count();
print $numSites . " sites\n";
for(my $index = 0; $index < $numSites; ++$index){
my $site=$sites->Item($index);
my $label = $site->Name;
my $score = $site->GetProperty("Score");
my $energy = $site->GetProperty("Energy");
my $badContacts = $site->GetProperty("Bad Contacts");
my $depth = $site->GetProperty("Residue Depth");
my $mobility = $site->GetProperty("Thermal Mobility");
my $sep = $site->GetProperty("Sequence Separation");
my $volchange = $site->GetProperty("Volume Change");
my $env = $site->GetProperty("Environment");
my $SA = $site->GetProperty("Solvent Accessibility");
my $chi3 = $site->GetProperty("Chi3");
print " site " . $label . " score " . $score . " energy " . $energy . " Bad contacts " . $badContacts ." residue depth " . $depth . " mobility " . $mobility . " sep " . $sep . " volchange " . $volchange . " env " . $env . " SA " . $SA . " chi3 " . $chi3 . "\n";

my $SG1Coord = $site->SG1Coord;
my $SG2Coord = $site->SG2Coord;
print " SG coordinates (" . $SG1Coord->X . ", " . $SG1Coord->Y . ", " . $SG1Coord->Z . ") and " .
"(" . $SG2Coord->X . ", " . $SG2Coord->Y . ", " . $SG2Coord->Z . ")\n";
my $residues = $site->ResiduesToMutate;
if($residues->Count == 2){
print "residue 1 " . $residues->Item(0)->Name . " residue 2 " . $residues->Item(1)->Name . "\n";
}else{
print " error - site should contain two residues\n";
}

#create S-S bridge from a site - the command works on any selected DisulfideBridgeSite
if($score > 80.0){
print "Score " . $score . " - Creating S-S bridge\n"; 
$site->Select();
$document->CreateDisulfideBridges();
$site->Deselect();
}

}

}
```

# Script Window Display Style dialog

## Script Window Display Style dialog

You can use the Script Window Display Style dialog to change the way text is displayed in the Script Window.

### Font

Font face: Changes the font used to display text in the Script Window's Script, Output and Arguments Views.

Font size: Changes the size of the font used to display text in the Script Window's Script, Output, and Arguments Views.

### Tabs

Indent size: Sets the number of spaces between tab stops in the Script Window.

Insert spaces: When selected, spaces are used to fill empty areas between tab stops in the Script Window.

Keep tabs: When selected, tabs are used to fill empty areas between tab stops in the Script Window.

### Indenting

None: When selected, indenting for new lines must be performed by the user.

Auto: When selected, new lines are started at the same starting point as the preceding line.

Smart: When selected, new lines are positioned to fit the Perl code context.

### Access methods

| Menu | View \| Display Style... |
| --- | --- |
| View toolbar | Display Style |
| Context menu | Display Style... |
| Keyboard shortcut | CTRL+D |

# Script Window Find Panel

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/dl_find-panel.htm

## Script Window Find Panel

The Find Panel in the Script Window allows you to search for occurrences of a text string in the 
active script document. Matches are highlighted in the Script Window.

For convenience, the Find Panel is embedded in the Script Window itself so that you can 
easily combine searching and editing.

The Find Panel contains the following controls:

Find: Specify the text string to be searched for.

Next: Finds the next instance of the specified text string in the active script document. When the search reaches the 
start or end of the script, it will restart from the bottom or top of the document, as appropriate.

Previous: Finds the previous instance of the specified text string in the active script document.

Match case: When checked, indicates that the specified text string will be matched only if the capitalization of every 
letter in the string in the currently active script document is the same as that specified in the Find what field.

Match words: When checked, indicates that the specified text string will be matched only if the string in the currently 
active script document represents a whole word bounded by white space or punctuation.

### Access methods

| Menu | Edit \| Find |
| --- | --- |
| Context menu | Find |

Using the Script Window

# Replace dialog

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/dl_replace.htm

## Replace dialog

The Replace dialog allows you to search for and substitute occurrences of a text string in the active script document. Matches are highlighted in 
the Script Window.

Find what: Specify the text string to be searched for.

Replace with: Specify the text string that will replace instances of the specified search string in the active script 
document.

Match whole word only: When checked, indicates that the specified text string will be matched only if the string in the 
currently active script document represents a whole word bounded by white space or punctuation.

Match case: When checked, indicates that the specified text string will be matched only if the capitalization of every 
letter in the string in the currently active script document is the same as that specified in the Find what field.

Find Next: Finds the next instance of the specified text string in the active script document. When the search reaches 
the start or end of the script, it will restart from the bottom or top of the document, as appropriate.

Replace: Replaces the selected text in the currently active script document with the text string specified in the Replace with field.

Replace All: Replaces all instances of the specified search string in the currently active script document with the 
text string specified in the Replace with field.

### Access methods

| Context menu | Replace... |
| --- | --- |

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Example for DockedProteinPoseAssembly Properties
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing docked protein poses\n";
print " 3 Enter a cluster ID in the Arguments tab\n";
print " 4 Run this script within Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

# This example script assumes the last active document contains Docked Protein Poses
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ($document);

# get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter
my $poseGroups = $document->DockedProteinPoseAssemblies;
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ( $poseGroups->Count > 0 );

# store the first pose group in a variable
# Note: there should be only one pose group object in a document
my $poseGroup = $poseGroups->Item(0);

# Get the receptor for the docked pose group
my $receptor = $poseGroup->Receptor;

# Copy receptor center into a point variable
my $receptorCenter = $poseGroup->ReceptorCenter;

# Print information
print "Receptor " . $receptor->Name . ",";
printf "is centered at coordinates (%5.2f,%5.2f,%5.2f)\n",
$receptorCenter->X, $receptorCenter->Y,
$receptorCenter->Z;

# Color receptor red
print "Coloring receptor red....\n\n";
$receptor->Select();
$document->SetColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 255, 0, 0 ) );

# Get the ligand for the docked pose group
my $ligand = $poseGroup->Ligand;

# Copy receptor center into a point variable
my $receptorCenter = $poseGroup->LigandCenter;
print "ligand " . $ligand->Name . ",";
printf "is centered at coordinates (%5.2f,%5.2f,%5.2f)\n",
$receptorCenter->X, $receptorCenter->Y,
$receptorCenter->Z;

# Color receptor blue
$ligand->Select();
print "Coloring ligand blue....\n\n";
$document->SetColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 0, 255 ) );

# Get the ligand for the docked pose group
my $angle = $poseGroup->StartingAngles;
printf "Starting angles used for docking: %5.2f\t%5.2f\t%5.2f\n", $angle->X,
$angle->Y, $angle->Z;
```

# DomainCount property

Source type: HTML

## DomainCount property

### Description

DomainCount specifies the number of chain domains in an Sdm::Alignment object.

### Applies to

The DomainCount property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the DomainCount property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->DomainCount;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate use of domain boundaries.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

# Connect to an open Sequence Window in Chain View layout.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(SdmModelType);
die "Please connect to a Sequence Window in Chain View layout."
unless $document
&& $document->Alignment
&& $document->Alignment->DomainCount > 0;

my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

# Get the number of domains
my $domainCount = $alignment->DomainCount;
print 'Sequence Window contains ' . $domainCount . " domains.\n";

for ( my $domain = 0 ; $domain < $domainCount ; ++$domain )
{
print 'Domain ' . $domain . "\n";

# Get the 0-based starting domain boundary.
my $domainStart = $alignment->DomainStart($domain);
print ' Starts at column ' . ( $domainStart + 1 ) . "\n";

# Get the 0-based ending domain boundary.
my $domainEnd = $alignment->DomainEnd($domain);
print ' Ends at column ' . $domainEnd . "\n";

# List the aligned chain sequence
print ' Chain symbols: ';
for ( my $column = $domainStart ; $column < $domainEnd ; ++$column )
{
print $alignment->Sequence(0)->Residue($column)->Symbol;
}
print "\n\n";
}

# If uncommented, this function will remove all domain boundaries.
#$alignment->RemoveDomainBoundaries();
$document->UpdateViews();

print "Done\n";
```

# DomainStart property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/domainstart_property.htm

## DomainStart property

### Description

DomainStart specifies the first alignment column for the indicated chain domain as a 0-based index.

### Applies to

The DomainStart property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the DomainStart property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->DomainStart( <index> );

my $integerValue = $object->DomainStart( { Index => <index> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate use of domain boundaries.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

# Connect to an open Sequence Window in Chain View layout.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(SdmModelType);
die "Please connect to a Sequence Window in Chain View layout."
unless $document
&& $document->Alignment
&& $document->Alignment->DomainCount > 0;

my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

# Get the number of domains
my $domainCount = $alignment->DomainCount;
print 'Sequence Window contains ' . $domainCount . " domains.\n";

for ( my $domain = 0 ; $domain < $domainCount ; ++$domain )
{
print 'Domain ' . $domain . "\n";

# Get the 0-based starting domain boundary.
my $domainStart = $alignment->DomainStart($domain);
print ' Starts at column ' . ( $domainStart + 1 ) . "\n";

# Get the 0-based ending domain boundary.
my $domainEnd = $alignment->DomainEnd($domain);
print ' Ends at column ' . $domainEnd . "\n";

# List the aligned chain sequence
print ' Chain symbols: ';
for ( my $column = $domainStart ; $column < $domainEnd ; ++$column )
{
print $alignment->Sequence(0)->Residue($column)->Symbol;
}
print "\n\n";
}

# If uncommented, this function will remove all domain boundaries.
#$alignment->RemoveDomainBoundaries();
$document->UpdateViews();

print "Done\n";
```

, Mdm::DisulfideBridgeSite , Mdm::DockedProteinPoseAssembly , Mdm::Document , Mdm::DonorFeature , Mdm::ExclusionFeature , Mdm::FixedAtomConstraint , Mdm::Geometric3d , Mdm::Group , Mdm::HarmonicAtomRestraint , Mdm::HydrogenBond , Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor , Mdm::Isosurface , Mdm::Label3d , Mdm::Label , Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::LocationFeature , Mdm::Object , Mdm::Offlineable , Mdm::OfflineableConformation , Mdm::PiBond , Mdm::PiCationMonitor , Mdm::PiInteractionMonitor , Mdm::PiPiMonitor , Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor , Mdm::PlanarPeptideViolationMonitor , Mdm::PlaneFeature , Mdm::PlaneMonitor , Mdm::PointFeature , Mdm::PointOffsetFeature , Mdm::Polydot , Mdm::PropertyLabel , Mdm::ProteinChiralityViolationMonitor , Mdm::ProteinNomenclatureViolationMonitor , Mdm::ProteinPose , Mdm::Query , Mdm::QueryAtom , Mdm::QueryBond , Mdm::QueryFeatureMap , Mdm::QueryOperator , Mdm::Residue , Mdm::Restraint , Mdm::RingAromaticFeature , Mdm::RotatableBondMonitor , Mdm::ScreenLabel , Mdm::Set , Mdm::ShapeFeature , Mdm::SideChainConformationViolationMonitor , Mdm::SlicingPlane , Mdm::Sphere , Mdm::Surface , Mdm::TorsionMonitor , Mdm::TupleMonitor , Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond , Mdm::Valence , Mdm::ValenceMonitor , Mdm::VectorFeature

### Using the DonorFeatures filter

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->DonorFeatures;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

# Create a query from a template molecules. Add HBAs to =O,
# HBD to N, and excluded volumes to all Halogens and
# projection points of HBAs and HBDs.

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles(
'OC(=O)C1=CC=C(C=C1)CN/C2=C/C=C(C=C2)C=CC(=O)C[Cl]');
AddHydrogens($document);

my $atoms = $document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $double_bond_oxygens = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $nitrogens = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $halogens = Mdm::Array::Create();

foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( ( $atom->Element eq 'O' ) && ( $atom->BondCount == 1 ) )
{
$double_bond_oxygens->AddItem($atom);
}
$nitrogens->AddItem($atom) if ( $atom->Element eq 'N' );
$halogens->AddItem($atom) if ( $atom->Element =~ /(Cl|F|Br|I)\b/i );
}

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Features and location constraints
my $featureCount = 0;
foreach my $atom (@$double_bond_oxygens)
{
++$featureCount;
my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
my $featureName = "HBA_" . $featureCount;
$acceptorOperator->Name($featureName);
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atom);

# create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );
}

foreach my $atom (@$nitrogens)
{
++$featureCount;
my $featureName = "HBD_" . $featureCount;
my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name($featureName);
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atom);

#create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );
}

# Add excluded volumes at the location of halogen atoms
foreach my $atom (@$halogens)
{
my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

# Add excluded volumes at the projection point of HBAs and HBDs
my $acceptorfeatures = $fitOperator->AcceptorFeatures;
foreach my $acceptor (@$acceptorfeatures)
{
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atom->XYZ = $acceptor->HeadXYZ();
$molecule->Select();

my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

my $donorfeatures = $fitOperator->DonorFeatures;
foreach my $donor (@$donorfeatures)
{
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atom->XYZ = $donor->HeadXYZ();
$molecule->Select();

my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

my $exclusionfeatures = $document->ExclusionFeatures();
my $exclusionfeatureCount = 0;
foreach my $exclusionfeature (@$exclusionfeatures)
{
++$exclusionfeatureCount;
my $name = "EV_" . $exclusionfeatureCount;
$exclusionfeature->Name($name);
}

# We will delete temporary atoms used to create EVs
# on projection points. Need to update objects before
# deleting so we preserve the X,Y,Z location.
$document->UpdateObjects();

# Delete temporary atoms
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# DreidingMinimize function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/dreidingminimize_function.htm

## DreidingMinimize function

### Description

DreidingMinimize minimizes molecular energy using the Dreiding forcefield using
the conjugate gradients method.

### Applies to

The DreidingMinimize function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the DreidingMinimize function

#### Instance

$object->DreidingMinimize( [iterationsteps], [convergencecriteria], [replaceatomtypes], [includeintermolecularforces], [calculategasteigercharges], [ignoreautocalculatechargesflag] );

$object->DreidingMinimize( { IterationSteps => [iterationsteps], ConvergenceCriteria => [convergencecriteria], ReplaceAtomTypes => [replaceatomtypes], IncludeIntermolecularForces => [includeintermolecularforces], CalculateGasteigerCharges => [calculategasteigercharges], IgnoreAutoCalculateChargesFlag => [ignoreautocalculatechargesflag] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [calculategasteigercharges] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [convergencecriteria] | Optional | 0.0001 | Real |
| [ignoreautocalculatechargesflag] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [includeintermolecularforces] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [iterationsteps] | Optional | 500 | Integer |
| [replaceatomtypes] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to the Dreiding Minimization function.
use strict;
use MdmCommands;

# Minimize a ligand in the presence of the protein

my $document = FileNew();
FileInsert( $document, PdbUrlPrefix .'3JZK.pdb' );

# calculate partial charges for the minimization step
$document->CalculateCharges();

#select the ligand for minimization
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);

# Select the ligand
SetSelection( $document, $ligands->Item(0) );

# Call the Dreiding minimizer to optimize the ligand in the binding pocket
$document->DreidingMinimize( 500, 0.001, True, True, True );

my $energy = $document->Molecules->Item(0)->GetProperty("Energy");
my $energyStart = $document->Molecules->Item(0)->GetProperty("Initial Energy");

printf("Ligand: %s\nInitial Energy: %.4f\nFinal Energy: %.4f\n", 
$ligands->[0]->Name, $energyStart, $energy);

my $atoms = $ligands->[0]->Atoms;
my $countAtoms = $atoms->Count;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $countAtoms ; ++$i )
{
printf "%3d) %4s %4s %.4f\n" , $i+1,
$atoms->Item($i)->GetProperty("Name"),
$atoms->Item($i)->GetProperty("ForcefieldType"),
$atoms->Item($i)->GetProperty("Partial Charge");
}
```

# DSCommands package

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/dscommands_package.htm

## DSCommands package

### Description

DSCommands provides high-level functions for accessing functionality
within other packages. You can use this file to include all the other
packages, however some of these packages may not be available in the free
visualizer.

### Using the DSCommands package

Access to the DSCommands API is through the Perl use directive:

```text
use strict;
use DSCommands;
```

The strict directive is optional, but strongly recommended as it restricts
the use of unsafe constructs. All available classes will be imported from the DSCommands module.

#### Uses

ForcefieldCommands , PharmacophoreCommands , SbdCommands , VisualizerCommands

#### Module

DSCommands.pm

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate use of DS and Protocol commands.
use strict;
use DSCommands;
use ProtocolCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1kim.pdb' );

# From MdmDiscoveryScript
print "Document contains " . $document->Atoms->Count() . " atom(s)\n";

# From MdmCommands
# note that if using this from a script in PipelinePilot, you may
# wish to precede with PerceiveLigandGroups if you wish to mimic the
# Discovery Studio ligand preferences

my $ligands = GetLigands($document);

# From SdmDiscoveryScript
my $sequence = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();

# From SdmCommands
my $sequenceString = CreateSequenceFromMolecule($document);

# From SbdCommands;
FindBindingSites($document);

# From SbdDiscoveryScript
my $site = $document->BindingSites->Item(0);
$document->PartitionBindingSite($site);

# From ProtocolDiscoveryScript
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();

# From ProtocolCommands
LaunchProtocol( "GetPPVersion", Protocol::ParameterMap::Create(),
$session->Server );
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
```
```text
# Demonstrate the use of various atom properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

# Define atom properties to list.
# This may be specified on the command line.
my $residueAtomName = 'THR2:CA';
if ( @ARGV != 0 )
{
($residueAtomName) = @ARGV;
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Get the specified atom.
my $atoms = FilterByString( $document, $residueAtomName );
die "Atom $residueAtomName not found. Aborting!\n\n"
if ( $atoms->Count == 0 );

my $atom = $atoms->[0];

# Print various atom properties. In the DiscoveryStudio client, the
# output will appear in the output pane of the scripting window.
print "List of properties for atom $residueAtomName:\n\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
print 'Element: ' . $atom->Element . "\n";
print 'Element Name: ' . $atom->ElementName . "\n";
print 'Element Symbol: ' . $atom->ElementSymbol . "\n";
print 'Mass: ' . $atom->Mass . "\n";
print 'Atomic number: ' . $atom->AtomicNumber . "\n";
print 'Charge: ' . $atom->Charge . "\n";
print 'Formal Charge: '
. $atom->FormalCharge->Numerator . "/"
. $atom->FormalCharge->Denominator . "\n";

print 'VDW Radius: ' . $atom->VdwRadius . "\n";
print 'Covalent Radius: ' . $atom->CovalentRadius . "\n";
print 'Chirality: ' . $atom->Chirality . "\n";
print 'Bond count: ' . $atom->BondCount . "\n";
print 'Bonding radius: ' . $atom->BondingRadius . "\n";
print 'Hybridization: ' . $atom->Hybridization . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen Count: ' . $atom->HydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'ImplicitHydrogen Count: ' . $atom->ImplicitHydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Acceptor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondAcceptor . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Donor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondDonor . "\n";
print 'Isotropic Displacement: ' . $atom->IsotropicDisplacement . "\n";
print 'Is Terminal Hydrogen: ' . $atom->IsTerminalHydrogen . "\n";
print 'Is Valence Satisfied: ' . $atom->IsValenceSatisfied . "\n";
print 'Lone Pair Count: ' . $atom->LonePairCount . "\n";
print 'Valence Count: ' . $atom->ValenceCount . "\n";
print 'Occupancy: ' . $atom->Occupancy . "\n";

printf "\n%s:\n", 'Display Properties';
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
```

```text
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Create an ethanol molecule
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create(MdmModelType);
$document->InsertFromSmiles("[CH3][CH2][OH]");

printf "%s %f\n","H radius: ", $document->ElementVdwRadius(Mdm::H);
```

# Enable function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enable_function.htm

## Enable function

### Description

Enable enables an Mdm::Constraint object. Enabled Mdm::Constraint objects can be selected when setting up a protocol. See also Disable .

### Applies to

The Enable function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Constraint , Mdm::DihedralRestraint , Mdm::DistanceRestraint , Mdm::FixedAtomConstraint , Mdm::HarmonicAtomRestraint , Mdm::Restraint

### Using the Enable function

#### Instance

$object->Enable();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Fix the backbone
my $backbone = FilterByString( $document, ':CA,C,N,O,HN,HA' );
my $fixed = $document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($backbone);

# Enable the constraint (this is not required, it is enabled by default)
$fixed->Enable();

# Fix the CB
my $backbone = FilterByString( $document, ':CB' );
my $restraint = $document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint($backbone);

# disable this constraint
$restraint->Disable();

# Loop over all constraints
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
foreach my $constraint (@$constraints)
{
print "Constraint: " . $constraint->Name . "\n";
if ( $constraint->IsEnabled )
{

# Highlight the enabled constraints in turn
$constraint->Color( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 0 ) );
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

# Reset color to default
$constraint->Color( $constraint->GetDefaultColor() );
}
}
```

# EnableUpdateViews function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enableupdateviews_function.htm

## EnableUpdateViews function

### Description

EnableUpdateViews enables or disables view updating.

In order to optimize performance, direct manipulations of objects do
not update the document's views. In these cases, run UpdateViews after completing a functional set of operations.

### Applies to

The EnableUpdateViews function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the EnableUpdateViews function

#### Command

$object->EnableUpdateViews( <refreshviewsaftercommands> );

$object->EnableUpdateViews( { RefreshViewsAfterCommands => <refreshviewsaftercommands> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <refreshviewsaftercommands> | Required | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to colors binding sites.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);

# Hide protein atoms.
TurnOffProteinAtoms($document);

# Use command in the DSCommands perl modules to remove ligands
# water from the complex.
Delete( $document, GetLigands($document) );
Delete( $document, GetWaters($document) );

print "Searching for binding sites...\n\n";
my $protein = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
$document->CreateBindingSitesFromCavities($protein);
my $bindingSites = $document->BindingSites;
print 'Found ' . $bindingSites->Count . " binding sites.\n\n";

# Color each binding site point with a random color.
foreach my $site (@$bindingSites)
{
$site->SetVisible; # make all sites visible
my $bindingSitePoints = $site->BindingSitePoints;
foreach my $bindingSitePoint (@$bindingSitePoints)
{
my $color = Mdm::Color::Create(
int( 255 * rand() ),
int( 255 * rand() ),
int( 255 * rand() )
);
$bindingSitePoint->Color = $color;
}
}

print "Color binding sites points using a random color for each point...\n\n";
$document->SetBindingSiteColorScheme(Mdm::bindingSiteColorByPoints);
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
```

# EndBatch function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/endbatch_function.htm

## EndBatch function

### Description

EndBatch ends a batch molecule or conformation property update
on a document. It is complemented by BeginBatch which begins a batch
molecule or conformation property update on a document.
Any molecule or conformation property modifications made between
a pair of BeginBatch and EndBatch statements will result in a bulk
update of these properties, which can result in a significant
improvement in performance.

### Applies to

The EndBatch function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the EndBatch function

#### Instance

$object->EndBatch();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w

use strict;

use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use Time::HiRes qw(time);
use POSIX qw(strftime);

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
my $molecule = $molecules->Item(0);

for (my $i = 0; $i < 1000; ++$i) {
my $name = "Property #" . ($i + 1);
$molecule->SetProperty($name, "DATA");
}

my $t = time;
$document->WaitForUpdater();
$t = time - $t;
print "Time spent waiting = " . sprintf("%.3f seconds\n", $t) ;

$document->BeginBatch();
for (my $i = 0; $i < 1000; ++$i) {
my $name = "Property #" . ($i + 1);
$molecule->SetProperty($name, "MORE DATA");
}
$document->EndBatch();

$t = time;
$document->WaitForUpdater();
$t = time - $t;
print "Time spent waiting = " . sprintf("%.3f seconds\n", $t) ;

$t = time;
$document->Save("Output.dsv", "dsv");
$t = time - $t;
print "Time spent saving = " . sprintf("%.3f seconds\n", $t) ;

$document->Close();
```

# EndPosition property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/endposition_property.htm

## EndPosition property

### Description

EndPosition specifies the end position of a sequence segment.

### Applies to

The EndPosition property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Segment

### Using the EndPosition property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->EndPosition;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::Segment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Segment class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence =
$document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASCDFACSGHACSJCKLA' );

# Create a location consisting of all cysteine residues.
print "Creating location for all cysteine residues\n";
my $location = Sdm::Location::Create(Sdm::locationTypeJoin);

my $sequenceString = $sequence->SequenceString;
my $residueCount = length($sequenceString);
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
if ( substr( $sequenceString, $i, 1 ) eq 'C' )
{
my $segment = Sdm::Segment::Create( $i, $i );
$location->AddSegment($segment);
}
}

my $segmentCount = $location->SegmentCount;
print "Location has $segmentCount segments\n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $segmentCount ; ++$index )
{
my $segment = $location->Segment($index);
printf( "Segment %d ...\n", $index + 1);
print "\tStart position:\t" . $segment->StartPosition . "\n";
print "\tEnd position:\t" . $segment->EndPosition . "\n";
print "\tSegement type:\t" . $segment->Type . "\n";
print "\tIs complement?:\t" . $segment->IsComplement . "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Create a feature to and add it to the sequence.
my $feature =
Sdm::Feature::CreateCustomFeature( 'Cysteine residues', $location );
$feature->AddQualifier("KeyName", 'Example feature qualifier');
$sequence->AddFeature($feature);

print 'The feature key name is ' . $feature->Key . "\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
```
```text
#
use strict;
use DiscoveryScript;

my $messageBoxResult = DiscoveryScript::MessageBox(
"An example message with Yes and No buttons to allow interactive user input.\nPlease click a button",
"More Detailed information about the message should appear here.\n",
DiscoveryScript::messageBoxFlagsYesNo,
DiscoveryScript::messageBoxIconInfo
);

if ( $messageBoxResult eq DiscoveryScript::messageBoxResultYes )
{
print "You clicked Yes.\n";
}
elsif ( $messageBoxResult eq DiscoveryScript::messageBoxResultNo )
{
print "You clicked No.\n";
}
elsif ( $messageBoxResult eq DiscoveryScript::messageBoxResultCancel )
{
print "You closed the window without answering the question.\n";
}
```

# enum Ffdm::ForceFieldStatus datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_ffdm__forcefieldstatus_datatype.htm

## enum Ffdm::ForceFieldStatus datatype

### Description

The Ffdm::ForceFieldStatus identifies the forcefield typing status of an Mdm::Document .

### Using the enum Ffdm::ForceFieldStatus datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Ffdm::applyForceFieldCompleted

* Ffdm::applyForceFieldFailed

* Ffdm::forceFieldNotApplied

#### Returned by

ApplyForceField , GetTypingStatus

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Example: Applies a forcefield to a molecule and gets the typing status
use strict;
use ForceFieldDiscoveryScript;
use File::Path;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

my $tempDir = DiscoveryScript::GetTemporaryFolder()."/typingEx";
mkdir $tempDir if(not -e $tempDir);

print "Creating CHARMm force field document\n";
my $forcefield = Ffdm::Document::Create(Ffdm::charmmForceField);

print "Applying CHARMm force field to 1crn\n";
$forcefield->ApplyForceField( $document, True, True, True,
Ffdm::useMomanyRonePartialCharges );
my $status = Ffdm::Document::GetTypingStatus($document);
if ( $status == Ffdm::applyForceFieldCompleted )
{
print "Successfully typed\n";
$forcefield->Save($tempDir."/1crn.ffml");
}
else
{
print "Failed to type\n";
}

# remove file
unlink ($tempDir.'/1crn.ffml');
rmtree $tempDir;
```

# enum Ffdm::ForceFieldType datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_ffdm__forcefieldtype_datatype.htm

## enum Ffdm::ForceFieldType datatype

### Description

The Ffdm::ForceFieldType identifies the various forcefields available.

### Using the enum Ffdm::ForceFieldType datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Ffdm::cffForceField

* Ffdm::charmm19ForceField

* Ffdm::charmm22ForceField

* Ffdm::charmm27ForceField

* Ffdm::charmm36ForceField

* Ffdm::charmmForceField

* Ffdm::charmmPolarHydrogenForceField

* Ffdm::mmffForceField

* Ffdm::xproligForceField

#### Used by

Ffdm::Document::Create

### Examples

```text
# Demonstrate creating a force field document
# and applying a forcefield to a molecule.
use strict;
use ForceFieldDiscoveryScript;
use File::Path;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

my $tempDir = DiscoveryScript::GetTemporaryFolder()."/typingEx";

mkdir $tempDir if(not -e $tempDir);

print "Creating CHARMm force field document.\n";
my $forcefield = Ffdm::Document::Create(Ffdm::charmmForceField);

print "Applying CHARMm force field to 1crn.\n";
my $status = $forcefield->ApplyForceField( $document, True, True, True,
Ffdm::useMomanyRonePartialCharges );

if ( $status == Ffdm::applyForceFieldCompleted )
{
print "Molecule successfully typed.\n";
$forcefield->Save($tempDir.'/1crn.ffml');
}
else
{
die "Failed to type molecule.\n";
}

my @properties = ("Forcefield","PartialChargeMethod","UseResidueTemplateCharge","ForcefieldBase" );
my $molecules = $document->Molecules()->Item(0);
foreach my $pname (@properties)
{
my $prop = $molecules->GetProperty($pname);
print "$pname: $prop\n";
}

print "\tName\tType\tCharge\n";
my $atoms = $molecules->Atoms;
my $count = 0;
foreach $a (@$atoms)
{
my $fftype = $a->GetProperty('ForcefieldType');
my $ffcharge = $a->GetProperty('Partial Charge');
printf("%5d)\t%-4s\t%-4s\t%.3f\n", ++$count, $a->Name , $fftype, $ffcharge);
}

# remove file
unlink ($tempDir.'/1crn.ffml');
rmtree $tempDir;
```

# enum Mdm::AcceptorFeatureOrientation datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__acceptorfeatureorientation_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::AcceptorFeatureOrientation datatype

### Description

The Mdm::AcceptorFeatureOrientation identifies the orientation of an acceptor feature.

### Using the enum Mdm::AcceptorFeatureOrientation datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::acceptorFeatureFirstLonePair

* Mdm::acceptorFeatureFree

* Mdm::acceptorFeatureProjection

* Mdm::acceptorFeatureSecondLonePair

* Mdm::acceptorFeatureThirdLonePair

#### Used by

Orientation

#### Returned by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles('C=O');

# Get the Oxygen atom to place the Hydrogen Bond Acceptors
my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
my $OxygenAtom;
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( $atom->Element eq "O" )
{
$OxygenAtom = $atom;
}
}

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create an HBA using the first lone pair.
my $operator1 = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$operator1->Name('HBA');
my $newAcceptor = $operator1->CreateAcceptorFeature($OxygenAtom);
$newAcceptor->Orientation('acceptorFeatureFirstLonePair');

# Create an HBA using the second lone pair.
my $operator2 = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$operator2->Name('HBA2');
my $newAcceptor2 = $operator2->CreateAcceptorFeature($OxygenAtom);
$newAcceptor2->Orientation('acceptorFeatureSecondLonePair');

$document->UpdateObjects();
```

# enum Mdm::AminoAcidCTerminalOxygenNames datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__aminoacidcterminaloxygennames_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::AminoAcidCTerminalOxygenNames datatype

### Description

The Mdm::AminoAcidCTerminalOxygenNames identifies the names given to C-terminal oxygen atoms in
protein building and editing operations. The PDB standard is
to set one as O and the other as OXT, but some software has
other conventions, e.g. CHARMm uses OCT1 and OCT2.

### Using the enum Mdm::AminoAcidCTerminalOxygenNames datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::oxygenNamesOAndOE

* Mdm::oxygenNamesOAndOT

* Mdm::oxygenNamesOAndOXT

* Mdm::oxygenNamesOCT1AndOCT2

* Mdm::oxygenNamesOT1AndOT2

* Mdm::oxygenNamesOX1AndOX2

#### Used by

CleanProtein , RemoveTerminalCappingGroups

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1u7e');

# this would use CleanProtein with default parameters
# my $cleanResults = $document->CleanProtein();

# However, to demonstrate the datatype for controlling terminal
# oxygen names, lets set a couple of arguments - this will give CHARMm-type
# nomenclature on the C terminal oxygens instead of O/OXT
my $cleanResults = $document->CleanProtein(
{
ModifyTermini => True,
TerminalOxygenNames => Mdm::oxygenNamesOCT1AndOCT2
}
);

# if you want to save the results to a file, $clean_results
# are in html format
open( OUTREPORT, '>cleanreport.html' )
or die "Cannot open cleanreport.html: $!";

print OUTREPORT $cleanResults;
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
```

## enum Mdm::AtomDisplayStyle datatype

### Description

The Mdm::AtomDisplayStyle identifies an atom display style.

### Using the enum Mdm::AtomDisplayStyle datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStick

* Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStickSingle

* Mdm::styleAtomCPK

* Mdm::styleAtomLine

* Mdm::styleAtomLineSingle

* Mdm::styleAtomNone

* Mdm::styleAtomPolyhedron

* Mdm::styleAtomScaledBallAndStick

* Mdm::styleAtomScaledBallAndStickSingle

* Mdm::styleAtomStick

* Mdm::styleAtomStickSingle

#### Used by

DisplayStyle , SetAtomDisplayStyle

#### Returned by

DisplayStyle

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to change the display style of selected atoms.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Generate array with AtomDisplayStyle values.
my @atomDisplayStyles = (
Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStick,
Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStickSingle,
Mdm::styleAtomCPK,
Mdm::styleAtomLine,
Mdm::styleAtomLineSingle,
Mdm::styleAtomNone,
Mdm::styleAtomPolyhedron,
Mdm::styleAtomScaledBallAndStick,
Mdm::styleAtomScaledBallAndStickSingle,
Mdm::styleAtomStick,
Mdm::styleAtomStickSingle,
);

print 'Change the atom and bond display style to ball-and-stick '
. "using the defaults sizes...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStick, -1.0, -1.0, -1.0,
False );
sleep(3);

print 'Change the atom and bond display style to ball-and-stick '
. "with 0.7 A balls and 0.5 A sticks...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(
{
DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStick,
StickSize => 0.5,
BallSize => 0.7,
UpdateDefaultValues => False
}
);
sleep(3);

print 'Change the atom and bond display style to CPK '
. "with 0.75 A CPK scale factor...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(
{
DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleAtomCPK,
CPKScale => 0.75,
UpdateDefaultValues => False
}
);
sleep(3);

foreach my $atomDisplayStyle (@atomDisplayStyles)
{
print "Change the display style to $atomDisplayStyle...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle($atomDisplayStyle);
sleep(3);
}

print "Reset the display style to ball-and-stick with default sizes...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStick, 0.2, 0.4, 1.0,
False );
```

# enum Mdm::AxisOriginType datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__axisorigintype_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::AxisOriginType datatype

### Description

The Mdm::AxisOriginType identifies the shape of the unit cell or the main symmetry axis for space groups where alternatives are possible.

### Using the enum Mdm::AxisOriginType datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::aUnique

* Mdm::bUnique

* Mdm::cUnique

* Mdm::hexagonal

* Mdm::origin1

* Mdm::origin2

* Mdm::rhombohedral

#### Used by

CreateCell , SetCellSpaceGroup

#### Returned by

AxisOriginType

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use Mdm::SpaceGroup objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Get space group from document.
my $cell = $document->Cells->Item(0);
my $spacegroup = $cell->SpaceGroup;

print "The following is a list of space group properties:\n";
print "Number:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->Number . "\n";
print "Short Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->Symbol . "\n";
print "SchoenfliesSymbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->SchoenfliesSymbol . "\n";
print "Full Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->FullSymbol . "\n";
print "Lattice type:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->LatticeType . "\n";
print "Cell choice:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->CellChoice . "\n";
print "AxisOriginType:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->AxisOriginType . "\n";
print "Number of sym. operator:\t\t"
. $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount . "\n";

my $count = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $operator = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperator($index);
print "Symmetry operator $index\n";
print "\tName: " . $operator->Name . "\n";

my $rotation = $operator->Rotation;
my $format = "\t %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n";
print "\tRotation Matrix:\n";
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 0, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 1, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 2 );

my $translation = $operator->Translation;
print "\tTranslation:\n";
printf "$format", $translation->X, $translation->Y, $translation->Z;
}
```

```text
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 1, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 2 );

my $translation = $operator->Translation;
print "\tTranslation:\n";
printf "$format", $translation->X, $translation->Y, $translation->Z;
}
```

# enum Mdm::ChargingMethod datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__chargingmethod_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::ChargingMethod datatype

### Description

The Mdm::ChargingMethod identifies the method used to assign
charges to atoms. This is used by the Clean function.

### Using the enum Mdm::ChargingMethod datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::calculateGasteigerCharges

* Mdm::calculateGasteigerChargesOnlyIfAllChargesAreSmall

* Mdm::calculateGasteigerChargesOnlyIfAllChargesAreZero

* Mdm::calculateGasteigerChargesOnlyIfSomeChargesAreSmall

* Mdm::calculateGasteigerChargesOnlyIfSomeChargesAreZero

* Mdm::useExistingCharges

#### Used by

Clean

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to access MDM objects and create a minimize molecule.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Create a document containing a molecule.
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom1 = $molecule->CreateAtom('C');
my $atom2 = $molecule->CreateAtom('C');
my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $atom1, $atom2, Mdm::doubleBond );

# Add hydrogen atoms.
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms();

# Calculate partial charges for the minimization step.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Perform a geometry minimization using the clean forcefield.
$document->Clean();

$molecule->Name = 'Ethene';
print "Created molecule " . $molecule->Name . ".\n";
```

# enum Mdm::DonorFeatureOrientation datatype

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__donorfeatureorientation_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::DonorFeatureOrientation datatype

### Description

The Mdm::DonorFeatureOrientation identifies the orientation of a donor feature.

### Using the enum Mdm::DonorFeatureOrientation datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::donorFeatureFirstHydrogen

* Mdm::donorFeatureFree

* Mdm::donorFeatureProjection

* Mdm::donorFeatureSecondHydrogen

* Mdm::donorFeatureThirdHydrogen

#### Used by

Orientation

#### Returned by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles('CN');
AddHydrogens($document);

# Get the Nitrogen atom to place the Hydrogen Bond Donors
my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
my $NitrogenAtom;
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( $atom->Element eq "N" )
{
$NitrogenAtom = $atom;
}
}

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create an HBD using the first Hydrogen.
my $donorOperator1 = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator1->Name('HBD');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator1->CreateDonorFeature($NitrogenAtom);
$newDonor->Orientation('donorFeatureFirstHydrogen');

# Create an HBD using the second Hydrogen.
my $donorOperator2 = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator2->Name('HBD2');
my $newDonor2 = $donorOperator2->CreateDonorFeature($NitrogenAtom);
$newDonor2->Orientation('donorFeatureSecondHydrogen');

$document->RotateView( 2.0, -10.0, 2.0 );
```

# enum Mdm::HarmonicRestraintType datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__harmonicrestrainttype_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::HarmonicRestraintType datatype

### Description

The Mdm::HarmonicRestraintType specifies the type of a harmonic restraint.
The Absolute type holds the atoms in a proximal cartesian space,
while the BestFit type allows for rotation and translation of the selected atoms.

### Using the enum Mdm::HarmonicRestraintType datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::Absolute

* Mdm::BestFit

#### Used by

CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Fix the backbone
my $backbone = FilterByString( $document, ':CA,C,N,O,HN,HA' );
$document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($backbone);

# Restrain beta carbon atoms
my $cbeta = FilterByString( $document, ':CB' );
$document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint( $cbeta, 10, Mdm::BestFit );

# Add cross-strand distance restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "THR2:CA" );
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "ILE34:CA" );
$document->CreateDistanceRestraint(
{
ArrayOfAtoms1 => $atom1,
ArrayOfAtoms2 => $atom2,
RMin => 2,
RMax => 5,
RMinForceConstant => 10,
RMaxForceConstant => 20,
ForceMaximum => 20
}
);

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
$document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);

# Print the total number of restraints (4)
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
print "There are ", $constraints->Count, " constraints\n";
```

# enum Mdm::IsosurfaceDisplayStyle datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__isosurfacedisplaystyle_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::IsosurfaceDisplayStyle datatype

### Description

The Mdm::IsosurfaceDisplayStyle identifies a display style used to represent isosurfaces.

### Using the enum Mdm::IsosurfaceDisplayStyle datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::isosurfaceStyleNone

* Mdm::isosurfaceStyleQuadMesh

* Mdm::isosurfaceStyleSolid

* Mdm::isosurfaceStyleTriMesh

* Mdm::isosurfaceStyleVolume

#### Used by

DisplayStyle

#### Returned by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
print "It operates on a document with grid data\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a structure with grid data\n";
print
" (for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
print " 3 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Connect to an Sdm::Document from the last active sequence window
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

# Get array with all isosurfaces using Isosurfaces filter
my $isosurfaces = $document->Isosurfaces;

if ( $isosurfaces->Count == 0 )
{
print "To run this script, please open a structure with grid data.\n";
print "(for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
exit;
}

# Get the first isosurface
my $isosurface = $isosurfaces->[0];

# Create a new isosurface at 0.5 isovalue
my $newContour = $isosurface->CreateIsosurface(0.5);
$newContour->ContextAtomArray( $document->Atoms );

if ( !$newContour->IsContextAtomArrayDefined() )
{
print "Please define a context atom array\n";
}
$newContour->IsNormalFlipped(False);
$newContour->IsBoundaryDrawn(True);
print "The line width is: $newContour->{LineWidth}\n";

# Print the isovalues
$isosurfaces = $document->Isosurfaces;
foreach my $surface (@$isosurfaces)
{
print $surface->Name . " has isovalue " . $surface->Isovalue . "\n";
}

# Array with available display styles
my @displayStyles = (
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleNone, Mdm::isosurfaceStyleQuadMesh,
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleSolid, Mdm::isosurfaceStyleTriMesh,
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleVolume
);

# Iterate over the available display styles
print "\nIterating over isosurface display styles:\n";
foreach my $displayStyle (@displayStyles)
{
sleep(1);
$newContour->DisplayStyle = $displayStyle;
print "$displayStyle\n";
$document->UpdateViews();
}

$newContour->RemoveContextAtomArray();
```

# enum Mdm::MembraneOrientationDisplayLocation datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__membraneorientationdisplaylocation_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::MembraneOrientationDisplayLocation datatype

### Description

The Mdm::MembraneOrientationDisplayLocation specifies the location of
the membrane coordinate frame. In the Mdm::objectCentered setting, the
coordinate frame is placed at the geometric center of the embedded
protein. In the Mdm::membraneCentered setting, the coordinate frame is
placed at the edge of the displayed membrane.

### Using the enum Mdm::MembraneOrientationDisplayLocation datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::membraneCentered

* Mdm::objectCentered

#### Used by

CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor , DisplayLocation

#### Returned by

DisplayLocation

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use properties of the MembraneOrientationMonitor
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load structure of BOVINE RHODOPSIN, 1f88 and keep only first chain
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# "Guess" some value for the membrane position
my $center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, -3.2 );
my $normal = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.521, 0.106, 0.847 );

my $membrane =
$document->CreateMembrane( $center, $normal, 60.0, 60.0, 30.0 );

$document->SetParent( $molecule, $membrane );

my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms();

# Illustrate on how to use MembraneOrientationMonitor preferences
my $membraneOrientation =
$molecule->CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor( $membrane, $atoms,
Mdm::objectCentered, Mdm::referenceAxisZ );

$document->UpdateViews();

my $monitors = $document->MembraneOrientationMonitors;
print "Number of membrane monitors: ". $monitors->Count. "\n";

my $membranes = $document->Membranes;
print "Number of membranes: ". $membranes->Count. "\n";

sleep(2);

$membraneOrientation->DisplayLocation = Mdm::membraneCentered;
$membraneOrientation->ProteinReferenceAxis = Mdm::referenceAxisX;
```
