# enum Mdm::NonbondCriterionType datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__nonbondcriteriontype_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::NonbondCriterionType datatype

### Description

The Mdm::NonbondCriteriaType identifies the non-bond distance and
angle criteria types associated with an Mdm::NonbondMonitor object.

| Non-bond criteria type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| electrostatic_AnionPi_AngleMaximum | Maximum angle between the anion-centroid vector and the normal to a Pi ring plane for an attractive interaction. |
| electrostatic_AnionPi_DistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between an anion and the centroid of a Pi ring for an attractive interaction. |
| electrostatic_CationPi_AngleMaximum | Maximum angle between the cation-centroid vector and the normal to a pi ring plane for an attractive interaction. |
| electrostatic_CationPi_DistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between a cation and the centroid of a Pi ring for an attractive interaction. |
| electrostatic_ChargeCharge_DistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between two charged atoms for an attractive or repulsive charge interaction. The minimum distance necessary for a charge-charge interaction is specified by the Mdm::NonbondMonitor object's unfavorable_Bump_FractionVdwDistanceMinimum criterion. |
| halogenBond_ClBrI_FractionVdwDistanceMaximum | Defines the fraction used to multiply the sum of the van der Waals radius for the interacting elements. This scaled distance specifies the maximum distance (Å) between a halogen atom (Cl, Br, or I) and an interacting atom needed to qualify as a halogen non-bond. A separate distance criterion is used for fluorine non-bond interactions (see halogenBond_F_DistanceMaximum criterion). The recommended range is between 80 and 100%. |
| halogenBond_CXB_AngleMinimum, halogenBond_CXB_AngleMaximum | Minimum and maximum angles formed by the atoms C—X—B in the interaction of a carbon-bound halogen X to a group B—Y where B is C, N, or O. |
| halogenBond_F_DistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between a fluorine atom and its interacting neighbor. This distance criterion is used for all fluorine interactions including hydrogen bonded fluorine atoms. |
| halogenBond_XBY_AngleMinimum, halogenBond_XBY_AngleMaximum | Minimum and maximum angles formed by the atoms X—B—Y in the interaction of a carbon-bound halogen X to a group B—Y where B is C, N, or O. |
| hydrogenBond_DAY_AngleMinimum, hydrogenBond_DAY_AngleMaximum | Minimum and maximum angles formed by the heavy atom donor, acceptor atom, and any atom bonded to the acceptor atom. This criterion applies when the hydrogen atom is absent and angle checking is enabled. |
| hydrogenBond_DHA_AngleMinimum, hydrogenBond_DHA_AngleMaximum | Minimum and maximum angles formed by the (heavy-atom) donor, hydrogen, and acceptor atoms for a hydrogen bond. This criterion always applies when the hydrogen atom is present. |
| hydrogenBond_DonorPi_AngleMaximum | Maximum angle between the donor heavy atom-centroid vector and the normal to a Pi ring plane for an attractive interaction. |
| hydrogenBond_DonorPi_DeviationAngleMaximum | Maximum deviation from linearity of the donor-hydrogen-centroid angle. |
| hydrogenBond_DonorPi_DistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between a donor heavy atom and the centroid of a Pi ring for an attractive interaction. |
| hydrogenBond_HAY_AngleMinimum, hydrogenBond_HAY_AngleMaximum | Minimum and maximum angles formed by the hydrogen atom, acceptor atom, and atom bonded to the acceptor atom. This criterion applies when the hydrogen atom is present and angle checking is enabled. |
| hydrogenBond_SaltBridge_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between the hydrogen heavy atom donor and the acceptor atoms for a salt bridge. The minimum distance necessary for a salt bridge is specified by the Mdm::NonbondMonitor object's bump definition (see unfavorable_Bump_FractionVdwDistanceMinimum criterion). |
| hydrogenBond_XDA_AngleMinimum, hydrogenBond_XDA_AngleMaximum, hydrogenBond_SpDonor_XDA_AngleMinimum | Minimum and maximum angles formed by atoms bound to the heavy atom donor, the heavy atom donor, and acceptor atom for a hydrogen bond. This criterion applies when the hydrogen atom is absent and angle checking is enabled. For a Sp hybridized heavy atom donor the hydrogenBond_SpDonor_XDA_AngleMinimum angle is used instead. |
| hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between the hydrogen heavy atom donor and the acceptor atoms for a hydrogen-bond. The minimum distance necessary for a hydrogen-bond is specified by the Mdm::NonbondMonitor object's bump definition (see unfavorable_Bump_FractionVdwDistanceMinimum criterion). |
| hydrogenBond_Weak_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between a hydrogen donor (heavy atom or atom group) and an acceptor for the weak interactions involving aromatic and acetylene CH donors. |
| hydrophobic_Alkyl_CenterDistanceMaximum | Defines the maximum distance between the centroids of two hydrophobic groups for an Alkyl or Pi-Alkyl interaction. |
| hydrophobic_Alkyl_SurfaceAreaScaleFactor | Defines the maximum size of a group considered to be an alkyl hydrophobic group, with 1.0 representing the size of a methyl group. |
| hydrophobic_PiAmideStacked_GammaAngleMaximum | Maximum angle between the ring and amide plane normals for a stacked Pi-Amide interaction. |
| hydrophobic_PiAmideStacked_ThetaAngleMaximum | Maximum angle between the normal to the ring and/or amide plane and the centroid-centroid vector for a stacked Pi-Amide interaction. |
| hydrophobic_PiPi_CenterDistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between the centroids of two Pi systems for an attractive interaction. |
| hydrophobic_PiPi_ClosestAtomDistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between at least one pair of atoms from two Pi systems. |
| hydrophobic_PiPiStacked_GammaAngleMaximum | Maximum angle between the ring normals for a stacked Pi-Pi interaction. |
| hydrophobic_PiPiStacked_ThetaAngleMaximum | Maximum angle between the normal to one or both rings and the centroid-centroid vector for a stacked Pi-Pi interaction. |
| hydrophobic_PiPiTShaped_GammaAngleMinimum | Minimum angle between the ring normals for a T-shaped Pi-Pi interaction. |
| hydrophobic_PiPiTShaped_ThetaAngleMaximum | Maximum angle between the normal to one or both rings and the centroid-centroid vector for a T-shaped Pi-Pi interaction. |
| hydrophobic_SigmaPi_AngleMaximum | Maximum angle between the carbon atom-centroid vector and the normal to a Pi ring plane for an attractive interaction. |
| hydrophobic_SigmaPi_DeviationAngleMaximum | Maximum deviation from linearity of the carbon-hydrogen-centroid angle. |
| hydrophobic_SigmaPi_DistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between a carbon atom and the centroid of a Pi ring for an attractive interaction. |
| lonePair_Pi_AngleMaximum | Maximum angle between the acceptor atom-centroid vector and the normal to a Pi ring plane for an attractive interaction. |
| lonePair_Pi_DistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between an acceptor atom and the centroid of a Pi ring for an attractive interaction. |
| sulfurBond_PiEdgeOn_AngleMinimum | Minimum angle between the sulfur atom-centroid vector and the normal to a Pi ring plane for an attractive edge-on interaction. |
| sulfurBond_PiEdgeOn_DistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between a sulfur atom and the centroid of a Pi ring for an attractive edge-on interaction. |
| sulfurBond_PiFaceOn_AngleMaximum | Maximum angle between the sulfur atom-centroid vector and the normal to a Pi ring plane for an attractive face-oninteraction. |
| sulfurBond_PiFaceOn_DistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between a sulfur atom and the centroid of a Pi ring for an attractive face-on interaction. |
| sulfurBond_SX_DeviationAngleMaximum | Maximum deviation from linearity of one of the Y—S—X angles where Y is one of the atoms bonded to the sulfur and X is an interacting S, O, or N atom. |
| sulfurBond_SX_FractionVdwDistanceMaximum | Defines the fraction used to multiply the sum of the van der Waals radius for the interacting elements. This scaled distance specifies the maximum distance (Å) between a sulfur atom and an interacting atom (S, O, or N) needed to qualify as a Sulfur-X non-bond. |
| sulfurBond_SX_ThetaAngleMaximum | In cases where the X atom is Sp2 hybridized, this is the maximum angle between the Y—S vector and the normal to the plane of X and its attached atoms. |
| unfavorable_AcceptorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum | Maximum distance (Å) between two acceptor atoms for a repulsive interaction. |
| unfavorable_ALA_AngleMinimum, unfavorable_ALA_AngleMaximum | Minimum and maximum acceptor-lonepair-acceptor angles for a repulsive interaction. |
| unfavorable_ALLA_TorsionAngleMaximum | Maximum acceptor—lonepair—lonepair—acceptor torsion angle for a repulsive interaction. |
| unfavorable_Bump_FractionVdwDistanceMinimum | Defines the fraction used to multiply the sum of the van der Waals radius for the interacting atom pair. Atoms closer than this distance are considered as having an unfavorable bump interaction. |
| unfavorable_HHD_AngleMinimum | Minimum hydrogen-hydrogen-donor angle for a repulsive interaction. |

### Using the enum Mdm::NonbondCriterionType datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::electrostatic_AnionPi_AngleMaximum

* Mdm::electrostatic_AnionPi_DistanceMaximum

* Mdm::electrostatic_CationPi_AngleMaximum

* Mdm::electrostatic_CationPi_DistanceMaximum

* Mdm::electrostatic_ChargeCharge_DistanceMaximum

* Mdm::halogenBond_CXB_AngleMaximum

* Mdm::halogenBond_XBY_AngleMaximum

* Mdm::halogenBond_XBY_AngleMinimum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_DAY_AngleMaximum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_DAY_AngleMinimum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_DHA_AngleMaximum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_DHA_AngleMinimum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_DonorPi_AngleMaximum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_DonorPi_DeviationAngleMaximum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_DonorPi_DistanceMaximum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_HAY_AngleMaximum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_HAY_AngleMinimum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_SaltBridge_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_SpDonor_XDA_AngleMinimum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_Weak_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_XDA_AngleMaximum

* Mdm::hydrogenBond_XDA_AngleMinimum

* Mdm::hydrophobic_Alkyl_CenterDistanceMaximum

* Mdm::hydrophobic_Alkyl_SurfaceAreaScaleFactor

* Mdm::hydrophobic_PiAmideStacked_GammaAngleMaximum

* Mdm::hydrophobic_PiAmideStacked_ThetaAngleMaximum

* Mdm::hydrophobic_PiPiStacked_GammaAngleMaximum

* Mdm::hydrophobic_PiPiStacked_ThetaAngleMaximum

* Mdm::hydrophobic_PiPiTShaped_GammaAngleMinimum

* Mdm::hydrophobic_PiPiTShaped_ThetaAngleMaximum

* Mdm::hydrophobic_PiPi_CenterDistanceMaximum

* Mdm::hydrophobic_PiPi_ClosestAtomDistanceMaximum

* Mdm::hydrophobic_SigmaPi_AngleMaximum

* Mdm::hydrophobic_SigmaPi_DeviationAngleMaximum

* Mdm::hydrophobic_SigmaPi_DistanceMaximum

* Mdm::lonePair_Pi_AngleMaximum

* Mdm::lonePair_Pi_DistanceMaximum

* Mdm::sulfurBond_PiEdgeOn_AngleMinimum

* Mdm::sulfurBond_PiEdgeOn_DistanceMaximum

* Mdm::sulfurBond_PiFaceOn_AngleMaximum

* Mdm::sulfurBond_PiFaceOn_DistanceMaximum

* Mdm::sulfurBond_SX_DeviationAngleMaximum

* Mdm::sulfurBond_SX_FractionVdwDistanceMaximum

* Mdm::sulfurBond_SX_ThetaAngleMaximum

* Mdm::unfavorable_ALA_AngleMaximum

* Mdm::unfavorable_ALA_AngleMinimum

* Mdm::unfavorable_ALLA_TorsionAngleMaximum

* Mdm::unfavorable_AcceptorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum

* Mdm::unfavorable_Bump_FractionVdwDistanceMinimum

* Mdm::unfavorable_HHD_AngleMinimum

#### Used by

DefaultNonbondCriterion , NonbondCriterion

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the basic non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "Create a non-bond monitor for a subset of atoms.\n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus();
$ligand->Select();
my $ligandAtoms = $document->SelectedObjects()->Atoms;
$document->FitView();
$document->DeselectAll();

my $monitor = $document->CreateNonbondMonitor($ligandAtoms);
$monitor->Name = "myname";
$document->UpdateViews();

my $monitors = $document->NonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d NonbondMonitor(s).\n", $monitors->Count;
print "\n";

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "The properties NonbondCriterion and DefaultNonbondCriterion \n";
print "access the parameters used to identify non-bonds (see the \n";
print "documentation for full description of criteria).\n\n";

print "A list of criteria a their values follows:\n";
my $allCriteria = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllNonbondCriterionTypes();
foreach my $criterionType (@$allCriteria)
{
printf "Mdm::%s:\t %6.2f (default: %6.2f) \n",
$criterionType,
$monitor->NonbondCriterion($criterionType),
$monitor->DefaultNonbondCriterion($criterionType);
}
print "\n";

# -- Changing an interaction criterion ------------------------------

print 'Using the default criteria, the number of non-bond '
. 'interactions is ' . $monitor->Nonbonds->Count . ".\n\n";

my $maxHBond = 1.0 + $monitor->NonbondCriterion(
Mdm::hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum);
print 'After increasing the classical hydrogen bond distance to '
. $maxHBond . " A, ";

$monitor->NonbondCriterion(
Mdm::hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum) = $maxHBond;
$document->UpdateObjects;
print 'the number of non-bond interactions increases to '
. $monitor->Nonbonds->Count . ".\n\n";

print "Changes made to the non-bond criteria can be reset " .
"to the original defaults using ResetNonbondCriteria.\n";
$monitor->ResetNonbondCriteria();
```

```text
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3fzm');
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;
$document->Zoom(15);
$document->IsHierarchyViewShown = True;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Create a non-bond monitor for a subset of atoms.\n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $monitor = $document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();

# -- Analyze the identified interactions. ---------------------------
my $nonbonds = $monitor->Nonbonds;
my $count = $nonbonds->Count;
printf "Found %d non-bond interactions (total):\n", $count;

print $monitor->FavorableNonbonds->Count 
. " of these are favorable interactions (such as H-bonds).\n";
print $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds->Count
. " of these are unfavorable interactions (such as bumps).\n\n";

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Analyze first non-bond interaction:\n";
my $nonbond = $nonbonds->Item(0);

my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$nonbond->Distance;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
my $unfavorableNonbonds = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds;
if ($unfavorableNonbonds->Count > 0) 
{
print "Analyze first unfavorable non-bond interaction:\n";
my $unfavorableNonbond = $unfavorableNonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $unfavorableNonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $unfavorableNonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$unfavorableNonbond->Distance;
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "All non-bonds of a particular type can be retrieved ";
print "using the NonbondsOfType filter.\n";
my $hBonds = $monitor->NonbondsOfType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType);
printf "Found %d hydrogen bonds using NonbondOfType filter.\n\n", $hBonds->Count;

print "Alternatively the IsMatchingNonbondType property can be used to \n";
print "identify interactions of a specific types. The following atom pairs \n";
print "indicate classical hydrogen bonding: \n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
if ($nonbond->IsMatchingNonbondType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType))
{
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);

print '* ' . $atom1->FullName . " (";
print 'donor ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrogenDonor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHalogen);
print 'positive ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPositive);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ') and ';

print $atom2->FullName . " (";
print 'acceptor ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrogenAcceptor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHalogen);
print 'negative ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsNegative);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ")\n";
}
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "\nThe NonbondTypes property can be used to identify all \n";
print "interaction types of a non-bond.\n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
printf "- %s (%s) and %s (%s):",
$nonbond->FromSite->Name,
$nonbond->FromSite->ChemistryName,
$nonbond->ToSite->Name,
$nonbond->ToSite->ChemistryName;

#these are the type enums 
print " Types: ";
my $nonbondTypes = $nonbond->NonbondTypes;
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
print "$type ";
}

#these are the category enums 
print " Categories: ";
my $nonbondCategories = $nonbond->NonbondCategories;
foreach my $category (@$nonbondCategories) {
print "$category ";
}

#these APIs give the name(s) of the type/categories as a string 
#(the same as appears in the Nonbond tab of the DS MDT)
print " : Type Names: ";
my $typeNames = $nonbond->TypeNames;
print "$typeNames";

print " : Category Names: ";
my $categories = $nonbond->CategoryNames;
print "$categories";

print "\n";
}
print "\n";
```

# enum Mdm::NucleicAcidChainType datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__nucleicacidchaintype_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::NucleicAcidChainType datatype

### Description

The Mdm::NucleicAcidChainType identifies a nucleic acid type
such as DNA duplex and RNA single strand.

### Using the enum Mdm::NucleicAcidChainType datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::dnaDuplex

* Mdm::dnaRnaHybrid

* Mdm::dnaSingleStrand

* Mdm::dnaTriplex

* Mdm::rnaDnaHybrid

* Mdm::rnaDuplex

* Mdm::rnaSingleStrand

#### Used by

CreateNucleicAcid

#### Returned by

NucleicAcidChainType

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to build nucleic acids.
use strict;
use NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create and append to a DNA duplex molecule.
my $naType = Mdm::dnaDuplex;
my $nucleicAcidMolecule =
$document->CreateNucleicAcid( "CGT", $naType, Mdm::aHelix );
my $senseChain1 = $nucleicAcidMolecule->Chains->Item(0);
my $na3Prime = $senseChain1->NucleotideAt3PrimeTerminus;
$na3Prime = $document->GrowNucleicAcid( $na3Prime, "GGG", Mdm::aHelix );

printf "Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$document->ModelName,
$document->Atoms->Count();

# Create and prepend to a second DNA duplex molecule.
my $nucleicAcid2 =
$document->CreateNucleicAcid( "ACT", $naType, Mdm::aHelix );
my $senseChain2 = $nucleicAcid2->Chains->Item(0);
my $na5Prime = $senseChain2->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus;
$na5Prime = $document->GrowNucleicAcid( $na5Prime, "AAA", Mdm::aHelix );

my $secondMoleculeName = "Nucleic Acid 2";
$nucleicAcid2->Name = $secondMoleculeName;

# Ligate the two molecules using the sense strand.
$document->DeselectAll();
$na3Prime->Select;
$na5Prime->Select;
$document->LigateNucleotides( $na3Prime, $na5Prime );

# Mutate first sense nucleotide to thymidine.
$document->DeselectAll();
$senseChain1->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus->Select;
$document->MutateNucleotide( $senseChain1->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus,
Mdm::thymidine );

# Change the nucleic acid display style.
$senseChain1->DisplayStyle = Mdm::styleDnaArrowLadder;
$nucleicAcidMolecule->Chains->Item(1)->DisplayStyle =
Mdm::styleDnaArrowLadder;

printf "Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$document->ModelName,
$document->Atoms->Count();
```

# enum Mdm::OverlaySettings datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__overlaysettings_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::OverlaySettings datatype

### Description

The Mdm::OverlaySettings identifies settings to be applied
to a molecular overlay calculation.

### Using the enum Mdm::OverlaySettings datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly

* Mdm::overlayDefault

* Mdm::overlayRestoreCoordinates

#### Used by

MolecularOverlay

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
# This script illustrates how to perform a molecular overlay.
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use SbdDiscoveryScript;

# Create a new MDM document.
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $name1 = 'Molecule1';
my $name2 = 'Molecule2';

my %MolecSMARTS = (
$name1 => 'O=C([O-])C1=CC(=CC=C1)C([O-])=O',
$name2 => 'C/C1=C/C=C(C=C1)C([O-])=O'
);

# Insert two molecules 'Molecule1' and 'Molecule2' from SMILES strings.
$document->InsertFromSmiles( $MolecSMARTS{$name1} );
my $molecule1 = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
$molecule1->Name($name1);

$document->InsertFromSmiles( $MolecSMARTS{$name2} );
my $molecule2 = $document->Molecules->Item(1);
$molecule2->Name($name2);

# name of the overlay similarity property
my $overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay Similarity/' . $molecule1->Name;

# Add rotatable bond monitors to both molecules.
# These are used with flexible field alignment.
$document->AddRotatableBondMonitors;

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection(10.0, 5.0, 0.0);
$document->DeselectAll;

# Calculate the similarity before the rigid field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using rigid field alignment, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated similarity is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Rigid field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the similarity before the rigid field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using rigid field alignment.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False
}
);

printf( "Rigid field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection(5.0, 10.0, 0.0);
$document->DeselectAll;

# Calculate the similarity before flexible field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using flexible field alignment, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated similarity is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Flexible field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the similarity before flexible field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay molecules using flexible field alignment.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True
}
);

$overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay Similarity/' . $molecule1->Name;
printf( "Flexible field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

#
# Overlay molecules using tethers (tuple monitors).
#

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection( 10, 10, 5 );
$document->DeselectAll;

my $molecule1Atoms = $molecule1->Atoms;
my $molecule2Atoms = $molecule2->Atoms;

# atom mapping indices
my %atomIndices = (
0 => 8,
2 => 9,
6 => 1
);

print(" Overlay with atom tethers\n");
foreach my $id1 (sort {$a <=> $b} keys %atomIndices) {
my $id2 = $atomIndices{$id1};
my $tupleArray = Mdm::Array::Create();
$tupleArray->AddItem( $molecule1Atoms->Item($id1) );
$tupleArray->AddItem( $molecule2Atoms->Item($id2) );
$document->CreateTupleMonitor($tupleArray);
printf( " Map %s atom: %d to: %s atom: %d\n",
$molecule1->Name, $id1 + 1, $molecule2->Name, $id2 + 1 );
}

# name of the property
$overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay RMS/' . $molecule1->Name;

# Calculate the RMSD value before the alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using tethers, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated RMSD is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the RMSD value before the alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using tethers.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Remove the tethers
my $monitors = $document->TupleMonitors;
foreach my $monitor (@$monitors)
{
$monitor->Select;
}
$document->DeleteObjects;

$document->FitView;
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# enum Mdm::PredictDisulfideScope datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__predictdisulfidescope_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::PredictDisulfideScope datatype

### Description

The Mdm::PredictDisulfideScope specifies whether disulfide prediction should find intra-chain bridges only, inter-chain bridges only, or both.

### Using the enum Mdm::PredictDisulfideScope datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::anyChainDisulfides

* Mdm::interChainDisulfides

* Mdm::intraChainDisulfides

#### Used by

PredictDisulfides

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
#This is used for the script apis
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $temp = 0;
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('4ins');

#By default, the script returns string containing a csv file of properties for the predicted disulfides.
#Only new disulfides are found, for any chain combination, minimum sequence separation 5,
#maximum energy 10.0
# i.e. default args are novelDisulfidesOnly, anyChainDisulfides, 5, 10.0, true will use this one to show how to get the residues/bonds

my $csvFile=$document->PredictDisulfides();

#save the csv file
my $name=$document->ModelName();
my $fileName=$name . "Predicted_New_Disulfides.csv";
open FILE, '>' . $fileName;
print FILE $csvFile;
close FILE;

my $molecules=$document->Molecules();

#note that if validation of existing disulfides is performed (by using Mdm::existingDisulfidesOnly#or Mdm::novelAndExistingDisulfides then a second molecule containing the modelled disulfide
#bridges and with additional properties on the bond and molecule 

my $numMols=$molecules->Count; 
if($numMols == 1){

$document->DeselectAll();
my $molecule=$molecules->Item(0);
my $residuePairsAssembly = $molecule->Filter(
{ Type=>"Assembly", Property => "Name", Name => "Predicted Disulfide Bridge Residues" } );
if($residuePairsAssembly->Count() == 1){
print "Potential residue pairs for mutation to cysteine to form disulfide bridge in ".$molecule->Name . ": \n";
my $residuePairs=$residuePairsAssembly->Item(0)->Groups();
foreach my $residuePair (@$residuePairs) {
my $residuePairList=$residuePair->ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder();
#should be 2 residues in here
if($residuePairList->Count == 2){
my $residue1 = $residuePairList->Item(0);
my $residue2 = $residuePairList->Item(1);
print "Group " . $residuePair->Name . " contains residues: ". $residue1->Name . " and " . $residue2->Name . "\n";
}
}
}

#this should now also contain predicted site objects from which we can extract more properties
print "Sites for mutation to cysteine\n";
my $sites = $document->DisulfideBridgeSites;
my $numSites = $sites->Count();
print $numSites . " sites\n";
for(my $index = 0; $index < $numSites; ++$index){
my $site=$sites->Item($index);
my $label = $site->Name;
my $score = $site->GetProperty("Score");
my $energy = $site->GetProperty("Energy");
my $badContacts = $site->GetProperty("Bad Contacts");
my $depth = $site->GetProperty("Residue Depth");
my $mobility = $site->GetProperty("Thermal Mobility");
my $sep = $site->GetProperty("Sequence Separation");
my $volchange = $site->GetProperty("Volume Change");
my $env = $site->GetProperty("Environment");
my $SA = $site->GetProperty("Solvent Accessibility");
my $chi3 = $site->GetProperty("Chi3");
print " site " . $label . " score " . $score . " energy " . $energy . " Bad contacts " . $badContacts ." residue depth " . $depth . " mobility " . $mobility . " sep " . $sep . " volchange " . $volchange . " env " . $env . " SA " . $SA . " chi3 " . $chi3 . "\n";

my $SG1Coord = $site->SG1Coord;
my $SG2Coord = $site->SG2Coord;
print " SG coordinates (" . $SG1Coord->X . ", " . $SG1Coord->Y . ", " . $SG1Coord->Z . ") and " .
"(" . $SG2Coord->X . ", " . $SG2Coord->Y . ", " . $SG2Coord->Z . ")\n";
my $residues = $site->ResiduesToMutate;
if($residues->Count == 2){
print "residue 1 " . $residues->Item(0)->Name . " residue 2 " . $residues->Item(1)->Name . "\n";
}else{
print " error - site should contain two residues\n";
}

#create S-S bridge from a site - the command works on any selected DisulfideBridgeSite
if($score > 80.0){
print "Score " . $score . " - Creating S-S bridge\n"; 
$site->Select();
$document->CreateDisulfideBridges();
$site->Deselect();
}

}

}
```

# enum Mdm::PredictDisulfideType datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__predictdisulfidetype_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::PredictDisulfideType datatype

### Description

The Mdm::PredictDisulfideType specifies whether the disulfide prediction should identify novel sites only, existing sites only, or both. The latter is used for validating the method.

### Using the enum Mdm::PredictDisulfideType datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::existingDisulfidesOnly

* Mdm::novelAndExistingDisulfides

* Mdm::novelDisulfidesOnly

#### Used by

PredictDisulfides

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
#This is used for the script apis
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $temp = 0;
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('4ins');

#By default, the script returns string containing a csv file of properties for the predicted disulfides.
#Only new disulfides are found, for any chain combination, minimum sequence separation 5,
#maximum energy 10.0
# i.e. default args are novelDisulfidesOnly, anyChainDisulfides, 5, 10.0, true will use this one to show how to get the residues/bonds

my $csvFile=$document->PredictDisulfides();

#save the csv file
my $name=$document->ModelName();
my $fileName=$name . "Predicted_New_Disulfides.csv";
open FILE, '>' . $fileName;
print FILE $csvFile;
close FILE;

my $molecules=$document->Molecules();

#note that if validation of existing disulfides is performed (by using Mdm::existingDisulfidesOnly#or Mdm::novelAndExistingDisulfides then a second molecule containing the modelled disulfide
#bridges and with additional properties on the bond and molecule 

my $numMols=$molecules->Count; 
if($numMols == 1){

$document->DeselectAll();
my $molecule=$molecules->Item(0);
my $residuePairsAssembly = $molecule->Filter(
{ Type=>"Assembly", Property => "Name", Name => "Predicted Disulfide Bridge Residues" } );
if($residuePairsAssembly->Count() == 1){
print "Potential residue pairs for mutation to cysteine to form disulfide bridge in ".$molecule->Name . ": \n";
my $residuePairs=$residuePairsAssembly->Item(0)->Groups();
foreach my $residuePair (@$residuePairs) {
my $residuePairList=$residuePair->ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder();
#should be 2 residues in here
if($residuePairList->Count == 2){
my $residue1 = $residuePairList->Item(0);
my $residue2 = $residuePairList->Item(1);
print "Group " . $residuePair->Name . " contains residues: ". $residue1->Name . " and " . $residue2->Name . "\n";
}
}
}

#this should now also contain predicted site objects from which we can extract more properties
print "Sites for mutation to cysteine\n";
my $sites = $document->DisulfideBridgeSites;
my $numSites = $sites->Count();
print $numSites . " sites\n";
for(my $index = 0; $index < $numSites; ++$index){
my $site=$sites->Item($index);
my $label = $site->Name;
my $score = $site->GetProperty("Score");
my $energy = $site->GetProperty("Energy");
my $badContacts = $site->GetProperty("Bad Contacts");
my $depth = $site->GetProperty("Residue Depth");
my $mobility = $site->GetProperty("Thermal Mobility");
my $sep = $site->GetProperty("Sequence Separation");
my $volchange = $site->GetProperty("Volume Change");
my $env = $site->GetProperty("Environment");
my $SA = $site->GetProperty("Solvent Accessibility");
my $chi3 = $site->GetProperty("Chi3");
print " site " . $label . " score " . $score . " energy " . $energy . " Bad contacts " . $badContacts ." residue depth " . $depth . " mobility " . $mobility . " sep " . $sep . " volchange " . $volchange . " env " . $env . " SA " . $SA . " chi3 " . $chi3 . "\n";

my $SG1Coord = $site->SG1Coord;
my $SG2Coord = $site->SG2Coord;
print " SG coordinates (" . $SG1Coord->X . ", " . $SG1Coord->Y . ", " . $SG1Coord->Z . ") and " .
"(" . $SG2Coord->X . ", " . $SG2Coord->Y . ", " . $SG2Coord->Z . ")\n";
my $residues = $site->ResiduesToMutate;
if($residues->Count == 2){
print "residue 1 " . $residues->Item(0)->Name . " residue 2 " . $residues->Item(1)->Name . "\n";
}else{
print " error - site should contain two residues\n";
}

#create S-S bridge from a site - the command works on any selected DisulfideBridgeSite
if($score > 80.0){
print "Score " . $score . " - Creating S-S bridge\n"; 
$site->Select();
$document->CreateDisulfideBridges();
$site->Deselect();
}

}

}
```

* Mdm::proteinColorByAminoAcidChain

* Mdm::proteinColorByCAlpha

* Mdm::proteinColorByCell

* Mdm::proteinColorByHydrophobicity

* Mdm::proteinColorByMolecule

* Mdm::proteinColorByNToCTerminal

* Mdm::proteinColorByPKa

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to colors amino acids and amino acid chains.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Create array with ProteinColorScheme values.
my @proteinColorOptions = (
Mdm::proteinColorByAminoAcidChain, Mdm::proteinColorByCAlpha,
Mdm::proteinColorByCell, Mdm::proteinColorByHydrophobicity,
Mdm::proteinColorByMolecule, Mdm::proteinColorByNToCTerminal,
Mdm::proteinColorByPKa, Mdm::proteinColorByResidue,
Mdm::proteinColorBySecondaryType, Mdm::proteinColorByRainbow
);
```

# enum Mdm::ProteinPoseDisplayStyle datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__proteinposedisplaystyle_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::ProteinPoseDisplayStyle datatype

### Description

The Mdm::ProteinPoseDisplayStyle identifies the symbol used to display docked protein poses.

### Using the enum Mdm::ProteinPoseDisplayStyle datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::styleProteinPoseDefault

* Mdm::styleProteinPoseJack

* Mdm::styleProteinPosePoint

* Mdm::styleProteinPoseSiteNone

* Mdm::styleProteinPoseSphere

#### Used by

DisplayStyle

#### Returned by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use ProteinPose properties.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing docked protein poses.\n";
print " 3 Enter a cluster ID in the Arguments tab.\n";
print " 4 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

my ($clusterID) = @ARGV;

if ( $clusterID !~ /^\d+$/ )
{
$clusterID = 1;
}

# The script assume the last active document contains ProteinPoses.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage( 'This example requires an open Molecule Window containing '
. 'docked protein poses.' )
unless ($document);

# Get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter.
my $poseGroups = $document->DockedProteinPoseAssemblies;
Usage( 'This example requires an open Molecule Window containing '
. 'docked protein poses.' )
unless ( $poseGroups->Count > 0 );

my $poses = $document->ProteinPoses;

my $topClusterPose;

# Show all poses in cluster $clusterID, color green.
foreach my $pose (@$poses)
{
if ( $pose->Cluster == $clusterID )
{
$pose->SetVisible();

# Represent best ranked pose in the cluster as sphere and color light green.
if ( $pose->IsTopClusterPose )
{
$pose->DisplayStyle(Mdm::styleProteinPoseSphere);
$pose->Color( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 0 ) );
$topClusterPose = $pose;
}

# Represent other cluster members as jacks and color dark green.
else
{
$pose->DisplayStyle(Mdm::styleProteinPoseJack);
$pose->Color( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 122, 0 ) );
}
}
else
{

# Hide all poses not in the cluster.
$pose->SetInvisible();
}
}
```

# enum Mdm::QueryBondType datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__querybondtype_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::QueryBondType datatype

### Description

The Mdm::QueryBondType specifies the bond types that can be matched by a 2D substructure query.

### Using the enum Mdm::QueryBondType datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::queryAnyBond

* Mdm::queryAromaticBond

* Mdm::queryDoubleBond

* Mdm::querySingleBond

* Mdm::queryTripleBond

#### Used by

AddBondType , RemoveBondType

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');

$document->CreateAndTopology();

# The query bonds are automatically created using
# the CreateAndTopology function. However, to show
# how to create them using CreateBondQuery, we will delete
# them and then add them again.

my $querybonds = $document->QueryBonds;
foreach my $querybond (@$querybonds)
{
$querybond->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

my $bonds = $document->Bonds;
foreach my $bond (@$bonds)
{
my $querybond =
$document->QueryOperators()->Item(0)->CreateQueryBond($bond);
$querybond->AddBondType('queryAnyBond');
}

# removes the first query bond's bond type
$document->QueryBonds->Item(0)->RemoveBondType('queryAnyBond');
```

# enum Mdm::QueryOperation datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__queryoperation_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::QueryOperation datatype

### Description

The Mdm::QueryOperation type identifies the type of a query operator
in a Catalyst query.
The type is used to specify query logic (and, or, exclude),
query type (fit, shape), or whether a standard feature is used
in the query (include).

### Using the enum Mdm::QueryOperation datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::queryAnd

* Mdm::queryExclude

* Mdm::queryFit

* Mdm::queryInclude

* Mdm::queryNoOperation

* Mdm::queryOr

* Mdm::queryShape

#### Used by

CreateQueryOperator , Type

#### Returned by

Type

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create some features on the query
# Create a donor feature at 0,0,0
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create an acceptor feature at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

# create the location constraint. The $fitOperator and the parent operator of $acceptorOperator are the same in this case.
# Either can be used to create the location constraint.
my $locationfeatureHead =
$acceptorOperator->GetParentOperator()
->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Check to see if a proper query has been made and print out some information
if ( $fitOperator->HasChildOperators() )
{
print "Query successfully made, fit operator has child operators.\n";
my $headPoint = $newAcceptor->HeadXYZ;
my $tailPoint = $newAcceptor->TailXYZ;
printf "Head : %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n", $headPoint->X, $headPoint->Y,
$headPoint->Z;
printf "Tail : %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n", $tailPoint->X, $tailPoint->Y,
$tailPoint->Z;
print "Radius of location constraint on tail "
. $newAcceptor->TailFeature()->LocationSphereRadius . "\n";
}
$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# enum Mdm::ReferenceAxis datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__referenceaxis_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::ReferenceAxis datatype

### Description

The Mdm::ReferenceAxis specifies which principal axis of a set of protein atoms is used to define an Mdm::Membrane object's orientation. Mdm::referenceAxisZ specifies the longest principal axis,
Mdm::referenceAxisX specifies the shortest.

The membrane properties MembraneRotation , MembraneShift , and MembraneTilt are defined relative to the specified Mdm::ReferenceAxis.

### Using the enum Mdm::ReferenceAxis datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::referenceAxisX

* Mdm::referenceAxisY

* Mdm::referenceAxisZ

#### Used by

CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor , ProteinReferenceAxis

#### Returned by

ProteinReferenceAxis

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use properties of the MembraneOrientationMonitor
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load structure of BOVINE RHODOPSIN, 1f88 and keep only first chain
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# "Guess" some value for the membrane position
my $center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, -3.2 );
my $normal = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.521, 0.106, 0.847 );

my $membrane =
$document->CreateMembrane( $center, $normal, 60.0, 60.0, 30.0 );

$document->SetParent( $molecule, $membrane );

my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms();

# Illustrate on how to use MembraneOrientationMonitor preferences
my $membraneOrientation =
$molecule->CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor( $membrane, $atoms,
Mdm::objectCentered, Mdm::referenceAxisZ );

$document->UpdateViews();

my $monitors = $document->MembraneOrientationMonitors;
print "Number of membrane monitors: ". $monitors->Count. "\n";

my $membranes = $document->Membranes;
print "Number of membranes: ". $membranes->Count. "\n";

sleep(2);

$membraneOrientation->DisplayLocation = Mdm::membraneCentered;
$membraneOrientation->ProteinReferenceAxis = Mdm::referenceAxisX;
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to access several residue properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1CRN.pdb' );

my $cysteineCount = 0;
my $alanineCount = 0;
my $sequence = "";

my $residues = $document->Residues;
foreach my $residue (@$residues)
{
print 'Residue Name: ' . $residue->Name . "\n\t";
print 'ID: ' . $residue->Id . "\n\t";
print 'PDB: ' . $residue->PDBName . "\n\t";
print 'SymbolandId: ' . $residue->SymbolAndId . "\n\t";
print 'Hydrophobicity: ' . $residue->Hydrophobicity . "\n\t";
print 'pKa: ' . $residue->pKa . "\n";

# Create the one-letter sequence from the symbol.
$sequence = $sequence . $residue->Symbol;

++$cysteineCount if ( $residue->Type eq Mdm::cys );
++$alanineCount if ( $residue->LongName eq 'Alanine' );
}

printf "Number of cysteine residues: %d \n", $cysteineCount;
printf "Number of alanine residues: %d \n", $alanineCount;
printf "Protein sequence is: %s\n", $sequence;
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w

use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9ins.pdb" );

printf "Structure %s atoms: %d residues %d\n", $document->ModelName, 
$document->Atoms->Count, $document->Residues->Count;

# Mark side chain conformation violations.
my $pink = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 255, 200, 200 );
$document->MarkSideChainConformationViolations( Mdm::oldfieldRotamerLibrary, 30.0, $pink );

# Note: if you want to use the mainchain-dependent Dunbrack library, the second
# argument is a sigma multiplier rather than an angle tolerance, thus:
$document->MarkSideChainConformationViolations( Mdm::dunbrackRotamerLibrary, 3.0 );

# Get the side chain conformation violation monitors.
my $monitors =
$document->FilterByProperty('SidechainConformationMonitor name="*"');

# Report the number of violations.
my $violationCount = $monitors->Count;
printf "Structure has %d side-chain conformation violations.\n\n",$violationCount;
# Print a table of violations.
if ( $violationCount > 0 )
{
printf("Index\t Name\t\t Residue \t\tChi Angles\n");
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $violationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s\t",
$index+1, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Residues") );
foreach (qw(Chi1 Chi2 Chi3 Chi4)) {
my $_chi = $monitor->GetProperty($_); 
printf("%8.3f ",$_chi ) if defined $_chi;
}
print("\n"); 
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# enum Mdm::SuperimposeProteinAtomType datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_mdm__superimposeproteinatomtype_datatype.htm

## enum Mdm::SuperimposeProteinAtomType datatype

### Description

The Mdm::SuperimposeProteinAtomType specifies whether all atoms,
only Carbon alpha atoms, or only protein backbone atoms
are employed in the superposition of two proteins.

### Using the enum Mdm::SuperimposeProteinAtomType datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingAllAtoms

* Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingBackboneAtoms

* Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms

#### Used by

GetSuperimposeProteinMatrix , SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs , SuperimposeProtein , SuperimposeProteinByAlignment

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use superimposition functions
# and RMSD calculation functions for amino acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load 2rcs (an unligated antibody) from PDB.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '2rcs.pdb' );

# Load 1aj7 (a ligated antibody having the same sequence as 2crs) from PDB.
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

my $molecule2rcs = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[1];

my $hv2rcs = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 2rcs H chain V domain
my $hv1aj7 = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 1aj7 H chain V domain

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $molecule2rcs->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv2rcs->AddItem($aminoAcid);

$aminoAcid = $molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv1aj7->AddItem($aminoAcid);
}

# Show the transformation matrix which would superimpose the Vh
# domains by C-alpha atoms. This does not alter the coordinates
# of either structure.
my $matrix = $document->GetSuperimposeProteinMatrix( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
print "Transformation matrix:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 4 ; ++$i )
{
print "\t";
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < 4 ; ++$j )
{
printf "%.3f ", $matrix->GetEntry( $i, $j );
}
print "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms
my $rmsd = $document->SuperimposeProtein( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
printf "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms: %.3f\n\n", $rmsd;

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD. Note that by default the functions return an
# array of per-residue RMSD values, finishing with the overall RMSD
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it in which case the value will be zero. This can happen
# for unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation
# only for selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the
# required atoms for the requested type of calculation. 
# If you do not want per-residue RMSDs, set the 4th parameter ResidueReport
# False. In this case the array will only contain the overall RMSD.
# In this example, the all protein rmsd has no residue values calculated
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True, False );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item(0);
print "\n";

#Show that the all protein array contains just the overall RMSD.
printf "Number of values returned for all protein is %d\n", $apRmsd->Count();

# Demonstrating that the array is for all residues plus overall value not
# just selected and that as the first chain(L) is unselected its values
# are 0.
printf "Number of values returned for sidechains is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0), $scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

#Create a C-Alpha monitor
my $caMonitor = $document->CreateCAlphaMonitor();

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs before superimposing.\n";
if ($cAlphaPairs->Count > 0) {
printf "The first C-alpha to C-alpha pair distance is %.3f Angstroms.\n",
$cAlphaPairs->Item(0)->Distance;
}

#Lets do it for all matching atoms just to show the argument
my $rmsdByCA =
$document->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( $document->Molecules(), $caMonitor,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingAllAtoms );

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs after superimposing.\n";

#The values returned are like for Superimpose By Alignment - the first value
# is ref-ref (ie 0) then ref-mover for each superimposed molecule.
my $numVal = $rmsdByCA->Count();
printf( "Number of values returned for SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs %d\n",
$numVal );
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $numVal ; ++$i )
{
printf( "RMSD %d is %f\n", $i, $rmsdByCA->[$i] );
}

# use the filter function to retrieve the CAlpha atoms
my $cAlphaMonitors = $document->CAlphaMonitors;
foreach my $m (@$cAlphaMonitors)
{
print $m->ClassName ." filter entries: " . $m->CAlphaPairs->Count. "\n";
}

print "Finished Superimpose Script Example\n";
```

* Mdm::surfaceColorByAromaticEdgeFace

* Mdm::surfaceColorByAtomCharge

* Mdm::surfaceColorByAtomColor

* Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential

* Mdm::surfaceColorByGrid

* Mdm::surfaceColorByHydrogenBondDonorAcceptor

* Mdm::surfaceColorByHydrophobicity

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to colors selected surfaces.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Generate array with Color Scheme values.
my @surfaceColorSchemes = (
Mdm::surfaceColorByAtomCharge,
Mdm::surfaceColorByAtomColor,
Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential,
Mdm::surfaceColorByParentColor
);

print "Creating a solid surface (this may take a few seconds)...\n\n";
my $allAtoms = $document->Atoms;
my $surface =
$document->CreateSolidSurface( $allAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent, False,
Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential, 1.3 );
sleep(1);

foreach my $surfaceColorScheme (@surfaceColorSchemes)
{
print "Color surface by surface color scheme: $surfaceColorScheme...\n\n";
$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);
$surface->Select();

$document->SetSurfaceColorScheme($surfaceColorScheme);

$surface->Deselect();
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(1);
}
```

# enum Protocol::State datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_protocol__state_datatype.htm

## enum Protocol::State datatype

### Description

The Protocol::State identifies the execution status of a protocol.

### Using the enum Protocol::State datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Protocol::taskCanceled

* Protocol::taskCancelling

* Protocol::taskComplete

* Protocol::taskDoneRunning

* Protocol::taskDownload

* Protocol::taskDownloadError

* Protocol::taskFailed

* Protocol::taskNotStarted

* Protocol::taskProcessingResults

* Protocol::taskRunning

* Protocol::taskStarted

* Protocol::taskStopping

* Protocol::taskSystemError

#### Returned by

State , WaitForCompletion

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

## enum Sdm::AlignmentLayoutType datatype

### Description

The Sdm::AlignmentLayoutType identifies the display layout of the
Sequence Window.

### Using the enum Sdm::AlignmentLayoutType datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Sdm::chainViewLayout

* Sdm::extendedLayout

* Sdm::fitToWidthLayout

* Sdm::wrappedLayout

#### Returned by

AlignmentLayout

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate use of alignment layout (client only).
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use strict;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

sub SetLayout($$$)
{
# This function will invoke the specified layout.
# Graphically, the UI will update after each action.

my ($document, $layout, $action) = @_;
my $originalLayout = $document->Alignment->AlignmentLayout;

print 'Change to ' . $layout . " layout ...\n";
$document->InvokeAction($action);

my $newLayout = $document->Alignment->AlignmentLayout;
die 'Failure: Layout not set to ' . $layout . " layout.\n"
unless ( $newLayout eq $layout );

sleep(2);
}

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences;
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(0, 'S1', 
'AAAAABBBBBCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(1, 'S2', 
'AAAAABBBBBCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(2, 'S3', 
'AAAAABBBBBCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(3, 'S4', 
'AAAAABBBBBCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC');

$alignment->Sequence(0)->MarkStartOfChain(5);
$alignment->Sequence(1)->MarkStartOfChain(5);
$document->UpdateViews();

SetLayout($document, "chainViewLayout", 'ActionChainViewLayout');
SetLayout($document, "extendedLayout", 'ActionExtendedViewLayout');
SetLayout($document, "wrappedLayout", 'ActionWrappedViewLayout');
```

# enum Sdm::AminoAcidSecondaryStructurePredictor datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_sdm__aminoacidsecondarystructurepredictor_datatype.htm

## enum Sdm::AminoAcidSecondaryStructurePredictor datatype

### Description

The Sdm::AminoAcidSecondaryStructurePredictor identifies the secondary structure prediction type.

### Using the enum Sdm::AminoAcidSecondaryStructurePredictor datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

| Prediction Type | Value |
| --- | --- |
| DSC definition | Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType |
| Kabsch and Sander definition | Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType |
| PDB definition | Sdm::pdbSecondaryStructureType |

#### Used by

AddProteinSecondaryStructure , IsSecondaryStructureVisible , ProteinSecondaryStructure , ProteinSecondaryStructureObject , ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity

#### Returned by

Predictor

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to predict and retrieve secondary structure.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

my $sequence =
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( $mdmDocument->Molecules->[0] );
$alignment->PredictSecondaryStructureByDsc();

# Example accessing the secondary structure string from sequence property.
my $kabschAndSander =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructure(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType);
print "Kabsch and Sander secondary structure:\n";
print "Encoded: $kabschAndSander\n";

# Ensure alignment is displaying secondary structure.
if ( !( $alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown ) )
{
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown = True;
}

# Ensure KAS is displayed
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureVisible(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType) =
True;

# Example accessing the secondary structure data from object.
print "DSC secondary structure:\n";
my $ssObject =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructureObject(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);

print 'Predictor: ' . $ssObject->Predictor . "\n";
print 'Has probabilities: ' . $ssObject->IsPredicted . "\n";

my $dsc = $ssObject->SecondaryStructureString;
print "Encoded: $dsc\n";

my $propensity =
$sequence
->ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);
print "Propensity: $propensity\n";

my $helicalResidueCount = 0;
my $sheetResidueCount = 0;
my $coilResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $ssObject->ResidueCount;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $ssObject->SsType($i);
++$helicalResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$sheetResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::sheet || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
++$coilResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::coil || $type eq Sdm::extracellular );
}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print 'Analysis: The DSC secondary structure for this sequence has '
. $helicalResidueCount
. ' amino acid residues in helical formations, '
. $sheetResidueCount
. ' in sheet formations and '
. $coilResidueCount
. " in coil formations.\n";

my $secstrucfilter = $sdmDocument->SecondaryStructures;
print "Number of secondary Structures: ", $secstrucfilter->Count . "\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to apply color schemes to the alignment window.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $sequence0 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'ASDFADS' );
my $sequence1 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S2', 'ASDFASD' );

# Color background by charge similarity.
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
$alignment->BackgroundColorScheme = Sdm::colorByChargeSimilarity;

$document->UpdateViews();

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to custom color the alignment window.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $sequence0 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'ASDFASD' );
my $sequence1 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S2', 'ASDFASD' );

# Enable custom coloring of residues (instead of auto coloring).
# NOTE: The existing colors are not changed until individual
# residues are colored
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
$alignment->BackgroundColorScheme = Sdm::colorByCustomColor;
$alignment->ForegroundColorScheme = Sdm::colorByCustomColor;

my $black = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 0, 0, 0 );
my $white = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 255, 255, 255 );

# Reset the colors to black text on a white background.
my $sequenceCount = $alignment->SequenceCount;
my $residueFgColorType = Sdm::colorText;
my $residueBgColorType = Sdm::colorBackground;
for (
my $sequenceIndex = 0 ;
$sequenceIndex < $sequenceCount ;
++$sequenceIndex
)
{
my $sequence = $alignment->Sequence($sequenceIndex);
my $residueCount = $sequence->ResidueCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $residueCount ; ++$index )
{
$sequence->Residue($index)->Color( $residueFgColorType, $black );
$sequence->Residue($index)->Color( $residueBgColorType, $white );
}
}

# Apply custom colors to residues foreground.
my $count = $sequence0->ResidueCount;
my $color = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 255, 0, 0 );
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
$sequence0->Residue($index)->Color( Sdm::colorText, $color );
}

$alignment->Sequence(2)->IsVisible = True;
$document->UpdateViews();

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w

# Sdm::Feature class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASDFGHJKL' );

. $color->Green . ' '
. $color->Blue . ")\n";

print "\t" . "Is label visible\t" . $feature->IsLabelVisible . "\n";
print "\t" . "Is label horizontal\t" . $feature->IsLabelHorizontal . "\n";

}
```

# enum Sdm::GeneticCodeType datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_sdm__geneticcodetype_datatype.htm

## enum Sdm::GeneticCodeType datatype

### Description

The Sdm::GeneticCodeType specifies the rules to translate genetic nucleic acid
information (encoded in DNA or RNA sequences) into amino acid sequences.

### Using the enum Sdm::GeneticCodeType datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Sdm::alternativeYeastNuclearGeneticCode

* Sdm::ascidianMitochondrialGeneticCode

* Sdm::bacterialAndPlantPlastidGeneticCode

* Sdm::blepharismaNuclearGeneticCode

* Sdm::chlorophyceanMitochondrialGeneticCode

* Sdm::ciliateDasycladaceanAndHexamitaNuclearGeneticCode

* Sdm::echinodermMitochondrialGeneticCode

* Sdm::euplotidNuclearGeneticCode

* Sdm::flatwormMitochondrialGeneticCode

* Sdm::invertebrateMitochondrialGeneticCode

* Sdm::moldMitochondrialGeneticCode

* Sdm::scenedesmusObliquusMitochondrialGeneticCode

* Sdm::thraustochytriumMitochondrialGeneticCode

* Sdm::trematodeMitochondrialGeneticCode

* Sdm::universalGeneticCode

* Sdm::vertebrateMitochondrialGeneticCode

* Sdm::yeastMitochondrialGeneticCode

#### Used by

TranslateSequence

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to translate a DNA sequence.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $dnaDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId({Id => 'y13252', Database => "nuccore"});

my $dnaSequence = $dnaDocument->Sequence(0);
printf "NA Sequence: %s\n", $dnaSequence->SequenceString();

# Translate the full sequence using the default options and store
# in a protein sequence document.
my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$document->Alignment->DeleteSequence(0);
my $sequence = $dnaSequence->TranslateSequence();
$document->Alignment->InsertSequence( 0, $sequence );

# Translate full sequences with an offset of 1.
# The arguments are:
# 1 - the starting position for translation (0-based residue index);
# 2 - the number of residues to include in translation (a negative count,
# the default, indicates the end of sequence);
# 3 - the genetic code (specifies the nucleic to amino acid mapping).
$sequence =
$dnaSequence->TranslateSequence( 1, -1, False, Sdm::universalGeneticCode );
$document->Alignment->InsertSequence( 1, $sequence );

# Translate full sequences with an offset of 2.
$sequence = $dnaSequence->TranslateSequence(2);
$document->Alignment->InsertSequence( 2, $sequence );
```

Type

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Location class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASDFGHJKL' );

# Create a join feature for residues DFGH.
my $segmentStart = 2;
my $segmentCount = 4;
my $location = Sdm::Location::Create( Sdm::locationTypeJoin, $segmentStart,
$segmentCount );

print "Location properties\n";

my $locationType = $location->Type;
print "Location type\t" . $locationType . "\n";

my $segmentCount = $location->SegmentCount;
print "Segment count\t$segmentCount \n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $segmentCount ; ++$index )
{
my $segment = $location->Segment($index);
print "Segment $index...\n";
print "\tStart position:\t" . $segment->StartPosition . "\n";
print "\tEnd position:\t" . $segment->EndPosition . "\n";
print "\tSegementType:\t" . $segment->Type . "\n";
print "\tIs complement?:\t" . $segment->IsComplement . "\n";
}

my $feature =
Sdm::Feature::CreateCustomFeature( 'Custom feature', $location );

# Add this feature to the sequence.
$sequence->AddFeature($feature);
```

# enum Sdm::SecondaryStructureDescriptorType datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_sdm__secondarystructuredescriptortype_datatype.htm

## enum Sdm::SecondaryStructureDescriptorType datatype

### Description

The Sdm::SecondaryStructureDescriptorType identifies
the secondary structure descriptor type. The type Sdm::secondaryStructureType
represents the amino acid secondary structure. The type
Sdm::transmembraneSecondaryStructureType represents the amino acid
location in a transmembrane protein.

### Using the enum Sdm::SecondaryStructureDescriptorType datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Sdm::secondaryStructureType

* Sdm::transmembraneSecondaryStructureDescriptorType

#### Used by

AddProteinSecondaryStructure

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl
# Illustrate how to add a secondary structure.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0);

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$sdmDocument->DeleteAlignmentSequences();
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule($molecule);

my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown = True;
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

my $sequence = $alignment->Sequence(0);
my $secondaryStructure = $sequence->AddProteinSecondaryStructure(
{
Predictor => Sdm::userDefinedSecondaryStructureType1,
SecondaryStructre => 'HHHHHHHHHHSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC',
UserDefinedPredictorHasProbabilityData => False,
UserDefinedDescriptor => Sdm::secondaryStructureType
}
);
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$sdmDocument->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $sdmDocument->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```
