# enum Sdm::SegmentType datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_sdm__segmenttype_datatype.htm

## enum Sdm::SegmentType datatype

### Description

The Sdm::SegmentType identifies a segment as a site or a range.
A range refers to a range of bases/residues in a sequence, notated
in GenBank by 1..N. A site refers to a site between
two bases/residues notated in GeneBank by 1^2.

### Using the enum Sdm::SegmentType datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Sdm::segmentRange

* Sdm::segmentSite

#### Used by

Type

#### Returned by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Location class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASDFGHJKL' );

# Create a join feature for residues DFGH.
my $segmentStart = 2;
my $segmentCount = 4;
my $location = Sdm::Location::Create( Sdm::locationTypeJoin, $segmentStart,
$segmentCount );

print "Location properties\n";

my $locationType = $location->Type;
print "Location type\t" . $locationType . "\n";

my $segmentCount = $location->SegmentCount;
print "Segment count\t$segmentCount \n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $segmentCount ; ++$index )
{
my $segment = $location->Segment($index);
print "Segment $index...\n";
print "\tStart position:\t" . $segment->StartPosition . "\n";
print "\tEnd position:\t" . $segment->EndPosition . "\n";
print "\tSegementType:\t" . $segment->Type . "\n";
print "\tIs complement?:\t" . $segment->IsComplement . "\n";
}

my $feature =
Sdm::Feature::CreateCustomFeature( 'Custom feature', $location );

# Add this feature to the sequence.
$sequence->AddFeature($feature);
```

# enum Sdm::SsType datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_sdm__sstype_datatype.htm

## enum Sdm::SsType datatype

### Description

The Sdm::SsType identifies the secondary structure type for
amino acids in the sequence. For standard secondary structures,
the types are helical, sheet, and coil. For transmembrane secondary
structures, valid types are helical, cytosol, and extracellular.

### Using the enum Sdm::SsType datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Sdm::coil

* Sdm::cytosol

* Sdm::extracellular

* Sdm::helical

* Sdm::sheet

#### Used by

SsType , SsTypeProbability

#### Returned by

SsType

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to predict and retrieve secondary structure.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

my $sequence =
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( $mdmDocument->Molecules->[0] );
$alignment->PredictSecondaryStructureByDsc();

# Example accessing the secondary structure string from sequence property.
my $kabschAndSander =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructure(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType);
print "Kabsch and Sander secondary structure:\n";
print "Encoded: $kabschAndSander\n";

# Ensure alignment is displaying secondary structure.
if ( !( $alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown ) )
{
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown = True;
}

# Ensure KAS is displayed
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureVisible(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType) =
True;

# Example accessing the secondary structure data from object.
print "DSC secondary structure:\n";
my $ssObject =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructureObject(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);

print 'Predictor: ' . $ssObject->Predictor . "\n";
print 'Has probabilities: ' . $ssObject->IsPredicted . "\n";

my $dsc = $ssObject->SecondaryStructureString;
print "Encoded: $dsc\n";

my $propensity =
$sequence
->ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);
print "Propensity: $propensity\n";

my $helicalResidueCount = 0;
my $sheetResidueCount = 0;
my $coilResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $ssObject->ResidueCount;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $ssObject->SsType($i);
++$helicalResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$sheetResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::sheet || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
++$coilResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::coil || $type eq Sdm::extracellular );
}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print 'Analysis: The DSC secondary structure for this sequence has '
. $helicalResidueCount
. ' amino acid residues in helical formations, '
. $sheetResidueCount
. ' in sheet formations and '
. $coilResidueCount
. " in coil formations.\n";

my $secstrucfilter = $sdmDocument->SecondaryStructures;
print "Number of secondary Structures: ", $secstrucfilter->Count . "\n";
```

# enum Sdm::UpdateFeatureAction datatype

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/enum_sdm__updatefeatureaction_datatype.htm

## enum Sdm::UpdateFeatureAction datatype

### Description

The Sdm::UpdateFeatureAction identifies the action for UpdateFeatures .

### Using the enum Sdm::UpdateFeatureAction datatype

#### Values

This datatype can be set to one of the following values:

* Sdm::addFeatures

* Sdm::mergeFeatures

* Sdm::replaceFeatures

#### Used by

UpdateFeatures

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to merge features from one sequence to another.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';
my $filePath = $samplesFolder . 'D.funebris ADH Gene.bsml';

my $document1 = DiscoveryScript::Open($filePath);
my $source = $document1->Sequence(0);

# Create a replicate sequence without features.
my $document2 = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $target = $document2->Sequence(0);
$target->Name = '1crn copy';
$target->InsetSequenceString( 0, $source->SequenceString() );
$document2->UpdateViews();

# Merge features from source to target.
$target->UpdateFeatures( $source, Sdm::mergeFeatures );
$document2->ShowAnnotations(0);
$document2->UpdateViews();

my $index = 0;
my $count = $document2->SequenceCount;
printf "Found %d sequences\n", $count;
while ( $index < $count )
{
my $sequence = $document2->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

# Erase function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/erase_function.htm

## Erase function

### Description

Erase deletes a range of residues in an Sdm::Alignment and replaces them with gaps.

### Applies to

The Erase function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment , Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the Erase function

#### Instance

$object->Erase( <index>, <startposition>, [count] );

$object->Erase( <startposition>, [count] );

$object->Erase( { Index => <index>, StartPosition => <startposition>, Count => [count] } );

$object->Erase( { StartPosition => <startposition>, Count => [count] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| <startposition> | Required | | Integer |
| [count] | Optional | 1 | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence Sdm::Sequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use SDM Erase function.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence1 =
$document->CreateSequence( 'Sequence1', 'AAAAPPPPCCCCCCCC' );
my $sequence2 =
$document->CreateSequence( 'Sequence2', 'AAAAEEEECCCCCCCC' );

my $alignmentData = $alignment->AlignmentStrings;
print "Initial sequences:\n";
print ' ' . $alignmentData->Item(0) . "\n";
print ' ' . $alignmentData->Item(1) . "\n\n";

# Example use of Sdm::Alignment::Erase.
my $sequenceIndex = 0;
my $residueIndex = 4; # Index of first P residue.
$alignment->Erase({
Index=>$sequenceIndex, 
StartPosition=>$residueIndex, 
Count=>4});

my $alignmentData = $alignment->AlignmentStrings;
print "Sequences after erasing via Sdm::Alignment::Erase function:\n";
print ' ' . $alignmentData->Item(0) . "\n";
print ' ' . $alignmentData->Item(1) . "\n\n";

# Example use of Sdm::Sequence::Erase.
my $residueIndex = 4; # Index of first P residue.
$sequence2->Erase({
StartPosition=>$residueIndex, 
Count=>4});

my $alignmentData = $alignment->AlignmentStrings;
print "Sequences after erasing via Sdm::Sequence::Erase function:\n";
print ' ' . $alignmentData->Item(0) . "\n";
print ' ' . $alignmentData->Item(1) . "\n\n";

# EraseSelection function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/eraseselection_function.htm

## EraseSelection function

### Description

EraseSelection deletes selected residues in an Sdm::Alignment and
replaces them with gaps. You can also use the DeleteSelection to remove gaps.

### Applies to

The EraseSelection function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the EraseSelection function

#### Instance

$object->EraseSelection();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to erase a selection (Also known as 
# replacing the selection with gaps.
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment= $document->Alignment;
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences;
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(0, 'S1', 'AAAAAABBBBBBCCCCCCCCCCC');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(1, 'S2', 'AAAAAABBBBBBCCCCCCCCCCC');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(2, 'S3', 'AAAAAABBBBBBCCCCCCCCCCC');

$alignment->Select(0, 4, 4); # Select columns [4,8) from S1 
$alignment->Select(1, 4, 4); # Select columns [4,8) from S2 
$alignment->Select(2, 4, 6); # Select columns [4,10) from S3 

# Replace selected residues with gaps.
$alignment->EraseSelection();

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

## EulerAngles property

### Description

### Applies to

### Using the EulerAngles property

#### Get

my $pointObject = $object->EulerAngles;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $pointObject | | | Mdm::Point |
| $object | | | Mdm::ProteinPose |

#### Set

$object->EulerAngles = <rotation>;

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <rotation> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| $object | | | Mdm::ProteinPose |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

Use for Mdm::ProteinPose :

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use ProteinPose properties.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing docked protein poses.\n";
print " 3 Enter a cluster ID in the Arguments tab.\n";
print " 4 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

my ($clusterID) = @ARGV;

if ( $clusterID !~ /^\d+$/ )
{
$clusterID = 1;
}

# The script assume the last active document contains ProteinPoses.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage( 'This example requires an open Molecule Window containing '
. 'docked protein poses.' )
unless ($document);

# Get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter.
my $poseGroups = $document->DockedProteinPoseAssemblies;
Usage( 'This example requires an open Molecule Window containing '
. 'docked protein poses.' )
unless ( $poseGroups->Count > 0 );

my $poses = $document->ProteinPoses;

my $topClusterPose;

# Show all poses in cluster $clusterID, color green.
foreach my $pose (@$poses)
{
if ( $pose->Cluster == $clusterID )
{
$pose->SetVisible();

# Represent best ranked pose in the cluster as sphere and color light green.
if ( $pose->IsTopClusterPose )
{
$pose->DisplayStyle(Mdm::styleProteinPoseSphere);
$pose->Color( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 0 ) );
$topClusterPose = $pose;
}

# Represent other cluster members as jacks and color dark green.
else
{
$pose->DisplayStyle(Mdm::styleProteinPoseJack);
$pose->Color( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 122, 0 ) );
}
}
else
{

# Hide all poses not in the cluster.
$pose->SetInvisible();
}
}
```

# ExactMolecularWeight property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/exactmolecularweight_property.htm

## ExactMolecularWeight property

### Description

ExactMolecularWeight indicates the exact molecular weight of a molecule. Instead of using the average atomic mass of all stable isotopes of each element type as done in calculating the molecular weight, the atomic mass of the single most abundant isotope is used to calculate the exact molecular weight.

### Applies to

The ExactMolecularWeight property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the ExactMolecularWeight property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->ExactMolecularWeight;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |

| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

MdmDiscoveryScript

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

$molecule->IsChargeCalculated = True;

print "The following is a list of molecule properties:\n";
print 'Name: ' . $molecule->Name . "\n";

print 'Molecular formula: ' . $molecule->MolecularFormula . "\n";
print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Radius of gyration: ' . $molecule->RadiusOfGyration . "\n";
print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Rotatable bond count: ' . $molecule->RotatableBondCount . "\n";
print 'Surface area: ' . $molecule->SurfaceArea . "\n";

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles(
'OC(=O)C1=CC=C(C=C1)CN/C2=C/C=C(C=C2)C=CC(=O)C[Cl]');
AddHydrogens($document);

my $atoms = $document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $double_bond_oxygens = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $nitrogens = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $halogens = Mdm::Array::Create();

foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( ( $atom->Element eq 'O' ) && ( $atom->BondCount == 1 ) )
{
$double_bond_oxygens->AddItem($atom);
}
$nitrogens->AddItem($atom) if ( $atom->Element eq 'N' );
$halogens->AddItem($atom) if ( $atom->Element =~ /(Cl|F|Br|I)\b/i );
}

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Features and location constraints
my $featureCount = 0;
foreach my $atom (@$double_bond_oxygens)
{
++$featureCount;
my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
my $featureName = "HBA_" . $featureCount;
$acceptorOperator->Name($featureName);
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atom);

# create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );
}

foreach my $atom (@$nitrogens)
{
++$featureCount;
my $featureName = "HBD_" . $featureCount;
my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name($featureName);
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atom);

#create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );
}

# Add excluded volumes at the location of halogen atoms
foreach my $atom (@$halogens)
{
my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

# Add excluded volumes at the projection point of HBAs and HBDs
my $acceptorfeatures = $fitOperator->AcceptorFeatures;
foreach my $acceptor (@$acceptorfeatures)
{
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atom->XYZ = $acceptor->HeadXYZ();
$molecule->Select();

my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

my $donorfeatures = $fitOperator->DonorFeatures;
foreach my $donor (@$donorfeatures)
{
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atom->XYZ = $donor->HeadXYZ();
$molecule->Select();

my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

my $exclusionfeatures = $document->ExclusionFeatures();
my $exclusionfeatureCount = 0;
foreach my $exclusionfeature (@$exclusionfeatures)
{
++$exclusionfeatureCount;
my $name = "EV_" . $exclusionfeatureCount;
$exclusionfeature->Name($name);
}

# We will delete temporary atoms used to create EVs
# on projection points. Need to update objects before
# deleting so we preserve the X,Y,Z location.
$document->UpdateObjects();

# Delete temporary atoms
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# Expand function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/expand_function.htm

## Expand function

### Description

Expand adds an atom ( Mdm::Atom ) adjacent to a selected bond
( Mdm::Bond ), thereby expanding a ring or chain by one atom.

### Applies to

The Expand function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the Expand function

#### Command

$object->Expand( [sprouthydrogens] );

$object->Expand( { SproutHydrogens => [sprouthydrogens] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [sprouthydrogens] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# create a benzene molecule
$document->InsertFromSmiles('C1=CC=CC=C1');
printf "Total Atoms: %d\n" , $document->Atoms->Count;
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;

# add hydrogens
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms();

# select a bond
my $bonds = $document->Bonds->Item(1)->Select;

# run Expand on the bond to get a 7 ring
$document->Expand();

$document->DeselectAll();
$document->UpdateViews();
printf "Total Atoms: %d\n" , $document->Atoms->Count;
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
```

# ExpandBindingSite function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/expandbindingsite_function.htm

## ExpandBindingSite function

### Description

ExpandBindingSite expands the size of a binding site.

### Applies to

The ExpandBindingSite function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ExpandBindingSite function

#### Command

$object->ExpandBindingSite( <bindingsite>, [numberofcycles] );

$object->ExpandBindingSite( { BindingSite => <bindingsite>, NumberOfCycles => [numberofcycles] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <bindingsite> | Required | | Mdm::BindingSite |
| [numberofcycles] | Optional | 1 | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

SbdDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate binding site expansion.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '4PHV.pdb' );

# Remove ligands and water from complex (using DSCommands).
Delete( $document, GetLigands($document) );
Delete( $document, GetWaters($document) );

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

# Change display to protein ribbon tubes.
TurnOffProteinAtoms($document);
ApplyProteinDisplayStyle( $document, Mdm::styleProteinRibbonTube );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Find binding sites.
$document->CreateBindingSitesFromCavities($molecule);
my $bindingSites = $document->BindingSites;
my $site = $bindingSites->Item(0);
my $volume = $site->GetProperty("Volume");

print "Volume before expansion: $volume\n";

# Expand a binding site by 4 cycles. After expansion, the binding
# sites objects will be recreated so we need to redefine the
# array $bindingSites and $site
$document->ExpandBindingSite( $site, 4 );
$bindingSites = $document->BindingSites;
$site = $bindingSites->Item(0);
$volume = $site->GetProperty("Volume");

print "Volume after expansion: $volume\n";
```

# ExpandShell function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/expandshell_function.htm

## ExpandShell function

### Description

ExpandShell progressively shows more supporting non-bond interactions
between the ligand and receptor of a Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor object. Each call to the ExpandShell function
includes additional receptor interactions with receptor residues
already identified as either interacting with the ligand or
supporting interactions with the ligand.
The function ContractShell progressively hides these
shells of interactions.

### Applies to

The ExpandShell function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor

### Using the ExpandShell function

#### Instance

my $booleanValue = $object->ExpandShell();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the create a ligand non-bond monitor, 
# browse ligands and show supporting non-bond interactions. 

use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('2FL6');
die "Failed to create a valid MDM document!" unless $document;

my $receptor = $document->ReceptorInFocus;
die "The open document does not have a defined receptor!" unless $receptor;

$document->FocusOnFirstLigand;
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
die "The open document does not have a defined ligand!" unless $ligand;

my $ligandNonbondMonitor =
$document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();
$document->UpdateViews();

my $nonbondMonitors = $document->NonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d NonbondMonitors.\n", $nonbondMonitors->Count;
my $ligandNonbondMonitors = $document->LigandNonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d LigandNonbondMonitors.\n", $ligandNonbondMonitors->Count;

# Step through the ligands
while ($document->FocusOnNextLigand())
{
sleep(2);
}

# Step through the ligands backwards
$document->FocusOnLastLigand();
while ($document->FocusOnPreviousLigand())
{
sleep(2);
}

# Expand shell to progressively view supporting interactions.
$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

# Contract shell to hide supporting interactions.
$ligandNonbondMonitor->ContractShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

print "Done\n";
```

#!/usr/bin/perl -w

# ExtracellularColor property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/extracellularcolor_property.htm

## ExtracellularColor property

### Description

ExtracellularColor specifies the color of the extra-cellular plane of an Mdm::Membrane object.
The extra-cellular plane is defined as the plane in the negative direction from the membrane Center (i.e., in the opposite direction of the membrane Normal ).

### Applies to

The ExtracellularColor property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Membrane

### Using the ExtracellularColor property

#### Get

my $colorObject = $object->ExtracellularColor;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $colorObject | | | DiscoveryScript::Color |
| $object | | | Mdm::Membrane |

#### Set

$object->ExtracellularColor = <color>;

$object->ExtracellularColor( <color> );

$object->ExtracellularColor( { Color => <color> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <color> | Required | | DiscoveryScript::Color |
| $object | | | Mdm::Membrane |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrate how to create a membrane.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

# Remove all chains except the first.
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# "Guess" some value for the membrane position.
my $center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, -3.2 );
my $normal = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.521, 0.106, 0.847 );
my $membrane =
$document->CreateMembrane( $center, $normal, 60.0, 60.0, 30.0 );

# Pick a different color scheme from default.
$membrane->CytosolColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 255 ) ); # cyan
$membrane->ExtracellularColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 255, 255, 0 ) ); # yellow
$document->SetParent( $molecule, $membrane );
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

# Change some membrane properties.
$center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, 3.2 );
$normal = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.521, -0.106, -0.847 );

$membrane->Thickness = 35;
$membrane->Normal = $normal;
$membrane->Center = $center;
```

# FavorableNonbonds filter

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/favorablenonbonds_filter.htm

## FavorableNonbonds filter

### Description

FavorableNonbonds indicates all favorable interactions in a specific context,
such as an Mdm::Array , Mdm::Set , Mdm::Document , or descendants of an Mdm::NonbondMonitor .

### Applies to

The FavorableNonbonds filter can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Array , Mdm::Document , Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::NonbondMonitor , Mdm::Set

### Using the FavorableNonbonds filter

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->FavorableNonbonds;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::Array Mdm::Document Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor Mdm::NonbondMonitor Mdm::Set |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the basic non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3fzm');
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;
$document->Zoom(15);
$document->IsHierarchyViewShown = True;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Create a non-bond monitor for a subset of atoms.\n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $monitor = $document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();

# -- Analyze the identified interactions. ---------------------------
my $nonbonds = $monitor->Nonbonds;
my $count = $nonbonds->Count;
printf "Found %d non-bond interactions (total):\n", $count;

print $monitor->FavorableNonbonds->Count 
. " of these are favorable interactions (such as H-bonds).\n";
print $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds->Count
. " of these are unfavorable interactions (such as bumps).\n\n";

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Analyze first non-bond interaction:\n";
my $nonbond = $nonbonds->Item(0);

my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$nonbond->Distance;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
my $unfavorableNonbonds = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds;
if ($unfavorableNonbonds->Count > 0) 
{
print "Analyze first unfavorable non-bond interaction:\n";
my $unfavorableNonbond = $unfavorableNonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $unfavorableNonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $unfavorableNonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$unfavorableNonbond->Distance;
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "All non-bonds of a particular type can be retrieved ";
print "using the NonbondsOfType filter.\n";
my $hBonds = $monitor->NonbondsOfType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType);
printf "Found %d hydrogen bonds using NonbondOfType filter.\n\n", $hBonds->Count;

print "Alternatively the IsMatchingNonbondType property can be used to \n";
print "identify interactions of a specific types. The following atom pairs \n";
print "indicate classical hydrogen bonding: \n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
if ($nonbond->IsMatchingNonbondType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType))
{
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);

print '* ' . $atom1->FullName . " (";
print 'donor ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrogenDonor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHalogen);
print 'positive ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPositive);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ') and ';

print $atom2->FullName . " (";
print 'acceptor ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrogenAcceptor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHalogen);
print 'negative ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsNegative);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ")\n";
}
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "\nThe NonbondTypes property can be used to identify all \n";
print "interaction types of a non-bond.\n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
printf "- %s (%s) and %s (%s):",
$nonbond->FromSite->Name,
$nonbond->FromSite->ChemistryName,
$nonbond->ToSite->Name,
$nonbond->ToSite->ChemistryName;

#these are the type enums 
print " Types: ";
my $nonbondTypes = $nonbond->NonbondTypes;
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
print "$type ";
}

#these are the category enums 
print " Categories: ";
my $nonbondCategories = $nonbond->NonbondCategories;
foreach my $category (@$nonbondCategories) {
print "$category ";
}

#these APIs give the name(s) of the type/categories as a string 
#(the same as appears in the Nonbond tab of the DS MDT)
print " : Type Names: ";
my $typeNames = $nonbond->TypeNames;
print "$typeNames";

print " : Category Names: ";
my $categories = $nonbond->CategoryNames;
print "$categories";

print "\n";
}
print "\n";
```

#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script will illustrate functions and properties of the
# Sdm::Feature class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASDFGHJKL' );

. $color->Green . ' '

print "\t"
. "Label color\t("
. $color->Red . ' '
. $color->Green . ' '
. $color->Blue . ")\n";
print "\t" . "Label type\t" . $feature->LabelFromType . "\n";
print "\t" . "Is label visible\t" . $feature->IsLabelVisible . "\n";
print "\t" . "Is label horizontal\t" . $feature->IsLabelHorizontal . "\n";
print "\t" . "Feature Location type\t" . $location->Type . "\n";
}

# Ffdm::Document::Create function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/ffdm__document__create_function.htm

## Ffdm::Document::Create function

### Description

Create creates one or more Ffdm::Document objects.

### Applies to

The Ffdm::Document::Create function can be used with the following objects:

Ffdm::Document

### Using the Ffdm::Document::Create function

#### Static

my $documentObject = Ffdm::Document::Create( <forcefieldtype>, [nodisplay] );

my $documentObject = Ffdm::Document::Create( { ForceFieldType => <forcefieldtype>, NoDisplay => [nodisplay] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | Ffdm::Document |
| <forcefieldtype> | Required | | enum Ffdm::ForceFieldType |
| [nodisplay] | Optional | False | Boolean |

#### Defined by

ForceFieldDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
# Demonstrate creating a force field document
# and applying a forcefield to a molecule.
use strict;
use ForceFieldDiscoveryScript;
use File::Path;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

my $tempDir = DiscoveryScript::GetTemporaryFolder()."/typingEx";

mkdir $tempDir if(not -e $tempDir);

print "Creating CHARMm force field document.\n";
my $forcefield = Ffdm::Document::Create(Ffdm::charmmForceField);

print "Applying CHARMm force field to 1crn.\n";
my $status = $forcefield->ApplyForceField( $document, True, True, True,
Ffdm::useMomanyRonePartialCharges );

if ( $status == Ffdm::applyForceFieldCompleted )
{
print "Molecule successfully typed.\n";
$forcefield->Save($tempDir.'/1crn.ffml');
}
else
{
die "Failed to type molecule.\n";
}

my @properties = ("Forcefield","PartialChargeMethod","UseResidueTemplateCharge","ForcefieldBase" );
my $molecules = $document->Molecules()->Item(0);
foreach my $pname (@properties)
{
my $prop = $molecules->GetProperty($pname);
print "$pname: $prop\n";
}

print "\tName\tType\tCharge\n";
my $atoms = $molecules->Atoms;
my $count = 0;
foreach $a (@$atoms)
{
my $fftype = $a->GetProperty('ForcefieldType');
my $ffcharge = $a->GetProperty('Partial Charge');
printf("%5d)\t%-4s\t%-4s\t%.3f\n", ++$count, $a->Name , $fftype, $ffcharge);
}

# remove file
unlink ($tempDir.'/1crn.ffml');
rmtree $tempDir;
```

### Description

The Ffdm::Document represents a forcefield data model document.
This document contains the forcefield name and any
new parameters estimated during the typing process.

### Using the Ffdm::Document object

The Ffdm::Document object can be accessed via the ForceFieldDiscoveryScript package.

#### Properties

ClassName , IsActiveWindow , ModelName , ModelType

ActivateWindow , ApplyForceField , ClearForceField , Close , CreateSimulationFiles , Ffdm::Document::Create , GetTypingStatus , Insert , InsertFromUrl , InvokeAction , InvokePluginAction , Load , Save , SaveImage

#### Returned by

Ffdm::Document::Create , Load

DiscoveryScript::Document -> DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

ForceFieldDiscoveryScript

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Example: Creates a force field document
use strict;

# Filter function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/filter_function.htm

## Filter function

### Description

Filter collects the objects that have the specified properties.
The properties are assumed to be expressed as a set of name-value pairs from the table below.
Each name-value pair is optional except that when a property is specified, both the
Property-PropertyName and the PropertyName-value pairs must be provided.

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | Object type as a String |
| TypeMode | Filter mode as an enum Mdm::FilterMode , Mdm::filterBlockMode or Mdm::filterPassMode (default) |
| Element | Element type as a String |
| ElementMode | Filter mode as an enum Mdm::FilterMode |
| Id | ID as a String or Integer |
| IdMode | Filter mode as an enum Mdm::FilterMode |
| Label | Label as a String |
| LabelMode | Filter mode as an enum Mdm::FilterMode |
| Selected | Flag as a Boolean (True or False) |
| SelectTopLevel | Flag as a Boolean (False is the default). Only applied when combined with a Selected filter. This can be used, for example, to filter selected atoms only in molecules that are not selected. |
| Visible | Flag as a Boolean |
| VisibleTopLevel | Flag as a Boolean (False is the default). Only applied when combined with a Visible filter. This can be used, for example, to filter visible atoms only in molecules that are not visible. |
| Property | Property name as a String |
| PropertyName | Property value as a String , Integer , or Real |
| PropertyMode | Filter mode as an enum Mdm::FilterMode (Mdm::filterPassMode is the default) |

### Applies to

The Filter function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AcceptorFeature , Mdm::AminoAcid , Mdm::AminoAcidChain , Mdm::AngleFeature , Mdm::AngleMonitor , Mdm::Animation , Mdm::Assembly , Mdm::Atom , Mdm::BindingSite , Mdm::BindingSitePoint , Mdm::Bond , Mdm::BondAngleViolationMonitor , Mdm::BondLengthViolationMonitor , Mdm::Bump , Mdm::BumpMonitor , Mdm::CAlphaMonitor , Mdm::CAlphaPair , Mdm::CAlphaViolationMonitor , Mdm::Cell , Mdm::CentroidFeature , Mdm::CentroidMonitor , Mdm::Chain , Mdm::Chiral , Mdm::ChiralityMonitor , Mdm::CisPeptideMonitor , Mdm::Conformation , Mdm::Conformer , Mdm::ConformerAtom , Mdm::ConformerBond , Mdm::ConformerModel , Mdm::Constraint , Mdm::Cylinder , Mdm::DihedralFeature , Mdm::DihedralRestraint , Mdm::DipoleMomentMonitor , Mdm::DistanceFeature , Mdm::DistanceMonitor , Mdm::DistanceRestraint , Mdm::DisulfideBridgeSite , Mdm::DockedProteinPoseAssembly , Mdm::Document , Mdm::DonorFeature , Mdm::ExclusionFeature , Mdm::FixedAtomConstraint , Mdm::Geometric3d , Mdm::Group , Mdm::HarmonicAtomRestraint , Mdm::HydrogenBond , Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor , Mdm::Isosurface , Mdm::Label3d , Mdm::Label , Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::LocationFeature , Mdm::MainChainConformationViolationMonitor , Mdm::Membrane , Mdm::MembraneOrientationMonitor , Mdm::MissingMainChainMonitor , Mdm::MissingSideChainMonitor , Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::MoleculeAssembly , Mdm::Monitor , Mdm::Neighbor , Mdm::NeighborMonitor , Mdm::Nonbond , Mdm::NonbondMonitor , Mdm::NormalFeature , Mdm::NormalMonitor , Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::NucleicAcidChain , Mdm::Nucleotide , Mdm::Object , Mdm::Offlineable , Mdm::OfflineableConformation , Mdm::PiBond , Mdm::PiCationMonitor , Mdm::PiInteractionMonitor , Mdm::PiPiMonitor , Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor , Mdm::PlanarPeptideViolationMonitor , Mdm::PlaneFeature , Mdm::PlaneMonitor , Mdm::PointFeature , Mdm::PointOffsetFeature , Mdm::Polydot , Mdm::PropertyLabel , Mdm::ProteinChiralityViolationMonitor , Mdm::ProteinNomenclatureViolationMonitor , Mdm::ProteinPose , Mdm::Query , Mdm::QueryAtom , Mdm::QueryBond , Mdm::QueryFeatureMap , Mdm::QueryOperator , Mdm::Residue , Mdm::Restraint , Mdm::RingAromaticFeature , Mdm::RotatableBondMonitor , Mdm::ScreenLabel , Mdm::ShapeFeature , Mdm::SideChainConformationViolationMonitor , Mdm::SlicingPlane , Mdm::Sphere , Mdm::Surface , Mdm::TorsionMonitor , Mdm::TupleMonitor , Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond , Mdm::Valence , Mdm::ValenceMonitor , Mdm::VectorFeature

### Using the Filter function

#### Instance

my $arrayObject = $object->Filter( <description> );

my $arrayObject = $object->Filter( { Description => <description> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| <description> | Required | | DiscoveryScript::ObjectMap |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#Collect the Carbon atoms:
$document->Filter( { Type => "Atom", Element => Mdm::carbon } );

#Collect the non-Carbon atoms:
$document->Filter( { Type => "Atom", Element => Mdm::carbon, ElementMode => Mdm::filterBlockMode } );

#Collect the non-Carbon atoms:
$document->Filter( { description => { Type => "Atom", Element => Mdm::carbon,
ElementMode => Mdm::filterBlockMode } } );

#Collect the objects with a property named "when" with a value of "now":
$document->Filter( { Property => "when", when => "now" } );

#Collect the atoms with a property named "when" with a value of "now":
$document->Filter( { Type => "Atom", Property => "when", when => "now" } );

#Collect the atoms without a property named "when" with a value of "now":
$document->Filter( { Type => "Atom", Property => "when", when => "now", PropertyMode => Mdm::filterBlockMode } );

#Collect the selected atoms whose parents are not selected
$document->Filter( { Type => "Atom", Selected => "True", SelectedTopLevel => True } );

#Collect the visible molecules
$document->Filter( { Type => "Molecule", Visible => "True" } );
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to create a transparent surface.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '101m.pdb' );

# Select heme atoms.
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="HEM.*"; Atom label="*"');

# Create an array of all heme atoms.
my $hemeAtoms = $document->Filter( { Selected => 1 } )->Atoms;

# Create transparent surface around the heme group.
my $transparentSurface =
$document->CreateTransparentSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential,
1.3, 0.6 );

$transparentSurface->IsBackSideColorEnabled(True);
$transparentSurface->IsBackSideTransparencyEnabled(True);

# Also create wiremesh surface around the heme group.
my $wiremeshSurface =
$document->CreateWiremeshSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential, 2.0 );

print "Surface area: "
. $transparentSurface->Area . "\n"
. "Surface Volume: "
. $transparentSurface->Volume . "\n";
print "Surface probe radius: "
. $transparentSurface->ProbeRadius . "\n"
. "Transparency Level: "
. $transparentSurface->TransparencyLevel . "\n";

# Select all atoms within 6A of the heme and the surface.
$document->SelectByRadius( 6.0, 'Atom' );
$transparentSurface->Select();

# Show only the heme and neighboring atoms (other than water).
$document->FitView();
$document->InvertSelection();
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue name="HOH.*"; Atom label="*"');
$document->Hide();
$document->DeselectAll();

# Display the wiremesh surface with delay.
sleep(2);
$wiremeshSurface->SetVisible();
```

# FilterByProperty function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/filterbyproperty_function.htm

## FilterByProperty function

### Description

FilterByProperty collects the objects that have the specified description.
The description is assumed to be string with the following format: [ Scope ; ] Object where,

Scope: Object Object: type property-expression type: Atom Bond Molecule etc. property-expression: name op value [ , name op value, ... ] name: string op: = != value: property-value property-value: string "regexp" number number-range number-range: "number-number"

### Applies to

The FilterByProperty function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the FilterByProperty function

#### Instance

my $arrayObject = $object->FilterByProperty( <description> );

my $arrayObject = $object->FilterByProperty( { Description => <description> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| <description> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
# Collect atoms with id = 5:
my $collection = $document->FilterByProperty('Atom id=5');

# Collect the carbon atoms in the molecule named molecule1:
my $collection = $document->FilterByProperty('Molecule name=molecule1; Atom element=Carbon');

# Collect the amino acids which are not alanine:
my $collection = $document->FilterByProperty('aminoacid 1-letter!=a');

# Collect the residues 4 through 7 and 38 through 44 in chains named A:
my $collection = $document->FilterByProperty('Chain name=A; Residue id="4-7", id="38-44"');
```

# FilterByString command

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/filterbystring_command.htm

## FilterByString command

### Description

Creates an array containing a set of objects using a simple string specifying
molecule, chain, residue and atom. For example,
"1db1:A:ARG121,128-130,140:N,C,CA" can be used to select N, C and CA atoms in
residues named ARG121, or with IDs 128-130 or 140 in chain A of a molecule
called 1db1.
The string is a semi-colon separated list of specifications. Each specification is a colon
separated list of names and ids. Each specification can have up to 4 fields. If only one is
given, that corresponds to a residue. Two corresponds to a residue:atom,
three is chain:residue:atom and the full specification of 4 is
molecule:chain:residue:atom.
For molecules and chains, the field should be a comma separated list of allowed names.
For residues the field can be either a 3-letter residue type (e.g. ALA - all alanine residues),
a range of IDs, (e.g. 140-150), or a residues name (e.g. ALA43). Any combination of these can be
given in a comma separated list.
For atoms, either names or IDs can be given.
The wildcard "*", or an empty string, "::", can be given to match anything.

### Using the FilterByString command

my $array = FilterByString( <document>, <input_string> );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

#### Defined by

MdmCommands

### Examples

Retrieves atoms from a document based on various criteria.

```text
use strict;
use MdmCommands;

# Retrieves all C-alpha and C-beta alanine atoms in the document
my $atoms = FilterByString($document,"*:*:ALA:CA,CB");
# Retrieves all backbone heavy atoms in chain A
my $atoms = FilterByString($document, "A::C,CA,N,O");
# Retrieves all residues with IDs 100-200
my $atoms = FilterByString($document, "100-200");
# Retrieves all atoms in chain B
my $atoms = FilterByString($document, "B:*:*");
# Retrieves all backbone and phenylalanine sidechain atoms
my $atoms = FilterByString($document, ":C,CA,N,O,HA;PHE:*");
# Retrieves all CA atoms in named residues of molecule 1crn
my $atoms = FilterByString($document, "1crn::ASN12,PHE13,ASN14:CA");
```

### Using the FindActiveConformation function

#### Instance

my $conformationObject = $object->FindActiveConformation();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $conformationObject | | | Mdm::Conformation |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Create a few conformations by rotating the phi torsion
# angle of the first amino acid residue.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Get first three amino acids
my $aminoAcid1 = $aminoAcids->Item(0);
my $aminoAcid2 = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
my $aminoAcid3 = $aminoAcids->Item(2);

# Creates a monitor for the phi angle
my $phiTorsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$aminoAcid1->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid2->AmideNitrogen,
$aminoAcid2->CAlpha, $aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon
);

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index <= 6 ; ++$index )
{
my $torsionValue = $index * 60.0;

# rotates the first residue's phi angle
$phiTorsion->SetProperty( "Angle", "$torsionValue" );

# creates a new conformation
my $conformation = $molecule->CreateConformation();
$conformation->MakeActive();

# sets the current conformation to be invisible
# so the next newly created conformation will be "active" and updated with new coordinates
$conformation->SetInvisible(True);
}
my $activeConformation = $aminoAcid1->FindActiveConformation();

# creates an animation using the newly created conformations
my $animation = $document->CreateAnimation( $molecule->Conformations );
my $frameCount = $animation->FrameCount;
print "Number of animation frames: $frameCount frames\n";

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $frameCount ; $i++ )
{
printf " Frame: %d\n", $i + 1; 
$animation->ActivateNextFrame();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(1);
}
```

# FindAggregationSites function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/findaggregationsites_function.htm

## FindAggregationSites function

### Description

For a molecule with calculated aggregation propensity values at a specified
radius rad, this finds patches of adjacent residues having aggregation
propensity values over a specified threshold. The residues are assigned to
groups that appear in the hierarchy as Aggregation Sites | Radius rad | Site n.
Residues that have been assigned to a patch group have a property Aggr Rrad SiteID
that contains the site ID of the patch.

### Applies to

The FindAggregationSites function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the FindAggregationSites function

#### Command

$object->FindAggregationSites( [radius], [minpeakcutoff], [minpatchcutoff] );

$object->FindAggregationSites( { Radius => [radius], MinPeakCutoff => [minpeakcutoff], MinPatchCutoff => [minpatchcutoff] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [minpatchcutoff] | Optional | 0.0 | Real |
| [minpeakcutoff] | Optional | 0.1 | Real |
| [radius] | Optional | 10 | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1hzh');

#This API calculates solvent accessible areas using the DS Client method and 
#then uses these to calculate aggregation propensities. It should be noted that
#this will not give the same results as the protocol.

# Calculate the Aggregation values 
my $gridNumber = 240;
my $radius = 5;

$document->ProteinAggregationPropensity(
$gridNumber, $radius
);

#Note that if you have precomputed the Solvent Accessible Areas for each atom
#and they are stored in atom property named SAA, then the following may be used
#instead - this is what is done in the Calculate Aggregation Scores protocol 
#which calculates the SAAs using CHARMm
# $document->ProteinAggregationPropensityFromSaa( $radius);

#Now create the patch groups
my $minPeakCutoff = 0.2;
my $minPatchCutoff = 0.0;

$document->FindAggregationSites($radius);

#Now do another radius
$radius=10;
$document->ProteinAggregationPropensity(
$gridNumber, $radius
);
$document->FindAggregationSites($radius);

#create surface colored by aggregation values

$radius=5;
$document->ShowAggregationSurface($radius);

sleep(5);

#now use the API with a different radius - it will recolor the existing
#surface
$radius=10;
$document->ShowAggregationSurface($radius);

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
printf "Aggregation 5A : %.4f\n", $molecule->GetProperty("Aggr R5");
printf "Aggregation 10A : %.4f\n", $molecule->GetProperty("Aggr R10");
printf "Total Solvent Accessibility %.1f\n", $molecule->GetProperty("Total Solvent Accessibility");
```

## FindAllAtomsInFragment function

### Description

FindAllAtomsInFragment finds all Mdm::Atom objects in the same fragment
as the supplied Mdm::Array subset of Atom objects.
The supplied collection must only contain unique Atom objects.
The function returns an array containing all the atoms in the fragment
if the supplied collection consists of
objects belonging to a single fragment.
Otherwise, the function returns an empty array.

### Applies to

The FindAllAtomsInFragment function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the FindAllAtomsInFragment function

#### Instance

my $arrayObject = $object->FindAllAtomsInFragment( <atomsubset> );

my $arrayObject = $object->FindAllAtomsInFragment( { AtomSubset => <atomsubset> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| <atomsubset> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
# Demonstrate the use of FindAllAtomsInFragment function.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3fzm');
die "Failed to download PDB file." unless $document;

$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
my $contents = $ligand->Array->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $atomInLigand = $contents->Item(0);

my $subset = Mdm::Array::Create();
$subset->AddItem($atomInLigand);

# FindAllAtomsInFragment returns an array of all the atoms
# in a fragment given a subset of the atoms. In this case, we
# supply one atom in the ligand and the method returns all
# the atoms.
my $allAtomsInLigand = $document->FindAllAtomsInFragment($subset);
print 'The ligand contains ' . 
$allAtomsInLigand->Count . " atoms.\n";

# FindBondTypes function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/findbondtypes_function.htm

## FindBondTypes function

### Description

FindBondTypes detects and fixes missing bonds and incorrect orders based
on the geometry of the structure. Residues having known templates are not
changed. An option is available to suppress the creation of missing bonds.

### Applies to

The FindBondTypes function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the FindBondTypes function

#### Instance

$object->FindBondTypes( [createmissingbonds] );

$object->FindBondTypes( { CreateMissingBonds => [createmissingbonds] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [createmissingbonds] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use the FindBondTypes function.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Create a ligand molecule.
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles(
'O=C3N=C2C=CC1=NC[S][C@]1([H])C2=C3CNc4ccc(cc4)[S](=O)(=O)Nc5ncccc5');

sleep(2);

# Reduce all bonds to single bonds.
printf "Setting all Bonds to Single\n\n";
my $bonds = $document->Bonds;
my $count = 0;
my @initialBonds = ();
foreach my $bond (@$bonds)
{
my $beforeType = $bond->BondType;
push ( @initialBonds, $beforeType);
$bond->BondType = Mdm::singleBond;
printf "%3d) %s \t changed to %s\n", ++$count, $beforeType, $bond->BondType;
}

$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

# Detect and assign bond types based on chemistry and 3D geometry.
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
printf "\nRecalculating Bonds....\n\n";
$molecule->FindBondTypes();
$document->UpdateViews();

# Check bond types
my $bonds = $document->Bonds;
my $count = 0;
printf "\t Initial \t\t Calculated\n";
foreach my $bond (@$bonds)
{
printf "%3d) \t %s \t\t %s\n", $count+1, $initialBonds[$count], $bond->BondType;
$count++;
}
```

# FindCommonAncestor function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/findcommonancestor_function.htm

## FindCommonAncestor function

### Description

FindCommonAncestor finds the ancestor that is common to all items in a collection.

### Applies to

The FindCommonAncestor function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Array , Mdm::Set

### Using the FindCommonAncestor function

#### Instance

my $objectObject = $object->FindCommonAncestor();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $objectObject | | | Mdm::Object |
| $object | | | Mdm::Array Mdm::Set |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to manipulate items in an Mdm::Array.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

my $atoms = $document->Atoms;

# Collect all cysteine atoms.
my $cysteineAtomArray = Mdm::Array::Create();
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
$cysteineAtomArray->AddItem($atom)
if ( $atom->GetProperty("Parent") =~ /CYS/i );
}

# Find the common ancestor of all atoms in the array in cysteineAtomArray.
my $parent = $cysteineAtomArray->FindCommonAncestor();
print "The common parent object of all CYS atoms: "
. $parent->ClassName . " "
. $parent->Name . "\n";

die "No cysteine atoms found! Exiting.\n" if $cysteineAtomArray->IsEmpty;

my $cysteineAtomCount = $cysteineAtomArray->Count;
print "Number of atoms in cysteine residues: " . $cysteineAtomCount . "\n";

# Delete all atoms except C-alpha and C-beta.
# Note: When deleting items from an array, the array is traversed in
# reverse order. This avoids having to account for changes in the item
# indices as the array is modified.
for ( my $i = $cysteineAtomCount - 1 ; $i >= 0 ; --$i )
{
my $atom = $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i);
if ( $atom->Name !~ /(cb|ca)\b/i )
{
$cysteineAtomArray->DeleteItem($i);
}
}
print "Number of C-alpha and C-beta atoms in cysteine residues: "
. $cysteineAtomArray->Count . "\n";

# Create a copy of the original array in reverse order.
$cysteineAtomCount = $cysteineAtomArray->Count;
my $reverseCysteineArray = Mdm::Array::Create();

# Use the AddItem function to insert the first atom.
# Note: the InsertItem function cannot be used on an empty array.
$reverseCysteineArray->AddItem( $cysteineAtomArray->Item(0) );
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $cysteineAtomCount ; ++$i )
{
$reverseCysteineArray->InsertItem( 0, $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i) );
}

# Swap the first two elements or the original array.
my $tempItem = $cysteineAtomArray->Item(0);
$cysteineAtomArray->ReplaceItem( 0, $cysteineAtomArray->Item(1) );
$cysteineAtomArray->ReplaceItem( 1, $tempItem );

# Print out the IDs of the atoms in the two arrays side by side.
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $cysteineAtomCount ; ++$i )
{
my $atom1Id = $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i)->Id;
my $atom2Id = $reverseCysteineArray->Item($i)->Id;
print "item $i\t $atom1Id\t $atom2Id\n";
}

# Remove all remaining items in the original array.
$cysteineAtomArray->ClearItems();
print "The array now has " . $cysteineAtomArray->Count . " elements\n";
```

use strict;

my $mdm = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('4phv');
my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures($mdm);
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

# Copy current document state to object attributes. Generally the 
# attribute data is not updated after loading a BSML file. To get 
# the current state as attributes call this function. 
$document->ClearBsmlAttributes();
$document->BuildBsmlAttributes();

# List the Alignment object attributes.
print "Alignment attributes...\n";
my $attributes = $alignment->AttributeMap;
my $key = $attributes->FirstKey;
while (!$key->IsEndKey)
{
print $key->Name . ":\t" . $attributes->Item($key) . "\n";
$key = $attributes->NextKey($key);
}
print "end\n\n";

# List the Sequence object attributes.
my $sequences = $document->Sequences;
my $i = 0;
foreach my $sequence (@$sequences)
{
print "Sequence $i attributes...\n";
my $attributes = $sequence->AttributeMap;
my $key = $attributes->FirstKey;
while (!$key->IsEndKey)
{
print $key->Name . ":\t" . $attributes->Item($key) . "\n";
$key = $attributes->NextKey($key);
}
print "end\n\n";

my $k = $attributes->FindItem('ResidueID');
print 'Find Name: ' . $k->Name . "\tValue: "
. $attributes->Item($k) . "\n\n";

# List the Feature object attributes.
my $features = $sequence->Features;
my $f = 0;
foreach my $feature (@$features)
{
print "Feature $f attributes...\n";
my $fattributes = $feature->AttributeMap;
my $fkey = $fattributes->FirstKey;
print $feature->Key . "\n";
while (!$fkey->IsEndKey)
{
print $fkey->Name . ":\t" . $fattributes->Item($fkey) . "\n";
$fkey = $fattributes->NextKey($fkey);
}

print "end\n\n";
++$f;
} 

++$i; 
}

# Update the current document to match attribute data.
$document->UpdateFromBsmlAttributes();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# FindSurfacePropertySites function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/findsurfacepropertysites_function.htm

## FindSurfacePropertySites function

### Description

For a molecule with specified calculated numeric residue property values, this finds patches of adjacent residues for which that property is over a specified threshold.
The residues are assigned to groups that appear in the hierarchy as <propertyName> Sites | Site n.
Residues that have been assigned to a patch group have a property <propertyName> SiteID that contains the site ID of the patch.
Setting the Negative option True allows patches at minima rather than maxima to be found.

### Applies to

The FindSurfacePropertySites function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the FindSurfacePropertySites function

#### Command

$object->FindSurfacePropertySites( <propertyname>, [saacutoff], [minpeakcutoff], [minpatchcutoff], [negative] );

$object->FindSurfacePropertySites( { PropertyName => <propertyname>, SAACutoff => [saacutoff], MinPeakCutoff => [minpeakcutoff], MinPatchCutoff => [minpatchcutoff], Negative => [negative] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <propertyname> | Required | | String |
| [minpatchcutoff] | Optional | 0.0 | Real |
| [minpeakcutoff] | Optional | 0.1 | Real |
| [negative] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [saacutoff] | Optional | 5.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
##########
#
# Assign various properties to amino acids and their atoms 
# These may then be used to calculate 'residue feature' values over spatial neighborhoods.
# 

use MdmDiscoveryScript; # For working with Molecule Window
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

# Set this False to calculate custom residue neighborhood feature set
my $default = "True";
#property for surface display and site creation can be set on the command line.
#note that it is case sensitive
my $propertyName = "0A_CX_average";

if(@ARGV != 0){
($propertyName) = @ARGV;
}

# to run on a molecule in the active window, use this instead of OpenURL
# my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl(PdbUrlPrefix. '1aqk.pdb');

# Return an error message and exit if there is not an active Molecule Window
die "No Molecule Window!" unless $document;
$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);
print "Calculating atom properties\n";
# Many of the residue features depend on solvent surface accessibility and require that the atoms 
# have a precomputed SAA property, which is typically calculated using CHARMm.
# However, for demonstration purposes we can use the DS method and rename the property.

#check if the first atom already has SAA property, if not then do calculation.
my $atoms = $document->Atoms();
my $atom = $atoms->Item(0);
if(! $atom->HasProperty("SAA")) {
print "No precomputed SAA properties, calculating Solvent Accessible Surface\n";
$document->SolventAccessibleSurface();
$document->RenameUserProperty("Atom Solvent Accessibility","SAA",$atom->ClassName());
$document->RenameUserProperty("Percent Sidechain Solvent Accessibility","Fractional Sidechain SAA",$atom->Parent()->ClassName()); 
$document->RenameUserProperty("Percent Solvent Accessibility","Fractional Residue SAA",$atom->Parent()->ClassName());
#convert the percent accessibilities to fractional values for consistency with the method below 
foreach my $atom(@$atoms){
if($atom->HasProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA")){
my $sa = $atom->GetProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA")/100.0;
$atom->SetProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA",$sa);
}
if($atom->HasProperty("Fractional Residue SAA")){
my $sa = $atom->GetProperty("Fractional Residue SAA")/100.0;
$atom->SetProperty("Fractional Residue SAA",$sa);
}
}
}else{
#This calculates the Sidechain and Residue fractional exposures, using the precomputed SAA atom properties.
#the extended tripeptide exposures have been calculated for various CHARMm forcefields, with the appropriate 
#set used according to the forcefield setting on the structure.
$document->CalculateFractionalResidueExposures(True,True);
}
#Set the Black and Mould hydrophobicities for each amino acid residue. The argument specifies whether to 'normalize' the values
#to set the hydrophobicity of glycine to zero.

$document->SetBlackAndMouldHydrophobicities(False);

#Calculate the 'protrusion indices'. This sets a property CX on each atom. If the 'approximate' method
# is used (first argument True) then there are no prerequisites - the calculation will be performed as
# in the original paper by Pintar et al, using only non-hydrogen atoms and a single atom volume of 20.1.
#Otherwise, all atoms are used; if they have a property VDWRadius set (eg corresponding to the CHARMm forcefield values)
#these will be used, otherwise the standard DS element VDW radii are used. The second argument is the sphere radius used
#for the calculation.

$document->CalculateProtrusionIndices(False,10.0);

#Calculate the 'depth indices'. This sets a property DPX on each atom. It requires precomputed atom SAA properties.
#Exposed atoms will always have a DPX of zero. In addition, atoms will have a property DPX_RAD assigned. This is the VDW radius of
#the nearest surface atom, which is required for the simple electrostatic potential calculation. If a property VDWRadius set
# (eg corresponding to the CHARMm forcefield values)
#these will be used, otherwise the standard DS element VDW radii are used.

$document->CalculateDepthIndices();

#Performs a simple electrostatic potential calculation and sets atom properties EPOT. It requires the DPX and DPX_RAD properties to get the distance of the
#atom from the surface, so will run the Depth Indices calculation if they aren't already set. It therefore also requires SAA atom properties.
#Ideally the atomic charges should be set using the desired CHARMm forcefield.

$document->CalculateElectrostaticPotentials();

#The following lines demonstrate how to calculate 'residue neighborhood features'.
#These are the result of taking an existing property value for each atom within a given radius of any atom
#in the residue for which the property is being calculated, and then performing operations such as total or average.
# Note that a radius of 0 will give the result of the operation on just the residue itself.
#The new residue property names will be formed from radius_property_operation eg
# 5A_SAA_hydrophilic
#
#The choice of operations is:
# average: average of the property over all the atoms in the neighborhood
# minimum: minimum value for the property in the neighborhood
# maximum: maximum value for the property in the neighborhood
# total: sum of the property over all atoms in the neighborhood
# hydrophobic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Ala,Ile,Leu,Met,Phe,Trp,Tyr or Val
# hydrophilic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Arg,His,Lys,Asp,Glu,Ser,Thr,Asn or Gln (His is any protonation state of histidine)
# positive: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Arg,Hsp or Lys (Hsp is positively charged Histidine)
# negative: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Asp or Glu
# aromatic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues His, Phe, Trp and Tyr
# backbone: sum over all backbone atoms C CA N O and attached hydrogens
# sidechain: sum over all non-backbone atoms
# exposed: sum over all surface exposed atoms. (obviously SAA is a prerequisite)
#
# The ExposedOnly argument allows the feature calculation to be restricted to residues which have some
# surface exposure ie atoms with SAA >0
# 
#The first form calculates these residue features for a default set of properties, operations and radii. These are:
# radii 0,3,5,7,10,12,15,20,25
# properties operations
# CX average,minimum,maximum 
# DPX average,minimum,maximum
# SAA total,hydrophobic,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,backbone,sidechain 
# Charge total,exposed
# EPOT total
#
#The second allows for any numeric user defined properties with any combination of operators, and any integer radii.

print "Calculating Residue Neighborhood Features, default $default\n";

if($default eq "True"){
$document->CalculateDefaultResidueNeighborhoodFeatures(False);
}else{
my $radii= DiscoveryScript::IntegerArray::Create();
$radii->AddItem(0);
$radii->AddItem(3);
$radii->AddItem(5);
$radii->AddItem(7);
my $featureNames = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
my $subTypes = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$featureNames->AddItem("CX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("DPX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("Charges");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,exposed");
$featureNames->AddItem("SAA");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,aromatic,backbone,sidechain");
$document->CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures($radii,$featureNames,$subTypes,False);
}
print "Finished calculating features\n";
#now demonstrate the generic patch group creation API
#get the maximum value for this property

my $residues = $document->Residues();
my $atoms = $document->Atoms();
my $max = -999999;
my $min = 999999;
my $minPatchCutoff = 0.0;
my $minPeakCutoff = 0.1;
foreach my $res (@$residues){
if($res->HasProperty($propertyName)){
my $val = $res->GetProperty($propertyName);
if($val > $max){$max = $val;}
if($val < $min){$min = $val;}
}
}
#the range setting may not be ideal for all properties. 
if($max != -999999){
$minPeakCutoff = $max/5;
$minPatchCutoff = $max/10;
$max = $max/2;
$min = -1.0*$max;

#create a surface colored by this property
my $surface = $document->CreateSolidSurface($atoms,Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent);
$surface->Name = "$propertyName Surface";

my $surfacePropertyColorScheme = Mdm::spectrumBlueWhiteRed;
$surface->Select();
$document->SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme( $propertyName,
$surfacePropertyColorScheme, 32, $min,$max, False, "" );
$surface->IsTransparent(True);
$surface->IsLegendShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll();
$document->FindSurfacePropertySites($propertyName,5.0,$max,$minPatchCutoff);
}else{
print "Property for surface patches $propertyName not present\n";
}
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
$document->UpdateViews();

print "Finished script example\n";
```

# FirstKey property

Source type: HTML

## FirstKey property

### Description

FirstKey specifies the first key of a map collection.

### Applies to

The FirstKey property can be used with the following objects:

DiscoveryScript::ObjectMap , Protocol::ParameterMap , Sdm::AttributeMap

### Using the FirstKey property

#### Get

my $attributemapkeyObject = $object->FirstKey;

my $stringValue = $object->FirstKey;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $attributemapkeyObject | | | Sdm::AttributeMapKey |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $object | | | DiscoveryScript::ObjectMap Protocol::ParameterMap Sdm::AttributeMap |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript , SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
print
"No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

my $protocolName = 'Minimization';
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );
my $map = $document->ParameterMap;
my $key = $map->FirstKey;
while ($key)
{
my $value = $map->Item($key);
print "Parameter name: $key\t\tValue: $value\n";
$key = $map->NextKey($key);

}

$key = 'Dielectric Constant';
my $newValue = 2.0;
my $hasItem = $document->ItemExists($key);
if ($hasItem)
{
print "\nProtocol has parameter '" . $key;
my $value = $document->Item($key);
my $type = $document->ParameterType($key);
print "\nThe type is $type. \nThe default value is $value.\n";
print "Changing parameter value of $key to $newValue.\n";
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $newValue );
}

#!/usr/bin/perl -w

, Mdm::Bond , Mdm::BondAngleViolationMonitor , Mdm::BondLengthViolationMonitor , Mdm::Bump , Mdm::BumpMonitor , Mdm::CAlphaMonitor , Mdm::CAlphaPair , Mdm::CAlphaViolationMonitor , Mdm::Cell ,
