# Guid property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/guid_property.htm

## Guid property

### Description

Guid specifies the Global Unique Identifier of a protocol.

### Applies to

The Guid property can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Document

### Using the Guid property

#### Get

my $stringValue = $object->Guid;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $object | | | Protocol::Document |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

### Using the HarmonicAtomRestraints filter

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->HarmonicAtomRestraints;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Example filter_constraints
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Fix backbone atoms in sheet or helix
my $helicalBackboneAtoms = $document->FilterByProperty(
'Residue Secondary="Helix",Secondary="Sheet"; Atom label="CA",label="C",label="O",label="N"'
);
$document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($helicalBackboneAtoms);

# Add harmonic constraint on all backbone atoms in coils
my $coiledBackboneAtoms = $document->FilterByProperty(
'Residue Secondary="Coil";Atom label="CA",label="C",label="O",label="N"');
$document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint(
{ ArrayOfAtoms => $coiledBackboneAtoms, ForceConstant => 1.2 } );

# Add cross-strand distance restraint
{
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "THR2:CA" );
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "ILE34:CA" );
$document->CreateDistanceRestraint(
{
ArrayOfAtoms1 => $atom1,
ArrayOfAtoms2 => $atom2,
RMin => 2,
RMax => 5
}
);
}

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
{
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
$document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);
}

# Get arrays with for each type of constraint using the corresponding filters
# Note that the constraint filter includes constraints and restraints
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
my $fixedAtomConstraints = $document->FixedAtomConstraints;

# Note that the restraint filter includes dihedral, distance and harmonic restraints
my $restraints = $document->Restraints;
my $dihedralRestraints = $document->DihedralRestraints;
my $distanceRestraints = $document->DistanceRestraints;
my $harmonicRestraints = $document->HarmonicAtomRestraints;

# Print out total number of constraints, along with a list of their names
print "There are " . $constraints->Count . " constraints (\t";
foreach my $constraint (@$constraints)
{
my $name = $constraint->GetProperty("Name");
print "$name\t";
}

# Print out the number of each type of constraints
print ")\nout of which ";
print $restraints->Count . " are Restraints :\n";
print " " . $dihedralRestraints->Count . " DihedralRestraint(s)\n";
print " " . $distanceRestraints->Count . " DistanceRestraint(s)\n";
print " " . $harmonicRestraints->Count . " HarmonicAtomRestraint(s)\n";
print "and \n";
print " " . $fixedAtomConstraints->Count . "FixedAtomConstraint(s)\n";
```

# HasAlignment property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/hasalignment_property.htm

## HasAlignment property

### Description

HasAlignment is a Boolean specifying if an Sdm::Document contains an Sdm::Alignment object.

### Applies to

The HasAlignment property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the HasAlignment property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->HasAlignment;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Sdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several alignment function.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();

$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $sequence0 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'MIASDFADSG' );
my $sequence1 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S2', 'MAASDFIDSA' );
my $sequence2 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S3', 'IIISDFADSA' );

if ( !$document->HasAlignment )
{
die "No alignment found!\n";
}

my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
$alignment->BackgroundColorScheme = Sdm::colorByChargeSimilarity;

# Insert two gaps into first sequence at 0-based position 2.
$alignment->InsertGap( { Index => 0, StartPosition => 2, Count => 2 } );

# Insert addition gaps in second and third sequences.
$alignment->InsertGap( 1, 1, 1 );
$alignment->InsertGap( 1, 2, 1 );
$alignment->InsertGap( 2, 2, 1 );
$alignment->InsertGap( 2, 3, 1 );

my $alignmentStrings = $alignment->AlignmentStrings();
my $alignmentLength = $alignment->AlignmentLength;

print "The first sequence in the alignment has gaps at positions:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $alignmentLength ; ++$i )
{
if ( $alignment->IsGap( 0, $i ) )
{
print "$i ";
}
}
print "\n";
```

# HasChildOperators function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/haschildoperators_function.htm

## HasChildOperators function

### Description

HasChildOperators checks if a query operator has child query operators.

### Applies to

The HasChildOperators function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the HasChildOperators function

#### Instance

my $booleanValue = $object->HasChildOperators();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create some features on the query
# Create a donor feature at 0,0,0
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create an acceptor feature at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

# create the location constraint. The $fitOperator and the parent operator of $acceptorOperator are the same in this case.
# Either can be used to create the location constraint.
my $locationfeatureHead =
$acceptorOperator->GetParentOperator()
->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Check to see if a proper query has been made and print out some information
if ( $fitOperator->HasChildOperators() )
{
print "Query successfully made, fit operator has child operators.\n";
my $headPoint = $newAcceptor->HeadXYZ;
my $tailPoint = $newAcceptor->TailXYZ;
printf "Head : %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n", $headPoint->X, $headPoint->Y,
$headPoint->Z;
printf "Tail : %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n", $tailPoint->X, $tailPoint->Y,
$tailPoint->Z;
print "Radius of location constraint on tail "
. $newAcceptor->TailFeature()->LocationSphereRadius . "\n";
}
$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# HasNcsMatrix function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/hasncsmatrix_function.htm

## HasNcsMatrix function

### Description

HasNcsMatrix returns true if one or more non-crystallographic symmetry transformations have been specified for the Molecule.

### Applies to

The HasNcsMatrix function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the HasNcsMatrix function

#### Instance

my $booleanValue = $object->HasNcsMatrix( <name> );

my $booleanValue = $object->HasNcsMatrix( { Name => <name> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| <name> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrates the transformation matrix properties and functions.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1rvf');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $ncsMatrixName = 'BIOMT_4';

my $translateX = 0.0;
my $translateY = 0.0;
my $translateZ = 0.0;

my $ncsMatrix = Mdm::Matrix4x4::Create(
-0.309017, 0.500000, 0.809017, 0.0,
-0.500000, -0.809017, 0.309017, 0.0,
0.809017, -0.309017, 0.500000, 0.0,
$translateX, $translateY, $translateZ, 1.0
);

# Add a transformation matrix to a molecule and
# verify the matrix exists a property of the molecule.
$molecule->NcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName) = $ncsMatrix;
print "Found matrix $ncsMatrixName.\n"
if ( $molecule->HasNcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName) );

# Apply the transformation matrix to molecule's coordinates.
$document->ApplyTransformationMatrix( $molecule, $ncsMatrixName );

# Remove the matrix from molecule.
$molecule->RemoveNcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName);
print "Removed matrix $ncsMatrixName.\n"
if ( not $molecule->HasNcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName) );
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the set property functions.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Illustrate how to get the first molecule.
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

# Illustrate how to add a properties to molecule. These will appear
# in the molecule tab of the Molecule Window's Data Table.
$molecule->SetPropertyAsBoolean( "My_Boolean_Prop", "True" );

$molecule->SetPropertyAsInteger( "My_Integer_Prop", 1 );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "My_Real_Prop", 1.5 );
$molecule->SetProperty( "My_Generic_Prop", "A Property" );
$molecule->SetProperty( "My_Hidden_Prop", "A Hidden Property" );

# Illustrate how to prevent the property from being displayed in the table.
$molecule->HideProperty("My_Hidden_Prop");

# Illustrate how to hide and show a property.
$molecule->SetProperty( "My_Reappearing_Prop", "A Once Hidden Property" );
$molecule->HideProperty("My_Reappearing_Prop");
$molecule->ShowProperty("My_Reappearing_Prop");

# Illustrate how to test for existence of a property.
my $propertyName = "My_Boolean_Prop";
if ( $molecule->HasProperty($propertyName) )
{
print $molecule->Name . " has the property \"$propertyName\".\n";
}
else
{
print $molecule->Name
. " does not have the property \"$propertyName\".\n";
}

# Illustrate how to rename a property.
$document->RenameUserProperty( "My_Real_Prop", "My_Renamed_Real_Prop",
$molecule->ClassName, False );

# Illustrate how to remove a property.
$document->RemoveUserProperty( "My_Renamed_Real_Prop", $molecule->ClassName,
False );
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the IsVisible and IsSelected properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# lock the visibility of the first molecule
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Select;
$document->LockVisibility( );
$document->DeselectAll( );

my $object = $document->Atoms->Item(0);

my $visible = $object->IsVisible;
if ($visible) # Implicit check for non-zero (i.e. True) values.
{
print "Do something when the object is visible.\n";
}

my $selected = $object->IsSelected;
if ( !$selected ) # Implicit check for zero (i.e. False) values.
{
print "Do something when the object is not selected.\n";
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::FixedBlock class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences;
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(0, 'S1', 'ALKDFLASDFLKASLFKASLFKD');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(1, 'S2', 'ALDFKLAFLASFLSAFADFALFAS');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(2, 'S3', '-');
$alignment->Sequence(0)->MarkStartOfChain(11);
$alignment->Sequence(1)->MarkStartOfChain(13);

# Create a fixed block using a Discovery Studio command.
$alignment->DeselectAll();
my $x0 = 9;
my $y0 = 0;
my $height = 2;
my $width = 10;
my $yN = $y0 + 2;
for (my $y = $y0; $y < $yN; ++$y)
{
$alignment->Select($y, $x0, $width);
}
$document->InvokeAction('ActionFixResidueBlock'); 

my $fixedBlock = $alignment->FixedBlocks->Item(0);
my $column = $fixedBlock->X + 1;
print 'A fixed block was created starting at column ' . $column
. ' of sequence ' . $alignment->Sequences->Item($fixedBlock->Y)->Name
. ' having a width of ' . $fixedBlock->Width 
. ' residues and a height of ' . $fixedBlock->Height . " sequences.\n";
```

Source file: scripting/hide_function.htm

## Hide function

### Description

Hide makes the selected objects invisible.

### Applies to

The Hide function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the Hide function

#### Command

$object->Hide();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to show and hide objects in an Mdm::Document.
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

# This example assumes the atoms are visible and their display style
# is not set to Mdm::styleAtomNone.
print "Make sure that visible atoms are displayed.\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleAtomStick);

print "Initially hide all objects.\n";
$document->HideAll();
sleep(1);

print 'Select and show backbone atoms and bonds. ';
print "All other objects remain hidden...\n";
SelectByString( $document, ':C,CA,N,O,HN,HA' );
$document->Show();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

print 'Hide the selected backbone atoms and bonds. ';
print "All other objects remain shown...\n";
$document->ShowAll();
$document->Hide();
sleep(3);

print "Show selected atoms and hide unselected...\n";
$document->ShowAll();
$document->ShowOnly();
sleep(3);

print "Show everything within 5 angstroms of the ligand...\n";
$document->DeselectAll();
$document->Hide();
my $ligand = $document->Chains->Item(2);
$ligand->Select();

# ShowByRadius considers only molecules which are marked as visible.
# Use ShowOnly to make sure any molecule containing the selection is visible.
$document->ShowOnly();

$document->ShowByRadius(5.0);
$document->DeselectAll();
$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# HideAllNonbonds function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/hideallnonbonds_function.htm

## HideAllNonbonds function

### Description

HideAllNonbonds hides all the non-bonds of an Mdm::NonbondMonitor object.

### Applies to

The HideAllNonbonds function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::NonbondMonitor

### Using the HideAllNonbonds function

#### Instance

$object->HideAllNonbonds();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor Mdm::NonbondMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the create a ligand non-bond monitor, 
# browse ligands and show supporting non-bond interactions. 

use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('2FL6');
die "Failed to create a valid MDM document!" unless $document;

my $receptor = $document->ReceptorInFocus;
die "The open document does not have a defined receptor!" unless $receptor;

$document->FocusOnFirstLigand;
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
die "The open document does not have a defined ligand!" unless $ligand;

my $ligandNonbondMonitor =
$document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();
$document->UpdateViews();

my $nonbondMonitors = $document->NonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d NonbondMonitors.\n", $nonbondMonitors->Count;
my $ligandNonbondMonitors = $document->LigandNonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d LigandNonbondMonitors.\n", $ligandNonbondMonitors->Count;

# Step through the ligands
while ($document->FocusOnNextLigand())
{
sleep(2);
}

# Step through the ligands backwards
$document->FocusOnLastLigand();
while ($document->FocusOnPreviousLigand())
{
sleep(2);
}

# Expand shell to progressively view supporting interactions.
$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

# Contract shell to hide supporting interactions.
$ligandNonbondMonitor->ContractShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

print "Done\n";
```

# HideHydrogenAtoms function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/hidehydrogenatoms_function.htm

## HideHydrogenAtoms function

### Description

HideHydrogenAtoms hides hydrogen atoms ( Mdm::Atom ) connected to the selected atoms.

### Applies to

The HideHydrogenAtoms function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the HideHydrogenAtoms function

#### Instance

$object->HideHydrogenAtoms( [hydrogenset] );

$object->HideHydrogenAtoms( { HydrogenSet => [hydrogenset] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [hydrogenset] | Optional | allHydrogenAtoms | enum Mdm::HydrogenSet |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate functions to manipulate hydrogen atoms.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# change display style
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStick );
printf "Total Atoms: %d\n" , $document->Atoms->Count;
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;

# Add all missing hydrogen atoms.
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms( Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms, True );
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Remove any non-polar hydrogen atoms.
$document->RemoveHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::nonEssentialHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Hide the remaining polar hydrogen atoms.
$document->HideHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::essentialHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;

sleep(1);

# Show the all existing hydrogen atoms.
$document->ShowHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Remove hydrogen atoms connected to specified atom.

$document->Atoms->Item(0)->RemoveHydrogens();
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Add chiral hydrogen atoms.
$document->RemoveHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;

$document->AddChiralHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
```

```text
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "My_Real_Prop", 1.5 );
$molecule->SetProperty( "My_Generic_Prop", "A Property" );
$molecule->SetProperty( "My_Hidden_Prop", "A Hidden Property" );

# Illustrate how to prevent the property from being displayed in the table.
$molecule->HideProperty("My_Hidden_Prop");

# Illustrate how to hide and show a property.
$molecule->SetProperty( "My_Reappearing_Prop", "A Once Hidden Property" );
$molecule->HideProperty("My_Reappearing_Prop");
$molecule->ShowProperty("My_Reappearing_Prop");

# Illustrate how to test for existence of a property.
my $propertyName = "My_Boolean_Prop";
if ( $molecule->HasProperty($propertyName) )
{
print $molecule->Name . " has the property \"$propertyName\".\n";
}
else
{
print $molecule->Name
. " does not have the property \"$propertyName\".\n";
}

# Illustrate how to rename a property.
$document->RenameUserProperty( "My_Real_Prop", "My_Renamed_Real_Prop",
$molecule->ClassName, False );

# Illustrate how to remove a property.
$document->RemoveUserProperty( "My_Renamed_Real_Prop", $molecule->ClassName,
```

# Host property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/host_property.htm

## Host property

### Description

Host specifies the server name of a protocol task.

### Applies to

The Host property can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Task

### Using the Host property

#### Get

my $stringValue = $object->Host;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $object | | | Protocol::Task |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

```text
{
($residueAtomName) = @ARGV;
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Get the specified atom.
my $atoms = FilterByString( $document, $residueAtomName );

if ( $atoms->Count == 0 );

my $atom = $atoms->[0];

# Print various atom properties. In the DiscoveryStudio client, the
# output will appear in the output pane of the scripting window.

print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
print 'Element: ' . $atom->Element . "\n";

print 'Atomic number: ' . $atom->AtomicNumber . "\n";
print 'Charge: ' . $atom->Charge . "\n";

. $atom->FormalCharge->Numerator . "/"

print 'Hybridization: ' . $atom->Hybridization . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen Count: ' . $atom->HydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'ImplicitHydrogen Count: ' . $atom->ImplicitHydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Acceptor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondAcceptor . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Donor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondDonor . "\n";
```

# HydrogenBondCount property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/hydrogenbondcount_property.htm

## HydrogenBondCount property

### Description

HydrogenBondCount indicates the number of hydrogen bonds monitored by a
hydrogen bond monitor.

### Applies to

The HydrogenBondCount property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor

### Using the HydrogenBondCount property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->HydrogenBondCount;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how use the hydrogen bond monitor and to change the distance cutoff.

use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Creates a hbond monitor between ligand atoms and receptor
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $LigName = $ligands->Item(0)->Name;
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $monitor = $document->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( $ligandAtoms,
Mdm::allAtomHydrogenBonds, Mdm::allMolecularHydrogenBonds );

# Shows the label for each of the hbonds
$monitor->IsLabelShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll(); 

printf "Default distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->DefaultDistanceCriterion;
printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor.\n\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $newHBDist = 3.0;
$monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared( $newHBDist* $newHBDist );

# update view to ensure the correct HB count
$document->UpdateViews();
printf "Set the distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared;

printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor:\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $hbonds = $document->HydrogenBonds;
my $count = $hbonds->Count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $hbond = $hbonds->Item($index);
my $dist = $hbond->Distance;
my $atom1 = $hbond->Atom1;
my $atom2 = $hbond->Atom2;
my $res = $atom1->Parent;

if ( $res->Name eq $LigName ) {
$atom2->Parent->Select; 
}
else{
$atom1->Parent->Select; 
}
printf "%d) Distance: %.3f A H-bond between Atom %s:%s:%s and Atom %s:%s:%s\n",
$index+1, $dist,
$atom1->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom1->Parent->Name, $atom1->Name,
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name ;
} 

$document->FitView(); 
my $display_style = { DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' };
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle($display_style);
$document->DeselectAll();
```

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of various atom properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

# Define atom properties to list.
# This may be specified on the command line.
my $residueAtomName = 'THR2:CA';
if ( @ARGV != 0 )
{
($residueAtomName) = @ARGV;
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Get the specified atom.
my $atoms = FilterByString( $document, $residueAtomName );
die "Atom $residueAtomName not found. Aborting!\n\n"
if ( $atoms->Count == 0 );

my $atom = $atoms->[0];

# Print various atom properties. In the DiscoveryStudio client, the
# output will appear in the output pane of the scripting window.
print "List of properties for atom $residueAtomName:\n\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
print 'Element: ' . $atom->Element . "\n";
print 'Element Name: ' . $atom->ElementName . "\n";
print 'Element Symbol: ' . $atom->ElementSymbol . "\n";
print 'Mass: ' . $atom->Mass . "\n";
print 'Atomic number: ' . $atom->AtomicNumber . "\n";
print 'Charge: ' . $atom->Charge . "\n";
print 'Formal Charge: '
. $atom->FormalCharge->Numerator . "/"
. $atom->FormalCharge->Denominator . "\n";

print 'VDW Radius: ' . $atom->VdwRadius . "\n";
print 'Covalent Radius: ' . $atom->CovalentRadius . "\n";
print 'Chirality: ' . $atom->Chirality . "\n";
print 'Bond count: ' . $atom->BondCount . "\n";
print 'Bonding radius: ' . $atom->BondingRadius . "\n";
print 'Hybridization: ' . $atom->Hybridization . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen Count: ' . $atom->HydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'ImplicitHydrogen Count: ' . $atom->ImplicitHydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Acceptor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondAcceptor . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Donor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondDonor . "\n";
print 'Isotropic Displacement: ' . $atom->IsotropicDisplacement . "\n";
print 'Is Terminal Hydrogen: ' . $atom->IsTerminalHydrogen . "\n";
print 'Is Valence Satisfied: ' . $atom->IsValenceSatisfied . "\n";
print 'Lone Pair Count: ' . $atom->LonePairCount . "\n";
print 'Valence Count: ' . $atom->ValenceCount . "\n";
print 'Occupancy: ' . $atom->Occupancy . "\n";

printf "\n%s:\n", 'Display Properties';
print 'DisplayStyle: ' . $atom->DisplayStyle . "\n";
print 'Ball Size: ' . $atom->BallSize . "\n";
print 'Ball Size Default: ' . $atom->BallSizeDefault . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale: ' . $atom->CPKScale . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale Default: ' . $atom->CPKScaleDefault . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius: ' . $atom->StickRadius . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius Default: ' . $atom->StickRadiusDefault . "\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
```

### Applies to

Mdm::PointFeature

### Using the HydrophobeAliphaticColor property

#### Static Get

my $colorObject = Mdm::PointFeature::HydrophobeAliphaticColor();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $colorObject | | | Mdm::Color |
| $object | | | Mdm::PointFeature |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create a Hydrophobe
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -14, 6, 0 );

my $hydrophobeOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$hydrophobeOperator->Name('Hydrophobe');
my $hydrophobe = $hydrophobeOperator->CreatePointFeature( $document->Atoms );
$hydrophobe->Type() = 'hydrophobePointFeature';
$hydrophobe->CreateLabel('Hydrophobe');
my $hydrophobeColor = $hydrophobe->HydrophobeColor();
print "RGB of a Hydrophobic is: "
. $hydrophobeColor->Red . " "
. $hydrophobeColor->Green . " "
. $hydrophobeColor->Blue . "\n";

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();

# Create a Hydrophobe Aromatic
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -14, 4.5, 0 );

my $hydrophobeOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');

print "RGB of a Hydrophobic Aromatic is: "
. $hydrophobeColor->Red . " "
. $hydrophobeColor->Green . " "
. $hydrophobeColor->Blue . "\n";

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->DeleteObjects();

# Create a Hydrophobe Aliphatic
```

# Hydrophobicity property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/hydrophobicity_property.htm

## Hydrophobicity property

### Description

Hydrophobicity specifies the hydrophobicity of a residue.
For standard amino acids, the initial values are the Kyte-Doolittle hydrophobicity values.

### Applies to

The Hydrophobicity property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid , Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::Nucleotide , Mdm::Residue

### Using the Hydrophobicity property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->Hydrophobicity;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid Mdm::NucleicAcid Mdm::Nucleotide Mdm::Residue |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to convert an amino acid property
# (Hydrophobicity) to an atom property and color the atoms by the
# new Hydrophobicity property.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

my $atoms = $document->Atoms;

# For each atom, create a Hydrophobicity property with
# the value of its parent residue's Hydrophobicity.
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
my $residue = $atom->Parent;
my $hydrophobicity = $residue->Hydrophobicity;
$atom->SetProperty( 'Hydrophobicity', $hydrophobicity );
}

# Color the atoms by the new atomic Hydrophobicity property.
$document->SetAtomPropertyColorScheme(
{
PropertyName => 'Hydrophobicity',
SpectrumType => Mdm::spectrumRedWhiteBlue,
NumberOfBands => 32,
RangeMinimum => -10,
RangeMaximum => 10,
Clip => 0
}
);

printf "Molecule Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$document->ModelName,$atoms->Count();
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of various atom properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

# Define atom properties to list.
# This may be specified on the command line.
my $residueAtomName = 'THR2:CA';
if ( @ARGV != 0 )
{
($residueAtomName) = @ARGV;
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Get the specified atom.
my $atoms = FilterByString( $document, $residueAtomName );
die "Atom $residueAtomName not found. Aborting!\n\n"
if ( $atoms->Count == 0 );

my $atom = $atoms->[0];

# Print various atom properties. In the DiscoveryStudio client, the
# output will appear in the output pane of the scripting window.
print "List of properties for atom $residueAtomName:\n\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
print 'Element: ' . $atom->Element . "\n";
print 'Element Name: ' . $atom->ElementName . "\n";
print 'Element Symbol: ' . $atom->ElementSymbol . "\n";
print 'Mass: ' . $atom->Mass . "\n";
print 'Atomic number: ' . $atom->AtomicNumber . "\n";
print 'Charge: ' . $atom->Charge . "\n";
print 'Formal Charge: '
. $atom->FormalCharge->Numerator . "/"
. $atom->FormalCharge->Denominator . "\n";

print 'VDW Radius: ' . $atom->VdwRadius . "\n";
print 'Covalent Radius: ' . $atom->CovalentRadius . "\n";
print 'Chirality: ' . $atom->Chirality . "\n";
print 'Bond count: ' . $atom->BondCount . "\n";
print 'Bonding radius: ' . $atom->BondingRadius . "\n";
print 'Hybridization: ' . $atom->Hybridization . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen Count: ' . $atom->HydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'ImplicitHydrogen Count: ' . $atom->ImplicitHydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Acceptor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondAcceptor . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Donor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondDonor . "\n";
print 'Isotropic Displacement: ' . $atom->IsotropicDisplacement . "\n";
print 'Is Terminal Hydrogen: ' . $atom->IsTerminalHydrogen . "\n";
print 'Is Valence Satisfied: ' . $atom->IsValenceSatisfied . "\n";
print 'Lone Pair Count: ' . $atom->LonePairCount . "\n";
print 'Valence Count: ' . $atom->ValenceCount . "\n";
print 'Occupancy: ' . $atom->Occupancy . "\n";

printf "\n%s:\n", 'Display Properties';
print 'DisplayStyle: ' . $atom->DisplayStyle . "\n";
print 'Ball Size: ' . $atom->BallSize . "\n";
print 'Ball Size Default: ' . $atom->BallSizeDefault . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale: ' . $atom->CPKScale . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale Default: ' . $atom->CPKScaleDefault . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius: ' . $atom->StickRadius . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius Default: ' . $atom->StickRadiusDefault . "\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
```

Sdm::Alignment , Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

#### Defined by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to insert a file into a document.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder =
$ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Quick Start Tutorials/';

my $document = DiscoveryScript::Open( $samplesFolder . '1aq1.pdb' );

printf "Molecule Count: %d Atom Count %d\n" , 
$document->Molecules->Count,
$document->Atoms->Count;

$document->Insert( $samplesFolder . '1aq1_lig.mol' );
$document->Molecules->Item(1)->Select();

printf "Molecule Count: %d Atom Count %d\n" , 
$document->Molecules->Count,
$document->Atoms->Count;
```

# Insert function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/insert_function.htm

## Insert function

### Description

Insert inserts the specified file defined by required argument Path into the existing document.
The following optional argument is available:

* FormatType is a string specifying the file format.
By default the format type is undefined and
the best matching type is used. See Save for a list of
supported formats.

### Applies to

The Insert function can be used with the following objects:

Chart::Document , DiscoveryScript::Document , Ffdm::Document , Mdm::Document , Protocol::Document , Sdm::Document

### Using the Insert function

#### Instance

$object->Insert( <path>, [formattype], [loadallobjects] );

$object->Insert( { Path => <path>, FormatType => [formattype], LoadAllObjects => [loadallobjects] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <path> | Required | | String |
| [formattype] | Optional | "" | String |
| [loadallobjects] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to insert a file into a document.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder =
$ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Quick Start Tutorials/';

my $document = DiscoveryScript::Open( $samplesFolder . '1aq1.pdb' );

printf "Molecule Count: %d Atom Count %d\n" , 
$document->Molecules->Count,
$document->Atoms->Count;

$document->Insert( $samplesFolder . '1aq1_lig.mol' );
```

# InsertAlignmentString function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/insertalignmentstring_function.htm

## InsertAlignmentString function

### Description

InsertAlignmentString inserts a new sequence of residues (represented by 1-letter codes) and gaps
into an Sdm::Alignment . The following arguments are available:

* Index specifies the 0-based sequence index for insertion.

* Name specifies name of the new sequence.

* AlignmentString specifies the sequence of residues (represented by 1-letter codes) and gaps to insert.

### Applies to

The InsertAlignmentString function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the InsertAlignmentString function

#### Instance

$object->InsertAlignmentString( <index>, <name>, <alignmentstring> );

$object->InsertAlignmentString( { Index => <index>, Name => <name>, AlignmentString => <alignmentstring> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <alignmentstring> | Required | | String |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| <name> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to insert and inset alignment strings.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

sub ShowContent($$)
{
my ( $document, $note ) = @_;

print "\n" . "Show content: $note\n";
my $count = $document->SequenceCount;
printf "Count: %d\n", $count;
my $sequences = $document->Sequences;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $count ; ++$i )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($i);
printf "%d: %s: '%s'\n", $i, $sequence->Name,
$sequence->SequenceString();
}
}

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument('SDM');
ShowContent( $document, 'new empty protein document' );

# Insert alignment string in existing row.
$document->Alignment->InsetAlignmentString( 0, 0, 'AAAAA-A' );
ShowContent( $document, 'after InsetAlignmentString' );

$document->Alignment->InsetAlignmentString( 0, 2, 'S--S' );
$document->UpdateViews();
ShowContent( $document, 'after InsetAlignmentString' );

# Insert alignment string in a new row.
$document->Alignment->InsertAlignmentString( 0, 'New1', "F-FFG-GGH-HH" );
$document->Alignment->InsertAlignmentString( 2, 'New2', "TP-FGGGH-GLHHH" );
ShowContent( $document, 'after InsertAlignmentString' );
```

## InsertAminoAcid function

### Description

InsertAminoAcid inserts one or more amino acid residues into an amino acid chain before or after a specified amino acid residue.

You can specify whether to hold the original structure rigid using the
holddistantaminoacidsrigid parameter.

### Applies to

The InsertAminoAcid function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the InsertAminoAcid function

#### Command

$object->InsertAminoAcid( <insertat>, <sequence>, [conformationtype], [hydrogenrepresentation], [isotropicdisplacement], [insertbefore], [holddistantaminoacidsrigid], [unusedbool], [unusedint] );

$object->InsertAminoAcid( { InsertAt => <insertat>, Sequence => <sequence>, ConformationType => [conformationtype], HydrogenRepresentation => [hydrogenrepresentation], IsotropicDisplacement => [isotropicdisplacement], InsertBefore => [insertbefore], HoldDistantAminoAcidsRigid => [holddistantaminoacidsrigid], UnusedBool => [unusedbool], UnusedInt => [unusedint] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <insertat> | Required | | Mdm::AminoAcid |
| <sequence> | Required | | String |
| [conformationtype] | Optional | extendedConformation | enum Mdm::SecondaryStructureType |
| [holddistantaminoacidsrigid] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [hydrogenrepresentation] | Optional | noHydrogenRepresentation | enum Mdm::HydrogenRepresentation |
| [insertbefore] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [isotropicdisplacement] | Optional | 20.0 | Real |
| [unusedbool] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [unusedint] | Optional | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate methods for building and editing proteins.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# This is how to create an amino acid chain containing an alanine residue:
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $chain = $molecule->CreateAminoAcidChain();
my $aminoAcid1 = $chain->CreateResidue(Mdm::alanine);

my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
my $count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The current number of amino acids is $count.\n";

# Define a string consisting of 1-letter amino acid residue codes.
my $wideSequence = "AlaPheGlyProHisIleLysAlaAlaAla";
my $sequence = Mdm::AminoAcidChain::ConvertToOneLetterSequence($wideSequence);

print
"Converted wide sequence: $wideSequence to narrow sequence: $sequence.\n";

# Demonstrate how to append a sequence of residues at the C-terminus.
# Let's make it helical rather than the default extended conformation.
$document->GrowAminoAcidChain(
{
InsertAt => $chain,
Sequence => $sequence,
ConformationType => Mdm::rightAlphaHelixConformation,
GrowAtNTerminal => False
}
);

$aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
$count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The number of amino acid residues after growing chain "
. "at the C-terminus is $count.\n";

# Demonstrate how to grow amino acid chain at the N terminal.
# This will prepend the residue His0.
$document->GrowAminoAcidChain(
{
InsertAt => $chain,
Sequence => "H",
GrowAtNTerminal => True
}
);

$aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
$count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The number of amino acid residues after growing chain "
. "at the N-terminus is $count.\n";

# Insertion a residue within the chain.
my $insertionpoint = $aminoAcids->Item( $count - 2 );
my $sequence = "GANDT";
$document->InsertAminoAcid( $insertionpoint, $sequence );

$aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
$count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The number of amino acid residues after insertion is $count.\n";

# Demonstrate how to mutate a residue.
my $residuetomutate = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
print 'Amino acid name before the mutation: '
. $residuetomutate->Name() . "\n";
$document->MutateAminoAcid( $residuetomutate, Mdm::tyr );
print 'Amino acid name after the mutation: '
. $residuetomutate->Name() . "\n";

# At this point we have various insertion codes - lets renumber
print "Residue names before renumbering: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
print " " . $aminoAcids->Item($index)->Name() . " ";
}
print "\n";

$document->RenumberSequence( $aminoAcids->Item(0), 1, $count, True );
print "Residue names after renumbering: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
print " " . $aminoAcids->Item($index)->Name() . " ";
}
print "\n";

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# InsertFromUrl function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/insertfromurl_function.htm

## InsertFromUrl function

### Description

InsertFromUrl inserts a file from the specified URL into the existing document.
The following optional argument is available:

* FormatType is a string specifying the file format.
By default the format is undefined and
the best matching type is used. See Save for a list of
supported formats.

### Applies to

The InsertFromUrl function can be used with the following objects:

Chart::Document , DiscoveryScript::Document , Ffdm::Document , Mdm::Document , Protocol::Document , Sdm::Document

### Using the InsertFromUrl function

#### Instance

$object->InsertFromUrl( <url>, [formattype], [loadallobjects] );

$object->InsertFromUrl( { Url => <url>, FormatType => [formattype], LoadAllObjects => [loadallobjects] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <url> | Required | | String |
| [formattype] | Optional | "" | String |
| [loadallobjects] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use superimposition functions
# and RMSD calculation functions for amino acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load 2rcs (an unligated antibody) from PDB.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '2rcs.pdb' );

# Load 1aj7 (a ligated antibody having the same sequence as 2crs) from PDB.
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

my $molecule2rcs = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[1];

my $hv2rcs = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 2rcs H chain V domain
my $hv1aj7 = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 1aj7 H chain V domain

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $molecule2rcs->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv2rcs->AddItem($aminoAcid);

$aminoAcid = $molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv1aj7->AddItem($aminoAcid);
}

# Show the transformation matrix which would superimpose the Vh
# domains by C-alpha atoms. This does not alter the coordinates
# of either structure.
my $matrix = $document->GetSuperimposeProteinMatrix( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
print "Transformation matrix:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 4 ; ++$i )
{
print "\t";
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < 4 ; ++$j )
{
printf "%.3f ", $matrix->GetEntry( $i, $j );
}
print "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms
my $rmsd = $document->SuperimposeProtein( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
printf "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms: %.3f\n\n", $rmsd;

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD. Note that by default the functions return an
# array of per-residue RMSD values, finishing with the overall RMSD
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it in which case the value will be zero. This can happen
# for unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation
# only for selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the
# required atoms for the requested type of calculation. 
# If you do not want per-residue RMSDs, set the 4th parameter ResidueReport
# False. In this case the array will only contain the overall RMSD.
# In this example, the all protein rmsd has no residue values calculated
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True, False );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item(0);
print "\n";

#Show that the all protein array contains just the overall RMSD.
printf "Number of values returned for all protein is %d\n", $apRmsd->Count();

# Demonstrating that the array is for all residues plus overall value not
# just selected and that as the first chain(L) is unselected its values
# are 0.
printf "Number of values returned for sidechains is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0), $scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

#Create a C-Alpha monitor
my $caMonitor = $document->CreateCAlphaMonitor();

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs before superimposing.\n";
if ($cAlphaPairs->Count > 0) {
printf "The first C-alpha to C-alpha pair distance is %.3f Angstroms.\n",
$cAlphaPairs->Item(0)->Distance;
}

#Lets do it for all matching atoms just to show the argument
my $rmsdByCA =
$document->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( $document->Molecules(), $caMonitor,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingAllAtoms );

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs after superimposing.\n";

#The values returned are like for Superimpose By Alignment - the first value
# is ref-ref (ie 0) then ref-mover for each superimposed molecule.
my $numVal = $rmsdByCA->Count();
printf( "Number of values returned for SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs %d\n",
$numVal );
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $numVal ; ++$i )
{
printf( "RMSD %d is %f\n", $i, $rmsdByCA->[$i] );
}

# use the filter function to retrieve the CAlpha atoms
my $cAlphaMonitors = $document->CAlphaMonitors;
foreach my $m (@$cAlphaMonitors)
{
print $m->ClassName ." filter entries: " . $m->CAlphaPairs->Count. "\n";
}

print "Finished Superimpose Script Example\n";
```

Sdm::Alignment

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several alignment function.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();

$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $sequence0 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'MIASDFADSG' );
my $sequence1 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S2', 'MAASDFIDSA' );
my $sequence2 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S3', 'IIISDFADSA' );

if ( !$document->HasAlignment )
{
die "No alignment found!\n";
}

my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
$alignment->BackgroundColorScheme = Sdm::colorByChargeSimilarity;

# Insert two gaps into first sequence at 0-based position 2.
$alignment->InsertGap( { Index => 0, StartPosition => 2, Count => 2 } );

# Insert addition gaps in second and third sequences.
$alignment->InsertGap( 1, 1, 1 );
$alignment->InsertGap( 1, 2, 1 );
$alignment->InsertGap( 2, 2, 1 );
$alignment->InsertGap( 2, 3, 1 );

my $alignmentStrings = $alignment->AlignmentStrings();
my $alignmentLength = $alignment->AlignmentLength;

print "The first sequence in the alignment has gaps at positions:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $alignmentLength ; ++$i )
{
if ( $alignment->IsGap( 0, $i ) )
{
print "$i ";
}
}
print "\n";
```

# InsertionCode property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/insertioncode_property.htm

## InsertionCode property

### Description

InsertionCode is the one-letter residue insertion code. It is used to ensure the uniqueness of residue sequence numbers in cases where homologous numbering is retained.

### Applies to

The InsertionCode property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid , Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::Nucleotide , Mdm::Residue

### Using the InsertionCode property

#### Get

my $stringValue = $object->InsertionCode;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid Mdm::NucleicAcid Mdm::Nucleotide Mdm::Residue |

#### Set

$object->InsertionCode = <insertioncode>;

$object->InsertionCode( <insertioncode> );

$object->InsertionCode( { InsertionCode => <insertioncode> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <insertioncode> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid Mdm::NucleicAcid Mdm::Nucleotide Mdm::Residue |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the usage of the InsertionCode property.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1IGY.pdb' );

# Count the number of residues with insertion codes.
my $insertionsCount = 0;
my $residues = $document->Residues;
foreach my $residue (@$residues)
{
++$insertionsCount if ( $residue->InsertionCode ne '' );
}

printf "Document contains %d residues with insertion codes.\n",
$insertionsCount;

#Insertion codes can also be set by the user.

#It can be done explicitly
my $residue1 = $residues->Item(0);
$residue1->InsertionCode = "A";

#or it can be done implicitly via the residue label.
my $residue2 = $residues->Item(1);
my $label = $residue2->Name;
$label = $label . "B";
$residue2->Name = $label;

#Suppose you want to re-label a loop as an insertion.
#This is using the residue positions within the whole molecule,
#but of course it can be done using positions within a chain.

#Get the residue before the loop to get the base residue number:
my $startRes = $residues->Item(2);
my $id = $startRes->Id();
my $code = "A";

#Then loop the loop
for ( my $i = 2 ; $i < 10 ; ++$i )
{
my $residue = $residues->Item($i);
my $type = $residue->Type();

#This concatenates the uppercased residue type, the id and the insertion code.
my $label = uc($type) . $id . $code;

#Setting the name will automatically update the ID number and insertion code
# to match
$residue->Name = $label;
$residue->InsertionCode = $code;

# incrementing an "A" gives "B" etc.
$code++;
}

printf(
"Look at the first ten residues to see the insertion codes set by the script.\n"
);
```

## InsertItem function

### Description

InsertItem inserts an object into a non-empty collection or map.

### Applies to

The InsertItem function can be used with the following objects:

DiscoveryScript::ColorArray , DiscoveryScript::DocumentArray , DiscoveryScript::IntegerArray , DiscoveryScript::ObjectMap , DiscoveryScript::RealArray , DiscoveryScript::StringArray , Mdm::Array , Mdm::OfflineableArray , Mdm::PointArray , Protocol::ParameterMap , Sdm::Array , Sdm::ResidueArray , Sdm::SequenceArray

### Using the InsertItem function

#### Instance

$object->InsertItem( <index>, <item> );

$object->InsertItem( <key>, <value> );

$object->InsertItem( { Index => <index>, Item => <item> } );

$object->InsertItem( { Key => <key>, Value => <value> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| <item> | Required | | DiscoveryScript::Object |
| <key> | Required | | String |
| <value> | Required | | DiscoveryScript::Object |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to manipulate items in an Mdm::Array.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

my $atoms = $document->Atoms;

# Collect all cysteine atoms.
my $cysteineAtomArray = Mdm::Array::Create();
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
$cysteineAtomArray->AddItem($atom)
if ( $atom->GetProperty("Parent") =~ /CYS/i );
}

# Find the common ancestor of all atoms in the array in cysteineAtomArray.
my $parent = $cysteineAtomArray->FindCommonAncestor();
print "The common parent object of all CYS atoms: "
. $parent->ClassName . " "
. $parent->Name . "\n";

die "No cysteine atoms found! Exiting.\n" if $cysteineAtomArray->IsEmpty;

my $cysteineAtomCount = $cysteineAtomArray->Count;
print "Number of atoms in cysteine residues: " . $cysteineAtomCount . "\n";

# Delete all atoms except C-alpha and C-beta.
# Note: When deleting items from an array, the array is traversed in
# reverse order. This avoids having to account for changes in the item
# indices as the array is modified.
for ( my $i = $cysteineAtomCount - 1 ; $i >= 0 ; --$i )
{
my $atom = $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i);
if ( $atom->Name !~ /(cb|ca)\b/i )
{
$cysteineAtomArray->DeleteItem($i);
}
}
print "Number of C-alpha and C-beta atoms in cysteine residues: "
. $cysteineAtomArray->Count . "\n";

# Create a copy of the original array in reverse order.
$cysteineAtomCount = $cysteineAtomArray->Count;
my $reverseCysteineArray = Mdm::Array::Create();

# Use the AddItem function to insert the first atom.
# Note: the InsertItem function cannot be used on an empty array.
$reverseCysteineArray->AddItem( $cysteineAtomArray->Item(0) );
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $cysteineAtomCount ; ++$i )
{
$reverseCysteineArray->InsertItem( 0, $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i) );
}

# Swap the first two elements or the original array.
my $tempItem = $cysteineAtomArray->Item(0);
$cysteineAtomArray->ReplaceItem( 0, $cysteineAtomArray->Item(1) );
$cysteineAtomArray->ReplaceItem( 1, $tempItem );

# Print out the IDs of the atoms in the two arrays side by side.
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $cysteineAtomCount ; ++$i )
{
my $atom1Id = $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i)->Id;
my $atom2Id = $reverseCysteineArray->Item($i)->Id;
print "item $i\t $atom1Id\t $atom2Id\n";
}

# Remove all remaining items in the original array.
$cysteineAtomArray->ClearItems();
print "The array now has " . $cysteineAtomArray->Count . " elements\n";
```

# InsertLoop function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/insertloop_function.htm

## InsertLoop function

### Description

InsertLoop inserts one or more amino acid residues into a gap in an amino acid chain after a specified amino acid residue.

### Applies to

The InsertLoop function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the InsertLoop function

#### Command

$object->InsertLoop( <insertat>, <sequence>, [isotropicdisplacement] );

$object->InsertLoop( { InsertAt => <insertat>, Sequence => <sequence>, IsotropicDisplacement => [isotropicdisplacement] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <insertat> | Required | | Mdm::AminoAcid |
| <sequence> | Required | | String |
| [isotropicdisplacement] | Optional | 20.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

#First clean the protein as the gap ends may well be faulty
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1kim');

# this would use CleanProtein with default parameters
my $cleanResults = $document->CleanProtein();

# if you want to save the results to a file, $clean_results
# are in html format
open( my $fhreport, '>cleanreport.html' );

#Find gaps
$document->MarkProteinGaps;

# Marked residues now have 'Gap End' or 'Gap Start' properties containing
# the missing sequence. We want the gap starts but will also get the ends
# to double-check its a real gap.
my $gapStartProp = "Gap Start";
my $gapEndProp = "Gap End";

my $aminoAcidChains = $document->AminoAcidChains;
my $chainCount = $aminoAcidChains->Count;

for ( my $c = 0 ; $c < $chainCount ; ++$c )
{
print "Looking for gaps in chain "
. $aminoAcidChains->Item($c)->Name . ".\n";
my $aminoAcids = $aminoAcidChains->Item($c)->AminoAcids;
my $aminoAcidCount = $aminoAcids->Count;

#loop to one before the end as we need a gap within the chain
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $aminoAcidCount - 1 ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $aminoAcids->Item($i);
my $nextAminoAcid = $aminoAcids->Item( $i + 1 );
if ( $aminoAcid->HasProperty($gapStartProp)
&& $nextAminoAcid->HasProperty($gapEndProp) )
{
my $property = $aminoAcid->GetProperty($gapStartProp);
print "Inserting sequence "
. $property
. " between residues "
. $aminoAcid->Name . " and "
. $nextAminoAcid->Name . ".\n";

$document->InsertLoop( $aminoAcid, $property );
}
}
}

if ( $fhreport ) {
print $fhreport $cleanResults;
close $fhreport;
}
```

# InsertSequence function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/insertsequence_function.htm

## InsertSequence function

### Description

InsertSequence inserts an Sdm::Sequence to an Sdm::Alignment at the specified 0-based index.

### Applies to

The InsertSequence function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the InsertSequence function

#### Instance

$object->InsertSequence( <index>, <sequence> );

$object->InsertSequence( { Index => <index>, Sequence => <sequence> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| <sequence> | Required | | Sdm::Sequence |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to copy sequences between documents
# either by insert at a specified index or appending.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $annotationDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId({Id => 'y13252', Database => "nuccore"});
my $sequence = $annotationDocument->Sequence(0);

# Append annotation window sequence to a new document.
my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateNucleotideDocument();
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();
$document->Alignment->AppendSequence($sequence);

# Insert sequence to a new document.
my $document2 = Sdm::Document::CreateNucleotideDocument();
$document2->DeleteAlignmentSequences();
$document2->Alignment->InsertSequence( 0, $sequence );
$document2->Alignment->InsertSequence( 1, $sequence );

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

```text

# Demonstrate how to inset residue abbreviations.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
```

Source type: HTML

## InsetAlignmentString function

### Description

InsetAlignmentString inserts a sequence of residues (represented by 1-letter codes) and gaps
into an Sdm::Alignment . The following arguments are available:

* Index specifies the 0-based sequence index.

* StartPosition specifies the 0-based residue position to insert into.

* AlignmentString specifies the sequence of residues (represented by 1-letter codes) and gaps to insert.

### Applies to

The InsetAlignmentString function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the InsetAlignmentString function

#### Instance

$object->InsetAlignmentString( <index>, <startposition>, <alignmentstring> );

$object->InsetAlignmentString( { Index => <index>, StartPosition => <startposition>, AlignmentString => <alignmentstring> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <alignmentstring> | Required | | String |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| <startposition> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to insert and inset alignment strings.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

sub ShowContent($$)
{
my ( $document, $note ) = @_;

print "\n" . "Show content: $note\n";
my $count = $document->SequenceCount;
printf "Count: %d\n", $count;
my $sequences = $document->Sequences;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $count ; ++$i )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($i);
printf "%d: %s: '%s'\n", $i, $sequence->Name,
$sequence->SequenceString();
}
}

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument('SDM');
ShowContent( $document, 'new empty protein document' );

# Insert alignment string in existing row.
$document->Alignment->InsetAlignmentString( 0, 0, 'AAAAA-A' );
ShowContent( $document, 'after InsetAlignmentString' );

$document->Alignment->InsetAlignmentString( 0, 2, 'S--S' );
$document->UpdateViews();
ShowContent( $document, 'after InsetAlignmentString' );

# Insert alignment string in a new row.
$document->Alignment->InsertAlignmentString( 0, 'New1', "F-FFG-GGH-HH" );
$document->Alignment->InsertAlignmentString( 2, 'New2', "TP-FGGGH-GLHHH" );
ShowContent( $document, 'after InsertAlignmentString' );
```

StartPosition specifies the 0-based residue position to insert into.

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

SdmDiscoveryScript

```text

# Insert a sequence into another sequence.
use strict;
```

# Invert (deprecated) function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/invert__deprecated__function.htm

## Invert (deprecated) function

### Description

Invert inverts the chirality of the selected atoms ( Mdm::Atom ),
bonds ( Mdm::Bond ), or molecules ( Mdm::Molecule ).
If a chiral atom is selected, its chirality is inverted.
If a bond is selected, the E or Z stereo chemistry of the bond is changed.
If a molecule is selected, all of the chiral atoms in the molecule are inverted.

### Applies to

The Invert (deprecated) function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the Invert (deprecated) function

#### Command

This function is deprecated. It has been renamed to InvertChirality in Mdm::Document .

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

# InvertAminoAcidChirality function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/invertaminoacidchirality_function.htm

## InvertAminoAcidChirality function

### Description

Inverts the chirality of selected amino acid residues (i.e., converts from
the L to the D isomer or vice versa). The residue name and type are adjusted
accordingly. If the whole protein is selected, the entire structure will
be inverted.

### Applies to

The InvertAminoAcidChirality function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the InvertAminoAcidChirality function

#### Command

$object->InvertAminoAcidChirality();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

#Add hydrogens. The protein chirality inverter works even if there
#are no hydrogens, they are being added merely to allow the before and
#after chirality to be reported.
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms;
#invert chirality of the first residue
my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
my $aminoAcid = $aminoAcids->[0];
my $atom = $aminoAcid->CAlpha;

print "Test inverting chirality of the first residue.\n";
print "Original amino acid name, PDB name and full type: " . $aminoAcid->Name . " ". $aminoAcid->PDBName() . " ". $aminoAcid->LongName . "\n";
print "Original Chirality (reported in R/S convention): " . $atom->Chirality . "\n";
$aminoAcid->Select();

$document->InvertAminoAcidChirality();
print "Inverted amino acid name, PDB name and full type: " . $aminoAcid->Name . " ". $aminoAcid->PDBName() ." ". $aminoAcid->LongName. "\n";

print "Inverted Chirality (reported in R/S convention): " . $atom->Chirality . "\n";

# Now do for whole molecule. Report for some arbitrary residue. 
# We will do this one without adding hydrogens, and report the phi/psi angles for a residue 
# to demonstrate that the entire structure is now its mirror image

my $document2 = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $aminoAcids2 = $document2->AminoAcids;
my $aminoAcid2 = $aminoAcids2->[24];
my $atom2 = $aminoAcid2->CAlpha;

print "\nTest inverting the entire structure. Results reported for an arbitrary residue.\n";
print "Original amino acid name, PDB name and full type: " . $aminoAcid2->Name . " ". $aminoAcid2->PDBName() . " ". $aminoAcid2->LongName . "\n";
printf "Original phi/psi angles: %.3f %.3f \n" , $aminoAcid2->PhiAngle, $aminoAcid2->PsiAngle;
$document2->SelectAll;
$document2->InvertAminoAcidChirality();
print "Inverted amino acid name, PDB name and full type: " . $aminoAcid2->Name . " ". $aminoAcid2->PDBName() ." ". $aminoAcid2->LongName. "\n";

printf "Inverted phi/psi angles: %.3f %.3f \n",$aminoAcid2->PhiAngle, $aminoAcid2->PsiAngle ;
```

# InvertChirality function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/invertchirality_function.htm

## InvertChirality function

### Description

InvertChirality inverts the chirality of the selected atoms ( Mdm::Atom ),
bonds ( Mdm::Bond ), or molecules ( Mdm::Molecule ).
If a chiral atom is selected, its chirality is inverted.
If a bond is selected, the E or Z stereo chemistry of the bond is changed.
If a molecule is selected, all of the chiral atoms in the molecule are inverted.

### Applies to

The InvertChirality function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the InvertChirality function

#### Command

$object->InvertChirality();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
$document->DeselectAll();
$molecule->Select();
$document->Invert(); # Inverts the chirality of all atoms.
```
