# IsLabelShown property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/islabelshown_property.htm

## IsLabelShown property

### Description

IsLabelShown is a Boolean specifying whether the
distance label is shown for the monitored objects such as a Mdm::HydrogenBond or Mdm::Nonbond object.

### Applies to

The IsLabelShown property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::BumpMonitor , Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor , Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::NeighborMonitor , Mdm::NonbondMonitor , Mdm::PiCationMonitor , Mdm::PiInteractionMonitor , Mdm::PiPiMonitor , Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor , Mdm::ValenceMonitor

### Using the IsLabelShown property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsLabelShown;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Set

$object->IsLabelShown = <show>;

$object->IsLabelShown( <show> );

$object->IsLabelShown( { Show => <show> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <show> | Required | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how use the hydrogen bond monitor and to change the distance cutoff.

use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Creates a hbond monitor between ligand atoms and receptor
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $LigName = $ligands->Item(0)->Name;
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $monitor = $document->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( $ligandAtoms,
Mdm::allAtomHydrogenBonds, Mdm::allMolecularHydrogenBonds );

# Shows the label for each of the hbonds
$monitor->IsLabelShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll(); 

printf "Default distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->DefaultDistanceCriterion;
printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor.\n\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $newHBDist = 3.0;
$monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared( $newHBDist* $newHBDist );

# update view to ensure the correct HB count
$document->UpdateViews();
printf "Set the distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared;

printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor:\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $hbonds = $document->HydrogenBonds;
my $count = $hbonds->Count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $hbond = $hbonds->Item($index);
my $dist = $hbond->Distance;
my $atom1 = $hbond->Atom1;
my $atom2 = $hbond->Atom2;
my $res = $atom1->Parent;

if ( $res->Name eq $LigName ) {
$atom2->Parent->Select; 
}
else{
$atom1->Parent->Select; 
}
printf "%d) Distance: %.3f A H-bond between Atom %s:%s:%s and Atom %s:%s:%s\n",
$index+1, $dist,
$atom1->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom1->Parent->Name, $atom1->Name,
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name ;
} 

$document->FitView(); 
my $display_style = { DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' };
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle($display_style);
$document->DeselectAll();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to change the display style of selected surfaces.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Generate array with Color Scheme values.
my @surfaceDisplayStyles = (
Mdm::surfaceStyleSoft, Mdm::surfaceStyleNone,
Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent, Mdm::surfaceStyleVDW
);

print 'Creating a solid surface with legend '
. "(this may take a few seconds)...\n\n";
my $allAtoms = $document->Atoms;
my $surface = $document->CreateSolidSurface($allAtoms);
$document->DeselectAll();
$surface->IsLegendShown(True);
sleep(3);

foreach my $surfaceDisplayStyle (@surfaceDisplayStyles)
{
print "Change the surface display style to $surfaceDisplayStyle...\n\n";
$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);
$surface->Select();

$document->SetSurfaceDisplayStyle($surfaceDisplayStyle);

$surface->Deselect();
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);
}
```

# IsLinked property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/islinked_property.htm

## IsLinked property

### Description

IsLinked is a Boolean indicating if a sequence is linked to a molecule.
The argument CheckEnabledState can be used to check for enabled or disabled links. By
default CheckEnabledState is True and IsLinked only returns True for active molecule-sequence links.

### Applies to

The IsLinked property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the IsLinked property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsLinked( [checkenabledstate] );

my $booleanValue = $object->IsLinked( { CheckEnabledState => [checkenabledstate] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| [checkenabledstate] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence Sdm::Sequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to link/delink SDM and MDM documents.
# NOTE: Sequence-Structure linking is only supported on the client.
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Create 1crn sequence manually so prevent auto-linking of documents.
# To link, the residue order, object names and chain breaks must match.
my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0);
$sequence->InsetAbbreviations( 0,
'ThrThrCysCysProSerIleValAlaArgSerAsnPheAsnValCysArgLeuProGlyThrProGlu'
. 'AlaIleCysAlaThrTyrThrGlyCysIleIleIleProGlyAlaThrCysProGlyAspTyrAlaAsn'
);
$sequence->Name = '1crn';

# Link documents (this will break any existing linked documents)
# and any match sequence-molecules.
# Note the sequence name shows the molecule icon indicating it is linked.
$sdmDocument->LinkMdmDocument($mdmDocument);

print 'Is sequence linked: ' . $sequence->IsLinked . "\n";

# Break document link.
# Uncomment to break the SDM-MDM document link.
#$sdmDocument->DelinkMdmDocument();
```

## IsMatchingNonbondType property

the Mdm::Nonbond object depicts an interaction of the

### Applies to

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| <nonbondtype> | Required | | enum Mdm::NonbondType |
| $object | | | Mdm::Nonbond |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the basic non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3fzm');
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;
$document->Zoom(15);
$document->IsHierarchyViewShown = True;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Create a non-bond monitor for a subset of atoms.\n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $monitor = $document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();

# -- Analyze the identified interactions. ---------------------------
my $nonbonds = $monitor->Nonbonds;
my $count = $nonbonds->Count;
printf "Found %d non-bond interactions (total):\n", $count;

print $monitor->FavorableNonbonds->Count 
. " of these are favorable interactions (such as H-bonds).\n";
print $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds->Count
. " of these are unfavorable interactions (such as bumps).\n\n";

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Analyze first non-bond interaction:\n";
my $nonbond = $nonbonds->Item(0);

my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$nonbond->Distance;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
my $unfavorableNonbonds = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds;
if ($unfavorableNonbonds->Count > 0) 
{
print "Analyze first unfavorable non-bond interaction:\n";
my $unfavorableNonbond = $unfavorableNonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $unfavorableNonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $unfavorableNonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$unfavorableNonbond->Distance;
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "All non-bonds of a particular type can be retrieved ";
print "using the NonbondsOfType filter.\n";
my $hBonds = $monitor->NonbondsOfType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType);
printf "Found %d hydrogen bonds using NonbondOfType filter.\n\n", $hBonds->Count;

print "Alternatively the IsMatchingNonbondType property can be used to \n";
print "identify interactions of a specific types. The following atom pairs \n";
print "indicate classical hydrogen bonding: \n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
if ($nonbond->IsMatchingNonbondType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType))
{
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);

print '* ' . $atom1->FullName . " (";
print 'donor ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrogenDonor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHalogen);
print 'positive ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPositive);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ') and ';

print $atom2->FullName . " (";
print 'acceptor ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrogenAcceptor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHalogen);
print 'negative ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsNegative);

print 'amide' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ")\n";
}
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "\nThe NonbondTypes property can be used to identify all \n";
print "interaction types of a non-bond.\n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
printf "- %s (%s) and %s (%s):",
$nonbond->FromSite->Name,
$nonbond->FromSite->ChemistryName,
$nonbond->ToSite->Name,
$nonbond->ToSite->ChemistryName;

#these are the type enums 
print " Types: ";
my $nonbondTypes = $nonbond->NonbondTypes;
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
print "$type ";
}

#these are the category enums 
print " Categories: ";
my $nonbondCategories = $nonbond->NonbondCategories;
foreach my $category (@$nonbondCategories) {
print "$category ";
}

#these APIs give the name(s) of the type/categories as a string 
#(the same as appears in the Nonbond tab of the DS MDT)
print " : Type Names: ";
my $typeNames = $nonbond->TypeNames;
print "$typeNames";

print " : Category Names: ";
my $categories = $nonbond->CategoryNames;
print "$categories";

print "\n";
}
print "\n";
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the basic non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3fzm');
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;
$document->Zoom(15);
$document->IsHierarchyViewShown = True;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Create a non-bond monitor for a subset of atoms.\n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $monitor = $document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();

# -- Analyze the identified interactions. ---------------------------
my $nonbonds = $monitor->Nonbonds;
my $count = $nonbonds->Count;
printf "Found %d non-bond interactions (total):\n", $count;

print $monitor->FavorableNonbonds->Count 
. " of these are favorable interactions (such as H-bonds).\n";
print $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds->Count
. " of these are unfavorable interactions (such as bumps).\n\n";

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Analyze first non-bond interaction:\n";
my $nonbond = $nonbonds->Item(0);

my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$nonbond->Distance;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
my $unfavorableNonbonds = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds;
if ($unfavorableNonbonds->Count > 0) 
{
print "Analyze first unfavorable non-bond interaction:\n";
my $unfavorableNonbond = $unfavorableNonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $unfavorableNonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $unfavorableNonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$unfavorableNonbond->Distance;
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "All non-bonds of a particular type can be retrieved ";
print "using the NonbondsOfType filter.\n";
my $hBonds = $monitor->NonbondsOfType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType);
printf "Found %d hydrogen bonds using NonbondOfType filter.\n\n", $hBonds->Count;

print "Alternatively the IsMatchingNonbondType property can be used to \n";
print "identify interactions of a specific types. The following atom pairs \n";
print "indicate classical hydrogen bonding: \n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
if ($nonbond->IsMatchingNonbondType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType))
{
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);

print '* ' . $atom1->FullName . " (";
print 'donor ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrogenDonor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHalogen);
print 'positive ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPositive);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ') and ';

print $atom2->FullName . " (";
print 'acceptor ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrogenAcceptor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHalogen);
print 'negative ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsNegative);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ")\n";
}
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "\nThe NonbondTypes property can be used to identify all \n";
print "interaction types of a non-bond.\n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
printf "- %s (%s) and %s (%s):",
$nonbond->FromSite->Name,
$nonbond->FromSite->ChemistryName,
$nonbond->ToSite->Name,
$nonbond->ToSite->ChemistryName;

#these are the type enums 
print " Types: ";
my $nonbondTypes = $nonbond->NonbondTypes;
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
print "$type ";
}

#these are the category enums 
print " Categories: ";
my $nonbondCategories = $nonbond->NonbondCategories;
foreach my $category (@$nonbondCategories) {
print "$category ";
}

#these APIs give the name(s) of the type/categories as a string 
#(the same as appears in the Nonbond tab of the DS MDT)
print " : Type Names: ";
my $typeNames = $nonbond->TypeNames;
print "$typeNames";

print " : Category Names: ";
my $categories = $nonbond->CategoryNames;
print "$categories";

print "\n";
}
print "\n";
```

# IsNonbondTypeShown property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/isnonbondtypeshown_property.htm

## IsNonbondTypeShown property

### Description

IsNonbondTypeShown is a Boolean specifying whether
the monitored Mdm::Nonbond objects matching the specified
non-bond type are shown. A Mdm::Nonbond object can match
multiple enum Mdm::NonbondType s. The non-bond will
be shown if any matching type is shown.

### Applies to

The IsNonbondTypeShown property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::NonbondMonitor

### Using the IsNonbondTypeShown property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsNonbondTypeShown( <nonbondtype> );

my $booleanValue = $object->IsNonbondTypeShown( { NonbondType => <nonbondtype> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| <nonbondtype> | Required | | enum Mdm::NonbondType |
| $object | | | Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor Mdm::NonbondMonitor |

#### Set

$object->IsNonbondTypeShown = <nonbondtype>, <show>;

$object->IsNonbondTypeShown( <nonbondtype>, <show> );

$object->IsNonbondTypeShown( { NonbondType => <nonbondtype>, Show => <show> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <nonbondtype> | Required | | enum Mdm::NonbondType |
| <show> | Required | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor Mdm::NonbondMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use of unsatisfied non-bonds.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "3fzm.pdb" );
die "Failed to create a valid MDM document!" unless $document;

my $ligandNonbondMonitor =
$document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor(
{RequirePredefinedLigand=>False});

$document->FocusOnFirstLigand;
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
$ligandNonbondMonitor->IsNonbondTypeShown(Mdm::nonInteracting) = True;

for (my $index = 0; $index < 3; ++$index)
{
my $unsatisfiedNonbonds = $ligandNonbondMonitor->UnsatisfiedNonbonds;

printf "Shell: %d\n", $ligandNonbondMonitor->Shell;
foreach my $unsatisfied (@$unsatisfiedNonbonds)
{
printf "Unsatisfied interaction on atom %s of type(s) %s\n", 
$unsatisfied->Name, $unsatisfied->ChemistryName;
}

$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
}
```

Source type: HTML

## IsNormalFlipped property

### Description

IsNormalFlipped is a Boolean specifying

### Applies to

Mdm::Isosurface

### Using the IsNormalFlipped property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsNormalFlipped;

##### Parameters

| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |

#### Set

$object->IsNormalFlipped = <flipnormal>;

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
print "It operates on a document with grid data\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a structure with grid data\n";
print
" (for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
print " 3 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Connect to an Sdm::Document from the last active sequence window
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

# Get array with all isosurfaces using Isosurfaces filter
my $isosurfaces = $document->Isosurfaces;

if ( $isosurfaces->Count == 0 )
{
print "To run this script, please open a structure with grid data.\n";
print "(for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
exit;
}

# Get the first isosurface
my $isosurface = $isosurfaces->[0];

# Create a new isosurface at 0.5 isovalue
my $newContour = $isosurface->CreateIsosurface(0.5);
$newContour->ContextAtomArray( $document->Atoms );

if ( !$newContour->IsContextAtomArrayDefined() )
{
print "Please define a context atom array\n";
}
$newContour->IsNormalFlipped(False);
$newContour->IsBoundaryDrawn(True);
print "The line width is: $newContour->{LineWidth}\n";

# Print the isovalues
$isosurfaces = $document->Isosurfaces;
foreach my $surface (@$isosurfaces)
{
print $surface->Name . " has isovalue " . $surface->Isovalue . "\n";
}

# Array with available display styles
my @displayStyles = (
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleNone, Mdm::isosurfaceStyleQuadMesh,
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleSolid, Mdm::isosurfaceStyleTriMesh,
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleVolume
);

# Iterate over the available display styles
print "\nIterating over isosurface display styles:\n";
foreach my $displayStyle (@displayStyles)
{
sleep(1);
$newContour->DisplayStyle = $displayStyle;
print "$displayStyle\n";
$document->UpdateViews();
}

$newContour->RemoveContextAtomArray();
```

# Isosurfaces filter

Source type: HTML

## Isosurfaces filter

### Description

Isosurfaces indicates all isosurfaces in a specific context,
such as a collection, a document, or the descendants of an object.

### Using the Isosurfaces filter

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->Isosurfaces;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
print "It operates on a document with grid data\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a structure with grid data\n";
print
" (for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
print " 3 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Connect to an Sdm::Document from the last active sequence window
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

# Get array with all isosurfaces using Isosurfaces filter
my $isosurfaces = $document->Isosurfaces;

if ( $isosurfaces->Count == 0 )
{
print "To run this script, please open a structure with grid data.\n";
print "(for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
exit;
}

# Get the first isosurface
my $isosurface = $isosurfaces->[0];

# Create a new isosurface at 0.5 isovalue
my $newContour = $isosurface->CreateIsosurface(0.5);
$newContour->ContextAtomArray( $document->Atoms );

if ( !$newContour->IsContextAtomArrayDefined() )
{
print "Please define a context atom array\n";
}
$newContour->IsNormalFlipped(False);
$newContour->IsBoundaryDrawn(True);
print "The line width is: $newContour->{LineWidth}\n";

# Print the isovalues
$isosurfaces = $document->Isosurfaces;
foreach my $surface (@$isosurfaces)
{
print $surface->Name . " has isovalue " . $surface->Isovalue . "\n";
}

# Array with available display styles
my @displayStyles = (
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleNone, Mdm::isosurfaceStyleQuadMesh,
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleSolid, Mdm::isosurfaceStyleTriMesh,
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleVolume
);

# Iterate over the available display styles
print "\nIterating over isosurface display styles:\n";
foreach my $displayStyle (@displayStyles)
{
sleep(1);
$newContour->DisplayStyle = $displayStyle;
print "$displayStyle\n";
$document->UpdateViews();
}

$newContour->RemoveContextAtomArray();
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of various atom properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

# Define atom properties to list.
# This may be specified on the command line.
my $residueAtomName = 'THR2:CA';
if ( @ARGV != 0 )
{
($residueAtomName) = @ARGV;
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Get the specified atom.
my $atoms = FilterByString( $document, $residueAtomName );
die "Atom $residueAtomName not found. Aborting!\n\n"
if ( $atoms->Count == 0 );

my $atom = $atoms->[0];

# Print various atom properties. In the DiscoveryStudio client, the
# output will appear in the output pane of the scripting window.
print "List of properties for atom $residueAtomName:\n\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
print 'Element: ' . $atom->Element . "\n";
print 'Element Name: ' . $atom->ElementName . "\n";
print 'Element Symbol: ' . $atom->ElementSymbol . "\n";
print 'Mass: ' . $atom->Mass . "\n";
print 'Atomic number: ' . $atom->AtomicNumber . "\n";
print 'Charge: ' . $atom->Charge . "\n";
print 'Formal Charge: '
. $atom->FormalCharge->Numerator . "/"
. $atom->FormalCharge->Denominator . "\n";

print 'VDW Radius: ' . $atom->VdwRadius . "\n";
print 'Covalent Radius: ' . $atom->CovalentRadius . "\n";
print 'Chirality: ' . $atom->Chirality . "\n";
print 'Bond count: ' . $atom->BondCount . "\n";
print 'Bonding radius: ' . $atom->BondingRadius . "\n";
print 'Hybridization: ' . $atom->Hybridization . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen Count: ' . $atom->HydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'ImplicitHydrogen Count: ' . $atom->ImplicitHydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Acceptor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondAcceptor . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Donor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondDonor . "\n";
print 'Isotropic Displacement: ' . $atom->IsotropicDisplacement . "\n";
print 'Is Terminal Hydrogen: ' . $atom->IsTerminalHydrogen . "\n";
print 'Is Valence Satisfied: ' . $atom->IsValenceSatisfied . "\n";
print 'Lone Pair Count: ' . $atom->LonePairCount . "\n";
print 'Valence Count: ' . $atom->ValenceCount . "\n";
print 'Occupancy: ' . $atom->Occupancy . "\n";

printf "\n%s:\n", 'Display Properties';
print 'DisplayStyle: ' . $atom->DisplayStyle . "\n";
print 'Ball Size: ' . $atom->BallSize . "\n";
print 'Ball Size Default: ' . $atom->BallSizeDefault . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale: ' . $atom->CPKScale . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale Default: ' . $atom->CPKScaleDefault . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius: ' . $atom->StickRadius . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius Default: ' . $atom->StickRadiusDefault . "\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
```

# IsPiSystem property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/ispisystem_property.htm

## IsPiSystem property

### Description

IsPiSystem is a Boolean that specifies if an Mdm::NonbondSite object is a pi-orbital system.

### Applies to

The IsPiSystem property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::NonbondSite

### Using the IsPiSystem property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsPiSystem;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::NonbondSite |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the basic non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3fzm');
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;
$document->Zoom(15);
$document->IsHierarchyViewShown = True;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Create a non-bond monitor for a subset of atoms.\n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $monitor = $document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();

# -- Analyze the identified interactions. ---------------------------
my $nonbonds = $monitor->Nonbonds;
my $count = $nonbonds->Count;
printf "Found %d non-bond interactions (total):\n", $count;

print $monitor->FavorableNonbonds->Count 
. " of these are favorable interactions (such as H-bonds).\n";
print $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds->Count
. " of these are unfavorable interactions (such as bumps).\n\n";

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Analyze first non-bond interaction:\n";
my $nonbond = $nonbonds->Item(0);

my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$nonbond->Distance;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
my $unfavorableNonbonds = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds;
if ($unfavorableNonbonds->Count > 0) 
{
print "Analyze first unfavorable non-bond interaction:\n";
my $unfavorableNonbond = $unfavorableNonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $unfavorableNonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $unfavorableNonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$unfavorableNonbond->Distance;
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "All non-bonds of a particular type can be retrieved ";
print "using the NonbondsOfType filter.\n";
my $hBonds = $monitor->NonbondsOfType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType);
printf "Found %d hydrogen bonds using NonbondOfType filter.\n\n", $hBonds->Count;

print "Alternatively the IsMatchingNonbondType property can be used to \n";
print "identify interactions of a specific types. The following atom pairs \n";
print "indicate classical hydrogen bonding: \n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
if ($nonbond->IsMatchingNonbondType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType))
{
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);

print '* ' . $atom1->FullName . " (";
print 'donor ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrogenDonor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHalogen);
print 'positive ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPositive);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ') and ';

print $atom2->FullName . " (";
print 'acceptor ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrogenAcceptor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHalogen);
print 'negative ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsNegative);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ")\n";
}
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "\nThe NonbondTypes property can be used to identify all \n";
print "interaction types of a non-bond.\n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
printf "- %s (%s) and %s (%s):",
$nonbond->FromSite->Name,
$nonbond->FromSite->ChemistryName,
$nonbond->ToSite->Name,
$nonbond->ToSite->ChemistryName;

#these are the type enums 
print " Types: ";
my $nonbondTypes = $nonbond->NonbondTypes;
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
print "$type ";
}

#these are the category enums 
print " Categories: ";
my $nonbondCategories = $nonbond->NonbondCategories;
foreach my $category (@$nonbondCategories) {
print "$category ";
}

#these APIs give the name(s) of the type/categories as a string 
#(the same as appears in the Nonbond tab of the DS MDT)
print " : Type Names: ";
my $typeNames = $nonbond->TypeNames;
print "$typeNames";

print " : Category Names: ";
my $categories = $nonbond->CategoryNames;
print "$categories";

print "\n";
}
print "\n";
```

### Using the IsPredicted property

my $booleanValue = $object->IsPredicted;

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Sdm::SecondaryStructure |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to predict and retrieve secondary structure.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

my $sequence =
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( $mdmDocument->Molecules->[0] );
$alignment->PredictSecondaryStructureByDsc();

# Example accessing the secondary structure string from sequence property.
my $kabschAndSander =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructure(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType);
print "Kabsch and Sander secondary structure:\n";
print "Encoded: $kabschAndSander\n";

# Ensure alignment is displaying secondary structure.
if ( !( $alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown ) )
{
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown = True;
}

# Ensure KAS is displayed
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureVisible(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType) =
True;

# Example accessing the secondary structure data from object.
print "DSC secondary structure:\n";
my $ssObject =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructureObject(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);

print 'Predictor: ' . $ssObject->Predictor . "\n";
print 'Has probabilities: ' . $ssObject->IsPredicted . "\n";

my $dsc = $ssObject->SecondaryStructureString;
print "Encoded: $dsc\n";

my $propensity =
$sequence
->ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);
print "Propensity: $propensity\n";

my $helicalResidueCount = 0;
my $sheetResidueCount = 0;
my $coilResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $ssObject->ResidueCount;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $ssObject->SsType($i);
++$helicalResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$sheetResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::sheet || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
++$coilResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::coil || $type eq Sdm::extracellular );
}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print 'Analysis: The DSC secondary structure for this sequence has '
. $helicalResidueCount
. ' amino acid residues in helical formations, '
. $sheetResidueCount
. ' in sheet formations and '
. $coilResidueCount
. " in coil formations.\n";

my $secstrucfilter = $sdmDocument->SecondaryStructures;
print "Number of secondary Structures: ", $secstrucfilter->Count . "\n";
```

# IsProtocolSuccessful property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/isprotocolsuccessful_property.htm

## IsProtocolSuccessful property

### Description

IsProtocolSuccessful is a Boolean representing whether the task completed
successfully. This is a short cut for testing that the ProtocolStatus
property matches "Success".

### Applies to

The IsProtocolSuccessful property can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Task

### Using the IsProtocolSuccessful property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsProtocolSuccessful;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Protocol::Task |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

# IsPurine property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/ispurine_property.htm

## IsPurine property

### Description

IsPurine is a Boolean indicating whether a nucleotide has a Purine ring system. The Adenosine and Guanosine bases each contain a Purine ring.

### Applies to

The IsPurine property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::Nucleotide

### Using the IsPurine property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsPurine;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::NucleicAcid Mdm::Nucleotide |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the use of Mdm::Nucleotide objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "3CRO.pdb" );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

print "Nucleic acid sequence: $molecule->{NucleicAcidSequence}\n";

my $nucleotides = $document->Nucleotides;
my $nucleotide1 = $nucleotides->Item(0);
my $nucleotide2 = $nucleotides->Item(1);
my $nucleotide3 = $nucleotides->Item(2);
my $nucleotide4 = $nucleotides->Item(3);

my $distance =
$document->CreateDistanceMonitor( $nucleotide1->C1Prime,
$nucleotide1->C2Prime );
printf
"Distance between C1' and C2' atoms of $nucleotide1->{Name}: %8.3f angstroms\n",
$distance->Distance;

my $angle =
$document->CreateAngleMonitor( $nucleotide2->C2, $nucleotide2->C3Prime,
$nucleotide2->C4 );

my $torsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide3->C4Prime, $nucleotide3->C5,
$nucleotide3->C5Prime, $nucleotide3->C6
);

my $torsion2 =
$document->CreateTorsionMonitor( $nucleotide3->N1, $nucleotide3->N3,
$nucleotide3->N7, $nucleotide3->N9 );

my $torsion3 = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide4->O1P, $nucleotide4->O2P,
$nucleotide4->O3Prime, $nucleotide4->O4Prime
);

print $nucleotide1->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsDeoxyribose );
print "a deoxyribose.\n";

print $nucleotide2->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsRibose );
print "a ribose.\n";

print $nucleotide3->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPurine );
print "have a purine ring system.\n";

print $nucleotide4->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPyrimidine );
print "have a pyrimidine ring system.\n";
```

# IsQueryAtomAliphatic property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/isqueryatomaliphatic_property.htm

## IsQueryAtomAliphatic property

### Description

IsQueryAtomAliphatic is a Boolean specifying if a query atom is aliphatic.

### Applies to

The IsQueryAtomAliphatic property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryAtom

### Using the IsQueryAtomAliphatic property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsQueryAtomAliphatic;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryAtom |

#### Set

$object->IsQueryAtomAliphatic = <aliphatic>;

$object->IsQueryAtomAliphatic( <aliphatic> );

$object->IsQueryAtomAliphatic( { Aliphatic => <aliphatic> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <aliphatic> | Required | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryAtom |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Creates a query that can be either benzene or pyridine
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create the molecules for the substructure query
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');
$document->InsertFromSmiles('C1=NC=CC=C1');

# Create the query which will fit benzene or pyridine
$document->CreateOrTopology();

# Make aliphatic and aromatic valid using property Set option. Also
# set all charges negative.
my $queryatoms = $document->QueryAtoms;
foreach my $queryatom (@$queryatoms)
{
$queryatom->IsQueryAtomAromatic = 1;
$queryatom->IsQueryAtomAliphatic = 1;
$queryatom->SetQueryAtomNegative(1);
}

# Use Get option to print some information
foreach my $queryatom (@$queryatoms)
{
my $atomName = $queryatom->Name();
print "$atomName is: \n";
if ( $queryatom->IsQueryAtomAromatic )
{
print "Aromatic\n";
}
if ( $queryatom->IsQueryAtomAliphatic )
{
print "Aliphatic\n";
}
if ( $queryatom->IsQueryAtomBridgehead )
{
print "a bridgehead atom\n";
}
if ( $queryatom->IsQueryAtomEndocyclic )
{
print "endocyclic\n";
}
if ( $queryatom->IsQueryAtomNegative )
{
print "has negative charges\n";
}
if ( $queryatom->IsQueryAtomStereo )
{
print "will use the defined stereo chemistry for this atom\n";
}
print "\n";
}
```

## IsResidueColorTypeShown property

### Description

IsResidueColorTypeShown is a Boolean specifying if an Sdm::Residue has the specified decoration displayed.
This property is intended to alter the visibility of the caret, overline,
and underline decorations on a residue.

### Applies to

The IsResidueColorTypeShown property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Residue

### Using the IsResidueColorTypeShown property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsResidueColorTypeShown( <type> );

my $booleanValue = $object->IsResidueColorTypeShown( { Type => <type> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| <type> | Required | | enum Sdm::ResidueColorType |
| $object | | | Sdm::Residue |

#### Set

$object->IsResidueColorTypeShown = <type>, <show>;

$object->IsResidueColorTypeShown( <type>, <show> );

$object->IsResidueColorTypeShown( { Type => <type>, Show => <show> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <show> | Required | | Boolean |
| <type> | Required | | enum Sdm::ResidueColorType |
| $object | | | Sdm::Residue |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to access a residue from a sequence.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures($mdmDocument);
my $sequence = $document->Sequence(0);

my $black = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 0, 0, 0 ); 
my $count = $sequence->ResidueCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $residue = $sequence->Residue($index);
printf "Residue %d is %s\n", $index, $residue->Symbol;

# Setting the color is sufficient to show the decoration. The property 
# IsResidueColorTypeShown can be used to independently toggle the 
# visibility.
$residue->IsResidueColorTypeShown(Sdm::colorCaret) = True;
$residue->Color(Sdm::colorCaret, $black);
}

$document->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->Close();
```

# IsRibose property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/isribose_property.htm

## IsRibose property

### Description

IsRibose is a Boolean indicating whether a
nucleotide has a ribose. A value of True is returned if the
nucleoside sugar unit contains an oxygen atom at the 2'
carbon atom.

### Applies to

The IsRibose property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::Nucleotide

### Using the IsRibose property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsRibose;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::NucleicAcid Mdm::Nucleotide |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the use of Mdm::Nucleotide objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "3CRO.pdb" );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

print "Nucleic acid sequence: $molecule->{NucleicAcidSequence}\n";

my $nucleotides = $document->Nucleotides;
my $nucleotide1 = $nucleotides->Item(0);
my $nucleotide2 = $nucleotides->Item(1);
my $nucleotide3 = $nucleotides->Item(2);
my $nucleotide4 = $nucleotides->Item(3);

my $distance =
$document->CreateDistanceMonitor( $nucleotide1->C1Prime,
$nucleotide1->C2Prime );
printf
"Distance between C1' and C2' atoms of $nucleotide1->{Name}: %8.3f angstroms\n",
$distance->Distance;

my $angle =
$document->CreateAngleMonitor( $nucleotide2->C2, $nucleotide2->C3Prime,
$nucleotide2->C4 );

my $torsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide3->C4Prime, $nucleotide3->C5,
$nucleotide3->C5Prime, $nucleotide3->C6
);

my $torsion2 =
$document->CreateTorsionMonitor( $nucleotide3->N1, $nucleotide3->N3,
$nucleotide3->N7, $nucleotide3->N9 );

my $torsion3 = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide4->O1P, $nucleotide4->O2P,
$nucleotide4->O3Prime, $nucleotide4->O4Prime
);

print $nucleotide1->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsDeoxyribose );
print "a deoxyribose.\n";

print $nucleotide2->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsRibose );
print "a ribose.\n";

print $nucleotide3->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPurine );
print "have a purine ring system.\n";

print $nucleotide4->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPyrimidine );
print "have a pyrimidine ring system.\n";
```

# IsRoot property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/isroot_property.htm

## IsRoot property

### Description

IsRoot is a Boolean specifying if the query operator is the root operator in a 3D query.

### Applies to

The IsRoot property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::QueryOperator

### Using the IsRoot property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsRoot;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Set

$object->IsRoot = <root>;

$object->IsRoot( <root> );

$object->IsRoot( { Root => <root> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <root> | Required | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::QueryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Create a distance constraint (7.5 to 9.5 angstroms) between O and [N,O,S]
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create Mdm::Array to store atoms to use for distance constraint.
my $atoms = Mdm::Array::Create();

# Create an oxygen atom at (-15.6, 2.2, 0.0).
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -15.6, 2.2, 0 );
$atoms->AddItem($atomObject);

# Create a Nitrogen atom at (-7.2, 2.3, 0.0).
my $molecule1 = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject1 = $molecule1->CreateAtom("N");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -7.2, 2.3, 0 );
$atoms->AddItem($atomObject1);

# Create an 'AND' query containing the selected molecules (all
# molecules are used if none selected). This will be used as the
# top level for the distance constraint.
$document->CreateAndTopology();

# Get the Root operator.
my $operators = $document->QueryOperators;
my $rootOperator;
foreach my $operator (@$operators)
{
if ( $operator->IsRoot )
{
$rootOperator = $operator;
}
}

# Create the distance constraint off the root operator.
my $distanceConstraint =
$rootOperator->CreateDistanceFeature( $atoms, 7.5, 9.5 );

# Get N QueryAtom and change it to N,O,S.
my $queryAtoms = $document->QueryAtoms;
foreach my $queryAtom (@$queryAtoms)
{
my $atomList = $queryAtom->GetProperty("List");
if ( $atomList eq 'N' )
{
$queryAtom->SetProperty( "List", "N O S" );
$queryAtom->Parent()->Select; # select it for the color command below
}
}

# Color the QueryAtom with multiple definitions another color
$document->SetColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 170, 85, 127 ) );
$document->DeselectAll();
```

# IsRunnable property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/isrunnable_property.htm

## IsRunnable property

### Description

IsRunnable is a Boolean specifying if a protocol task is runnable.

### Applies to

The IsRunnable property can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Task

### Using the IsRunnable property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsRunnable;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Protocol::Task |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

# IsSecondaryStructureShown property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/issecondarystructureshown_property.htm

## IsSecondaryStructureShown property

### Description

IsSecondaryStructureShown is a Boolean indicating
if visible secondary structures are displayed in the Sequence Window.
In order for secondary structures to show in the Sequence Window,
both this property and the secondary structure's visibility must be True
(see IsVisible ).

### Applies to

The IsSecondaryStructureShown property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the IsSecondaryStructureShown property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsSecondaryStructureShown;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Set

$object->IsSecondaryStructureShown = <visible>;

$object->IsSecondaryStructureShown( <visible> );

$object->IsSecondaryStructureShown( { Visible => <visible> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <visible> | Required | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to predict and retrieve secondary structure.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

my $sequence =
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( $mdmDocument->Molecules->[0] );
$alignment->PredictSecondaryStructureByDsc();

# Example accessing the secondary structure string from sequence property.
my $kabschAndSander =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructure(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType);
print "Kabsch and Sander secondary structure:\n";
print "Encoded: $kabschAndSander\n";

# Ensure alignment is displaying secondary structure.
if ( !( $alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown ) )
{
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown = True;
}

# Ensure KAS is displayed
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureVisible(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType) =
True;

# Example accessing the secondary structure data from object.
print "DSC secondary structure:\n";
my $ssObject =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructureObject(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);

print 'Predictor: ' . $ssObject->Predictor . "\n";
print 'Has probabilities: ' . $ssObject->IsPredicted . "\n";

my $dsc = $ssObject->SecondaryStructureString;
print "Encoded: $dsc\n";

my $propensity =
$sequence
->ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);
print "Propensity: $propensity\n";

my $helicalResidueCount = 0;
my $sheetResidueCount = 0;
my $coilResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $ssObject->ResidueCount;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $ssObject->SsType($i);
++$helicalResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$sheetResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::sheet || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
++$coilResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::coil || $type eq Sdm::extracellular );
}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print 'Analysis: The DSC secondary structure for this sequence has '
. $helicalResidueCount
. ' amino acid residues in helical formations, '
. $sheetResidueCount
. ' in sheet formations and '
. $coilResidueCount
. " in coil formations.\n";

my $secstrucfilter = $sdmDocument->SecondaryStructures;
print "Number of secondary Structures: ", $secstrucfilter->Count . "\n";
```

```text
my $coilResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $ssObject->ResidueCount;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $ssObject->SsType($i);
++$helicalResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$sheetResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::sheet || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
++$coilResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::coil || $type eq Sdm::extracellular );
}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print 'Analysis: The DSC secondary structure for this sequence has '
. $helicalResidueCount
. ' amino acid residues in helical formations, '
. $sheetResidueCount
. ' in sheet formations and '
. $coilResidueCount
. " in coil formations.\n";

my $secstrucfilter = $sdmDocument->SecondaryStructures;
print "Number of secondary Structures: ", $secstrucfilter->Count . "\n";
```

# IsSecondaryStructureVisible property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/issecondarystructurevisible_property.htm

## IsSecondaryStructureVisible property

### Description

IsSecondaryStructureVisible is a Boolean indicating
if a secondary structure's visibility is True.
In order for secondary structures to show in the Sequence Window,
the secondary structure's visibility must be True and the IsSecondaryStructureShown must also be True.

### Applies to

The IsSecondaryStructureVisible property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the IsSecondaryStructureVisible property

#### Set

$object->IsSecondaryStructureVisible = <predictor>, <visible>;

$object->IsSecondaryStructureVisible( <predictor>, <visible> );

$object->IsSecondaryStructureVisible( { Predictor => <predictor>, Visible => <visible> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <predictor> | Required | | enum Sdm::AminoAcidSecondaryStructurePredictor |
| <visible> | Required | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to predict and retrieve secondary structure.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

my $sequence =
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( $mdmDocument->Molecules->[0] );
$alignment->PredictSecondaryStructureByDsc();

# Example accessing the secondary structure string from sequence property.
my $kabschAndSander =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructure(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType);
print "Kabsch and Sander secondary structure:\n";
print "Encoded: $kabschAndSander\n";

# Ensure alignment is displaying secondary structure.
if ( !( $alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown ) )
{
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown = True;
}

# Ensure KAS is displayed
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureVisible(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType) =
True;

# Example accessing the secondary structure data from object.
print "DSC secondary structure:\n";
my $ssObject =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructureObject(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);

print 'Predictor: ' . $ssObject->Predictor . "\n";
print 'Has probabilities: ' . $ssObject->IsPredicted . "\n";

my $dsc = $ssObject->SecondaryStructureString;
print "Encoded: $dsc\n";

my $propensity =
$sequence
->ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);
print "Propensity: $propensity\n";

my $helicalResidueCount = 0;
my $sheetResidueCount = 0;
my $coilResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $ssObject->ResidueCount;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $ssObject->SsType($i);
++$helicalResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$sheetResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::sheet || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
++$coilResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::coil || $type eq Sdm::extracellular );
}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print 'Analysis: The DSC secondary structure for this sequence has '
. $helicalResidueCount
. ' amino acid residues in helical formations, '
. $sheetResidueCount
. ' in sheet formations and '
. $coilResidueCount
. " in coil formations.\n";

my $secstrucfilter = $sdmDocument->SecondaryStructures;
print "Number of secondary Structures: ", $secstrucfilter->Count . "\n";
```

DiscoveryScript

| $object | | | DiscoveryScript |

#### Defined by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how connect to active documents.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.\n";
print "Please load Discovery Studio and try again.\n";
exit;
}

# Get the current active Discovery Studio document.
# NOTE: This may produce a warning if there is no scripting
# interface the active document.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::ActiveDocument();
if ($document)
{
printf "The current active document is type: %s\n", $document->ClassName;
}

# Get the last active MDM document (Molecule Window) in Discovery Studio.
my $document2 = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
if ($document2)
{
printf "I have an Mdm document, type: %s\n", $document2->ClassName;
}
```

# IsStartOfChain property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/isstartofchain_property.htm

## IsStartOfChain property

### Description

IsStartOfChain is a Boolean specifying if the residue at the 0-based index starts a new polymer chain.

### Applies to

The IsStartOfChain property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Residue

### Using the IsStartOfChain property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsStartOfChain;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Sdm::Residue |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrates how to manipulate chain breaks in sequences.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();

$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $sequence0 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'MIASDFADSG' );
my $sequence1 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S2', 'MAACDFIDSA' );

# Insert chain breaks by marking the start of new chains using
# 0-based residue indices.
$sequence0->MarkStartOfChain(4);
$sequence1->MarkStartOfChain(4);
$sequence1->MarkStartOfChain(6);

# Find the starting residue index for each new chain.
my $residueCount0 = $sequence0->ResidueCount;
print "In the first sequence, there is a start of chain at ";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount0 ; ++$i )
{
if ( $sequence0->Residue($i)->IsStartOfChain )
{
print "$i ";
}
}
print "\n";
$document->UpdateViews();

$sequence1->DeleteStartOfChainMark(4);
$document->UpdateViews();

# Find the starting residue index for each new chain in
# second sequence.
my $residueCount1 = $sequence1->ResidueCount;
print "In the second sequence, there is a start of chain at ";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount1 ; ++$i )
{
if ( $sequence1->Residue($i)->IsStartOfChain )
{
print "$i ";
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# IsStopped property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/isstopped_property.htm

## IsStopped property

### Description

IsStopped is a Boolean specifying if a protocol task has been stopped.

### Applies to

The IsStopped property can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Task

### Using the IsStopped property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsStopped;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Protocol::Task |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of various atom properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

# Define atom properties to list.
# This may be specified on the command line.
my $residueAtomName = 'THR2:CA';
if ( @ARGV != 0 )
{
($residueAtomName) = @ARGV;
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Get the specified atom.
my $atoms = FilterByString( $document, $residueAtomName );
die "Atom $residueAtomName not found. Aborting!\n\n"
if ( $atoms->Count == 0 );

my $atom = $atoms->[0];

# Print various atom properties. In the DiscoveryStudio client, the
# output will appear in the output pane of the scripting window.
print "List of properties for atom $residueAtomName:\n\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
print 'Element: ' . $atom->Element . "\n";
print 'Element Name: ' . $atom->ElementName . "\n";
print 'Element Symbol: ' . $atom->ElementSymbol . "\n";
print 'Mass: ' . $atom->Mass . "\n";
print 'Atomic number: ' . $atom->AtomicNumber . "\n";
print 'Charge: ' . $atom->Charge . "\n";
print 'Formal Charge: '
. $atom->FormalCharge->Numerator . "/"
. $atom->FormalCharge->Denominator . "\n";

print 'VDW Radius: ' . $atom->VdwRadius . "\n";
print 'Covalent Radius: ' . $atom->CovalentRadius . "\n";
print 'Chirality: ' . $atom->Chirality . "\n";
print 'Bond count: ' . $atom->BondCount . "\n";
print 'Bonding radius: ' . $atom->BondingRadius . "\n";
print 'Hybridization: ' . $atom->Hybridization . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen Count: ' . $atom->HydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'ImplicitHydrogen Count: ' . $atom->ImplicitHydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Acceptor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondAcceptor . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Donor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondDonor . "\n";
print 'Isotropic Displacement: ' . $atom->IsotropicDisplacement . "\n";
print 'Is Terminal Hydrogen: ' . $atom->IsTerminalHydrogen . "\n";
print 'Is Valence Satisfied: ' . $atom->IsValenceSatisfied . "\n";
print 'Lone Pair Count: ' . $atom->LonePairCount . "\n";
print 'Valence Count: ' . $atom->ValenceCount . "\n";
print 'Occupancy: ' . $atom->Occupancy . "\n";

printf "\n%s:\n", 'Display Properties';
print 'DisplayStyle: ' . $atom->DisplayStyle . "\n";
print 'Ball Size: ' . $atom->BallSize . "\n";
print 'Ball Size Default: ' . $atom->BallSizeDefault . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale: ' . $atom->CPKScale . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale Default: ' . $atom->CPKScaleDefault . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius: ' . $atom->StickRadius . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius Default: ' . $atom->StickRadiusDefault . "\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
```

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use ProteinPose properties.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing docked protein poses.\n";
print " 3 Enter a cluster ID in the Arguments tab.\n";
print " 4 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

my ($clusterID) = @ARGV;

if ( $clusterID !~ /^\d+$/ )
{
$clusterID = 1;
}

# The script assume the last active document contains ProteinPoses.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage( 'This example requires an open Molecule Window containing '
. 'docked protein poses.' )
unless ($document);

# Get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter.
my $poseGroups = $document->DockedProteinPoseAssemblies;
Usage( 'This example requires an open Molecule Window containing '
. 'docked protein poses.' )
unless ( $poseGroups->Count > 0 );

my $poses = $document->ProteinPoses;

my $topClusterPose;

# Show all poses in cluster $clusterID, color green.
foreach my $pose (@$poses)
{
if ( $pose->Cluster == $clusterID )
{
$pose->SetVisible();

# Represent best ranked pose in the cluster as sphere and color light green.
if ( $pose->IsTopClusterPose )
{
$pose->DisplayStyle(Mdm::styleProteinPoseSphere);
$pose->Color( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 0 ) );
$topClusterPose = $pose;
}

# Represent other cluster members as jacks and color dark green.
else
{
$pose->DisplayStyle(Mdm::styleProteinPoseJack);
$pose->Color( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 122, 0 ) );
}
}
else
{

# Hide all poses not in the cluster.
$pose->SetInvisible();
}
}
```

# IsTransient property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

## IsTransient property

### Description

IsTransient is a Boolean indicating a sequence is transient. The consensus sequence is an
example of a transient sequence.

### Applies to

The IsTransient property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the IsTransient property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsTransient;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence Sdm::Sequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script will identify and list transient sequences.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument('SDM');
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $sequence0 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'ASDFADS' );

my $sequences = $document->Sequences;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $sequences->Count ; ++$index )
{
my $sequence = $sequences->Item($index);
my $state = ' is ';
$state = $state . 'not ' unless ( $sequence->IsTransient );
print $sequence->Name . $state . "transient\n";
}
```

# IsTransparent property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/istransparent_property.htm

## IsTransparent property

### Description

IsTransparent is a Boolean specifying whether a graphics object is transparent.

### Applies to

The IsTransparent property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Cylinder , Mdm::Isosurface , Mdm::Sphere , Mdm::Surface

### Using the IsTransparent property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsTransparent;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Cylinder Mdm::Isosurface Mdm::Sphere Mdm::Surface |

#### Set

$object->IsTransparent = <transparent>;

$object->IsTransparent( <transparent> );

$object->IsTransparent( { Transparent => <transparent> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <transparent> | Required | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Cylinder Mdm::Isosurface Mdm::Sphere Mdm::Surface |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Creates an empty molecule
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();

# Create oxygen atoms
my $O1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);
my $O2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

# Assign coordinates to atoms
my $xyz1 = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O1->XYZ = $xyz1;

my $xyz2 = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O2->XYZ = $xyz2;

# Create Spheres centered on atom position
my $sphere1 = $O1->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz1, Radius => 0.4 } );
my $sphere2 = $O2->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz2, Radius => 0.4 } );

# Create Cylinder
my $cylinder =
$O1->CreateCylinder( { Begin => $xyz1, End => $xyz2, Radius => 0.2 } );
my $bottom = $cylinder->{BottomCenter};
printf "Cylinder bottom center: %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n Radius: %8.3f\n",
$bottom->X, $bottom->Y, $bottom->Z, $cylinder->Radius;

# Make cylinder transparent
$cylinder->IsTransparent(True);

# Create a slicing plane perpendicular to the cylinder axis
my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
my $slicingplaneObject = $document->CreateSlicingPlane(
{
Index => 1,
ArrayOfObjects => $atoms,
Origin => Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 ),
Normal => Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 )
}
);

# Get all 3D Objects
my $objects3d = $document->Geometric3ds;

# Print their name and class name
foreach my $object (@$objects3d)
{
print $object->ClassName . "\t" . $object->Name . "\n";
}

# Get all slicing planes
my $slicplanes = $document->SlicingPlanes;
print "Number of slicing planes" . $slicplanes->Count. "\n";
```

# IsUnderValence property

Source type: HTML
