## IsUnderValence property

### Description

IsUnderValence is a Boolean specifying whether an atom is under the expected valence.

### Applies to

The IsUnderValence property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Valence

### Using the IsUnderValence property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsUnderValence;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Valence |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of ValenceMonitor objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "3ptb.pdb" );

# Creates a hydrogen-bond monitor between ligand and receptor atoms.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $monitor = $document->CreateValenceMonitor($ligandAtoms);

$monitor->IsUnderValenceShown = True;

print "Found " . $monitor->OverValenceCount . " atoms over valence.\n";
print "Found " . $monitor->UnderValenceCount . " atoms under valence.\n";

my $valences = $monitor->Valences;

my $count = $valences->Count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $valence = $valences->Item($index);
printf "Expected valence (for %s): %d \t Current valence: %d\n",
$valence->Name, $valence->ExpectedValence, $valence->Valence;
}
```

# IsUsingMassWeighting property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/isusingmassweighting_property.htm

## IsUsingMassWeighting property

### Description

IsUsingMassWeighting is a Boolean specifying whether the harmonic atom
restraints should be weighted by the mass of the atom during simulation.

### Applies to

The IsUsingMassWeighting property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::HarmonicAtomRestraint

### Using the IsUsingMassWeighting property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsUsingMassWeighting;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::HarmonicAtomRestraint |

#### Set

$object->IsUsingMassWeighting = <use>;

$object->IsUsingMassWeighting( <use> );

$object->IsUsingMassWeighting( { Use => <use> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <use> | Required | | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::HarmonicAtomRestraint |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Restrain the backbone
my $backbone = FilterByString( $document, ':CA,C,N,O,HN,HA' );
my $restraint = $document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint($backbone);

# The default (and recommended) setting is to use mass weighting
# Override that here for illustration
$restraint->IsUsingMassWeighting(False);

printf "Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$document->Molecules->Item(0)->Name,
$document->Atoms->Count();

# Print the total number of restraints (4)
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
printf "There are: %d constraints\n", $constraints->Count;
for ( my $i= 0 ; $i < $constraints->Count ; ++$i )
{
printf "%d) constraint: %s\n",$i+1,$constraints->Item($i)->Name;
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of various atom properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

# Define atom properties to list.
# This may be specified on the command line.
my $residueAtomName = 'THR2:CA';
if ( @ARGV != 0 )
{
($residueAtomName) = @ARGV;
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Get the specified atom.
my $atoms = FilterByString( $document, $residueAtomName );
die "Atom $residueAtomName not found. Aborting!\n\n"
if ( $atoms->Count == 0 );

my $atom = $atoms->[0];

# Print various atom properties. In the DiscoveryStudio client, the
# output will appear in the output pane of the scripting window.
print "List of properties for atom $residueAtomName:\n\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
print 'Element: ' . $atom->Element . "\n";
print 'Element Name: ' . $atom->ElementName . "\n";
print 'Element Symbol: ' . $atom->ElementSymbol . "\n";
print 'Mass: ' . $atom->Mass . "\n";
print 'Atomic number: ' . $atom->AtomicNumber . "\n";
print 'Charge: ' . $atom->Charge . "\n";
print 'Formal Charge: '
. $atom->FormalCharge->Numerator . "/"
. $atom->FormalCharge->Denominator . "\n";

print 'VDW Radius: ' . $atom->VdwRadius . "\n";
print 'Covalent Radius: ' . $atom->CovalentRadius . "\n";
print 'Chirality: ' . $atom->Chirality . "\n";
print 'Bond count: ' . $atom->BondCount . "\n";
print 'Bonding radius: ' . $atom->BondingRadius . "\n";
print 'Hybridization: ' . $atom->Hybridization . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen Count: ' . $atom->HydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'ImplicitHydrogen Count: ' . $atom->ImplicitHydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Acceptor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondAcceptor . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Donor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondDonor . "\n";
print 'Isotropic Displacement: ' . $atom->IsotropicDisplacement . "\n";
print 'Is Terminal Hydrogen: ' . $atom->IsTerminalHydrogen . "\n";
print 'Is Valence Satisfied: ' . $atom->IsValenceSatisfied . "\n";
print 'Lone Pair Count: ' . $atom->LonePairCount . "\n";
print 'Valence Count: ' . $atom->ValenceCount . "\n";
print 'Occupancy: ' . $atom->Occupancy . "\n";

printf "\n%s:\n", 'Display Properties';
print 'DisplayStyle: ' . $atom->DisplayStyle . "\n";
print 'Ball Size: ' . $atom->BallSize . "\n";
print 'Ball Size Default: ' . $atom->BallSizeDefault . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale: ' . $atom->CPKScale . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale Default: ' . $atom->CPKScaleDefault . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius: ' . $atom->StickRadius . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius Default: ' . $atom->StickRadiusDefault . "\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w

use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# lock the visibility of the first molecule
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Select;
$document->LockVisibility( );
$document->DeselectAll( );

my $object = $document->Atoms->Item(0);

my $visible = $object->IsVisible;
if ($visible) # Implicit check for non-zero (i.e. True) values.
{
print "Do something when the object is visible.\n";
}

my $selected = $object->IsSelected;
if ( !$selected ) # Implicit check for zero (i.e. False) values.
{
print "Do something when the object is not selected.\n";
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to create a transparent surface.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '101m.pdb' );

# Select heme atoms.
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="HEM.*"; Atom label="*"');

# Create an array of all heme atoms.
my $hemeAtoms = $document->Filter( { Selected => 1 } )->Atoms;

# Create transparent surface around the heme group.
my $transparentSurface =
$document->CreateTransparentSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential,
1.3, 0.6 );

$transparentSurface->IsBackSideColorEnabled(True);
$transparentSurface->IsBackSideTransparencyEnabled(True);

# Also create wiremesh surface around the heme group.
my $wiremeshSurface =
$document->CreateWiremeshSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential, 2.0 );

print "Surface area: "
. $transparentSurface->Area . "\n"
. "Surface Volume: "
. $transparentSurface->Volume . "\n";
print "Surface probe radius: "
. $transparentSurface->ProbeRadius . "\n"
. "Transparency Level: "
. $transparentSurface->TransparencyLevel . "\n";

# Select all atoms within 6A of the heme and the surface.
$document->SelectByRadius( 6.0, 'Atom' );
$transparentSurface->Select();

# Show only the heme and neighboring atoms (other than water).
$document->FitView();
$document->InvertSelection();
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue name="HOH.*"; Atom label="*"');
$document->Hide();
$document->DeselectAll();

# Display the wiremesh surface with delay.
sleep(2);
$wiremeshSurface->SetVisible();
```

Source type: HTML

## Item property

### Description

Item accesses an item in an array or map.

### Applies to

The Item property can be used with the following objects:

DiscoveryScript::ColorArray , DiscoveryScript::DocumentArray , DiscoveryScript::IntegerArray , DiscoveryScript::ObjectMap , DiscoveryScript::RealArray , DiscoveryScript::StringArray , Mdm::Array , Mdm::OfflineableArray , Mdm::PointArray , Protocol::Document , Protocol::ParameterMap , Sdm::Array , Sdm::AttributeMap , Sdm::ResidueArray , Sdm::SequenceArray

### Using the Item property

#### Get

my $objectObject = $object->Item( <index> );

my $objectObject = $object->Item( <key> );

my $objectObject = $object->Item( { Index => <index> } );

my $objectObject = $object->Item( { Key => <key> } );

my $stringValue = $object->Item( <key> );

my $stringValue = $object->Item( { Key => <key> } );

my $valueValue = $object->Item( <key> );

my $valueValue = $object->Item( { Key => <key> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $objectObject | | | DiscoveryScript::Object |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $valueValue | | | Value |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| <key> | Required | | String Sdm::AttributeMapKey |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript , ProtocolDiscoveryScript , SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to manipulate items in an Mdm::Array.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

my $atoms = $document->Atoms;

# Collect all cysteine atoms.
my $cysteineAtomArray = Mdm::Array::Create();
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
$cysteineAtomArray->AddItem($atom)
if ( $atom->GetProperty("Parent") =~ /CYS/i );
}

# Find the common ancestor of all atoms in the array in cysteineAtomArray.
my $parent = $cysteineAtomArray->FindCommonAncestor();
print "The common parent object of all CYS atoms: "
. $parent->ClassName . " "
. $parent->Name . "\n";

die "No cysteine atoms found! Exiting.\n" if $cysteineAtomArray->IsEmpty;

my $cysteineAtomCount = $cysteineAtomArray->Count;
print "Number of atoms in cysteine residues: " . $cysteineAtomCount . "\n";

# Delete all atoms except C-alpha and C-beta.
# Note: When deleting items from an array, the array is traversed in
# reverse order. This avoids having to account for changes in the item
# indices as the array is modified.
for ( my $i = $cysteineAtomCount - 1 ; $i >= 0 ; --$i )
{
my $atom = $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i);
if ( $atom->Name !~ /(cb|ca)\b/i )
{
$cysteineAtomArray->DeleteItem($i);
}
}
print "Number of C-alpha and C-beta atoms in cysteine residues: "
. $cysteineAtomArray->Count . "\n";

# Create a copy of the original array in reverse order.
$cysteineAtomCount = $cysteineAtomArray->Count;
my $reverseCysteineArray = Mdm::Array::Create();

# Use the AddItem function to insert the first atom.
# Note: the InsertItem function cannot be used on an empty array.
$reverseCysteineArray->AddItem( $cysteineAtomArray->Item(0) );
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $cysteineAtomCount ; ++$i )
{
$reverseCysteineArray->InsertItem( 0, $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i) );
}

# Swap the first two elements or the original array.
my $tempItem = $cysteineAtomArray->Item(0);
$cysteineAtomArray->ReplaceItem( 0, $cysteineAtomArray->Item(1) );
$cysteineAtomArray->ReplaceItem( 1, $tempItem );

# Print out the IDs of the atoms in the two arrays side by side.
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $cysteineAtomCount ; ++$i )
{
my $atom1Id = $cysteineAtomArray->Item($i)->Id;
my $atom2Id = $reverseCysteineArray->Item($i)->Id;
print "item $i\t $atom1Id\t $atom2Id\n";
}

# Remove all remaining items in the original array.
$cysteineAtomArray->ClearItems();
print "The array now has " . $cysteineAtomArray->Count . " elements\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate Mdm::Set class.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Create a set of every 4th object in the document.
my $setOfForths = Mdm::Set::Create();
my $objects = $document->Objects;
my $count = $objects->Count;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $count ; $i += 4 )
{
$setOfForths->AddItem( $objects->Item($i) );
}

my $residues = $document->Residues;
foreach my $residue (@$residues)
{
if ( $setOfForths->ItemExists($residue) )
{
print 'Residue ' . $residue->Name . " found in set.\n";
}

{
print 'Residue ' . $residue->Name . " not found in set.\n";
}
}

$document->Close();
```

# JoinFeatures function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/joinfeatures_function.htm

## JoinFeatures function

### Description

JoinFeatures combines two features on an Sdm::Sequence . To join two
features, they must have matching Key values, have distinct residues,
and be parented by the same sequence. The joined features contain
an Sdm::Location spanning the original two features.

### Applies to

The JoinFeatures function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the JoinFeatures function

#### Instance

my $featureObject = $object->JoinFeatures( <feature1>, <feature2> );

my $featureObject = $object->JoinFeatures( { Feature1 => <feature1>, Feature2 => <feature2> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $featureObject | | | Sdm::Feature |
| <feature1> | Required | | Sdm::Feature |
| <feature2> | Required | | Sdm::Feature |
| $object | | | Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence Sdm::Sequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to split and join sequence features.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId('1CRN_A');

my $sequence = $document->Sequence(0);
my $count = $sequence->FeatureCount;

my $secStrFeature;
my $i = $count;
while ( $i > 0 )
{
--$i;
my $feature = $sequence->Feature($i);
if ( $feature->Key eq "SecStr" )
{
if ( !$secStrFeature )
{
$secStrFeature = $feature;
}
else
{
$secStrFeature =
$sequence->JoinFeatures( $secStrFeature, $feature );
}
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(5);

$sequence->SplitFeature($secStrFeature);

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Publication class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'Y13252-truncated',
'TCTAGAGTAACATTTAGAATTAAGGTGGGAAATTATCTTAAAATCT' );

my $title =
'Nonfixed duplication containing the Adh gene and a truncated form '
. 'of the Adhr gene in the Drosophila funebris species group: different '
. 'modes of evolution of Adh relative to Adhr in Drosophila';

# Create publication object with sample data.
my $publication01 = Sdm::Publication::Create( 'Amador, A., Juan, E.',
$title, 'Molec. Biol. Evol.' );

# Create publication and add content separately.
my $publication02 = Sdm::Publication::Create();
$publication02->Authors = 'Amador, A., Juan, E.';
$publication02->Title = $title;
$publication02->Journal = 'Molec. Biol. Evol.';
$publication02->Reference = '16(11): 1439--1456 (1999)';
$publication02->PubMedId = '10555275';
$publication02->Comment = 'y13252';

#$publication02->Consortium = '';
#$publication02->DigitalObjectId = '';
#$publication02->MedlineId = '';
#$publication02->PubMedId = '';

# Associate publications with a sequence object.
# NOTE: To see the publications in Discovery Studio, double-click on the
# sequence in the sequence window to open a sequence annotation window.
# Publications are listed in the data table's Literature Citation tab.
$sequence->AddPublication($publication01);
$sequence->AddPublication($publication02);

my $publicationCount = $sequence->PublicationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $publicationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $publication = $sequence->Publication($index);
printf "%d: %s, %s. %s %s.\n",
$index + 1,
$publication->Authors,
$publication->Title,
$publication->Journal,
$publication->Reference;
}

$sequence->DeletePublication(0);
```

# KillTask function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/killtask_function.htm

## KillTask function

### Description

KillTask cancels a protocol task.

### Applies to

The KillTask function can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Task

### Using the KillTask function

#### Instance

$object->KillTask();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Protocol::Task |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

# LastActiveDocument property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/lastactivedocument_property.htm

## LastActiveDocument property

### Description

This function allows you to access the last active document of a particular
type. In the interface, this is the document of that type
that was most recently clicked. This function is useful for
creating scripts that run a set of commands on the current window. Any string can be
used for the model type. A null object is returned if there is no such type.
See the ModelType for a list of most commonly used model types.

Note. When run outside of Discovery Studio, this property will always return a null object.

### Applies to

The LastActiveDocument property can be used with the following objects:

DiscoveryScript

### Using the LastActiveDocument property

#### Static Get

my $documentObject = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument( [modeltype], [needsapplytowindow] );

my $documentObject = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument( { ModelType => [modeltype], needsApplyToWindow => [needsapplytowindow] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | DiscoveryScript::Document |
| [modeltype] | Optional | "" | String |
| [needsapplytowindow] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | DiscoveryScript |

#### Defined by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how connect to active documents.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.\n";
print "Please load Discovery Studio and try again.\n";
exit;
}

# Get the current active Discovery Studio document.
# NOTE: This may produce a warning if there is no scripting
# interface the active document.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::ActiveDocument();
if ($document)
{
printf "The current active document is type: %s\n", $document->ClassName;
}

# Get the last active MDM document (Molecule Window) in Discovery Studio.
my $document2 = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
if ($document2)
{
printf "I have an Mdm document, type: %s\n", $document2->ClassName;
}
```

Mdm::SpaceGroup

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use Mdm::SpaceGroup objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Get space group from document.
my $cell = $document->Cells->Item(0);
my $spacegroup = $cell->SpaceGroup;

print "The following is a list of space group properties:\n";
print "Number:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->Number . "\n";
print "Short Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->Symbol . "\n";
print "SchoenfliesSymbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->SchoenfliesSymbol . "\n";
print "Full Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->FullSymbol . "\n";
print "Lattice type:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->LatticeType . "\n";
print "Cell choice:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->CellChoice . "\n";
print "AxisOriginType:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->AxisOriginType . "\n";
print "Number of sym. operator:\t\t"
. $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount . "\n";

my $count = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $operator = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperator($index);
print "Symmetry operator $index\n";
print "\tName: " . $operator->Name . "\n";

my $rotation = $operator->Rotation;
my $format = "\t %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n";
print "\tRotation Matrix:\n";
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 0, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 1, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 2 );

my $translation = $operator->Translation;
print "\tTranslation:\n";
printf "$format", $translation->X, $translation->Y, $translation->Z;
}
```

# Launch function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/launch_function.htm

## Launch function

### Description

Launch creates and then runs a protocol for the specified document.

### Applies to

The Launch function can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Session

### Using the Launch function

#### Instance

my $taskObject = $object->Launch( <document>, [maximumfilesizefordownload], [saveintermediatefiles], [showjobcompletedialog] );

my $taskObject = $object->Launch( { Document => <document>, MaximumFileSizeForDownload => [maximumfilesizefordownload], SaveIntermediateFiles => [saveintermediatefiles], ShowJobCompleteDialog => [showjobcompletedialog] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $taskObject | | | Protocol::Task |
| <document> | Required | | Protocol::Document |
| [maximumfilesizefordownload] | Optional | 255 | Integer |
| [saveintermediatefiles] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [showjobcompletedialog] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Protocol::Session |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

# Length property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/length_property.htm

## Length property

### Description

Length is the length of a bond. When setting the bond length, and the bond
is part of a ring, only the first atom is moved. Otherwise, the fragment
connected to the second atom is moved.

### Applies to

The Length property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AcceptorFeature , Mdm::Bond , Mdm::ConformerBond , Mdm::DonorFeature , Mdm::RingAromaticFeature

### Using the Length property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->Length;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::AcceptorFeature Mdm::Bond Mdm::ConformerBond Mdm::DonorFeature Mdm::RingAromaticFeature |

#### Set

$object->Length = <length>;

$object->Length( <length> );

$object->Length( { Length => <length> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <length> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::AcceptorFeature Mdm::Bond Mdm::ConformerBond Mdm::DonorFeature Mdm::RingAromaticFeature |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

# Ligand property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/ligand_property.htm

## Ligand property

### Description

Ligand specifies the ligand molecule in docked protein poses.

### Applies to

The Ligand property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::DockedProteinPoseAssembly , Mdm::ProteinPose

### Using the Ligand property

#### Get

my $moleculeObject = $object->Ligand;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $moleculeObject | | | Mdm::Molecule |
| $object | | | Mdm::DockedProteinPoseAssembly Mdm::ProteinPose |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

Use for Mdm::DockedProteinPoseAssembly :

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Example for DockedProteinPoseAssembly Properties
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing docked protein poses\n";
print " 3 Enter a cluster ID in the Arguments tab\n";
print " 4 Run this script within Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

# This example script assumes the last active document contains Docked Protein Poses
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ($document);

# get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter
my $poseGroups = $document->DockedProteinPoseAssemblies;
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ( $poseGroups->Count > 0 );

# store the first pose group in a variable
# Note: there should be only one pose group object in a document
my $poseGroup = $poseGroups->Item(0);

# Get the receptor for the docked pose group
my $receptor = $poseGroup->Receptor;

# Copy receptor center into a point variable
my $receptorCenter = $poseGroup->ReceptorCenter;

# Print information
print "Receptor " . $receptor->Name . ",";
printf "is centered at coordinates (%5.2f,%5.2f,%5.2f)\n",
$receptorCenter->X, $receptorCenter->Y,
$receptorCenter->Z;

# Color receptor red
print "Coloring receptor red....\n\n";
$receptor->Select();
$document->SetColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 255, 0, 0 ) );

# Get the ligand for the docked pose group
my $ligand = $poseGroup->Ligand;

# Copy receptor center into a point variable
my $receptorCenter = $poseGroup->LigandCenter;
print "ligand " . $ligand->Name . ",";
printf "is centered at coordinates (%5.2f,%5.2f,%5.2f)\n",
$receptorCenter->X, $receptorCenter->Y,
$receptorCenter->Z;

# Color receptor blue
$ligand->Select();
print "Coloring ligand blue....\n\n";
$document->SetColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 0, 255 ) );

# Get the ligand for the docked pose group
my $angle = $poseGroup->StartingAngles;
printf "Starting angles used for docking: %5.2f\t%5.2f\t%5.2f\n", $angle->X,
$angle->Y, $angle->Z;
```

Use for Mdm::ProteinPose :

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use ProteinPose properties.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing docked protein poses.\n";
print " 3 Enter a cluster ID in the Arguments tab.\n";
print " 4 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
Usage('This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.')
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

# The script assume the last active document contains ProteinPoses.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage( 'This example requires an open Molecule Window containing '
. 'docked protein poses.' )
unless ($document);

# Get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter.
my $poses = $document->ProteinPoses;
Usage( 'This example requires an open Molecule Window containing '
. 'docked protein poses.' )
unless ( $poses->Count > 0 );

# Store the first pose in a variable.
my $pose1 = $poses->Item(0);

print "Properties of Pose1:\n\t";
print "Receptor: " . $pose1->Receptor->Name . "\n\t";
print "Ligand: " . $pose1->Ligand->Name . "\n\t";
my $translation = $pose1->Translation;
printf "Translation: (%5.2f,%5.2f,%5.2f)\n\t",
$translation->X,
$translation->Y,
$translation->Z;
my $rotation = $pose1->Rotation;
printf "Rotation Euler Angles: %5.2f,%5.2f,%5.2f\n", $rotation->X,
$rotation->Y, $rotation->Z;
```

Source type: HTML

## LigandFitBindingSiteFileText property

### Description

LigandFitBindingSiteFileText indicates the contents of the LigandFit binding site file.

### Applies to

The LigandFitBindingSiteFileText property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::BindingSite

### Using the LigandFitBindingSiteFileText property

#### Get

my $stringValue = $object->LigandFitBindingSiteFileText;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |

| $stringValue | | | String |

#### Defined by

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to create binding sites from ligands.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

print 'Remove water molecules. '
. "Identify and move ligand molecule out of the binding pocket...\n\n";
Delete( $document, GetWaters($document) );
my $movedLigand = MoveIntoNewMolecule( $document, GetLigands($document) );
sleep(3);

print "Change the protein display to a solid ribbon tube...\n\n";
TurnOffProteinAtoms($document);
ApplyProteinDisplayStyle( $document, Mdm::styleProteinRibbonTube );
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms();
sleep(3);

print "Create binding sites from the ligand molecule...\n\n";
my $receptor = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $ReceptorHeavyAtomRadius = 2.5;
my $ReceptorHydrogenRadius = 2.0;
my $LigandHeavyAtomRadius = 2.5;
my $LigandHydrogenRadius = 2.0;
my $GridResolution = 0.4;
my $SiteOpening = 10.0;
my $MinimumSitePointCount = 100;
$document->CreateBindingSitesFromLigand(
$receptor, $movedLigand,
$ReceptorHeavyAtomRadius, $ReceptorHydrogenRadius,
$LigandHeavyAtomRadius, $LigandHydrogenRadius,
$GridResolution, $SiteOpening,
$MinimumSitePointCount
);
sleep(3);

my $site = $document->BindingSites->Item(0);
my $volume = $site->GetProperty('Volume');
print "Volume of principle binding site: $volume\n\n";

my $fileName = 'LigandFitSite.txt';
print "Saving LigandFit binding site data to file $fileName...\n\n";
my $ligandFitSiteFileText = $site->LigandFitBindingSiteFileText();
open FH, "> $fileName" or die "Cannot open $fileName: $!";
print FH $ligandFitSiteFileText;
close FH;
```

## LigandInFocus property

### Description

LigandInFocus specifies the Mdm::Group or Mdm::Molecule identifying the

set to an Mdm::Molecule or an Mdm::Group object.

### Applies to

The LigandInFocus property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the LigandInFocus property

#### Get

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |

#### Set

my $booleanValue = $object->LigandInFocus = <ligandobject>;

my $booleanValue = $object->LigandInFocus( <ligandobject> );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the create a ligand non-bond monitor, 
# browse ligands and show supporting non-bond interactions. 

use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('2FL6');
die "Failed to create a valid MDM document!" unless $document;

my $receptor = $document->ReceptorInFocus;
die "The open document does not have a defined receptor!" unless $receptor;

$document->FocusOnFirstLigand;
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
die "The open document does not have a defined ligand!" unless $ligand;

my $ligandNonbondMonitor =
$document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();
$document->UpdateViews();

my $nonbondMonitors = $document->NonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d NonbondMonitors.\n", $nonbondMonitors->Count;
my $ligandNonbondMonitors = $document->LigandNonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d LigandNonbondMonitors.\n", $ligandNonbondMonitors->Count;

# Step through the ligands
while ($document->FocusOnNextLigand())
{
sleep(2);
}

# Step through the ligands backwards
$document->FocusOnLastLigand();
while ($document->FocusOnPreviousLigand())
{
sleep(2);
}

# Expand shell to progressively view supporting interactions.
$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

# Contract shell to hide supporting interactions.
$ligandNonbondMonitor->ContractShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

print "Done\n";
```

### Using the LigandNonbondMonitors filter

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->LigandNonbondMonitors;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the ligand non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );
die "Failed to create a valid MDM document!" unless $document;

print "To create a ligand interaction monitor, first ensure the ligand ";
print "is defined. \n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand;
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
die "Failed to identify a ligand! Try setting the ligand manually\n" .
"using the LigandInFocus property." unless $ligand;
printf "Ligand: %s\n\n", $ligand->Name;

my $monitor = $document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();
die "The ligand and or receptor is not undefined!" unless $monitor;
$document->UpdateViews();

my $monitors = $document->LigandNonbondMonitors();
printf "Document contains %d LigandNonbondMonitors.\n", $monitors->Count;

# Ligand non-bond monitors are also NonbondMonitor.
$monitors = $document->NonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d NonbondMonitors.\n", $monitors->Count;
print "\n";

# Analyze the identified interactions.
my $nonbonds = $monitor->Nonbonds;
my $count = $nonbonds->Count;
my $favorableNonbonds = $monitor->FavorableNonbonds;
my $favorableCount = $favorableNonbonds->Count;
my $unfavorableCount = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds->Count;
printf "Found %d non-bond interactions (total):\n", $count;
printf " %d of these are favorable interactions (such as H-bonds)\n",
$favorableCount;
printf " %d of these are unfavorable interactions (such as bumps).\n",
$unfavorableCount;
print "\n";

print "Analyze first non-bond interaction:\n";
my $nonbond = $nonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n",
$nonbond->Distance;
print "\n";

my $unfavorableNonbonds = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds;
if ($unfavorableNonbonds->Count > 0) 
{
print "Analyze first unfavorable non-bond interaction:\n";
my $unfavorableNonbond = $unfavorableNonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $unfavorableNonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $unfavorableNonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n",
$unfavorableNonbond->Distance;
print "\n";
}

print "All non-bonds of a particular type can be retrieved ";
print "using the NonbondsOfType filter.\n";
my $hBonds = $monitor->NonbondsOfType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType);
printf "Found %d hydrogen bonds using NonbondOfType filter.\n\n", $hBonds->Count;

print "Alternatively the IsMatchingNonbondType property can be used to \n";
print "identify interactions of a various type. The following atom pairs \n";
print "indicate classical hydrogen bonding: \n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
if ($nonbond->IsMatchingNonbondType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType))
{
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);

print '* ' . $atom1->FullName . " (";
print 'donor ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrogenDonor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHalogen);
print 'positive ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPositive);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ') and ';

print $atom2->FullName . " (";
print 'acceptor ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrogenAcceptor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHalogen);
print 'negative ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsNegative);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ")\n";
}
}
print "\n";

print "The NonbondTypes property can be used to identify all \n";
print "interaction types of a non-bond.\n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
printf "- %s (%s) and %s (%s):", 
$nonbond->FromSite->Name,
$nonbond->FromSite->ChemistryName,
$nonbond->ToSite->Name,
$nonbond->ToSite->ChemistryName;

my $nonbondTypes = $nonbond->NonbondTypes;
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
print " $type";
}

print "\n";
}
print "\n";

print "The properties NonbondCriterion and DefaultNonbondCriterion are \n";
print "access the parameters used to identify non-bonds (see the \n";
print "documentation for full description of criteria):\n";
my $allCriteria = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllNonbondCriterionTypes();
foreach my $criterionType (@$allCriteria)
{
printf "Mdm::%s:\t %6.2f (default: %6.2f) \n",
$criterionType,
$monitor->NonbondCriterion($criterionType),
$monitor->DefaultNonbondCriterion($criterionType);
}
print "\n";

# Changing an interaction criterion.
my $maxHBond = 1.0 + $monitor->NonbondCriterion(
Mdm::hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum);
printf "After increasing the classical hydrogen bond distance to %f A, \n",
$maxHBond;
$monitor->NonbondCriterion(
Mdm::hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum) = $maxHBond;
$document->UpdateObjects;
printf "the number of non-bond interactions increases to %d.\n",
$monitor->Nonbonds->Count;
print "\n";

print "Changes made to the non-bond criteria can be reset " .
"to the original defaults using ResetNonbondCriteria.\n";
$monitor->ResetNonbondCriteria();
print "\n";

print "The visibility of various non-bond types can be shown or hidden.\n";
print "This code demonstrates how to show only non-bond identifying \n";
print "classical hydrogen bond interactions with distance labels.\n";
$monitor->HideAllNonbonds();
$monitor->IsNonbondTypeShown(Mdm::conventionalHBondType) = True;
$monitor->IsLabelShown = True;
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

print "The default settings are to show all non-bond interactions \n";
print "(without distance labels). This is accomplished as follows.\n";
$monitor->ShowAllNonbonds({ ShowDistanceLabels=>False });
$document->UpdateViews();
print "\n";

print "The static AllNonbondTypes function can be loop through all";
print "the non-bond interaction types.\n";
my $allNonbondTypes = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllNonbondTypes();
foreach my $type (@$allNonbondTypes) {
printf "- %s \n", $type;
}
print "\n";

print "The static AllFavorableNonbondTypes function can be loop\n";
print "favorable non-bond interaction types.\n";
my $nonbondTypes = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllFavorableNonbondTypes();
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
printf "- %s \n", $type;
}
print "\n";

print "The static AllFavorableNonbondTypes function can be loop\n";
print "unfavorable non-bond interaction types.\n";
my $nonbondTypes = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllUnfavorableNonbondTypes();
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
printf "- %s \n", $type;
}
print "\n";
```

# LigateNucleotides function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/ligatenucleotides_function.htm

## LigateNucleotides function

### Description

LigateNucleotides ligates (bonds) two nucleic acid molecules. Specify
a 3' nucleotide and 5' nucleotide from either the sense or antisense strands
of two nucleic acids to ligate the corresponding molecules.

### Applies to

The LigateNucleotides function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the LigateNucleotides function

#### Instance

$object->LigateNucleotides( <nucleotide3prime>, <nucleotide5prime> );

$object->LigateNucleotides( { Nucleotide3Prime => <nucleotide3prime>, Nucleotide5Prime => <nucleotide5prime> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <nucleotide3prime> | Required | | Mdm::Nucleotide |
| <nucleotide5prime> | Required | | Mdm::Nucleotide |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to build nucleic acids.
use strict;
use NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create and append to a DNA duplex molecule.
my $naType = Mdm::dnaDuplex;
my $nucleicAcidMolecule =
$document->CreateNucleicAcid( "CGT", $naType, Mdm::aHelix );
my $senseChain1 = $nucleicAcidMolecule->Chains->Item(0);
my $na3Prime = $senseChain1->NucleotideAt3PrimeTerminus;
$na3Prime = $document->GrowNucleicAcid( $na3Prime, "GGG", Mdm::aHelix );

printf "Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$document->ModelName,
$document->Atoms->Count();

# Create and prepend to a second DNA duplex molecule.
my $nucleicAcid2 =
$document->CreateNucleicAcid( "ACT", $naType, Mdm::aHelix );
my $senseChain2 = $nucleicAcid2->Chains->Item(0);
my $na5Prime = $senseChain2->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus;
$na5Prime = $document->GrowNucleicAcid( $na5Prime, "AAA", Mdm::aHelix );

my $secondMoleculeName = "Nucleic Acid 2";
$nucleicAcid2->Name = $secondMoleculeName;

# Ligate the two molecules using the sense strand.
$document->DeselectAll();
$na3Prime->Select;
$na5Prime->Select;
$document->LigateNucleotides( $na3Prime, $na5Prime );

# Mutate first sense nucleotide to thymidine.
$document->DeselectAll();
$senseChain1->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus->Select;
$document->MutateNucleotide( $senseChain1->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus,
Mdm::thymidine );

# Change the nucleic acid display style.
$senseChain1->DisplayStyle = Mdm::styleDnaArrowLadder;
$nucleicAcidMolecule->Chains->Item(1)->DisplayStyle =
Mdm::styleDnaArrowLadder;

printf "Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$document->ModelName,
$document->Atoms->Count();
```

Source type: HTML

## LineWidth property

### Description

LineWidth is the width of displayed lines in a Molecule Window.

### Applies to

The LineWidth property can be used with the following objects:

### Using the LineWidth property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->LineWidth;

##### Parameters

#### Set

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <width> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document Mdm::Isosurface |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
print "It operates on a document with grid data\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a structure with grid data\n";
print
" (for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
print " 3 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Connect to an Sdm::Document from the last active sequence window
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

# Get array with all isosurfaces using Isosurfaces filter
my $isosurfaces = $document->Isosurfaces;

if ( $isosurfaces->Count == 0 )
{
print "To run this script, please open a structure with grid data.\n";
print "(for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
exit;
}

# Get the first isosurface
my $isosurface = $isosurfaces->[0];

# Create a new isosurface at 0.5 isovalue
my $newContour = $isosurface->CreateIsosurface(0.5);
$newContour->ContextAtomArray( $document->Atoms );

if ( !$newContour->IsContextAtomArrayDefined() )
{
print "Please define a context atom array\n";
}
$newContour->IsNormalFlipped(False);
$newContour->IsBoundaryDrawn(True);
print "The line width is: $newContour->{LineWidth}\n";

# Print the isovalues
$isosurfaces = $document->Isosurfaces;
foreach my $surface (@$isosurfaces)
{
print $surface->Name . " has isovalue " . $surface->Isovalue . "\n";
}

# Array with available display styles
my @displayStyles = (
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleNone, Mdm::isosurfaceStyleQuadMesh,
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleSolid, Mdm::isosurfaceStyleTriMesh,
Mdm::isosurfaceStyleVolume
);

# Iterate over the available display styles
print "\nIterating over isosurface display styles:\n";
foreach my $displayStyle (@displayStyles)
{
sleep(1);
$newContour->DisplayStyle = $displayStyle;
print "$displayStyle\n";
$document->UpdateViews();
}

$newContour->RemoveContextAtomArray();
```

# LinkedMdmResidues filter

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/linkedmdmresidues_filter.htm

## LinkedMdmResidues filter

### Description

LinkedMdmResidues returns the Mdm::Residue objects
that are linked to an Sdm::Sequence object. In general,
only a subset of the Mdm::Residue s in an Mdm::Molecule are mapped to the linked Sdm::Sequence .
This method returns only the linked subset.

### Applies to

The LinkedMdmResidues filter can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the LinkedMdmResidues filter

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->LinkedMdmResidues;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence Sdm::Sequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script will illustrate the use of LinkedMdmResidues filter.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdm = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3CRO');
my $sdm = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures($mdm, False);

my $sequence = $sdm->Sequences->Item(0);
my $linkedMdmResidues = $sequence->LinkedMdmResidues;

print 'Found ' . $linkedMdmResidues->Count 
. ' linked Mdm::Residues matching ' . $sequence->Residues->Count
. " Sdm::Residues.\n";
foreach my $residue (@$linkedMdmResidues)
{
print $residue->Name . "\n";
}
```

# LinkedSdmDocument function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/linkedsdmdocument_function.htm

## LinkedSdmDocument function

### Description

LinkedSdmDocument retrieves the Sdm::Document object linked to the specified Mdm::Document object. By default, the linked protein sequence document is returned.
To retrieve the linked nucleic acid sequence document, set the parameter Dna to "true".

### Applies to

The LinkedSdmDocument function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the LinkedSdmDocument function

#### Static

my $documentObject = Sdm::Document::LinkedSdmDocument( <mdmdocument>, [dna] );

my $documentObject = Sdm::Document::LinkedSdmDocument( { MdmDocument => <mdmdocument>, Dna => [dna] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | Sdm::Document |
| <mdmdocument> | Required | | Mdm::Document |
| [dna] | Optional | False | Boolean |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to get a linked SDM document from an
# MDM document.
# NOTE: Sequence-Structure linking is only supported on the client.
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

# Get the active Molecule Window or load 1crn.
my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
if (!$mdmDocument) 
{
$mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $tmp = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures($mdmDocument);
}

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::LinkedSdmDocument(
{ MdmDocument => $mdmDocument, Dna => 0});
die "MDM Document is not linked to a protein sequence document" unless $sdmDocument;

print "Found linked SDM Document.\n";
my $sequences = $sdmDocument->Sequences();
my $i = 0;
foreach my $sequence (@$sequences)
{
++$i;
print "Sequence $i: " . $sequence->Name . "\n";
}
```

# LinkedSequence property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/linkedsequence_property.htm

## LinkedSequence property

### Description

Linked sequence finds the sequence linked to a molecule. Note that
linking is only available in the Discovery Studio client.

### Applies to

The LinkedSequence property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the LinkedSequence property

#### Get

my $sequenceObject = $object->LinkedSequence( <molecule> );

my $sequenceObject = $object->LinkedSequence( { Molecule => <molecule> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $sequenceObject | | | Sdm::Sequence |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| $object | | | Sdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate accessing linked sequences and sequence indices.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

my $sdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(SdmAlignmentModelType);
my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

print "This example requires an open active Sequence Window with sequences "
. "linked to molecules in the last active Molecule Window."
unless ( $sdmDocument && $mdmDocument );

my $molecules = $mdmDocument->Molecules;

my $superposeMolecules = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $alignmentStrings = $sdmDocument->Alignment->AlignmentStrings;
my $alignment = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();

foreach my $molecule (@$molecules)
{
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->LinkedSequence($molecule);
if ($sequence)
{
print $sequence->Name . "\n";
$superposeMolecules->AddItem($molecule);
my $index = $sdmDocument->Alignment->SequenceIndex($sequence);
my $sequenceString = $alignmentStrings->[$index];
$alignment->AddItem($sequenceString);
}
}

my $r =
$mdmDocument->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment( $superposeMolecules,
$alignment, Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingBackboneAtoms );
```

# LinkMdmDocument function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/linkmdmdocument_function.htm

## LinkMdmDocument function

### Description

LinkMdmDocument links matching Mdm::Molecule objects in the
specified Mdm::Document to Sdm::Sequence objects
in the Sdm::Document . To match, the molecule's sequence and
name must match one of the Sdm::Sequence objects.
Documents can only be linked to one other document (MDM to SDM or SDM to MDM).
If two are documents linked, and you link one of them to another document, the original link will be broken (delinked).

### Applies to

The LinkMdmDocument function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the LinkMdmDocument function

#### Instance

$object->LinkMdmDocument( <mdmdocument> );

$object->LinkMdmDocument( { MdmDocument => <mdmdocument> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <mdmdocument> | Required | | Mdm::Document |
| $object | | | Sdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to link/delink SDM and MDM documents.
# NOTE: Sequence-Structure linking is only supported on the client.
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Create 1crn sequence manually so prevent auto-linking of documents.
# To link, the residue order, object names and chain breaks must match.
my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0);
$sequence->InsetAbbreviations( 0,
'ThrThrCysCysProSerIleValAlaArgSerAsnPheAsnValCysArgLeuProGlyThrProGlu'
. 'AlaIleCysAlaThrTyrThrGlyCysIleIleIleProGlyAlaThrCysProGlyAspTyrAlaAsn'
);
$sequence->Name = '1crn';

# Link documents (this will break any existing linked documents)
# and any match sequence-molecules.
# Note the sequence name shows the molecule icon indicating it is linked.
$sdmDocument->LinkMdmDocument($mdmDocument);

print 'Is sequence linked: ' . $sequence->IsLinked . "\n";

# Break document link.
# Uncomment to break the SDM-MDM document link.
#$sdmDocument->DelinkMdmDocument();
```

# LinkSequenceStructure function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/linksequencestructure_function.htm

## LinkSequenceStructure function

### Description

LinkSequenceStructure establishes a link between an Sdm::Sequence and
an Mdm::Molecule . The residue sequence in both objects must match.

Note. This function has no effect when run outside of Discovery Studio.

### Applies to

The LinkSequenceStructure function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the LinkSequenceStructure function

#### Instance

my $booleanValue = $object->LinkSequenceStructure( <sequence>, <molecule> );

my $booleanValue = $object->LinkSequenceStructure( { Sequence => <sequence>, Molecule => <molecule> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| <sequence> | Required | | Sdm::Sequence |
| $object | | | Sdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate linking a sequence to a structure.
# NOTE: Sequences and structures can only be linked in the DS client.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId('1CRN_A');
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0);

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0);

# Link the 1crn sequence and molecule.
$sdmDocument->LinkSequenceStructure( $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0),
$mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0) );
print "The sequence and molecule are now linked.\n";

# Selecting (and deselecting) the molecule also selects the sequence
# after updating the view. Here the update views call is required
# not only to display the sequence selection, but to synchronize the
# data models.
$molecule->Select();
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();
print 'After selecting the molecule and updating the SDM document view, '
. "the sequence is also selected.\n"
if ( $sequence->IsSelected() );

# Selecting (and deselecting) from the sequence does not
# require an update views call to synchronize the data models.
# The call is requires to display the updated sequence
# selection.
$sequence->Deselect( 0, 10 );
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();

# Break the sequence and molecule link.
$sdmDocument->BreakSequenceStructureLink( $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0) );
print "The sequence-molecule link is now broken.\n";

$sequence->Select( 0, 5 );
print "The first 5 residues in sequence are selected.\n"
if ( $sdmDocument->Alignment->IsSelected( 0, 0, 5 ) );

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();
print "The first 5 residues in sequence are selected.\n"
if ( $sdmDocument->Alignment->IsSelected( 0, 0, 5 ) );
```

# LipinskiViolationCount property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/lipinskiviolationcount_property.htm

## LipinskiViolationCount property

### Description

LipinskiViolationCount indicates the number of Lipinski violations
in a molecule. The Lipinski rule contains a set of simple rules to select compounds with drug-like properties: (1) The molecular weight is nor more than 500; (2) The AlogP is no more than 5; (3) The number of hydrogen bond donors is no more than 5; (4) The number of hydrogen bond acceptors is no more than 10.

### Applies to

The LipinskiViolationCount property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the LipinskiViolationCount property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->LipinskiViolationCount;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This scripts illustrates how to access several properties of
# the Mdm::Molecule object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

$molecule->IsChargeCalculated = True;

print "The following is a list of molecule properties:\n";
print 'Name: ' . $molecule->Name . "\n";
print 'Approximate volume: ' . $molecule->ApproximateVolume . "\n";
print 'Atom count: ' . $molecule->AtomCount . "\n";

my $centerOfMass = $molecule->CenterOfMass;
printf "Center of mass: %8.3f\t%8.3f\t%8.3f\n",
$centerOfMass->X,
$centerOfMass->Y,
$centerOfMass->Z;

print 'Chiral center count: ' . $molecule->ChiralCenterCount . "\n";
print 'Composition: ' . $molecule->Composition . "\n";
print 'Density: ' . $molecule->Density . "\n";
print 'Exact molecular weight: ' . $molecule->ExactMolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen bond acceptor count: '
. $molecule->HydrogenBondAcceptorCount . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen bond donor count: '
. $molecule->HydrogenBondDonorCount . "\n";
print 'Lipinski violation count: ' . $molecule->LipinskiViolationCount . "\n";
print 'Molecular formula: ' . $molecule->MolecularFormula . "\n";
print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Radius of gyration: ' . $molecule->RadiusOfGyration . "\n";
print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Rotatable bond count: ' . $molecule->RotatableBondCount . "\n";
print 'Surface area: ' . $molecule->SurfaceArea . "\n";
```

# Load function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/load_function.htm

## Load function

### Description

Load loads an embedded forcefield from a typed molecule into a Ffdm::Document .

### Applies to

The Load function can be used with the following objects:

Ffdm::Document

### Using the Load function

#### Static

my $documentObject = Ffdm::Document::Load( <mdmdocument>, [nodisplay] );

my $documentObject = Ffdm::Document::Load( { MdmDocument => <mdmdocument>, NoDisplay => [nodisplay] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | Ffdm::Document |
| <mdmdocument> | Required | | Mdm::Document |
| [nodisplay] | Optional | False | Boolean |

#### Defined by

ForceFieldDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use the Load/CreateSimFiles functions to create simulation files
# from a typed molecule.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ForceFieldDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';
my $outputFolder = DiscoveryScript::GetTemporaryFolder()."/typing";

my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . 'Bacteriorhodopsin Trajectory.dsv';
my $document = DiscoveryScript::Open($inputFile);
printf "Loading embedded forcefield from a typed molecule %s\n" , $document->ModelName;
my $forcefield = Ffdm::Document::Load($document);
if ($forcefield)
{
printf "Creating simulation files\n"; 
$forcefield->CreateSimulationFiles( $document, $outputFolder );
}
$document->Close();

# list all files in the output directory
opendir my $dh, $outputFolder or die "Could not open '$outputFolder' for reading '$!'\n";
my @files = grep {$_ ne '.' and $_ ne '..'} readdir $dh;
closedir $dh;

my $count = 0;
foreach my $file (sort @files) {
printf "%d) %s\n", ++$count, $file;
}
```

# LocalizeBonds function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/localizebonds_function.htm

## LocalizeBonds function

### Description

Partial bonds are converted to single and double bonds, and partial formal
charges are localized to full charges.

### Applies to

The LocalizeBonds function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the LocalizeBonds function

#### Instance

$object->LocalizeBonds();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to perceive aromatic bonds.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Subroutine to print bond orders and formal charges.
sub ListBondOrderAndCharge($$)
{
my ( $document, $bonds ) = @_;

my $index = 0;
foreach my $b (@$bonds)
{
my $charge1 =
$b->Atom1->FormalCharge->Numerator /
$b->Atom1->FormalCharge->Denominator;
my $charge2 =
$b->Atom2->FormalCharge->Numerator /
$b->Atom2->FormalCharge->Denominator;
print ++$index
. ') Bond: '
. $b->Atom1->Name . "("
. $charge2 . ") to:"
. $b->Atom2->Name . " ("
. $charge2 . ")"
. " order: "
. $b->BondOrder . "\n";
}
print "\n";
sleep(3);
$document->UpdateViews();
}

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1C(=O)[O-]');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $bonds = $molecule->Bonds;
my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms;
print "Initial formal charges and bonds orders:\n";
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );

print "Modified formal charges and bonds orders...\n";
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( $atom->Element eq 'O' )
{
$atom->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 2 );
my $carbon = $atom->AttachedAtom(0);
my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $carbon, $atom );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::partialDoubleBond;
}
}
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );

print "Localizing bond orders and formal charges...\n\n";
$molecule->LocalizeBonds();
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );

print "De-localizing bond orders and formal charges...\n\n";
$molecule->PerceiveAromaticBonds();
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );
```

# Location property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/location_property.htm

## Location property

### Description

Location specifies the residues associated with an Sdm::Feature object.

### Applies to

The Location property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Feature

### Using the Location property

#### Get

my $locationObject = $object->Location;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $locationObject | | | Sdm::Location |
| $object | | | Sdm::Feature |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script will illustrate functions and properties of the
# Sdm::Feature class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASDFGHJKL' );

# Create a join feature for residues DFGH and add it the sequence.
my $segmentStart = 2;
my $segmentCount = 4;
my $feature = $sequence->CreateCustomSequenceFeature( 'Custom feature',
Sdm::locationTypeJoin, $segmentStart, $segmentCount );
$feature->AddQualifier("InfoKey", 'Example feature');

$sequence->AddFeature($feature);

my $count = $sequence->FeatureCount;
print "Sequence has $count features\n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $feature = $sequence->Feature($index);
my $location = $feature->Location;

print "Feature $index properties\n";
print "\tComment\t" . $feature->Comment . "\n";
print "\tKey\t" . $feature->Key . "\n";
print "\tShape\t" . $feature->Shape . "\n";
print "\tShape fill style\t" . $feature->ShapeFillStyle . "\n";
my $color = $feature->FillColor;
print "\tFill color\t("
. $color->Red . ' '
. $color->Green . ' '
. $color->Blue . ")\n";
$color = $feature->OutlineColor;
print "\tOutline color\t("
. $color->Red . ' '
. $color->Green . ' '
. $color->Blue . ")\n";
print "\t" . "Label\t" . $feature->LabelText . "\n";
$color = $feature->LabelColor;
print "\t"
. "Label color\t("
. $color->Red . ' '
. $color->Green . ' '
. $color->Blue . ")\n";
print "\t" . "Label type\t" . $feature->LabelFromType . "\n";
print "\t" . "Is label visible\t" . $feature->IsLabelVisible . "\n";
print "\t" . "Is label horizontal\t" . $feature->IsLabelHorizontal . "\n";
print "\t" . "Feature Location type\t" . $location->Type . "\n";
}
```

# LocationSphereRadius property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/locationsphereradius_property.htm

## LocationSphereRadius property

### Description

LocationSphereRadius gets the radius of the location sphere
appropriate for the 3D point feature the location feature is
associated with. The radius is specified in angstroms.

### Applies to

The LocationSphereRadius property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::PointFeature

### Using the LocationSphereRadius property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->LocationSphereRadius;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::PointFeature |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create some features on the query
# Create a donor feature at 0,0,0
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create an acceptor feature at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

# create the location constraint. The $fitOperator and the parent operator of $acceptorOperator are the same in this case.
# Either can be used to create the location constraint.
my $locationfeatureHead =
$acceptorOperator->GetParentOperator()
->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Check to see if a proper query has been made and print out some information
if ( $fitOperator->HasChildOperators() )
{
print "Query successfully made, fit operator has child operators.\n";
my $headPoint = $newAcceptor->HeadXYZ;
my $tailPoint = $newAcceptor->TailXYZ;
printf "Head : %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n", $headPoint->X, $headPoint->Y,
$headPoint->Z;
printf "Tail : %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n", $tailPoint->X, $tailPoint->Y,
$tailPoint->Z;
print "Radius of location constraint on tail "
. $newAcceptor->TailFeature()->LocationSphereRadius . "\n";
}
$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```
