# LockVisibility function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/lockvisibility_function.htm

## LockVisibility function

### Description

LockVisibility locks the selected objects visible state.
Once the visible state is locked, hidden objects remain hidden and
visible objects remain visible until the visible state is unlocked.

### Applies to

The LockVisibility function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the LockVisibility function

#### Command

$object->LockVisibility( [unlock] );

$object->LockVisibility( { Unlock => [unlock] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [unlock] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the IsVisible and IsSelected properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# lock the visibility of the first molecule
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Select;
$document->LockVisibility( );
$document->DeselectAll( );

my $object = $document->Atoms->Item(0);

my $visible = $object->IsVisible;
if ($visible) # Implicit check for non-zero (i.e. True) values.
{
print "Do something when the object is visible.\n";
}

my $selected = $object->IsSelected;
if ( !$selected ) # Implicit check for zero (i.e. False) values.
{
print "Do something when the object is not selected.\n";
}
```

# LogMessages property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/logmessages_property.htm

## LogMessages property

### Description

LogMessages contains all the client messages produced by the protocol
during a protocol run.

### Applies to

The LogMessages property can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Task

### Using the LogMessages property

#### Get

my $stringarrayObject = $object->LogMessages;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::StringArray |
| $object | | | Protocol::Task |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

## LongName property

LongName specifies the common residue name.

### Applies to

Mdm::AminoAcid , Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::Nucleotide , Mdm::Residue

### Using the LongName property

#### Get

my $stringValue = $object->LongName;

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid Mdm::NucleicAcid Mdm::Nucleotide Mdm::Residue |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to access several residue properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1CRN.pdb' );

my $cysteineCount = 0;
my $alanineCount = 0;
my $sequence = "";

my $residues = $document->Residues;
foreach my $residue (@$residues)
{
print 'Residue Name: ' . $residue->Name . "\n\t";
print 'ID: ' . $residue->Id . "\n\t";
print 'PDB: ' . $residue->PDBName . "\n\t";
print 'SymbolandId: ' . $residue->SymbolAndId . "\n\t";
print 'Hydrophobicity: ' . $residue->Hydrophobicity . "\n\t";
print 'pKa: ' . $residue->pKa . "\n";

# Create the one-letter sequence from the symbol.
$sequence = $sequence . $residue->Symbol;

++$cysteineCount if ( $residue->Type eq Mdm::cys );
++$alanineCount if ( $residue->LongName eq 'Alanine' );
}

printf "Number of cysteine residues: %d \n", $cysteineCount;
printf "Number of alanine residues: %d \n", $alanineCount;
printf "Protein sequence is: %s\n", $sequence;
```

# MakeActive function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/makeactive_function.htm

## MakeActive function

### Description

MakeActive makes a conformation the active conformation.

### Applies to

The MakeActive function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Conformation , Mdm::OfflineableConformation

### Using the MakeActive function

#### Instance

$object->MakeActive();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Conformation Mdm::OfflineableConformation |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Create a few conformations by rotating the phi torsion
# angle of the first amino acid residue.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Get first three amino acids
my $aminoAcid1 = $aminoAcids->Item(0);
my $aminoAcid2 = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
my $aminoAcid3 = $aminoAcids->Item(2);

# Creates a monitor for the phi angle
my $phiTorsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$aminoAcid1->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid2->AmideNitrogen,
$aminoAcid2->CAlpha, $aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon
);

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index <= 6 ; ++$index )
{
my $torsionValue = $index * 60.0;

# rotates the first residue's phi angle
$phiTorsion->SetProperty( "Angle", "$torsionValue" );

# creates a new conformation
my $conformation = $molecule->CreateConformation();
$conformation->MakeActive();

# sets the current conformation to be invisible
# so the next newly created conformation will be "active" and updated with new coordinates
$conformation->SetInvisible(True);
}
my $activeConformation = $aminoAcid1->FindActiveConformation();

# creates an animation using the newly created conformations
my $animation = $document->CreateAnimation( $molecule->Conformations );
my $frameCount = $animation->FrameCount;
print "Number of animation frames: $frameCount frames\n";

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $frameCount ; $i++ )
{
printf " Frame: %d\n", $i + 1; 
$animation->ActivateNextFrame();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(1);
}
```

# MakeCTerminus function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/makecterminus_function.htm

## MakeCTerminus function

### Description

MakeCTerminus changes an amino acid into a C-terminal residue, in either
charged or uncharged state.

### Applies to

The MakeCTerminus function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid

### Using the MakeCTerminus function

#### Instance

my $booleanValue = $object->MakeCTerminus( [charged] );

my $booleanValue = $object->MakeCTerminus( { Charged => [charged] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| [charged] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This example shows how to alter the characteristics of protein termini.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Subroutine to print atoms in N terminal residue.
sub PrintNTerminus($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $chains = $document->AminoAcidChains;
my $nTerminus = $chains->Item(0)->NTerminus();
my $atoms = $nTerminus->Atoms;
my $atomCount = $atoms->Count;
printf "Number of atoms in N terminal residue %s : %d\n",
$nTerminus->Name(), $atomCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atomCount ; ++$index )
{
my $atom = $atoms->Item($index);
printf
" Name : %s Formal charge %d/%d\n",
$atom->Name(),
$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,
$atom->FormalCharge->Denominator;
}
}

# Subroutine to print atoms in C terminal residue.
sub PrintCTerminus($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $chains = $document->AminoAcidChains;
my $nTerminus = $chains->Item(0)->CTerminus();
my $atoms = $nTerminus->Atoms;
my $atomCount = $atoms->Count;
printf "Number of atoms in C terminal residue %s : %d\n",
$nTerminus->Name(), $atomCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atomCount ; ++$index )
{
my $atom = $atoms->Item($index);
printf
" Name : %s Formal charge %d/%d\n",
$atom->Name(),
$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,
$atom->FormalCharge->Denominator;
}
}

# Subroutine to print atoms in N and C terminal residues.
sub PrintTermini($$)
{
my ( $document, $title ) = @_;
printf "\n%s :\n", $title;
PrintNTerminus($document);
PrintCTerminus($document);
}

# Load molecule from PDB.
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Mutate the termini to alanine. With the side chain removed,
# the atom listing will be clearer.
my $chain = $document->AminoAcidChains->Item(0);
my $nTerminus = $chain->NTerminus();
my $cTerminus = $chain->CTerminus();

$document->MutateAminoAcid( $nTerminus, Mdm::ala );
$document->MutateAminoAcid( $cTerminus, Mdm::ala );
$document->DeselectAll();

# Uncomment this line to add hydrogen atoms.
# AddHydrogens($document);

# List atoms in current configuration.
PrintTermini( $document, "At start" );

# Remove terminal residue characteristics and list atoms.
$chain->RemoveNTerminusCap();
$chain->RemoveCTerminusCap();
PrintTermini( $document, "After removing caps" );

# Make termini normal (i.e. charged) and list atoms.
$nTerminus->MakeNTerminus(True);
$cTerminus->MakeCTerminus(True);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making charged termini" );

# Make termini uncharged and list atoms.
$nTerminus->MakeNTerminus(False);
$cTerminus->MakeCTerminus(False);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making neutral termini" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 1.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(1.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(1.0);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 1.0" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 7.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(7.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(7.0);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 7.0" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 13.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(13.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(130);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 13.0" );

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# MakeNTerminus function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/makenterminus_function.htm

## MakeNTerminus function

### Description

MakeNTerminus changes an amino acid into an N-terminus acid. It requires that the N atom exists and has no
connections other than to CA. If the input parameter is true, the N will receive a +1 formal
charge. Otherwise, the N will have zero formal charge. If there are hydrogens attached, they are removed.

### Applies to

The MakeNTerminus function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid

### Using the MakeNTerminus function

#### Instance

my $booleanValue = $object->MakeNTerminus( [charged] );

my $booleanValue = $object->MakeNTerminus( { Charged => [charged] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| [charged] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text

{
my ($document) = @_;

my $atoms = $nTerminus->Atoms;

printf

$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,

}
}

{

printf "Number of atoms in C terminal residue %s : %d\n",

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atomCount ; ++$index )

my $atom = $atoms->Item($index);
printf
" Name : %s Formal charge %d/%d\n",
$atom->Name(),
$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,

}

sub PrintTermini($$)
{
```

# MakeNTerminusAtpH function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/makenterminusatph_function.htm

## MakeNTerminusAtpH function

### Description

MakeNTerminusAtpH changes a residue into an N-terminal residue charged appropriately for the specified pH value.

### Applies to

The MakeNTerminusAtpH function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcidChain

### Using the MakeNTerminusAtpH function

#### Instance

my $aminoacidObject = $object->MakeNTerminusAtpH( [ph], [usepredictedpk] );

my $aminoacidObject = $object->MakeNTerminusAtpH( { pH => [ph], UsePredictedpK => [usepredictedpk] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $aminoacidObject | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |
| [ph] | Optional | 7.0 | Real |
| [usepredictedpk] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcidChain |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This example shows how to alter the characteristics of protein termini.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Subroutine to print atoms in N terminal residue.
sub PrintNTerminus($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $chains = $document->AminoAcidChains;
my $nTerminus = $chains->Item(0)->NTerminus();
my $atoms = $nTerminus->Atoms;
my $atomCount = $atoms->Count;
printf "Number of atoms in N terminal residue %s : %d\n",
$nTerminus->Name(), $atomCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atomCount ; ++$index )
{
my $atom = $atoms->Item($index);
printf
" Name : %s Formal charge %d/%d\n",
$atom->Name(),
$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,
$atom->FormalCharge->Denominator;
}
}

# Subroutine to print atoms in C terminal residue.
sub PrintCTerminus($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $chains = $document->AminoAcidChains;
my $nTerminus = $chains->Item(0)->CTerminus();
my $atoms = $nTerminus->Atoms;
my $atomCount = $atoms->Count;
printf "Number of atoms in C terminal residue %s : %d\n",
$nTerminus->Name(), $atomCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atomCount ; ++$index )
{
my $atom = $atoms->Item($index);
printf
" Name : %s Formal charge %d/%d\n",
$atom->Name(),
$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,
$atom->FormalCharge->Denominator;
}
}

# Subroutine to print atoms in N and C terminal residues.
sub PrintTermini($$)
{
my ( $document, $title ) = @_;
printf "\n%s :\n", $title;
PrintNTerminus($document);
PrintCTerminus($document);
}

# Load molecule from PDB.
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Mutate the termini to alanine. With the side chain removed,
# the atom listing will be clearer.
my $chain = $document->AminoAcidChains->Item(0);
my $nTerminus = $chain->NTerminus();
my $cTerminus = $chain->CTerminus();

$document->MutateAminoAcid( $nTerminus, Mdm::ala );
$document->MutateAminoAcid( $cTerminus, Mdm::ala );
$document->DeselectAll();

# Uncomment this line to add hydrogen atoms.
# AddHydrogens($document);

# List atoms in current configuration.
PrintTermini( $document, "At start" );

# Remove terminal residue characteristics and list atoms.
$chain->RemoveNTerminusCap();
$chain->RemoveCTerminusCap();
PrintTermini( $document, "After removing caps" );

# Make termini normal (i.e. charged) and list atoms.
$nTerminus->MakeNTerminus(True);
$cTerminus->MakeCTerminus(True);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making charged termini" );

# Make termini uncharged and list atoms.
$nTerminus->MakeNTerminus(False);
$cTerminus->MakeCTerminus(False);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making neutral termini" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 1.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(1.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(1.0);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 1.0" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 7.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(7.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(7.0);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 7.0" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 13.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(13.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(130);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 13.0" );

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# MarkBondAngleViolations function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/markbondangleviolations_function.htm

## MarkBondAngleViolations function

### Description

MarkBondAngleViolations checks for bond angle violations.

### Applies to

The MarkBondAngleViolations function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the MarkBondAngleViolations function

#### Instance

$object->MarkBondAngleViolations( [tolerance], [color] );

$object->MarkBondAngleViolations( { Tolerance => [tolerance], Color => [color] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [color] | Optional | DiscoveryScript::Color::Create(170, 170, 255) | DiscoveryScript::Color |
| [tolerance] | Optional | 3.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the MarkBondAngleViolations function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '9INS.pdb' );

# Mark bond angle violations.
my $tolerance = 3.0;
my $blue = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 200, 200, 255 );
$document->MarkBondAngleViolations( $tolerance, $blue );

# Get the bond angle violation monitors, a type of AngleMonitor.
my $monitors = $document->AngleMonitors;
my $monitors = $document->FilterByProperty('BondAngleViolationMonitor name="*"');

my $allmonitors = $document->Monitors;
print "Total number of monitors: ". $allmonitors->Count ."\n";

# Report the number of violations.
my $violationCount = $monitors->Count();
print "Structure has " . $violationCount . " bond angle violations.\n\n";

# print a table of violations
printf("Index\t Violation name\t Angle\t Expected\t Minimum\t Maximum \n");
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $violationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);
printf(
"%d \t %s \t %f \t %f \t %f \t %f\n",
$index, $monitor->Name(),
$monitor->Angle(), $monitor->GetProperty("Expected"),
$monitor->GetProperty("Minimum"), $monitor->GetProperty("Maximum")
);

$monitors->Item($index)->SetVisible;
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the MarkChiralityViolations function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Open a protein structure having D-amino acids so we see some violations.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1c4b.pdb' );

# This structure has multiple models - select just the first (we could also
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the MarkCisPeptideViolations function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1ce1.pdb' );

# Mark cis-peptide violations.
my $blue = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 200, 200, 255 );
$document->MarkCisPeptideViolations( 30.0, $blue );

# Get the cis-peptide violation monitors.
my $monitors = $document->Monitors;
my $monitors = $document->FilterByProperty('CisPeptideMonitor label="*"');

# Report the number of violations (one of the monitor created in
# the protein health functions is actually a hidden monitor of

my $monitorCount = $monitors->Count();
my $violationCount = $monitorCount - 1;
print "Structure has " . $violationCount . " cis-peptide violations.\n\n";

# Print a table of violations.
printf("Index\t Name\t Angle\t Residues \n") if ( $violationCount > 0 );

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $monitorCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);

# Verify we have a Mdm::CisPeptideMonitor object.
if ( $monitor->ClassName eq 'Mdm::CisPeptideMonitor' )
{
printf(
"%d \t %s \t %f \t %s\n",
$index, $monitor->Name(),
$monitor->GetProperty("Angle"),
$monitor->GetProperty("Residues")
);
}

$monitors->Item($index)->SetVisible;
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# MarkInvalidResidues function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/markinvalidresidues_function.htm

## MarkInvalidResidues function

### Description

MarkInvalidResidues identifies invalid and non-standard residues in the protein sequence.

For all residues for which there is an internal or user-defined template, the
actual structure will be checked and those that do not conform are
colored and added to a "Invalid Residues" group. If the residue is missing
atoms relative to the template, then a user-property "Missing Atoms" is
added to the residue. If there are atoms in the residue that are not in the
template, then a user-property "Unexpected Atoms" is added. The value is a
list of the names of these atoms. Additionally, all residues are marked with a
user-property "Non-Standard" with a value of "No" for all residues for
which a template exists, and "Yes" for untemplated residues.

The following arguments are supported:

* ColorResidues specifies if invalid residues are to be colored.

* Color specified the color to mark invalid residues.

### Applies to

The MarkInvalidResidues function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the MarkInvalidResidues function

#### Instance

$object->MarkInvalidResidues( [colorboundingresidues], [color] );

$object->MarkInvalidResidues( { ColorBoundingResidues => [colorboundingresidues], Color => [color] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [color] | Optional | DiscoveryScript::Color::Create(100, 0, 255) | DiscoveryScript::Color |
| [colorboundingresidues] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use the MarkProteinGaps function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load a protein containing missing residues (gaps) and the full sequence
# specified in the SEQRES record.
# Note that if an mmCIF file is opened, the gap information from 
# _pdbx_poly_seq_scheme records is automatically processed and can be used in 
# the same way as that derived from PDB SEQRES records.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1kim.pdb' );

# Detect and mark gaps. By default, the residues adjacent to the gaps are
# colored magenta.
$document->MarkProteinGaps;

# Marked residues now have 'Gap End' or 'Gap Start' properties containing
# the missing sequence.
my $gapEndProp = "Gap End";
my $gapStartProp = "Gap Start";

my $aminoAcidChains = $document->AminoAcidChains;
my $chainCount = $aminoAcidChains->Count;

for ( my $c = 0 ; $c < $chainCount ; ++$c )
{
print "Looking for gaps in chain "
. $aminoAcidChains->Item($c)->Name . ".\n";
my $aminoAcids = $aminoAcidChains->Item($c)->AminoAcids;
my $aminoAcidCount = $aminoAcids->Count;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $aminoAcidCount ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $aminoAcids->Item($i);
if ( $aminoAcid->HasProperty($gapEndProp) )
{
my $property = $aminoAcid->GetProperty($gapEndProp);
print "Residue "
. $aminoAcid->Name
. " is at the end of a gap with missing sequence "
. $property . ".\n";
}

if ( $aminoAcid->HasProperty($gapStartProp) )
{
my $property = $aminoAcid->GetProperty($gapStartProp);
print "Residue "
. $aminoAcid->Name
. " is at the start of a gap with missing sequence "
. $property . ".\n";
}
}

#can also create mark and create groups for invalid residues
$document->MarkInvalidResidues;
}
```

ProteinDiscoveryScript

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate use of main chain violation analysis.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Open a protein structure having missing atoms.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "5cha.pdb" );

# mark violations. If we wanted the defaults we would just do:
# $document->MarkChiralityViolations();
# But if we want to change the color we can:
my $pink = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 255, 200, 200 );
$document->MarkMissingMainChainViolations($pink);

# Get the violation monitors.
# in a later release we should be able to get the specific class thus:
# my $chiralityviolationmonitors = $document->ChiralityViolationMonitors;
# but for now we will just use the class from which it is derived. In this
# case its CentroidMonitor
my $monitors = $document->CentroidMonitors;

# Report the number of violations
my $violationCount = $monitors->Count();
print "Structure has "
. $violationCount
. " residues with missing main-chain atoms\n\n";

# print a table of violations
if ( $violationCount > 0 )
{
printf("Index\t Name\t\t Residue \n");
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $violationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Residues") );

# and set the visibility on
$monitors->Item($index)->SetVisible;
}
}

# update view
$document->UpdateViews();
```

```text
# mark violations. If we wanted the defaults we would just do:
# $document->MarkChiralityViolations();
# But if we want to change the color we can:
my $pink = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 255, 200, 200 );
$document->MarkMissingSideChainViolations($pink);

# Get the violation monitors.
# in a later release we should be able to get the specific class thus:
# my $chiralityviolationmonitors = $document->ChiralityViolationMonitors;
# but for now we will just use the class from which it is derived. In this
# case its CentroidMonitor
my $monitors = $document->CentroidMonitors;

# Report the number of violations
my $violationCount = $monitors->Count();
print "Structure has "
. $violationCount
. " residues with missing side-chain atoms\n\n";

# print a table of violations
if ( $violationCount > 0 )
{
printf("Index\t Name\t\t Residue \n");
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $violationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Residues") );

# and set the visibility on
$monitors->Item($index)->SetVisible;
}
}

# update view
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# MarkProteinGaps function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/markproteingaps_function.htm

## MarkProteinGaps function

### Description

MarkProteinGaps identifies gaps in the protein sequence.

When the PDB SEQRES record is defined, gaps are identified by
comparing the amino acid structure with the PDB SEQRES record.
For each identified gap
in the sequence, the residues before and after the gap are colored. In
addition, these bracketing residues are marked with the user-properties
"Start Gap" or "End Gap". For missing residues at the start of a chain,
the first residue will have a "Gap End" property. For missing residues at
the end of a chain, the last residue will have a "Gap Start" property.
In both cases, the value of the property is the missing residue sequence.

If no PDB SEQRES record is available, breaks in connectivity within a chain
are used to identify gaps. The missing number of residues is estimated from the
difference in the residue ID numbers on each side of the gap. The value of
the "Start Gap" and "End Gap" properties is a string of Xs since the missing
residues are not known. This approach cannot identify missing terminal residues.

The following arguments are supported:

* ColorBoundingResidues specifies if residues adjacent to gaps are colored.

* Color specified the color to mark adjacent residues.

### Applies to

The MarkProteinGaps function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the MarkProteinGaps function

#### Instance

$object->MarkProteinGaps( [colorboundingresidues], [color] );

$object->MarkProteinGaps( { ColorBoundingResidues => [colorboundingresidues], Color => [color] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [color] | Optional | DiscoveryScript::Color::Create(255, 0, 255) | DiscoveryScript::Color |
| [colorboundingresidues] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use the MarkProteinGaps function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load a protein containing missing residues (gaps) and the full sequence
# specified in the SEQRES record.
# Note that if an mmCIF file is opened, the gap information from 
# _pdbx_poly_seq_scheme records is automatically processed and can be used in 
# the same way as that derived from PDB SEQRES records.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1kim.pdb' );

# Detect and mark gaps. By default, the residues adjacent to the gaps are
# colored magenta.
$document->MarkProteinGaps;

# Marked residues now have 'Gap End' or 'Gap Start' properties containing
# the missing sequence.
my $gapEndProp = "Gap End";
my $gapStartProp = "Gap Start";

my $aminoAcidChains = $document->AminoAcidChains;
my $chainCount = $aminoAcidChains->Count;

for ( my $c = 0 ; $c < $chainCount ; ++$c )
{
print "Looking for gaps in chain "
. $aminoAcidChains->Item($c)->Name . ".\n";
my $aminoAcids = $aminoAcidChains->Item($c)->AminoAcids;
my $aminoAcidCount = $aminoAcids->Count;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $aminoAcidCount ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $aminoAcids->Item($i);
if ( $aminoAcid->HasProperty($gapEndProp) )
{
my $property = $aminoAcid->GetProperty($gapEndProp);
print "Residue "
. $aminoAcid->Name
. " is at the end of a gap with missing sequence "
. $property . ".\n";
}

if ( $aminoAcid->HasProperty($gapStartProp) )
{
my $property = $aminoAcid->GetProperty($gapStartProp);
print "Residue "
. $aminoAcid->Name
. " is at the start of a gap with missing sequence "
. $property . ".\n";
}
}

#can also create mark and create groups for invalid residues
$document->MarkInvalidResidues;
}
```

# MarkSideChainConformationViolations function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/marksidechainconformationviolations_function.htm

## MarkSideChainConformationViolations function

### Description

MarkSideChainConformationViolations colors amino acids whose side-chain
conformations deviate from the specified rotamer library. Users must specify
the rotamer library and the allowed deviation or tolerance. The Dunbrack
rotamer library contains standard deviation data for each rotamer and the
tolerance argument specifies the allowed deviation as a multiple of the
standard deviations. For the remaining rotamer libraries, the tolerance is
the absolute chi angle deviation allowed, in degrees.

### Applies to

The MarkSideChainConformationViolations function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the MarkSideChainConformationViolations function

The function can be used as follows:

```text
$document->MarkSideChainConformationViolations(
Mdm::dunbrackRotamerLibrary, 3.0);
```

```text
$document->MarkSideChainConformationViolations(
Mdm::ponderAndRichardsRotamerLibrary, 30.0);
```

#### Instance

$object->MarkSideChainConformationViolations( <rotamerlibrary>, <tolerance>, [color] );

$object->MarkSideChainConformationViolations( { RotamerLibrary => <rotamerlibrary>, Tolerance => <tolerance>, Color => [color] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <rotamerlibrary> | Required | | enum Mdm::RotamerLibrary |
| <tolerance> | Required | | Real |
| [color] | Optional | DiscoveryScript::Color::Create(85, 170, 255) | DiscoveryScript::Color |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the MarkSideChainConformationViolations function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9ins.pdb" );

printf "Structure %s atoms: %d residues %d\n", $document->ModelName, 
$document->Atoms->Count, $document->Residues->Count;

# Mark side chain conformation violations.
my $pink = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 255, 200, 200 );
$document->MarkSideChainConformationViolations( Mdm::oldfieldRotamerLibrary, 30.0, $pink );

# Note: if you want to use the mainchain-dependent Dunbrack library, the second
# argument is a sigma multiplier rather than an angle tolerance, thus:
$document->MarkSideChainConformationViolations( Mdm::dunbrackRotamerLibrary, 3.0 );

# Get the side chain conformation violation monitors.
my $monitors =
$document->FilterByProperty('SidechainConformationMonitor name="*"');

# Report the number of violations.
my $violationCount = $monitors->Count;
printf "Structure has %d side-chain conformation violations.\n\n",$violationCount;
# Print a table of violations.
if ( $violationCount > 0 )
{
printf("Index\t Name\t\t Residue \t\tChi Angles\n");
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $violationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s\t",
$index+1, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Residues") );
foreach (qw(Chi1 Chi2 Chi3 Chi4)) {
my $_chi = $monitor->GetProperty($_); 
printf("%8.3f ",$_chi ) if defined $_chi;
}
print("\n"); 
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# MarkStartOfChain function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/markstartofchain_function.htm

## MarkStartOfChain function

### Description

MarkStartOfChain marks residue at the 0-based index as the start of a new polymer chain.

### Applies to

The MarkStartOfChain function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the MarkStartOfChain function

#### Instance

$object->MarkStartOfChain( <index> );

$object->MarkStartOfChain( { Index => <index> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence Sdm::Sequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrates how to manipulate chain breaks in sequences.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();

$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $sequence0 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'MIASDFADSG' );
my $sequence1 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S2', 'MAACDFIDSA' );

# Insert chain breaks by marking the start of new chains using
# 0-based residue indices.
$sequence0->MarkStartOfChain(4);
$sequence1->MarkStartOfChain(4);
$sequence1->MarkStartOfChain(6);

# Find the starting residue index for each new chain.
my $residueCount0 = $sequence0->ResidueCount;
print "In the first sequence, there is a start of chain at ";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount0 ; ++$i )
{
if ( $sequence0->Residue($i)->IsStartOfChain )
{
print "$i ";
}
}
print "\n";
$document->UpdateViews();

$sequence1->DeleteStartOfChainMark(4);
$document->UpdateViews();

# Find the starting residue index for each new chain in
# second sequence.
my $residueCount1 = $sequence1->ResidueCount;
print "In the second sequence, there is a start of chain at ";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount1 ; ++$i )
{
if ( $sequence1->Residue($i)->IsStartOfChain )
{
print "$i ";
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of various atom properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

# Define atom properties to list.
# This may be specified on the command line.
my $residueAtomName = 'THR2:CA';
if ( @ARGV != 0 )
{
($residueAtomName) = @ARGV;
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Get the specified atom.
my $atoms = FilterByString( $document, $residueAtomName );
die "Atom $residueAtomName not found. Aborting!\n\n"
if ( $atoms->Count == 0 );

my $atom = $atoms->[0];

# Print various atom properties. In the DiscoveryStudio client, the
# output will appear in the output pane of the scripting window.
print "List of properties for atom $residueAtomName:\n\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
print 'Element: ' . $atom->Element . "\n";
print 'Element Name: ' . $atom->ElementName . "\n";
print 'Element Symbol: ' . $atom->ElementSymbol . "\n";
print 'Mass: ' . $atom->Mass . "\n";
print 'Atomic number: ' . $atom->AtomicNumber . "\n";
print 'Charge: ' . $atom->Charge . "\n";
print 'Formal Charge: '
. $atom->FormalCharge->Numerator . "/"
. $atom->FormalCharge->Denominator . "\n";

print 'Chirality: ' . $atom->Chirality . "\n";

print 'Bonding radius: ' . $atom->BondingRadius . "\n";
print 'Hybridization: ' . $atom->Hybridization . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen Count: ' . $atom->HydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'ImplicitHydrogen Count: ' . $atom->ImplicitHydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Acceptor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondAcceptor . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Donor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondDonor . "\n";
print 'Isotropic Displacement: ' . $atom->IsotropicDisplacement . "\n";
print 'Is Terminal Hydrogen: ' . $atom->IsTerminalHydrogen . "\n";

print 'CPK Scale: ' . $atom->CPKScale . "\n";
```

MatrialAmbient specifies the ambient property of a document. Use this property in conjunction with the other four material properties to specify the appearance of spherical and cylindrical object surfaces. The default value of this property is -0.06.

The MaterialAmbient property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the MaterialAmbient property

my $realValue = $object->MaterialAmbient;

| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Set

$object->MaterialAmbient = <scale>;

$object->MaterialAmbient( <scale> );

$object->MaterialAmbient( { Scale => <scale> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <scale> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to change the material properties of the
# Molecule Window display.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my ($useLastActive) = @ARGV;

my $document;

# If an input argument is entered, use the last active Molecule Window.
if ($useLastActive)
{
$document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
}

# Otherwise, load a small molecule from PDB.
else
{
$document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );
}

# Reset graphics quality.
$document->GraphicsQuality = Mdm::graphicsQualityMedium;

# Set display style to CPK.
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleAtomCPK);
print "current Atom Display Style : CPK\n\n";
print "Setting the materials properties to defaults\n\n";

# Set materials to default appearance.
$document->MaterialAmbient = -0.06;
$document->MaterialDiffuse = 0;
$document->MaterialEmission = -1;
$document->MaterialShininess = 50;
$document->MaterialSpecular = 0.48;

sleep(2);
print "Setting the materials properties to chalk.\n\n";

# Set materials to chalk appearance.
$document->MaterialAmbient = -0.5151;
$document->MaterialDiffuse = 0.0303;
$document->MaterialEmission = -1.0;
$document->MaterialShininess = 10;
$document->MaterialSpecular = -0.9393;

sleep(2);
print "Setting the materials properties to metallic.\n\n";

# Set materials to metallic appearance.
$document->MaterialAmbient = -0.7575;
$document->MaterialDiffuse = -0.1515;
$document->MaterialEmission = -1.0;
$document->MaterialShininess = 128;
$document->MaterialSpecular = 2.0;

sleep(2);
print "Setting the materials properties to plastic.\n\n";

# Set materials to plastic appearance.
$document->MaterialAmbient = -0.6060;
$document->MaterialDiffuse = 0.0;
$document->MaterialEmission = -1.0;
$document->MaterialShininess = 75;
$document->MaterialSpecular = 0.9393;

sleep(2);
print "Setting the materials properties to rubber.\n\n";

# Set materials to rubber appearance
$document->MaterialAmbient = -0.3333;
$document->MaterialDiffuse = 0.0303;
$document->MaterialEmission = -1.0;
$document->MaterialShininess = 36;
$document->MaterialSpecular = -0.2121;
sleep(2);
```

```text
# Set materials to default appearance.

$document->MaterialDiffuse = 0;
$document->MaterialEmission = -1;
$document->MaterialShininess = 50;
$document->MaterialSpecular = 0.48;

sleep(2);
print "Setting the materials properties to chalk.\n\n";

# Set materials to chalk appearance.
$document->MaterialAmbient = -0.5151;
$document->MaterialDiffuse = 0.0303;
$document->MaterialEmission = -1.0;
$document->MaterialShininess = 10;
$document->MaterialSpecular = -0.9393;

sleep(2);
print "Setting the materials properties to metallic.\n\n";

# Set materials to metallic appearance.
$document->MaterialAmbient = -0.7575;
$document->MaterialDiffuse = -0.1515;
$document->MaterialEmission = -1.0;
$document->MaterialShininess = 128;
$document->MaterialSpecular = 2.0;

sleep(2);

$document->MaterialDiffuse = 0.0303;
$document->MaterialEmission = -1.0;
$document->MaterialShininess = 36;
$document->MaterialSpecular = -0.2121;
sleep(2);
```

# MaximumCenterDistance property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/maximumcenterdistance_property.htm

## MaximumCenterDistance property

### Description

Stacked and staggered pi-pi interactions are found by performing the following tests:

* The distance between the centroid of each pair of pi rings is used to
find those which fall within the Maximum Center Distance cutoff (default 8 Å).

* For these, an atom from each ring must be within the Closest Atom Distance
cutoff (default 4.5 Å).

* The angle θ between the normal of one ring and the centroid-centroid vector
must fall between 0Å and ± the Theta Angle cutoff (default 60Å), and the angle
λ between the normal to each ring must fall between 0° and ± the Lambda Angle
cutoff (default 30°).

### Applies to

The MaximumCenterDistance property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::PiPiMonitor

### Using the MaximumCenterDistance property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->MaximumCenterDistance;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::PiPiMonitor |

#### Set

$object->MaximumCenterDistance = <distance>;

$object->MaximumCenterDistance( <distance> );

$object->MaximumCenterDistance( { Distance => <distance> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <distance> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::PiPiMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script shows how to create pi interaction monitors.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1kim.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Creates pi interaction monitors
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

#if no array of atoms is passed in then the monitor is created
#for the whole molecule (or other object).
my $pipiMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor();
my $piCationMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiCationMonitor();
my $piSigmaMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiSigmaMonitor();

$pipiMonitor->Name = "Pi-Pi";
$piCationMonitor->Name = "Pi-Cation";
$piSigmaMonitor->Name = "Pi-Sigma";

my $piPiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piPiInteractionCount = $piPiInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piPiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

# Change criteria settings to non-default values.
$piCationMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piCationMonitor->MinimumAngle = 60.0;
my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule\n";

$piSigmaMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->MinimumAngle = 30.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->AngleDeviation = 15.0;
my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

$pipiMonitor->MaximumCenterDistance = 7.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumClosestAtomDistance = 4.0;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumLambda = 20.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumTheta = 45.;
my $pipiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount = $pipiInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $pipiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piInteractions = $molecule->PiInteractionMonitors();
my $piCount = $piInteractions->Count();
print "\nThere are " . $piCount . " pi interaction monitors: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $piCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $piInteractions->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Interactions") );
}

#If we want to limit the scope of the monitoring, we can pass in
#an array of atoms. This is similar to creating a monitor from the UI
# when atoms are selected. Pi interactions will then be calculated within
#these, and between these and the parent object
my $residue = FilterByString( $document, "THM1" )->Item(0);
my $atom_array = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $atoms = $residue->Atoms();
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atoms->Count() ; ++$index )
{
$atom_array->AddItem( $atoms->Item($index) );
}
my $pipiMonitor2 = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor($atom_array);
my $pipiInteractions2 = $pipiMonitor2->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount2 = $pipiInteractions2->Count();
print "Number of pi-pi interactions between "
. $residue->Name()
. " and the rest of the molecule: "
. $pipiInteractionCount2 . "\n";

my $picatmonitors = $document->PiCationMonitors;
print "Number of pi-cation monitors: ". $picatmonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pipimonitors = $document->PiPiMonitors;
print "Number of pi-pi monitors: ". $pipimonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pisigmonitors = $document->PiSigmaMonitors;
print "Number of pi-sigma monitors: ". $pisigmonitors->Count . "\n";
```

# MaximumFileSizeForDownload property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/maximumfilesizefordownload_property.htm

## MaximumFileSizeForDownload property

### Description

MaximumFileSizeForDownload specifies the maximum size (in bytes)
of output files to be downloaded to the client after a protocol finishes.
Large files will remain on the server.

### Applies to

The MaximumFileSizeForDownload property can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Task

### Using the MaximumFileSizeForDownload property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->MaximumFileSizeForDownload;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Protocol::Task |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

The MaximumLambda property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::PiPiMonitor

my $realValue = $object->MaximumLambda;

| $object | | | Mdm::PiPiMonitor |

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script shows how to create pi interaction monitors.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1kim.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Creates pi interaction monitors
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

#if no array of atoms is passed in then the monitor is created
#for the whole molecule (or other object).
my $pipiMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor();
my $piCationMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiCationMonitor();
my $piSigmaMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiSigmaMonitor();

$pipiMonitor->Name = "Pi-Pi";
$piCationMonitor->Name = "Pi-Cation";
$piSigmaMonitor->Name = "Pi-Sigma";

my $piPiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piPiInteractionCount = $piPiInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piPiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

# Change criteria settings to non-default values.
$piCationMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piCationMonitor->MinimumAngle = 60.0;
my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule\n";

$piSigmaMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->MinimumAngle = 30.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->AngleDeviation = 15.0;
my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

$pipiMonitor->MaximumCenterDistance = 7.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumClosestAtomDistance = 4.0;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumLambda = 20.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumTheta = 45.;
my $pipiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount = $pipiInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $pipiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piInteractions = $molecule->PiInteractionMonitors();
my $piCount = $piInteractions->Count();
print "\nThere are " . $piCount . " pi interaction monitors: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $piCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $piInteractions->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Interactions") );
}

#If we want to limit the scope of the monitoring, we can pass in
#an array of atoms. This is similar to creating a monitor from the UI
# when atoms are selected. Pi interactions will then be calculated within
#these, and between these and the parent object
my $residue = FilterByString( $document, "THM1" )->Item(0);
my $atom_array = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $atoms = $residue->Atoms();
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atoms->Count() ; ++$index )
{
$atom_array->AddItem( $atoms->Item($index) );
}
my $pipiMonitor2 = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor($atom_array);
my $pipiInteractions2 = $pipiMonitor2->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount2 = $pipiInteractions2->Count();
print "Number of pi-pi interactions between "
. $residue->Name()
. " and the rest of the molecule: "
. $pipiInteractionCount2 . "\n";

my $picatmonitors = $document->PiCationMonitors;
print "Number of pi-cation monitors: ". $picatmonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pipimonitors = $document->PiPiMonitors;
print "Number of pi-pi monitors: ". $pipimonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pisigmonitors = $document->PiSigmaMonitors;
print "Number of pi-sigma monitors: ". $pisigmonitors->Count . "\n";
```

# MaximumTheta property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/maximumtheta_property.htm

## MaximumTheta property

### Description

Stacked and staggered pi-pi interactions are found by performing the following
tests:

* The distance between the centroid of each pair of pi rings is used
to
find the ones that fall within the Maximum Center Distance cutoff (default 8 Å).

* For these, an atom from each ring must be within the Closest Atom
Distancecutoff (default 4.5 Å).

* The angle θ between the normal of one ring and the centroid-centroid
vector
must fall between 0° and ± the Theta Angle cutoff (default 60°), and the angle
λ between the normal to each ring must fall between 0° and ± the Lambda Angle
cutoff (default 30°).

### Applies to

The MaximumTheta property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::PiPiMonitor

### Using the MaximumTheta property

my $realValue = $object->MaximumTheta;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::PiPiMonitor |

#### Set

$object->MaximumTheta = <theta>;

$object->MaximumTheta( <theta> );

$object->MaximumTheta( { Theta => <theta> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <theta> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::PiPiMonitor |

# Mdm::AcceptorFeature class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdm__acceptorfeature_class.htm

## Mdm::AcceptorFeature class

### Description

The Mdm::AcceptorFeature represents an acceptor feature in a
pharmacophore model.

The AcceptorFeature has a tail location which represents the location of an acceptor Atom.
It also has a head location which represents the location of a donor Atom.

### Using the Mdm::AcceptorFeature object

The Mdm::AcceptorFeature object can be accessed via the MdmDiscoveryScript package.

Mdm::Monitor -> Mdm::Geometric3d -> Mdm::Object -> DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

# Create a query from a template molecules. Add HBAs to =O,
# HBD to N, and excluded volumes to all Halogens and
# projection points of HBAs and HBDs.

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles(
'OC(=O)C1=CC=C(C=C1)CN/C2=C/C=C(C=C2)C=CC(=O)C[Cl]');
AddHydrogens($document);

my $atoms = $document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $double_bond_oxygens = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $nitrogens = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $halogens = Mdm::Array::Create();

foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( ( $atom->Element eq 'O' ) && ( $atom->BondCount == 1 ) )
{
$double_bond_oxygens->AddItem($atom);
}
$nitrogens->AddItem($atom) if ( $atom->Element eq 'N' );
$halogens->AddItem($atom) if ( $atom->Element =~ /(Cl|F|Br|I)\b/i );
}

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Features and location constraints
my $featureCount = 0;
foreach my $atom (@$double_bond_oxygens)
{
++$featureCount;
my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
my $featureName = "HBA_" . $featureCount;
$acceptorOperator->Name($featureName);
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atom);

# create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );
}

foreach my $atom (@$nitrogens)
{
++$featureCount;
my $featureName = "HBD_" . $featureCount;
my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name($featureName);
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atom);

#create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );
}

# Add excluded volumes at the location of halogen atoms
foreach my $atom (@$halogens)
{
my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

# Add excluded volumes at the projection point of HBAs and HBDs
my $acceptorfeatures = $fitOperator->AcceptorFeatures;
foreach my $acceptor (@$acceptorfeatures)
{
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atom->XYZ = $acceptor->HeadXYZ();
$molecule->Select();

my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

my $donorfeatures = $fitOperator->DonorFeatures;
foreach my $donor (@$donorfeatures)
{
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atom->XYZ = $donor->HeadXYZ();
$molecule->Select();

my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

my $exclusionfeatures = $document->ExclusionFeatures();
my $exclusionfeatureCount = 0;
foreach my $exclusionfeature (@$exclusionfeatures)
{
++$exclusionfeatureCount;
my $name = "EV_" . $exclusionfeatureCount;
$exclusionfeature->Name($name);
}

# We will delete temporary atoms used to create EVs
# on projection points. Need to update objects before
# deleting so we preserve the X,Y,Z location.
$document->UpdateObjects();

# Delete temporary atoms
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# Mdm::AminoAcid class

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdm__aminoacid_class.htm

## Mdm::AminoAcid class

### Description

The Mdm::AminoAcid represents an amino acid in the Molecular Data Model. In addition to being a specialized residue unique to the
chemistry of amino acids, it contributes knowledge of the chemical make-up of an amino acid. For example, all amino
acids have a nitrogen, two carbons, and an oxygen in their backbone and at least one side-chain.

The supported amino acid types are described in enum Mdm::ResidueType .

### Using the Mdm::AminoAcid object

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage()
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing conformations.\n";
print " 3 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Opens a molecule with conformations from the active Molecule Window.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage() unless ($document);
Usage() unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );
Usage() unless ( $document->Conformations->Count > 0 );

print "Create an animation using conformation objects.\n";
my $animation = $document->CreateAnimation( $document->Conformations );
my $frameCount = $animation->FrameCount;
print "Number of animation frames: $frameCount frames.\n";

print "Saving the first frame to file.\n";
$animation->ActivateFirstFrame();
$document->Save( "FirstFrame.mol2", "mol2" );

# Illustrate how to activate the next and previous frames.
$animation->ActivateNextFrame();
$animation->ActivatePreviousFrame();

print "Saving the last frame to file.\n";
$animation->ActivateLastFrame();
$document->Save( "LastFrame.mol2", "mol2" );

print "Removing the first frame.\n";
my $firstFrame = $document->Conformations->Item(0);
$animation->RemoveFrame($firstFrame);

print "Adding the first frame back.\n";
$animation->AddFrame($firstFrame);
my $isTracked = $animation->IsFrameSelectionTracked();
if ($isTracked)
{
print "Frame selection is tracked.\n";
}
else
{
print "Frame selection is not tracked.\n";
}

print "Removing and de-activating all animation frames.\n";
$animation->RemoveAllFrames();
$animation->ResetFrame();
```

## Mdm::Array::Create function

### Description

Create creates one or more Mdm::Array objects.

### Applies to

The Mdm::Array::Create function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Array

### Using the Mdm::Array::Create function

#### Static

my $arrayObject = Mdm::Array::Create();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use the Mdm::Array class.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
my $cACBAtoms = Mdm::Array::Create();

# loop over all atoms
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{

# Add C-alpha and C-beta atom to the array.
$cACBAtoms->AddItem($atom) if ( $atom->Name =~ /(Cb|Ca)\b/i );
}

print "Number of C-alpha and C-beta atoms in document: "
. $cACBAtoms->Count . ".\n";
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the use of BindingSite objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

Delete( $document, GetLigands($document) );
Delete( $document, GetWaters($document) );

my $protein = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

# Find all binding site from receptor cavities.
my $bindingSites = $document->CreateBindingSitesFromCavities($protein);
print "Number of binding sites found: " . $bindingSites->Count . "\n";

# Loop through all binding sites and determine volume, point count
# and min/max dimension.
my $bsCount = 0;

foreach my $s (@$bindingSites)
{
my $volume = $s->GetProperty("Volume");
my $bcount = $s->BindingSitePoints->Count;
my $bindingSitePoints = $s->BindingSitePoints;
print " Site: " . ++$bsCount . "\n";
print "\tVolume: $volume\n";
print "\tPoint count: $bcount\n";

# Loop over the binding site points to find
# the minimum and maximum values.
my $max = Mdm::Point::Create( -1.e6, -1.e6, -1.e6 );
my $min = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.e6, 1.e6, 1.e6 );
foreach my $xyz (@$bindingSitePoints)
{
$max->X = $xyz->XYZ->X if ( $max->X < $xyz->XYZ->X );
$max->Y = $xyz->XYZ->Y if ( $max->Y < $xyz->XYZ->Y );
$max->Z = $xyz->XYZ->Z if ( $max->Z < $xyz->XYZ->Z );
$min->X = $xyz->XYZ->X if ( $min->X > $xyz->XYZ->X );
$min->Y = $xyz->XYZ->Y if ( $min->Y > $xyz->XYZ->Y );
$min->Z = $xyz->XYZ->Z if ( $min->Z > $xyz->XYZ->Z );
}
print "\tSite Minimum: x: "
. $min->X . " y: "
. $min->Y . " z: "
. $min->Z . "\n";
print "\tSite Maximum: x: "
. $max->X . " y: "
. $max->Y . " z: "
. $max->Z . "\n";
}
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the MarkBondAngleViolations function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '9INS.pdb' );

# Mark bond angle violations.
my $tolerance = 3.0;
my $blue = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 200, 200, 255 );
$document->MarkBondAngleViolations( $tolerance, $blue );

# Get the bond angle violation monitors, a type of AngleMonitor.
my $monitors = $document->AngleMonitors;
my $monitors = $document->FilterByProperty('BondAngleViolationMonitor name="*"');

my $allmonitors = $document->Monitors;
print "Total number of monitors: ". $allmonitors->Count ."\n";

# Report the number of violations.
my $violationCount = $monitors->Count();
print "Structure has " . $violationCount . " bond angle violations.\n\n";

# print a table of violations
printf("Index\t Violation name\t Angle\t Expected\t Minimum\t Maximum \n");
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $violationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);
printf(
"%d \t %s \t %f \t %f \t %f \t %f\n",
$index, $monitor->Name(),
$monitor->Angle(), $monitor->GetProperty("Expected"),
$monitor->GetProperty("Minimum"), $monitor->GetProperty("Maximum")
);

$monitors->Item($index)->SetVisible;
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
```
```text
# Search for and print bumps between ligand and receptor.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Add hydrogen atoms to all heavy atoms.
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms( Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms, True );

# Creates a bump monitor between ligand and receptor atoms.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $bumpMonitor = $document->CreateBumpMonitor( $ligandAtoms, False );

$bumpMonitor->IsLabelShown = True;
$bumpMonitor->IsIntermolecularOnlyShown = False;

print "Default percent VDW Radius: $bumpMonitor->{DefaultPercentVdwRadius}\n";
print "$bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} bumps between ligand and receptor.\n";

$bumpMonitor->PercentVdwRadius = 90;

print "$bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} bumps between ligand and receptor "
. "when VDW radius set to 90%.\n";

my $bumps = $bumpMonitor->Bumps;
my $count = $bumps->Count;

# Create a bump hash.
my %bumpHash;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $bump = $bumps->Item($index);
$bumpHash{$index}{'bump'} = $bump;
$bumpHash{$index}{'Id1'} = $bump->Atom1->Id;
$bumpHash{$index}{'Id2'} = $bump->Atom2->Id;
}

# Print information for each bump, sorted by Atom1->Id followed by Atom2->Id.
my $counter = 0;
for my $b (
sort { 
my $x = $bumpHash{$a}{'Id1'};
my $y = $bumpHash{$b}{'Id1'};
($x != $y) ? ($x <=> $y) : ($bumpHash{$a}{'Id2'} <=> $bumpHash{$b}{'Id2'})
}
keys %bumpHash
)
{
my $bump = $bumpHash{$b}{'bump'};
my $atom1 = $bump->Atom1;
my $atom2 = $bump->Atom2;
printf
"%3d) Bump: %.3f A between Atom id %d %s:%s:%s and Atom id %d %s:%s:%s\n",
++$counter, $bump->Distance(),
$bumpHash{$b}{'Id1'},
$atom1->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom1->Parent->Name, $atom1->Name,
$bumpHash{$b}{'Id2'},
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name;
}
```

# Mdm::CAlphaMonitor class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdm__calphamonitor_class.htm

## Mdm::CAlphaMonitor class

### Description

The Mdm::CAlphaMonitor identifies pairs of C-alpha atoms in different protein
molecules within a specified cutoff distance (default
2.5 Å). This can be used to assess the fit between superimposed protein
molecules, and also as a means of finding matching residue pairs for
performing superimposition. The observed C-alpha pairs identified by the
monitor are indicated by Mdm::CAlphaPair objects.

### Using the Mdm::CAlphaMonitor object

The Mdm::CAlphaMonitor object can be accessed via the MdmDiscoveryScript package.
