### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create some features on the query
# Create a ring aromatic
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Name("benzene");
my $ringAromaticOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$ringAromaticOperator->Name('RA1');
my $ringAromaticFeatureObject =
$ringAromaticOperator->CreateRingAromaticFeature(
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Atoms );
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Select(); # delete later

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature(
$ringAromaticFeatureObject->CentroidFeature(), 1.6 );
my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature(
$ringAromaticFeatureObject->NormalFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create a donor feature
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -2, -4, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# Give the hydrogen bond donor a higher weight (2.0) than the default (1.0)
$donorOperator->Weight(2.0);

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create an acceptor feature at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );

printf "%s Head: x: %.4f y: %.4f z: %.4f\n",
$locationFeatureHead->ClassName, 
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->X, 
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->Y,
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->Z;

my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

printf "%s Tail: x: %.4f y: %.4f z: %.4f\n",
$locationFeatureHead->ClassName,
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->X, 
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->Y,
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->Z;

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# Mdm::NormalMonitor class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdm__normalmonitor_class.htm

## Mdm::NormalMonitor class

### Description

The Mdm::NormalMonitor is a geometry monitor that monitors a Mdm::PlaneMonitor and the three-dimensional location of an Mdm::Geometric3d object. It computes a normal vector to the plane by projecting the point onto the plane. The default length of the
vector is 1.0, though any value can be specified using a class attribute.

### Using the Mdm::NormalMonitor object

The Mdm::NormalMonitor object can be accessed via the MdmDiscoveryScript package.

```text
$document->UpdateViews;
```

# Mdm::Nucleotide class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdm__nucleotide_class.htm

## Mdm::Nucleotide class

### Description

The Mdm::Nucleotide represents a nucleotide residue in the Molecular
Data Model. In addition to being a specialized residue unique to the
chemistry of nucleic acids, it contributes knowledge of the chemical
make-up of a nucleic acid. For example, all nucleic acids have either
a ribose sugar (for RNA strands) or a 2'-deoxyribose sugar (for DNA strands)
attached to a phosphate to make up the backbone of the strand. Also,
a heterocyclic base is attached through the beta linkage of the sugar.

The supported nucleotide types are described in enum Mdm::ResidueType .

### Using the Mdm::Nucleotide object

The Mdm::Nucleotide object can be accessed via the MdmDiscoveryScript package.

# Mdm::Object class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdm__object_class.htm

## Mdm::Object class

### Description

The Mdm::Object represents a generic object in the Molecular Data Model that is a placeholder for a more specific type of object. It provides the
framework for the following features:

* Object model access

* Generic object property access

* Graphic display attribute access

* Graphic display generation

The ClassName property can be queried to determine the actual
type of the object in question.

### Using the Mdm::Object object

The Mdm::Object object can be accessed via the MdmDiscoveryScript package.

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate Mdm::Set class.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Create a set of every 4th object in the document.
my $setOfForths = Mdm::Set::Create();
my $objects = $document->Objects;
my $count = $objects->Count;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $count ; $i += 4 )
{
$setOfForths->AddItem( $objects->Item($i) );
}

my $residues = $document->Residues;
foreach my $residue (@$residues)
{
if ( $setOfForths->ItemExists($residue) )
{
print 'Residue ' . $residue->Name . " found in set.\n";
}
else
{
print 'Residue ' . $residue->Name . " not found in set.\n";
}
}

$document->Close();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use the offline commands for offline Molecules.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';

my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . 'Sample Drug Molecules.dsv';
my $document =
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $inputFile, LoadAllObjects => False } );
my $onlineMolecules = $document->Molecules;
my $allMolecules = $document->AllMolecules;
print "There are " . $allMolecules->Count . " molecules in the file.\n";
print "There are "
. $onlineMolecules->Count
. " molecules loaded in memory.\n";
print "Visualize the first 10 molecules...\n";

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 10 ; $i++ )
{
my $mol = $allMolecules->Item($i);
print "Visualize " . $mol->Name() . "\n";
$mol->SetVisible();
}
print "Offline all the visible molecules to release memory.\n";
my $count = $allMolecules->Count;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $count ; $i++ )
{
my $mol = $allMolecules->Item($i);
if ( $mol->IsVisible() )
{
$mol->Offline();
}
}
print "Closing the document.\n";
$document->Close();
```

# Mdm::PiBond class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdm__pibond_class.htm

## Mdm::PiBond class

### Description

The Mdm::PiBond identifies various interactions of pi ring systems. The
interaction is displayed as an orange line with symbols depending on the type
of interaction. There are three types:

* pi-pi: between the centers of a pair of pi rings. Each end is marked with a Greek pi symbol.

* pi-cation: between the centers of a pi ring and a cation. The ring is marked with a pi symbol and the cation with a plus sign.

* pi-sigma: between the centers of a pi ring and the end of a sigma bond. The ring is marked with a pi symbol and the sigma bond with a Greek sigma character.

### Using the Mdm::PiBond object

The Mdm::PiBond object can be accessed via the MdmDiscoveryScript package.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script shows how to create pi interaction monitors.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1kim.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Creates pi interaction monitors
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

#if no array of atoms is passed in then the monitor is created
#for the whole molecule (or other object).
my $pipiMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor();
my $piCationMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiCationMonitor();
my $piSigmaMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiSigmaMonitor();

$pipiMonitor->Name = "Pi-Pi";
$piCationMonitor->Name = "Pi-Cation";
$piSigmaMonitor->Name = "Pi-Sigma";

my $piPiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piPiInteractionCount = $piPiInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piPiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

# Change criteria settings to non-default values.
$piCationMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piCationMonitor->MinimumAngle = 60.0;
my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule\n";

$piSigmaMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->MinimumAngle = 30.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->AngleDeviation = 15.0;
my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

$pipiMonitor->MaximumCenterDistance = 7.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumClosestAtomDistance = 4.0;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumLambda = 20.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumTheta = 45.;
my $pipiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount = $pipiInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $pipiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piInteractions = $molecule->PiInteractionMonitors();
my $piCount = $piInteractions->Count();
print "\nThere are " . $piCount . " pi interaction monitors: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $piCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $piInteractions->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Interactions") );
}

#If we want to limit the scope of the monitoring, we can pass in
#an array of atoms. This is similar to creating a monitor from the UI
# when atoms are selected. Pi interactions will then be calculated within
#these, and between these and the parent object
my $residue = FilterByString( $document, "THM1" )->Item(0);
my $atom_array = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $atoms = $residue->Atoms();
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atoms->Count() ; ++$index )
{
$atom_array->AddItem( $atoms->Item($index) );
}
my $pipiMonitor2 = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor($atom_array);
my $pipiInteractions2 = $pipiMonitor2->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount2 = $pipiInteractions2->Count();
print "Number of pi-pi interactions between "
. $residue->Name()
. " and the rest of the molecule: "
. $pipiInteractionCount2 . "\n";

my $picatmonitors = $document->PiCationMonitors;
print "Number of pi-cation monitors: ". $picatmonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pipimonitors = $document->PiPiMonitors;
print "Number of pi-pi monitors: ". $pipimonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pisigmonitors = $document->PiSigmaMonitors;
print "Number of pi-sigma monitors: ". $pisigmonitors->Count . "\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script shows how to create pi interaction monitors.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1kim.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Creates pi interaction monitors
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

#if no array of atoms is passed in then the monitor is created
#for the whole molecule (or other object).
my $pipiMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor();
my $piCationMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiCationMonitor();
my $piSigmaMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiSigmaMonitor();

$pipiMonitor->Name = "Pi-Pi";
$piCationMonitor->Name = "Pi-Cation";
$piSigmaMonitor->Name = "Pi-Sigma";

my $piPiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piPiInteractionCount = $piPiInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piPiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

# Change criteria settings to non-default values.
$piCationMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piCationMonitor->MinimumAngle = 60.0;
my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule\n";

$piSigmaMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->MinimumAngle = 30.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->AngleDeviation = 15.0;
my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

$pipiMonitor->MaximumCenterDistance = 7.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumClosestAtomDistance = 4.0;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumLambda = 20.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumTheta = 45.;
my $pipiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount = $pipiInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $pipiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piInteractions = $molecule->PiInteractionMonitors();
my $piCount = $piInteractions->Count();
print "\nThere are " . $piCount . " pi interaction monitors: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $piCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $piInteractions->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Interactions") );
}

#If we want to limit the scope of the monitoring, we can pass in
#an array of atoms. This is similar to creating a monitor from the UI
# when atoms are selected. Pi interactions will then be calculated within
#these, and between these and the parent object
my $residue = FilterByString( $document, "THM1" )->Item(0);
my $atom_array = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $atoms = $residue->Atoms();
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atoms->Count() ; ++$index )
{
$atom_array->AddItem( $atoms->Item($index) );
}
my $pipiMonitor2 = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor($atom_array);
my $pipiInteractions2 = $pipiMonitor2->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount2 = $pipiInteractions2->Count();
print "Number of pi-pi interactions between "
. $residue->Name()
. " and the rest of the molecule: "
. $pipiInteractionCount2 . "\n";

my $picatmonitors = $document->PiCationMonitors;
print "Number of pi-cation monitors: ". $picatmonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pipimonitors = $document->PiPiMonitors;
print "Number of pi-pi monitors: ". $pipimonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pisigmonitors = $document->PiSigmaMonitors;
print "Number of pi-sigma monitors: ". $pisigmonitors->Count . "\n";
```

the CA-C-N-CA atoms between amino acids. It is created from the
MarkPlanarPeptideViolations function.

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the MarkPlanarPeptideViolations function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1ce1.pdb" );

# Mark planar peptide violations. Setting the tolerance
# low so we see some violations.
my $blue = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 200, 200, 255 );
$document->MarkPlanarPeptideViolations( 15.0, $blue );

# Get the planar peptide violation monitors.
my $monitors =
$document->FilterByProperty('PlanarPeptideViolationMonitor name="*"');

# Report the number of violations.
my $violationCount = $monitors->Count;
print "Structure has " . $violationCount . " planar peptide violations.\n\n";

# Print a table of violations.
print "Index\t Name\t\t Angle\t Residues \n"
if ( $violationCount > 0 );

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $violationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);

printf(
"%d \t %s \t %f \t %s\n",
$index, $monitor->Name(),
$monitor->GetProperty("Angle"),
$monitor->GetProperty("Residues")
);

$monitors->Item($index)->SetVisible;
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# Mdm::Point class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdm__point_class.htm

## Mdm::Point class

### Description

The Mdm::Point is a coordinate in a three-dimensional system.
It can represent a single point or the head of a vector whose
tail is located at the origin.

Note about modifying returned Mdm::Point objects: Functions and properties typically return
an Mdm::Point object containing a copy of the coordinates
in question (rather than referring to the original coordinates).
As a result, if the values on the returned Mdm::Point object
are changed, it only affects the local copy of the values,
not the original values that were queried.

If the intent is to change the original values, the modified values need to be
assigned back. Please see the examples below for clarification.

#### Example that correctly changes the coordinates of an atom:

```text
# Step 1: Query the XYZ property - this returns a copy of the coordinates
my $xyz = $atom->XYZ;

# Step 2: Modify the coordinates - does NOT modify the atom's coordinates,
# but rather the X value of the duplicate coordinates.
$xyz->X = 1.0;

# Step 3: Assign the coordinates back - this WILL modify the atom's coordinates
$atom->XYZ = $xyz;
```

#### Example that does NOT work as expected:

```text
# This modifies the copy of the coordinates, without assigning it back.
# As a result, the atom's coordinates are unchanged (only the X value of the
# temporary Mdm::Point value is modified and immediately discarded). In
# effect, this is identical to Steps 1 and 2 above, but is missing step 3
# where the changed coordinates are assigned back to the atom.
$atom->XYZ->X = 1.0;
```

### Using the Mdm::Point object

The Mdm::Point object can be accessed via the MdmDiscoveryScript package.

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to create a polydot object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $pointArray = Mdm::PointArray::Create();
my $colorArray = DiscoveryScript::ColorArray::Create();

# Generate 500 random points and colors.
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 500 ; ++$i )
{
my $randX = rand();
my $randY = rand();
my $randZ = rand();
my $randColor = Mdm::Color::Create(
int( $randX * 255 ),
int( $randY * 255 ),
int( $randZ * 255 )
);
my $newPt = Mdm::Point::Create( $randX, $randY, $randZ );
$pointArray->AddItem($newPt);
$colorArray->AddItem($randColor);
}

# Create a new polydot object from the point and color arrays.
$molecule->CreatePolydot(
{ ArrayOfDots => $pointArray, ArrayOfColors => $colorArray } );

# Find and name the polydot object.
my $polydotArray = $document->Polydots;
$polydotArray->Item(0)->Name('Point Cloud 1');
$document->FitView();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

## Mdm::PointFeature class

### Description

The Mdm::PointFeature represents a point feature used as part of
a 3D pharmacophore query.
The PointFeature has 3D coordinates that can be used to query
for other objects at that location or outside of that location.
It is common to use a Mdm::LocationFeature in conjunction with a
PointFeature to provide for an area of possible locations instead of
a single, specific location.

```text
#/usr/bin/perl -w

# Create a point offset feature

use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $atom1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::C);

$atoms->AddItem($atom2);

my $andOperator = $query->CreateQueryOperator(Mdm::queryAnd);
my $offset = 5.0;
my $isPercentOffset = False;
my $pointOffsetFeature =
$andOperator->CreatePointOffsetFeature(
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w

use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $pointArray = Mdm::PointArray::Create();
my $colorArray = DiscoveryScript::ColorArray::Create();

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 500 ; ++$i )
{
my $randX = rand();
my $randY = rand();
my $randZ = rand();

int( $randX * 255 ),
int( $randY * 255 ),
int( $randZ * 255 )
);
my $newPt = Mdm::Point::Create( $randX, $randY, $randZ );
$pointArray->AddItem($newPt);
$colorArray->AddItem($randColor);
}

# Create a new polydot object from the point and color arrays.
$molecule->CreatePolydot(
{ ArrayOfDots => $pointArray, ArrayOfColors => $colorArray } );

# Find and name the polydot object.
my $polydotArray = $document->Polydots;
$polydotArray->Item(0)->Name('Point Cloud 1');
$document->FitView();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the MarkChiralityViolations function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Open a protein structure having D-amino acids so we see some violations.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1c4b.pdb' );

# This structure has multiple models - select just the first (we could also
# make a loop and check for violations in each model).
my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
$molecules->Item(0)->Select();

# Mark chirality violations.
my $pink = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 255, 200, 200 );
$document->MarkChiralityViolations($pink);

# Get the chirality violation monitors.
my $monitors =
$document->FilterByProperty('ProteinChiralityMonitor name="*"');

# Report the number of violations.
my $violationCount = $monitors->Count;
print "Structure has "
. $violationCount
. " CAlpha chirality violations.\n\n";

# Print a table of violations.
if ( $violationCount > 0 )
{
printf("Index\t Name\t\t Residue \n");
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $violationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);

printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Residues") );

$monitors->Item($index)->SetVisible;
}
}

$document->DeselectAll(); 
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# Mdm::ProteinPose class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdm__proteinpose_class.htm

## Mdm::ProteinPose class

### Description

The Mdm::ProteinPose represents a protein pose. It specifies a rigid body translation and rotation operation
that orients the ligand in a docked conformation with respect to the receptor protein.

The example below demonstrates how Mdm::ProteinPose objects are created from scripting. Please note however
that most of the functions connected to generating Mdm::ProteinPose objects are designed to process output
from the Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) protocols. The numbers specifying the translation, rotation and other
properties hard-coded for convenience in the example script below are derived from the output of a Dock
Proteins (ZDOCK) run on two small proteins: chain A of 2ptn and chain I of 2sta.
They cannot be easily generated by hand.

### Using the Mdm::ProteinPose object

The Mdm::ProteinPose object can be accessed via the MdmDiscoveryScript package.

#### Properties

#### Returned by

#### Derived from

Mdm::Geometric3d -> Mdm::Object -> DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates the use for scripting functions for the protein-protein
# docking area.
# NOTE: Most of the functions connected to generating the DockedPoseAssembly and
# DockedProtein objects are designed to process output from the Dock Proteins (ZDOCK)
# protocols, which generates a set of numbers describing the relative orientations
# of the two proteins in a docked protein complex. Those numbers are necessary to
# generate the objects described in the this example but cannot be easily
# generated by hand. The numerical values hard-coded to avoid having
# to load a Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) output file . The values used are derived
# from the output of a Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) run on two small proteins: chain A of 2ptn and
# chain I of 2sta.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document =
DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "2ptn.pdb" ); # receptor
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "2sta.pdb" ); # ligand

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
my $receptor = $molecules->Item(0);
my $ligand = $molecules->Item(1);

# Only keep ligand chain that was used in ZDOCK run
my $ligandChains = $ligand->Chains;
foreach my $chain (@$ligandChains)
{
if ( $chain->Name ne "I" )
{
$chain->Select();
}
}

# Only keep receptor chain that was used in ZDOCK run
my $receptorChains = $receptor->Chains;
foreach my $chain (@$receptorChains)
{
if ( $chain->Name ne "A" )
{
$chain->Select();
}
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# Label receptor and ligand with identifying tags
# These tags are used by other commands
$receptor->SetProperty( "COMPLEX_TYPE", "RECEPTOR" );
$ligand->SetProperty( "COMPLEX_TYPE", "LIGAND" );

# Define general properties of the structures in the complex
# Note that these numbers are part of the output generated by the
# ZDock protein docking program.
# All numerical values were taken from ZDock run output for this system
my $N = 84;
my $spacing = 1.2;
my $receptorCenter = Mdm::Point::Create( 2.5130, 7.5200, 23.7720 );
my $ligandCenter = Mdm::Point::Create( 14.5890, 21.1360, 40.4300 );
my $startingAngles = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 );

# Create the DockedProteinPoseAssembly object which contains
# information about the proteins in the docked complex that
# common to all poses
my $poseAssembly =
$document->CreateDockedProteinPoseAssembly( $ligand, $ligandCenter,
$receptor, $receptorCenter, $startingAngles );

# The next three commands are redundant with the constructor above
# and are only included as example of how they are used.
# However, they can be used to set the DockedProteinPoseAssembly
# properties to different values if desired
$poseAssembly->LigandCenter($ligandCenter);
$poseAssembly->ReceptorCenter($receptorCenter);
$poseAssembly->StartingAngles($startingAngles);

# Set the ZDock grid size and grid spacing
# These values are internally used by the ZDock program
# they are stored mainly to be able to produce input files
# for the Process Poses and Refine Docked Protein protocols
$poseAssembly->SetPropertyAsInteger( "N", $N );
$poseAssembly->SetPropertyAsReal( "spacing", $spacing );
$poseAssembly->HideProperty("N");
$poseAssembly->HideProperty("spacing");

$poseAssembly->SetProperty( "Center", "Receptor" );
$poseAssembly->Name = "Docked Poses";

# Generate the numeric data for the first docked pose
# All numerical values taken from pose 1 of ZDock run output
my $position = Mdm::Point::Create( -5.1821, 20.9576, 21.2807 );
my $translation = Mdm::Point::Create( 6.0000, -16.8000, 2.4000 );
my $rotation = Mdm::Point::Create( 120.0000, 171.0266, 111.9815 );
my $cluster = 1;
my $topClusterPose = 1;
my ( $receptorCenterX, $receptorCenterY, $receptorCenterZ ) =
( 0.018, 14.954, 22.56 );
my ( $ligandCenterX, $ligandCenterY, $ligandCenterZ ) =
( 12.464, 24.22, 40.03 );

# Generate a new pose. The parameters of the constructor function are
# the position of the spherical pose representation
# the translation of the ligand from the starting to the docked position
# the rotation of the ligand from the starting to the docked position
# the cluster the pose belongs to
# whether or not the pose is the best ranked pose in the cluster 
my $newPose =
$poseAssembly->CreateProteinPose( $position, $translation, $rotation,
$cluster, $topClusterPose );

# The following sets of number represent the coordinates center of the binding interface
# on the receptor and the ligand. The values are store as properties which are
# used to toggle between receptor and ligand centric views in the DS client
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_x", "$receptorCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_y", "$receptorCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_z", "$receptorCenterZ" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_x", "$ligandCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_y", "$ligandCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_z", "$ligandCenterZ" );

# Set the name of the pose
$newPose->Name = "Pose1";

# Generate the numeric data for a second docked pose.
# All numerical values taken from pose 2 of ZDock run output
my $position = Mdm::Point::Create( 6.1596049, 17.94953, 5.095075 );
my $translation = Mdm::Point::Create( 4.8000, -14.4000, 4.8000 );
my $rotation = Mdm::Point::Create( 90.0000, 107.4457, 6.1356 );
my $cluster = 1;
my $topClusterPose = 0;
my ( $receptorCenterX, $receptorCenterY, $receptorCenterZ ) =
( 6.88, 14.615, 5.83 );
my ( $ligandCenterX, $ligandCenterY, $ligandCenterZ ) =
( 2.522, 27.292, 11.48 );
$newPose =
$poseAssembly->CreateProteinPose( $position, $translation, $rotation,
$cluster, $topClusterPose );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_x", "$receptorCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_y", "$receptorCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_z", "$receptorCenterZ" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_x", "$ligandCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_y", "$ligandCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_z", "$ligandCenterZ" );
$newPose->Name = "Pose2";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Create a distance constraint (7.5 to 9.5 angstroms) between O and [N,O,S]
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create Mdm::Array to store atoms to use for distance constraint.
my $atoms = Mdm::Array::Create();

# Create an oxygen atom at (-15.6, 2.2, 0.0).
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -15.6, 2.2, 0 );
$atoms->AddItem($atomObject);

# Create a Nitrogen atom at (-7.2, 2.3, 0.0).
my $molecule1 = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject1 = $molecule1->CreateAtom("N");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -7.2, 2.3, 0 );
$atoms->AddItem($atomObject1);

# Create an 'AND' query containing the selected molecules (all
# molecules are used if none selected). This will be used as the
# top level for the distance constraint.
$document->CreateAndTopology();

# Get the Root operator.
my $operators = $document->QueryOperators;
my $rootOperator;
foreach my $operator (@$operators)
{
if ( $operator->IsRoot )
{
$rootOperator = $operator;
}
}

# Create the distance constraint off the root operator.
my $distanceConstraint =
$rootOperator->CreateDistanceFeature( $atoms, 7.5, 9.5 );

# Get N QueryAtom and change it to N,O,S.
my $queryAtoms = $document->QueryAtoms;
foreach my $queryAtom (@$queryAtoms)
{
my $atomList = $queryAtom->GetProperty("List");
if ( $atomList eq 'N' )
{
$queryAtom->SetProperty( "List", "N O S" );
$queryAtom->Parent()->Select; # select it for the color command below
}
}

# Color the QueryAtom with multiple definitions another color
$document->SetColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 170, 85, 127 ) );
$document->DeselectAll();
```

```text
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# The query bonds are automatically created using
# the CreateAndTopology function. However, to show

# them and then add them again.

my $querybonds = $document->QueryBonds;
foreach my $querybond (@$querybonds)
{

}
$document->DeleteObjects();

my $bonds = $document->Bonds;
foreach my $bond (@$bonds)
{
my $querybond =
$document->QueryOperators()->Item(0)->CreateQueryBond($bond);
$querybond->AddBondType('queryAnyBond');
}

# removes the first query bond's bond type
$document->QueryBonds->Item(0)->RemoveBondType('queryAnyBond');
```

# Mdm::Rational::Create function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdm__rational__create_function.htm

## Mdm::Rational::Create function

### Description

Create creates one or more Mdm::Rational objects.

### Applies to

The Mdm::Rational::Create function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Rational

### Using the Mdm::Rational::Create function

#### Static

my $rationalObject = Mdm::Rational::Create( [numerator], [denominator] );

my $rationalObject = Mdm::Rational::Create( { Numerator => [numerator], Denominator => [denominator] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $rationalObject | | | Mdm::Rational |
| [denominator] | Optional | 1 | Integer |
| [numerator] | Optional | | Integer |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to perceive aromatic bonds.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Subroutine to print bond orders and formal charges.
sub ListBondOrderAndCharge($$)
{
my ( $document, $bonds ) = @_;

my $index = 0;
foreach my $b (@$bonds)
{
my $charge1 =
$b->Atom1->FormalCharge->Numerator /
$b->Atom1->FormalCharge->Denominator;
my $charge2 =
$b->Atom2->FormalCharge->Numerator /
$b->Atom2->FormalCharge->Denominator;
print ++$index
. ') Bond: '
. $b->Atom1->Name . "("
. $charge2 . ") to:"
. $b->Atom2->Name . " ("
. $charge2 . ")"
. " order: "
. $b->BondOrder . "\n";
}
print "\n";
sleep(3);
$document->UpdateViews();
}

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1C(=O)[O-]');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $bonds = $molecule->Bonds;
my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms;
print "Initial formal charges and bonds orders:\n";
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );

print "Modified formal charges and bonds orders...\n";
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( $atom->Element eq 'O' )
{
$atom->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 2 );
my $carbon = $atom->AttachedAtom(0);
my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $carbon, $atom );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::partialDoubleBond;
}
}
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );

print "Localizing bond orders and formal charges...\n\n";
$molecule->LocalizeBonds();
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );

print "De-localizing bond orders and formal charges...\n\n";
$molecule->PerceiveAromaticBonds();
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );
```

# Mdm::Rational class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdm__rational_class.htm

## Mdm::Rational class

### Description

The Mdm::Rational is a rational number (a fraction) representing the ratio of
two integers.

### Using the Mdm::Rational object

The Mdm::Rational object can be accessed via the MdmDiscoveryScript package.

#### Properties

ClassName , Denominator , Numerator

#### Functions

Mdm::Rational::Create

#### Used by

FormalCharge

#### Returned by

FormalCharge , Mdm::Rational::Create

#### Derived from

DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

```text
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $alanineCount = 0;

my $residues = $document->Residues;

{

++$cysteineCount if ( $residue->Type eq Mdm::cys );
++$alanineCount if ( $residue->LongName eq 'Alanine' );
}

printf "Number of cysteine residues: %d \n", $cysteineCount;
printf "Number of alanine residues: %d \n", $alanineCount;
printf "Protein sequence is: %s\n", $sequence;
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Fix the backbone
my $backbone = FilterByString( $document, ':CA,C,N,O,HN,HA' );
$document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($backbone);

# Restrain beta carbon atoms
my $cbeta = FilterByString( $document, ':CB' );
$document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint( $cbeta, 10, Mdm::BestFit );

# Add cross-strand distance restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "THR2:CA" );
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "ILE34:CA" );
$document->CreateDistanceRestraint(
{
ArrayOfAtoms1 => $atom1,
ArrayOfAtoms2 => $atom2,
RMin => 2,
RMax => 5,
RMinForceConstant => 10,
RMaxForceConstant => 20,
ForceMaximum => 20
}
);

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
$document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);

# Print the total number of restraints (4)
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
print "There are ", $constraints->Count, " constraints\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create some features on the query
# Create a ring aromatic
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Name("benzene");
my $ringAromaticOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$ringAromaticOperator->Name('RA1');
my $ringAromaticFeatureObject =
$ringAromaticOperator->CreateRingAromaticFeature(
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Atoms );
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Select(); # delete later

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature(
$ringAromaticFeatureObject->CentroidFeature(), 1.6 );
my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature(
$ringAromaticFeatureObject->NormalFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create a donor feature
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -2, -4, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# Give the hydrogen bond donor a higher weight (2.0) than the default (1.0)
$donorOperator->Weight(2.0);

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create an acceptor feature at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );

printf "%s Head: x: %.4f y: %.4f z: %.4f\n",
$locationFeatureHead->ClassName, 
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->X, 
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->Y,
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->Z;

my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

printf "%s Tail: x: %.4f y: %.4f z: %.4f\n",
$locationFeatureHead->ClassName,
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->X, 
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->Y,
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->Z;

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

## Mdm::RingPerception class

### Description

The Mdm::RingPerception returns information about bonded rings of atoms.

### Using the Mdm::RingPerception object

The Mdm::RingPerception object can be accessed via the MdmDiscoveryScript package.

#### Properties

AllPerceivedAromaticRingBonds , AllPerceivedRingAtoms , AllPerceivedRingBonds , AromaticRingCount , ClassName , PerceivedLonePairDonors , PerceivedRingAtoms , PerceivedRingBonds , RingCount

#### Returned by

PerceiveRings

#### Derived from

DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the perceive rings class.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $smilesString =
'O=C(C/C1=C/C=C[S]1)N(Cc2ccccc2OC)[C@@]([H])(c3cc(OC)c(cc3)OC)C(=O)N[C@]4([H])CCCCC4';

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles($smilesString);

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
foreach my $molecule (@$molecules)
{
my $ringPerception = $molecule->PerceiveRings(
{
FindSmallestSetOfRings => True,
PerceiveAromaticity => True,
FindLonePairDonors => True
}
);

my $ringCount = $ringPerception->RingCount;
my $aromaticRingCount = $ringPerception->AromaticRingCount;

print "Ring analysis of molecule: $smilesString\n";
print "Molecule has: " . $ringCount . " rings\n";
print "Molecule has: " . $aromaticRingCount . " aromatic rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all atoms in rings.
my $ringAtoms = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedRingAtoms;
print "Molecule has: " . $ringAtoms->Count . " atoms in rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all bonds in rings.
my $ringBonds = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedRingBonds;
print "Molecule has: " . $ringBonds->Count . " bonds in rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all aromatic bonds in rings.
my $aromaticRingBonds = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedAromaticRingBonds;
print "Molecule has: "
. $aromaticRingBonds->Count
. " aromatic bonds in rings.\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all lone pair donor atoms in aromatic rings.
my $lonePairDonors = $ringPerception->PerceivedLonePairDonors;
print "Molecule has: "
. $lonePairDonors->Count
. " lone pair donor atoms in rings.\n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $ringCount ; ++$index )
{

# Get an Mdm::Array of atoms in the specified ring.
my $atoms = $ringPerception->PerceivedRingAtoms($index);

# Get an Mdm::Array of bonds in the specified ring.
my $bonds = $ringPerception->PerceivedRingBonds($index);

my $ringnum = $index + 1;
print "Ring ( $ringnum ) contains "
. $atoms->Count
. " atoms and "
. $bonds->Count
. " bonds.\n";
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to create rotatable bond monitors for a molecule.
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Remove all atoms except the first ligand found.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
$ligands->Item(0)->Select();
$document->InvertSelection();
$document->DeleteObjects();
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

print "Creating rotatable bond monitors for ligand...\n";
my $rotatableBondMonitorCount = $molecule->CreateRotatableBondMonitors();
print "Found $rotatableBondMonitorCount rotatable bonds.\n";
my $arrayrotbonds = $document->RotatableBondMonitors; 
print "Number of rotatable bonds monitors: ". $arrayrotbonds->Count. "\n";

my $j = 0;
foreach my $monitor (@$arrayrotbonds) { 
my @IDs = ();
for (my $i = 0; $i < 4; ++$i) {
my $atom = $monitor->Object($i);
push (@IDs,$atom->Id. " " . $atom->Name );
}
my $IDscal = join(", ", @IDs);
printf "%3i) Id/Name: %s Torsion %.4f\n ", ++$j, $IDscal , $monitor->Angle;
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
```

Source type: HTML

## Mdm::Set class

### Description

The Mdm::Set is a collection of elements as a set. For example, using set collections, you can find the intersection of two sets.
Other operations include: union, exclusive OR, and difference. In addition to these functions, you can set the size of the
collection, add and remove elements from the collection, and construct the set collection in various ways.

The Mdm::Set object can be accessed via the MdmDiscoveryScript package.

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the MarkSideChainConformationViolations function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9ins.pdb" );

printf "Structure %s atoms: %d residues %d\n", $document->ModelName, 
$document->Atoms->Count, $document->Residues->Count;

# Mark side chain conformation violations.
my $pink = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 255, 200, 200 );
$document->MarkSideChainConformationViolations( Mdm::oldfieldRotamerLibrary, 30.0, $pink );

# Note: if you want to use the mainchain-dependent Dunbrack library, the second
# argument is a sigma multiplier rather than an angle tolerance, thus:
$document->MarkSideChainConformationViolations( Mdm::dunbrackRotamerLibrary, 3.0 );

# Get the side chain conformation violation monitors.
my $monitors =
$document->FilterByProperty('SidechainConformationMonitor name="*"');

# Report the number of violations.
my $violationCount = $monitors->Count;
printf "Structure has %d side-chain conformation violations.\n\n",$violationCount;
# Print a table of violations.
if ( $violationCount > 0 )
{
printf("Index\t Name\t\t Residue \t\tChi Angles\n");
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $violationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s\t",
$index+1, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Residues") );
foreach (qw(Chi1 Chi2 Chi3 Chi4)) {
my $_chi = $monitor->GetProperty($_); 
printf("%8.3f ",$_chi ) if defined $_chi;
}
print("\n"); 
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

## Mdm::SlicingPlane class

### Description

The Mdm::SlicingPlane is a plane in three dimensions specified by
an origin and a normal vector. The normal vector determines
the orientation of the slicing plane.
Objects or parts of objects which lie on the opposite side of
the slicing plane's normal vector are not displayed in the
Graphics view.

Mdm::Geometric3d -> Mdm::Object -> DiscoveryScript::Object

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Creates an empty molecule
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();

# Create oxygen atoms
my $O1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);
my $O2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

# Assign coordinates to atoms
my $xyz1 = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O1->XYZ = $xyz1;

my $xyz2 = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O2->XYZ = $xyz2;

# Create Spheres centered on atom position
my $sphere1 = $O1->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz1, Radius => 0.4 } );
my $sphere2 = $O2->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz2, Radius => 0.4 } );

# Create Cylinder
my $cylinder =
$O1->CreateCylinder( { Begin => $xyz1, End => $xyz2, Radius => 0.2 } );
my $bottom = $cylinder->{BottomCenter};
printf "Cylinder bottom center: %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n Radius: %8.3f\n",
$bottom->X, $bottom->Y, $bottom->Z, $cylinder->Radius;

# Make cylinder transparent
$cylinder->IsTransparent(True);

# Create a slicing plane perpendicular to the cylinder axis
my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
my $slicingplaneObject = $document->CreateSlicingPlane(
{
Index => 1,
ArrayOfObjects => $atoms,
Origin => Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 ),
Normal => Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 )
}
);

# Get all 3D Objects
my $objects3d = $document->Geometric3ds;

# Print their name and class name
foreach my $object (@$objects3d)
{
print $object->ClassName . "\t" . $object->Name . "\n";
}

# Get all slicing planes
my $slicplanes = $document->SlicingPlanes;
print "Number of slicing planes" . $slicplanes->Count. "\n";
```

#### Properties

AxisOriginType , CellChoice , ClassName , FullSymbol , LatticeType , Number , SchoenfliesSymbol , Symbol , SymmetryOperationCount , SymmetryOperator

#### Returned by

SpaceGroup

#### Derived from

DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use Mdm::SpaceGroup objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Get space group from document.
my $cell = $document->Cells->Item(0);
my $spacegroup = $cell->SpaceGroup;

print "The following is a list of space group properties:\n";
print "Number:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->Number . "\n";
print "Short Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->Symbol . "\n";
print "SchoenfliesSymbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->SchoenfliesSymbol . "\n";
print "Full Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->FullSymbol . "\n";
print "Lattice type:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->LatticeType . "\n";
print "Cell choice:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->CellChoice . "\n";
print "AxisOriginType:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->AxisOriginType . "\n";
print "Number of sym. operator:\t\t"
. $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount . "\n";

my $count = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $operator = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperator($index);
print "Symmetry operator $index\n";
print "\tName: " . $operator->Name . "\n";

my $rotation = $operator->Rotation;
my $format = "\t %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n";
print "\tRotation Matrix:\n";
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 0, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 1, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 2 );

my $translation = $operator->Translation;
print "\tTranslation:\n";
printf "$format", $translation->X, $translation->Y, $translation->Z;
}
```

```text
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 2 );

my $translation = $operator->Translation;
print "\tTranslation:\n";
printf "$format", $translation->X, $translation->Y, $translation->Z;
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Creates an empty molecule
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();

# Create oxygen atoms
my $O1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);
my $O2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

# Assign coordinates to atoms
my $xyz1 = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O1->XYZ = $xyz1;

my $xyz2 = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O2->XYZ = $xyz2;

# Create Spheres centered on atom position
my $sphere1 = $O1->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz1, Radius => 0.4 } );
my $sphere2 = $O2->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz2, Radius => 0.4 } );

# Create Cylinder
my $cylinder =
$O1->CreateCylinder( { Begin => $xyz1, End => $xyz2, Radius => 0.2 } );
my $bottom = $cylinder->{BottomCenter};
printf "Cylinder bottom center: %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n Radius: %8.3f\n",
$bottom->X, $bottom->Y, $bottom->Z, $cylinder->Radius;

# Make cylinder transparent
$cylinder->IsTransparent(True);

# Create a slicing plane perpendicular to the cylinder axis
my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
my $slicingplaneObject = $document->CreateSlicingPlane(
{
Index => 1,
ArrayOfObjects => $atoms,
Origin => Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 ),
Normal => Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 )
}
);

# Get all 3D Objects
my $objects3d = $document->Geometric3ds;

# Print their name and class name
foreach my $object (@$objects3d)
{
print $object->ClassName . "\t" . $object->Name . "\n";
}

# Get all slicing planes
my $slicplanes = $document->SlicingPlanes;
print "Number of slicing planes" . $slicplanes->Count. "\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to create a transparent surface.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '101m.pdb' );

# Select heme atoms.
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="HEM.*"; Atom label="*"');

# Create an array of all heme atoms.
my $hemeAtoms = $document->Filter( { Selected => 1 } )->Atoms;

# Create transparent surface around the heme group.
my $transparentSurface =
$document->CreateTransparentSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential,
1.3, 0.6 );

$transparentSurface->IsBackSideColorEnabled(True);
$transparentSurface->IsBackSideTransparencyEnabled(True);

# Also create wiremesh surface around the heme group.
my $wiremeshSurface =
$document->CreateWiremeshSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential, 2.0 );

print "Surface area: "
. $transparentSurface->Area . "\n"
. "Surface Volume: "
. $transparentSurface->Volume . "\n";
print "Surface probe radius: "
. $transparentSurface->ProbeRadius . "\n"
. "Transparency Level: "
. $transparentSurface->TransparencyLevel . "\n";

# Select all atoms within 6A of the heme and the surface.
$document->SelectByRadius( 6.0, 'Atom' );
$transparentSurface->Select();

# Show only the heme and neighboring atoms (other than water).
$document->FitView();
$document->InvertSelection();
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue name="HOH.*"; Atom label="*"');
$document->Hide();
$document->DeselectAll();

# Display the wiremesh surface with delay.
sleep(2);
$wiremeshSurface->SetVisible();
```

# Mdm::TorsionMonitor class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdm__torsionmonitor_class.htm

## Mdm::TorsionMonitor class

### Description

The Mdm::TorsionMonitor monitors the dihedral angle between two planes. The two planes are defined by the coordinates of four geometric objects.
Each plane shares the two geometric objects from the intersection between the two planes. Every torsion monitor requires four unique
geometric objects to calculate a dihedral angle. If the four geometric objects are called A, B, C, and D, then one plane is
defined by the points ABC and the other plane by the points BCD.

### Using the Mdm::TorsionMonitor object

The Mdm::TorsionMonitor object can be accessed via the MdmDiscoveryScript package.

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
# This script illustrates how to perform a molecular overlay.
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use SbdDiscoveryScript;

# Create a new MDM document.
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $name1 = 'Molecule1';
my $name2 = 'Molecule2';

my %MolecSMARTS = (
$name1 => 'O=C([O-])C1=CC(=CC=C1)C([O-])=O',
$name2 => 'C/C1=C/C=C(C=C1)C([O-])=O'
);

# Insert two molecules 'Molecule1' and 'Molecule2' from SMILES strings.
$document->InsertFromSmiles( $MolecSMARTS{$name1} );
my $molecule1 = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
$molecule1->Name($name1);

$document->InsertFromSmiles( $MolecSMARTS{$name2} );
my $molecule2 = $document->Molecules->Item(1);
$molecule2->Name($name2);

# name of the overlay similarity property
my $overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay Similarity/' . $molecule1->Name;

# Add rotatable bond monitors to both molecules.
# These are used with flexible field alignment.
$document->AddRotatableBondMonitors;

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection(10.0, 5.0, 0.0);
$document->DeselectAll;

# Calculate the similarity before the rigid field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using rigid field alignment, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated similarity is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Rigid field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the similarity before the rigid field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using rigid field alignment.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False
}
);

printf( "Rigid field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection(5.0, 10.0, 0.0);
$document->DeselectAll;

# Calculate the similarity before flexible field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using flexible field alignment, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated similarity is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Flexible field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the similarity before flexible field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay molecules using flexible field alignment.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True
}
);

$overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay Similarity/' . $molecule1->Name;
printf( "Flexible field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

#
# Overlay molecules using tethers (tuple monitors).
#

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection( 10, 10, 5 );
$document->DeselectAll;

my $molecule1Atoms = $molecule1->Atoms;
my $molecule2Atoms = $molecule2->Atoms;

# atom mapping indices
my %atomIndices = (
0 => 8,
2 => 9,
6 => 1
);

print(" Overlay with atom tethers\n");
foreach my $id1 (sort {$a <=> $b} keys %atomIndices) {
my $id2 = $atomIndices{$id1};
my $tupleArray = Mdm::Array::Create();
$tupleArray->AddItem( $molecule1Atoms->Item($id1) );
$tupleArray->AddItem( $molecule2Atoms->Item($id2) );
$document->CreateTupleMonitor($tupleArray);
printf( " Map %s atom: %d to: %s atom: %d\n",
$molecule1->Name, $id1 + 1, $molecule2->Name, $id2 + 1 );
}

# name of the property
$overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay RMS/' . $molecule1->Name;

# Calculate the RMSD value before the alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using tethers, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated RMSD is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the RMSD value before the alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using tethers.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Remove the tethers
my $monitors = $document->TupleMonitors;
foreach my $monitor (@$monitors)
{
$monitor->Select;
}
$document->DeleteObjects;

$document->FitView;
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdm__unsatisfiednonbond_class.htm

## Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond class

### Description

The Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond identifies an atom as being a conventional
hydrogen donor, hydrogen acceptor, or charged atom but not participating
in an Mdm::Nonbond interaction.
Unsatisfied interactions are not monitored if the Mdm::NonbondMonitor 's enum Mdm::MolecularScope is intermolecular or if the enum Mdm::MonitoredPairScope is interactionsExternalToMonitoredScope.
In both cases, it is not possible to distinguish between a non-bond
outside of the search scope and a truly unsatisfied interaction.
The same argument applies when the enum Mdm::MonitoredPairScope scope is interactionsWithinMonitoredScope.
However in this case, the unsatisfied non-bond atoms near the surface that are available to form interactions are highlighted.

### Using the Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond object

The Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond object can be accessed via the MdmDiscoveryScript package.

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use of unsatisfied non-bonds.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "3fzm.pdb" );
die "Failed to create a valid MDM document!" unless $document;

my $ligandNonbondMonitor =
$document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor(
{RequirePredefinedLigand=>False});

$document->FocusOnFirstLigand;
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
$ligandNonbondMonitor->IsNonbondTypeShown(Mdm::nonInteracting) = True;

for (my $index = 0; $index < 3; ++$index)
{
my $unsatisfiedNonbonds = $ligandNonbondMonitor->UnsatisfiedNonbonds;

printf "Shell: %d\n", $ligandNonbondMonitor->Shell;
foreach my $unsatisfied (@$unsatisfiedNonbonds)
{
printf "Unsatisfied interaction on atom %s of type(s) %s\n", 
$unsatisfied->Name, $unsatisfied->ChemistryName;
}

$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of ValenceMonitor objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "3ptb.pdb" );

# Creates a hydrogen-bond monitor between ligand and receptor atoms.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $monitor = $document->CreateValenceMonitor($ligandAtoms);

$monitor->IsUnderValenceShown = True;

print "Found " . $monitor->OverValenceCount . " atoms over valence.\n";
print "Found " . $monitor->UnderValenceCount . " atoms under valence.\n";

my $valences = $monitor->Valences;

my $count = $valences->Count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $valence = $valences->Item($index);
printf "Expected valence (for %s): %d \t Current valence: %d\n",
$valence->Name, $valence->ExpectedValence, $valence->Valence;
}
```

# MdmCommands package

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

## MdmCommands package

### Description

MdmCommands provides high-level functions for accessing functionality
within MdmDiscoveryScript . These commands provide a more simple interface
to working with molecules.

### Using the MdmCommands package

Access to the MdmCommands API is through the Perl use directive:

```text
use strict;
use MdmCommands;
```

The strict directive is optional, but strongly recommended as it restricts
the use of unsafe constructs. All available classes will be imported from the MdmCommands module.

# MdmSequenceResidues function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mdmsequenceresidues_function.htm

## MdmSequenceResidues function

### Description

MdmSequenceResidues returns the Mdm::Residue objects
that correspond to an Sdm::Sequence object. In general,
only a subset of the Mdm::Residue s in an Mdm::Molecule are mapped to an Sdm::Sequence .
This method returns only the linked subset.

### Applies to

The MdmSequenceResidues function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the MdmSequenceResidues function

#### Static

my $arrayObject = Sdm::AminoAcidSequence::MdmSequenceResidues( <molecule>, [dna] );

my $arrayObject = Sdm::AminoAcidSequence::MdmSequenceResidues( { Molecule => <molecule>, Dna => [dna] } );

my $arrayObject = Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence::MdmSequenceResidues( <molecule>, [dna] );

my $arrayObject = Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence::MdmSequenceResidues( { Molecule => <molecule>, Dna => [dna] } );

my $arrayObject = Sdm::Sequence::MdmSequenceResidues( <molecule>, [dna] );

my $arrayObject = Sdm::Sequence::MdmSequenceResidues( { Molecule => <molecule>, Dna => [dna] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| <molecule> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| [dna] | Optional | False | Boolean |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script will illustrate the use of Sdm::Sequence::MdmSequenceResidues.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3CRO');

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

my $aaResidues = Sdm::Sequence::MdmSequenceResidues($molecule);
print 'Found ' . $aaResidues->Count 
. ' Mdm::Residues corresponding to an amino acid sequence out of '
. $molecule->Residues->Count . " total residues \n";

my $naResidues = Sdm::Sequence::MdmSequenceResidues($molecule, True);
print 'Found ' . $naResidues->Count 
. ' Mdm::Residues corresponding to a nucleic acid sequence out of '
. $molecule->Residues->Count . " total residues \n";
```

# MedlineId property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/medlineid_property.htm

## MedlineId property

### Description

MedlineId specifies the Medline ID in a Sdm::Publication .

### Applies to

The MedlineId property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Publication

### Using the MedlineId property

#### Get

my $stringValue = $object->MedlineId;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $object | | | Sdm::Publication |

#### Set

$object->MedlineId = <id>;

$object->MedlineId( <id> );

$object->MedlineId( { Id => <id> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <id> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Sdm::Publication |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Publication class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'Y13252-truncated',
'TCTAGAGTAACATTTAGAATTAAGGTGGGAAATTATCTTAAAATCT' );

my $title =
'Nonfixed duplication containing the Adh gene and a truncated form '
. 'of the Adhr gene in the Drosophila funebris species group: different '
. 'modes of evolution of Adh relative to Adhr in Drosophila';

# Create publication object with sample data.
my $publication01 = Sdm::Publication::Create( 'Amador, A., Juan, E.',
$title, 'Molec. Biol. Evol.' );

# Create publication and add content separately.
my $publication02 = Sdm::Publication::Create();
$publication02->Authors = 'Amador, A., Juan, E.';
$publication02->Title = $title;
$publication02->Journal = 'Molec. Biol. Evol.';
$publication02->Reference = '16(11): 1439--1456 (1999)';
$publication02->PubMedId = '10555275';
$publication02->Comment = 'y13252';

#$publication02->Consortium = '';
#$publication02->DigitalObjectId = '';
#$publication02->MedlineId = '';
#$publication02->PubMedId = '';

# Associate publications with a sequence object.
# NOTE: To see the publications in Discovery Studio, double-click on the
# sequence in the sequence window to open a sequence annotation window.
# Publications are listed in the data table's Literature Citation tab.
$sequence->AddPublication($publication01);
$sequence->AddPublication($publication02);

my $publicationCount = $sequence->PublicationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $publicationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $publication = $sequence->Publication($index);
printf "%d: %s, %s. %s %s.\n",
$index + 1,
$publication->Authors,
$publication->Title,
$publication->Journal,
$publication->Reference;
}

$sequence->DeletePublication(0);
```

my $arrayObject = $object->MembraneOrientationMonitors;

#### Defined by

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use properties of the MembraneOrientationMonitor
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load structure of BOVINE RHODOPSIN, 1f88 and keep only first chain
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# "Guess" some value for the membrane position
my $center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, -3.2 );
my $normal = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.521, 0.106, 0.847 );

my $membrane =
$document->CreateMembrane( $center, $normal, 60.0, 60.0, 30.0 );

$document->SetParent( $molecule, $membrane );

my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms();

# Illustrate on how to use MembraneOrientationMonitor preferences
my $membraneOrientation =
$molecule->CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor( $membrane, $atoms,
Mdm::objectCentered, Mdm::referenceAxisZ );

$document->UpdateViews();

my $monitors = $document->MembraneOrientationMonitors;
print "Number of membrane monitors: ". $monitors->Count. "\n";

my $membranes = $document->Membranes;
print "Number of membranes: ". $membranes->Count. "\n";

sleep(2);

$membraneOrientation->DisplayLocation = Mdm::membraneCentered;
$membraneOrientation->ProteinReferenceAxis = Mdm::referenceAxisX;
```

# MembraneRotation property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/membranerotation_property.htm

## MembraneRotation property

### Description

MembraneRotation specifies the rotation of the Mdm::Membrane object with respect to the principal axis of
a set of protein atoms. The rotation angle is the angle between and the second principal axis of the set of atoms and
the normal to the plane defined by the first principal axis and the membrane normal.

### Applies to

The MembraneRotation property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::MembraneOrientationMonitor

### Using the MembraneRotation property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->MembraneRotation;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::MembraneOrientationMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with membranes.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

# Remove all chains except the first.
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# "Guess" some value for the membrane position
my $center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, -3.2 );
my $normal = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.521, 0.106, 0.847 );

my $membrane =
$document->CreateMembrane( $center, $normal, 60.0, 60.0, 30.0 );

# Pick a different color scheme from default
$membrane->CytosolColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 255 ) );
$membrane->ExtracellularColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 255, 255, 0 ) );

$document->SetParent( $molecule, $membrane );

my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms();

my $membraneOrientation =
$molecule->CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor( $membrane, $atoms,
Mdm::objectCentered, Mdm::referenceAxisZ );
my $shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
my $tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
my $rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);

$document->UpdateViews();

sleep(4);

$center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, 3.2 );
$normal = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.521, -0.106, -0.847 );

$membrane->Thickness = 35;
$membrane->Normal = $normal;
$membrane->Center = $center;
$document->UpdateObjects();

$shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
$tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
$rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);
```

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use properties of the MembraneOrientationMonitor
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load structure of BOVINE RHODOPSIN, 1f88 and keep only first chain
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# "Guess" some value for the membrane position
my $center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, -3.2 );
my $normal = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.521, 0.106, 0.847 );

my $membrane =
$document->CreateMembrane( $center, $normal, 60.0, 60.0, 30.0 );

$document->SetParent( $molecule, $membrane );

my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms();

# Illustrate on how to use MembraneOrientationMonitor preferences
my $membraneOrientation =
$molecule->CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor( $membrane, $atoms,
Mdm::objectCentered, Mdm::referenceAxisZ );

$document->UpdateViews();

my $monitors = $document->MembraneOrientationMonitors;
print "Number of membrane monitors: ". $monitors->Count. "\n";

my $membranes = $document->Membranes;
print "Number of membranes: ". $membranes->Count. "\n";

sleep(2);

$membraneOrientation->DisplayLocation = Mdm::membraneCentered;
$membraneOrientation->ProteinReferenceAxis = Mdm::referenceAxisX;
```

## MembraneShift property
