| $object | | | Mdm::MembraneOrientationMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with membranes.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

# Remove all chains except the first.
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# "Guess" some value for the membrane position
my $center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, -3.2 );
my $normal = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.521, 0.106, 0.847 );

my $membrane =
$document->CreateMembrane( $center, $normal, 60.0, 60.0, 30.0 );

# Pick a different color scheme from default
$membrane->CytosolColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 255 ) );
$membrane->ExtracellularColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 255, 255, 0 ) );

$document->SetParent( $molecule, $membrane );

my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms();

my $membraneOrientation =
$molecule->CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor( $membrane, $atoms,
Mdm::objectCentered, Mdm::referenceAxisZ );
my $shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
my $tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
my $rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);

$document->UpdateViews();

sleep(4);

$center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, 3.2 );
$normal = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.521, -0.106, -0.847 );

$membrane->Thickness = 35;
$membrane->Normal = $normal;
$membrane->Center = $center;
$document->UpdateObjects();

$shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
$tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
$rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);
```

# MergeChains function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mergechains_function.htm

## MergeChains function

### Description

Merges the contents of one chain into another. If a destination chain is not specified, then the contents of the given chain will be merged into the preceding chain of the same type (AminoAcidChain, NucleicAcidChain or generic Chain). In the case of AminoAcidChains, then the terminal chemistry will be removed from the original C-terminal and N-terminal as apt, including removing any capping group at the N-terminal. If the C and N atoms at the join are within bonding distance a peptide bond will be created

### Applies to

The MergeChains function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the MergeChains function

#### Command

$object->MergeChains( <chaintomerge>, [chaintomergeinto] );

$object->MergeChains( { ChainToMerge => <chaintomerge>, ChainToMergeInto => [chaintomergeinto] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <chaintomerge> | Required | | Mdm::Chain |
| [chaintomergeinto] | Optional | | Mdm::Chain |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
# Demonstrates the use of the SwapChainOrder, MergeChains and SplitChain
# functions.
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;

#Note - this script should be run from DS client 

# subroutine to print information about the structure
sub PrintInfo($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
printf( " Number of molecules %d\n", $molecules->Count );
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $molecules->Count ; ++$index )
{
my $molecule = $molecules->Item($index);
printf( " molecule number %d name %s\n",
$index + 1, $molecule->Name );
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
for ( my $index2 = 0 ; $index2 < $chains->Count ; ++$index2 )
{
my $chain = $chains->Item($index2);
printf(
" chain number %d name %s number of residues %d\n",
$index2 + 1,
$chain->Name, $chain->Residues->Count
);
}
}
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4ins.pdb" );

$document->InvokeAction('ActionViewHierarchy');

print("Before swap:\n");
PrintInfo($document);

$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

my $chains = $document->Chains();

$document->SwapChainOrder($chains->Item(0),$chains->Item(1));

print("after swap 1 and 2:\n");
PrintInfo($document);
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

$document->MergeChains($chains->Item(3),$chains->Item(2));

print ("after merge 3 and 4:\n");
PrintInfo($document);
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

my $chainsNow = $document->Chains();
my $residues = $chainsNow->Item(0)->Residues();

#find a residue somewhere in the middle of the first chain
my $numRes = $residues->Count();
my $breakRes = $residues->Item( int($numRes/2) );

$document->SplitChain($breakRes);

print("After splitting chain 1:\n");

PrintInfo($document);

print("You should now have amino acid chains B,B,A,C with the ion/water chains unaffected.\n");

# update view
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# MergeQueries function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mergequeries_function.htm

## MergeQueries function

### Description

MergeQueries merges the queries in the supplied collection into a single query.
The objects in the supplied collection must be queries.

### Applies to

The MergeQueries function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the MergeQueries function

#### Command

$object->MergeQueries( <query>, <querytomerge> );

$object->MergeQueries( { Query => <query>, QueryToMerge => <querytomerge> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <query> | Required | | Mdm::Query |
| <querytomerge> | Required | | Mdm::Query |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty queries
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();
my $query2 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create some features on the queries
# Create a donor feature on query1 at 0,0,0
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# Create an acceptor feature on query2 at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $query2->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

# Merge two queries into one:
my $queries = $document->Queries;
$document->MergeQueries( @$queries[0], @$queries[1] );

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

response to the message can also be retrieved.

the Discovery Studio Visualizer.

my $messageboxresultEnum = DiscoveryScript::MessageBox( <message>, [detailedmessage], [flags], [icon], [position], [donotshownexttimetag] );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |

| [detailedmessage] | Optional | "" | String |
| [donotshownexttimetag] | Optional | "" | String |
| [flags] | Optional | DiscoveryScript::messageBoxFlagsOk | enum DiscoveryScript::MessageBoxFlags |
| [icon] | Optional | DiscoveryScript::messageBoxIconInfo | enum DiscoveryScript::MessageBoxIcon |
| [position] | Optional | DiscoveryScript::dialogPositionCenter | enum DiscoveryScript::DialogPosition |

#### Defined by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use DiscoveryScript;

my $messageBoxResult = DiscoveryScript::MessageBox(
"An example message with Yes and No buttons to allow interactive user input.\nPlease click a button",
"More Detailed information about the message should appear here.\n",
DiscoveryScript::messageBoxFlagsYesNo,
DiscoveryScript::messageBoxIconInfo
);

if ( $messageBoxResult eq DiscoveryScript::messageBoxResultYes )
{
print "You clicked Yes.\n";
}
elsif ( $messageBoxResult eq DiscoveryScript::messageBoxResultNo )
{
print "You clicked No.\n";
}
elsif ( $messageBoxResult eq DiscoveryScript::messageBoxResultCancel )
{
print "You closed the window without answering the question.\n";
}
```

# MinimumAngle property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/minimumangle_property.htm

## MinimumAngle property

### Description

When finding pi-cation interactions, the angle between the cation-centroid vector and the ring plane must be more
than the Minimum Angle (default 45°).

### Applies to

The MinimumAngle property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::PiCationMonitor , Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor

### Using the MinimumAngle property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->MinimumAngle;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::PiCationMonitor Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor |

#### Set

$object->MinimumAngle = <angle>;

$object->MinimumAngle( <angle> );

$object->MinimumAngle( { Angle => <angle> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <angle> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::PiCationMonitor Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script shows how to create pi interaction monitors.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1kim.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Creates pi interaction monitors
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

#if no array of atoms is passed in then the monitor is created
#for the whole molecule (or other object).
my $pipiMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor();
my $piCationMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiCationMonitor();
my $piSigmaMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiSigmaMonitor();

$pipiMonitor->Name = "Pi-Pi";
$piCationMonitor->Name = "Pi-Cation";
$piSigmaMonitor->Name = "Pi-Sigma";

my $piPiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piPiInteractionCount = $piPiInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piPiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

# Change criteria settings to non-default values.
$piCationMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piCationMonitor->MinimumAngle = 60.0;
my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule\n";

$piSigmaMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->MinimumAngle = 30.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->AngleDeviation = 15.0;
my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

$pipiMonitor->MaximumCenterDistance = 7.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumClosestAtomDistance = 4.0;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumLambda = 20.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumTheta = 45.;
my $pipiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount = $pipiInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $pipiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piInteractions = $molecule->PiInteractionMonitors();
my $piCount = $piInteractions->Count();
print "\nThere are " . $piCount . " pi interaction monitors: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $piCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $piInteractions->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Interactions") );
}

#If we want to limit the scope of the monitoring, we can pass in
#an array of atoms. This is similar to creating a monitor from the UI
# when atoms are selected. Pi interactions will then be calculated within
#these, and between these and the parent object
my $residue = FilterByString( $document, "THM1" )->Item(0);
my $atom_array = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $atoms = $residue->Atoms();
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atoms->Count() ; ++$index )
{
$atom_array->AddItem( $atoms->Item($index) );
}
my $pipiMonitor2 = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor($atom_array);
my $pipiInteractions2 = $pipiMonitor2->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount2 = $pipiInteractions2->Count();
print "Number of pi-pi interactions between "
. $residue->Name()
. " and the rest of the molecule: "
. $pipiInteractionCount2 . "\n";

my $picatmonitors = $document->PiCationMonitors;
print "Number of pi-cation monitors: ". $picatmonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pipimonitors = $document->PiPiMonitors;
print "Number of pi-pi monitors: ". $pipimonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pisigmonitors = $document->PiSigmaMonitors;
print "Number of pi-sigma monitors: ". $pisigmonitors->Count . "\n";
```

### Description

MinimumSimilarityTolerance specifies the minimum similarity ratio to
match a shape query.

Mdm::ShapeFeature

### Using the MinimumSimilarityTolerance property

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create napthalene
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c12ccccc1cccc2');

# Create shape query based on napthalene
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();
my $shapeOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryShape');
my $shapefeatureObject =
$shapeOperator->CreateShapeFeature( $document->Atoms );

# Print properties
print "Minimum similarity tolerance: "
. $shapefeatureObject->MinimumSimilarityTolerance . "\n";
print "Maximum similarity tolerance: "
. $shapefeatureObject->MaximumSimilarityTolerance . "\n\n";
print "Minimum volume extents ratio: "
. $shapefeatureObject->MinimumVolumeExtentsRatio . "\n";
print "Maximum volume extents ratio: "
. $shapefeatureObject->MaximumVolumeExtentsRatio . "\n\n";
print "Minimum X, Y, and Z extents: "
. $shapefeatureObject->MinimumXExtentsRatio . ", ";
print $shapefeatureObject->MinimumYExtentsRatio 
. ", and "
. $shapefeatureObject->MinimumZExtentsRatio . "\n";
print "Maximum X, Y, and Z extents: "
. $shapefeatureObject->MaximumXExtentsRatio . ", ";
print $shapefeatureObject->MaximumYExtentsRatio 
. ", and "
. $shapefeatureObject->MaximumZExtentsRatio . "\n\n";

# Change Minimum Similarity from a default of 0.5 to 0.8
$shapefeatureObject->MinimumSimilarityTolerance(0.8);

print "Minimum similarity tolerance is now: "
. $shapefeatureObject->MinimumSimilarityTolerance . "\n";
```

DiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to access open documents.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use ForceFieldDiscoveryScript;
use ChartDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0);

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule($molecule);

my $documents = DiscoveryScript::Documents();
print 'Number of open documents found: ' . $documents->Count . "\n";

my $count = $documents->Count;
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $count )
{
my $document = $documents->Item($index);

print ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: ' . $document->ModelName . "\t";
print 'Model type: ' . $document->ModelType . "\n";
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This scripts illustrates how to access several properties of
# the Mdm::Molecule object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

$molecule->IsChargeCalculated = True;

print "The following is a list of molecule properties:\n";
print 'Name: ' . $molecule->Name . "\n";
print 'Approximate volume: ' . $molecule->ApproximateVolume . "\n";
print 'Atom count: ' . $molecule->AtomCount . "\n";

my $centerOfMass = $molecule->CenterOfMass;
printf "Center of mass: %8.3f\t%8.3f\t%8.3f\n",
$centerOfMass->X,
$centerOfMass->Y,
$centerOfMass->Z;

print 'Chiral center count: ' . $molecule->ChiralCenterCount . "\n";
print 'Composition: ' . $molecule->Composition . "\n";
print 'Density: ' . $molecule->Density . "\n";
print 'Exact molecular weight: ' . $molecule->ExactMolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen bond acceptor count: '
. $molecule->HydrogenBondAcceptorCount . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen bond donor count: '
. $molecule->HydrogenBondDonorCount . "\n";
print 'Lipinski violation count: ' . $molecule->LipinskiViolationCount . "\n";
print 'Molecular formula: ' . $molecule->MolecularFormula . "\n";
print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Radius of gyration: ' . $molecule->RadiusOfGyration . "\n";
print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Rotatable bond count: ' . $molecule->RotatableBondCount . "\n";
print 'Surface area: ' . $molecule->SurfaceArea . "\n";
```

# MolecularOverlay function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/molecularoverlay_function.htm

## MolecularOverlay function

### Description

MolecularOverlay can perform several overlay functions for aligning small molecules, equivalent to the functionality in Structure | Superimpose | Molecular Overlay.

If FieldFit is True, a molecular field based overlay will be performed, otherwise a tether based overlay will be done. For a tether based overlay, the tethers must be defined.

StericPercentage refers to the percentage of a field fit overlay weighted towards the steric field, the remainder will be an electrostatic field. To perform a purely steric alignment, for example, set this to 100. This value is not used for tether based alignments.

TargetMolecule, if specified, is the molecule to target the alignment towards. If you do not specify a target, a consensus alignment will be performed.

If Flexible is True, the alignment will rotate around any specified rotatable bonds (see CreateRotatableBondMonitor) in order to optimize the alignment. Otherwise the alignment will only use the existing conformations of the molecules.

The function will create properties on the molecules containing the results of the alignment. The property "OverlayLabel" will contain a unique name for each molecule, and will be the molecule name if that is unique. Properties beginning "Overlay Similarity" or "Overlay RMSD" will be created for Field or tether based alignments respectively. For example, if you have two molecules called mol1 and mol2 the similarity to mol1 after a field based alignment will be in a property on mol2 called "Overlay Similarity/mol1".

If OverlaySettings is overlayDefault, the molecular properties reflect the results of the alignment and the atomic coordinates of the molecules involved in the alignment are updated.

If OverlaySettings is overlayRestoreCoordinates, the molecular properties reflect the results of the alignment, but the atomic coordinates of the molecules involved in the alignment are not updated.

If OverlaySettings is overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly, alignment is not performed, and the molecular properties are calculated based on the current atomic coordinates.

### Applies to

The MolecularOverlay function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the MolecularOverlay function

#### Instance

$object->MolecularOverlay( <fieldfit>, <stericpercentage>, [targetmolecule], [flexible], [overlaysettings] );

$object->MolecularOverlay( { FieldFit => <fieldfit>, StericPercentage => <stericpercentage>, TargetMolecule => [targetmolecule], Flexible => [flexible], OverlaySettings => [overlaysettings] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <fieldfit> | Required | | Boolean |
| <stericpercentage> | Required | | Real |
| [flexible] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [overlaysettings] | Optional | overlayDefault | enum Mdm::OverlaySettings |
| [targetmolecule] | Optional | | Mdm::Molecule |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
# This script illustrates how to perform a molecular overlay.
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use SbdDiscoveryScript;

# Create a new MDM document.
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $name1 = 'Molecule1';
my $name2 = 'Molecule2';

my %MolecSMARTS = (
$name1 => 'O=C([O-])C1=CC(=CC=C1)C([O-])=O',
$name2 => 'C/C1=C/C=C(C=C1)C([O-])=O'
);

# Insert two molecules 'Molecule1' and 'Molecule2' from SMILES strings.
$document->InsertFromSmiles( $MolecSMARTS{$name1} );
my $molecule1 = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
$molecule1->Name($name1);

$document->InsertFromSmiles( $MolecSMARTS{$name2} );
my $molecule2 = $document->Molecules->Item(1);
$molecule2->Name($name2);

# name of the overlay similarity property
my $overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay Similarity/' . $molecule1->Name;

# Add rotatable bond monitors to both molecules.
# These are used with flexible field alignment.
$document->AddRotatableBondMonitors;

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection(10.0, 5.0, 0.0);
$document->DeselectAll;

# Calculate the similarity before the rigid field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using rigid field alignment, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated similarity is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Rigid field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the similarity before the rigid field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using rigid field alignment.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => False
}
);

printf( "Rigid field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection(5.0, 10.0, 0.0);
$document->DeselectAll;

# Calculate the similarity before flexible field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using flexible field alignment, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated similarity is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Flexible field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the similarity before flexible field alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Pre-alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay molecules using flexible field alignment.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => True,
StericPercentage => 50,
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True
}
);

$overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay Similarity/' . $molecule1->Name;
printf( "Flexible field alignment similarity (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

#
# Overlay molecules using tethers (tuple monitors).
#

# Move the molecule centers apart.
$molecule1->Select;
$document->TranslateSelection( 10, 10, 5 );
$document->DeselectAll;

my $molecule1Atoms = $molecule1->Atoms;
my $molecule2Atoms = $molecule2->Atoms;

# atom mapping indices
my %atomIndices = (
0 => 8,
2 => 9,
6 => 1
);

print(" Overlay with atom tethers\n");
foreach my $id1 (sort {$a <=> $b} keys %atomIndices) {
my $id2 = $atomIndices{$id1};
my $tupleArray = Mdm::Array::Create();
$tupleArray->AddItem( $molecule1Atoms->Item($id1) );
$tupleArray->AddItem( $molecule2Atoms->Item($id2) );
$document->CreateTupleMonitor($tupleArray);
printf( " Map %s atom: %d to: %s atom: %d\n",
$molecule1->Name, $id1 + 1, $molecule2->Name, $id2 + 1 );
}

# name of the property
$overlayPropertyName = 'Overlay RMS/' . $molecule1->Name;

# Calculate the RMSD value before the alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using tethers, then restore their coordinates.
# The calculated RMSD is based on the coordinates of the aligned molecules.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayRestoreCoordinates"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Calculate the RMSD value before the alignment by setting
# OverlaySettings to "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly".
# This is the same value as calculated earlier since the coordinates
# were restored in the previous overlay.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True,
OverlaySettings => "overlayCalculatePropertiesOnly"
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Overlay the molecules using tethers.
$document->MolecularOverlay(
{
FieldFit => False,
StericPercentage => 50, # unused for tethers
TargetMolecule => $molecule1,
Flexible => True
}
);

printf( "Manual tether RMSD (%s): %.4f\n",
$overlayPropertyName, $molecule2->GetProperty($overlayPropertyName) );

# Remove the tethers
my $monitors = $document->TupleMonitors;
foreach my $monitor (@$monitors)
{
$monitor->Select;
}
$document->DeleteObjects;

$document->FitView;
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# MolecularScope property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/molecularscope_property.htm

## MolecularScope property

### Description

MolecularScope specifies the molecular scope used when counting
hydrogen bonds in hydrogen bond monitors.

### Applies to

The MolecularScope property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor , Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::NonbondMonitor

### Using the MolecularScope property

#### Get

my $molecularscopeEnum = $object->MolecularScope;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $molecularscopeEnum | | | enum Mdm::MolecularScope |
| $object | | | Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor Mdm::NonbondMonitor |

#### Set

$object->MolecularScope = <scope>;

$object->MolecularScope( <scope> );

$object->MolecularScope( { Scope => <scope> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <scope> | Required | | enum Mdm::MolecularScope |
| $object | | | Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor Mdm::NonbondMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how use the hydrogen bond monitor and to change the distance cutoff.

use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Creates a hbond monitor between ligand atoms and receptor
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $LigName = $ligands->Item(0)->Name;
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $monitor = $document->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( $ligandAtoms,
Mdm::allAtomHydrogenBonds, Mdm::allMolecularHydrogenBonds );

# Shows the label for each of the hbonds
$monitor->IsLabelShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll(); 

printf "Default distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->DefaultDistanceCriterion;
printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor.\n\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $newHBDist = 3.0;
$monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared( $newHBDist* $newHBDist );

# update view to ensure the correct HB count
$document->UpdateViews();
printf "Set the distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared;

printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor:\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $hbonds = $document->HydrogenBonds;
my $count = $hbonds->Count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $hbond = $hbonds->Item($index);
my $dist = $hbond->Distance;
my $atom1 = $hbond->Atom1;
my $atom2 = $hbond->Atom2;
my $res = $atom1->Parent;

if ( $res->Name eq $LigName ) {
$atom2->Parent->Select; 
}
else{
$atom1->Parent->Select; 
}
printf "%d) Distance: %.3f A H-bond between Atom %s:%s:%s and Atom %s:%s:%s\n",
$index+1, $dist,
$atom1->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom1->Parent->Name, $atom1->Name,
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name ;
} 

$document->FitView(); 
my $display_style = { DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' };
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle($display_style);
$document->DeselectAll();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the MarkChiralityViolations function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Open a protein structure having D-amino acids so we see some violations.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1c4b.pdb' );

# This structure has multiple models - select just the first (we could also
# make a loop and check for violations in each model).
my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
$molecules->Item(0)->Select();

# Mark chirality violations.
my $pink = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 255, 200, 200 );
$document->MarkChiralityViolations($pink);

# Get the chirality violation monitors.
my $monitors =
$document->FilterByProperty('ProteinChiralityMonitor name="*"');

# Report the number of violations.
my $violationCount = $monitors->Count;
print "Structure has "
. $violationCount
. " CAlpha chirality violations.\n\n";

# Print a table of violations.
if ( $violationCount > 0 )
{
printf("Index\t Name\t\t Residue \n");
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $violationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);

printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Residues") );

$monitors->Item($index)->SetVisible;
}
}

$document->DeselectAll(); 
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# MonitoredPairScope property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/monitoredpairscope_property.htm

## MonitoredPairScope property

### Description

MonitoredPairScope specifies which other atoms each monitored atom can
interact with.
This option is only valid when an array of atoms to be monitored is specified.
The following options are available:

* interactionsWithinMonitoredScope: Specifies that only non-bond interactions within the defined atom array are tracked.

* interactionsExternalToMonitoredScope: Specifies that only non-bond interactions with one end within the defined atom array and one end outside the defined atom array are tracked.

* allInteractions: Specifies that any non-bond interactions involving atoms in the defined array are tracked.

### Applies to

The MonitoredPairScope property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::NonbondMonitor

### Using the MonitoredPairScope property

#### Get

my $monitoredpairscopeEnum = $object->MonitoredPairScope;

##### Parameters

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| $object | | | Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor Mdm::NonbondMonitor |

#### Set

$object->MonitoredPairScope = <scope>;

$object->MonitoredPairScope( <scope> );

$object->MonitoredPairScope( { Scope => <scope> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <scope> | Required | | enum Mdm::MonitoredPairScope |
| $object | | | Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor Mdm::NonbondMonitor |

```text
my $monitor = $document->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( $ligandAtoms,
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the MarkBondAngleViolations function.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '9INS.pdb' );

# Mark bond angle violations.
my $tolerance = 3.0;
my $blue = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 200, 200, 255 );
$document->MarkBondAngleViolations( $tolerance, $blue );

# Get the bond angle violation monitors, a type of AngleMonitor.
my $monitors = $document->AngleMonitors;
my $monitors = $document->FilterByProperty('BondAngleViolationMonitor name="*"');

my $allmonitors = $document->Monitors;
print "Total number of monitors: ". $allmonitors->Count ."\n";

# Report the number of violations.
my $violationCount = $monitors->Count();
print "Structure has " . $violationCount . " bond angle violations.\n\n";

# print a table of violations
printf("Index\t Violation name\t Angle\t Expected\t Minimum\t Maximum \n");
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $violationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $monitors->Item($index);
printf(
"%d \t %s \t %f \t %f \t %f \t %f\n",
$index, $monitor->Name(),
$monitor->Angle(), $monitor->GetProperty("Expected"),
$monitor->GetProperty("Minimum"), $monitor->GetProperty("Maximum")
);

$monitors->Item($index)->SetVisible;
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# MutateAminoAcid function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/mutateaminoacid_function.htm

## MutateAminoAcid function

### Description

MutateAminoAcid mutates an amino acid.

### Applies to

The MutateAminoAcid function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the MutateAminoAcid function

#### Command

$object->MutateAminoAcid( <residue>, <toresiduetype>, [isotropicdisplacement] );

$object->MutateAminoAcid( { Residue => <residue>, ToResidueType => <toresiduetype>, IsotropicDisplacement => [isotropicdisplacement] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <residue> | Required | | Mdm::AminoAcid |
| <toresiduetype> | Required | | enum Mdm::ResidueType |
| [isotropicdisplacement] | Optional | 20.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate methods for building and editing proteins.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# This is how to create an amino acid chain containing an alanine residue:
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $chain = $molecule->CreateAminoAcidChain();
my $aminoAcid1 = $chain->CreateResidue(Mdm::alanine);

my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
my $count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The current number of amino acids is $count.\n";

# Define a string consisting of 1-letter amino acid residue codes.
my $wideSequence = "AlaPheGlyProHisIleLysAlaAlaAla";
my $sequence = Mdm::AminoAcidChain::ConvertToOneLetterSequence($wideSequence);

print
"Converted wide sequence: $wideSequence to narrow sequence: $sequence.\n";

# Demonstrate how to append a sequence of residues at the C-terminus.
# Let's make it helical rather than the default extended conformation.
$document->GrowAminoAcidChain(
{
InsertAt => $chain,
Sequence => $sequence,
ConformationType => Mdm::rightAlphaHelixConformation,
GrowAtNTerminal => False
}
);

$aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
$count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The number of amino acid residues after growing chain "
. "at the C-terminus is $count.\n";

# Demonstrate how to grow amino acid chain at the N terminal.
# This will prepend the residue His0.
$document->GrowAminoAcidChain(
{
InsertAt => $chain,
Sequence => "H",
GrowAtNTerminal => True
}
);

$aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
$count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The number of amino acid residues after growing chain "
. "at the N-terminus is $count.\n";

# Insertion a residue within the chain.
my $insertionpoint = $aminoAcids->Item( $count - 2 );
my $sequence = "GANDT";
$document->InsertAminoAcid( $insertionpoint, $sequence );

$aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
$count = $aminoAcids->Count;
print "The number of amino acid residues after insertion is $count.\n";

# Demonstrate how to mutate a residue.
my $residuetomutate = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
print 'Amino acid name before the mutation: '
. $residuetomutate->Name() . "\n";
$document->MutateAminoAcid( $residuetomutate, Mdm::tyr );
print 'Amino acid name after the mutation: '
. $residuetomutate->Name() . "\n";

# At this point we have various insertion codes - lets renumber
print "Residue names before renumbering: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
print " " . $aminoAcids->Item($index)->Name() . " ";
}
print "\n";

$document->RenumberSequence( $aminoAcids->Item(0), 1, $count, True );
print "Residue names after renumbering: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
print " " . $aminoAcids->Item($index)->Name() . " ";
}
print "\n";

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# N1 property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/n1_property.htm

## N1 property

### Description

N1 looks for the nucleotide base nitrogen atom labeled N1.

### Applies to

The N1 property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::Nucleotide

### Using the N1 property

#### Get

my $atomObject = $object->N1;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $atomObject | | | Mdm::Atom |
| $object | | | Mdm::NucleicAcid Mdm::Nucleotide |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the use of Mdm::Nucleotide objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "3CRO.pdb" );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

print "Nucleic acid sequence: $molecule->{NucleicAcidSequence}\n";

my $nucleotides = $document->Nucleotides;
my $nucleotide1 = $nucleotides->Item(0);
my $nucleotide2 = $nucleotides->Item(1);
my $nucleotide3 = $nucleotides->Item(2);
my $nucleotide4 = $nucleotides->Item(3);

my $distance =
$document->CreateDistanceMonitor( $nucleotide1->C1Prime,
$nucleotide1->C2Prime );
printf
"Distance between C1' and C2' atoms of $nucleotide1->{Name}: %8.3f angstroms\n",
$distance->Distance;

my $angle =
$document->CreateAngleMonitor( $nucleotide2->C2, $nucleotide2->C3Prime,
$nucleotide2->C4 );

my $torsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide3->C4Prime, $nucleotide3->C5,
$nucleotide3->C5Prime, $nucleotide3->C6
);

my $torsion2 =
$document->CreateTorsionMonitor( $nucleotide3->N1, $nucleotide3->N3,
$nucleotide3->N7, $nucleotide3->N9 );

my $torsion3 = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide4->O1P, $nucleotide4->O2P,
$nucleotide4->O3Prime, $nucleotide4->O4Prime
);

print $nucleotide1->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsDeoxyribose );
print "a deoxyribose.\n";

print $nucleotide2->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsRibose );
print "a ribose.\n";

print $nucleotide3->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPurine );
print "have a purine ring system.\n";

print $nucleotide4->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPyrimidine );
print "have a pyrimidine ring system.\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to access MDM objects and create a minimize molecule.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Create a document containing a molecule.
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom1 = $molecule->CreateAtom('C');
my $atom2 = $molecule->CreateAtom('C');
my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $atom1, $atom2, Mdm::doubleBond );

# Add hydrogen atoms.
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms();

# Calculate partial charges for the minimization step.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Perform a geometry minimization using the clean forcefield.
$document->Clean();

$molecule->Name = 'Ethene';
print "Created molecule " . $molecule->Name . ".\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use Mdm::SpaceGroup objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Get space group from document.
my $cell = $document->Cells->Item(0);
my $spacegroup = $cell->SpaceGroup;

print "The following is a list of space group properties:\n";
print "Number:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->Number . "\n";
print "Short Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->Symbol . "\n";
print "SchoenfliesSymbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->SchoenfliesSymbol . "\n";
print "Full Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->FullSymbol . "\n";
print "Lattice type:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->LatticeType . "\n";
print "Cell choice:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->CellChoice . "\n";
print "AxisOriginType:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->AxisOriginType . "\n";
print "Number of sym. operator:\t\t"
. $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount . "\n";

my $count = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $operator = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperator($index);
print "Symmetry operator $index\n";
print "\tName: " . $operator->Name . "\n";

my $rotation = $operator->Rotation;
my $format = "\t %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n";
print "\tRotation Matrix:\n";
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 0, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 1, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 2 );

my $translation = $operator->Translation;
print "\tTranslation:\n";
printf "$format", $translation->X, $translation->Y, $translation->Z;
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the usage of several sequence properties.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId({Id =>'y13252', Database => "nuccore"});

my $sequence = $document->Sequences->Item(0);

# For sequence properties with empty fields, set value to 'Unspecified'.
$sequence->Description = 'Unspecified' if ( $sequence->Description eq "" );
$sequence->Locus = 'Unspecified' if ( $sequence->Locus eq "" );
$sequence->GeneName = 'Unspecified' if ( $sequence->GeneName eq "" );
$sequence->Name = 'Unspecified' if ( $sequence->Name eq "" );

print " Description\t" . $sequence->Description . "\n";
print " Locus\t" . $sequence->Locus . "\n";
print " Gene name\t" . $sequence->GeneName . "\n";
print " Name\t" . $sequence->Name . "\n";
```

### Applies to

The NcsMatrix property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the NcsMatrix property

The property can be used to both define and retrieve the non-crystallographic
symmetry matrix on a molecule as shown below:

```text
$molecule->NcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName) = $matrix4x4;
```

```text
my $matrix4x4 = $molecule->NcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName);
```

#### Get

my $matrix4x4Object = $object->NcsMatrix( <name> );

my $matrix4x4Object = $object->NcsMatrix( { Name => <name> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $matrix4x4Object | | | Mdm::Matrix4x4 |
| <name> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Set

$object->NcsMatrix = <name>, <matrix>;

$object->NcsMatrix( <name>, <matrix> );

$object->NcsMatrix( { Name => <name>, Matrix => <matrix> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <matrix> | Required | | Mdm::Matrix4x4 |
| <name> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrates the transformation matrix properties and functions.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1rvf');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $ncsMatrixName = 'BIOMT_4';

my $translateX = 0.0;
my $translateY = 0.0;
my $translateZ = 0.0;

my $ncsMatrix = Mdm::Matrix4x4::Create(
-0.309017, 0.500000, 0.809017, 0.0,
-0.500000, -0.809017, 0.309017, 0.0,
0.809017, -0.309017, 0.500000, 0.0,
$translateX, $translateY, $translateZ, 1.0
);

# Add a transformation matrix to a molecule and
# verify the matrix exists a property of the molecule.
$molecule->NcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName) = $ncsMatrix;
print "Found matrix $ncsMatrixName.\n"
if ( $molecule->HasNcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName) );

# Apply the transformation matrix to molecule's coordinates.
$document->ApplyTransformationMatrix( $molecule, $ncsMatrixName );

# Remove the matrix from molecule.
$molecule->RemoveNcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName);
print "Removed matrix $ncsMatrixName.\n"
if ( not $molecule->HasNcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName) );
```

The NegativeIonColor property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::PointFeature

### Using the NegativeIonColor property

#### Static Get

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $colorObject | | | Mdm::Color |
| $object | | | Mdm::PointFeature |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create a negative ionizable
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -14, 6, 0 );

my $negativeIonOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$negativeIonOperator->Name('Negative Ion');
my $negativeIonFeature =
$negativeIonOperator->CreatePointFeature( $document->Atoms );
$negativeIonFeature->Type() = 'ionizableNegativePointFeature';
$negativeIonFeature->CreateLabel('Negative Ionizable');
my $color = $negativeIonFeature->NegativeIonColor();
print "RGB of positive ionizable is: "
. $color->Red . " "
. $color->Green . " "
. $color->Blue . "\n";

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();

# Create a positive ionizable

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -14, 4.5, 0 );

my $positiveIonOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$positiveIonOperator->Name('Positive Ion');
my $positiveIonFeature =
$positiveIonOperator->CreatePointFeature( $document->Atoms );
$positiveIonFeature->Type() = 'ionizablePositivePointFeature';
$positiveIonFeature->CreateLabel('Positive Ionizable');
my $color = $positiveIonFeature->PositiveIonColor();
print "RGB of positive ionizable is: "
. $color->Red . " "
. $color->Green . " "
. $color->Blue . "\n";

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

The NeighborCount property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::NeighborMonitor

### Using the NeighborCount property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->NeighborCount;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::NeighborMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script shows how to create a neighbor monitor.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Creates a neighbor monitor near ligand atoms.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;

my $neighborMonitor = $document->CreateNeighborMonitor( $ligandAtoms, 3 );
$neighborMonitor->IsLabelShown(True);
$neighborMonitor->IsIntermolecularOnlyShown(False);

my $neighbors = $neighborMonitor->Neighbors;
my $count = $neighbors->Count;

print "Found $count atoms within "
. $neighborMonitor->NeighborRadius
. " angstroms of ligand.\n";

my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $count )
{
my $bump = $neighbors->Item($index);
my $atom2 = $bump->Atom2;
printf "\t%4d %s:%s:%s \n", ++$index,
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name;
}
```

#### Get

my $attributemapkeyObject = $object->NextKey( <previouskey> );

my $attributemapkeyObject = $object->NextKey( { PreviousKey => <previouskey> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $attributemapkeyObject | | | Sdm::AttributeMapKey |

| <previouskey> | Required | | String Sdm::AttributeMapKey |
| $object | | | DiscoveryScript::ObjectMap Protocol::ParameterMap Sdm::AttributeMap |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript , SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
print
"No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

my $protocolName = 'Minimization';
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );
my $map = $document->ParameterMap;
my $key = $map->FirstKey;
while ($key)
{
my $value = $map->Item($key);
print "Parameter name: $key\t\tValue: $value\n";
$key = $map->NextKey($key);

}

$key = 'Dielectric Constant';
my $newValue = 2.0;
my $hasItem = $document->ItemExists($key);
if ($hasItem)
{
print "\nProtocol has parameter '" . $key;
my $value = $document->Item($key);
my $type = $document->ParameterType($key);
print "\nThe type is $type. \nThe default value is $value.\n";
print "Changing parameter value of $key to $newValue.\n";
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $newValue );
}
```

# NonbondCategories property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/nonbondcategories_property.htm

## NonbondCategories property

### Description

NonbondCategories specifies an array containing the interaction
categories that an Mdm::Nonbond object is participating in.

### Applies to

The NonbondCategories property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Nonbond

### Using the NonbondCategories property

#### Get

my $stringarrayObject = $object->NonbondCategories;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::StringArray |
| $object | | | Mdm::Nonbond |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the basic non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3fzm');
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;
$document->Zoom(15);
$document->IsHierarchyViewShown = True;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Create a non-bond monitor for a subset of atoms.\n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $monitor = $document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();

# -- Analyze the identified interactions. ---------------------------
my $nonbonds = $monitor->Nonbonds;
my $count = $nonbonds->Count;
printf "Found %d non-bond interactions (total):\n", $count;

print $monitor->FavorableNonbonds->Count 
. " of these are favorable interactions (such as H-bonds).\n";
print $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds->Count
. " of these are unfavorable interactions (such as bumps).\n\n";

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Analyze first non-bond interaction:\n";
my $nonbond = $nonbonds->Item(0);

my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$nonbond->Distance;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
my $unfavorableNonbonds = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds;
if ($unfavorableNonbonds->Count > 0) 
{
print "Analyze first unfavorable non-bond interaction:\n";
my $unfavorableNonbond = $unfavorableNonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $unfavorableNonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $unfavorableNonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$unfavorableNonbond->Distance;
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "All non-bonds of a particular type can be retrieved ";
print "using the NonbondsOfType filter.\n";
my $hBonds = $monitor->NonbondsOfType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType);
printf "Found %d hydrogen bonds using NonbondOfType filter.\n\n", $hBonds->Count;

print "Alternatively the IsMatchingNonbondType property can be used to \n";
print "identify interactions of a specific types. The following atom pairs \n";
print "indicate classical hydrogen bonding: \n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
if ($nonbond->IsMatchingNonbondType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType))
{
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);

print '* ' . $atom1->FullName . " (";
print 'donor ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrogenDonor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHalogen);
print 'positive ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPositive);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ') and ';

print $atom2->FullName . " (";
print 'acceptor ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrogenAcceptor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHalogen);
print 'negative ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsNegative);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ")\n";
}
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "\nThe NonbondTypes property can be used to identify all \n";
print "interaction types of a non-bond.\n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
printf "- %s (%s) and %s (%s):",
$nonbond->FromSite->Name,
$nonbond->FromSite->ChemistryName,
$nonbond->ToSite->Name,
$nonbond->ToSite->ChemistryName;

#these are the type enums 
print " Types: ";
my $nonbondTypes = $nonbond->NonbondTypes;
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
print "$type ";
}

#these are the category enums 
print " Categories: ";
my $nonbondCategories = $nonbond->NonbondCategories;
```

# NonbondCriterion property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/nonbondcriterion_property.htm

## NonbondCriterion property

### Description

NonbondCriterion specifies the distance and angle criteria used
by the Mdm::NonbondMonitor .
See enum Mdm::NonbondCriterionType for a description
of the various criterion.

### Applies to

The NonbondCriterion property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::NonbondMonitor

### Using the NonbondCriterion property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->NonbondCriterion( <criterion> );

my $realValue = $object->NonbondCriterion( { Criterion => <criterion> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| <criterion> | Required | | enum Mdm::NonbondCriterionType |
| $object | | | Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor Mdm::NonbondMonitor |

#### Set

$object->NonbondCriterion = <criterion>, <value>;

$object->NonbondCriterion( <criterion>, <value> );

$object->NonbondCriterion( { Criterion => <criterion>, Value => <value> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <criterion> | Required | | enum Mdm::NonbondCriterionType |
| <value> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor Mdm::NonbondMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the basic non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "Create a non-bond monitor for a subset of atoms.\n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus();
$ligand->Select();
my $ligandAtoms = $document->SelectedObjects()->Atoms;
$document->FitView();
$document->DeselectAll();

my $monitor = $document->CreateNonbondMonitor($ligandAtoms);
$monitor->Name = "myname";
$document->UpdateViews();

my $monitors = $document->NonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d NonbondMonitor(s).\n", $monitors->Count;
print "\n";

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "The properties NonbondCriterion and DefaultNonbondCriterion \n";
print "access the parameters used to identify non-bonds (see the \n";
print "documentation for full description of criteria).\n\n";

print "A list of criteria a their values follows:\n";
my $allCriteria = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::AllNonbondCriterionTypes();
foreach my $criterionType (@$allCriteria)
{
printf "Mdm::%s:\t %6.2f (default: %6.2f) \n",
$criterionType,
$monitor->NonbondCriterion($criterionType),
$monitor->DefaultNonbondCriterion($criterionType);
}
print "\n";

# -- Changing an interaction criterion ------------------------------

print 'Using the default criteria, the number of non-bond '
. 'interactions is ' . $monitor->Nonbonds->Count . ".\n\n";

my $maxHBond = 1.0 + $monitor->NonbondCriterion(
Mdm::hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum);
print 'After increasing the classical hydrogen bond distance to '
. $maxHBond . " A, ";

$monitor->NonbondCriterion(
Mdm::hydrogenBond_Strong_DonorAcceptor_DistanceMaximum) = $maxHBond;
$document->UpdateObjects;
print 'the number of non-bond interactions increases to '
. $monitor->Nonbonds->Count . ".\n\n";

print "Changes made to the non-bond criteria can be reset " .
"to the original defaults using ResetNonbondCriteria.\n";
$monitor->ResetNonbondCriteria();
```

# Nonbonds filter

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/nonbonds_filter.htm

## Nonbonds filter

### Description

Nonbonds indicates all Mdm::Nonbond objects in a specific context,
such as an Mdm::Array , Mdm::Set , Mdm::Document , or descendants of an Mdm::NonbondMonitor .

### Applies to

The Nonbonds filter can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Array , Mdm::Document , Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::NonbondMonitor , Mdm::Set

### Using the Nonbonds filter

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->Nonbonds;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::Array Mdm::Document Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor Mdm::NonbondMonitor Mdm::Set |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the basic non-bond monitor 
# and non-bond objects.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3fzm');
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;
$document->Zoom(15);
$document->IsHierarchyViewShown = True;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Create a non-bond monitor for a subset of atoms.\n";
$document->FocusOnFirstLigand();
my $monitor = $document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();

# -- Analyze the identified interactions. ---------------------------
my $nonbonds = $monitor->Nonbonds;
my $count = $nonbonds->Count;
printf "Found %d non-bond interactions (total):\n", $count;

print $monitor->FavorableNonbonds->Count 
. " of these are favorable interactions (such as H-bonds).\n";
print $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds->Count
. " of these are unfavorable interactions (such as bumps).\n\n";

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "Analyze first non-bond interaction:\n";
my $nonbond = $nonbonds->Item(0);

my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$nonbond->Distance;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
my $unfavorableNonbonds = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds;
if ($unfavorableNonbonds->Count > 0) 
{
print "Analyze first unfavorable non-bond interaction:\n";
my $unfavorableNonbond = $unfavorableNonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $unfavorableNonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $unfavorableNonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$unfavorableNonbond->Distance;
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "All non-bonds of a particular type can be retrieved ";
print "using the NonbondsOfType filter.\n";
my $hBonds = $monitor->NonbondsOfType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType);
printf "Found %d hydrogen bonds using NonbondOfType filter.\n\n", $hBonds->Count;

print "Alternatively the IsMatchingNonbondType property can be used to \n";
print "identify interactions of a specific types. The following atom pairs \n";
print "indicate classical hydrogen bonding: \n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
if ($nonbond->IsMatchingNonbondType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType))
{
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);

print '* ' . $atom1->FullName . " (";
print 'donor ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrogenDonor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHalogen);
print 'positive ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPositive);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ') and ';

print $atom2->FullName . " (";
print 'acceptor ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrogenAcceptor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHalogen);
print 'negative ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsNegative);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ")\n";
}
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "\nThe NonbondTypes property can be used to identify all \n";
print "interaction types of a non-bond.\n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
printf "- %s (%s) and %s (%s):",
$nonbond->FromSite->Name,
$nonbond->FromSite->ChemistryName,
$nonbond->ToSite->Name,
$nonbond->ToSite->ChemistryName;

#these are the type enums 
print " Types: ";
my $nonbondTypes = $nonbond->NonbondTypes;
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
print "$type ";
}

#these are the category enums 
print " Categories: ";
my $nonbondCategories = $nonbond->NonbondCategories;
foreach my $category (@$nonbondCategories) {
print "$category ";
}

#these APIs give the name(s) of the type/categories as a string 
#(the same as appears in the Nonbond tab of the DS MDT)
print " : Type Names: ";
my $typeNames = $nonbond->TypeNames;
print "$typeNames";

print " : Category Names: ";
my $categories = $nonbond->CategoryNames;
print "$categories";

print "\n";
}
print "\n";
```

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |

| [includehiddennonbonds] | Optional | True | Boolean |

```text
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$nonbond->Distance;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
my $unfavorableNonbonds = $monitor->UnfavorableNonbonds;
if ($unfavorableNonbonds->Count > 0) 
{
print "Analyze first unfavorable non-bond interaction:\n";
my $unfavorableNonbond = $unfavorableNonbonds->Item(0);

my $atomGroup1 = $unfavorableNonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $source1 = ($atom1->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

my $atomGroup2 = $unfavorableNonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);
my $source2 = ($atom2->IsMemberOf($ligand)) ? 'ligand' : "receptor";

printf "* interaction is between %s (%s) and %s (%s).\n",
$atom1->FullName, $source1,
$atom2->FullName, $source2;
printf "* interacting atoms separated by %f Angstrom.\n\n",
$unfavorableNonbond->Distance;
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "All non-bonds of a particular type can be retrieved ";
print "using the NonbondsOfType filter.\n";
my $hBonds = $monitor->NonbondsOfType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType);
printf "Found %d hydrogen bonds using NonbondOfType filter.\n\n", $hBonds->Count;

print "Alternatively the IsMatchingNonbondType property can be used to \n";
print "identify interactions of a specific types. The following atom pairs \n";
print "indicate classical hydrogen bonding: \n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
if ($nonbond->IsMatchingNonbondType(Mdm::conventionalHBondType))
{
my $atomGroup1 = $nonbond->FromSite->Atoms;
my $atomGroup2 = $nonbond->ToSite->Atoms;
my $atom1 = $atomGroup1->Item(0);
my $atom2 = $atomGroup2->Item(0);

print '* ' . $atom1->FullName . " (";
print 'donor ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrogenDonor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHalogen);
print 'positive ' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPositive);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->FromSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ') and ';

print $atom2->FullName . " (";
print 'acceptor ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrogenAcceptor);
print 'halogen ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHalogen);
print 'negative ' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsNegative);
print 'pi-system' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsPiSystem);
print 'amide' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsAmide);
print 'hydrophobic group' if ($nonbond->ToSite->IsHydrophobicGroup);
print ")\n";
}
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
print "\nThe NonbondTypes property can be used to identify all \n";
print "interaction types of a non-bond.\n";
foreach my $nonbond (@$nonbonds)
{
printf "- %s (%s) and %s (%s):",
$nonbond->FromSite->Name,
$nonbond->FromSite->ChemistryName,
$nonbond->ToSite->Name,
$nonbond->ToSite->ChemistryName;

#these are the type enums 
print " Types: ";
my $nonbondTypes = $nonbond->NonbondTypes;
foreach my $type (@$nonbondTypes) {
print "$type ";
}

#these are the category enums 
print " Categories: ";
my $nonbondCategories = $nonbond->NonbondCategories;
foreach my $category (@$nonbondCategories) {
print "$category ";
}

#these APIs give the name(s) of the type/categories as a string 
#(the same as appears in the Nonbond tab of the DS MDT)
print " : Type Names: ";
my $typeNames = $nonbond->TypeNames;
print "$typeNames";

print " : Category Names: ";
my $categories = $nonbond->CategoryNames;
print "$categories";

print "\n";
}
print "\n";
```

# NonbondTypesByCategory function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/nonbondtypesbycategory_function.htm

## NonbondTypesByCategory function

### Description

NonbondTypesByCategory specifies an array containing all
possible values of enum Mdm::NonbondType of a given enum Mdm::NonbondCategory .

### Applies to

The NonbondTypesByCategory function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::NonbondMonitor

### Using the NonbondTypesByCategory function

#### Static

my $stringarrayObject = Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor::NonbondTypesByCategory( <nonbondcategory> );

my $stringarrayObject = Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor::NonbondTypesByCategory( { NonbondCategory => <nonbondcategory> } );

my $stringarrayObject = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::NonbondTypesByCategory( <nonbondcategory> );

my $stringarrayObject = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::NonbondTypesByCategory( { NonbondCategory => <nonbondcategory> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::StringArray |
| <nonbondcategory> | Required | | enum Mdm::NonbondCategory |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to create non-bond monitors.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('3fzm');
die "PDB file download failed!" unless $document;
$document->Zoom(20);
$document->IsHierarchyViewShown = True;

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "Create a monitor for all non-bond interactions.\n";
my $allAtoms = $document->Atoms;
my $nonbondMonitor = 
$document->CreateNonbondMonitor($allAtoms);
$nonbondMonitor->Name = 'Monitor All Nonbonds';

$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(1);
$nonbondMonitor->IsVisible = False;
$document->UpdateViews();

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "Create a monitor for unfavorable interactions only.\n";
my $unfavorableTypes = Mdm::NonbondMonitor::NonbondTypesByCategory(
Mdm::allUnfavorableNonbondTypes);

my $unfavorableMonitor = $document->CreateNonbondMonitor({
ArrayOfMonitoredAtoms => $document->Atoms,
MonitoredNonbondTypes => $unfavorableTypes,
IsUnsatisfiedCalculated=> False});
$unfavorableMonitor->Name = 'Monitor Unfavorable';

$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(1);
$unfavorableMonitor->IsVisible = False;
$document->UpdateViews();

# -------------------------------------------------------------------

print "Create a custom monitor for specific interaction types only.\n";
my $nonbondTypes = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$nonbondTypes->AddItem(Mdm::saltBridgeType);
$nonbondTypes->AddItem(Mdm::unfavorableVdwBumpType);

my $customMonitor = $document->CreateNonbondMonitor({
ArrayOfMonitoredAtoms => $document->Atoms,
MonitoredNonbondTypes => $nonbondTypes,
IsUnsatisfiedCalculated=> False});
$customMonitor->Name = 'Monitor Custom';
$document->UpdateViews();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "9INS.pdb" );

my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
my $aminoAcid2 = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
my $aminoAcid3 = $aminoAcids->Item(2);

$collection->AddItem( $aminoAcid2->AmideOxygen );

$document->CreateNormalMonitor( $planeMonitor, $aminoAcid2->CAlpha );
```
