# NormalFeature property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/normalfeature_property.htm

## NormalFeature property

### Description

NormalFeature specifies the Mdm::NormalFeature in a ring aromatic feature.

### Applies to

The NormalFeature property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::RingAromaticFeature

### Using the NormalFeature property

#### Get

my $pointfeatureObject = $object->NormalFeature;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $pointfeatureObject | | | Mdm::PointFeature |
| $object | | | Mdm::RingAromaticFeature |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create some features on the query
# Create a ring aromatic
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Name("benzene");
my $ringAromaticOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$ringAromaticOperator->Name('RA1');
my $ringAromaticFeatureObject =
$ringAromaticOperator->CreateRingAromaticFeature(
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Atoms );
$document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Select(); # delete later

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature(
$ringAromaticFeatureObject->CentroidFeature(), 1.6 );
my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature(
$ringAromaticFeatureObject->NormalFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create a donor feature
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -2, -4, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# Give the hydrogen bond donor a higher weight (2.0) than the default (1.0)
$donorOperator->Weight(2.0);

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create an acceptor feature at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

# create the location constraints
my $locationFeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );

printf "%s Head: x: %.4f y: %.4f z: %.4f\n",
$locationFeatureHead->ClassName, 
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->X, 
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->Y,
$locationFeatureHead->XYZ->Z;

my $locationFeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

printf "%s Tail: x: %.4f y: %.4f z: %.4f\n",
$locationFeatureHead->ClassName,
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->X, 
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->Y,
$locationFeatureTail->XYZ->Z;

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# NTerminus property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/nterminus_property.htm

## NTerminus property

### Description

NTerminus specifies the N-terminus Mdm::AminoAcid of an Mdm::AminoAcidChain .

### Applies to

The NTerminus property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcidChain

### Using the NTerminus property

#### Get

my $aminoacidObject = $object->NTerminus;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $aminoacidObject | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcidChain |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This example shows how to alter the characteristics of protein termini.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Subroutine to print atoms in N terminal residue.
sub PrintNTerminus($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $chains = $document->AminoAcidChains;
my $nTerminus = $chains->Item(0)->NTerminus();
my $atoms = $nTerminus->Atoms;
my $atomCount = $atoms->Count;
printf "Number of atoms in N terminal residue %s : %d\n",
$nTerminus->Name(), $atomCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atomCount ; ++$index )
{
my $atom = $atoms->Item($index);
printf
" Name : %s Formal charge %d/%d\n",
$atom->Name(),
$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,
$atom->FormalCharge->Denominator;
}
}

# Subroutine to print atoms in C terminal residue.
sub PrintCTerminus($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $chains = $document->AminoAcidChains;
my $nTerminus = $chains->Item(0)->CTerminus();
my $atoms = $nTerminus->Atoms;
my $atomCount = $atoms->Count;
printf "Number of atoms in C terminal residue %s : %d\n",
$nTerminus->Name(), $atomCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atomCount ; ++$index )
{
my $atom = $atoms->Item($index);
printf
" Name : %s Formal charge %d/%d\n",
$atom->Name(),
$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,
$atom->FormalCharge->Denominator;
}
}

# Subroutine to print atoms in N and C terminal residues.
sub PrintTermini($$)
{
my ( $document, $title ) = @_;
printf "\n%s :\n", $title;
PrintNTerminus($document);
PrintCTerminus($document);
}

# Load molecule from PDB.
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Mutate the termini to alanine. With the side chain removed,
# the atom listing will be clearer.
my $chain = $document->AminoAcidChains->Item(0);
my $nTerminus = $chain->NTerminus();
my $cTerminus = $chain->CTerminus();

$document->MutateAminoAcid( $nTerminus, Mdm::ala );
$document->MutateAminoAcid( $cTerminus, Mdm::ala );
$document->DeselectAll();

# Uncomment this line to add hydrogen atoms.
# AddHydrogens($document);

# List atoms in current configuration.
PrintTermini( $document, "At start" );

# Remove terminal residue characteristics and list atoms.
$chain->RemoveNTerminusCap();
$chain->RemoveCTerminusCap();
PrintTermini( $document, "After removing caps" );

# Make termini normal (i.e. charged) and list atoms.
$nTerminus->MakeNTerminus(True);
$cTerminus->MakeCTerminus(True);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making charged termini" );

# Make termini uncharged and list atoms.
$nTerminus->MakeNTerminus(False);
$cTerminus->MakeCTerminus(False);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making neutral termini" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 1.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(1.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(1.0);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 1.0" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 7.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(7.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(7.0);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 7.0" );

# Make termini appropriate for different pH = 13.0 and list atoms.
$chain->MakeNTerminusAtpH(13.0);
$chain->MakeCTerminusAtpH(130);
PrintTermini( $document, "After making termini at pH 13.0" );

$document->UpdateViews();
```

Source file: scripting/nucleicaciddiscoveryscript_package.htm

## NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript package

### Description

NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript provides functions, properties, and constants that can be used
to manipulate Discovery Studio nucleic acid data.

### Using the NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript package

Access to the NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript API is through the Perl use directive:

```text
use strict;
use NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript;
```

The strict directive is optional, but strongly recommended as it restricts
the use of unsafe constructs. All available classes will be imported from the NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript module.

# NucleicAcidSequence property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/nucleicacidsequence_property.htm

## NucleicAcidSequence property

### Description

NucleicAcidSequence specifies the nucleic acid sequence of an Mdm::Molecule as a text string.

### Applies to

The NucleicAcidSequence property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the NucleicAcidSequence property

#### Get

my $stringValue = $object->NucleicAcidSequence;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the use of Mdm::Nucleotide objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "3CRO.pdb" );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

print "Nucleic acid sequence: $molecule->{NucleicAcidSequence}\n";

my $nucleotides = $document->Nucleotides;
my $nucleotide1 = $nucleotides->Item(0);
my $nucleotide2 = $nucleotides->Item(1);
my $nucleotide3 = $nucleotides->Item(2);
my $nucleotide4 = $nucleotides->Item(3);

my $distance =
$document->CreateDistanceMonitor( $nucleotide1->C1Prime,
$nucleotide1->C2Prime );
printf
"Distance between C1' and C2' atoms of $nucleotide1->{Name}: %8.3f angstroms\n",
$distance->Distance;

my $angle =
$document->CreateAngleMonitor( $nucleotide2->C2, $nucleotide2->C3Prime,
$nucleotide2->C4 );

my $torsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide3->C4Prime, $nucleotide3->C5,
$nucleotide3->C5Prime, $nucleotide3->C6
);

my $torsion2 =
$document->CreateTorsionMonitor( $nucleotide3->N1, $nucleotide3->N3,
$nucleotide3->N7, $nucleotide3->N9 );

my $torsion3 = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide4->O1P, $nucleotide4->O2P,
$nucleotide4->O3Prime, $nucleotide4->O4Prime
);

print $nucleotide1->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsDeoxyribose );
print "a deoxyribose.\n";

print $nucleotide2->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsRibose );
print "a ribose.\n";

print $nucleotide3->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPurine );
print "have a purine ring system.\n";

print $nucleotide4->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPyrimidine );
print "have a pyrimidine ring system.\n";
```

# NucleotideAt3PrimeTerminus property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/nucleotideat3primeterminus_property.htm

## NucleotideAt3PrimeTerminus property

### Description

NucleotideAt3PrimeTerminus specifies the nucleotide residue
at the 3' terminus of a nucleic acid chain.

### Applies to

The NucleotideAt3PrimeTerminus property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::NucleicAcidChain

### Using the NucleotideAt3PrimeTerminus property

#### Get

my $nucleotideObject = $object->NucleotideAt3PrimeTerminus;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $nucleotideObject | | | Mdm::Nucleotide |
| $object | | | Mdm::NucleicAcidChain |

#### Defined by

NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to build nucleic acids.
use strict;
use NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create and append to a DNA duplex molecule.
my $naType = Mdm::dnaDuplex;
my $nucleicAcidMolecule =
$document->CreateNucleicAcid( "CGT", $naType, Mdm::aHelix );
my $senseChain1 = $nucleicAcidMolecule->Chains->Item(0);
my $na3Prime = $senseChain1->NucleotideAt3PrimeTerminus;
$na3Prime = $document->GrowNucleicAcid( $na3Prime, "GGG", Mdm::aHelix );

printf "Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$document->ModelName,
$document->Atoms->Count();

# Create and prepend to a second DNA duplex molecule.
my $nucleicAcid2 =
$document->CreateNucleicAcid( "ACT", $naType, Mdm::aHelix );
my $senseChain2 = $nucleicAcid2->Chains->Item(0);
my $na5Prime = $senseChain2->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus;
$na5Prime = $document->GrowNucleicAcid( $na5Prime, "AAA", Mdm::aHelix );

my $secondMoleculeName = "Nucleic Acid 2";
$nucleicAcid2->Name = $secondMoleculeName;

# Ligate the two molecules using the sense strand.
$document->DeselectAll();
$na3Prime->Select;
$na5Prime->Select;
$document->LigateNucleotides( $na3Prime, $na5Prime );

# Mutate first sense nucleotide to thymidine.
$document->DeselectAll();
$senseChain1->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus->Select;
$document->MutateNucleotide( $senseChain1->NucleotideAt5PrimeTerminus,
Mdm::thymidine );

# Change the nucleic acid display style.
$senseChain1->DisplayStyle = Mdm::styleDnaArrowLadder;
$nucleicAcidMolecule->Chains->Item(1)->DisplayStyle =
Mdm::styleDnaArrowLadder;

printf "Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$document->ModelName,
$document->Atoms->Count();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
```

```text
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "3CRO.pdb" );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

print "Nucleic acid sequence: $molecule->{NucleicAcidSequence}\n";

my $nucleotides = $document->Nucleotides;
my $nucleotide1 = $nucleotides->Item(0);
my $nucleotide2 = $nucleotides->Item(1);
my $nucleotide3 = $nucleotides->Item(2);
my $nucleotide4 = $nucleotides->Item(3);

my $distance =
$document->CreateDistanceMonitor( $nucleotide1->C1Prime,
$nucleotide1->C2Prime );
printf
"Distance between C1' and C2' atoms of $nucleotide1->{Name}: %8.3f angstroms\n",
$distance->Distance;

my $angle =
$document->CreateAngleMonitor( $nucleotide2->C2, $nucleotide2->C3Prime,
$nucleotide2->C4 );

my $torsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide3->C4Prime, $nucleotide3->C5,
$nucleotide3->C5Prime, $nucleotide3->C6
);

my $torsion2 =
$document->CreateTorsionMonitor( $nucleotide3->N1, $nucleotide3->N3,
$nucleotide3->N7, $nucleotide3->N9 );

my $torsion3 = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$nucleotide4->O1P, $nucleotide4->O2P,
$nucleotide4->O3Prime, $nucleotide4->O4Prime
);

print $nucleotide1->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsDeoxyribose );
print "a deoxyribose.\n";

print $nucleotide2->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsRibose );
print "a ribose.\n";

print $nucleotide3->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPurine );
print "have a purine ring system.\n";

print $nucleotide4->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPyrimidine );
print "have a pyrimidine ring system.\n";
```

# Number property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/number_property.htm

## Number property

### Description

Number specifies the space group table number as defined by the
International Union of Crystallography.

### Applies to

The Number property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::SpaceGroup

### Using the Number property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->Number;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::SpaceGroup |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use Mdm::SpaceGroup objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Get space group from document.
my $cell = $document->Cells->Item(0);
my $spacegroup = $cell->SpaceGroup;

print "The following is a list of space group properties:\n";
print "Number:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->Number . "\n";
print "Short Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->Symbol . "\n";
print "SchoenfliesSymbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->SchoenfliesSymbol . "\n";
print "Full Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->FullSymbol . "\n";
print "Lattice type:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->LatticeType . "\n";
print "Cell choice:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->CellChoice . "\n";
print "AxisOriginType:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->AxisOriginType . "\n";
print "Number of sym. operator:\t\t"
. $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount . "\n";

my $count = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $operator = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperator($index);
print "Symmetry operator $index\n";
print "\tName: " . $operator->Name . "\n";

my $rotation = $operator->Rotation;
my $format = "\t %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n";
print "\tRotation Matrix:\n";
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 0, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 1, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 2 );

my $translation = $operator->Translation;
print "\tTranslation:\n";
printf "$format", $translation->X, $translation->Y, $translation->Z;
}
```

# Numerator property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

## Numerator property

### Description

Numerator specifies the numerator of a rational.

### Applies to

The Numerator property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Rational

### Using the Numerator property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->Numerator;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Rational |

#### Set

$object->Numerator = <numerator>;

$object->Numerator( <numerator> );

$object->Numerator( { Numerator => <numerator> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <numerator> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Rational |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

```text
print "a deoxyribose.\n";

print $nucleotide2->Name . ' is ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsRibose );
print "a ribose.\n";

print $nucleotide3->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPurine );
print "have a purine ring system.\n";

print $nucleotide4->Name . ' does ';
print 'not ' if ( not $nucleotide1->IsPyrimidine );
print "have a pyrimidine ring system.\n";
```

#### Defined by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of various atom properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

# Define atom properties to list.
# This may be specified on the command line.
my $residueAtomName = 'THR2:CA';
if ( @ARGV != 0 )
{
($residueAtomName) = @ARGV;
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Get the specified atom.
my $atoms = FilterByString( $document, $residueAtomName );
die "Atom $residueAtomName not found. Aborting!\n\n"
if ( $atoms->Count == 0 );

my $atom = $atoms->[0];

# Print various atom properties. In the DiscoveryStudio client, the
# output will appear in the output pane of the scripting window.
print "List of properties for atom $residueAtomName:\n\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
print 'Element: ' . $atom->Element . "\n";
print 'Element Name: ' . $atom->ElementName . "\n";
print 'Element Symbol: ' . $atom->ElementSymbol . "\n";
print 'Mass: ' . $atom->Mass . "\n";
print 'Atomic number: ' . $atom->AtomicNumber . "\n";
print 'Charge: ' . $atom->Charge . "\n";
print 'Formal Charge: '
. $atom->FormalCharge->Numerator . "/"
. $atom->FormalCharge->Denominator . "\n";

print 'VDW Radius: ' . $atom->VdwRadius . "\n";
print 'Covalent Radius: ' . $atom->CovalentRadius . "\n";
print 'Chirality: ' . $atom->Chirality . "\n";
print 'Bond count: ' . $atom->BondCount . "\n";
print 'Bonding radius: ' . $atom->BondingRadius . "\n";
print 'Hybridization: ' . $atom->Hybridization . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen Count: ' . $atom->HydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'ImplicitHydrogen Count: ' . $atom->ImplicitHydrogenCount . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Acceptor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondAcceptor . "\n";
print 'Is Hydrogen Bond Donor: ' . $atom->IsHydrogenBondDonor . "\n";
print 'Isotropic Displacement: ' . $atom->IsotropicDisplacement . "\n";
print 'Is Terminal Hydrogen: ' . $atom->IsTerminalHydrogen . "\n";
print 'Is Valence Satisfied: ' . $atom->IsValenceSatisfied . "\n";
print 'Lone Pair Count: ' . $atom->LonePairCount . "\n";
print 'Valence Count: ' . $atom->ValenceCount . "\n";
print 'Occupancy: ' . $atom->Occupancy . "\n";

printf "\n%s:\n", 'Display Properties';
print 'DisplayStyle: ' . $atom->DisplayStyle . "\n";
print 'Ball Size: ' . $atom->BallSize . "\n";
print 'Ball Size Default: ' . $atom->BallSizeDefault . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale: ' . $atom->CPKScale . "\n";
print 'CPK Scale Default: ' . $atom->CPKScaleDefault . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius: ' . $atom->StickRadius . "\n";
print 'Stick Radius Default: ' . $atom->StickRadiusDefault . "\n";
print 'Name: ' . $atom->Name . "\n";
```

# Offline function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/offline_function.htm

## Offline function

### Description

IMPORTANT! This is a prototype. The API may be changed or removed
in the future and its use is not currently supported.

Offline releases the memory used by an offlineable object.
Molecules and conformations are offlineable objects.
Any objects that have references to the object being offlined
or its contents, but are not contained within the object will
be updated or removed.

The effect on those objects is the same as if the object
being offlined had been removed.
For example, a distance monitor that connects an atom in
a molecule being offlined with another atom will be removed.
If the molecule that has been offlined is made visible again,
the distance monitor is not restored.

### Applies to

The Offline function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AcceptorFeature , Mdm::AminoAcid , Mdm::AminoAcidChain , Mdm::AngleFeature , Mdm::AngleMonitor , Mdm::Animation , Mdm::Assembly , Mdm::Atom , Mdm::BindingSite , Mdm::BindingSitePoint , Mdm::Bond , Mdm::BondAngleViolationMonitor , Mdm::BondLengthViolationMonitor , Mdm::Bump , Mdm::BumpMonitor , Mdm::CAlphaMonitor , Mdm::CAlphaPair , Mdm::CAlphaViolationMonitor , Mdm::Cell , Mdm::CentroidFeature , Mdm::CentroidMonitor , Mdm::Chain , Mdm::Chiral , Mdm::ChiralityMonitor , Mdm::CisPeptideMonitor , Mdm::Conformation , Mdm::Conformer , Mdm::ConformerAtom , Mdm::ConformerBond , Mdm::ConformerModel , Mdm::Constraint , Mdm::Cylinder , Mdm::DihedralFeature , Mdm::DihedralRestraint , Mdm::DipoleMomentMonitor , Mdm::DistanceFeature , Mdm::DistanceMonitor , Mdm::DistanceRestraint , Mdm::DisulfideBridgeSite , Mdm::DockedProteinPoseAssembly , Mdm::Document , Mdm::DonorFeature , Mdm::ExclusionFeature , Mdm::FixedAtomConstraint , Mdm::Geometric3d , Mdm::Group , Mdm::HarmonicAtomRestraint , Mdm::HydrogenBond , Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor , Mdm::Isosurface , Mdm::Label3d , Mdm::Label , Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::LocationFeature , Mdm::MainChainConformationViolationMonitor , Mdm::Membrane , Mdm::MembraneOrientationMonitor , Mdm::MissingMainChainMonitor , Mdm::MissingSideChainMonitor , Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::MoleculeAssembly , Mdm::Monitor , Mdm::Neighbor , Mdm::NeighborMonitor , Mdm::Nonbond , Mdm::NonbondMonitor , Mdm::NormalFeature , Mdm::NormalMonitor , Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::NucleicAcidChain , Mdm::Nucleotide , Mdm::Object , Mdm::Offlineable , Mdm::OfflineableConformation , Mdm::PiBond , Mdm::PiCationMonitor , Mdm::PiInteractionMonitor , Mdm::PiPiMonitor , Mdm::PiSigmaMonitor , Mdm::PlanarPeptideViolationMonitor , Mdm::PlaneFeature , Mdm::PlaneMonitor , Mdm::PointFeature , Mdm::PointOffsetFeature , Mdm::Polydot , Mdm::PropertyLabel , Mdm::ProteinChiralityViolationMonitor , Mdm::ProteinNomenclatureViolationMonitor , Mdm::ProteinPose , Mdm::Query , Mdm::QueryAtom , Mdm::QueryBond , Mdm::QueryFeatureMap , Mdm::QueryOperator , Mdm::Residue , Mdm::Restraint , Mdm::TorsionMonitor , Mdm::TupleMonitor , Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond , Mdm::Valence , Mdm::ValenceMonitor , Mdm::VectorFeature

### Using the Offline function

#### Instance

$object->Offline();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Command

$object->Offline( <object> );

$object->Offline( { Object => <object> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <object> | Required | | Mdm::Object |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use the offline commands for offline Molecules.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';

my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . 'Sample Drug Molecules.dsv';
my $document =
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $inputFile, LoadAllObjects => False } );
my $onlineMolecules = $document->Molecules;
my $allMolecules = $document->AllMolecules;
print "There are " . $allMolecules->Count . " molecules in the file.\n";
print "There are "
. $onlineMolecules->Count
. " molecules loaded in memory.\n";
print "Visualize the first 10 molecules...\n";

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 10 ; $i++ )
{
my $mol = $allMolecules->Item($i);
print "Visualize " . $mol->Name() . "\n";
$mol->SetVisible();
}
print "Offline all the visible molecules to release memory.\n";
my $count = $allMolecules->Count;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $count ; $i++ )
{
my $mol = $allMolecules->Item($i);
if ( $mol->IsVisible() )
{
$mol->Offline();
}
}
print "Closing the document.\n";
$document->Close();
```

| $offlineablearrayObject | | | Mdm::OfflineableArray |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use the offline commands for offline conformations.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';

my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . 'Bacteriorhodopsin Trajectory.dsv';
my $document =
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $inputFile, LoadAllObjects => False } );
my $onlineConformations = $document->Conformations;
my $offlineConformations = $document->AllConformations;
print "There are "
. $offlineConformations->Count
. " conformations in the file.\n";
print "There are "
. $onlineConformations->Count
. " conformations loaded in memory.\n";
print "Visualize the first 10 conformations...\n";

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 10 ; $i++ )
{
my $conf = $offlineConformations->Item($i);
$conf->SetVisible();
}
$onlineConformations = $document->Conformations;
print "There are "
. $onlineConformations->Count
. " conformations loaded in memory now.\n";
print "Offline all the online conformations to release memory.\n";
my $count = $onlineConformations->Count;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $count ; $i++ )
{
my $conf = $offlineConformations->Item($i);
$conf->Offline();
}
print "Closing the document.\n";
$document->Close();
```

# Open function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/open_function.htm

## Open function

### Description

Open opens the specified file defined by required argument Path. The following optional arguments are available:

* NoDisplay only applies when run from Discovery Studio
and specifies if a view of the document will be opened. By default NoDisplay
is False and a view will be open if one is available.

* ModelType is a string specifying the document used
to open the file. By default the model type is undefined and the best
matching document and view type will be used.
When running from Discovery Studio, the ModelType provides a hint
along with the client preferences to determine the best matching type.
See the ModelType for a list of most commonly used model types.

* FormatType is a string specifying the file format
type used to import the file. By default the format type is undefined and
the best matching type will be used. See Save for a list of
format types.

### Applies to

The Open function can be used with the following objects:

DiscoveryScript

### Using the Open function

#### Static

my $documentObject = DiscoveryScript::Open( <path>, [nodisplay], [modeltype], [formattype], [loadallobjects] );

my $documentObject = DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => <path>, NoDisplay => [nodisplay], ModelType => [modeltype], FormatType => [formattype], LoadAllObjects => [loadallobjects] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | DiscoveryScript::Document |
| <path> | Required | | String |
| [formattype] | Optional | "" | String |
| [loadallobjects] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [modeltype] | Optional | "" | String |
| [nodisplay] | Optional | False | Boolean |

#### Defined by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Create an MDM document containing small molecules.
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles(
'OC(=O)C1=CC=C(C=C1)CN/C2=C/C=C(C=C2)C=CC(=O)C[Cl]');
$document->InsertFromSmiles('[CH3][CH2][OH]');
$document->InsertFromSmiles('C1=CC=CC=C1');
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');
$document->InsertFromSmiles('C1=NC=CC=C1');
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c12ccccc1cccc2');

printf "Document contains Molecules: %d Total Atoms: %d\n", $document->Molecules->Count,$document->Atoms->Count;

my $outputFolder = DiscoveryScript::GetTemporaryFolder();
my $filename = $outputFolder.'/ExampleOpen.sd';
my $format = 'mol';
$document->Save( $filename, $format );
$document->Close();
sleep(1);

# Open MDM document in Molecule Window
my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::Open(
{
Path => $filename,
ModelType => MdmModelType
}
);

printf "Document contains Molecules: %d Total Atoms: %d\n", $mdmDocument->Molecules->Count,$mdmDocument->Atoms->Count;
sleep(1);
$mdmDocument->Close();

# remove file
unlink ($filename);
```

# Operation property

## Operation property

### Description

Operation specifies a 4x4 symmetry matrix operation in Mdm::SpaceGroupSymmetryOperator objects.

### Applies to

The Operation property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::SpaceGroupSymmetryOperator

### Using the Operation property

#### Get

my $matrix4x4Object = $object->Operation;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $matrix4x4Object | | | Mdm::Matrix4x4 |
| $object | | | Mdm::SpaceGroupSymmetryOperator |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to access Mdm::SpaceGroup properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Get space group from document.
my $cell = $document->Cells->Item(0);
my $spacegroup = $cell->SpaceGroup;

print "The following is a list of space group properties:\n";
print "Number:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->Number . "\n";
print "Short Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->Symbol . "\n";
print "SchoenfliesSymbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->SchoenfliesSymbol . "\n";
print "Full Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->FullSymbol . "\n";
print "Lattice type:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->LatticeType . "\n";
print "Cell choice:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->CellChoice . "\n";
print "AxisOriginType:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->AxisOriginType . "\n";
print "Number of sym. operator:\t\t"
. $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount . "\n";

my $count = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $operator = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperator($index);
print "Symmetry operator $index\n";
print "\tName: " . $operator->Name . "\n";

my $operation = $operator->Operation;
my $format = "\t %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n";
print "\t4x4 Matrix:\n";
printf "$format",
$operation->GetEntry( 0, 0 ), $operation->GetEntry( 0, 1 ),
$operation->GetEntry( 0, 2 ), $operation->GetEntry( 0, 3 );
printf "$format",
$operation->GetEntry( 1, 0 ), $operation->GetEntry( 1, 1 ),
$operation->GetEntry( 1, 2 ), $operation->GetEntry( 1, 3 );
printf "$format",
$operation->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $operation->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$operation->GetEntry( 2, 2 ), $operation->GetEntry( 2, 3 );
printf "$format",
$operation->GetEntry( 3, 0 ), $operation->GetEntry( 3, 1 ),
$operation->GetEntry( 3, 2 ), $operation->GetEntry( 3, 3 );
}
```

# Orientation property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/orientation_property.htm

## Orientation property

### Description

Orientation is an enum Mdm::AcceptorFeatureOrientation specifying the
orientation of an Mdm::AcceptorFeature object or
orientation is an enum Mdm::DonorFeatureOrientation specifying the
orientation of an Mdm::DonorFeature object.

### Applies to

The Orientation property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AcceptorFeature , Mdm::DonorFeature

### Using the Orientation property

#### Get

my $acceptorfeatureorientationEnum = $object->Orientation;

my $donorfeatureorientationEnum = $object->Orientation;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $acceptorfeatureorientationEnum | | | enum Mdm::AcceptorFeatureOrientation |
| $donorfeatureorientationEnum | | | enum Mdm::DonorFeatureOrientation |
| $object | | | Mdm::AcceptorFeature Mdm::DonorFeature |

#### Set

$object->Orientation = <orientation>;

$object->Orientation( <orientation> );

$object->Orientation( { Orientation => <orientation> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <orientation> | Required | | enum Mdm::AcceptorFeatureOrientation enum Mdm::DonorFeatureOrientation |
| $object | | | Mdm::AcceptorFeature Mdm::DonorFeature |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles('C=O');

# Get the Oxygen atom to place the Hydrogen Bond Acceptors
my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
my $OxygenAtom;
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( $atom->Element eq "O" )
{
$OxygenAtom = $atom;
}
}

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create an HBA using the first lone pair.
my $operator1 = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$operator1->Name('HBA');
my $newAcceptor = $operator1->CreateAcceptorFeature($OxygenAtom);
$newAcceptor->Orientation('acceptorFeatureFirstLonePair');

# Create an HBA using the second lone pair.
my $operator2 = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$operator2->Name('HBA2');
my $newAcceptor2 = $operator2->CreateAcceptorFeature($OxygenAtom);
$newAcceptor2->Orientation('acceptorFeatureSecondLonePair');

$document->UpdateObjects();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script will illustrate functions and properties of the
# Sdm::Feature class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASDFGHJKL' );

# Create a join feature for residues DFGH and add it the sequence.
my $segmentStart = 2;
my $segmentCount = 4;
my $feature = $sequence->CreateCustomSequenceFeature( 'Custom feature',
Sdm::locationTypeJoin, $segmentStart, $segmentCount );
$feature->AddQualifier("InfoKey", 'Example feature');

$sequence->AddFeature($feature);

{

my $color = $feature->FillColor;
print "\tFill color\t("
. $color->Red . ' '
. $color->Green . ' '
. $color->Blue . ")\n";
$color = $feature->OutlineColor;
print "\tOutline color\t("
. $color->Red . ' '
. $color->Green . ' '
. $color->Blue . ")\n";
print "\t" . "Label\t" . $feature->LabelText . "\n";
$color = $feature->LabelColor;
print "\t"
. "Label color\t("
. $color->Red . ' '
. $color->Green . ' '
. $color->Blue . ")\n";
print "\t" . "Label type\t" . $feature->LabelFromType . "\n";
print "\t" . "Is label visible\t" . $feature->IsLabelVisible . "\n";
print "\t" . "Is label horizontal\t" . $feature->IsLabelHorizontal . "\n";
print "\t" . "Feature Location type\t" . $location->Type . "\n";
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of ValenceMonitor objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "3ptb.pdb" );

# Creates a hydrogen-bond monitor between ligand and receptor atoms.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $monitor = $document->CreateValenceMonitor($ligandAtoms);

$monitor->IsUnderValenceShown = True;

print "Found " . $monitor->UnderValenceCount . " atoms under valence.\n";

my $count = $valences->Count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{

$valence->Name, $valence->ExpectedValence, $valence->Valence;
```

# ParameterMap property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/parametermap_property.htm

## ParameterMap property

### Description

Returns a map containing all the parameters of a protocol document.

### Applies to

The ParameterMap property can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Document

### Using the ParameterMap property

#### Get

my $parametermapObject = $object->ParameterMap;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $parametermapObject | | | Protocol::ParameterMap |
| $object | | | Protocol::Document |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
print
"No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

my $protocolName = 'Minimization';
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );
my $map = $document->ParameterMap;
my $key = $map->FirstKey;
while ($key)
{
my $value = $map->Item($key);
print "Parameter name: $key\t\tValue: $value\n";
$key = $map->NextKey($key);

}

$key = 'Dielectric Constant';
my $newValue = 2.0;
my $hasItem = $document->ItemExists($key);
if ($hasItem)
{
print "\nProtocol has parameter '" . $key;
my $value = $document->Item($key);
my $type = $document->ParameterType($key);
print "\nThe type is $type. \nThe default value is $value.\n";
print "Changing parameter value of $key to $newValue.\n";
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $newValue );
}
```

```text
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
print
"No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

my $protocolName = 'Minimization';
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );
my $map = $document->ParameterMap;
my $key = $map->FirstKey;
while ($key)
{
my $value = $map->Item($key);
print "Parameter name: $key\t\tValue: $value\n";
$key = $map->NextKey($key);

}

$key = 'Dielectric Constant';
my $newValue = 2.0;
my $hasItem = $document->ItemExists($key);
if ($hasItem)
{
print "\nProtocol has parameter '" . $key;
my $value = $document->Item($key);
my $type = $document->ParameterType($key);
print "\nThe type is $type. \nThe default value is $value.\n";
print "Changing parameter value of $key to $newValue.\n";
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $newValue );
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to convert an amino acid property
# (Hydrophobicity) to an atom property and color the atoms by the
# new Hydrophobicity property.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

my $atoms = $document->Atoms;

# For each atom, create a Hydrophobicity property with
# the value of its parent residue's Hydrophobicity.
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
my $residue = $atom->Parent;
my $hydrophobicity = $residue->Hydrophobicity;
$atom->SetProperty( 'Hydrophobicity', $hydrophobicity );
}

# Color the atoms by the new atomic Hydrophobicity property.
$document->SetAtomPropertyColorScheme(
{
PropertyName => 'Hydrophobicity',
SpectrumType => Mdm::spectrumRedWhiteBlue,
NumberOfBands => 32,
RangeMinimum => -10,
RangeMaximum => 10,
Clip => 0
}
);

printf "Molecule Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$document->ModelName,$atoms->Count();
```

# PartialChargeSum property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/partialchargesum_property.htm

## PartialChargeSum property

### Description

PartialChargeSum calculates the sum of partial charges of a molecule,
weighted by the atom occupancies.

### Applies to

The PartialChargeSum property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the PartialChargeSum property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->PartialChargeSum;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

# PartitionBindingSite function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/partitionbindingsite_function.htm

## PartitionBindingSite function

### Description

PartitionBindingSite partitions the points within a binding site.

### Applies to

The PartitionBindingSite function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the PartitionBindingSite function

#### Command

$object->PartitionBindingSite( <bindingsite>, [maximumpartitioncount], [userandomseed], [randomseed] );

$object->PartitionBindingSite( { BindingSite => <bindingsite>, MaximumPartitionCount => [maximumpartitioncount], UseRandomSeed => [userandomseed], RandomSeed => [randomseed] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <bindingsite> | Required | | Mdm::BindingSite |
| [maximumpartitioncount] | Optional | 5 | Integer |
| [randomseed] | Optional | 123456 | Integer |
| [userandomseed] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

SbdDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to access binding site properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

Delete( $document, GetLigands($document) );
Delete( $document, GetWaters($document) );

my $protein = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

# Find all binding site from receptor cavities.
$document->CreateBindingSitesFromCavities($protein);
my $bindingSites = $document->BindingSites;

# Create two partition on each site.
foreach my $site (@$bindingSites)
{
$document->PartitionBindingSite( $site, 2 );
}

print "Binding site properties:\n";
print "Site Volume Threshold Points\n";
my $bsCount = 0;
foreach my $site (@$bindingSites)
{
$site->SetVisible();

my $volume = $site->GetProperty("Volume");
my $threshold = $site->GetProperty("Threshold");
my $points = $site->GetProperty("Point Count");

printf "%4d %8.3f %10.3f %7d\n", ++$bsCount, $volume, $threshold,
$points;
}

$document->EnableUpdateViews(1);
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to access several residue properties.
# In particular it demonstrates aspects of the PDB Name property, which is now also known as the RCSB CCD ID
# Whereas the original PDB structures had PDB Names limited to 3 characters, newer mmCIF files may have residues
# with 5 character CCD IDs
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '7gsa.cif' );
print "Molecule " . $document->Molecules->Item(0)->Name . " contains chains:\n\t";
my $chains = $document->Chains;
foreach my $chain (@$chains) {
print "Chain Name: " . $chain->Name . "\n\t";
print "MDM Object Class :" . $chain->ClassName . "\n\t";
}

my $residue = $chains->Item(0)->Residues->Item(0);
print "The first residue of the first chain is:\n\t";
print 'Residue Name: ' . $residue->Name . "\n\t";
print 'ID: ' . $residue->Id . "\n\t";
print 'PDB Name: ' . $residue->PDBName . "\n\t";
print 'Residue Type: ' . $residue->Type . "\n\t";
print "MDM Object Class: " . $residue->ClassName . "\n\t";

print "Try to reset the PDB name to NEW:\n\t";
$residue->PDBName = "NEW";
print "PDB Name now: " . $residue->PDBName . "\n";
print "Note that the PDB Name cannot be reset for standard residues with a defined Type\n\n";

$residue = $chains->Item(1)->Residues->Item(0);
print "The first residue of the second chain is:\n\t";
print 'Residue Name: ' . $residue->Name . "\n\t";
print 'ID: ' . $residue->Id . "\n\t";
print 'PDB Name: ' . $residue->PDBName . "\n\t";
print 'Residue Type: ' . $residue->Type . "\n\t";
print "MDM Object Class: " . $residue->ClassName . "\n\t";

print "Try to reset the PDB name to ABCDE:\n\t";
$residue->PDBName = "ABCDE";
print "PDB Name now: " . $residue->PDBName . "\n";
print "Note that the PDB Name of nonstandard residues with unknown Type may be reset and can be 5 characters long.\n";
print "This should be used with caution if retaining correspondence with standard RCSB CCD IDs is required.\n\n"; 

$residue = $chains->Item(1)->Residues->Item(1);
print "The second residue of the second chain is:\n\t";
print 'Residue Name: ' . $residue->Name . "\n\t";
print 'ID: ' . $residue->Id . "\n\t";
print 'PDB Name: ' . $residue->PDBName . "\n\t";
print 'Residue Type: ' . $residue->Type . "\n\t";
print "MDM Object Class: " . $residue->ClassName . "\n";

print "Note that the mmCIF input file contains a residue with a 5 character CCD ID\n";
print "Try to reset the PDB name to LONGID:\n\t";
$residue->PDBName = "LONGID";
print "PDB Name now: " . $residue->PDBName . "\n";
print "Note that the PDB Name may not be set to more than 5 characters long.\n\n";

$residue = $chains->Item(2)->Residues->Item(0);
print "The first residue of the third chain is:\n\t";
print 'Residue Name: ' . $residue->Name . "\n\t";
print 'ID: ' . $residue->Id . "\n\t";
print 'PDB Name: ' . $residue->PDBName . "\n\t";
print 'Residue Type: ' . $residue->Type . "\n\t";
print "MDM Object Class: " . $residue->ClassName . "\n\t";

print "Try to reset the PDB name to WAT:\n\t";
$residue->PDBName = "WAT";
print "PDB Name now: " . $residue->PDBName . "\n";
print "Note that the PDB Name cannot be reset for standard residues with a defined Type\n\n";
```

# PerceiveAromaticBonds function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/perceivearomaticbonds_function.htm

## PerceiveAromaticBonds function

### Description

Single and double bonds in aromatic ring systems are converted to aromatic bonds.

### Applies to

The PerceiveAromaticBonds function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the PerceiveAromaticBonds function

#### Instance

$object->PerceiveAromaticBonds();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to perceive aromatic bonds.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Subroutine to print bond orders and formal charges.
sub ListBondOrderAndCharge($$)
{
my ( $document, $bonds ) = @_;

my $index = 0;
foreach my $b (@$bonds)
{
my $charge1 =
$b->Atom1->FormalCharge->Numerator /
$b->Atom1->FormalCharge->Denominator;
my $charge2 =
$b->Atom2->FormalCharge->Numerator /
$b->Atom2->FormalCharge->Denominator;
print ++$index
. ') Bond: '
. $b->Atom1->Name . "("
. $charge2 . ") to:"
. $b->Atom2->Name . " ("
. $charge2 . ")"
. " order: "
. $b->BondOrder . "\n";
}
print "\n";
sleep(3);
$document->UpdateViews();
}

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1C(=O)[O-]');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $bonds = $molecule->Bonds;
my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms;
print "Initial formal charges and bonds orders:\n";
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );

print "Modified formal charges and bonds orders...\n";
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( $atom->Element eq 'O' )
{
$atom->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 2 );
my $carbon = $atom->AttachedAtom(0);
my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $carbon, $atom );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::partialDoubleBond;
}
}
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );

print "Localizing bond orders and formal charges...\n\n";
$molecule->LocalizeBonds();
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );

print "De-localizing bond orders and formal charges...\n\n";
$molecule->PerceiveAromaticBonds();
ListBondOrderAndCharge( $document, $bonds );
```

# PerceivedLonePairDonors property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/perceivedlonepairdonors_property.htm

## PerceivedLonePairDonors property

### Description

PerceivedLonePairDonors specifies all lone pair donor atoms in aromatic rings
identified by an Mdm::RingPerception object.

### Applies to

The PerceivedLonePairDonors property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::RingPerception

### Using the PerceivedLonePairDonors property

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->PerceivedLonePairDonors;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Mdm::Array |
| $object | | | Mdm::RingPerception |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the perceive rings class.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $smilesString =
'O=C(C/C1=C/C=C[S]1)N(Cc2ccccc2OC)[C@@]([H])(c3cc(OC)c(cc3)OC)C(=O)N[C@]4([H])CCCCC4';

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles($smilesString);

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
foreach my $molecule (@$molecules)
{
my $ringPerception = $molecule->PerceiveRings(
{
FindSmallestSetOfRings => True,
PerceiveAromaticity => True,
FindLonePairDonors => True
}
);

my $ringCount = $ringPerception->RingCount;
my $aromaticRingCount = $ringPerception->AromaticRingCount;

print "Ring analysis of molecule: $smilesString\n";
print "Molecule has: " . $ringCount . " rings\n";
print "Molecule has: " . $aromaticRingCount . " aromatic rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all atoms in rings.
my $ringAtoms = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedRingAtoms;
print "Molecule has: " . $ringAtoms->Count . " atoms in rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all bonds in rings.
my $ringBonds = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedRingBonds;
print "Molecule has: " . $ringBonds->Count . " bonds in rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all aromatic bonds in rings.
my $aromaticRingBonds = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedAromaticRingBonds;
print "Molecule has: "
. $aromaticRingBonds->Count
. " aromatic bonds in rings.\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all lone pair donor atoms in aromatic rings.
my $lonePairDonors = $ringPerception->PerceivedLonePairDonors;
print "Molecule has: "
. $lonePairDonors->Count
. " lone pair donor atoms in rings.\n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $ringCount ; ++$index )
{

# Get an Mdm::Array of atoms in the specified ring.
my $atoms = $ringPerception->PerceivedRingAtoms($index);

# Get an Mdm::Array of bonds in the specified ring.
my $bonds = $ringPerception->PerceivedRingBonds($index);

my $ringnum = $index + 1;
print "Ring ( $ringnum ) contains "
. $atoms->Count
. " atoms and "
. $bonds->Count
. " bonds.\n";
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

| $object | | | Mdm::RingPerception |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the perceive rings class.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $smilesString =
'O=C(C/C1=C/C=C[S]1)N(Cc2ccccc2OC)[C@@]([H])(c3cc(OC)c(cc3)OC)C(=O)N[C@]4([H])CCCCC4';

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles($smilesString);

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
foreach my $molecule (@$molecules)
{
my $ringPerception = $molecule->PerceiveRings(
{
FindSmallestSetOfRings => True,
PerceiveAromaticity => True,
FindLonePairDonors => True
}
);

my $ringCount = $ringPerception->RingCount;
my $aromaticRingCount = $ringPerception->AromaticRingCount;

print "Ring analysis of molecule: $smilesString\n";
print "Molecule has: " . $ringCount . " rings\n";
print "Molecule has: " . $aromaticRingCount . " aromatic rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all atoms in rings.
my $ringAtoms = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedRingAtoms;
print "Molecule has: " . $ringAtoms->Count . " atoms in rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all bonds in rings.
my $ringBonds = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedRingBonds;
print "Molecule has: " . $ringBonds->Count . " bonds in rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all aromatic bonds in rings.
my $aromaticRingBonds = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedAromaticRingBonds;
print "Molecule has: "
. $aromaticRingBonds->Count
. " aromatic bonds in rings.\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all lone pair donor atoms in aromatic rings.
my $lonePairDonors = $ringPerception->PerceivedLonePairDonors;
print "Molecule has: "
. $lonePairDonors->Count
. " lone pair donor atoms in rings.\n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $ringCount ; ++$index )
{

# Get an Mdm::Array of atoms in the specified ring.
my $atoms = $ringPerception->PerceivedRingAtoms($index);

# Get an Mdm::Array of bonds in the specified ring.
my $bonds = $ringPerception->PerceivedRingBonds($index);

my $ringnum = $index + 1;
print "Ring ( $ringnum ) contains "
. $atoms->Count
. " atoms and "
. $bonds->Count
. " bonds.\n";
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# PerceiveLigandGroups function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/perceiveligandgroups_function.htm

## PerceiveLigandGroups function

### Description

PerceiveLigandGroups detects small molecules in an Mdm::Molecule object and stores them under an Mdm::Assembly object named "Ligand Groups". This
function mimics the automated behavior in the Discovery Studio
client. You can use it to redefine the ligand groups in the
client or to extend this functionality outside the client.
The following options are available:

* MaximumNumberOfHeavyAtoms specifies the maximum permissible
number of atoms (excluding hydrogen) in a ligand.

* RequireCarbonContent is a Boolean datatype specifying if
ligands excluding carbon atoms are considered valid.

### Applies to

The PerceiveLigandGroups function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable

### Using the PerceiveLigandGroups function

#### Instance

my $integerValue = $object->PerceiveLigandGroups( [maximumnumberofheavyatoms], [requirecarboncontent] );

my $integerValue = $object->PerceiveLigandGroups( { MaximumNumberOfHeavyAtoms => [maximumnumberofheavyatoms], RequireCarbonContent => [requirecarboncontent] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| [maximumnumberofheavyatoms] | Optional | 100 | Integer |
| [requirecarboncontent] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrates how to find all residues belonging to the 
# same ligand as a given residue.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use MdmCommands;
use strict;

# Load an example structure.
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('2AEP');
die "Failed to create a valid MDM document!" unless $document;

# Pick a specific target ligand residue in the structure.
my $ligandResidue = SelectByString($document,"NAG1");
my $queryResidue = $ligandResidue->Residues->Item(0);
my $queryResidueId = $queryResidue->UniqueId;

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

# This creates/updates the ligand groups. Each ligand 
# consists of a set of covalently bonded residues.
my $nLigands = $molecule->PerceiveLigandGroups( 
{ MaximumNumberOfHeavyAtoms => 100, RequireCarbonContent => True } );

# Get the ligand group assembly.
my $ligandGroups = $molecule->Filter( 
{ Type=>"Assembly", Property => "Name", Name => "Ligand Groups" } );
if ($ligandGroups->Count == 1) {

# Iterate over all ligands groups.
my $ligands = $ligandGroups->Item(0)->Groups; 
foreach my $ligand (@$ligands) { 

# Get the group content in a defined order.
# Use Array() if the order in which group members are returned
# is not important.
my $ligandResidueList = $ligand->ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder();
my $found = 0;
# Check if this is the group that contains the target residue.
foreach my $ligandResidue (@$ligandResidueList ) {

if ( $ligandResidue->IsA('Mdm::Residue') ) {
if ($ligandResidue->UniqueId == $queryResidueId) {

$found = 1;
last;
}
}
}

# Print out information about the ligand if we found it.
if ($found) {

print "Found residue " . $queryResidue->Name . 
" in " . $ligand->Name . ".\n";

print "This Ligand Consists of residue(s):\n";
foreach my $ligandResidue (@$ligandResidueList ) {
print " - " .$ligandResidue->Name . "\n";
}

$ligand->Select();
last;
}
}
}

print "Done\n";
```

# PerceiveRings function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/perceiverings_function.htm

## PerceiveRings function

### Description

PerceiveRings detects bonded rings of atom. While this function can be
called from any object, it is only meaningfully applied to objects having
atoms and bonds (e.g., molecules and chains). There are several optional
parameters:

* FindSmallestSetOfRings is a Boolean datatype specifying whether to reduce
the base set of rings to the smallest set of rings.

* PerceiveAromaticity is a Boolean datatype specifying whether aromatic bonds will be searched for.

* FindLonePairDonors is a Boolean datatype specifying whether to collect lone pair donor atoms.

* ScopeArrayOfAtomsOrBonds is an Mdm::Array specifying a list of atoms and/or
bonds such that aromaticity is checked only for
rings which contain at least one of the specified
atoms and/or bonds.

* ApplyPerception is a Boolean datatype specifying whether bond orders should be changed.

### Applies to

The PerceiveRings function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AcceptorFeature , Mdm::AminoAcid , Mdm::AminoAcidChain , Mdm::AngleFeature , Mdm::AngleMonitor , Mdm::Animation , Mdm::Assembly , Mdm::Atom , Mdm::BindingSite , Mdm::BindingSitePoint , Mdm::Bond Mdm::HydrogenBond , Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor , Mdm::Isosurface , Mdm::Label3d , Mdm::Label , Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::LocationFeature , Mdm::MainChainConformationViolationMonitor , Mdm::Membrane , Mdm::MembraneOrientationMonitor , Mdm::MissingMainChainMonitor , Mdm::MissingSideChainMonitor , Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::MoleculeAssembly , Mdm::Monitor , Mdm::Neighbor , # PercentVdwRadius property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/percentvdwradius_property.htm

## PercentVdwRadius property

### Description

PercentVdwRadius specifies the van der Waals percentage when counting
bumps for bump monitors.

### Applies to

The PercentVdwRadius property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::BumpMonitor

### Using the PercentVdwRadius property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->PercentVdwRadius;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::BumpMonitor |

#### Set

$object->PercentVdwRadius = <percentradius>;

$object->PercentVdwRadius( <percentradius> );

$object->PercentVdwRadius( { PercentRadius => <percentradius> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <percentradius> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::BumpMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Search for and print bumps between ligand and receptor.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Add hydrogen atoms to all heavy atoms.
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms( Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms, True );

# Creates a bump monitor between ligand and receptor atoms.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $bumpMonitor = $document->CreateBumpMonitor( $ligandAtoms, False );

$bumpMonitor->IsLabelShown = True;
$bumpMonitor->IsIntermolecularOnlyShown = False;

print "Default percent VDW Radius: $bumpMonitor->{DefaultPercentVdwRadius}\n";
print "$bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} bumps between ligand and receptor.\n";

$bumpMonitor->PercentVdwRadius = 90;

print "$bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} bumps between ligand and receptor "
. "when VDW radius set to 90%.\n";

my $bumps = $bumpMonitor->Bumps;
my $count = $bumps->Count;

# Create a bump hash.
my %bumpHash;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $bump = $bumps->Item($index);
$bumpHash{$index}{'bump'} = $bump;
$bumpHash{$index}{'Id1'} = $bump->Atom1->Id;
$bumpHash{$index}{'Id2'} = $bump->Atom2->Id;
}

# Print information for each bump, sorted by Atom1->Id followed by Atom2->Id.
my $counter = 0;
for my $b (
sort { 
my $x = $bumpHash{$a}{'Id1'};
my $y = $bumpHash{$b}{'Id1'};
($x != $y) ? ($x <=> $y) : ($bumpHash{$a}{'Id2'} <=> $bumpHash{$b}{'Id2'})
}
keys %bumpHash
)
{
my $bump = $bumpHash{$b}{'bump'};
my $atom1 = $bump->Atom1;
my $atom2 = $bump->Atom2;
printf
"%3d) Bump: %.3f A between Atom id %d %s:%s:%s and Atom id %d %s:%s:%s\n",
++$counter, $bump->Distance(),
$bumpHash{$b}{'Id1'},
$atom1->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom1->Parent->Name, $atom1->Name,
$bumpHash{$b}{'Id2'},
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name;
}
```

# Periodicity property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/periodicity_property.htm

## Periodicity property

### Description

Periodicity describes the number of times a minimum dihedral energy will
repeat in a complete rotation. When zero, this means the selected angle is
the only minimum and the force constant has units of kcal/mol/rad/rad. When
not equal to zero, the force constant has units of kcal/mol and a cosine
formula is used.

### Applies to

The Periodicity property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::DihedralRestraint

### Using the Periodicity property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->Periodicity;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::DihedralRestraint |

#### Set

$object->Periodicity = <periodicity>;

$object->Periodicity( <periodicity> );

$object->Periodicity( { Periodicity => <periodicity> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <periodicity> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::DihedralRestraint |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
my $restraint = $document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);

printf( "The current angle is: %.4f.\n ", $restraint->DihedralAngle );
print "The dihedral atom names are:\n";
my $atoms = $restraint->DihedralAtoms;

# loop over all dihedral atoms
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
my $atomName = $atom->Name;
print $atomName;
print "\n";
}
```

# PharmacophoreCommands package

## PharmacophoreCommands package

### Description

PharmacophoreCommands provides high-level functions for accessing functionality
within PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript . These commands provide a more simple interface
to working with pharmacophores.

### Using the PharmacophoreCommands package

Access to the PharmacophoreCommands API is through the Perl use directive:

```text
use strict;
use PharmacophoreCommands;
```

The strict directive is optional, but strongly recommended as it restricts
the use of unsafe constructs. All available classes will be imported from the PharmacophoreCommands module.

#### Used by

VisualizerCommands

#### Module

PharmacophoreCommands.pm

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");

$document->CreateAndTopology();

$document->QueryAtoms->Item(0)->SetProperty( "List", "halogen" );
$document->QueryAtoms->Item(0)->AddQueryAtomValence(1);
$document->QueryAtoms->Item(0)->AddQueryAtomValence(2);
$document->QueryAtoms->Item(0)->AddQueryAtomValence(3);
my $atomValences = $document->QueryAtoms->Item(0)->QueryAtomValences();

print "Atom valences are:\n";
foreach my $atomValence (@$atomValences)
{
print "$atomValence \n";
}

my $newatomValences = DiscoveryScript::IntegerArray::Create();
$newatomValences->AddItem(0);
$newatomValences->AddItem(2);
$newatomValences->AddItem(3);
$document->QueryAtoms->Item(0)->QueryAtomValences = $newatomValences;

my $newatomValences = $document->QueryAtoms->Item(0)->QueryAtomValences();
print "\nNew lone pair counts are :\n";
foreach my $newatomValence (@$newatomValences)
{
print "$newatomValence \n";
}
```

# PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript package

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/pharmacophorediscoveryscript_package.htm

## PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript package

### Description

PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript provides functions, properties, constants, and data structures that can be used
to manipulate Discovery Studio pharmacophore data from scripts.

### Using the PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript package

Access to the PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript API is through the Perl use directive:

```text
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;
```

The strict directive is optional, but strongly recommended as it restricts
the use of unsafe constructs. All available classes will be imported from the PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript module.

#### Functions

CreateAndTopology CreateExcludeTopology CreateFitQueryOperator CreateMapping CreateOrTopology MergeQueries ShowHideFeature

#### Uses

MdmDiscoveryScript

#### Module

PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript.pm

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

# Create a query from a template molecules. Add HBAs to =O,
# HBD to N, and excluded volumes to all Halogens and
# projection points of HBAs and HBDs.

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles(
'OC(=O)C1=CC=C(C=C1)CN/C2=C/C=C(C=C2)C=CC(=O)C[Cl]');
AddHydrogens($document);

my $atoms = $document->Molecules()->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $double_bond_oxygens = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $nitrogens = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $halogens = Mdm::Array::Create();

foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( ( $atom->Element eq 'O' ) && ( $atom->BondCount == 1 ) )
{
$double_bond_oxygens->AddItem($atom);
}
$nitrogens->AddItem($atom) if ( $atom->Element eq 'N' );
$halogens->AddItem($atom) if ( $atom->Element =~ /(Cl|F|Br|I)\b/i );
}

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Features and location constraints
my $featureCount = 0;
foreach my $atom (@$double_bond_oxygens)
{
++$featureCount;
my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
my $featureName = "HBA_" . $featureCount;
$acceptorOperator->Name($featureName);
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atom);

# create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );
}

foreach my $atom (@$nitrogens)
{
++$featureCount;
my $featureName = "HBD_" . $featureCount;
my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name($featureName);
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atom);

#create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );
}

# Add excluded volumes at the location of halogen atoms
foreach my $atom (@$halogens)
{
my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

# Add excluded volumes at the projection point of HBAs and HBDs
my $acceptorfeatures = $fitOperator->AcceptorFeatures;
foreach my $acceptor (@$acceptorfeatures)
{
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atom->XYZ = $acceptor->HeadXYZ();
$molecule->Select();

my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

my $donorfeatures = $fitOperator->DonorFeatures;
foreach my $donor (@$donorfeatures)
{
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atom->XYZ = $donor->HeadXYZ();
$molecule->Select();

my $exclusionFeature = $fitOperator->CreateExclusionFeature( $atom, 1.2 );
}

my $exclusionfeatures = $document->ExclusionFeatures();
my $exclusionfeatureCount = 0;
foreach my $exclusionfeature (@$exclusionfeatures)
{
++$exclusionfeatureCount;
my $name = "EV_" . $exclusionfeatureCount;
$exclusionfeature->Name($name);
}

# We will delete temporary atoms used to create EVs
# on projection points. Need to update objects before
# deleting so we preserve the X,Y,Z location.
$document->UpdateObjects();

# Delete temporary atoms
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# PhiAngle property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/phiangle_property.htm

## PhiAngle property

### Description

PhiAngle specifies the dihedral angle in degrees defined by the C-N-CA-C atoms of peptide backbone.
Note this angle is not defined for the N-terminus residue.

### Applies to

The PhiAngle property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid

### Using the PhiAngle property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->PhiAngle;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |

#### Set

$object->PhiAngle = <angle>;

$object->PhiAngle( <angle> );

$object->PhiAngle( { Angle => <angle> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <angle> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use the phi and psi angle
# properties of amino acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $document->AminoAcidChains->Count ; ++$i )
{
my $chain = $document->AminoAcidChains->[$i];
for ( my $j = 1 ; $j < $chain->AminoAcids->Count - 1 ; ++$j )
{
my $aminoAcid = $chain->AminoAcids->[$j];
printf "%s:%s\tpshi=%.3f\tpsi=%.3f\n",
$chain->Name, $aminoAcid->Name,
$aminoAcid->PhiAngle, $aminoAcid->PsiAngle;
}
}
```

#### Defined by
