### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script shows how to create pi interaction monitors.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1kim.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Creates pi interaction monitors
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

#if no array of atoms is passed in then the monitor is created
#for the whole molecule (or other object).
my $pipiMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor();
my $piCationMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiCationMonitor();
my $piSigmaMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiSigmaMonitor();

$pipiMonitor->Name = "Pi-Pi";
$piCationMonitor->Name = "Pi-Cation";
$piSigmaMonitor->Name = "Pi-Sigma";

my $piPiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piPiInteractionCount = $piPiInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piPiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

# Change criteria settings to non-default values.
$piCationMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piCationMonitor->MinimumAngle = 60.0;
my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule\n";

$piSigmaMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->MinimumAngle = 30.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->AngleDeviation = 15.0;
my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

$pipiMonitor->MaximumCenterDistance = 7.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumClosestAtomDistance = 4.0;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumLambda = 20.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumTheta = 45.;
my $pipiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount = $pipiInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $pipiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piInteractions = $molecule->PiInteractionMonitors();
my $piCount = $piInteractions->Count();
print "\nThere are " . $piCount . " pi interaction monitors: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $piCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $piInteractions->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Interactions") );
}

#If we want to limit the scope of the monitoring, we can pass in
#an array of atoms. This is similar to creating a monitor from the UI
# when atoms are selected. Pi interactions will then be calculated within
#these, and between these and the parent object
my $residue = FilterByString( $document, "THM1" )->Item(0);
my $atom_array = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $atoms = $residue->Atoms();
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atoms->Count() ; ++$index )
{
$atom_array->AddItem( $atoms->Item($index) );
}
my $pipiMonitor2 = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor($atom_array);
my $pipiInteractions2 = $pipiMonitor2->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount2 = $pipiInteractions2->Count();
print "Number of pi-pi interactions between "
. $residue->Name()
. " and the rest of the molecule: "
. $pipiInteractionCount2 . "\n";

my $picatmonitors = $document->PiCationMonitors;
print "Number of pi-cation monitors: ". $picatmonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pipimonitors = $document->PiPiMonitors;
print "Number of pi-pi monitors: ". $pipimonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pisigmonitors = $document->PiSigmaMonitors;
print "Number of pi-sigma monitors: ". $pisigmonitors->Count . "\n";
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script shows how to create pi interaction monitors.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1kim.pdb" );
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Creates pi interaction monitors
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

#if no array of atoms is passed in then the monitor is created
#for the whole molecule (or other object).
my $pipiMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor();
my $piCationMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiCationMonitor();
my $piSigmaMonitor = $molecule->CreatePiSigmaMonitor();

$pipiMonitor->Name = "Pi-Pi";
$piCationMonitor->Name = "Pi-Cation";
$piSigmaMonitor->Name = "Pi-Sigma";

my $piPiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piPiInteractionCount = $piPiInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piPiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

# Change criteria settings to non-default values.
$piCationMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piCationMonitor->MinimumAngle = 60.0;
my $piCationInteractions = $piCationMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piCationInteractionCount = $piCationInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piCationInteractionCount
. " pi-cation interactions in this molecule\n";

$piSigmaMonitor->DistanceCutoff = 5.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->MinimumAngle = 30.0;
$piSigmaMonitor->AngleDeviation = 15.0;
my $piSigmaInteractions = $piSigmaMonitor->PiBonds();
my $piSigmaInteractionCount = $piSigmaInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $piSigmaInteractionCount
. " pi-sigma interactions in this molecule.\n";

$pipiMonitor->MaximumCenterDistance = 7.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumClosestAtomDistance = 4.0;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumLambda = 20.;
$pipiMonitor->MaximumTheta = 45.;
my $pipiInteractions = $pipiMonitor->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount = $pipiInteractions->Count();
print "There are now "
. $pipiInteractionCount
. " pi-pi interactions in this molecule.\n";

my $piInteractions = $molecule->PiInteractionMonitors();
my $piCount = $piInteractions->Count();
print "\nThere are " . $piCount . " pi interaction monitors: \n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $piCount ; ++$index )
{
my $monitor = $piInteractions->Item($index);
printf( "%d \t %s \t %s \n",
$index, $monitor->Name(), $monitor->GetProperty("Interactions") );
}

#If we want to limit the scope of the monitoring, we can pass in
#an array of atoms. This is similar to creating a monitor from the UI
# when atoms are selected. Pi interactions will then be calculated within
#these, and between these and the parent object
my $residue = FilterByString( $document, "THM1" )->Item(0);
my $atom_array = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $atoms = $residue->Atoms();
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atoms->Count() ; ++$index )
{
$atom_array->AddItem( $atoms->Item($index) );
}
my $pipiMonitor2 = $molecule->CreatePiPiMonitor($atom_array);
my $pipiInteractions2 = $pipiMonitor2->PiBonds();
my $pipiInteractionCount2 = $pipiInteractions2->Count();
print "Number of pi-pi interactions between "
. $residue->Name()
. " and the rest of the molecule: "
. $pipiInteractionCount2 . "\n";

my $picatmonitors = $document->PiCationMonitors;
print "Number of pi-cation monitors: ". $picatmonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pipimonitors = $document->PiPiMonitors;
print "Number of pi-pi monitors: ". $pipimonitors->Count . "\n";

my $pisigmonitors = $document->PiSigmaMonitors;
print "Number of pi-sigma monitors: ". $pisigmonitors->Count . "\n";
```

# pKa property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/pka_property.htm

## pKa property

### Description

pKa is the pKa value of a residue.

Initial values for standard amino acids (Creighton T.E. PROTEINS Structures and Molecular Properties. IInd Edition; W.H.Freeman and Co.: New York 2002 ).

### Applies to

The pKa property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid , Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::Nucleotide , Mdm::Residue

### Using the pKa property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->pKa;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid Mdm::NucleicAcid Mdm::Nucleotide Mdm::Residue |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to access several residue properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1CRN.pdb' );

my $cysteineCount = 0;
my $alanineCount = 0;
my $sequence = "";

my $residues = $document->Residues;
foreach my $residue (@$residues)
{
print 'Residue Name: ' . $residue->Name . "\n\t";
print 'ID: ' . $residue->Id . "\n\t";
print 'PDB: ' . $residue->PDBName . "\n\t";
print 'SymbolandId: ' . $residue->SymbolAndId . "\n\t";
print 'Hydrophobicity: ' . $residue->Hydrophobicity . "\n\t";
print 'pKa: ' . $residue->pKa . "\n";

# Create the one-letter sequence from the symbol.
$sequence = $sequence . $residue->Symbol;

++$cysteineCount if ( $residue->Type eq Mdm::cys );
++$alanineCount if ( $residue->LongName eq 'Alanine' );
}

printf "Number of cysteine residues: %d \n", $cysteineCount;
printf "Number of alanine residues: %d \n", $alanineCount;
printf "Protein sequence is: %s\n", $sequence;
```

# PointCount property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/pointcount_property.htm

## PointCount property

### Description

PointCount indicates the number of Mdm::BindingSitePoint objects
associated with a Mdm::BindingSite object.

### Applies to

The PointCount property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::BindingSite

### Using the PointCount property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->PointCount;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::BindingSite |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to access binding site properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

Delete( $document, GetLigands($document) );
Delete( $document, GetWaters($document) );

my $protein = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

# Find all binding site from receptor cavities.
$document->CreateBindingSitesFromCavities($protein);
my $bindingSites = $document->BindingSites;

# Create two partition on each site.
foreach my $site (@$bindingSites)
{
$document->PartitionBindingSite( $site, 2 );
}

print "Binding site properties:\n";
print "Site Volume Threshold Points\n";
my $bsCount = 0;
foreach my $site (@$bindingSites)
{
$site->SetVisible();

my $volume = $site->GetProperty("Volume");
my $threshold = $site->GetProperty("Threshold");
my $points = $site->GetProperty("Point Count");

printf "%4d %8.3f %10.3f %7d\n", ++$bsCount, $volume, $threshold,
$points;
}

$document->EnableUpdateViews(1);
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to create a polydot object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $pointArray = Mdm::PointArray::Create();
my $colorArray = DiscoveryScript::ColorArray::Create();

# Generate 500 random points and colors.
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 500 ; ++$i )
{
my $randX = rand();
my $randY = rand();
my $randZ = rand();
my $randColor = Mdm::Color::Create(
int( $randX * 255 ),
int( $randY * 255 ),
int( $randZ * 255 )
);
my $newPt = Mdm::Point::Create( $randX, $randY, $randZ );
$pointArray->AddItem($newPt);
$colorArray->AddItem($randColor);
}

# Create a new polydot object from the point and color arrays.
$molecule->CreatePolydot(
{ ArrayOfDots => $pointArray, ArrayOfColors => $colorArray } );

# Find and name the polydot object.
my $polydotArray = $document->Polydots;
$polydotArray->Item(0)->Name('Point Cloud 1');
$document->FitView();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# PositiveIonColor property

Source type: HTML

Source file: scripting/positiveioncolor_property.htm

## PositiveIonColor property

### Description

PositiveIonColor specifies the color of a point feature which represents a
positive ionizable standard query feature.

### Applies to

The PositiveIonColor property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::PointFeature

### Using the PositiveIonColor property

#### Static Get

my $colorObject = Mdm::PointFeature::PositiveIonColor();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $colorObject | | | Mdm::Color |
| $object | | | Mdm::PointFeature |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create a negative ionizable
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -14, 6, 0 );

my $negativeIonOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$negativeIonOperator->Name('Negative Ion');
my $negativeIonFeature =
$negativeIonOperator->CreatePointFeature( $document->Atoms );
$negativeIonFeature->Type() = 'ionizableNegativePointFeature';
$negativeIonFeature->CreateLabel('Negative Ionizable');
my $color = $negativeIonFeature->NegativeIonColor();
print "RGB of positive ionizable is: "
. $color->Red . " "
. $color->Green . " "
. $color->Blue . "\n";

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();

# Create a positive ionizable

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -14, 4.5, 0 );

my $positiveIonOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$positiveIonOperator->Name('Positive Ion');
my $positiveIonFeature =
$positiveIonOperator->CreatePointFeature( $document->Atoms );
$positiveIonFeature->Type() = 'ionizablePositivePointFeature';
$positiveIonFeature->CreateLabel('Positive Ionizable');
my $color = $positiveIonFeature->PositiveIonColor();
print "RGB of positive ionizable is: "
. $color->Red . " "
. $color->Green . " "
. $color->Blue . "\n";

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# PredictDisulfides function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/predictdisulfides_function.htm

## PredictDisulfides function

### Description

PredictDisulfides predicts sites for mutation of a pair of residues to form a disulfide bridge, creating Mdm::DisulfideBridgeSite objects from which disulfide bridges can be created.
The following arguments are available:

* Type is the enum Mdm::PredictDisulfideType that specifies whether to predict novel or existing bridges.

* Scope is the enum Mdm::PredictDisulfideScope that specifies whether to predict intra- or inter-chain bridges.

* MinimumSequenceSeparation specifies the minimum sequential separation of the residue pair in a chain.

* MaximumEnergyCutoff specifies the maximum energy for predicted sites.

* CreateCsv specifies whether to create .csv or .html output.

### Applies to

The PredictDisulfides function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the PredictDisulfides function

#### Instance

my $stringValue = $object->PredictDisulfides( [type], [scope], [minimumsequenceseparation], [maximumenergycutoff], [createcsv] );

my $stringValue = $object->PredictDisulfides( { Type => [type], Scope => [scope], MinimumSequenceSeparation => [minimumsequenceseparation], MaximumEnergyCutoff => [maximumenergycutoff], CreateCsv => [createcsv] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| [createcsv] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [maximumenergycutoff] | Optional | 10.0 | Real |
| [minimumsequenceseparation] | Optional | 5 | Integer |
| [scope] | Optional | anyChainDisulfides | enum Mdm::PredictDisulfideScope |
| [type] | Optional | novelDisulfidesOnly | enum Mdm::PredictDisulfideType |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
#This is used for the script apis
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $temp = 0;
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('4ins');

#By default, the script returns string containing a csv file of properties for the predicted disulfides.
#Only new disulfides are found, for any chain combination, minimum sequence separation 5,
#maximum energy 10.0
# i.e. default args are novelDisulfidesOnly, anyChainDisulfides, 5, 10.0, true will use this one to show how to get the residues/bonds

my $csvFile=$document->PredictDisulfides();

#save the csv file
my $name=$document->ModelName();
my $fileName=$name . "Predicted_New_Disulfides.csv";
open FILE, '>' . $fileName;
print FILE $csvFile;
close FILE;

my $molecules=$document->Molecules();

#note that if validation of existing disulfides is performed (by using Mdm::existingDisulfidesOnly#or Mdm::novelAndExistingDisulfides then a second molecule containing the modelled disulfide
#bridges and with additional properties on the bond and molecule 

my $numMols=$molecules->Count; 
if($numMols == 1){

$document->DeselectAll();
my $molecule=$molecules->Item(0);
my $residuePairsAssembly = $molecule->Filter(
{ Type=>"Assembly", Property => "Name", Name => "Predicted Disulfide Bridge Residues" } );
if($residuePairsAssembly->Count() == 1){
print "Potential residue pairs for mutation to cysteine to form disulfide bridge in ".$molecule->Name . ": \n";
my $residuePairs=$residuePairsAssembly->Item(0)->Groups();
foreach my $residuePair (@$residuePairs) {
my $residuePairList=$residuePair->ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder();
#should be 2 residues in here
if($residuePairList->Count == 2){
my $residue1 = $residuePairList->Item(0);
my $residue2 = $residuePairList->Item(1);
print "Group " . $residuePair->Name . " contains residues: ". $residue1->Name . " and " . $residue2->Name . "\n";
}
}
}

#this should now also contain predicted site objects from which we can extract more properties
print "Sites for mutation to cysteine\n";
my $sites = $document->DisulfideBridgeSites;
my $numSites = $sites->Count();
print $numSites . " sites\n";
for(my $index = 0; $index < $numSites; ++$index){
my $site=$sites->Item($index);
my $label = $site->Name;
my $score = $site->GetProperty("Score");
my $energy = $site->GetProperty("Energy");
my $badContacts = $site->GetProperty("Bad Contacts");
my $depth = $site->GetProperty("Residue Depth");
my $mobility = $site->GetProperty("Thermal Mobility");
my $sep = $site->GetProperty("Sequence Separation");
my $volchange = $site->GetProperty("Volume Change");
my $env = $site->GetProperty("Environment");
my $SA = $site->GetProperty("Solvent Accessibility");
my $chi3 = $site->GetProperty("Chi3");
print " site " . $label . " score " . $score . " energy " . $energy . " Bad contacts " . $badContacts ." residue depth " . $depth . " mobility " . $mobility . " sep " . $sep . " volchange " . $volchange . " env " . $env . " SA " . $SA . " chi3 " . $chi3 . "\n";

my $SG1Coord = $site->SG1Coord;
my $SG2Coord = $site->SG2Coord;
print " SG coordinates (" . $SG1Coord->X . ", " . $SG1Coord->Y . ", " . $SG1Coord->Z . ") and " .
"(" . $SG2Coord->X . ", " . $SG2Coord->Y . ", " . $SG2Coord->Z . ")\n";
my $residues = $site->ResiduesToMutate;
if($residues->Count == 2){
print "residue 1 " . $residues->Item(0)->Name . " residue 2 " . $residues->Item(1)->Name . "\n";
}else{
print " error - site should contain two residues\n";
}

#create S-S bridge from a site - the command works on any selected DisulfideBridgeSite
if($score > 80.0){
print "Score " . $score . " - Creating S-S bridge\n"; 
$site->Select();
$document->CreateDisulfideBridges();
$site->Deselect();
}

}

}
```

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to predict and retrieve secondary structure.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

my $sequence =
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( $mdmDocument->Molecules->[0] );
$alignment->PredictSecondaryStructureByDsc();

# Example accessing the secondary structure string from sequence property.
my $kabschAndSander =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructure(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType);
print "Kabsch and Sander secondary structure:\n";
print "Encoded: $kabschAndSander\n";

# Ensure alignment is displaying secondary structure.
if ( !( $alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown ) )
{
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown = True;
}

# Ensure KAS is displayed
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureVisible(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType) =
True;

# Example accessing the secondary structure data from object.
print "DSC secondary structure:\n";
my $ssObject =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructureObject(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);

print 'Predictor: ' . $ssObject->Predictor . "\n";
print 'Has probabilities: ' . $ssObject->IsPredicted . "\n";

my $dsc = $ssObject->SecondaryStructureString;
print "Encoded: $dsc\n";

my $propensity =
$sequence
->ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);
print "Propensity: $propensity\n";

my $helicalResidueCount = 0;
my $sheetResidueCount = 0;
my $coilResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $ssObject->ResidueCount;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $ssObject->SsType($i);
++$helicalResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$sheetResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::sheet || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
++$coilResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::coil || $type eq Sdm::extracellular );
}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print 'Analysis: The DSC secondary structure for this sequence has '
. $helicalResidueCount
. ' amino acid residues in helical formations, '
. $sheetResidueCount
. ' in sheet formations and '
. $coilResidueCount
. " in coil formations.\n";

my $secstrucfilter = $sdmDocument->SecondaryStructures;
print "Number of secondary Structures: ", $secstrucfilter->Count . "\n";
```

# PredictTransmembraneSecondaryStructure function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/predicttransmembranesecondarystructure_function.htm

## PredictTransmembraneSecondaryStructure function

### Description

PredictTransmembraneSecondaryStructure uses a Hidden Markov Model to predict the transmembrane helices for each protein sequence of the alignment. The optional usealignment parameter is not available.

### Applies to

The PredictTransmembraneSecondaryStructure function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the PredictTransmembraneSecondaryStructure function

#### Instance

$object->PredictTransmembraneSecondaryStructure( [usealignment] );

$object->PredictTransmembraneSecondaryStructure( { UseAlignment => [usealignment] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [usealignment] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to predict and retrieve transmembrane predictions.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

# Load structure of BOVINE RHODOPSIN, 1f88 and keep only first chain
my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');
my $molecule = $mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$mdmDocument->DeleteObjects();

# Access the amino acid sequence of 1f88 and predict transmembrane helices
my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

my $sequence =
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( $mdmDocument->Molecules->[0] );

$alignment->PredictTransmembraneSecondaryStructure();

# Example accessing the transmembrane prediction from sequence property.
my $tmObject =
$sequence
->ProteinSecondaryStructureObject(Sdm::transmembraneSecondaryStructureType);

print 'Predictor: ' . $tmObject->Predictor . "\n";
print 'Has probabilities: ' . $tmObject->IsPredicted . "\n";

my $tmStr = $tmObject->SecondaryStructureString;
print "Encoded: $tmStr\n\n";

my $propensity = $sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity
(Sdm::transmembraneSecondaryStructureType);
print "Propensity: $propensity\n\n";

my $membraneResidueCount = 0;
my $nonmembraneResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $tmObject->ResidueCount;

print "Probabilities:\n";
print "index\tHelical\tInside\tOutside\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $tmObject->SsType($i);
++$membraneResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$nonmembraneResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::extracellular || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
my $pHelical = $tmObject->SsTypeProbability( $i, Sdm::helical );
my $pInside = $tmObject->SsTypeProbability( $i, Sdm::cytosol );
my $pOutside = $tmObject->SsTypeProbability( $i, Sdm::extracellular );
printf "$i\t%3.2f\t%3.2f\t%3.2f\n", $pHelical, $pInside, $pOutside;

}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print "\n\n"
. "Analysis: The TRANSMEM prediction for this sequence suggests that\n "
. $membraneResidueCount
. " amino acid residues belong to a transmembrane helix and\n "
. $nonmembraneResidueCount
. " amino acids are outside the transmembrane helices.\n";
```

# PrimeNucleotide function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/primenucleotide_function.htm

## PrimeNucleotide function

### Description

PrimeNucleotide reverts the action of capping ( CapNucleotide ).
It converts the 5' terminal hydroxyl to a phosphate group and removes
the hydrogen from the 3' terminal oxygen. The resulting 3' terminus
contains a free 3' oxygen atom (not bound to hydrogen), and the
resulting 5' terminus contains a free 5' phosphate group.
Priming also changes the residue inside a chain when there is a break
(i.e., two consecutive residues are not bonded to each other in the chain).

### Applies to

The PrimeNucleotide function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::NucleicAcid , Mdm::Nucleotide

### Using the PrimeNucleotide function

#### Instance

$object->PrimeNucleotide();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::NucleicAcid Mdm::Nucleotide |

#### Defined by

NucleicAcidDiscoveryScript

#### Set

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to create a transparent surface.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '101m.pdb' );

# Select heme atoms.
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="HEM.*"; Atom label="*"');

# Create an array of all heme atoms.
my $hemeAtoms = $document->Filter( { Selected => 1 } )->Atoms;

# Create transparent surface around the heme group.
my $transparentSurface =
$document->CreateTransparentSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential,
1.3, 0.6 );

$transparentSurface->IsBackSideColorEnabled(True);
$transparentSurface->IsBackSideTransparencyEnabled(True);

# Also create wiremesh surface around the heme group.
my $wiremeshSurface =
$document->CreateWiremeshSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential, 2.0 );

print "Surface area: "
. $transparentSurface->Area . "\n"
. "Surface Volume: "
. $transparentSurface->Volume . "\n";
print "Surface probe radius: "
. $transparentSurface->ProbeRadius . "\n"
. "Transparency Level: "
. $transparentSurface->TransparencyLevel . "\n";

# Select all atoms within 6A of the heme and the surface.
$document->SelectByRadius( 6.0, 'Atom' );
$transparentSurface->Select();

# Show only the heme and neighboring atoms (other than water).
$document->FitView();
$document->InvertSelection();
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue name="HOH.*"; Atom label="*"');
$document->Hide();
$document->DeselectAll();

# Display the wiremesh surface with delay.
sleep(2);
$wiremeshSurface->SetVisible();
```

descendants of an object.

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This example shows how to access all properties of an MDM object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

my $propertyNames = $molecule->PropertyNames();

print "The following is a list of all properties of a molecule:\n";
my $count = $propertyNames->Count;
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $count )
{
my $propertyName = $propertyNames->Item($index);
printf "%4d %s: ", ++$index, $propertyName;
print $molecule->GetProperty($propertyName) . "\n";
}
```

# ProteinAggregationPropensity function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/proteinaggregationpropensity_function.htm

## ProteinAggregationPropensity function

### Description

Calculates the Protein Aggregation Propensity of amino acid residues in a protein
molecule. This first calculates the solvent accessibilities using the DS Client method and then uses these to determine aggregation scores. Note that this will yield different results from the Calculate Aggregation Scores protocol, which computes the solvent accessibilities using CHARMm and then uses the ProteinAggregationPropensityFromSaa API to calculate the aggregation scores.

### Applies to

The ProteinAggregationPropensity function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ProteinAggregationPropensity function

#### Command

$object->ProteinAggregationPropensity( [gridnumber], [radius], [contextselected] );

$object->ProteinAggregationPropensity( { GridNumber => [gridnumber], Radius => [radius], ContextSelected => [contextselected] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [contextselected] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [gridnumber] | Optional | 240 | Integer |
| [radius] | Optional | 10 | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1hzh');

#This API calculates solvent accessible areas using the DS Client method and 
#then uses these to calculate aggregation propensities. It should be noted that
#this will not give the same results as the protocol.

# Calculate the Aggregation values 
my $gridNumber = 240;
my $radius = 5;

$document->ProteinAggregationPropensity(
$gridNumber, $radius
);

#Note that if you have precomputed the Solvent Accessible Areas for each atom
#and they are stored in atom property named SAA, then the following may be used
#instead - this is what is done in the Calculate Aggregation Scores protocol 
#which calculates the SAAs using CHARMm
# $document->ProteinAggregationPropensityFromSaa( $radius);

#Now create the patch groups
my $minPeakCutoff = 0.2;
my $minPatchCutoff = 0.0;

$document->FindAggregationSites($radius);

#Now do another radius
$radius=10;
$document->ProteinAggregationPropensity(
$gridNumber, $radius
);
$document->FindAggregationSites($radius);

#create surface colored by aggregation values

$radius=5;
$document->ShowAggregationSurface($radius);

sleep(5);

#now use the API with a different radius - it will recolor the existing
#surface
$radius=10;
$document->ShowAggregationSurface($radius);

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
printf "Aggregation 5A : %.4f\n", $molecule->GetProperty("Aggr R5");
printf "Aggregation 10A : %.4f\n", $molecule->GetProperty("Aggr R10");
printf "Total Solvent Accessibility %.1f\n", $molecule->GetProperty("Total Solvent Accessibility");
```

# ProteinAggregationPropensityFromSaa function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/proteinaggregationpropensityfromsaa_function.htm

## ProteinAggregationPropensityFromSaa function

### Description

Calculates the Protein Aggregation Propensity of amino acid residues in a protein
molecule based on pre-calculated Solvent Accessible Area (SAA) values.
This method can only be used if there are per-atom properties named SAA available; to obtain the same results as the Calculate Aggregation Scores protocol these have to be computed using CHARMm. Note that the Pipeline Pilot component 'Calculate Aggregation Propensity' performs both the CHARMm SAA and this aggregation propensity calculation.

### Applies to

The ProteinAggregationPropensityFromSaa function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ProteinAggregationPropensityFromSaa function

#### Command

$object->ProteinAggregationPropensityFromSaa( [radius] );

$object->ProteinAggregationPropensityFromSaa( { Radius => [radius] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [radius] | Optional | 10 | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

# ProteinDiscoveryScript package

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/proteindiscoveryscript_package.htm

## ProteinDiscoveryScript package

### Description

ProteinDiscoveryScript provides functions, properties and constants that can be used
to manipulate Discovery Studio protein data from scripts.

### Using the ProteinDiscoveryScript package

Access to the ProteinDiscoveryScript API is through the Perl use directive:

```text
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;
```

The strict directive is optional, but strongly recommended as it restricts
the use of unsafe constructs. All available classes will be imported from the ProteinDiscoveryScript module.

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrates the transformation matrix properties and functions.
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1rvf');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $ncsMatrixName = 'BIOMT_4';

my $translateX = 0.0;
my $translateY = 0.0;
my $translateZ = 0.0;

my $ncsMatrix = Mdm::Matrix4x4::Create(
-0.309017, 0.500000, 0.809017, 0.0,
-0.500000, -0.809017, 0.309017, 0.0,
0.809017, -0.309017, 0.500000, 0.0,
$translateX, $translateY, $translateZ, 1.0
);

# Add a transformation matrix to a molecule and
# verify the matrix exists a property of the molecule.
$molecule->NcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName) = $ncsMatrix;
print "Found matrix $ncsMatrixName.\n"
if ( $molecule->HasNcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName) );

# Apply the transformation matrix to molecule's coordinates.
$document->ApplyTransformationMatrix( $molecule, $ncsMatrixName );

# Remove the matrix from molecule.
$molecule->RemoveNcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName);
print "Removed matrix $ncsMatrixName.\n"
if ( not $molecule->HasNcsMatrix($ncsMatrixName) );
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use superimposition functions
# and RMSD calculation functions for amino acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load 2rcs (an unligated antibody) from PDB.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '2rcs.pdb' );

# Load 1aj7 (a ligated antibody having the same sequence as 2crs) from PDB.
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

my $molecule2rcs = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[1];

my $hv2rcs = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 2rcs H chain V domain
my $hv1aj7 = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 1aj7 H chain V domain

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $molecule2rcs->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv2rcs->AddItem($aminoAcid);

$aminoAcid = $molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv1aj7->AddItem($aminoAcid);
}

# Show the transformation matrix which would superimpose the Vh
# domains by C-alpha atoms. This does not alter the coordinates
# of either structure.
my $matrix = $document->GetSuperimposeProteinMatrix( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
print "Transformation matrix:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 4 ; ++$i )
{
print "\t";
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < 4 ; ++$j )
{
printf "%.3f ", $matrix->GetEntry( $i, $j );
}
print "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms
my $rmsd = $document->SuperimposeProtein( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
printf "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms: %.3f\n\n", $rmsd;

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD. Note that by default the functions return an
# array of per-residue RMSD values, finishing with the overall RMSD
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it in which case the value will be zero. This can happen
# for unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation
# only for selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the
# required atoms for the requested type of calculation. 
# If you do not want per-residue RMSDs, set the 4th parameter ResidueReport
# False. In this case the array will only contain the overall RMSD.
# In this example, the all protein rmsd has no residue values calculated
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True, False );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item(0);
print "\n";

#Show that the all protein array contains just the overall RMSD.
printf "Number of values returned for all protein is %d\n", $apRmsd->Count();

# Demonstrating that the array is for all residues plus overall value not
# just selected and that as the first chain(L) is unselected its values
# are 0.
printf "Number of values returned for sidechains is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0), $scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

#Create a C-Alpha monitor
my $caMonitor = $document->CreateCAlphaMonitor();

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs before superimposing.\n";
if ($cAlphaPairs->Count > 0) {
printf "The first C-alpha to C-alpha pair distance is %.3f Angstroms.\n",
$cAlphaPairs->Item(0)->Distance;
}

#Lets do it for all matching atoms just to show the argument
my $rmsdByCA =
$document->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( $document->Molecules(), $caMonitor,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingAllAtoms );

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs after superimposing.\n";

#The values returned are like for Superimpose By Alignment - the first value
# is ref-ref (ie 0) then ref-mover for each superimposed molecule.
my $numVal = $rmsdByCA->Count();
printf( "Number of values returned for SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs %d\n",
$numVal );
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $numVal ; ++$i )
{
printf( "RMSD %d is %f\n", $i, $rmsdByCA->[$i] );
}

# use the filter function to retrieve the CAlpha atoms
my $cAlphaMonitors = $document->CAlphaMonitors;
foreach my $m (@$cAlphaMonitors)
{
print $m->ClassName ." filter entries: " . $m->CAlphaPairs->Count. "\n";
}

print "Finished Superimpose Script Example\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use alignment superimposition functions and
# RMSD calculation functions for amino acids or non-standard residues.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1gaf.pdb' );

my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1gaf = $document->Molecules->[1];

# H chain V domains only
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
$molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
$molecule1gaf->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
}

my $Sequence1aj7 = $molecule1aj7->AminoAcidSequence;
my $Sequence1gaf = $molecule1gaf->AminoAcidSequence;
my $sequences = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1aj7);
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1gaf);

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms. The function returns an array
# of RMSD values between the reference and all molecules, starting with itself.
my $rmsds =
$document->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment( $document->Molecules, $sequences,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms, True );

print "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $document->Molecules->Count() ; ++$i )
{
print "\t"
. $document->Molecules->[$i]->Name . " to "
. $molecule1aj7->Name . ": ";
printf "%.3f\n", $rmsds->[$i];
}
print "\n";

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD
# Note that these functions return an array of real numbers. These are the
# per residue RMSD values plus, in the last element, the overall RMSD.
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it (the value will be zero). This can happen for
# unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation only for
# selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the required atoms for
# the requested type of calculation.
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item( $apRmsd->Count() - 1 );
print "\n";

# This demonstrates that the array is for all residues plus overall
# value, not just selected, and that as the first chain(L) is
# unselected (its values are 0).
printf "Number of values returned is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain.
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H chain.
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

# Get antigen NPE from 1aj7.
my $antigen1 = $document->Molecules->[0]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Get antigen NPE from 1gaf.
my $antigen2 = $document->Molecules->[1]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Copy antigen residues to a new document.
my $tmpDocument = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $tmpMolecule1 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen1Copy = $antigen1->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen1Copy, $tmpMolecule1 );
my $tmpMolecule2 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen2Copy = $antigen2->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen2Copy, $tmpMolecule2 );

$tmpDocument->FitView();

# Calculate NPE RMSD.
my $rmsd =
$tmpDocument->CalculateOtherResidueRmsd( $tmpMolecule1, $tmpMolecule2 );
printf "NPE RMSD: %.3f\n", $rmsd->[1];
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use ProteinPose properties.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing docked protein poses.\n";
print " 3 Enter a cluster ID in the Arguments tab.\n";
print " 4 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

my ($clusterID) = @ARGV;

if ( $clusterID !~ /^\d+$/ )
{
$clusterID = 1;
}

# The script assume the last active document contains ProteinPoses.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage( 'This example requires an open Molecule Window containing '
. 'docked protein poses.' )
unless ($document);

# Get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter.
my $poseGroups = $document->DockedProteinPoseAssemblies;
Usage( 'This example requires an open Molecule Window containing '
. 'docked protein poses.' )
unless ( $poseGroups->Count > 0 );

my $poses = $document->ProteinPoses;

my $topClusterPose;

# Show all poses in cluster $clusterID, color green.
foreach my $pose (@$poses)
{
if ( $pose->Cluster == $clusterID )
{
$pose->SetVisible();

# Represent best ranked pose in the cluster as sphere and color light green.
if ( $pose->IsTopClusterPose )
{
$pose->DisplayStyle(Mdm::styleProteinPoseSphere);
$pose->Color( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 0 ) );
$topClusterPose = $pose;
}

# Represent other cluster members as jacks and color dark green.
else
{
$pose->DisplayStyle(Mdm::styleProteinPoseJack);
$pose->Color( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 122, 0 ) );
}
}
else
{

# Hide all poses not in the cluster.
$pose->SetInvisible();
}
}
```

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use properties of the MembraneOrientationMonitor
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load structure of BOVINE RHODOPSIN, 1f88 and keep only first chain
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# "Guess" some value for the membrane position
my $center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, -3.2 );
my $normal = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.521, 0.106, 0.847 );

my $membrane =
$document->CreateMembrane( $center, $normal, 60.0, 60.0, 30.0 );

$document->SetParent( $molecule, $membrane );

my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms();

# Illustrate on how to use MembraneOrientationMonitor preferences
my $membraneOrientation =
$molecule->CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor( $membrane, $atoms,
Mdm::objectCentered, Mdm::referenceAxisZ );

$document->UpdateViews();

my $monitors = $document->MembraneOrientationMonitors;
print "Number of membrane monitors: ". $monitors->Count. "\n";

my $membranes = $document->Membranes;
print "Number of membranes: ". $membranes->Count. "\n";

sleep(2);

$membraneOrientation->DisplayLocation = Mdm::membraneCentered;
$membraneOrientation->ProteinReferenceAxis = Mdm::referenceAxisX;
```

# ProteinSecondaryStructure property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/proteinsecondarystructure_property.htm

## ProteinSecondaryStructure property

### Description

ProteinSecondaryStructure specifies the amino acid secondary structure as a string.
The characters in the string indicate the predicted or known secondary structure.

### Applies to

The ProteinSecondaryStructure property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence

### Using the ProteinSecondaryStructure property

#### Get

my $stringValue = $object->ProteinSecondaryStructure( <predictor> );

my $stringValue = $object->ProteinSecondaryStructure( { Predictor => <predictor> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| <predictor> | Required | | enum Sdm::AminoAcidSecondaryStructurePredictor |
| $object | | | Sdm::AminoAcidSequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to predict and retrieve secondary structure.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

my $sequence =
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( $mdmDocument->Molecules->[0] );
$alignment->PredictSecondaryStructureByDsc();

# Example accessing the secondary structure string from sequence property.
my $kabschAndSander =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructure(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType);
print "Kabsch and Sander secondary structure:\n";
print "Encoded: $kabschAndSander\n";

# Ensure alignment is displaying secondary structure.
if ( !( $alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown ) )
{
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown = True;
}

# Ensure KAS is displayed
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureVisible(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType) =
True;

# Example accessing the secondary structure data from object.
print "DSC secondary structure:\n";
my $ssObject =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructureObject(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);

print 'Predictor: ' . $ssObject->Predictor . "\n";
print 'Has probabilities: ' . $ssObject->IsPredicted . "\n";

my $dsc = $ssObject->SecondaryStructureString;
print "Encoded: $dsc\n";

my $propensity =
$sequence
->ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);
print "Propensity: $propensity\n";

my $helicalResidueCount = 0;
my $sheetResidueCount = 0;
my $coilResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $ssObject->ResidueCount;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $ssObject->SsType($i);
++$helicalResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$sheetResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::sheet || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
++$coilResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::coil || $type eq Sdm::extracellular );
}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print 'Analysis: The DSC secondary structure for this sequence has '
. $helicalResidueCount
. ' amino acid residues in helical formations, '
. $sheetResidueCount
. ' in sheet formations and '
. $coilResidueCount
. " in coil formations.\n";

my $secstrucfilter = $sdmDocument->SecondaryStructures;
print "Number of secondary Structures: ", $secstrucfilter->Count . "\n";
```

# ProteinSurfaceChargeMap function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/proteinsurfacechargemap_function.htm

## ProteinSurfaceChargeMap function

### Description

Calculates the Protein Surface Charge Map for a protein
molecule based on pre-calculated Solvent Accessible Area (SAA) values.
This method can only be used if there are per-atom properties named SAA available; to obtain the same results as the Calculate Formulation Properties protocol these have to be computed using CHARMm. Note that the Pipeline Pilot component 'Calculate Surface Maps' performs both the CHARMm SAA and this surface charge map calculation.

### Applies to

The ProteinSurfaceChargeMap function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ProteinSurfaceChargeMap function

#### Command

$object->ProteinSurfaceChargeMap( [radius] );

$object->ProteinSurfaceChargeMap( { Radius => [radius] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [radius] | Optional | 10 | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#This script requires that the loaded molecule has precomputed 
#solvent accessible surface area properties (SAA) on the atoms 
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
my $radius = 10.0;
print "Calculating Surface Charge Map...\n";
$document->ProteinSurfaceChargeMap( $radius);

$document->UpdateViews();

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

printf "Qmap Scores 10A Negative : %.4f Positive %.4f\n", $molecule->GetProperty("Negative QMap R10"),$molecule->GetProperty("Positive QMap R10");
```

# Protocol::Document::Create function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/protocol__document__create_function.htm

## Protocol::Document::Create function

### Description

Create creates one or more Protocol::Document objects.

### Applies to

The Protocol::Document::Create function can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Document

### Using the Protocol::Document::Create function

#### Static

my $documentObject = Protocol::Document::Create( <protocolname>, <session> );

my $documentObject = Protocol::Document::Create( { ProtocolName => <protocolname>, Session => <session> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $documentObject | | | Protocol::Document |
| <protocolname> | Required | | String |
| <session> | Required | | Protocol::Session |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";

print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

{

sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages;

if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";

my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

# Protocol::ParameterMap class

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/protocol__parametermap_class.htm

## Protocol::ParameterMap class

### Description

The Protocol::ParameterMap stores all the parameters of a protocol document.

Note. Requires a connection to a Pipeline Pilot server.

### Using the Protocol::ParameterMap object

The Protocol::ParameterMap object can be accessed via the ProtocolDiscoveryScript package.

#### Properties

ClassName , Count , FirstKey , IsEmpty , Item , ItemExists , NextKey

#### Functions

AddItem , ClearItems , DeleteItem , InsertItem , Protocol::ParameterMap::Create , ReplaceItem

#### Returned by

ParameterMap , Protocol::ParameterMap::Create

#### Derived from

DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
print
"No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

my $protocolName = 'Minimization';
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );
my $map = $document->ParameterMap;
my $key = $map->FirstKey;
while ($key)
{
my $value = $map->Item($key);
print "Parameter name: $key\t\tValue: $value\n";
$key = $map->NextKey($key);

}

$key = 'Dielectric Constant';
my $newValue = 2.0;
my $hasItem = $document->ItemExists($key);
if ($hasItem)
{
print "\nProtocol has parameter '" . $key;
my $value = $document->Item($key);
my $type = $document->ParameterType($key);
print "\nThe type is $type. \nThe default value is $value.\n";
print "Changing parameter value of $key to $newValue.\n";
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $newValue );
}
```

# ProtocolCommands package

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/protocolcommands_package.htm

## ProtocolCommands package

### Description

ProtocolCommands provides high-level functions for accessing functionality
within ProtocolDiscoveryScript . These commands provide a more simple
interface to working with protocols.

### Using the ProtocolCommands package

Access to the ProtocolCommands API is through the Perl use directive:

```text
use strict;
use ProtocolCommands;
```

The strict directive is optional, but strongly recommended as it restricts
the use of unsafe constructs. All available classes will be imported from the ProtocolCommands module.

#### Commands

LaunchProtocol

#### Uses

MdmCommands

#### Module

ProtocolCommands.pm

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use ProtocolCommands;

# From ProtocolDiscoveryScript
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();

# From ProtocolCommands
LaunchProtocol( "GetPPVersion", Protocol::ParameterMap::Create(),
$session->Server );
```

```text
for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

# PsiAngle property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/psiangle_property.htm

## PsiAngle property

### Description

PsiAngle specifies the dihedral angle in degrees defined by the N-CA-C-N atoms of peptide backbone.
Note this angle is not defined for the C-terminus residue.

### Applies to

The PsiAngle property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid

### Using the PsiAngle property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->PsiAngle;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |

#### Set

$object->PsiAngle = <angle>;

$object->PsiAngle( <angle> );

$object->PsiAngle( { Angle => <angle> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <angle> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use the phi and psi angle
# properties of amino acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $document->AminoAcidChains->Count ; ++$i )
{
my $chain = $document->AminoAcidChains->[$i];
for ( my $j = 1 ; $j < $chain->AminoAcids->Count - 1 ; ++$j )
{
my $aminoAcid = $chain->AminoAcids->[$j];
printf "%s:%s\tpshi=%.3f\tpsi=%.3f\n",
$chain->Name, $aminoAcid->Name,
$aminoAcid->PhiAngle, $aminoAcid->PsiAngle;
}
}
```

# Publication property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/publication_property.htm

## Publication property

### Description

Publication specifies the publication associated with an Sdm::Sequence .

### Applies to

The Publication property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the Publication property

#### Get

my $publicationObject = $object->Publication( <index> );

my $publicationObject = $object->Publication( { Index => <index> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $publicationObject | | | Sdm::Publication |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence Sdm::Sequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Publication class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'Y13252-truncated',
'TCTAGAGTAACATTTAGAATTAAGGTGGGAAATTATCTTAAAATCT' );

my $title =
'Nonfixed duplication containing the Adh gene and a truncated form '
. 'of the Adhr gene in the Drosophila funebris species group: different '
. 'modes of evolution of Adh relative to Adhr in Drosophila';

# Create publication object with sample data.
my $publication01 = Sdm::Publication::Create( 'Amador, A., Juan, E.',
$title, 'Molec. Biol. Evol.' );

# Create publication and add content separately.
my $publication02 = Sdm::Publication::Create();
$publication02->Authors = 'Amador, A., Juan, E.';
$publication02->Title = $title;
$publication02->Journal = 'Molec. Biol. Evol.';
$publication02->Reference = '16(11): 1439--1456 (1999)';
$publication02->PubMedId = '10555275';
$publication02->Comment = 'y13252';

#$publication02->Consortium = '';
#$publication02->DigitalObjectId = '';
#$publication02->MedlineId = '';
#$publication02->PubMedId = '';

# Associate publications with a sequence object.
# NOTE: To see the publications in Discovery Studio, double-click on the
# sequence in the sequence window to open a sequence annotation window.
# Publications are listed in the data table's Literature Citation tab.
$sequence->AddPublication($publication01);
$sequence->AddPublication($publication02);

my $publicationCount = $sequence->PublicationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $publicationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $publication = $sequence->Publication($index);
printf "%d: %s, %s. %s %s.\n",
$index + 1,
$publication->Authors,
$publication->Title,
$publication->Journal,
$publication->Reference;
}

$sequence->DeletePublication(0);
```

#### Defined by

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate use of Sdm::Qualifier objects.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';
my $filePath = $samplesFolder . 'D.funebris ADH Gene.bsml';

my $document = DiscoveryScript::Open($filePath);
my $feature = $document->Features->Item(0);

# Add qualifier to feature
$feature->AddQualifier( 'Test', "Value of Test" );

# Get qualifiers using filter
my $qualifiers = $feature->Qualifiers;
my $count = $qualifiers->Count();
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $count ; ++$i )
{

# List qualifier Key-Value data
my $qualifier = $qualifiers->Item($i);
print 'Qualifier Key: '
. $qualifier->Key . "\t"
. ' Value: '
. $qualifier->Value . "\n";
}

print "All qualifiers can be printed using the Comments property.\n";
print "Comments: " . $feature->Comment;

# Remove qualifier from feature
$feature->DeleteQualifier('TestKey');
```

Mdm::RingAromaticFeature , Mdm::RotatableBondMonitor , Mdm::ScreenLabel , Mdm::Set , Mdm::ShapeFeature , Mdm::SideChainConformationViolationMonitor , Mdm::SlicingPlane , Mdm::Sphere , Mdm::Surface , ```text
```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty queries
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();
my $query2 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create some features on the queries
# Create a donor feature on query1 at 0,0,0
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# Create an acceptor feature on query2 at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $query2->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

# Merge two queries into one:
my $queries = $document->Queries;
$document->MergeQueries( @$queries[0], @$queries[1] );

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Create a distance constraint (7.5 to 9.5 angstroms) between O and [N,O,S]
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create Mdm::Array to store atoms to use for distance constraint.
my $atoms = Mdm::Array::Create();

# Create an oxygen atom at (-15.6, 2.2, 0.0).
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -15.6, 2.2, 0 );
$atoms->AddItem($atomObject);

# Create a Nitrogen atom at (-7.2, 2.3, 0.0).
my $molecule1 = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject1 = $molecule1->CreateAtom("N");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( -7.2, 2.3, 0 );
$atoms->AddItem($atomObject1);

# Create an 'AND' query containing the selected molecules (all
# molecules are used if none selected). This will be used as the
# top level for the distance constraint.
$document->CreateAndTopology();

# Get the Root operator.
my $operators = $document->QueryOperators;
my $rootOperator;
foreach my $operator (@$operators)
{
if ( $operator->IsRoot )
{
$rootOperator = $operator;
}
}

# Create the distance constraint off the root operator.
my $distanceConstraint =
$rootOperator->CreateDistanceFeature( $atoms, 7.5, 9.5 );

# Get N QueryAtom and change it to N,O,S.
my $queryAtoms = $document->QueryAtoms;
foreach my $queryAtom (@$queryAtoms)
{
my $atomList = $queryAtom->GetProperty("List");
if ( $atomList eq 'N' )
{
$queryAtom->SetProperty( "List", "N O S" );
$queryAtom->Parent()->Select; # select it for the color command below
}
}

# Color the QueryAtom with multiple definitions another color
$document->SetColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 170, 85, 127 ) );
$document->DeselectAll();
```

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles('c1ccccc1');

$document->CreateAndTopology();

# The query bonds are automatically created using
# the CreateAndTopology function. However, to show
# how to create them using CreateBondQuery, we will delete
# them and then add them again.

my $querybonds = $document->QueryBonds;
foreach my $querybond (@$querybonds)
{
$querybond->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

my $bonds = $document->Bonds;
foreach my $bond (@$bonds)
{
my $querybond =
$document->QueryOperators()->Item(0)->CreateQueryBond($bond);
$querybond->AddBondType('queryAnyBond');
}

# removes the first query bond's bond type
$document->QueryBonds->Item(0)->RemoveBondType('queryAnyBond');
```

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <radius> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::BindingSitePoint Mdm::Cylinder Mdm::ExclusionFeature Mdm::LocationFeature Mdm::Sphere |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Creates an empty molecule
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();

# Create oxygen atoms
my $O1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);
my $O2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

# Assign coordinates to atoms
my $xyz1 = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O1->XYZ = $xyz1;

my $xyz2 = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O2->XYZ = $xyz2;

# Create Spheres centered on atom position
my $sphere1 = $O1->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz1, Radius => 0.4 } );
my $sphere2 = $O2->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz2, Radius => 0.4 } );

# Create Cylinder
my $cylinder =
$O1->CreateCylinder( { Begin => $xyz1, End => $xyz2, Radius => 0.2 } );
my $bottom = $cylinder->{BottomCenter};
printf "Cylinder bottom center: %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n Radius: %8.3f\n",
$bottom->X, $bottom->Y, $bottom->Z, $cylinder->Radius;

# Make cylinder transparent
$cylinder->IsTransparent(True);

# Create a slicing plane perpendicular to the cylinder axis
my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
my $slicingplaneObject = $document->CreateSlicingPlane(
{
Index => 1,
ArrayOfObjects => $atoms,
Origin => Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 ),
Normal => Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 )
}
);

# Get all 3D Objects
my $objects3d = $document->Geometric3ds;

# Print their name and class name
foreach my $object (@$objects3d)
{
print $object->ClassName . "\t" . $object->Name . "\n";
}

# Get all slicing planes
my $slicplanes = $document->SlicingPlanes;
print "Number of slicing planes" . $slicplanes->Count. "\n";
```

# RadiusOfGyration property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/radiusofgyration_property.htm

## RadiusOfGyration property

### Description

RadiusOfGyration indicates the radius of gyration of a molecule or conformation. It is calculated as the average distance of all atoms to its geometric center: R g = (Σr 2 ) 1/2 /N, where r is the distance between an atom and the geometric center and N is the total number of atoms. Note that this version is not mass-weighted. The RadOfGyration in the Calculate Molecular Properties tool is mass-weighted.

### Applies to

The RadiusOfGyration property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Conformation , Mdm::Molecule , Mdm::Offlineable , Mdm::OfflineableConformation

### Using the RadiusOfGyration property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->RadiusOfGyration;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Conformation Mdm::Molecule Mdm::Offlineable Mdm::OfflineableConformation |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This scripts illustrates how to access several properties of
# the Mdm::Molecule object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

$molecule->IsChargeCalculated = True;

print "The following is a list of molecule properties:\n";
print 'Name: ' . $molecule->Name . "\n";
print 'Approximate volume: ' . $molecule->ApproximateVolume . "\n";
print 'Atom count: ' . $molecule->AtomCount . "\n";

my $centerOfMass = $molecule->CenterOfMass;
printf "Center of mass: %8.3f\t%8.3f\t%8.3f\n",
$centerOfMass->X,
$centerOfMass->Y,
$centerOfMass->Z;

print 'Chiral center count: ' . $molecule->ChiralCenterCount . "\n";
print 'Composition: ' . $molecule->Composition . "\n";
print 'Density: ' . $molecule->Density . "\n";
print 'Exact molecular weight: ' . $molecule->ExactMolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen bond acceptor count: '
. $molecule->HydrogenBondAcceptorCount . "\n";
print 'Hydrogen bond donor count: '
. $molecule->HydrogenBondDonorCount . "\n";
print 'Lipinski violation count: ' . $molecule->LipinskiViolationCount . "\n";
print 'Molecular formula: ' . $molecule->MolecularFormula . "\n";
print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Radius of gyration: ' . $molecule->RadiusOfGyration . "\n";
print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
print 'Rotatable bond count: ' . $molecule->RotatableBondCount . "\n";
print 'Surface area: ' . $molecule->SurfaceArea . "\n";
```

```text
# this should be -1
print "Random number seed = " . $rns . "\n";
die "Unexpected result" if $rns != -1;

$hrns = $document->HasRandomNumberSeed;
print "Has random number seed = " . $hrns . "\n";
die "Unexpected result" if $hrns != 0;

$rns = -314;
$document->RandomNumberSeed = $rns;

$rns = $document->RandomNumberSeed;
# this should be -1
print "Random number seed = " . $rns . "\n";
die "Unexpected result" if $rns != -1;
```
