### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Example filter_constraints
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Fix backbone atoms in sheet or helix
my $helicalBackboneAtoms = $document->FilterByProperty(
'Residue Secondary="Helix",Secondary="Sheet"; Atom label="CA",label="C",label="O",label="N"'
);
$document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($helicalBackboneAtoms);

# Add harmonic constraint on all backbone atoms in coils
my $coiledBackboneAtoms = $document->FilterByProperty(
'Residue Secondary="Coil";Atom label="CA",label="C",label="O",label="N"');
$document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint(
{ ArrayOfAtoms => $coiledBackboneAtoms, ForceConstant => 1.2 } );

# Add cross-strand distance restraint
{
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "THR2:CA" );
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "ILE34:CA" );
$document->CreateDistanceRestraint(
{
ArrayOfAtoms1 => $atom1,
ArrayOfAtoms2 => $atom2,
RMin => 2,
RMax => 5
}
);
}

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
{
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
$document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);
}

# Get arrays with for each type of constraint using the corresponding filters
# Note that the constraint filter includes constraints and restraints
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
my $fixedAtomConstraints = $document->FixedAtomConstraints;

# Note that the restraint filter includes dihedral, distance and harmonic restraints
my $restraints = $document->Restraints;
my $dihedralRestraints = $document->DihedralRestraints;
my $distanceRestraints = $document->DistanceRestraints;
my $harmonicRestraints = $document->HarmonicAtomRestraints;

# Print out total number of constraints, along with a list of their names
print "There are " . $constraints->Count . " constraints (\t";
foreach my $constraint (@$constraints)
{
my $name = $constraint->GetProperty("Name");
print "$name\t";
}

# Print out the number of each type of constraints
print ")\nout of which ";
print $restraints->Count . " are Restraints :\n";
print " " . $dihedralRestraints->Count . " DihedralRestraint(s)\n";
print " " . $distanceRestraints->Count . " DistanceRestraint(s)\n";
print " " . $harmonicRestraints->Count . " HarmonicAtomRestraint(s)\n";
print "and \n";
```

# Reverse function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/reverse_function.htm

## Reverse function

### Description

Reverse reverses the residue order in an Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence .
There are several parameters:

* StartPosition is the index of the first residue to perform a complement.

* Count is the number of residues to complement.

### Applies to

The Reverse function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the Reverse function

#### Instance

$object->Reverse( <startposition>, [count] );

$object->Reverse( { StartPosition => <startposition>, Count => [count] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <startposition> | Required | | Integer |
| [count] | Optional | 1 | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence Sdm::Sequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate sequence complement and reverse functions.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateNucleotideDocument();
my $sequence =
$document->CreateSequence( 'Seq', 'CGACCTCGCGGGTTTTCGCTATTTATGAAA' );
my $residueCount = $sequence->ResidueCount;

print 'Sequence is ' . $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";

$sequence->Complement( 0, $residueCount );
print 'Complement of sequence is ' . $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";

$sequence->Reverse( 0, $residueCount );
print 'Reverse of sequence is ' . $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";

$sequence->ReverseComplement( 0, $residueCount );
print 'Reverse complement of sequence is ' . $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
```

# ReverseComplement function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/reversecomplement_function.htm

## ReverseComplement function

### Description

ReverseComplement reverses and then complements nucleotides in the range (StartPosition, StartPosition + Count).
SDM Features that overlap the range have locations reversed before ReverseComplement splits on the boundaries.
There are several parameters:

* StartPosition is the index of the first residue to perform a complement.

* Count is the number of residues to complement.

### Applies to

The ReverseComplement function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the ReverseComplement function

# RingCount property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/ringcount_property.htm

## RingCount property

### Description

RingCount specifies the number of rings of atoms identified by an Mdm::RingPerception .

### Applies to

The RingCount property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::RingPerception

### Using the RingCount property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->RingCount;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::RingPerception |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the perceive rings class.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $smilesString =
'O=C(C/C1=C/C=C[S]1)N(Cc2ccccc2OC)[C@@]([H])(c3cc(OC)c(cc3)OC)C(=O)N[C@]4([H])CCCCC4';

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
$document->InsertFromSmiles($smilesString);

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
foreach my $molecule (@$molecules)
{
my $ringPerception = $molecule->PerceiveRings(
{
FindSmallestSetOfRings => True,
PerceiveAromaticity => True,
FindLonePairDonors => True
}
);

my $ringCount = $ringPerception->RingCount;
my $aromaticRingCount = $ringPerception->AromaticRingCount;

print "Ring analysis of molecule: $smilesString\n";
print "Molecule has: " . $ringCount . " rings\n";
print "Molecule has: " . $aromaticRingCount . " aromatic rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all atoms in rings.
my $ringAtoms = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedRingAtoms;
print "Molecule has: " . $ringAtoms->Count . " atoms in rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all bonds in rings.
my $ringBonds = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedRingBonds;
print "Molecule has: " . $ringBonds->Count . " bonds in rings\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all aromatic bonds in rings.
my $aromaticRingBonds = $ringPerception->AllPerceivedAromaticRingBonds;
print "Molecule has: "
. $aromaticRingBonds->Count
. " aromatic bonds in rings.\n";

# Get an Mdm::Array of all lone pair donor atoms in aromatic rings.
my $lonePairDonors = $ringPerception->PerceivedLonePairDonors;
print "Molecule has: "
. $lonePairDonors->Count
. " lone pair donor atoms in rings.\n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $ringCount ; ++$index )
{

# Get an Mdm::Array of atoms in the specified ring.
my $atoms = $ringPerception->PerceivedRingAtoms($index);

# Get an Mdm::Array of bonds in the specified ring.
my $bonds = $ringPerception->PerceivedRingBonds($index);

my $ringnum = $index + 1;
print "Ring ( $ringnum ) contains "
. $atoms->Count
. " atoms and "
. $bonds->Count
. " bonds.\n";
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# RMax property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/rmax_property.htm

## RMax property

### Description

RMax is the maximum distance allowed for a distance restraint. Above this
value a force will be applied during simulation equal to the deviation from
this value squared, times the RMax force constant. This formula applies up to
the ForceMaximum value, when a linear relationship is used.

### Applies to

The RMax property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::DistanceRestraint

### Using the RMax property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->RMax;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::DistanceRestraint |

#### Set

$object->RMax = <rmax>;

$object->RMax( <rmax> );

$object->RMax( { RMax => <rmax> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <rmax> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::DistanceRestraint |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Fix the backbone
my $backbone = FilterByString( $document, ':CA,C,N,O,HN,HA' );
$document->CreateFixedAtomConstraint($backbone);

# Restrain beta carbon atoms
my $cbeta = FilterByString( $document, ':CB' );
$document->CreateHarmonicAtomRestraint( $cbeta, 10, Mdm::BestFit );

# Add cross-strand distance restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "THR2:CA" );
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "ILE34:CA" );
$document->CreateDistanceRestraint(
{
ArrayOfAtoms1 => $atom1,
ArrayOfAtoms2 => $atom2,
RMin => 2,
RMax => 5,
RMinForceConstant => 10,
RMaxForceConstant => 20,
ForceMaximum => 20
}
);

# Add Chi1 dihedral restraint
my $atom1 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:N" )->Item(0);
my $atom2 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CA" )->Item(0);
my $atom3 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CB" )->Item(0);
my $atom4 = FilterByString( $document, "TYR29:CG" )->Item(0);
$document->CreateDihedralRestraint(
{
Atom1 => $atom1,
Atom2 => $atom2,
Atom3 => $atom3,
Atom4 => $atom4,
ForceConstant => 20,
ReferenceAngle => 180
}
);

# Print the total number of restraints (4)
my $constraints = $document->Constraints;
print "There are ", $constraints->Count, " constraints\n";
```

# RootObject property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/rootobject_property.htm

## RootObject property

### Description

RootObject specifies the Mdm::Object that is
the hierarchical ancestor of all other objects in an Mdm::Document .

### Applies to

The RootObject property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the RootObject property

#### Get

my $objectObject = $object->RootObject;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $objectObject | | | Mdm::Object |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script will illustrate the use of RootObject and ChangeObjectParent.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
die "An open Molecule Window is required to " 
. "run this example script." unless $document;

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
printf "Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$molecule->Name,$molecule->Atoms->Count();

# Create a copy of the molecule.
my $moleculeCopy = $molecule->Copy();

# Reparent the copy to a new document's root object.
my $newDocument = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $newDocumentRoot = $newDocument->RootObject;
$newDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $moleculeCopy, $newDocumentRoot );

$newDocument->FitView();

printf "Name: %s Atom count: %d\n",$newDocument->Molecules->Item(0)->Name,
$newDocument->Atoms->Count();
```

# RotamerCount property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/rotamercount_property.htm

## RotamerCount property

### Description

RotamerCount specifies the number of rotamers available for a specified
residue. There is one required argument, the amino acid residue, and an
optional argument specifying the rotamer library to be used, which
defaults to Mdm::ponderAndRichardsRotamerLibrary. The other valid options
are Mdm::sutcliffeRotamerLibrary, Mdm::oldfieldRotamerLibrary, and
Mdm::richardsonAndRichardsonRotamerLibrary.

### Applies to

The RotamerCount property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the RotamerCount property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->RotamerCount( <residue>, [rotamerlibrary] );

my $integerValue = $object->RotamerCount( { Residue => <residue>, RotamerLibrary => [rotamerlibrary] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| <residue> | Required | | Mdm::AminoAcid |
| [rotamerlibrary] | Optional | ponderAndRichardsRotamerLibrary | enum Mdm::RotamerLibrary |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

#Script which demonstrates how to step through rotamers for an amino acid
#including some methods of assessment.
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# create an array of all aminoacids in the system
my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;

#get one to search - (this is TYR29)
my $aminoAcid = $aminoAcids->Item(28);

# retrieve the residue name
my $aminoAcidName = $aminoAcid->Name;

#and the atoms - we really only want the sidechain. There may be a better way to do this!
my $aaAtoms = $aminoAcid->Atoms;
my $sideChainAtoms = Mdm::Array::Create();
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $aaAtoms->Count ; ++$i )
{
my $atomName = $aaAtoms->Item($i)->Name;
if ( ( $atomName ne 'N' )
&& ( $atomName ne 'CA' )
&& ( $atomName ne 'C' )
&& ( $atomName ne 'O' )
&& ( $atomName ne 'HN' )
&& ( $atomName ne 'HA' ) )
{
$sideChainAtoms->AddItem( $aaAtoms->Item($i) );
}
}

#Get the original coordinates so we can restore them at the end if we want to
my $originalCoordinates = Mdm::PointArray::Create();
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $sideChainAtoms->Count ; ++$i )
{
$originalCoordinates->AddItem( $sideChainAtoms->[$i]->XYZ );
}

#Make some monitors so we can assess the rotamers
my $bumpMonitor = $document->CreateBumpMonitor( $sideChainAtoms, False );
print
"Number of bumps to original side-chain position: $bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} \n";
my $hbondMonitor = $document->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( $sideChainAtoms,
Mdm::allAtomHydrogenBonds, Mdm::allMolecularHydrogenBonds );
print
"Number of hydrogen bonds between side-chain and the rest of protein $hbondMonitor->{HydrogenBondCount}\n";
print "\nPerforming rotamer search for $aminoAcidName \n";

my $numRotamers =
$document->RotamerCount( $aminoAcid, Mdm::oldfieldRotamerLibrary );
print "Number of rotamers is $numRotamers\n";

if ( $numRotamers > 0 )
{
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i <= $numRotamers ; ++$i )
{
my $probability = $document->RotamerProbability( $i, $aminoAcid,
Mdm::oldfieldRotamerLibrary );
print "Applying rotamer $i, probability $probability\n";
$document->ApplyRotamer( $i, $aminoAcid,
Mdm::oldfieldRotamerLibrary );

#Check the number of bumps and hbonds. One might want to keep track of fewest bumps/most hbonds
#to decide which monitor to
print
"Number of bumps $bumpMonitor->{BumpCount} ;number of hydrogen bonds $hbondMonitor->{HydrogenBondCount}\n";

#for demo purposes so we can see each rotamer
sleep(2);
}
}

#restore original
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $sideChainAtoms->Count ; ++$i )
{
$sideChainAtoms->[$i]->XYZ = $originalCoordinates->[$i];
}
```

## RotatableBondCount property

### Description

RotatableBondCount indicates the number of rotatable bonds in a molecule. A bond is considered to be rotatable if it is single, acyclic and no terminal atom is involved.

```text
# This scripts illustrates how to access several properties of
# the Mdm::Molecule object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

print "The following is a list of molecule properties:\n";
print 'Name: ' . $molecule->Name . "\n";
print 'Approximate volume: ' . $molecule->ApproximateVolume . "\n";

print 'Molecular weight: ' . $molecule->MolecularWeight . "\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to create rotatable bond monitors for a molecule.
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Remove all atoms except the first ligand found.
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
$ligands->Item(0)->Select();
$document->InvertSelection();
$document->DeleteObjects();
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

print "Creating rotatable bond monitors for ligand...\n";
my $rotatableBondMonitorCount = $molecule->CreateRotatableBondMonitors();
print "Found $rotatableBondMonitorCount rotatable bonds.\n";
my $arrayrotbonds = $document->RotatableBondMonitors; 
print "Number of rotatable bonds monitors: ". $arrayrotbonds->Count. "\n";

my $j = 0;
foreach my $monitor (@$arrayrotbonds) { 
my @IDs = ();
for (my $i = 0; $i < 4; ++$i) {
my $atom = $monitor->Object($i);
push (@IDs,$atom->Id. " " . $atom->Name );
}
my $IDscal = join(", ", @IDs);
printf "%3i) Id/Name: %s Torsion %.4f\n ", ++$j, $IDscal , $monitor->Angle;
}
```

#### Instance

This function is deprecated. It has been replaced by RotateShapeFeature in Mdm::ShapeFeature .

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the matrix function Rotate.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $xAxisVector = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 );

print "Creating a matrix M to rotate 90 degrees around X-axis.\n";
my $matrix = Mdm::Matrix3x3::Create();
$matrix->SetRotation( $xAxisVector, 90.0 );

printf " %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\t\n",
$matrix->GetEntry( 0, 0 ), $matrix->GetEntry( 0, 1 ),
$matrix->GetEntry( 0, 2 );
printf " %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\t\n",
$matrix->GetEntry( 1, 0 ), $matrix->GetEntry( 1, 1 ),
$matrix->GetEntry( 1, 2 );
printf " %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\t\n\n",
$matrix->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $matrix->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$matrix->GetEntry( 2, 2 );

my $vector = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 1.0, 0.0 );
printf "Vector before rotation: (%8.3f %8.3f %8.3f)\n",
$vector->X, $vector->Y, $vector->Z;

$vector = $matrix->Rotate($vector);
printf "Vector after rotation: (%8.3f %8.3f %8.3f)\n",
$vector->X, $vector->Y, $vector->Z;
```

# RotateAndTranslate function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/rotateandtranslate_function.htm

## RotateAndTranslate function

### Description

RotateAndTranslate applies the matrix transformation (rotation and translation) to a point.

### Applies to

The RotateAndTranslate function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Matrix4x4

### Using the RotateAndTranslate function

#### Instance

my $pointObject = $object->RotateAndTranslate( <point> );

my $pointObject = $object->RotateAndTranslate( { Point => <point> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $pointObject | | | Mdm::Point |
| <point> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| $object | | | Mdm::Matrix4x4 |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the use of the Mdm::Matrix4x4 object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# The following subroutine prints a matrix.
sub PrintMatrix($)
{
my ($matrix) = @_;
my $size = 3;
$size = 4 if ( $matrix->ClassName eq 'Mdm::Matrix4x4' );

for ( my $row = 0 ; $row < $size ; ++$row )
{
for ( my $column = 0 ; $column < $size ; ++$column )
{
printf " %8.3f", $matrix->GetEntry( $row, $column );
}
print "\n";
}
}

# Create a 4x4 matrix.
my $matrix4x4 = Mdm::Matrix4x4::Create(
2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 0.0, 6.0, 7.0, 8.0, 0.0,
8.0, 7.0, 6.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 1.0
);
print "Matrix 4x4: \n";
PrintMatrix($matrix4x4);

# List the rotation matrix.
my $matrix3x3 = $matrix4x4->RotationMatrix();
print "Rotation Matrix: \n";
PrintMatrix($matrix3x3);

# List the translation vector.
my $translationVector = $matrix4x4->Translation;
printf "Translation Vector:\n %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n",
$translationVector->X, $translationVector->Y, $translationVector->Z;

# Create a matrix to rotate 90 degrees around X-axis.
print "Matrix to rotate 90 degrees around X-axis:\n";
my $xAxis = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 );
$matrix3x3->SetRotation( $xAxis, 90.0 );
PrintMatrix($matrix3x3);

# Create a vector to translate along Z-axis.
$translationVector = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 3.0 );

# Define 4x4 matrix from rotation and translation.
$matrix4x4->RotationMatrix = $matrix3x3;
$matrix4x4->Translation = $translationVector;
print "New rotation/translation matrix: \n";
PrintMatrix($matrix4x4);

# Define a vector in the XY-plane.
my $vector = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 1.0, 0.0 );
printf "Vector before transformation:\n %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n",
$vector->X, $vector->Y, $vector->Z;

# Rotate vector 90 about X-axis and translate.
$vector = $matrix4x4->RotateAndTranslate($vector);
printf "Vector after transformation:\n %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n",
$vector->X, $vector->Y, $vector->Z;
```

Mdm::ShapeFeature

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create napthalene
$document->InsertFromSmiles('c12ccccc1cccc2');

# Create shape query based on the two molecules
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();
my $shapeOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryShape');
my $shapefeatureObject =
$shapeOperator->CreateShapeFeature( $document->Molecules->[0]->Atoms );

# Rotate shape

my $xyz1 = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );
my $xyz2 = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );
$shapefeatureObject->RotateShapeFeature( $xyz1, 130.0, $xyz2 );

# Print properties
print "Minimum similarity tolerance: "
. $shapefeatureObject->MinimumSimilarityTolerance . "\n";
print "Maximum similarity tolerance: "
. $shapefeatureObject->MaximumSimilarityTolerance . "\n\n";
print "Minimum volume extents ratio: "
```

# RotateView function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/rotateview_function.htm

## RotateView function

### Description

RotateView rotates the view point by the specified angles,
optionally resetting the view rotation first.
The angles are assumed to be expressed in degrees.

### Applies to

The RotateView function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the RotateView function

#### Instance

$object->RotateView( <a>, <b>, <c>, [reset] );

$object->RotateView( { A => <a>, B => <b>, C => <c>, Reset => [reset] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a> | Required | | Real |
| <b> | Required | | Real |
| <c> | Required | | Real |
| [reset] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles('CN');
AddHydrogens($document);

# Get the Nitrogen atom to place the Hydrogen Bond Donors
my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
my $NitrogenAtom;
foreach my $atom (@$atoms)
{
if ( $atom->Element eq "N" )
{
$NitrogenAtom = $atom;
}
}

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create an HBD using the first Hydrogen.
my $donorOperator1 = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator1->Name('HBD');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator1->CreateDonorFeature($NitrogenAtom);
$newDonor->Orientation('donorFeatureFirstHydrogen');

# Create an HBD using the second Hydrogen.
my $donorOperator2 = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator2->Name('HBD2');
my $newDonor2 = $donorOperator2->CreateDonorFeature($NitrogenAtom);
$newDonor2->Orientation('donorFeatureSecondHydrogen');

$document->RotateView( 2.0, -10.0, 2.0 );
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use Mdm::SpaceGroup objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Get space group from document.
my $cell = $document->Cells->Item(0);
my $spacegroup = $cell->SpaceGroup;

print "The following is a list of space group properties:\n";
print "Number:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->Number . "\n";
print "Short Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->Symbol . "\n";
print "SchoenfliesSymbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->SchoenfliesSymbol . "\n";
print "Full Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->FullSymbol . "\n";
print "Lattice type:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->LatticeType . "\n";
print "Cell choice:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->CellChoice . "\n";
print "AxisOriginType:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->AxisOriginType . "\n";
print "Number of sym. operator:\t\t"
. $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount . "\n";

my $count = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $operator = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperator($index);
print "Symmetry operator $index\n";
print "\tName: " . $operator->Name . "\n";

my $rotation = $operator->Rotation;
my $format = "\t %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n";
print "\tRotation Matrix:\n";
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 0, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 1, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 2 );

my $translation = $operator->Translation;
print "\tTranslation:\n";
printf "$format", $translation->X, $translation->Y, $translation->Z;
}
```

# RotationMatrix property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/rotationmatrix_property.htm

## RotationMatrix property

### Description

RotationMatrix specifies the Mdm::Matrix3x3 3D rotation
matrix embedded in a Mdm::Matrix4x4 .

### Applies to

The RotationMatrix property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Matrix4x4

### Using the RotationMatrix property

#### Get

my $matrix3x3Object = $object->RotationMatrix;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $matrix3x3Object | | | Mdm::Matrix3x3 |
| $object | | | Mdm::Matrix4x4 |

#### Set

$object->RotationMatrix = <rotationmatrix>;

$object->RotationMatrix( <rotationmatrix> );

$object->RotationMatrix( { RotationMatrix => <rotationmatrix> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <rotationmatrix> | Required | | Mdm::Matrix3x3 |
| $object | | | Mdm::Matrix4x4 |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the use of the Mdm::Matrix4x4 object.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# The following subroutine prints a matrix.
sub PrintMatrix($)
{
my ($matrix) = @_;
my $size = 3;
$size = 4 if ( $matrix->ClassName eq 'Mdm::Matrix4x4' );

for ( my $row = 0 ; $row < $size ; ++$row )
{
for ( my $column = 0 ; $column < $size ; ++$column )
{
printf " %8.3f", $matrix->GetEntry( $row, $column );
}
print "\n";
}
}

# Create a 4x4 matrix.
my $matrix4x4 = Mdm::Matrix4x4::Create(
2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 0.0, 6.0, 7.0, 8.0, 0.0,
8.0, 7.0, 6.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 1.0
);
print "Matrix 4x4: \n";
PrintMatrix($matrix4x4);

# List the rotation matrix.
my $matrix3x3 = $matrix4x4->RotationMatrix();
print "Rotation Matrix: \n";
PrintMatrix($matrix3x3);

# List the translation vector.
my $translationVector = $matrix4x4->Translation;
printf "Translation Vector:\n %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n",
$translationVector->X, $translationVector->Y, $translationVector->Z;

# Create a matrix to rotate 90 degrees around X-axis.
print "Matrix to rotate 90 degrees around X-axis:\n";
my $xAxis = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 );
$matrix3x3->SetRotation( $xAxis, 90.0 );
PrintMatrix($matrix3x3);

# Create a vector to translate along Z-axis.
$translationVector = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 3.0 );

# Define 4x4 matrix from rotation and translation.
$matrix4x4->RotationMatrix = $matrix3x3;
$matrix4x4->Translation = $translationVector;
print "New rotation/translation matrix: \n";
PrintMatrix($matrix4x4);

# Define a vector in the XY-plane.
my $vector = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 1.0, 0.0 );
printf "Vector before transformation:\n %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n",
$vector->X, $vector->Y, $vector->Z;

# Rotate vector 90 about X-axis and translate.
$vector = $matrix4x4->RotateAndTranslate($vector);
printf "Vector after transformation:\n %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n",
$vector->X, $vector->Y, $vector->Z;
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the alignment ruler.
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdm = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1oyt');
my $molecule = $mdm->Molecules->Item(0);

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures($mdm);
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $ruler = $alignment->Ruler;

$ruler->DisplayStyle = Sdm::styleRuler1stResidueId;

my $rulerIds = $ruler->RulerIds;

$document->UpdateViews();

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

# RunFolder property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/runfolder_property.htm

## RunFolder property

### Description

RunFolder is the running path of a protocol.

### Applies to

The RunFolder property can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Session

### Using the RunFolder property

#### Get

my $stringValue = $object->RunFolder;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $object | | | Protocol::Session |

#### Set

$object->RunFolder = <path>;

$object->RunFolder( <path> );

$object->RunFolder( { Path => <path> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <path> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Protocol::Session |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

# Save function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/save_function.htm

## Save function

### Description

Save saves the document to a file. The required arguments
are the file name and the format/format type.

File formats for saving documents of the Mdm::Document class include:

* cpd - Catalyst Structure

* crd - CHARMm Coordinates

* csv - Comma Separated Values

* dae - Collaborative Design Activity - format type = JsonMDM2

* dcd - CHARMm Trajectory Coordinates

* ds_chm - Catalyst Hypothesis

* dsv - Discovery Studio Viewer (default format)

* dsx - Discovery Studio Viewer

* ent - Protein Data Bank - format type = pdb

* json - JavaScript Object Notation - format type = JsonMDM2

* map - CNX Map

* mbk - QUANTA Brick Map

* mol - MDL MOL/SD

* mol2 - Sybyl MOL2

* msv - Discovery Studio Viewer

* pdb - Protein Data Bank

* pdb1 - Protein Data Bank - format type = pdb

* pov - POV-Ray

* psf - CHARMm Structure

* sd - MDL MOL/SD

* smi - SMILES

* wrl - VRML World

* xyz - XYZ Coordinates

Unless stated otherwise, the format type is equal to the file format.

File formats for saving documents of the Sdm::Document class include:

* aa - FASTA Sequence - format type = FASTA

* align - BIOSYM Sequence Alignment

* aln - Clustal/ClustalW Sequence Alignment - format type = CALN

* bsml - Bioinformatic Sequence Markup Language (default format)

* xml - Bioinformatic Sequence Markup Language - format type = BSML

* aaa_bsml - Bioinformatic Sequence Markup Language - format type = BSML

* naa_bsml - Bioinformatic Sequence Markup Language - format type = BSML

* aas_bsml - Bioinformatic Sequence Markup Language - format type = BSML

* nas_bsml - Bioinformatic Sequence Markup Language - format type = BSML

* fa - FASTA Sequence - format type = FASTA

* fasta - FASTA Sequence - format type = FASTA

* fsa - FASTA Sequence - format type = FASTA

* gb - NCBI GenBank Sequence

* gcg - GCG Sequence

* gde - Genetic Data Environment

* msf - GCG Multiple Sequence Format

* nbrf - National Biomedical Research Foundation Sequence - format type = PIR

* pir - Protein Information Resource - format type = PIR

* rsf - GCG Rich Sequence Format - format type = RSF

* ssf - GCG Single Sequence Format - format type = RSF

Ffdm::Document objects will save to the FORCEFIELD format, Protocol::Document objects will save to the pr_xml format
and Chart::Document objects can only be saved to image files (i.e., jpg, png, and 'bmp') on the client.

In the examples, the documentation describes the second argument as <FormatType>. However, for MDM, SDM and FF Document classes, you should use <Format>.

### Applies to

The Save function can be used with the following objects:

Chart::Document , DiscoveryScript::Document , Ffdm::Document , Mdm::Document , Protocol::Document , Sdm::Document

### Using the Save function

#### Instance

$object->Save( <path>, <formattype> );

$object->Save( { Path => <path>, FormatType => <formattype> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <formattype> | Required | | String |
| <path> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $outputFolder = DiscoveryScript::GetTemporaryFolder();

# Create a document containing a molecule.
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atom1 = $molecule->CreateAtom('C');
my $atom2 = $molecule->CreateAtom('C');
my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $atom1, $atom2, Mdm::doubleBond );
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms( );
sleep(1);
$document->Clean();

printf "Document contains Molecules: %d Total Atoms: %d\n", $document->Molecules->Count,$document->Atoms->Count;

# Save as a .dsv file
my $filenameDSV = 'ethene.dsv';
my $filenameSD = 'ethene.sd';

my $fullNameDSV = $outputFolder.'/' . $filenameDSV;
my $fullNameSD = $outputFolder.'/' . $filenameSD;

$document->Save( $fullNameDSV, 'dsv' );

print "Saved: $filenameDSV\n" if (-s $fullNameDSV);
# Save as a .sd file

$document->Save( $fullNameSD, 'mol' );
print "Saved: $filenameSD\n" if (-s $fullNameSD);

unlink($fullNameDSV);
unlink($fullNameSD);
```

# SaveImage function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/saveimage_function.htm

## SaveImage function

### Description

SaveImage saves the document to an image file.
A file format must be supplied as the second argument.
This function executes Discovery Studio client actions and is only available to scripts run within the client.
Valid file formats include:

* .png - Portable Network Graphics

* .bmp - Bitmap

* .jpg/.jpeg - Joint Photographic Experts Group

### Applies to

The SaveImage function can be used with the following objects:

Chart::Document , DiscoveryScript::Document , Ffdm::Document , Mdm::Document , Protocol::Document , Sdm::Document

### Using the SaveImage function

#### Instance

$object->SaveImage( <path>, <formattype>, [width], [height], [transparent] );

$object->SaveImage( { Path => <path>, FormatType => <formattype>, Width => [width], Height => [height], Transparent => [transparent] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <formattype> | Required | | String |
| <path> | Required | | String |
| [height] | Optional | | Integer |
| [transparent] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [width] | Optional | | Integer |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

DiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Save document view to an image file (client only)
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Create a document containing a molecule.
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Save as a .png file with default sizes.
$document->SaveImage( '1crn.png', 'png' );

# Save as a .png file with specified height.
$document->SaveImage(
{
Path => '1crnH.jpg',
FormatType => 'jpg',
Height => 500
}
);

# Save as a .png file with specified width.
$document->SaveImage(
{
Path => '1crnW.jpg',
FormatType => 'jpg',
Width => 500
}
);

# Save as a .png file requesting a transparent background.
$document->SaveImage(
{
Path => '1crnW.jpg',
FormatType => 'jpg',
Transparent => True
}
);
```

# SaveTwoDView function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/savetwodview_function.htm

## SaveTwoDView function

### Description

SaveTwoDView saves the 2D receptor-ligand interaction view
derived from the given document to a file.
The file name (Path) is a required argument.
The file format (Format) is an optional argument.
By default, the SVG file format is used.
Currently supported file formats are SVG and JSON.
Optionally, parameters affecting the display (Parameters)
can be specified as an optional argument.
The optional argument is a text string containing
name=value pairs separated with semicolons, i.e.
NameA=ValueA;...;NameZ=ValueZ.
The following names and values are supported:
Name=ShowSolventAccessibility with possible values
on, true, or yes to show solvent accessibility,
and off, false, or no to not show solvent accessibility.
The default value is off.
Name=NeighborDistance with a numerical value between
0 and 6 Angstroms. This parameter controls the distance
between the ligand residue and receptor residues for the
receptor residues to be considered as contributing
van der Waals interactions.
The default value is 4 Angstroms.
Name=KeepHydrogens with possible values All, Interacting,
OnlyPolar and Polar controls whether and which types of
ligand hydrogen atoms should be included in the interaction
view.
The default value is Interacting.
Name=LigandQuality with possible values Low, Medium, and
High controls the quality of the 2d coordinates generated
for the ligand.
The default value is Medium.
Name=AtomStyle with possible values Line, Disc, Stick, and
BallAndStick controls the ligand atom display style.
The default value is Line.
Name=ResidueStyle with possible values Disc, Ball, and
Plate controls the residue display style.
The default value is Ball.

### Applies to

The SaveTwoDView function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SaveTwoDView function

#### Instance

$object->SaveTwoDView( <path>, [format], [parameters] );

$object->SaveTwoDView( { Path => <path>, Format => [format], Parameters => [parameters] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <path> | Required | | String |
| [format] | Optional | "svg" | String |
| [parameters] | Optional | "" | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

# SbdCommands package

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/sbdcommands_package.htm

## SbdCommands package

### Description

SbdCommands provides high-level functions for accessing functionality
within SbdDiscoveryScript . These commands provide a more simple interface
to working with binding sites and hotspots.

### Using the SbdCommands package

Access to the SbdCommands API is through the Perl use directive:

```text
use strict;
use SbdCommands;
```

The strict directive is optional, but strongly recommended as it restricts
the use of unsafe constructs. All available classes will be imported from the SbdCommands module.

#### Commands

CreateAndPartitionBindingSites CreateHotSpotsLabels FindBindingSites FindBindingSitesFromLigands LoopThroughBindingSites

#### Uses

MdmCommands

#### Used by

DSCommands

#### Module

SbdCommands.pm

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use SbdCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1kim.pdb" );

# From SbdCommands;
FindBindingSites($document);

# From SbdDiscoveryScript
my $site = $document->BindingSites->Item(0);
$document->PartitionBindingSite($site);
my $bindingSites = $document->BindingSites;

print "Binding site properties:\n";
print "Site Volume Threshold Points\n";
my $bsCount = 0;
foreach my $site (@$bindingSites)
{
$site->SetVisible();

my $volume = $site->GetProperty("Volume");
my $threshold = $site->GetProperty("Threshold");
my $points = $site->GetProperty("Point Count");

printf "%4d %8.3f %10.3f %7d\n", ++$bsCount, $volume, $threshold,
$points;
}
```

## SbdDiscoveryScript package

### Description

SbdDiscoveryScript provides functions, properties and constants that can be used
to manipulate Discovery Studio structure-based design data from scripts.

### Using the SbdDiscoveryScript package

Access to the SbdDiscoveryScript API is through the Perl use directive:

```text
use strict;
use SbdDiscoveryScript;
```

The strict directive is optional, but strongly recommended as it restricts
the use of unsafe constructs. All available classes will be imported from the SbdDiscoveryScript module.

#### Properties

LigandFitBindingSiteFileText

#### Functions

CalculateAllAtomRmsd CalculateHeavyAtomRmsd ContractBindingSite CreateBindingSitesFromCavities CreateBindingSitesFromLigand ExpandBindingSite PartitionBindingSite

#### Uses

MdmDiscoveryScript

#### Module

SbdDiscoveryScript.pm

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Find and partition binding site cavities.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

# Remove ligands from the protein.
Delete( $document, GetLigands($document) );

# Find and partition binding site cavities.
my $bindingSites = CreateAndPartitionBindingSites($document);
print "Number of BindingSites found: " . $bindingSites->Count . "\n";
```

# ScaleView function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/scaleview_function.htm

## ScaleView function

### Description

ScaleView changes the view size using the specified scale.

### Applies to

The ScaleView function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ScaleView function

#### Instance

$object->ScaleView( <scale> );

$object->ScaleView( { Scale => <scale> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <scale> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Zoom in and out of a Molecule Window using a relative scale.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

$document->InsertFromSmiles('C1=CC=CC=C1');
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms();

# Decrease view size and zoom into center.
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 50 ; ++$i )
{
$document->ScaleView(0.9);
printf "%d %.4f\n", $i+1, $document->Zoom;
}

sleep(1);

# Enlarge view size and zoom out.
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 50 ; ++$i )
{
$document->ScaleView(1.1111);
printf "%d %.4f\n", $i+1, $document->Zoom;

}
```

## SchoenfliesSymbol property

### Description

SchoenfliesSymbol specifies the Schoenflies symbol of a spacegroup.

### Applies to

The SchoenfliesSymbol property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::SpaceGroup

### Using the SchoenfliesSymbol property

#### Get

my $stringValue = $object->SchoenfliesSymbol;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::SpaceGroup |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use Mdm::SpaceGroup objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Get space group from document.
my $cell = $document->Cells->Item(0);
my $spacegroup = $cell->SpaceGroup;

print "The following is a list of space group properties:\n";
print "Number:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->Number . "\n";
print "Short Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->Symbol . "\n";
print "SchoenfliesSymbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->SchoenfliesSymbol . "\n";
print "Full Hermann-Mauguin symbol:\t\t" . $spacegroup->FullSymbol . "\n";
print "Lattice type:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->LatticeType . "\n";
print "Cell choice:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->CellChoice . "\n";
print "AxisOriginType:\t\t\t" . $spacegroup->AxisOriginType . "\n";
print "Number of sym. operator:\t\t"
. $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount . "\n";

my $count = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $operator = $spacegroup->SymmetryOperator($index);
print "Symmetry operator $index\n";
print "\tName: " . $operator->Name . "\n";

my $rotation = $operator->Rotation;
my $format = "\t %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n";
print "\tRotation Matrix:\n";
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 0, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 0, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 1, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 1, 2 );
printf "$format",
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $rotation->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$rotation->GetEntry( 2, 2 );

my $translation = $operator->Translation;
print "\tTranslation:\n";
printf "$format", $translation->X, $translation->Y, $translation->Z;
}
```

## Arguments View of the Script Window

The Arguments View of the Script Window can be used to pass command line arguments to the script.

The parsing of the arguments entered in the Argument window is similar to parsing arguments on the command line. Arguments are passed to the @ARGV array in a perl script. Individual arguments are separated by white spaces. Single or double quotes can be used to delimit arguments that contain white spaces.

# Output View of the Script Window

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/script-window_output-pane.htm

## Output View of the Script Window

The Script Window Output View displays messages generated by Perl interpreter while running and debugging scripts. The 
following types of messages are displayed in the Output window

* Perl syntax errors.

* Perl interpreter warning and error messages.

* Script output messages.

All text displayed in the Output View can be copied to the clipboard.

### Context menu

The Script Window Output view context menu extends the Output view capabilities as described below.

* Copy - This command is the same as the corresponding command under the Edit 
menu .

* Select All - Selects all text in the current document.

# Deprecated DiscoveryScript API

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/scripting_deprecated.htm

## Deprecated DiscoveryScript API

### Description

Certain functions and properties are deprecated, meaning that they may no longer be fully supported.
Depending on the type of deprecation, they may still work. However, it is better to update
the scripts according to the instructions as the deprecated API may be removed in future releases.

### Using scripting

There are four different types of deprecation:

#### Marked as deprecated, but still fully functional

The API still works as it did in previous releases, but it is marked to become deprecated and possibly
removed from future releases. It is best to update the scripts according to the documentation as it will
continue to generate warnings until it is replaced with its non-deprecated counterpart(s).

#### Deprecated and replaced with one or more counterparts

The API no longer works because it has been replaced with one or more non-compatible APIs. Please update the
scripts that use it according to the documentation to make the script functional again.

#### Deprecated and renamed

The API has been renamed with an otherwise compatible API of a different name. It will continue to work
as the new API with a different name in the current release, but may be removed from future releases.
It is best to update the scripts according to the documentation as it will continue to generate warnings
until it is replaced with its non-deprecated counterpart(s).

#### Deprecated and removed

The API has been removed and is no longer supported. Please consult the documentation for how to update
the scripts accordingly.

# Sample Script Files

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/scripting_samples.htm

## Sample Script Files

The files included in the Samples | Scripts folder are intended to illustrate the 
capabilities of the Discovery Studio Perl Application Programming Interface (API). The scripts can 
be opened and run using one of two methods:

* From the Files Explorer , right-click the file and choose Open With | Script Window . The Script Window allows you to view, edit, and execute a script. To run the script, right-click the window and choose Run or click the Run button in the Scripting toolbar .

* From the Files Explorer, double-click the file, or right-click it and choose Open With | Run as DS Script .

Most of the sample scripts will open a new window
to display output.

All of the sample files are designed to run from within
Discovery Studio or from the command line. The command line syntax is described in the comments section of the script source code.

The following scripts demonstrate different capabilities of the DiscoveryScript
API:

| File | Description |
| --- | --- |
| CAlphDistances.pl | Measures the distance between C-alpha carbon atoms in adjacent amino acids. The scripts adds the results as properties of the protein, which can be viewed in the AminoAcid tab of the Molecule Window or in the Script Window output tab. |
| CountHydrogenBonds.pl | Counts the number of hydrogen bonds in a trajectory. |
| CreateEthene.pl | Creates an ethene molecule from scratch, cleans it, and then measures the length of the C=C bond. |
| CreateSequenceFeatures.pl | Creates an Sdm::Document containing an Sdm::AminoAcidSequence for each protein molecule. Also, Sdm::Feature objects are created for each Mdm::Group in the Mdm::Molecule . In DiscoveryStudio, the Sdm::Document is displayed in a Sequence Window. To see the created features, open an Annotation View by double-clicking a sequence. |
| ExtractAlternateConformer.pl | Replaces a protein's reference conformer with an alternate conformer. |
| ExtractAngles.pl | Searches input molecules for specified valence or torsion and extracts angle values. The angles are stored as a Molecule property (named User Torsion), which can be viewed in the AminoAcid tab of the Molecule Window or in the Script Window output tab. |
| ExtractChiAngles.pl | Finds all chi angles in a protein and lists chi angles as properties of the amino acids. |
| MinimizationProtocol.pl | Uses the ProtocolDiscoveryScript API to open and run the Minimization protocol. The script also types the input molecule using the ForceFieldDiscoveryScript API. |
| NewScript.pl | Default Perl template used when opening a new Script Window . |
| Redirect.pl | Demonstrates a technique to redirect standard output that is otherwise displayed in the Script Window, or in the command window when run from the command line. |
| RenderLigand.pl | Demonstrates how to identify a ligand and the corresponding active site and render the system for viewing in the Molecule Window. |
| ReportCentroid.pl | Calculates and reports the centroid of a molecule from the position and masses of the atoms. |

# ScriptPath property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/scriptpath_property.htm

## ScriptPath property

### Description

ScriptPath indicates the path of the script file that is being executed.

### Applies to

The ScriptPath property can be used with the following objects:

DiscoveryScript

### Using the ScriptPath property

#### Static Get

my $stringValue = DiscoveryScript::ScriptPath();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $object | | | DiscoveryScript |

#### Defined by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to access the script path.
use strict;
use DiscoveryScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

$document->Save( '1crn.msv', 'msv' );

my $isStandalone = DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone();
my $path = DiscoveryScript::ScriptPath();

print 'Saved file 1crn.msv to directory ' . $path . ".\n";
```

# Working with scripts

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/scripts.htm

## Working with scripts

Discovery Studio provides a client interface for working with a variety
of documents and protocols. Occasionally, however, it may be
desirable to access specific Discovery Studio functionality
programmatically to:

* Automate repetitive tasks

* Link several tasks or calculations together in sequence

* Explore calculations that are not available from any of the application's modules

* Integrate with other software

Perl scripts enable you to perform tasks, such as those listed above, by
allowing you to manipulate objects in the application's environment,
both at the command line and interactively. 
There are a variety of excellent sources of information on Perl, 
including "Programming Perl" by Larry Wall, 
Tom Christiansen, and Jon Orwant, 
and the CPAN (Comprehensive Perl Archive Network) Web site. Both are recommended

# Sdm::Alignment::Deselect function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/sdm__alignment__deselect_function.htm

## Sdm::Alignment::Deselect function

### Description

Deselect de-selects the specified aligned residues and gaps.
The following arguments are supported:

* Index specifies the 0-based sequence index (row).

* StartPosition specifies the 0-based alignment position (column) to begin the de-selection.

* Count is the number of residues and/or gaps to deselect.

### Applies to

The Sdm::Alignment::Deselect function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the Sdm::Alignment::Deselect function

#### Instance

$object->Deselect( <index>, <startposition>, [count] );

$object->Deselect( { Index => <index>, StartPosition => <startposition>, Count => [count] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| <startposition> | Required | | Integer |
| [count] | Optional | 1 | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to deselect aligned residues and gaps.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';
my $filePath = $samplesFolder . 'GPCR Alignment.bsml';

my $document = DiscoveryScript::Open($filePath);
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

my $sequenceIndex = 2;
my $column = 4;
my $count = 5;

$alignment->SelectSequence($sequenceIndex);
if ( $sequenceIndex < $alignment->SequenceCount
&& $column < $alignment->AlignmentLength )
{
$alignment->Deselect( $sequenceIndex, $column, $count );
}

my $index = 0;
my $count = $document->SequenceCount;
printf "Found %d sequences\n", $count;
while ( $index < $count )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

residues and gaps are selected.
The following arguments are supported:

* Index specifies the 0-based sequence index.

* StartPosition specifies the 0-based alignment position to begin checking.

* Count is the number of residues and/or gaps to check for selection.

### Applies to

The Sdm::Alignment::IsSelected property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the Sdm::Alignment::IsSelected property

#### Get

my $booleanValue = $object->IsSelected( <index>, <startposition>, [count] );

my $booleanValue = $object->IsSelected( { Index => <index>, StartPosition => <startposition>, Count => [count] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| <startposition> | Required | | Integer |
| [count] | Optional | 1 | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate use of Sdm::Alignment::IsSelected function.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(SdmModelType);
die "Please open a Sequence Window in Discovery Studio and try again.\n"
unless ( $document && $document->Alignment );

my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequences = $alignment->Sequences;
my $length = $alignment->AlignmentLength;
foreach my $sequence (@$sequences)
{
my $sequenceIndex = $alignment->SequenceIndex($sequence);
print "Sequence $sequenceIndex has select columns:";
for ( my $column = 0 ; $column < $length ; ++$column )
{
if ( $alignment->IsSelected( $sequenceIndex, $column ) )
{
print " $column";
}
}
print ".\n";
}
```

# Sdm::AminoAcidSequence::Deselect function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/sdm__aminoacidsequence__deselect_function.htm

## Sdm::AminoAcidSequence::Deselect function

### Description

Deselect de-selects the specified residues.
The following arguments are supported:

* StartPosition specifies the 0-based sequence position to begin the de-selection.

* Count is the number of residues to de-select.

### Applies to

The Sdm::AminoAcidSequence::Deselect function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence

### Using the Sdm::AminoAcidSequence::Deselect function

#### Instance

$object->Deselect( <startposition>, [count] );

$object->Deselect( { StartPosition => <startposition>, Count => [count] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <startposition> | Required | | Integer |
| [count] | Optional | 1 | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::AminoAcidSequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate linking a sequence to a structure.
# NOTE: Sequences and structures can only be linked in the DS client.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId('1CRN_A');
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0);

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0);

# Link the 1crn sequence and molecule.
$sdmDocument->LinkSequenceStructure( $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0),
$mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0) );
print "The sequence and molecule are now linked.\n";

# Selecting (and deselecting) the molecule also selects the sequence
# after updating the view. Here the update views call is required
# not only to display the sequence selection, but to synchronize the
# data models.
$molecule->Select();
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();
print 'After selecting the molecule and updating the SDM document view, '
. "the sequence is also selected.\n"
if ( $sequence->IsSelected() );

# Selecting (and deselecting) from the sequence does not
# require an update views call to synchronize the data models.
# The call is requires to display the updated sequence
# selection.
$sequence->Deselect( 0, 10 );
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();

# Break the sequence and molecule link.
$sdmDocument->BreakSequenceStructureLink( $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0) );
print "The sequence-molecule link is now broken.\n";

$sequence->Select( 0, 5 );
print "The first 5 residues in sequence are selected.\n"
if ( $sdmDocument->Alignment->IsSelected( 0, 0, 5 ) );

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();
print "The first 5 residues in sequence are selected.\n"
if ( $sdmDocument->Alignment->IsSelected( 0, 0, 5 ) );
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate use of Sdm::Array.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';
my $filePath = $samplesFolder . 'GPCR Alignment.bsml';

my $sdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::Open($filePath);

my $sequenceArray = Sdm::Array::Create();

my $count = $sdmDocument->{SequenceCount};
print "Document contains $count sequences.\n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->Sequence($index);
print "Sequence $index contains $sequence->{ResidueCount} residues.\n";
my $rawSequence = $sequence->SequenceString();
print "dump: $rawSequence\n";

$sequenceArray->AddItem($sequence);
}

my $sequenceCount = $sequenceArray->Count();
print "Sequence array contains $sequenceCount items.\n";

print "Ending\n";
```

## Sdm::AttributeMap class

### Description

The Sdm::AttributeMap contains the attributes of an Sdm::ObjectWithAttributes as key-value pairs.
The attributes are persisted in BSML files. You can
store non-standard data in BSML files using attributes.

### Using the Sdm::AttributeMap object

AddItem , DeleteItem , FindItem

#### Returned by

AttributeMap

#### Derived from

DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the Sdm::AttributeMap.
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $mdm = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('4phv');
my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures($mdm);
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

# Copy current document state to object attributes. Generally the 
# attribute data is not updated after loading a BSML file. To get 
# the current state as attributes call this function. 
$document->ClearBsmlAttributes();
$document->BuildBsmlAttributes();

# List the Alignment object attributes.
print "Alignment attributes...\n";
my $attributes = $alignment->AttributeMap;
my $key = $attributes->FirstKey;
while (!$key->IsEndKey)
{
print $key->Name . ":\t" . $attributes->Item($key) . "\n";
$key = $attributes->NextKey($key);
}
print "end\n\n";

# List the Sequence object attributes.
my $sequences = $document->Sequences;
my $i = 0;
foreach my $sequence (@$sequences)
{
print "Sequence $i attributes...\n";
my $attributes = $sequence->AttributeMap;
my $key = $attributes->FirstKey;
while (!$key->IsEndKey)
{
print $key->Name . ":\t" . $attributes->Item($key) . "\n";
$key = $attributes->NextKey($key);
}
print "end\n\n";

my $k = $attributes->FindItem('ResidueID');
print 'Find Name: ' . $k->Name . "\tValue: "
. $attributes->Item($k) . "\n\n";

# List the Feature object attributes.
my $features = $sequence->Features;
my $f = 0;
foreach my $feature (@$features)
{
print "Feature $f attributes...\n";
my $fattributes = $feature->AttributeMap;
my $fkey = $fattributes->FirstKey;
print $feature->Key . "\n";
while (!$fkey->IsEndKey)
{
print $fkey->Name . ":\t" . $fattributes->Item($fkey) . "\n";
$fkey = $fattributes->NextKey($fkey);
}

print "end\n\n";
++$f;
} 

++$i; 
}

# Update the current document to match attribute data.
$document->UpdateFromBsmlAttributes();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

#### Properties

ClassName , CursorColumnIndex , CursorSequenceIndex , IsCursorBeforeBoundary

#### Returned by

Cursor

#### Derived from

DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to manipulate the alignment cursor.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
print "Please try running again from within Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences;
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(0, 'S1', 'ALKDFLASDFLKASLFKASLFKD');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(1, 'S2', 'ALDFKLAFLASFLSAFADFALFAS');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(2, 'S3', '-');
$alignment->Sequence(0)->MarkStartOfChain(11);
$alignment->Sequence(1)->MarkStartOfChain(13);
$document->InvokeAction('ActionChainViewLayout');

# Move cursor to start of second domain.
my $cursor = $alignment->Cursor;
$cursor->CursorColumnIndex = $alignment->DomainStart(1);
$cursor->CursorSequenceIndex = 0;
$cursor->IsCursorBeforeBoundary = False;
$alignment->InsetSymbolsAtCursor('BEGIN-');

# Move cursor to end of first domain.
my $cursor = $alignment->Cursor;
$cursor->CursorColumnIndex = $alignment->DomainEnd(0);
$cursor->CursorSequenceIndex = 0;
$cursor->IsCursorBeforeBoundary = True;
$alignment->InsetSymbolsAtCursor('-END');
```

# Sdm::Document::RenumberSequence function

Source type: HTML

Source file: scripting/sdm__document__renumbersequence_function.htm

## Sdm::Document::RenumberSequence function

### Description

RenumberSequence modifies protein sequence residue ID values
to be consecutive. The following arguments are supported:

* Index is the index of the sequence to be renumbered.

* NewId is the index applied to the first residue.

* StartPosition is the index of the first residue to be renumbered.

* Count is the number of residues to renumber.

* ClearInsertionCodes will remove insertion codes when set to True.

### Applies to

The Sdm::Document::RenumberSequence function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Document

### Using the Sdm::Document::RenumberSequence function

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to apply color schemes to the alignment window.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $sequence0 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'ASDFADS' );
my $sequence1 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S2', 'ASDFASD' );

# Color background by charge similarity.
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
$alignment->BackgroundColorScheme = Sdm::colorByChargeSimilarity;

$document->UpdateViews();

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to copy sequences between documents
# either by insert at a specified index or appending.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $annotationDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId({Id => 'y13252', Database => "nuccore"});
my $sequence = $annotationDocument->Sequence(0);

# Append annotation window sequence to a new document.
my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateNucleotideDocument();
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();
$document->Alignment->AppendSequence($sequence);

# Insert sequence to a new document.
my $document2 = Sdm::Document::CreateNucleotideDocument();
$document2->DeleteAlignmentSequences();
$document2->Alignment->InsertSequence( 0, $sequence );
$document2->Alignment->InsertSequence( 1, $sequence );

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Segment class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence =
$document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASCDFACSGHACSJCKLA' );

# Create a location consisting of all cysteine residues.
print "Creating location for all cysteine residues\n";
my $location = Sdm::Location::Create(Sdm::locationTypeJoin);

my $sequenceString = $sequence->SequenceString;
my $residueCount = length($sequenceString);
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
if ( substr( $sequenceString, $i, 1 ) eq 'C' )
{
my $segment = Sdm::Segment::Create( $i, $i );
$location->AddSegment($segment);
}
}

my $segmentCount = $location->SegmentCount;
print "Location has $segmentCount segments\n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $segmentCount ; ++$index )
{
my $segment = $location->Segment($index);
printf( "Segment %d ...\n", $index + 1);
print "\tStart position:\t" . $segment->StartPosition . "\n";
print "\tEnd position:\t" . $segment->EndPosition . "\n";
print "\tSegement type:\t" . $segment->Type . "\n";
print "\tIs complement?:\t" . $segment->IsComplement . "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Create a feature to and add it to the sequence.
my $feature =
Sdm::Feature::CreateCustomFeature( 'Cysteine residues', $location );
$feature->AddQualifier("KeyName", 'Example feature qualifier');
$sequence->AddFeature($feature);

print 'The feature key name is ' . $feature->Key . "\n";
```

## Sdm::FixedBlock class

### Description

The Sdm::FixedBlock represents a block of aligned residues and gaps in the Sequence Window spanning more than one sequence. When gaps are inserted into sequences, the fixed block moves together to retain the alignment.

### Using the Sdm::FixedBlock object

The Sdm::FixedBlock object can be accessed via the SdmDiscoveryScript package.

#### Properties

ClassName , Height , Width , X , Y

#### Derived from

Sdm::Object -> DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::FixedBlock class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;

$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences;
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(0, 'S1', 'ALKDFLASDFLKASLFKASLFKD');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(1, 'S2', 'ALDFKLAFLASFLSAFADFALFAS');
$alignment->InsertAlignmentString(2, 'S3', '-');
$alignment->Sequence(0)->MarkStartOfChain(11);
$alignment->Sequence(1)->MarkStartOfChain(13);

# Create a fixed block using a Discovery Studio command.
$alignment->DeselectAll();
my $x0 = 9;
my $y0 = 0;
my $height = 2;
my $width = 10;
my $yN = $y0 + 2;
for (my $y = $y0; $y < $yN; ++$y)
{
$alignment->Select($y, $x0, $width);
}
$document->InvokeAction('ActionFixResidueBlock'); 

my $fixedBlock = $alignment->FixedBlocks->Item(0);
my $column = $fixedBlock->X + 1;
print 'A fixed block was created starting at column ' . $column
. ' of sequence ' . $alignment->Sequences->Item($fixedBlock->Y)->Name
. ' having a width of ' . $fixedBlock->Width 
. ' residues and a height of ' . $fixedBlock->Height . " sequences.\n";
```

## Sdm::Location class

### Description

The Sdm::Location specifies the residues associated with
a sequence feature as a collection of Sdm::Segment objects.
Each Sdm::Segment object defines a start and end
residue index for a range of residues in the feature. See
the Sdm::Alignment 's ResidueIndex for converting alignment indices to sequence-residue indices.

The Sdm::Location object can be accessed via the SdmDiscoveryScript package.

#### Properties

#### Functions

#### Used by

CreateCustomFeature

#### Returned by

Location , Sdm::Location::Create

DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Location class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASDFGHJKL' );

# Create a join feature for residues DFGH.
my $segmentStart = 2;
my $segmentCount = 4;
my $location = Sdm::Location::Create( Sdm::locationTypeJoin, $segmentStart,
$segmentCount );

print "Location properties\n";

my $locationType = $location->Type;
print "Location type\t" . $locationType . "\n";

my $segmentCount = $location->SegmentCount;
print "Segment count\t$segmentCount \n";

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $segmentCount ; ++$index )
{
my $segment = $location->Segment($index);
print "Segment $index...\n";
print "\tStart position:\t" . $segment->StartPosition . "\n";
print "\tEnd position:\t" . $segment->EndPosition . "\n";
print "\tSegementType:\t" . $segment->Type . "\n";
print "\tIs complement?:\t" . $segment->IsComplement . "\n";
}

my $feature =
Sdm::Feature::CreateCustomFeature( 'Custom feature', $location );

# Add this feature to the sequence.
$sequence->AddFeature($feature);
```
