# Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence::Deselect function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/sdm__nucleicacidsequence__deselect_function.htm

## Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence::Deselect function

### Description

Deselect de-selects the specified residues.
The following arguments are supported:

* StartPosition specifies the 0-based sequence position to begin the de-selection.

* Count is the number of residues to de-select.

### Applies to

The Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence::Deselect function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence

### Using the Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence::Deselect function

#### Instance

$object->Deselect( <startposition>, [count] );

$object->Deselect( { StartPosition => <startposition>, Count => [count] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <startposition> | Required | | Integer |
| [count] | Optional | 1 | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate linking a sequence to a structure.
# NOTE: Sequences and structures can only be linked in the DS client.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId('1CRN_A');
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0);

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0);

# Link the 1crn sequence and molecule.
$sdmDocument->LinkSequenceStructure( $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0),
$mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0) );
print "The sequence and molecule are now linked.\n";

# Selecting (and deselecting) the molecule also selects the sequence
# after updating the view. Here the update views call is required
# not only to display the sequence selection, but to synchronize the
# data models.
$molecule->Select();
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();
print 'After selecting the molecule and updating the SDM document view, '
. "the sequence is also selected.\n"
if ( $sequence->IsSelected() );

# Selecting (and deselecting) from the sequence does not
# require an update views call to synchronize the data models.
# The call is requires to display the updated sequence
# selection.
$sequence->Deselect( 0, 10 );
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();

# Break the sequence and molecule link.
$sdmDocument->BreakSequenceStructureLink( $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0) );
print "The sequence-molecule link is now broken.\n";

$sequence->Select( 0, 5 );
print "The first 5 residues in sequence are selected.\n"
if ( $sdmDocument->Alignment->IsSelected( 0, 0, 5 ) );

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();
print "The first 5 residues in sequence are selected.\n"
if ( $sdmDocument->Alignment->IsSelected( 0, 0, 5 ) );
```

# Sdm::Publication::Create function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/sdm__publication__create_function.htm

## Sdm::Publication::Create function

### Description

Create creates one or more Sdm::Publication objects.

### Applies to

The Sdm::Publication::Create function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Publication

### Using the Sdm::Publication::Create function

#### Static

my $publicationObject = Sdm::Publication::Create( [authors], [title], [journal] );

my $publicationObject = Sdm::Publication::Create( { Authors => [authors], Title => [title], Journal => [journal] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $publicationObject | | | Sdm::Publication |
| [authors] | Optional | "" | String |
| [journal] | Optional | "" | String |
| [title] | Optional | "" | String |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Publication class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $sequence = $document->CreateSequence( 'Y13252-truncated',
'TCTAGAGTAACATTTAGAATTAAGGTGGGAAATTATCTTAAAATCT' );

my $title =
'Nonfixed duplication containing the Adh gene and a truncated form '
. 'of the Adhr gene in the Drosophila funebris species group: different '
. 'modes of evolution of Adh relative to Adhr in Drosophila';

# Create publication object with sample data.
my $publication01 = Sdm::Publication::Create( 'Amador, A., Juan, E.',
$title, 'Molec. Biol. Evol.' );

# Create publication and add content separately.
my $publication02 = Sdm::Publication::Create();
$publication02->Authors = 'Amador, A., Juan, E.';
$publication02->Title = $title;
$publication02->Journal = 'Molec. Biol. Evol.';
$publication02->Reference = '16(11): 1439--1456 (1999)';
$publication02->PubMedId = '10555275';
$publication02->Comment = 'y13252';

#$publication02->Consortium = '';
#$publication02->DigitalObjectId = '';
#$publication02->MedlineId = '';
#$publication02->PubMedId = '';

# Associate publications with a sequence object.
# NOTE: To see the publications in Discovery Studio, double-click on the
# sequence in the sequence window to open a sequence annotation window.
# Publications are listed in the data table's Literature Citation tab.
$sequence->AddPublication($publication01);
$sequence->AddPublication($publication02);

my $publicationCount = $sequence->PublicationCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $publicationCount ; ++$index )
{
my $publication = $sequence->Publication($index);
printf "%d: %s, %s. %s %s.\n",
$index + 1,
$publication->Authors,
$publication->Title,
$publication->Journal,
$publication->Reference;
}

$sequence->DeletePublication(0);
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate use of Sdm::Qualifier objects.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/';
my $filePath = $samplesFolder . 'D.funebris ADH Gene.bsml';

my $document = DiscoveryScript::Open($filePath);
my $feature = $document->Features->Item(0);

# Add qualifier to feature
$feature->AddQualifier( 'Test', "Value of Test" );

# Get qualifiers using filter
my $qualifiers = $feature->Qualifiers;

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $count ; ++$i )
{

# List qualifier Key-Value data
my $qualifier = $qualifiers->Item($i);
print 'Qualifier Key: '
. $qualifier->Key . "\t"
. ' Value: '
. $qualifier->Value . "\n";
}

print "All qualifiers can be printed using the Comments property.\n";
print "Comments: " . $feature->Comment;

# Remove qualifier from feature
$feature->DeleteQualifier('TestKey');
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to access a residue from a sequence.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateDocumentFromStructures($mdmDocument);
my $sequence = $document->Sequence(0);

my $black = DiscoveryScript::Color::Create( 0, 0, 0 ); 
my $count = $sequence->ResidueCount;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $residue = $sequence->Residue($index);
printf "Residue %d is %s\n", $index, $residue->Symbol;

# Setting the color is sufficient to show the decoration. The property 
# IsResidueColorTypeShown can be used to independently toggle the 
# visibility.
$residue->IsResidueColorTypeShown(Sdm::colorCaret) = True;
$residue->Color(Sdm::colorCaret, $black);
}

$document->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->Close();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to access the alignment and
# sequences in an SDM document.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a Sequence Window\n";
print " (for example open 1a27_profile.pir from the Samples folder)\n";
print " 3 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

my $sdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(SdmAlignmentModelType);

die "No active sequence found!" if not defined $sdmDocument;

# Get the alignment object from an SDM document.
my $sdmAlignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

# Get an Sdm::Array of sequence objects.
my $sequenceArray = $sdmAlignment->Sequences;

# Report the number of sequences in the alignment. This count
# includes both visible and hidden sequences.
print "Number of sequences in alignment: " . $sequenceArray->Count;
```

## Sdm::SecondaryStructure class

### Description

The Sdm::SecondaryStructure represents the secondary structure of
amino acids in the Sequence Data Model.

### Using the Sdm::SecondaryStructure object

The Sdm::SecondaryStructure object can be accessed via the SdmDiscoveryScript package.

#### Properties

ClassName , IsPredicted , IsVisible , Predictor , Propensity , ResidueCount , SecondaryStructureString , SsType , SsTypeCount , SsTypeProbability

#### Returned by

AddProteinSecondaryStructure , ProteinSecondaryStructureObject

#### Derived from

Sdm::Object -> DiscoveryScript::Object

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to predict and retrieve secondary structure.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

my $sequence =
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( $mdmDocument->Molecules->[0] );
$alignment->PredictSecondaryStructureByDsc();

# Example accessing the secondary structure string from sequence property.
my $kabschAndSander =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructure(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType);
print "Kabsch and Sander secondary structure:\n";
print "Encoded: $kabschAndSander\n";

# Ensure alignment is displaying secondary structure.
if ( !( $alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown ) )
{
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown = True;
}

# Ensure KAS is displayed
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureVisible(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType) =
True;

# Example accessing the secondary structure data from object.
print "DSC secondary structure:\n";
my $ssObject =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructureObject(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);

print 'Predictor: ' . $ssObject->Predictor . "\n";
print 'Has probabilities: ' . $ssObject->IsPredicted . "\n";

my $dsc = $ssObject->SecondaryStructureString;
print "Encoded: $dsc\n";

my $propensity =
$sequence
->ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);
print "Propensity: $propensity\n";

my $helicalResidueCount = 0;
my $sheetResidueCount = 0;
my $coilResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $ssObject->ResidueCount;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $ssObject->SsType($i);
++$helicalResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$sheetResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::sheet || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
++$coilResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::coil || $type eq Sdm::extracellular );
}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print 'Analysis: The DSC secondary structure for this sequence has '
. $helicalResidueCount
. ' amino acid residues in helical formations, '
. $sheetResidueCount
. ' in sheet formations and '
. $coilResidueCount
. " in coil formations.\n";

my $secstrucfilter = $sdmDocument->SecondaryStructures;
print "Number of secondary Structures: ", $secstrucfilter->Count . "\n";
```

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Segment class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence =
$document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASCDFACSGHACSJCKLA' );

# Create a location consisting of all cysteine residues.
print "Creating location for all cysteine residues\n";
my $location = Sdm::Location::Create(Sdm::locationTypeJoin);

my $sequenceString = $sequence->SequenceString;
my $residueCount = length($sequenceString);
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
if ( substr( $sequenceString, $i, 1 ) eq 'C' )
{
my $segment = Sdm::Segment::Create( $i, $i );
$location->AddSegment($segment);
}
}

my $segmentCount = $location->SegmentCount;
print "Location has $segmentCount segments\n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $segmentCount ; ++$index )
{
my $segment = $location->Segment($index);
printf( "Segment %d ...\n", $index + 1);
print "\tStart position:\t" . $segment->StartPosition . "\n";
print "\tEnd position:\t" . $segment->EndPosition . "\n";
print "\tSegement type:\t" . $segment->Type . "\n";
print "\tIs complement?:\t" . $segment->IsComplement . "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Create a feature to and add it to the sequence.
my $feature =
Sdm::Feature::CreateCustomFeature( 'Cysteine residues', $location );
$feature->AddQualifier("KeyName", 'Example feature qualifier');
$sequence->AddFeature($feature);

print 'The feature key name is ' . $feature->Key . "\n";
```

# Sdm::Sequence::Deselect function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/sdm__sequence__deselect_function.htm

## Sdm::Sequence::Deselect function

### Description

Deselect de-selects the specified residues.
The following arguments are supported:

* StartPosition specifies the 0-based sequence position to begin the de-selection.

* Count is the number of residues to de-select.

### Applies to

The Sdm::Sequence::Deselect function can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Sequence

### Using the Sdm::Sequence::Deselect function

#### Instance

$object->Deselect( <startposition>, [count] );

$object->Deselect( { StartPosition => <startposition>, Count => [count] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <startposition> | Required | | Integer |
| [count] | Optional | 1 | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::Sequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate linking a sequence to a structure.
# NOTE: Sequences and structures can only be linked in the DS client.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId('1CRN_A');
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0);

my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');
my $molecule = $mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0);

# Link the 1crn sequence and molecule.
$sdmDocument->LinkSequenceStructure( $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0),
$mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0) );
print "The sequence and molecule are now linked.\n";

# Selecting (and deselecting) the molecule also selects the sequence
# after updating the view. Here the update views call is required
# not only to display the sequence selection, but to synchronize the
# data models.
$molecule->Select();
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();
print 'After selecting the molecule and updating the SDM document view, '
. "the sequence is also selected.\n"
if ( $sequence->IsSelected() );

# Selecting (and deselecting) from the sequence does not
# require an update views call to synchronize the data models.
# The call is requires to display the updated sequence
# selection.
$sequence->Deselect( 0, 10 );
$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();

# Break the sequence and molecule link.
$sdmDocument->BreakSequenceStructureLink( $sdmDocument->Sequences->Item(0) );
print "The sequence-molecule link is now broken.\n";

$sequence->Select( 0, 5 );
print "The first 5 residues in sequence are selected.\n"
if ( $sdmDocument->Alignment->IsSelected( 0, 0, 5 ) );

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();
$mdmDocument->UpdateViews();
print "The first 5 residues in sequence are selected.\n"
if ( $sdmDocument->Alignment->IsSelected( 0, 0, 5 ) );
```

```text
my $sequence = $document->Sequences->Item(0);

# For sequence properties with empty fields, set value to 'Unspecified'.

$sequence->Locus = 'Unspecified' if ( $sequence->Locus eq "" );
```

```text
}

my $sdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(SdmAlignmentModelType);

die "No active sequence found!" if not defined $sdmDocument;

# Get the alignment object from an SDM document.
my $sdmAlignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

# Get an Sdm::Array of sequence objects.
my $sequenceArray = $sdmAlignment->Sequences;

# Report the number of sequences in the alignment. This count
# includes both visible and hidden sequences.
print "Number of sequences in alignment: " . $sequenceArray->Count;
```

# SdmCommands package

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/sdmcommands_package.htm

## SdmCommands package

### Description

SdmCommands provides high-level functions for accessing functionality
within SdmDiscoveryScript . These commands provide a more simple interface
to working with sequences.

### Using the SdmCommands package

Access to the SdmCommands API is through the Perl use directive:

```text
use strict;
use SdmCommands;
```

The strict directive is optional, but strongly recommended as it restricts
the use of unsafe constructs. All available classes will be imported from the SdmCommands module.

#### Commands

CreateSequenceFromMolecule GetRandomAminoAcidString

#### Used by

DSCommands , VisualizerCommands

#### Module

SdmCommands.pm

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use SdmCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1kim.pdb" );

# From SdmDiscoveryScript
my $sequence = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();

# From SdmCommands
my $sequenceString = CreateSequenceFromMolecule($document);

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$sequence->SequenceCount;
```

# SecondaryStructure property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/secondarystructure_property.htm

## SecondaryStructure property

### Description

SecondaryStructure specifies the secondary structure type of an amino acid residue.

### Applies to

The SecondaryStructure property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid

### Using the SecondaryStructure property

#### Get

my $aminoacidsecondarystructureEnum = $object->SecondaryStructure;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $aminoacidsecondarystructureEnum | | | enum Mdm::AminoAcidSecondaryStructure |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |

#### Set

$object->SecondaryStructure = <secondarystructure>;

$object->SecondaryStructure( <secondarystructure> );

$object->SecondaryStructure( { SecondaryStructure => <secondarystructure> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <secondarystructure> | Required | | enum Mdm::AminoAcidSecondaryStructure |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the secondary structure API in the Molecular Data Model.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1avd');

my $helicalResidueCount = 0;
my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
foreach my $aminoAcid (@$aminoAcids)
{
my $type = $aminoAcid->SecondaryStructure;
++$helicalResidueCount if ( $type eq "aminoAcidHelix" );
}

print 'This molecule has '
. $helicalResidueCount
. " amino acid residues in helical formations.\n";
```

# SecondaryStructures filter

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/secondarystructures_filter.htm

## SecondaryStructures filter

### Description

SecondaryStructures indicates all Sdm::SecondaryStructure objects in a specific context, such as an Sdm::Alignment , Sdm::Document ,
or Sdm::AminoAcidSequence .

### Applies to

The SecondaryStructures filter can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment , Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::Document

### Using the SecondaryStructures filter

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->SecondaryStructures;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Sdm::Array |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to predict and retrieve secondary structure.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

my $sequence =
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( $mdmDocument->Molecules->[0] );
$alignment->PredictSecondaryStructureByDsc();

# Example accessing the secondary structure string from sequence property.
my $kabschAndSander =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructure(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType);
print "Kabsch and Sander secondary structure:\n";
print "Encoded: $kabschAndSander\n";

# Ensure alignment is displaying secondary structure.
if ( !( $alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown ) )
{
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown = True;
}

# Ensure KAS is displayed
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureVisible(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType) =
True;

# Example accessing the secondary structure data from object.
print "DSC secondary structure:\n";
my $ssObject =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructureObject(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);

print 'Predictor: ' . $ssObject->Predictor . "\n";
print 'Has probabilities: ' . $ssObject->IsPredicted . "\n";

my $dsc = $ssObject->SecondaryStructureString;
print "Encoded: $dsc\n";

my $propensity =
$sequence
->ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);
print "Propensity: $propensity\n";

my $helicalResidueCount = 0;
my $sheetResidueCount = 0;
my $coilResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $ssObject->ResidueCount;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $ssObject->SsType($i);
++$helicalResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$sheetResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::sheet || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
++$coilResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::coil || $type eq Sdm::extracellular );
}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print 'Analysis: The DSC secondary structure for this sequence has '
. $helicalResidueCount
. ' amino acid residues in helical formations, '
. $sheetResidueCount
. ' in sheet formations and '
. $coilResidueCount
. " in coil formations.\n";

my $secstrucfilter = $sdmDocument->SecondaryStructures;
print "Number of secondary Structures: ", $secstrucfilter->Count . "\n";
```

# Segment property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/segment_property.htm

## Segment property

### Description

Segment specifies Sdm::Segment s in an Sdm::Location .

### Applies to

The Segment property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Location

### Using the Segment property

#### Get

my $segmentObject = $object->Segment( <index> );

my $segmentObject = $object->Segment( { Index => <index> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $segmentObject | | | Sdm::Segment |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::Location |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Segment class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence =
$document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASCDFACSGHACSJCKLA' );

# Create a location consisting of all cysteine residues.
print "Creating location for all cysteine residues\n";
my $location = Sdm::Location::Create(Sdm::locationTypeJoin);

my $sequenceString = $sequence->SequenceString;
my $residueCount = length($sequenceString);
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
if ( substr( $sequenceString, $i, 1 ) eq 'C' )
{
my $segment = Sdm::Segment::Create( $i, $i );
$location->AddSegment($segment);
}
}

my $segmentCount = $location->SegmentCount;
print "Location has $segmentCount segments\n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $segmentCount ; ++$index )
{
my $segment = $location->Segment($index);
printf( "Segment %d ...\n", $index + 1);
print "\tStart position:\t" . $segment->StartPosition . "\n";
print "\tEnd position:\t" . $segment->EndPosition . "\n";
print "\tSegement type:\t" . $segment->Type . "\n";
print "\tIs complement?:\t" . $segment->IsComplement . "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Create a feature to and add it to the sequence.
my $feature =
Sdm::Feature::CreateCustomFeature( 'Cysteine residues', $location );
$feature->AddQualifier("KeyName", 'Example feature qualifier');
$sequence->AddFeature($feature);

print 'The feature key name is ' . $feature->Key . "\n";
```

$object->Select( [includechildren] );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [includechildren] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1avd');

# retrieve the third chain in 1avd. These are the ligands
my $ligandsChain = $document->Chains->[2];

# select this chain
$ligandsChain->Select();

# select all amino acids that are within 3 angstrom of the ligands
$document->SelectByRadius( 3.0, 'AminoAcid' );

printf("Selected objects: %d\n", $document->SelectedObjects->Count );

# de-select the ligands chain so that the remaining selection
# is just the amino acid residues in the vicinity of the ligands
$ligandsChain->Deselect();
```

Mdm::Document , Sdm::Alignment

### Using the SelectAll function

#### Instance

$object->SelectAll();

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript , SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to select or deselect all MDM objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

print "Selecting all objects...\n\n";
$document->SelectAll();

my $selection = $document->SelectedObjects();
printf "%s selection %d\n" , $document->ModelName, $selection->Count;
my $count = 0;
foreach my $atom (@$selection)
{
printf "%d %s\n",++$count, $atom->Name;
}

$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

print "De-selecting all objects...\n";

$document->DeselectAll();
$document->UpdateViews();

my $selection = $document->SelectedObjects();
printf "%s selection %d\n" , $document->ModelName, $selection->Count;
```

Source file: scripting/selectbyproperty_function.htm

## SelectByProperty function

### Description

SelectByProperty selects all objects which have the specified description.
The description is the same as the description used by the FilterByProperty
( FilterByProperty ) function.

### Applies to

The SelectByProperty function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SelectByProperty function

#### Instance

$object->SelectByProperty( <description> );

$object->SelectByProperty( { Description => <description> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <description> | Required | | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to create a transparent surface.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '101m.pdb' );

# Select heme atoms.
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue Name="HEM.*"; Atom label="*"');

# Create an array of all heme atoms.
my $hemeAtoms = $document->Filter( { Selected => 1 } )->Atoms;

# Create transparent surface around the heme group.
my $transparentSurface =
$document->CreateTransparentSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential,
1.3, 0.6 );

$transparentSurface->IsBackSideColorEnabled(True);
$transparentSurface->IsBackSideTransparencyEnabled(True);

# Also create wiremesh surface around the heme group.
my $wiremeshSurface =
$document->CreateWiremeshSurface( $hemeAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent,
False, Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential, 2.0 );

print "Surface area: "
. $transparentSurface->Area . "\n"
. "Surface Volume: "
. $transparentSurface->Volume . "\n";
print "Surface probe radius: "
. $transparentSurface->ProbeRadius . "\n"
. "Transparency Level: "
. $transparentSurface->TransparencyLevel . "\n";

# Select all atoms within 6A of the heme and the surface.
$document->SelectByRadius( 6.0, 'Atom' );
$transparentSurface->Select();

# Show only the heme and neighboring atoms (other than water).
$document->FitView();
$document->InvertSelection();
$document->SelectByProperty('Residue name="HOH.*"; Atom label="*"');
$document->Hide();
$document->DeselectAll();

# Display the wiremesh surface with delay.
sleep(2);
$wiremeshSurface->SetVisible();
```

# SelectByRadius function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/selectbyradius_function.htm

## SelectByRadius function

### Description

SelectByRadius selects objects inside the specified radius. The radius origin
is specified by the center of the currently selected objects. The arguments include:

* Radius specified in angstroms.

* ClassName specifies the type of objects to be selected. To select all
types of objects, use an empty string for the ClassName argument.

* ReplaceSelection specifies if the selection before
running this function should be retained or replaced. By default, the current
selection is retained.

* SelectOutsideRadius (optional) specifies if objects outside the radius
should be selected. By default, SelectOutsideRadius is False and objects inside the
radius are selected.

### Applies to

The SelectByRadius function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SelectByRadius function

#### Instance

$object->SelectByRadius( <radius>, <classname>, [replaceselection], [selectoutsideradius] );

$object->SelectByRadius( { Radius => <radius>, ClassName => <classname>, ReplaceSelection => [replaceselection], SelectOutsideRadius => [selectoutsideradius] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <classname> | Required | | String |
| <radius> | Required | | Real |
| [replaceselection] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [selectoutsideradius] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1avd');

# retrieve the third chain in 1avd. These are the ligands
my $ligandsChain = $document->Chains->[2];

# select this chain
$ligandsChain->Select();

# select all amino acids that are within 3 angstrom of the ligands
$document->SelectByRadius( 3.0, 'AminoAcid' );

printf("Selected objects: %d\n", $document->SelectedObjects->Count );

# de-select the ligands chain so that the remaining selection
# is just the amino acid residues in the vicinity of the ligands
$ligandsChain->Deselect();
```

# SelectDockingInterface function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/selectdockinginterface_function.htm

## SelectDockingInterface function

### Description

SelectDockingInterface selects the residues at the binding interface of two docked proteins.
The binding interface for the ligand is defined as any residue of the ligand that has any atom
within a cutoff distance from a receptor atom. Similarly, the binding interface for the receptor
is defined as any residue of the receptor that has any atom within a cutoff distance from a ligand atom.

The function is typically applied to the output of the Protein Docking protocols.
To run the example below, such a document should be loaded. Alternatively, the
example script for the Mdm::ProteinPose can be executed to generate
a small set of example data.

### Applies to

The SelectDockingInterface function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SelectDockingInterface function

#### Instance

$object->SelectDockingInterface( <pose>, [interfacecutoff] );

$object->SelectDockingInterface( { Pose => <pose>, InterfaceCutoff => [interfacecutoff] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <pose> | Required | | Mdm::ProteinPose |
| [interfacecutoff] | Optional | 5.0 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates the use for scripting functions for the protein-protein
# docking area.
# NOTE: Most of the functions connected to generating the DockedPoseAssembly and
# DockedProtein objects are designed to process output from the Dock Proteins (ZDOCK)
# protocols, which generates a set of numbers describing the relative orientations
# of the two proteins in a docked protein complex. Those numbers are necessary to
# generate the objects described in the this example but cannot be easily
# generated by hand. The numerical values hard-coded to avoid having
# to load a Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) output file . The values used are derived
# from the output of a Dock Proteins (ZDOCK) run on two small proteins: chain A of 2ptn and
# chain I of 2sta.

use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load receptor an ligand structures
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "2ptn.pdb" );
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "2sta.pdb" );

my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
my $receptor = $molecules->Item(0);
my $ligand = $molecules->Item(1);

# Only keep ligand chain that was used in ZDOCK run
my $ligandChains = $ligand->Chains;
foreach my $chain (@$ligandChains)
{
if ( $chain->Name ne "I" )
{
$chain->Select();
}
}

# Only keep receptor chain that was used in ZDOCK run
my $receptorChains = $receptor->Chains;
foreach my $chain (@$receptorChains)
{
if ( $chain->Name ne "A" )
{
$chain->Select();
}
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# Label receptor and ligand with identifying tags
# These tags are used by other commands
$receptor->SetProperty( "COMPLEX_TYPE", "RECEPTOR" );
$ligand->SetProperty( "COMPLEX_TYPE", "LIGAND" );

# Define general properties of the structures in the complex
# Note that these numbers are part of the output generated by the
# ZDock protein docking program.
# numerical values taken from ZDock run output
my $N = 84;
my $spacing = 1.2;
my $receptorCenter = Mdm::Point::Create( 2.5130, 7.5200, 23.7720 );
my $ligandCenter = Mdm::Point::Create( 14.5890, 21.1360, 40.4300 );
my $startingAngles = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 );

# Create the DockedProteinPoseAssembly object which contains
# information about the proteins in the docked complex that
# common to all poses
my $poseAssembly =
$document->CreateDockedProteinPoseAssembly( $ligand, $ligandCenter,
$receptor, $receptorCenter, $startingAngles );

# The next three commands are redundant with the constructor above
# and are only included as example of how they are used.
# However, they can be used to set the DockedProteinPoseAssembly
# properties to different values if desired
$poseAssembly->LigandCenter($ligandCenter);
$poseAssembly->ReceptorCenter($receptorCenter);
$poseAssembly->StartingAngles($startingAngles);

# Set the ZDock grid size and grid spacing
# These values are internally used by the ZDock program
# they are stored mainly to be able to produce input files
# for the Process Poses and Refine Docked Protein protocols
$poseAssembly->SetPropertyAsInteger( "N", $N );
$poseAssembly->SetPropertyAsReal( "spacing", $spacing );
$poseAssembly->HideProperty("N");
$poseAssembly->HideProperty("spacing");

$poseAssembly->SetProperty( "Center", "Receptor" );
$poseAssembly->Name = "Docked Poses";

# Generate the numeric data for the first docked pose
# numerical values taken from pose 1 of ZDock run output
my $position = Mdm::Point::Create( -5.1821, 20.9576, 21.2807 );
my $translation = Mdm::Point::Create( 6.0000, -16.8000, 2.4000 );
my $rotation = Mdm::Point::Create( 120.0000, 171.0266, 111.9815 );
my $cluster = 1;
my $topClusterPose = 1;
my ( $receptorCenterX, $receptorCenterY, $receptorCenterZ ) =
( 0.018, 14.954, 22.56 );
my ( $ligandCenterX, $ligandCenterY, $ligandCenterZ ) =
( 12.464, 24.22, 40.03 );

# Generate a new pose. The parameters of the constructor function are
# the position of the spherical pose representation
# the translation of the ligand from the starting to the docked position
# the rotation of the ligand from the starting to the docked position
# the cluster the pose belongs to
# whether or not the pose is the top ranked pose in the cluster 
my $newPose =
$poseAssembly->CreateProteinPose( $position, $translation, $rotation,
$cluster, $topClusterPose );

# The following sets of number represent the coordinates center of the binding interface
# on the receptor and the ligand. The values are store as properties which are
# used to toggle between receptor and ligand centric views in the DS client
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_x", "$receptorCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_y", "$receptorCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_z", "$receptorCenterZ" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_x", "$ligandCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_y", "$ligandCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_z", "$ligandCenterZ" );

# Set the name of the pose
$newPose->Name = "Pose1";

# Generate the numeric data for a second docked pose
# numerical values taken from pose 1 of ZDock run output
my $position = Mdm::Point::Create( 6.1596049, 17.94953, 5.095075 );
my $translation = Mdm::Point::Create( 4.8000, -14.4000, 4.8000 );
my $rotation = Mdm::Point::Create( 90.0000, 107.4457, 6.1356 );
my $cluster = 1;
my $topClusterPose = 0;
my ( $receptorCenterX, $receptorCenterY, $receptorCenterZ ) =
( 6.88, 14.615, 5.83 );
my ( $ligandCenterX, $ligandCenterY, $ligandCenterZ ) =
( 2.522, 27.292, 11.48 );
$newPose =
$poseAssembly->CreateProteinPose( $position, $translation, $rotation,
$cluster, $topClusterPose );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_x", "$receptorCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_y", "$receptorCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "rec_ctr_z", "$receptorCenterZ" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_x", "$ligandCenterX" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_y", "$ligandCenterY" );
$newPose->SetPropertyAsReal( "lig_ctr_z", "$ligandCenterZ" );
$newPose->Name = "Pose2";

# store the first pose in a variable using the ProteinPoses Filter
my $pose1 = $document->ProteinPoses->Item(0);

# generate the full coordinates of the receptor and ligand structures for the pose
$document->ShowDockedProteins($pose1);

# Select the residues at the binding interface for the docked pose
$document->SelectDockingInterface($pose1);

# Calculate the ligand binding interface RMSD using the interface residues of the
# first pose as reference
my $rmsds = $document->CalculateDockedRmsd( $pose1, $document->ProteinPoses );

# Output RMSD values
my $count = $rmsds->Count();
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < $count ; ++$j )
{
my $rms = $rmsds->Item($j);
$rms =~ s/\s+//g;
print "$j\t$rms\n";
}
```

# SelectGroup function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/selectgroup_function.htm

## SelectGroup function

### Description

SelectGroup selects a group (a Mdm::Group instance) without selecting the group's contents.

### Applies to

The SelectGroup function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Group

### Using the SelectGroup function

#### Static

Mdm::Group::SelectGroup( <group> );

Mdm::Group::SelectGroup( { Group => <group> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <group> | Required | | Mdm::Group |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Example for the Mdm::Group::SelectGroup function.
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );
die "The document could not be opened" unless $document;

# Get an array of all groups (Mdm::Group instances) in the document using the Groups filter
my $groups = $document->Groups;
die "The model contains no groups" unless $groups;

my $countGroups = $groups->Count;
die "The model contains no groups" unless $countGroups > 0;

# Use the first group for this demonstration.
my $group = $groups->Item(0);
die unless $group;

my $groupId = $group->UniqueId;

my $groupContents = $group->Array;
die unless $groupContents;
my $countGroupContents = $groupContents->Count;
my $groupName = $group->Name;
print "The group <" . $groupName . "> contains " . $countGroupContents . " objects.\n";

#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Select the group without selecting the contents of the group.
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Mdm::Group::SelectGroup($group);

# Verify that only one object is selected.
my $selectedObjects = $document->SelectedObjects;
die "There are no selected objects" unless ($selectedObjects and $selectedObjects->Count > 0);

my $countSelectedObjects = $selectedObjects->Count;
print "The number of selected objects is " . $countSelectedObjects . ".\n";

die "A single object should be selected" unless ($countSelectedObjects == 1);

# Verify that the group is selected by comparing the unique identifiers.
my $selectedObject = $selectedObjects->Item(0);
my $selectedObjectId = $selectedObject->UniqueId; 
die "The group has not been selected" unless ($groupId == $selectedObjectId);

print "The group <" . $groupName . "> has been selected.\n";

$document->Close();
$document = undef;
```

# SelectionScope property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/selectionscope_property.htm

## SelectionScope property

### Description

SelectionScope specifies the selection scope used when counting
hydrogen bonds in hydrogen bond monitors.

### Applies to

The SelectionScope property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor

### Using the SelectionScope property

#### Get

my $selectionscopeEnum = $object->SelectionScope;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $selectionscopeEnum | | | enum Mdm::SelectionScope |
| $object | | | Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor |

#### Set

$object->SelectionScope = <scope>;

$object->SelectionScope( <scope> );

$object->SelectionScope( { Scope => <scope> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <scope> | Required | | enum Mdm::SelectionScope |
| $object | | | Mdm::HydrogenBondMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how use the hydrogen bond monitor and to change the distance cutoff.

use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1fax.pdb" );

# Creates a hbond monitor between ligand atoms and receptor
my $ligands = GetLigands($document);
my $LigName = $ligands->Item(0)->Name;
my $ligandAtoms = $ligands->Item(0)->Atoms;
my $monitor = $document->CreateHydrogenBondMonitor( $ligandAtoms,
Mdm::allAtomHydrogenBonds, Mdm::allMolecularHydrogenBonds );

# Shows the label for each of the hbonds
$monitor->IsLabelShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll(); 

printf "Default distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->DefaultDistanceCriterion;
printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor.\n\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $newHBDist = 3.0;
$monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared( $newHBDist* $newHBDist );

# update view to ensure the correct HB count
$document->UpdateViews();
printf "Set the distance criterion for counting Hbonds: %.3f [A]\n",
sqrt $monitor->HydrogenBondDistanceSquared;

printf "%d hydrogen bonds between ligand and receptor:\n",
$monitor->HydrogenBondCount;

my $hbonds = $document->HydrogenBonds;
my $count = $hbonds->Count;
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $count ; ++$index )
{
my $hbond = $hbonds->Item($index);
my $dist = $hbond->Distance;
my $atom1 = $hbond->Atom1;
my $atom2 = $hbond->Atom2;
my $res = $atom1->Parent;

if ( $res->Name eq $LigName ) {
$atom2->Parent->Select; 
}
else{
$atom1->Parent->Select; 
}
printf "%d) Distance: %.3f A H-bond between Atom %s:%s:%s and Atom %s:%s:%s\n",
$index+1, $dist,
$atom1->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom1->Parent->Name, $atom1->Name,
$atom2->Parent->Parent->Name, $atom2->Parent->Name, $atom2->Name ;
} 

$document->FitView(); 
my $display_style = { DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' };
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle($display_style);
$document->DeselectAll();
```

SelectSequence selects all the residues and gaps belonging to the Sdm::Sequence at the specified 0-based index in an Sdm::Alignment .

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the SelectSequence function

$object->SelectSequence( <index> );

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to select an entire row of an alignment.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId('1CRN_A');
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
$alignment->InsertGap( 0, 2, 3 );

my $i = 0;
if ( $i < $alignment->SequenceCount )
{
$alignment->SelectSequence($i);
}

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

# SequenceCount property

Source type: HTML

## SequenceCount property

### Description

SequenceCount specifies the number of sequences in
an Sdm::Document or Sdm::Alignment . The
sequence count includes sequences with visibility turned off

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the usage of several sequence properties.

$samplesFolder . 'Tutorials/Quick Start Tutorials/kinases.fasta' );

my $count = $document->SequenceCount;
printf "Found %d sequences\n", $count;

my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $count )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
```

# SequenceIdentity property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/sequenceidentity_property.htm

## SequenceIdentity property

### Description

Sequence identity describes the percentage of alignment
positions that have identical residues.
This property has three optional arguments:

* IncludeGaps: If True (default), gaps are treated as valid residue
types when calculating the sequence identity.

* IncludeUnalignedTerminalResidues: If False (default), unaligned
terminal residues are excluded from the calculation.

* SelectedOnly: If False (default), all non-transient sequences
are in the calculation. Otherwise, only selected residues are included.
All selected residues must have the same columns selected.

### Applies to

The SequenceIdentity property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the SequenceIdentity property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->SequenceIdentity( [includegaps], [includeunalignedterminalresidues], [selectedonly] );

my $realValue = $object->SequenceIdentity( { IncludeGaps => [includegaps], IncludeUnalignedTerminalResidues => [includeunalignedterminalresidues], SelectedOnly => [selectedonly] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| [includegaps] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [includeunalignedterminalresidues] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [selectedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the sequence identity
# and similarity functions.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$document->DeleteAlignmentSequences();

my $sequence0 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S1', 'ASDFADS' );
my $sequence1 = $document->CreateSequence( 'S2', 'ASDFSDA' );

my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
printf "Sequence identity\t%8.3f\n", $alignment->SequenceIdentity;
printf "Sequence similarity\t%8.3f\n", $alignment->SequenceSimilarity;

my $seqIndex = 0;
my $array = $alignment->SequenceIdentityArray($seqIndex);
#my $array = $alignment->SequenceSimilarityArray($seqIndex);

my $count = $array->Count;
for (my $i = 0; $i < $count; ++$i)
{
my $value = $array->Item($i);
if ($i == $seqIndex) {
print "Self sequence identity is " . $array->Item($i) . "\n";
}
elsif ($value == -1) {
print "Sequence identity with non-transient sequence is skipped.";
}
else {
printf "Sequence identity for pair ($seqIndex, $i) is \t%8.3f\n", $array->Item($i);
}
}
```

# SequenceIndex property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/sequenceindex_property.htm

## SequenceIndex property

### Description

Sequence index specifies the position of the sequence in an alignment. If the
sequence is not found in the alignment, -1 is returned.

### Applies to

The SequenceIndex property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment

### Using the SequenceIndex property

#### Get

my $integerValue = $object->SequenceIndex( <sequence> );

my $integerValue = $object->SequenceIndex( { Sequence => <sequence> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $integerValue | | | Integer |
| <sequence> | Required | | Sdm::Sequence |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate accessing linked sequences and sequence indices.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

my $sdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(SdmAlignmentModelType);
my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

print "This example requires an open active Sequence Window with sequences "
. "linked to molecules in the last active Molecule Window."
unless ( $sdmDocument && $mdmDocument );

my $molecules = $mdmDocument->Molecules;

my $superposeMolecules = Mdm::Array::Create();
my $alignmentStrings = $sdmDocument->Alignment->AlignmentStrings;
my $alignment = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();

foreach my $molecule (@$molecules)
{
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->LinkedSequence($molecule);
if ($sequence)
{
print $sequence->Name . "\n";
$superposeMolecules->AddItem($molecule);
my $index = $sdmDocument->Alignment->SequenceIndex($sequence);
my $sequenceString = $alignmentStrings->[$index];
$alignment->AddItem($sequenceString);
}
}

my $r =
$mdmDocument->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment( $superposeMolecules,
$alignment, Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingBackboneAtoms );
```

# Sequences filter

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/sequences_filter.htm

## Sequences filter

### Description

Sequences indicates all SDM sequence objects in a specific context,
such as an Sdm::Alignment or Sdm::Document .
The sequence array can includes sequences with visibility turned off
(see IsVisible ). As an example, a Sequence Window with
one visible sequence will report a sequence count of 2 since the
consensus sequence is present but not visible.

### Applies to

The Sequences filter can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::Alignment , Sdm::Document

### Using the Sequences filter

#### Get

my $arrayObject = $object->Sequences;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $arrayObject | | | Sdm::Array |
| $object | | | Sdm::Alignment Sdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to access the alignment and
# sequences in an SDM document.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio.
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a Sequence Window\n";
print " (for example open 1a27_profile.pir from the Samples folder)\n";
print " 3 Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

my $sdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(SdmAlignmentModelType);

die "No active sequence found!" if not defined $sdmDocument;

# Get the alignment object from an SDM document.
my $sdmAlignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

# Get an Sdm::Array of sequence objects.
my $sequenceArray = $sdmAlignment->Sequences;

# Report the number of sequences in the alignment. This count
# includes both visible and hidden sequences.
print "Number of sequences in alignment: " . $sequenceArray->Count;
```

# SetAtomColorScheme function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setatomcolorscheme_function.htm

## SetAtomColorScheme function

### Description

SetAtomColorScheme recolors the selected atoms using the specified scheme. If no atoms are selected, the color scheme is applied to all atoms. The possible color schemes are enumerated in enum Mdm::AtomColorScheme .

### Applies to

The SetAtomColorScheme function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetAtomColorScheme function

#### Command

$object->SetAtomColorScheme( <colorscheme> );

$object->SetAtomColorScheme( { ColorScheme => <colorscheme> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <colorscheme> | Required | | enum Mdm::AtomColorScheme |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to colors atoms.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Generate array with AtomColorScheme values.
my @atomColorOptions = (
Mdm::atomColorByCarbonsOnly, Mdm::atomColorByCell,
Mdm::atomColorByChain, Mdm::atomColorByCharge,
Mdm::atomColorByChirality, Mdm::atomColorByElement,
Mdm::atomColorByGroup, Mdm::atomColorByIsotropicDisplacement,
Mdm::atomColorByMolecule, Mdm::atomColorByMoleculeColor,
Mdm::atomColorByParentColor, Mdm::atomColorByPartialCharge,
Mdm::atomColorByResidue,
);

print "Change to color by element color scheme: atomColorByElement...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomColorScheme(Mdm::atomColorByElement);
sleep(3);

foreach my $atomColorOption (@atomColorOptions)
{
$document->SetAtomColorScheme($atomColorOption);
print "Change to color by color scheme: $atomColorOption...\n\n";
sleep(3);
}
```

# SetAtomDisplayStyle function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setatomdisplaystyle_function.htm

## SetAtomDisplayStyle function

### Description

SetAtomDisplayStyle changes the display of the selected atoms to the
specified style and, optionally, changes the stick size, ball size, and CPK scale.
If no atoms are selected, the display style is applied to all atoms. The possible display styles are enumerated in enum Mdm::AtomDisplayStyle .

Parameters:

* DisplayStyle : Defines the display style as specified in enum Mdm::AtomDisplayStyle

* StickSize : Sets the thickness of lines representing bonds for display styles that display bonds as sticks.

* BallSize : Sets the size of the spheres representing atoms for display styles that display atoms as balls.

* CPKScale : Scale factor to multiply VDW radius to determine size of the spheres representing atoms.

* UpdateDefaultValues : If set to True, the current values are will be used as default values.

### Applies to

The SetAtomDisplayStyle function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetAtomDisplayStyle function

#### Command

$object->SetAtomDisplayStyle( <displaystyle>, [sticksize], [ballsize], [cpkscale], [updatedefaultvalues] );

$object->SetAtomDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => <displaystyle>, StickSize => [sticksize], BallSize => [ballsize], CPKScale => [cpkscale], UpdateDefaultValues => [updatedefaultvalues] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <displaystyle> | Required | | enum Mdm::AtomDisplayStyle |
| [ballsize] | Optional | -1.0 | Real |
| [cpkscale] | Optional | -1.0 | Real |
| [sticksize] | Optional | -1.0 | Real |
| [updatedefaultvalues] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to change the display style of selected atoms.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Generate array with AtomDisplayStyle values.
my @atomDisplayStyles = (
Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStick,
Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStickSingle,
Mdm::styleAtomCPK,
Mdm::styleAtomLine,
Mdm::styleAtomLineSingle,
Mdm::styleAtomNone,
Mdm::styleAtomPolyhedron,
Mdm::styleAtomScaledBallAndStick,
Mdm::styleAtomScaledBallAndStickSingle,
Mdm::styleAtomStick,
Mdm::styleAtomStickSingle,
);

print 'Change the atom and bond display style to ball-and-stick '
. "using the defaults sizes...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStick, -1.0, -1.0, -1.0,
False );
sleep(3);

print 'Change the atom and bond display style to ball-and-stick '
. "with 0.7 A balls and 0.5 A sticks...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(
{
DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStick,
StickSize => 0.5,
BallSize => 0.7,
UpdateDefaultValues => False
}
);
sleep(3);

print 'Change the atom and bond display style to CPK '
. "with 0.75 A CPK scale factor...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(
{
DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleAtomCPK,
CPKScale => 0.75,
UpdateDefaultValues => False
}
);
sleep(3);

foreach my $atomDisplayStyle (@atomDisplayStyles)
{
print "Change the display style to $atomDisplayStyle...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle($atomDisplayStyle);
sleep(3);
}

print "Reset the display style to ball-and-stick with default sizes...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStick, 0.2, 0.4, 1.0,
False );
```

# SetAtomPropertyColorScheme function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setatompropertycolorscheme_function.htm

## SetAtomPropertyColorScheme function

### Description

SetAtomPropertyColorScheme recolors the selected atoms according to a property using the specified color scheme.
If no atoms are selected, all atoms are recolored. The color schemes are enumerated in enum Mdm::SpectrumType .

Parameters:

* PropertyName : name of a numeric atom property to be used for coloring.

* SpectrumType : color map as specified in enum Mdm::SpectrumType

* NumberOfBands : The number of different colors from the spectrum to be used for coloring.

* RangeMinimium : Property value mapped to low end of color spectrum.

* RangeMaximum : Property value mapped to high end of color spectrum.

* Clip : If true, atoms with property values outside the range (RangeMinimum-RangeMaximum) are not drawn.

### Applies to

The SetAtomPropertyColorScheme function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetAtomPropertyColorScheme function

#### Command

$object->SetAtomPropertyColorScheme( <propertyname>, [spectrumtype], [numberofbands], [rangeminimum], [rangemaximum], [clip] );

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrates how to colors the atom display of selected atoms
# by an atom property.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Generate array with Color Scheme values.
my @atomPropertyColorSchemes = (
Mdm::spectrumBlackWhite, Mdm::spectrumBlueGreenRed,
Mdm::spectrumBlueRed, Mdm::spectrumBlueWhiteRed,
Mdm::spectrumRainbow1, Mdm::spectrumRainbow1Reversed,
Mdm::spectrumRainbow2, Mdm::spectrumRainbow2Reversed,

SpectrumType => Mdm::spectrumBlueWhiteRed,
NumberOfBands => 32,
RangeMinimum => 1,
RangeMaximum => 327,
Clip => False
}
);

print "Color atoms by atom ID (atom number) with clipping...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomPropertyColorScheme(
{
PropertyName => "ID",
SpectrumType => Mdm::spectrumBlueWhiteRed,
NumberOfBands => 32,
RangeMinimum => 20,
RangeMaximum => 300,
Clip => True
}
);
sleep(3);

foreach my $atomPropertyColorScheme (@atomPropertyColorSchemes)
{
print 'Color by Isotropic Displacement property using color scheme: '
. $atomPropertyColorScheme
. "...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomPropertyColorScheme( "Isotropic Displacement",
$atomPropertyColorScheme, 32, 3, 16, False );
sleep(3);
}
```

##### Parameters

| <colorscheme> | Required | | enum Mdm::BindingSiteColorScheme |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to colors binding sites.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);

# Hide protein atoms.
TurnOffProteinAtoms($document);

# Use command in the DSCommands perl modules to remove ligands
# water from the complex.
Delete( $document, GetLigands($document) );
Delete( $document, GetWaters($document) );

print "Searching for binding sites...\n\n";
my $protein = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
$document->CreateBindingSitesFromCavities($protein);
my $bindingSites = $document->BindingSites;
print 'Found ' . $bindingSites->Count . " binding sites.\n\n";

# Color each binding site point with a random color.
foreach my $site (@$bindingSites)
{
$site->SetVisible; # make all sites visible
my $bindingSitePoints = $site->BindingSitePoints;
foreach my $bindingSitePoint (@$bindingSitePoints)
{
my $color = Mdm::Color::Create(
int( 255 * rand() ),
int( 255 * rand() ),
int( 255 * rand() )
);
$bindingSitePoint->Color = $color;
}
}

print "Color binding sites points using a random color for each point...\n\n";
$document->SetBindingSiteColorScheme(Mdm::bindingSiteColorByPoints);
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to change the display style of binding sites.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

print "Changing the display style to a protein ribbon tubes...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleAtomNone } );
ApplyProteinDisplayStyle( $document, Mdm::styleProteinRibbonTube );

print "Turning on visibility of all binding sites...\n\n";
foreach my $site (@$bindingSites)
{
$site->SetVisible();
}
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
sleep(3);

print "Changing the display style to solid surface...\n\n";
$document->SetBindingSiteDisplayStyle( Mdm::styleBindingSiteSolidSurface,
False );
```

# SetBlackAndMouldHydrophobicities function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setblackandmouldhydrophobicities_function.htm

## SetBlackAndMouldHydrophobicities function

### Description

Sets a property named B-M Hydrophobicity for each amino acid residue.
By default the values lie between 0 (Arg) to 1.0 (Phe) , but setting the Normalize argument True adjusts them such that glycine has a value of 0, in which case Arg has a value of -0.501 and Phe is 0.499.

### Applies to

The SetBlackAndMouldHydrophobicities function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetBlackAndMouldHydrophobicities function

#### Command

$object->SetBlackAndMouldHydrophobicities( [normalize] );

$object->SetBlackAndMouldHydrophobicities( { Normalize => [normalize] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [normalize] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
##########
#
# Assign various properties to amino acids and their atoms 
# These may then be used to calculate 'residue feature' values over spatial neighborhoods.
# 

use MdmDiscoveryScript; # For working with Molecule Window
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

# Set this False to calculate custom residue neighborhood feature set
my $default = "True";
#property for surface display and site creation can be set on the command line.
#note that it is case sensitive
my $propertyName = "0A_CX_average";

if(@ARGV != 0){
($propertyName) = @ARGV;
}

# to run on a molecule in the active window, use this instead of OpenURL
# my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl(PdbUrlPrefix. '1aqk.pdb');

# Return an error message and exit if there is not an active Molecule Window
die "No Molecule Window!" unless $document;
$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);
print "Calculating atom properties\n";
# Many of the residue features depend on solvent surface accessibility and require that the atoms 
# have a precomputed SAA property, which is typically calculated using CHARMm.
# However, for demonstration purposes we can use the DS method and rename the property.

#check if the first atom already has SAA property, if not then do calculation.
my $atoms = $document->Atoms();
my $atom = $atoms->Item(0);
if(! $atom->HasProperty("SAA")) {
print "No precomputed SAA properties, calculating Solvent Accessible Surface\n";
$document->SolventAccessibleSurface();
$document->RenameUserProperty("Atom Solvent Accessibility","SAA",$atom->ClassName());
$document->RenameUserProperty("Percent Sidechain Solvent Accessibility","Fractional Sidechain SAA",$atom->Parent()->ClassName()); 
$document->RenameUserProperty("Percent Solvent Accessibility","Fractional Residue SAA",$atom->Parent()->ClassName());
#convert the percent accessibilities to fractional values for consistency with the method below 
foreach my $atom(@$atoms){
if($atom->HasProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA")){
my $sa = $atom->GetProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA")/100.0;
$atom->SetProperty("Fractional Sidechain SAA",$sa);
}
if($atom->HasProperty("Fractional Residue SAA")){
my $sa = $atom->GetProperty("Fractional Residue SAA")/100.0;
$atom->SetProperty("Fractional Residue SAA",$sa);
}
}
}else{
#This calculates the Sidechain and Residue fractional exposures, using the precomputed SAA atom properties.
#the extended tripeptide exposures have been calculated for various CHARMm forcefields, with the appropriate 
#set used according to the forcefield setting on the structure.
$document->CalculateFractionalResidueExposures(True,True);
}
#Set the Black and Mould hydrophobicities for each amino acid residue. The argument specifies whether to 'normalize' the values
#to set the hydrophobicity of glycine to zero.

$document->SetBlackAndMouldHydrophobicities(False);

#Calculate the 'protrusion indices'. This sets a property CX on each atom. If the 'approximate' method
# is used (first argument True) then there are no prerequisites - the calculation will be performed as
# in the original paper by Pintar et al, using only non-hydrogen atoms and a single atom volume of 20.1.
#Otherwise, all atoms are used; if they have a property VDWRadius set (eg corresponding to the CHARMm forcefield values)
#these will be used, otherwise the standard DS element VDW radii are used. The second argument is the sphere radius used
#for the calculation.

$document->CalculateProtrusionIndices(False,10.0);

#Calculate the 'depth indices'. This sets a property DPX on each atom. It requires precomputed atom SAA properties.
#Exposed atoms will always have a DPX of zero. In addition, atoms will have a property DPX_RAD assigned. This is the VDW radius of
#the nearest surface atom, which is required for the simple electrostatic potential calculation. If a property VDWRadius set
# (eg corresponding to the CHARMm forcefield values)
#these will be used, otherwise the standard DS element VDW radii are used.

$document->CalculateDepthIndices();

#Performs a simple electrostatic potential calculation and sets atom properties EPOT. It requires the DPX and DPX_RAD properties to get the distance of the
#atom from the surface, so will run the Depth Indices calculation if they aren't already set. It therefore also requires SAA atom properties.
#Ideally the atomic charges should be set using the desired CHARMm forcefield.

$document->CalculateElectrostaticPotentials();

#The following lines demonstrate how to calculate 'residue neighborhood features'.
#These are the result of taking an existing property value for each atom within a given radius of any atom
#in the residue for which the property is being calculated, and then performing operations such as total or average.
# Note that a radius of 0 will give the result of the operation on just the residue itself.
#The new residue property names will be formed from radius_property_operation eg
# 5A_SAA_hydrophilic
#
#The choice of operations is:
# average: average of the property over all the atoms in the neighborhood
# minimum: minimum value for the property in the neighborhood
# maximum: maximum value for the property in the neighborhood
# total: sum of the property over all atoms in the neighborhood
# hydrophobic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Ala,Ile,Leu,Met,Phe,Trp,Tyr or Val
# hydrophilic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Arg,His,Lys,Asp,Glu,Ser,Thr,Asn or Gln (His is any protonation state of histidine)
# positive: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Arg,Hsp or Lys (Hsp is positively charged Histidine)
# negative: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues Asp or Glu
# aromatic: sum over all atoms in the neighborhood which are in residues His, Phe, Trp and Tyr
# backbone: sum over all backbone atoms C CA N O and attached hydrogens
# sidechain: sum over all non-backbone atoms
# exposed: sum over all surface exposed atoms. (obviously SAA is a prerequisite)
#
# The ExposedOnly argument allows the feature calculation to be restricted to residues which have some
# surface exposure ie atoms with SAA >0
# 
#The first form calculates these residue features for a default set of properties, operations and radii. These are:
# radii 0,3,5,7,10,12,15,20,25
# properties operations
# CX average,minimum,maximum 
# DPX average,minimum,maximum
# SAA total,hydrophobic,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,backbone,sidechain 
# Charge total,exposed
# EPOT total
#
#The second allows for any numeric user defined properties with any combination of operators, and any integer radii.

print "Calculating Residue Neighborhood Features, default $default\n";

if($default eq "True"){
$document->CalculateDefaultResidueNeighborhoodFeatures(False);
}else{
my $radii= DiscoveryScript::IntegerArray::Create();
$radii->AddItem(0);
$radii->AddItem(3);
$radii->AddItem(5);
$radii->AddItem(7);
my $featureNames = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
my $subTypes = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$featureNames->AddItem("CX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("DPX");
$subTypes->AddItem("average,minimum,maximum");
$featureNames->AddItem("Charges");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,exposed");
$featureNames->AddItem("SAA");
$subTypes->AddItem("total,hydrophilic,hydrophobic,positive,negative,aromatic,backbone,sidechain");
$document->CalculateResidueNeighborhoodFeatures($radii,$featureNames,$subTypes,False);
}
print "Finished calculating features\n";
#now demonstrate the generic patch group creation API
#get the maximum value for this property

my $residues = $document->Residues();
my $atoms = $document->Atoms();
my $max = -999999;
my $min = 999999;
my $minPatchCutoff = 0.0;
my $minPeakCutoff = 0.1;
foreach my $res (@$residues){
if($res->HasProperty($propertyName)){
my $val = $res->GetProperty($propertyName);
if($val > $max){$max = $val;}
if($val < $min){$min = $val;}
}
}
#the range setting may not be ideal for all properties. 
if($max != -999999){
$minPeakCutoff = $max/5;
$minPatchCutoff = $max/10;
$max = $max/2;
$min = -1.0*$max;

#create a surface colored by this property
my $surface = $document->CreateSolidSurface($atoms,Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent);
$surface->Name = "$propertyName Surface";

my $surfacePropertyColorScheme = Mdm::spectrumBlueWhiteRed;
$surface->Select();
$document->SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme( $propertyName,
$surfacePropertyColorScheme, 32, $min,$max, False, "" );
$surface->IsTransparent(True);
$surface->IsLegendShown(True);
$document->DeselectAll();
$document->FindSurfacePropertySites($propertyName,5.0,$max,$minPatchCutoff);
}else{
print "Property for surface patches $propertyName not present\n";
}
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
$document->UpdateViews();

print "Finished script example\n";
```

# SetCellDisplayStyle function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting
