## SetCellDisplayStyle function

### Description

SetCellDisplayStyle changes the display of the selected cells to the specified style.

### Applies to

The SetCellDisplayStyle function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetCellDisplayStyle function

#### Command

$object->SetCellDisplayStyle( <displaystyle> );

$object->SetCellDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => <displaystyle> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <displaystyle> | Required | | enum Mdm::CellDisplayStyle |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to manipulate cell properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

$document->SetCellDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleCellLine);

# Illustrate how to change cell settings.
my $cell = $document->Cells->Item(0);

print "Original crystal cell parameters:\n";
my $a = $cell->LengthA;
my $b = $cell->LengthB;
my $c = $cell->LengthC;
my $alpha = $cell->AngleAlpha;
my $beta = $cell->AngleBeta;
my $gamma = $cell->AngleGamma;

my $format = "\t%s = %8.3f\n\t%s = %8.3f\n\t%s = %8.3f\n";
printf $format, 'a', $a, 'b', $b, 'c', $c;
printf $format, 'alpha', $alpha, 'beta', $beta, 'gamma', $gamma;
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

$document->SetCellParameters( 40.0, 40.0, 90.0, 90.0, 90.0 );
print "New crystal cell parameters:\n";
printf $format, 'a', $cell->LengthA, 'b', $cell->LengthB, 'c', $cell->LengthC;
printf $format,
'alpha', $cell->AngleAlpha,
'beta', $cell->AngleBeta,
'gamma', $cell->AngleGamma;

print "Restoring original PDB cell parameters...\n\n";
$document->SetCellParameters( $a, $b, $c, $alpha, $beta, $gamma );

print "Changing the preferences to fill one cell...\n\n";
$document->SetCellPreferences(Mdm::symmetryBuildOneCell);
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

print 'Changing the preferences to apply all symmetry operators, ';
print 'with default special position tolerance, no symmetry bonding ';
print "and 2 cells along each axis...\n\n";
$document->SetCellPreferences( Mdm::symmetryBuildOriginal, 0.001, False, 2, 2,
2 );
$document->FitView();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

print "Changing the preferences to get rid of the symmetry copies...\n\n";
$document->SetCellPreferences(Mdm::symmetryBuildPositions);

# Illustrate how to change space Group settings.
my $spacegroup = $cell->SpaceGroup;
my $originalName = $spacegroup->Symbol;
my $fullname = $spacegroup->FullSymbol;
print 'Original space group is ' . $originalName . ".\n\n";

my $sgIucNumber = 14;
$document->SetCellSpaceGroup($sgIucNumber);
print 'Changing space group to IUC number ' . $sgIucNumber . "\n";
print 'New space group is ' . $spacegroup->Symbol . ".\n\n";

# Set alternative cell choice to yield P21/N.
# NOTE: The name and qualifier strings are exactly the values seen the first
# two drop-down lists of the dialog if you set the space group via the GUI.
my $sgName = "14 P21/C";
my $sgQualifier = "B-Unique Choice: 2";
$document->SetCellSpaceGroupByName( $sgName, $sgQualifier );
print 'Changing space group to Name: ' 
. $sgName
. ' Qualifier: '
. $sgQualifier . "\n";
print 'New space group set by name is ' . $spacegroup->Symbol . ".\n\n";
```

$object->SetCellPreferences( <symmetrybuildtype>, [tolerance], [bonding], [axisareplicatecount], [axisbreplicatecount], [axiscreplicatecount] );

$object->SetCellPreferences( { SymmetryBuildType => <symmetrybuildtype>, Tolerance => [tolerance], Bonding => [bonding], AxisAReplicateCount => [axisareplicatecount], AxisBReplicateCount => [axisbreplicatecount], AxisCReplicateCount => [axiscreplicatecount] } );

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to manipulate cell properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

$document->SetCellDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleCellLine);

# Illustrate how to change cell settings.
my $cell = $document->Cells->Item(0);

print "Original crystal cell parameters:\n";
my $a = $cell->LengthA;
my $b = $cell->LengthB;
my $c = $cell->LengthC;
my $alpha = $cell->AngleAlpha;
my $beta = $cell->AngleBeta;
my $gamma = $cell->AngleGamma;

my $format = "\t%s = %8.3f\n\t%s = %8.3f\n\t%s = %8.3f\n";
printf $format, 'a', $a, 'b', $b, 'c', $c;
printf $format, 'alpha', $alpha, 'beta', $beta, 'gamma', $gamma;
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

$document->SetCellParameters( 40.0, 40.0, 90.0, 90.0, 90.0 );
print "New crystal cell parameters:\n";
printf $format, 'a', $cell->LengthA, 'b', $cell->LengthB, 'c', $cell->LengthC;
printf $format,
'alpha', $cell->AngleAlpha,
'beta', $cell->AngleBeta,
'gamma', $cell->AngleGamma;

print "Restoring original PDB cell parameters...\n\n";
$document->SetCellParameters( $a, $b, $c, $alpha, $beta, $gamma );

print "Changing the preferences to fill one cell...\n\n";
$document->SetCellPreferences(Mdm::symmetryBuildOneCell);
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

print 'Changing the preferences to apply all symmetry operators, ';
print 'with default special position tolerance, no symmetry bonding ';
print "and 2 cells along each axis...\n\n";
$document->SetCellPreferences( Mdm::symmetryBuildOriginal, 0.001, False, 2, 2,
2 );
$document->FitView();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

print "Changing the preferences to get rid of the symmetry copies...\n\n";
$document->SetCellPreferences(Mdm::symmetryBuildPositions);

# Illustrate how to change space Group settings.
my $spacegroup = $cell->SpaceGroup;
my $originalName = $spacegroup->Symbol;
my $fullname = $spacegroup->FullSymbol;
print 'Original space group is ' . $originalName . ".\n\n";

my $sgIucNumber = 14;
$document->SetCellSpaceGroup($sgIucNumber);
print 'Changing space group to IUC number ' . $sgIucNumber . "\n";
print 'New space group is ' . $spacegroup->Symbol . ".\n\n";

# Set alternative cell choice to yield P21/N.
# NOTE: The name and qualifier strings are exactly the values seen the first
# two drop-down lists of the dialog if you set the space group via the GUI.
my $sgName = "14 P21/C";
my $sgQualifier = "B-Unique Choice: 2";
$document->SetCellSpaceGroupByName( $sgName, $sgQualifier );
print 'Changing space group to Name: ' 
. $sgName
. ' Qualifier: '
. $sgQualifier . "\n";
print 'New space group set by name is ' . $spacegroup->Symbol . ".\n\n";
```

# SetCellSpaceGroupByName function

### Description

SetCellSpaceGroupByName sets the space group of a three-dimensional crystal structure specified by its name and qualifier.
The name is actually a string containing the IUC number followed by the name, and the qualifier
allows specification of the unique axis and origin choice.
For the default axis and origin, use an empty string for the QualifierString argument.

The SetCellSpaceGroupByName function can be used with the following objects:

# SetCurrent3dPointerResidue function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setcurrent3dpointerresidue_function.htm

## SetCurrent3dPointerResidue function

### Description

SetCurrent3dPointerResidue moves a molecule's
( Mdm::Molecule ) 3D pointer to the selected residue
( Mdm::Residue ).
If the residue has a CA atom ( Mdm::Atom ),
the pointer is moved to the CA atom's coordinates.
Otherwise, the pointer is placed at the residue center-of-geometry.

### Applies to

The SetCurrent3dPointerResidue function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetCurrent3dPointerResidue function

#### Command

$object->SetCurrent3dPointerResidue();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate the use of 3D pointer functions.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;
use MdmCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );

# Create 3D pointer at the center.
$document->Create3dPointer();

my ( $maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ) = Get3DWindowExtents( $document );
printf "Window Max: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f Min: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n",$maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ;

# Translate document to illustrate pointer functions.
$document->Translate( 10, 10, 10 );
sleep(1);

my ( $maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ) = Get3DWindowExtents( $document );
printf "Window Max: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f Min: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n",$maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ;

# Center the view on the 3D point.
$document->Goto3dPointer();
sleep(1);

my ( $maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ) = Get3DWindowExtents( $document );
printf "Window Max: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f Min: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n",$maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ;

# Remove the pointer.
$document->Remove3dPointer();

# Place the pointer at ALA38.
$document->AminoAcids->[37]->Select();
$document->SetCurrent3dPointerResidue();
$document->Goto3dPointer();

my ( $maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ) = Get3DWindowExtents( $document );
printf "Window Max: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f Min: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n",$maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ;
sleep(1);

# Move to the next residue.
$document->GotoNext3dPointerResidue();

my ( $maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ) = Get3DWindowExtents( $document );
printf "Window Max: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f Min: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n",$maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ;
sleep(1);

# Move to the previous residue.
$document->GotoPrevious3dPointerResidue();
my ( $maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ) = Get3DWindowExtents( $document );
printf "Window Max: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f Min: %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n",$maxx, $maxy, $maxz, $minx, $miny, $minz ;

sleep(1);
```

# SetDisplayExtent function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setdisplayextent_function.htm

## SetDisplayExtent function

### Description

SetDisplayExtent sets the display extents of an Mdm::Isosurface .

### Applies to

The SetDisplayExtent function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Isosurface

### Using the SetDisplayExtent function

#### Instance

$object->SetDisplayExtent( <bottomleft>, <topright> );

$object->SetDisplayExtent( { BottomLeft => <bottomleft>, TopRight => <topright> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <bottomleft> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| <topright> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| $object | | | Mdm::Isosurface |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
print "This example is intended to run inside Discovery Studio\n";
print "It operates on a document with grid data\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1. Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2. Open a structure with grid data\n";
print
" (for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
print " 3. Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}
else
{

}

# Connect to an Sdm::Document from the last active sequence window
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

# Get array with all isosurfaces using Isosurfaces filter
my $isosurfaces = $document->Isosurfaces;

if ( $isosurfaces->Count == 0 )
{
print "To run this script, please open a structure with grid data.\n";
print "(for example open DensityVolume.dsv from the Samples folder)\n";
exit;
}

$document->ShowAll();
my $chain1 = $document->Chains->[0];

# Get the first isosurface
my $isosurface = $isosurfaces->[0];

# Create a isosurfaces at 0.5 and 0.4 isovalue
my $newContour = $isosurface->CreateIsosurface(0.5);
my $newContour2 = $isosurface->CreateIsosurface(0.4);

# Set the context array for the first surface
$chain1->Select();
$newContour->DisplayStyle(Mdm::isosurfaceStyleSolid);
$newContour->ContextAtomArray( $chain1->Atoms );
$document->UpdateViews();

sleep(1);

# Set Display extend for second isosurface
$document->DeselectAll();

# Pick 2 arbitrary atoms and get their coordinates
my $atom1 = $document->Atoms->[4324];
my $atom2 = $document->Atoms->[5100];
$atom1->Select();
$atom2->Select();
my $xyz1 = $atom1->XYZ;
my $xyz2 = $atom2->XYZ;
print $xyz1->X . "\t" . $xyz1->Y . "\t" . $xyz1->Z . "\n";
print $xyz2->X . "\t" . $xyz2->Y . "\t" . $xyz2->Z . "\n";

# Set style to isosurfaceStyleQuadMesh
$newContour2->DisplayStyle(Mdm::isosurfaceStyleQuadMesh);
$newContour2->SetDisplayExtent( $xyz1, $xyz2 );
$document->UpdateViews();

sleep(1);

# Display full extend of second isosurface
$newContour2->DisplayAll();
```

## SetDnaColorScheme function

### Description

SetDnaColorScheme recolors the selected nucleotides ( Mdm::Nucleotide )
using the specified scheme. If no objects are selected, all nucleotides are recolored.

The possible color schemes are listed in enum Mdm::DnaColorScheme .
Note that the color scheme is only applied if nucleotides are displayed in ladder or
ring display styles (see SetDnaDisplayStyle ).

### Applies to

The SetDnaColorScheme function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to colors nucleic acids nucleic amino acid chains.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1bna.pdb" );

# Create array with DnaColorScheme values.
my @dnaColorOptions = (
Mdm::dnaColorByBaseType, Mdm::dnaColorByCell,
Mdm::dnaColorByMolecule, Mdm::dnaColorByNucleicAcidChain,
Mdm::dnaColorByResidue,
);

print "Change the display to tubes and ladders...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleAtomNone } );
$document->SetDnaDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleDNATubeLadder);

print "Color by residue color scheme...\n\n";
$document->SetDnaColorScheme(Mdm::dnaColorByResidue);
sleep(3);

foreach my $dnaColorOption (@dnaColorOptions)
{
print "Color by color scheme: $dnaColorOption...\n\n";
$document->SetDnaColorScheme($dnaColorOption);

}
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Example : SetDnaDisplayStyle
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my ($useLastActive) = @ARGV;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1bna.pdb" );

# Create array with DnaDisplayStyle values
my @dnaDisplayStyles = (
Mdm::styleDnaArrow, Mdm::styleDnaArrowRings,
Mdm::styleDnaNone, Mdm::styleDnaTube,
Mdm::styleDnaTubeLadder, Mdm::styleDnaTubeRings
);

$document->SetDnaColorScheme(Mdm::dnaColorByResidue);
print "Color by ResidueScheme Scheme : dnaColorByResidue\n\n";
sleep(1);

# Iterate over all options - with 1 second delay
foreach my $dnaDisplayStyle (@dnaDisplayStyles)
{
sleep(1);
$document->SetDnaDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => $dnaDisplayStyle } );
print "current Display Style : $dnaDisplayStyle\n";
}

# Include color backbone by residues
my @cbbrOptions = ( False, True );

foreach my $dnaDisplayStyle (@dnaDisplayStyles)
{
foreach my $cbbr (@cbbrOptions)
{
sleep(1);
$document->SetDnaDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => $dnaDisplayStyle, ColorBackboneByResidues => $cbbr } );
print "current Display Style : $dnaDisplayStyle\n";

}
```

# SetDnaPropertyColorScheme function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setdnapropertycolorscheme_function.htm

## SetDnaPropertyColorScheme function

### Description

SetDnaPropertyColorScheme recolors the selected nucleotides
( Mdm::Nucleotide ) using the specified property scheme.
If no objects are selected, all nucleotides are recolored.

The color schemes are enumerated in enum Mdm::SpectrumType . The following arguments are available:

* PropertyName is the name of a numeric nucleotide property to be used for coloring.

* SpectrumType is the color map as specified in enum Mdm::SpectrumType

* NumberOfBands is the number of colors from the spectrum to be used for coloring.

* RangeMinimium is the property value mapped to low end of color spectrum.

* RangeMaximum is the property value mapped to high end of color spectrum.

* Clip is a boolean value that determines whether nucleotides with property values outside the range (RangeMinimum-RangeMaximum) are drawn.

Note. The color scheme is only applied
if nucleotides are displayed in ladder or ring display styles
(see SetDnaDisplayStyle ).

### Applies to

The SetDnaPropertyColorScheme function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetDnaPropertyColorScheme function

#### Command

$object->SetDnaPropertyColorScheme( <propertyname>, [spectrumtype], [numberofbands], [rangeminimum], [rangemaximum], [clip] );

$object->SetDnaPropertyColorScheme( { PropertyName => <propertyname>, SpectrumType => [spectrumtype], NumberOfBands => [numberofbands], RangeMinimum => [rangeminimum], RangeMaximum => [rangemaximum], Clip => [clip] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <propertyname> | Required | | String |
| [clip] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [numberofbands] | Optional | 4 | Integer |
| [rangemaximum] | Optional | 1.0 | Real |
| [rangeminimum] | Optional | 0.0 | Real |
| [spectrumtype] | Optional | spectrumBlueGreenRed | enum Mdm::SpectrumType |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrates how to colors the DNA display of selected nucleic

use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1bna.pdb" );

# Generate array with Color Scheme values.
my @dnaPropertyColorSchemes = (
Mdm::spectrumBlackWhite, Mdm::spectrumBlueGreenRed,
Mdm::spectrumBlueRed, Mdm::spectrumBlueWhiteRed,
Mdm::spectrumRainbow1, Mdm::spectrumRainbow1Reversed,
Mdm::spectrumRainbow2, Mdm::spectrumRainbow2Reversed,
Mdm::spectrumRedBlue, Mdm::spectrumRedGreenBlue,
Mdm::spectrumRedWhiteBlue, Mdm::spectrumWhiteBlack,
);

print "Change the display to tubes and ladders...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleAtomNone } );
$document->SetDnaDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleDNATubeRings);
sleep(3);

# Iterate over all options, color by Isotropic Displacement - with 1 second delay

. $dnaPropertyColorScheme
. "...\n\n";
$document->SetDnaPropertyColorScheme( "ID", $dnaPropertyColorScheme, 24,
1, 24, False );
sleep(3);
}
```

# SetEntry function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setentry_function.htm

## SetEntry function

### Description

SetEntry sets the value of a particular entry in the 3x3 or 4x4 matrix. Row and column must be less then the matrix dimension (uses zero-based indexing).

### Applies to

The SetEntry function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Matrix3x3 , Mdm::Matrix4x4

### Using the SetEntry function

#### Instance

$object->SetEntry( <row>, <column>, <value> );

$object->SetEntry( { Row => <row>, Column => <column>, Value => <value> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <column> | Required | | Integer |
| <row> | Required | | Integer |
| <value> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Matrix3x3 Mdm::Matrix4x4 |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the matrix functions SetEntry and GetEntry.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# This subroutine exercises the matrix functions to set and get elements.
sub CreateAndListMatrix($)
{
my ($matrix) = @_;

print "Define matrix entries using SetEntry function.\n";

my $size = 3;
$size = 4 if ( $matrix->ClassName eq 'Mdm::Matrix4x4' );

my $value = 2;
for ( my $row = 0 ; $row < $size ; ++$row )
{
for ( my $column = 0 ; $column < $size ; ++$column )
{
$matrix->SetEntry( $row, $column, $value );
++$value;
}
}
$matrix->SetEntry( $size - 1, $size - 1, 2.0 );

print "List the entries in the matrix.\n";
print "Matrix: \n";
for ( my $row = 0 ; $row < $size ; ++$row )
{
for ( my $column = 0 ; $column < $size ; ++$column )
{
printf " %8.3f", $matrix->GetEntry( $row, $column );
}
print "\n";
}

# Find the determinant
print "\n";
print "The determinant of the matrix is: "
. $matrix->Determinant . "\n\n";
}

my $matrix3x3 = Mdm::Matrix3x3::Create();
CreateAndListMatrix($matrix3x3);

my $matrix4x4 = Mdm::Matrix4x4::Create();
CreateAndListMatrix($matrix4x4);
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Create a few conformations by rotating the phi torsion
# angle of the first amino acid residue.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1crn.pdb' );
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

# Get first three amino acids
my $aminoAcid1 = $aminoAcids->Item(0);
my $aminoAcid2 = $aminoAcids->Item(1);
my $aminoAcid3 = $aminoAcids->Item(2);

# Creates a monitor for the phi angle
my $phiTorsion = $document->CreateTorsionMonitor(
$aminoAcid1->AmideCarbon, $aminoAcid2->AmideNitrogen,
$aminoAcid2->CAlpha, $aminoAcid2->AmideCarbon
);

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index <= 6 ; ++$index )
{
my $torsionValue = $index * 60.0;

# rotates the first residue's phi angle
$phiTorsion->SetProperty( "Angle", "$torsionValue" );

# creates a new conformation
my $conformation = $molecule->CreateConformation();
$conformation->MakeActive();

# sets the current conformation to be invisible
# so the next newly created conformation will be "active" and updated with new coordinates
$conformation->SetInvisible(True);
}
my $activeConformation = $aminoAcid1->FindActiveConformation();

# creates an animation using the newly created conformations
my $animation = $document->CreateAnimation( $molecule->Conformations );
my $frameCount = $animation->FrameCount;
print "Number of animation frames: $frameCount frames\n";

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $frameCount ; $i++ )
{
printf " Frame: %d\n", $i + 1; 
$animation->ActivateNextFrame();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(1);
}
```

# SetIsosurfaceGridColorScheme function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setisosurfacegridcolorscheme_function.htm

## SetIsosurfaceGridColorScheme function

### Description

SetIsosurfaceGridColorScheme recolors the selected isosurfaces using the specified grid.
The following parameters are available:

* GridName: Name of the Grid (e.g., from Electrostatics Potential Calculation) to be used for coloring.

* SpectrumType: The color map as specified in enum Mdm::SpectrumType .

* NumberOfBands: The number of different colors from the spectrum to be used for coloring.

* RangeMinimium: Property value mapped to low end of the color spectrum.

* RangeMaximum: Property value mapped to high end of the color spectrum.

* Clip: If true, vertices with property values outside the range (RangeMinimum..RangeMaximum) are not drawn.

### Applies to

The SetIsosurfaceGridColorScheme function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetIsosurfaceGridColorScheme function

#### Instance

$object->SetIsosurfaceGridColorScheme( <gridname>, <spectrumtype>, <numberofbands>, <rangeminimum>, <rangemaximum>, <clip> );

$object->SetIsosurfaceGridColorScheme( { GridName => <gridname>, SpectrumType => <spectrumtype>, NumberOfBands => <numberofbands>, RangeMinimum => <rangeminimum>, RangeMaximum => <rangemaximum>, Clip => <clip> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <clip> | Required | | Boolean |
| <gridname> | Required | | String |
| <numberofbands> | Required | | Integer |
| <rangemaximum> | Required | | Real |
| <rangeminimum> | Required | | Real |
| <spectrumtype> | Required | | enum Mdm::SpectrumType |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to colors the selected isosurfaces by grid.
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

sub PrintUsage()
{
print "This example is intended to run inside Discovery Studio.\n";
print "It operates on a document with suitably named grid data.\n";
print "To run this script:\n";
print " 1. Start Discovery Studio.\n";
print " 2. Open a structure with suitably named grid data\n";
print
" (for example open Isosurfaces.dsv from the Samples folder).\n";
print " 3. Run this script within Discovery Studio.\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
if ( DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() )
{
PrintUsage();
exit;
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);

die "There is no active molecule window" unless $document;

my $grids = $document->Isosurfaces();

die "There are not enough isosurfaces for this example" if $grids->Count < 2;

my $grid1 = $grids->Item(0);
my $grid2 = $grids->Item(1);

$grid1->Select();

# Assuming there is an isosurface named Grid #2 color the selected isosurface
# using the Rainbow 1 spectrum with 16 distinct colors,
# a range of -0.2 ... 0.2 and mapping values outside the range to the colors
# used for the minimum and maximum value of the range, respectively.

$document->SetIsosurfaceGridColorScheme(
"Grid #2",
Mdm::spectrumRainbow1,
16,
-0.2,
0.2,
False);

$grid1->Deselect();

$grid2->Select();

# Assuming there is an isosurface named Grid #1 color the selected isosurface
# using the Red-Green-Blue spectrum with 16 distinct colors,
# a range of 0.0 ... 0.25 and disregarding values outside the range.

$document->SetIsosurfaceGridColorScheme(
"Grid #1",
Mdm::spectrumRedGreenBlue,
16,
0.0,
0.25,
True);

$grid2->Deselect();
```

# SetMembraneOrientation function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setmembraneorientation_function.htm

## SetMembraneOrientation function

### Description

SetMembraneOrientation the orientation an Mdm::Membrane with respect to a set of
protein Mdm::Atom .
The following parameters are available:

* ArrayOfAtoms specifies the set of atoms used as reference to define the membrane orientation.

* Membrane specifies the implicit membrane.

* Offset specifies the shift of the membrane center with respect to the reference atoms.

* Tilt specifies the tilt of the membrane with respect to the reference atoms.

* Rotation specifies the rotation of the membrane with respect to the reference atoms.

* ReferenceAxis specifies principal axis used to define the membrane orientation.

### Applies to

The SetMembraneOrientation function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetMembraneOrientation function

#### Instance

$object->SetMembraneOrientation( <arrayofatoms>, <membrane>, <offset>, <tilt>, <rotation>, [referenceaxis] );

$object->SetMembraneOrientation( { ArrayOfAtoms => <arrayofatoms>, Membrane => <membrane>, Offset => <offset>, Tilt => <tilt>, Rotation => <rotation>, ReferenceAxis => [referenceaxis] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <arrayofatoms> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| <membrane> | Required | | Mdm::Membrane |
| <offset> | Required | | Real |
| <rotation> | Required | | Real |
| <tilt> | Required | | Real |
| [referenceaxis] | Optional | | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate creation, placement and orientation of a membrane.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

# Remove all chains except the first.
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

my $membrane = $document->AddAndOrientMembrane($molecule);
$membrane->Select();

my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms();
my $membraneOrientation =
$molecule->CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor( $membrane, $atoms,
Mdm::objectCentered, Mdm::referenceAxisZ );

print "Original membrane position:\n";
my $shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
my $tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
my $rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);

print "Modified membrane position:\n";
$document->SetMembraneOrientation( $atoms, $membrane, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 );
$shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
$tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
$rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);

print "Modified membrane position:\n";
$document->SetMembraneOrientation( $atoms, $membrane, 10.0, 30.0, 90.0 );
$shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
$tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
$rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);

my $transmembraneResidues =
$document->TransmembraneResidues( $molecule, $membrane );
$document->SplitTransmembraneSegments( $molecule, $membrane,
$transmembraneResidues );

foreach my $residue (@$transmembraneResidues)
{
$residue->Select();
}
```

# SetParent function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setparent_function.htm

## SetParent function

### Description

SetParent sets an object as the parent of another object
analogous to the client's drag and drop functionality in the
Molecular Data Model's Hierarchy View. This function allows
for reparenting of Mdm::Molecule and Mdm::Chain objects. Both the child and parent
objects must be defined and contained within the same document.

Molecules can be reparented to the root, a cell, or another
molecule object. When a molecule is reparented to another molecule,
only the molecule contents are moved so that the molecules are merged in effect.

A chain object can be reparented to another molecule or the root.
When reparenting a chain to the root object, a new molecule is created
as the chain's parent.

See also ChangeObjectParent for additional advanced
reparenting options.

### Applies to

The SetParent function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetParent function

#### Command

$object->SetParent( <parent>, <child> );

$object->SetParent( { Parent => <parent>, Child => <child> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <child> | Required | | Mdm::Object |
| <parent> | Required | | Mdm::Object |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Reparent a chain under a new molecule.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# 1atp.pdb contains a chain with residues ATP1, MN2, and MN3.
my $document =
DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl(PdbUrlPrefix . '1atp.pdb');

$document->IsHierarchyViewShown = True;
sleep(1);

# Reparent a chain under a new molecule.
my $residue = $document->FilterByProperty("Residue label=\"ATP355\"");
my $chain = $residue->Item(0)->Parent;
$document->SetParent($document->RootObject, $chain);
```

Mdm::ScreenLabel , Mdm::ShapeFeature , Mdm::SideChainConformationViolationMonitor , Mdm::SlicingPlane , Mdm::Sphere , Mdm::Surface , Mdm::TorsionMonitor , Mdm::TupleMonitor , Mdm::UnsatisfiedNonbond , Mdm::Valence , Mdm::ValenceMonitor , Mdm::VectorFeature

### Using the SetPropertyAsReal function

$object->SetPropertyAsReal( <propertyname>, <propertyvalue> );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <propertyname> | Required | | String |
| <propertyvalue> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

# SetProteinColorScheme function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setproteincolorscheme_function.htm

## SetProteinColorScheme function

### Description

SetProteinColorScheme recolors the selected amino acids ( Mdm::AminoAcid )
and amino acid chains ( Mdm::AminoAcidChain ) using the specified scheme.
If no objects are selected, all amino acid chains are recolored.

The possible color schemes are listed in enum Mdm::ProteinColorScheme .
Note that the color scheme is only visible if the protein is displayed in a
style other than Mdm::styleProteinNone (see SetProteinDisplayStyle ).

### Applies to

The SetProteinColorScheme function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetProteinColorScheme function

#### Command

$object->SetProteinColorScheme( <colorscheme> );

$object->SetProteinColorScheme( { ColorScheme => <colorscheme> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <colorscheme> | Required | | enum Mdm::ProteinColorScheme |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to colors amino acids and amino acid chains.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Create array with ProteinColorScheme values.
my @proteinColorOptions = (
Mdm::proteinColorByAminoAcidChain, Mdm::proteinColorByCAlpha,
Mdm::proteinColorByCell, Mdm::proteinColorByHydrophobicity,
Mdm::proteinColorByMolecule, Mdm::proteinColorByNToCTerminal,
Mdm::proteinColorByPKa, Mdm::proteinColorByResidue,
Mdm::proteinColorBySecondaryType, Mdm::proteinColorByRainbow
);

print "Change the display to a solid protein ribbon tube...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleAtomNone } );
$document->SetProteinDisplayStyle(
{ DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleProteinRibbonTube } );

print "Color by secondary structure type...\n\n";
$document->SetProteinColorScheme(Mdm::proteinColorBySecondaryType);
sleep(3);

foreach my $proteinColorOption (@proteinColorOptions)
{
print "Color by color scheme: $proteinColorOption...\n\n";
$document->SetProteinColorScheme($proteinColorOption);
sleep(3);
}
```

# SetProteinPropertyColorScheme function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setproteinpropertycolorscheme_function.htm

## SetProteinPropertyColorScheme function

### Description

SetProteinPropertyColorScheme recolors the protein display of selected amino acids
( Mdm::AminoAcid ) and amino acid chains
( Mdm::AminoAcidChain ) using the specified property scheme.
If no objects are selected, all amino acid chains are recolored.

The color schemes are enumerated in enum Mdm::SpectrumType .

Parameters:

* PropertyName : name of a numeric residue property to be used for coloring.

* SpectrumType : color map as specified in enum Mdm::SpectrumType

* NumberOfBands : The number of different colors from the spectrum to be used for coloring.

* RangeMinimium : Property value mapped to low end of color spectrum.

* RangeMaximum : Property value mapped to high end of color spectrum.

* Clip : If true, residues with property values outside the range (RangeMinimum-RangeMaximum) are not drawn.

Note. The color scheme is only
visible if the protein is displayed in a style other than
Mdm::styleProteinNone (see SetProteinDisplayStyle ).

### Applies to

The SetProteinPropertyColorScheme function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetProteinPropertyColorScheme function

# SetRotation function

## SetRotation function

### Description

SetRotation sets the rotation of a Matrix3x3 object to the specified vector and angle

### Applies to

Mdm::Matrix3x3

### Using the SetRotation function

#### Instance

my $matrix3x3Object = $object->SetRotation( <vector>, <angle> );

my $matrix3x3Object = $object->SetRotation( { Vector => <vector>, Angle => <angle> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $matrix3x3Object | | | Mdm::Matrix3x3 |
| <angle> | Required | | Real |
| <vector> | Required | | Mdm::Point |
| $object | | | Mdm::Matrix3x3 |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the matrix function Rotate.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $xAxisVector = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 );

print "Creating a matrix M to rotate 90 degrees around X-axis.\n";
my $matrix = Mdm::Matrix3x3::Create();
$matrix->SetRotation( $xAxisVector, 90.0 );

printf " %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\t\n",
$matrix->GetEntry( 0, 0 ), $matrix->GetEntry( 0, 1 ),
$matrix->GetEntry( 0, 2 );
printf " %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\t\n",
$matrix->GetEntry( 1, 0 ), $matrix->GetEntry( 1, 1 ),
$matrix->GetEntry( 1, 2 );
printf " %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\t\n\n",
$matrix->GetEntry( 2, 0 ), $matrix->GetEntry( 2, 1 ),
$matrix->GetEntry( 2, 2 );

my $vector = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 1.0, 0.0 );
printf "Vector before rotation: (%8.3f %8.3f %8.3f)\n",
$vector->X, $vector->Y, $vector->Z;

$vector = $matrix->Rotate($vector);
printf "Vector after rotation: (%8.3f %8.3f %8.3f)\n",
$vector->X, $vector->Y, $vector->Z;
```

# SetSideChainProtonation function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setsidechainprotonation_function.htm

## SetSideChainProtonation function

### Description

SetSideChainProtonation modifies protein side-chain formal charges, bonding protonation of ionizable residues as appropriate for charged or neutral state.
The ionizable amino acids are ARG, ASP, CYS, GLU, HIS,LYS and TYR

### Applies to

The SetSideChainProtonation function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid

### Using the SetSideChainProtonation function

#### Instance

my $booleanValue = $object->SetSideChainProtonation( <charged>, [addmissinghydrogens], [histidinehydrogenonnd1] );

my $booleanValue = $object->SetSideChainProtonation( { Charged => <charged>, AddMissingHydrogens => [addmissinghydrogens], HistidineHydrogenOnND1 => [histidinehydrogenonnd1] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| <charged> | Required | | Boolean |
| [addmissinghydrogens] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [histidinehydrogenonnd1] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This example shows how to alter sidechain protonation
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# subroutine to print atoms in a residue
sub PrintResidue($)
{
my ($residue) = @_;
my $atoms = $residue->Atoms;
my $atomCount = $atoms->Count;

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atomCount ; ++$index )
{
my $atom = $atoms->Item($index);
my $name = $atom->Name();

#Do not bother listing mainchain atoms or any carbons
if ( ( $name ne 'N' )
&& ( $name ne 'O' )
&& ( $atom->Element ne 'C' ) )
{
printf " Name : %s Formal charge %d/%d\n", $name,
$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,
$atom->FormalCharge->Denominator;
}
}
}

# create a peptide to play around with. This will contain all the
# ionizable amino acids plus ala on either end
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();

my $chain = $molecule->CreateAminoAcidChain();
my $aminoAcid1 = $chain->CreateResidue(Mdm::alanine);

# now for a sequence of the ionizable amino acids
my $wideSequence = "ArgAspCysGluHisLysTyrAla";
my $sequence = Mdm::AminoAcidChain::ConvertToOneLetterSequence($wideSequence);
$document->GrowAminoAcidChain(
{
InsertAt => $chain,
Sequence => $sequence,
GrowAtNTerminal => False
}
);

# Now alter protonation state for each in turn
my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
my $count = $aminoAcids->Count;
for ( my $index = 1 ; $index < $count - 1 ; ++$index )
{
my $aminoAcid = $aminoAcids->Item($index);
printf( "\nNormal (pH 7) ionization for %s\n", $aminoAcid->Name() );
PrintResidue($aminoAcid);

# The second argument controls whether to adjust hydrogens. We have not added any
# to start with so will use False for now.
$aminoAcid->SetSideChainProtonation( True, False );
print("Set to charged state\n");
PrintResidue($aminoAcid);
$aminoAcid->SetSideChainProtonation( False, False );
print("Set to uncharged state\n");
PrintResidue($aminoAcid);

# Now set by pH. Note that, as for the above there is an optional
# 3rd argument which controls the protonation position for Histidine,
# and also a 4th which controls whether to set according to predicted pKa values.
$aminoAcid->SetSideChainProtonationBypH( 1.0, False );
print("Set for pH 1\n");
PrintResidue($aminoAcid);
$aminoAcid->SetSideChainProtonationBypH( 13.0, False );
print("Set for pH 13\n");
PrintResidue($aminoAcid);
$aminoAcid->SetSideChainProtonationBypH( 7.0, False );
print("Set for pH 7\n");
PrintResidue($aminoAcid);

}

# For neutral Histidine, we can control the protonation position ND1 or NE2
# Lets add the hydrogens this time to make it clear
my $histidine = $aminoAcids->Item(5);
print("\nNeutral Histidine protonation:\n");
$histidine->SetSideChainProtonation( False, True, True );
print("Hydrogen should be on ND1\n");
PrintResidue($histidine);
$histidine->SetSideChainProtonation( False, True, False );
print("Hydrogen should be on NE2\n");
PrintResidue($histidine);

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# SetSideChainProtonationBypH function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setsidechainprotonationbyph_function.htm

## SetSideChainProtonationBypH function

### Description

SetSideChainProtonationBypH adjusts formal charges, bonding and hydrogens as appropriate for the given pH.
The ionizable amino acids are ARG, ASP, CYS, GLU, HIS,LYS and TYR

### Applies to

The SetSideChainProtonationBypH function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AminoAcid

### Using the SetSideChainProtonationBypH function

#### Instance

my $booleanValue = $object->SetSideChainProtonationBypH( [ph], [addmissinghydrogens], [histidinehydrogenonnd1], [usepredictedpk] );

my $booleanValue = $object->SetSideChainProtonationBypH( { pH => [ph], AddMissingHydrogens => [addmissinghydrogens], HistidineHydrogenOnND1 => [histidinehydrogenonnd1], UsePredictedpK => [usepredictedpk] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| [addmissinghydrogens] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [histidinehydrogenonnd1] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [ph] | Optional | 7.0 | Real |
| [usepredictedpk] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::AminoAcid |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This example shows how to alter sidechain protonation
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# subroutine to print atoms in a residue
sub PrintResidue($)
{
my ($residue) = @_;
my $atoms = $residue->Atoms;
my $atomCount = $atoms->Count;

for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $atomCount ; ++$index )
{
my $atom = $atoms->Item($index);
my $name = $atom->Name();

#Do not bother listing mainchain atoms or any carbons
if ( ( $name ne 'N' )
&& ( $name ne 'O' )
&& ( $atom->Element ne 'C' ) )
{
printf " Name : %s Formal charge %d/%d\n", $name,
$atom->FormalCharge->Numerator,
$atom->FormalCharge->Denominator;
}
}
}

# create a peptide to play around with. This will contain all the
# ionizable amino acids plus ala on either end
my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();

my $chain = $molecule->CreateAminoAcidChain();
my $aminoAcid1 = $chain->CreateResidue(Mdm::alanine);

# now for a sequence of the ionizable amino acids
my $wideSequence = "ArgAspCysGluHisLysTyrAla";
my $sequence = Mdm::AminoAcidChain::ConvertToOneLetterSequence($wideSequence);
$document->GrowAminoAcidChain(
{
InsertAt => $chain,
Sequence => $sequence,
GrowAtNTerminal => False
}
);

# Now alter protonation state for each in turn
my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;
my $count = $aminoAcids->Count;
for ( my $index = 1 ; $index < $count - 1 ; ++$index )
{
my $aminoAcid = $aminoAcids->Item($index);
printf( "\nNormal (pH 7) ionization for %s\n", $aminoAcid->Name() );
PrintResidue($aminoAcid);

# The second argument controls whether to adjust hydrogens. We have not added any
# to start with so will use False for now.
$aminoAcid->SetSideChainProtonation( True, False );
print("Set to charged state\n");
PrintResidue($aminoAcid);
$aminoAcid->SetSideChainProtonation( False, False );
print("Set to uncharged state\n");
PrintResidue($aminoAcid);

# Now set by pH. Note that, as for the above there is an optional
# 3rd argument which controls the protonation position for Histidine,
# and also a 4th which controls whether to set according to predicted pKa values.
$aminoAcid->SetSideChainProtonationBypH( 1.0, False );
print("Set for pH 1\n");
PrintResidue($aminoAcid);
$aminoAcid->SetSideChainProtonationBypH( 13.0, False );
print("Set for pH 13\n");
PrintResidue($aminoAcid);
$aminoAcid->SetSideChainProtonationBypH( 7.0, False );
print("Set for pH 7\n");
PrintResidue($aminoAcid);

}

# For neutral Histidine, we can control the protonation position ND1 or NE2
# Lets add the hydrogens this time to make it clear
my $histidine = $aminoAcids->Item(5);
print("\nNeutral Histidine protonation:\n");
$histidine->SetSideChainProtonation( False, True, True );
print("Hydrogen should be on ND1\n");
PrintResidue($histidine);
$histidine->SetSideChainProtonation( False, True, False );
print("Hydrogen should be on NE2\n");
PrintResidue($histidine);

$document->UpdateViews();
```

# SetSurfaceColorScheme function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setsurfacecolorscheme_function.htm

## SetSurfaceColorScheme function

### Description

SetSurfaceColorScheme recolors the selected surfaces using the specified scheme.
When there is no grid, use an empty string for the GridName argument.

### Applies to

The SetSurfaceColorScheme function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetSurfaceColorScheme function

#### Instance

$object->SetSurfaceColorScheme( <colorscheme>, [gridname] );

$object->SetSurfaceColorScheme( { ColorScheme => <colorscheme>, GridName => [gridname] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <colorscheme> | Required | | enum Mdm::SurfaceColorScheme |
| [gridname] | Optional | "" | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to colors selected surfaces.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Generate array with Color Scheme values.
my @surfaceColorSchemes = (
Mdm::surfaceColorByAtomCharge,
Mdm::surfaceColorByAtomColor,
Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential,
Mdm::surfaceColorByParentColor
);

print "Creating a solid surface (this may take a few seconds)...\n\n";
my $allAtoms = $document->Atoms;
my $surface =
$document->CreateSolidSurface( $allAtoms, Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent, False,
Mdm::surfaceColorByElectrostaticPotential, 1.3 );
sleep(1);

foreach my $surfaceColorScheme (@surfaceColorSchemes)
{
print "Color surface by surface color scheme: $surfaceColorScheme...\n\n";
$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);
$surface->Select();

$document->SetSurfaceColorScheme($surfaceColorScheme);

$surface->Deselect();
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(1);
}
```

## SetSurfaceDisplayStyle function

### Description

SetSurfaceDisplayStyle changes the display of the selected surfaces to the specified style.

The display styles differ in how the surfaces are defined (e.g. solvent accessible surface, van der Waals surface).
The available display styles are given by enum Mdm::SurfaceDisplayStyle .

### Applies to

The SetSurfaceDisplayStyle function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetSurfaceDisplayStyle function

#### Command

$object->SetSurfaceDisplayStyle( <displaystyle> );

$object->SetSurfaceDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => <displaystyle> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <displaystyle> | Required | | enum Mdm::SurfaceDisplayStyle |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to change the display style of selected surfaces.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Generate array with Color Scheme values.
my @surfaceDisplayStyles = (
Mdm::surfaceStyleSoft, Mdm::surfaceStyleNone,
Mdm::surfaceStyleSolvent, Mdm::surfaceStyleVDW
);

print 'Creating a solid surface with legend '
. "(this may take a few seconds)...\n\n";
my $allAtoms = $document->Atoms;
my $surface = $document->CreateSolidSurface($allAtoms);
$document->DeselectAll();
$surface->IsLegendShown(True);
sleep(3);

foreach my $surfaceDisplayStyle (@surfaceDisplayStyles)
{
print "Change the surface display style to $surfaceDisplayStyle...\n\n";
$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);
$surface->Select();

$document->SetSurfaceDisplayStyle($surfaceDisplayStyle);

$surface->Deselect();
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);
}
```

# SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/setsurfacepropertycolorscheme_function.htm

## SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme function

### Description

SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme recolors the selected surfaces using the specified property scheme.

Parameters:

* PropertyName : name of a numeric residue property to be used for coloring.

* SpectrumType : color map as specified in enum Mdm::SpectrumType .

* NumberOfBands : The number of different colors from the spectrum to be used for coloring.

* RangeMinimium : Property value mapped to low end of color spectrum.

* RangeMaximum : Property value mapped to high end of color spectrum.

* Clip : If true, residues with property values outside the range (RangeMinimum-RangeMaximum) are not drawn.

* GridName : Name of the Grid (e.g. from Electrostatics Potential Calculation) to be used for coloring.

For default behavior, use Mdm::spectrumBlueGreenRed for the SpectrumType argument, 4 for the
NumberOfBands argument, 0.0 for the RangeMinimum argument, 1.0 for the RangeMaximum argument,
false for the Clip argument, and an empty string for the GridName argument.

### Applies to

The SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme function

#### Instance

$object->SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme( <propertyname>, <spectrumtype>, <numberofbands>, <rangeminimum>, <rangemaximum>, <clip>, [gridname] );

$object->SetSurfacePropertyColorScheme( { PropertyName => <propertyname>, SpectrumType => <spectrumtype>, NumberOfBands => <numberofbands>, RangeMinimum => <rangeminimum>, RangeMaximum => <rangemaximum>, Clip => <clip>, GridName => [gridname] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <clip> | Required | | Boolean |
| <numberofbands> | Required | | Integer |
| <propertyname> | Required | | String |
| <rangemaximum> | Required | | Real |
| <rangeminimum> | Required | | Real |
| <spectrumtype> | Required | | enum Mdm::SpectrumType |
| [gridname] | Optional | "" | String |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to colors the selected surfaces by property.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# Generate array with Color Scheme values.
my @surfacePropertyColorSchemes = (
Mdm::spectrumBlackWhite, Mdm::spectrumBlueGreenRed,
Mdm::spectrumBlueRed, Mdm::spectrumBlueWhiteRed,
Mdm::spectrumRainbow1, Mdm::spectrumRainbow1Reversed,
Mdm::spectrumRainbow2, Mdm::spectrumRainbow2Reversed,
Mdm::spectrumRedBlue, Mdm::spectrumRedGreenBlue,
Mdm::spectrumRedWhiteBlue, Mdm::spectrumWhiteBlack,
);

print "Creating a solid surface (this may take a few seconds)...\n\n";
my $allAtoms = $document->Atoms;

foreach my $surfacePropertyColorScheme (@surfacePropertyColorSchemes)
{
print 'Color by atom charge property using surface color scheme: '
. $surfacePropertyColorScheme
. "...\n\n";

$surfacePropertyColorScheme, 32, -0.7, 0.7, False, "" );

$surface->Deselect();
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);

sleep(1);
}
```

# SetTemporaryFolder function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/settemporaryfolder_function.htm

## SetTemporaryFolder function

### Description

SetTemporaryFolder sets the temporary folder path.
The function returns True if the temporary folder path has
been set as specified.
The caller of this function is responsible for making sure
that the folder exists, and is writable.
If the folder does not exist or is not writable, the function
returns False.

### Applies to

The SetTemporaryFolder function can be used with the following objects:

DiscoveryScript

### Using the SetTemporaryFolder function

#### Static

my $booleanValue = DiscoveryScript::SetTemporaryFolder( [path] );

my $booleanValue = DiscoveryScript::SetTemporaryFolder( { Path => [path] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $booleanValue | | | Boolean |
| [path] | Optional | "" | String |

#### Defined by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use DiscoveryScript;

my $s = DiscoveryScript::GetTemporaryFolder();
print "Temporary folder = $s\n";

# This path is assumed to be valid.
DiscoveryScript::SetTemporaryFolder($s);

$s = DiscoveryScript::GetTemporaryFolder();
print "Temporary folder = $s\n";
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate the function SetToIdentityMatrix.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

print "Creating a matrix.\n";
my $matrix = Mdm::Matrix3x3::Create( 2., 3., 4., 5., 6., 7., 8., 9., 1. );

$matrix->GetEntry( 2, 2 );
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to change the display style of binding sites.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

print "Changing the display style to a protein ribbon tubes...\n\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( { DisplayStyle => Mdm::styleAtomNone } );
ApplyProteinDisplayStyle( $document, Mdm::styleProteinRibbonTube );

# Use command in the DSCommands perl modules to remove ligands
# water from the complex.
Delete( $document, GetLigands($document) );
Delete( $document, GetWaters($document) );
sleep(3);

my $protein = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

print "Searching for binding sites...\n\n";
$document->EnableUpdateViews(False);
$document->CreateBindingSitesFromCavities($protein);
my $bindingSites = $document->BindingSites;
print 'Found ' . $bindingSites->Count . " binding sites.\n\n";

print "Turning on visibility of all binding sites...\n\n";
foreach my $site (@$bindingSites)
{
$site->SetVisible();
}
$document->EnableUpdateViews(True);
sleep(3);

print "Changing the display style to solid surface...\n\n";
$document->SetBindingSiteDisplayStyle( Mdm::styleBindingSiteSolidSurface,
False );
```

```text
print "Point2 is: (" . $xy2->X . "," . $xy2->Y . ")\n";
print "Sum of squares of Point1 is: " . $xy1->SumSquares . "\n";

my $distance = $xy1->CalculateDistance($xy2);
print "The distance between these points is: $distance\n";

print "The dot product between points is: "
. $xy1->CalculateDotProduct($xy2) . "\n";

$xy1->SetXY( 2.0, 2.0 );
print "Changing Point1 to: (" . $xy1->X . "," . $xy1->Y . ")\n\n";

# Working with 3D points.
my $xyz = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 );
print "Creating 3D point with value: ("
. $xyz->X . ","
. $xyz->Y . ","
. $xyz->Z . ")\n";

$xyz->SetXYZ( 0.0, 1.0, 2.0 );
print "Changing 3D point to: ("
. $xyz->X . ","
. $xyz->Y . ","
. $xyz->Z . ")\n";
```

# SG1Coord property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/sg1coord_property.htm

## SG1Coord property

### Description

SG1Coord indicates the predicted position for the first SG atom
in the disulfide bridge site monitor.

### Applies to

The SG1Coord property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::DisulfideBridgeSite

### Using the SG1Coord property

#### Get

my $pointObject = $object->SG1Coord;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $pointObject | | | Mdm::Point |
| $object | | | Mdm::DisulfideBridgeSite |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
#This is used for the script apis
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $temp = 0;
my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('4ins');

#By default, the script returns string containing a csv file of properties for the predicted disulfides.
#Only new disulfides are found, for any chain combination, minimum sequence separation 5,
#maximum energy 10.0
# i.e. default args are novelDisulfidesOnly, anyChainDisulfides, 5, 10.0, true will use this one to show how to get the residues/bonds

my $csvFile=$document->PredictDisulfides();

#save the csv file
my $name=$document->ModelName();
my $fileName=$name . "Predicted_New_Disulfides.csv";
open FILE, '>' . $fileName;
print FILE $csvFile;
close FILE;

my $molecules=$document->Molecules();

#note that if validation of existing disulfides is performed (by using Mdm::existingDisulfidesOnly#or Mdm::novelAndExistingDisulfides then a second molecule containing the modelled disulfide
#bridges and with additional properties on the bond and molecule 

my $numMols=$molecules->Count; 
if($numMols == 1){

$document->DeselectAll();
my $molecule=$molecules->Item(0);
my $residuePairsAssembly = $molecule->Filter(
{ Type=>"Assembly", Property => "Name", Name => "Predicted Disulfide Bridge Residues" } );
if($residuePairsAssembly->Count() == 1){
print "Potential residue pairs for mutation to cysteine to form disulfide bridge in ".$molecule->Name . ": \n";
my $residuePairs=$residuePairsAssembly->Item(0)->Groups();
foreach my $residuePair (@$residuePairs) {
my $residuePairList=$residuePair->ArrayInDepthFirstHierarchyOrder();
#should be 2 residues in here
if($residuePairList->Count == 2){
my $residue1 = $residuePairList->Item(0);
my $residue2 = $residuePairList->Item(1);
print "Group " . $residuePair->Name . " contains residues: ". $residue1->Name . " and " . $residue2->Name . "\n";
}
}
}

#this should now also contain predicted site objects from which we can extract more properties
print "Sites for mutation to cysteine\n";
my $sites = $document->DisulfideBridgeSites;
my $numSites = $sites->Count();
print $numSites . " sites\n";
for(my $index = 0; $index < $numSites; ++$index){
my $site=$sites->Item($index);
my $label = $site->Name;
my $score = $site->GetProperty("Score");
my $energy = $site->GetProperty("Energy");
my $badContacts = $site->GetProperty("Bad Contacts");
my $depth = $site->GetProperty("Residue Depth");
my $mobility = $site->GetProperty("Thermal Mobility");
my $sep = $site->GetProperty("Sequence Separation");
my $volchange = $site->GetProperty("Volume Change");
my $env = $site->GetProperty("Environment");
my $SA = $site->GetProperty("Solvent Accessibility");
my $chi3 = $site->GetProperty("Chi3");
print " site " . $label . " score " . $score . " energy " . $energy . " Bad contacts " . $badContacts ." residue depth " . $depth . " mobility " . $mobility . " sep " . $sep . " volchange " . $volchange . " env " . $env . " SA " . $SA . " chi3 " . $chi3 . "\n";

my $SG1Coord = $site->SG1Coord;
my $SG2Coord = $site->SG2Coord;
print " SG coordinates (" . $SG1Coord->X . ", " . $SG1Coord->Y . ", " . $SG1Coord->Z . ") and " .
"(" . $SG2Coord->X . ", " . $SG2Coord->Y . ", " . $SG2Coord->Z . ")\n";
my $residues = $site->ResiduesToMutate;
if($residues->Count == 2){
print "residue 1 " . $residues->Item(0)->Name . " residue 2 " . $residues->Item(1)->Name . "\n";
}else{
print " error - site should contain two residues\n";
}

#create S-S bridge from a site - the command works on any selected DisulfideBridgeSite
if($score > 80.0){
print "Score " . $score . " - Creating S-S bridge\n"; 
$site->Select();
$document->CreateDisulfideBridges();
$site->Deselect();
}

}

}
```

# Shape property

Source type: HTML

## Shape property

Shape is an enum Sdm::FeatureShape specifying the graphical shape of an Sdm::Feature .

Sdm::Feature

### Using the Shape property

#### Get

my $featureshapeEnum = $object->Shape;

##### Parameters

#### Set

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| $object | | | Sdm::Feature |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Segment class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence =
$document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASCDFACSGHACSJCKLA' );

# Create a location consisting of all cysteine residues.
print "Creating location for all cysteine residues\n";
my $location = Sdm::Location::Create(Sdm::locationTypeJoin);

my $sequenceString = $sequence->SequenceString;
my $residueCount = length($sequenceString);
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
if ( substr( $sequenceString, $i, 1 ) eq 'C' )
{
my $segment = Sdm::Segment::Create( $i, $i );
$location->AddSegment($segment);
}
}

my $segmentCount = $location->SegmentCount;
print "Location has $segmentCount segments\n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $segmentCount ; ++$index )
{
my $segment = $location->Segment($index);
printf( "Segment %d ...\n", $index + 1);
print "\tStart position:\t" . $segment->StartPosition . "\n";
print "\tEnd position:\t" . $segment->EndPosition . "\n";
print "\tSegement type:\t" . $segment->Type . "\n";
print "\tIs complement?:\t" . $segment->IsComplement . "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Create a feature to and add it to the sequence.
my $feature =
Sdm::Feature::CreateCustomFeature( 'Cysteine residues', $location );
$feature->AddQualifier("KeyName", 'Example feature qualifier');
$sequence->AddFeature($feature);

print 'The feature key name is ' . $feature->Key . "\n";
```

### Using the Shell property

my $integerValue = $object->Shell;

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use of unsatisfied non-bonds.
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "3fzm.pdb" );
die "Failed to create a valid MDM document!" unless $document;

my $ligandNonbondMonitor =
$document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor(
{RequirePredefinedLigand=>False});

$document->FocusOnFirstLigand;
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
$ligandNonbondMonitor->IsNonbondTypeShown(Mdm::nonInteracting) = True;

for (my $index = 0; $index < 3; ++$index)
{
my $unsatisfiedNonbonds = $ligandNonbondMonitor->UnsatisfiedNonbonds;

printf "Shell: %d\n", $ligandNonbondMonitor->Shell;
foreach my $unsatisfied (@$unsatisfiedNonbonds)
{
printf "Unsatisfied interaction on atom %s of type(s) %s\n", 
$unsatisfied->Name, $unsatisfied->ChemistryName;
}

$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
}
```

# Show function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/show_function.htm

## Show function

### Description

Show makes the selected objects visible.

### Applies to

The Show function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the Show function

#### Command

$object->Show();

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to show and hide objects in an Mdm::Document.
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

# This example assumes the atoms are visible and their display style
# is not set to Mdm::styleAtomNone.
print "Make sure that visible atoms are displayed.\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleAtomStick);

print "Initially hide all objects.\n";
$document->HideAll();
sleep(1);

print 'Select and show backbone atoms and bonds. ';
print "All other objects remain hidden...\n";
SelectByString( $document, ':C,CA,N,O,HN,HA' );
$document->Show();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

print 'Hide the selected backbone atoms and bonds. ';
print "All other objects remain shown...\n";
$document->ShowAll();
$document->Hide();
sleep(3);

print "Show selected atoms and hide unselected...\n";
$document->ShowAll();
$document->ShowOnly();
sleep(3);

print "Show everything within 5 angstroms of the ligand...\n";
$document->DeselectAll();
$document->Hide();
my $ligand = $document->Chains->Item(2);
$ligand->Select();

# ShowByRadius considers only molecules which are marked as visible.
# Use ShowOnly to make sure any molecule containing the selection is visible.
$document->ShowOnly();

$document->ShowByRadius(5.0);
$document->DeselectAll();
$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

### Description

For a molecule with calculated aggregation propensity values at a specified
radius rad, this function colors a solvent accessible surface, Aggregation
Propensity Surface, according to those values. If the surface does not exist, the
function creates it.

### Applies to

The ShowAggregationSurface function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ShowAggregationSurface function

#### Command

$object->ShowAggregationSurface( [radius], [create] );

$object->ShowAggregationSurface( { Radius => [radius], Create => [create] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [create] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [radius] | Optional | 10 | Integer |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1hzh');

#This API calculates solvent accessible areas using the DS Client method and 
#then uses these to calculate aggregation propensities. It should be noted that
#this will not give the same results as the protocol.

# Calculate the Aggregation values 
my $gridNumber = 240;
my $radius = 5;

$document->ProteinAggregationPropensity(
$gridNumber, $radius
);

#Note that if you have precomputed the Solvent Accessible Areas for each atom
#and they are stored in atom property named SAA, then the following may be used
#instead - this is what is done in the Calculate Aggregation Scores protocol 
#which calculates the SAAs using CHARMm
# $document->ProteinAggregationPropensityFromSaa( $radius);

#Now create the patch groups
my $minPeakCutoff = 0.2;
my $minPatchCutoff = 0.0;

$document->FindAggregationSites($radius);

#Now do another radius
$radius=10;
$document->ProteinAggregationPropensity(
$gridNumber, $radius
);
$document->FindAggregationSites($radius);

#create surface colored by aggregation values

$radius=5;
$document->ShowAggregationSurface($radius);

sleep(5);

#now use the API with a different radius - it will recolor the existing
#surface
$radius=10;
$document->ShowAggregationSurface($radius);

my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
printf "Aggregation 5A : %.4f\n", $molecule->GetProperty("Aggr R5");
printf "Aggregation 10A : %.4f\n", $molecule->GetProperty("Aggr R10");
printf "Total Solvent Accessibility %.1f\n", $molecule->GetProperty("Total Solvent Accessibility");
```

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to show and hide objects in an Mdm::Document.
use strict;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

# This example assumes the atoms are visible and their display style
# is not set to Mdm::styleAtomNone.
print "Make sure that visible atoms are displayed.\n";
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle(Mdm::styleAtomStick);

print "Initially hide all objects.\n";
$document->HideAll();
sleep(1);

print 'Select and show backbone atoms and bonds. ';
print "All other objects remain hidden...\n";
SelectByString( $document, ':C,CA,N,O,HN,HA' );
$document->Show();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

print 'Hide the selected backbone atoms and bonds. ';
print "All other objects remain shown...\n";
$document->ShowAll();
$document->Hide();
sleep(3);

print "Show selected atoms and hide unselected...\n";
$document->ShowAll();
$document->ShowOnly();
sleep(3);

print "Show everything within 5 angstroms of the ligand...\n";
$document->DeselectAll();
$document->Hide();
my $ligand = $document->Chains->Item(2);
$ligand->Select();

# ShowByRadius considers only molecules which are marked as visible.
# Use ShowOnly to make sure any molecule containing the selection is visible.
$document->ShowOnly();

$document->ShowByRadius(5.0);
$document->DeselectAll();
$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# ShowAllNonbonds function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/showallnonbonds_function.htm

## ShowAllNonbonds function

### Description

ShowAllNonbonds makes all the non-bonds of an Mdm::NonbondMonitor object visible.
By default this function will hide any displayed distance labels.
An optional argument, ShowDistanceLabels, is available to
show distance labels.

### Applies to

The ShowAllNonbonds function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor , Mdm::NonbondMonitor

### Using the ShowAllNonbonds function

#### Instance

$object->ShowAllNonbonds( [showdistancelabels] );

$object->ShowAllNonbonds( { ShowDistanceLabels => [showdistancelabels] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [showdistancelabels] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::LigandNonbondMonitor Mdm::NonbondMonitor |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to use the create a ligand non-bond monitor, 
# browse ligands and show supporting non-bond interactions. 

use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use strict;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('2FL6');
die "Failed to create a valid MDM document!" unless $document;

my $receptor = $document->ReceptorInFocus;
die "The open document does not have a defined receptor!" unless $receptor;

$document->FocusOnFirstLigand;
my $ligand = $document->LigandInFocus;
die "The open document does not have a defined ligand!" unless $ligand;

my $ligandNonbondMonitor =
$document->CreateLigandNonbondMonitor();
$document->UpdateViews();

my $nonbondMonitors = $document->NonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d NonbondMonitors.\n", $nonbondMonitors->Count;
my $ligandNonbondMonitors = $document->LigandNonbondMonitors;
printf "Document contains %d LigandNonbondMonitors.\n", $ligandNonbondMonitors->Count;

# Step through the ligands
while ($document->FocusOnNextLigand())
{
sleep(2);
}

# Step through the ligands backwards
$document->FocusOnLastLigand();
while ($document->FocusOnPreviousLigand())
{
sleep(2);
}

# Expand shell to progressively view supporting interactions.
$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

$ligandNonbondMonitor->ExpandShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

# Contract shell to hide supporting interactions.
$ligandNonbondMonitor->ContractShell();
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

print "Done\n";
```

$object->ShowAnnotations( <index> );

| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::Document |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Example for
# Function Sdm::Document::ShowAnnotations
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
$sdmDocument->Alignment->DeleteSequence(0);
printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$sdmDocument->SequenceCount; 

$sdmDocument->CreateSequence( 'Seq1', 'ASDFGHJK' );
printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$sdmDocument->SequenceCount; 

$sdmDocument->CreateSequence( 'Seq2', 'LKJHGFDSAASDFGHJK' );
printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$sdmDocument->SequenceCount; 

# Open sequence annotation window (client only).
$sdmDocument->ShowAnnotations(0);

$sdmDocument->ShowAnnotations(1);
printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$sdmDocument->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $sdmDocument->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $sdmDocument->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```
