# ShowDockedProteins function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/showdockedproteins_function.htm

## ShowDockedProteins function

### Description

ShowDockedProteins shows the full structure of a docked protein pose.
A copy of the ligand protein is added to the document.

The function is typically applied to the output of the Protein Docking protocols.
To run the example below, such a document should be loaded. Alternatively, the
example script for the Mdm::ProteinPose can be executed to generate
a small set of example data.

### Applies to

The ShowDockedProteins function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ShowDockedProteins function

#### Instance

$object->ShowDockedProteins( <pose> );

$object->ShowDockedProteins( { Pose => <pose> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <pose> | Required | | Mdm::ProteinPose |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing docked protein poses\n";
print " 3 Enter a cluster ID in the Arguments tab\n";
print " 4 Run this script within Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

# The script assume the last active document contains ProteinPoses
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ($document);

# get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter
my $poses = $document->ProteinPoses;
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ( $poses->Count > 0 );

# store the first pose in a variable
my $pose1 = $poses->Item(0);

# generate the full coordinates of the receptor and ligand structures for the pose
$document->ShowDockedProteins($pose1);
```

# ShowHideFeature function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/showhidefeature_function.htm

## ShowHideFeature function

### Description

ShowHideFeature shows or hides the specified query features and/or their associated location spheres.

### Applies to

The ShowHideFeature function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ShowHideFeature function

#### Command

$object->ShowHideFeature( <featuretype>, <visibilitytype>, [showhidelocationsphere] );

$object->ShowHideFeature( { FeatureType => <featuretype>, VisibilityType => <visibilitytype>, ShowHideLocationSphere => [showhidelocationsphere] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <featuretype> | Required | | enum Mdm::FeatureType |
| <visibilitytype> | Required | | enum Mdm::FeatureVisibilityType |
| [showhidelocationsphere] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create some features on the query
# Create a donor feature at 0,0,0
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# Create an acceptor feature at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
sleep(3);

# hide HBA
$document->ShowHideFeature( 'acceptorFeature', 'hideFeature' );
sleep(3);

# show HBA and hide HBD
$document->ShowHideFeature( 'acceptorFeature', 'showFeature' );
$document->ShowHideFeature( 'donorFeature', 'hideFeature' );
sleep(3);

# show all
$document->ShowHideFeature( 'donorFeature', 'showFeature' );
```

# ShowHydrogenAtoms function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/showhydrogenatoms_function.htm

## ShowHydrogenAtoms function

### Description

ShowHydrogenAtoms shows hydrogen atoms ( Mdm::Atom ) connected to the selected atoms.

### Applies to

The ShowHydrogenAtoms function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the ShowHydrogenAtoms function

#### Instance

$object->ShowHydrogenAtoms( [hydrogenset] );

$object->ShowHydrogenAtoms( { HydrogenSet => [hydrogenset] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [hydrogenset] | Optional | allHydrogenAtoms | enum Mdm::HydrogenSet |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate functions to manipulate hydrogen atoms.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "1crn.pdb" );

# change display style
$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle( Mdm::styleAtomBallAndStick );
printf "Total Atoms: %d\n" , $document->Atoms->Count;
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;

# Add all missing hydrogen atoms.
$document->AddHydrogenAtoms( Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms, True );
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Remove any non-polar hydrogen atoms.
$document->RemoveHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::nonEssentialHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Hide the remaining polar hydrogen atoms.
$document->HideHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::essentialHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;

sleep(1);

# Show the all existing hydrogen atoms.
$document->ShowHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Remove hydrogen atoms connected to specified atom.

$document->Atoms->Item(0)->RemoveHydrogens();
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
sleep(1);

# Add chiral hydrogen atoms.
$document->RemoveHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;

$document->AddChiralHydrogenAtoms(Mdm::allHydrogenAtoms);
printf "Hydrogen count: %d\n", $document->FilterByProperty('Atom element=Hydrogen')->Count;
```

| $object | | | Objects listed as Applies to |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates how to work with atomic charges.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
$molecule->Name = 'Nitrous oxide';
my $N1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $N2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::N);
my $O = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

if ( $N1->IsHeteroAtom() )
{
print "$N1->{Name} is a hetero atom.\n";
}

# Charge N2 +1 and O -1.
$N2->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( 1, 1 );
$O->FormalCharge = Mdm::Rational::Create( -1, 1 );

my $bond = $document->CreateBond( $N1, $N2 );
$bond->BondType = Mdm::tripleBond;
$document->CreateBond( $N2, $O );

my $attached = $N1->AttachedAtom(0);
$document->Clean(50);

print "Bond between $N1->{Name} and $N2->{Name}: \n";
print "Bond order: $bond->{BondOrder}\n";
print "Bond length: $bond->{Length}\n";
print "NN("
. $N2->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")O("
. $O->FormalCharge->Numerator . ")\n";

# Calculates partial charges.
$document->CalculateCharges();

# Changes N2's partial charge.
$N2->Charge = 0.3;

# Selects O and changes its formal charge.
$O->Select();
$document->ChangeFormalCharge( 1, 1 );

# Calculates the sum of formal and partial charges.
my $formalSum = $molecule->FormalChargeSum();
my $partialSum = $molecule->PartialChargeSum();

$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "FormalChargeSum", $formalSum );
$molecule->SetPropertyAsReal( "PartialChargeSum", $partialSum );

$molecule->HideProperty("PartialChargeSum");
$molecule->ShowProperty("PartialChargeSum");
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w

use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Creates an empty molecule

# Create oxygen atoms
my $O1 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);
my $O2 = $molecule->CreateAtom(Mdm::O);

# Assign coordinates to atoms
my $xyz1 = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O1->XYZ = $xyz1;

my $xyz2 = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.6, 0.0, 0.0 );
$O2->XYZ = $xyz2;

# Create Spheres centered on atom position
my $sphere1 = $O1->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz1, Radius => 0.4 } );
my $sphere2 = $O2->CreateSphere( { XYZ => $xyz2, Radius => 0.4 } );

# Create Cylinder
my $cylinder =
$O1->CreateCylinder( { Begin => $xyz1, End => $xyz2, Radius => 0.2 } );
my $bottom = $cylinder->{BottomCenter};
printf "Cylinder bottom center: %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n Radius: %8.3f\n",
$bottom->X, $bottom->Y, $bottom->Z, $cylinder->Radius;

# Make cylinder transparent
$cylinder->IsTransparent(True);

# Create a slicing plane perpendicular to the cylinder axis
my $atoms = $document->Atoms;
my $slicingplaneObject = $document->CreateSlicingPlane(
{
Index => 1,
ArrayOfObjects => $atoms,
Origin => Mdm::Point::Create( 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 ),
Normal => Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 0.0, 0.0 )
}
);

# Get all 3D Objects
my $objects3d = $document->Geometric3ds;

# Print their name and class name
foreach my $object (@$objects3d)
{
print $object->ClassName . "\t" . $object->Name . "\n";
}

# Get all slicing planes
my $slicplanes = $document->SlicingPlanes;
print "Number of slicing planes" . $slicplanes->Count. "\n";
```

# SolventAccessibleSurface function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/solventaccessiblesurface_function.htm

## SolventAccessibleSurface function

### Description

SolventAccessibleSurface determines which amino acid residues are exposed to solvent,
and which amino acid residues are buried. Exposed and buried residues can be colored.
The cutoffs are defined with respect to the percentage of the actual relative to the
maximum possible solvent accessible surface area.

### Applies to

The SolventAccessibleSurface function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SolventAccessibleSurface function

#### Command

$object->SolventAccessibleSurface( [gridnumber], [proberadius], [createsubsets], [colorburiedobjects], [buriedobjectscolor], [buriedcutoff], [colorexposedobjects], [exposedobjectscolor], [exposedcutoff], [contextselected], [intermolecular] );

$object->SolventAccessibleSurface( { GridNumber => [gridnumber], ProbeRadius => [proberadius], CreateSubsets => [createsubsets], ColorBuriedObjects => [colorburiedobjects], BuriedObjectsColor => [buriedobjectscolor], BuriedCutOff => [buriedcutoff], ColorExposedObjects => [colorexposedobjects], ExposedObjectsColor => [exposedobjectscolor], ExposedCutOff => [exposedcutoff], ContextSelected => [contextselected], Intermolecular => [intermolecular] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [buriedcutoff] | Optional | 10.0 | Real |
| [buriedobjectscolor] | Optional | DiscoveryScript::Color::Create(0, 255, 0) | DiscoveryScript::Color |
| [colorburiedobjects] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [colorexposedobjects] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [contextselected] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [createsubsets] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [exposedcutoff] | Optional | 75.0 | Real |
| [exposedobjectscolor] | Optional | DiscoveryScript::Color::Create(0, 0, 255) | DiscoveryScript::Color |
| [gridnumber] | Optional | 20 | Integer |
| [intermolecular] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [proberadius] | Optional | 1.4 | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
#
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1crn');

# Calculate the solvent accessible surface per residue
# (also calculates % SAS and sidechain SAS).
my $gridNumber = 20;
my $probeRadius = 1.4;
my $createSubsets = True;
my $colorBuriedObjects = True;
my $buriedColor = Mdm::Color::Create( 255, 0, 0 );
my $buriedCutoff = 40.0;
my $colorExposedObjects = True;
my $exposedColor = Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 0 );
my $exposedCutoff = 60.0;

$document->SolventAccessibleSurface(
$gridNumber, $probeRadius, $createSubsets,
$colorBuriedObjects, $buriedColor, $buriedCutoff,
$colorExposedObjects, $exposedColor, $exposedCutoff
);

# create an array of all aminoacids in the system
my $aminoAcids = $document->AminoAcids;

# Loop over array of aminoacids.
foreach my $aminoacid (@$aminoAcids)
{

# retrieve the residue name
my $aminoAcidName = $aminoacid->Name;

# retrieve the Residue Solvent Accessibility
my $sas = $aminoacid->GetProperty('Residue Solvent Accessibility');
if ( $sas > 30 )
{
print "$aminoAcidName : $sas\n";
}
}
```

# SpecialPositionTolerance property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/specialpositiontolerance_property.htm

## SpecialPositionTolerance property

### Description

SpecialPositionTolerance specifies the largest distance (in angstroms) below which a 3D point
and its symmetry image in a 3D Cell are considered identical. In this case, the 3D point is
said to lie on a special position. If no symmetry image falls within this distance threshold,
the 3D point is said to lie on a general position.

### Applies to

The SpecialPositionTolerance property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Cell

MdmDiscoveryScript

# SplitChain function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/splitchain_function.htm

## SplitChain function

### Description

Splits a chain before the specified residue. The new chain will be of the same type as the original parent chain (AminoAcidChain, NucleicAcidChain or generic Chain) and will have the same label. If the residues either side of the break point are amino acids, then the peptide bond will be removed and the residues adjusted to neutral C-terminal and N-terminal chemistry.

### Applies to

The SplitChain function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SplitChain function

#### Command

$object->SplitChain( <firstresidueofnewchain> );

$object->SplitChain( { FirstResidueOfNewChain => <firstresidueofnewchain> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <firstresidueofnewchain> | Required | | Mdm::Residue |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
# Demonstrates the use of the SwapChainOrder, MergeChains and SplitChain
# functions.
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;

#Note - this script should be run from DS client 

# subroutine to print information about the structure
sub PrintInfo($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
printf( " Number of molecules %d\n", $molecules->Count );
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $molecules->Count ; ++$index )
{
my $molecule = $molecules->Item($index);
printf( " molecule number %d name %s\n",
$index + 1, $molecule->Name );
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
for ( my $index2 = 0 ; $index2 < $chains->Count ; ++$index2 )
{
my $chain = $chains->Item($index2);
printf(
" chain number %d name %s number of residues %d\n",
$index2 + 1,
$chain->Name, $chain->Residues->Count
);
}
}
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4ins.pdb" );

$document->InvokeAction('ActionViewHierarchy');

print("Before swap:\n");
PrintInfo($document);

$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

my $chains = $document->Chains();

$document->SwapChainOrder($chains->Item(0),$chains->Item(1));

print("after swap 1 and 2:\n");
PrintInfo($document);
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

$document->MergeChains($chains->Item(3),$chains->Item(2));

print ("after merge 3 and 4:\n");
PrintInfo($document);
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

my $chainsNow = $document->Chains();
my $residues = $chainsNow->Item(0)->Residues();

#find a residue somewhere in the middle of the first chain
my $numRes = $residues->Count();
my $breakRes = $residues->Item( int($numRes/2) );

$document->SplitChain($breakRes);

print("After splitting chain 1:\n");

PrintInfo($document);

print("You should now have amino acid chains B,B,A,C with the ion/water chains unaffected.\n");

# update view
$document->UpdateViews();
```

Sdm::AminoAcidSequence , Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence , Sdm::Sequence

### Using the SplitFeature function

#### Instance

$object->SplitFeature( <feature> );

$object->SplitFeature( { Feature => <feature> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <feature> | Required | | Sdm::Feature |
| $object | | | Sdm::AminoAcidSequence Sdm::NucleicAcidSequence Sdm::Sequence |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to split and join sequence features.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateFromSequenceId('1CRN_A');

my $sequence = $document->Sequence(0);
my $count = $sequence->FeatureCount;

my $secStrFeature;
my $i = $count;
while ( $i > 0 )
{
--$i;
my $feature = $sequence->Feature($i);
if ( $feature->Key eq "SecStr" )
{
if ( !$secStrFeature )
{
$secStrFeature = $feature;
}
else
{
$secStrFeature =
$sequence->JoinFeatures( $secStrFeature, $feature );
}
}
}

$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(5);

$sequence->SplitFeature($secStrFeature);

printf "sequence count: %3d\n",$document->SequenceCount; 
my $index = 0;
while ( $index < $document->SequenceCount )
{
my $sequence = $document->Sequence($index);

print 'Sequence: ' . ++$index . "\t";
print 'Name: "' . $sequence->Name . "\"\n\t";
print 'Description: "' . $sequence->Description . "\"\n\t";
print 'Locus: "' . $sequence->Locus . "\"\n\t";
print 'Gene name: "' . $sequence->GeneName . "\"\n\t";
print 'Residues: ', $sequence->SequenceString . "\n";
}
```

# SplitProtein function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/splitprotein_function.htm

## SplitProtein function

### Description

SplitProtein splits a protein structure into different molecules.
Can be used to separate chains, or protein from ligand etc.

### Applies to

The SplitProtein function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SplitProtein function

#### Instance

$object->SplitProtein( [movenonprotein], [keepcell], [keepbondedchains], [keepmatchingchainnames] );

$object->SplitProtein( { MoveNonProtein => [movenonprotein], KeepCell => [keepcell], KeepBondedChains => [keepbondedchains], KeepMatchingChainNames => [keepmatchingchainnames] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [keepbondedchains] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [keepcell] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| [keepmatchingchainnames] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [movenonprotein] | Optional | True | Boolean |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# subroutine to print information about the structure
sub PrintInfo($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
printf( " Number of molecules %d\n", $molecules->Count );
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $molecules->Count ; ++$index )
{
my $molecule = $molecules->Item($index);
printf( " molecule number %d name %s\n",
$index + 1, $molecule->Name );
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
for ( my $index2 = 0 ; $index2 < $chains->Count ; ++$index2 )
{
my $chain = $chains->Item($index2);
printf(
" chain number %d name %s number of residues %d\n",
$index2 + 1,
$chain->Name, $chain->Residues->Count
);
}
}
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4ins.pdb" );

print("Before split:\n");
PrintInfo($document);

$document->SplitProtein;

print("After default split:\n");
PrintInfo($document);

# reload and use some different options
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4ins.pdb" );
$document->SplitProtein(
{
MoveNonProtein => False,
KeepBondedChains => True
}
);
printf("After split with MoveNonProtein only False\n");
PrintInfo($document);

# reload and use some different options
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4ins.pdb" );
$document->SplitProtein(
{
MoveNonProtein => False,
KeepBondedChains => False
}
);
printf(
"After split with MoveNonProtein only False and KeepBondedChains false\n"
);
PrintInfo($document);

# update view
$document->UpdateViews();
```

# SplitTransmembraneSegments function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/splittransmembranesegments_function.htm

## SplitTransmembraneSegments function

### Description

SplitTransmembraneSegments splits the transmembrane segments of a protein into separate chains. The transmembrane segments
are the residues provided in the ArrayOfTransmembraneResidues parameter. The data for this
parameter can be generated using the TransmembraneResidues . Any residues
not listed in the ArrayOfTransmembraneResidues parameters will be removed.
The following parameters are available:

* Protein specifies the membrane protein.

* Membrane specifies the implicit membrane.

* ArrayOfTransmembraneResidues specifies the set of residues inside the membrane.

### Applies to

The SplitTransmembraneSegments function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SplitTransmembraneSegments function

#### Instance

$object->SplitTransmembraneSegments( <protein>, <membrane>, <arrayoftransmembraneresidues> );

$object->SplitTransmembraneSegments( { Protein => <protein>, Membrane => <membrane>, ArrayOfTransmembraneResidues => <arrayoftransmembraneresidues> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <arrayoftransmembraneresidues> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| <membrane> | Required | | Mdm::Membrane |
| <protein> | Required | | Mdm::Molecule |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate creation, placement and orientation of a membrane.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

# Remove all chains except the first.
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

my $membrane = $document->AddAndOrientMembrane($molecule);
$membrane->Select();

my $atoms = $molecule->Atoms();
my $membraneOrientation =
$molecule->CreateMembraneOrientationMonitor( $membrane, $atoms,
Mdm::objectCentered, Mdm::referenceAxisZ );

print "Original membrane position:\n";
my $shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
my $tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
my $rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);

print "Modified membrane position:\n";
$document->SetMembraneOrientation( $atoms, $membrane, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 );
$shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
$tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
$rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);

print "Modified membrane position:\n";
$document->SetMembraneOrientation( $atoms, $membrane, 10.0, 30.0, 90.0 );
$shift = $membraneOrientation->MembraneShift();
$tilt = $membraneOrientation->MembraneTilt();
$rotation = $membraneOrientation->MembraneRotation();
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "shift", $shift);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "tilt", $tilt);
printf(" %-10s: %.4f\n", "rotation", $rotation);

my $transmembraneResidues =
$document->TransmembraneResidues( $molecule, $membrane );
$document->SplitTransmembraneSegments( $molecule, $membrane,
$transmembraneResidues );

foreach my $residue (@$transmembraneResidues)
{
$residue->Select();
}
```

Source type: HTML

## SsType property

### Description

SsType specifies the enum Sdm::SsType for a given sequence residue index.

### Applies to

The SsType property can be used with the following objects:

Sdm::SecondaryStructure

### Using the SsType property

#### Get

my $sstypeEnum = $object->SsType( <index> );

my $sstypeEnum = $object->SsType( { Index => <index> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $sstypeEnum | | | enum Sdm::SsType |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| $object | | | Sdm::SecondaryStructure |

#### Set

$object->SsType = <index>, <sstype>;

$object->SsType( <index>, <sstype> );

$object->SsType( { Index => <index>, SsType => <sstype> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <index> | Required | | Integer |
| <sstype> | Required | | enum Sdm::SsType |
| $object | | | Sdm::SecondaryStructure |

#### Defined by

SdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to predict and retrieve secondary structure.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );

my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

my $sequence =
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( $mdmDocument->Molecules->[0] );
$alignment->PredictSecondaryStructureByDsc();

# Example accessing the secondary structure string from sequence property.
my $kabschAndSander =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructure(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType);
print "Kabsch and Sander secondary structure:\n";
print "Encoded: $kabschAndSander\n";

# Ensure alignment is displaying secondary structure.
if ( !( $alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown ) )
{
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureShown = True;
}

# Ensure KAS is displayed
$alignment->IsSecondaryStructureVisible(Sdm::kasSecondaryStructureType) =
True;

# Example accessing the secondary structure data from object.
print "DSC secondary structure:\n";
my $ssObject =
$sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructureObject(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);

print 'Predictor: ' . $ssObject->Predictor . "\n";
print 'Has probabilities: ' . $ssObject->IsPredicted . "\n";

my $dsc = $ssObject->SecondaryStructureString;
print "Encoded: $dsc\n";

my $propensity =
$sequence
->ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity(Sdm::dscSecondaryStructureType);
print "Propensity: $propensity\n";

my $helicalResidueCount = 0;
my $sheetResidueCount = 0;
my $coilResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $ssObject->ResidueCount;
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $ssObject->SsType($i);
++$helicalResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$sheetResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::sheet || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
++$coilResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::coil || $type eq Sdm::extracellular );
}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print 'Analysis: The DSC secondary structure for this sequence has '
. $helicalResidueCount
. ' amino acid residues in helical formations, '
. $sheetResidueCount
. ' in sheet formations and '
. $coilResidueCount
. " in coil formations.\n";

my $secstrucfilter = $sdmDocument->SecondaryStructures;
print "Number of secondary Structures: ", $secstrucfilter->Count . "\n";
```

#### Defined by

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to predict and retrieve transmembrane predictions.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

# Load structure of BOVINE RHODOPSIN, 1f88 and keep only first chain
my $mdmDocument = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');
my $molecule = $mdmDocument->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$mdmDocument->DeleteObjects();

# Access the amino acid sequence of 1f88 and predict transmembrane helices
my $sdmDocument = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $sdmDocument->Alignment;

my $sequence =
$sdmDocument->CreateSequenceFromMolecule( $mdmDocument->Molecules->[0] );

$alignment->PredictTransmembraneSecondaryStructure();

# Example accessing the transmembrane prediction from sequence property.
my $tmObject =
$sequence
->ProteinSecondaryStructureObject(Sdm::transmembraneSecondaryStructureType);

print 'Predictor: ' . $tmObject->Predictor . "\n";
print 'Has probabilities: ' . $tmObject->IsPredicted . "\n";

my $tmStr = $tmObject->SecondaryStructureString;
print "Encoded: $tmStr\n\n";

my $propensity = $sequence->ProteinSecondaryStructurePropensity
(Sdm::transmembraneSecondaryStructureType);
print "Propensity: $propensity\n\n";

my $membraneResidueCount = 0;
my $nonmembraneResidueCount = 0;
my $residueCount = $tmObject->ResidueCount;

print "Probabilities:\n";
print "index\tHelical\tInside\tOutside\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
my $type = $tmObject->SsType($i);
++$membraneResidueCount if ( $type eq Sdm::helical );
++$nonmembraneResidueCount
if ( $type eq Sdm::extracellular || $type eq Sdm::cytosol );
my $pHelical = $tmObject->SsTypeProbability( $i, Sdm::helical );
my $pInside = $tmObject->SsTypeProbability( $i, Sdm::cytosol );
my $pOutside = $tmObject->SsTypeProbability( $i, Sdm::extracellular );
printf "$i\t%3.2f\t%3.2f\t%3.2f\n", $pHelical, $pInside, $pOutside;

}

$sdmDocument->UpdateViews();

print "\n\n"
. "Analysis: The TRANSMEM prediction for this sequence suggests that\n "
. $membraneResidueCount
. " amino acid residues belong to a transmembrane helix and\n "
. $nonmembraneResidueCount
. " amino acids are outside the transmembrane helices.\n";
```

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Example for DockedProteinPoseAssembly Properties
# NOTE: This script MUST be run from the DS client
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

sub Usage($)
{
my $message = $@;
print "$message\n";
print "To run this script\n";
print " 1 Start Discovery Studio\n";
print " 2 Open a Molecule Window containing docked protein poses\n";
print " 3 Enter a cluster ID in the Arguments tab\n";
print " 4 Run this script within Discovery Studio\n";
exit;
}

# Check that script is being run from within Discovery Studio
Usage("This example script is intended to run inside Discovery Studio")
unless ( !DiscoveryScript::IsStandalone() );

# This example script assumes the last active document contains Docked Protein Poses
my $document = DiscoveryScript::LastActiveDocument(MdmModelType);
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ($document);

# get the array of protein poses using the ProteinPoses Filter
my $poseGroups = $document->DockedProteinPoseAssemblies;
Usage(
"This example requires an open Molecule Window containing docked protein poses"
) unless ( $poseGroups->Count > 0 );

# store the first pose group in a variable
# Note: there should be only one pose group object in a document
my $poseGroup = $poseGroups->Item(0);

# Get the receptor for the docked pose group
my $receptor = $poseGroup->Receptor;

# Copy receptor center into a point variable
my $receptorCenter = $poseGroup->ReceptorCenter;

# Print information
print "Receptor " . $receptor->Name . ",";
printf "is centered at coordinates (%5.2f,%5.2f,%5.2f)\n",
$receptorCenter->X, $receptorCenter->Y,
$receptorCenter->Z;

# Color receptor red
print "Coloring receptor red....\n\n";
$receptor->Select();
$document->SetColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 255, 0, 0 ) );

# Get the ligand for the docked pose group
my $ligand = $poseGroup->Ligand;

# Copy receptor center into a point variable
my $receptorCenter = $poseGroup->LigandCenter;
print "ligand " . $ligand->Name . ",";
printf "is centered at coordinates (%5.2f,%5.2f,%5.2f)\n",
$receptorCenter->X, $receptorCenter->Y,
$receptorCenter->Z;

# Color receptor blue
$ligand->Select();
print "Coloring ligand blue....\n\n";
$document->SetColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 0, 255 ) );

# Get the ligand for the docked pose group
my $angle = $poseGroup->StartingAngles;
printf "Starting angles used for docking: %5.2f\t%5.2f\t%5.2f\n", $angle->X,
$angle->Y, $angle->Z;
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrates several properties and functions of the
# Sdm::Segment class.
use strict;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Sdm::Document::CreateProteinDocument();
my $alignment = $document->Alignment;
my $sequence =
$document->CreateSequence( 'SequenceName', 'ASCDFACSGHACSJCKLA' );

# Create a location consisting of all cysteine residues.
print "Creating location for all cysteine residues\n";
my $location = Sdm::Location::Create(Sdm::locationTypeJoin);

my $sequenceString = $sequence->SequenceString;
my $residueCount = length($sequenceString);
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $residueCount ; ++$i )
{
if ( substr( $sequenceString, $i, 1 ) eq 'C' )
{
my $segment = Sdm::Segment::Create( $i, $i );
$location->AddSegment($segment);
}
}

my $segmentCount = $location->SegmentCount;
print "Location has $segmentCount segments\n";
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $segmentCount ; ++$index )
{
my $segment = $location->Segment($index);

print "\tEnd position:\t" . $segment->EndPosition . "\n";
print "\tSegement type:\t" . $segment->Type . "\n";
print "\tIs complement?:\t" . $segment->IsComplement . "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Create a feature to and add it to the sequence.
my $feature =
Sdm::Feature::CreateCustomFeature( 'Cysteine residues', $location );
$feature->AddQualifier("KeyName", 'Example feature qualifier');
$sequence->AddFeature($feature);

print 'The feature key name is ' . $feature->Key . "\n";
```

# State property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/state_property.htm

## State property

### Description

State is an enum Protocol::State specifying the run state of a Protocol::Task .
Note that both successful and failed protocols return Protocol::taskComplete.
To determine if a protocol is successful, use the IsProtocolSuccessful property.

### Applies to

The State property can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Task

### Using the State property

#### Get

my $stateEnum = $object->State;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stateEnum | | | enum Protocol::State |
| $object | | | Protocol::Task |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

## SumSquares property

### Description

SumSquares calculates the sum of a point's squared coordinates.

### Applies to

The SumSquares property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Point2d , Mdm::Point

### Using the SumSquares property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->SumSquares;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Point2d Mdm::Point |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to use the Mdm::Point objects.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

# Working with 2D points.
my $xy1 = Mdm::Point2d::Create( -1.0, -1.0 );
my $xy2 = Mdm::Point2d::Create( 1.0, 1.0 );

print "Point1 is: (" . $xy1->X . "," . $xy1->Y . ")\n";
print "Point2 is: (" . $xy2->X . "," . $xy2->Y . ")\n";
print "Sum of squares of Point1 is: " . $xy1->SumSquares . "\n";

my $distance = $xy1->CalculateDistance($xy2);
print "The distance between these points is: $distance\n";

print "The dot product between points is: "
. $xy1->CalculateDotProduct($xy2) . "\n";

$xy1->SetXY( 2.0, 2.0 );
print "Changing Point1 to: (" . $xy1->X . "," . $xy1->Y . ")\n\n";

# Working with 3D points.
my $xyz = Mdm::Point::Create( 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 );
print "Creating 3D point with value: ("
. $xyz->X . ","
. $xyz->Y . ","
. $xyz->Z . ")\n";

$xyz->SetXYZ( 0.0, 1.0, 2.0 );
print "Changing 3D point to: ("
. $xyz->X . ","
. $xyz->Y . ","
. $xyz->Z . ")\n";
```

# SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/superimposebycalphapairs_function.htm

## SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs function

### Description

SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs superimposes one or more protein structures onto a reference protein. The function has two required arguments specifying the molecules and a CAlphaMonitor object. The first array contains Mdm::Molecule objects, starting with the reference protein. The CAlphaMonitor object defines the pairs of C-Alpha atoms in different proteins within a cutoff distance (default 2.5 Å). These are used to determine the matching pairs for superimposition.

An optional argument allows you to specify how to superimpose proteins (i.e., by C-alpha, backbone, or all heavy atoms). When superimposing by all heavy atoms, this function uses/matches heavy atoms with the same atom name for each pair of residues. Other atoms are ignored.

### Applies to

The SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs function

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( <arrayofmolecules>, <calphamonitor>, [type], [matrixname] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( { ArrayOfMolecules => <arrayofmolecules>, CAlphaMonitor => <calphamonitor>, Type => [type], MatrixName => [matrixname] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <arrayofmolecules> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| <calphamonitor> | Required | | Mdm::CAlphaMonitor |
| [matrixname] | Optional | "NCS" | String |
| [type] | Optional | superimposeProteinUsingBackboneAtoms | enum Mdm::SuperimposeProteinAtomType |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use superimposition functions
# and RMSD calculation functions for amino acids.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load 2rcs (an unligated antibody) from PDB.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '2rcs.pdb' );

# Load 1aj7 (a ligated antibody having the same sequence as 2crs) from PDB.
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

my $molecule2rcs = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[1];

my $hv2rcs = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 2rcs H chain V domain
my $hv1aj7 = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 1aj7 H chain V domain

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $molecule2rcs->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv2rcs->AddItem($aminoAcid);

$aminoAcid = $molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv1aj7->AddItem($aminoAcid);
}

# Show the transformation matrix which would superimpose the Vh
# domains by C-alpha atoms. This does not alter the coordinates
# of either structure.
my $matrix = $document->GetSuperimposeProteinMatrix( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
print "Transformation matrix:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 4 ; ++$i )
{
print "\t";
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < 4 ; ++$j )
{
printf "%.3f ", $matrix->GetEntry( $i, $j );
}
print "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms
my $rmsd = $document->SuperimposeProtein( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
printf "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms: %.3f\n\n", $rmsd;

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD. Note that by default the functions return an
# array of per-residue RMSD values, finishing with the overall RMSD
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it in which case the value will be zero. This can happen
# for unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation
# only for selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the
# required atoms for the requested type of calculation. 
# If you do not want per-residue RMSDs, set the 4th parameter ResidueReport
# False. In this case the array will only contain the overall RMSD.
# In this example, the all protein rmsd has no residue values calculated
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True, False );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item(0);
print "\n";

#Show that the all protein array contains just the overall RMSD.
printf "Number of values returned for all protein is %d\n", $apRmsd->Count();

# Demonstrating that the array is for all residues plus overall value not
# just selected and that as the first chain(L) is unselected its values
# are 0.
printf "Number of values returned for sidechains is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0), $scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

#Create a C-Alpha monitor
my $caMonitor = $document->CreateCAlphaMonitor();

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs before superimposing.\n";
if ($cAlphaPairs->Count > 0) {
printf "The first C-alpha to C-alpha pair distance is %.3f Angstroms.\n",
$cAlphaPairs->Item(0)->Distance;
}

#Lets do it for all matching atoms just to show the argument
my $rmsdByCA =
$document->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( $document->Molecules(), $caMonitor,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingAllAtoms );

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs after superimposing.\n";

#The values returned are like for Superimpose By Alignment - the first value
# is ref-ref (ie 0) then ref-mover for each superimposed molecule.
my $numVal = $rmsdByCA->Count();
printf( "Number of values returned for SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs %d\n",
$numVal );
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $numVal ; ++$i )
{
printf( "RMSD %d is %f\n", $i, $rmsdByCA->[$i] );
}

# use the filter function to retrieve the CAlpha atoms
my $cAlphaMonitors = $document->CAlphaMonitors;
foreach my $m (@$cAlphaMonitors)
{
print $m->ClassName ." filter entries: " . $m->CAlphaPairs->Count. "\n";
}

print "Finished Superimpose Script Example\n";
```

# SuperimposeProtein function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/superimposeprotein_function.htm

## SuperimposeProtein function

### Description

SuperimposeProtein superimposes a pair of proteins by overlaying a contiguous set of residues
from each structure and returns the RMSD between the overlaid sections.

An optional argument allows you to specify how to superimpose proteins
(i.e., by C-alpha, by backbone, or by all heavy atoms)
When superimposing by all heavy atoms, this function uses/matches heavy atoms with the same atom name for each pair of residues. Other atoms are ignored.

### Applies to

The SuperimposeProtein function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SuperimposeProtein function

#### Instance

my $realValue = $object->SuperimposeProtein( <arrayofsuperimposedaminoacids>, <arrayofsuperimposingaminoacids>, [type], [matrixname] );

my $realValue = $object->SuperimposeProtein( { ArrayOfSuperimposedAminoAcids => <arrayofsuperimposedaminoacids>, ArrayOfSuperimposingAminoAcids => <arrayofsuperimposingaminoacids>, Type => [type], MatrixName => [matrixname] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| <arrayofsuperimposedaminoacids> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| <arrayofsuperimposingaminoacids> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| [matrixname] | Optional | "NCS" | String |
| [type] | Optional | superimposeProteinUsingBackboneAtoms | enum Mdm::SuperimposeProteinAtomType |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

```text
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Load 2rcs (an unligated antibody) from PDB.
my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '2rcs.pdb' );

# Load 1aj7 (a ligated antibody having the same sequence as 2crs) from PDB.
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );

$document->SetAtomDisplayStyle({ DisplayStyle=>'styleAtomStick' });

my $molecule2rcs = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[1];

my $hv2rcs = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 2rcs H chain V domain
my $hv1aj7 = Mdm::Array::Create(); # 1aj7 H chain V domain

for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
my $aminoAcid = $molecule2rcs->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv2rcs->AddItem($aminoAcid);

$aminoAcid = $molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i];
$aminoAcid->Select();
$hv1aj7->AddItem($aminoAcid);
}

# Show the transformation matrix which would superimpose the Vh
# domains by C-alpha atoms. This does not alter the coordinates
# of either structure.
my $matrix = $document->GetSuperimposeProteinMatrix( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
print "Transformation matrix:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 4 ; ++$i )
{
print "\t";
for ( my $j = 0 ; $j < 4 ; ++$j )
{
printf "%.3f ", $matrix->GetEntry( $i, $j );
}
print "\n";
}
print "\n";

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms
my $rmsd = $document->SuperimposeProtein( $hv2rcs, $hv1aj7,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms );
printf "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms: %.3f\n\n", $rmsd;

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD. Note that by default the functions return an
# array of per-residue RMSD values, finishing with the overall RMSD
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it in which case the value will be zero. This can happen
# for unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation
# only for selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the
# required atoms for the requested type of calculation. 
# If you do not want per-residue RMSDs, set the 4th parameter ResidueReport
# False. In this case the array will only contain the overall RMSD.
# In this example, the all protein rmsd has no residue values calculated
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinRmsd( $molecule2rcs, $molecule1aj7, True, False );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item(0);
print "\n";

#Show that the all protein array contains just the overall RMSD.
printf "Number of values returned for all protein is %d\n", $apRmsd->Count();

# Demonstrating that the array is for all residues plus overall value not
# just selected and that as the first chain(L) is unselected its values
# are 0.
printf "Number of values returned for sidechains is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0), $scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain %f %f\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

#Create a C-Alpha monitor
my $caMonitor = $document->CreateCAlphaMonitor();

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs before superimposing.\n";
if ($cAlphaPairs->Count > 0) {
printf "The first C-alpha to C-alpha pair distance is %.3f Angstroms.\n",
$cAlphaPairs->Item(0)->Distance;
}

#Lets do it for all matching atoms just to show the argument
my $rmsdByCA =
$document->SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs( $document->Molecules(), $caMonitor,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingAllAtoms );

my $cAlphaPairs = $caMonitor->CAlphaPairs;
print "Found " . $cAlphaPairs ->Count . " C-alpha pairs after superimposing.\n";

#The values returned are like for Superimpose By Alignment - the first value
# is ref-ref (ie 0) then ref-mover for each superimposed molecule.
my $numVal = $rmsdByCA->Count();
printf( "Number of values returned for SuperimposeByCAlphaPairs %d\n",
$numVal );
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $numVal ; ++$i )
{
printf( "RMSD %d is %f\n", $i, $rmsdByCA->[$i] );
}

# use the filter function to retrieve the CAlpha atoms
my $cAlphaMonitors = $document->CAlphaMonitors;
foreach my $m (@$cAlphaMonitors)
{
print $m->ClassName ." filter entries: " . $m->CAlphaPairs->Count. "\n";
}

print "Finished Superimpose Script Example\n";
```

# SuperimposeProteinByAlignment function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/superimposeproteinbyalignment_function.htm

## SuperimposeProteinByAlignment function

### Description

SuperimposeProteinByAlignment superimposes one or more protein structures
which have aligned sequences onto a reference protein. The function has
two required arguments specifying the molecules and corresponding available
sequence alignments to be used. The first array contains Mdm::Molecule objects, starting with the reference protein.
The second array contains the aligned sequence strings, including gaps.
Addition optional arguments allow you to specify how to superimpose proteins
(i.e., by C-alpha, by backbone, or by all heavy atoms), and if only selected amino acids should be
superimposed.

The function returns an array of RMSD values between the reference protein
and all proteins in their specified order. Note the first represents the
reference protein superimposed upon itself which should always be 0.0.

The applied transformation matrix is stored as a property on the superimposed
molecule(s) with a name specified by the last argument. The transformation
matrix can be retrieved from the molecule using the NcsMatrix property.

In the cases to superimpose by all heavy atoms, this function uses/matches heavy atoms with the same atom name for each pair of residues. Other atoms are ignored.

### Applies to

The SuperimposeProteinByAlignment function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SuperimposeProteinByAlignment function

The function can be used as follows:

```text
my $rmsdArray = $document->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment(
$moleculeArray, $sequenceStringArray);
```

#### Instance

my $realarrayObject = $object->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment( <arrayofmolecules>, <arrayofsequences>, [type], [selectedonly], [matrixname] );

my $realarrayObject = $object->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment( { ArrayOfMolecules => <arrayofmolecules>, ArrayOfSequences => <arrayofsequences>, Type => [type], SelectedOnly => [selectedonly], MatrixName => [matrixname] } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realarrayObject | | | DiscoveryScript::RealArray |
| <arrayofmolecules> | Required | | Mdm::Array |
| <arrayofsequences> | Required | | DiscoveryScript::StringArray |
| [matrixname] | Optional | "NCS" | String |
| [selectedonly] | Optional | False | Boolean |
| [type] | Optional | superimposeProteinUsingBackboneAtoms | enum Mdm::SuperimposeProteinAtomType |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# This script demonstrates how to use the SuperimposeProteinByAlignment function.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use SdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

# Open MDM document with 1tgn and 3est.
my $mdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1tgn.pdb' );
$mdmDocument->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '3est.pdb' );

## Create an pir file (AlignedProteins.pir) containing the
## following alignment information for 1tgn and 3est.
## ---------------8<----------------------------------------
open( PIRFILE, '>AlignedProteins.pir' );
print PIRFILE ">P1;1tgn\n";
print PIRFILE "PDB sequence\n";
print PIRFILE
"-VGGYTCGANTVPYQVSLN--SG---YHFCGGSLINSQWVVSAAHCYKSGIQVR--LGEDNINVVEGNEQFISASKSIVHPSYNSNTLNN--DIMLIKLKSAASLNSRVASISLPTSCASAG--TQCLISGWGNTKSSGTSYPDVLKCLKAPILSDSSCKS-AYPGQITSN-MFCAGYLEGGKDSCQGDSGGPVVCSG----KLQGIVSWGS--GCAQKNKPGVYTKVCNYVSWIKQTIASN*\n";
print PIRFILE ">P1;3est\n";
print PIRFILE "PDB sequence\n";
print PIRFILE
"VVGGTEAQRNSWPSQISLQYRSGSSWAHTCGGTLIRQNWVMTAAHCVDRELTFRVVVGEHNLNQNNGTEQYVGVQKIVVHPYWNTDDVAAGYDIALLRLAQSVTLNSYVQLGVLPRAGTILANNSPCYITGWGLTRTNG-QLAQTLQQAYLPTVDYAICSSSSYWGSTVKNSMVCAGGD-GVRSGCQGDSGGPLHCLVNGQYAVHGVTSFVSRLGCNVTRKPTVFTRVSAYISWINNVIASN*\n";
close PIRFILE;
## ---------------8<----------------------------------------

# Load the alignment file and get the aligned sequence data as strings.
my $sdmDocument = DiscoveryScript::Open('AlignedProteins.pir');

my $alignmentStrings = $sdmDocument->Alignment->AlignmentStrings;
die "Incorrect number of sequences. Expected 3 including consensus sequence.\n"
unless ($alignmentStrings->Count == 3);

# Remove the consensus string for input to superimpose method.
$alignmentStrings->DeleteItem(2);

# Superimpose
my $rmsds = $mdmDocument->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment(
$mdmDocument->Molecules,
$alignmentStrings,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms
);

# The return value from the function is an array of RMSDs between each molecule
# and itself. So the one we want to quote here, for the RMSD between 1tgn and
# 1est, is 1 not 0.
my $format = "RMSD = %8.3f\n";
printf $format , $rmsds->[1];
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Demonstrate how to use alignment superimposition functions and
# RMSD calculation functions for amino acids or non-standard residues.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1aj7.pdb' );
$document->InsertFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1gaf.pdb' );

my $molecule1aj7 = $document->Molecules->[0];
my $molecule1gaf = $document->Molecules->[1];

# H chain V domains only
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < 110 ; ++$i )
{
$molecule1aj7->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
$molecule1gaf->Chains->Item(1)->AminoAcids->[$i]->Select();
}

my $Sequence1aj7 = $molecule1aj7->AminoAcidSequence;
my $Sequence1gaf = $molecule1gaf->AminoAcidSequence;
my $sequences = DiscoveryScript::StringArray::Create();
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1aj7);
$sequences->AddItem($Sequence1gaf);

# Superimpose the Vh domains by C-alpha atoms. The function returns an array
# of RMSD values between the reference and all molecules, starting with itself.
my $rmsds =
$document->SuperimposeProteinByAlignment( $document->Molecules, $sequences,
Mdm::superimposeProteinUsingCAlphaAtoms, True );

print "Superimposition Vh domain RMSD by C-alpha atoms:\n";
for ( my $i = 0 ; $i < $document->Molecules->Count() ; ++$i )
{
print "\t"
. $document->Molecules->[$i]->Name . " to "
. $molecule1aj7->Name . ": ";
printf "%.3f\n", $rmsds->[$i];
}
print "\n";

# Calculate Vh domain RMSD
# Note that these functions return an array of real numbers. These are the
# per residue RMSD values plus, in the last element, the overall RMSD.
# A value is returned for each residue even if no calculation was actually
# performed for it (the value will be zero). This can happen for
# unselected residues if you are using the option to do the calculation only for
# selected residues, or if the residue does not contain the required atoms for
# the requested type of calculation.
my $caRmsd =
$document->CalculateCAlphaAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $mcRmsd =
$document->CalculateMainChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $scRmsd =
$document->CalculateSideChainAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );
my $apRmsd =
$document->CalculateAllProteinAlignmentRmsd( $molecule1aj7, $Sequence1aj7,
$molecule1gaf, $Sequence1gaf, True );

# Print out the last element of each returned array - the overall RMSD for
# each type of calculation.
printf "Vh domain RMSD:\n";
printf "\tC-alpha RMSD: %.3f\n", $caRmsd->Item( $caRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tMain-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $mcRmsd->Item( $mcRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tSide-chain RMSD: %.3f\n", $scRmsd->Item( $scRmsd->Count() - 1 );
printf "\tAll heavy atoms RMSD: %.3f\n",
$apRmsd->Item( $apRmsd->Count() - 1 );
print "\n";

# This demonstrates that the array is for all residues plus overall
# value, not just selected, and that as the first chain(L) is
# unselected (its values are 0).
printf "Number of values returned is %d\n", $scRmsd->Count();

# Get the number of residues in the first chain.
my $chain0ResidueCount = $document->Chains->Item(0)->AminoAcids->Count;

# Print first and last values for the L chain and for our selected domain of H chain.
printf "L chain unselected; first and last values are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item(0),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount - 1 );
printf
"Side-chain RMSD for first and last residue selected in H chain are %f %f.\n",
$scRmsd->Item($chain0ResidueCount),
$scRmsd->Item( $chain0ResidueCount + 110 - 1 );
print "\n";

# Get antigen NPE from 1aj7.
my $antigen1 = $document->Molecules->[0]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Get antigen NPE from 1gaf.
my $antigen2 = $document->Molecules->[1]->Chains->[2]->Residues->[0];

# Copy antigen residues to a new document.
my $tmpDocument = Mdm::Document::Create();
my $tmpMolecule1 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen1Copy = $antigen1->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen1Copy, $tmpMolecule1 );
my $tmpMolecule2 = $tmpDocument->CreateMolecule();
my $antigen2Copy = $antigen2->Copy();
$tmpDocument->ChangeObjectParent( $antigen2Copy, $tmpMolecule2 );

$tmpDocument->FitView();

# Calculate NPE RMSD.
my $rmsd =
$tmpDocument->CalculateOtherResidueRmsd( $tmpMolecule1, $tmpMolecule2 );
printf "NPE RMSD: %.3f\n", $rmsd->[1];
```

# SwapChainOrder function

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/swapchainorder_function.htm

## SwapChainOrder function

### Description

Swaps the order of two chains within a molecule.

### Applies to

The SwapChainOrder function can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Document

### Using the SwapChainOrder function

#### Command

$object->SwapChainOrder( <chain1>, <chain2> );

$object->SwapChainOrder( { Chain1 => <chain1>, Chain2 => <chain2> } );

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <chain1> | Required | | Mdm::Chain |
| <chain2> | Required | | Mdm::Chain |
| $object | | | Mdm::Document |

When used within the Discovery
Studio Client, this function will 
result in interactive updates.

#### Defined by

ProteinDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
# Demonstrates the use of the SwapChainOrder, MergeChains and SplitChain
# functions.
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;
use DiscoveryStudioScript;

#Note - this script should be run from DS client 

# subroutine to print information about the structure
sub PrintInfo($)
{
my ($document) = @_;
my $molecules = $document->Molecules;
printf( " Number of molecules %d\n", $molecules->Count );
for ( my $index = 0 ; $index < $molecules->Count ; ++$index )
{
my $molecule = $molecules->Item($index);
printf( " molecule number %d name %s\n",
$index + 1, $molecule->Name );
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
for ( my $index2 = 0 ; $index2 < $chains->Count ; ++$index2 )
{
my $chain = $chains->Item($index2);
printf(
" chain number %d name %s number of residues %d\n",
$index2 + 1,
$chain->Name, $chain->Residues->Count
);
}
}
}

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4ins.pdb" );

$document->InvokeAction('ActionViewHierarchy');

print("Before swap:\n");
PrintInfo($document);

$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

my $chains = $document->Chains();

$document->SwapChainOrder($chains->Item(0),$chains->Item(1));

print("after swap 1 and 2:\n");
PrintInfo($document);
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

$document->MergeChains($chains->Item(3),$chains->Item(2));

print ("after merge 3 and 4:\n");
PrintInfo($document);
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(3);

my $chainsNow = $document->Chains();
my $residues = $chainsNow->Item(0)->Residues();

#find a residue somewhere in the middle of the first chain
my $numRes = $residues->Count();
my $breakRes = $residues->Item( int($numRes/2) );

$document->SplitChain($breakRes);

print("After splitting chain 1:\n");

PrintInfo($document);

print("You should now have amino acid chains B,B,A,C with the ion/water chains unaffected.\n");

# update view
$document->UpdateViews();
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
```
```text
# This script illustrates how to access several residue properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . '1CRN.pdb' );

my $cysteineCount = 0;
my $alanineCount = 0;
my $sequence = "";

my $residues = $document->Residues;
foreach my $residue (@$residues)
{
print 'Residue Name: ' . $residue->Name . "\n\t";
print 'ID: ' . $residue->Id . "\n\t";
print 'PDB: ' . $residue->PDBName . "\n\t";
print 'SymbolandId: ' . $residue->SymbolAndId . "\n\t";
print 'Hydrophobicity: ' . $residue->Hydrophobicity . "\n\t";
print 'pKa: ' . $residue->pKa . "\n";

# Create the one-letter sequence from the symbol.
$sequence = $sequence . $residue->Symbol;

++$cysteineCount if ( $residue->Type eq Mdm::cys );
++$alanineCount if ( $residue->LongName eq 'Alanine' );
}

printf "Number of cysteine residues: %d \n", $cysteineCount;
printf "Number of alanine residues: %d \n", $alanineCount;
printf "Protein sequence is: %s\n", $sequence;
```

# TailFeature property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/tailfeature_property.htm

## TailFeature property

### Description

TailFeature specifies the tail point in a vector feature of a query.

### Applies to

The TailFeature property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::AcceptorFeature , Mdm::DonorFeature

### Using the TailFeature property

#### Get

my $pointfeatureObject = $object->TailFeature;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $pointfeatureObject | | | Mdm::PointFeature |
| $object | | | Mdm::AcceptorFeature Mdm::DonorFeature |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
use strict;
use PharmacophoreDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::Create();

# Create empty query
my $query1 = $document->CreateQuery();

# Create top level fit operator
my $fitOperator = $query1->CreateQueryOperator('queryFit');

# Create some features on the query
# Create a donor feature at 0,0,0
my $molecule = $document->CreateMolecule();
my $atomObject = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 0, 0 );

my $donorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$donorOperator->Name('HBD1');
my $newDonor = $donorOperator->CreateDonorFeature($atomObject);

# create the location constraints
my $locationfeatureHead =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newDonor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Create an acceptor feature at 0,6,2
my $atomObject1 = $molecule->CreateAtom("O");
$atomObject1->XYZ = Mdm::Point::Create( 0, 6, 2 );

my $acceptorOperator = $fitOperator->CreateQueryOperator('queryInclude');
$acceptorOperator->Name('HBA1');
my $newAcceptor = $acceptorOperator->CreateAcceptorFeature($atomObject1);

# create the location constraint. The $fitOperator and the parent operator of $acceptorOperator are the same in this case.
# Either can be used to create the location constraint.
my $locationfeatureHead =
$acceptorOperator->GetParentOperator()
->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->HeadFeature(), 2.2 );
my $locationfeatureTail =
$fitOperator->CreateLocationFeature( $newAcceptor->TailFeature(), 1.6 );

# Check to see if a proper query has been made and print out some information
if ( $fitOperator->HasChildOperators() )
{
print "Query successfully made, fit operator has child operators.\n";
my $headPoint = $newAcceptor->HeadXYZ;
my $tailPoint = $newAcceptor->TailXYZ;
printf "Head : %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n", $headPoint->X, $headPoint->Y,
$headPoint->Z;
printf "Tail : %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f\n", $tailPoint->X, $tailPoint->Y,
$tailPoint->Z;
print "Radius of location constraint on tail "
. $newAcceptor->TailFeature()->LocationSphereRadius . "\n";
}
$molecule->Select(); # Select this to delete at end

$document->UpdateObjects();
$document->DeleteObjects();
```

# TaskId property

Source type: HTML

Source section: scripting

Source file: scripting/taskid_property.htm

## TaskId property

### Description

TaskId is the identification number of a launched protocol job.

### Applies to

The TaskId property can be used with the following objects:

Protocol::Task

### Using the TaskId property

#### Get

my $stringValue = $object->TaskId;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $stringValue | | | String |
| $object | | | Protocol::Task |

#### Defined by

ProtocolDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Describes how to launch a protocol.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProtocolDiscoveryScript;

my $samplesFolder = $ENV{ACCELRYS_ROOT} . '/share/Samples/Tutorials/Receptor-Ligand Interactions/';
my $infileName = '1EQG-ibuprofen.sd';
my $inputFile = $samplesFolder . $infileName;

# Protocol name and parameters
my $protocolName = 'Generate Conformations';
my %parameterHash = ( "Input Ligands" => $inputFile,
"Conformation Method" => "CAESAR", 
"Maximum Conformations" => 100,
);

print "Connecting to server...\n";
my $session = Protocol::Document::DefaultSession();
if ($session)
{
print "Connected to $session->{Server} as user $session->{User}.\n";
}
else
{
die "No Pipeline Pilot server found. Please connect to a valid server and try again.\n";
}

# Print default running folder, which can be changed
print "Running in $session->{RunFolder}...\n";

print "Open protocol document for $protocolName\n";
my $document = Protocol::Document::Create( $protocolName, $session );

my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n"; 
my $guid = $document->Guid();
print "Protocol guid: $guid\n";

my $version = $document->Version();
print "Protocol version: $version\n";
## Setup the protocol parameters

for my $key (keys %parameterHash) {
if ( $document->ItemExists($key) ) {
$document->ReplaceItem( $key, $parameterHash{$key} );
print "Set parameter '$key' : $parameterHash{$key}\n"; 
}
else{
print "\n<warning> not a valid parameter '$key'\n\n"; 
}
}

## Launch Pipeline Pilot protocol

my $saveIntermediateFiles = True;
my $maxFilesizeToDownload = 256;
my $showJobCompleteDialog = False;
my $task = $session->Launch(
$document, $maxFilesizeToDownload,
$saveIntermediateFiles, $showJobCompleteDialog
);

print "\nLaunch the protocol: $protocolName \n";
print "Task info\n";
print "Name: $task->{ProtocolName}\n";
print "Host: $task->{Host}\n";
print "RunPath: $task->{RunPath}\n";
print "TaskId: $task->{TaskId}\n";

## Track progress of task
print " $protocolName Task is running...\n";
my $times = 0;
while ( $task->IsRunnable() )
{
print "Status: $task->{State}\n";
sleep(5);
++$times;
if ( $times > 5 )
{
$task->KillTask();
}
}

$task->WaitForCompletion();

# get the log file
my $messages = $task->LogMessages;
print "$protocolName Log messages:\n";
map { print "$_\n"; } @$messages; 

my $finalStatus = $task->State;
my $finalMolecularData;
if ( $finalStatus eq Protocol::taskComplete )
{
print "$protocolName completed\n";
my $path = $task->RunPath;
my $outFile = "$path/Output/$infileName";
die "Output file was not found please check report!" if ( not -e $outFile );
# load the results 
DiscoveryScript::Open( { Path => $outFile, LoadAllObjects => True } ); 
}
else
{
print " $protocolName Task failed with status $finalStatus\n";
}
```

Thickness specifies the thickness (Å) of an Mdm::Membrane object.
It represents the extent of the low dielectric region of the lipid bilayer occupied
by the hydrocarbon chains of the lipids.

### Applies to

The Thickness property can be used with the following objects:

Mdm::Membrane

### Using the Thickness property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->Thickness;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Membrane |

#### Set

$object->Thickness = <thickness>;

$object->Thickness( <thickness> );

$object->Thickness( { Thickness => <thickness> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <thickness> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::Membrane |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/use/bin/perl -w
# This script illustrate how to create a membrane.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use ProteinDiscoveryScript;

my $document = Mdm::Document::CreateFromPdbId('1f88');

# Remove all chains except the first.
my $molecule = $document->Molecules->Item(0);
my $chains = $molecule->Chains;
my $chainCount = $chains->Count;
for ( my $i = 1 ; $i < $chainCount ; ++$i )
{
$chains->Item($i)->Select();
}
$document->DeleteObjects();

# "Guess" some value for the membrane position.
my $center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, -3.2 );
my $normal = Mdm::Point::Create( 0.521, 0.106, 0.847 );
my $membrane =
$document->CreateMembrane( $center, $normal, 60.0, 60.0, 30.0 );

# Pick a different color scheme from default.
$membrane->CytosolColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 0, 255, 255 ) ); # cyan
$membrane->ExtracellularColor( Mdm::Color::Create( 255, 255, 0 ) ); # yellow
$document->SetParent( $molecule, $membrane );
$document->UpdateViews();
sleep(2);

# Change some membrane properties.
$center = Mdm::Point::Create( 61.54, 14.04, 3.2 );
$normal = Mdm::Point::Create( -0.521, -0.106, -0.847 );

$membrane->Thickness = 35;
$membrane->Normal = $normal;
$membrane->Center = $center;
```

Mdm::BindingSite

### Using the Threshold property

#### Get

my $realValue = $object->Threshold;

##### Parameters

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $realValue | | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::BindingSite |

#### Set

$object->Threshold = <threshold>;

$object->Threshold( <threshold> );

$object->Threshold( { Threshold => <threshold> } );

| Name | Optional/Required | Default value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <threshold> | Required | | Real |
| $object | | | Mdm::BindingSite |

#### Defined by

MdmDiscoveryScript

### Examples

```text
#!/usr/bin/perl -w
# Illustrate how to access binding site properties.
use strict;
use MdmDiscoveryScript;
use DSCommands;

my $document = DiscoveryScript::OpenFromUrl( PdbUrlPrefix . "4PHV.pdb" );

Delete( $document, GetLigands($document) );
Delete( $document, GetWaters($document) );

my $protein = $document->Molecules->Item(0);

# Find all binding site from receptor cavities.
$document->CreateBindingSitesFromCavities($protein);
my $bindingSites = $document->BindingSites;

# Create two partition on each site.
foreach my $site (@$bindingSites)
{
$document->PartitionBindingSite( $site, 2 );
}

print "Binding site properties:\n";
print "Site Volume Threshold Points\n";
my $bsCount = 0;
foreach my $site (@$bindingSites)
{
$site->SetVisible();

my $volume = $site->GetProperty("Volume");
my $threshold = $site->GetProperty("Threshold");
my $points = $site->GetProperty("Point Count");

printf "%4d %8.3f %10.3f %7d\n", ++$bsCount, $volume, $threshold,
$points;
}

$document->EnableUpdateViews(1);
```
