Shifts are defined as three pairs of numbers separated by semicolons (e.g. -3,2;0,4;0,0) for each of the domain types Kappa, Lambda, and Heavy.
Each pair of numbers specifies the relative shift of the start and end of the respective region (CDR1; CDR2; CDR3). The shifts are calculated with respect to the IMGT loop definition (i.e., -2,2 specifies a loop region that is extended by two residues on both ends compared to the corresponding loop based on the IMGT numbering scheme).

Specifies the set of loop types to model.

Valid Values: LIGHT_CDR1 , LIGHT_CDR2 , LIGHT_CDR3 , HEAVY_CDR1 , HEAVY_CDR2 , HEAVY_CDR3

Specifies which of the loop types listed in Loops To Model should be filtered by canonical structure type. For the loop types selected, only antibody domains that match the canonical structure type of the corresponding CDR loop region of the query structure are considered as templates.

See Also:

* Morea, V.; Lesk, A.M.; and Tramontano, A. Antibody Modeling: Implications for Engineering and Design. Methods 2000 , 20(3), 267-279.

Valid Values: LIGHT_CDR1, LIGHT_CDR2, LIGHT_CDR3, HEAVY_CDR1, HEAVY_CDR2

Specify a full length antibody structure to graft the predicted Fab structure onto. This option should not be used if the predicted structure is an Fv region or an unpaired light or heavy chain.

The available options are:

* No template specified, just build the Fab or Fv region with no grafting.

* 1igy : crystal structure of an intact mouse monoclonal antibody, subclass IgG1.

* 1hzh : crystal structure of an intact human monoclonal antibody, subclass IgG1, with two loops, K:SER128-K:GLY136 and K:THR236-K:THR238 modeled.

* 1igt_model : model for an IgG2 antibody, based on the pdb crystal structure 1igt.

* 5dk3 : crystal structure of a full length antibody, subclass IgG4, with two loops, B:PRO230-B:PRO323 and G:PRO230-G:LEU235 modeled.

* User : use your own template file specified by the Input Template Structure parameter located under Template Source

Valid Values: , User

Select a template structure.
This parameter will be used only if the Full Length Graft Template parameter is set to User.

Exclude antibody CDR regions from the sequence similarity and identity calculations used to rank framework templates.

If this option is True, ranking of the templates will be performed using the following criteria in order to resolve tie-breaks:

* Similarity excluding the CDR regions

* Identity excluding the CDR regions

* Similarity for the full sequence

* Identity for the full sequence

If this option is False then only the full sequence similarity and identity will be used for the ranking.

Valid Values: True , False

Name or NCBI taxonomy id of the organisms to be selected from the framework and CDR template hits. If no organism is specified, all hits are reported.

Organism names should preferably be the scientific name of the organism. However, a number of common synonyms are supported, as specified in the NCBI Taxonomy database.

Examples: "human", "Homo sapiens", "house mouse", "Mus musculus" or "Caenorhabditis elegans"

Only framework and CDR template structures with an X-ray resolution (Å) better than the Resolution Threshold are reported.

Note:

* Only X-ray structures are affected. Structures for which the resolution is not defined, such as NMR structures, will not be filtered out, but they will be ranked lower than X-ray structures. The resolution for such structures will be reported as n/a.

* High/Medium/Low: Different levels of sampling in simulated annealing step.

* None: No molecular dynamics with simulated annealing.

Higher levels of sampling can produce more accurate models but also require more computation time.

Valid Values: High , Medium, Low, None

Number of models to be created.

Specifies the maximum number of protein templates for each loop.

# Antibody Modeling Cascade

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsmacromolecules

Source file: tsmacromolecules/protein_modeling_model_antibody_cascade.htm

## Antibody Modeling Cascade

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

The Antibody Modeling Cascade protocol automatically generates 3D model structures for one or more antibody Fab or Fv regions, starting from a set of light and heavy antibody chain sequences.

Antibody Modeling Cascade performs the following steps:

* Identify the antibody domains of the input sequences, and split any that contain both light and heavy domains into two chains.

* Pair light and heavy chains by matching their sequence names or by permutations of each light chain with each heavy chain. Alternatively, the sequences to be modeled can be all light or all heavy chains.

* For each resulting target sequence, identify framework templates within the antibody database that contain the same domains and have the highest sequence similarity.

* Use the templates to build homology models for the framework regions.

* Identify CDR templates and use them to refine the CDR loop regions.

* Optionally, predicted Fab structures can be grafted onto a template full length structure. This creates an approximate full length structure by superimposing the beta sheets of the model Fab CL and CH1 domains onto the corresponding residues of each half of the full length template. The two template Fab regions are replaced and the geometries of the recreated peptide bonds and linker region disulfide bridges are cleaned.

If you prefer to model individual antibody structures by manually selecting templates for each modeling step, use the individual protocols Identify Framework Templates , Model Antibody Framework and Model Antibody Loops , which correspond to steps 3-5, in a stepwise manner.
For more detailed modeling of a full length antibody structure, use the Model Full Length Antibody protocol.

* Open the light and heavy chain sequences to be modeled in a Sequence Window.

* If only a subset of these chains are to be modeled, select them.

* Open the Macromolecules | Model Antibody tools and click Antibody Modeling Cascade... to open the Antibody Modeling Cascade dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Sequences Select the sequences to be used as input. Chain Permutation Specify whether to pair light and heavy chains by name or generate permutations. Framework Template Type Specify the set of templates used to construct the framework regions. Loops to Model Specify the set of loops to model. To model the framework only, deselect all loops. For details about the remaining parameters, see Antibody Modeling Cascade - Parameters .

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Sequences | Select the sequences to be used as input. |
| Chain Permutation | Specify whether to pair light and heavy chains by name or generate permutations. |
| Framework Template Type | Specify the set of templates used to construct the framework regions. |
| Loops to Model | Specify the set of loops to model. To model the framework only, deselect all loops. |

For details about the remaining parameters, see Antibody Modeling Cascade - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

When the job finishes, a report opens that contains links that you can click to display model structures for each target sequence, and a detailed report for each model.

Click on a link in the Models column of the report to open a specific final model structure in a Molecule Window, or click on View Results to open all models in one window. If you have created grafted full length structures, the report will have a Grafted Models column containing links to open these; the View Results button will open all the grafted structures and there will be an additional link Open all Fab Structures for the ungrafted structures.

Click the Molecule tab in the Data Table View to examine the PDF Total Energy, PDF Physical Energy, and DOPE Score of each model. Lower PDF energy indicates that the model satisfies the homology restraints better. A lower DOPE Score also indicates a better model.

A set of groups is defined in each structure for the modeled antibody loops. In the Hierarchy View, the groups are located in CDR Loops under the input molecule. One group is defined for each loop selected in the Loops to Model parameter (e.g., Heavy CDR1, Light_CDR2, etc.) The loop ranges are determined by the setting of the CDR Loop Definition parameter. Loop definitions are described in the parameter help and in Model Antibody theory .

Click on a link in the Details column of the report to open a detailed report for a model. This consists of three sections:

* Framework: Similar to the Identify Framework Templates report and allows examination of the framework templates.

* CDRs: Similar to the loop tables in the Model Antibody Loops report.

* Models: PDF Total Energy, PDF Physical Energy, and DOPE Score, and the loop regions.

#### Troubleshooting

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |

Additionally, there is a folder for each modeled sequence that contains the final model structure in .mol2 and .pdb formats, the detailed report .html file, and subfolders named IAFT, FRModels, and CDRModels containing the output from each stage of the modeling procedure.

#### Further information

Identify Framework Templates Model Antibody Framework Model Antibody Loops Run a parallel calculation

# Model Antibody Framework - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsmacromolecules

Source file: tsmacromolecules/protein_modeling_model_antibody_framework-para.htm

## Model Antibody Framework - Parameters

### Builds homology models for an antibody framework structure

Builds homology models of an antibody Fab or Fv domain from a framework template. Optionally, the models will be built from a chimeric template, which are generated by superimposing light and heavy chain templates onto an Interface Template that determines the relative spatial orientation of the four domains in the Fab region or the two domains in the Fv region.

The following steps are performed:

* Optionally, superimpose the domains of the light and heavy chain templates onto the corresponding domains of the interface template to create the chimeric template if the Light and/or Heavy Chain Template are specified.

* Align input light and heavy chain sequences to the framework template specified in the Interface Template parameter or the chimeric template.

* Build homology models based on the framework template (or chimeric template) and alignment obtained in step 2.

Notes:

* The residue numbering in the light chain and heavy chain input sequences are used to number the residues of the models produced by the protocol. However, if residue numbers are not defined in the input sequences, the residues are numbered sequentially. Also, if Single Chain Model is set to True , residues are numbered sequentially to avoid duplicate residue numbers.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Light Chain Sequence | Sequence of the Antibody Light Chain. In Pipeline Pilot, specify a sequence file. Supported file formats include BSML, PIR, and FASTA. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of sequences in any open Sequence Windows. |
| Heavy Chain Sequence | Sequence of the Antibody Heavy Chain. In Pipeline Pilot, specify a sequence file. Supported file formats include BSML, PIR, and FASTA. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of sequences in any open Sequence Windows. |
| Interface Template | Select a template structure with a light and heavy antibody chain to specify light chain-heavy chain interface. The Interface Template determines the overall orientation of the domains in the model. If no Light or Heavy Chain Templates are specified, the Interface Template is used to build the model. If Light and/or Heavy Chain Templates are specified, their domains are superimposed to the corresponding domains in the Interface Template and used to construct the chimeric framework template. |
| Light Chain Template | Select a template structure for the light chain. If a template for the light chain is specified, it will be used to build a chimeric antibody framework template. In the chimeric template, the CL and VL domains of the Interface Template are replaced by the corresponding domains from the Light Chain Template . The domains from the light chain template are oriented to superimpose with the corresponding Interface Template domains. If no Light Chain Template is specified, the light chain from the Interface Template is used. |
| Heavy Chain Template | Select a template structure for the heavy chain. If a template for the heavy chain is specified, it will be used to build a chimeric antibody framework template. In the chimeric template, the CL and VL domains of the Interface Template are replaced by the corresponding domains from the Heavy Chain Template . The domains from the heavy chain template are oriented to superimpose with the corresponding Interface Template domains. If no Heavy Chain Template is specified, the heavy chain from the Interface Template is used. |
| Number of Models | Number of models to be created. |
| Start Model Index | MODELER randomizes the initial structure before producing each final model. Use Start Model Index to change the randomization seed to build models from different initial structures. Start Model Index is also used in the output model names. For example, if you build two models for sequence "xyz" with Start Model Index ="3", the output model names are "xyz.B99990003" and "xyz.B99990004". |
| Advanced | Contains less commonly used parameters. |
| Optimization Level | Specifies the amount of molecular dynamics with simulated annealing to perform. High/Medium/Low : Different levels of sampling in simulated annealing step. None : No molecular dynamics with simulated annealing. Higher levels of sampling can produce more accurate models but also require more computation time. Valid Values: High , Medium, Low, None |
| Copy Ligands | Copy ligands from the template structures to the model. All the ligands in the Interface Template , and any ligands that are close to any regions of the Light Chain or Heavy Chain Template used to construct the final overall template are copied into the model. A ligand is defined as a chain in a protein that does not contain amino acids, nucleic acids, or waters, but does contain at least one carbon atom. Notes: Ligands from multiple templates (e.g., Interface , Light Chain and Heavy Chain Template ) may overlap with each other. Ligands from Interface Template may also have clashes with amino acid residues in the chimeric template constructed from the Light and Heavy Chain Template . Carefully inspect the ligands in the model after the models are created. If there are bad clashes between the amino acid residues and the ligands in the model, delete unwanted ligands from templates accordingly and rerun the protocol. If a template structure contains multiple amino acid chains, only ligands with the same chain id as the chain used as template will be copied into the model. Valid Values: True , False |
| Single Chain Model | Build a single chain antibody model. In a single chain model, the regions of the model corresponding to the input Light Chain and Heavy Chain Sequences are covalently bonded to form a single chain. The order of the sequences in the model can be specified by the Chain Order sub-parameter. Use this option to build models for the single-chain variable fragment (scFv). Note: Ensure that the spatial gap in the Interface Template between the chain termini to be connected in the model is small enough to be bridged by the corresponding linking region in the model sequence. If the linking region is too short, the model around the linking region could be distorted with elongated backbone bonds. Valid Values: True, False |
| Chain Order | Order of antibody chains in the output model. For single chain models, this determines the connectivity of the model generated as follows: light - heavy : C-terminal of the Light Chain Sequence is bonded to the N-terminal of the Heavy Chain Sequence . heavy - light : C-terminal of the Heavy Chain Sequence is bonded to the N-terminal of the Light Chain Sequence . Valid Values: light - heavy, heavy - light |
| Parallel Processing | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. Valid Values: True, False |
| Parallel Processing Server | Comma separated list of servers (server-name:port-number) to be used for parallel processing. Add "localhost" to include the local server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where "localhost" requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster). |
| Parallel Processing Server Processes | Comma separated list of the maximum batches that can be simultaneously executed on each server. Each value must correspond with an entry in the list of servers. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. |
| Parallel Processing Preserve Order | Preserve the initial order of the data records. Valid Values: True , False |

# Model Antibody Framework

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsmacromolecules

Source file: tsmacromolecules/protein_modeling_model_antibody_framework.htm

## Model Antibody Framework

* Description

* Setting Up and Running

* Analyzing Results

The Model Antibody Framework protocol allows you to build a homology model for an antibody 
Fv or Fab domain based on their sequence.

The protocol requires two input model sequences: one for the light chain and one for the heavy chain.
It also requires an input structure (interface template). This structure specifies the relative orientation
of the antibody domains. If better templates are available for the light or the heavy chain, you can specify them separately to improve the overall quality of the model. The protocol will build a chimeric template by structurally 
superimposing the light chain template onto the light chain domains of the interface template and the heavy 
chain template onto the heavy chain domains of the interface template. The superimposed light
chain template and heavy chain template will be merged into one structure, which results in the chimeric
template for modeling. The advantage of a chimeric template is that it can use the best available templates to model 
structural details of the light and heavy chain domains, while preserving the overall orientation of the domains 
specified by the interface template.
If light or heavy chain templates are not specified, the model is built based on the interface template alone.

The input template structures for the interface and light and heavy chains can be identified using Identify Framework Templates protocol.

* Load the sequences for the light chain and the heavy chain of the antibody you want to model in a Sequence Window.

* From the Report of a completed Identify Framework Templates job, choose an overall template you want to use and click the corresponding link in the Overall Templates table
to open the template in a Molecule Window.

* If you choose to use separate light or heavy chain template structures, click on the links in the corresponding tables in the Report to open
them into separate Molecule Windows.

* Open the Macromolecules | Model Antibody tools and click Model Antibody Framework... to open the Model Antibody Framework dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Light Chain Sequence Select the sequence for the light chain. Heavy Chain Sequence Select the sequence for the heavy chain. Interface Template Select the template structure that specifies the spatial orientation of light and heavy chain. Light Chain Template Optionally, select the template structure for the light chain. Heavy Chain Template Optionally, select the template structure for the heavy chain. Advanced:Copy Ligands Set to True if you want to copy the ligands present in the template structures. Advanced:Single Chain Model Set to True if you want to build a single chain antibody model, in particular, a single-chain variable fragment (scFv). Number of Models Specify how many models to create, each from a different initial
structure. You can expand this group and set Start Model Index to use different initial structures.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Light Chain Sequence | Select the sequence for the light chain. |
| Heavy Chain Sequence | Select the sequence for the heavy chain. |
| Interface Template | Select the template structure that specifies the spatial orientation of light and heavy chain. |
| Light Chain Template | Optionally, select the template structure for the light chain. |
| Heavy Chain Template | Optionally, select the template structure for the heavy chain. |
| Advanced:Copy Ligands | Set to True if you want to copy the ligands present in the template structures. |
| Advanced:Single Chain Model | Set to True if you want to build a single chain antibody model, in particular, a single-chain variable fragment (scFv). |
| Number of Models | Specify how many models to create, each from a different initial structure. You can expand this group and set Start Model Index to use different initial structures. |

* Set the remaining parameters as desired. For details, see Model Antibody Framework - Parameters

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

* Analyzing output models

* Analyzing output alignment

* Troubleshooting

When the interactive job finishes, the output models and the sequence alignment are opened into new Molecule Window and
Sequence Window. For a background job, double-click it in the Jobs Explorer to
open the report, and then open the experiment report and open the model structure and sequence alignment from the Results section in the report.

The new Molecule Window opened contains all antibody models and the chimeric template. The models and template are superimposed.

Click the Molecule tab in the Data Table View to examine the PDF Total Energy , PDF Physical Energy , and DOPE Score of each model. 
Smaller PDF energy indicates that the model satisfies the homology
restraints better. Lower DOPE Score also indicates a better model.

Click the AminoAcid tab to examine the 40 PDF energy properties added
to each residue. All these property names are prefixed with PDF for clarity. PDF property names that contain N_ indicate
normalized PDF energies. You can select these properties and use the commands under the Chart menu to
create plots to aid in their analysis. Also, refer to the PDF Energy and PDF Energy Key sections in Build Homology Models for more information.

Residues that
are identical or similar between model sequence and template sequence, or are insertions in the model sequence are grouped. Expand the Hierarchy view and review the groups under Modeler Groups for each model structure.

The new Sequence Window contains alignment between
the chimeric template and the models. The alignment is automatically generated by separately aligning the sequences 
for the light and the heavy chains and concatenating the resulting alignments. Carefully examine the alignment
and, if necessary, adjust them manually and rerun the model creation with the refined alignment using the Build Homology Models protocol.

There is one sequence entry for each model in the alignment with each linked to the corresponding
model structure in the Molecule Window.

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary that includes input and output files, the PDF Total Energy, the PDF Physical Energy, and the DOPE Score, and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| *.dsv | Structural superposition of models and template. |
| *.bsml | Sequence alignment of models to template. |

# Model Antibody Loops - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsmacromolecules

Source file: tsmacromolecules/protein_modeling_model_antibody_loops-para.htm

## Model Antibody Loops - Parameters

### Identifies and optimizes the CDR loop regions of an antibody structure

Uses Hidden Markov Models (HMM) to identify variable antibody domains in the Input Protein Molecule and performs a similarity search against pre-compiled antibody domain and CDR loop databases to identify Complementarity Determining Regions (CDR). An alignment is created for each CDR loop against the most similar hits in the database. Set Build Models to "True" to use MODELER to generate homology models of the structure based on the hits.

The following steps are performed:

* Identifies antibody loops

* Builds models

Steps in italics may be skipped depending on settings.

Note:

* CDR loops will be stored as residue groups in the output DSV file.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Protein Molecule | In Pipeline Pilot Client, specify an antibody protein structure file. Supported file formats include DSV, MSV, PDB, and MOL2. In Discovery Studio, choose an antibody protein structure from the list of all visible proteins. |
| Maximum Templates Per Loop | Specifies the maximum number of protein templates for each loop. |
| CDR Loop Definition | Specifies the numbering scheme used to define the Complementarity Determining Region (CDR). The following options are available: IMGT : Numbering scheme described in "The IMGT unique numbering for immunoglobulins, T cell Receptors and Ig-like domains". Lefranc, M.-P., The Immunologist , 1999 , 7 , 132-136 "IMGT unique numbering for immunoglobulin and T cell receptor variable domains and Ig superfamily V-like domains", LeFranc, et al. Dev. Comp. Immunol. , 2003 , 27 , 55-77. This scheme is used as a reference to define the CDR definitions for the other schemes. Chothia : Method described in the following papers: "Canonical Structures for the Hypervariable Regions of Immunoglobulins". Chothia, C. and Lesk, A.M., J. Mol. Biol. , 1987 , 196 , 901-917 "Standard Conformations for the Canonical Structures of Immunoglobulins". Al-Lazikani, et al. J. Mol. Biol. 1997 , 273 , 927-948. "Conformations of the Third Hypervariable Region in the VH Domain of Immunoglobulins". Morea, et al. J. Mol. Biol. 1998 , 275 , 269-294 "Antibody Modeling: Implications for Engineering and Design". Morea, et al. Methods , 2000 , 20(3) , 267-279. The CDR definitions for the Chothia scheme correspond to the following shifts with respect to the IMGT CDR definitions: Kappa: -1,0;0,0;2,-1 Lambda: -2,0;0,0;2,-1 Heavy: 0,-1;2,-2;3,-1 Kabat : Numbering scheme detailed in "Sequences of Proteins of Immunological Interest". Kabat, E. A., Wu, T. T., Perry, H. M., Gottesman, K. S., and Foeller, C., U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, NIH, Bethesda, MD., 1991 . The CDR definitions for the Kabat scheme correspond to the following shifts with respect to the IMGT CDR definitions: Kappa: -3,2;0,4;0,0 Lambda: -3,2;0,4;0,0 Heavy: 5,2;-1,8;2,0 Honegger : Numbering scheme described in "Yet Another Numbering Scheme for Immunoglobulin Variable Domains: An Automatic Modeling and Analysis Tool". Honegger, A. and Plückthun, A., J. Mol. Biol. , 2001 , 309 , 657-670. The CDR definitions for the Honegger scheme correspond to the following shifts with respect to the IMGT CDR definitions: Kappa: -2,0;0,9;2,-1 Lambda: -2,0;0,9;2,-1 Heavy: -2,0;0,9;2,-1 Shifts are defined as three pairs of numbers separated by semicolons (e.g. -3,2;0,4;0,0) for each of the domain types Kappa, Lambda, and Heavy. Each pair of numbers specifies the relative shift of the start and end of the respective region (CDR1; CDR2; CDR3). The shifts are calculated with respect to the IMGT loop definition (i.e., -2,2 specifies a loop region that is extended by two residues on both ends compared to the corresponding loop based on the IMGT numbering scheme). Valid Values: User |
| CDR Loop Definition Kappa | Specifies the user loop definition for kappa variable domain using the shifts with respect to IMGT definition. |
| CDR Loop Definition Lambda | Specifies the user loop definition for lambda variable domain using the shifts with respect to IMGT definition. |
| CDR Loop Definition Heavy | Specifies the user loop definition for heavy variable domain using the shifts with respect to IMGT definition. |
| Loops to Model | Specifies the set of loop types to model. If no specific set of loops is selected, all loops will be modeled. Valid Values: LIGHT_CDR1 , LIGHT_CDR2 , LIGHT_CDR3 , HEAVY_CDR1 , HEAVY_CDR2 , HEAVY_CDR3 |
| Filter By Canonical Structure | Specifies which of the loop types listed in Loops To Model should be filtered by canonical structure type. For the loop types selected, only antibody domains that match the canonical structure type of the corresponding CDR loop region of the query structure are considered as templates. For a discussion of canonical loop structures, see: Morea, V.; Lesk, A.M.; and Tramontano, A. "Antibody Modeling: Implications for Engineering and Design." Methods 2000 , 20(3), 267-279. Valid Values: LIGHT_CDR1, LIGHT_CDR2, LIGHT_CDR3, HEAVY_CDR1, HEAVY_CDR2 |
| Organism | Name or NCBI taxonomy id of the organisms to be selected from the template hits. If no organism is specified, all hits are reported. |
| Resolution Threshold | Only template structures with a resolution better than the Resolution Threshold are reported. Note: Only X-ray structures are affected. Structures, for which the resolution is not defined, such as NMR structures, will not be filtered out, but they will be ranked lower than X-ray structures. The resolution for such structures will be reported as n/a. |
| Build Models | If True, use MODELER to generate homology models of the input structure based on the identified antibody templates. Valid Values: True , False |
| Number of Models | Specifies the number of models to be created. |
| Start Model Index | Uses different Start Model Index to specify different random initial structures. |
| Optimization Level | Specifies the amount of molecular dynamics annealing to perform. Valid Values: High , Medium, Low, None |
| Renumber Target Sequences | Renumber the sequence of the Input Protein Molecule and any models built according to the numbering scheme specified in CDR Loop Definition . Valid Values: True , False |
| Parallel Processing | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. Valid Values: True, False |

This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where "localhost" requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster). |
| Parallel Processing Server Processes | Comma separated list of the maximum batches that can be simultaneously executed on each server. Each value must correspond with an entry in the list of servers. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. |
| Parallel Processing Preserve Order | Preserve the initial order of the data records. Valid Values: True , False |

# Model Antibody Loops

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsmacromolecules

Source file: tsmacromolecules/protein_modeling_model_antibody_loops.htm

## Model Antibody Loops

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

* Selecting specific templates for individual CDR loops

The Model Antibody Loops protocol identifies templates for 
Complementarity Determining Regions (CDRs) in an antibody structure and builds models for the CDRs using these templates.

Antibody domains and the corresponding CDRs in the input structure are identified and aligned against a database of pre-aligned antibody variable domains using Hidden Markov Models (HMM). Based on the HMM data, the protocol generates an alignment of the sequence of the input protein and the best matches in the databases. It then uses the alignment to Build Homology Models for the CDRs in the input antibody structure.

* Load an antibody structure into a Molecule Window .

* Open the Macromolecules | Model Antibody tools and click Model Antibody Loops... to open the Model Antibody Loops dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Protein Molecule Select a protein to use as input. Maximum Templates per Loop Maximum number of protein templates for each loop. Loops to Model Set of loops that should be modeled. Filter By Canonical Structure Set of loops (if any) that should be filtered by canonical structure type. See Theory - Model Antibody Loops (Canonical Structures) . Build Models Set to True to build models of the antibody. For details about the remaining parameters, see Model Antibody Loops - Parameters .

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Protein Molecule | Select a protein to use as input. |
| Maximum Templates per Loop | Maximum number of protein templates for each loop. |
| Loops to Model | Set of loops that should be modeled. |
| Filter By Canonical Structure | Set of loops (if any) that should be filtered by canonical structure type. See Theory - Model Antibody Loops (Canonical Structures) . |
| Build Models | Set to True to build models of the antibody. |

For details about the remaining parameters, see Model Antibody Loops - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

When the interactive job finishes, the structures and the corresponding sequence alignment will be opened automatically and 
a dialog with the experiment summary is displayed. Click the Report button in the Dialog to open the experiment report.

If you ran the job in the background, expand the results in the Jobs Explorer, click View Results to open the structures and the sequence alignment, and then double-click the job in the Jobs Explorer to open the experiment report.

In the report, the loop residues, canonical structure type (if selected), and identified templates with the template loop scores for each CDR region are listed in a separate table. 
If the input protein has multiple chains, the loops are listed for each chain. Each loop can have multiple templates according to the Maximum Templates per Loop parameter.
The templates are sorted by Score, which is a similarity score for the loop region, described in Theory - Model Antibody Loops .

The Graphics View contains the input structure with all the templates and any models that were built. 
The input structure, models (if applicable), and the templates are superimposed. Each structure, including the models has a corresponding sequence
in the Sequence Window. Only the first structure is set to be visible initially and linked to the corresponding sequence in Sequence Window.

A set of groups are defined in the input antibody structure for the antibody loops. In the Hierarchy View, the groups are located in CDR Loops under the input molecule. One group is defined for each loop selected in the Loops to Model parameter (e.g., Heavy_CDR1 , Light_CDR2 , etc.) The loop ranges are determined by the setting of the CDR Loop Definition parameter. Loop definitions are described in the parameter help and in Model Antibody theory .

If you chose not the build the model, the first two sequences in the alignment taken from the input protein appear in the Sequence Window. One is used as the
model sequence and is named <Input Protein Molecule>_M , and the other is linked to the input antibody structure. The CDR loops of these two sequences are fully unaligned, so the
input antibody structure is only used to build the framework region of the model, and the loops are modeled by the identified loop templates.

If you have chosen to build models, the first set of sequences correspond to the models generated, followed by the input protein and the individual loop templates.

The templates for each loop are aligned to the model sequence with the hit loop completely aligned and other loops completely shifted. The alignments outside the loop
regions are derived from the residue numbers corresponding to the selected CDR Loop Definition scheme. One template structure can potentially be used to model more than one CDR loop. If this is the case, the template will appear as multiple sequence entries in the alignment (each with a corresponding structure in the Molecule Window). Each entry is named by the template domain name appended by the CDR number. 
You can re-evaluate the alignment and manually adjust it to build models again following the steps described in the next section.

#### Selecting specific templates to rebuild CDR loops

In the output structure and alignment files, there is one template for each CDR region. Each sequence or structure name is appended with the loop number
to indicate which CDR region they are a template for (e.g., "<name>_CDR1" is a template for CDR1, "<name>_CDR2" 
is a template for CDR2, etc.) Take the following steps to select a subset of templates from the output and recreate the models using the Build Homology Models... protocol.

* Delete all loop model structures (if they exist) in the Molecule Window for easy navigation.

* Determine which templates you want to use for each loop region by inspecting the sequences and structures.

* Adjust the sequence alignment manually if desired.

* Turn on the visibility of all the templates you select in the Molecule Window and verify that they are properly linked to the corresponding sequences in the Sequence Window.

* In the Molecule Window, select the antibody structure you used as input to the Model Antibody Loops.. protocol in the first step (this should be the first structure in the Hierarchy View).

* Open the Macromolecules | Create Homology Models tools and click Build Homology Models... to open the Build Homology Models dialog.

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Sequence Alignment Select the alignment returned by the Model Antibody Loops.. protocol. Input Template Structures Select the input antibody structure and the template structures that you want to use to model the CDR regions. Input Model Sequence Select the model sequence name. This will be the first sequence in the Sequence Window, identified by a "_M" in the sequence name. Copy From Templates | Protein Select the antibody structure you used as input to the Model Antibody Loops.. protocol in the Protein parameter 
and select the range of residues listed in Copy Regions parameter. If you also want to preserve the side chain conformations of the 
framework regions, set the Optimize Sidechains parameter to False . It is important to set the parameters in this group correctly in order to preserve the coordinates for the framework regions from the input structure 
so that only the CDR regions are remodeled. The full structure of the input protein is selected for copying into the model sequence. However, only the framework regions will be copied 
since copying is done based on the sequence alignment and the CDR regions of the model sequence are not aligned with the input antibody structure 
selected for modeling. For details about the remaining parameters, see Build Homology Models - Parameters .

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Sequence Alignment | Select the alignment returned by the Model Antibody Loops.. protocol. |
| Input Template Structures | Select the input antibody structure and the template structures that you want to use to model the CDR regions. |
| Input Model Sequence | Select the model sequence name. This will be the first sequence in the Sequence Window, identified by a "_M" in the sequence name. |
| Copy From Templates \| Protein | Select the antibody structure you used as input to the Model Antibody Loops.. protocol in the Protein parameter and select the range of residues listed in Copy Regions parameter. If you also want to preserve the side chain conformations of the framework regions, set the Optimize Sidechains parameter to False . It is important to set the parameters in this group correctly in order to preserve the coordinates for the framework regions from the input structure so that only the CDR regions are remodeled. The full structure of the input protein is selected for copying into the model sequence. However, only the framework regions will be copied since copying is done based on the sequence alignment and the CDR regions of the model sequence are not aligned with the input antibody structure selected for modeling. |

It is important to set the parameters in this group correctly in order to preserve the coordinates for the framework regions from the input structure 
so that only the CDR regions are remodeled.

The full structure of the input protein is selected for copying into the model sequence. However, only the framework regions will be copied 
since copying is done based on the sequence alignment and the CDR regions of the model sequence are not aligned with the input antibody structure 
selected for modeling.

For details about the remaining parameters, see Build Homology Models - Parameters .

Analyze the results as described in Build Homology Models... .

#### Troubleshooting

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| <input protein molecule>.bsml | The alignment of the model sequence with the templates. |
| <input protein molecule>.dsv | The input protein and models (if the Build Models parameter is set to True ) superimposed with the templates. |

#### Further information

Theory - Model Antibody Loops Theory - Model Antibody Loops (Canonical Structures) Build Homology Models [Honegger and Plückthun, 2001] [Kabat et al., 1991] Run a parallel calculation

# Model Full Length Antibody - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsmacromolecules

Source file: tsmacromolecules/protein_modeling_model_full_length_antibody-para.htm

## Model Full Length Antibody - Parameters

### Builds homology models for a full length antibody

Builds full length homology models for Immunoglobulin G based on templates for IgG1 and IgG2.

The following steps are performed:

* Optionally, graft a Fab structure onto the selected full-length template.

* Build an alignment to the selected template based on the input sequences for the light and heavy chains.

* Map inter and intra chains disulfide bridges.

* Build homology models based on the template and alignment obtained in step 1

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Light Chain Sequence | Sequence of the Antibody Light Chain. In Pipeline Pilot, specify a sequence file. Supported file formats include BSML, PIR, and FASTA. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of sequences in any open Sequence Windows. |
| Heavy Chain Sequence | Sequence of the Antibody Heavy Chain. In Pipeline Pilot, specify a sequence file. Supported file formats include BSML, PIR, and FASTA. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of sequences in any open Sequence Windows. |
| Template Source | Select the template structure used to build the antibody model. The available options are: 1igy : crystal structure of an intact mouse monoclonal antibody, subclass IgG1. 1hzh : crystal structure of an intact human monoclonal antibody, subclass IgG1, with two loops, K:SER128-K:GLY136 and K:THR236-K:THR238 modeled. 1igt_model : model for an IgG2 antibody, based on the pdb crystal structure 1igt. 5dk3 : crystal structure of a full length antibody, subclass IgG4, with two loops, B:PRO230-B:PRO323 and G:PRO230-G:LEU235 modeled. User : use your own template file specified by the Input Template Structure parameter located under Template Source Valid Values: User |
| Input Template Structure | Select a template structure. This parameter will be used only if the Template Source parameter is set to User. |
| Fab Template | Optional Fab template structure which will be grafted onto the full length template prior to the usual homology modeling procedure. |
| User Disulfide Bridges | The parameters in this group specify the cysteine residues which form disulfide bridges. In Discovery Studio, use the Define Disulfide Bridges dialog from each of the parameters to specify the list of disulfide bridges. In Pipeline Pilot, enter a comma separated list of disulfide bridges. A disulfide bridge consists of two cysteine residues connected by '-', where a cysteine residue is defined by :CYS[residue number]. The residue number is the sequential index of the residue, or if input sequence is read from a bsml file, residue numbers can be non-sequential (user specified) and may include insertion codes. Examples: ":CYS32-:CYS70,:CYS85-:CYS105" or ":CYS22-:CYS71A,:CYS45A-:CYS102". |
| LC-LC-intrachain | Defines the pairs of Cysteine residues in the light chain to form a disulfide bridge within the chain. These will be applied to both copies of the light chain, except if a second light chain has been specified. |
| LC-HC-interchain | Defines the disulfide bridges between Cysteine residues in the light chain and Cysteine residues in the heavy chain. The interchain bridges will be applied to both pairs of light and heavy chains, unless second light and heavy chains have been specified. |
| HC-HC-intrachain | Defines the pairs of Cysteine residues in the heavy chain to form disulfide bridges within the chain. These will be applied to both copies of the heavy chain, unless a second heavy chain has been specified. |
| HC-HC-interchain | Defines the disulfide bridges formed between the Cysteine residues in the first copy of the heavy chain and the Cysteine residues in the second copy of the heavy chain. Note that if modeling a bispecific antibody, the HC-HC2-interchain parameter should be specified instead. |
| Bispecific Modeling | This group of options allows for modeling of bispecific antibodies. Instead of using two identical copies of the light and heavy chain sequences, a second light and heavy chain can be specified, with their own User Disulfide Bridge definitions. Valid Values: True, False |
| Light Chain Sequence 2 | Optionally, a second light chain sequence can be specified, to allow modeling of bispecific antibodies. In Pipeline Pilot, specify a sequence file. Supported file formats include BSML, PIR, and FASTA. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of sequences in any open Sequence Windows. |
| Heavy Chain Sequence 2 | Optionally, a second light chain sequence can be specified, to allow modeling of bispecific antibodies. In Pipeline Pilot, specify a sequence file. Supported file formats include BSML, PIR, and FASTA. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of sequences in any open Sequence Windows. |
| Fab Template 2 | If desired, a second Fab structure can be specified for grafting onto the full-length template when modeling bispecific antibodies. |
| User Disulfide Bridges 2 | The parameters in this group specify the cysteine residues which form disulfide bridges between the second set of chains when modeling bispecific antibodies. Note that any disulfide bridges between the two heavy chains are specified by the HC-HC2-interchain parameter instead of the usual HC-HC-interchain parameter. In Discovery Studio, use the Define Disulfide Bridges dialog from each of the parameters to specify the list of disulfide bridges. In Pipeline Pilot, enter a comma separated list of disulfide bridges. A disulfide bridge consists of two cysteine residues connected by '-', where a cysteine residue is defined by :CYS[residue number]. The residue number is the sequential index of the residue, or if input sequence is read from a bsml file, residue numbers can be non-sequential (user specified) and may include insertion codes. Examples: ":CYS32-:CYS70,:CYS85-:CYS105" or ":CYS22-:CYS71A,:CYS45A-:CYS102". |
| LC2-LC2-intrachain | Defines the pairs of Cysteine residues in the second light chain to form disulfide bridges within this chain. |
| LC2-HC2-interchain | Defines the disulfide bridges between Cysteine residues in the second light chain and Cysteine residues in the second heavy chain. |
| HC2-HC2-intrachain | Defines the pairs of Cysteine residues in the second heavy chain to form disulfide bridges within this chain. |
| HC-HC2-interchain | Defines the disulfide bridges formed between the Cysteine residues in the first heavy chain and the Cysteine residues in the second heavy chain. Note that when modeling a bispecific antibody, this parameter is used instead of HC-HC-interchain . |
| Copy Ligands | Copy ligands from the template structure to the model. A ligand is defined as a chain in the Input Protein that does not contain any amino acids, nucleic acids or waters, but does contain at least one carbon atom. It can also be a molecule that does not contain chains but does contain at least one carbon atom. Valid Values: True , False |
| Number of Models | Number of models to be created. |
| Start Model Index | MODELER randomizes the initial structure before producing each final model. Use Start Model Index to change the randomization seed to build models from different initial structures. Start Model Index is also used in the output model names. For example, if you build two models for sequence xyz with Start Model Index = 3 , the output model names are xyz.M0003 and xyz.M0004 . |
| Optimization Level | Specifies the amount of molecular dynamics with simulated annealing to perform. High,Medium,Low: Different levels of sampling in simulated annealing step. None: No molecular dynamics with simulated annealing. Please refer Help pages in Discovery Studio for Details. Valid Values: High , Medium, Low, None |
| Parallel Processing | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. The parameters in this group specify the cysteine residues which form disulfide bridges. In Discovery Studio, use the Define Disulfide Bridges dialog from each of the parameters to specify the list of disulfide bridges.

The residue number is the sequential index of the residue, or if input sequence is read from a bsml file, residue numbers can be non-sequential (user specified) and may include insertion codes. # Model Full Length Antibody

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsmacromolecules

Source file: tsmacromolecules/protein_modeling_model_full_length_antibody.htm

## Model Full Length Antibody

* Description

* Setting Up and Running

* Analyzing Results

The Model Full Length Antibody protocol builds full length homology models for Immunoglobulin G based on templates for IgG1, IgG2 and IgG4.

The protocol requires the sequences for the light and heavy chain of the antibody to be modeled, which are usually duplicated to generate the sequence for the full length antibody. The protocol aligns the sequence 
to one of the predefined template structures or a user specified template.
The alignment is then used to build homology models using MODELER.

Optionally, you can modify the full length template by grafting a Fab (Fragment, antigen-binding region) structure onto it prior to the homology modeling. The Fab structure can be experimentally determined or the result of modeling using the Build Antibody Fab Regions tools such as the Antibody Modeling Cascade .

In addition, modeling bispecific antibodies is supported. In this case, two light and heavy chain sequences (and optionally, Fab structures) are provided instead of duplication.

* Load the sequences for the light chain and the heavy chain of the antibody you want to model into a Sequence Window.

* If grafting is required, load the Fab structure into a Molecule Window.

* Open the Macromolecules | Model Antibody tools and click Model Full Length Antibody ... to open the Model Full Length Antibody dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Light Chain Sequence Select the sequence for the light chain. Heavy Chain Sequence Select the sequence for the heavy chain. Template Source Select the template for the full length antibody model: 1igy: PDB crystal structure of an intact monoclonal antibody, subclass IgG1. 1hzh: crystal structure of an intact human monoclonal antibody, subclass IgG1, with two loops, K:SER128-K:GLY136 and K:THR236-K:THR238 modeled. 1igt_model: Model for a human IgG2 antibody, based on mouse PDB crystal structure 1igt. 5dk3: crystal structure of a full length antibody, subclass IgG4, with two loops, B:PRO230-B:PRO323 and G:PRO230-G:LEU235 modeled. User: Your own template specified by the Template Source | Input Template Structure parameter. Fab Template Select a Fab structure if grafting is required. User Disulfide Bridges Specify disulfide bridges for the model: LC-LC-intrachain: Opens the Define Disulfide Bridges dialog to select pairs of Cysteine residues in the light chains to connect by a disulfide bridge. These are intrachain bridges that are applied to both copies of the light chain. LC-HC-interchain: Opens the Define Disulfide Bridges dialog . Select Cysteine residues in the light chains to connect to Cysteine residues in the heavy chains via disulfide bridges. These interchain bridges are applied to both pairs of light and heavy chains. HC-HC-intrachain: Opens the Define Disulfide Bridges dialog . Select pairs of Cysteine residues in the heavy chains to connect via disulfide bridge. These intrachain bridges are applied to both copies of the heavy chain. HC-HC-interchain:> Opens the Define Disulfide Bridges dialog .
Select Cysteine residues in the first heavy chain to Cysteine residues in the second heavy chain to connect via disulfide bridge. Bispecific Modeling Specify parameters in this group, which replicates those above, if you want to build a bispecific model. Copy Ligands Set to True if you want to copy the ligands present in the template structure to the model. Number of Models Specify how many models to create, each from a different initial
structure. You can expand this group and set Start Model Index to use different initial structures.

* Set the remaining parameters as desired. For details, see Model Full Length Antibody - Parameters

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

* Analyzing output models

* Analyzing output alignment

* Troubleshooting

When the interactive job finishes, the output models and the sequence alignment are opened into new Molecule Window and 
Sequence Window. For a background job, double-click it in the Jobs Explorer to
open the report, and then open the model structure and sequence alignment from the Results section in the report.

The new Molecule Window contains all antibody models and the selected template. The models and template are superimposed.

Click the Molecule tab in the Data Table View to examine the PDF Total Energy , PDF Physical Energy , and DOPE Score of each model. 
Lower PDF energy indicates that the model satisfies the homology
restraints better. A lower DOPE Score also indicates a better model.

Click the AminoAcid tab to examine the 40 PDF energy properties added
to each residue. All of the property names are prefixed with PDF for clarity. PDF property names that contain N_ indicate
normalized PDF energies. You can select these properties and use the commands under the Chart menu to
create plots to aid in their analysis. Also, refer to the PDF Energy and PDF Energy Key sections in Build Homology Models for more information.

Residues that
are identical or similar between model sequence and template sequence, or are insertions in the model sequence are grouped. Expand the Hierarchy view and review the groups under Modeler Groups for each model structure.

The new Sequence Window contains the alignment between
the template and the models. The alignment is automatically generated by separately aligning the sequences 
for the light and the heavy chains, and then concatenating the resulting alignments. Carefully examine the alignment
and, if necessary, adjust them manually and rerun the model creation with the refined alignment using Build Homology Models protocol.

There is one sequence entry for each model in the alignment with each linked to the corresponding
model structure in the Molecule Window.

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| Report.htm | Job summary that includes input and output files, the PDF Total Energy, the PDF Physical Energy, and the DOPE Score, and the parameters used. |
| --- | --- |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| *.dsv | Structural superposition of models and template. |
| *.bsml | Sequence alignment of models to template. |

## Predict Antibody Paratopes - Parameters

### Predict Antibody Paratopes

Use Paragraph algorithm to predict the antibody paratope in the antibody complementary determining regions (CDR).

With antibody variable domain structures as input, the Paragraph algorithm uses equivariant graph neural network layers to predict the probability of the antibody CDR loop residues and the two stem residues on each side of the loop to bind to an antigen.

See Also:

* Chinery, L.; Wahome, N.; Moal, I.; Deane, C.M. Paragraph-antibody paratope prediction using graph
neural networks with minimal feature vectors. Bioinformatics 2023 , 39(1).

| Paratope Cutoff | Specifies the cutoff score to define the paratope residues. The predicted residue paratope scores range from 0 to 1 and the residues with score above the cutoff will be added into Paratope group in Discovery Studio Simulation Client for viewing. # Predict Antibody Paratopes

Source type: HTML

## Predict Antibody Paratopes

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Output

* Analyzing results

Predict Antibody Paratopes uses the Paragraph algorithm [Chinery et al. 2023] to predict the antigen binding site within the antibody complementary determining regions (CDR). The algorithm uses one or more antibody variable domain structures as input, and uses equivariant graph neural network layers to predict the probability of the antibody CDR loop residues and two stem residues on each side of the loop that bind to an antigen.

* Load one or more antibody variable domain structures into a Molecule Window.

* With the Molecule Window selected, open the Macromolecules | Model Antibody tools and click Predict Antibody Paratopes to open the Predict Antibody Paratopes dialog.

* For Input Proteins , choose All or Visible to set the input to all molecules or only the visible molecules in the active Molecule Window.

* Click Run .

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to the background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs.

The following files are created in the output directory.

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input files, output files, parameters used, and protocol results. Click the links in the summary table to view the relevant information for the corresponding input antibody. Check the Summary and Error sections if the protocol failed. Check the Warnings and Details section if the protocol completes with warnings. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| subfolders | There is a subfolder for each input antibody, containing the annotated molecule in a .mol2 file and the predicted paratope residues in a .csv file. |

A summary report includes a table, one row per input protein, with links to the annotated antibodies and the predicted paratope residue tables. 
Click the molecule link to load the antibody into the Molecule Window, showing the antibody atoms in CPK and spectrum color with paratope residues in red. 
Two groups of paratope residues are created: one with residues above the Paratope Cutoff parameter value, and another with residues that have a paratope score > 0.

# Predict Excipient Interactions - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsmacromolecules

Source file: tsmacromolecules/protein_modeling_predict_excipient_interactions-para.htm

## Predict Excipient Interactions - Parameters

### Predicts antibody-excipient preferential interactions using machine learning models

The properties of candidate therapeutic antibodies which are important for formulation such as solubility, viscosity and aggregation can be affected by the presence of various common excipients in the solution. In particular, the tendency of excipients to be preferentially included or excluded at hydrophobic or charged surface sites may be particularly important.

The preferential interaction coefficients can be calculated using molecular dynamics simulations. However, these are computationally expensive. Therefore, a method using such results to generate machine learning models which can quickly predict the interactions has been developed. The results are qualitatively similar to those from the MD calculations. This work is described in detail in the references below.

This protocol performs predictions using the same methodology. In addition to the excipient interaction predictions, the Aggregation Propensity and Charge Maps are calculated so that the excipient interactions at sites with high aggregation or surface charge can be assessed.

See Also:

* Cloutier, T.K.; Sudrik, C.; Mody, N.; Sathish, H.A. and Trout, B.L., Machine Learning Models of Antibody-Excipient Preferential Interactions for Use in Computational Formulation Design. Mol. Pharmaceutics. 2020 , 17 (9) , 3589-3599.

* Cloutier, T.K.; Sudrik, C.; Mody, N.; Sathish, H.A. and Trout, B.L., Molecular Computations of Preferential Interaction Coefficients of IgG1 Monoclonal Antibodies with Sorbitol, Sucrose, and Trehalose and the Impact of These Excipients on Aggregation and Viscosity. Mol. Pharmaceutics. 2019 , 16 (8) ,3657-3664.

* Cloutier, T.K.; Sudrik, C.; Mody, N.; Sathish, H.A.; Trout, B.L.,
Molecular computations of preferential interactions of Proline, arginine.HCl, and NaCl with IgG1 antibodies and their impact on aggregation and viscosity. Mabs. 2020 , 12 (1) .

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Proteins | In Pipeline Pilot, specify one or more protein structure files. Supported file formats include PDB, DSV, MSV, and MOL2. In Discovery Studio, choose All, Selected or Visible protein molecules in the active window or Browse for protein structure files. Supported forcefields for the calculations are CHARMm and charmm36. The input molecules that are not typed or typed with another forcefield will be typed or re-typed automatically. Use the Forcefield parameter to select one of the supported forcefields. Although the input can be any type of protein, it should be noted that the machine learning models were trained using target values calculated for antibody structures. |
| Prediction Method | The machine learning prediction method to use. The options are: SVM: Support Vector Machine. EN: Elastic Network. The EN and SVM models were implemented using the ElasticNet and SVR functions in scikit-learn using the methods for choosing hyperparameters and performing validation described in Cloutier et al 2020. The models were trained on a subset of the published data excluding those derived from proprietary sequences (~18,600 residues) and a slightly smaller feature set (175 features); the shape index features were omitted as they are computationally demanding but did not appear to contribute significantly to the models. See Also: Cloutier, T.K.; Sudrik, C.; Mody, N.; Sathish, H.A. and Trout, B.L., Machine Learning Models of Antibody-Excipient Preferential Interactions for Use in Computational Formulation Design. Mol. Pharmaceutics. 2020 , 17 (9) , 3589-3599. * SVM: Support Vector Machine.

* EN: Elastic Network.

The EN and SVM models were implemented using the ElasticNet and SVR functions in scikit-learn using the methods for choosing hyperparameters and performing validation described in Cloutier et al 2020. The models were trained on a subset of the published data excluding those derived from proprietary sequences (~18,600 residues) and a slightly smaller feature set (175 features); the shape index features were omitted as they are computationally demanding but did not appear to contribute significantly to the models.

* Pedregosa, F.; Varoquaux, G.; Gramfort, A.; Michel, V.; Thirion, B.; Grisel, O.; Blondel, M.; Prettenhofer, P.; Weiss, R.; Dubourg, V.; Vanderplas, J., Scikit-learn: Machine learning in Python. J. Mach. Learn. Res. 2011 , 12 , 2825-2830.

Valid Values: SVM , EN

# Predict Excipient Interactions

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsmacromolecules

Source file: tsmacromolecules/protein_modeling_predict_excipient_interactions.htm

## Predict Excipient Interactions

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

The properties of candidate therapeutic antibodies, which are important for formulation such as solubility, viscosity and aggregation, can be affected by the presence of various common excipients in the solution.
In particular, the tendency of excipients to be preferentially included or excluded at hydrophobic or charged surface sites may be particularly important [Cloutier et al., 2019] , [Cloutier et al., 2020a] . The preferential interaction coefficients can be calculated using molecular dynamics simulations, but such calculations are computationally expensive. Therefore, a method has been developed using such results to generate machine learning models that can quickly predict the interactions. The results are qualitatively similar to those from the MD calculations. This work is described in detail in published work [Cloutier et al., 2020b] . The Predict Excipient Interactions protocol makes predictions using this methodology. In addition to the excipient interaction predictions, the Aggregation Propensity and Charge Maps are calculated so that the excipient interactions at sites with high aggregation or surface charge can be assessed. Although the protocol can be run on any type of protein structure, it should be noted that the machine learning models were trained and validated using target values calculated for antibody structures. Setting up and running Load one or more protein structures into the Graphics View . Ensure that antibody structures consist of one biological domain such as a Fv or Fab region, or a full-length structure. Use the Prepare Protein tools to clean the protein structures and protonate them with the required pH and other solution conditions. You can run the Prepare Proteins protocol to do this automatically. Alternatively, set the preferences in the Clean Protein subpage - Preferences dialog dialog so that the Clean Protein tool will remove alternate conformations, add termini, and patch missing side-chain atoms, and then run the tool. Use the Calculate Protein Ionization and Residue pK protocol to protonate at the appropriate pH. Open the Macromolecules | Predict Protein Formulation Properties tools and click Predict Excipient Interactions... to open the Predict Excipient Interactions dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer . Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Protein Molecules Choose the proteins for the calculation. Display Colors Specify whether to display the results using normalized values or not. For details about the remaining parameters, see Predict Excipient Interactions - Parameters . Click Run to start the calculation. The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer . Analyzing results When the interactive job finishes, a Report window opens. Click View Results to open the result structures in one Molecule Window. The calculated feature values and the predicted preferential interaction coefficients for all excipients can be viewed in the AminoAcid tab of the Data Table. The report includes a table of clickable links which display detailed results and individual structures. The Molecule Windows opened contain tiled copies of the structure, each with a surface and atoms colored by aggregation scores, charge map scores, or excipient preferential interaction coefficients. The tiled copies are transformed synchronously, allowing the different properties to be compared. Aggregation Propensity Surface: This surface is colored according to atomic aggregation scores. The regions predicted to be more susceptible to aggregation are red. You can perform a detailed analysis of the Aggregation Sites using the View Aggregation Sites viewing tools on the Predict Protein Formulation Properties tools panel. Charge Map Surface: This surface is colored according to surface charge map scores (QMap R10 Score property on the Atom tab of the Data Table). For antibody structures, negative electrostatic patches on the Fv region, which correlate with higher viscosity, are red.
Additionally, the Hierarchy View contains groups for QMap R10 Sites and Negative QMap R10 Sites. You can select and focus using standard Discovery Studio functionality. The surface is transparent and the atoms are also colored using the QMap R10 property to facilitate analysis of the site groups. Excipient Surface: The surface is colored according to the excipient coefficients, with areas of inclusion red and exclusion blue. Sites of high inclusion are created as groups on the Hierarchy View . If the All SVM/EN Predictions link is used, then a copy is created for each excipient type. A second table contains links that generate different types of plots. They require that a molecule containing excipient, aggregation, and charge map properties is active in Discovery Studio . The plots are created only for the first visible molecule so that they do not repeat the same data when used with the windows containing tiled copies of the same molecule. Toggling the visibility of molecules updates the plot accordingly. If you ran the job in the background, expand the results in the
Jobs Explorer, click the Report link, and then click View Results to open the result structures in one window, or click the table links to open individual structures with surfaces. To further investigate aggregation sites and aggregation propensity scores, 
refer to the Calculate Aggregation Scores section of the Predict Protein Formulation Properties tools panel. Troubleshooting If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory: File name Description Report.htm Job summary including tabulated results, links to display detailed reports and individual structures, input and output files and the parameters used. Output.log Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. ViewMolecules.ds_pl Script which opens a Molecule Window in Discovery Studio containing all the structures for which the excipient values could be predicted. AllPredictedValues.csv A comma separated value file containing all of the predicted excipient interaction coefficients for all molecules. AllResidueFeatures.csv A comma separated value file containing all of the residue feature values for all molecules. The Output directory also contains a subfolder for each input molecule, containing the output structures and detailed properties. The PlotScripts folder contains scripts which allow various plots to be created for molecules opened in Discovery Studio . Further information Theory - Excipient Interactions Predict Protein Formulation Properties tools Predict Excipient Interactions - Parameters

In particular, the tendency of excipients to be preferentially included or excluded at hydrophobic or charged surface sites may be particularly important [Cloutier et al., 2019] , [Cloutier et al., 2020a] .

The preferential interaction coefficients can be calculated using molecular dynamics simulations, but such calculations are computationally expensive. Therefore, a method has been developed using such results to generate machine learning models that can quickly predict the interactions. The results are qualitatively similar to those from the MD calculations. This work is described in detail in published work [Cloutier et al., 2020b] .

The Predict Excipient Interactions protocol makes predictions using this methodology. In addition to the excipient interaction predictions, the Aggregation Propensity and Charge Maps are calculated so that the excipient interactions at sites with high aggregation or surface charge can be assessed.

* Although the protocol can be run on any type of protein structure, it should be noted that the machine learning models were trained and validated using target values calculated for antibody structures.

* Use the Prepare Protein tools to clean the protein structures and protonate them with the required pH and other solution conditions. You can run the Prepare Proteins protocol to do this automatically. Alternatively, set the preferences in the Clean Protein subpage - Preferences dialog dialog so that the Clean Protein tool will remove alternate conformations, add termini, and patch missing side-chain atoms, and then run the tool. | --- | --- |

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

When the interactive job finishes, a Report window opens. Click View Results to open the result structures in one Molecule Window. The calculated feature values and the predicted preferential interaction coefficients for all excipients can be viewed in the AminoAcid tab of the Data Table.

The report includes a table of clickable links which display detailed results and individual structures. The Molecule Windows opened contain tiled copies of the structure, each with a surface and atoms colored by aggregation scores, charge map scores, or excipient preferential interaction coefficients. The tiled copies are transformed synchronously, allowing the different properties to be compared.

* Aggregation Propensity Surface: This surface is colored according to atomic aggregation scores. The regions predicted to be more susceptible to aggregation are red. You can perform a detailed analysis of the Aggregation Sites using the View Aggregation Sites viewing tools on the Predict Protein Formulation Properties tools panel.
