# Common Feature Pharmacophore Generation

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_common_feature_pharmacophore_generation.htm

## Common Feature Pharmacophore Generation

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

The Common Feature Pharmacophore Generation protocol generates
pharmacophores that are common to a set of active ligands. Optionally,
it can add excluded volumes to the pharmacophores based on
information from a set of inactive ligands.

In the Data Table , you can add the molecular property Principal to the molecules to set a value to make it
active ( 2 ), moderately active ( 1 ), or inactive ( 0 ).
You can also add the
molecular property MaxOmitFeat to indicate how many features are allowed
to miss for each molecule. If no values are set for these properties, the default value for all molecules for Principal is 2 and for MaxOmitFeat is 0 .

To ensure proper exploration of the ligand conformational and pharmacophoric space,
run the Generate Conformations protocol before running this protocol. You can also generate the conformations on-the-fly using the Conformation Generation parameter and associated parameters.

#### Set up a Common Feature Pharmacophore Generation protocol run

* Ensure that the input ligands have Principal (representing the ligand's activity) and MaxOmitFeat (indicates how many features are allowed to miss for each molecule) properties. If the properties are not present in the data, add them to the molecules by right-clicking the Data Table View and choosing Add Attribute : Set Principal to indicate activity as follows: Active= 2 , Moderately Active= 1 , or Inactive= 0 . Set MaxOmitFeat to indicate how many features are allowed to miss for each molecule. If no values are set for these properties, the default value for all molecules for Principal is 2 and MaxOmitFeat is 0 .

* Set Principal to indicate activity as follows: Active= 2 , Moderately Active= 1 , or Inactive= 0 .

* Set MaxOmitFeat to indicate how many features are allowed to miss for each molecule.

If no values are set for these properties, the default value for all molecules for Principal is 2 and MaxOmitFeat is 0 .

* Open the Pharmacophores | Create a Pharmacophore Automatically tools and click Common Feature Pharmacophore Generation to open the Common Feature Pharmacophore Generation dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the Input Ligands . For details, see Specifying Ligands .

* Set the pharmacophore Features . You can
select the desired pharmacophore features and the minimum and
maximum values desired for the final pharmacophores. For details about the remaining parameters, see Common Feature Pharmacophore Generation - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

#### Set up a Common Feature Pharmacophore Generation protocol with the inclusion of excluded volumes

* Set the molecular properties in the input ligands as above.

* Specify the maximum number of excluded volumes to be added to a pharmacophore using the Maximum Excluded Volumes parameter.

* The Input Ligands must also include a set of inactive molecules when attempting to
add excluded volumes. Set the Principal value to 0 for all the inactive
molecules. If the Principal property is not set, all ligands are automatically
assigned a Principal value of 2 (active).

* The MaxOmitFeat molecular
property also serves a purpose for inactive molecules when identifying
candidate excluded volume locations. A value of 1 means that all mappings where
either all n or a subset of n-1 features will be considered. For more
complicated data sets, it may be better to set MaxOmitFeat to 0 for the
inactive molecules to avoid placing too many excluded volumes.

* If using
the Maximum Excluded Volumes parameter, we recommend using a value of 100 .

* If the ligand source is a Graphics View of molecules that contain conformations (for example, created by importing .cpd files), only a single conformation is
employed in the protocol for each molecule. If you intend to use all conformations,
you should convert .cpd files to the .sd file format before importing them into
the application.

For details about interpreting the log file generated by this protocol, see Analyzing Common Feature Pharmacophore Log Files .

#### Troubleshooting

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| Query_N.ds_chm | Contains pharmacophore models generated by the algorithm, where N is the corresponding model ranked by the cost values. |
| Query_N.sd | Contains the input ligands aligned to the corresponding pharmacophore model. |
| ViewResults_N.ds_pl | Opening this file will show the input ligands aligned to the corresponding (N) pharmacophore. |
| Query.log | A log file generated during the run. For details about interpreting the log file, see Analyzing Common Feature Pharmacophore Log Files . |
| Query_full.log | A more extensive log file that is generated during the run. |

#### Further information

Run a parallel calculation Distributed grid computing Adding Molecular Data using Add Attribute Theory - Generating common feature pharmacophores

# Create 3D Fingerprints - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_create_3d_fingerprints-para.htm

## Create 3D Fingerprints - Parameters

### Generates 3 or 4-point pharmacophore fingerprints from ligands or pharmacophores

Identifies all feature locations and enumerates all 3 or 4-point fingerprints according to the binning methods. All conformations of ligands in the input are used. The input can be a 3D database or a pre-calculated set of ligand conformations. Optionally ligand conformations can be generated on-the-fly. Alternatively a fingerprint can be identified from an existing pharmacophore.

The fingerprints are stored as an array of "on bits" for each molecule (optionally, each conformation) or pharmacophore. They can be used in any protocol that uses fingerprints. For example: Create Bayesian Model and Find Similar Molecules by Fingerprints.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Type | Three types of input are provided: Database: a set of compounds from the database. Ligands: a set of compounds from an MDL MOL/SD file, or a Molecule window. Pharmacophore: a chemical feature pharmacophore model. Valid Values: Database, Ligands , Pharmacophore |
| Input Database | Database to perform search on, specified by its Catalyst database (.bdb) file. All database files are located in $PipelinePilot_Install_Directory/public/DS/CatalystDB on the server. Each database file is in a separate folder with the same name as the database. |
| Input Database Maximum | The maximum number of molecules to read from the database. |
| All Conformations | Read all conformations of the molecules from the database for fingerprint generation. Valid Values: True, False |
| Input Ligands | Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. |
| Conformation Generation | Each molecule in Input Ligands must have a good set of conformations. If they are not present, then three conformer generation algorithms can be used: FAST: quickly provides diverse low-energy conformations. BEST: ensures the best coverage of conformational space (requires more CPU time). CAESAR: very quickly provides conformations by sampling torsions. Valid Values: NONE , FAST, BEST, CAESAR |
| Maximum Conformations | Maximum number of conformations to be generated. |
| Discard Existing Conformations | If True, discard existing input conformations, otherwise use all existing input conformations. Valid Values: True , False |
| Energy Threshold | Conformations are created within this relative energy threshold (kcal/mol). For a molecule with stereo isomers, this threshold applies to conformations for each individual isomer. |
| Ring Fragments File | File (fragments.data) that contains the ring conformations to use. The Catalyst Ring Fragment Writer component can be used to generate the file. Molecules that contain rings also found in the file will only use these ring conformations. Conformations for rings not found in the file are generated from scratch. Note: Only FAST and CAESAR will use this file. It have no effect on other methods. By default this parameter is blank and all ring conformations are generated from scratch. |
| Save Conformations | Save the generated conformations in a MDL MOL/SD file. Valid Values: True, False |
| Parallel Processing | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. Valid Values: True, False |
| Parallel Processing Batch Size | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. |
| Parallel Processing Server | Comma separated list of servers (server-name:port-number) to be used for parallel processing. Add "localhost" to include the local server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where "localhost" requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster). |
| Parallel Processing Server Processes | Comma separated list of the maximum batches that can be simultaneously executed on each server. Each value must correspond with an entry in the list of servers. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. |
| Parallel Processing Preserve Order | Preserve the initial order of the data records. Valid Values: True , False |
| Input Pharmacophore | The Catalyst pharmacophore to generate 3D fingerprints from. In Discovery Studio, this can be a query in a Molecule Window or a ds_chm file. |
| Pharmacophore Features | The pharmacophore features for which mappings are to be returned for 3D fingerprint generation. A standard set of features can be used to create fingerprints. In addition, up to 3 customized pharmacophore features can be used to compute the fingerprints. Customized features that are named CUSTOM_X, CUSTOM_Y, or CUSTOM_Z can be used if they have been created. Use the Customize Pharmacophore Features tool to create customized features. The standard (predefined)features are: HB_ACCEPTOR HB_ACCEPTOR_lipid HB_DONOR HYDROPHOBIC HYDROPHOBIC_aromatic HYDROPHOBIC_aliphatic NEG_CHARGE NEG_IONIZABLE POS_CHARGE POS_IONIZABLE RING_AROMATIC In Discovery Studio, a dialog lists the predefined features as well as any customized features. Customized features can be built using the Customize Pharmacophore Features tool. Features created by this tool are written to a dictionary file located at: [Settings Folder]/Catalyst/conf/Dictionary.ds_chm In Pipeline Pilot, when using customized features you must also set the location of the Dictionary.ds_chm that contains the definition of the customized feature using the CustomDictionary implementation parameter. Valid Values: HB_ACCEPTOR , HB_ACCEPTOR_projection, HB_DONOR , HB_DONOR_projection, HYDROPHOBIC , NEG_IONIZABLE, NEG_CHARGE, POS_IONIZABLE, POS_CHARGE, RING_AROMATIC, RING_AROMATIC_projection, CUSTOM_X, CUSTOM_Y, CUSTOM_Z |

## Create 3D Fingerprints

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Output and input files

The Create 3D Fingerprints protocol computes all possible feature locations from the inputs and uses the information to build 3-point or 4-point
pharmacophore fingerprints. The input can be a ligand database built using the Build 3D Database protocol, a set of ligands, or a set of pharmacophore
features. The fingerprints are stored as an array of on bits for each molecule or, optionally, each conformation. For more information about working with 3D Fingerprints, see Tasks - 3D Fingerprints .

* In the Protocols Explorer , open Pharmacophore | Create 3D Fingerprints .

* In the Parameters Explorer, set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Type Choose from Database , Ligands , and Pharmacophore . Input Database If the Input Type is Database , choose a database. Input Ligands If the Input Type is Ligands , select the ligands. For details, see Specifying Ligands . Input Pharmacophore If the Input Type is Pharmacophore , select a pharmacophore. Click the button to select the query from a Molecule Window or a file. Pharmacophore Features Pharmacophore features for which mappings are to be returned for 3D fingerprint generation. For details about the remaining parameters, see Create 3D Fingerprints - Parameters .

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Type | Choose from Database , Ligands , and Pharmacophore . |
| Input Database | If the Input Type is Database , choose a database. |
| Input Ligands | If the Input Type is Ligands , select the ligands. For details, see Specifying Ligands . |
| Input Pharmacophore | If the Input Type is Pharmacophore , select a pharmacophore. Click the button to select the query from a Molecule Window or a file. |
| Pharmacophore Features | Pharmacophore features for which mappings are to be returned for 3D fingerprint generation. |

For details about the remaining parameters, see Create 3D Fingerprints - Parameters .

* In the Protocols menu bar, click the Run button.

* Monitor the status in the Jobs Explorer .

When the job finishes, double-click it in the Jobs Explorer to open the Output folder in the Files Explorer. See Output and input files for details about the files generated by this protocol. If the job did not run successfully, the Jobs Explorer will report an error. See Troubleshooting - Protocols for details.

By default, intermediate files generated by this protocol are not saved. To save the intermediate files, select the Save intermediate files when running protocols option on the Protocols page of the Preferences dialog.

#### Output files

The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| Output.sd | Contains the conformation of ligands with 3D fingerprint property. This file can be generated when the Input Type parameter is Database or Ligands . |
| Output_fail.sd | Contains the molecules failed in 3D fingerprint generation. This file can only be generated when the Input Type parameter is Database or Ligands . |
| queryFP.sd | Contains the fingerprints of the input query. This file can only be generated when the Input Type parameter is Pharmacophore . |

#### Input files

The following files are created in the Input directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Dictionary.ds_chm | The feature dictionary used for 3D fingerprint generation. |
| Query.ds_chm | The input 3D query for 3D fingerprint generation. This file is only generated when the Input Type parameter is Pharmacophore . |
| Protocol.pr_xml | The saved protocol and job parameters. You can load this file at any time to re-run this protocol with the same settings. You can also share it with other users. For details see Discovery Studio Parameters (PR_XML) . |

## Create Features from SMARTS - Parameters

### Converts SMARTS to substructure queries

Each SMARTS listed in the SMARTS parameter is converted to a substructure query. These queries can be used for many different purposes (e.g. you can search a database using Search 3D Database or you can assemble the substructure queries to create a customized feature using the Customize Pharmacophore Features tool in Discovery Studio).

Notes:

* Recursive SMARTS, such as A[#6;!$(C(F)(F)F)] are not supported.

* Reaction SMARTS, such as C>>C are not supported.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| SMARTS | A series of SMARTS strings. Each line should contain 2 TAB-delimited columns Valid SMARTS pattern Name for the SMARTS pattern Each SMARTS in the series is converted to a substructure type pharmacophore query. These queries can be used for many different purposes (e.g. you can search a database using the Search 3D Database protocol or you can assemble the substructure queries to create a customized feature using the Customize Pharmacophore Features tool). |

* Valid SMARTS pattern

* Name for the SMARTS pattern

Source section: tspharmacophores

## Create Features from SMARTS

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

The Create Features from SMARTS protocol generates a substructure type pharmacophore query
from each input SMARTS entry. These queries can be used for many different purposes. For example,
you can search a database using the Search 3D Database protocol or you can assemble the substructure queries to create a customized feature using
the Customize Pharmacophore Features tool.

Known limitations:

* Recursive SMARTS, such as A[#6;!$(C(F)(F)F)] are not supported.

* Reaction SMARTS, such as C>>C are not supported.

* Open the Pharmacophores | Customize Pharmacophore Features tools and click Create Features from SMARTS to open the Create Features from SMARTS dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

you want to use to create substructure pharmacophore queries.

# Ensemble Pharmacophore Generation - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_ensemble_pharmacophore_generation-para.htm

## Ensemble Pharmacophore Generation - Parameters

### Generates ensemble pharmacophore models

Uses HipHop to generate an ensemble of common feature pharmacophores from the Input Active Ligands .

The Input Active Ligands are clustered using fingerprints. Each cluster is then used to generate pharmacophore models.
In the next step, the Input Active Ligands and Input Inactive Ligands are screened against all pharmacophores to find the best pharmacophore for that cluster. A ROC analysis table is generated with the data for each cluster.

The protocol contains the following steps:

* The Input Active Ligands are clustered using pharmacophore fingerprints.

* Pharmacophores are created for every cluster that has more than 10 members.

* Each pharmacophore is then screened against the Input Active Ligands in the cluster and the Input Inactive Ligands . Optionally, a table including all Input Active Ligands can be created.

* The top scoring pharmacophore for each cluster is reported (the score is calculated using the AUC ROC value).

Notes:

* HipHop is a program for identifying common pharmacophore features in an input set of lead compounds.

* Several statistics are presented in the results table for each pharmacophore, including true positives, true negatives, sensitivity, and selectivity. These properties are calculated using an optimum cutoff fit value (also listed in the table) for the pharmacophore. The cutoff fit value is selected so that the balanced accuracy (BA) is maximized: BA = (TP/P + TN/N) / 2 Where TP is true positives, P is total positives, TN is true negatives, and N is total negatives. The pharmacophore is updated with the cutoff as the minimum allowed fit. In future analysis, ligands that fit the pharmacophore below this cutoff value will be considered non-fitting ligands.

BA = (TP/P + TN/N) / 2

Where TP is true positives, P is total positives, TN is true negatives, and N is total negatives. The pharmacophore is updated with the cutoff as the minimum allowed fit. In future analysis, ligands that fit the pharmacophore below this cutoff value will be considered non-fitting ligands.

See Also:

* Barnum, D.; Greene, J.; Smellie, A.; Sprague, P. Identification of common functional configurations among molecules. J. Chem. Inf. Comput. Sci. 1996 , 36, 563-571.

# Ensemble Pharmacophore Generation

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_ensemble_pharmacophore_generation.htm

## Ensemble Pharmacophore Generation

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

The Ensemble Pharmacophore Generation protocol generates an ensemble of common feature pharmacophores from a set of active ligands. The active ligands are clustered using 2D fingerprints. For each cluster, 5 ligands are selected from the cluster center to create pharmacophores using the common feature pharmacophores algorithm. For each cluster the pharmacophore fit is calculated using the active ligands and the specified set inactive ligands. Subsequently, the best pharmacophore for each cluster is determined using ROC analysis. A detailed report is generated detailing the best pharmacophore and various statistical information for each cluster.

This protocol requires a set of active and inactive ligand structures as input.

* Open the Pharmacophores | From a Set of Ligands tools and click Ensemble Pharmacophore Generation to open the Ensemble Pharmacophore Generation dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Active Ligands Specify the ligand source. For details, see Specifying Ligands . Input Inactive Ligands Specify the inactive ligand source. For details, see Specifying Ligands . For details about the remaining parameters, see Ensemble Pharmacophore Generation - Parameters .

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Active Ligands | Specify the ligand source. For details, see Specifying Ligands . |
| Input Inactive Ligands | Specify the inactive ligand source. For details, see Specifying Ligands . |

For details about the remaining parameters, see Ensemble Pharmacophore Generation - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

After the run has been completed, a table in the report contains detailed information for each pharmacophore created. Several statistics are presented in the results table for each pharmacophore, including true positives, true negatives, sensitivity, and selectivity. These properties are calculated using an optimum cutoff fit value (also listed in the table) for the pharmacophore. The cutoff fit value is selected so that the balanced accuracy (BA) is maximized:

BA = (TP/P + TN/N) / 2

Where TP is true positives, P is total positives, TN is true negatives, and N is total negatives. The pharmacophore is updated with the cutoff as the minimum allowed fit. In future analysis, ligands that fit the pharmacophore below this cutoff value will be considered non-fitting ligands.

#### Troubleshooting

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| ViewResults.ds_pl | This file is a script that allows you to view a table with the pharmacophore clusters. |
| EnsembleP4Results.htm | Detailed report for each cluster containing statistical analysis data. |

# Enumerate from Fragments - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_enumerate_from_fragments-para.htm

## Enumerate from Fragments - Parameters

### Creates ligands by joining a set of aligned fragments

Joins fragments with close atoms to create larger molecules. A minimum of two fragments is required, and a maximum of three fragments is allowed. The protocol is intended to be used to create de novo combinatorial libraries from the results of fragment-based approaches.

The closest atoms between fragments from each source are fused, linking the fragments together. If the link atoms are different, both variations are enumerated. This produces a resulting library containing all combinations of assembled fragments and all link site variations.

The resulting ligands are standardized as follows:

* Molecules are neutralized.

* Hydrogens are adjusted accordingly.

* Bad valence filter is applied.

* Molecules that pass the filters are minimized using the Clean forcefield. The property Minimized_Energy contains the value of the energy at the end of the minimization.

You can optionally remove poor high throughput screening (HTS) candidates. You can also build a 3D database from the results.

See Also:

* For more information about the Clean forcefield see, Hahn, M. Receptor Surface Models. 1. Definition and Construction. J. Med. Chem. 1995 , 38(12), 2080-2090.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Fragment A | Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. |
| Fragment B | Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. |
| Fragment C | Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. |
| Library Name | Name used for the output MDL MOL/SD file and the multi-conformation ligand database if built using Build 3D Database from Results . |
| Apply HTS Filter | Molecules are removed from the final set that are likely to be poor candidates for high-throughput screening. Molecules that are removed include those containing non-organic atom types, reactive substructures, and those with a molecular weight < 150. Valid Values: True , False |
| Build 3D Database from Results | Uses Catalyst to build a multi-conformation ligand database using the merged fragments as input. The database will be named using the value set in the Library Name parameter. Valid Values: True, False |
| Conformation Method | Algorithm for generating conformations: FAST: quickly provides diverse low-energy conformations. BEST: ensures the best coverage of conformational space (requires more CPU time). CAESAR: very quickly provides conformations by sampling torsions. Valid Values: FAST , BEST, CAESAR |

* Description

## Feature Mapping

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

The Feature Mapping protocol computes all possible pharmacophore feature mappings for selected ligands and features. A maximum of 1000 pharmacophore features will be enumerated.

* Open the Pharmacophores | Edit and Cluster Features tools and click Feature Mapping to open the Feature Mapping dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Ligands Specify the ligands to be used by the protocol. For details, see Specifying Ligands . Features Predefined or customized pharmacophore features. For details about the remaining parameters, see Feature Mapping - Parameters .

| --- | --- |

| Features | Predefined or customized pharmacophore features. |

For details about the remaining parameters, see Feature Mapping - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

The solvent-accessible pharmacophore features are added to the Graphics View aligned to the input ligands. You can use the Pharmacophore tools to:

* Create a template pharmacophore from the features

* Cluster the features to create a pharmacophore

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

# Interaction Generation - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_interaction_generation-para.htm

## Interaction Generation - Parameters

### Enumerates pharmacophore features from a protein active site

Creates a pharmacophore query from a Ludi interaction map.

The interaction map is created in a receptor active site sphere and consists of hydrogen bond acceptor, hydrogen bond donor, and hydrophobic features.

See Also:

* Böhm, H. J. The computer program LUDI: A new method for the de novo design of enzyme inhibitors. J. Comput.-Aided Mol. Design 1992 , 6, 61-78.

* Böhm, H. J. LUDI: rule based automatic design of new substituents for enzyme inhibitor leads. J. Comput.-Aided Mol. Design 1992 , 6, 593-606.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Receptor | Structure to use as the receptor. Ensure receptors have hydrogens and complete valence shells. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all visible molecules. Notes: The receptor should not contain alternate conformations. You can use the protein tools in Discovery Studio to prepare a receptor. |
| Input Site Sphere | Defines a sphere in the receptor where receptor-ligands interactions are permitted. In Pipeline Pilot, define the sphere as x,y,z,r where x,y,z specifies the coordinates of the center and r is the radius of the sphere ( e.g. , 83.2,-43.3,42.24,6). In Discovery Studio, define the sphere using the Define and Edit Binding Site tools and then select the coordinates from the list. |
| Density of Lipophilic Sites | When Ludi creates an interaction map, it populates the site with points or vectors that represent the geometry of the site. This parameter specifies how dense Ludi should make the population of points in interaction sites for lipophilic atoms. A higher value increases the complexity of the pharmacophore query. |
| Density of Polar Sites | When Ludi creates an interaction map, it populates the site with points or vectors that represent the geometry of the site. This parameter specifies how dense Ludi should make the population of vectors in interaction sites for hydrogen bonds. A higher value increases the complexity of the pharmacophore query. |

In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all visible molecules.

Notes:

* You can use the protein tools in Discovery Studio to prepare a receptor.

In Discovery Studio, define the sphere using the Define and Edit Binding Site tools and then select the coordinates from the list.

# Interaction Pharmacophore Generation - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_interaction_pharmacophore_generation-para.htm

## Interaction Pharmacophore Generation - Parameters

### Generates non-bond interaction pharmacophore models

Uses the non-bond interactions between the Input Receptor and the Input Ligand to enumerate pharmacophores. 
The pharmacophores are ranked with a GFA (Genetic Function Approximation) model, and the top pharmacophores containing Minimum Features to Maximum Features are reported.

See Also:

* For more information on non-bond interactions theory, please consult the Discovery Studio help.

* Meslamani, J.; Li, J.; Sutter, J.; Stevens, A.; Bertrand, H.-O.; Rognan, D., 
Protein-Ligand-Based Pharmacophores: Generation and Utility Assessment in Computational Ligand Profiling, J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2012 , 52(4) 943-955.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Receptor | Structure to use as the receptor binding to a ligand. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all visible molecules. Notes: The receptor should not contain alternate conformations. You can use the protein tools in Discovery Studio to remove alternative conformations. |
| Input Ligand | Structure to use as the ligand binding to a receptor. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all visible molecules. |
| Rotated Atoms Property | Name of a property which contains the flexible receptor atom coordinates. For example, after running ligand minimization with flexible receptor atoms or residues, a property named "Receptor.Positions" will be created for each of the flexible receptor atoms with the 3D coordinate in the following format: X1 Y1 Z1 atno AtomIndex1 X2 Y2 Z2 atno AtomIndex2 If this property is not found in the input ligands, it will be ignored and rigid receptor will be used in the calculation. Note : The flexible atom property will no longer be valid after changing the receptor atom order (such as after typing). |
| Maximum Pharmacophores | The maximum number of the best scoring pharmacophores to retain. |
| Minimum Features | Minimum number of features required in each pharmacophore. |
| Maximum Features | Maximum number of features permitted in each pharmacophore. |
| Pharmacophore Scoring Method | Method used to score and rank the top pharmacophores: Diverse: The top pharmacophore is selected based on the GFA model score that predicts selectivity. The remaining pharmacophores are selected based on the maximum distance from the previously placed pharmacophores. Top Scoring: All pharmacophores are scored using the GFA model and the top Export Top N Pharmacophores pharmacophores are selected. Valid Values: Diverse , Top Scoring |
| Validation | Validation of the generated pharmacophore models using active/inactive ligands. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves as well as optimal cutoff values are reported. Evaluate the pharmacophore model by reviewing the area of the ROC curve (AUC). A value closer to 1 indicates good selectivity, whereas a value closer to 0.5 indicates random selection. The cutoff indicates the best pharmacophore fit value that gives the highest accuracy as calculated by the following equation: (TP+TN)/(TP+TN+FP+FN) where: TP: number of true positives TN: number of true negatives FP: number of false positives FN: number of false negatives Valid Values: True, False |
| Active Ligands | Input data set of active ligands for validation. Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. |
| Inactive Ligands | Input data set of inactive ligands for validation. Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. |
| Conformation Generation | Each molecule in Active Ligands and Inactive Ligands must have a good set of conformations. If they are not present in the input data, they can be added using one of the following algorithms: FAST: quickly provides diverse low-energy conformations. BEST: ensures the best coverage of conformational space (requires more CPU time). CAESAR: very quickly provides conformations by sampling torsions. NONE: uses existing conformations. Valid Values: NONE, FAST , BEST, CAESAR |
| Maximum Conformations | Maximum number of conformations for each ligand to be generated for validation. |
| Discard Existing Conformations | Discard existing conformations for conformation generation in validation. Valid Values: True , False |
| Ring Fragments File | File (fragments.data) that contains the ring conformations to use. The Catalyst Ring Fragment Writer component can be used to generate the file. Molecules that contain rings also found in the file will only use these ring conformations. Conformations for rings not found in the file are generated from scratch. Note: Only FAST and CAESAR will use this file. It have no effect on other methods. By default this parameter is blank and all ring conformations are generated from scratch. |
| Energy Threshold | Conformations are created within this relative energy threshold (kcal/mol). For a molecule with stereo isomers, this threshold applies to conformations for each individual isomer. |
| Fitting Method | Choose the type of fitting to use: Rigid: Performs rigid fit between ligand and pharmacophore. Flexible: Each conformation of the ligand may be slightly modified to better fit the pharmacophore. Valid Values: Rigid , Flexible |
| Maximum Omitted Features | The maximum number of features that are allowed to miss when mapping the ligand to the pharmacophore. A value of -1 has special meaning: It instructs the server to consider all feature subsets of the pharmacophore. It is equivalent to n-1 , where n is the total number of features in the pharmacophore. For a pharmacophore with 5 features, -1 allows up to 4 features to miss. The number of subsets grows very quickly as the total number of features in the pharmacophore increases. To avoid excessive memory use and calculation time, Maximum Omitted Features is limited in the fitting calculation (not the client): Total Features = 1-6: Maximum Omitted Features limited to (Total Features - 1) or less Total Features = 7-9: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 4 or less Total Features = 10: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 3 or less Total Features = 11-19: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 2 or less Total Features = 20+: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 1 or less |
| Advanced | Contains less commonly used parameters. |
| Minimum Interfeature Distance | Minimum distance between features in Å. |
| Steric Features | The type of features to use for modeling the steric contribution of the pharmacophore. The choices are: Shape : Uses the input ligand to create a shape constraint. Excluded Volumes : Uses the location of protein atoms to create exclusion volumes around a ligand. Atoms with a distance larger than the Maximum Exclusion Volume Distance value to the nearest ligand atom will be ignored. None : Does not provide a steric contribution for the pharmacophore. Valid Values: Shape, Excluded Volumes , None |
| Minimum Shape Similarity | Shape similarity threshold for the shape constraint of the generated pharmacophore. |
| Maximum Exclusion Volume Distance | Protein atoms with a distance larger than this to the nearest ligand atom will be ignored when placing excluded volumes. Note : A minimum distance cutoff of greater than 4.0 Å is required to avoid clashes. |
| Non-bond Interactions | Non-bond interactions to include when creating the features: conventionalHBondType - Conventional Hydrogen Bond carbonHBondType - Carbon Hydrogen Bond piDonorType - Pi Donor Hydrogen Bond saltBridgeType - Salt Bridge attractiveChargeType - Attractive Charges piCationType - Pi-Cation piAnionType - Pi-Anion piPiStackedType - Pi-Pi Stacked piPiTShapedType - Pi-Pi T-Shaped piAmideType - Amide-Pi Stacked alkylType - Alkyl piSigmaType - Pi-Sigma piAlkylType - Pi-Alkyl halogenFluorineType - Halogen (Fluorine) halogenClBrIType - Halogen (Cl, Br, I) metalAcceptorType - Metal-Acceptor sulfurType - Sulfur-X piSulfurType - Pi-Sulfur piLonePairType - Pi-Lone Pair Note : Please refer to the Discovery Studio theory for more information on the non-bond types. Valid Values: conventionalHBondType , carbonHBondType, piDonorType , saltBridgeType , attractiveChargeType , piCationType , piAnionType , piPiStackedType , piPiTShapedType , piAmideType , alkylType , piSigmaType , piAlkylType , halogenFluorineType , halogenClBrIType , metalAcceptorType , sulfurType , piSulfurType , piLonePairType |
| Use Custom Criteria | Use custom settings to control how non-bonded interactions are perceived. Valid Values: True, False |
| Use Custom Criteria Non-Bond Settings | Non-bonded criteria to control how non-bonded interactions are calculated. |
| Parallel Processing | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. Valid Values: True, False |

| Parallel Processing Server | Comma separated list of Pipeline Pilot servers (server-name:port-number) to be used for parallel processing. Add "localhost" to include the local server. # Interaction Pharmacophore Generation

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_interaction_pharmacophore_generation.htm

## Interaction Pharmacophore Generation

* Description

* Setting Up and Running

* Analyzing Results

The Interaction Pharmacophore Generation protocol generates a set of selective pharmacophore models from the non-bond interactions between a receptor and a ligand [Meslamani et. al, 2012] . The pharmacophore models are generated from features that correspond to the non-bond interactions. 
The following ligand features types are considered:

* Hydrogen Bond Acceptor

* Hydrogen Bond Acceptor (Salt)

* Hydrogen Bond Donor

* Hydrogen Bond Donor (Salt)

* Hydrogen Bond Donor (Carbon)

* Hydrophobic

* Hydrophobic Aromatic

* Negative Ionizable

* Positive Ionizable

* Ring Aromatic

* Halogen

* Fluorine

* Amide Group

* N, O, or S Interaction

* Sulfur Interaction

* Sigma Carbon

Candidate pharmacophore models are enumerated from the features. A set of pharmacophore models with the highest selectivity as predicted by a Genetic Function Approximation (GFA) model are selected.

This protocol requires a receptor and ligand structure as input.

* Load the receptor complex into the Graphics View .

* Load the ligand into the Graphics View .

* Open the Pharmacophores | Create Pharmacophore Automatically tools and click Interaction Pharmacophore Generation to open the Interaction Pharmacophore Generation dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set Input Ligand and Input Receptor .

* Set the remaining parameters as desired. For details, see Interaction Pharmacophore Generation - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

When the job is done, the generated pharmacophore models, the receptor, and ligand will be displayed in a new 3D Window. Only the first pharmacophore model is set visible. You can check other models by switching the visibility.

If the job ran in background mode, open Report.htm . To display the result, click the View Results button.

#### Troubleshooting

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <Input Ligand>.sd | Input ligand. |
| AllFeatures.ds_chm | All the pharmacophore features generated based on the receptor-ligand interactions. This pharmacophore contains all matching features and should not be used as the final pharmacophore since it will violate the minimum inter-feature distance constraints. |
| <PharmacophoreName>_<Number>.ds_chm | Generated pharmacophore models numbered according to their selectivity. |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. The number and types of pharmacophore features is reported for each pharmacophore. Depending on parameter settings, other analysis measures will be reported as well, such as ROC plots, sensitivity, specificity, the number of true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |

This pharmacophore contains all matching features and should not be used as the final pharmacophore since it will violate the minimum inter-feature distance constraints.

#### Further information

Interaction Pharmacophore Generation - Parameters Theory - Interaction Pharmacophore Generation Tutorial - Generating interaction pharmacophores from a protein-ligand complex

# Ligand Pharmacophore Mapping - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_ligand_pharmacophore_mapping-para.htm

## Ligand Pharmacophore Mapping - Parameters

### Maps and aligns ligands to a pharmacophore

Uses Catalyst to identify ligands that map to a pharmacophore, and aligns the ligands to the query. The pharmacophore can contain combinations of substructures, 3D constraints, features, shapes, excluded volumes, etc. Depending on the pharmacophore, additional properties may be added, these include:

* FitValue : A measure of how well the ligand fits the pharmacophore. The higher the fit score, the better the match.

* ShapeSimilarity : A value between zero and one that measures the overlap of the mapped conformation and the shape constraint.

* MappedAtoms : An array of atoms that map the pharmacophore in the format AtomIndex, X, Y, Z, Tolerance, Location feature name.

* {FeatureName}_fit : The contribution to the fit value for the named pharmacophore feature. A separate property exists for each pharmacophore feature.

* {FeatureName}_atom : The atom number that fits the named pharmacophore feature. A separate property exists for each pharmacophore feature.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Pharmacophore | Specify the pharmacophore model identified from a file in ds_chm format. In Discovery Studio, this may be identified either from a Molecule Window or from a file in ds_chm format. |
| NOT Features | Specify a pharmacophore model containing a feature or features that cannot be present after the ligand is aligned to Input Pharmacophore . Identified from a file in ds_chm format. In Discovery Studio, this may be identified either from a Molecule Window or from a file in ds_chm format. |
| Input Ligands | Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. |
| Conformation Generation | Each molecule in Input Ligands must have a good set of conformations. If they are not present in the input data, they can be added using one of the following algorithms: FAST: quickly provides diverse low-energy conformations. BEST: ensures the best coverage of conformational space (requires more CPU time). CAESAR: very quickly provides conformations by sampling torsions. NONE: uses existing conformations. Valid Values: NONE, FAST , BEST, CAESAR |
| Maximum Conformations | Maximum number of conformations to be generated. |
| Discard Existing Conformations | If True, discard existing input conformations, otherwise use all existing input conformations. Valid Values: True , False |
| Separate Conformations | If True, each record is treated separately (including enantiomers) and a set of conformations is generated for each record. If False, consecutive structures, which only differ in stereo-chemistry (e.g., enantiomers) are enumerated. Note : Set this option to True if you want to ensure that all ligands are enumerated, regardless of stereo-chemistry. Valid Values: True, False |
| Energy Threshold | Conformations are created within this relative energy threshold (kcal/mol). For a molecule with stereo isomers, this threshold applies to conformations for each individual isomer. |
| Ring Fragments File | File (fragments.data) that contains the ring conformations to use. The Catalyst Ring Fragment Writer component can be used to generate the file. Molecules that contain rings also found in the file will only use these ring conformations. Conformations for rings not found in the file are generated from scratch. Note: Only FAST and CAESAR will use this file. It have no effect on other methods. By default this parameter is blank and all ring conformations are generated from scratch. |
| Save Conformations | Save the generated conformations in a MDL MOL/SD file. Valid Values: True, False |
| Best Mapping Only | If True, only the best mapping for each ligand will be returned. Otherwise all mappings will be returned for each ligand. Choose the option of the best mapping: Fit most features: Find the fit that has the highest fit value, within the set that map the most features. Find highest fit: Find the fit that has the highest fit value. This fit may not match all features in the query. Valid Values: True , False |
| Options | Choose the option of the best mapping: Fit most features: Find the fit that has the highest fit value, within the set that map the most features. Find highest fit: Find the fit that has the highest fit value. This fit may not match all features in the query. Valid Values: Fit most features , Find highest fit |
| Maximum Omitted Features | The maximum number of features that are allowed to miss when mapping the ligand to the pharmacophore. A value of -1 has special meaning: It instructs the server to consider all feature subsets of the pharmacophore. It is equivalent to n-1 , where n is the total number of features in the pharmacophore. For a pharmacophore with 5 features, -1 allows up to 4 features to miss. The number of subsets grows very quickly as the total number of features in the pharmacophore increases. To avoid excessive memory use and calculation time, Maximum Omitted Features is limited in the fitting calculation (not the client): Total Features = 1-6: Maximum Omitted Features limited to (Total Features - 1) or less Total Features = 7-9: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 4 or less Total Features = 10: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 3 or less Total Features = 11-19: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 2 or less Total Features = 20+: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 1 or less |
| Fitting Method | Choose the type of fitting to use: Rigid: performs rigid fit between ligand and pharmacophore. Flexible: Each conformation of the ligand may be slightly modified to better fit the pharmacophore. Overlap: first finds the conformation with the highest fit score, then finds a conformation from each of the remaining ligands that fits the pharmacophore and is the best overlap with the first conformation. None: computes fit in current location. Does not transform the ligands. Valid Values: Rigid , Flexible, Overlap, None |
| Advanced | Contains less commonly used parameters. |
| Stereoisomers As Different Molecules | If True, each stereoisomer is treated as a different molecule. Valid Values: True, False |
| Input Type | Two types of input are supported: Ligands: a set of compounds from an MDL MOL/SD file, or a Molecule window. Database: a set of compounds from a Catalyst ligand database. Valid Values: Database, Ligands |
| Input Database | Database to perform search on, specified by its Catalyst database (.bdb) file. All database files are located in $PipelinePilot_Install_Directory/public/DS/CatalystDB on the server. Each database file is in a separate folder with the same name as the database. Either Input Ligands or Input Database must be specified. Note: Processing large databases requires significant disk space. During the protocol run, all conformations of all compounds in the database will be written to SD files in an intermediate directory. After they are processed, these files will be removed, unless the protocol is run in debug mode. |
| Input Database Limit Hits | Limit the number of hits returned First N: return the first N ligands All: return all ligands. Valid Values: First N, All |
| Input Database Maximum | The maximum number ( n ) of molecules to read from the database. All conformations of the first n molecules are read from the database and submitted to further analysis. There is no guarantee that these molecules will fit the pharmacophore features. If you would like to only extract molecules that fit some of the pharmacophore features, you can generate a hitlist using the Search 3D Database protocol for example. You can then use the Hitlist parameter to extract these molecules from the database. Note that each molecule that shares the same Name property with a ligand in the hitlist is extracted from the database including all its conformations. Conformations are not required to be in the ligands designated in the Hitlist parameter. Only the names are important. |
| Input Database Hitlist | Ligands in the database that have the same Names as these ligands will be extracted from the database. |
| Minimum Interfeature Distance | Minimum distance between features in Å. Default value is "2.0". A value of "0.0" will allow a single atom to map to multiple features. For example, an NH 2 group could match two hydrogen bond donor features depending on the surface accessibility of the ligand. |
| Map Each Conformation Separately | When mapping separate conformations, consecutive conformations of a molecule are each mapped to the ligand independently. Otherwise, consecutive conformations are mapped to the ligand as a single multi-conformation molecule. Mapping separate conformations retains the ConfNumber property. Valid Values: True, False |
| Property Names | Parameters to set the names of newly created properties. |
| Fit Name | Name to use for the "fit value" property. |
| Shape Name | Name to use for the "shape similarity" property. |
| Estimate Name | Name to use for the "activity estimate" property. |
| MapID Name | Name to use for the "mappingID" property. |
| Pharmprint Name | Name to use for the "pharmprint" property. |
| Pharmtype Name | Name to use for the "pharmtype" property. |
| Specify Energy Threshold | Specify the energy threshold for molecules (kcal/mol). Default is to use the energy threshold of the conformation model. Valid Values: True, False |
| Mapping Energy Threshold | The energy threshold for molecules (kcal/mol). |
| Output Non-Fitting Ligands | Output ligands that do not fit. Valid Values: True, False |
| Scale Fit Values | Scale fit values to 0.0 - 1.0 range. The weight values of each feature in the pharmacophore are summed to get the maximum fit (default is 1.0 per feature). OutputFit = Fit Value / Maximum Fit Value. Valid Values: True, False |
| Sort Fit Values | Sort molecules by FitValue and group them by Name . If FitValue is not defined, ShapeSimilarity is used. If neither is defined, sorting is skipped. Valid Values: True , False |
| Limit Hits | Limit the number of hits returned Best N : return the N ligands with the best fit values All : return all ligands that hit. Valid Values: Best N, All |
| Maximum Hits | Maximum number of ligands returned. |
| Keep Per Molecule | Keep only the N best fits for each molecule. |
| Catalyst Parameter File | File containing .Catalyst parameter settings to define the default behavior of Catalyst programs. The file can be created using the Catalyst Parameter Settings component. This parameter is typically only changed by experts. A default .Catalyst parameter settings file can be created in the users directory on the server: $PipelinePilot_Install_Directory/public/users/ username /Catalyst.cfg If it exists, it is used when this parameter is left blank. |
| Parallel Processing | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. Valid Values: True, False |
| Parallel Processing Batch Size | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. |
| Parallel Processing Server | Comma separated list of servers (server-name:port-number) to be used for parallel processing. Add "localhost" to include the local server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where "localhost" requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster). |
| Parallel Processing Server Processes | Comma separated list of the maximum batches that can be simultaneously executed on each server. Each value must correspond with an entry in the list of servers. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. |
| Parallel Processing Preserve Order | Preserve the initial order of the data records. Valid Values: True , False |

# Ligand Pharmacophore Mapping

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_ligand_pharmacophore_mapping.htm

## Ligand Pharmacophore Mapping

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Troubleshooting

The Ligand Pharmacophore Mapping protocol compares a set of ligands
to a pharmacophore. The relevant ligand-pharmacophore mappings are
exported aligned to the pharmacophore.

To ensure proper exploration of the ligand conformational and pharmacophoric space,
run the Generate Conformations protocol before running this protocol. You can also generate the conformations on-the-fly using the Conformation Generation parameter and associated parameters.

* Open the Pharmacophores | Compare Pharmacophore to Ligands tools and click Ligand Pharmacophore Mapping to open the Ligand Pharmacophore Mapping dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the Input Ligands . It is possible to select All , Visible , or Selected ligands from a Molecule Window . It is also possible to browse to a file using the Browse... option.

* You can also use a database as input by changing the Input Type to Database , then selecting the database
for Input Database . By default, all conformations of all ligands in the databases will be used in the
calculation. The parameters Limit Hits , Maximum , and Hitlist can be used to restrict the number of ligands. Hitlist will limit the calculation to only those ligands that have the
same name as the ligands in Hitlist and the conformation in the Hitlist is ignored.

* Set Input Pharmacophore . The list
contains all pharmacophores from one of the open Molecule Windows and an option to Browse... to a file.

* For details about the remaining parameters, see Ligand Pharmacophore Mapping - Parameters . By default every
conformation will be considered when mapping to a pharmacophore.
It is possible to restrict the pharmacophore to map to conformations
within a certain energy threshold to the lowest energy conformation
using Mapped Energy Threshold . This
parameter becomes activated when Best Mapping
Only is set to False (all conformations are considered when
finding the best mapping) and Specify Energy
Threshold is True.

By default every
conformation will be considered when mapping to a pharmacophore.
It is possible to restrict the pharmacophore to map to conformations
within a certain energy threshold to the lowest energy conformation
using Mapped Energy Threshold . This
parameter becomes activated when Best Mapping
Only is set to False (all conformations are considered when
finding the best mapping) and Specify Energy
Threshold is True.

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| MoleculesQuery.sd | Contains the ligands that mapped to the input pharmacophore. |
| ViewResults.ds_pl | Opening this file allows you to view the mapped ligands and the input pharmacophore. |

#### Further information

Run a parallel calculation Distributed grid computing

# Ligand Profiler - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_ligand_profiler-para.htm

## Ligand Profiler - Parameters

### Maps a set of ligands against a set of pharmacophores

Uses Catalyst to map a set of input ligands to a set of input pharmacophores.

Pharmacophore selection includes:

* Queries in Discovery Studio 3D windows

* Catalyst Query .ds_chm files

* Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore database

Depending on the pharmacophore, additional properties may be added, these include:

* FitValue : A measure of how well the ligand fits the pharmacophore. The higher the fit score, the better the match. The name of the FitValue property is the Pharmacophore name.

* Estimate : Pharmacophores that are able to predict activity values will have an Estimate property, which is the estimate of the activity value. This property is named "Pharmacophore Name#Estimate".

See Also:

* Meslamani, J.; Li, J.; Sutter, J.; Stevens, A.; Bertrand, H.-O.; Rognan, D., 
Protein-Ligand-Based Pharmacophores: Generation and Utility Assessment in Computational Ligand Profiling, J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2012, 52(4) 943-955.

| Input File Pharmacophores | A comma separated list of pharmacophore files to read. In Discovery Studio, pharmacophores present in DS Molecule Windows can also be selected. Examples: /home/Data/2hbd1hba.ds_chm,/home/Data/Conv1.ds_chm /home/Data/*.ds_chm C:\Data\TestShape.ds_chm,C:\Data\Exp1\*.ds_chm |

To use it, save it in the Pipeline Pilot users' directory on the server: $PipelinePilot_Install_Directory/public/users/ username /Catalyst.cfg If it exists, it is used when this parameter is left blank. |
| Parallel Processing | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. Valid Values: True, False |
| Parallel Processing Batch Size | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. |
| Parallel Processing Server | Comma separated list of servers (server-name:port-number) to be used for parallel processing. Add "localhost" to include the local server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where "localhost" requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster). |
| Parallel Processing Server Processes | Comma separated list of the maximum batches that can be simultaneously executed on each server. Each value must correspond with an entry in the list of servers. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. |

Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation.

In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance.

A comma separated list of pharmacophore files to read.

In Discovery Studio, pharmacophores present in DS Molecule Windows can also be selected.

Examples:

* /home/Data/2hbd1hba.ds_chm,/home/Data/Conv1.ds_chm

* /home/Data/*.ds_chm

* C:\Data\TestShape.ds_chm,C:\Data\Exp1\*.ds_chm

In Discovery Studio, a list of pharmacophores from the LigandProfiler Pharmacophore database. (Use the Add to Ligand Profiler Database protocol to create this database.)

In Pipeline Pilot, a comma separated list of pharmacophore files to read.

Create Conformations. Each molecule in Input Ligands must have a good set of conformations.

If they are not present in the input data, they can be added using one of the following algorithms:

* FAST: Quickly provide diverse low-energy conformations.

* BEST: Ensure the best coverage of conformational space (requires more CPU time).

* CAESAR: Very quickly provide conformations by sampling torsions.

* NONE: Uses existing conformations.

Valid Values: NONE, FAST , BEST, CAESAR

Maximum number of conformations to be generated.

Discard existing input conformations. If False, use all existing input conformations.

Valid Values: True , False

Conformations are created within this relative energy threshold (kcal/mol). For a molecule with stereo isomers, this threshold applies to conformations for each isomer.

File (fragments.data) that contains the ring conformations to use. Molecules that contain rings found in the file will only use these ring conformations. Conformations for rings not in the file are generated from scratch.

Notes:

* Only FAST and CAESAR will use this file. It have no effect on other methods. By default this parameter is blank and all ring conformations are generated from scratch.

* In Pipeline Pilot, the Catalyst Ring Fragment Writer component can be used to generate the file.

Save the generated conformations in a MDL MOL/SD file.

Valid Values: True, False

Contains less commonly used parameters.

* Ligands: A set of compounds from an MDL MOL/SD file, or a Molecule window.

* Database: A set of compounds from a Catalyst ligand database.

Valid Values: Database, Ligands

Database to search, specified by its Catalyst database (.bdb) file.

All database files are located in $PipelinePilot_Install_Directory/public/DS/CatalystDB on the server.

Each database file is in a separate folder with the same name as the database.

Either Input Ligands or Input Database must be specified.

Note:

* Processing large databases requires significant disk space. During the calculation, all conformations of all compounds in the database will be written to SD files in the intermediate directory. After they are processed, these files are removed unless the protocol is run in debug mode.

Limit the number of hits returned.

* First N: Return the first N ligands

* All: Return all ligands.

Valid Values: First N , All

The maximum number ( n ) of molecules to read from the database.

All conformations of the first n molecules are read from the database and analyzed further. There is no guarantee that these molecules will fit the pharmacophore features. To only extract molecules that fit some of the pharmacophore features, you can generate a hitlist (e.g., using the Search 3D Database protocol). You can then use the Hitlist parameter to extract these molecules from the database. Note that each molecule that shares the same Name property with a ligand in the hitlist is extracted from the database including all of its conformations. Conformations are not required to be in the ligands designated in the Hitlist parameter. Only the names are important.

Ligands in the database that have the same Names as these ligands are extracted from the database.

Choose the type of fitting to use:

* Rigid: Performs a rigid fit between ligand and pharmacophore.

* Flexible: Allow slight modification of each ligand conformation to better fit the pharmacophore.

Valid Values: Rigid , Flexible

The maximum number of features allowed to miss when mapping the ligand to the pharmacophore.

A value of -1 has special meaning: it instructs the server to consider all feature subsets of the pharmacophore. It is equivalent to n-1 , where n is the total number of features in the pharmacophore. For a pharmacophore with 5 features, -1 allows up to 4 features to miss.

The number of subsets grows very quickly as the total number of features in the pharmacophore increases.
To avoid excessive memory use and calculation time, Maximum Omitted Features is limited in the fitting calculation:

* Total Features = 1-6: Maximum Omitted Features limited to (Total Features - 1) or less

* Total Features = 7-9: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 4 or less

* Total Features = 10: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 3 or less

* Total Features = 11-19: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 2 or less

* Total Features = 20+: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 1 or less

Choose the option of the best mapping:

* Fit most features: Find the fit that has the highest fit value, within the set that map the most features.

* Find highest fit: Find the fit that has the highest fit value. This fit may not match all features in the query.

Valid Values: Fit most features , Find highest fit

Minimum distance between features in Å. A value of "0.0" will allow a single atom to map to multiple features. For example, an NH 2 group could match two hydrogen bond donor features depending on the surface accessibility of the ligand.

Scale fit values to a range of 0.0 - 1.0.

The weight values of each feature in the pharmacophore are summed to get the maximum fit (the default is 1.0 per feature).

OutputFit = Fit Value / Maximum Fit Value.

If there are no fits to a given pharmacophore, remove the fit scores for that pharmacophore from the output molecular properties (as they would all be zero).

If there are no fits to a given molecule, remove that molecule from the output (as all fit scores for it would be zero).

Ligand profiling requires a "good" set of conformations in the Input Ligands .

Usually, it is easier to understand the output when the multiple conformations of each ligand are removed. This results in one fit value for each ligand with each pharmacophore.

Optionally, you can include all of the input conformations in the output.

Save the aligned ligands in MDL MOL/SD files.

An individual MDL MOL/SD file is created for each ds_chm file that has mappings.

Note :

* The saved files can use a large amount of disk space.

The name of the property containing molecular activity data.

If the input molecules contain activity data and the pharmacophores can estimate activity, the output molecules will contain activity and estimated activity values.

If empty Activ is used.

* Internally, this property is converted to Activ , so any messages will refer to that name.

# Ligand Profiler

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_ligand_profiler.htm

## Ligand Profiler

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Troubleshooting

The Ligand Profiler protocol maps a set of ligands against a set of pharmacophores [Meslamani et. al, 2012] . The pharmacophores can come from .ds_chm files,
Molecule Window, or Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore database.

* Open the Pharmacophores | Search and Build Pharmacophore Database tools and click Ligand Profiler to open the Ligand Profiler dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Specify the ligands to be used by the protocol. For details, see Specifying Ligands .

* Choose Pharmacophores using one the following methods: Use Input File Pharmacophores to navigate to a queries file. Use the Input LigandProfilerDB Pharmacophores parameter to specify queries in the LigandProfilerDB
Pharmacophores dialog. A tree of queries is displayed, branching by a cascading set of query properties that can be checked or unchecked. The leaf nodes contain individual queries.

* Use Input File Pharmacophores to navigate to a queries file.

* Use the Input LigandProfilerDB Pharmacophores parameter to specify queries in the LigandProfilerDB
Pharmacophores dialog. A tree of queries is displayed, branching by a cascading set of query properties that can be checked or unchecked. The leaf nodes contain individual queries.

* For details about the remaining parameters, see Ligand Profiler - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| MoleculeFits.htm | Summary of the pharmacophores that fit each ligand. |
| PharmacophoreFits.htm | Summary of the ligands that fit each pharmacophore. |
| ViewResults.ds_pl | Perl script to view results in graphics. |
| Molecules_profiled.sd | Contains the conformations of the input ligands. |

If the Save Aligned Ligands parameter is set to True , a .sd file is generated for each pharmacophore with aligned ligands. You can use the accompanying pharmacophore_view.ds_pl script to view the mapped ligands and the input pharmacophore.

#### Further information

Run a parallel calculation Distributed grid computing
