## Pharmacophore Comparison - Parameters

### Aligns two pharmacophores

Maps and aligns two pharmacophores. A root-mean-squared error is reported for the matching pharmacophore features. The Best Mapping Only parameter can be changed to return multiple mappings. The mappings are ranked primarily by the number of pairs of location constraints that match and then by the minimum rms displacement.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Reference Pharmacophore | Pharmacophore used as the reference in comparison. This may be identified from a file in ds_chm format. In Discovery Studio, this may be identified either from a Molecule Window or from a file in ds_chm format. |
| Tethers | Tethers connect a location feature in the reference pharmacophore to a location feature in the input pharmacophore, chosen from a list of all location features in each pharmacophore. Valid Values: True, False |
| Input Reference Pharmacophore Tether Feature 1 | A location feature in this pharmacophore that is tethered to a location feature in the other pharmacophore, chosen from a list of all location features in each pharmacophore. If Input Reference Pharmacophore is a file, the list of all location features is produced by a minimal parsing of the ds_chm file. Choose the desired location feature from the list of all location features. In Discovery Studio, if Input Reference Pharmacophore is a query from a Molecule Window and there are location features connected by tethers, the location feature may be chosen from among them. |
| Input Reference Pharmacophore Tether Feature 2 | A location feature in this pharmacophore that is tethered to a location feature in the other pharmacophore, chosen from a list of all location features in each pharmacophore. If Input Reference Pharmacophore is a file, the list of all location features is produced by a minimal parsing of the ds_chm file. Choose the desired location feature from the list of all location features. In Discovery Studio, if Input Reference Pharmacophore is a query from a Molecule Window and there are location features connected by tethers, the location feature may be chosen from among them. |
| Input Reference Pharmacophore Tether Feature 3 | A location feature in this pharmacophore that is tethered to a location feature in the other pharmacophore, chosen from a list of all location features in each pharmacophore. If Input Reference Pharmacophore is a file, the list of all location features is produced by a minimal parsing of the ds_chm file. Choose the desired location feature from the list of all location features. In Discovery Studio, if Input Reference Pharmacophore is a query from a Molecule Window and there are location features connected by tethers, the location feature may be chosen from among them. |
| Input Pharmacophore | Input pharmacophore to be compared. Identified from a file in ds_chm format. In Discovery Studio, this may be identified either from a Molecule Window or from a file in ds_chm format. |

# PharmaDB Filter - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_pharmadb_filter-para.htm

## PharmaDB Filter - Parameters

### Filters the PharmaDB entries based on the selected properties

Filters the PharmaDB annotations file or a subset set by Input Hitlist based on the properties and values selected. The output is a hitlist.csv file which can either be used as an input to this protocol in order to further refine the list or as input to the PharmaDB Profiler protocol in order to score a set ligands against the pharmacophores corresponding to the entries in the hitlist.

The PharmaDB is a large collection of receptor-ligand based pharmacophores. It contains over 800,000 diverse pharmacophores derived from over 41,000 entries from the 2024 release of the scPDB ( http://bioinfo-pharma.u-strasbg.fr/scPDB ). The PharmaDB annotations file contains several properties derived from the pdb entry, the ligand properties, and the binding site properties.

See Also:

* Meslamani, J.; Li, J.; Sutter, J.; Stevens, A.; Bertrand, H.-O.; Rognan, D., 
Protein-Ligand-Based Pharmacophores: Generation and Utility Assessment in Computational Ligand Profiling, J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2012, 52(4) 943-955.

# PharmaDB Filter

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_pharmadb_filter.htm

## PharmaDB Filter

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Next steps

The PharmaDB Filter protocol generates a hitlist file of PharmaDB entries that match specified properties. The hit list can then be used in the PharmaDB Profiler protocol.

* Open the Pharmacophores | Search, Screen, and Profile tools and click PharmaDB Filter to open the PharmaDB Filter dialog.

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Hitlist Use this to filter an existing hitlist further. Leave this blank to use all entries in the pharmacophore database. Date Property To limit the results to a specific date range, set Minimum and Maximum to the required range. Use YYYY-MM-DD for these values. Numeric Property To limit the results to a specific range, set Minimum and Maximum to the required range. String Property Set Value to the required property value. Regular expressions are supported. For example, if ligand_het_code is selected for String Property and Value is set to ^(?!.*(NDP|FAD|NAD|ADP|ATP)) , all entries that have either NDP, FAD, NAD, AMP, ADP, or ATP set as the ligand_het_code are excluded from the hitlist. Category Property Choose a Value to filter the hits by the selected category. For details about the parameters, see PharmaDB Filter - Parameters .

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Hitlist | Use this to filter an existing hitlist further. Leave this blank to use all entries in the pharmacophore database. |
| Date Property | To limit the results to a specific date range, set Minimum and Maximum to the required range. Use YYYY-MM-DD for these values. |
| Numeric Property | To limit the results to a specific range, set Minimum and Maximum to the required range. |
| String Property | Set Value to the required property value. Regular expressions are supported. For example, if ligand_het_code is selected for String Property and Value is set to ^(?!.*(NDP\|FAD\|NAD\|ADP\|ATP)) , all entries that have either NDP, FAD, NAD, AMP, ADP, or ATP set as the ligand_het_code are excluded from the hitlist. |
| Category Property | Choose a Value to filter the hits by the selected category. |

For details about the parameters, see PharmaDB Filter - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation. The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to the background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to the background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

Click the hitlist link in the Results tab to open the filter results in a new tab. Select the tab and choose File > Save as from the menu to save a copy. You can also locate the file in your default output folder.

* To filter the hit list further, use it as input to this protocol and run it again.

* To map ligands against the hit list, use it as input to the PharmaDB Profiler protocol.

# PharmaDB Profiler - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_pharmadb_profiler-para.htm

## PharmaDB Profiler - Parameters

### Maps a set of ligands against pharmacophores from the PharmaDB

Uses a series of Catalyst compare/fit operations to map a set of input ligands to a set of pharmacophores from the PharmaDB.

The pharmacophores come from the Input PharmaDB Hitlist which is a csv file that is a subset of the PharmaDB annotations file. The subset can be generated using the PharmaDB Filter protocol.

Depending on the pharmacophore, additional properties may be added, these include:

* FitValue : A measure of how well the ligand fits the pharmacophore. The higher the fit score, the better the match. The name of the FitValue property is the Pharmacophore name.

* Estimate : Pharmacophores that are able to predict activity values will have an Estimate property, which is the estimate of the activity value. This property is named "Pharmacophore Name#Estimate".

* Shape Similarity : Pharmacophores that have a shape feature will report a similarity to the shape between 0.0 and 1.0. 1.0 is a ligand that is a perfect match to the shape in the pharmacophore. This property is named "Pharmacophore Name#ShapeSimilarity".

* Percent Filled : Pharmacophores that have a shape feature will report what percent the matching ligand occupies the shape feature of the pharmacophore. The value can be between 0.0 and 100.0. A value of 100.0 means that the shape of the ligand completely occupies the shape feature. This property is named "Pharmacophore Name#PercentFilled".

Notes :

* PharmaDB is a large collection of receptor-ligand based pharmacophores. It contains over 800,000 diverse pharmacophores derived from over 41,000 entries from the 2024 release of the scPDB ( http://bioinfo-pharma.u-strasbg.fr/scPDB ).

See Also:

* Meslamani, J.; Li, J.; Sutter, J.; Stevens, A.; Bertrand, H.-O.; Rognan, D., 
Protein-Ligand-Based Pharmacophores: Generation and Utility Assessment in Computational Ligand Profiling, J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2012, 52(4) 943-955.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Ligands | Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. |
| Input PharmaDB Hitlist | A csv file that is a subset of the PharmaDB annotations file. The subset can be generated using the PharmaDB Filter protocol. All entries in the PharmaDB are used if Input PharmaDB Hitlist is blank Note: The PharmaDB Pharmacophore database was created from the sc-PDB protein data bank, i.e., http://bioinfo-pharma.u-strasbg.fr/scPDB . The current version of PharmaDB Pharmacophore database is based on sc-PDB 2024 and contains over 800,000 pharmacophore models. For each protein target, multiple diverse pharmacophores with shape or excluded volume constraints were generated. |
| Model Selection | Specify pharmacophore models for each selected protein target. Two options are available. Most Selective: The most selective model for each selected protein target. All Models: All diverse pharmacophore models for the selected protein. Note : The PharmaDB was built using the Diverse option for Pharmacophore Scoring Method , which has been shown to produce a good pharmacophore more often. However, the good pharmacophore is not always the top scoring pharmacophore. Therefore, it may be beneficial to use All Models when screening a small set of targets. Valid Values: Most Selective , All Models |
| Steric Features | Determines the steric constraint to use with the pharmacophore: Excluded Volumes: Uses excluded volumes derived from atoms on the protein target. Shape: Uses the shape of the ligand. Both: Uses both types of pharmacophores. Valid Values: Excluded Volumes , Shape, Both |
| Conformation Generation | Create Conformations. Each molecule in Input Ligands must have a good set of conformations. If they are not present in the input data, they can be added using one of the following algorithms: FAST: Quickly provide diverse low-energy conformations. BEST: Ensure the best coverage of conformational space (requires more CPU time). CAESAR: Very quickly provide conformations by sampling torsions. NONE: Uses existing conformations. Valid Values: NONE, FAST , BEST, CAESAR |
| Maximum Conformations | Maximum number of conformations to be generated. |
| Discard Existing Conformations | Discard existing input conformations. If False, use all existing input conformations. Valid Values: True , False |
| Energy Threshold | Conformations are created within this relative energy threshold (kcal/mol). For a molecule with stereo isomers, this threshold applies to conformations for each isomer. |
| Ring Fragments File | File (fragments.data) that contains the ring conformations to use. Molecules that contain rings found in the file will only use these ring conformations. Conformations for rings not in the file are generated from scratch. Notes: Only FAST and CAESAR will use this file. It have no effect on other methods. By default this parameter is blank and all ring conformations are generated from scratch. In Pipeline Pilot, the Catalyst Ring Fragment Writer component can be used to generate the file. |
| Save Conformations | Save the generated conformations in a MDL MOL/SD file. Valid Values: True, False |
| Advanced | Contains less commonly used parameters. |
| Fitting Method | Choose the type of fitting to use: Rigid: Performs a rigid fit between ligand and pharmacophore. Flexible: Allow slight modification of each ligand conformation to better fit the pharmacophore. Valid Values: Rigid , Flexible |
| Maximum Omitted Features | The maximum number of features allowed to miss when mapping the ligand to the pharmacophore. A value of -1 has special meaning: it instructs the server to consider all feature subsets of the pharmacophore. It is equivalent to n-1 , where n is the total number of features in the pharmacophore. For a pharmacophore with 5 features, -1 allows up to 4 features to miss. The number of subsets grows very quickly as the total number of features in the pharmacophore increases. To avoid excessive memory use and calculation time, Maximum Omitted Features is limited in the fitting calculation: Total Features = 1-6: Maximum Omitted Features limited to (Total Features - 1) or less Total Features = 7-9: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 4 or less Total Features = 10: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 3 or less Total Features = 11-19: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 2 or less Total Features = 20+: Maximum Omitted Features limited to 1 or less |
| Options | Choose the option of the best mapping: Fit most features: Find the fit that has the highest fit value, within the set that map the most features. Find highest fit: Find the fit that has the highest fit value. This fit may not match all features in the query. Valid Values: Fit most features , Find highest fit |
| Minimum Interfeature Distance | Minimum distance between features in Å. A value of "0.0" will allow a single atom to map to multiple features. For example, an NH 2 group could match two hydrogen bond donor features depending on the surface accessibility of the ligand. |
| Scale Fit Values | Scale fit values to a range of 0.0 - 1.0. The weight values of each feature in the pharmacophore are summed to get the maximum fit (the default is 1.0 per feature). OutputFit = Fit Value / Maximum Fit Value. Valid Values: True , False |
| Prune Empty Fits | If there are no fits to a given pharmacophore, remove the fit scores for that pharmacophore from the output molecular properties (as they would all be zero). Valid Values: True, False |
| Prune Missed Molecules | If there are no fits to a given molecule, remove that molecule from the output (as all fit scores for it would be zero). Valid Values: True , False |
| Keep Input Conformations | Ligand profiling requires a "good" set of conformations in the Input Ligands . Usually, it is easier to understand the output when the multiple conformations of each ligand are removed. This results in one fit value for each ligand with each pharmacophore. Optionally, you can include all of the input conformations in the output. Valid Values: True, False |
| Save Aligned Ligands | Save the aligned ligands in MDL MOL/SD files. An individual MDL MOL/SD file is created for each ds_chm file that has mappings. Note : The saved files can use a large amount of disk space. Valid Values: True, False |
| Activity Property | The name of the property containing molecular activity data. If the input molecules contain activity data and the pharmacophores can estimate activity, the output molecules will contain activity and estimated activity values. If empty Activ is used. Note : Internally, this property is converted to Activ , so any messages will refer to that name. |
| Catalyst Parameter File | File containing parameter settings to define the default behavior of Catalyst programs. This parameter is typically only changed by experts. In Pipeline Pilot, this file can be created using the Catalyst Parameter Settings component. To use it, save it in the Pipeline Pilot users' directory on the server: $PipelinePilot_Install_Directory/public/users/ username /Catalyst.cfg If it exists, it is used when this parameter is left blank. |
| Parallel Processing | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. Valid Values: True, False |
| Parallel Processing Batch Size | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. |
| Parallel Processing Server | Comma separated list of servers (server-name:port-number) to be used for parallel processing. Add "localhost" to include the local server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where "localhost" requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster). |
| Parallel Processing Server Processes | Comma separated list of the maximum batches that can be simultaneously executed on each server. Each value must correspond with an entry in the list of servers. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. |
| Parallel Processing Preserve Order | Preserve the initial order of the data records. Valid Values: True , False |

# PharmaDB Profiler

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_pharmadb_profiler.htm

## PharmaDB Profiler

* Description

* Before you start

* Setting up and running

* Output

The PharmaDB Profiler protocol maps a set of ligands against a hitlist of filtered PharmaDB entries.

Run the PharmaDB Filter protocol to generate a hitlist for PharmaDB entries filtered by property.

* Open the Pharmacophores | Search, Screen and Profile tools and click PharmaDB Profiler to open the PharmaDB Profiler dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Choose the Ligands to use. For details, see Specifying Ligands .

* For Pharmacophores , choose the hitlist.csv file that you generated using the PharmaDB Filter protocol.

* For details about the remaining parameters, see PharmaDB Profiler - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to the background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

You can inspect the individual output files that were generated in the Output directory of the run. The contents of this directory can be viewed by selecting the job in the Jobs Explorer, right-clicking and choosing Locate. The file names may differ from those listed here.

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| MoleculeFits.htm | Summary of the pharmacophores that fit each ligand. |
| PharmacophoreFits.htm | Summary of the ligands that fit each pharmacophore. |
| ViewResults.ds_pl | Script to view results in graphics. |
| Molecules_profiled.sd | Contains the conformations of the input ligands. |

## Remove from Ligand Profiler Database - Parameters

### Removes a pharmacophore from the Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore Database

Pharmacophore to Remove contains a list of pharmacophores in the Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore Database. Select the pharmacophore to remove.

If no pharmacophores have been added to the database, the list will be empty.

After removing pharmacophores, close and reopen the protocol to repopulate the pharmacophore list.

Use Add To Ligand Profiler Database to add pharmacophores.

The Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore Database is located at: PipelinePilot_Install_Directory/public/DS/LigandProfilerDB/Standard

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Pharmacophore to Remove | Select the pharmacophore to remove from the Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore Database from a list of the pharmacophores present. If there are no pharmacophores in the Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore Database, the list will be empty. |

Select the pharmacophore to remove from the Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore Database from a list of the pharmacophores present. If there are no pharmacophores in the Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore Database, the list will be empty.

## Remove from Ligand Profiler Database

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Troubleshooting

The Remove from Ligand Profiler Database protocol removes a pharmacophore from the Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore database. The pharmacophores in
this database can be accessed using the Input LigandProfilerDB Pharmacophores parameter of the Ligand Profiler protocol. A
pharmacophore can be added to the Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore database using the Add to Ligand Profiler Database protocol.

* Open the Pharmacophores | Search and Build Pharmacophore Database tools and click Remove from Ligand Profiler Database to open the Remove from Ligand Profiler Database dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Select a Pharmacophore to Remove from the list of pharmacophores in the Ligand Profiler Database.

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |

# Screen Library - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_screen_library-para.htm

## Screen Library - Parameters

### Screens ligands using many subset pharmacophores

Enumerates many possible subset pharmacophores from a query and screens the input ligands against each pharmacophore. The pharmacophores are created based on the parameters
of the protocol.

For example, if there are a total of 8 pharmacophore features in the input query, 
the Minimum Features parameter is set to 4, 
the Maximum Features parameter is set to 6, and the Maximum Subset of Pharmacophores parameter is set to 100, 
then a 100 pharmacophore subset of all possible 4, 5, and 6 feature pharmacophores from the 8 features 
will be used in the analysis.

The protocol analyzes large collections of pharmacophore features to extract the most relevant pharmacophore models. It is intended to support the Structure Based Pharmacophore tools within Discovery Studio (e.g., analyzing output from Interaction Generation), but can be used to analyze any set of pharmacophore features.

Note:

* It is possible to specify combinations of Minimum Features, Maximum Features, Required Features, and Feature Groups such that there are no legal candidate pharmacophores to test.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Pharmacophore | Specify the pharmacophore model. Identified from a file in ds_chm format. In Discovery Studio, this may be identified either from a Molecule Window or from a file in ds_chm format. Note : The pharmacophore should have less than 32 features. |
| Require Features | Specify a list of the pharmacophore features that are required to be present in every pharmacophore tested in a screen library run. Valid Values: True, False |
| Required Features | A list of the pharmacophore features that are required to be present in every pharmacophore tested in a screen library run. If Input Pharmacophore is a file, the list of all features is produced by a minimal parsing of the ds_chm file. Choose the desired features from the list of all features. In Discovery Studio, if Input Pharmacophore is a query from a Molecule Window and there are selected features, then the selected features may be chosen. In this case, the choice is between all selected features and none. Note: It is possible to specify combinations of Minimum Features, Maximum Features, Required Features, and Feature Groups such that there are no legal candidate pharmacophores to test. |
| Feature Groups | Specify groups of features. Each group is composed of a list of pharmacophore features and a Minimum and Maximum value. Valid Values: True, False |
| Feature Group 1 | A list of the pharmacophore features in the group. Every pharmacophore tested in a screen library run will include at least Minimum and at most Maximum features from the group. If Input Pharmacophore is a file, the list of all features is produced by a minimal parsing of the ds_chm file. Choose the desired features from the list of all features. In Discovery Studio, if Input Pharmacophore is a query from a Molecule Window and there are named groups of features, the choice is one or none of the named groups. Use Edit\|Group to create a named groups using the currently selected features. Notes: A feature may be present in more than one Feature Group . It is possible to specify combinations of Minimum Features, Maximum Features, Required Features, and Feature Groups such that there are no legal candidate pharmacophores to test. |
| Feature Group 1 Minimum | The minimum number N of features from this group of features. Each query generated in a screen library run will contain at least N features from this group of features. |
| Feature Group 1 Maximum | The maximum number N of features from this group of features. Each query generated in a screen library run will contain at most N features from this group of features. |
| Feature Group 2 | A list of the pharmacophore features in the group. Every pharmacophore tested in a screen library run will include at least Minimum and at most Maximum features from the group. If Input Pharmacophore is a file, the list of all features is produced by a minimal parsing of the ds_chm file. Choose the desired features from the list of all features. In Discovery Studio, if Input Pharmacophore is a query from a Molecule Window and there are named groups of features, the choice is one or none of the named groups. Use Edit\|Group to create a named groups using the currently selected features. Notes: A feature may be present in more than one Feature Group . It is possible to specify combinations of Minimum Features, Maximum Features, Required Features, and Feature Groups such that there are no legal candidate pharmacophores to test. |

Valid Values: NONE, FAST , BEST, CAESAR |

# Screen Library

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_screen_library.htm

## Screen Library

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

The Screen Library protocol enumerates several possible pharmacophores from an input set of pharmacophore
features and screens an input set of ligands. The pharmacophores are created based on the parameters
of the protocol. For example, if there are a total of eight pharmacophore features in the input query,
the Minimum Features parameter is set to 4 ,
the Maximum Features parameter is set to 6 , and the Maximum Subset of Pharmacophores parameter is set to 100 ,
then a 100 pharmacophore subset of all possible four, five, and six feature pharmacophores from the eight features
will be used in the analysis.

To compare a single pharmacophore to a set of ligands, use the Ligand Pharmacophore Mapping protocol instead.

To ensure proper exploration of the ligand conformational and pharmacophoric space,
it is recommended that you run the Generate Conformations protocol
before running this protocol.

* Open the Pharmacophores | Compare Pharmacophore to Ligands tools and click Screen Library to open the Screen Library dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Ligands Specify the ligands to be used by the protocol. For details, see Specifying Ligands . Input Pharmacophore The list contains all pharmacophores from one of the open Molecule Windows as well as an option to Browse... to a file. Minimum Features The minimum number of features that each enumerated pharmacophore will have. Maximum Features The maximum number of features that each enumerated pharmacophore will have. Maximum Subset of Pharmacophores The maximum number of pharmacophores
that will be enumerated. Advanced | Total Number of Features/Number of Possible Pharmacophores These are automatically updated based on the pharmacophore model in the Molecule Window, Minimum and Maximum Features parameters.
If the Number of Possible Pharmacophores is greater than the Maximum Subset of Pharmacophores , the latter will
be used. In this situation, the pharmacophores are selected at random using selection without replacement so that the selection is
sampled uniformly. To get more hits, increase Maximum Subset of Pharmacophores . For details about the remaining parameters, see Screen Library - Parameters . By default every
conformation will be considered when mapping to a pharmacophore.
It is possible to restrict the pharmacophore to map to conformations
within a certain energy threshold to the lowest energy conformation
by setting Specify Energy Threshold to True and setting an energy threshold for Mapped Energy Threshold .

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Ligands | Specify the ligands to be used by the protocol. For details, see Specifying Ligands . |
| Input Pharmacophore | The list contains all pharmacophores from one of the open Molecule Windows as well as an option to Browse... to a file. |
| Minimum Features | The minimum number of features that each enumerated pharmacophore will have. |
| Maximum Features | The maximum number of features that each enumerated pharmacophore will have. |
| Maximum Subset of Pharmacophores | The maximum number of pharmacophores that will be enumerated. |
| Advanced \| Total Number of Features/Number of Possible Pharmacophores | These are automatically updated based on the pharmacophore model in the Molecule Window, Minimum and Maximum Features parameters. If the Number of Possible Pharmacophores is greater than the Maximum Subset of Pharmacophores , the latter will be used. In this situation, the pharmacophores are selected at random using selection without replacement so that the selection is sampled uniformly. To get more hits, increase Maximum Subset of Pharmacophores . |

For details about the remaining parameters, see Screen Library - Parameters .

By default every
conformation will be considered when mapping to a pharmacophore.
It is possible to restrict the pharmacophore to map to conformations
within a certain energy threshold to the lowest energy conformation
by setting Specify Energy Threshold to True and setting an energy threshold for Mapped Energy Threshold .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

Load the results from the report page by clicking ViewResults.ds_pl or ViewBestResults.ds_pl . After the results have been loaded, you can step through the table and view the mapped features
of various pharmacophores. Only features that are mapped are shown, the unmapped features
are hidden or dimmed depending on the settings on the Molecule Window page of the Preferences dialog.
Each of the features of the input pharmacophore are represented as a new
property in the .sd file, where mapped features are represented by 1 and
unmapped features by 0

With regard to the nature of the hits, only one mapping, ligand, pharmacophore is reported. For example,
a specific 3-feature pharmacophore has only one instance (conformation) of a specific molecule (i.e., a molecule, or the conformation of the molecule, only appears once within a pharmacophore.)
Only the best mapping of a specific molecule within a pharmacophore is reported.
This helps reduce the amount of data that is generated. Additionally,
the following properties are reported in all the hits .sd files:

* Mapped Atoms : An array of atoms that map the pharmacophore in the format AtomIndex, X, Y, Z, Tolerance, and Location feature name.

* Fit Value : Measure of the fit.

* Pharmprint : Represents a pharmacophore as a string of
1's and 0's that indicate which features match (1), and which miss (0).
For example, 1001011 means that the pharmacophore
features 1, 4, 6, and 7 map to the ligand, and features 2, 3, and 5 miss.

* PharmprintFrequency : Frequency of a pharmacophore.

* PharmType : Gives the pharmacophore type or the number of features in the pharmacophore.

The results can also be analyzed using the grouping, representing, and sorting capabilities of the Data Table View (see Analyzing results with the Data Table View for details).
In addition, columns of data can be selected in the table and plotted using the charting capabilities.

You can also use the Edit and Cluster Features tools to determine which features or non-features are
displayed and create a pharmacophore model.

Once one or more suitable pharmacophores are identified, you can use
the Lasso tool on the View toolbar to select only the displayed features
and optionally excluded volumes, and Copy and Paste the
subset of features to a separate pharmacophore. You can then use the Ligand Pharmacophore Mapping protocol
to perform a compare or fit operation with the new pharmacophore
and a possible set of inactive compounds. Other protocols among
the Pharmacophores tools collection may also be used for further analysis.

#### Troubleshooting

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| <N>FeatureHits.sd | These files contain the hits for each pharmacophore, where <N> is determined by the Minimum Features and Maximum Features parameters. |
| <N>FeatureBestFitHits.sd | These files only contain the best fit hits for each pharmacophore, where <N> is determined by the Minimum Features and Maximum Features parameters. The data in these files has already been grouped by pharmacophore and sorted by the best fit value. |
| BestFitHits.sd | This is a consolidated file of only the best fit hits across all the pharmacophore types. The data in this file has already been grouped by pharmacophore and sorted by the best fit value. |
| AllHits.sd | This is a consolidated file of all the hits across all the pharmacophore types. |
| ViewResults.ds_pl | Displays all the hits within the context of the input pharmacophore model. |
| ViewBestResults.ds_pl | Displays the best fit hits across all the pharmacophore types within the context of the input pharmacophore model. |

# Search 3D Database - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_search_3d_database-para.htm

## Search 3D Database - Parameters

### Performs 3D pharmacophore searches of Catalyst compound databases

Uses Catalyst to identify ligands in a database that map to a pharmacophore, and optionally aligns the ligands to the query. The pharmacophore can contain combinations of substructures, 3D constraints, features, shapes, excluded volumes, etc. Depending on the pharmacophore, additional properties may be added, these include:

* FitValue : A measure of how well the ligand fits the pharmacophore. The higher the fit score, the better the match.

* ShapeSimilarity : A value between zero and one that measures the overlap of the mapped conformation and the shape constraint.

If no pharmacophore is supplied, a browse of the database is performed. The databases can be built using Build 3D Database.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Database | Database to perform search on, specified by its Catalyst database (.bdb) file. All database files are located in $PipelinePilot_Install_Directory/public/DS/CatalystDB on the server. Each database file is in a separate folder with the same name as the database. |
| Input Hitlist | The search will be restricted to the ligands in the database that have the same Names as these ligands. |
| Input Pharmacophore | Searches the database with the specified pharmacophore. This may be identified either from a Molecule Window, or from a file in ds_chm format. If a pharmacophore file is not specified, a database browse will be performed instead. |
| Align Ligands | If True, the ligands are returned aligned to the query. This option can increase search times since the best mapping, rather than the first mapping is found. Valid Values: True , False |
| Search Method | Type of search to perform. Fast: performs a rigid fit of the ligand conformations against the pharmacophore. Best: performs a flexible fit of the ligand conformations against the pharmacophore. Valid Values: Fast , Best |
| Limit Hits | Limit the number of hits returned First N: return the first N ligands that hit (may run faster than other options). Best N: return the N ligands with the best fit values. All: return all ligands that hit. Valid Values: All , First N, Best N |
| Maximum Hits | Maximum number of ligands returned. |
| Advanced | Contains less commonly used parameters. |
| Database File | Specify the location of a DBName .bdb file accessible by the server. By default all database data files are created in PipelinePilot_Install_Directory/public/DS/CatalystDB/ DBName on the server and are automatically displayed using the Input Database parameter. The Database File parameter can be used to point to databases that exist in another location. If you are accessing a remote server, you must have permissions to access the specified file. If the client is unable to browse to the directory, you can manually enter the path on the server as a value for the Database File parameter. Notes: On a cloud installation this parameter has no effect. Windows mapped drives may not be accessible to the server. When using Database File , it is imperative that the directory on their machine has the correct permissions = 2775 or 2777. One can use the chmod command on a linux machine to set correct permissions: chmod -R 2775 DatabaseFileDirectory where DatabaseFileDirectory is the directory that contains the database files. |
| What To Output | Select the kind of output: Hitlist: Exports the names of the ligands that match the Input Pharmacophore . The molecular data is not exported. One Conformation: Exports a single conformation for each ligand that matches the Input Pharmacophore . All Conformations: Exports all conformations that match the Input Pharmacophore for each ligand. Note: If no Input Pharmacophore is specified, a database browse is performed. The output will either be the ligand names, a single conformation for each ligand, or all conformations for each ligand depending on the What To Output parameter. Valid Values: Hitlist, One Conformation , All Conformations |
| Descriptors | Export shape descriptor properties. Valid Values: True, False |

By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. Valid Values: True, False |

# Steric Refinement with Excluded Volumes - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophore_steric_refinement_with_excluded_volumes-para.htm

## Steric Refinement with Excluded Volumes - Parameters

### Adds excluded volumes to a pharmacophore

Uses Catalyst HypoRefine to add excluded volumes to an input pharmacophore. The algorithm identifies areas of space that are occupied by inactive ligands and strategically places excluded volumes in these regions to reduce the number of inactives that can map the pharmacophore.

The input ligands should contain the following properties:

* Principal: Indicates whether the ligand is active (2), moderately active (1) or inactive (0).

* MaxOmitFeat: Indicates how many features are allowed to miss for each molecule. If missing, MaxOmitFeat is set to 0.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Pharmacophore | Pharmacophore to refine. Identified from a file in ds_chm format. In Discovery Studio, this may be identified either from a Molecule Window or from a file in ds_chm format. |
| Input Active Ligands | Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. The input ligands use the property Principal to indicate which are active. If Principal is not set for a ligand, it is set to 2 (active). Possible values for Principal are: 0: Inactive (Use for Excluded Volume Placement) 1: Moderately Active 2: Active If Principal is set, it will not be changed, i.e., inactive ligands (Principal=0) are allowed. If a spreadsheet file is supplied using the Spreadsheet File parameter, it will override the values. At least one active ligand and one inactive ligand are required to refine a pharmacophore. Notes: It is best to use a file when the atom and bond parity flags should be preserved. |
| Input Inactive Ligands | Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. Notes: This parameter is optional. This parameter is similar to Input Active Ligands except the Principal property is set to 0 (inactive) if not set. If a spreadsheet file is supplied using Spreadsheet File , it will override the values in these ligands. At least one active ligand and one inactive ligand are required to refine a pharmacophore. |
| Maximum Excluded Volumes | Maximum number of excluded volumes to add to the pharmacophore. |
| Conformation Generation | Each molecule in Input Active Ligands or Input Inactive Ligands must have a good set of conformations. If they are not present in the input data, they can be added using one of the following algorithms: FAST: quickly provides diverse low-energy conformations. BEST: ensures the best coverage of conformational space (requires more CPU time). CAESAR: very quickly provides conformations by sampling torsions. NONE: uses existing conformations. Valid Values: NONE, FAST , BEST, CAESAR |
| Maximum Conformations | Maximum number of conformations to be generated. |
| Discard Existing Conformations | If True, discard existing input conformations, otherwise use all existing input conformations. Valid Values: True , False |
| Energy Threshold | Conformations are created within this relative energy threshold (kcal/mol). For a molecule with stereo isomers, this threshold applies to conformations for each individual isomer. |
| Ring Fragments File | File (fragments.data) that contains the ring conformations to use. The Catalyst Ring Fragment Writer component can be used to generate the file. Molecules that contain rings also found in the file will only use these ring conformations. Conformations for rings not found in the file are generated from scratch. Note: Only FAST and CAESAR will use this file. It have no effect on other methods. By default this parameter is blank and all ring conformations are generated from scratch. |
| Save Conformations | Save the generated conformations in a MDL MOL/SD file. Valid Values: True, False |
| Parallel Processing | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. Valid Values: True, False |
| Parallel Processing Batch Size | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. |
| Parallel Processing Server | Comma separated list of servers (server-name:port-number) to be used for parallel processing. Add "localhost" to include the local server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where "localhost" requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster). |
| Parallel Processing Server Processes | Comma separated list of the maximum batches that can be simultaneously executed on each server. Each value must correspond with an entry in the list of servers. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. |
| Parallel Processing Preserve Order | Preserve the initial order of the data records. Valid Values: True , False |
| Advanced | Contains less commonly used parameters. |
| Maximum Mappings | Ignore mappings beyond this many top mappings. |
| Maximum Confs Per Mapping | Ignore conformations beyond this many top conformations per mapping. |
| Catalyst Parameter File | File containing .Catalyst parameter settings to define the default behavior of Catalyst programs. The file can be created using the Catalyst Parameter Settings component. This parameter is typically only changed by experts. A default .Catalyst parameter settings file can be created in the users directory on the server: $PipelinePilot_Install_Directory/public/users/ username /Catalyst.cfg If it exists, it is used when this parameter is left blank. |

## Steric Refinement with Excluded Volumes

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Troubleshooting

The Steric Refinement with Excluded Volumes protocol adds excluded volumes to an input pharmacophore.
The excluded volumes are placed on regions of
space that are occupied by the inactive molecules but not the active molecules.

You can add the molecular property Principal to designate
active and inactive molecules. Set the Principal value to 2 for all the active
molecules and to 0 for all the inactive molecules. If the Principal property is not
set, all ligands set by the Input Active Ligands parameter are
automatically assigned a Principal value of 2 (active) and the ligands set by
the Input Inactive Ligands are assigned a value of 0 (inactive).

* Open the Pharmacophores | Create a Pharmacophore Automatically tools and click Steric Refinement with Excluded Volumes to open the Steric Refinement with Excluded Volumes dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Pharmacophore You can select all pharmacophores from one of the open Molecule Windows , or Browse... to a file. Input Active Ligands Specify the ligand source. For details, see Specifying Ligands . The Input Active Ligands parameter can
contain the molecular property Principal to indicate
active ( 2 ) and inactive molecules ( 0 ).
If no value is set for these molecular properties, Principal is automatically set to 2 . Input Inactive Ligands (optional) Includes a large set of molecules as inactive without having to set the Principal value.
If the input ligands do not contain the molecular property Principal ,
the Principal value is automatically set to 0 (Inactive). For details about the remaining parameters, see Steric Refinement with Excluded Volumes - Parameters . During the
placement of excluded volumes, the MaxOmitFeat molecular property determines which mappings
are considered. A value of 1 for MaxOmitFeat means that all mappings
where either all n or a subset of n-1 features map
will be considered. For more complicated data sets, it may be better
to set MaxOmitFeat to 0 for the inactive
molecules to avoid placing too many excluded volumes.

## Work with pharmacophores

The use of pharmacophores is often central to a successful drug discovery project. Generating a pharmacophore
is usually the first step towards understanding the interaction between a receptor and a ligand. Over
the years, pharmacophores have been successfully used in lead generation, scaffold hopping, mining
small molecule databases, etc. There are several methods for generating pharmacophores, which are chosen based
on the information available. For example, if you only have receptor information, you can use structure-based pharmacophore
generation methods. Several algorithms exist for generating pharmacophores from a set of ligands, and if you have
receptor and ligand information it is possible to inspect the interactions and build a pharmacophore by hand. Discovery
Studio has several methods for generating pharmacophores described in the Pharmacophores tools section. Additionally, there are tools available to create and edit 3D pharmacophores in the Molecule Window . This is primarily done with the Query toolbar .

### Pharmacophores

In Discovery Studio , a pharmacophore is defined as the essential features
and their corresponding 3D locations responsible for the similar biological activities
in a set of small molecules. The essential features can be defined as molecular substructures with specific
atom and bond types or pharmacophore features that will fit to one of many different substructures. The
3D locations of the features can be specified using different types of constraints, for example location,
distance, angle, torsion, shape constraints, and excluded volumes (regions of space
where ligand atoms must not occupy after being aligned to the pharmacophore).

For example, upon inspecting a set of ligands that are active against a certain target, you may discover that
each ligand contains a phenyl group, a carboxyl group, and a Nitrogen atom, and each is within a certain
distance range relative to each other. It is possible to create a pharmacophore that contains these three 
groups with appropriate distance constraints similar to the pharmacophore shown in Figure 1.

Figure 1: Simple pharmacophore containing 
substructures with distance constraints

You could then use this pharmacophore to search a database of small molecules. Molecules that fit the pharmacophore may also be active. 
You may modify the pharmacophore to make it more or less specific depending on 
the results of the search. For example, you could
change the atom definitions to allow multiple elements, change the bond 
definitions, etc.

Another way to make this pharmacophore more general is to replace each
substructure with one of the pre-defined pharmacophore feature available in Discovery Studio (as shown in Figure 2). Replacing the phenyl
group with a hydrophobic feature, the Nitrogen with a positive ionizable,
and the carboxyl group with a negative ionizable may match molecules
the have similar activity but different substructures.

Figure 2: Pharmacophore containing features and distance constraints

It is often more beneficial to use location constraints rather than
distance constraints for pharmacophores containing features (as shown in Figure 3).
Location constraints will still confine the relative distance between
the features to be within a certain range (governed by the radius of
the location constraints), but offer a way to rank hits fit value . The closer the matching portion of the molecule is to the centroid
of the location constraint, the higher the fit value will be.

Figure 3: Pharmacophore containing features and location constraints.

### Pharmacophore features

Typically, pharmacophore features include hydrophobic, aromatic,
hydrogen bond acceptor, hydrogen bond donor, positive ionizable, and negative ionizable groups.

Each pre-defined pharmacophore feature in Discovery Studio has a
precise definition. For instance, a positive ionizable feature is defined as follows:

It will match a primary, secondary, or tertiary amine, an amidine group, a guanidine group, an amidine group with a Hydrogen, and a positive charged group. 
It is possible to designate where the mapping will take place. For example, the amidine H group will map to the centroid of the three heavy atoms. The 
definitions also include any exclusions. For example, the positive group excludes positive charges that are directly bonded to an atom with a negative charge.
In addition to the predefined features, Discovery Studio allows you to define a feature and use it in pharmacophore generation.

Create pharmacophores Work with pharmacophores in the Data Table View Work with pharmacophores in the Hierarchy View Query toolbar Pharmacophore tools tutorials

# Create pharmacophores

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophores_creating.htm

## Create pharmacophores

There are many ways to generate pharmacophores in Discovery Studio . It is 
possible to automatically create pharmacophores from a set of ligands with
measured activity, create common features pharmacophores from a set of active
ligands, enumerate pharmacophore features from a binding site of a receptor, or 
from a set of ligands. There are also many interactive tools available that 
allow you to cluster, merge, and customize pharmacophore
features. For more information on the protocols and tools used to create and
manipulate pharmacophores and pharmacophore features see Pharmacophores tools . 
This topic describes how to build pharmacophore models from a 
ligand template.

There are two basic types of pharmacophore features in Discovery Studio : vectors (e.g., hydrogen bond acceptors) and single points (e.g., negative ionizable features). Typically, the vector features have one
point that represents the location on the ligand and another point that represents the location
of the complimentary feature on the receptor needed for the interaction.

| Feature | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Hydrogen bond acceptor | Vector |
| Hydrogen bond donor | Vector |
| Aromatic ring | Vector |
| Hydrophobic | Single point |
| Hydrophobic Aromatic | Single point |
| Hydrophobic Aliphatic | Single point |
| Negative charge | Single point |
| Negative ionizable | Single point |
| Positive charge | Single point |
| Positive ionizable | Single point |

In addition to the
features, there are other features that can be added to constrain how a pharmacophore maps to 
a ligand including location constraints, exclusion constraints, and shape constraints.
Adding location constraints to the pharmacophore features defines the relative position of 
the features required for a ligand to map. An exclusion constraint represents areas of space where no 
ligand atoms can be present after being aligned to the pharmacophore. A shape constraint ensures
that only ligands that have a similar shape to the shape feature will be considered. 
You can add all these pharmacophore features by selecting an appropriate set of atoms
on a template ligand and then adding them using either of the following two methods:

* Choose Structure | Query Feature... from the menu bar.

* Use the Query toolbar.

Both methods enable appropriate options based on the type of atoms selected. Simple
rules are used to enable the appropriate features types. For example,
if three or more sp2 hybridized atoms in a ring are selected, the aromatic ring feature is enabled and can be used to add an aromatic ring feature.

For efficiency, simple atom definitions are used to enable 
the features. It is possible to add a feature to a set of atoms that would not actually be considered
a map when comparing that ligand to the pharmacophore. In order to ensure that the ligand atoms will
map the pharmacophore features, use the Feature Mapping protocol.

### Adding a single point feature

To create one of the single point features, select a set of atoms and click the Point Feature button
on the Query toolbar .

To change the type of the Point Feature, and thus the nature of the query, make sure the PointFeature tab in the Data Table View is 
visible, and choose one of the following types from the Type cell:

* Hydrophobe

* Hydrophobe_Aromatic

* Hydrophobe_Aliphatic

* Ionizable_Negative

* Ionizable_Positive

* Charged_Negative

* Charged_Positive

Or choose Structure | Query Feature... and choose Point as the Feature and (Hydrophobe, Hydrophobe_Aromatic, etc.) as the Type on the Create Feature dialog.

### Adding a vector feature

After selecting an appropriate set of atoms (e.g., an oxygen atom attached to a carbon atom for hydrogen bond acceptor, 
oxygen with a hydrogen attached for a
hydrogen bond donor, or atoms from an aromatic ring for the aromatic ring feature), use the 
Acceptor Feature button to add a hydrogen bond acceptor feature, the Donor Feature button to 
add a hydrogen bond donor, or the Aromatic Ring button
to at the aromatic ring feature.

Alternatively, choose Structure | Query Feature... from the menu bar and choose Acceptor , Donor , or RingAromatic as the Feature on the Create Feature dialog.

### Adding constraints

To create a location constraint feature

* Select one of the following: atom Hydrogen Bond Acceptor Feature Hydrogen Bond Donor Feature Centroid Feature Aromatic Ring Feature top level query operator on a pharmacophore (often called QueryRoot), which will add location constraints to the features

* atom

* Hydrogen Bond Acceptor Feature

* Hydrogen Bond Donor Feature

* Centroid Feature

* Aromatic Ring Feature

* top level query operator on a pharmacophore (often called QueryRoot), which will add location constraints to the features

* select the Location Constraint Feature button. Alternatively, choose Structure | Query Feature... from the menu bar and choose Location as the Feature
on the Create Feature dialog .

Alternatively, choose Structure | Query Feature... from the menu bar and choose Location as the Feature
on the Create Feature dialog .

To create a shape constraint

* Select part or all of a ligand.

* Choose the
Shape Feature button.

* Alternatively, choose Structure | Query Feature... and choose Shape as the Feature
on the Create Feature dialog .

When adding a shape to a pharmacophore, the pharmacophore 
features must have a minimum of three location constraints.

#### Exclusion constraints

To create Exclusion Constraint Features

* Select an atom or set of atoms.

* Click the Exclusion
Constraint button.

* Alternatively, choose Structure | Query Feature... and choose ExclusionSphere as the Feature
on the Create Feature dialog .

#### Further information

After creating the pharmacophore, you can manipulate feature attributes from the Data Table View or the Hierarchy View. For example, you can change the vector
orientation of a hydrogen bond acceptor, change the radius of an excluded volume, change the type of a point feature,
etc. See the following topics for more information:

Work with pharmacophores in the Data Table View Work with pharmacophores in the Hierarchy View Pharmacophore tools tutorials

# Work with pharmacophores in the Data Table View

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/pharmacophores_data-table.htm

## Work with pharmacophores in the Data Table View

After creating a pharmacophore in
Discover Studio, you may want to
modify some of the feature attributes. You can use the Hierarchy View or the Data Table View to make these changes. This topic covers how to use the Data Table View to make the following changes:

* Change the vector orientation

* Change the feature type of a single point feature

* Change the constraint radius

When adding a hydrogen bond donor feature to a template molecule, a default
orientation of the vector head is used. You may want to move the orientation
of this vector if you have an idea of where the receptor interaction is
occurring.

To change the orientation from the Data Table View

* Click the DonorFeature tab.

* Find the attribute labeled Orientation and choose the desired option from the list.

Figure 1: Changing the orientation of a
hydrogen bond donor from the Data Table View

You can make similar changes to hydrogen bond acceptor and aromatic ring
features by changing the appropriate attributes on the AcceptorFeature or RingAromaticFeature tabs.

After using the Point Feature button
on the Query toolbar to place a single point
pharmacophore feature, you may want to change the feature type. You can 
do this from the Data Table View by navigating to the PointFeature tab and
changing the Type for the appropriate PointFeature as shown in Figure 2.

Figure 2: Changing the feature type 
in the Data Table View

There are several types to choose from. However, only the following types are appropriate when creating a single point pharmacophore feature:

* Hydrophobe

* Hydrophobe_Aromatic

* Hydrophobe_Aliphatic

* Ionizable_Negative

* Ionizable_Positive

* Charged_Negative

* Charged_Positive

Location constraints are added with a default radius based on the feature type:

| Feature Type | Default Radius |
| --- | --- |
| Location constraint on a single point feature | 1.6 angstroms |
| Location constraint on a vector feature | 1.6 angstroms on the vector tail 2.2 angstroms on the vector head |
| Exclusion constraint | 1.2 angstroms |

In essence, the radius of location constraints determine how
close the ligand must be to the centroid of the feature in
order to be considered a match.
The radius of the exclusion constraint defines the region of space where
an atom from the ligand cannot occupy after it is aligned to the pharmacophore.
You can make the constraints more or less restrictive be changing
the default radius:

* Select the feature in the
Data Table View

* Right-click and choose Attributes of
Constraint Name...

* Change the Radius attribute to a numeric
value.

Figure 3: Changing the
radius of an exclusion constraint in the Data Table View

## Analyzing 3D QSAR Pharmacophore Log Files

The following table describes the sections of the query log file generated by the 3D QSAR Pharmacophore Generation protocol:

| Comments | Section |
| --- | --- |
| Pharmacophore generation parameters | |
| Features selected Values for Min and Max number of features | |
| Description of the pharmacophore including the feature definitions, feature weights, tolerance values, and x, y, z coordinates. | |
| Interfeature distance (Å) matrix. | |
| Training set summary If Est > Act the Error = Est/Act If Est < Act the Error = -Act/Est | |
| Cost of hypothesis (i.e., cost of the pharmacophore). The Fixed cost and the Null cost are both theoretical cost values. The Fixed cost represents the cost of a perfect pharmacophore (the lower bound) and the Null cost represents the cost of the worst possible pharmacophore (the upper bound). It is the cost that the pharmacophore would be if all activity values were predicted to be the average activity value. The actual cost of the pharmacophore should be somewhere between these two values. The closer it is to the Fixed cost, the more likely it is to be a true correlation rather than chance. See Cost Analysis in HypoGen for more information. | |

* If Est > Act the Error = Est/Act

* If Est < Act the Error = -Act/Est

The actual cost of the
pharmacophore should be somewhere between these two values. The closer it
is to the Fixed cost, the more likely it is to be a true correlation rather than
chance. See Cost Analysis in HypoGen for more information.

# Build Database tools

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/phcp_blpdt.htm

## Build Database tools

These tools allow you to build ligand and pharmacophore databases.

### Build Indexed Ligand DB for Fast Searching

Build 3D Database: Opens the Build 3D Database protocol dialog. This protocol uses Catalyst to generate a multiconformation ligand database. The database is automatically indexed with sub-structure, pharmacophore feature, and shape information for fast database searching.

After creating a database, use Search 3D Database to search or Browse 3D Database to browse it.

By default, databases are visible to all users on the a Pipeline Pilot Server . Use the Advanced | Visibility parameter to create a database only visible to you.

### Add/Remove from Pharmacophore DB

Add to Ligand Profiler Database: Opens the Add to Ligand Profiler Database protocol dialog. This protocol adds a pharmacophore to the Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore Database.

The Ligand Profiler database can be searched using the Ligand Profiler protocol.

You can classify the pharmacophores according to a hierarchy of categories.

In addition to the Input Pharmacophore , the following parameters can be defined: Target Class, Target Subclass, Target Family, Target Acronym, Target, Drug Classification, Therapeutic Classification, Action Mode, Notes, Bibliography, and Actives.

Some parameters take predefined or custom single or multiple values, or extended text. For details see Add to Ligand Profiler Database - Parameters .

Note: The Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore database can be searched using the Ligand Profiler protocol. When accessing the Input LigandProfilerDB Pharmacophores parameter, the Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore database is displayed in a searchable list with the following hierarchy:

Target Class Target Subclass Target Family Target Acronym

This parameter makes it easy to search for and select all the pharmacophores derived from a particular target class, subclass, or family and use them to screen a set of ligands.

The Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore Database is located at: $(SciTegicRoot)/public/DS/LigandProfilerDB/Standard

Remove from Ligand Profiler Database: Opens the Remove from Ligand Profiler Database protocol dialog. This protocol removes a pharmacophore from the Ligand Profiler Pharmacophore Database.

### Access methods

| Menu | Tools \| Pharmacophores \| Build Database |

# Create Pharmacophore Automatically tools

Source type: HTML

Source section: tspharmacophores

Source file: tspharmacophores/phcp_cpat.htm

## Create Pharmacophore Automatically tools

The Create Pharmacophore Automatically tools allow you to automatically build pharmacophore models from a ligand, receptor, or a receptor-ligand complex.

### From a Bioactive Conformation

Auto Pharmacophore Generation: Opens the Auto Pharmacophore Generation protocol dialog. This protocol enumerates all pharmacophore features, scores all possible pharmacophore combinations, and returns the top pharmacophores. The score is based on a predictive model that uses simple descriptors derived from the type and relative location of the pharmacophore features to predict the number of hits from a diverse database.

### From a Receptor-Ligand Complex

Interaction Pharmacophore Generation: Opens the Interaction Pharmacophore Generation protocol dialog. This protocol generates pharmacophores from a ligand and a receptor. All selected non-bond interactions are enumerated between the receptor and ligand. Each non-bond interaction is replaced with a corresponding pharmacophore feature on the ligand. All pharmacophore combinations are enumerated and scored. The score is based on a predictive model that uses simple descriptors derived from the type and relative location of the pharmacophore features to predict the number of hits from a diverse database. The top pharmacophores, or a diverse set of pharmacophores, are returned from all possibilities depending on the settings.

Similar to the top scoring method, the diverse method uses the top scoring pharmacophore for the first pharmacophore. However, the remaining pharmacophores are placed based on the maximum average distance from the pharmacophores that have already been placed. The distance between two pharmacophores is computed as 1.0 minus a similarity measure. The similarity is a function based on the number of matching pharmacophore feature pairs and the root-mean-square fits between the matching features normalized by the function for each pharmacophore compared to itself. A perfect match between two pharmacophores results in a similarity of 1 and a distance of 0. Two pharmacophores that have no common pharmacophore features will have a similarity of 0 and a distance of 1. For details of the equations used see the clustering topic.

### From a Set of Ligands

Common Feature Pharmacophore Generation: Opens the Common Feature Pharmacophore Generation protocol dialog. This protocol generates common feature pharmacophores from a set of active ligands. The algorithm can also optionally use information from inactive ligands to place excluded volume features.

The input ligands must contain the following properties:

* Principal: Indicates whether the ligand is active ( 2 ), moderately active ( 1 )
or inactive ( 0 ). 2 is used if the property is missing.

* MaxOmitFeat: Indicates how many features are allowed to miss for each molecule. 0 is used if the property is missing.

Ensemble Pharmacophore Generation: Opens the Ensemble Pharmacophore Generation protocol dialog. This protocol generates an ensemble of pharmacophores from a set of active ligands. Pharmacophores are created and evaluated using active and inactive ligands using a ROC score. Based on the ROC score the best pharmacophores are selected for each active ligand cluster. A detailed report is presented for each active ligand cluster.

### Advanced

3D QSAR Pharmacophore Generation: Opens the 3D QSAR Pharmacophore Generation protocol dialog. This protocol derives Structure Activity Relationship (SAR) pharmacophore models from a set of molecules for which activity values are known. It optionally generates excluded volume features using inactive compounds.

Input ligand data must contain the following properties:

* Activ: The compound's tested activity. Data such as IC50 values should be used and all values should be greater than 0.0. Ideally the data should span 4 orders of magnitude. If logarithmic data is used, Logarithmic Activity must be set to True .

* Uncert: the uncertainty in the activity value, a ratio of the reported value to the minimum and maximum values,
must be greater than 1.0. 3.0 is used if the property is missing.

Steric Refinement with Excluded Volumes: Opens the Steric Refinement with Excluded Volumes protocol dialog. This protocol adds excluded volumes to an input pharmacophore. The algorithm identifies areas of space that are occupied by inactive ligands and strategically places excluded volumes in these regions to reduce the number of inactives that can map the pharmacophore.

* Principal: Indicates whether the ligand is active ( 2 ), moderately active ( 1 )
or inactive ( 0 ).

* MaxOmitFeat: Indicates how many features are allowed to miss for each molecule. If missing, MaxOmitFeat is set to 0.

### Access methods

| Tool bar | Pharmacophores \| Create Pharmacophore Automatically |
| --- | --- |
| Menu | Tools \| Pharmacophores \| Create Pharmacophore Automatically |
| Menu | View \| Tool Panels \| Create Pharmacophore Automatically |

Pharmacophores tools Pharmacophore Features
