# Consensus Score - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsrlinteractions

Source file: tsrlinteractions/receptor-ligand_interactions_consensus_score-para.htm

## Consensus Score - Parameters

### Finds the consensus between a set of scoring functions

Consensus scoring is a fast way to identify ligands that score high in more than one scoring function. For each specified scoring function, the ligands are listed by score in descending order. The consensus score for a molecule is equal to the number of scores that are in the top rank percentile. The top rank percentile can be changed using Consensus Percentage .

The following property is output:

* Consensus : The consensus score is an integer between zero (none of the scores are in the top ranking percentile) and the total number of scores (all of the scores are in the top ranking percentile) listed in Input Properties . The name of the property can be changed using Consensus Property Name .

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Ligands | Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. |
| Input Properties | Score property names for calculating a consensus score. The consensus scoring algorithm assumes that each score represents the interested scientific features in descending order, meaning that a higher score value is better. Any property that does not obey this rule may not produce the desired results. For example, the lower the internal-energy of a system, the more stable the system becomes. Hence, in order to generate meaningful consensus scores, such a property should not be selected. |
| Advanced | Contains less commonly used parameters. |
| Consensus on Group | If set to True, the consensus score is calculated on ligand groups. Ligand groups are created by a specified property (see parameter below). Valid Values: True, False |
| Consensus on Group Property | The ligands are grouped by the specified property name before calculating the consensus score on each group. The property value needs to be numeric. |
| Consensus Property Name | Name of the consensus score property added to each molecule. |
| Consensus Percentage | Percentage of top molecules to include in the consensus. Ligands in the top percentile are assigned "1". The remaining entries in the ranking lists are set to "0". The consensus score for each molecule is obtained by summing over all its list entries. |
| Use Best Pose Only | Use only the highest ranked ligand pose (by score). Valid Values: True , False |
| Group by Property | Property name for grouping ligand poses when Use Best Pose Only is enabled. For each group the best scoring pose is determined. |

# Consensus Score

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsrlinteractions

Source file: tsrlinteractions/receptor-ligand_interactions_consensus_score.htm

## Consensus Score

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Output and input files

* Analyzing results

The Consensus Score protocol calculates the consensus
scores of a series of docked ligands for which other scores have been
previously computed.

Consensus scoring is a fast way of identifying ligands that score
high in more than one scoring function. For each selected scoring
function, the ligands are listed by score in descending order. The
consensus score for a molecule is equal to its frequency of occurrence
in the top rank percentile of each scoring function. The rank
percentile considered in the consensus score is variable and configurable
in the protocol.

Consensus Score jobs can be run in two modes.

* By default, every entry in the input is treated separately.

* If Use Best Pose Only is selected, then the ligands
are grouped. This option is typically used to group molecules with
multiple poses from a docking run, such that the score for each molecule or scoring function combination is taken from the corresponding
best scoring pose for that combination. This produces a single consensus score value for each ligand rather than for each pose.

* In the Protocols Explorer , open Receptor-Ligand Interaction | Consensus Score .

* In the Parameters Explorer, set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Ligands Specify the ligands to be used by the protocol. For details, see Specifying Ligands . Input Properties Select the score property names to calculate the consensus scores. For details about the remaining parameters, see Consensus Score - Parameters .

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Ligands | Specify the ligands to be used by the protocol. For details, see Specifying Ligands . |
| Input Properties | Select the score property names to calculate the consensus scores. |

For details about the remaining parameters, see Consensus Score - Parameters .

* In the Protocols menu bar, click the Run button.

* Monitor the status in the Jobs Explorer .

When the job finishes, double-click it in the Jobs Explorer to open the Output folder in the Files Explorer. See Output and input files for details about the files generated by this protocol. If the job did not run successfully, the Jobs Explorer will report an error. See Troubleshooting - Protocols for details.

By default, intermediate files generated by this protocol are not saved. To save the intermediate files, select the Save intermediate files when running protocols option on the Protocols page of the Preferences dialog.

#### Output files

The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| <ligands>.sd | Contains the scored ligands. |
| <ligands>_fail.sd | Contains ligands which failed the protocol. |
| <ligands>_CScore.txt | Log file generated by the server containing information on how the consensus was calculated. |

#### Input files

The following files are created in the Input directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| <ligands>.sd | The ligands used in the calculation. |
| Protocol.pr_xml | The saved protocol and job parameters. You can load this file at any time to re-run this protocol with the same settings. You can also share it with other users. For details see Discovery Studio Parameters (PR_XML) . |

The Consensus Score protocol calculates the consensus scores of a series of ligands from a set of previously computed scores. The net result is a
set of ligands with a new integer consensus property representing the number of different scoring functions that highly rank the ligand (based on a
user configurable percentage). This property can be used like any other; for example, structures can be sorted by it in the Data Table View and it can be used to chart plots . For details about viewing, sorting, and filtering the results in the Data Table View, see Analyzing results with the Data Table View .

#### Further information

Specify Ligands Theory - Scoring

# De Novo Evolution - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsrlinteractions

Source file: tsrlinteractions/receptor-ligand_interactions_de_novo_evolution-para.htm

## De Novo Evolution - Parameters

### Uses a fragment based approach to suggests novel ligands from a scaffold

Adds small fragments from a library to a scaffold in a protein active site. Fragments are placed in complementary positions to the receptor using a calculated interaction map to produce a collection of high scoring molecules. The nature of fragment selection and construction of new ligands depends on Evolution Mode .

This protocol adds many properties to the data stream (depending on the Evolution Mode ) including:

* GENERATION : generation number.

* FAMILY : family number.

* FRAG_ADDED : number of fragments added.

* SCORE_SUM_FRAG : sum of Ludi fragment scores.

* FRAGMENTS : linked fragment names.

* SCORE_SUM_FRAG : sum of the Ludi fragment scores added to the scaffold.

* MW : ligand molecular weight.

* BUMP_VIOL : number of fragment bumps in Combinatorial mode.

Note:

* A fragment library can be created using De Novo Library Generation protocol.

See Also:

* Böhm, H. J. The computer program LUDI: A new method for the de novo design of enzyme inhibitors. J. Comput.-Aided Mol. Design 1992 , 6, 61-78.

* Böhm, H. J. LUDI: rule based automatic design of new substituents for enzyme inhibitor leads. J. Comput.-Aided Mol. Design 1992 , 6, 593-606.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Receptor | Structure to use as the receptor. Ensure receptors have hydrogens and complete valence shells. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all visible molecules. Notes: The receptor should not contain alternate conformations. You can use the protein tools in Discovery Studio to prepare a receptor. |
| Input Receptor Target Atoms | Only fragments which interact with all specified receptor atoms are selected. Specified atoms should be in the site sphere. In Discovery Studio, select a group containing the desired receptor atoms. In Pipeline Pilot, the receptor atoms are specified in a comma separated list with atom indices ( e.g. , 14,444,333). |
| Input Ligand Scaffold | Specify the ligand scaffold (limited to 200 atoms). In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all visible molecules. Notes: The scaffold must have hydrogens and complete valence shells. |
| Input Fragment Libraries | Select a link fragment library file. Fragment libraries consist of two files that need to be in the same directory, however, only one needs to be selected. Note : In combinatorial mode multiple libraries can be selected. |
| Evolution Mode | Mode for De Novo evolution: Full Evolution : Molecules are built in an evolutionary fashion starting from a scaffold. Fragments are fused and molecules are selected by score for the next iteration. Quick : Fragments are consecutively fused to the scaffold molecule at each generation. Combinatorial : Fragments are only fused to the specified scaffold positions to create a combinatorial library. Valid Values: Full Evolution , Quick, Combinatorial |
| Input Site Sphere | Defines a sphere in the receptor where receptor-ligands interactions are permitted. In Pipeline Pilot, define the sphere as x,y,z,r where x,y,z specifies the coordinates of the center and r is the radius of the sphere ( e.g. , 83.2,-43.3,42.24,6). In Discovery Studio, define the sphere using the Define and Edit Binding Site tools and then select the coordinates from the list. |
| Evolution Scoring Function | Scoring function to use during evolution. The fitness of the newly created ligand (scaffold and fused fragment) is evaluated by this function. The following functions are available: LigScore1 and LigScore2 PLP1 and PLP2 Jain PMF and PMF04 Ludi1, Ludi2, and Ludi3 Note: The score value returned may be the negative of the selected score to provide a consistent interpretation of that data, i.e. ,a more positive value indicates a better score. See Also: Krammer, A.; Kirchhoff, P. D.; Jiang, X.; Venkatachalam, C. M.; Waldman, M. LigScore: a novel scoring function for predicting binding affinities. J. Mol. Graph. Model. 2005, 23, 395-407. Gehlhaar, D. K.; Bouzida, D.; Rejto, P. A. Rational Drug Design: Novel Methodology and Practical Applications; Parrill, L.; Rami Reddy, M; Series title: ACS symposium series, 719; American Chemical Society: Washington, DC., 1999; pp. 292-311. Gehlhaar, D. K.; Verkhivker, G. M.; Rejto, P. A.; Sherman, C. J.; Fogel, D. B.; Fogel, L. J.; Freer, S. T. Molecular Recognition of the Inhibitor AG-1343 by HIV-1 Protease: Conformationally Flexible Docking by Evolutionary Programming. Chemistry & Biology 1995, 2, 317. Jain, A. N. Scoring noncovalent protein-ligand interactions: A continuous differentiable function tuned to compute binding affinities. J. Comput.-Aided Mol. Design 1996, 10, 427-440. Muegge, I.; Martin, Y. C. A General and Fast Scoring Function for Protein-Ligand Interactions: A Simplified Potential Approach. J. Med. Chem. 1999, 42, 791. Muegge, I. PMF Scoring Revisited. J. Med. Chem. 2005, 49, 5895. Böhm, H. J. Prediction of binding constants of protein ligands: A fast method for the prioritization of hits obtained from the de novo design or 3D database search programs. J. Comput.-Aided Mol. Design 1998, 12, 309-323. Valid Values: LigScore1, LigScore2, PLP1, PLP2, Jain, PMF, PMF04, Ludi Energy Estimate 1, Ludi Energy Estimate 2, Ludi Energy Estimate 3 |
| LigScore | Parameters for LigScore scoring functions. |
| Scoring LigScore Forcefield | Forcefield to use for LigScore1 and LigScore2: Dreiding : DREIDING forcefield with Gasteiger charges. CFF : Consistent Force Field. Valid Values: Dreiding , CFF |
| PMF | Parameters for PMF scoring function. |
| Scoring PMF Ignore Hydrogens | Ignore hydrogen atom contributions. Valid Values: True , False |
| Scoring PMF Carbon-Carbon Cutoff | Cutoff distance for carbon-carbon interactions (Å). Please note, the default value of 12 showed an improved score-activity correlation (Krammer et al ., 2005) than the originally published value of 6 (Muegge and Martin, 1999). |
| Scoring PMF Other Interactions Cutoff | Cutoff distance for other atom interactions (Å). Please note, the default value of 12 showed an improved score-activity correlation (Krammer et al ., 2005) than the originally published value of 9 (Muegge and Martin, 1999). |
| PMF04 | Parameters for PMF04 scoring function. |
| Scoring PMF04 Ignore Hydrogens | Ignore hydrogen atom contributions. Valid Values: True , False |
| Scoring PMF04 Carbon-Carbon Cutoff | Cutoff distance for carbon-carbon interactions (Å). |
| Scoring PMF04 Other Interactions Cutoff | Cutoff distance for other atom interactions (Å). |
| Jain | Parameters for the Jain scoring function. |
| Scoring Jain Ignore Non-Polar Hydrogens | Ignore non-polar hydrogen atoms when computing the score. Valid Values: True, False |
| Scoring Jain Ignore Water | Ignore water molecules when computing the score. Valid Values: True, False |
| Evolution | Evolution parameters. |
| Evolution Maximum Number Generations | Maximum number of generations before the evolution is terminated. |
| Evolution Maximum Number Survivors | Maximum number of hits surviving each generation. For "Quick" mode, the maximum number of fragments to attach to the scaffold in each generation. |
| Evolution Maximum Population Size | Maximum number of hits in the population. |
| Evolution Save All Survivors | Save fragments and molecules files in the Intermediate directory. Valid Values: True, False |
| Evolution Random Fragments | Replace the lowest scoring surviving fragment with a randomly chosen one from the remaining pool. Valid Values: True, False |
| Combinatorial | Parameters for Combinatorial mode. |
| Combinatorial Link Points | Scaffold-atom indices to use as link points. Only the first 20 suitable atoms in the list will be used (e.g., 3 10 44). Note : Link points should have only one atom singly bonded (e.g., the fluorine in R-CH2- F ) In Discovery Studio, choose a Group containing the atoms to use as link points, or create a new Group from the current selection. |
| Input Library Mapping | Mapping of which libraries correspond to which scaffold link point. The same library can be selected more than once. In the following example, the peptidex library will be used for link points 1 and 3, and the organicx for link point 5: Input Fragment Libraries = peptidex.str,organicx.str Combinatorial Link Points = 1,3,5 Input Library Mapping = peptidex,peptidex,organicx |
| Combinatorial Radius | A search sphere is created at each link point with the specified radius (Å). |
| Advanced | Contains less commonly used parameters. |
| Link Points Maximum Alignment Angle | Maximum alignment angle limits the search for fragments whose alignment angle to the link site is less than or equal to a specified value. The alignment angle is formed by a bond in the fragment and the X-H bond that defines the link site in the partially built molecule. A value between 10° and 15° is recommended for most applications. |
| Fitting | Parameter that control the fragment fitting. |
| Fitting Scoring Function | Ludi scoring function to use to prioritize the fragment hits for receptor-based runs. Three different algorithms are available, each estimates the change in free energy upon binding the fragment to the receptor. Each fragment is evaluated as a function of the potential number of hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic and ionic contacts it can make and an estimate is made of the penalty due to freezing the internal degrees of freedom of the ligand. The following scoring functions are available: Energy estimate 1 Energy estimate 2 Energy estimate 3 Valid Values: Energy estimate 1, Energy estimate 2, Energy estimate 3 |
| Fitting Link Weight | Relative weight for aligning a fragment with the ligand link sites. A factor of 2 can be effective. |
| Fitting Lipophilic Weight | Relative weight for aligning a fragment with lipophilic interaction sites. A factor of 10 can be effective. |
| Fitting Polar Weight | Relative weight for aligning a fragment with the hydrogen bond interaction sites. A factor of 10 can be effective. |
| Fitting Maximum Fit Attempts | Specifies the maximum number of attempts to fit a fragment to a set of interaction sites (maximum 1000000). |
| Fitting Bond Rotation | Generate fragment conformations: None : only existing library conformations are used. One at a Time : conformations are generated by rotating each rotatable bond without changing the angle of other rotatable bonds in the fragment. Two at a Time : rotatable bonds are altered in pairs to generate new fragment conformations. Note : The degree of rotation depends on the periodicity of the dihedral angle. For bonds connecting two sp3 carbons, the rotation is done in 120° increments. For bonds connecting two sp2 carbons, the rotation is done in 180° increments. For fragments with multiple rotatable bonds, only one bond is modified at a time. Valid Values: None, One at a time, Two at a time |
| Fitting Invert Coordinates | Generate and fit both the fragments in the library and their mirror image. Valid Values: True, False |
| Fitting Maximum RMSD | Maximum root mean square deviation (RMSD) from maximal receptor ligand interaction (Å). At each receptor interaction site there is some range of interaction geometry between the ligand and receptor that maximizes the interaction. Deviation from this maximum, therefore, constitutes a measure of the quality of fit. Poor fits have high deviations and good fits have low deviations. As Ludi fits each fragment to the interaction sites, the RMSD is computed. For most fragments, if the RMSD exceeds the value of Maximum RMSD, the fragment is discarded. If Ludi is trying to fit a large fragment, it may allow the RMSD to exceed the value of the Maximum RMSD parameter. |
| Fragment Filters | Parameters for filtering fragments. |
| Fragment Filters Remove Duplicates | Unique SMILES filtering is performed to remove duplicates after each generation. Valid Values: True , False |
| Fragment Filters Clash-Check | Perform clash check when linking fragments to the scaffold. Without this check structures may be produced containing atoms that clash. Note : In "Full Evolutionary" mode, no clash check is required. Valid Values: True , False |
| Fragment Filters Required Groups | Only accept fragments containing groups, specified as linear descriptions of how the atoms are connected, e.g., a carboxylate group should be entered as OCO, not COO. Only elements with a one letter chemical symbol can be used. Multiple groups should be comma separated, e.g., OCO, NC. It is not possible to specify the bond order within a group, chirality, or branched groups. A fragment is only accepted if all specified groups are found. |
| Fragment Filters Rejected Groups | Reject fragments containing groups, specified as linear descriptions of how the atoms are connected, e.g., a carboxylate group should be entered as OCO, not COO. Only elements with a one letter chemical symbol can be used. Multiple groups should be comma separated, e.g., OCO, NC. It is not possible to specify the bond order within a group, chirality, or branched groups. A fragment is rejected if any of the specified groups is found. |
| Fragment Filters Required Elements | Only accept fragments containing the specified elements. Multiple elements should be comma separated, e.g., B,C,F. A fragment is accepted if all of the specified elements are found. |
| Fragment Filters Rejected Elements | Reject fragments containing the specified elements. Only elements with a one letter chemical symbol can be used. Multiple elements should be comma separated, e.g., B,C,F. A fragment is rejected if any of the specified elements is found. |
| Fragment Filters Minimum Atoms in Fragment | Minimum number of atoms in a fragment. |
| Fragment Filters Maximum Atoms in Fragment | Maximum number of atoms in a fragment (for libraries with larger fragments a value of 150 is suggested). |
| Fragment Filters Required Formal Charge | Require fragments to contain charged functional groups. The following choices are available: No formal charge requirement : no fragment charge required Positive (ammonium, amidino, guanidino) : positive fragment charge required Negative (carboxylate) : negative fragment charge required Valid Values: No formal charge requirement , Positive (ammonium, amidino, guanidino), Negative (carboxylate) |
| Fragment Filters Fragment Range | Comma separated range of fragments in the library to search. The first fragment in the library is indicated by 1. The last fragment is indicated by END. |
| Hit Criteria | Parameters for controlling the criteria for a hit. |
| Hit Criteria Minimum Separation | Minimum distance (Å) that must separate intermolecular pairs of carbon atoms. As Ludi considers each library fragment, it fits the fragment onto the interaction sites, then checks that the fragment's carbon atoms do not overlap receptor carbon atoms. Pairs of carbon atoms whose centers are separated by a distance less than or equal this value are considered to have undesirable overlap. Although the value for the Minimum Separation parameter only pertains to pairs of carbons, Ludi derives threshold distances for other atom pairs from it and checks all intermolecular pairs for overlap. The threshold distances for non-carbon atoms are obtained by scaling the specified value in a manner consistent with the relative sizes of the carbon and non-carbon van der Waals radii. A value between 3.0 and 3.5 is recommended. |
| Hit Criteria Minimum Surface | Minimum percentage of surface area contact between the fragment and receptor. When Ludi considers whether it is appropriate to suggest a particular fragment, one of the criteria it considers is the percentage of the fragment surface area that is in contact with the receptor. If this percentage is less than the specified value, the fragment is discarded. For example, a value of 70 means that only those fragments whose surfaces are 70% in contact with the receptor are suggested by Ludi. A value of zero for this parameter means that the surface area contact criterion is not used. Increasing the value of the Minimum Surface parameter will reduce the number of hits. The algorithm that Ludi uses to calculate the surface area yields only approximate values, so the Minimum Surface parameter should be viewed as a rough paring method. |
| Hit Criteria Minimum Score | Minimum score for a fragment fit. Note : If you modify this parameter, you may get different results, even if you do not adjust the other parameters. This is because the algorithm will pursue more iterations to satisfy the score threshold. |
| Hit Criteria Maximum Unfilled Cavity | Maximum size for buried cavities produced by a fragment fit (Å 3 ). If the specified value is larger than 0, Ludi searches for buried cavities after fitting a fragment, and, if the cavity is larger than the value specified, the fit is rejected. The size of the cavity is determined by the number of unoccupied cubes between the protein and the ligand with no connection to bulk solvent. |
| Hit Criteria Search Method | Determines the fragment search method. The following options are available: FAST : as soon as a hit has been found with a matching set of interaction sites, no further attempts are made to fit this set of fragment target sites to any of the matched interaction sites. The fragment position with the highest score is saved. BEST : fitting is exhaustive, allowing all combinations of interaction sites to be matched against a specific set of target sites on the fragment, and the fragment position with the best score is saved. Note : The combinations of target sites that Ludi considers for a specific fragment is specified in the target library file. Valid Values: FAST , BEST |
| Hit Criteria Reject Bifurcated Hydrogen Bonds | Reject bifurcated hydrogen bonds. A bifurcated hydrogen bond is one in which an acceptor is symmetrically paired with two donors or vice versa. Valid Values: True, False |
| Hit Criteria Reject Unpaired Buried Polar Groups | Reject hits that bury unpaired polar groups on either the fitted fragment or the receptor. Valid Values: True , False |
| Hit Criteria Minimum Electrostatic Repulsion Distance | Reject electrostatic repulsions of the specified minimum distance or less (Å). Leave blank to consider all interactions. For example, if fragments are being fit at a metal ion coordination sites. The distance separating polar oxygen pairs or oxygen/nitrogen pairs is compared to the value of the parameter plus 0.8 Å. A default value of 2.5 Å is recommended. |
| Interaction Site | Parameters that control the interaction site generation. |
| Interaction Site Density of Lipophilic Sites | Density of lipophilic sites. When Ludi finds an interaction site, it populates the site with points or vectors that represent the geometry of the site. This parameter specifies how dense Ludi should make the population of points in interaction sites for lipophilic atoms. Too large a value here slows down the Ludi program though it increases the chances of finding suitable fragments. A value between 10 and 25 is recommended. |
| Interaction Site Density of Polar Sites | Density of polar sites. When Ludi finds an interaction site, it populates the site with points or vectors that represent the geometry of the site. This parameter specifies how dense Ludi should make the population of vectors in interaction sites for hydrogen bonds. Too large a value here slows down the Ludi program though it increases the chances of finding suitable fragments. A value between 15 and 25 is recommended. |
| Interaction Site Preselection Factor | Preselection factor controls the Ludi algorithm for selecting the combination of interaction sites onto which a fragment is fit. Ludi searches the list of interaction sites by distance criteria for suitable pairs, triplets, and quadruplets to match the fragments. For each set of interaction sites, the distances between interaction sites are compared to the fragment's corresponding intramolecular distances. For any corresponding pair of interaction site distance and fragment intramolecular distance, if the difference between the two is greater than the product of the values of the Preselection Factor parameter and the Maximum RMSD (see Fitting ), then the fragment is not fit to that set of interaction sites. Recommended values are between 1.5 and 2.5. Values larger than this tend to increase the time it takes for Ludi to fit fragments but can increase the number of fragments that Ludi is able to suggest. Values smaller than this speed up the Ludi program at the expense of sometimes missing a potentially useful fragment. |
| Interaction Site Differentiate Lipophilic Interactions | Match aliphatic fragment atoms with aliphatic receptor atoms, or aromatic fragment atoms to aromatic receptor atoms. Valid Values: True, False |

* Link points should have only one atom singly bonded (e.g., the fluorine in R-CH2- F )

In Discovery Studio, choose a Group containing the atoms to use as link points, or create a new Group from the current selection.

Mapping of which libraries correspond to which scaffold link point. The same library can be selected more than once.

In the following example, the peptidex library will be used for link points 1 and 3, and the organicx for link point 5:

Input Fragment Libraries = peptidex.str,organicx.str

Combinatorial Link Points = 1,3,5

Input Library Mapping = peptidex,peptidex,organicx

A search sphere is created at each link point with the specified radius (Å).

Contains less commonly used parameters.

Maximum alignment angle limits the search for fragments whose alignment angle to the link site is less than or equal to a specified value. The alignment angle is formed by a bond in the fragment and the X-H bond that defines the link site in the partially built molecule. A value between 10° and 15° is recommended for most applications.

Parameter that control the fragment fitting.

Ludi scoring function to use to prioritize the fragment hits for receptor-based runs.

Three different algorithms are available, each estimates the change in free energy upon binding the fragment to the receptor. Each fragment is evaluated as a function of the potential number of hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic and ionic contacts it can make and an estimate is made of the penalty due to freezing the internal degrees of freedom of the ligand.

The following scoring functions are available:

* Energy estimate 1

* Energy estimate 2

* Energy estimate 3

Valid Values: Energy estimate 1, Energy estimate 2, Energy estimate 3

Relative weight for aligning a fragment with the ligand link sites. A factor of 2 can be effective.

Relative weight for aligning a fragment with lipophilic interaction sites.
A factor of 10 can be effective.

Relative weight for aligning a fragment with the hydrogen bond interaction sites.
A factor of 10 can be effective.

Specifies the maximum number of attempts to fit a fragment to a set of interaction sites (maximum 1000000).

* None : only existing library conformations are used.

* One at a Time : conformations are generated by rotating each rotatable bond without changing the angle of other rotatable bonds in the fragment.

* Two at a Time : rotatable bonds are altered in pairs to generate new fragment conformations.

* The degree of rotation depends on the periodicity of the dihedral angle. For bonds connecting two sp3 carbons, the rotation is done in 120° increments. For bonds connecting two sp2 carbons, the rotation is done in 180° increments. For fragments with multiple rotatable bonds, only one bond is modified at a time.

Valid Values: None, One at a time, Two at a time

Generate and fit both the fragments in the library and their mirror image.

Maximum root mean square deviation (RMSD) from maximal receptor ligand interaction (Å). At each receptor interaction site there is some range of interaction geometry between the ligand and receptor that maximizes the interaction. Deviation from this maximum, therefore, constitutes a measure of the quality of fit. Poor fits have high deviations and good fits have low deviations. As Ludi fits each fragment to the interaction sites, the RMSD is computed. For most fragments, if the RMSD exceeds the value of Maximum RMSD, the fragment is discarded. If Ludi is trying to fit a large fragment, it may allow the RMSD to exceed the value of the Maximum RMSD parameter.

Parameters for filtering fragments.

Unique SMILES filtering is performed to remove duplicates after each generation.

Perform clash check when linking fragments to the scaffold.
Without this check structures may be produced containing atoms that clash.

* In "Full Evolutionary" mode, no clash check is required.

Only accept fragments containing groups, specified as linear descriptions of how the atoms are connected, e.g., a carboxylate group should be entered as OCO, not COO. Only elements with a one letter chemical symbol can be used. Multiple groups should be comma separated, e.g., OCO, NC. It is not possible to specify the bond order within a group, chirality, or branched groups.

A fragment is only accepted if all specified groups are found.

Reject fragments containing groups, specified as linear descriptions of how the atoms are connected, e.g., a carboxylate group should be entered as OCO, not COO. Only elements with a one letter chemical symbol can be used. Multiple groups should be comma separated, e.g., OCO, NC. It is not possible to specify the bond order within a group, chirality, or branched groups.

A fragment is rejected if any of the specified groups is found.

A fragment is accepted if all of the specified elements are found.

A fragment is rejected if any of the specified elements is found.

Minimum number of atoms in a fragment.

Maximum number of atoms in a fragment (for libraries with larger fragments a value of 150 is suggested).

Require fragments to contain charged functional groups.

* No formal charge requirement : no fragment charge required

* Positive (ammonium, amidino, guanidino) : positive fragment charge required

* Negative (carboxylate) : negative fragment charge required

Valid Values: No formal charge requirement , Positive (ammonium, amidino, guanidino), Negative (carboxylate)

Comma separated range of fragments in the library to search. The first fragment in the library is indicated by 1. The last fragment is indicated by END.

Parameters for controlling the criteria for a hit.

Minimum distance (Å) that must separate intermolecular pairs of carbon atoms. As Ludi considers each library fragment, it fits the fragment onto the interaction sites, then checks that the fragment's carbon atoms do not overlap receptor carbon atoms. Pairs of carbon atoms whose centers are separated by a distance less than or equal this value are considered to have undesirable overlap.
Although the value for the Minimum Separation parameter only pertains to pairs of carbons, Ludi derives threshold distances for other atom pairs from it and checks all intermolecular pairs for overlap. The threshold distances for non-carbon atoms are obtained by scaling the specified value in a manner consistent with the relative sizes of the carbon and non-carbon van der Waals radii.
A value between 3.0 and 3.5 is recommended.

Minimum percentage of surface area contact between the fragment and receptor. When Ludi considers whether it is appropriate to suggest a particular fragment, one of the criteria it considers is the percentage of the fragment surface area that is in contact with the receptor. If this percentage is less than the specified value, the fragment is discarded. For example, a value of 70 means that only those fragments whose surfaces are 70% in contact with the receptor are suggested by Ludi. A value of zero for this parameter means that the surface area contact criterion is not used. Increasing the value of the Minimum Surface parameter will reduce the number of hits. The algorithm that Ludi uses to calculate the surface area yields only approximate values, so the Minimum Surface parameter should be viewed as a rough paring method.

Minimum score for a fragment fit.

* If you modify this parameter, you may get different results, even if you do not adjust the other parameters.
This is because the algorithm will pursue more iterations to satisfy the score threshold.

The size of the cavity is determined by the number of unoccupied cubes between the protein and the ligand with no connection to bulk solvent.

Determines the fragment search method. 
The following options are available:

* FAST : as soon as a hit has been found with a matching set of interaction sites, no further attempts are made to fit this set of fragment target sites to any of the matched interaction sites. The fragment position with the highest score is saved.

* BEST : fitting is exhaustive, allowing all combinations of interaction sites to be matched against a specific set of target sites on the fragment, and the fragment position with the best score is saved.

* The combinations of target sites that Ludi considers for a specific fragment is specified in the target library file.

Valid Values: FAST , BEST

Reject bifurcated hydrogen bonds. A bifurcated hydrogen bond is one in which an acceptor is symmetrically paired with two donors or vice versa.

Reject hits that bury unpaired polar groups on either the fitted fragment or the receptor.

Reject electrostatic repulsions of the specified minimum distance or less (Å). Leave blank to consider all interactions. For example, if fragments are being fit at a metal ion coordination sites. The distance separating polar oxygen pairs or oxygen/nitrogen pairs is compared to the value of the parameter plus 0.8 Å. A default value of 2.5 Å is recommended.

Parameters that control the interaction site generation.

Density of lipophilic sites. When Ludi finds an interaction site, it populates the site with points or vectors that represent the geometry of the site. This parameter specifies how dense Ludi should make the population of points in interaction sites for lipophilic atoms.

Too large a value here slows down the Ludi program though it increases the chances of finding suitable fragments. A value between 10 and 25 is recommended.

Density of polar sites. When Ludi finds an interaction site, it populates the site with points or vectors that represent the geometry of the site. This parameter specifies how dense Ludi should make the population of vectors in interaction sites for hydrogen bonds.

Too large a value here slows down the Ludi program though it increases the chances of finding suitable fragments.
A value between 15 and 25 is recommended.

Preselection factor controls the Ludi algorithm for selecting the combination of interaction sites onto which a fragment is fit. Ludi searches the list of interaction sites by distance criteria for suitable pairs, triplets, and quadruplets to match the fragments. For each set of interaction sites, the distances between interaction sites are compared to the fragment's corresponding intramolecular distances. For any corresponding pair of interaction site distance and fragment intramolecular distance, if the difference between the two is greater than the product of the values of the Preselection Factor parameter and the Maximum RMSD (see Fitting ), then the fragment is not fit to that set of interaction sites.
Recommended values are between 1.5 and 2.5. Values larger than this tend to increase the time it takes for Ludi to fit fragments but can increase the number of fragments that Ludi is able to suggest. Values smaller than this speed up the Ludi program at the expense of sometimes missing a potentially useful fragment.

Match aliphatic fragment atoms with aliphatic receptor atoms, or aromatic fragment atoms to aromatic receptor atoms.

# De Novo Evolution

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsrlinteractions

Source file: tsrlinteractions/receptor-ligand_interactions_de_novo_evolution.htm

## De Novo Evolution

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Troubleshooting

This protocol creates complete molecules in the binding site of the receptor based stating from an initial scaffold. The Ludi program is
used to fit fragments, which are then covalently fused to the scaffold to produce a collection of molecules with higher scores.
The nature of fragment selection and construction of new molecules depends on the evolution mode.

The protocol runs in three distinct modes:

* Full Evolution - selects survivors from generations of inhibitors
ranked by a scoring function. At each generation one fragment is fused to the scaffold.

* Quick - selects survivors from generations of inhibitors
ranked by a scoring function. At each generation multiple fragment are fused to the scaffold.

* Combinatorial - enumerates all fitted fragment combinations at the
specified scaffold link sites (for more details, refer to the theory section ).

Libraries for this protocol can be generated using the De Novo
Library Generation protocol.

* Load the structure you want to define as the receptor
into the Graphics View .

* Select the receptor and ensure that hydrogens are added and all atom valencies are satisfied so that atoms can be properly typed.

* Open the Define and Edit Binding Site tool panel and
click Define Receptor .

* Click From Current Selection .

* Open the structure you want to define as the ligand scaffold 
in a Molecule Window.

* You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Receptor Choose the selected receptor from the list. Input
Ligand Scaffold Choose the selected ligand scaffold from the list. Input Fragment Libraries Specify a receptor fragment library. For more information, see Selecting the library to search .
For Combinatorial mode, you may select
several different libraries and use the Input Library Mapping parameter to associate different libraries for each link point. Evolution Mode Choose Full Evolution, Quick, or Combinatorial mode. For Full Evolution and Quick modes, you can control the
evolution process with the Evolution parameter group. For Combinatorial mode you must also: Define the Combinatorial | Link Points parameter. Select a
previously defined group of atoms defined in the Molecule Window containing
the ligand scaffold, or create a new group based on the current
selection by choosing Create New Group from selection... from the Combinatorial | Link Points parameter. The link
points are labeled R1-Rn upon selection of a group containing valid
atoms. Only terminal, single-bonded atoms in the Input Ligand Scaffold are
valid link points. Set the Input Library Mapping parameter to determine which of the
selected fragment libraries to use for each link point ( RGroup ). Only
those R-groups defined need to have a library assigned. For Combinatorial mode, the Combinatorial radius controls the size
of the sphere used to generate the interactions. A sphere of this radius
is generated at each link point. Input Site Sphere Choose the coordinates of the sphere where receptor-ligand interactions are permitted. Note that the sphere can be defined using the Define and Edit Binding Site tool panel. For details about the remaining parameters, see De Novo Evolution - Parameters .

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Receptor | Choose the selected receptor from the list. |
| Input Ligand Scaffold | Choose the selected ligand scaffold from the list. |
| Input Fragment Libraries | Specify a receptor fragment library. For more information, see Selecting the library to search . For Combinatorial mode, you may select several different libraries and use the Input Library Mapping parameter to associate different libraries for each link point. |
| Evolution Mode | Choose Full Evolution, Quick, or Combinatorial mode. For Full Evolution and Quick modes, you can control the evolution process with the Evolution parameter group. For Combinatorial mode you must also: Define the Combinatorial \| Link Points parameter. Select a previously defined group of atoms defined in the Molecule Window containing the ligand scaffold, or create a new group based on the current selection by choosing Create New Group from selection... from the Combinatorial \| Link Points parameter. The link points are labeled R1-Rn upon selection of a group containing valid atoms. Only terminal, single-bonded atoms in the Input Ligand Scaffold are valid link points. Set the Input Library Mapping parameter to determine which of the selected fragment libraries to use for each link point ( RGroup ). Only those R-groups defined need to have a library assigned. For Combinatorial mode, the Combinatorial radius controls the size of the sphere used to generate the interactions. A sphere of this radius is generated at each link point. |
| Input Site Sphere | Choose the coordinates of the sphere where receptor-ligand interactions are permitted. Note that the sphere can be defined using the Define and Edit Binding Site tool panel. |

For Full Evolution and Quick modes, you can control the
evolution process with the Evolution parameter group.

For Combinatorial mode you must also:

* Define the Combinatorial | Link Points parameter. Select a
previously defined group of atoms defined in the Molecule Window containing
the ligand scaffold, or create a new group based on the current
selection by choosing Create New Group from selection... from the Combinatorial | Link Points parameter. The link
points are labeled R1-Rn upon selection of a group containing valid
atoms. Only terminal, single-bonded atoms in the Input Ligand Scaffold are
valid link points.

* Set the Input Library Mapping parameter to determine which of the
selected fragment libraries to use for each link point ( RGroup ). Only
those R-groups defined need to have a library assigned.

* For Combinatorial mode, the Combinatorial radius controls the size
of the sphere used to generate the interactions. A sphere of this radius
is generated at each link point.

For details about the remaining parameters, see De Novo Evolution - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| <mode>.log | Full-Evolution, Combinatorial, or Quick mode log file created by the De Novo Evolution protocol, which provides details such as the fragment selection and scores during the run. |
| <ludilibrary>.sd | Contains the molecules created by the De Novo Evolution protocol. |
| <ludilibrary>_fail.sd | Contains the failed scaffold. |
| Ludi.interactionmap.mol2 | Contains the Ludi interaction map (refer to Interaction site generation ). Ludi models the H-donor and H-acceptor interaction sites with vectors (atom pairs) to account for the strong directionality of hydrogen bonds. H-donor vectors are represented by N-H , and H-acceptor vectors are represented by C=0 . Lone carbon atoms indicate Ludi aliphatic and aromatic sites. Link points on the input ligand scaffold are represented by S-S atom pairs. |
| Ludi.log | Contains the Ludi output for each generation. Ludi (inhibitor) is executed by the De Novo Evolution protocol at each generation. |
| combi_frags*.sd | In Combinatorial mode, contains the hits for each link point. Hits are then assembled in a combinatorial fashion into the <ludilibrary>.sd file. |
| ViewResults.ds_pl | Open this file to view the output fragments with the input target receptor in a Molecule Window with the view centered on the binding site. Use the View Interactions tools to identify fragment hydrogen bonds, bumps, and Pi interactions. For details about viewing, sorting, and filtering the results in the Data Table View, see Analyzing results with the Data Table View . |

## De Novo Library Generation

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Troubleshooting

The De Novo Library Generation protocol creates libraries in text or binary format
for use in De Novo Receptor or De Novo Link protocols.

There are two different types of Ludi fragment libraries:

* A standard library for De Novo Receptor

* A link library for De Novo Link and De Novo Evolution

The resulting fragment library consists of two files:

* A file that specifies the fragment topologies (ending with .str )

* A file that specifies the interaction types of fragment functional groups (ending with .trg )

Only valid 3D molecules, with hydrogens added, should be used when creating Ludi
libraries.

* Open the Receptor-Ligand Interactions | Fragment Based Design tools and click De Novo Library Generation to open the De Novo Library Generation dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Ligands Specify the ligands to be used by the protocol. For details, see Specifying Ligands . The ligands should have no more than 300 atoms. Library Type Set the fragment library type.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Ligands | Specify the ligands to be used by the protocol. For details, see Specifying Ligands . The ligands should have no more than 300 atoms. |
| Library Type | Set the fragment library type. |

* For details about the remaining parameters, see De Novo Library Generation - Parameters . By default, a De Novo library is created that can be used with the De Novo Receptor protocol.
To create a link library that can be used with the De Novo Link or De Novo Evolution protocol
set the Library Type parameter to link .

By default, a De Novo library is created that can be used with the De Novo Receptor protocol.
To create a link library that can be used with the De Novo Link or De Novo Evolution protocol
set the Library Type parameter to link .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| <ligands>.str and <ligands>.trg | The generated libraries. |
| <ligands>.log | Log file from the fragment library generation server. You can inspect these files to see how many molecules were processed or if any errors occurred. |

# De Novo Link - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsrlinteractions

Source file: tsrlinteractions/receptor-ligand_interactions_de_novo_link-para.htm

## De Novo Link - Parameters

### Suggests novel ligands by linking one or two scaffolds

Uses Ludi to add small fragments from a library to a scaffold in a protein active site. Fragments are placed in complementary positions to the receptor using a calculated interaction map, but are not fused to the core. This protocol is mostly superseded by De Novo Evolution , however, this version allows you to find suggestions for a linker between two docked scaffolds.

This protocol adds many properties to the data stream including:

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_FRAGMENTID : hit identification number.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_FRAGMENTLABEL : fragment label.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_RMSD : RMSD of the aligned fragment.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_CONTACT : number of contacts.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_NLIP : number of lipophilic contacts.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_NHBOND : number of hydrogen bonds.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_SCORE : Ludi score.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_HBONDSCO : Ludi hydrogen-bond score.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_LIPSCO : Ludi lipophilic score.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_LINKSCO : Ludi link score.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_NION : number of ionic contacts.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_IONSCO : Ludi ionic score.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_NROT : number of rotatable fragment bonds.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_ROTSCO : Ludi rotatable bond score.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_NARO : number of aromatic contributions.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_AROSCO : Ludi aromatic score.

* LudiLink : link atom information.

* LudiHydrophobic : hydrophobic atom receptor atom contacts.

Notes:

* Ludi_[1|2|3] indicates the selected Fitting Scoring Function .

* A fragment library can be created using the De Novo Library Generation protocol.

See Also:

* Böhm, H. J. The computer program LUDI: A new method for the de novo design of enzyme inhibitors. J. Comput.-Aided Mol. Design 1992 , 6, 61-78.

* Böhm, H. J. LUDI: rule based automatic design of new substituents for enzyme inhibitor leads. J. Comput.-Aided Mol. Design 1992 , 6, 593-606.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Receptor | Structure to use as the receptor. Ensure receptors have hydrogens and complete valence shells. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all visible molecules. Notes: The receptor should not contain alternate conformations. You can use the protein tools in Discovery Studio to prepare a receptor. |
| Input Receptor Target Atoms | Only fragments which interact with all specified receptor atoms are selected. Specified atoms should be in the site sphere. In Discovery Studio, select a group containing the desired receptor atoms. In Pipeline Pilot, the receptor atoms are specified in a comma separated list with atom indices ( e.g. , 14,444,333). |
| Input Site Sphere | Defines a sphere in the receptor where receptor-ligands interactions are permitted. In Pipeline Pilot, define the sphere as x,y,z,r where x,y,z specifies the coordinates of the center and r is the radius of the sphere ( e.g. , 83.2,-43.3,42.24,6). In Discovery Studio, define the sphere using the Define and Edit Binding Site tools and then select the coordinates from the list. |
| Input Ligand Scaffold | Specify the ligand scaffold (limited to 200 atoms). In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all visible molecules. Note: The scaffold must have hydrogens and complete valence shells. |
| Input Fragment Libraries | Select a link fragment library file. Fragment libraries consist of two files that need to be in the same directory, however, only one needs to be selected. |
| Link Points | The following options are available for selecting link site on the scaffold: Use all hydrogen atoms : All hydrogens of the link scaffold are considered as potential link sites. Find fragments that bridge ligand scaffold : only fragments are chosen that bridge a scaffold consisting of two disconnected parts. All hydrogens of the link scaffold are considered as potential link sites. User specified : requires a list of link and antecedent atoms. Valid Values: Use all hydrogen atoms , Find fragments that bridge ligand scaffold, User specified |
| Link Atoms | Specify a set of scaffold-atom indices to use as link points (list can be comma or space separated). Only the first 10 suitable atoms in the list will be used (e.g., 3 10 44). Note : Link points should have only one atom singly bonded (e.g., the fluorine in R-CH2-F). |
| Advanced | Contains less commonly used parameters. |
| Link Points Maximum Alignment Angle | Maximum alignment angle limits the search for fragments whose alignment angle to the link site is less than or equal to a specified value. The alignment angle is formed by a bond in the fragment and the X-H bond that defines the link site in the partially built molecule. A value between 10° and 15° is recommended for most applications. When Link Points is set to "Find fragments that bridge ligand scaffold", a value up to 30° is recommended. |
| Fitting | Parameter that control the fragment fitting. |
| Fitting Scoring Function | Ludi scoring function to use to prioritize the fragment hits for receptor-based runs. Three different algorithms are available, each estimates the change in free energy upon binding the fragment to the receptor. Each fragment is evaluated as a function of the potential number of hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic and ionic contacts it can make and an estimate is made of the penalty due to freezing the internal degrees of freedom of the ligand. The following scoring functions are available: Energy estimate 1 Energy estimate 2 Energy estimate 3 Valid Values: Energy estimate 1, Energy estimate 2, Energy estimate 3 |
| Fitting Link Weight | Relative weight for aligning a fragment with the ligand link sites. A factor of 2 can be effective. |
| Fitting Lipophilic Weight | Relative weight for aligning a fragment with lipophilic interaction sites. A factor of 10 can be effective. |
| Fitting Polar Weight | Relative weight for aligning a fragment with the hydrogen bond interaction sites. A factor of 10 can be effective. |
| Fitting Maximum Fit Attempts | Specifies the maximum number of attempts to fit a fragment to a set of interaction sites (maximum 1000000). |
| Fitting Maximum RMSD | Maximum root mean square deviation (RMSD) from maximal receptor ligand interaction (Å). At each receptor interaction site there is some range of interaction geometry between the ligand and receptor that maximizes the interaction. Deviation from this maximum, therefore, constitutes a measure of the quality of fit. Poor fits have high deviations and good fits have low deviations. As Ludi fits each fragment to the interaction sites, the RMSD is computed. For most fragments, if the RMSD exceeds the value of Maximum RMSD, the fragment is discarded. If Ludi is trying to fit a large fragment, it may allow the RMSD to exceed the value of the Maximum RMSD parameter. |
| Fitting Bond Rotation | Generate fragment conformations: None : only existing library conformations are used. One at a Time : conformations are generated by rotating each rotatable bond without changing the angle of other rotatable bonds in the fragment. Two at a Time : rotatable bonds are altered in pairs to generate new fragment conformations. Note : The degree of rotation depends on the periodicity of the dihedral angle. For bonds connecting two sp3 carbons, the rotation is done in 120° increments. For bonds connecting two sp2 carbons, the rotation is done in 180° increments. For fragments with multiple rotatable bonds, only one bond is modified at a time. Valid Values: None, One at a time, Two at a time |
| Fitting Invert Coordinates | Generate and fit both the fragments in the library and their mirror image. Valid Values: True, False |
| Fragment Filters | Parameters for filtering fragments. |
| Fragment Filters Required Groups | Only accept fragments containing groups, specified as linear descriptions of how the atoms are connected, e.g., a carboxylate group should be entered as OCO, not COO. Only elements with a one letter chemical symbol can be used. Multiple groups should be comma separated, e.g., OCO, NC. It is not possible to specify the bond order within a group, chirality, or branched groups. A fragment is only accepted if all specified groups are found. |
| Fragment Filters Rejected Groups | Reject fragments containing groups, specified as linear descriptions of how the atoms are connected, e.g., a carboxylate group should be entered as OCO, not COO. Only elements with a one letter chemical symbol can be used. Multiple groups should be comma separated, e.g., OCO, NC. It is not possible to specify the bond order within a group, chirality, or branched groups. A fragment is rejected if any of the specified groups is found. |
| Fragment Filters Required Elements | Only accept fragments containing the specified elements. Multiple elements should be comma separated, e.g., B,C,F. A fragment is accepted if all of the specified elements are found. |
| Fragment Filters Rejected Elements | Reject fragments containing the specified elements. Only elements with a one letter chemical symbol can be used. Multiple elements should be comma separated, e.g., B,C,F. A fragment is rejected if any of the specified elements is found. |
| Fragment Filters Minimum Atoms in Fragment | Minimum number of atoms in the fragments. |
| Fragment Filters Maximum Atoms in Fragment | Maximum number of atoms in the fragments (for libraries with larger fragments a value of 150 is suggested). |
| Fragment Filters Required Formal Charge | Require fragments to contain charged functional groups. The following choices are available: No formal charge requirement : no fragment charge required Positive (ammonium, amidino, guanidino) : positive fragment charge required Negative (carboxylate) : negative fragment charge required Valid Values: No formal charge requirement , Positive (ammonium, amidino, guanidino), Negative (carboxylate) |
| Fragment Filters Fragment Range | Comma separated range of fragments in the library to search. The first fragment in the library is indicated by 1. The last fragment is indicated by END. |
| Hit Criteria | Parameters for controlling the criteria for a hit. |
| Hit Criteria Minimum Separation | Minimum distance (Å) that must separate intermolecular pairs of carbon atoms. As Ludi considers each library fragment, it fits the fragment onto the interaction sites, then checks that the fragment's carbon atoms do not overlap receptor carbon atoms. Pairs of carbon atoms whose centers are separated by a distance less than or equal this value are considered to have undesirable overlap. Although the value for the Minimum Separation parameter only pertains to pairs of carbons, Ludi derives threshold distances for other atom pairs from it and checks all intermolecular pairs for overlap. The threshold distances for non-carbon atoms are obtained by scaling the specified value in a manner consistent with the relative sizes of the carbon and non-carbon van der Waals radii. A value between 3.0 and 3.5 is recommended. |
| Hit Criteria Minimum Surface | Minimum percentage of surface area contact between the fragment and receptor. When Ludi considers whether it is appropriate to suggest a particular fragment, one of the criteria it considers is the percentage of the fragment surface area that is in contact with the receptor. If this percentage is less than the specified value, the fragment is discarded. For example, a value of 70 means that only those fragments whose surfaces are 70% in contact with the receptor are suggested by Ludi. A value of zero for this parameter means that the surface area contact criterion is not used. Increasing the value of the Minimum Surface parameter will reduce the number of hits. The algorithm that Ludi uses to calculate the surface area yields only approximate values, so the Minimum Surface parameter should be viewed as a rough paring method. |
| Hit Criteria Minimum Score | Minimum score for a fragment fit. Note : If you modify this parameter, you may get different results, even if you do not adjust the other parameters. This is because the algorithm will pursue more iterations to satisfy the score threshold. |
| Hit Criteria Maximum Unfilled Cavity | Maximum size for buried cavities produced by a fragment fit (Å 3 ). If the specified value is larger than 0, Ludi searches for buried cavities after fitting a fragment, and, if the cavity is larger than the value specified, the fit is rejected. The size of the cavity is determined by the number of unoccupied cubes between the protein and the ligand with no connection to bulk solvent. |
| Hit Criteria Limit Number of Hits | Limit the number of hits returned. The value can be set in Hit Criteria Maximum Number of Hits . Valid Values: True, False |
| Hit Criteria Maximum Number of Hits | Maximum number of fragments Ludi suggests. When the number of accepted fragments equals the specified value, Ludi discontinues searching the fragment library. |
| Hit Criteria Search Method | Determines the fragment search method. The following options are available: FAST : as soon as a hit has been found with a matching set of interaction sites, no further attempts are made to fit this set of fragment target sites to any of the matched interaction sites. The fragment position with the highest score is saved. BEST : fitting is exhaustive, allowing all combinations of interaction sites to be matched against a specific set of target sites on the fragment, and the fragment position with the best score is saved. Note : The combinations of target sites that Ludi considers for a specific fragment is specified in the target library file. Valid Values: FAST , BEST |
| Hit Criteria Reject Bifurcated Hydrogen Bonds | Reject bifurcated hydrogen bonds. A bifurcated hydrogen bond is one in which an acceptor is symmetrically paired with two donors or vice versa. Valid Values: True, False |
| Hit Criteria Reject Unpaired Buried Polar Groups | Reject hits that bury unpaired polar groups on either the fitted fragment or the receptor. Valid Values: True , False |
| Hit Criteria Minimum Electrostatic Repulsion Distance | Reject electrostatic repulsions of the specified minimum distance or less (Å). Leave blank to consider all interactions. For example, if fragments are being fit at a metal ion coordination sites. The distance separating polar oxygen pairs or oxygen/nitrogen pairs is compared to the value of the parameter plus 0.8 Å. A default value of 2.5 Å is recommended. |
| Interaction Site | Parameters that control the interaction site generation. |
| Interaction Site Density of Lipophilic Sites | Density of lipophilic sites. When Ludi finds an interaction site, it populates the site with points or vectors that represent the geometry of the site. This parameter specifies how dense Ludi should make the population of points in interaction sites for lipophilic atoms. Too large a value here slows down the Ludi program though it increases the chances of finding suitable fragments. A value between 10 and 25 is recommended. |
| Interaction Site Density of Polar Sites | Density of polar sites. When Ludi finds an interaction site, it populates the site with points or vectors that represent the geometry of the site. This parameter specifies how dense Ludi should make the population of vectors in interaction sites for hydrogen bonds. Too large a value here slows down the Ludi program though it increases the chances of finding suitable fragments. A value between 15 and 25 is recommended. |
| Interaction Site Preselection Factor | Preselection factor controls the Ludi algorithm for selecting the combination of interaction sites onto which a fragment is fit. Ludi searches the list of interaction sites by distance criteria for suitable pairs, triplets, and quadruplets to match the fragments. For each set of interaction sites, the distances between interaction sites are compared to the fragment's corresponding intramolecular distances. For any corresponding pair of interaction site distance and fragment intramolecular distance, if the difference between the two is greater than the product of the values of the Preselection Factor parameter and the Maximum RMSD (see Fitting ), then the fragment is not fit to that set of interaction sites. Recommended values are between 1.5 and 2.5. Values larger than this tend to increase the time it takes for Ludi to fit fragments but can increase the number of fragments that Ludi is able to suggest. Values smaller than this speed up the Ludi program at the expense of sometimes missing a potentially useful fragment. |
| Interaction Site Differentiate Lipophilic Interactions | Match aliphatic fragment atoms with aliphatic receptor atoms, or aromatic fragment atoms to aromatic receptor atoms. Valid Values: True, False |

Structure to use as the receptor. Ensure receptors have hydrogens and complete valence shells.

In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all visible molecules.

* The receptor should not contain alternate conformations.

* You can use the protein tools in Discovery Studio to prepare a receptor.

Only fragments which interact with all specified receptor atoms are selected. 
Specified atoms should be in the site sphere.

In Discovery Studio, select a group containing the desired receptor atoms.

Defines a sphere in the receptor where receptor-ligands interactions are permitted.

In Pipeline Pilot, define the sphere as x,y,z,r where x,y,z specifies the coordinates of the center and r is the radius of the sphere ( e.g. , 83.2,-43.3,42.24,6).

In Discovery Studio, define the sphere using the Define and Edit Binding Site tools and then select the coordinates from the list.

Specify the ligand scaffold (limited to 200 atoms).

Note:

* The scaffold must have hydrogens and complete valence shells.

Select a link fragment library file. Fragment libraries consist of two files that need to be in the same directory, however, only one needs to be selected.

* Use all hydrogen atoms : All hydrogens of the link scaffold are considered as potential link sites.

* Find fragments that bridge ligand scaffold : only fragments are chosen that bridge a scaffold consisting of two disconnected parts. All hydrogens of the link scaffold are considered as potential link sites.

* User specified : requires a list of link and antecedent atoms.

Valid Values: Use all hydrogen atoms , Find fragments that bridge ligand scaffold, User specified

Specify a set of scaffold-atom indices to use as link points (list can be comma or space separated). Only the first 10 suitable atoms in the list will be used (e.g., 3 10 44).

Note :

* Link points should have only one atom singly bonded (e.g., the fluorine in R-CH2-F).

Contains less commonly used parameters.

Maximum alignment angle limits the search for fragments whose alignment angle to the link site is less than or equal to a specified value. The alignment angle is formed by a bond in the fragment and the X-H bond that defines the link site in the partially built molecule. A value between 10° and 15° is recommended for most applications. When Link Points is set to "Find fragments that bridge ligand scaffold", a value up to 30° is recommended.

Parameter that control the fragment fitting.

Ludi scoring function to use to prioritize the fragment hits for receptor-based runs.

Three different algorithms are available, each estimates the change in free energy upon binding the fragment to the receptor. Each fragment is evaluated as a function of the potential number of hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic and ionic contacts it can make and an estimate is made of the penalty due to freezing the internal degrees of freedom of the ligand.

The following scoring functions are available:

* Energy estimate 1

* Energy estimate 2

* Energy estimate 3

Valid Values: Energy estimate 1, Energy estimate 2, Energy estimate 3

Relative weight for aligning a fragment with the ligand link sites. A factor of 2 can be effective.

Relative weight for aligning a fragment with lipophilic interaction sites.
A factor of 10 can be effective.

Relative weight for aligning a fragment with the hydrogen bond interaction sites.
A factor of 10 can be effective.

Specifies the maximum number of attempts to fit a fragment to a set of interaction sites (maximum 1000000).

Maximum root mean square deviation (RMSD) from maximal receptor ligand interaction (Å). At each receptor interaction site there is some range of interaction geometry between the ligand and receptor that maximizes the interaction. Deviation from this maximum, therefore, constitutes a measure of the quality of fit. Poor fits have high deviations and good fits have low deviations. As Ludi fits each fragment to the interaction sites, the RMSD is computed. For most fragments, if the RMSD exceeds the value of Maximum RMSD, the fragment is discarded. If Ludi is trying to fit a large fragment, it may allow the RMSD to exceed the value of the Maximum RMSD parameter.

* The degree of rotation depends on the periodicity of the dihedral angle. For bonds connecting two sp3 carbons, the rotation is done in 120° increments. For bonds connecting two sp2 carbons, the rotation is done in 180° increments. For fragments with multiple rotatable bonds, only one bond is modified at a time.

Valid Values: None, One at a time, Two at a time

Generate and fit both the fragments in the library and their mirror image.

Valid Values: True, False

# De Novo Link

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsrlinteractions

Source file: tsrlinteractions/receptor-ligand_interactions_de_novo_link.htm

## De Novo Link

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Troubleshooting

The De Novo Link protocol suggests modifications and additions to a ligand that is placed in the binding site of a receptor, in order to enhance binding to the receptor. The algorithm suggests modifications to a ligand scaffold to increase binding by placing fragments from the specified Ludi library into the specified binding site, according to the Ludi-generated interaction map. The placed fragments are scored using a Ludi energy estimate.

This protocol uses libraries of fragments to suggest novel ligands with the potential to bind to a target receptor.

Libraries for this protocol can be generated using the De Novo Library Generation protocol.

* Load the structure you want to define as the receptor
into the Graphics View .

* Ensure that the receptor has hydrogens added and atom valencies are satisfied so that atoms can be properly typed.

* From the Graphics View, select the receptor.

* Open the Define and Edit Binding Site tool panel and
click Define Receptor .

* Use the Define and Edit Binding Site tool panel to define a receptor sphere.

* Open the Receptor-Ligand Interactions | Fragment Based Design tools and click De Novo Link to open the De Novo Link dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Receptor Choose the selected receptor. Input Site Sphere Choose the coordinates of the sphere where receptor-ligand interactions are permitted. Note that the sphere can be defined using the Define and Edit Binding Site tool panel. Input Fragment Libraries Specify a receptor fragment library . For details about the remaining parameters, see De Novo Link - Parameters .

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Receptor | Choose the selected receptor. |
| Input Site Sphere | Choose the coordinates of the sphere where receptor-ligand interactions are permitted. Note that the sphere can be defined using the Define and Edit Binding Site tool panel. |
| Input Fragment Libraries | Specify a receptor fragment library . |

For details about the remaining parameters, see De Novo Link - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| DeNovoLink.log | Contains the output from the Ludi inhibitor program. |
| <ludilibrary>.sd | Contains all the fragments identified by Ludi as a hit. |
| Ludi.interactionmap.mol2 | Contains the Ludi interaction map (see Interaction site generation ). Ludi models the H-donor and H-acceptor interaction sites with vectors (atom pairs) to account for the strong directionality of hydrogen bonds. H-donor vectors are represented by N-H , and H-acceptor vectors are represented by C=0 . Lone carbon atoms indicate Ludi aliphatic and aromatic sites. Link points on the input ligand scaffold are represented by S-S atom pairs. |
| Ludi.targetsites.txt | contains the Ludi target sites. During a Ludi run, up to 6 fragment atoms, or groups of fragment atoms, are fit to the receptor. This file lists the fragment target atoms selected from the fragment library file during the fitting procedure. |
| ViewResults.ds_pl | Open this file to view the output fragments with the input target receptor in a Molecule Window with the view centered on the binding site. Use the View Interactions tools to identify fragment hydrogen bonds, bumps, and Pi interactions. For details about viewing, sorting, and filtering the results in the Data Table View, see Analyzing results with the Data Table View . |

#### Further information

# De Novo Receptor - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsrlinteractions

Source file: tsrlinteractions/receptor-ligand_interactions_de_novo_receptor-para.htm

## De Novo Receptor - Parameters

### Suggests fragments that form interactions in a receptor active site

Uses Ludi to search a library of small fragments to find candidates that bind in an active site. Fragments in the library that overlay with a calculated interaction map are found.

This protocol adds many properties to the data stream including:

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_FRAGMENTID : hit identification number.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_FRAGMENTLABEL : fragment label.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_RMSD : RMSD of the aligned fragment.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_CONTACT : number of contacts.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_NLIP : number of lipophilic contacts.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_NHBOND : number of hydrogen bonds.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_SCORE : Ludi score.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_HBONDSCO : Ludi hydrogen-bond score.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_LIPSCO : Ludi lipophilic score.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_LINKSCO : Ludi link score.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_NION : number of ionic contacts.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_IONSCO : Ludi ionic score.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_NROT : number of rotatable fragment bonds.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_ROTSCO : Ludi rotatable bond score.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_NARO : number of aromatic contributions.

* Ludi_[1|2|3]_AROSCO : Ludi aromatic score.

* LudiHydrophobic : hydrophobic atom receptor atom contacts.

Notes:

* Ludi_[1|2|3] indicates the selected Fitting Scoring Function .

* A fragment library can be created using the De Novo Library Generation protocol.

See Also:

* Böhm, H. J. The computer program LUDI: A new method for the de novo design of enzyme inhibitors. J. Comput.-Aided Mol. Design 1992 , 6, 61-78.

* Böhm, H. J. LUDI: rule based automatic design of new substituents for enzyme inhibitor leads. J. Comput.-Aided Mol. Design 1992 , 6, 593-606.
