# Dock Ligands (GOLD) - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsrlinteractions

Source file: tsrlinteractions/receptor-ligand_interactions_dock_ligands_gold-para.htm

## Dock Ligands (GOLD) - Parameters

### Docks ligands into an active site using a genetic algorithm

Ligand docking using the GOLD (Genetic Optimization for Ligand Docking) program. GOLD uses a genetic algorithm for docking flexible ligands into receptor binding sites. GOLD is also able to dock covalently bound ligands.

Notes :

* GOLD is a program developed by: 
Cambridge Crystallographic Data Centre ( https://www.ccdc.cam.ac.uk/solutions/csd-discovery/components/gold/ ).

* A valid GOLD license must be obtained from CCDC before the GOLD Docking protocol can be run.
Free evaluations of GOLD can be obtained by contacting: support@ccdc.cam.ac.uk 
phone: +44 (0)1223 336408

* Ensure that the GOLD installation folder is correctly specified in the
$(Pipeline Pilot Install Folder)/apps/scitegic/dscore/server/share/SBD/GOLD_location file.
GOLD will attempt to automatically locate a valid license file
(csd_licence.dat) in the CSD database directory (if present), or the home directory of the user running it. If you experience licensing issues, GOLD can also locate a valid license file located in its installation/GoldSuite_YEAR directory (e.g., GoldSuite_2018), or by setting the environment variable CCDC_CSD_LICENCE_FILE to point to the license file explicitly.

* If licensing issues persist, please contact support@ccdc.cam.ac.uk

See Also :

* Hartshorn, M.J.; Verdonk, M.L.; Chessari, G.; Brewerton, S.C.; Mooij, W.T.M.; Mortenson, P.N.; Murray, C.W. Diverse High-Quality Test Set for the Validation of Protein-Ligand Docking Performance, J. Med. Chem. , 2007 , 50 , 726-741.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Receptor | Structure to use as the receptor. Ensure the receptor has hydrogens and complete valence shells. Ensemble docking can be performed by selecting multiple receptors which should be aligned. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all visible molecules. Notes: The receptor should not contain alternate conformations. You can use the protein tools in Discovery Studio to prepare a receptor. Ensemble docking is only available for GOLD version 5 and higher. |
| Flexible Side Chains | Amino acid residues that can undergo rotation as specified in the GOLD rotamer library (up to 10 residues). In Discovery Studio, select a group containing the desired residues. In Pipeline Pilot, the residues are specified as: The residues are defined by a space separated list: [chain]:[residue name][residue sequence number][insertion code] (insertion code is optional) Example: A:TYR33 A:LEU44 Notes: This option is not available when docking with multiple receptors (ensemble docking). The rotamer library file $(GOLD_DIR)/gold/rotamer_library.txt contains information taken from the paper "The Penultimate Rotamer Library", S. C. Lovell, J. M. Word, J. S. Richardson & D. C. Richardson, Proteins, 40, 389-408, 2000. This is a compilation of the most commonly observed side-chain conformations for the naturally occurring amino acids. |
| Input Receptor Fix All Bonds | During docking, receptor serine, threonine, lysine NH3+, and tyrosine hydroxyl groups are optimized, i.e. rotated. If this is undesirable this rotation can be disabled by setting the value to True. Valid Values: True, False |
| Input Ligands | Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. |
| Input Site Sphere | Defines a sphere in the receptor where receptor-ligands interactions are permitted. In Pipeline Pilot, define the sphere as x,y,z,r where x,y,z specifies the coordinates of the center and r is the radius of the sphere ( e.g. , 83.2,-43.3,42.24,6). In Discovery Studio, define the sphere using the Define and Edit Binding Site tools and then select the coordinates from the list. |
| Input Site Atoms | Receptor atom indices that define the binding site for ligand docking. The atom list should be comma separated. In Discovery Studio, select a group containing the desired atoms. |
| Fitness Function | GOLD offers the following scoring functions: Goldscore : original scoring function provided with GOLD. It has been optimized for the prediction of ligand binding positions and takes into account factors such as H-bonding energy, van der Waals energy and ligand torsion strain. Chemscore : estimates the total free energy change that occurs on ligand binding and was trained by regression against binding affinity data. ASP : Astex Statistical Potential (ASP) is an atom-atom potential derived from a database of protein-ligand complexes and can be compared to other such scoring potentials, e.g. PMF and Drugscore. ASP has comparable accuracy to Chemscore and Goldscore. CHEMPLP : Piecewise Linear Potential is an empirical fitness functions optimized for pose prediction. The Piecewise Linear Potential (PLP) is used to model the steric complementarity between protein and ligand, while for CHEMPLP additionally the distance- and angle-dependent hydrogen and metal bonding terms from Chemscore are considered. Note: The fitness scores are dimensionless and cannot be used explicitly for binding energy or binding affinity calculation. For more information consult the help text provided by GOLD. Valid Values: Goldscore, Chemscore, ASP, CHEMPLP |
| GA Parameters | Pre-defined GOLD Generic Algorithm (GA) settings, which controls speed and quality of the results. The following options are available: GOLD Default : delivers high predictive accuracy but is relatively slow. 2 times speed up : faster docking. 3 times speed up : even faster docking 7-8 times speed up : fastest docking speed Automatic : automatic parameters. Automatic Library Screening : fastest setting and as a consequence is the least reliable. Automatic Virtual Screening : suitable for routine work and usually gives comparable predictive accuracy to the slower settings, unless the ligand has a large number of rotatable torsions. Automatic Default : GOLD will attempt to apply optimal settings for each ligand. Automatic Very Flexible : recommended for large highly flexible ligands. This setting delivers high predictive accuracy but is relatively slow. Valid Values: GOLD Default, 2 times speed up, 3 times speed up, 7-8 times speed up, Automatic , Automatic Library Screening, Automatic Virtual Screening, Automatic Default, Automatic Very Flexible |
| GA Automatic Search Efficiency | Search Efficiency (%) controls the speed of docking and the predictive accuracy. When automatic settings are selected the GA parameters will be determined on-the-fly and are optimized for each ligand. Since the genetic algorithm relies on change to find solutions, limiting the number of operations causes the search space to be more limited. This must be offset however against the gain in speed that can be attained this way. This parameter allows the user to reduce the coverage of the search space (reliability) and increase the speed of docking. Scaling down may be useful for screening purposes if faster docking times are required. Using the default setting (100%), GOLD will attempt to apply optimal settings for each ligand. For a medium sized ligand with 5 rotatable bonds, this will be around 30,000 GA operations. When set to 50%, this value will be scaled down prior to docking this ligand, to a value of 15,000, speeding up the docking by a factor of 2. The parameter should be set between 10% and 200%. Note : If blank, an automatic preset based on the GA Parameters is used. |
| GA Automatic Minimum Operations | Subject each ligand to a minimum number of operations. Note : If blank an automatic preset based on the GA Parameters is used. |
| GA Automatic Maximum Operations | Restrict each ligand to a maximum number of operations. Note : If blank an automatic preset based on the GA Parameters is used. |
| Options | Options that control the ligand docking. |
| Options Number of Dockings | GOLD will dock each ligand several times starting each time from a different random population of ligand orientations. The results of the different docking runs are ranked by fitness score. The total time spent docking a ligand obviously depends on the number of docking runs, so you can make GOLD go faster by reducing this number. However, it is useful to perform at least a few docking runs on each ligand. This increases the chances of getting the right answer. Also, if the same answer is found in several different docking runs, it is usually a strong indicator that the answer is correct. The Early Termination options can be used to prevent GOLD wasting time performing multiple docking runs on easy ligands. |
| Options Detect Cavity | Cavity detection algorithm can be used to restrict the region of interest to concave, solvent-accessible surfaces. Valid Values: True , False |
| Options Solvate All | Each atom in the defined binding site is tested for solvent accessibility. This process has the following steps: First, the solvent accessible surface of each atom in the defined binding site is calculated. Potential donor and acceptor fitting points (used for ligand placement) are then generated for only those protein atoms that are accessible. Second, the potential fitting points are themselves tested for solvent accessibility, and only those fitting points that are accessible are used. Note : For example, this option can be used to avoid problems with solvent accessibility of backbone carbonyls in kinases where one of the carbonyl lone pairs is typically desolvated by a neighboring atom. Valid Values: True, False |
| Output Level | GOLD output file level: 0 : No GOLD log files are created. Recommended for high-throughput virtual screening. 1 : Minimal information is returned with warnings log and GOLD main log file. 2 : All GOLD log files are returned. This option may create a large amount of data and depending on the number of input ligands, may affect speed. Valid Values: 0, 1 , 2 |
| Covalent Docking | Enables docking of covalently bound ligands to the receptor. Notes : GOLD requires that there is just one atom linking a ligand to the protein (e.g., the O in a serine residue). Both protein and ligand should contain the link atom (for example, if the serine O is the link atom, it should be present in both protein and ligand). Ideally, the link atom, in both the ligand and the protein, will have a free valence available through which the link can be made. If the link atom on the ligand does not have a free valence, having a hydrogen instead, then the docking will proceed and the hydrogen will be ignored in terms of its contribution to the fitness score. However, the hydrogen is still present in the docked poses. The GOLD least-squares fitting routine forces the link atom of the ligand to fit onto the link atom of the protein. In order to make sure that the geometry of the bound ligand is correct, the angle-bending potential from the Tripos Force Field has been incorporated into the fitness function. On evaluating the score of the docked ligand, the angle-bending energy for the link atom is included in the calculation of the fitness score. Since the protein is held rigid (apart from hydroxyl hydrogen atoms), it does require that the position of the link atom in the protein is feasible. Valid Values: True, False |
| Covalent Docking Protein Link Atom | Protein atom ID that forms the link to the ligand. Notes : The link atom needs to be present in the protein and the ligand. In Discovery Studio you may select the protein link atom and use the Create New Group from Selection , or use an existing group. Please ensure that the selection contains only a single entry. In Pipeline Pilot, please enter the protein atom ID. |
| Covalent Docking Ligand Substructure | Ligand substructure with the link atom. Note : The substructure can only contain one link atom which needs to be present in the receptor and the substructure. |
| Covalent Docking Ligand Substructure Link Atom | Substructure link atom ID. Notes : The link atom needs to be present in the protein and the ligand. In Discovery Studio you may select the link atom and use the Create New Group from Selection , or use an existing group. Please ensure that the selection contains only a single entry. In Pipeline Pilot, please enter the atom ID. |
| Covalent Docking Topology Matching | Enable topology matching to check equivalent atoms. If the constraint refers to a substructure atom (and therefore a ligand atom) which is topologically equivalent to other atoms (e.g., oxygen atoms of an ionized carboxylate group), GOLD will then use the atom that gives the best result. Valid Values: True , False |
| Generate Diverse Solutions | Enforce pose diversity during ligand mapping. As the ligand is constructed and mapped into the binding site, GOLD checks the Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD) of the current solution against those that have already been generated. If the RMSD is below the diversity threshold or the maximum number of solutions per cluster has been reached, the mapping is rejected and the process repeated until an acceptable solution is generated. GOLD keeps track of any failures; once the failure threshold has been reached the diverse solutions code is switched off. Valid Values: True, False |
| Generate Diverse Solutions Cluster Size | Number of diverse ligand poses in a cluster within the defined Generate Diverse Solutions RMSD . |
| Generate Diverse Solutions RMSD | RMSD cut-off (Å) for determining if diverse solutions are in the same cluster or not. |
| Early Termination | Allow docking of a ligand to terminate as soon as a specified number of runs have given essentially the same pose. Valid Values: True , False |
| Early Termination Number of Solutions | Number of solutions to generate before early termination. GOLD will terminate docking on a given ligand if this number of the top poses are within Early Termination RMSD Å of each other. For example, if set to 3 and Early Termination RMSD is set to 1.5 the docking will terminate if the top 3 solutions are within 1.5 Å RMSD of each other. Note : Early termination does not always save as much time as you might think, because it tends to be invoked for easy (i.e., relatively rigid) ligands, which are quick to dock anyway. |
| Early Termination RMSD | Root Mean Square Deviation (Å) for early termination. See Early Termination Number of Solutions |
| Options Input Waters | Select a structure with water molecules to be included during docking. From this structure you can select groups with the following options: Group Spin : GOLD rotates (spins) the water molecule. Group Toggle : GOLD decides whether the water should be present or absent (i.e. bound or displaced by the ligand). Group Translate : Waters are allowed to translate and to spin during the docking (only available with GOLD 5). Notes: In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all visible molecules. In Pipeline Pilot select a single MOL2 or PDB file containing the water molecules. Any non-water molecules will be ignored. Ensure that the specified water molecules are not present in the protein structure, this can lead to clashes. |
| Options Input Waters Group Spin | Selected waters are allowed to spin during the optimization Notes: In Discovery Studio, select a group containing the desired waters from the Input Waters . In Pipeline Pilot, specify the atom numbers of the water oxygens from the Input Waters (space or comma separated). |
| Options Input Waters Group Toggle | Specified water molecules may be toggled. For waters in this list GOLD will decide whether the water should be present or absent (i.e. bound or displaced by the ligand) during docking. Notes: In Discovery Studio, select a group containing the desired waters from the Input Waters . In Pipeline Pilot, specify the atom numbers of the water oxygens from the Input Waters (space or comma separated). |
| Options Input Waters Group Translate | Specified water molecules are allowed to translate and spin. Notes: In Discovery Studio, select a group containing the desired waters. In Pipeline Pilot, specify the atom numbers of the water oxygens from the Input Waters (space or comma separated). The maximum translation can be specified in Distance . This feature is only available for GOLD 5. |
| Options Input Waters Group Translate Distance | Maximum distance that waters specified in Options Translate Water Group are allowed to translate (Å). |
| Constraints | Options which control the docking constraints. |
| Interaction Filters | Protein atoms that should form hydrogen bonds with a ligand. The interactions can be defined using the Dock Ligands tools in Discovery Studio using the "Define Interaction Site" command. In Pipeline Pilot, specify the constraint weight, geometry weight, and atom IDs. The constraint weight defines the strength of bias applied to the formation of a specified hydrogen bond by GOLD. The geometry weight defines how good a hydrogen bonding interaction has to be in order for it to be considered a hydrogen bond by GOLD (range 0 to 1, default 0.005). For example : 10 0.005 1983 1984 will specify a constraint weight of 10 and a geometry weight of 0.005 for atoms 1983 and 1984. Notes : This option is not available when docking with multiple receptors (ensemble docking). The weights can be set in Discovery Studio under in the Data Table or the Preferences. |
| Constraints Input Scaffolds | Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands or fragments to be used for constraining the matches. The scaffold match constraint can be used to place a fragment at an exact specified position in the binding site, the geometry of the fragment will not be altered during docking. The scaffold, can, for example, be a common core, a fragment, or a substructure known to adopt a certain binding position. For a given ligand, it is not possible to match multiple scaffolds at the same time. Scaffolds are evaluated in the order supplied by the user and the scaffold that matches the ligand first will be used. This means that it is possible to specify two or more different scaffolds, and GOLD will use the scaffold that matches the ligand first. This can be useful when docking multiple different series of compounds. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. |
| Constraints Input Scaffolds Constraint Weight | Determines how closely ligand atoms fit onto the scaffold. Setting a higher weight will force the ligand to be placed onto the scaffold locations more strictly. |
| Constraints Force Constraints | Ligands are not docked when the specified constraint(s) are physically impossible to satisfy (e.g. if no suitable group is present in the ligand to form the required H-bond constraint). Valid Values: True, False |
| Data Files | GOLD data files. |
| Data Files Gold Configuration File | Override docking parameters with specified configuration file, except, the input ligands. Use this option on a pre-prepared configuration file. Notes : The format of the parameter file is strict and incorrect syntax may cause GOLD to behave in unexpected ways or even to crash. Because of the large number of parameters, no guarantee can be given that the program will behave reliably with anything other than the default parameterization. When running from the Pipeline Pilot Client or Web Port, ensure that the data file path in the GOLD configuration are correctly specified and visible to the server. |
| Data Files GOLD Parameters | Parameter file that contains parameters used by GOLD (e.g., hydrogen bond energies, atom radii and polarizabilities, torsion potentials, hydrogen bond directionalities, etc.). It also contains parameters that control the general behavior of GOLD, e.g., whether the final solution from a genetic algorithm run is to be minimized via a simplex procedure before being saved. Notes : If blank, the GOLD default settings will be used. The format of the parameter file is strict and incorrect syntax may cause GOLD to behave in unexpected ways or even to crash. Because of the large number of parameters, no guarantee can be given that the program will behave reliably with anything other than the default parameterization. |
| Data Files Fitness Function Parameters | Customized parameter file for the specified Fitness Function . If blank, GOLD default settings will be used. Note : The format of the parameter file is strict and incorrect syntax may cause GOLD to behave in unexpected ways or even to crash. Because of the large number of parameters, no guarantee can be given that the program will behave reliably with anything other than the default parameterization. A full description of the meaning of the various parameters is given elsewhere. |
| Data Files Torsion Angle Distribution | Ligand torsion distribution file to restrict the conformational space sampled by the genetic algorithm. Notes : Left blank, the default GOLD torsion distribution file will be used. By selecting an empty file all torsions are sampled. Several torsion distribution files exist in the GOLD installation directory. The format of the parameter file is strict. Incorrect syntax may cause GOLD to behave unexpectedly. |
| Data Files Seed File | It is possible to supply the seed for the random number generator used by the genetic algorithm in GOLD. This provides a mechanism for introducing a non-random start facility. Normally, a new GOLD calculation will be seeded in this way in order to reproduce identical results for repeat runs. You could also use this mechanism to manually specify a seed for a new GOLD calculation. Note: The format of this file is strict. Incorrect syntax may cause GOLD to behave unexpectedly. |
| Flexibility | Options which control the ligand flexibility. |
| Flexibility Explore Ring Conformations | Methods for exploring ring conformations during docking. The following options are available: Rigid : No conformational ring search. Flip Ring Corners : Enable a limited conformational search of cyclic systems by allowing free corners of rings to flip above or below the plane of their neighboring atoms. Match Template Conformations : Identifies each ring in the ligand and attempts to match it to the Cambridge Structural Database (CSD) ring template. For each template the number of alternative conformations that will be explored during docking will vary depending on the abundance and suitability of data within the CSD. See Also : A. W. R. Payne and R. C. Glen, J. Mol. Graphics, 10 , 74-91 (1993). Valid Values: Rigid , Flip Ring Corners, Match Template Conformations |
| Flexibility Flip Amide Bonds | During ligand initialization, ligand amide groups (including thioamides, ureas, and thioureas) will be set to the trans conformation. Flattening to the trans conformation will also occur if the (O)C-N(H) torsion is greater than 20° out of plane. In order to flip between cis and trans conformations the CO-NRR' torsion is first made planar (at the initialized trans conformation). Note : If the (O)C-N(H) torsion is greater than five but less than 20° out of the trans plane, the bond will not be flattened. Valid Values: True, False |
| Flexibility Flip Planar R-NR1R2 | Allow planar trigonal nitrogens in the ligand (bound to sp2 carbons) to flip between cis and trans conformations during docking (otherwise, they will be held fixed at the input geometry). The following options are available: Fixed : Fixed bonds at their input conformation. Flip non-ring only : Flip non-ring only. Flip non-ring and ring-NHR1 : allows non-ring and ring-NHR1 to flip (i.e. rotate 180°). Flip non-ring and ring-NR1R2 : allows non-ring and ring-NR1R2 to flip (i.e. rotate 180°). Flip all : allow all to flip. Valid Values: Fixed, Flip non-ring only, Flip non-ring and ring-NHR1, Flip non-ring and ring-NR1R2, Flip all |
| Flexibility Flipping Pyramidal Nitrogens | Allow pyramidal (i.e. non-planar sp3) nitrogens to invert during docking (otherwise, they will be held fixed at the input geometry). Given a non-planar group RR'R"N or tetrahedrally surrounded RR'R"NH, the Flip pyramidal N switch enables flipping of the local stereochemistry around the nitrogen (the energy barrier for this umbrella-like change of geometry around the nitrogen is low). Note : Flipping only changes the stereochemistry around RR'R"N and RR'R"NH nitrogens. It does not affect other chiral centers. Valid Values: True, False |
| Flexibility Intramolecular Hydrogen Bonds | Allow intramolecular hydrogen bonds in the ligand to be formed during docking. Note : Use this with care as it can make ligands like methotrexate curl up. Valid Values: True, False |
| Flexibility Protonated Carboxylic Acids | Control the behavior of protonated carboxylic acids during docking. The following options are available: Fixed : held rigid at their input conformation. Flip : allowed to flip (i.e. rotate 180°). Rotate Freely : allow to rotate freely. Valid Values: Fixed, Flip , Freely Rotate |
| Fix Rotatable Bonds | Fix the geometry of specific bonds or of part of the ligand, e.g. in order to study the possible binding of a pre-determined ligand geometry. The following options are available: None : Allow for full flexibility. All : Fix all rotatable bonds, i.e., keep input conformation. All But Terminal : Fix all non-terminal rotatable bonds (i.e. not -CH3, -OH, etc.), at their input conformation: Note : When fixing all rotatable bonds at their input conformation (i.e. performing a rigid ligand docking) GOLD will try to find the best orientation of the ligand in the binding site by mapping donor-acceptor (as well as hydrophobic-hydrophobic) fitting points. However, GOLD will not perform a local optimization (simplex) on the final solution. This may lead to penalization of near-optimal conformations. Performing a few cycles of molecular-mechanics minimization before docking may help to take the ligand close to its local potential-energy minimum. Valid Values: None , All, All But Terminal |
| Flexibility Torsion Angle Distribution | Select the torsion angle distribution library to restrict the ligand conformational space sampled by the genetic algorithm. Using torsion angle library may improve the chances of GOLD finding the correct answer by biasing the search towards ligand torsion-angle values that are commonly observed in crystal structure. The following settings are available: Default : New default torsion distribution library introduced in 2023.3 (Penner et al 2022). Original : Default torsion library prior to the 2023.3 release. MIMUMBA : Torsion library by Klebe and Mietzner 1994. False : Do not use a torsion library to guide the search. Custom : User defined library file specified in: Data Files Torsion Angle Distribution See Also: : The Torsion Library: Semi-automated Improvement of Torsion Rules with SMARTScompare. (Penner et al, J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2022, 62, 7, 1644-1653). A fast and efficient method to generate biologically relevant conformations, Klebe and Mietzner, J.Comput.-Aided Mol.Des., 8, 583-606, 1994). Valid Values: Default , Original, MIMUMBA, False, Custom |
| Pose Saving | Parameters for saving poses. |
| Pose Saving Maximum Poses Retained | Maximum number of poses that should be saved. Blank or less than 1 saves all solutions otherwise keeps that number of poses for each docked ligand. |
| Pose Saving Rotated Hydrogens | Save optimized positions of polar protein hydrogen atoms that are generated during docking (these will usually be different for each docked ligand pose). This option controls if positions of rotated protein hydrogen atoms are saved to the docked solution files: Gold.Protein.RotatedTorsions : Rotated atom torsion. Gold.Protein.ActiveResidue : Active residues. Gold.Protein.RotatedAtoms : Rotated atoms. Valid Values: True , False |
| Pose Saving Fitness Threshold | Filters all solutions with fitness scores lower than a specified value. Filtering reduces the number of poses by keeping only the best solutions. Disabled if blank. |
| Pose Saving Per Atom Score | Add the scoring contributions properties of individual ligand and protein atoms to the docked solution. For each atom its contribution to the total fitness score and also the constituent scoring terms will be added. Valid Values: True, False |
| Pose Saving Internal Energy Offset | Correct the internal energy terms (internal torsion, internal vdW, and internal Hbond) according to the best energy encountered for these terms during the run. By applying this correction the internal energy will be calculated with respect to that of a close to optimal non-bound structure, thereby taking into account any irreducible internal energy. Valid Values: True , False |
| Use Docking Templates | Use the GOLD template specified in: Docking Template . Note: The parameters set in the template file will override the equivalent protocol parameters. Valid Values: True, False |
| Docking Template | Docking templates assign optimized setting for a number of different docking protocols. The following default templates are provided with a GOLD installation: chemscore_kinase : Optimized for kinase docking. chemscore_p450_csd : Optimized for cytochrome P450 docking. gold_folate_enzymes_VS : Virtual screening template designed for identifying active molecules for folates enzyme. gold_kinase_VS : Virtual screening template designed for identifying active molecules for kinases. gold_metallo_protease_gen_VS : Virtual screening template designed for identifying active molecules for metallo protease. gold_nuclear_hormone_rec_VS : Virtual screening template designed for identifying active molecules for nuclear hormones. gold_phosphodiesterase_VS : Virtual screening template designed for identifying active molecules for phosphodiesterases. gold_serine_protease_VS : Virtual screening template designed for identifying active molecules for serine proteases. Goldscore is used as the docking scoring function and ASP as the rescoring function. goldscore_p450_csd : Optimized template for cytochrome P450 docking. Notes The parameter lists all template files available in the GOLD/templates directory. You can easily add or modify files in the GOLD/templates directory Any parameter specified in a template file will override any parameter set in the protocol interface. An error is thrown when the GOLD/templates directory is not found. |
| Parallel Processing | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. Valid Values: True, False |
| Parallel Processing Batch Size | Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records. Notes : Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size. By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. |
| Parallel Processing Server | Comma separated list of servers (server-name:port-number) to be used for parallel processing. Add "localhost" to include the local server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where "localhost" requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster). |
| Parallel Processing Server Processes | Comma separated list of the maximum batches that can be simultaneously executed on each server. Each value must correspond with an entry in the list of servers. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers. |
| Parallel Processing Preserve Order | Preserve the initial order of the data records. Valid Values: True , False |

Structure to use as the receptor. Ensure the receptor has hydrogens and complete valence shells.
Ensemble docking can be performed by selecting multiple receptors which should be aligned.

In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all visible molecules.

Notes:

* The receptor should not contain alternate conformations.

* You can use the protein tools in Discovery Studio to prepare a receptor.

* Ensemble docking is only available for GOLD version 5 and higher.

Amino acid residues that can undergo rotation as specified in the GOLD rotamer library (up to 10 residues).

In Discovery Studio, select a group containing the desired residues.

In Pipeline Pilot, the residues are specified as:

The residues are defined by a space separated list:
[chain]:[residue name][residue sequence number][insertion code] (insertion code is optional)

Example: A:TYR33 A:LEU44

* This option is not available when docking with multiple receptors (ensemble docking).

* The rotamer library file $(GOLD_DIR)/gold/rotamer_library.txt contains information taken from the paper "The Penultimate Rotamer Library", S. C. Lovell, J. M. Word, J. S. Richardson & D. C.
Richardson, Proteins, 40, 389-408, 2000. This is a compilation of the most commonly observed
side-chain conformations for the naturally occurring amino acids.

During docking, receptor serine, threonine, lysine NH3+, and tyrosine hydroxyl groups are optimized, i.e. rotated. If this is undesirable this rotation can be disabled by setting the value to True.

Valid Values: True, False

Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files
that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation.

In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance.

Defines a sphere in the receptor where receptor-ligands interactions are permitted.

In Pipeline Pilot, define the sphere as x,y,z,r where x,y,z specifies the coordinates of the center and r is the radius of the sphere ( e.g. , 83.2,-43.3,42.24,6).

In Discovery Studio, define the sphere using the Define and Edit Binding Site tools and then select the coordinates from the list.

Receptor atom indices that define the binding site for ligand docking.

GOLD offers the following scoring functions:

* Goldscore : original scoring function provided with GOLD. It has been optimized for the prediction of ligand binding positions and takes into account factors such as H-bonding energy, van der Waals energy and ligand torsion strain.

* Chemscore : estimates the total free energy change that occurs on ligand binding and was trained by regression against binding affinity data.

* ASP : Astex Statistical Potential (ASP) is an atom-atom potential derived from a database of protein-ligand complexes and can be compared to other such scoring potentials, e.g. PMF and Drugscore. ASP has comparable accuracy to Chemscore and Goldscore.

* CHEMPLP : Piecewise Linear Potential is an empirical fitness functions optimized for pose prediction. The Piecewise Linear Potential (PLP) is used to model the steric complementarity between protein and ligand, while for CHEMPLP additionally the distance- and angle-dependent hydrogen and metal bonding terms from Chemscore are considered.

Note:

* The fitness scores are dimensionless and cannot be used explicitly for binding energy or binding affinity calculation. For more information consult the help text provided by GOLD.

Valid Values: Goldscore, Chemscore, ASP, CHEMPLP

Pre-defined GOLD Generic Algorithm (GA) settings,
which controls speed and quality of the results.

The following options are available:

* GOLD Default : delivers high predictive accuracy but is relatively slow.

* 2 times speed up : faster docking.

* 3 times speed up : even faster docking

* 7-8 times speed up : fastest docking speed

* Automatic : automatic parameters.

* Automatic Library Screening : fastest setting and as a consequence is the least reliable.

* Automatic Virtual Screening :
suitable for routine work and usually gives comparable predictive accuracy to the slower settings, unless the ligand has a large number of rotatable torsions.

* Automatic Default : GOLD will attempt to apply optimal settings for each ligand.

* Automatic Very Flexible : recommended for large highly flexible ligands. This setting delivers high predictive accuracy but is relatively slow.

Valid Values: GOLD Default, 2 times speed up, 3 times speed up, 7-8 times speed up, Automatic , Automatic Library Screening, Automatic Virtual Screening, Automatic Default, Automatic Very Flexible

Search Efficiency (%) controls the speed of docking and the predictive accuracy. When automatic settings are selected the GA parameters will be determined on-the-fly and are optimized for each ligand. Since the genetic algorithm relies on change to find solutions, limiting the number of operations causes the search space to be more limited. This must be offset however against the gain in speed that can be attained this way. This parameter allows the user to reduce the coverage of the search space (reliability) and increase the speed of docking.

Scaling down may be useful for screening purposes if faster docking times are required. Using the default setting (100%), GOLD will attempt to apply optimal settings for each ligand. For a medium sized ligand with 5 rotatable bonds, this will be around 30,000 GA operations. When set to 50%, this value will be scaled down prior to docking this ligand, to a value of 15,000, speeding up the docking by a factor of 2. The parameter should be set between 10% and 200%.

Note :

* If blank, an automatic preset based on the GA Parameters is used.

Subject each ligand to a minimum number of operations.

* If blank an automatic preset based on the GA Parameters is used.

Restrict each ligand to a maximum number of operations.

Options that control the ligand docking.

GOLD will dock each ligand several times starting each time from a different random population of ligand orientations. The results of the different docking runs are ranked by fitness score. The total time spent docking a ligand obviously depends on the number of docking runs, so you can make GOLD go faster by reducing this number. However, it is useful to perform at least a few docking runs on each ligand. This increases the chances of getting the right answer. Also, if the same answer is found in several different docking runs, it is usually a strong indicator that the answer is correct.

The Early Termination options can be used to prevent GOLD wasting time performing multiple docking runs on easy ligands.

Cavity detection algorithm can be used to restrict the region of interest to concave, solvent-accessible surfaces.

Valid Values: True , False

* First, the solvent accessible surface of each atom in the defined binding site is calculated. Potential donor and acceptor fitting points (used for ligand placement) are then generated for only those protein atoms that are accessible.

* Second, the potential fitting points are themselves tested for solvent accessibility, and only those fitting points that are accessible are used.

* For example, this option can be used to avoid problems with solvent accessibility of backbone carbonyls in kinases where one of the carbonyl lone pairs is typically desolvated by a neighboring atom.

GOLD output file level:

* 0 : No GOLD log files are created. Recommended for high-throughput virtual screening.

* 1 : Minimal information is returned with warnings log and GOLD main log file.

* 2 : All GOLD log files are returned. This option may create a large amount of data and depending on the number of input ligands, may affect speed.

Valid Values: 0, 1 , 2

Enables docking of covalently bound ligands to the receptor.

* GOLD requires that there is just one atom linking a ligand to the protein (e.g., the O in a serine residue). Both protein and ligand should contain the link atom (for example, if the serine O is the link atom, it should be present in both protein and ligand). Ideally, the link atom, in both the ligand and the protein, will have a free valence available through which the link can be made. If the link atom on the ligand does not have a free valence, having a hydrogen instead, then the docking will proceed and the hydrogen will be ignored in terms of its contribution to the fitness score. However, the hydrogen is still present in the docked poses.

* The GOLD least-squares fitting routine forces the link atom of the ligand to fit onto the link atom of the protein.

* In order to make sure that the geometry of the bound ligand is correct, the angle-bending potential from the Tripos Force Field has been incorporated into the fitness function. On evaluating the score of the docked ligand, the angle-bending energy for the link atom is included in the calculation of the fitness score.

* Since the protein is held rigid (apart from hydroxyl hydrogen atoms), it does require that the position of the link atom in the protein is feasible.

Protein atom ID that forms the link to the ligand.

* The link atom needs to be present in the protein and the ligand.

* In Discovery Studio you may select the protein link atom and use the Create New Group from Selection , or use an existing group. Please ensure that the selection contains only a single entry.

* In Pipeline Pilot, please enter the protein atom ID.

Ligand substructure with the link atom.

* The substructure can only contain one link atom which needs to be present in the receptor and the substructure.

Substructure link atom ID.

* In Discovery Studio you may select the link atom and use the Create New Group from Selection , or use an existing group. Please ensure that the selection contains only a single entry.

* In Pipeline Pilot, please enter the atom ID.

Enable topology matching to check equivalent atoms. If the constraint refers to a substructure atom (and therefore a ligand atom) which is topologically equivalent to other atoms (e.g., oxygen atoms of an ionized carboxylate group), GOLD
will then use the atom that gives the best result.

Enforce pose diversity during ligand mapping. As the ligand is constructed and mapped into the binding site, GOLD checks the Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD) of the current solution against those that have already been generated.

If the RMSD is below the diversity threshold or the maximum number of solutions per cluster has been reached, the mapping is rejected and the process repeated until an acceptable solution is generated. GOLD keeps track of any failures; once the failure threshold has been reached the diverse solutions code is switched off.

Number of diverse ligand poses in a cluster within the defined Generate Diverse Solutions RMSD .

RMSD cut-off (Å) for determining if diverse solutions are in the same cluster or not.

Allow docking of a ligand to terminate as soon as a specified number of runs have given essentially the same pose.

Number of solutions to generate before early termination. GOLD will terminate docking on
a given ligand if this number of the top poses are within Early Termination RMSD Å of each other.

For example, if set to 3 and Early Termination RMSD is set to 1.5
the docking will terminate if the top 3 solutions are within 1.5 Å RMSD of each other.

* Early termination does not always save as much time as you might
think, because it tends to be invoked for easy (i.e., relatively rigid) ligands, which are quick to dock anyway.

Root Mean Square Deviation (Å) for early termination. See Early Termination Number of Solutions

Select a structure with water molecules to be included during docking. From this structure you can select groups with the following options:

* Group Spin : GOLD rotates (spins) the water molecule.

* Group Toggle : GOLD decides whether the water should be present or absent (i.e. bound or displaced by the ligand).

* Group Translate : Waters are allowed to translate and to spin during the docking (only available with GOLD 5).

* In Pipeline Pilot select a single MOL2 or PDB file containing the water molecules.

* Any non-water molecules will be ignored.

* Ensure that the specified water molecules are not present in the protein structure, this can lead to clashes.

Selected waters are allowed to spin during the optimization

* In Discovery Studio, select a group containing the desired waters from the Input Waters .

* In Pipeline Pilot, specify the atom numbers of the water oxygens from the Input Waters (space or comma separated).

Specified water molecules may be toggled. For waters in this list GOLD will decide whether the water should be present or absent (i.e. bound or displaced by the ligand) during docking.

Specified water molecules are allowed to translate and spin.

* In Discovery Studio, select a group containing the desired waters.

* The maximum translation can be specified in Distance .

* This feature is only available for GOLD 5.

Maximum distance that waters specified in Options Translate Water Group are allowed to translate (Å).

Options which control the docking constraints.

Protein atoms that should form hydrogen bonds with a ligand.

The interactions can be defined using the Dock Ligands tools in Discovery Studio using the "Define Interaction Site" command.
In Pipeline Pilot, specify the constraint weight, geometry weight, and atom IDs.
The constraint weight defines the strength of bias applied to the
formation of a specified hydrogen bond by GOLD.

The geometry weight defines how good a hydrogen bonding interaction has to be in order for it to be considered a hydrogen bond by GOLD (range 0 to 1, default 0.005).

* The weights can be set in Discovery Studio under in the Data Table or the Preferences.

Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files
that contain the ligands or fragments to be used for constraining the matches.
The scaffold match constraint can be used to place a fragment at an exact specified position in
the binding site, the geometry of the fragment will not be altered during docking. The scaffold, can, for example, be a common core, a fragment, or a substructure known to adopt a certain binding position.

For a given ligand, it is not possible to match multiple scaffolds at the same time. Scaffolds are evaluated in the order supplied by the user and the scaffold that matches the ligand first will be used. This means that it is possible to specify two or more different scaffolds, and GOLD will use the scaffold that matches the ligand first. This can be useful when docking multiple different series of compounds.

In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected,
or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file
offers the best performance.

Determines how closely ligand atoms fit onto the scaffold. Setting a higher weight will force the ligand to be placed onto the scaffold locations more strictly.

Ligands are not docked when the specified constraint(s) are physically impossible to satisfy (e.g. if no suitable group is present in the ligand to form the required H-bond constraint).

GOLD data files.

Override docking parameters with specified configuration file, except, the input ligands. Use this option on a pre-prepared configuration file.

* The format of the parameter file is strict and incorrect syntax may cause GOLD to behave in unexpected ways or even to crash. Because of the large number of parameters, no guarantee can be given that the program will behave reliably with anything other than the default parameterization.

* When running from the Pipeline Pilot Client or Web Port, ensure that the data file path in the GOLD configuration are correctly specified and visible to the server.

Parameter file that contains parameters used by GOLD (e.g., hydrogen bond energies, atom radii and polarizabilities, torsion potentials, hydrogen bond directionalities, etc.). 
It also contains parameters that control the general behavior of GOLD, e.g., whether the final solution from a genetic algorithm run is to be minimized via a simplex procedure before being saved.

* If blank, the GOLD default settings will be used.

Customized parameter file for the specified Fitness Function . If blank, GOLD default settings will be used.

* The format of the parameter file is strict and incorrect syntax may cause GOLD to behave in unexpected ways or even to crash. Because of the large number of parameters, no guarantee can be given that the program will behave reliably with anything other than the default parameterization. A full description of the meaning of the various parameters is given elsewhere.

Ligand torsion distribution file to restrict the
conformational space sampled by the genetic algorithm.

* Left blank, the default GOLD torsion distribution file will be used.

* By selecting an empty file all torsions are sampled.

* Several torsion distribution files exist in the GOLD installation directory.

* The format of the parameter file is strict. Incorrect syntax may cause GOLD to behave unexpectedly.

It is possible to supply the seed for the random number generator used by the genetic algorithm in GOLD.
This provides a mechanism for introducing a non-random start facility. Normally, a new GOLD
calculation will be seeded in this way in order to reproduce identical results for repeat runs. You could also use this mechanism to manually specify a seed for a new GOLD calculation.

* The format of this file is strict. Incorrect syntax may cause GOLD to behave unexpectedly.

Options which control the ligand flexibility.

Methods for exploring ring conformations during docking.

* Rigid : No conformational ring search.

* Flip Ring Corners : Enable a limited conformational search of cyclic systems by allowing free corners of rings to flip above or below the plane of their neighboring atoms.

* Match Template Conformations : Identifies each ring in the ligand and attempts to match it to the Cambridge Structural Database (CSD) ring template. For each template the number of alternative conformations that will be explored during docking will vary depending on the abundance and suitability of data within the CSD.

* A. W. R. Payne and R. C. Glen, J. Mol. Graphics, 10 , 74-91 (1993).

Valid Values: Rigid , Flip Ring Corners, Match Template Conformations

During ligand initialization, ligand amide groups (including thioamides, ureas, and thioureas) will be set to the trans conformation. Flattening to the trans conformation will also occur if the (O)C-N(H) torsion is greater than 20° out of plane.

In order to flip between cis and trans conformations the CO-NRR' torsion is first made planar (at the initialized trans conformation).

* If the (O)C-N(H) torsion is greater than five but less than 20° out of the trans plane, the bond will not be flattened.

Allow planar trigonal nitrogens in the ligand (bound to sp2 carbons) to flip between cis and trans conformations during docking (otherwise, they will be held fixed at the input geometry).

* Fixed : Fixed bonds at their input conformation.

* Flip non-ring only : Flip non-ring only.

* Flip non-ring and ring-NHR1 : allows non-ring and ring-NHR1 to flip (i.e. rotate 180°).

* Flip non-ring and ring-NR1R2 : allows non-ring and ring-NR1R2 to flip (i.e. rotate 180°).

* Flip all : allow all to flip.

Valid Values: Fixed, Flip non-ring only, Flip non-ring and ring-NHR1, Flip non-ring and ring-NR1R2, Flip all

Allow pyramidal (i.e. non-planar sp3) nitrogens to invert during docking (otherwise, they will be held fixed at the input geometry). Given a non-planar group RR'R"N or tetrahedrally surrounded RR'R"NH, the Flip pyramidal N switch enables flipping of the local stereochemistry around the nitrogen (the energy barrier for this umbrella-like change of geometry around the nitrogen is low).

* Flipping only changes the stereochemistry around RR'R"N and RR'R"NH nitrogens. It does not affect other chiral centers.

Allow intramolecular hydrogen bonds in the ligand to be formed during docking.

* Use this with care as it can make ligands like methotrexate curl up.

Control the behavior of protonated carboxylic acids during docking.

* Fixed : held rigid at their input conformation.

* Flip : allowed to flip (i.e. rotate 180°).

* Rotate Freely : allow to rotate freely.

Valid Values: Fixed, Flip , Freely Rotate

Fix the geometry of specific bonds or of part of the ligand, e.g. in order to study the possible binding of a pre-determined ligand geometry. The following options are available:

* None : Allow for full flexibility.

* All : Fix all rotatable bonds, i.e., keep input conformation.

* All But Terminal : Fix all non-terminal rotatable bonds (i.e. not -CH3, -OH, etc.), at their input conformation:

When fixing all rotatable bonds at their input conformation (i.e. performing a rigid ligand 
docking) GOLD will try to find the best orientation of the ligand in the binding site by mapping 
donor-acceptor (as well as hydrophobic-hydrophobic) fitting points. However, GOLD will not 
perform a local optimization (simplex) on the final solution. This may lead to penalization of 
near-optimal conformations. Performing a few cycles of molecular-mechanics minimization 
before docking may help to take the ligand close to its local potential-energy minimum.

Valid Values: None , All, All But Terminal

Select the torsion angle distribution library to restrict the ligand conformational space sampled by the genetic algorithm. Using torsion angle library may improve the chances of GOLD finding the correct answer by biasing the search towards ligand torsion-angle values that are commonly observed in crystal structure.

The following settings are available:

* Default : New default torsion distribution library introduced in 2023.3 (Penner et al 2022).

* Original : Default torsion library prior to the 2023.3 release.

* MIMUMBA : Torsion library by Klebe and Mietzner 1994.

* False : Do not use a torsion library to guide the search.

* Custom : User defined library file specified in: Data Files Torsion Angle Distribution

See Also: :

* The Torsion Library: Semi-automated Improvement of Torsion Rules with SMARTScompare. (Penner et al, J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2022, 62, 7, 1644-1653).

* A fast and efficient method to generate biologically relevant conformations, Klebe and Mietzner, J.Comput.-Aided Mol.Des., 8, 583-606, 1994).

Valid Values: Default , Original, MIMUMBA, False, Custom

Parameters for saving poses.

Maximum number of poses that should be saved. Blank or less than 1 saves all solutions otherwise keeps that number of poses for each docked ligand.

* Gold.Protein.RotatedTorsions : Rotated atom torsion.

* Gold.Protein.ActiveResidue : Active residues.

* Gold.Protein.RotatedAtoms : Rotated atoms.

Filters all solutions with fitness scores lower than a specified value.
Filtering reduces the number of poses by keeping only the best solutions.
Disabled if blank.

Add the scoring contributions properties of individual ligand and protein atoms to the docked solution. For each atom its contribution to the total fitness score and also the constituent scoring terms will be added.

Correct the internal energy terms (internal torsion, internal vdW, and internal Hbond) according to the best energy encountered for these terms during the run. By applying this correction the internal energy will be calculated with respect to that of a close to optimal non-bound structure, thereby taking into account any irreducible internal energy.

Use the GOLD template specified in: Docking Template .

* The parameters set in the template file will override the equivalent protocol parameters.

Docking templates assign optimized setting for a number of different docking protocols.

The following default templates are provided with a GOLD installation:

* chemscore_kinase : Optimized for kinase docking.

* chemscore_p450_csd : Optimized for cytochrome P450 docking.

* gold_folate_enzymes_VS : Virtual screening template designed for identifying active molecules for folates enzyme.

* gold_kinase_VS : Virtual screening template designed for identifying active molecules for kinases.

* gold_metallo_protease_gen_VS : Virtual screening template designed for identifying active molecules for metallo protease.

* gold_nuclear_hormone_rec_VS : Virtual screening template designed for identifying active molecules for nuclear hormones.

* gold_phosphodiesterase_VS : Virtual screening template designed for identifying active molecules for phosphodiesterases.

* gold_serine_protease_VS : Virtual screening template designed for identifying active molecules for serine proteases. Goldscore is used as the docking scoring function and ASP as the rescoring function.

* goldscore_p450_csd : Optimized template for cytochrome P450 docking.

Notes

* The parameter lists all template files available in the GOLD/templates directory.

* You can easily add or modify files in the GOLD/templates directory

* Any parameter specified in a template file will override any parameter set in the protocol interface.

* An error is thrown when the GOLD/templates directory is not found.

Execute this protocol in parallel on Pipeline Pilot servers. You can set the number of data records sent in each process batch, the name of the servers, the number of protocol processes executed on each server, and whether to preserve the order of the processed data records.

* Not all parts of the protocol are run in parallel, which may affect scaling. In general, performance improves when the parallelization benefits outweigh the data transfer overhead for the specified batch size.

* By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal.

Comma separated list of servers (server-name:port-number) to be used for parallel processing.

Add "localhost" to include the local server. This can be helpful on multi-CPU/multi-core systems (where the subprotocol jobs are spawned on the same machine) and Pipeline Pilot Linux clusters (where "localhost" requests spawning the subprotocol jobs on the same cluster).

Comma separated list of the maximum batches that can be simultaneously executed on each server. Each value must correspond with an entry in the list of servers. The number of entries in this parameter must equal the number of servers.

Preserve the initial order of the data records.

# Dock Ligands (GOLD)

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsrlinteractions

Source file: tsrlinteractions/receptor-ligand_interactions_dock_ligands_gold.htm

## Dock Ligands (GOLD)

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

The Dock Ligands (GOLD) protocol is an interface to the CCDC GOLD Protein-Ligand Docking program
( [Jones et al., 1995] and [Jones et al., 1997] ).

GOLD (Genetic Optimization for Ligand Docking) is a genetic algorithm for docking flexible ligands into a protein binding site.

Predicting how a small molecule will bind to a protein is difficult, and no method can guarantee success. The best approach is to measure as accurately as possible the reliability of the method (i.e., the chance that it will make a successful prediction in a given instance). For this reason, GOLD has been tested on a large number of complexes extracted from the Protein Data Bank. The overall conclusion of these tests was that the top-ranked GOLD solution was correct in 70-80% of cases.

The Dock Ligands (GOLD) protocol offers several scoring functions for docking:

| Scoring Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| GoldScore | Original docking function [Jones et al., 1995] |
| GoldScore | Estimates the total free-energy change that occurs on ligand binding [Eldridge et al., 1997] |
| ASP | Atom-atom potential derived from a database [Korb et al., 2009] |
| CHEMPLP | Empirical fitness functions optimized for pose prediction [Korb et al., 2009] |
| GoldScore/Chemscore Templates | Templates optimized for kinase and cytochrome docking. |

GOLD uses a genetic algorithm (GA) to search favorable ligand poses. A population of chromosomes is manipulated during a GA run, with each chromosome representing a trial docking. A chromosome contains all the information needed to completely define a trial ligand pose and is associated with a fitness value, computed from the scoring function [Cole et al., 2005] . Different values of the genetic algorithm parameters may be used to control the balance between the speed of GOLD and the reliability of its predictions. GOLD will only produce reliable results if it is used properly.

For more detailed information, refer to the GOLD documentation at CCDC .

For a description and details about the strengths and weaknesses of the available docking protocols, see Choose a docking protocol .

* Load the structure you want to define as the receptor
into the Graphics View .
For ensemble docking, the proteins must be superimposed because only one binding site definition is used. See Superimposing protein structures for more information.

* Ensure that the receptor has hydrogens added and all atom valencies are satisfied so that atoms can be properly typed.

* From the Graphics View, select the receptor.

* Open the Define and Edit Binding Site tool panel and
click Define Receptor .

* Click From Current Selection . Ensure the
sphere is selected in the Parameters Explorer. Alternately, select the site atoms, right-click and choose Group... .

* Open the Receptor-Ligand Interactions | Dock Ligands tools and click Dock Ligands (GOLD) to open the Dock Ligands (GOLD) dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Receptor Choose the selected receptor. For ensemble docking you can specify multiple receptors. For more information, see GOLD user guide . Input Ligands Specify the ligands to be used by the protocol. For details, see Specifying Ligands . Input Site Sphere or Input Site Atoms Choose the selected sphere or group of atoms defined as the receptor.
Note that the sphere can be defined using the Define and Edit Binding Site tool panel. By default, GOLD is run with automatic GA mode and internally calculates an optimal number of operations for a given ligand, thereby making the most efficient use of search time, e.g. small ligands containing only one or two rotatable bonds will generally require fewer genetic operations than larger highly flexible ligands.
For details about the remaining parameters, see Dock Ligands (GOLD) - Parameters . The Dock Ligands (GOLD) protocol also allows you to dock ligands by using settings from an already existing GOLD configuration
( *.conf ) file. Ligand files specified in this GOLD configuration file are overwritten with the Input Ligands . However, all other parameters shown in the Dock Ligands (GOLD) protocol will not be used for this run. Therefore,
ensure that all parameter settings and file path in the selected GOLD configuration file are correctly specified.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Receptor | Choose the selected receptor. For ensemble docking you can specify multiple receptors. For more information, see GOLD user guide . |
| Input Ligands | Specify the ligands to be used by the protocol. For details, see Specifying Ligands . |
| Input Site Sphere or Input Site Atoms | Choose the selected sphere or group of atoms defined as the receptor. Note that the sphere can be defined using the Define and Edit Binding Site tool panel. |

By default, GOLD is run with automatic GA mode and internally calculates an optimal number of operations for a given ligand, thereby making the most efficient use of search time, e.g. small ligands containing only one or two rotatable bonds will generally require fewer genetic operations than larger highly flexible ligands.
For details about the remaining parameters, see Dock Ligands (GOLD) - Parameters .

The Dock Ligands (GOLD) protocol also allows you to dock ligands by using settings from an already existing GOLD configuration
( *.conf ) file. Ligand files specified in this GOLD configuration file are overwritten with the Input Ligands .

However, all other parameters shown in the Dock Ligands (GOLD) protocol will not be used for this run. Therefore,
ensure that all parameter settings and file path in the selected GOLD configuration file are correctly specified.

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

View the docked ligands in the Molecule Window .
The Input Receptor is also
shown, with the view centered on the binding site. This view allows you to browse through the ligands and view the 3D structure, a 2D
depiction, and property data simultaneously. Use the View Interactions tools to identify ligand hydrogen bonds, bumps, and Pi interactions. For details about viewing, sorting, and filtering the results in the Data Table View, see Analyzing results with the Data Table View .

GOLD uses a genetic algorithm (GA) for ligand docking. Therefore, repeated GOLD runs may produce different results. In addition, the number of top scoring poses returned may also change.

#### Troubleshooting

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| <ligand>.sd | Contains the docked ligands. |
| <ligand>_fail.sd | Contains any ligands that failed the protocol. |
| <receptor>_complex.dsv | Contains the receptor (or receptors when run in ensemble docking mode). In addition, water atoms are added when they are specified as a separate molecule. |
| gold-<receptor>.log | GOLD log file. |
| gold-<receptor>-docking.log | Log file containing detailed information for each ligand, if docking mode was selected. |
| gold-<receptor>-scoring.log | Log file containing detailed information on each ligand, if scoring mode was selected. |
| gold-<receptor>.cfg | GOLD configuration file. Note, this file cannot be used to re-run a GOLD protocol using the Data Files Gold Configuration File parameter. |
| gold-<receptor>-warnings.log | Log file containing warnings reported by GOLD, if file exists. |
| gold-<receptor>-errors.log | Contains any error messages reported by GOLD. |
| ViewResults.ds_pl | Open this file to view the docked ligands with the input receptor (or receptors for ensemble docking) in a Molecule Window . |

#### Further information

Scoring Ligand Poses CCDC GOLD documentation Run a parallel calculation Distributed grid computing

# Dock Ligands (LibDock) - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsrlinteractions

Source file: tsrlinteractions/receptor-ligand_interactions_dock_ligands_libdock-para.htm

## Dock Ligands (LibDock) - Parameters

### Docks ligands into an active site using hotspots

LibDock is a high-throughput algorithm for docking ligands into an active receptor site. Ligand conformations are aligned to polar and apolar receptor interaction sites (hotspots) and the best scoring poses are reported. Ligand conformations can be pre-calculated or generated on the fly using Catalyst.

Since some of the output poses may have hydrogen atoms in close proximity to the receptor, a CHARMm minimization step can be enabled to optimize the docked poses further (increases CPU time).

The following steps are performed:

* Calculates ligand conformations

* Docks the conformations using LibDock

* Minimizes docked poses using CHARMm

Steps in italics may be skipped depending on settings.

This protocol adds many properties to the data stream including:

* AbsoluteEnergy : Absolute conformation energy.

* RelativeEnergy : Relative conformation energy.

* ConfNumber : Conformation number.

* MOL_NUMBER : Molecule number.

* POSE_NUMBER : Pose number.

* LibDockScore : LibDock score.

* HotSpots : Hotspot coordinates.

* -In-Situ Starting Energy : Negative of the start in-situ energy.

* -In-Situ Final Energy : Negative of the final in-situ energy.

See Also:

* High Throughput Docking for Library Design and Library Prioritization, David J. Diller and Kenneth M. Merz, Jr., PROTEINS: Structure, Function, and Genetics 2001, 43,113-124.

* Kinases, Homology Models, and High Throughput Docking, David J. Diller and Rixin Li, J. Med. Chem. 2003, 46, 4638-4647.

* Validation Studies of the Site-Directed Docking Program LibDock, S.N. Rao, M.S. Head, A. Kulkarni, and J.M. Lalonde, J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2007 47(6), 2159-2171.

### Parameters

| Name | Description | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input Receptor | Structure to use as the receptor. Ensure the receptor has hydrogens and complete valence shells. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all visible molecules. Notes: The receptor should not contain alternate conformations. You can use the protein tools in Discovery Studio to prepare a receptor. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
| Input Ligands | Specify one or more MDL MOL/SD files that contain the ligands to be used for the calculation. In Discovery Studio, you also have the option to specify all, selected, or visible ligands in an active Molecule Window. However, specifying a file offers the best performance. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
| Input Site Sphere | Defines a sphere in the receptor where receptor-ligands interactions are permitted. In Pipeline Pilot, define the sphere as x,y,z,r where x,y,z specifies the coordinates of the center and r is the radius of the sphere ( e.g. , 83.2,-43.3,42.24,6). In Discovery Studio, define the sphere using the Define and Edit Binding Site tools and then select the coordinates from the list. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
| Number of Hotspots | Number of polar or apolar receptor hotspots for conformer matching. A larger number will increase the computational time. Note: If an existing hotspot file is specified, the number will be determined automatically. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
| Docking Tolerance | LibDock employs a hotspots matching algorithm to dock ligands. This matching algorithm employs an RMSD tolerance (Å) to accept or reject any given match. Increasing the tolerance will generally result in more docked poses. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
| Docking Preferences | LibDock can perform docking in four different modes: High Quality Fast Search Fast Search for SASA (Solvent Accessible Surface Area) User Specified Fast Search is most appropriate for docking a very large dataset. In the User Specified mode all advanced parameters are accessible.
