The equilibration can be run in MPI mode with multiple CPU cores.

* For details about the remaining parameters, see Solvate with Explicit Membrane - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

* All Simulation protocols require that the simulated system be typed using an appropriate forcefield. If a molecule is not typed when the protocol is launched, it will be automatically typed using the forcefield selected in the Change Forcefield tools.

* This protocol only allows charmm36 forcefield, which supports more than 400 types of lipids.

* If the automatic typing is unsuccessful, the protocol will not run. Use the Change Forcefield tools to investigate typing failures.

You can inspect the final solvated system by opening the <molecule>.dsv file in a Molecule Window. Lipid groups including Lipids for full lipid molecules, Lipid Heads for polar lipid heads, and Lipid Tails for the heavy atom at the tip of the lipid tail are created for easy selection
and analysis. If equilibration is performed, the report will have information on the temperature, total energy, and density of the system versus simulation time.

#### Output

The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here. If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run.

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| <molecule>.dsv | The output molecule with explicit membrane, water and optionally counterions added. |
| <molecule>_restart.pdb | The coordinate restart file from the equilibration. Only present if equilibration is performed. |
| <molecule>_restart.vel | The velocity restart file from the equilibration. Only present if equilibration is performed. |
| <molecule>_restart.xsc | The extended system restart file from the equilibration. Only present if equilibration is performed. |
| namd.log | Contains detailed log messages generated by the NAMD simulation engine. Only present if equilibration is performed. |

# CHARMm Relative FEP Calculations (GPU) - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tssimulation

Source file: tssimulation/simulation_free_energy_perturbation_charmm_gpu-para.htm

## CHARMm Relative FEP Calculations (GPU) - Parameters

### Run relative FEP on GPU using CHARMm DOMDEC

Runs alchemical Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) dynamics simulations using CHARMm DOMDEC platform.
Prior to using this protocol, the input structures containing dual topology ligands must be prepared using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol . This protocol can run multiple simulations either in serial or parallel mode. In parallel mode, when run on a grid enabled server with GPUs, individual lambda windows are run independently and in parallel, thus reducing runtime. The protocol implements a full transformation of the input structure from lambda 0 to 1 using a user chosen lambda schedule or number of lambda windows, and sampling time. The FEP data collected during the equilibration stage at each window is NOT used for the free energy calculation. The protocol performs a short energy minimization prior to running the FEP calculation.

Each input structure prepared by the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol is expected to contain two groups, namely FEP_0 and FEP_1, which can be selected by the user to visually inspect the disappearing and appearing atoms from the initial and final ligands, respectively. During the FEP dynamics simulation, the vdW and electrostatic interactions of disappearing atoms are gradually turned off between lambda 0 and 1, and for appearing atoms turned on during the same period.

Three types of input structures can be provided: Solvated protein-ligand complexes, free ligands, and ligands in vacuum. Alternatively, hydration free energies can be calculated by providing free ligands in solvent and in vacuum as inputs.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input FEP Systems | Input systems to perform FEP calculations on. Valid Values: Binding , Hydration, Single |
| Input FEP Systems Solvated Complexes | Specify the solvated protein-ligand complex molecular structures prepared using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol on which to perform the FEP calculations. In Pipeline Pilot, specify a file containing the prepared FEP systems, the supported file formats are DSV and MOL2. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all the visible typed structures. |
| Input FEP Systems Solvated Ligands | Specify the solvated ligand molecular structures prepared using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol on which to perform the FEP calculations. In Pipeline Pilot, specify a file containing the prepared FEP systems, the supported file formats are DSV and MOL2. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all the visible typed structures. |
| Input FEP Systems Vacuum Ligands | Specify the ligand molecular structures in vacuum prepared using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol on which to perform the FEP calculations. In Pipeline Pilot, specify a file containing the prepared FEP systems, the supported file formats are DSV and MOL2. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all the visible typed structures. |
| FEP Simulation Schedule | Parameters pertaining to the FEP simulation |
| Custom Lambda Schedule | Specifies the lambda values at which free energy simulations are run. A custom schedule allows for narrowly spaced windows near the end states for increased accuracy. |
| Number of Lambda Windows | Number of Lambda windows or intermediate states to be used in the FEP simulation. Only allowed values are those that result in a rational Lambda window width. This option can be used only when the Custom Lambda Schedule parameter is set to blank. |
| Simulation Time per Lambda Window (ps) | The time length (ps) to perform the dynamics simulation per lambda window. Since multiple lambda windows are simulated, the total simulation time from lambda 0 to 1 is the number of lambda windows times this parameter. |

# CHARMm Relative FEP 
Calculations (GPU)

Source type: HTML

Source section: tssimulation

Source file: tssimulation/simulation_free_energy_perturbation_charmm_gpu.htm

## CHARMm Relative FEP 
Calculations (GPU)

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

The CHARMm Relative FEP Calculations (GPU) protocol allows you to 
run alchemical free energy simulations in the NPT thermodynamic ensemble. The protocol uses the 
CHARMm molecular dynamics program's DOMDEC GPU platform.

The free energy pertubation (FEP) simulation is designed to calculate the change in free energy during an alchemical transformation, for example one ligand is alchemically transformed into another. If two such FEP calculations are performed, one in the protein binding pocket, and another one in solvent, the difference between the two alchemical free energies results in the relative binding free energy between the two ligands.

The figure below illustrates this by depicting two ligands (Ligand 1 and Ligand 2) in the complexed and free solvated states. The relative binding affinity ΔΔG(1->2) of the two ligands equals to ΔG2 - ΔG1, where ΔG1 and ΔG2 correspond to the physical process of transferring the ligands from their solvated environments to the protein.

These two values are expensive to compute. Instead, in relative FEP calculations, alchemical quantities ΔG3 and ΔG4 are computed, which are the free energies of chemically modifying Ligand 1 to 2 in the solvent and protein environment. From the diagram, the relative binding free energy ΔΔG(1->2) = ΔG2 - ΔG1 = ΔG4 - ΔG3.

Relative binding free energy between ligand pairs computed this way can be useful in lead optimization projects where it can inform the chemist which compound to make next to improve its binding affinity.

The CHARMm Relative FEP Calculations (GPU) protocol allows you to run the relative FEP calculation on a series of input systems that each include the free ligand in solution and the protein-ligand complex in solution. The inputs include a set of molecular systems prepared using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol. This protocol represents the fifth in the series of steps comprising the FEP workflow:

* Generate Analog Conformations

* Type Ligands with MATCH (Prototype) , or alternatively, use Change Forcefield tools to type ligands with CHARMm forcefield.

* Generate Ligand Pairs for FEP

* Set Up Relative FEP Calculations

* CHARMm Relative FEP Calculations (GPU)

The protocol implements a full transformation of the input structure from the initial to the final state using a series of intermediate steps defined by the lambda variable, which changes from 0 to 1 as the simulation progresses from the initial to the final state. In effect, as lambda progresses from 0 to 1, the interactions involving the initial state or groups unique to Ligand 1 are "turned off", and the same for Ligand 2 are "turned on" by tuning the non-bonded interactions off and on, respectively. By default, 15 lambda windows are simulated. The total simulation time is thus 15 times the Simulation Time per Lambda Window (ps) 
+ Equilibration Time per Lambda Window (ps) .

At the beginning of 
each window, an equilibration of the structure is performed prior to FEP 
data collection. The FEP data collected during the equilibration stage 
at each window is not used for the free energy calculation. You can 
specify a different Custom Lambda Schedule or change the N umber 
of Lambda Windows to values that exactly divide unity.

The input molecules prepared by the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol are expected to contain FEP_0 and FEP_1 groups, which you can use to visually inspect the disappearing and appearing atoms from the initial and final ligands. During the FEP dynamics simulation, the vdW 
and electrostatic interactions of disappearing atoms are gradually 
turned off between lambda 0 and 1, and for appearing atoms turned on 
during the same period.

Upon the completion of the simulations, the output files from each 
lambda window are post-processed and a statistical analysis is performed. The total free energy change for each system is reported along with the associated statistical error. Also, a detailed free energy report containing values for each lambda window and associated statistical error is accessible from the main report.

### Considerations for running

* The protocol is not supported on Windows servers.

* It is recommended that the protocol be run on the DOMDEC GPU 
platform for speed. The DOMDEC GPU platform only supports a single 
GPU.

* When running on a GPU platform, increasing the Number of Processors from 1 to 2, 4, or 8 will typically result in better performance.

* Binding, 
Hydration, and Single free energy calculations are supported Binding requires the 
solvated complex and solvated ligand as inputs. Hydration requires the solvated ligand and vacuum ligand as 
inputs. Single runs one of the three 
possible systems. After running two single type calculations, 
manually combine the results to obtain binding 
or hydration free energies.

* Binding requires the 
solvated complex and solvated ligand as inputs.

* Hydration requires the solvated ligand and vacuum ligand as 
inputs.

* Single runs one of the three 
possible systems. After running two single type calculations, 
manually combine the results to obtain binding 
or hydration free energies.

* To run the protocol on a server with a grid engine: Enable Parallel Processing and Run on Grid , and specify Grid Options to request one GPU and the appropriate number of CPUs. The Number of Processors and Grid Options parameters should specify the same number of CPU cores. The Number of Processors and Grid Options values 
pertain to a single simulation, and the protocol 
automatically requests the specified resource for each 
independent simulation and lambda window separately.

* Enable Parallel Processing and Run on Grid , and specify Grid Options to request one GPU and the appropriate number of CPUs.

* The Number of Processors and Grid Options parameters should specify the same number of CPU cores.

* The Number of Processors and Grid Options values 
pertain to a single simulation, and the protocol 
automatically requests the specified resource for each 
independent simulation and lambda window separately.

* To run the protocol on a non-grid server, set GPU Device to a specific GPU index and the Number of Processors to the appropriate number of CPUs. 
If multiple GPUs are available, the GPU indices can be specified 
separated by comma (for example, 0,1). The protocol will run different 
systems and lambda windows on the specified GPUs.

* Prepare the input structure using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol. Prior to running FEP, this protocol automatically performs an energy minimization for 
100 steps to remove any bad contacts. All Simulation protocols require that the simulated system be typed using an appropriate forcefield. Since an FEP calculation involves an alchemical transformation between two molecules, the forcefield assignment requires special treatment. Therefore, it is important that you generate the input to this protocol using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol. Other tools for forcefield typing should not be used.

All Simulation protocols require that the simulated system be typed using an appropriate forcefield. Since an FEP calculation involves an alchemical transformation between two molecules, the forcefield assignment requires special treatment. Therefore, it is important that you generate the input to this protocol using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol. Other tools for forcefield typing should not be used.

* Load the structures into the Graphics View.

* Open the Simulation | Run Free Energy Simulations tools and click CHARMm Relative FEP Calculations... to open the dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the Input FEP Systems .

* By default, the simulation time per Lambda window is set to 500 ps, which is short. Depending on the available resources, you may want to increase this using the Simulation Time per Lambda Window (ps) parameter. The simulation uses 15 lambda windows by default, and therefore, the total simulation length would be 15 times 
the sum of this parameter value and Equilibration Time per Lambda Window (ps) parameter value.

* By default, the equilibration time per Lambda window is set to 200 ps. Depending on the production time per lambda window, you may want to change this. 
During equilibration, FEP data is not included for free energy evaluation.

* If you increase the simulation time, evaluate and reset
the Save Results Interval (ps) parameter accordingly so that no more than several hundred frames are saved. Saving a lot of frames requires heavy system resources at the end of the run, especially for large solvated molecular systems.

* Set the Number of Processors parameter to the number of CPU cores you want to use for each simulation. If running on a cluster or grid, the number of 
processors specified should be less or equal to the number of processors on a single node.

* Set the Lead Ligand Name parameter to 
the name of the reference ligand with a known binding free energy. Set 
the Lead Ligand Free Energy parameter to 
its experimentally known binding free energy. If zero, the 
calculated free energies of other ligands will be relative to that 
of the lead ligand.

* For details about the remaining parameters, see CHARMm Relative FEP Calculations (GPU) - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

Upon the completion of the run, the free energy data that is saved during the simulations is analyzed and the results are presented. The Results section tabulates the 
relative free energy change associated with each system that finished successfully. 
Each relative FEP entry specifies the name of the ligands involved in 
the perturbation (Lig1Name, Lig2Name). The aggregate free energy change during the entire transformation, which is a sum of the values over all the lambda windows simulated, is presented as Calc ΔG 
for the ligand and complex states. For each window spanning lambda i and i+1 , 
the change in free energy is computed using the thermodynamic 
perturbation formula. While the aggregate Calc ΔG and StDev values are 
reported in the table, the individual values for each lambda window are 
presented in the FEP report for each simulation.

If you specified the Lead Ligand Name parameter, the absolute free energies ΔG are computed for the entire set, which are tabulated as with the ΔΔG values.
When absolute free energies ΔG are computed, a graph showing the connectivity network of the ligands and their pairwise ΔΔG values is created and can be opened by ViewResults in the protocol Report .

#### Troubleshooting

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| Pairwise ddGs: | Contains ΔΔG values obtained from the FEP calculations. |
| Absolute dGs | Contains ΔG values of ligands |

#### Further information

Run Free Energy Simulations tool

# Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tssimulation

Source file: tssimulation/simulation_free_energy_perturbation_namd-para.htm

## Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) - Parameters

### Performs Free Energy Perturbation simulations using NAMD

Runs alchemical Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) dynamics simulations using NAMD, a parallel molecular dynamics code designed for high-performance simulation of large biomolecular systems.
Prior to using this protocol, the input structures containing dual topology ligands must be prepared using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol. This protocol can run multiple simulations either in serial or parallel mode. The protocol implements a full transformation of the input structure from lambda 0 to 1 using a user chosen number of lambda windows and sampling time. The FEP data collected during the equilibration stage at each window is NOT used for the free energy calculation. The protocol performs a short energy minimization prior to running the FEP calculation.

Each input structure prepared by the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol is expected to contain two groups, namely FEP_0 and FEP_1, which can be selected by the user to visually inspect the disappearing and appearing atoms from the initial and final ligands, respectively. During the FEP dynamics simulation, the vdW interactions of disappearing atoms are gradually turned off between lambda 0 and 1, and for appearing atoms turned on during the same period. However, the electrostatic interactions of the disappearing atoms are turned off from lambda 0 to 0.5, whereas those of appearing atoms turned on from 0.5 to 1, in order to prevent singularity problems.

Upon the completion of the simulation, the output file containing the FEP data (*.fepout) is post-processed for each completed simulation and a statistical analysis is performed. The free energy values for each input system and associated statistical error is presented.
The protocol provides an option for generating just the NAMD input files, which would allow the FEP calculation to be run separately from the command line.

Note:

* More information on NAMD can be found at http://www.ks.uiuc.edu/Research/namd

See Also:

* James C. Phillips, Rosemary Braun, Wei Wang, James Gumbart, Emad Tajkhorshid, Elizabeth Villa, Christophe Chipot, Robert D. Skeel, Laxmikant Kale, and Klaus Schulten,
Scalable molecular dynamics with NAMD. Journal of Computational Chemistry , 26:1781-1802, 2005 .

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input FEP Systems | Specify the molecular structures prepared using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol on which to perform the FEP calculations. In Pipeline Pilot, specify a file containing the prepared FEP systems, the supported file formats are DSV and MOL2. In Discovery Studio, choose from the list of all the visible typed structures. |
| FEP Simulation Schedule | Parameters pertaining to the FEP simulation |
| Number of Lambda Windows | Number of Lambda windows or intermediate states to be used in the FEP simulation. Only allowed values are those that result in a rational Lambda window width. |
| Direction | Direction of the FEP simulation. Forward specifies the FEP simulation to run from Lambda 0 to 1, whereas Reverse is from 1 to 0. Valid Values: Forward , Reverse |
| Simulation Time per Lambda Window (ps) | The time length (ps) to perform the dynamics simulation per lambda window. Since multiple lambda windows are simulated, the total simulation time from lambda 0 to 1 is the number of lambda windows times this parameter. |
| Equilibration Time per Lambda Window (ps) | Time length (ps) out of the simulation time per lambda window to be considered as equilibration. The time length over which the FEP data is considered for the free energy evaluation per lambda window is the (Simulation Time - the Equilibration Time). |
| FEP Data Output Frequency (ps) | Frequency (ps) of output for FEP data, which contain the energy values at initial and final lambda in each window. The FEP Output file is used upon the completion of the simulation to post-process and calculate the free energy change. |
| Minimization Steps | Number of steps of minimization prior to initiating the FEP calculation. |
| Production | Production parameters. FEP production is performed in the NPT ensemble, with the Langevin dynamics method used for temperature control and Langevin piston method to maintain pressure at 1 atm. The switching method is used for nonbonded interactions. |
| Production Time Step (fs) | Time step (fs) to use in the dynamics simulation. |

| Production Target Temperature | Target temperature (K) for the dynamics simulation. |
| Random Number Seed | Number used to seed the random number generator if temperature control or langevin dynamics is selected. This can be used so that consecutive simulations produce the same results. If no value is specified, NAMD will choose a pseudo-random value based on the computer clock time. The random number seed will be output during the simulation startup so that its value is known and can be reused for subsequent simulations. Note that if Langevin dynamics are used in a parallel simulation (i.e., a simulation using more than one processor) even using the same seed will not guarantee reproducible results. |
| Nonbonded Cutoffs | |
| Switching Distance | Distance at which to activate switching/splitting function for electrostatic and van der Waals calculations (Å). The value must be less than or equal to the value of Cutoff , since the switching function is only applied on the range from Switch Distance to Cutoff . |

This parameter is used when switching is set to on to specify the allowable distance between atoms for inclusion in the pair list. This parameter is equivalent to the X-PLOR parameter CUTNb. If this parameter is not specified and switching is set to True , the value of Cutoff is used. A value of at least one greater than Cutoff is recommended. |

By default, Pipeline Pilot servers are configured to allow a maximum of four processes per protocol. You can adjust this on the Pipeline Pilot Server Administration Portal. | Parallel Processing Server Run On Grid Grid Options | Grid engine specific command line parameters for the job submission. Leave blank to use defaults. Notes : Ensure that the Number of Cores per Simulation is specified to be the same as Number of Cores here. The former parameter controls the number of threads for NAMD and the latter parameter controls reserving the cores with the queuing system. In Pipeline Pilot, this is an array of command line options to send to the Grid engine submit command. In Discovery Studio, the options are comma separated. There are a number of parameters are translated to the correct command line options for whichever supported Grid Engine you are using. Example - Supported parameters Account=<Project/Account name> Maximum Execution Time=<DD:MM:SS> - LSF ignores seconds Number of Cores=<16> Parallel Environment=<The Parallel Environment to use> - Only needed for SGE Other=<Additional Parameters sent directly to submit command line> If you just include one line, whatever you enter will be sent "as is" to the submission command. Example - sending options directly to command line - LSF -n 16 -W 48:00 -R "span[hosts=1]" |

# Free Energy Perturbation (FEP)

Source type: HTML

Source section: tssimulation

Source file: tssimulation/simulation_free_energy_perturbation_namd.htm

## Free Energy Perturbation (FEP)

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

The Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) protocol allows you to perform alchemical transformations during molecular dynamics simulations in the NPT thermodynamic ensemble. The protocol uses the NAMD parallel molecular dynamics program designed for high-performance simulation of large biomolecular systems [Phillips et al., 2005] .
For more information see http://www.ks.uiuc.edu/Research/namd/ .

The free energy pertubation (FEP) simulation is designed to calculate the change in free energy during an alchemical transformation, e.g. one ligand is alchemically transformed into another. If two such FEP calculations are performed, one in the protein binding pocket, and another one in solvent, the difference between the two alchemical free energies results in the relative binding free energy between the two ligands. The figure below shows this concept by depicting two ligands namely Ligand 1 and Ligand 2 in the complexed and free solvated states. The relative binding affinity ΔΔG(1->2) of the two ligands equals to ΔG2 - ΔG1, where ΔG1 and ΔG2 correspond to the physical process of transferring the ligands from their solvated environments to the protein. These two values are expensive to compute. Instead, in relative FEP calculations, one computes the alchemical quantities ΔG3 and ΔG4, which are the free energies of chemically modifying Ligand 1 to 2 in the solvent and protein environment, respectively. From the diagram, the relative binding free energy ΔΔG(1->2) = ΔG2 - ΔG1 = ΔG4 - ΔG3.

Relative binding free energy between ligand pairs computed this way can be useful in lead optimization projects where it can inform the chemist on what compound to make next in order to improve its binding affinity.

The Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) protocol allows you to run the relative FEP calculation on a series of input systems comprising either the free ligand in solution or the protein-ligand complex in solution. The inputs include a set of molecular systems prepared using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol. This protocol represents the fifth in the series of steps comprising the FEP workflow:

* Generate Analog Conformations

* Type Ligands with MATCH (Prototype) , or alternatively, use Change Forcefield tools to type ligands with CHARMm forcefield.

* Generate Ligand Pairs for FEP

* Set Up Relative FEP Calculations

* Collate FEP Simulation Results

The protocol implements a full transformation of the input structure from the initial to the final state using a series of intermediate steps defined by the lambda variable which changes from 0 to 1 as the simulation progresses from the initial to the final state. In effect, as lambda progresses from 0 to 1, the interactions involving the initial state or groups unique to Ligand 1 are "turned off", and the same for Ligand 2 are "turned on" by tuning the non-bonded interactions off and on, respectively. By default, 16 lambda windows or intermediates are simulated. The total simulation time is thus 16 times the Simulation Time per Lambda Window (ps) . At the beginning of each window an equilibration of the structure is performed prior to FEP data collection. The FEP data collected during the equilibration stage at each window is not used for the free energy calculation. You can change the number of lambda windows to values that exactly divide unity.

The input molecules prepared by the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol are expected to contain FEP_0 and FEP_1 groups, which you can use to visually inspect the disappearing and appearing atoms from the initial and final ligands, respectively. During the FEP dynamics simulation, the vdW interactions of disappearing atoms are gradually turned off between lambda 0 and 1, and for appearing atoms turned on during the same period. However, the electrostatic interactions of the disappearing atoms are turned off from lambda 0 to 0.5, whereas that of appearing atoms turned on from 0.5 to 1, in order to prevent singularity problems.

Upon the completion of the protocol, the output .fepout files from each successfully completed simulation are post-processed and a statistical analysis is performed. The total free energy change for each system is reported along with the associated statistical error. A detailed free energy report accessible via a link in the main report containing values for each lambda window and associated statistical error are also presented.

* Prepare the input structure using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol. Prior to running FEP, this protocol automatically performs an energy minimization for 500 steps to remove any bad contacts.

* Load the structures into the Graphics View.

* Open the Simulation | Run Free Energy Simulations tools and click Free Energy Perturbation (FEP)... to open the dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the Input FEP Systems .

* By default, the simulation time per Lambda window is set to 500 ps, which is short. Depending on the scale of resources available, you may want to increase this using the Simulation Time per Lambda Window (ps) parameter. The simulation uses 16 lambda windows by default, and therefore, the total simulation length would be 16 times this parameter value.

* By default, the equilibration time per Lambda window is set to 250 ps. Depending on the production time per lambda window, you may want to change this. The equilibration time is a subset of the production time. During equilibration, FEP data is not saved to the output file to be considered for free energy evaluation.

* If you increase the simulation time, be sure to evaluate and reset
the Save Results Interval (ps) parameter accordingly so that no more than several hundred frames are saved. Saving a lot of frames requires heavy system resources at the end of the run, especially for large solvated molecular systems.

* Set the Number of Cores per Simulation parameter to the number of CPU cores you wish to use for each NAMD simulation. If running on a cluster or grid, the number of cores specified should be less or equal to the number of processors on a single node.

* If you want to run the multiple FEP systems sequentially, use the default option for Parallel Processing set to False. If you have large enough multi-core server or a cluster, you could also run the multiple FEP systems in parallel for higher throughput. If run in parallel, you can also choose to run the calculation on a grid installation by setting the Run on Grid parameter to True.

* For details about the remaining parameters, see Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

All Simulation protocols require that the simulated system be typed using an appropriate forcefield. Since an FEP calculation involves an alchemical transformation between two molecules, the forcefield assignment requires special treatment. Therefore, it is important that you generate the input to this protocol using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations protocol. Other tools for forcefield typing should not be used.

Upon the completion of the run, the free energy data that is saved during the simulations is analyzed and the results are presented. The Results section tabulates the free energy change associated with each system that successfully finished. The aggregate free energy change during the entire transformation, which is a sum of the values over all the lambda windows simulated, is presented as Calc ΔG. For each window spanning lambda i and i+1 , the change in free energy is computed using the thermodynamic perturbation formula as follows:

Where Beta is the reciprocal of the product of the Boltzmann constant and the absolute temperature T (K). The ΔE value distribution is also used to compute the variance associated with the transformation in each window as follows and an aggregate value over the entire simulation is reported in the table as StDev. Please see [Liu at al., 2012] for more details.

While the aggregate Calc ΔG and StDev values are reported in the table, the individual values for each lambda window are presented in the FEP Report for each simulation. Each row in the table also indicates the type of simulation, which could be either Ligand or Complex, indicating the free ligand and the complex states, respectively. For instructive purposes, if the dual topology ligands in vacuum are run, the simulation type would be Vacuum.

Additionally, you can perform structural analysis of an FEP simulation in the same way as a regular MD simulation. The simulation trajectories are accessible from the results table as a link to the full FEP dynamics trajectory and a trajectory without solvent. For a description of the different ways of analyzing an MD simulation, see Dynamics (NAMD) .

The next step of the FEP workflow involves collating the results from the FEP simulations of free ligand and complex states for multiple ligand pairs using the Collate FEP Simulation Results protocol. This protocol will take the output of the Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) protocol as input to collate and analyze results. Use the Jobs Explorer to locate the Output folder which will serve as one of the inputs for the Collate FEP Simulation Results protocol.

#### Troubleshooting

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| OutputSystems.mol2 | The output molecular systems without conformations. In this file, the molecules have the final coordinate of the dynamics simulation. |
| <moleculename>/<moleculename>_trajectory.dsv | The output molecular systems. This output file for each system is separately located in sub-directories named by the input molecule names. In this file, trajectory frames are stored as a collection of conformations in sequential order. You can sample and analyze the trajectory using the Analyze Trajectory tool panel , or the Analyze Trajectory protocol. |
| <moleculename>/<moleculename>_trajectory_nosolvent.dsv | The output molecular systems. This output file for each system is separately located in sub-directories named by the input molecule names. In this file, trajectory frames are stored as a collection of conformations in sequential order, without the solvent. You can sample and analyze the trajectory using the Analyze Trajectory tool panel , or the Analyze Trajectory protocol. |
| <moleculename>/<moleculename>_output.dcd | The trajectory file generated by NAMD. It saves the coordinates of each step for this dynamics simulation. You can import the trajectory frames to the molecule using Structure \| Animation \| Load... , or by sampling it with the Analyze Trajectory protocol . |
| <moleculename>/namd.log | Contains detailed log messages generated by the NAMD simulation engine. |
| <moleculename>/fepdata.fepout | Contains data relevant for FEP postprocessing calculation. |

#### Further information

Dynamics (NAMD) Run Free Energy Simulations tool Analyze Trajectory tool panel Analyze Trajectory Structure | Animation Run a parallel calculation

# Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE) - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tssimulation

Source file: tssimulation/simulation_free_energy_perturbation_openfe-para.htm

## Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE) - Parameters

### Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE)

Runs alchemical free energy calculations using the OpenFE framework and the OpenMM simulation engine. Prior to using this protocol, the input ligand perturbation network must be prepared using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE) protocol, and the input receptor must be cleaned up using a protocol such as Prepare Proteins . In this protocol, the input system is solvated with TIP3P waters and 0.15 M NaCl around the solute. Additionally, the input protein is parametrized with the Amber ff14SB force field while the ligands are parametrized with OpenFF Sage 2.1.1.

The equilibration and production simulations are carried out for the alchemical system using Hamiltonian Replica Exchange (HREX) as the multistate lambda sampling method. At the end of the calculations, the results are collected and analyzed to generate free energy tables and figures.

Notes:

* It is recommended to prepare the input protein using the Prepare Proteins protocol first.

* Membrane proteins and cofactors (e.g., ADP) are not supported.

* If a specific ligand transformation involves charge changes, then the parameters Charge Change Equilibration Time, Charge Change Production Time, and Charge Change Lambda Windows are used.

* This protocol can also generate estimated absolute free energies using Maximum Likelihood Estimation when the Number of Simulations is greater than 1 and when the input ligand perturbation network has at least 3 edges and no isolated subgraphs.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Molecule | Specifies a prepared protein. Crystallographic waters and ions may be included. Notes: It is recommended to prepare the input protein using the Prepare Proteins protocol first. Membrane proteins and cofactors (e.g. ADP) are not supported. |
| Ligand Perturbation Network | Specifies a ligand perturbation network GraphML file as generated in the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE) protocol. This file should describe a directed graph connecting ligands according to their atom mapping. |
| Number of Simulations | Number of independent simulations to run per system. |
| Simulation Settings | Simulation Parameters |
| Equilibration Time (ns) | The time length (ns) to equilibrate the system prior to running dynamics. Notes: This parameter is only used when a particular ligand transformation does not involve charge changes. |
| Production Time (ns) | The time length (ns) to perform the dynamics simulation. Notes: This parameter is only used when a particular ligand transformation does not involve charge changes. |
| Lambda Windows | Specifies the number of lambda windows or intermediate states to be used in the FEP simulation. Notes: This parameter also specifies the number of replicas to be used in the FEP simulation. This parameter is only used when a particular ligand transformation does not involve charge changes. |
| Charge Change Equilibration Time (ns) | The time length (ns) to equilibrate the system prior to running dynamics. Notes: This parameter is only used when a particular ligand transformation involves charge changes. |
| Charge Change Production Time (ns) | The time length (ns) to perform the dynamics simulation. Notes: This parameter is only used when a particular ligand transformation involves charge changes. |
| Charge Change Lambda Windows | Specifies the number of lambda windows or intermediate states to be used in the FEP simulation. Notes: This parameter also specifies the number of replicas to be used in the FEP simulation. This parameter is only used when a particular ligand transformation involves charge changes. |
| Hydrogen Mass Repartitioning | Specifies whether to use Hydrogen Mass Repartitioning which can allow for a larger time step to be used. Valid Values: True , False |

| Temperature | Target temperature (in K) for the dynamics simulation. |
| Number of Retries | Number of times to attempt a ligand transformation calculation in the event of a failure. Notes: Generally when failures do occur, they take place within the first 10 minutes of a calculation so it is recommended to leave this at the default of value of 2 as a follow-up attempt is likely to resolve the issue. |

# Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE)

Source type: HTML

Source section: tssimulation

Source file: tssimulation/simulation_free_energy_perturbation_openfe.htm

## Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE)

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Output

* Analyzing results

The Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE) protocol allows you to perform alchemical free energy calculations using the OpenFE framework and the OpenMM simulation engine [Eastman et al., 2024] . In a thermodynamic cycle (see CHARMm Relative FEP 
Calculations (GPU) ), one ligand is converted into the other ligand by alchemically transforming the atoms that vary between the two ligands. The transformation is carried out in the solvent (ΔGsolv) and in the binding site (ΔGsite) for Relative Binding Free Energy (RBFE) calculations. Relative binding free energy between ligand pairs computed this way can be useful in lead optimization projects where it can inform the chemist on which compound to make next to improve its binding affinity.

The protocol implements a full transformation of the input structure from the initial to the final state using a series of intermediate steps defined by discrete lambda windows, where lambda changes from 0 to 1 as the simulation progresses. Only parameters that differ between the initial state (lambda=0) and final state (lambda=1) are interpolated. The transformation follows a specific sequence: The electrostatic interactions of the initial state are turned off while simultaneously turning on the steric interactions of the final state. Then the steric interactions of the initial state are turned off while simultaneously turning on the electrostatic interactions of the final state. Bonded interactions are interpolated linearly throughout the entire lambda range. A soft-core potential [Gapsys et al., 2012] is applied to the Lennard-Jones interactions to prevent instabilities during intermediate lambda windows.

As part of the simulation steps, the input system is solvated with TIP3P waters and 0.15 M NaCl around the solute. In addition, the input protein is parametrized with the Amber ff14SB force field [Maier et al., 2015] , while the ligands are parametrized with OpenFF Sage 2.1.1 [Boothroyd et al., 2023] , and then all are minimized. Equilibration and production simulations are carried out using Hamiltonian Replica Exchange (HREX) as the multistate lambda sampling method under NPT conditions using the LangevinMiddleIntegrator [Zhang et al., 2019] and a MonteCarloBarostat. At the end of the calculations, the results are collected and analyzed to generate free energy tables and figures.

* Prepare the input receptor using the Prepare Proteins protocol to ensure it is cleaned. Crystallographic waters can be retained.

* Load the structure into the Graphics View.

* Prepare the input ligand perturbation network GraphML file using the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE) protocol.

* Open the Simulation | Run Free Energy Simulations tools and click Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE)... to open the dialog.

* Set the input receptor as Input Molecule and specify the input ligand perturbation network GraphML file as Ligand Perturbation Network .

* Choose an appropriate value for Number of Simulations . By default it is 1, but for better statistical redundancy you might want to choose 3 at the cost of a longer run time. Also, estimated absolute free energies are only provided when Number of Simulations is 2 or greater.

* The default values for the parameters under Simulation Settings are at recommended values. Changing these values can affect the run time and accuracy, but it could be appropriate to do so depending on your system. The Charge Change parameters are specifically applied when an alchemical transformation involves a charge change.

* For details about the remaining parameters, see Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE) - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to the background. Sending a job to the background closes the status dialog and allows you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer .

It is important to check that your input ligands are appropriately aligned and positioned correctly in the frame of the protein as recommended in the Set Up Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE) protocol. Also verify that the proposed transformations are appropriate.
For more information, see Set Up Relative FEP Calculations (OpenFE) .

You can inspect the individual output files that were generated in the Output directory of the run. The contents of this directory can be viewed by selecting the job in the Jobs Explorer, right-clicking and choosing Locate. The file names may differ from those listed here.

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| Detailed_FEP_Report.htm | Report that displays a table of the raw results of each leg of the free energy calculations, their runtime, and links to corresponding MBAR Convergence Matrix plots. |
| raw_free_energies.csv | Table of the raw results of each leg of the free energy calculations and corresponding details. |
| est_abs_free_energies_dg.csv | Optional table of estimated absolute free energies using Maximum Likelihood Estimation. It is only generated when Number of Simulations is 2 or greater and when the input ligand perturbation network has at least 3 edges and no isolated subgraphs. |
| fep_sim_results_ddg.csv | Table of calculated FEP simulation results showing the ΔΔG values of each ligand transformation and the corresponding uncertainties. |
| MBAR_convergence_matrices | Directory containing MBAR convergence matrix figures for each leg of the free energy calculations. Each matrix element represents the probability of a sample from one lambda state being observable in another state. This diagnostic assesses phase space overlap between lambda states, which is critical for MBAR accuracy. The plot should show a tridiagonal structure with sufficient diagonal width, ensuring all states connect through neighbors. First off-diagonal elements should be at least 0.03 for reliable estimates—lower values indicate poor overlap and suggest additional intermediate lambda values are required. [Mey et al., 2020] |

#### Further information

Run Free Energy Simulations tool Calculating relative binding free energies with OpenFE alchemical free energy perturbation
