# View a Recursive Partitioning Tree in a Dendrogram Window

Source type: HTML

Source section: tssmallmolecules

Source file: tssmallmolecules/tsk_view-recursive-partitioning-tree.htm

## View a Recursive Partitioning Tree in a Dendrogram Window

The Create Recursive Partitioning Model protocol generates one or more 
result scripts ( .ds_pl ) that open an .sd file in a Molecule Window and a creates a recursive 
partitioning tree plot in a Dendrogram Window. The two windows are linked interactively. If you select a branch or leaf in the 
dendrogram window, all the molecules belonging to the branch or leaf in the data window are also selected and vice versa. 
The ruler shows the tree depth of each node. The splitting criteria are shown as branch labels.

The leaf label shown on the right hand side of each leaf is the node ID of the leaf, 
not the number of compounds belong to the node or leaf. To get the number of compounds in the node, you can make a selection in the 
dendrogram and list selected objects only in the corresponding molecule window using the context menu (right mouse click).
By looking at the row index of the last compound, you can get the number of compounds easily.

If multiple dependent properties are specified in the model, there will be multiple scripts for the same tree. Each
corresponds to a single dependent property. Due to dendrogram limitations, it is not possible to show a multiple-Y tree in a single 
dendrogram. However, you can run each script for the same tree and arrange the dendrograms in a layout as shown below. 
The generic portion of the tree has the same splitting criteria, while the Y-specific portion uses different splitting criteria:

# Fit Loop dialog

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/dl_loop-fit.htm

## Fit Loop dialog

The Fit Loop dialog displays a table consisting of the original and best conformers (as many as 10) found
while the loop fitting algorithm is running. The command is initiated by selecting a series of continuous residues and
selecting the Fit Loop command on the Build and Refine X-ray Structure tools panel.

The table is dynamically updated while the command runs, and it contains two columns:

Conformers: The first entry is the original conformer. The remaining entries are the best conformers found by
the Fit Loop command as it runs.

Score: The score is a measure of the electron density overlap. The higher the score, the better the fit.

Additional controls are available to stop or cancel the search:

Stop: Click this button to pause the
fitting algorithm while it is running. This action renames the button
to Continue . Pressing Continue resumes
the fitting algorithm.

When fitting is stopped or completed, selecting one or more conformers in the table causes
the unselected conformers to be hidden in the Molecule Window.

[progress bar] At the bottom of the dialog, you can view the progress bar, which indicates how many Monte
Carlo trials have been completed by percentage. Set the number of Monte Carlo trials to perform on the Build and Refine X-ray Structure subpage of the Preferences dialog.

OK: This button is only enabled when fitting is stopped or completed and a single conformer is selected.
Clicking this button applies the selected geometry to the Molecule Window.

### Access methods

| Tools Explorer | Build and Refine X-ray Structure tools \| Fit Loop |
| --- | --- |

# Crystal Parameters page - Reflection Data Window

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/dl_reflection-data-viewer_crystal-parameters.htm

## Crystal Parameters page - Reflection Data Window

The Crystal Parameters dialog allows you to 
specify values for the unit cell parameters of a crystal cell.

Unit cell parameters determine the length and orientation of unit cell 
vectors in space. Any translation of an atom by an integer multiple of a 
unit cell vector results in that atom reaching the position of another 
identical atom in the crystal.

### Space Group

[Crystal Class]: Allows you to select one of the seven crystal classes.

[Space Group Name]: Allows you to select one of the space groups (as defined in the International Tables of 
Crystallography, Volume A ) within the specified crystal class.

[Origin Choice]: Fixes the reference frame within the unit cell. Specific to the space group.

Equivalent Positions: Specifies the location 
of symmetry mates relative to the asymmetric unit.

Additional Information: Lists the IUCr and Shoenflies naming conventions, as well as the 
number of symmetry operators.

### Cell Lengths

A , B , and C: Specify the lengths (in Ångstroms) of the unit 
cell vectors.

### Cell Angles

Alpha , Beta , 
and Gamma: Specify the angles (in 
Degrees) between the unit cell vectors.

### Access methods

| Menu | File \| Open... a reflection file and click the Crystal Parameters tab |
| --- | --- |
| Files Explorer | Double-click a reflection file and click the Crystal Parameters tab |

#### Further information

Working with X-ray data Reflection Data Window Contents page - Reflection Data Window View page - Reflection Data Window

# Binding Site Search dialog

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/dl_search-binding-site.htm

## Binding Site Search dialog

This dialog allows you to specify the parameters of a binding site search.

### Select ligand molecule

Specify the ligand molecule. 
The ligand molecule list box consists of molecules from any open Graphics View having no more than 250 atoms, 20 
residues, and 1 chain. 
If only one ligand is available, it is automatically selected.

### Other command

Sigma threshold: This allows you to specify the map level (in sigma) at which the search for possible ligand sites is made. Higher 
thresholds result in more sites being found
and also increase the extent of the volume of each site that does not overlap the protein. 
Lower thresholds often result in the overlap of sites, giving fewer, larger sites.

### Select electron density map

Specify the electron density map from the current Graphics View. If only one electron density map is loaded, 
it is selected by default.

### Search volume

Receptor volume: The volume around the receptor that is searched for sites. 
The receptor volume is the default.

User-defined volume: Select this if you wish to specify a search volume.

Radius (Å) :
The user-defined search volume is a sphere of the given radius centered at the origin of either the selected atom(s) 
or receptor molecule.

Set origin at selection :
This option fixes the search sphere origin at the geometrical center of the selected atoms. If unchecked, 
the origin is the geometric center of the receptor.

### Resulting receptor molecules

Displays a list of molecules that are considered part of the receptor. The receptor consists of all molecules 
in the current Graphics View except the ligand molecule.

All molecules except the selected ligand must be parented under a single Cell.

### Access methods

| Tools explorer | Place and Refine X-ray Ligand \| Binding Site \| Search... |

# Navigate and Label 3D Structure tools

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/prot_3d-tools.htm

## Navigate and Label 3D Structure tools

### 3D Pointer

The 3D Pointer allows you to mark, label, and add objects to a given point in 3D
coordinate space. The pointer is particularly useful if you wish 
to rotate a structure around a particular point in space. Additionally, the 
3D Pointer can be used to step forward and back through the residues 
within a protein or nucleic acid structure.

If you set the background color 
of the Graphics View to white, the 3D Pointer object is not visible.

Display Pointer: Creates a 3D pointer at the center 
of mass of the structure(s) in the current Graphics View.

Place Pointer at Selection: Places a new or existing 
pointer at the selected atom or at the center of mass of a group of selected 
atoms.

If atom(s) are not selected in the current Graphics View, this command 
is grayed out.

Go To Pointer: Centers the 3D Pointer in
the current Graphics View. If an electron Density Map is available,
the visible block of the map is redrawn to center on the pointer.

If no pointer has been created in the current Graphics View, this command 
is grayed out.

Remove Pointer: Deletes the pointer in the current 
Graphics View. Note that this does not hide the pointer, it deletes it. 
If you wish to restore the pointer to the same location, you must make a selection 
of atom(s) at or around the desired location or step through the sequence until 
the pointer has returned to the desired location.

Next Residue: Moves the 3D Pointer to the next 
residue.

If no pointer has been placed at a selected residue in the current Graphics 
View, this command is grayed out.

Previous Residue: Moves the 3D Pointer to the 
previous residue.

### 3D Labels

The tools in this tool group allow you to place a label at the current position 
of the 3D Pointer. The label remains at that position even if the pointer is 
moved or removed.

If no pointer has been created in the current Graphics View, these commands are grayed out.

These tools allow you to display, hide or remove all 3D labels at once. You can also edit labels individually from the Hierarchy View or from the context menu.

Add Label...: Launches the Add
Text at 3D Pointer dialog , allowing you to specify the text
and font style for a label at the current position of the 3D Pointer.

Display All Labels: Displays all labels created 
with the Add Label... command. Note that other kinds 
of labels are unaffected.

If no label has been created in the current Graphics View, this command is grayed out.

Edit Label...: Launches the Edit 
Text dialog allowing you to edit a label you select from a list.

Remove All Labels: Removes all labels created 
with the Add Label... command. Note that other kinds 
of labels are unaffected.

Hide All Labels: Hides all labels but does not delete them.
Note that other kinds of labels are unaffected.

Go To Label: Moves the 3D pointer to
the selected label and centers the 3D pointer in the current Graphics
View. If there is only one label in the current Graphics View,
that pointer is centered. If an electron Density Map is available,
the map is redrawn.

Next Label: Moves the 3D Pointer to the next label.

If only one label has been created in the current Graphics View, this command is grayed out.

Previous Label: Moves the 3D Pointer to the previous 
label.

| Tool bar | X-ray \| Navigate and Label 3D Structure |

| Menu | Tools \| X-ray \| Navigate and Label 3D Structure |
| Menu | View \| Tool Panels \| Navigate and Label 3D Structure |

# How to use the Navigate and Label 3D Structure tools

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/prot_3d-tools_hw.htm

## How to use the Navigate and Label 3D Structure tools

This section describes the use of the tools available in the Navigate and Label 3D Structure Tool Panel. The following tasks are covered:

* Place a 3D pointer

* Navigate the structure using the 3D Pointer

* Add a 3D label

* Edit a 3D label

### 3D Pointer

To place a 3D pointer

* Ensure that there is a current Graphics View with a structure containing at least one amino acid.

* To place the 3D Pointer at the structure's center of mass, click Display 
Pointer .

* To place the 3D Pointer at the center of mass of the selected atom(s),
click Place Pointer at Selection .

To verify that
a Graphics View is current, click its tab or caption bar.

To navigate the structure using the 3D Pointer

* Ensure there is a current Graphics View with a structure containing
at least one amino acid, and that you have a 3D Pointer visible in
the Graphics View.

* Click Next Residue and Previous
Residue to move forward and back along the amino acid sequence.

* You may need to click Go To Pointer to center
the Graphics View on the current 3D Pointer, especially if the
3D Pointer is off the screen.

### 3D Labels

To add a 3D label

* Ensure there is a current Graphics View with a structure containing at least one amino acid.

* Ensure you have a 3D Pointer visible in the current Graphics
View, and position the 3D Pointer at a selection
or residue where you want the label to appear.

* Click Add Label... to open the Add
Text at 3D Pointer dialog .

* Enter the label text in the Label Text text box.

* Specify a Font and Color for your label text if you wish.

* Click OK .

* To add another label, use the Next
Residue and Previous Residue buttons
in the 3D Pointer tool group to navigate to the desired residue,
or create another pointer at a selection by using the Place
Pointer at Selection button.

To assure that a
Graphics View is "current", click its tab or caption bar.

To edit a 3D label

* Use the Go to Label , Next
Label , or Previous Label buttons
to navigate to the label you wish to edit.

* When the appropriate label is selected, click Edit
Label...

* Edit the label text in the Label Text text box.

* Edit the Font and Color options
for your label text if you wish.

Navigate and Label 3D Structure tools

# Validate Protein Structure tools

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/prot_pht.htm

## Validate Protein Structure tools

The Validate Protein Structure tool panel allows you to check for abnormalities in protein structure. These may be due to errors in the structure determination, but can also indicate areas of structural interest (e.g., unusual conformations around an active site). For details of the types of violations examined see Protein Structure Abnormalities .

For details about performing specific tasks using these tools, see How to use the Validate Protein Structure tools .

### Perform Validation

Check Structure: Performs the structural checks
specified in the Violation Types preferences . Optionally, a text report lists the violations found. Violation monitors are created for the various types of problems encountered, which can be examined using the View Violations tool group. 
They also appear in the Data Table and can be examined and manipulated like other monitor objects.

### View Violations

Choose Type: Choose from a list of violations that were found. Violations that were not found are grayed out. The possible types of violation are:

* Main-Chain Conformation

* Side-Chain Conformation

* Bond Lengths

* Bond Angles

* Nonplanar Peptide Bond

* Cis Peptides

* CA to CA Distances

* Missing Main-Chain Atoms

* Missing Side-Chain Atoms

* Nonstandard Names

* Chirality

* Alternate Conformations

Color Atoms: Colors the atoms in violation according to the preference for the chosen type.

Select: Selects the atoms or residues in violation.

Show All: Shows all violation monitors for the chosen type.

Hide All: Hides all violation monitors for the chosen type.

Next: Selects and displays the next monitor of the chosen type, starting with the first violation found. By default, the view is adjusted to focus on this monitor.

Previous: Selects and displays the previous monitor of the chosen type. By default, the view is adjusted to focus on this monitor.

Reset Display: Resets the atom colors and deletes any violation monitors and groups. This provides a convenient way to restore the state of the model after performing checks and examining violations.

Show Report: Displays a text report for the last structure check performed.

# How to use the Validate Protein Structure tools

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/prot_pht_hw.htm

## How to use the Validate Protein Structure tools

The Validate Protein Structure tool panel allows you to identify abnormalities in a protein structure. The tools require one or more protein structures to be visible in a current Graphics View. The following tasks are covered:

* Perform checking

* Examine violations

To access these tools, open X-ray | Validate Protein Structure .

To perform checking

* Set the preferences for controlling checking on the Validate Protein Structure page and 
the Violation Types subpage of the Preferences dialog.

* Click Check Structure . A health report opens if the preference 
to display it has been checked. If the preference to make the structure gray is checked, the 3D structure will be recolored.

To examine violations

* Review the violation report. If you have not set the preference to automatically display the report, click Show Report . Choose File | Save As from the menu bar if you want to save it.

* To graphically examine the violations, select a violation type from the Choose Type list. Only types with violations are enabled. You must choose a violation type to enable the remaining tools.

* To visualize the areas of the structure with the selected violation type, click Color Atoms . This tool colors all atoms with the selected violation according to set preferences.

* To display all violation monitors of the chosen type, click Show All .

* To hide all violation monitors of the chosen type, click Hide All .

* To navigate through the violations one at a time, use the Next and Previous buttons.

* Repeat these steps as desired to examine other violation types.

You can also examine the violations in the Data Table (a new tab is created 
for each populated class). The violation monitors can be treated in the same way as any other monitor object; use the standard Visualizer methods to control their selection, display, and deletion.

To restore the display after use

After examining the violations, click Reset Display to reset the atom colors and delete violation monitors and groups.

# Edit X-ray Structure tools, Add Object

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

## Edit X-ray Structure tools, Add Object

The tools in this tool group allow you to place atom(s), water(s), or residue(s) 
at the 3D pointer, to create alternate conformations of residues, and to add 
amino acids to the terminal end of your protein.

Atom at 3D Pointer: [element] . Adds an element at the 3D Pointer position 
and, if a default density map is present, performs a real space refinement on the atom. Eight common elements, C , N , O , H , S , P , F , Cl ,
can be selected directly from the menu and added to the pointer position. Other elements can be specified in the Change Element dialog by first clicking Table... .

If no pointer has been created in the current Graphics View, this command is grayed out.

Water at 3D Pointer : Places a water molecule at the 3D Pointer position
and, if a default density map is present, performs a real space refinement on the atom. With default parameters, 
the newly added water is appended to the existing water list, if any, of the 
first molecule in the Hierarchy View. If there is no existing water in the first 
molecule, this command starts a new chain.

Note that the behavior of this command can be altered using the options under Add Water at 3D Pointer in the X-ray 
page - Preferences dialog .

If no pointer exists in the current Graphics View, this command is grayed out.

Residue at 3D Pointer... : Launches the Add Residue at 3D Pointer dialog allowing you to add a 
protein residue at the 3D Pointer position.

Alternate Conformation : Adds an additional conformation 
to a residue. The new conformation is a duplicate of the original with 
a small variation in space. All atoms in alternative conformations share equal 
occupancy. Each conformation has a designated identification and can be edited 
independently.

If a side-chain atom or one complete residue is not selected in the current 
Graphics View, this command is grayed out.

If an atom is selected, the duplicate is the portion following the selected 
atom, unless the selected atom is a non-branching point, in which case the complete 
side-chain is duplicated.

If a complete residue is selected, the additional conformation is the duplicate of the complete residue
with a small translation in space.

Amino Acid at Terminus: [amino acid] . Adds the specified amino acid at the selected 
terminus in the current Graphics View. Twenty-five amino acids are available to choose from.

If no residue is selected in the current Graphics View, this command 
is grayed out. If the selected residue is not a terminal residue, this command does not execute successfully.

The tools in this tool group allow you to fix or unfix atom(s) during Build and Refine X-ray Structure regularization

Fix Selected Atoms : Defines a fixed constraint for the coordinates of 
the currently selected atoms in the current Graphics View. Fixed atoms remain 
immobile in subsequent Build and Refine X-ray Structure regularization commands. The fixed constraint is removed when one of the Unfix commands is executed for the affected atoms.

If no atom(s) are selected in the current Graphics View, this command is 
grayed out.

Unfix Selected Atoms : Removes the fixed constraints 
of the currently selected atom(s) in the current Graphics View.

If no atom(s) are fixed in the current Graphics View, this command is grayed 
out.

Unfix All : Removes the fixed constraints of all 
atoms in the current Graphics View.

The Unfix commands work only on atoms that have been fixed using the Fix 
Selected Atoms command.

do not change during subsequent Build and Refine X-ray Structure regularization commands.

change during any regularization commands subsequently executed 
from the Build and Refine X-ray Structure tools , including Regularize 
Selected Zone , Move Atom and Regularize Zone , 
and Refine Selected Zone .

To unfix atom(s)

selected.

* Click Unfix Selected Atoms . OR Make sure there is a current Graphics View that contains fixed atoms.

* Click Unfix All .

# General X-ray tasks

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/tsk_xray-general.htm

## General X-ray tasks

The tasks below are basic tasks for working with X-ray data.
For a comprehensive list of X-ray tasks that include basic tasks and tasks that involve working with the X-ray tool set, see Tasks - X-ray .

* Display and hide density maps

* Export density maps to external files

* Import density maps from external files

To display and hide Density Maps

The visibility of Density Map contours can be changed using the Visibility commands
on the View menu .

To hide a contour of the density map, select a contour in any of the Molecule Window views and execute the Visibility | Hide command.

To show a contour of the hidden density map, select the map from either the Hierarchy or Data Table views of the Molecule Window and execute the Visibility | Show command. You can also set the Visible column on the Data Table View to Yes to show the map or
leave it unchecked to not show the map.

To change the visible extents of a density map's contours, use the commands in either the Structure | Isosurface menu or the Navigate and Label 3D Structure tools . The Fit To Screen command also centers density map contours.

Density map selection can be disabled. To enable or disable
density map selection, see the X-ray page of the Preferences dialog.

To export density maps to external files

To export a Density Map to an external file, select a contour of the map and choose File | Save As... from the menu bar. In the Save As dialog, change the Files of Type to either CNX Map Files ( *.map ) or Quanta Brick Map Files ( *.mbk ) .

Density map selection can be disabled. To enable or disable density map selection,
see the X-ray page of the Preferences dialog.

It is recommended that you give the density map a different name from the structure. This allows you to immediately import
the density map back into the application without having to save and close your structure.

To import density maps from external files

To import a Density Map file into a Molecule Window, execute Insert From | File... from the File menu and select a file to insert. To narrow the file type search, change Files of Type to either CNX Map Files ( *.map ) or Quanta Brick Map Files ( *.mbk ) .

The imported density map is contoured by default at 1 σ (the RMSD of the density map). The display properties can be edited directly
in the Data Table View of the Molecule Window or by using the commands on the Structure | Isosurface menu. Additional contours of the density map are created using Structure | Isosurface | New Contour... .

Density map selection can be disabled. To enable or disable density map selection;
see the X-ray page of the Preferences dialog.

# How to use Density Maps and Contours

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/tsk_xray_hw_manipulating-contour-levels.htm

## How to use Density Maps and Contours

Contours of Density Maps are controlled mainly by the Density Map tab of the Data Table in the Molecule Window (they can also be controlled using the Structure | Isosurface menu). Each row in the table lists a contour with editable controls for the name, color, contour value and display extents.

Within the Density Map tab of the Data Table , a contour can have the following properties adjusted:

To adjust the Contour Level

* Double-click the Contour Level cell.

* Edit the contour level directly by typing in text portion of the cell.

To display extents

* Click the Viewing Extents cell and click the button to open the interactive Isosurface Edit Extents dialog box.

* Edit the values of the Width, Depth, and Height. As you move the sliders, the values in the Viewing Extents cell are updated automatically. The first three values in the Viewing Extents cell correspond to the X, Y, and Z location. The other three values correspond to the Width, Depth, and Height of the Isosurface.

To color contours

* Click the Color cell.

* Click the button to open the Select color dialog .

To add new contours

* Select a contour on the Density Map of interest.

* Choose Structure | Isosurface | New Contour... from the menu bar. A dialog will prompt you for the contour level.

To delete contours

Select the contour and press the delete key on your keyboard or choose Structure | Isosurface | Remove from the menu bar.

To display electron density contours using different scales

You can adjust contour levels using either unscaled density units or a relative scale in units of the density RMSD value. To do this, change the Display contour levels without electron density scaling option from the X-ray page of the Preferences dialog.

To hide or show contours

Hide or show contours using the Visibility commands on the View menu.

To disable or enable selection

You can disable or enable the selection of Density Map contours by changing the Disable Map selection in Molecule Window option in the X-ray page of the Preferences dialog.

Some commands require that a Density Map be selected.

### Information only fields

* Default Map for Build and Refine X-ray Structure: Shows whether the map is displayed (TRUE) or not (FALSE)

* Parent: If there is a parent, this field displays the parents of the listed map(s)

* Sigma Value: The standard deviation(s) of the listed maps

* Maximum Density: The largest value of the listed maps

* Minimum Density: the smallest value of the listed maps

# Working with X-ray data

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/usng_dvw_x-ray-reflection-data-window.htm

## Working with X-ray data

### Introduction to X-ray reflection data

The Reflection Data Window allows you to visualize the processed X-ray diffraction data
(H,K,L) and their corresponding intensities and/or amplitudes. The Reflection Data window
provides the current test set size, the total number of reflections, and allows you to quickly 
modify this value. A view of the Crystal Parameters is
also provided that allows you to quickly verify and modify the Space Group and Cell
parameters (cell length and cell angles) if needed. The data view window opens when you open 
one of the following reflection file formats:

* CCP4 Reflection Data (MTZ)

* CNX Reflection Data (CV, FOB, HKL)

* Discovery Studio X-ray Reflection Data (XDM)

* Scalepack Reflection (SCA)

Reflection data from RCSB CIF format structure factor files (-sf.cif, -sf.cif.gz) can 
be used as input to X-ray protocols but cannot be opened in Discovery Studio Client. 
For a general introduction to the PDBx/mmCIF format, see Beginner’s Guide to PDB Structures and the PDBx/mmCIF Format .
For details of CIF reflection data, see Data Category refln .

Three different views of the imported data are available from the following 
tabs:

* Contents : General information

* Crystal Parameters : Unit cell dimensions and space group

* View : Data table

Opening of a reflection file with the Reflection Data Window loads the X-ray data into 
memory. This process allows you to quickly input the reflection data into protocols 
used in macromolecular X-ray crystallography. Note that the protocols used for X-ray 
refinement and other crystallographic tasks are currently in development and will be available 
in future releases of Discovery Studio .

### Types of reflection data

Depending on the desired X-ray target function, the input reflection data file must
contain certain arrays and the array names must conform to the following naming conventions.

* MLHL : To use this target you must supply the following 
arrays: HLA (type: real), HLB (type: real), HLC (type: real), and HLD (type: real).

* MLI : When the crystallographic optimization is performed 
on this maximum likelihood target function, the arrays OBS_I (type: real) 
and OBS_SIGI (type: real) must be present in the input data.

* RESIDUAL : This target function requires the presence of 
the array OBS_W (type: real).

* VECTOR : To optimize this target function you must supply 
the arrays OBS_W (type: real) and OBS_PHASE (type: complex). Also, this target 
requires declaration of the array FCALC (type complex) in the input reflection 
file.

* MIXED : This target requires the following arrays: OBS_PHASE 
(type: complex) and OBS_FOM (type: real).

# Generate Electron Density Maps

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/x-ray_generate_electron_density_maps.htm

## Generate Electron Density Maps

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

The Generate Electron Density Maps protocol is used to generate one or more electron density maps from a molecular
structure and its corresponding X-ray reflection data. Three types of maps are available:

* Fo-Fc

* 2Fo-Fc

* 3Fo-2Fc

In addition, the map category can be adjusted to generate the following complex maps:

* Model Maps

* Annealed Omit Maps

* Composite Omit Maps

Additional options are available for adjusting various map generation parameters,
including the method of typing, defining the reflection data limits, and defining the reflection data test set.

Protein molecules will be detected automatically by the Input Protein Molecule parameter. However, you will need to explicitly point to the appropriate reflection data file.

For this release, only amplitude data will be used for all
X-ray related calculations. Working with Intensities or Phases is possible using CNX in standalone mode.

* Open the X-ray | Build and Refine X-ray Structure tools and click Generate Electron Density Maps... to open the Generate Electron Density Maps dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Protein Molecule Select the molecule you will be generating the electron density map for. Input Reflection Data Select a reflection data window or browse to a reflection data file for the protein molecule. For details about the remaining parameters, see Generate Electron Density Maps - Parameters . Only two parameters are required to run the protocol, an input structure and a reflection file. The protocol will automatically calculate the
resolution limits from the reflection data, but there is also an option to provide these values explicitly. In addition, the protocol will also
automatically extract the space group and cell information from the reflection data and/or the structure file. An automatic data consistency
check for space group and cell dimensions will be made. If the data provided by the reflection file is different from the
molecular structure data, the protocol will fail. In this case, you should check for space group and cell dimension consistency and rerun the protocol. The map generation protocol can create Fo - Fc, 2Fo - Fc, and/or 3Fo - 2Fc maps.
The weighting scheme is SigmaA by default. The generated maps can cover the entire molecule (or part), the crystal unit cell,
the asymmetric unit, or an arbitrarily defined box. The grid size is editable. By default, the exported maps are normalized and
the map format is CNX ascii.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Protein Molecule | Select the molecule you will be generating the electron density map for. |
| Input Reflection Data | Select a reflection data window or browse to a reflection data file for the protein molecule. |

For details about the remaining parameters, see Generate Electron Density Maps - Parameters .

Only two parameters are required to run the protocol, an input structure and a reflection file. The protocol will automatically calculate the
resolution limits from the reflection data, but there is also an option to provide these values explicitly. In addition, the protocol will also
automatically extract the space group and cell information from the reflection data and/or the structure file. An automatic data consistency
check for space group and cell dimensions will be made. If the data provided by the reflection file is different from the
molecular structure data, the protocol will fail. In this case, you should check for space group and cell dimension consistency and rerun the protocol.

The map generation protocol can create Fo - Fc, 2Fo - Fc, and/or 3Fo - 2Fc maps.
The weighting scheme is SigmaA by default. The generated maps can cover the entire molecule (or part), the crystal unit cell,
the asymmetric unit, or an arbitrarily defined box. The grid size is editable. By default, the exported maps are normalized and
the map format is CNX ascii.

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. If the job is sent to the background, the dialog window will close, allowing you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can then monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer . If the job is not sent to the background, the job will then continue to completion and a report window will be displayed. Various links to result files will be available to help you retrieve the output of the map generation run.

If the job was sent to the background, you can double click the Jobs Explorer and drag and drop your new map from the Output folder into your input structure that you used to generate the map from. The name of the map will follow the convention <molecule_name>_<map_type>.map , where the map_type is fo-fc, 2fo-fc, or 3fo-2fc. 
If the job was interactive, you can select the file called Density Map in the report that is displayed after the job completes, and then add the structure to the map by using the copy and paste function to include the input protein model into the same window. You may also use the File | Insert From | File and select the corresponding protein model.

Once the map is loaded, you can adjust various map properties from the Density tab in the Data Table View . Here you can change the viewing extents and change the color and the sigma level of the map.

Additional options for enabling or disabling map selection and contour
maps with or without scaling can be found on the X-ray
page of the Preferences dialog.

#### Troubleshooting

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files and the parameters used. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| <molecule_name>_<map_type>.map | Name of the generated map. For example: 2bla_2fo-fc.map would be the name of a 2fo-fc map for molecule with name 2bla . |
| cnx_map_stdout.txt | CNX log file from the map generation run. |

# Generate Electron Density Maps - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/x-ray_map_generation-para.htm

## Generate Electron Density Maps - Parameters

### Generates electron density maps for crystal structures

Generates electron density maps in CNX/CNS format (.map).

The map categories available are:

* Model Map

* Annealed Omit Map

* Composite Omit Map

The types of maps that can be generated are:

* 2Fo-Fc

* Fo-Fc

* 3Fo-2Fc

Note:

* Advanced options are available for solvent and initial B-factor correction, as well as options for different refinement target functions used for gradient weighting.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Protein Molecule | Selects a protein structure to read. |
| Input Reflection Data | Select a reflection data to read. |
| Field Mapping | Assigns field mapping for CNX/CNS format. |
| Amplitude Field | The field name for amplitudes. |
| Amplitude Deviation Field | The field name for amplitude standard deviation. |
| Intensity Field | The field name for intensities. |
| Intensity Deviation Field | The field name for intensity standard deviation. |
| Map Type | Specifies the type of map to generate. Map Type options include: 2Fo-Fc Fo-Fc 3Fo-2Fc Valid Values: 2Fo-Fc , Fo-Fc , 3Fo-2Fc |
| Keep Existing | If True and the input data record already has the forcefield assigned as specified by Forcefield Name , the input data record is turned out of the pass port without any change. Valid Values: True , False |
| Advanced | Options for advanced users wanting to modify various default parameters related to: Map Category Solvent Correction B-factor Correction Simulated Annealing Refinement Target Forcefield selection Resolution limits |
| Map Category | Specifies the category of map to generate. Model Map : Calculate a map using phases from the model. Annealed Omit Map : Calculate an annealed omit map with a spherical omitted region. Composite Omit Map : Calculate a composite annealed omit map. Valid Values: Model Map , Annealed Omit Map, Composite Omit Map |
| Solvent Correction | Specifies solvent correction method to use. Valid Values: none, babinet, mask |
| Initial B-factor Correction | Specifies an initial correction, known also as overall B-factor refinement, that can be applied to B-factors of model atoms. Three correction schemes are available: Isotropic : Applies an isotropic correction to the current model. Anisotropic : Applies the isotropic component of the correction to the model and the anisotropic component to the observed data. Anisotropic_fixed_isotropic : Applies only the anisotropic component of the correction to the data; the isotropic component is not applied to the model. Valid Values: none, isotropic, anisotropic-fixed isotropic, anisotropic |
| Simulated Annealing | Option to perform Simulated Annealing when the option for Map Category is selected to either: Annealed Omit Map or Composite Omit Map. Valid Values: True , False |
| Simulated Annealing Type | Specifies the type of simulated annealing to use. torsion : Performs the molecular dynamics in torsion angle space. By default you should use a value of 2500.0 for Starting Temperature . cartesian : Performs the molecular dynamics in Cartesian space. By default you should use a value of 500.0 for Starting Temperature . Valid Values: torsion , cartesian |
| Starting Temperature | Starting temperature to use for simulated annealing procedure. The default of 2500.0 is appropriate for Torsion Angle Dynamics simulated annealing. The value 500.0 should be used as a default for Cartesian Dynamics. |
| Temperature Drop per Cycle | Specifies the temperature drop for each cycle when using slow cooling simulated annealing. |
| Omit Atoms | Specifies the atoms to be omitted from the map calculation. This option is only used for an Annealed Omit Map. You should type in a selection, using the standard CNX atom specification. A region around these atoms is also omitted; the size of this region can be specified using the Size of Neighborhood Omitted parameter. Example of selection: chainid A and resid 23 |
| Size of Neighborhood Omitted | Specifies the size of the region around the atoms that is omitted for an Annealed Omit Map. |
| Maximum % of Model to be Omitted | Specifies the maximum percentage of the map to be omitted for a Composite Omit Map. This should be no more than 10%. |
| Refinement Target | When gradient weighting is selected, the map is weighted by the gradient of the crystallographic target with respect to Fc. Note: For this release of the collection, we will only support the mlf refinement target. However standalone CNX does supports a variety of refinement targets such as: mlf : Maximum likelihood target using amplitudes mli : Maximum likelihood target using intensities mlhl : Maximum likelihood target using amplitudes and phase probability distribution residual : Standard crystallographic residual vector : Vector residual mixed : (1-fom)*residual + fom*vector e2e2 : Correlation coefficient using normalized E2 1e1 : Correlation coefficient using normalized E f2f2 : Correlation coefficient using F2 f1f1 : Correlation coefficient using Fe Valid Values: mlf |
| Number of Bins | Number of bins to use during refinement (determined automatically if the value is -1). |
| Map | Options for Map generation: Map Weighting Scheme Map Normalization Map Grid Size List of atoms to Omit Selection of atoms used to build the map Extent of the map Map Cushion in Å |
| Map Weighting Scheme | Specifies the weighting scheme to use for map generation. Available weighting schemes: sigmaa : (u m\|Fo\| - v D\|Fc\|)^exp(i phi_calc), where m and D calculated from sigmaa. unweighted : (u \|Fo\| - v k\|Fc\|)^exp(i phi_calc), no figure-of-merit weighting. combined : (u m\|Fo\|^exp(i phi_comb) - v D\|Fc\|^exp(i phi_calc)), where model and experimental phases combined, m and D from sigmaa. observed : (u m\|Fo\|^exp(i phi_obs) - v k m\|Fc\|^exp(i phi_calc)), where observed phases and phase from probability distribution. gradient : d(target)/dFc, using gradient of the current crystallographic target with respect to Fc. Valid Values: sigmaa , unweighted, gradient |
| Normalize Map | If this is turned on the map is normalized by dividing by the rms sigma of the map. Otherwise, the map is on an absolute scale. Valid Values: True , False |
| Relative Map Grid Size | Specifies the resolution of the grid for maps, relative to the high-resolution limit of the reflection data. In general, the resolution of the grid for maps is 1/3 to 1/4 of the high resolution in reciprocal space. For example, given a relative grid size of 0.33, if the high-resolution limit of the diffraction data is 3 Å, the grid spacing of the map is about 1 Å in each dimension. Valid Values: 0.33 , 0.25 |
| Atom Selection | Specifies the atoms that are to be included in the map calculation. Valid Values: (all), (none), (known), (unknown), (hydrogen), (name CA), (name N or name CA or name C or name O), (not(name N or name CA or name C or name O)), (name N or name CA or name C or name O or name CB), (known and not hydrogen) |
| Extent | Defines how far the grid boundary points are from the solute as a percentage (%). Valid Values: molecule , asymmetric, unit, box, fractional |
| Map Cushion | Specifies size (in Å) of cushion around the molecule during map generation. |
| Forcefield Typing | Molecular Typing is performed automatically using forcefield based atom types and parameters provided by the XPROLIG forcefield. An alternate option for parameter and topology definition has been included using the third party algorithm XPLO2D for ligand atom typing, and the generate.inp script for protein typing. Setting the parameter Forcefield Name to XPLO2D will use the generate.inp molecular typing procedure. Please ensure that the XPLO2D executable has been properly installed as per the instructions provided in the Forcefield Name parameter help. Note: The XPLO2D code is licensed by the UPPSALA Software factory, and any inquiries should be made directly to: http://xray.bmc.uu.se/usf |
| Forcefield Name | Specifies which forcefield to assign. For XPLO2D , you need to have the lx_xplo2d executable installed, and set up the global property lx_xplo2d_exe to point to the executable. For example, set lx_xplo2d_exe to /opt/xutil_linux/lx_xplo2d . You can use SciTegic Server Administration Portal to set up lx_xplo2d_exe for all users. Note: Currently only the Linux version of lx_xplo2d is available. See Also: http://xray.bmc.uu.se/mbprogs/mb_usf.html Valid Values: XPROLIG , XPLO2D |
| XPROLIG | The XPROLIG forcefield is a CHARMm based forcefield which has been designed to automate the process of molecular typing for X-ray refinement using CNX. Modifications to the estimated forcefield parameters can be easily made using the Discovery Studio Client. |
| Input FFML Filename | The FFML file which may contain customized parameters and atom types. When specified, this will override the Forcefield Name parameter. |
| Automatic Parameter Estimation | Specifies whether automatic parameter estimation is on or off. The default is True . Valid Values: True , False |
| Reflection Data Limits | Reflection Data resolution limits are automatically calculated and used by the protocol. These limits may be overwritten by providing values for these two parameters: High Resolution Limit Low Resolution Limit |
| High Resolution Limit | Limit on the reflection data that will be used for the individual coordinates and B-factor refinement. If left blank, values will be derived from the reflection data set. |
| Low Resolution Limit | Limit on the reflection data that will be used for the individual coordinates and B-factor refinement. If left blank, values will be derived from the reflection data set. |
| Reflection Data Test Set | The following parameters allow the user to keep the existing selection of reflections to be used for the R-free calculation. The selection may be made anew , by setting the Keep Existing parameter to False . The percentage of reflections selected for the test set may also be defined by the Probability parameter. A threshold for the number of reflections selected for the test set is also provided to avoid nonsense refinement. |
| Reflection Data Test Set Keep Existing | Keep the existing test set unless its TestSetPercentage is zero or 1. Valid Values: True , False |
| Probability | Specified the probability that a reflection is to be selected into the test set. |
| Percentage Threshold | The data record is to be turned out of the Fail port if its TestSetPercentage is larger than the specified value. |

# Validate Model Molecule - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/x-ray_model_validation-para.htm

## Validate Model Molecule - Parameters

### Validates crystal structure using a set of test criteria

Tests the quality of the input structure by assessing the following:

* Bond length violations.

* CA-CA distance violations.

* Valence angle violations.

* Peptide bond planarity violations.

* Cis peptide bonds.

* Ramachandran map violations.

* Planarity violations.

* Chi1 angle violations.

* Chi2 angle violations.

* Chirality violations.

* Non-bonded clashes.

* Residue B-factor distribution.

Note:

* Additional tests may be accessible by promoting parameters from the Run DS_XRay_validate.inp component from the CNX Validate Model main component. You will need access to the Pipeline Pilot Client to do this.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Protein Molecule | Select a protein structure to read. |
| Input Reflection Data | Select a reflection data to read. |
| Field Mapping | Assigns field mapping for CNX/CNS format. |
| Amplitude Field | The field name for amplitude. |
| Amplitude Deviation Field | The field name for amplitude standard deviation. |
| Intensity Field | The field name for intensity. |
| Intensity Deviation Field | The field name for intensity standard deviation. |
| Structure Quality | Specifies the structure quality, which is used to determine the default thresholds to be used for reporting violations. Valid Values: refined , partially_refined, high_resolution |
| Solvent Correction | Specifies solvent correction method to use. Valid Values: mask , babinet, none |
| Rotamer Library | Specifies the rotamer library to be used for verifying side-chain torsion angles. Valid Values: Ponder_Richards , Sutcliffe, Oldfield |
| Advanced | Advanced options for selecting which type of structure tests to perform. |
| Structure Tests | Test Bond Length Violations: Specifies to check all bond lengths. Test CA-CA Distances: Specifies to check for deviations of distances between adjacent CA atoms along the protein chain. Tests are only to be performed between CA's within a single chain. Test Valence Angle Violations: Specifies to check all valence angles. Test Peptide Bond Planarity Violations: Specifies to check for non-planar peptides by checking for deviations of omega torsion angles from the expected values of 0 or 180 degrees. Test Cis Peptide Bonds: Specifies to check Cis Peptide bonds by listing all omega torsion angles that are between -90 and +90 degrees. Test Ramachandran Map Violations: Specifies to test for Ramachandran map violations. Lists the phi and the psi values of all residues and specifies whether that lie inside the core (hard sphere) region ("OK"), between the hard sphere region and the 10% overlap region ("PARTIAL"), or outside the 10% overlap region ("EXCLUDED") of the Ramachandran Map. Test Planarity Violations: Specifies to check for planarity violations, which are evaluated by measuring violations of improper torsion angles and reporting those that correspond to groups that should be planar. Test Chi1 Angle Violations: Specifies to check Chi1 angles against values defined in the rotamer library (independently of backbone or other side-chain torsion angles; that is, it checks only Chi1, not correct Chi1/Chi2 combinations). Test Chi2 Angle Violations: Specifies to check Chi2 angles against values defined in the rotamer library (independently of backbone or other side-chain torsion angles; that is, it checks only Chi2, not correct Chi1/Chi2 combinations). Test Chirality Violations: Specifies to check chirality violations, evaluated by measuring violations of improper torsion angles and reporting those that correspond to chiral atoms (CA or side chain). Incorrect chirality is indicated by an improper torsion angle with the wrong sign. Deviations of a few degrees indicates distortion, but not incorrect chirality. Test Non-Bonded Clashes: Specifies to check for non-bonded clashes by calculating non-bonded distances. Checks for real-symmetry atom clashes as well as real-real atom clashes. Test Residue B-factor Distribution: Specifies to test for residue B-factor distribution, producing a table of the B-factors for each residue (averaged over all atoms in the residue). Valid Values: Bond Length Violations , CA-CA Distances , Valence Angles Violations , Peptide Bond Planarity Violations , Cis Peptide Bonds , Ramachandran Map Violations , Planarity Violations , Chi1 Angle Violations , Chi2 Angle Violations , Chirality Violations , Non-Bonded Clashes , Residue B-factor Distribution |
| Threshold for Bond Length Violations | Threshold to use for bond length violations, in Å. |
| Threshold for CA-CA Distances | Threshold for deviations from CA-CA distances, in Å. |
| Threshold for Valence Angle Violations | Threshold to use for valence angle violations, in degrees. |
| Threshold for Peptide Planarity Violations | Threshold to use for peptide planarity violations, in degrees. |
| Ramachandran Tolerance | Tolerance to use for Ramachandran map violations checking. |
| List Ramachandran Maps for All Residues | If True, lists all residues in the output of the Ramachandran Map check. Otherwise, only residues in disallowed regions are listed. Valid Values: True , False |
| Threshold for Planarity Violations | Threshold to use for planarity violations, in degrees. |
| Threshold for Chi1 Violations | Threshold to use for Chi1 violations, in degrees. |
| Threshold for Chi2 Violations | Threshold to use for Chi2 violations, in degrees. |
| Threshold for Chirality Violations | Threshold to use for monitoring chirality violations, in degrees. |
| Threshold for Non-Bonding Clashes | Threshold to use for identifying non-bond clashes, in Å. |

* Test Bond Length Violations: Specifies to check all bond lengths.

* Test CA-CA Distances: Specifies to check for deviations of distances between adjacent CA atoms along the protein chain. Tests are only to be performed between CA's within a single chain.

* Test Valence Angle Violations: Specifies to check all valence angles.

* Test Peptide Bond Planarity Violations: Specifies to check for non-planar peptides by checking for deviations of omega torsion angles from the expected values of 0 or 180 degrees.

# Pick Water

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/x-ray_pick_water.htm

## Pick Water

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

The Pick Water protocol generates a map (default: Fo - Fc; SigmaA), and then searches for unoccupied electron density.
The positions of the density peaks detected in the map are tentatively assigned to water molecules. The chosen peaks
are then filtered based on peak height, proximity to protein atoms, and to other water molecules. H-bonding geometry and
distance can assist in filtering of viable candidates to remain as water molecules. Waters can be removed from special positions,
and can also be shifted (i.e., subjected to symmetry operations) to the same asymmetric unit as the protein structure.
Water B-factor values are allowed to vary within a user-defined maximum range.

The protocol requires a protein model and a reflection data set as input. Other options include:

* Selection of maximum number of density peaks to search

* Type of map to be used in the water picking process

* Distance-based criteria for filtering of selected waters

* Coordinate and B-factor minimization of model after addition of waters

* Resolution range

* Solvent correction

* Map Generation of final model

* Load the structure you want to add waters to into a Molecule Window.

* Open the X-ray | Build and Refine X-ray Structure tools and click Pick Water... to open the Pick Water dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Protein Molecule Choose the loaded structure. Input Reflection Data Select a reflection data window or browse for the reflection file of
the input molecule. For details about the remaining parameters, see Pick Water - Parameters .

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Protein Molecule | Choose the loaded structure. |
| Input Reflection Data | Select a reflection data window or browse for the reflection file of the input molecule. |

For details about the remaining parameters, see Pick Water - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. If the job is sent to the background, the dialog window will close allowing you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can then monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer . If the job is not sent to the background, the job will then continue to completion and a report window will be displayed. Various links to result files will be available to help you retrieve the output of the water placement run.

If the results were sent to the background, open <name of molecule>_water.mol2 from the Output folder to start your inspection of the waters placed. Optionally, you can copy or paste the input protein model into the same window, or choose File | Insert From | File... from the menu bar and insert the initial protein model with the goal of comparing the models before and after the run. 
If the job was run interactively, a report opens automatically. From the report, open Structure with Water to start your analysis of the waters placed.

#### Troubleshooting

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

# Place Ligands - Parameters

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/x-ray_place_ligands-para.htm

## Place Ligands - Parameters

### Automatically places ligands into an electron density map

Generates or reads an electron density map, and automatically places one or more ligands into the non-occupied X-ray electron density.

The main process of placing a ligand involves the following steps:

* Site search of available density.

* Conformational search of the ligand.

* Real-space refinement of the ligand into electron density.

Enhancements to the ligand placement methodology encompass the ability to accurately place multiple ligands for a single receptor expected to have multiple ligands present.

The full process is described in the following steps:

* Initial Search for first ligand with Sigma N : The algorithm will search the electron density map for non-occupied sites for the first ligand (sites 1 to m). For each of the top sites, ligand conformations are generated and scored according to their fit to the electron density. The top conformation is further refined using real-space refinement, and its score stored.

* Second Search for first ligand with Sigma N-0.5 : Using a gradient step of 0.5 sigma units, several sigma levels may be used to find the best fit possible for a ligand, by comparing the new ligand fit score to the previously stored score. Such strategy enables the program to deal with cases in which ligands have poor density or excess unoccupied density is available, which may prevent the proper placement of a ligand.

The same process is then repeated for the next input ligand. By having the first ligand placed into electron density, only updated available density will be used during the Site Search step.

Note :

* To prevent fitting ligands to density which is clearly too small for the size of the ligand, we have implemented an arbitrary rejection criteria called Rejection Threshold . Rejection of a ligand placement solution will occur if the best density fit score divided by the ligand's Molecular_Weight is less than the specified value (default=9). This value is arbitrary and may need to be adjusted by the user on a case by case basis.

### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Receptor | Select a protein structure to read. |
| Input Density Map | Select a density map to read. If no density map is available, select Input Reflection Data to generate the density map. |
| Input Reflection Data | Select a reflection data to read. |
| Field Mapping | Assigns field mapping for CNX/CNS format. |
| Amplitude Field | The field name for amplitude. |
| Amplitude Deviation Field | The field name for amplitude standard deviation. |
| Intensity Field | The field name for intensity. |
| Intensity Deviation Field | The field name for intensity standard deviation. |
| Input Ligands | Select one or more ligands to read. |
| Place Ligands by Weight | If True, heavier ligands will be placed first. Otherwise ligands will be placed in the order in which they were read. Note: It is recommended to place larger ligands first, in order to avoid placing smaller ligands into electron density belonging to a larger ligand. Valid Values: True , False |
| Place Ligands | Place Ligands Settings related to: Sigma Threshold Top Sites Search Conformations Perform Real Space Refinement Rejection Threshold criteria |
| Sigma Threshold | Specifies the map level (in sigma) at which the search for possible ligand sites is made. Higher thresholds result in more sites being found and also increase the extent of the volume of each site that does not overlap the protein. Lower thresholds often result in the overlap of sites, giving fewer, larger sites. In general, set the value to 1.5 for 2Fo-Fc density maps and 2.5 for Fo-Fc density maps. |
| Top Sites | Specifies the number of top sites (sorted by volume) used for conformation searches and refinement. Increase the value if the fit conformations are expected to be very different from the input ones. |
| Search Conformations | If True , searches possible conformations to find the fittest conformation for each ligand. Searching will stop if either the conformations converge or the time elapses as defined by the Search Time parameter. Valid Values: True , False |
| Search Time | Specified the maximum time in minutes for conformation searching. |
| Fit in Stages | Fits the portions of the ligand with better density (based on shape-matching) before fitting the rest of the ligand molecule. Valid Values: True , False |
| Real Space Refinement | If True , performs a real space refinement calculation on the placed ligand. The positions, orientations, and all defined torsion angles, are refined to the electron density by least squares. Valid Values: True , False |
| Rejection Threshold | A ligand placement is to be rejected if the best density fit score divided by the ligand's Molecular_Weight is less than the specified value. |
| Advanced | Options for advanced users wanting to modify various default parameters related to: Map Generation Resolution limits Forcefield selection |
| Map | Maps used for ligand placement are Model Maps . Additional options are available: Type Refinement Target Solvent Correction |
| Map Type | Specifies the type of map to generate. Valid Values: 2Fo-Fc, 3Fo-2Fc, Fo-Fc |
| Map Weighting Scheme | Specifies the weighting scheme to use for map generation. Available weighting schemes: sigmaa : Weights calculated from sigmaA unweighted : No figure-of-merit weighting gradient : Gradient of the current crystallographic target with respect to Fc Note: Two additional weighting schemes are available from CNX standalone: combined : Combines model and experimental phases. observed : Uses observed phases and fom from phase probability distribution. Valid Values: sigmaa , unweighted, gradient |
| Normalize Map | If this is turned on the map is normalized by dividing by the rms sigma of the map. Otherwise, the map is on an absolute scale. Valid Values: True , False |
| Relative Map Grid Size | Specifies the resolution of the grid for maps, relative to the high-resolution limit of the reflection data. In general, the resolution of the grid for maps is 1/3 to 1/4 of the high resolution in reciprocal space. For example, given a relative grid size of 0.33, if the high-resolution limit of the diffraction data is 3 Å, the grid spacing of the map is about 1 Å in each dimension. Valid Values: 0.33 , 0.25 |
| Extent | Defines how far the grid boundary points are from the solute as a percentage (%). Valid Values: molecule , asymmetric, unit, box, fractional |
| Map Cushion | Specifies size (in Å) of cushion around the molecule during map generation. |
| Refinement Target | When gradient weighting is selected, the map is weighted by the gradient of the crystallographic target with respect to Fc. Note: For this release of the collection, we will only support the mlf refinement target. However standalone CNX does supports a variety of refinement targets such as: mlf : Maximum likelihood target using amplitudes. mli : Maximum likelihood target using intensities. mlhl : Maximum likelihood target using amplitudes and phase probability distribution. residual : Standard crystallographic residual. vector : Vector residual. mixed : (1-fom)*residual + fom*vector. e2e2 : Correlation coefficient using normalized E2. 1e1 : Correlation coefficient using normalized E. f2f2 : Correlation coefficient using F2. f1f1 : Correlation coefficient using Fe. Valid Values: mlf |
| Number of Bins | Number of bins to use during refinement (determined automatically if the value is -1). |
| Solvent Correction | Specifies solvent correction method to use. Valid Values: none, babinet, mask |
| Reflection Data Limits | Reflection Data resolution limits are automatically calculated and used by the protocol. These limits may be overwritten by providing values for these two parameters: High Resolution Limit Low Resolution Limit |
| High Resolution Limit | Limit on the reflection data that will be used for the individual coordinates and B-factor refinement. If left blank, values will be derived from the reflection data set. |
| Low Resolution Limit | Limit on the reflection data that will be used for the individual coordinates and B-factor refinement. If left blank, values will be derived from the reflection data set. |
| Forcefield Typing | Molecular Typing is performed automatically using forcefield based atom types and parameters provided by the XPROLIG forcefield. An alternate option for parameter and topology definition has been included using the third party algorithm XPLO2D for ligand atom typing, and the generate.inp script for protein typing. Setting the parameter Forcefield Name to XPLO2D will use the generate.inp molecular typing procedure. Please ensure that the XPLO2D executable has been properly installed as per the instructions provided in the Forcefield Name parameter help. Note: The XPLO2D code is licensed by the UPPSALA Software factory, and any inquiries should be made directly to: http://xray.bmc.uu.se/usf |
| Forcefield Name | Specifies which forcefield to assign. For XPLO2D , you need to have the lx_xplo2d executable installed, and set up the global property lx_xplo2d_exe to point to the executable, for example set lx_xplo2d_exe to /opt/xutil_linux/lx_xplo2d . You can use SciTegic Server Administration Portal to set up lx_xplo2d_exe for all users. Note: Currently only the Linux version of lx_xplo2d is available. See Also: http://xray.bmc.uu.se/usf Valid Values: XPROLIG , XPLO2D |
| Keep Existing | If True and the input data record already has the forcefield assigned as specified by Forcefield Name , the input data record is turned out of the pass port without any change. Valid Values: True , False |
| XPROLIG | The XPROLIG forcefield is a CHARMm based forcefield which has been designed to automate the process of molecular typing for X-ray refinement using CNX. Modifications to the estimated forcefield parameters can be easily made using the Discovery Studio Client. |
| Input FFML Filename | The FFML file which may contain customized parameters and atom types. When specified, this will override the Forcefield Name parameter. |
| Automatic Parameter Estimation | Specifies whether automatic parameter estimation is on or off. This is only applicable to the CHARMm forcefield. The default is true. Valid Values: True , False |

# Place Ligands

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/x-ray_place_ligands.htm

## Place Ligands

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Analyzing results

The Place Ligands protocol will automatically position one or more ligands into unoccupied electron density. The process of placing a ligand involves the following steps:

* Site Search: A search for unoccupied electron density representing the putative location of the ligand is performed, and possible sites are ranked
according to their size.

* Conformational Search: Ligand conformations are generated and ranked according to their fit to the
electron density. The longer the conformational search is performed, the higher the likelihood of finding
a better matching ligand conformation that fits the electron density will be.

* Real-Space Refinement: Final stage of the ligand placement process. The position of the ligand is automatically
optimized using real-space fitting techniques that improve the overall fit of the ligand to the electron density.

Additional enhancements to the ligand placement methodology include the ability to accurately place multiple ligands for a single receptor expected to have multiple bound ligands.
The process is as follows:

* Initial Search for the first ligand with Sigma N: The algorithm searches the electron density map for non-occupied sites
for the first ligand (sites 1 to m). For each of the top sites, ligand conformations are generated and scored according to
their fit to the electron density. The top conformation is further refined using real-space refinement, and its score stored.

* Second Search for the first ligand with Sigma N-0.5: Using a gradient step of 0.5 sigma units, a range of sigma levels
may be used to find the best fit possible for a ligand by comparing the new ligand fit score to the previously score. This
strategy deals with cases where ligands have poor density or excess unoccupied density is available, which may prevent the proper placement of a ligand.

The same process is then repeated for the next input ligand. By having the first ligand placed into electron density, only the updated density is used during the Site Search step.

There is an arbitrary criteria, Rejection Threshold, that prevents fitting ligands to density that is too small for the ligand. A ligand placement solution is rejected
if the best density fit score divided by the ligand's Molecular_Weight is less than the specified value (default is 9). This
value is arbitrary and can be adjusted on a case-by-case basis.

* Load a receptor into a Molecule Window.

* Load one or more ligand molecules into another Molecule Window.

* Open the X-ray | Place and Refine X-ray Ligand tools and click Place Ligands... to open the Place Ligands dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Receptor Choose the loaded receptor. Input Ligands Choose the loaded ligands to be placed into electron density. For details, see Specifying Ligands . Input Reflection Data The protocol can read an electron density map directly or it can calculate one on the fly. Use this parameter to select a reflection data window or browse for an appropriate reflection file to automatically calculate the electron density map. Place Ligands | Rejection Threshold The default value for this parameter is 9. However if no ligands are placed, you should lower this value. For details about the remaining parameters, see Place Ligands - Parameters .

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Receptor | Choose the loaded receptor. |
| Input Ligands | Choose the loaded ligands to be placed into electron density. For details, see Specifying Ligands . |
| Input Reflection Data | The protocol can read an electron density map directly or it can calculate one on the fly. Use this parameter to select a reflection data window or browse for an appropriate reflection file to automatically calculate the electron density map. |
| Place Ligands \| Rejection Threshold | The default value for this parameter is 9. However if no ligands are placed, you should lower this value. |

For details about the remaining parameters, see Place Ligands - Parameters .

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. If the job is sent to the background, the dialog window will close allowing you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can then monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer . If the job is not sent to the background, the job will then continue to completion and a report window will be displayed. Various links to the result files will be available to help you retrieve the output of the ligand placement job.

The goal of a Place Ligands calculation is to automatically position ligand molecules into available electron density.
As with any automated tool, results need to be verified prior to further refinement.
To verify the results, open <molecule>_complex.mol2 , and drag and drop in the corresponding electron density file. If an Fo-Fc map was used for the calculation, then drag and drop the file named <molecule>_fo-fc.map .

Once the files are loaded you will need to adjust the Contour Level of the map. Display the Data Table
by pressing CTRL+T , and then click the Density Map tab. For Fo-Fc maps
enter the value of 2.5 , which will render the difference map at 2.5 sigma level. Select the ligand from the structure, and then click Fit To Screen in the toolbar. The electron density will be rendered around the ligand and you will be able to visually assess the
quality of the fit.

#### Troubleshooting

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names may differ from those listed here:

| File name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Report.htm | Job summary including input and output files, summary of experiment information such as Unit Cell, Space Group, resolution limits used, and calculated values for R-factor and R-free. The report also indicates all of the parameters used in the calculation. |
| Output.log | Detailed messages generated by the protocol. If errors occur during the run, they are listed here. |
| <molecule>_complex.mol2 | The output structure of the protein-ligand complex after ligand placement. |
| <molecule>_fo-fc.map or <molecule>_2fo-fc.map | The map used for placement of ligands. |
| cnx_map_stdout.txt | CNX raw log file of the map generation step. |

#### Further information

Validate Model Molecule

# Refinement Cascade

Source type: HTML

Source section: tsxray

Source file: tsxray/x-ray_refinement_cascade.htm

## Refinement Cascade

* Description

* Setting up and running

* Troubleshooting

The Refinement Cascade protocol has been designed to perform a series of refinement steps on a molecular structure
having its corresponding X-ray reflection file. The refinement steps are performed in the following order:

* Rigid Body Minimization

* Simulated Annealing

* Coordinate Minimization

* Group Occupancy Minimization

* Individual Occupancy Minimization

* Group B-factor Minimization

* Individual B-factor Minimization

* Residue B-factor Minimization

* Generate Electron Density Maps

You are not required to perform all the steps in the cascade. Every
step in the cascade is optional, and depending on the refinement strategy, certain steps may not be necessary as the
structure becomes further refined.

* Load the structure you wish to refine into the 3D Structure View.

* Open the X-ray | Build and Refine X-ray tools and click Refinement Cascade... to open the Refinement Cascade dialog. You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

You can also run this protocol using the Protocols Explorer .

* Set the following parameters: Parameter Description Input Protein Molecule Choose the loaded structure. Input Reflection Data Select a reflection data window or browse for the reflection file of
the molecule being refined. Refinement Cascade Check the box for the refinement step you want to perform.
Refinement steps left unchecked will be excluded from the refinement. For details about the remaining parameters, see Refinement Cascade - Parameters . The Torsion Angle Dynamics option supports up to 20 independent topological entities. In addition, torsion dynamics should not be used as a simulated annealing method for protein-ligand complexes. Ligands may be added to the refinement process once the model has converged using the simulated annealing methodology.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input Protein Molecule | Choose the loaded structure. |
| Input Reflection Data | Select a reflection data window or browse for the reflection file of the molecule being refined. |
| Refinement Cascade | Check the box for the refinement step you want to perform. Refinement steps left unchecked will be excluded from the refinement. |

For details about the remaining parameters, see Refinement Cascade - Parameters .

The Torsion Angle Dynamics option supports up to 20 independent topological entities. In addition, torsion dynamics should not be used as a simulated annealing method for protein-ligand complexes. Ligands may be added to the refinement process once the model has converged using the simulated annealing methodology.

* Click Run to start the calculation.

The job status is displayed in a dialog that includes an option to send the job to background. If the job is sent to the background, the dialog window will close allowing you to continue using Discovery Studio while the job runs. You can then monitor the status of a background job and open the results from the Jobs Explorer . If the job is not sent to the background, the job will then continue to completion and a report window will be displayed. Various links to result files will be available to help you retrieve the output of the refinement run.

If there were problems with the results, you can inspect the individual output files that were generated by the run. The following files are created in the Output directory. The file names and their order may differ from those listed here:

Some files are only created when certain options are selected.

| cnx_map_stdout.txt | CNX log file for the map generation run. |

If the option to keep the Intermediate folder was selected, the following files will also be available. The file names and their order may differ from those listed here:

| anneal_best.pdb | Coordinate file of the molecule after all the simulated annealing refinement steps. |
